name: Katsu-Hama
document: Katsu-Hama. cuisine: Japanese. located in New York. at 11 East 47th Street. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Katsu Hama is a no-frills Japanese spot specializing in pork katsu, and they might just be the masters of it. It is possibly the best I’ve had outside of Japan. The katsu is surprisingly light, not greasy at all, and I didn’t feel heavy/“yeet hay” after finishing the entire set.

I went on a weekday night and didn’t have to wait for a table. The restaurant has plenty of seating, though it felt a bit understaffed.

＊5th Avenue Set $25
I wanted to try a bit of everything so I got one of their assorted sets, which came with pork loin, prawn, and shrimp cream croquette. I felt like this is a smart move as I was so amazed by how delicious the prawn and the croquette were, even though they specialize in pork. The prawn was HUGE, meaty and bouncy, while the croquette was creamy with bits of shrimp meat.

＊Berkshire Pork Loin Katsu Curry $27
I personally prefer the pork loin over this berkshire pork loin, which was more expensive but somehow tougher than the pork loin. It was indeed meatier, but it was tougher. The curry though was surprisingly delicious. They didn’t only use store-bought curry cubes as I could taste bits of beef (?) in the curry.

** Set A comes with miso soup, cabbage salad, and potato salad, while Set B is about $2 cheaper and comes with everything except the potato salad.

It was fine. You really couldn’t put your name on  waitlist as they seat by table+size availability. This spot had decently large portions. I don’t love Katsu but people said it was very good. I liked that I could have a full meal if appetizers like agedasho tofu (recommend), eggplant, and okonomiaki. I wish the okonomiaki was a little less organized but recognize this spot is primarily a Katsu spot.

Casual katsu place in midtown. The katsu is very good, crispy not greasy, tender but with a nice chew. The fried shrimp is also really good. We ordered the sashimi salad and tofu agedashi. Both were served after we received our main dish, a timing issue. Either way I would skip both these dishes next time. The fish was fresh but the salad and dressing were meh. The tofu was a bit soggy. Stick to the katsu which comes with shredded cabbage that you douse with their homemade dressing that was very good. I got the katsu curry, curry was delish. Also tried the KATSUDON also very good. We had the Berkshire pork but you can opt for the regular pork if you want. Just rating the Katsu, would give it 5 stars

I read the latest comments and I’m surprised about the service critics as the host was very friendly and efficient when he saw us with our toddler.

Wait time was around 8 minutes for lunch.

The Berkshire Loin Katsu Teishoku was Wow! Juicy and lots of flavor, good presentation.

Chicken Katsu Curry was very very crispy! Loved it! I can’t remember the last time I had one like that. Perfect juicy and crispy! I wish it had more pieces! The rice was also very good and the curry sauce was very good, not as spicy and it had some ingredient that made it taste a bit different than the traditional, more to a little sweetness at the end.

The service from the rest of the team was very good. It’s the first we go to a restaurant where the server understand our needs with a toddler and offered to bring us the rice 🍚 bowl for him in advanced! Love that!

We will certainly come back and I’d Highly Recommend it!

This jap restaurant has been my go-to whenever I'm in new york. My ultimate comfort food whatever season it is. I cant recommend and rate this enough.

I always order the same thing and it hits me hard every single time. I order this combo, cheese tonkatsu with tempura and potato croquette. Tastes quality and everything goes well together. Paired with Sapporo, my fave japanese beer.

Service was quick and the staff are fairly nice. I always dine solo so I dont really have to wait that long. Atmosphere was perfect for me too.

name: Up Thai
document: Up Thai. cuisine: Thai. located in New York. at 1411 2nd Avenue. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Absolutely loved the food at Up Thai! Poh Tak Thai-style was comforting and flavorful, packed with fresh shrimp, mussels, and squid. The broth was aromatic, and the garlic bread on top was a perfect touch. Everything tasted fresh and well-balanced. Also, The host(Jern) was incredibly kind and welcoming. Definitely coming back!

We decided to have lunch here recently and check out the lunch specials.  The location is in the middle of the block on second avenue between 73 and 74. It was really busy and there is very little warm space to stand as we waited for a table.
The lunch specials menu is pretty good. Lots of choices.
We ordered Pad Khing with beef and   Kya Gai with chicken.  Large portions. We each had tofu vegetable soup and I got crispy spring Roll and she got steamed dumplings.  All very tasty.
A lively place full of young people, many Asians.
Prices are very reasonable.
Definitely will go again.

What an amazing a meal! The standout dishes for me were the Hoi Jor, Crispy Shrimp and Squid, Duck Tamarind and Beef Short Rib Panang. Service was great and the decor was on point! I think they just finished remodeling the restaurant. Highly recommend!

This was my second time at Up Thai and it somehow managed to be even better than the first. I came straight from Brazil with my mom and was truly impressed to see how packed and vibrant the restaurant is. It’s clearly a place people love coming back to, and now I understand why.

The food is absolutely outstanding and the quality is consistently impeccable. Every dish is beautifully prepared and full of flavor.

What made the evening even more special was the service. Pearl and Mali were exceptional. They were warm, attentive, incredibly professional, and made us feel genuinely welcomed. Their hospitality elevated the entire experience.

Up Thai is one of those rare restaurants where everything works perfectly: the food, the atmosphere, and the people. I will absolutely come back every time I’m in New York and will continue recommending it to everyone I know.

FOOD WAS INCREDIBLE deceivingly large portions. 4 guys came to eat and we got 4 entrees and 2 appetizers and had leftovers. We were serviced by Malee and she was the sweetest, super attentive to us and made this experience so seamless

name: Soothr
document: Soothr. cuisine: Thai Noodles Cocktail Bars. located in New York. at East 13th Street. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Our dinner was absolutely spectacular! Our server, Nina was warm, attentive, and offered excellent recommendations that truly elevated the entire experience. It was a great dining experience thanks to her!

We started with the Lobster and Ha Gao from the Lunar New Year menu. The lobster was incredibly delicious which perfectly cooked and generously coated in a spicy sauce that complemented the sweetness of the meat beautifully. The Ha Gao were delicate and flavorful, with a satisfying bite.

The Hoo Johr was also a standout! It was crispy on the outside, savory on the inside, and perfect as an appetizer to share.

For our mains, the Panang Duck Lychee Curry was hands down the best rich, creamy, and packed with bold flavors, with just the right balance of sweetness from the lychee. The Shrimp Pad Thai was equally impressive, featuring plump shrimp, well-balanced seasoning, and perfectly cooked noodles.

We ended the meal with mango sticky rice. Even though mango isn’t in season, the dessert was absolutely amazing! The sticky rice was warm and fragrant, paired with sweet coconut milk, mango Ice cream and fresh mango.. it was the perfect ending to a fantastic dinner. Highly recommend!

This restaurant  really blow my mind  and reset my taste  for thai food. I have always like it.  Been on several restaurants. But none like Soothr.  Food was amazing. Unique experience with each bite.  Service  was fantastic, and staff supper friendly . Restaurant overall is everything  you need if u looking for great food.

We start with some crispy Chiken,  fried dumplings 10/10   pad thai 😍, duck in curry sauce, wow 👌  those too were also fantastic. Can't wait to go back  .  Dessert  was sweet and delicious...
While im writing this im having a smile in my face,enjoying my food again

Had a great experience at Soothr today! Jesse provided excellent service, she was very attentive, friendly, and made us feel very welcome throughout the meal. The crab roe curry noodles (Karee Pu Noodles) were absolutely delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly balanced. The food came out quickly, and the overall service was efficient and very nice. Definitely would come back again!

I was in town for the weekend and couldn't wait to co to Soothr because of their reputation. I was starting to get packed and it was tight. It was like a Thai-Chinatown (Yaowarat) vibe. We were given an hour and a half time limit which is normal but I feel like we were being rushed.
Started off with drinks, I wasn't a fan of my cocktail. Duck egg rolls had more wood ear mushrooms than duck. I was excited about Karee Pu (crab curry) the texture of the noodles were great. The curry was extra thick and had a strong cumin taste to it, we weren't a fan. We also got the duck noodles, once again the noodles were great. The duck was cooked perfectly but the gravy was so sweet and that was it, sweet. I love Thai food because of the mix of flavors, sweet, spicy, sour, salty, but this place didn't do it for us. I really wanted to like it but we were pretty underwhelmed.

Jane was our server and did an amazing job explaining all the dishes and options! We went for the Valentine's special and the crab croquett and Yaowarat Pad Mii were delicious. Would come back and try some more next time! Thanks Jane for making our Valentine's memorable 🥹

name: Dim Sum Palace
document: Dim Sum Palace. cuisine: Dim Sum Seafood Cantonese. located in New York. at 28 West 56th Street. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Dim Sum Palace is an Excellent choice for old school Chinese fare.
Authentic flavors and served fresh and hot.
Service was friendly, genuine and our tabletop was never empty.
We ordered Fried shrimp, soup dumplings, meatballs, Mongolian beef, Honey walnut shrimp and Chix fried rice. Every dish was Superb in taste and presentation.
We had a Tremendous dinner and Thank You.

This hit the spot! Every few months I fly to NYC for the day--first flight in and last flight out--and this time, being from the midwest, I HAD to get my hands on some good dim sum before I left. I had been thinking about it all week, lol.

Well, Asian Jewels didn't mesh with my schedule, so I just said screw it and went to Manhattan to go to MoMA. I spent way more time there than expected and, with my flight time drawing closer, I realized I needed to get that dim sum I'd been craving for weeks, STAT.

Dim Sum Palace to the rescue! They were just around the corner from MoMA and on the way to the F train. The man who took my hurried order was polite and knowledgeable. Not even fifteen minutes later, I was on my way back to LGA with a fat bag of dim sum in tow.

With the exception of the pork buns (kinda mediocre, sorry), everything I had was fantastic. Their crystal shrimp dumplings, siu mai, and shrimp and sausage dumplings were all phenomenal and still tasted fresh by the time I cleared security. PSA: the shrimp, sausage, and chive dumplings will give you TERRIBLE breath, so be careful with what your plans are after you eat them lol. I owe the lady who sat next to me on my flight home an apology. 🤣😭

Worth it!!!
Friendly place. Dim sum was excellent we had the dim sum platter and shrimp beef and chicken fried rice. The food was great. Nice atmosphere
Wow! Me and my friend split the pork dumplings and the purple taro buns and we’re both full and satisfied. Delicious food.

Perfect dim Sum place in midtown. We didn’t have time to go to Chinatown and we really wanted authentic dim sum. Everything was delicious. Even the mochi for dessert. Service was efficient. The atmosphere was what you would expect for dim sum. Not the rolling cart kind of place though. Mark up the menu with your choices and get it hot. Then add more as desired.

name: Cuerno
document: Cuerno. cuisine: Steakhouses Seafood Mexican. located in New York. at 121 West 50th Street. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: This review is specifically for the Enrique Olvera tasting menu offered in early March. It consisted of crudites with guacamole, tortilla soup with lobster broth (delicious, this may have been my favorite dish), strip steak with black peppercorn sauce, radicchio salad with roquefort (another favorite), a mushroom side that included ants - gives it a crunchy taste I was told (I tried it but can't say I ate the whole thing), and finally the sweet corn tamal served with pixtle ice cream. The food was good - I can't say it was exceptional - especially at the price (with 2 cocktails and a bottle of water - $350 for one). What was exceptional is the service - warm, attentive, helpful - really welcoming. I will add this was after, for whatever reason, I was initially sat at the bar vs. at a table and offered zero service for over 30 minutes. I finally called over the manager and asked him why I was seated at the bar for the tasting menu. He was mortified and immediately sat me in the dining room and I was both very impressed and grateful for how beautifully the team recovered from an obvious snafu. Bottom line: Cuerno is a very beautiful midtown restaurant absolutely ideal for wining and dining business clients. For somebody who loves more intimate, cozy restaurants, it's a tad too corporate.

If you are looking for an elevated taste of Northern Mexico, look no further, Cuerno is an absolute must-visit.  Still processing the amazing service, atmosphere, and food that Cuerno provided. Amazing cocktails! Bartenders / Mixologists have a great knowledge of Mezcal and Tequila and make exquisite drinks. Started with Chicharron de Pulpo which was a unique flavorful take on octopus.  Taco Taquero was a true highlight of the overall experience. It was prepared tableside with salt-charred skirt steak, and bone marrow that's acts like butter- its indulgent, interactive, and easily 10/10.
Also had Ribeye, perfectly cooked in a salt crust, making it incredibly juicy packed with deep, smoky flavor. Coliflor Habanero, thecharcoal-roasted cauliflower with pistachio truffle habanero sauce was a superb side dish.

My experience at Cuerno was top notch. We were quickly offered tasty welcome drinks and offered sparkling wine after entrees on the house. We had the best server in JP. The service given by our JP was some of the best I’ve experienced. He was extremely knowledgeable about the cuisine down to the ingredients, notes, and locations it’s sourced from. The food was incredible. Some of the best food I’ve eaten. There were 5 different salsas served and the guacamole and chips were fresh. The ribeye con tuétano and the octopus appetizer were absolutely delicious. So tender and flavorful. They scooped the bone marrow on top of the ribeye and it brought the steak to another level! The cocktails were well crafted and explained perfectly by JP. The menu has detailed descriptions and celebrate Mexican cuisine in a way that’s so enriching. This was everything I wanted in a dining experience and they delivered on all pillars of great service. Cuerno is now one of my favorite restaurants. Well done! Cuerno will become one of your favorites too!

My husband and I celebrated our wedding anniversary at Cuerno on 11/13. Despite the packed, bustling dining room, we were seated immediately at a table with a lovely view of Radio City. Our waiter JP gave us a warm introduction and enthusiastically supported our pre-researched choices while offering thoughtful drink recommendations.

The complimentary chips and salsas were phenomenal with warm, fresh chips and a flight of salsas (the sesame seed one was my favorite). The Frijoles Veneno with fresh tortillas was a flavor bomb. For mains, we ordered the Steak Norteño and Taco Taquero, the latter served table side with an indulgent amount of bone marrow which was quite the anniversary show. The grilled veggies and esquites rounded out the meal perfectly. We left with leftovers that we promptly finished after walking off dinner along 5th Avenue’s holiday decorations.

The vibe isn’t romantic, but you’ll feel special. The entire staff is dedicated to creating an experience. Everyone we encountered was kind and knowledgeable. Despite the crowd, it never felt frantic; it felt like being at the hottest spot with the best food and company. Don’t skip the wine list, our sommelier Garrett recommended a 2019 Bodega Numantia that was perfect with our meal.

Thank you to JP, Garrett, and the entire team for a special evening.

I came here for my 24th birthday and from the minute I stepped in the host and staff were incredibly welcoming! Sirce, our server, made our experience super memorable and exciting. She had such an inviting and positive energy. The chocolate cake at the end was a beautiful touch to end the night. I recommend trying the Coliflor! Personally, the branzino tacos were a little bit too creamy for me. Other than that rest of the food and presentations were beautiful. Thank you so much Cuerno for an unforgettable experience.

name: Farmer J
document: Farmer J. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch Buffets. located in New York. at 31 West 52nd Street. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
NEW FOOD SPOT ALERT!

Working around Rockefeller Center can honestly be a food desert because you have to go a minimum of 2 to 5 blocks to get something good to eat at an affordable price but lo and behold. There is a new spot for delicious healthy food in town and the name is.

FARMER J

Here are the rules of engagement:
You are going to get on line

You will pick out a base I chose the brown rice

You will pick up protein I went with the Bavette steak which the guy who took my order, advised me to also add the aïoli sauce and it was most definitely a hit

You will then choose two sides
I went with what everybody advised which was the maple brown sugar, sweet potatoes, which were divine and the mac & cheese, which does have some leaves in it. I think it is spinach perhaps

And being a cookie kind of sore, they have a delicious selection of desserts, and I went with the chocolate chip cookie

Today I stumbled upon this gem and devoured their food so fast I dropped my fork while eating outside. The service was fabulous as well; Raymond explained their concept to me with style and ease, Jack recommended delicious toppings like green tahini, and the charming Harmonei made check out seamless. And in the end, they were happy to assist with a spare fork. Try this place.

Farmer J has potential. I just wish the food wasn't so heavily salted/seasoned. I ate J's Classic yesterday and build my own bowl today. I prefer the Harissa over Amba chicken. The only thing in J's Classic that was too salty was the mac 'n cheese. Harissa chicken was relatively salty but the brown rice and tahini sauce balanced it out. But today's order (farmer's grain, amba chicken, maple spiced sweet potatoes, miso eggplant with a side of pickles and smoky eggplant sauce) was unbearably salty. If I had to pick one decent thing, it was the sweet potatoes. I paid almost $20, so I wasn't not going to eat it. Everything just didn't sit well together because the overly seasoned food clashed against each other. The tahini sauce was good, but I had to throw out the smoky eggplant sauce and pickles---they were bad. If your ingredients are as good as you advertised, the freshness of the food will speak for itself.

Ambience and servers were nice. Brownies was good. If you're going to pay $20 for lunch, this spot is filling enough to make it worth it. Good mix of carb, protein and fiber, but wouldn't say it's the healthiest due to all the oil, sauce, and seasoning. It's a new spot, so expect a bit of a wait---around 15 to 20 minutes and this was close to 1pm. I'll wait a bit longer for quality control to get better and try again.

The service and atmosphere is fine. Chocolate chip cookie is fine. The food is not great. The portion size first of all: tiny. The steak was absolutely inedible and so chewy gross not well made. The broccoli chewy with crispy pieces of kale which is extremely bland. The miso eggplant covered in dressing which lets be real makes it good right but healthy as promoted? No. Hot chocolate… pass. The steak not cut well and cooked unevenly to point inedible. Could not get teeth through it. Terrible .
Great new lunch spot! My photo doesn’t do justice to all the elements on the plate, everything was super flavorful and clearly made with fresh, local ingredients. Will definitely be back!

name: Metropolis
document: Metropolis. cuisine: American Cocktail Bars. located in New York. at 251 Fulton Street. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
​Metropolis is an elevated escape right inside the new PAC on Fulton (adjacent to the 9/11 Memorial plaza). The space is stunning—modern, elegant, and surprisingly spacious. Unlike many cramped FiDi happy hour spots, there are plenty of seating options here.

​One important heads-up: Because it is inside the PAC, there is a security screening upon entering the building. Don't let this deter you—it’s quick, and honestly, it makes the venue feel a bit more exclusive.

​We stopped in after work and ordered from the Happy Hour menu (5-7 PM). The cocktail list is solid ($10 drinks in this area is a steal), but the bar bites stole the show.
​The Metropolis Burger is excellent and comes with a signature "M" branded onto the bun—a nice touch.  ​The Berbere Fried Olives and Red Cornbread with goat's milk butter were perfect for sharing.
​Definitely save room for the dessert; the presentation is fantastic.

​The live DJ was the cherry on top. It was pleasantly unexpected and created a relaxing backdrop for unwinding—energetic but not too loud for conversation.

​If you work near the World Trade Center and want a sophisticated place to decompress, this is it. Just be ready for the brief bag check!

We had a wonderful dinner at Metroplis while we waited for the start of "A Christmas Carol." There were a number of standouts in the menu. You must order the cornbread to start your meal. It is flavorful and especially rich when you have it with the accompanying "sauces." The tuna tartare is also a good starting point. As for the "mains" the Harlem Express is the way to go. The fried chicken was crispy with a pleasing spiciness. To finish the meal the Almond cake is just what you want in a dessert. It was smooth, creamy,  crunchy and comforting. The service and decor were both top notch.

I never leave negative reviews, but this evening was so riddled with errors that I felt it was important for the restaurant staff to note. Especially with Marcus Samuelsson's name attached.

What was good:
-The food. We ordered the cornbread, the salad and the steak tartare.

-The cornbread was hot and fresh with a crunch on the outside and delectable moistness on the inside. The red miso spread that came with it was actually inspired. Brilliant and delicious.

-The salad was not only the prettiest salad we ever did see, but it was also inspired. Never knew cabbage could be so good.

-The steak tartare was unique in appearance but it was delicious. My dinner partner is a connoisseur of tartare and he said it was one of the best he’s ever had.

-The lighting and flatware were thoughtful and well-designed.

What was bad:
-We were sat at a half chair half booth table. The booth seats are too low for the table. I’m 5’4 and if I hadn’t used my coat to form myself a booster seat, my chest would have been parallel to the edge of the table.

-Our first dish arrived before our water. We also had no napkins and had to ask for them.

-Our second dish arrived before our cocktails. We decided to let it sit awhile, hoping the cocktails would arrive. After some time, we flagged the waitress and she said they would be out soon.

-Our third and final dish, the steak tartare, arrived but the runner said it was steak and eggs. We asked him to clarify mentioning that we ordered the steak tartare and he said “oh yeah, same thing.”

-The Jerusalem bagel that came with the tartare was TOUGH. If we hadn’t been on the clock to get to a play in the building, I would have mentioned it to the staff. We had to wrench it with our teeth like stale taffy. My partner gave up. I tried a little longer, and my teeth hurt the rest of the evening.

-Our cocktails only arrived to the table after the 3rd dish was placed down and my friend’s drink order arrived incorrect. He asked for a bone dry martini. It arrived with vermouth. He didn’t even order it “bone dry” He specifically said “no vermouth”
I had wanted to try the “Ebenezer’s Cap” but when it arrived, I saw that it should have been placed on the After Dinner drinks list because it was nightcap-esque (I probably should have deduced this from the name and the ingredients). So, I decided to save the drink for the end of the meal and placed an order for a martini.

-Halfway through our final course, I checked on the status of the martini and was asked "Would you like your martini now?" I expressed my confusion over the question. The waitress then explained that they have to-go drinks for the theater. I was not aware of this and it was not what I asked for. The martini then only arrived after we finished our meal.

-We asked to split the check. The waitress put the whole thing on my friend’s credit card.

When the martini arrived after our meal, I asked if the restaurant could make things right. They did eventually remove one of the drinks from our bill, which was very appreciated, but there was a certain lack of hospitality that we had to inquire.

I don’t think I’ve ever given a restaurant 5 stars in every category, but here I am giving Metropolis one of the best reviews I’ve ever written. Already, upon entrance, I was smitten with the atmosphere and decor. Not only was it extremely lively, but it was filled with attentive waiters, a spectacular DJ, and Marcus Samuelsson himself! He introduced himself to each table, neglecting no one! We ordered so many dishes and each one kept getting better as we went. Personally, the brisket was by far the star of the show! We ordered extra bread on the side just so we could dip each plate’s sauce into it. The flavors were that delicious! Thank you for a wonderful evening and we will definitely be back!

What a full on sensory experience! Food, ambiance, entertainment, hospitality, decor, all immaculate.

Booked a reservation for two for my significant other’s birthday. My partner and I try to out-do each other every year with amazing dining experiences but thanks to Metropolis by Marcus, I think I have him beat for at least the next few.

Menu:
-Concise number of menu options that all work together. We ordered the Steak and Eggs (which our amazing server, Ira, described as a take on a traditional Ethiopian dish), the Cornbread, the Sugar Hill Nights (the juiciest fried chicken I’ve ever had outside my mother’s kitchen), and the M Steak. Every dish was not only delicious but also intriguing as there were various tastes, textures, colors, and fragrances all beautifully plated.

Ambiance:
-Walking up the staircase to enter the restaurant, we felt as though we were a part of the city yet entering a specially curated experience. The security staff were thorough and friendly.
-A live music performance by a lovely songstress (apologies I did not get her name but she performed 05/02/25) began around 5:30PM. She sang one of my favorite songs, Allen Stone’s Give You Blue, and I was sold!

Hospitality:
-Our main server Nelly was absolutely excellent. She communicated effectively, inquired about allergies, checked in, and even made sure we left on time to travel from the restaurant to our Broadway play on time.
-Ira who I mentioned earlier was kind and very informative about the menu’s intention and design.
-Isaiah politely stopped us on our way out to invite us to return soon on a Thursday-Saturday evening and enjoy once again.
-There was a gentleman at the entrance who confirmed our reservation and escorted us to our table who was very kind and made us feel welcomed!

Absolutely recommend, run—don’t walk! See attached photos if you’re a foodie :)

One of our favorite places for brunch. Nice, healthy food, efficient service, and super friendly staff with a cute ambiance inside. Their Egg Benedict is a win! Excellent healthy food options.  Got the steak and chicken with a side of kale.  Great preparations and quick to come out of the kitchen.  The water service could be a bit quicker and colder temperature but overall a great experience and would definitely go back!

Looking for a brunch spot for you and your friends can be very overwhelming because there are so many options. The staff was friendly and the service was fast. But the food was DELICIOUS and didn't break the bank. This was one of the better brunches that I've been to in the city. We all ordered different things and they were all home runs. I had the Kale Salad with Salmon and as simple as it was, it was perfectly paired with the right flavors. Definitely going there again!

Great place for lunch! We did a late lunch which worked well since we arrived as most of the lunch crowd was departing. A great place for a group since there is something for everyone. The pozole was so delicious, my only regret is getting the cup and not bowl (quite zesty with the lime which makes it). 🤍🙊🤍🤍🤍

This spot had been on our list for a while, and after finally trying it, I completely understand the hype. The carbonara was creamy and rich, easily the best I've ever had. Everything we ordered tasted fresh and delicious!

We had a reservation for 7:45 pm. on a Friday but ended up being seated around 8pm due to how popular the restaurant has become online. Even with the short wait, the experience was well worth it.

Olio e più at the Bryant Park location is a beautiful place with a good and cozy atmosphere to go on dates and celebrate with family and friends, the food is delicious everything fresh and authentically Italian, the carbonara was amazing it really brought me back to Italy. Many good options on the menu for food and drinks and amazing service. Our server Gokce was super nice and sweet! 10/10 recommend and totally coming back!

​This is a nice place for Italian food in New York. The ambiance is very charming, and they greet you with a complimentary olive bread which is a really nice touch.
​The menu offers a great variety of pastas and meat dishes. We tried the Carbonara—which seems to be their most popular dish—and the Trout. Both were delicious and well-prepared.
​While it might not be a place that "reinvents the wheel," it is incredibly consistent. You know you’re going to have a good meal in a beautiful setting. It’s a reliable choice that always delivers.
​Price: Around $50 per person (excluding alcohol).

For a pre-Valentine's Day dinner accompanied by my fiancé, we opted to try Olio e piu on Greenwich Avenue. We arrived around 5 pm, where the seating was mildly packed in-house; we were greeted by a wonderful host who arranged seating for us near the window in the back. Giving us two menus and a drink menu, we were excited to try some great dishes given the tremendous outstanding choices of food on the menu. I opted for the tagliata e verdure medium rare , and my fiancé chose the ravioli di short rib al ragu. Our server, Turgut, was phenomenal - attentive to detail, very attentive, and friendly. When I first tried to pronounce his name, I called him 'too-good,' which brought laughter. The food was excellent, and I had to order another round of the short rib al ragu for myself. I paired my lovely meal with a Cabernet red wine, which was Turgut's choice. As time went by, the place got really packed - a beautiful atmosphere with decor and ambiance. I will absolutely try this place again, giving it a 10/10, with no complaints at all, except wishing they had better options for still water.

name: Little Collins
document: Little Collins. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch Sandwiches. located in New York. at 708 3rd Avenue. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
A very cozy and busy brunch location in midtown. They don’t take reservations so we had to wait 30 minutes but it was well worth the wait. The eggs Benny was very tasty and the bread has the perfect amount of crunch. The French toast was one of the best I’ve ever had. The espresso drinks had a nice richness and not too acidic.

Taking off one star because the male hostess who was seating people was extremely rude when we asked about wait time. All the other staff were lovely and helpful.

I was craving pancakes, and found this spot near our place. Good thing, this was close by and the wait wasn’t too long!

While waiting, I ordered a cappuccino. Good amount of kick to start my day. We got seated after maybe 10 minutes? Order my pancakes and my husband ordered the eggs benny.

Pancakes were good, and it didn’t need syrup. I liked that it had toasted hazelnuts! Couldn’t finish all three, so my husband finished the last one. The eggs benny was good too. Hollandaise could be a bit more tangy in taste, but that is just my preference. The potatoes that came with it were 👌🏽👌🏽👌🏽 Ordered a cup of drip coffee. It was a good end to the meal.

Would come back!

The buttermilk pancakes (despite having honeycomb) hit a perfect balance on flavors and are not at all too sweet! The toasted hazelnuts and banana really pulled through nice flavors without overpowering.

The shakshuka had some nice zing to it, but a bit heavy on the silantro. Same high quality ingredients cooked with care for the other dishes too. Overall, whatever you pick on the menu you’ll be very happy!

The coffee is “chefs kiss”, and the hot chocolate too is not too sweet and just great quality. The wait is probably a bit too long to become my go to takeaway spot but in terms of quality it’s right at the top of my list in NYC.

The service felt a bit rushed and inexperienced. We asked for a table and were given a time to return, but then someone else had been given it and without an ounce of embarrassment were asked to wait 25 mins again. There’s also a lot of movement happening collecting dishes etc for not a lot of output, e.g. they don’t make eye contact etc in the process so it’s hard to ask for things. The waiting staff’s quality felt especially surprising given the contrast when compared to the focussed execution of both the baristas and kitchen staff.

However the service is made up for by a cozy ambience, great soundtrack (and appropriate volume) and comfortable lighting and chatter noise.

Can strongly recommend but hope they can work together on raising the professionalism bar of the waiting staff.

The service was great! Everyone was very attentive and friendly.
I got the fried chicken sandwich with a salad. It was a very good chicken sandwich, crispy with a lot of flavor, but for the price the portions were really lackluster. The side salad was super sad, just some lettuce with dressing, it could have used some tomato or onions to make it interesting.

If you prefer a healthy breakfast, this is the perfect spot. Everything we tried was incredibly delicious, and the coffees were excellent as well.
Since the place is quite small, you may need to wait a little while for a table.

Oh this place was amazing. I expected it to be good and it exceeded my expectations. The meatballs were super flavorful and delicious, worth writing home about. The malfadine with the meat sauce is also delicious.
I loved the chocolate lava cake. And the tiramisu was superb.
The portions and prices are completely fair, which is a nice find in NYC.

This place wowed me. My husband and I booked this on a whim on New Year’s Day since we were in the area.. Can I just say how happy I am that we did? Food: incredible, homemade, authentic Italian dishes. The fried mozzarella was amazing and that sauce!!! The sauce!! So good. We split the chicken parm (which was massive) and we soon wished we had double of the pasta that came with it. As if it couldn’t get any better, the gelato was probably one of the best desserts we have ever had. The service was great and our server/bartender was attentive, friendly, and overall a joy! Especially for having to work on a holiday. We will absolutely make it a point to be back- and we are from PA! So happy we found this.

Ambiance (5/5): There was plenty of seating both indoor and outdoors so we were seated immediately on a weekday. The inside is minimalistic but sleek, and has plenty of space between the diners. Booth seating along the walls and areas that can accommodate larger groups.
Service (5/5): We were helped throughout the dining experience. Additional freshly grated cheese offered at the start of the meal!
Hot Louie : The pizza was delicious (although something could be improved in the dough)! After we finished eating, we asked our server if he preferred the Sicilian vs the regular and he preferred the regular. Pro tip: you can also ask for the Hot Louie but cooked on normal pizza.
Mafaldine Bolognese (5/5): I loved the pasta more than the pizza! It just had so much flavor and was generous on the meat portions.
I would definitely recommend and come again to try their other dishes!

document: Miss Nellie's. cuisine: American Cocktail Bars Seafood. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
My wife and I had an incredible meal at Miss Nellie’s — easily one of the best dining experiences in NYC. From the moment we walked in, we were impressed by the chic, yet cozy ambiance that set the stage for a memorable evening.

We started with the Caviar Lobster Rolls, three mini rolls filled with perfectly cooked lobster, topped with caviar and a hint of lemon. Paired with crisp house chips, this dish was a perfect balance of indulgence and freshness.

The Lemon Ricotta Tortellini was a highlight — the lemon ricotta cream paired beautifully with fresno and piquillo peppers, garlic, and white wine. It was rich, bright, and utterly comforting.

The Pan-Fried Snapper stole the show. The snapper was perfectly crispy and tender, and the broccolini, roasted peppers, and olive salsa complemented it beautifully.

The cocktails were equally exceptional. The Filthy One, made with olive oil fat-washed Bombay gin and blue cheese olives, was a bold, unforgettable take on a classic martini. But Fogg & Fancies was the real showstopper — a bourbon-based cocktail presented inside a stack of books that released a cloud of smoke when opened, adding a dramatic flair to the already delicious drink.

Every dish, every drink, and every detail was crafted with care, making this a top-tier dining experience. The service was impeccable, and the overall vibe of Miss Nellie’s made it a night to remember. We can't wait to return and highly recommend it to anyone looking for an unforgettable meal in NYC.

What an amazing experience all around. We were celebrating an early birthday before attending a show. Once we walked in we were greeted by every staff member that we saw and I was given a cute hand written birthday card. The drinks, the food and of course the service were all top notch. Cailinn our waitress was so nice and made us feel right at home. I got the French dip sandwich which was excellent. They also gave us a birthday desert on the house, which made my night. I would highly recommend this restaurant! You will not be disappointed.

The atmosphere and service in this restaurant is the reason I’d come back! Our waitress Sam was very friendly and attentive to our needs. The art and decorations here are unbelievably stunning. The food was pretty good, but aside from the Lemon Ricotta Tortellini, it was fairly average in my family’s opinion. My mom and sister ordered drinks and my sister loved her espresso martini. We also got the Mediterranean Dips app and I liked the pita and hummus. The chicken parm meatballs were pretty good and my mom ordered the smashburger and said it was average. If you plan on coming here for a meal, I recommend getting a cocktail and the Lemon Ricotta Tortellini. I typically hate citrus, but this meal was a mild lemony flavor that was so good. Our waitress gave us complimentary shots at the end of our meal and was so kind to give me a non-alcoholic option since she didn’t think I drank (which is accurate).

Came here for brunch as a walk-in. Had the Mc Nellie's B.E.C.- bacon, egg, hash brown, and cheese with sauce on a toasted English muffin - absolutely delicious! The combination was perfectly balanced and the sauce gave it an amazing flavor. The ambiance is unique and charming, a cozy spot that feels both casual and special. The service was great, everyone was friendly and attentive. Definitely want to come back and try dinner next time!

What a dreamy spot! We had a reservation & couldn’t leave the bar. It was too fun. Incredible cocktails. Decent food (we loved the crispy tuna/rice), great music, and an overall fantastic vibe! Stopped in here before seeing a show, and would absolutely come back.

name: 1803 Nyc
document: 1803 Nyc. cuisine: Cajun/Creole Seafood Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I had such a lovely time at their jazz brunch. Everything we tried was absolutely delicious and full of flavor. The cocktail pitchers were a great touch and perfect for sharing at the table. The live music created a pleasant vibe and felt like a nice extra to the whole experience. It was easy to enjoy conversations without the music overpowering the space, which made the brunch even more enjoyable. Definitely a five star experience for me.

Great Creole restaurant with an awesome vibe!

Came here on a weeknight. I made sure to make reservations ahead of time, since the restaurant tends to be busy. The place was crowded, but we got a table on the second floor right away.

For appetizers, we ordered the Honey Chili Brussels Sprouts and the Cajun Shrimp Skewers. Both were delicious with a ton of flavor. 5/5 for appetizers.

For my entree, I had the Cornmeal-crusted Black Sea Bass. It was also really good. The fish was seared perfectly, the vegetables and lemon butter sauce combined with it perfectly. 4.5/5 for entree.

For dessert, we shared the Hummingbird cake. I enjoyed the cake filling, which was coffee flavor, more than the rest of the cake. 4/5 for dessert. I think next time I might order the Beignets or Bread Pudding.

The atmosphere gets a 5/5 for me. And the service was very good. I think this is a great restaurant to experience the New Orleans vibe without leaving NYC.

Hello!! We stopped by for the Mardi Gras celebrations! And it was sooo much fun!! They had dancers and live music! Now the cocktails and food were sooo good :). I got the shrimp Po-boy  and Woww!  The Veggie Jambalaya! Was so good too! The bartenders were super fun :)

What up, y’all! I’m back again with another date night review ✨this time for 1803 NYC; a Cajun restaurant located in Tribeca. First off, I love the aesthetic of the place. Decorated with floral elements and fluer de lis fencing, it’s like a small burst of NOLA in NYC. They also sometimes have a band playing live jazz 🎺 Since Babe and I have been exploring all of the raw oyster options we can, I HAD to put him on to the charbroiled version! 1803 NYC does an amazing job with them too; buttery with the perfect amount of spice, they’re definitely a 10/10. We also got some raw oysters, of course. Those were delicious too 🦪 We then got the Brussels sprouts and the sea bass. The Brussel Sprouts were cooked to perfection with a crunchy outer texture and a pillowy inside. And the chilli sauce it comes in? Absolutely BAGING! 🌱As for the sea bass 🐟I wasn’t expecting it to come fried (though I don’t know what I expected after reading cornmeal crusted but ya live and learn right 😭). Either way, the fish was super meaty and well cooked. I also loved the lemon butter caper sauce it came with. Though I personally wasn’t a big fan of the frying mixture used and think the fish would be better served grilled, I enjoyed my overall dining experience✨ Def recommend this spot for a date night or an after work drink 🍸 SN: I LOVE the sauces that come on the table. The Fresno chilli has a vibrant kick while the green sauce was a bit more mellow but packed with flavor. 🌶️

I also wanted to give a quick shoutout to our server, Bridgette! She was super sweet and not only accommodating but also ingenious. When I wanted a refill of my glass, she left me with my original glass and returned with a carafe. I just thought that was so smart (though I’m sure for her it was a no brainer 😂)

The service was great! Everyone was friendly, from our server to the food runners.

The food was overall good.

The charbroiled oysters were delicious, and the Brussels sprouts could have been cooked a little longer, but they tasted great.

For our mains, the sauce on the Branzino made it a bit soggy, and the short rib Ragú pasta could have been a bit more al dente.

Sorry for the very opinionated review, but it’s with good intentions.

name: The Warren
document: The Warren. cuisine: Gastropubs. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Unbelievable reviews clearly show that only the most disgruntled seem to post reviews. This is alarming. I will gladly reverse the trend by saying that I SPECIFICALLY REQUEST Warren Memorial for ALL my procedures, tests, and imaging, only going elsewhere if they don't provide the service I need, which hasn't happened yet. Some of the finest humans on earth work here, and I haven't met one that isn't precious, caring, and competent yet. I love the layout of this hospital (very efficient!), the check-in process, the surgical options available so close to home, and then there's the outstanding food available in the bistro! Thanks team...I consider you my extended family!

SHAME ON YOU.

My mother required emergency surgery after a slip-and-fall accident that resulted in a broken hip. The procedure went well, and during her hospital stay the staff was friendly, attentive, and extremely helpful. For that, I was truly grateful.

However, everything changed when it was time for her discharge. We were told there were only two rehabilitation options: Evergreen Health & Rehabilitation in Winchester or another facility in Warrenton. Living in Alexandria, I trusted the hospital’s guidance in choosing the best and safest place for my mother’s recovery. Based on their recommendation, we proceeded with Evergreen in Winchester.

Evergreen was horrific. The environment felt more like a graveyard than a rehabilitation center. My mother endured 50 hours there before I arranged an urgent transfer to a facility that was actually capable of providing proper care.

Warren Memorial should immediately remove Evergreen Health & Rehabilitation from its list of referral options. No patient or family should ever be placed in a facility with such poor conditions—especially when the hospital is fully aware of its reputation and performance.

Please do not let this happen to another family.

I was referred to Warren Memorial Center as part of Valley Health for imaging as part of an endocrine evaluation. Warren’s staff were excellent. However, The initial radiology report created significant confusion between Valley Health providers and the UVA endocrine team regarding which adrenal gland contained a lesion and whether an adrenal gland was enlarged. Because imaging findings were central to surgical decision-making, this lack of clarity had real downstream consequences and contributed to the clinical pathway toward adrenalectomy.

Additionally, the report did not initially note that I was born with a single kidney, which is a significant anatomical finding that should be documented in imaging interpretation. The issue was later corrected after a UVA endocrinologist raised the concern (which I relayed), and I do want to acknowledge that Dr. Sweedan responded quickly to have the report amended once the problem was identified.

However, it is concerning that the kidney appears to have been documented during the PET scan only after I raised UVA’s concern about a “missing kidney” prior to the exam.

There are also ongoing access issues: the imaging links provided to me are currently broken, which means I cannot review my own imaging and must rely on manually forwarding studies to the UVA team for independent review.

Hospital is nicely laid out and most staff are polite .
My favorite pic I took was the button in the elevator " Emergency Cafeteria" .
Otherwise they helped my Mom with her surgery and she's doing lots better .
One complaint which is weird is if you look at some of the pics I posted of the windows you can still see the large suction ring from the installers years ago . I would think a hospital would  have been much cleaner 🤔.

Bottom line up front: I will be writing the hospital and the board over a truly negligent doctor.

I have had poor hospital experiences before, but the sheer lack of empathy and professional care should concern the residents of the surrounding area and the hospital. My pregnant wife, was in the worst pain of her life. This is our second child and she said she would have taken contractions over the pain. Front Royal Urgent care sent her to Warren county Memorial after considering that the ER could do more for her, and they thought it was safer for her to get care there. But when she got to the hospital the doctor barely looked at her, didn’t check her ears, or her nose for signs of sinus infection, don’t listen to her, or take notes, he just dismissed her after lecturing her on the (unfounded) risks (?) of taking Tylenol. He told her to wait it out and go home. She has suffered for five days without much improvement, and when she finally went to urgent care by Walmart, they checked her, listened to her, actually examined her, and without question determined she had a severe sinus infection. At urgent care she was able to get the care and the medicine she needed.

document: Bad Roman. cuisine: New American Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
I ate at Bad Roman last night after seeing it go viral on TikTok, and I fully expected it not to live up to the hype but I was completely wrong. It was absolutely fabulous from start to finish.

The atmosphere is intimate and upscale, and I really appreciated the overall design of the restaurant. Every detail feels intentional, even the ladies’ bathroom was beautiful and thoughtfully designed. The food was incredible, and the drinks were creative and unique. The truffle pasta was out of this world, and the viral filet with the ravioli on top truly deserves all the attention it gets. It is 100% worth ordering.

The desserts completely blew me away, we ate every last bite. Even my very hard-to-please family was impressed, which says a lot. The servers were extremely knowledgeable about the menu and very attentive throughout the meal, adding to an already great experience.

It’s a little off-putting at first that the restaurant is located inside a shopping mall, but once you’re inside, you completely forget about that. Bad Roman is perfect for a fun date night, a special occasion dinner, or anyone visiting NYC looking for a memorable meal. Highly recommend.

Bad Roman delivers a standout dining experience that effortlessly blends elevated Italian-American cuisine with a bold, high-energy atmosphere. The third-floor setting at Columbus Circle feels stylish, lively, and distinctly New York, making it perfect for a special night out or a celebratory dinner.

The food was exceptional across the board. The Eggplant Pull-a-Parm is a must-order crispy, cheesy, indulgent, and ideal for sharing, with rich flavors that immediately set the tone for the meal. The Filet Cacio e Pepe was a highlight, featuring a beautifully cooked filet paired with a luxurious, pepper-forward sauce that transforms the classic dish into something memorable and refined. Dessert sealed the experience with the Lemon Cheesecake, which was bright, balanced, and not overly sweet an excellent, refreshing finish after a rich main course.

Service truly elevated the entire evening. Our waiter was impeccable throughout our time there attentive without hovering, professional, and genuinely warm. Courses were perfectly paced, recommendations were spot-on, and every detail was handled smoothly. The service felt polished and effortless, making us feel taken care of while still relaxed.

Overall, Bad Roman fully lives up to the hype. Exceptional food, a vibrant atmosphere, and impeccable service make this an easy five-star experience and a place well worth returning to.

Bad Roman is Good.
Our server was really great. The manager went out of his was to check on us and not just us. I could see him watching everyone.
We have two picky-ish children. Sometimes their mood will allow them to try new things. Other times not so much. Our server understood children. She made our daughter feel part of the meal. She helped her make another choice rather than turn off and turn her nose up.
All of us ended up really having a nice meal. The food was very good. And dessert really did look like this!

Food was delicious. Loved the crudo. Branzino was excellent. Spectacular creative desserts. Fun vibe, nice views and attentive service (server was Dan V - he was knowledgeable and his recommendations were spot-on). Coming back soon.

This trendy, upscale restaurant is serving up some of the best Italian food in the city with a modern twist. The ambiance is very grown and sexy and the decor is very unique. The staff is very friendly and extremely attentive. JOSE was our server and he had a great energy. He made some exceptional menu recommendations. The food is next level and very flavorful. Top notch quality. The presentation for everything we ordered was phenomenal. Drinks were creative and delicious. This is a must visit.

We reserved a table at Tony’s Friday night in the lower level. It was super busy almost full house.

We got a much bigger steak though. I noticed it was bigger but didn’t see the mismatch till I checked the receipt later on

The Lasagna was phenomenal

The calamari and the salad were also huge!
We ended up not finishing the steak.

There were a few birthdays going on downstairs and it was pretty loud for our liking but I liked the vibe.
The restaurant is beautiful. A gorgeous wall painting downstairs and some cool portraits upstairs make it look very interesting.

Ate at Tony’s Di Napoli and absolutely loved it. This place is always busy, but for good reason. The food is delicious, classic Italian, and served family-style with HUGE portions — definitely come hungry and ready to share.

The atmosphere is lively and welcoming, perfect for families, groups, or celebrations. It feels like a big Italian family dinner with nonstop energy, great service, and plates that just keep coming.
Everything we tried was flavorful and satisfying, and leftovers are basically guaranteed.
If you’re looking for a fun, family-friendly spot with amazing food and generous portions, this place delivers every time. Totally worth it.

Dined here due to its closeness to Belasco theatre. Perfect date night before a Broadway show. The drinks weren’t outrageously expensive for the size. And the food was elevated, but it still reminded me of a classic Italian dinner.

Food was excellent ! And company even better!! Ordered calamari for appetizer and the chicken parm and penne pasta with marinera sauce for an entree. name: Or'esh
document: Or'esh. cuisine: Mediterranean Beer Bar Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
O’resh is the kind of new Soho spot that actually lives up to the hype.

We started with the Big Bluefin Slice, clean and bright with garum, red onion, urfa chili, and lime zest. The Crispy Potato Pastel topped with golden osetra caviar was rich without being heavy. The Golden Halloumi Kadayif with fresh za’atar and hot honey was so good we ordered it twice, salty, crispy, sweet, and completely addictive.

The Or’esh Market Salad with Greenmarket vegetables, stone yogurt, and Jerusalem bagel croutons somehow made vegetables feel like the main event. The American Red Snapper with English peas and lemon za’atar butter was simple and flawless.

And the Cardamom Soft Serve with caramelized kataifi crumble, honey, lemon zest, and olive oil… I genuinely don’t have the words. It was one of those desserts you think about the next day.

Every dish hit. No notes. The service was warm and polished, especially impressive for a buzzy new restaurant. We put our name down at 4:30 for bar seating and cancellations and were seated by 5:10, which felt like a win.

It felt like eating at someone’s home, just more elevated. Can’t wait to go back.

An awesome night with stunning ambiance. The staff was wonderful, and every dish was on point. The Big Bluefin slice was outstanding, and the 18 layer Wagyu New York strip was one of the best steaks I’ve ever had. Truly an exceptional restaurant.

Fantastic new spot with a foundation in good ingredients which is hard to find even in most upscale restaurants. Love that they don’t use seed oils and buy local from farmers market. Vibe is great, but I had a foodie influencer sitting next to me with a really bright light on the whole time. The restaurant should consider other guests if this was an invitation. How would they feel if I left my phone flash light on the brightest setting?

Food wise, I was very impressed and found a highly rated burgundy white at a great price point. The bagel is a must, really enjoyed the raw fish. Kebab was super. Will be back for the layered Wagyu.

Bailey deserves a shout out. Excellent service!

We came the first week they opened and thoroughly enjoyed our night at Or’esh. The marinated olive martini was so well balanced, the crispy potato caviar bites and golden halloumi were standout small plates, and the red snapper was cooked perfectly, it was fresh, light, and full of flavor. Our server suggested each of the hits and specialties of the chef and they did not disappoint.

A big thank you to our bartender, Aiden, for the warm, knowledgeable service, and to the whole team for being so attentive throughout the evening. We had such a great experience from start to finish and we’re already looking forward to coming back.

Just Wow. Eugene Remm is a genius. We were fortunate enough to get a reservation here last night and we were speechless. The decor is absolutely beautiful and every attention to detail has been perfected. Additionally, the food is out of this world. We loved the big sliced tuna and the bagel. This is Eugene and team’s third restaurant in a short time and his legend continues.

document: Rampoldi. cuisine: French Italian Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Really good experience in a beautiful open venue. Service was perfect with good attention from multiple staff but not overbearing by any means. We especially loved the duck confit, soufflé, and complementary bread.

There’s live music if it’s not too late. The ambience is great for a special occasion. The red lightning is interesting. Maybe not for everyone. Would come back again for another special event.

The good: elegant atmosphere and service was good. We loved the live music, and appreciated the complimentary flute of prosecco at the door! The bad: the food was just good, not great. We had the foie gras appetizer, a filet and the scallops. Nothing was bad by any means, but it was just okay. Would have loved a little better sear on the steak, and the scallops were kinda bland. Also our martinis were just fine. Giving them a break here since they weren’t technically a drink offering but still, any respectable bar should be able to nail a martini. I shouldn’t be sitting there wishing I had made it myself while paying $24 for it haha. Overall just felt like they didn’t really deliver. That said, the prices seemed fair and portions were okay.

Steak was great, make sure to get medium rare. Got the tartare for appetizers and the apple pie + vanilla ice cream for dessert. The live music piano and bass jazz was absolutely amazing, even had a friend request a song! Service was excellent as well. Very high end though, but you get what you pay for

Rampoldi has become one of those rare New York restaurants I return to again and again—and after more than four visits, it’s firmly earned its place as one of my favorites in the city. From the moment you step inside, the ambience feels effortlessly elevated: refined, intimate, and unmistakably upscale without ever feeling stiff or pretentious.

The service is consistently exceptional—warm, attentive, and polished in a way that makes every visit feel special and personal. It’s the kind of hospitality that enhances the experience rather than interrupts it, striking the perfect balance between professionalism and genuine care.

The food is, quite simply, delightful. Every dish is thoughtfully prepared, beautifully presented, and rich in flavor, making it clear that quality and detail are at the heart of Rampoldi’s kitchen. Whether it’s a first visit or a repeat one, the experience never loses its charm.

Rampoldi isn’t just a great restaurant—it’s a dependable favorite, ideal for celebrating, impressing, or simply indulging in a truly refined dining experience. In a city overflowing with options, that level of consistency and elegance is what sets it apart. Shoutout to Jose and Milena who served us tonight!!

I originally intended to make a reservation at their sister restaurant Atlantic Grill around the corner before a show at Lincoln Center but when that team couldn’t locate my reservation, they sent me next door to their sister restaurant Rampoldi which shares the same kitchen I believe and is connected.

When I first entered the space I was impressed by the ambiance and red/pink lighting that reminded me of passion and romance. We got seated in the back dining room which worked perfectly, especially since we didn’t have a reservation.

The establishment had a pri fixe option available for pre-show meals at a reasonable price ($68) but we decided to pick our own dishes instead.

Ordered the half dozen oysters and calamari to start and everything was just ok
My espresso martini was well crafted but my filthy gin martini left a little more to be desired. Unfortunately they didn’t get the memo on the filthy and no one came up to check so I just stuck with it and wasn’t able to finish it.

Service was also pretty bad as I sat with an empty class a couple of times, they could’ve just left a bottle of water for us to serve ourselves rather than have me sitting there thirsty. That same lack of foresight and care unfortunately applied throughout the meal as we almost missed our exit time despite them asking us beforehand if we had a show to get to.

The calamari were just alright. Not well seasoned or cooked and pretty bland, the oysters were oysters hard to mess those up and my scallops were pretty tasty as was my friend’s sea bass which was probably the best thing we collectively ordered as a table
When I received the check, I was genuinely shocked at the cost vs. quality of the meal and service

If we had more time and were assisted in advance as offered upon initially entering, I would have been able to share this feedback firstly with the team.

google_reviews.text:
We’ve visited Supra twice already this month, and every time the experience has been amazing. The food is incredibly flavorful, satisfying, and beautifully presented you can truly feel the care in every detail.
I especially want to recognize Ana for her outstanding service. She is attentive to every detail and always there exactly when you need her. She gave fantastic recommendations that made choosing dishes easy and enjoyable. And a special thank you to GM Sergei, who always welcomes us with a warm smile and checks in throughout the evening to make sure everything is perfect.

Supra has officially become our favorite restaurant again. Thank you for such a wonderful experience.

This was my first time trying out Georgian cuisine, and boy did it live up to my expectations! The restaurant was pretty packed for a Sunday night, but we were seated within ten minutes of our arrival. We were served complimentary champagne while we perused the menu.

We started off with some chicken croquettes that were crispy and mildly flavoured to begin with. Then, we had their ajaruli khachapuri — this was sooooo good. The combination of the cheese mixed with the butter and egg tasted delicious. The khachapuri was pretty big and can easily be started between four people. Then came the pork and beef khinkali which basically consists of three/five huge dumplings(you can choose the amount) — the mincemeat stuffing is mildly spiced and the whole dumpling is kinda soupy but it tastes great.

After all these dishes we were sorta full, but still decided to order the mixed grill platter which came with three kinds of meat (pork, chicken, and lamb), roasted potatoes, roasted bell peppers and three kinds of dips. The kebab pieces were again quite generously sized and we were unable to finish them all so we decided to pack them up.
I don’t know where we had the space after all this to think about dessert but we did!! 😅 We ended up getting their honey cake which tasted great and was totally worth it!

All in all, the whole experience — service, food, ambience — was simply superb. Loved it absolutely. :)

Went for a Galentines celebration brunch. Every dish was delicious and fresh! Only one server for the main area so service was slow but once we ordered the food came out fast! Would recommend: pancakes, mushroom omelette, cheese/potato dumpings, sokos khachapuri, and Lobio kotanshi.

FANTASTIC!! Everything was phenomenal! Service was friendly & attentive. The lamb chops were especially delicious and the khachapuri will satisfy any cheese lovers palate. An excellent choice for medium to large groups so you can share as much as possible!

Also, I noticed the separate bar area which was spacious and tucked away from the rest of the bustling restaurant which looks like a great date spot!

Staff is friendly and diverse. Very fast service and the restaurant itself does feel
georgian.

Food was horrible though. Maybe for an untrained american tastebud it would be different and full of flavors but in reality the food was, to say the most, edible.

They do not have anything actually authentic outside of sauces and lemonade.

Pork Mtsvadi (bbq) came absolutely raw. The inside was dripping blood and not in a way that’s actually tasty.
I sliced one and they replaced only one slice after that, I sliced all of it and discovered all of them were raw. Again, not in a way that was actually tasty or on purpose. They just plain undercooked it. Gladly, it was taken out of the check. Staff was friendly.

Khinkali dough was not machine kneaded it was hand knead so it was uneven and unprofessional, in my opinion. The beef in Khinkali was dense. It was like biting into a meatball rather than what it actually should have been.

Potatos with tarragon sauce were mildly good.

I would not recommend to go here because it didn’t taste Georgian at all. I am Georgian so I would know.
They do not have actual unique or authentic Georgian tastes.

Went there hoping to taste home for a minute. Ended up angry.

name: LumLum
document: LumLum . cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: One of the best thai restaurants I have ever been too. The thai tea was one of the best I have ever had. For entrees we got the crying tiger the soft shell crab curry and the duck curry. Everything was amazing. The duck was my favorite because it was so tender. The wait wasn’t even that long when they were busy. The price is definitely worth the food and experience

Excellent spot for tangy and flavor-packed Thai food. I recommend getting the chive pancake by a lot. The texture is very nice, glutinous but not too heavy. I also recommend the tiger shrimp which was cooked perfectly from head to toe as a light cook, accompanied by a ridiculously excellent spicy green sauce.

The steamed fish had great texture, meaty and moist without being dry, and the sauce would go well with rice on its own. The sauce is very tangy and thus works well with the fish's flesh. I would order this again for two people.

The crying tiger had a great rice but the steak was just normal. I was thinking about why I think the steak is normal and I realize that in most of these preparations you get flecks of salt that bring out the meatiness. Also in those preparations the meat is piping hot. Here the meat is a normal cut but could be better with a bit more technique.

The space looks like a classic Thai place with the bamboo seats and wooden accents. For being "near" Times Square, it's an excellent find. One note: the mains are now $40+. Welcome to 2025 inflation.

Wow! What a fantastic and thai meal to remember at Lum Lum.  My wife did a lot of research before choosing Lum Lum for dinner in Hells Kitchen.  Note: this place is popular!  So reservations are highly recommended. We came on a Friday night and oh boy it was slammed!  My wife made a reservation well in advance and they had a table waiting for us when we arrived at our reservation time.  Primo service and kind servers add to the 5 star restaurant Lum Lum is.

We ordered Khao Soi, Crying Tiger, and a Fried Pork for appetizer.  Cocktail drinks were fantastic as well.

5 solid stars for Lum Lum and thank you for a stellar meal!

First time here (on a solo adventure) and I will gladly come back! I had two servers recommend the Penang Nue for my first time, and it did not disappoint. The meat was cooked perfectly, the curry was so flavorful and the right amount of spice for me…Just a little sniffle lol…Even the plain rice was tasty. I had a seasonal cocktail, the green curry, that was pretty bland especially for $18…so I can’t speak on the cocktails being great. The mango sticky rice was out of season so I tried the taro mochi coconut dessert instead and loved it! I would definitely give this spot a try if you haven’t!

I had a good experience at Lum Lum! The food was delicious — the dumplings were super tasty, and the Pad Thai was beautifully presented and full of flavor. The restaurant is nicely decorated and has a great vibe.

The only thing is that the tables are quite close to each other, so it’s not the best spot for a quiet or intimate dinner. But overall, the atmosphere is really nice, and the food makes it totally worth it. I’d definitely go back!

name: Little Ruby's East Village
document: Little Ruby's East Village. cuisine: Australian Breakfast & Brunch Burgers. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This restaurant serves really good food, but the only downside is the poor service — and they still expect tips. When we had one extra person and asked for another set of cutlery, we waited for a long time and the waiter never brought it. In the end, we had to grab one ourselves from another table.
Beef and Tomato Sandwich: Very delicious, the beef was cooked perfectly.
Shrimp Pasta: The sauce was excellent, I really loved it.
Coconut Milkshake: Tasted great too, quite nice.

Finally got to come after my family went without me once before and raved about it. Came for lunch and we ordered chicken avocado salad, breakfast burrito, shrimp pasta, and spicy vodka pasta. Everything was so very fresh and delicious. The salad came in an impressive heap on a big plate and fully mixed. Both pastas were perfectly al dente with rich and flavorful sauce. I ordered the spicy vodka pasta with an extra addon of crispy chicken. The chicken (while well made and tasty) was completely unnecessary. It's a pretty busy spot so come prepared to wait a bit, but totally worth it!

Loved the truffle fries with ailoi, they are nice and crispy.
Although the spicy vodka pasta rigatoni & shrimp pasta have relatively good flavors but the sauce is too runny almost like water. Vodka pasta had too much oil so not a fan! This city has many better options!

We had such a lovely meal at Little Ruby’s East Village, one of the newer locations of this beloved Australian café that first opened in Nolita back in 2002. Over the years, Ruby’s has expanded to SoHo and Midtown, building a reputation for blending Australian café culture with Italian and Mediterranean comfort foods. It’s casual and approachable, but every dish has a sense of intention a nod to tradition with a playful, modern twist.

The spicy Italian sausage rigatoni was pure comfort with character. Rigatoni, a pasta shape that comes from central and southern Italy, is known for its ridges that cling to rich sauces. Here, it was perfectly al dente, coated in a balanced tomato cream sauce that was bright but also indulgent. Parmesan gave it a nutty, salty finish, while the baby peas added a subtle sweetness. The sausage was distinctly southern Italian in style spicy, fennel-laced, and hearty enough to ground the dish. It felt like a modern echo of cucina povera, the rustic Italian tradition of stretching ingredients into bold, nourishing meals.

The Bronte burger is a Ruby’s signature, and for good reason. Named after Sydney’s Bronte Beach, it reflects the fresh, multicultural spirit of Australian café food. The 7oz beef patty was juicy and flavorful, layered with tomato, spinach, swiss, and a sweet chili–mayo combo on toasted ciabatta. Ciabatta, a relatively recent invention from 1980s Italy, was the perfect choice airy and chewy inside, crisp outside, sturdy enough to hold everything together. The side of fries was just as memorable: thin, crisp, tossed with herbs and garlic, perfect for dipping. It’s the kind of burger-and-fries plate that feels indulgent but elevated.

For dessert, the date cake with vanilla ice cream and toffee sauce was the highlight. Sticky, warm, and spiced with cinnamon, it came drenched in buttery toffee sauce that melted into the cake and balanced beautifully with the cold vanilla ice cream. This version leaned closer to the traditional British sticky toffee pudding, a mid-20th century classic born out of home baking, where dates provided natural sweetness and richness. Ruby’s take felt nostalgic yet modern, capturing the essence of that pudding but with a lighter café touch.

The East Village location carries Ruby’s laid-back Aussie ethos into one of New York’s liveliest neighborhoods. While Nolita, SoHo, and Midtown each bring their own personality, the East Village outpost feels especially cozy and vibrant. And we have to mention the service our waiter Miguel was fantastic, attentive, warm, and knowledgeable, which made the whole experience even better.

This place is great for brunch or dinner. I went with a friend, our reservation was for 7:30pm, it was busy but service was fast. We ate the bronte burguer and it was perfectly cooked. The patty was very well seasoned, ciabatta was soft, chewy interior and the crust was crispy. Delicious. We also order some sweet potato fries and they add more aioli for us. Always a good choice. ✨

google_reviews.text: Awesome restaurant for locals and tourists alike. Very big, suitable for large groups or date nights.
