name: Ci Siamo
document: Ci Siamo. cuisine: Italian Bars Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Instantly became one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Everything is delicious. The Gnocco Fritto is a standout, alongside the rib eye. The focaccia bread is so fresh, no notes. It’s on the pricey side but totally worth it. I made a reservation for the wrong date and they kindly sat us at the bar, best decision, the service was impeccable. I highly recommend Ci Siamo.

Ci Siamo is one of those places where you can’t really go wrong no matter what you order!

For apps, we started off with the insalata verde with toasted garlic. I actually loved this salad because it didn’t have too much going on. No major callout here but if you need a tasty green just to say you had one, I’d recommend. Next, and know I’m not usually a fan of goat cheese, I loved  the thin layer they added to the bottom of the light yet crispy gnocco frito made for the perfect pairing. Definitely a must order in my opinion. The last starter was the scallop tartare and unfortunately, this was the most disappointing part of the meal. I just felt like it was too fishy, but the texture and citrus within the dish was well balanced.

For our mains, we shared the pappardelle with beef and the cavatelli with spicy crab. Both were a 10/10 so I highly recommend, but if I have to pick between the two I’m leaning more towards the  pappardelle… just because the spicy crab had a couple of shells in it.

For dessert, they gave us a complementary glass of white wine as a pallet cleanser to go with our lemon sorbet. Call me crazy but even though the sorbet was refreshing, it was too lemony/sour-y for me (geez I’m making up words).

I had such a great experience at Ci Siamo. I was in the city for work, and my aunt from Long Island met me for dinner before I headed back to Boston. My husband had eaten here before while he was in NYC for work and told me I had to try the onion torta—he was absolutely right.

Our server, Jonathan, was truly wonderful. He was so inviting and kind without being overbearing. He helped me choose dishes that worked with my dietary restrictions, and my water glass was never even close to empty before he refilled it. His overall presence was just so pleasant, and he really made us feel taken care of.

The food was amazing—big compliments to Chef Hillary—and honestly the whole staff made the entire experience feel special. I’ll definitely be coming back, and I’m happy to recommend Ci Siamo to anyone looking for a great dinner in NYC.

Dina was our waiter and was fantastic, speaking French, Italian and she gave us great wine recommendations.  The rabbit pasta was great and I’d recommend getting the focaccia and use it to get the thin sauce.  The smoked carrots had a mix of fresh herbs, and were good, but really only a slight hint of smoke.  A great experience.

Came here for Valentine's lunch and enjoyed our meal very much.  Service was friendly and efficient and food was absolutely marvelous.  My wife did a lot of research before choosing Ci Siamo as part of our New York trip itinerary and frankly she nailed it.  Ambiance is upscale and bustling but not too loud that you can't have a great time with your wife or partner.

5 stars and two thumbs up!

document: Empanada Mama - Hell's Kitchen. cuisine: Latin American Empanadas Food Delivery Services. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Five days in the Big Apple means countless food options, but since we were seeing Hell's Kitchen on Broadway, I sought out local eats in the neighborhood—and Empanada Mama was the major discovery. I'm hitting this spot up fa' sho on my next NYC visit!
They offer flavors galore that will satisfy every tastebud. The moment I saw their Jerk Chicken and Viagra (seafood) empanadas, I was sold. Our appetizer of plantain chips and guac was hittin', and the entire meal was fantastic. To top it off, the service was fast, friendly, and top-notch. I will say the music was a little loud; maybe because we were sitting by the DJ booth, but we’re music lovers, so it didn’t take away from the vibe. Just be prepared because this 24-hour spot might be jammin’ when you visit!

Everything was so good! We tried the jerk cheese and the Cuban empanadas. The crust has a nice crunch and they’re packed with filling. Jerk cheese was my favorite bc it had a great cheese pull. The bandeja paisa was huge! It’s def a two person serving size. It comes with flavorful rice and beans, an egg, half an avocado, a chorizo sausage great grill taste, steak was so perfectly cooked and juicy and a ton of crispy chicharron. It was so much food plus sodas and we had a whole serving to take home and came out to ~$40pp it was def enough food for three tho

I have never seen an empanada place with this many options before. The classic shell that they use is light and crispy and is PACKED with filling. I really appreciate that. I'm a fiend for sweet and savory flavor combos and they have no shortage of that here—praise the Lawd for that. This is my new favorite empanada spot. I think they messed up on the filling on one of my orders, the el Toro, but that's alright because it was still delicious. The el jefe and jerk & cheese slapped hard. I would definitely come back to try more flavors and some of my favorites again!

We love us empanada mamas, whenever im in nyc I have to stop at one normally on LES but today we stopped by the hells kitchen location. Food is always on point. Staff is kind and no wait to be seated. If you like flavorful food this is the spot to go to. Can't go wrong with a empanada or a full meal.

the managers jen bryant and hiram are amazing!! they told me all about the menu and they are very welcoming! we sat at the bar with ian, drinks are really good and strong! arroz con pollo taste really good and i had to order more for to go!!! staff are really nice as well, always smiling!!

name: Addictive NYC
document: Addictive NYC. cuisine: Wine Bars Tapas Bars Spanish. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Made a reservation here and I’m so happy I did. Addictive NYC is one of those rare spots that makes you forget you’re even in Midtown. You walk down a set of stairs and suddenly the noise, the crowds, the chaos is all gone.

The staff couldn’t have been nicer. Our waiter knew the menu and the wine list like the back of his hand, and every recommendation he made hit the mark. Speaking of the wine list it’s unreal. They have wines from all over the world and even have their own brand. Easily one of the best I’ve seen in the city, with bottles you don’t see anywhere else.

The food is honestly outstanding. If I could eat here everyday I would. Every plate looked beautiful and tasted even better You can tell the kitchen here really cares about what they’re putting out.

If you’re looking for a place that’s intimate, elevated, and a real break from the city madness, this is it.

Such a warm, cozy, and relaxed gem. The staff were incredibly kind with a fun sense of humor. Cuisine was bursting with authentic flavors and attitude. Grateful to have enjoyed a festive and quaint Christmas dinner here.

My husband and I are frequent visitors of Spain, and we had our Valentine’s Day dinner here.

My only food criticism is the size of the lamb cuts we were served, but every dish was absolutely sensational in terms of flavor. I think we also had a miscommunication with the waiter and we were only sent one fixed dinner rather than 2, and since our dinner was timed, we figured there wasn’t much point in asking for the second meal to be made; but it was lovely nonetheless.

The burrata and smoked salmon & goat cheese dishes were amazing. My husband LOVED the hummus paired with the lamb; It was so light and decadent. Every dish felt fresh and the style of the room was classy and warm.

I would have loved a warmer location away from the constant door breeze, but there is still no corner of this restaurant that isn’t beautiful to look at. My table probably should be the cut off point because we spent the entire dinner with incoming guests standing next to us. It was a busy holiday, so with that in mind, the restaurant did pretty well and I would absolutely go again!

We came by on a rainy Thursday night. We were a bit early for our reservation, but that didn't seem to be an issue at all, because the welcome was warm and seamless. While there isn't a traditional host stand, the service from the moment we walked in was impeccable. A special thanks to our waiter, Stefano, whose attentiveness and genuine care elevated our entire evening. He was warm, knowledgeable, and made sure every detail was just right!

The atmosphere at Addictive NYC is both charming and thoughtfully designed. Floral decorations add a soft, fun, and trendy touch, line lights cast a warm glow throughout the space, and little details like corks in glass jars and wine bottles artfully lined up along the wall give it a cozy yet curated feel. The restaurant is somewhat small, but the layout is arranged in a way that doesn't feel cramped. We were spaced out enough to enjoy a relaxed dinner without feeling like we were on top of other tables.

The food was absolutely phenomenal, especially for Restaurant Week. Some places don't bring their best or serve meager portions during RW, leaving you wondering why you even bothered but that wasn't the case here. Everything was done with care and full flavor.

We started with two versions of the Ensalada de Setas, one without tomatoes (per my request) and one without mushrooms (per theirs). Both were earthy, flavorful, and beautifully balanced.

For my entrée, I had the Costillas de Cordero, which were tender and perfectly seasoned one of the best lamb dishes I've had at a NYC restaurant. It's served with a hummus I was initially skeptical about, but it was flavorful and paired wonderfully with the lamb.

We ended with Torta Santiago, a traditional Spanish almond cake that was moist, subtly sweet, and a delightful way to close out the meal.

Honorable mention goes to the other entrée, the salmon with roasted vegetables, which was expertly seasoned, cooked just right, and paired with fresh, vibrant veggies. You can tell there's real passion behind the food here.
All paired with a shared bottle of wine.

Addictive NYC truly lives up to its name. Between the incredible food, the cozy and stylish ambiance, and Stefano's top-tier hospitality, this is a place I'll absolutely return to. It's a perfect choice for a girls' night, a date night, or catching up with friends.

A quick tip: since the space is small, it's best to make a reservation, especially for larger groups. Also, keep in mind that there's a 3% surcharge for credit card payments, and totals are split between cash and card.

Can't wait to come back!

All in all a great experience! We were very fortunate to have this place a block away from our hotel, and we were utterly charmed by the space and the decor. The food was very good and surprisingly reasonably priced for the location and atmosphere… portions small, of course, but three of us had an ample meal with wine for basically $100, which feels like a bargain these days. Great find!

Raku: A Timeless Experience Defined by Consistency and Excellence

​Raku Japanese restaurant isn't just a place we eat; it's a true culinary constant in our lives. Having been loyal patrons for many years, we can confidently attest that the quality here has been unfailingly high—it’s been consistently good every single time, a rarity in the dining scene.

​The entire dining experience begins with the atmosphere. The ambiance is wonderfully cozy, creating a relaxed and intimate space that feels both welcoming and refined. Matched perfectly with the setting is the excellent service. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely focused on making every visit special, which is a major reason for our lasting loyalty.

​While every dish at Raku is prepared with care, our personal gold standard—the dish we measure all others by—is the Tuna Tartare. We've tried this classic appetizer at countless other highly-regarded restaurants over the years, but they are simply not the same. Raku’s version achieves a perfect balance of texture and flavor that is unmatched, proving its uniqueness and mastery in preparation. It’s an absolute must-try for any first-time visitor.

​For anyone seeking exceptional Japanese cuisine backed by years of unwavering quality, fantastic service, and a dish that truly stands out, Raku is the place to be.

name: Momofuku Noodle Bar - Uptown
document: Momofuku Noodle Bar - Uptown. cuisine: New American Noodles Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The food was excellent! All the dishes were so tasty. The cucumber salad, the pickled daikon, the mushroom miso ramen, garlic chicken ramen, mushroom bao bun - all so so good and flavorful. The desserts were also fantastic. The miso brown butter cookie was soft and the tahini soft serve with crunchy bits was a perfect way to end the night.

The service was frustrating. Our food took a long time to arrive and they forgot one dish until the end. Same thing happened with dessert, they seemed to keep forgetting to serve us, which was a bit disappointing. I want to go back and try more dishes, hoping to get better service next time.

From Apps to Entrees everything was stellar and delicious. We ordered the kimchi, pickled Daikon and cucumbers with jalapeños. Crispy chicken with Bao bun and pork belly with ramen noodles and to finish it off the steak with greens! They offer NA beers which is perfect for dry January! What an amazing experience.

The downtown 11th street momofuku is better in terms of food and service. But the atmosphere is better here.

The steak was chewy and salty. The chicken was overtly salty and dry. Total waste of money. The pork ramen was very good but they brought my friend’s ramen out first, with a 6 minute lag between his and mine. My friend had to wait for my ramen to be served.

They also didn’t provide a fork or knife for the steak. Service was subpar given the price of the food. However they did fill my water frequently.

Don’t bother with this place. Go to the  downtown one.

As we had a $150 coupon / credit from our Chase credit card for dining at an exclusive list of restaurants, we were happy to find this more affordable and casual style restaurant was included and nearby to a show we were attending at Lincoln Center Theatre.  We reserved through OpenTable one day prior (definitely recommended) and arrived to the shopping mall (Columbus Circle) and took the escalator up and walked to the far end of the floor to find the restaurant. They had a very friendly and professional hostess who immediately seated us at a table for two (which was basically a large booth split with 2 smallish tables so we were crammed in and rubbing shoulders with another party right next to us).  The place is pretty small and by the time we got our drinks, every table was full with a line waiting.  It isn't fancy at all and is very casual with no pretension. The kitchen is open and viewable in the side of the restaurant.  Service was shared among a few waiter staff who stopped by a few times but weren't particularly friendly or focused on any particular table.  Food was brought out very quickly and serving sizes are generally LARGE so don't over order on appetizers.  We had appetizers, entree, and were checked out and leaving in under an hour.  Everything was delicious, well prepared, and great flavors without being particularly spicy. The only slight miss was our order of Ginger Scallion Noodles, which had great flavor but surprisingly zero sauce or broth, so was a little dry and heavy. We didn't use it but they also had a nicely priced fixed price menu.  I wouldn't necessarily take a date here, but for a quick sit down lunch, the food was great and the service was fast.  Our coupon /  credit posted from our credit card within 24 hours, so win all around.

Very delicious food and good service but definitely on the pricier side.
A reservation is highly recommended!

Appetizer: Fried Fingerling Potatoes (3/5)
The sauce to dip the potatoes in was delicious and had a hint of spiciness to it. The potatoes tasted very potato-y and not too fried / oily, and this is what I expect the average potato wedge to be cooked. However, was it worth $10...probably not.

Main 1: Garlic Chicken Ramen (3/5)
The chicken was cooked very well! It wasn't too dry. Big fan of the texture of the noodles. They were bouncy and absorbed the broth very well. The broth was too salty to drink. I had to essentially use the remaining rice from my other dish to add to the broth to dilute the saltiness of it. This was a very good portion size, but not big enough for the bowl to be $22. There are a ton of ramen spots in NYC, and this is definitely priced at the Momofuku brand.

Main 2: Black pepper steak (5/5)
This steak was cooked to its perfection. The perfect medium rare, not too dry, and very well seasoned. The pea shoots were also perfect and absorbed the sauce very well. Highly recommend this dish!

You can spend quality time here, enjoying a cold beer 'to go', especially considering their generous pitchers at incredibly attractive prices - starting from $19. Before you, like on a palm, unfolds the majestic Manhattan, with its soaring skyscrapers creating a unique urban landscape. Undoubtedly, this is one of the best places for a budget tourist in New York! The cuisine amazes with a variety of dishes, but my heart is forever devoted to this corner of Manhattan. I wholeheartedly recommend it.

This place is cool. Lots of excellent food options. Very clean and organized, and the people are friendly. Ms. Yolo was the best place to eat! From service to quality of food!! Will definitely eat there again when I return. You can mix up your empanadas as the are marked in the batter so no guessing. We went back and ordered more!!!

We will definitely come back and try the other food option.

Can’t decide on what to eat? Fighting over who wants what? Problem solved! Vanderbilt Market’s got it covered. With 15 different restaurants, you can choose from various cuisines, bars, sweets, and much more! They even have table service with the friendliest staffs that allows guests to sit comfortable at the table and skip the line. You can also tap a card on the table to orders seamlessly. Brings people together. We enjoyed tacos, pizza, and sushi along with a pitcher of refreshing beer. Service is quick and efficient with deliciously made food. Best of all, prices are fair and reasonable! Vanderbilt Market’s brings people together while enjoying drinking and eating. Stop by and enjoy time with friends and family!

Fumo: A Must-Visit Italian Gem in Harlem
​Fumo on Amsterdam Ave and 137th Street is, without a doubt, a must-visit culinary destination in Harlem. My recent dinner here with my wife was nothing short of exceptional, offering a perfect blend of great atmosphere, attentive service, and truly amazing food.
​From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was vibrant yet cozy, setting the ideal stage for a memorable night out. The energy is fantastic without being overwhelming, making it a perfect spot for either a special occasion or a casual weeknight treat. The service was equally good—our server was helpful, prompt, and genuinely friendly, ensuring we felt welcomed and well-cared for throughout the meal.
​The true highlight, however, was the food. I ordered the classic Spaghetti Carbonara and it was sublime. The sauce was rich and creamy, coated the perfectly al dente pasta, and was exactly the comforting, authentic dish I was craving. The Garlic Bread served alongside was crisp, buttery, and the ideal accompaniment.
​My wife opted for the Penne alla Vodka and was equally impressed. The sauce achieved that perfect balance—tangy from the tomato and decadent from the cream—a clear testament to high-quality ingredients and skillful preparation.
​Fumo offers a complete and unforgettable dining package. If you’re in the area and looking for high-quality Italian cuisine that backs up its reputation, stop searching. This place is an absolute gem.
​Highly, highly recommended!

We were promptly seated inside and served shortly after. The first server, Steven, took our drink orders and gave us a little time to peruse the menu. We ultimately chose a rigatoni bolognese (friend's daughter), a penne vodka with meatballs (friend), a naked penne vodka for my mom and I had a spaghetti vongole. For drinks, my mom and I each had a raspberry lemonade and my friend and her daughter had a Fumo mocktail and a coke, respectively.

Now after enjoying our meals, two other servers came and we requested extra bread from one and he never brought it, even after asking an additional time. Steven immediately brought it right after we were able to get his attention. Also while busting the table, the other server from the two mentioned earlier, reached across without asking for clearance which rubbed us all the wrong way because he passed really close to my face.
This turned us off from tipping extra because the service was not great and I just thought I should make a note of it but other than that, everything else was good to go. I'll be back to try the brunch and other menu items.

She received her wine before we received our drinks and her food before we received our appetizer, even though we were clearly there first.

The situation made me feel unwelcome, especially given that this occurred during Black History Month. My waiter never came back. Fortunately, another waiter, Miguel, completely turned the experience around. He was attentive, professional, and ensured that the remainder of our visit was pleasant. While the food was excellent and the drinks were good, the overall experience left a lasting negative impression. Due to how we were treated, I would not return. google_reviews.text: An absolutely awesome meal from start to finish! My partner and I had dinner here last night and it was the best meal I have had in years. We loved it. We have been wanting to eat sugar toads again for years and they are so hard to find. But we were amazed to see them on the menu here, they where delicious and very thoughtfully prepared with the guacamole bedding and greens with the glaze and fried green tomatoes everything came together beautifully! I was surprised to see fried green tomatoes this time of year. Also we LOVE West Virginia pepperoni rolls! They also had these on the menu that we could get as add-ons which we did and they were fantastic! We could taste how nice and smoky the pepperoni was and What tasted like fennel in it. We were surprised to see you that it came with a sauce as to our knowledge West Virginia pepperoni rolls are usually had room temp and without suace , but the way they served them with a tomato sauce and slightly warmed was a nice way to make them appropriate for a sit down restaurant. We also got the elderberry cream on top of a Fudgy brownie for dessert and that was delicious! Especially since you don’t see elderberry on menus very often. Our server was fantastic and so was all the servers in the dinning room, they worked together great and had fantastic attitudes and they was working hard because they were very very very busy. Although we didn’t need reservations And we didn’t have to wait to get a table they have plenty of tables. This restaurant is the best place to eat in all of the eastern panhandle of West Virginia and beyond honestly. My partner and I love visiting West Virginia but we have had absolutely no luck in finding any good places to eat, including in this town, until we found this gem! delicious! incredible pies, fried chicken, brunswick stew, and mac n cheese. can’t wait to go back. this plate made me so happy, and their staff did a great job serving our large group ~20 people for friday lunch

name: Huso
document: Huso. cuisine: Wine Bars Seafood. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Huso is my new favorite restaurant in NYC, and the finest overall dining experience I’ve had in nearly 19 years of living here and eating at the very best. From start to finish, the evening was pure perfection. The ambiance was serene and beautiful — like a high-end spa — setting the tone for a meal that was as thoughtful as it was exceptional.

The 10+ course tasting menu was exquisite, highly original, and perfectly portioned; unlike most prix fixe meals, I left feeling neither hungry nor overfull. While the entire meal was one collective standout, the egg and lobster with caviar, scallop with sunchoke and kombucha, beef with mushroom and périgord, and the grape, Sauternes, and olive oil palate cleanser were especially memorable. The flavors were unusual, precise, and utterly flawless. Pacing was spot on throughout.

Now, onto the service, which was not merely excellent but genuinely rare. Every interaction was intuitive, seamless, and perfectly calibrated: warm but professional, polished without stiffness, attentive without intrusion. The staff anticipated needs before they arose and executed each moment with calm confidence and absolute precision. It was, quite simply, the most refined and enjoyable service experience I have ever had, anywhere. I regret not noting every name, but I want to give special thanks to Gurman, Holly, and Madeline, each of whom exemplified this standard. You are all outstanding at what you do — thank you so much!

An unexpected highlight was a tour of the kitchen, which is itself stunning (and immaculately clean). Getting to watch Buddha Lo and his team in their element was a privilege and underscored just how much intention and craft sits behind every course. Additional Michelin recognition feels inevitable, and I already can’t wait to return for the spring menu.

Had a wonderful dining experience at Huso celebrating my birthday. It's been somewhere I've wanted to try for a while having followed chef Buddha Lo's journey. The experience did not disappoint. The Fall 2015 tasting menu is phenomenally innovative, with nods to seasonal ingredients, flavors and presentation. They are very much deserving of their recent Michelin star.

I highly recommend a wine pairing. The non alcoholic pairing was wonderful and went perfectly with each course. Although every course was delicious and memorable, my favorite was the milk roll, foie gras, truffle course with mushroom tea.

The hospitality team also went above and beyond to ensure my birthday was memorable. I loved the birthday dessert presentation, tour of the kitchen, and signed Polaroid to remember the experience.

Huso is a beautiful restaurant to spend a special occasion and I can't wait to see what chef does next. I might just have to come back for each seasonal menu!

Huso was probably the most special meal I’ve ever had. It truly felt like an experience from start to finish. The food was incredibly unique, elegant, and complex, with nothing feeling like an afterthought. Every course was beautifully prepared and memorable, making it impossible to choose a single favorite. The staff were exceptional, and I especially appreciated the kitchen tour and the chance to talk with Chef Buddha Lo. The food was unlike anything I’ve had before, and the entire evening truly special.

We celebrated my birthday at Huso not long after they opened, and it was such a memorable night. One of the coolest things about the restaurant is that they own their own caviar farm in Florida, and it definitely shows with caviar is woven into the tasting menu in a really generous way.

It’s a very small, intimate space with only about 8–10 tables, which made the whole evening feel special and personal. The service was smooth and attentive. The food itself was incredible, with really interesting flavor combinations and beautiful presentation, though it’s definitely a caviar-forward experience.

The tasting menu was easily 15–20 courses including all the little bites. By the end I was completely stuffed and honestly a little nauseous (in the best way?), and I haven’t done another tasting menu since. :)) Still, it was an unforgettable way to celebrate and a truly unique dining experience. It was clear they’d get a Michelin star and i was delighted to hear they recently did. Well deserved!

We are big fans of Chef Buddha and had dined at the old Huso location uptown before their move to Tribeca. While the new restaurant is beautiful, same with the food, we found the courses to be a bit too fussy and flavors muted. Many of the courses tasted good but nothing exceptional, and the dessert and sweets were average. We were a bit disappointed by the food, maybe because we had such high expectations. We did not enjoy the non-alcoholic pairing. We were hoping for more creative mocktail like pairings that we had at other similar Michelin star restaurants.

We had dinner in the private dining room downstairs with a nice view of the kitchen. The service was great with a friendly and professional staff. Overall, we had a good dining experience here and will come back for another try when there's a new menu.

"Delicata Squash" - atrocious taste and texture. Taste -  I roast sweet potatoes for my dog, and my sweet potatoes are 20 times sweeter and tastier. Texture - gritty (how was that possible to achive?).

"Artichoke Tempura" - worse taste and texture. Artichokes clearly came from a can. Peculiar sourish taste to them and moist texture from pickling liquid.

Bar area looks really good!

Expensive restaurant. Things need some refinement in my opinion.

Definitely will be back again!!!

document: Junior's Restaurant. cuisine: Bakeries Breakfast & Brunch Burgers. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We went to juniors in the early afternoon for a quick meal before heading back to the square and the wife had the burger special D and I had the soup and sandwich lunch special with split pea soup and a Pastrami sandwich. My wife said the burger was good and the fries were actually the highlight of her meal. The burger was a little think for her liking but maybe okay for some. We think a thinner patty maybe even two thinner patties would be better but that is our opinion of course. The meat was good quality. I had the split pea and pastrami and both were very good. The pastrami was in my top 10 which I would say is very very good and the split pea would be in my top 25. It was good but was missing some heavy stock and cream flavor in my opinion. We did enjoy our meal and would go back though. We were too full for cheesecake which we wanted but just couldn’t eat.  Please note they have Pepsi and not Coke products. The waiter told us they had Diet Coke but my wife knew instantly it wasn’t…if you know, you know!!

First night in NYC and came straight to Juniors off of a recommendation and it did not disappoint! I had the steak sandwich which was cooked to a great medium and seasoned well. We also had the pastrami sandwich that was tasty and had a great thousand island dressing to go with it. My boys split the chicken and ribs dish which was super tasty. We also had a crease chicken salad that had great flavor. Overall, great food at a reasonable price and good portions.

Was going to see the Bueno Vista Social Club show on 45thth street in NYC & noticed this restaurant 1/2 a block away and had plenty of time to have lunch.  What a find. The food was exceptional.  It reminded me of my youth in NYC and traditional Delis

We were stuffed but could not leave without having their famous cheesecake for desert.  We ordered the raspberry swirl and was unbelievably light tasty. We had small bottles of Proseco to top off our meal.  The price and wait to get a table was well worth it. When we left the restaurant,  the line was queuing up for our show; perfect timing.

I liked the warm setting and helpful staff. Even though I had a reservation, I still waited about 15 minutes to be seated, but the food made the delay easier to overlook. The pastrami burger was good, and the chocolate cheesecake was the best part of the meal. Overall, the experience was solid with a few small bumps.

Went to Junior's just for dessert and everything was great. We got their:

- Pumpkin pie cheesecake - this is a slice from a pie that was half pumpkin pie on the bottom with a cheesecake on top.

- Carrot cake cheesecake - a real, hearty carrot cake layered in between cheese cake.

- Fox's U-Bet Brooklyn egg cream - old-timey chocolate soda.

Service was polite, quick and accommodating. Don't sleep on Junior's famous cheese cakes and desserts!

document: The Shell Restaurant. cuisine: Seafood Mediterranean Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: After a few visits, I can really endorse this place for top quality, fresh, well prepared seafood. I’ve had the salmon and branzino, the oysters and calamari, salad, clam chowder, warm fresh bread, and vegetables. The staff is always friendly and full of advice about the menu. Ambiance is cozy and low key yet classy enough for a Saturday night out. Even their restaurant week menu is high quality and top value, in keeping with the rest of the offerings. Also have midweek paella specials! Neighborhood favorite that’s really popular for their summer outdoor cafe.

I came here with 3 friends and we had an amazing time. The restaurant is located on Amsterdam and 91st, with both indoor seating and a lovely terrace outside. Even though it’s on a busy street, it’s surprisingly quiet and peaceful. The outdoor space is super welcoming with some nice background music.

The owner and the waiters were absolutely fantastic super warm and friendly.

We all ordered the $55 menu of the day, which included an appetizer, main course, and dessert. For starters, we had a choice of oysters, shrimp, or calamari. I had the calamari, which were excellent, and the oysters were fresh and delicious too.

For mains, I had the lobster ravioli perfectly cooked. My friends had salmon, which was beautifully cooked and served with an amazing sauce.

We also shared two bottles of white wine, with prices starting around $70–90. Not cheap, but fair for NYC.

For dessert, we had tiramisu. All in all, a fantastic experience. The food was excellent, the service outstanding, and the atmosphere very pleasant. We ended up paying about $460 total for four people (including tip), which felt reasonable for the quality. I’ll definitely be back and will recommend it to friends!

This place is a gem. We stumbled upon it while in the neighborhood. We got a side order of the crab cake, which was mediocre at best.

I always come here after work. The atmosphere is great. The service is amazing specialize your quality and the owner. He is so loving so sweet and so friendly and he spoils his guest. This place is a must and the food is amazing. The drinks are the bomb.

name: Katz's Delicatessen
document: Katz's Delicatessen. cuisine: Delis American. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I tried the pastrami and corned beef sandwiches, and honestly, I think this is why I don’t usually get excited about viral food spots. The sandwiches were pretty mediocre. The meat didn’t have much flavor, the sandwich was served super cold, and the texture was too tough to really enjoy.
The bread, though, was excellent, probably the best part of the whole thing. The russian sauce is sweet relish nothing special. I felt that the restaurant was overrated and that’s why I didn’t enjoy that much.
It’s not something I’d go back for, and if you haven’t tried it yet, you’re not really missing much. That said, the historical vibe of the restaurant was cool. But it has a crazy line to wait to go in and then wait for available cutter. I wouldn’t personally recommend it, but if you’re curious about viral places, it might still be worth checking out just for the experience.

Just left Katz’s Delicatessen and it absolutely lived up to the hype.

There was a huge lineup when we got there, but it moved fast. We were inside in about 10 minutes. We lined up at cutter #7 and that took another 15 minutes or so. Even with the crowd, they were running a super smooth operation. You can tell they’ve been doing this for a long time.

We ordered the pastrami on club with cheese, corned beef on rye, a potato latke, and fries. The sandwiches came with pickles, both half sour and full sour, which were great.

The pastrami was out of this world. Easily the best I’ve had. Tender, juicy, packed with flavor. The latke was also excellent, crispy on the outside and soft inside.

The corned beef just wasn’t for me, but that’s personal preference. I do wish I had tried the brisket instead.

Overall, a classic NYC experience and definitely worth the visit.

Katz’s Delicatessen is definitely an NYC classic and a must-visit at least once. The atmosphere is super authentic and chaotic in a fun way — it really feels like a piece of New York history.

The food is very good, especially the pastrami sandwich. The meat is tender, flavorful, and the portions are huge (easily enough to share). You can tell the quality is there and that they know what they’re doing.

That said, it’s extremely crowded and the system can feel a bit stressful and confusing, especially if it’s your first time. Sometimes it’s not very clear where you’re supposed to pay or if you can add more items to your order, which makes the experience a little overwhelming.

Prices are also quite high for what you get, even though it’s iconic.

Overall, it’s a great experience and worth trying for the vibe and the food, but probably not a place I’d go to regularly. Still, a solid 4 stars for the quality and the legendary NYC feel.

The food was fine and about what you would expect from a decent delicatessen. They're fairly consistent with their level of quality and portion sizes as well. If your goal was to get a great pastrami sandwich, you're probably better off just going somewhere else (and it would be a lot cheaper, too). But this is a NY staple and is a great place to visit once (and I mean just once).

Their prices reflect their mainstream popularity so just keep that in mind. Their portion sizes are also huge so that offsets it somewhat. Just something to keep in mind.

Lines can get long but you can avoid that by going earlier or later. You could also order pickup if you don't want to stand inside for long.

I mentioned earlier that if your goal was to get a great pastrami sandwich, you could go elsewhere. I'm not going to list any places since that would be inappropriate on someone else's business page, but you could find them through google. Alternatively, if your goal was just to go to any random delicatessen, you could walk down the street.

Katz’s Delicatessen is not just a restaurant — it’s a piece of New York history. From the moment you walk in, you feel the authentic, old-school atmosphere that has made this place legendary for over a century.

The pastrami sandwich is simply iconic. The meat is hand-carved right in front of you, incredibly tender, juicy, and packed with flavor. Served on fresh rye bread with just the right amount of mustard, it’s easily one of the best sandwiches you’ll ever taste. The portions are generous — you definitely won’t leave hungry.

The atmosphere is lively, energetic, and uniquely New York. The walls are covered with photos and memories from decades past, adding to the charm and authenticity of the experience. It’s busy, it’s loud, and that’s exactly what makes it special.

The staff is efficient and experienced, keeping things moving even when the place is packed. Despite the crowds, the service remains organized and professional.

If you want to experience real, classic New York deli culture, Katz’s Delicatessen is an absolute must. Legendary food, historic atmosphere, and unforgettable flavors. Highly recommended

The coffee is blow away and roasted in Brooklyn and the owner is beyond nice and service oriented he even gave me some beans to take home! Try the ricotta toast or anything it’s all extremely good!

Very small place with wait lines regularly on the weekends. Somebody was always hitting my chair trying to walk by. The location is very convenient near Penn Station. I went on Tuesday and it was pretty much empty. The food was good but overhyped and not worth the price.  I tried chicken katsu that was just underwhelming in flavor and quality.

Food is on point, just the chia latte is lacking in flavor. The place is small, so the wait feels long. This place is best for dates or one-on-one. Fortunately, we have a kid. They are very accommodating. Also, our kid isn’t loud.

está chido la comida, está buena, la mesa están un poquito pequeñas, pero da igual

Great breakfast spot. My kids and I were lucky, we came here early enough to not have to wait, around 9:20am on a Saturday. When we were leaving the line was very long.

Everything we ordered came quickly. The Shakshuka was not good at all, however everything else was really yummy. Next time i want to order a toast with cheese and figs, I saw it on other tables, looked great!
The service was great too.

I have travelled the world extensively over 40 years. I ate at all restaurants ranging from pop & mom’s to Michelin three stars. This is my honest review of the breakfast spot In Common NYC next to Manhattan West / Hudson Yards in NYC, USA.

One of the best breakfast spots in the neighborhood! It’s very popular, so you might have to wait 5–10 minutes for a table, but it’s absolutely worth it. The place is clean, well kept, and the service is fast and friendly. The menu is varied — we tried the whipped ricotta tart and the avocado toast, both excellent, and the specialty coffees were perfectly prepared. You’ll leave happy and full, ready to take on a New York day! Prices are a bit on the high side, but quite standard for this area.

name: Rubirosa
document: Rubirosa. cuisine: Italian Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Fun, quintessential little Italy vibes of an established New York City restaurant. Great service, and menu is much brighter than just pizza. Braised beef braciole and short rib anglotti were favorites for our table.
Reservations took extensive planning and setting a timer at midnight to jump on it, but totally worth it. We went on a cold day where wait times were short, but I don’t think this is typical.
Waiter was particularly attentive to our food, allergies, and double checked with the kitchen on ingredients.
The menu is not overwhelming and there’s a focused list of desserts and beverages. The kind of place where options have been carefully honed over years of service.
We also tried the tie-dye and honey pie pizzas. Crust was exceptionally thin. This is what New York style pizza is traditionally known for. If this is your thing, you’ll love it. They have it down to a science.
A definite repeat. Would rate 7.5/10 for the pizza experience, but all else was a solid 9+.

The pizzas are absolutely delicious—perfectly crispy crust, flavorful sauce, and great quality toppings every time. Their drinks are just as impressive and pair perfectly with the food. The vibe is lively yet cozy. Always a go-to when I’m craving amazing pizza in the city! 🍕🍸

It is a rustic yet homey restaurant serving traditional Italian fares. Their thin crust pizza is crispy and chewy, and pasta is fresh with rich garlic savory pasta sauce.  Their zappoli is perfectly fried crispy outside and doughy soft inside 🙂, and cocktails are delicious!  It is a popular go to place and is crowded. So, you should make a reservation to avoid the long wait

Wow this meal was unreal. Everything hit the mark. No joke the pizza has me looking up Rubirosa sauce jars to order because the pizza was that good. Great arugula salad with the tastiest dressing and an absolutely delicious ravioli dish in the butter sauce. I don’t *want* to come back… I NEED to come back. ❤️

After months of trying to get a reservation (yes, it’s that hard), I finally decided to just try going without one. The wait was around 45 minutes but it was worth it because the food was great! I loved the half & half pizza (tie-dye and vodka) and the mini rice balls. Definitely a must try for thin crust, cheesy, NY-style pizza.

name: Gurumé
document: Gurumé. cuisine: Korean Tapas/Small Plates Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Gurumé is such a fun Korean tapas spot near Rockafeller Center 🤍 I came here with three of my girlfriends on a Saturday night and we made a reservation which I’d definitely recommend. The vibes were lively but still perfect for a girls night out ✨

We started with their festive espresso martini called the Rudolph 🍸🎄 It had a hint of caramel and came with a little marshmallow on the side which was such a cute touch. Sweet smooth and the perfect way to kick off the night.

For food we ordered a bunch to share which is 100% the move here. The crispy corn and cheese was one of my favorites and such a great starter 🌽🧀 Then we tried the birria mandu and wow!! This is a must order. It was so good that we got it again. Super savory packed with flavor and the meat was unreal 🥟

We also got the everything tteokbokki which were so fun and satisfying and the baby back ribs were insanely tender and falling right off the bone 🍖 Definitely one of my top dishes of the night.

We ended with the black sesame bread pudding and I’m not exaggerating when I say it was insanely good 🍮 I’ve never had anything like it and I’ve literally come back just for this dessert alone.

It was also my birthday and it was so sweet that they sang happy birthday 🥹🎉 The food came out quickly the waiters were super attentive and overall the experience was amazing. I would absolutely come back and already can’t wait to return 💖🍽️✨

Steak & potatoes, corn cheese, and the black sesame bread pudding stood out.

The dumplings had good skin but I personally didn’t vibe with the fusion. The chicken wings had crunchy skin but the wings themselves were not super flavorful. Beet salad was ok, good as a palette cleanser but can probably be skipped

Josephine was incredible! We arrived around 6:10 with tickets to the Stranger Things play at 7pm, and she wasted no time walking us through the menu and helping us choose the perfect dishes. Dinner was absolutely delicious, and thanks to her efficiency and attention, we made it to our show right on time. Amazing staff, amazing food , we can’t wait to come back!

This was a good place but compared to other more authentic Korean food places this place was meh.
Food: the wings were amazing, great balance of sweet an and savory with extreme crunch. The ramen was a bit over the top with the spiciness and muted the actual flavors that would’ve stood out kid better had they not been drowned in the spicy sauce. The soft boiled onsen egg was impressive but it would’ve been better if it wasn’t ice cold. The chip bits at the beginning were super oily and were a bit like the dregs at th bottom of a deep fryer or what’s leftover at the end of a bag of potato chips.
Price: way over priced for the portion sizes even for NYC. If you’re going to be a tapas place then make the living and portions match
Service: very kind servers and attentive, they took the time to let us know our wings might be slightly delayed and to describe each dish in detail and our water was promptly refilled each time without needing to ask
Ambience: very loud that we struggled to hear the staff and had to keep repeating our prefer because they couldn’t hear us either

We were staying next door and went for dinner pre broadway show. What a great concept, a tapa style service with Korean food, like Spanish food meant to share and to marinate with a drink. Service was very good and fast. We had korean chicken wings, steak and potatos, pork belly and Korean radish, tuna tartar. Everything was delicious, drinks were very good too. Highly recommended.

The atmosphere here is charming, and the food never disappoints. What I enjoy the most are the drinks - they serve perfectly balanced tequila cocktails with fresh juice that are not too strong or sweet. It's just perfect! I'll definitely keep coming back whenever I'm in NYC.

Simple Mexican located near Radio City.  Dinner was bustling downstairs and upstairs but food comes out quick.  Spice level on the enchiladas was medium to spicy so beware. name: Farida
document: Farida. cuisine: Uzbek Halal Modern European. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
We had an amazing experience at this restaurant today! Maria, who served us, was absolutely wonderful. She was very friendly and recommended many delicious dishes for us, including the plov and the milk tea. Everything tasted incredibly authentic and flavorful.

I’m from China, and the flavors here are very close to the cuisine from the Xinjiang region back home, which made it even more special for me. It truly felt authentic and comforting.

Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for real Central Asian flavors. Amazing food and excellent service!

Farida Restaurant is an absolute gem! The food was outstanding, and the hospitality truly made the experience unforgettable.

Max, our host, and Abu, our server and co-host, were incredibly warm, friendly, and welcoming. From the moment we arrived, they made us feel completely at home. Their recommendations were spot-on, and their attention and kindness made the evening extra special.

We ordered the Tender Veal Liver with Mushrooms, the Mediterranean Breeze, and the ground lamb kebab—everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. You can truly taste the quality and care in every dish.

To top off an already amazing feast, Max and the restaurant generously treated us to the Chak Chak dessert on the house—and wow, it was absolutely delicious! Such a wonderful and thoughtful surprise. Do yourself a favor and try this amazing dessert—it’s so, so good!

What really sets this place apart is the exceptional customer service. Max and Abu went above and beyond to take care of us, and their genuine hospitality is the reason this has become one of my favorite restaurants in New York.

Incredible food, incredible people, and a wonderful atmosphere.
I absolutely love this place—highly recommended! 🌟🍽️

I really enjoyed visiting this Kazakh restaurant. I tried the lagman and the buns with meat, cheese, and spinach. Everything was incredibly tasty and freshly prepared. The dishes impressed me with their rich flavors. The atmosphere in the restaurant is very cozy and welcoming. I would also like to highlight the attentive and friendly staff. I will definitely come back and recommend this place to my friends.

We had such a wonderful experience at this restaurant! The food was absolutely delicious — everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked.
The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, with beautiful traditional touches that made the whole experience feel special.
A special thank you to our waitress, Maria. She was incredibly kind, attentive, and professional. She made sure we had everything we needed and gave great recommendations. Her warm attitude truly made our evening even better.

this place is super cute! I loved all the little embroidery on the chairs and how welcoming and warm they make it.
They have a large bar in the front with smaller seating and they have a room at the back for larger tables as well as private events if you want to throw them
We tried the Manti and we love the pumpkin ones as well as the spinach. I would definitely come back for the kebabs. They were amazing. I also really love the herring in a fur coat. The one dish would pass on would be the dessert which was sort of fried noodles with ice cream. but I think everything else was outstanding.
The service was really good as well. They have a very sweet young girl who explains all the dishes to you and answer your questions and helps you to decide what you would like especially if the food is not familiar to you. I would definitely recommend this place and would come back.

google_reviews.text: Many thanks to the staff for providing ADA accommodations for my spouse and me.  The show was great… only thing: your cocktail prices approach usury.  $25 for a draft beer & well ranch water.  Pro-tip: try catch a buzz before you go!

Great venue... it's a classic though plan on standing for the show. The bat had a great selection, including my favorite bourbon to so for hours.  Love this place... glad it's still in business all these years!
One of the very best music venues in SF, can't go wrong with a show here

Happy New Year 2026 and cheers to hopefully a year of more concerts and performances.

I came to see David Archuleta on his Earthly Delights tour and was so impressed by how intimate and comfortable the experience was at The Independent.

The staging area felt small but meant you could really get up close and personal with the artists. There was ample seating on the sides and on the second floor too if you'd like to avoid too much of the crowd, but can't go wrong with the space and being so close to the stage.

When it did get packed with guests coming in after the opener, I could tell the AC getting cranked up a notch to help with the sweltering gay heat exuding from all of us inside the venue.

Drinks here were served by the friendliest of bartenders with cocktails going for $14, not the worst for a concert venue. I enjoyed my Passion Fruit Rum that I got to nurse through the night.

Ticket checks were easy, bag checks were seamless, and I have to give props to the staff for making it a great experience.

Good music venue.  It is relatively small so you can get close to the performers.  Lighting was well done.  Sound seemed to echo a bit much.  The first performer was cool.  He played a guitar made with a shovel.  The second band was not good.  The headliner was okay.  Patrons were not the nicest.  The staff seemed professional.  Wish the floor was not sticky.

I had the Cucumber Fresh mocktail and it was delicious. My brother ordered the Bee-Hind mocktail, which was on the sweeter side but not overly sweet. My boyfriend had the Redfreshment—it was a bit bitter, but I actually liked that since I enjoy bitter flavors.

document: The Smith. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Food here was really good. Stopped by with a friend on a random weekday and this place was packed. We ordered everything from the calamari, spicy salmon tartare, braised short rib mafaldine, bistro burger and the honeycrisp apple pie. The calamari had some surprising additions, but very delicious and a must order if you love calamari. The salmon tartare was really fresh and tasty. The mafaldine was cooked al dente and the short rib you could tell was slowly braised for hours.

My friend and I really enjoyed our experience here. The ambience is very warm, bright and definitely loud. If you want a private more intimate place this may not be it unless you have a private dining room. The servers were attentive and I loved how they bring out still water and sparkling. Highly recommend making reservations in advance.

My family and I visited The Smith on a busy Sunday around 5 pm. Thankfully we had reservations, otherwise it may have been a bit of a wait. The atmosphere was lively, and the food was solid across the board.

We ordered the calamari, kids cheeseburger, the Smith burger, and the braised short rib mafaldine. Everything was well prepared, with the short rib mafaldine standing out as rich and comforting.

A nice touch was the fresh bread service and the option of house still or sparkling water. Our server was friendly, though service slowed at times due to the crowd.

Overall, The Smith is a reliable choice for good food.

My wife and I had dinner here on Thursday and had a wonderful time. We had great service. Allyne took great care of us during our meal.
Our cocktails were excellent. I had a Whiskey Sour and My wife had the Yozu Gimlet. Both were well-made and perfect.
We started with the oyster sampler and it was fantastic. If you like oysters, you should give it a try.
We shared the ribeye and it was perfectly cooked, flavorful, and very tender.
Dessert was the Sticky Toffee Pudding, which was to-die-for. Rich, but not too sweet, it was a great way to end the meal.
Overall, it was a good experience and well worth the visit.

This feels like the place to go for business dinners and celebration occasions, yet it's comfortable enough for friends to meet or a nice date night.

The food is really good.   It's not a huge menu, but what is served is really good.

We had two vegetarians in our group and each person had something different, and our burger loving friend was super happy.   My husband really loved the muscles...so lots of options for everyone.

The drink menu is extensive a d we all tried something new.  The ladies tried the elegant cocktails, the gentlemen, the whiskeys and bourbon.  Everyone enjoyed their drinks.

I would definitely recommend trying The Smiths the next time you need a great restaurant and a really good cocktail!

After a day at the Mall, we went to The Smith for lunch. We were seated immediately, and our server greeted us as we sat down although it was busy. The sourdough bread was very good. I opted to get the veggie burger which was moist and flavorful. The fries were crisp. My friend had the Vanilla Bean French Toast. I ordered the Cucumber Mule mocktail which was delicious. We went during brunch but would have loved a few more options on the menu. Overall the food, staff and atmosphere were impressive. Definitely recommend.

document: Thai Diner. cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The funny thing about this place is I didn’t know anything about it until recently. My coworker. I work at food for workspace would constantly talk about how this is her favorite place and constantly talk about.

The funny thing is that I booked a reservation here with my partner and then the next night my coworker took us all to Thai Diner so I had this place two times in a row completely different experiences

The food here is amazing. The portions are large. It’s authentic the papaya salad alone makes you wanna come back for so much more the way it’s made is perfect and I’m literally salivating as I talk about it.

I haven’t had a dish here I haven’t liked we also had a loaded disco fries, which is extremely crispy and tasty. They were even delivered to work one day and got cold and I still ate them which I don’t recommend in that way they’re delicious fresh

All the noodle dishes were good but there’s also a big sundae dessert thing that is highly recommended. Oh my God it blew me away Huge beautiful and exciting. See the pictures.

The ambience alone is stunning. It’s very warm. I got a great feel inside and out. The look is so cool like a New York City diner mixed with a Thai restaurant, stunning authentically, beautiful all the way through they thought of everything

Go here or go often the staff is amazing. I really don’t have anything bad to save this place. It’s one of my top restaurants in 2025.

The service was great and the food was delicious.  Oysters were fresh and loved the green sauce, the duck wonton soup had really great flavor and wonton filling was juicy and flavorful, the crab fried rice had nice large pieces of crab and came with the delicious green seafood sauce. The cocktails were strong. The coconut sundae was big and good to share the candied peanuts added a nice crunch and caramel flavor whipped cream was creamy and ice cream delicious. I understand the hype and its worth a try.

This was an unexpected surprise and I enjoyed every minute of it!

I was in the area and happened to search for a breakfast spot, and this popped up as a nearby recommendation. I was intrigued because I have never seen breakfast at a Thai restaurant. What’s sit out most was the Elephant Ear French toast.

The wait was quick just 20 minutes and we were seated for a party of two. The service was just as quick despite it being a busy and packed restaurant.

I’m so happy I ordered the French toast. It was so unique and delicious. It has the flavors of a chai tea wrapped up in a delicious elephant ear French toast. Highly recommended.

I will be back soon for more!

drunken dumplings 4/5
- dipping sauce was to die for, so flavorful and had a spicy kick to it!

phat thai w/chicken  5/5
- cant go wrong with a classic, right amount of tamarind sauce so the noodles weren’t dry at all (though they could have given us half a lime not barely 1/4 of it)

panang neuh 5/5
- braised beef was soooo tender, curry was so yummy though my friend found it a bit salty but would def recommend and get again, a must have!!

cheesesteak phat bai horapha w/fries 2/5
- probably wouldnt order this again… was thrilled at first to make it before the cut off time to order this but (saying this as a big lover of cheese) the one they used made this overly salty and hard to eat… had about 1-2 bites before i set it to the side, removed the contents and ended up pairing it with the white rice from the panang neuh to dilute the saltiness of it. loved the fries though, were very crispy!

aside from the food, cant say too much about the atmosphere from INSIDE the actual diner, I understand adding a secondary attachment to the business to being able to serve more customers but it was 18 degrees outside when we went. We got seated on the outside attachment near the windows and had to keep our coats on with how much draft air was coming in, noted about 3 or so space heaters on the roof but could barely feel them working at all especially when you aren’t seated under one. Also note the lack of space between each table and the servers having to wait at the end of the row because there was only enough room for people to leave in a single file line (all while having to make sure that none of their garments aren’t accidentally ending up in your food as they’re leaving or arriving). This caused them to barely notice when we had to set plates to the side and stack them so we had more room on our table, (also note again if you are seated at a table for 2 you have to play tetris to have multiple plates fit on such a small table). Or when we were ready for the check (couldnt flag someone down to come/took a while for them to finally ring us up).

Would definitely come again to try their other dishes but maybe during the warmer months or if they’re able to seat us inside next time/come during a slower period. :)

What an excellent restaurant. They have the classics and then fresh new spins on diner food. I really enjoyed it.

My favorite was starting off with the scallops and ultimately the snapper was the winner for all of us. Other highlights include the Khao Soi and oysters. Get the broiled ones.

Highly recommend and the cocktails are great too. 🇹🇭🍹🍽️

name: The Flatiron Room Murray Hill
document: The Flatiron Room Murray Hill. cuisine: New American Jazz & Blues Lounges. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: This place is phenomenal. I took my fiancé here yesterday for his birthday and we absolutely adored the ambiance of this place. Well decorated and has great live music! Upon arrival we were given two complimentary servings of champagne and wished a happy birthday. The appetizers were great; the kimchi fried rice was so delicious I will be thinking about it for months. Omakase box was tasty, fresh, and light. The gin and vodka martinis were strong but very light. We also got complimentary dessert! The service was excellent and I can’t wait to come back!!!

Great vibes, great food, great music!

Went for a friend’s birthday got the chefs tasting menu, was pleasantly surprised with the quality and quantity of food. Our server Erin was very kind and the manager Ben provided amazing customer service. Will definitely come back!

The place is very cozy. We saw Brian Newman on Saturday night and he was fantastic. I would go back just to see him.
The service was very good. The cocktails delicious. The food was ok to good

I truly loved my time at this restaurant. Everything from the atmosphere to the service felt spot on. The steak completely stole the show, tender, juicy, and cooked exactly the way it should be. Every bite was packed with rich flavor. The drinks were equally enjoyable and complemented the food beautifully. It was one of those meals that leaves you genuinely satisfied and excited to come back again.

10s, 10s, 10s across the board! Wow was I impressed with this place! The minute you step into The Flatiron Room it feels like walking in the door of a 1930s jazz club in the most fabulous way! We came on Saturday because we wanted a jazz show. We got WAY more than we bargained for. The ambiance of the place was stellar. Everything from the caged bottles stacked all along the upper part of the wall, to the cozy booths and classic looking bar tucked off in the corner leaving room to see the stage. Next, the service - on point! Erin, our server, was top notch, helpful, always available, and uber friendly, but that’s also true of the rest of the staff we interacted with. The food - amazing! WAY better than any “dinner and a show” type places I’ve ever tried. Highly recommend the Yellow Fish appetizer. Also the cheese board is really well done, really enjoyed that. If you don’t order the sphere desert thing, you’re truly missing out on life (I’m not kidding)! But the stars of the night were the Brian Newman Quintet. Man, talk about an excellent exhibition of a unique twist on iconic jazz. They are an exceptionally talented group of (very good looking 😉) musicians who really put on a great show. You can find them there every Sat night from 9pm - 12am. It’s no wonder the place has a lot of repeaters, and what’s even more amazing is these guys actually take the time to remember your name! My husband and I were floored. We got a chance to exchange a few words with Brian and Tommy (the owner of this fine establishment) outside and I didn’t hesitate to tell them then that we would be back! Honestly the only thing missing for me and I’m super nitpicking is if there was a small dance area somewhere because honestly I kept fighting the urge to jiggle my body to the tunes 😆. I even forgive that I have to come to midtown for this place - I’ll suck it up to go there again. Anyway moral of this story - high class joint, high class meal, high class service, high class entertainment (for no added cost). Great night out, worth every penny!

google_reviews.text:
We joined the online wait list at 10, but the line moved up very fast we ended up getting a table very quickly. This is my first time here and I was so in awe when I saw the restaurant. It was very spacious but full of customers. The staff were very generous and helpful. Someone broke some cups not too far from us and at least 3 staff came up to us and asked if we were okay. I was so touched.

The food was very good. The crab soup dumplings was delicious and not fishy. I'm generally not a big fan of green beans, but these beans were so addictive! My favorite would be the chocolate dumplings. I personally like to wait until they firmed up a bit so the chocolate filling was not super runny. It's very rich though so if you're not a big chocolate fan, it might be a bit too much for you. Well.. not for me! lol

Overall, a very good experience. I would definitely come back!

Absolutely loved our meal at Din Tai Fung. The spicy wontons were the standout, perfectly delicate wrappers with a flavorful filling and just the right kick of heat. The chicken xiao long bao were beautifully crafted, with that signature burst of rich, savory broth in every bite.

The spicy noodles had great texture and depth, bold but not overwhelming, and tied everything together. And the mochi dessert was the perfect finish: soft, lightly sweet, and just indulgent enough. Everything tasted incredibly fresh and thoughtfully prepared. We’ll definitely be back.

I went to din tai fung with my family for the first time, and after trying to get a reservation forever (this place is so popular), we finally made it and it absolutely did not disappoint. This is easily one of my favorite restaurants I’ve been to in a long time. We started with appetizers: the cucumber salad and the sweet and sour pork baby back ribs. Both were delicious and honestly exceeded our expectations. For dumplings, we had the chicken dumplings (great) and the shrimp & pork shao mai, which were also excellent. We ordered the string beans with garlic, plus two noodle dishes the sesame oil noodles and the spicy noodles. Both were amazing, but just a heads up: the spicy noodles definitely have a kick 🌶️For dessert, we got the chocolate & mochi xiao long bao, and wow… those were fantastic. Next time I’m definitely ordering two orders! Drinks were just as good. I had the pear lychee martini and an espresso martini with a nice twist  both were excellent. We also took a honey lemonade with boba to go, and that was the perfect sweet finish. The service was great,very attentive and I really liked how the food came out one dish at a time. It gave us time to enjoy everything without feeling rushed. Highly recommend. This is officially one of my new favorite spots, and my family already can’t wait to go back and try more dishes we didn’t get to this time.

Din Tai Fung absolutely lives up to the hype. From the moment you walk in, the service is warm, attentive, and incredibly polished. The food is consistently outstanding — the soup dumplings are perfection with delicate wrappers, rich broth, and perfectly seasoned filling. Every dish we tried was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully executed.

The space itself is modern, clean, and buzzing without feeling overwhelming, making it great for everything from a casual lunch to a special night out. You can really tell how much care goes into both the food and the overall experience.

The hype this place gets… it’s all REAL! this was by far the best dinner I have had in NYC!

Let’s start with the important part… get the chocolate dumplings…. We ordered it and then ordered another bc it was too good to share and we needed more!

We also had the chicken dumplings, chicken long bao, spicy chicken wontons, shrimp fried rice and the fried noodles….. alll soooooo good. I don’t eat seafood so I had some of the rice and usually you can taste the fishiness in stuff like that but nope, it was still soooo good. I am not exaggerating, there was not one thing we didn’t love.

They were out of the beans when we went so we got the garlic broccoli and idk how they made them but I think I could have possibly gotten my picky eating kids to love them (they were not with me lol) but they were delicious! The cucumber salad was good…not amazing but still good. I kinda wish the cucumbers were sliced thinner but it was still good!

Truly the best meal I’ve had. Make reservations early or get on the waitlist early. It’s absolutely worth it!

I went to Seasalt for my birthday dinner and it exceeded all of my expectations. When we walked in we immediately felt the energetic vibe of the restaurant packed with locals accommodating large and small crowds with a packed bar and a swanky lounge. We also appreciated our server who was bright, bubbly, and incredibly knowledgeable on menu items and wines. We got the octopus and ceviche to start. Our servers recommend we take every element of the dish and eat it in one bite to get the full experience and she was absolutely  spot on. The crispy salty capers, chilis, and citrus complimented the octopus so well. The ceviche which featured grouper was some of the best I’ve ever. Light yet packed with flavor. Overall, Seasalt is great for any occasion. Every element of each dish was carefully curated to highlight the fish. It’s upscale dining yet casual atmosphere made it the perfect evening to celebrate my birthday.

The first time we went, Kristen took care of us. She recognized us last night!  She has a great memory and is a wonderful server.

The service was great too — friendly, attentive, and everything arrived quickly despite how busy it was.

If you love seafood and want a truly unique dining experience, this is 100% worth it. Definitely one of the most memorable AYCE spots I’ve ever been to.

The food was outstanding. The baked oysters were absolutely delicious — rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. And the duck pappardelle was a true standout: tender, deeply savory, and beautifully executed. Every dish felt thoughtful and satisfying.

A spot we’ll definitely be coming back to.

Michael is such an impressive chef, and I was hyped to try this restaurant after having Porchetta Shop in Charleston - it far exceeded my high expectations. I haven’t had pasta that got me this excited since I was in Rome, and at da Toscano we shared two pasta dishes that were a perfect 10/10 - no notes. On top of that the focaccia appetizer and pistachio tres leches were outstanding, and the service was warm and friendly. My wife and I were grateful to be able to celebrate our upcoming anniversary here and will likely visit again next time we’re in NYC.

Crazy good. Amazing place. Best Italian restaurant in the city!

Went here for a friend’s birthday after not losing out on a Carbone reservation. What serendipity! Everything we ordered turned out to be perfect!

- Warm Rosemary Focaccia
- Octopus carpaccio

5/5

Can’t wait to return and try everything else on the menu!

The artichoke salad is excellent and definitely worth trying. The octopus carpaccio was very tasty. The sea bass sauce was presented very well. The service was friendly, but the atmosphere was a bit cold. I would definitely recommend it.

I spontaneously walked in today, not knowing what to expect. It ended up being one of the best experiences I've had with Italian. The server's recommendations were on point and just right. Simply astounding, I can't wait to come back and try their other dishes.

name: Kajiken
document: Kajiken. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This place was bustling on a Friday afternoon. We approached the host and told him that we are vegetarian and do not eat meat or seafood. He suggested the options we could choose from the menu and quickly seated us.

Everything in the buffet section was properly labeled with all the ingredients used, especially if it contained seafood, fish sauce, nuts, etc. This was great for people with allergies, food sensitivities, and also for people like me. I wish they had a few more veggie options like fried rice or noodles vegetarian version in the buffet and veggie curry. That would have made it 10/10.

We went with the overall BBQ and hot pot option. They suggested we go for the tomato base for the hot pot, as it’s the vegetarian version with no meat or seafood base, perfect even for vegans. There were decent veggie options and enough protein choices to try from.

Our server was excellent, very attentive, and checked on us many times to make sure we were taken care of. We also got the green iced tea and the Thai iced tea, both were delicious and included in the price.

Desserts were decent, but nothing really stood out to me. However, they also serve ice cream with four different flavors, mini cakes, sticky rice, etc.

We spent a good two hours there for lunch and enjoyed it thoroughly.

We ended up waiting for happy hour, which starts at 4:30, and had a couple of drinks. Both were delicious. The bartenders were super nice and took great care of us.

Overall, a great experience. A must try for vegans and vegetarians.

My husband was craving tonkatsu ramen, so we came here specifically for that. But when we arrived, they told us they were completely sold out. It wasn’t even late or a busy weekend. It was just a regular weekday, so it was a bit hard to understand how they ran out that early.

They only had Tori Shoyu, so my husband ordered the Tori Shoyu and I ordered the Homura. I didn’t get a photo of his, but taste wise, the broth was actually pretty good, almost like there was ginseng or something aromatic in it. However, the meat smell was really strong. It felt like they didn’t remove that odor at all during cooking, and that’s been an issue every time we’ve visited. The broth is nice, but the meat smell really takes away from it.

As for my Homura, it feels like their own restaurant style take on maze soba, but if you’re expecting traditional maze soba, you’ll be disappointed. The flavor was okay, but there was barely any chives, which threw the balance off.

Overall, good broth but the strong meat smell and running out of ramen so early really need improvement.

There was about a 20-minute wait at dinner time on the weekend. It was no problem as there's a Teso Life store a few stores down to waste time. The place is designed to seat 2 or 4 people at most seats so if your party has 5 or more, the wait may be longer. If I'm not wrong, they have like four 6-seaters.

How's the food? The appetizers are alright. Main noodle? Stick to the special dry noodles - abura soba. The ramen here is meh. I wouldn't get it. If you really don't know what to order, try the "SUKIYAKI" with beef brisket. I'd recommend ordering some chilli oil on the side if you want a little kick.

This was my first visit. The noodles were a bit too salty for me, and overall the food was okay. The service was good initially, but I didn’t feel comfortable when the server presented the screen with an 18% tip already selected and asked me to sign. I was planning to leave that amount, but it felt awkward.

This is an outstanding place to satisfy my craving for authentic Japanese noodles, especially their signature Aburasoba! The service is quick and the ambiance is charming/inviting. It has definitely become one of my favorite go-to spots in Rockville!
