name: Animo
document: Animo. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Mexican Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I have been to this tasty Mexican place, which is reopening soon enough, twice now. The inside is casual, the service is very friendly, and the food is overall very tasty, almost unexpectedly good for an area where the only other Mexican options nearby are chains such as Rosa Mexicano.

The first time, I only stopped for a snack because I wanted something small for breakfast, I believe, after an appointment or something similar. I went with a Kekito de Pan de Elote, or, in other words, a little corn cake, which was maybe around $4.50. It was mildly sweet, almost like a thick custard in texture, and delicious. The corn flavor shone through, and it worked quite well with a coffee I made at home, though they do have some beverages, such as Café de Olla.

The other time I was here was in early November, as they used that week to celebrate Día de los Muertos. They had a special menu, as seen in the photos, and instead of the more expensive Chamorro, which was very tempting, I went with two relatively cheaper dishes.

The Pozole Rojo for $17 was a traditional hominy stew with slow-cooked pork or chicken in a red chili broth, and garnished with fresh toppings. There was also a Verde option for the same price point in a tomatillo-poblano broth with avocado and radish, but I generally prefer red pozole. I have had pozole from plenty of places, and this was outstanding. There was plenty of corn and soft, tender pork. The broth was as complex as it should be, with an earthy, slightly spicy flavor. This was excellent, and I hope they add it to the main menu when they reopen in their new, larger space.

My other dish was Tamales Oxaqueños with two tamales, for $22. This consisted of steamed corn masa wrapped in banana leaves and filled with chicken in mole negro. The tamales had a good texture, being soft and less dense than the typical lower-quality ones you find in most other restaurants and antojitos carts. There was plenty of chicken inside, and the mole was complex with very mild sweetness, a good amount of heat, some bitterness, and a wide variety of spices. At least from what I can tell, this was probably the most comparable mole to my favorite at Mama Lupita's Bistro in Sunset Park, which serves outstanding enmoladas, or enchiladas con mole. This was filling and again very tasty.

This is very good Mexican food for pretty reasonable prices, at least for Midtown East. I would definitely go back here for breakfast, brunch, or dinner. I look forward to going back once they reopen.

Animo on the Upper East Side really took me back to Mexico City the moment I walked in the decor, the energy, and even the scent of palo santo burning gave it that authentic vibe. The food came out fast and everything was extremely flavorful. You can tell they use highquality ingredients in every dish. The staff is very attentive and friendly, which made the experience even better. The hot sauces are excellent too, especially the pineapple one great flavor and a perfect kick. Overall, a beautiful spot with amazing food and atmosphere. Would definitely return.

Absolutely thrilled to get to experience Ánimo immediately post renovation. Incredible dishes and cocktails, great atmosphere. Perfect for a post work happy hour or group dinner, plenty of space for big group birthdays or celebrations, and awesome bar to just hang at on your own to meet new people. The food was amazing. Highlight recommend the steak, shrimp tacos and the cheese appetizer and the mezcalitza is epic.

We visited this restaurant for lunch. We ordered Chilaquiles Verdes, Molletes with Chorizo, and Tres Leches Cake. The Chilaquiles had a delightful flavor and were perfectly complemented by the avocado. However, be mindful that the dish is quite spicy. The Molletes were equally delicious, and the addition of chorizo enhanced the overall taste. We highly recommend asking for salsa verde on the side; it created a fantastic combination. The Tres Leches Cake was an absolute must-try! Don’t miss out on this incredible dessert. For drinks with ordered Agua Fresca de Horchata and Horchata Latte. The restaurant offers indoor seating, and the decor, lighting, and overall ambiance were truly captivating. The staff was attentive and friendly, providing excellent customer service. We thoroughly enjoyed our experience and are definitely planning to return to explore more of the menu!

I know some tend to exaggerate on here, but this was legitimately some of the best Mexican food that I have had in years. I popped in off the street, expecting to just have a quick bite, however I left with the FATTEST food baby. Everything that was recommended to me by my waiter was delicious, from the drinks to the desert! It was so good, in fact, that I was this close 🤏 to having to be rolled out of the restaurant.

document: The Modern. cuisine: New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
The Modern @ 9W 53rd st. NY NY 10019
To the right of The Museum of Modern Art is the magnificent Michelin starred restaurant serving all the top shelf hits!
It doesn't have the most obvious entrance- nor is it the most beautiful doorway- that being said-the food is definitively on par with a Michelin rating!
I must say, my wife & I had a great evening sampling the exquisite tasting menu.
The drinks were delicious as well. We were seated in the main dining room, in a beautiful white table clothed booth-  facing a large courtyard.  The service was very good, but not excellent. I was expecting excellent. Our main server eventually disappeared but we were in great hands with Izzy & Vanessa. Our evening was topped off with a quick tour of the kitchen. The kitchen was in tip top shape- as Id expected. We always confer after an evening out and we both agreed we would definitively return & we do recommend The Modern.

The service was great. Upscale atmosphere with the New York pace. I really enjoyed the mini crab appetizer, it gave you the punch of the ocean. I love how the chef made the light cream full of strong scent, of orange and bonito without any curdling. Seafood is so delightful and fresh, you can taste the sweetness of the fish. The mini pumpkin dumplings are so creamy and tasty with the fried spinach leaf, the sweet lobster with the super thin slices of lemon was delicious. The duck special is on the chef(thank you!) and its skin is so crispy the melt in your mouth meat! Five course menu is enough for me; it will be too much! Highly recommended you to go and find out your own! Or finding little excuses to celebrate there! It’s a lovely restaurant to dine in with or without a company (prefer to share with other friends and family though)!

P.s. I also saw an older lady with her family there, it remind me of my family growing up going out with grandparents every week to have a family meal together.

I went to The Modern for lunch and did the tasting menu. The food itself was great, everything was thoughtfully done and delicious. I especially loved the “eggs on eggs on eggs” and the little tartlet served at the beginning. Overall, the food absolutely lived up to expectations.
That said, the service really fell short, which was disappointing given that this is a Michelin-star restaurant where service is a big part of the experience. We felt quite rushed throughout the meal. There was an event happening at MoMA, and we were one of the last lunch reservations before they closed for the rest of the day, which clearly affected the pacing.
Even if there’s an event afterward, guests are paying a lot for the full experience, and it shouldn’t feel like you’re being pushed out. It took away from what could’ve been a really special meal.
I do think the experience might be better at a time when there isn’t an event happening or for dinner, and I’d be open to coming back under different circumstances. The food was excellent, I just wish the service had matched it.

The food was interesting, but they had their own unique styles. Each carefully curated menus were great to experience and staffs were very well trained. I especially loved the menu eggs on eggs on eggs. Name sparked my interest and the presentation was stunning as well. Great place to visit.

First visit to The Modern, and it was an exceptional experience.
The food was refined and beautifully executed, the service was attentive and polished, and the atmosphere was perfect for a honeymoon—elegant yet warm, sophisticated without being stiff.

A special thank you to Chef Yoshua, who hosted us so graciously and made the evening truly memorable. The kitchen tour was a fantastic touch—eye-opening, inspiring, and honestly… wow.

Thoughtful hospitality, excellent cuisine, and a team that clearly takes pride in what they do.
A honeymoon dinner done right. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Went here for a work dinner and it did not disappoint.  Serrano’s delivers classic Italian comfort without the fuss. The fried zucchini is crisp and light, served with bright marinara and creamy aioli. Mozzarella sticks have that perfect stretch, and the square-cut pepperoni pizza features crispy edges and gooey cheese. Chicken parm is hearty and well-balanced with tangy sauce and melted mozzarella. Pastas were rich but not heavy. The cozy setting makes it ideal for sharing dishes and hanging out.

Definitely a great spot

I had an amazing experience at Seranos Italian Restaurant! From start to finish, everything was top-notch. The food is absolutely fantastic, every dish we tried was full of flavor and made with care. The appetizers were fresh and flavorful, the pasta dishes were perfectly cooked with rich, authentic sauces, and the pizza was simply incredible with a perfect crust and delicious toppings.

The service at Seranos is also outstanding. The staff is attentive, friendly, and genuinely welcoming, making you feel right at home. They were happy to answer questions about the menu and gave great recommendations.

The restaurant itself has a warm and inviting atmosphere, ideal for a casual meal with friends, a date night, or even a business dinner. On top of that, the location is very convenient, just a short walk from Penn Station, which makes it easy to get to and from.

Overall, Seranos Italian Restaurant exceeded my expectations in every way. The combination of delicious food, excellent service, and a great location makes it one of my favorite spots in the city. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for authentic Italian cuisine with a welcoming atmosphere. I can’t wait to come back and try more dishes 🤩👍👍👍👍👍

Wonderful! Happy to call this a place I am happy to come back to visit and frequent!!

It’s a very cozy and welcoming restaurant with a warm and friendly wait staff.  We had 0 issue with service and they were very attentive to our needs.

I thought the arancini were wonderfully done — you could taste the individual grains of rice that sometimes restaurants overlook in their version of arancini.

The rigatoni vodka was delicious. Comforting, warm, not too creamy, well-done!

Their pizzas use cheese in their crust to give it this crispy exterior. Some might hate it; I was indifferent to it. I thought the Hot Louie tasted great and the pepperoni topping was solid. Would I spend $25 for that pizza again? Not particularly, but I wasn’t upset that I ordered it.  It’s midtown 🤷‍♂️

The Tiramisu was a bit of a dud. At $14, it comes in a small bowl - it’s just not as creamy as you’d expect and the coffee taste isn’t as vibrant. Most definitely not worth ordering again.

Despite my criticisms — they’re all nitpicky in nature. I’d be happy to come back and take my friends here! If I’m ever in the area,  I’d definitely stick to the pasta, some wine, and maybe another appetizer.  Can pass on the pizza and dessert.

google_reviews.text:
Dimsum Palace was an absolutely incredible experience from start to finish. The rotating carts of freshly prepared dishes created such a fun and authentic atmosphere — you can continuously pick and choose what catches your eye, which makes the whole meal interactive and exciting. Every item I tried was flavorful, well-prepared, and exceeded expectations.

The service was quick, attentive, and kept everything moving smoothly despite how busy it gets. And trust me — it does get packed. Make sure you plan ahead and allow extra time, especially during peak hours.

If you’re looking for a lively dining experience with consistently amazing food, this spot is a must-visit.

We’ve been regulars for dim sum, but when we crave canto comfort food, this place can hit the spot! Love that dim sum is available for dinner too. My kids want dim sum at all hours and it’s great we can get both!

My daughter requested dim sum and Chinese for her birthday. Service has always been friendly and attentive, but when I asked if they do anything for birthdays, I was told not really which was totally fine by me. I just thought I’d inquire to make my daughter feel a little special.

They went above and beyond and gifted my daughter with egg tarts with a candle, and then also a gift set of bowls and chopsticks. It was so sweet and unexpected. Thanks for a wonderful family dinner, and making my daughter feel special on her birthday!

Not to detract from the food, everything is solid but the mandarin pork chops and peking duck really stood out tonight!

Solid dim sum option! Servers were very attentive. Dim sum options were decent; had all the standards plus a few surprises.  My husband really liked the Hong Kong noodles; I thought it was ok.  My favorite were the pan fried shrimp and chive dumplings.

I was a little confused by the menu as it didn’t specify what are in carts vs what you had to ask for.   Maybe I missed something.

Dim Sum Palace food is totally authentic and they make everything fresh right in the house. You have to try the roast pork—it is unbelievably good. A combination of crispy and juicy meat make it perfect. All their dim sum is delicious, but the siu mai (the pork and shrimp dumplings) are a special favorite; they are so fresh and flavorful. If you want real, high-quality Chinese food, this is the place to go.
Our first time getting actual dim sum cart service. A little overwhelming at times, but it was very good. Everything was very delicious!

name: La Perla Nascosta
document: La Perla Nascosta. cuisine: Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️A simply spectacular experience. From the very first moment in La Perla Nascosta you can tell that the cuisine is truly authentic Italian, with traditional flavors, fresh ingredients, and recipes that honor the real essence of Italy. Every dish is perfectly crafted, with the balance and passion that can only be found in genuine Italian gastronomy.
The service is equally impeccable: attentive, professional, and always willing to make the experience even more special. Without a doubt, a place I will return to and highly recommend to anyone looking to enjoy true Italian tradition with exceptional service.

★★★★★

La Perla Nascosta is a true hidden gem. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, intimate, and authentically Italian.

We started with the Octopus Carpaccio, and it was outstanding. Thinly sliced, incredibly fresh, perfectly balanced with arugula, capers, and olive oil. Light, elegant, and full of flavor.

The Linguine Neri was the highlight. The seafood was tender and perfectly cooked, the sauce rich but not heavy, and the pasta had that authentic al dente texture that’s hard to find. Every bite tasted fresh and carefully prepared.

For dessert, the White Chocolate Mousse was the perfect finish. Smooth, creamy, not overly sweet, and beautifully presented. It felt indulgent without being overwhelming.

Service was attentive and friendly, and the overall experience felt elevated but still welcoming. If you’re looking for high-quality Italian cuisine with fresh seafood and a cozy atmosphere, this place delivers.

Definitely coming back.

La Perla Nascosta is such a cozy gem of an Italian restaurant. The atmosphere is intimate and welcoming , a perfect spot for friends gathering or celebrating a birthday. It truly feels like stepping into a little corner of Rome.
We started with the baked clams and shrimp, both full of flavor and beautifully prepared. The Pizza Margherita was outstanding,  simple, authentic, and absolutely delicious. The Linguine Frutti di Mare was fresh and perfectly cooked, with generous seafood in every bite. We also loved the branzino, seasoned just right and cooked to perfection.
Great food, warm vibes, and a wonderful place to enjoy Italian comfort dishes with good company. Definitely coming back 🇮🇹🍝🍕

I would highly recommend Perla Nascosta as one of my preferred dining destinations. The atmosphere was pleasant and inviting, and our waiter, Florian (if I correctly recall his name), provided exceptional service, demonstrating attentiveness and friendliness throughout our visit.

The culinary offerings were outstanding, with notable dishes including the arugula salad with grilled chicken, tuna tartare, linguine vongole, daily special octopus dish, pizza funghi, and branzino.

Additionally, the beverages were superb, particularly the gardenia, which I thoroughly enjoyed. We had a wonderful time at Perla Nascosta, and I appreciate the complimentary dessert and excellent coffee.

Overall, I highly recommend Perla Nascosta for its excellent food, service, and ambiance.

La Perla nascosta reminds me of a classic Italian restaurant I used to go to in brooklyn when I was younger. The atmosphere is warm and inviting. The service is incredible and the food is delicious! We tried the fried calamari, artichokes, meatball pasta, and broccoli rabe sausage pasta. They were all phenomenal dishes! I cannot wait to return soon. What a lovely place! I did not get a picture of the chocolate mousse for dessert because we dug right in. It was so rich and delightful!

name: Chama Mama
document: Chama Mama. cuisine: Georgian Wine Bars Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
🇬🇪 A Georgian Culinary Journey in Chelsea

If you’re looking to break away from the usual dinner routine, Chama Mama is an absolute must. We came here for a work dinner of four, and it was the perfect blend of a professional atmosphere and a genuinely fun, unique vibe.

The Highlights:
• The Food: Traditional Georgian flavors that feel both adventurous and comforting. Every dish was a conversation starter.

• The Service: Truly top-tier. Our server was originally from Georgia and treated us like guests in their own home. They were incredibly patient, helping us navigate the menu and giving us "the whole 9 yards" on the proper way to eat the traditional dishes.

• The Drinks & Vibe: Relaxed yet polished. The environment is pleasant, the drinks are great, and it’s a fantastic spot for groups.

🍰 Don't Skip Dessert:
You have to order the Napoleon cake. It is quite literally to die for—it has the perfect amount of crunch and flavor without being overly sweet. It was the highlight of the night!

Verdict: 5/5 stars. Great food, even better service. Highly recommended for team dinners or anyone wanting a delicious "culinary trip" to Tbilisi without leaving Manhattan. 🥂

We absolutely loved Chama Mama! First time having Georgian food. So much to love. Flavorful food, honest craftsmanship, stunning drinks, incredibly friendly staff, beautiful design of the space. While I've seen and understand criticisms of the steep pricepoint for "homey" food, the investment in a meal at Chama Mama is worth the authentic experience, and most of all the DELECTABLE food. Stars of the show were the Beef Kharcho Soup (delicious tomato flavor, hint of spice, stewed beef, wheat), the Khinkali (excellently spiced beef & pork in our case, bathing in a wonderful meat broth inside the dumpling wrapper), and the Khachapuri (cheesy, delicious bread, a must-try food experience), and don't sleep on the mocktails and lemonades. Fantastic restaurant, from the food all the way to the branding.

Absolutely incredible experience at Chama Mama!
The food was rich, flavorful, and truly felt like a journey into Georgian cuisine. The khachapuri was perfection — crispy on the outside, warm and cheesy on the inside — and the khinkali were juicy and full of flavor. Every dish tasted homemade and cooked with real care.

The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, and the staff made us feel right at home from the moment we walked in. It’s the perfect place to share plates, enjoy amazing wine, and discover something new and delicious.

Hands down one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. Can’t wait to come back!

Our server, she was very kind and professional, wine tastings, cocktails, were all above expectations and quite delicious. The food though? Excellent, phenomenal, superb! We enjoyed our meal quite a bit. Easily a place we’d come back to. Georgian food is a must try, and Chama Mama does it justice!

This was our second visit, and it was just as amazing as the first!

We ordered the Adjaruli khachapuri, chicken mtsvadi, honey cake ice cream, and chocolate cloud cake, along with the drinks (passionfruit caramel lemonade and Château Buera – Rkatsiteli). Every single item was absolutely delicious.

The service was also top-notch! Truly outstanding. Easily a 10 out of 10. We can’t wait to come back! ❤️❤️❤️

name: Moono
document: Moono. cuisine: Korean. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Beautiful upscale spot for a celebration, but come hungry for a heavy meal!

The ambiance here is perfect for a date night. The food is high-quality and punchy, though the menu leans quite rich.
• Spicy Fried Chicken: Perfectly juicy and garlicky. I loved that the sauce was served on the side so the crispiness could shine.
• Assorted Pancakes: Great variety; the shrimp was the standout.
• Galbi-jjim: Very decadent. Definitely pair this with rice to cut through the richness.
• Uni Sotbap: Incredibly flavorful and satisfying.

Note: The meal is definitely on the "heavier" side. I felt a bit sluggish afterward and wished there were lighter dessert or side options to balance the richness. Still a delicious, high-end experience!

We came at 5 PM on a Wednesday and it was calm and peaceful. The food tasted clean with a focus on the ingredients natural flavor. The chicken was fried very well and it's taste was fairly light with a hint of MSG. The galbi-jjim was tender and youll find yourself dipping it back in the sauce after each bite. Nothing was excessive in flavor which might be a downside for someone expecting heavy pocha style flavors. Even the kimchi wasn't too sour and had a crunch to it. It's unique and healthy, plus the place is gorgeous and a great place for a date.

The interior of Moono is so beautiful and the service and food is always top-tier. I’ve been here twice now, most recently for the restaurant week menu. The chicken is some of the best I’ve had and the Galbi-jjim is so tender. The sides are also phenomenal and all unique. For the restaurant week menu we got the wine pairings as well and I definitely recommend that, they go perfectly with each course. Overall, love this place! I’ve also had the bossam and naengmyeon before which are also good, but I think my favorite dish so far has been the Galbi-jjim!

Stopped by Moono with friends after spending the day in New York City, and it was such a great meal.
We ordered Pyongyang-style cold noodles, stir-fried cuttlefish, and mixed sashimi salad, and everything was spot on.

The Pyongyang cold noodles had a clean, deeply flavorful broth that was light but satisfying, with great texture on the noodles.
The stir-fried cuttlefish was full of smoky flavor, not overly spicy, and went perfectly with rice.
The mixed sashimi salad was fresh and well balanced, with bright, refreshing flavors.

Overall, the food was thoughtful and well executed, making it perfect for sharing with friends.
The atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable, which made it easy to enjoy the meal and spend time together.

Definitely a place I’d come back to with friends again.

A delightful and delicious meal that made me regret that I wasn't particularly celebrating anything that day that warranted me eating such well prepared food.

The kalbi, squid, umi rice, were standouts for me. We left very full and happy. The staff were also very attentive and helpful. Excellent restaurant well worth a visit when restaurant week rolls around in the summer.

google_reviews.text: I had a wonderful experience at QI this week. I was traveling for business and dining alone, which can be somewhat intimidating. Wilson was my server and made the evening incredibly enjoyable. He offered suggestions and was very attentive even though it was a busy night. The cocktails were top tier. The raw salmon was refreshing. The sol could’ve fed my entire family and the fries…. Crispy potato bites of heaven  I was surprised with (hands down) the best dessert I have ever experienced in NYC-a sorbet cheesecake situation that I will be back for every time I’m in town. Thank you to everyone there for such a wonderful experience!

Wow this place was very good! It was our first night here in NYC and we weren’t sure were to go but a friend recommended us here. So we got a reservation which is a must have and got seated right around 7:30 (which was our reservation). It was scrubbusy in here and my only concerns were the lighting was really low and the music was so loud so we could barley hear. Our waiter was nice but I think it was like his first day because he seemed a little frazzled and messed the check up. The service was quick though. We got the ricotta with honey and baby kale salad. Both of these were so delicious and flavorful. The nuts on the ricotta really added the extra. Then we all got pasta for dinner and the truffle cacio de Pepe was my favorite. It wasn’t to creamy which I like and the noodles were long and perfect. The truffle flavor was just right not overpowering. We were to stuffed for dessert. It was pricey but I expected that. So overall great way to end the night!

Great restaurant with amazing food and friendly staff. I went in for lunch and loved everything I tried. For the appetizer, I went with the whipped ricotta. Very tasty. For my main, I ordered the Porterhouse Agnolotti. It was a great mix of slightly sweet and savory. My appetizers consisted of the crispy Brussels sprouts and the corn crème brûlée. Both of which were extremely flavorful. Lastly, I ordered the sticky toffee pudding which was a mix of caramel and sea salt. I finished my meal with a cappuccino. Overall, I enjoyed my visit to quality Italian and would return again.

Some highs and lows with our visit. We had reservations and didn’t have to wait to be seated. We were seated at probably the worst table in the house, right at the entrance to the kitchen and it was nonstop traffic right at our table. Other than that the ambiance in the restaurant was very nice. Our server was very good other than he didn’t return to the table after each course was served to ask if everything came out ok. The food was mostly great, the octopus app was very good, the veal also was good, the spicy lobster was not. The pasta and sauce was very good but the lobster was a tiny tail that they over cooked and stick to the shell. I got very little meat for one of the most expensive mains on the menu. The best part of the evening was the dessert, Sticky Toffee pudding. IYKYK. Order it.

For me a rating is based on total experience and this restaurant excelled in every area.  The main dining room is on the second floor but on the first floor is a bar with a few tables and garage doors that open fully. We went for lunch and it was a beautiful day so we sat at a table which was open to the outside, perfection for me.  Service was great, friendly, attentive and knowledgeable, can’t ask for anything more.  I definitely need to return to try more menu items but for this visit the gnocchi was the star.  Literally melt in your mouth and the leek in the sauce was present but not overwhelming.   Absolute 10 out of 10 in my opinion. Ricotta appetizer was delicious and creamy. Very mild flavor.  I asked for extra honey which was great and would have loved more pine nuts also because the texture added a lot to the dish.  The tomato and Stracciatella was very good but wasn’t wowed.  Likely my fault should not have ordered two cheese appetizers. They start the meal with a small pan of bread.  Yummm!!! Flavorful and chewy in the best way.   Drinks also very good.  Highly recommend this restaurant and plan on returning soon.

name: Pranakhon Thai Restaurant
document: Pranakhon Thai Restaurant. cuisine: Thai Salad Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Highly recommended! The fish dishes are must-try. Crab rice was good! Service was amazing (and definitely looking for their recommendations if you have never been there before). Sundae was made of corn, peach and sticky rice with coconut ice cream. Big bite would be enjoyed. Great treat if you walked whole day. Thai iced tea and Thai iced coffee are both good for spicy foods while I do see many people who come here often order cocktails (from I have observed)
Also I usually do not enjoy sitting on the bar and this time I would say the people who serve on the bar make this experience great!

At Pranakhon, you can taste and experience various foods, inspired from outdoor alley (soi) of Thailand. After my friends and I had dined here for a birthday celebration, we can see how they earned Michelin Stars for three years!

For starters, we ordered Klui Goong and Gai Manow. The Klui Goong was light, crispy, and the combination of pork and seafood was delicious. The sauce added a nice sweet-sour taste too.

We also ordered various entrée such as Khao Soi Haeng, Khao Na Ped, Kang Dang Moo, Moo Grob Prik Khing, and Ped Ruan. The Kang Dang Moo was creamy with the coconut milk and fragrant with the basil leaf. Luckily, it was not too sweet, although I would prefer it a little bit spicier. The highlight of the night was definitely the Moo Grob Prik Khing, stir-fried crispy pork with string beans, kaffir lime, and chili paste! The pork had a nice crisp crunch. It was perfectly cooked so it was not too tender and not too crispy. The seasoning made the crispy pork flavor burst and it was a delight to share amongst the table!

So good. All the food hit. Not too oily or salty, but strong flavors and good spice. Underrated starters were the curry pancakes. They had an Indian profile and  the sweet sauce on the side paired so well either way it. Khao soi was a dry dish which was interesting. Steak was cooked to perfection.

Service was fantastic. Server came up periodically to refill in the water. She was present but never pushy despite the long line of people waiting for weekend dinner.

Interior vibes are cool and take me to Thailand.

There were so many options it was hard to choose. We got the pad thai and mussaman short ribs. Both were delicious. The short ribs were very tender with a nice sauce. The pad thai was also really tasty and had a fun presentation. Although, it was not the best pad thai I have ever had. Looking around at other tables’ orders, the presentation of many dishes looked really good. For a popular place, the restaurant was huge and had plenty of seating, so there was hardly any wait time during a busy hour.

Pranakhon is one of my favourite Thai restaurants in the city. The atmosphere is always very lively, and they have such a wide variety of authentic dishes that I'm always very impressed by.

I often order one of their rice dishes, and they are all so delicious. My favourite is the kaprow moo sub, which comes at a very (authentic) level of spiciness; I also liked the pad krapow and khao moo dang -- pork is always so juicy and tender (crispy pork belly so flavourful).

The mee kati was a pleasant surprise when I tried it -- I liked how the flavour of the fresh mangos paired with the tamarind flavour of the noodles / sauce. It was a bit heavy, and some of the noodles started to clump together.

For a less spicy option, I really enjoyed the preaw wan. The sweet and sour flavour was a refreshing contrast from the richer flavours of other dishes like the curries, and I liked the eclectic mix of pineapples, tomatoes, nuts, onions, etc. Made for a very interesting overall dish.

While the menu is a little pricey, the lunch special is quite worth it if you're able to come for a weekday lunch. I am a big fan of the Pranakhon salad (which comes as a side for the lunch combo) -- the mango ginger dressing is so delicious and the shredded mango is always SO fresh.

Always very keen to come back to try something else off their menu. They can get a bit busy at peak times, so definitely try to make a reservation in advance.

We had a great experience at this pub, and I truly want to highlight how impressive the staff was.

We were a little caught off guard at first because there was a $10 cover charge at the entrance due to an event happening that night — something we didn’t expect. However, once inside, everything completely changed in the best way.

Despite the large crowd and the high volume of guests, the entire team (servers, bartenders, host, and the person at the door) was extremely organized, professional, and clearly well-trained on how to provide great service under pressure. That says a lot about the place.

name: Artesano Peruvian Cuisine
document: Artesano Peruvian Cuisine. cuisine: Peruvian Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
An unforgettable dining experience

We chose Artesano to celebrate our wedding anniversary, and it was truly one of the best dining experiences we have ever had. From the moment we arrived, the service was warm, professional, and attentive to every detail, creating an elegant yet very welcoming atmosphere.

The food was exceptional, a true expression of high end Peruvian cuisine. Every dish from the tasting menu was beautifully executed, with bold yet perfectly balanced flavors and impeccable presentation. You can truly feel the quality of the ingredients and the level of technique behind every plate.

A very special and heartfelt thank you to Chef César for his outstanding talent, creativity, and genuine hospitality. Not only is his cuisine exceptional, but his personal involvement made the experience even more meaningful. He took the time to come to our table, ask about our preferences, explain the inspiration behind each dish, and ensure that everything was perfect. His passion for his craft and his attention to guests truly elevate the entire dining experience.

We would also like to recognize the incredible work of the sous chefs and the entire kitchen team for their dedication, precision, and professionalism.

We also want to highlight the incredible service provided by Renzo, whose knowledge, kindness, and detailed explanations of each course made the experience even more memorable. His service, along with the rest of the staff, was absolutely top tier.

The combination of quality, service, attention to detail, and atmosphere makes Artesano a truly unique restaurant. We highly recommend it for any special occasion or for anyone looking for a world class dining experience.

Thank you, Artesano, for making our anniversary celebration truly unforgettable. We will definitely be back.

Good vibe and excellent service.  My wife and I both had the 7 course tasting menu.  Everything tasted great and was presented beuatifully.  Tasting menu was $140 per person.   This was quite different than less gourmet Peruvian food I have had in the past, but quite tasty.  Would recommend Artesano.

Artesano serves upscale Peruvian cuisine in an upbeat modern environment. The quality and flavor combinations were consistently excellent from dish to dish based on 7 different dishes. I can confirm that the product is worth the price tag. The dessert was the cherry on top, left me speechless.

Like a 22yo newlywed dispensing martial advice, Artesano has all the right elements but isn't quite ready for primetime yet.

Our dinner started off well. We were seated quickly and enjoyed the cozy, quiet, beautifully decorated ambience.

The first few courses were stellar: The Artesano Ceviche was everything a classic mixto should be and had plenty of seafood variety, tiger's milk, choclo and sweet potato. The Pulpo al Olivo arrived nicely chewy with a unique accompaniment of tapioca crisps.

The entrees were where the inexperience started to show. I will say that our Branzino a La Parrilla was perfectly cooked, but the accompanying aji panca marinade seemed like overkill and was largely unnecessary when you already have a sauced and grilled fish that well done. The spring salad was nice, though, and not too tart.

The Mushroom Chifero was a huge disappointment. I was hoping for some true Peruvian-Chinese innovation (a la modern chifa), but this was mostly just large-grained sticky rice with roasted maitake mushrooms that were ruined by a completely unnecessary sweet and tart tamarind sauce. It felt like, in the interest of being creative and unique, they decided to throw in a fruit sauce to stir things up--but what is the point of serving a fried rice dish with fried garlic, scallions and mushrooms if you're just going to drown it in tamarind?

I didn't want to order this but was convinced to get aside dish of Truffle Yuca Fries. They were fine, but the truffle flavor was weak and they really needed the accompanying huancaina sauce to import any flavor. I get that yuca is a pretty flavorless starch vegetable, which is why I didn't really want to pay $18 (yes, $18) for this side dish.

After the entrees, the service team dropped the ball harder than Aaron Rodgers last month in Dublin. We waited at least 20 min, but no one came to clear our plates, check on us or ask if we wanted dessert. By this time, the restaurant had filled up and the vibe had turned distinctly clubby: my geriatric ears could hardly hear anything over the thunderous bass of DJ Whats-His-Face and MC Who-Knows-That.

When we finally flagged down a server, ordered dessert and finished it, well....it wasn't worth the hassle. I forget the name of the dessert, but it was Choclo something and featured corn sponge cake, corn mousse, chulpi praline, and mango gel. The sponge cake had perfect texture but barely any corn flavor. The corn mousse was lovely, but the mango gel overwhelmed it and felt unnecessary.

When we paid and left, no one acknowledged us or thanked us. Guess they couldn't hear us through the pulsating beats. All in all, a tepid finish to a promising start.

Came here for lunch with a party of four during the week. We had a reservation, but didn't seem like there was much need for one. The place is on the smaller side and could be easily be missed from the street (we almost did!) but once inside is a very earthy and warm feeling restaurant. We were sat right away and our waitress was not only incredibly helpful and accommodating, she was also super knowledgeable about all the menu offerings which certainly helped our diet diverse party. I went for the Arroz Chaufa, a Peruvian take on fried rice with chicken. It was delicious and warming, especially on a cool fall day. One thing to note that I don't usually pick up on, but I loved their stoneware, the bowls felt so organic and natural looking, it made me want to get some of my own! We finished off the meal with a nice cup of cappuccino that was as good as any coffee shop I've been to in the area. The lunch menu is a little on the limited side, but that just left me wanting to come back again for dinner to try what else they might have. This is definitely a place I'm keeping in the back of my mind when I want to take people out for something that isn't your usual NYC fare.

document: Monkey Bar. cuisine: American Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Beautiful atmosphere, great service. I was not sure what to expect from the food because of so many mixed reviews, here is my honest breakdown:
1. Whitefish Caesar salad 10/10. A must try, I can eat a pound of this it was so delicious.
2. Short rib pasta is slept on. It is one of the best pasta dishes with thr softest short rib I’ve ever tired
3. The burger is very good. Better than Au Cheval, but not mind blowing. It is just very good, but not a “must” get
4. Crab Wontons were a fun app, the sauce is delicious, I would get these again
5. Carrot cake was incredible. 10/10

Loved it!! Had no reservation, so showed up just before opening time and got a great table in bar area. Really friendly staff and wonderful food. The monkey bread still has me dreaming about it!! Great cocktails too. Atmosphere was fantastic and we were not rushed out. Will definitely be back next time we’re in NYC!

We had an excellent experience at monkey bar. I’ve been wanting to go for years and finally got my shot to go on my girlfriend’s birthday.

When you walk in, it’s not clear where to go in the front area. There should be someone for first timers making sure you know to walk in towards the hostess, which is not visible from the front when it’s busy (which is all the time). I stood there like an idiot for 30 seconds. We waited 15 minutes for our reservation that we showed up on time for. No one told us we could order a cocktail as we watched others (smarter than us) do that.

Chris was one of the best waiters I’ve ever had in New York. The ambience is spectacular. The reason for docking a star is because when you have a reputation and pricing like monkey bar, I expect perfection and the food was great but not perfect. The monkey bread was insane, best thing on the menu. I don’t think bread can get much better than that. The Caesar salad was a little disappointing. I had to remind my girlfriend there was potato chips in it because they had gotten soggy sitting and dressing. Chu Toro tuna was great but the crisp bread it came with it was underwhelming. Crab Rangoon’s were good but not great. Important note is that Chris threw in the monkey bread and crab Rangoon’s and dessert on the house, which is so generous! Shoutout Chris.

Truffle mac & cheese was one of my favorite things. The crispy top is awesome. The steak frites was good. Steak was great, but the Bernaise sauce and fries were very average. Fries particularly confusing. The most disappointing thing on the menu was the famous French dip. I feel like a jerk saying this, but it tasted like something I would get at the bodega. I would enjoy it from the bodega, but that’s not where I’m at. Chocolate pie was fantastic. Would definitely come back, but the food was a bit below what I expected for such an impossible reservation. 4.3/5

Worth the hype, ambiance is 10/10 we got seated a corner booth nice a private and roomy. Excellently crafted menu and the food was great our server was absolutely amazing. Honestly the best service I’ve ever had in a restaurant. The wagyu burger was melt in your mouth and the dry aged strip had the perfect crust. The mashed potatoes are a must, Some of the best I’ve ever had I can live without the creamed spinach and rangoons next time. But the truffle bread is definitely worth it, fluffy sweet savory and earthy. Truffle Mac is also excellent. Definitely going back to try even more of the menu. Honorable mention is the carrot cake. Super moist and spiced and very decently sized to share.

A gorgeous, old-school Upper East Side New York classic.

Service: Solid but unremarkable. The waiter was a bit hard to hear, though service overall was fine.

Food:
The menu is excellent with something for everyone, from lighter options to indulgent classics.
•	Crab cakes: Outstanding! crisp, golden exterior with a tender, incredibly meaty center.
•	White fish Caesar salad: The name gave me pause, but it worked beautifully. Light, fresh, and well-balanced. Enough to share for two, maybe three.
•	Burger: Heavenly. Juicy, perfectly cooked, and simply done.
•	French fries: The only letdown; lacked the crispness and salt.

Martinis: Top-notch—cold, clean, and expertly made.

document: Leyla. cuisine: Turkish Mediterranean Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: The service and food at Leyla's are equally spectacular! We were warmly greeted by the host and, during the meal, enjoyed our excellent service by all the staff. The food is very good, and we especially enjoyed the portions, which were neither too big nor too small. The restaurant also has a very nice feel to it, the kind of place were you want to hang out and enjoy good food with good company. Highly recommended!

Leyla. Got me on my knees, Leyla. Begging darling please, Leyla.

10,000 geriatric millennial points to Ravenclaw if you got that reference. And this one.

No? Then you're too young to be reading my reviews. Go out and touch grass. Me, I'll be enjoying memories of the Turkish feast I had on the UWS one chilly night. Our large group had:

- Slow Cooked Short Rib Pide: My favorite dish of the night and easily the rock star of their menu. Perfectly crisp flatbread meets melt-in-your-mouth shredded beef loaded with spices and accompanied by a rich eggplant spread and kashar cheese. What's Turkish for yummers?

- Lahmacun: I ate my weight in lahmacun when I went Turkey a couple of years ago. This was a nice facsimile, loaded with plenty of minced meat and sumac.

- Muhammara: For those who like salty-sweet, you might enjoy this antioxidant-rich dip of pomegranate molasses, walnut, red pepper paste and olive oil. Mmmm

- Atom: Another dip, this of charred eggplant puree, roasted garlic, smoked labneh, and cumin topped. Spicy and hot, like Halle Berry in a sombrero.

- Erişte: K, I lied. I think *this* was my favorite dish of the night. Think bite-sized pasta, lamb cubes, cumin, and all the sumac your nose can inhale. Carbalicious!

- Vegetarian Mantı: More flavorful than many meat-filled manti, probably because of all the charred eggplant puree in smoked yogurt, and mint paprika butter glaze. Hearty!

- Izmir Kofte: Surprisingly, the most meh dish of the table. It was fine, but I feel like the sausages could've been way more flavorful, and the veg accompaniment was too watery.

Wash it all down with some Turkish Tea, and you've got the recipe for a  proper cross-continental meal. Going cold turkey never felt so good--get it, cuz it's winter and we're talking about Turkish food?

I'll see myself out.

Had an amazing dinner at Leyla, authentic Turkish food, superb service, and a cozy atmosphere. Our server Sultan made great recommendations and was very attentive. The highlight was the Pistachio Mud Heaven dessert, absolutely a must as well as greek salad, pide and Turkish coffee. Everything from start to finish felt fresh,
genuine and delicious.
The atmosphere and the food are delicious. You can look forward to enjoying excellent Turkish cuisine. Additionally, the staff are very welcoming.

Superb experience overall! Our server was very attentive and made great suggestions. Everything we ordered was delicious and I would get again, photos attached. Branzino with potatoes with dill was the highlight.

document: Pastis. cuisine: French. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
We chose a beautiful Sunday morning in rainy New York to go out for brunch with friends, and it turned out to be a wonderful experience. There were six of us, and we were given a lovely round table where it was comfortable to sit and talk. The restaurant was full, yet the hostess greeted us with a smile and kindly showed us to our table, even though two of our friends were running late. That was especially nice, knowing how strict New York restaurants usually are about seating incomplete parties.

Each of us ordered something different, and everyone was happy with their choice. I had an omelet with Gruyère — soft, delicate, and absolutely delicious. It came with perfectly roasted potatoes, cooked in a special way that made them extra flavorful. My friends had salmon Benedicts, Norwegian eggs, and croque-madame — everything was excellent.

We especially remember the French toast with strawberries and cream — heavenly! And for dessert, we shared profiteroles with ice cream, which were out of this world.

The staff kept refilling our coffee and making sure our glasses were never empty. The atmosphere was lively and cheerful, full of people and energy. Even the restroom caught our attention — surrounded by shelves of wine bottles, it felt stylish and unique.

We left feeling like part of a fashionable New York crowd — full, happy, and already planning to come back.

It was a good experience. The servers were great and very attentive. Expect a wait during busy times even with a reservation.
The food was nice and was served quickly.
The toilets had some fun decorations in them.
The booths made the restaurant seem quite private even when the whole restaurant was full. There was no difficulty hearing conversations.

Excellent food, great service, and super pretty space. This is one of my favorite French spots in nyc. The Entrecôte steak was 10 / 10 and dirty martini drink was one of the best in the city. Great place to bring friends and family visiting. I will definitely be back !!

Finally, I visited this restaurant. I had been planning for a long time and didn’t regret my visit.
Firstly, the vibe was great.
Secondly, our server was charming and attentive.
Thirdly, everything was super delicious!!!
We had a great time and will visit Pastis for dinner soon!
Thank you for our wonderful brunch!

This restaurant is very conveniently located in the meatpacking district and the interior is amazingly decorated. We went on a Wednesday evening with a reservation and the restaurant got pretty packed around 6pm. We tried their beef tartare, sautéed spinach, scallops, escargot and mussels with chips. Our favourite was the escargot, it came with freshly baked baguette for you to dip in the buttery garlic parsley sauce. Overall everything was good but nothing hit the spot, hence the 4 stars.

Chili’s is probably the only major chain restaurant in town that’s still worth visiting, but it can be hit or miss. Sometimes the food is spot-on, other times it’s lacking, but it’s still miles better than Glory Days or Ruby Tuesday these days. We come here every couple of months with the kids and usually enjoy a decent meal. I really like the Chipotle Fresh Mex Bowl with Street Corn, and of course the Molten Chocolate Cake. My wife prefers the ribs or wings, though the wings can definitely be hit or miss.

This location looks much nicer after its renovation some years back, which is a plus. Service is also inconsistent. We’ve had servers who were slow or inattentive, but the bar staff is almost always great, kind, attentive, and quick. So while service isn’t perfect, it’s not universally bad either.

Dinner rush can be rough here, so we try to go right before or after peak hours. Otherwise, wait times can hit 45 minutes or more.

Overall, it’s the better option among the three big chains in town (not counting Buffalo Wild Wings). Is it great? No. But for a chain restaurant in 2025, it’s about what you’d realistically expect.

google_reviews.text: We scored a reservation for 4:15pm for  a part of 4. We arrived on time and were seated pretty promptly. Where we were seated initially was pretty cramped and we realized fairly quickly it just wasn’t going to be comfortable for us. When we asked if a larger table that wasn’t so close to neighboring tables might be available we were quickly and graciously accommodated without hesitation. We ordered stuffed flatbread, chrysanthemum salad, buffalo milk caramelle, calamari fried rice, sourdough pasta cacciatore, steak limone, and the ravioli for the table to share for dinner. Our party also shared the tiramisu and pear sorbet for dessert. Everything we ate was a home run, not one bite missed, not even a little. Also worth mentioning, every dish was measurably different from the next, Don Angie plays many notes on our palates it seems. The atmosphere is upscale but not uptight.

As always, Don Angie is the most incredible culinary experience — the food is outstanding, unique, and special. The service is unparalleled and the staff leads all their actions with kindness and attention to the guest experience. It is always such a special occasion to join them for a meal and I certainly hope to be back soon!

Dish Highlights: The Japanese sweet potatoes and the chrysanthemum salad are MUST gets. The BBQ calamari were a unique and yummy app. The sourdough pasta cacciatore never disappoints, nor does the shell steak al limone or lasagna for two.

Decent vegetarian options for appetizers / pasta. Was able to grab a seat at the bar when they opened with no res. Cocktails and everything we ordered was very delicious, and fairly quick service. Very nice atmosphere, didn’t feel too crowded / loud despite restaurant being almost at full capacity. Would definitely come back to try more dishes here (:

I was able to get a lunch reservation a week in advance on OpenTable and it was worth it! Everything was delicious and lived up to expectations. We ordered the chrysanthemum salad, calamari w/pepperoni rice, caramelle pasta, and the lasagna to share and everything was beyond expectations. The calamari really surprised us, but the salad is a must order. The lasagna is delicious and the portions are huge. The bread it is served with is amazing. Highly recommend this restaurant as “worth it” if you’re trying to get a reservation: keep trying!

Second visit and just as incredible as the first. We had the lasagna and chrysanthemum salad again—both flawless and absolutely worth the hype. The lasagna continues to be a standout.

This time we also tried the scallop crudo and the sourdough pasta cacciatore. Every dish was excellent. The pasta had beautifully balanced flavors with subtle olive brine and perfectly seasoned chicken. The scallop crudo was fresh and delicious, though the portion was small and left us wanting more.

We enjoyed a great bottle of Cabernet Sauvignon and finished with the black cocoa tiramisu, which was the perfect ending. Overall, a 10/10 experience and a restaurant that truly lives up to its reputation.

google_reviews.text: I always have an amazing experience here, no matter how many times I go! The place is so beautiful, from the inside and out. The atmosphere is always gorgeous, best decoration, and the view through windows are simply beautiful, expecially when they have the winter scene out. It's such a shame it comes out only once a year! Usually places with good presentation don't have the best food, but that is DEFINITELY not the case for this restaurant. Every dish is not only so pleasing to the eyes but also so delicious! I've had many different kinds of food here, but from meat, to vegetable, to even pasta, everything is cooked to perfection and it tastes perfect too! The menu changes ever so often, so you'll never be bored of the options any time you go as well. The servers are so kind and attentive, I have never felt like I was neglected at my table, even on the most busiest of days. I personally love the poke chips, and although I know many people do not find raw fish appealing, this is one place you just have to try it. Because you might just change your mind! From appetizers, entrees, Dinner, desert, and anything else, I'm sure that any food you'll have here will be GOOD food. Also the drinks are fantastic! Not alot of places have such a diverse and tasty selection of non alcoholic beverages, but I suppose Tavern On the Green is simply in a league of its own. I've been here multiple times, but I'd definitely recommend anyone to go and Im sure I'll be back again!!

I had an absolutely wonderful experience! From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm and inviting. The food was incredible—every dish was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. You can truly taste the quality and care that goes into each meal.
What really stood out, though, was the outstanding customer service. The staff was friendly, attentive, and genuinely made us feel valued and welcomed. They went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect.
I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for great food and an exceptional dining experience. I’ll definitely be coming back!

What a fantastic lunch we enjoyed here today. It was truly an experience. The venue was stunning. Well decorated, it felt like stepping into a gingerbread house. The decor was incredible. The food was really tasty. The drinks, desserts, and even the coffee were delightful. The service were very attentive, even though the place was super busy. We received the attention we needed. The only downside was the lack of a parking lot, requiring a walk of about a block to reach a garage, but that’s to be expected in New York City. This is definitely a spot I recommend for both tourists and locals, especially during the holiday season.

The date I visited coincided with New York Restaurant Week... and I was able to enjoy their special menu.  Honestly, the food at this restaurant was delicious.  Even though I'm not usually a big fan of Western cuisine, I really enjoyed it. The view was also great, the restaurant atmosphere was wonderful, and the service from the manager to the staff was very attentive. Of course, the tip started at 20%

The glass-encased area is a gorgeous place to be for brunch. Service was good, but interesting choices were made re: triage of task completion. We sat for a few minutes staring at our main course waiting for new flatware. Not a huge issue I guess, but eggs don't hold well, even after just a few minutes. There were too many people on the floor for there not to be a more efficient procedure for this.

Biscuits and gravy - if you're from the south (we're TN natives), skip this. The gravy was bland and the biscuit was really more of a scone. They attempted to ellevate a staple from another region, but instead just made a worse version of it.
Onion soup - fine; we've had worse, but we've had better, too.
Steak and Eggs - not a fan, but I'll give the concession that I may just not like this cut of meat personally; maybe if you like sirloin, your feelings would be opposite mine. I'm a rare fillet guy myself, so its toughness was off-putting. The potatoes were just not good thanks to the addition of bell peppers overpowering the entire side dish. All I could taste was over-cooked, mushy bell pepper; it was like no other seasoning in it at all. We found on our trip that the higher the prices are, the less flavorful the food is; Tavern on the Green is the prime example of this. The over-easy eggs were cooked perfectly.
Eggs Benny (w/ Lobster) - I don't have enough experience with lobster to make this claim with much authority, but my heart told me the lobster was dry and overdone. Same potato situation. The poached eggs were cooked perfectly; why are we only nailing the cheapest part of these dishes?

Look, it's a cute spot. That's about all I can offer though because the prices they're charging for what you're eating are insulting.

document: Kong Sihk Tong 港食堂. cuisine: Chinese Hong Kong Style Cafe. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Such a delicious spot for HK breakfast & comforting Cantonese dishes! Love the iced yuanyang here - great tea & coffee blend.

Service is always so nice & the food just makes me feel at home. Baked pork chop tomato rice is sooo good (lil fattier on the pork, but I like it that way!). Beef chow fun, spaghetti with beef & black pepper, and eggplant with pork and salty fish are also incredible. For a sweet treat, must get the golden lava french toast!

Fantastic prices (sub 11 for most things on the menu) with really decent portion sizes and delicious food. They give you small water cups and do a really good job of filling them up consistently - the servers were really efficient and nice, and even turned on a big heater when we said we were cold. Beef chow fun is as good as ones twice its price, but my standout was the baked fried rice/ spaghetti with porkchop. So good! Cash or venmo only

I’ve been back so many times, love this place! Def top 3 best restaurants in Manhattan Chinatown. The line/wait can get long during peak lunch and dinner times, but worth the wait! Pay with cash or Venmo

- Golden lava toast: 11/10, best item on the menu. I’m always craving this. Would come here just for this, MUST GET
- Chicken wings in grapefruit honey sauce: 11/10, sounds weird, but it’s SO good (underrated). Sweet and savory! MUST GET
- Salt & pepper fried squid: 10/10, good flavor and texture
- Baked fried rice w/ pork chop and tomato sauce: 10/10, love the sauce flavor. MUST GET
- Satay beef & enoki mushroom chow fun ($13.50): 8/10, solid! Would consider getting again bc the beef had great flavor and was tender

Today was my first time at Kong Sihk Tong, so I really didn’t know what to expect. Given the busy schedule in the evening, we waited about 10-15 minutes prior to getting seated. Keep in mind that this restaurant only takes cash or Venmo, so be prepared in advance. First off, the quantity of food for the price was really good. We ordered the beef chow fun, lemongrass pork chop with rice, and the baked pork with rice. The meat was so juicy and tender and the noodles and rice were so well seasoned and didn’t feel greasy at all! To top it off, we ordered Hong Kong milk tea, and the best compliment you can get from an Asian when you order drinks is “not too sweet”, the tea was so well balanced and refreshing. The food came out really quick too! We waited about 5-7 minutes, and they all came out so fresh. Overall I had an excellent first experience here and would recommend to anyone wanting to try Hong Kong style street food, at an affordable price point. I will definitely be back!

There’s no place in NYC that resembles an authentic Hong Kong cafe as much as Kong Sihk Tong does. I’ve been here a couple times and the food is authentic and consistently so delicious. The lava toast, baked rice/spaghetti dishes, and iced Hong Kong milk tea are must-try’s. It’s ALWAYS worth the wait, and even outside of mealtimes I’ll stop by to get HK milk tea to-go. The menu is super expansive and there’s endless new things to try. Hands down my most favorite spot in Chinatown.

The staff here are so kind and attentive, shout out to Simon who was the absolute sweetest, he made our whole evening!

name: Okdongsik
document: Okdongsik. cuisine: Korean Soup. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
It’s… good? Look. I’m a clear soup GIRLIE. But this is just not very flavorful. Also… the dumplings are frozen.
That said, the meat is actually good and the broth is well balanced. The rice stays nicely cooked after being soaked.
The dumplings are really good. But again, surprisingly from frozen.
The kimchi is free refills yay.

The atmosphere is very calming, which was my favorite part of the experience!!

I went on a Sunday night, 10mins before they opened. We got in right when they opened. But this was a VERY cold day, so the line was short.

This was one of the best Korean restaurants I've been to. The broth is so clear yet rich. Not oily or heavy at all. The pork is so tender and pairs well with their housemade gochuji paste.

The mandu was very soft and tender and filled with meat. The dumpling skin is very thin. Pairs very well with the dwaeji gomtang. The naeng jaeyuk was so tender as well and goes well with the gochuji.

Their kimchi was actually really good. Had to ask for refills. More on the less ripe side yet flavorful, cruncy and fresh.

Overall very hearty and healthy meal. The 45 min wait was very worth it (we went on a Monday during lunch time).

Can I be honest? It was ridiculous of me to wait almost 2 hours in the freezing cold for this… but that was my personal decision. I also now learned you can order online which would be much less of a wait!!

I will say, the meal did not disappoint. I was still so excited to try, given the general hype about the restaurant and even more hype from Chef Ok’s feature on Culinary Class Wars. I think some of the reviews are pretty harsh. It seemed a lot of work and skill goes into making a clean and flavorful broth as this. The dumplings were pricey ($3 a pc basically), but that’s NYC baby!!!
The staff is very efficient and nice. They allow refills on the Kimchi, spicy sauce, and rice, so I got a refill on the kimchi bc I personally really enjoyed and gobbled it up before the broth (very shortly) arrived. (I guess standing outside in the cold burns a lot of calories…)

All of that to say, I think waiting that long for this meal in the freezing cold is a one-time thing for me. However, I would definitely be down to do an online order to taste this yummy broth again :)

I went here for lunch on Sunday after seeing the chef on Culinary Class Wars. My friend and I did a walk in for two on a snowy (half the city shut down level snowstorm) Sunday. We got there at about 11:40am when they just opened at 11:30 and got the last two walk-in seats. The couple that came after us was quoted 30 minutes and after that quotes became an hour to hour and a half wait - so if you’re doing a walk-in I recommend right when they open. I got kimchi mandoo and the dweji-gomtang with extra pork.

The kimchi mandoo were very tasty, though I would probably skip them on my next visit (I try to maximize dining when in NY and after getting to try them once, I think I’d save the room to be hungry for another snack or meal to try 😅).

The dweji-gomtang was everything you’d want on a cold snowy day. The broth was very light and very fragrant, and the rice and pork paired very well with it. I loved the side of gochuji to dip the pork in - it complemented everything very well. The kimchi they give is ok, but not the best I’ve ever had. I also really enjoyed the tea they provide while you’re eating.

I rushed straight to a Broadway show from the meal and despite finishing everything - my soup, three of the dumplings (my friend ate the fourth), and my kimchi - I didn’t feel uncomfortably full or heavy after the meal.

The space is small with just about 14 counter seats. The chefs, who are also the ones to confirm your order, are on the other side preparing the food. There is no waiting area, so if you are quoted a wait you have to go somewhere else to pass the time (they’ll text you when your table is ready).

Overall, very pleased with my meal, though if I’d waited an hour and a half like others were quoted I may have felt differently. If you can snag a reservation or a short wait, I highly recommend!

The kimchi dumplings were *excellent*, the solution was surprisingly tasty, lemonade is on the sweet side for me. The warm pork broth over perfectly chewy rice was so comforting. The generous slices of pork were so tender and simultaneously bouncy -- a texture that is so rare! My only thing is I should have asked for more kimchi - it went so well with everything.

Would line up again for this.

However, Don disappeared and only a female bartender (didn’t get her name nor do I think she would give it based on her attitude… Black hair put up in bun, spoke both English and Spanish, mid 30s) was left to tend. I wanted to make sure that I didn’t mistakingly get someone else’s order as she placed the incorrect  food order down in front of us. I informed her that we ordered 12 instead of 6 and just wanted to make sure this was part of our order before I touched the food and potentially caused a headache for someone else. I was met with the most unprofessional behavior and rude attitude/response that was completely uncalled for. This behavior ruined our mood and taste for the restaurant. “Ok, what do you want me to do about it?! I didn’t take your order! Do you want me to put in another one or not?!” (Whisk rolling her eyes and giving nasty looks) This was followed by her completely ignoring us and walking past multiple times while I tried to get another drink. When she finally acknowledged us again I tried to order another drink. She rang it up and never gave it to me (simple bottle beer). Instead we were again ignored and I watched her check in and serve several other people. We finally had enough and felt so uncomfortable that we asked to close out. When I got my bill I was charged for the drink I never got. We then had to wait for it to be corrected after she looked confused when I brought it up. I’ve had a handful of pleasant experiences at this establishment, but service is everything. That was by far the worst service I’ve ever experienced. I would not spend my hard earned money at a place where I’m treated like that nor would I in good faith recommend it. The food I’ve gotten on other occasions including this one have been good when we actually got what we ordered,  and Don was very pleasant/personable on Saturday, but you go out for the overall experience. Overall, that experience was overwhelmingly distasteful.

Awesome ambiance and a big industry hang out. Great happy hour and lots of small plates including flat breads, tandoori chicken kebab, chicken & pork sliders, chili, Mac & cheese, chicken wings, anti pasta, chicken & pork sliders, mezza plates and decent desserts too. Mike always takes care of my buddy Roy & I!

Sexiest bar in dc. I don’t drink anymore but they have solid food and killer decor. Heard Renee is running it now, he’s a dope dude. Definitely check it out, they have pool, food, cocktails, beer and party. Recommend 10/10.

Me and my wife went to Lola’s recently after spending a day in Capital Hill going to Eastern Market. We went to Lola’s to get a quick drink and ended up spending some time there. We got drinks, wings, mac and cheese and it was delicious. The host was very accommodating. This bar is a lot bigger than what it looks like from the front. They have a pool table on the top floor and another bar on the middle floor. I plan to go back soon. Love this place.

I’ve rarely had a burger with no taste/flavor but that’s what I had tonight and it was over cooked. Incredibly disappointed as its sister restaurant Hawk n Dove has great burgers. Also, I think there were like 12 fries on my plate. Really????  Also, the new bartender didn’t know the answers to any questions which would understand but she didn’t go get the answers.  Not sure I’ll return.

name: Carmine's Italian Restaurant - Upper West Side
document: Carmine's Italian Restaurant - Upper West Side. cuisine: Italian Desserts Seafood. located in Manhattan. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Had a birthday dinner for my neice.  The wait staff was very cordial and attentive. The table setting and atmosphere was nice, music not to my taste but tolerable.  The dishes of food was quite a lot and of course sharable. If you compared the price to the average plate every one would have ordered separately somewhere else would of cost about $25 - $35 each however, the bill was not modest at all and the drinks a little pricey as well. Plenty of food but not so delicious. Something different in the sauce. Either my palate has changed or the recipe 🤔. I've been coming here over 10 years either for work gatherings or birthdays. Tonite was underwhelming.

We love this family style old school super popular Italian restaurant! Their eggplant parmigiana is the absolute best, and comes in a huge serving size enough to feed four or more people! Or two with leftovers, which taste even better the next day. We've dined in which is usually crowded-- esp on weekends, but not as crowded as the Times Square location, and also have taken out on many occasions, which has a separate pick up entrance and is super convenient.
Their salads, fried calamari, pasta, pretty much all dishes-- are all fantastic and served in family sized portions-- add pasta for a very small upcharge. Focaccia also delicious.
Their sauce is extremely flavorful with few ingredients and no sugar.

Happy hour review. The food is good and plentiful. Drinks are reasonable. I finally had the opportunity to go to Carmine during their limited happy hour (Monday to Thursdays only 3-5pm and after 9pm). The calamari is as good as I remembered from the early 1990’s when they first opened, although now, the marinara sauce is less garlicky and more cooked. Serving size is perfect for 2 to share. The best deal was the sliders (2 for $5): the foccacia bread was great, the portion large and the extra sauce was a bonus touch. The mussels were good too but the sauce was not (chili) spicy - it also came with 2 whole stewed tomatoes. The house red was a young montepulciano d’abruzzo (2024) served in a drinking style glass (like in Italy). Lunch menu (sandwiches and smaller pasta portions is available all day at the bar. For those with soy allergy: canola oil is used exclusively in the kitchen. But they don’t make the focaccia and the bread they use in the meatballs in house, so ask your server. Looking forward to returning. Feb 2026

Carmine’s UWS location was so beautifully decorated in this wonderful Christmas season. From the moment you walk-in, hostess greets you with a warm smile and managers walk around the dining room to ensure everyone’s needs are met. Our server Juan was extremely friendly, courteous, attentive and made my birthday lunch special. Portions are huge and everything was delicious. The cheesecake was very different than regular New York style cheesecake, which was delightful surprise. We thoroughly enjoyed our lunch and we were stuffed by the end of the meal. Can’t recommend enough how friendly everyone was and we certainly would love to return to try different items next time. Thank you again for your warm hospitality, Carmine’s UWS team!

Stopped in for my birthday dinner . The restaurant  was very crowded  I'm happy we made reservations even though we weren't seated on time . The table my family had was very cramped for my family of 8 and if we sneezed too hard we could hit the other party next to us 😩.

For the food it was tasty but not the best. I expected more from carmines . It was extremely busy so I might give it another try to see if it was just a bad night . Everything was family style portioned appropriately and priced well . The drinks weren't that strong but tasted good . They charge a $4 sur charge per person if you bring a birthday cake to cut fyi !! . Happy eating 😋🍽️
