name: Yumpling
document: Yumpling. cuisine: Taiwanese Noodles Asian Fusion. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This place is really special. A friend at work who loves her foodie spots suggested this little gem and she was spot on with these juicy delicious huge dumplings that will fill you up! The short story about the beginnings of this little dumpling empire started off as a small stand at the LIC Flea market  before opening up their food truck in Long Island city in 2017. After a short while, and lots of word of mouth the owner finally opened up a location here in the greatest city on earth🌐🏙, right in Midtown on 52nd St. The other store location is still in Long Island city on Vernon Blvd. Besides their famous dumplings the menu consists of noodles, Bian Dang rice bowls, fried chicken sandwiches, Taiwanese popcorn chicken, garlicky cucumbers, shaved ice and plenty of other sides. Specialty drinks include Bubble tea, Tai beer, Iced Taro lattes and more. But the "piece de resistance" is their mouth watering dumplings. We have consistently ordered the pork & chive dumplings which is made with their homemade chili oil, sesame seeds and scallions & cilantro. My wife and I split the large portion which consists of 12pcs. It's more then enough for 2 people. You can also order the half & half or the Yumpling trio to try them all out. I plan on trying the beef noodle soup and the popcorn chicken next time, but I might have to get the small order of 4pcs dumplings because they are sooo addictive. If your around the midtown area, Yumpling is the place for takeout or dine in if you want to try the most stuffed and delectable dumplings on this planet.👍🏼👍🏼🍜🍽😋🤤🤤😋🤤😋🥟🥟🥟🥟🥟❤️

Surprisingly delicious! Thought this was just some random take out place with the sign outside, but the quality of ingredients is great. The fried chicken cutlet was juicy thigh meat and crunchy on the outside. The Lu rou rice beneath was solidly good, and reminds me of my Taiwanese auntie’s cooking. I wish the inside space was bigger, but the decor is cute too if you can grab a seat. I will totally come back here the next time in the area.

Good to see you in manhattan! After years of schlepping to LIC for good, reasonably priced Taiwanese food, we finally have this option in the city! The lu ro fan is my go to; but everything is good here. The space is also a lot bigger and nicer than the original location.

The chicken Bian Dang ($15 plus tax), a crispy breaded chicken breast over rice with sides, is their best value. Their namesake pork and chive yumplings
($7.75 for 4), disappointingly were too salty. Skip the iced taro latte boba ($6.50) as it was too sweet; get your bubble tea fix elsewhere.

With only a few stools and a communal table, Yumpling could use more indoor seating.

I can see why this place has nothing but 5 stars and I couldn’t agree more! I got the steamed pork yumplings and crispy chicken rice bowl w the pickled cabbage & cucumbers as my sides. The dumplings were out of this world tasty, I devoured them in 5 seconds lol. The chicken is juicy, flavored impeccably, and an excellent portion size for the price. On top of that, the space itself is super cute, beyond efficient ordering process, and top notch customer service. My only regret is that I didn’t find this place sooner!! Can’t wait to come back soon

name: Tanner Smiths
document: Tanner Smiths. cuisine: Cocktail Bars New American Beer Bar. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Make a reservation, especially if you have a party larger than 2 because this place is packed ok ! Parking is hard to find but that’s NYC for ya ! We parked at a garage a few blocks away ($25) and walked back to the restaurant. While you enter, there’s a live band playing music which is cool but it makes the bar area / front of restaurant loud. It’s a bit quieter towards the back. The place is huge and the decor gives “grandma’s house”. Bathrooms were very clean and smelled so good. Now let’s get to the GOOD STUFF !! The food is 1000/10 omg ! The waffle literally melts on your tongue 😛 I would highly recommend the Birria Chimichanga. A bunch of chaotic goodness wrapped together. Portions are great too. I don’t remember our waitresses name but she was so sweet and attentive. The drink menu is overwhelming. There’s an option for everything and everyone. I do like that they break each section down and provide an explanation for the drinks in each section. I can appreciate that. Ultimately, we went with the bottomless mimosa and it did not disappoint. Overall, a great brunch experience. Would highly recommend this restaurant.

I love the vibe of Tanner Smith’s!! The food was GREAT! The drinks were strong! The vibe was amazing! They have a nice upstairs vibe for people who want to eat or chill and have a drink. The downstairs is where the parties at for people who want a party! The waitress was really nice, and recommended some great food. She even helped me make a couple of drink decisions! It was my birthday and they gave me a frozen shot! Please stop by if you are in New York.

Made a reservation in advance since I had a party of five and when I realized my party was arriving a few mins later than the reservation time I was able to ask the hostess to adjust the reservation and it was done very smoothly and I was able to sit at the bar while waiting for more of the party to show up. Very friendly and welcoming space. Had live music playing when we went on a Saturday. The brunch options were very good and the bottomless drinks were a good touch. Was super glad when the server gave us a notice for when the 90 mins were nearing for bottomless drinks and allowed us to put in one last round of drinks. The birria chimichanga were really filling and a good portion size. One of my friends had the avocado toast and it was a bit cold.

Would def visit again whether solo, for a date or for a group session. But advice for if doing more than 2 ppl and you don’t want to sit at the bar, definitely reserve before going as it is rather busy.

We stopped into Tanner Smith’s and ended up heading down to their speakeasy called Polly, which was a great surprise. The atmosphere had that classic speakeasy vibe, lively but not overwhelming, and the aesthetic of the space felt unique compared to a lot of other Midtown spots. Even on a Wednesday night the place was busy with a good mix of people, many on first dates or casual nights out. It felt less touristy than other bars near Times Square, which gave it a more local energy.

We kept it simple with food, sharing the chicken tenders and the everything pretzel bites, which hit the spot for bar bites. For drinks, I ordered the Irish Bill and we also tried the Cantinero. Both were well made and balanced, and the bar menu overall had a strong mix of creative cocktails and classics.

The staff were friendly, attentive, and made the experience even smoother. Between the atmosphere, the drinks, and the food, Tanner Smith’s stood out as a fun and easygoing spot to wind down after a long day. I would definitely recommend it if you are looking for a good bar near Times Square that still feels a little more authentic than the usual tourist stops.

This place was awesome! You actually felt like you were in a 1920s speakeasy that had multiple rooms and Bars throughout so you can have more space. The decor was great and the canapes were so fun. I went there for a private event but would go there again and again!

document: Westmoreland Cafe. cuisine: Cafes. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Came in for drinks and bites after an afternoon checking out the new Frick. Enjoyed our cocktails and whatever the cheese plate was incredible. Each bite and nibble so flavorful. Would love to come back and try more of the menu.

My friend’s specialty cocktail looked great and my rose was nice and crisp.

I sat at the bar by myself at Westmoreland at The Frick and was taken care of by Ricardo, who was absolutely wonderful. The space is stunning and elegant, light-filled, and beautifully designed, with every detail feeling thoughtful and refined. I had a Cosmopolitan and a croissant, which was the best I’ve ever had. The atmosphere is both sophisticated and welcoming, and Ricardo’s attentive service made the experience exceptional. A perfect spot to unwind and enjoy something truly special.

I must say the service today must have improved from the previous comments from other patrons. I had a great experience on all fronts. The food was lovely. The decoration and design of the dining room is very nice and lively . The lady matre’ D manager Emily is wonderful. She is professional , friendly and attentive. She makes my entire lunch more pleasant.

Really outstanding museum cafe with some of the best food I’ve ever eaten a museum, with terrific service and a wonderful atmosphere. Been three times already: The trout, chicken Milanese, pasta and salads are all excellent, as are the desserts. The quiche was too salty is the only complaint. Service is excellent. A great place to go in connection with a Frick visit.

HOW TO GET IN: you can ask reception at the Frick once you come into the museum to make a reservation. I think the inside of the restaurant is very beautiful and a wonderful ode to Frick family. It was the first day so things were very busy but I was upset the hosts kept giving tables away to people with no reservations when I had been waiting for 20 minutes and they kept giving my seat away when I had a reservation. The hosts were terrible. However the staff inside was very lovely. The food is good but I wouldn’t say I was particularly blown away. I had the heirloom tomato soup and the Caesar salad. I loved the pineapple fizz mocktail and it was very solid Bloody Mary. The drinks are supposed to be based on cocktails with a curator but I didn’t see anything mention of that on the menu. I think that’s a very unique part of the restaurant but I would have no idea if I didn’t read about it beforehand. I think they should advertise that more.

google_reviews.text:
Definition of a 5-star meal. My friend and I did the chef’s tasting menu which was a very reasonably priced $85 including 3 courses, starting with the tuna cannolis (out of this world) and crudo, onto the main course featuring head and tail-on prawns, melt in your mouth fish and the most tender, juicy truffle chicken.

Our server Jo and the rest of the staff kept the meal moving at a steady pace with excellent service. Fun, upbeat vibe as well.

We’ve passed Little Maven so many times and always meant to try it.  Last night we finally did for NYE.  It was absolutely a great experience.

From our wonderful server, Vanessa, to the outstanding food, we had a night to remember.

We started with the Tuna Cannoli and the Caesar endive, both perfect for sharing and packed with layers of flavor.  The scallops with caviar were rich and decadent, a little on the salty side.  For entrées, we had the dry-aged duck and the steak frites, both incredibly tender. The portion of fries was extremely generous, more than enough to share.

Even though we were completely full, we couldn’t pass up the homemade cookies and ice cream for dessert.

Highly recommend making a reservation.

Food was good, appetizer portions were underwhelming. I'd highly recommend the Caesar salad, duck agnolotti and desert cookie. I would not recommend the steak frites as the steak was tough to cut through and lacked flavour.

Service was phenomenal and the staff went above and beyond.

Absolutely fantastic experience. The food was superb and the hospitality top notch. Celebrated a birthday dinner and felt wildly special. That’s not always the case in a busy establishment, but they took the time and energy to make one feel seen and very taken care of. Highly recommend

name: Nari
document: Nari. cuisine: Korean. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Overall the food and service was amazing. The decor was also nice. We chose the tasting menu so we can try more dishes. The stand out items were the duck curry puff, pork jowel, and ox tail curry. These were top notch. The other items we had were executed well, but not quite at a higher level. Our overall experience was great and we would return and probably pick from the à la carte menu.

Nari has a very nice ambiance, but unfortunately everything beyond that was a disappointment. While the space itself is polished and inviting, the overall dining experience fell far short of expectations.

Service was a major issue. Our server came across as rushed, unwelcoming, and disengaged. At first, I assumed it might have been an off moment, but after watching his interactions with nearby tables, it was clearly consistent. There was no warmth, no effort to explain dishes, and no sense of hospitality it felt as though he either didn’t want to be there or was overwhelmed with too many tables.

The menu itself is heavily pork-focused. If you are not a pork eater, I would strongly recommend skipping this restaurant, as the majority of the dishes include pork in some form, leaving very limited alternatives.

We ordered two beers, both of which were poorly poured, arriving with approximately three to four inches of foam more foam than beer. It looked like beer topped with whipped cream, which immediately set a negative tone for the meal.

For food, we ordered the Prik King Gai (crispy chicken stir-fried in sweet and spicy curry paste) and the Gaeng Bumbai Aubergine (crispy eggplant in spicy Bumbai curry). We were warned that the Prik King Gai was very spicy, so we planned to switch dishes if needed. When the food arrived, both dishes were equally and overwhelmingly spicy, with no depth of flavor beyond heat. The eggplant dish offered nothing but spice, and the chicken dish had the texture and taste of burnt crumbs tossed in dry chili no balance, no complexity, and no discernible flavors coming through.

Overall, this was not an experience I would return for or recommend to others. While the ambiance is nice, poor service, limited menu balance, poorly executed drinks, and flavorless, overly spicy food made this a very disappointing visit.

I finally tried this Thai place after walking past it for ages, and I'm so glad I did! The food had an amazing, strong spicy flavor that really hit the spot. The service was also excellent, and the staff were very friendly and attentive. It's a nice spot to enjoy a delicious meal, especially since the area is great for a walk afterward. I would highly recommend it!

I had dinner at Nari, and it was an incredible experience from start to finish. The restaurant has a beautiful, modern atmosphere that still feels warm and welcoming. Service was attentive, knowledgeable, and thoughtful throughout the evening.
The food was the real highlight—each dish was layered with bold, complex flavors that truly showcased the depth of Thai cuisine in a contemporary style. The presentation was elegant without feeling overdone, and every plate felt carefully balanced. Standouts included the creative small plates, the perfectly cooked proteins, and the way spices and herbs came together in harmony.
Nari is definitely on the higher end in terms of pricing, but the quality and experience make it well worth it. It’s a perfect spot for a special dinner in San Francisco.

Context:
I took a date here for Valentines day on Feb 15th 2026. The restaurant atmospher was beautiful, but food was poor, especially for the price and status.

Food:
Overall everything was incredibly salty. We had the squid and pork jowl, namtok nuea and crab curry with garlic noodles. The pork and jowl was tolerable, the nomtok nuea was nearly inedible. We had to wrap it with a lot of lettuce and cucumber in order to stomach it. Crab curry was alright but fairly mild for curry. We only ate through half of everything and couldn't stomach the rest.

Service:
Slow. Wait was about ~45min for the food. They gave us an extra appetizer as an apology which was nice, food was poor though. It was Valentines day and packed so more understandable.

Drinks:
We had the kanitha and utai. Not sure if it's my fault for getting a more fruity cocktail but they weren't very strong.

Price:
Felt like robbery, we could barely stomach half of it yet walked away with a 400$ bill for everything I listed above.

Overall: not worth the price, reservation logistics, or wait. I gave it 2 stars because the date went well gave us a fun story to talk about how overated the place was.

google_reviews.text:
Our dinner was absolutely spectacular! Our server, Nina was warm, attentive, and offered excellent recommendations that truly elevated the entire experience. It was a great dining experience thanks to her!

We started with the Lobster and Ha Gao from the Lunar New Year menu. The lobster was incredibly delicious which perfectly cooked and generously coated in a spicy sauce that complemented the sweetness of the meat beautifully. The Ha Gao were delicate and flavorful, with a satisfying bite.

The Hoo Johr was also a standout! It was crispy on the outside, savory on the inside, and perfect as an appetizer to share.

For our mains, the Panang Duck Lychee Curry was hands down the best rich, creamy, and packed with bold flavors, with just the right balance of sweetness from the lychee. The Shrimp Pad Thai was equally impressive, featuring plump shrimp, well-balanced seasoning, and perfectly cooked noodles.

We ended the meal with mango sticky rice. Even though mango isn’t in season, the dessert was absolutely amazing! The sticky rice was warm and fragrant, paired with sweet coconut milk, mango Ice cream and fresh mango.. it was the perfect ending to a fantastic dinner. Highly recommend!

This restaurant  really blow my mind  and reset my taste  for thai food. I have always like it.  Been on several restaurants. But none like Soothr.  Food was amazing. Unique experience with each bite.  Service  was fantastic, and staff supper friendly . Restaurant overall is everything  you need if u looking for great food.

We start with some crispy Chiken,  fried dumplings 10/10   pad thai 😍, duck in curry sauce, wow 👌  those too were also fantastic. Can't wait to go back  .  Dessert  was sweet and delicious...
While im writing this im having a smile in my face,enjoying my food again

Had a great experience at Soothr today! Jesse provided excellent service, she was very attentive, friendly, and made us feel very welcome throughout the meal. The crab roe curry noodles (Karee Pu Noodles) were absolutely delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly balanced. The food came out quickly, and the overall service was efficient and very nice. Definitely would come back again!

I was in town for the weekend and couldn't wait to co to Soothr because of their reputation. I was starting to get packed and it was tight. It was like a Thai-Chinatown (Yaowarat) vibe. We were given an hour and a half time limit which is normal but I feel like we were being rushed.
Started off with drinks, I wasn't a fan of my cocktail. Duck egg rolls had more wood ear mushrooms than duck. I was excited about Karee Pu (crab curry) the texture of the noodles were great. The curry was extra thick and had a strong cumin taste to it, we weren't a fan. We also got the duck noodles, once again the noodles were great. The duck was cooked perfectly but the gravy was so sweet and that was it, sweet. I love Thai food because of the mix of flavors, sweet, spicy, sour, salty, but this place didn't do it for us. I really wanted to like it but we were pretty underwhelmed.

Jane was our server and did an amazing job explaining all the dishes and options! We went for the Valentine's special and the crab croquett and Yaowarat Pad Mii were delicious. Would come back and try some more next time! Thanks Jane for making our Valentine's memorable 🥹

document: Lillie's Victorian Establishment. cuisine: Bars Gastropubs Burgers. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Edited slightly. The more I reflect on this experience, the more disappointed I am in the poor value for the price. I've done many afternoon teas in many cities, and this is unquestionably the worst experience I've had so far.

Went for afternoon tea here and it was a bit of a mixed bag. I really enjoyed the scones and extra-thick clotted cream. Tea for two people should have two of everything - four macarons in four flavors means sharing them all or missing out on two flavors. The tea sandwiches were lackluster - I didn't care for the chopped celery in the egg salad personally, and the cucumber sandwiches were very soggy. (This is why cucumber sandwiches are usually made with cold butter - to protect the bread from moisture). The fresh fruit was delicious but baffling; blueberries and grapes are best enjoyed with the fingers, however they had been needlessly dusted with powdered sugar. The tea on offer was nice, but weak as they only provided a single tea bag per pot and the water wasn't as hot as should be for brewing a black tea. Lastly, I can excuse sugar packets, but plastic stir straws instead of teaspoons just feels wrong.

The high-top seating was very difficult for my 4'10" self to climb up into. That said, service was very attentive and the space was charming.

(This review is from a dining experience in Nov '25.)

Had a work dinner at this location, and everything was very unique and engaging.
Food was very good, and the lingering decor from Halloween was very extensive, well done, and interesting to look at.
Service was pretty good, given the fact that this night the location was packed full of people. They took good care of our large party.
Understand that this is a popular restaurant in NYC, so it's going to be packed with people at most dining times, tight maneuvering, and loud.
It's a unique dining experience in a city full of them, and if you can book a table here I would highly recommend it.

The interior is mostly high-top seating, so there isn’t much difference in comfort, and everything feels cozy. The table seating areas look especially comfortable for larger parties of four or five.

We ordered Prosecco, Pinot Grigio, and although our original plan was brunch, we decided on a cheese and charcuterie board instead. It was delicious. The cheese portions were generous, well-sized, and fairly priced. The grapes were very fresh, the jam was excellent, and the cured meats were well selected. Everything was beautifully presented.

Beyond the Victorian style, there’s an abundance of floral decor that adds to the charm. It does get busy, so I definitely recommend making a reservation at least one day in advance. Two or three days ahead would be even better.

I would absolutely recommend it for a morning date or a relaxed outing with a friend.

Had an excellent time at Lillie’s before seeing Book of Mormon. Literally right across the street from the theater. This extended our time here so we could have a long relaxing dinner.

We started off with some drinks which were yummy! We also had the calamari for an appetizer.  I was a little perplexed about why they would put pickled onions with calamari but I couldn’t get enough of this combo once I started eating them.

Then we had the chicken pot pie and the buttermilk chicken sandwich with the truffles fries. All of this with no disappointments.

We did sit at the bar bc we did not make a reservation. So, if that’s not your thing I would highly recommend making one. We were there on a Thursday at 5 and there was plenty of room at the bar, but by about 545. You could not get a seat. Plan ahead.

The winter and Valentine’s Day decor combo was spot on.

Been to the other location in October and Lillies never seems to disappoint with their decor.

Almost forgot to add our servers were super attentive. They did not hover but they were available enough to make our 2 hour bar visit and absolute pleasure.

Came here with the family for a pre-theatre lunch. We originally planned to enjoy the beautiful floral decor, but as luck would have it, they’d just switched over to Halloween that week — in September!

Theme-heavy spots near Times Square can be hit or miss, so expectations were modest. The place was pretty full (long and narrow layout), but thankfully we had a reservation and were seated right away. While the decorations were over-the-top — the “kitsch index” was high — the sheer volume of Halloween props covering every inch of the high ceilings actually made this die-hard New Yorker begrudgingly appreciate it. At least they commit.

Most importantly, the food was actually good — surprisingly good. My Cobb salad was huge and fresh (oddly, it listed avocado as an extra add-on, but mine came with it anyway). The burrata disappeared in seconds, the burger was juicy with crisp potatoes and greens, and the croque madame came topped with a perfectly runny, “sexy” sunny-side-up egg. Everything was delicious, and we cleared our plates in record time to make our show.

Service was attentive, with staff constantly circulating and easy to flag down. We’ll definitely be back once the flowers bloom again — next time, without the Halloween pumpkins watching us eat.

document: Fish Cheeks. cuisine: Seafood Thai Live/Raw Food. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I had a great experience at Fish Cheeks. The food was outstanding — especially the fried rainbow trout, which was absolutely delicious, and the crab fried rice, which was packed with flavor. Our waiter, Vincent, was wonderful — super attentive and gave fantastic recommendations throughout the meal. The music added a great vibe to the dining experience, and even the restrooms were spotless, which I appreciated. The only dish that didn’t quite hit was the wok-fried morning glory, which was just okay compared to everything else. Overall, this place is a total gem and I’d definitely come back!

Overall this was not a good experience.
The good: We ordered two appetizers and three entrees. We loved the mussel gorlae, which tasted like barbeque mussels with a delicious peanut based sauce. The mussels were cooked perfectly, which is not an easy feat. The entrees of the choo chee scallop was also cooked perfectly and the sauce was spicy and aromatic, it was our favorite dish of the night. We also got the grilled mackrel. It was light, refreshing, crunchy, sweet and salty.  A perfect blend of  flavors and our second favorite dish of the night. Servers were great and service was quick.

The not so good:
We also got the shrimp in 3 crab sauce. I personally found it to be way too acidic with no other elements to balance. I personally did not enjoy it but my partner did. The shrimps were a nice soft texture however.
The crab curry was something we were looking forward to as we had had it at previous visits. It was okay. The crab was cooked nicely. The curry was just okay. It was lacking in flavor. It was also room temperature when it arrived at the table, I am not sure if its meant to be served like that.
All this would have been okay and I would have given a 4/5 rating,  but the worst part of this experience was the COLD! We were seated close to the door and we had our jackets on and freezing the entire time. We saw other diners who were also close to the door asking to move tables. We were never apologized to for the cold or offered anything. I think this was really poor hospitality on their part. The servers and hostesses were working hard and I know this is probably out of their control. I think management needs to remember why they are in this business. We rushed eating our dinner and didn't bother with dessert because we were so cold and just wanted to get out of there. Overall just not a great experience.

Conclusion: I would recommend this restaurant if its a warm day or if you can specifically ask for a table far from the main entrance or upstairs but I won't be returning any time soon!

One of the strongest Thai dinner programs in the city.

I have been going to Fish Cheeks for several years so I have watched it change, expand, and evolve. I want to begin this review by noting that their menu seems to have been mellowed out flavor wise. While I am not certain if this is to appease the weak taste buds of the neighborhood or another reason, I unfortunately feel this has weakened the appeal of the restaurant for me. It is still delicious but I miss how much the spice here used to hit.

On the most recent visit I ordered the steamed whole fish, the corn salad, the fried cabbage, and the 30 day aged beef.

The meal begins with complimentary puffed rice cakes and a sweet dipping sauce. While not filling at all, it is a nice touch that elevates the experience and provides a warm welcome.

The corn salad is delicious with a punchy acidic level and beautifully fresh vegetables. My only note is that the portion changes every single visit. Thankfully on this visit is was the largest we have ever had. It seems like a simple dish but it really hits the spot.

While not ordered on this visit the zaab zaab wings are amazing. They taste like a more acidic taki seasoning on chicken wings. Again, the number of wings has changed each time we have ordered it so we decided against getting it this visit.

A must order is one or the whole fish offerings (or all of them). On this visit we got the steamed fish. It is full of lime, cilantro and other fresh herbs and perfectly cooked. It is kept piping hot by a burner on the table. This fish is one of the best seafood preparations in the city. I could eat the entire thing myself even with how filling it is.

The fried cabbage is a great side for the mains at this restaurant. Perfectly cooked while also being crispy fresh.

We decided to get the 30 days aged beef this visit. It was fine but the flavored were mellow compared to everything else and the ground texture was a negative contrast with the lightness of the fish we ordered. I would get something else next time.

The service was attentive and professional. With such a busy restaurant the hosts do a great job of managing the seating and turnover of tables.

This restaurant is probably one of the best I’ve been to in awhile. We ordered the Zaab Wings, the Fried Fish Garden Salad, and the Duck Curry. Everything arrived promptly but I never felt like they rushed us out. Food was extremely fresh and packed with flavor. The fried fish was my favorite, texture was perfectly crisp and it had so much flavor with just a hint of spice. The Zaab wings were also a standout, perfect texture with juicy meat inside, the spicy lime flavor had a really nice depth to it. I enjoyed the duck curry as well but didn’t stand out as much as the other dishes and while I loved the taste, I felt the duck was a bit on the chewy side. Portions were great though for 2 people, everything is meant to be shared and we felt it was the perfect amount of food.

Atmosphere was nice as well, I really loved their commitment to the fish decor, it’s nice when restaurants have a theme in my opinion, and the service was really good. My only complaint was it felt a little crowded, tables were pretty close together and it was a bit loud.

Stopped in for lunch yesterday while in the area. The restaurant is super cute, vibes immaculate. I was expecting the food to be excellent and the flavors still blew me away. I probably could have downed a hundred oysters, but just ordered 2 as I was in a time crunch. I’m not exactly sure that the toppings were but the texture and spices were new to me and were amazing. The half chicken was juicy and tasty, can’t wait to try more of the menu as I am going to be in the neighborhood all week for work. Only downside was the barstools, looked great, but not very comfortable. Highly recommend this spot.

For dessert, I tried the tiramisu — freshly made right in front of us, and it was pretty good!
All in all, the service here was incredibly nice. Such a pleasant dining experience!

this place is great for anything — dates, family, friends, etc I stg. especially great if you like meat. mix grill platter was phenomenal (takes like 45 minutes so) overall would say to expect dinner to be on the longer side here

name: Bourbon and Branch
document: Bourbon and Branch. cuisine: Bars Venues & Event Spaces American. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
The atmosphere was pleasant and welcoming, exuding a cozy Irish-British style. The pub was adorned with extensive oak and mahogany, featuring sturdy traditional wooden tables with dark finishes. High back stools lined the bar, and on this particular Sunday evening, there was a nice little crowd and everyone seemed to be having a good time. We decided to order the seitan wings, vegan nachos, and a vegan cheesesteak, along with two mocktails. The wings and the nachos arrived together, but we found the wings to be overly crispy and hard, with a dry inside that made them difficult to eat. After requesting for them to be fried for half the time, the wings came back out much better - crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and paired perfectly with a hot honey sauce, vegan ranch, and fresh cut celery and carrot sticks as sides.

The vegan nachos were generously piled high and layered with vegan chorizo, tomatoes, black beans, cheese sauce, and cilantro. About halfway through the nachos, we realized the absence of guacamole and vegan sour cream. The server promptly apologized and brought out the missing sides, along with the cut limes we had requested, as is common with nacho orders. As for the vegan cheesesteak, we had planned to take a bite and save the rest for later. It tasted good, but we felt that the bread should have been toasted. After a quick stint in the air fryer, the roll came out perfect - crusty on the outside with a soft cheesy inside and tender seitan meat.

Complementing our meal were the mocktails - the Arnold Schwartz with cucumber, lemonade, and iced tea, missing the mint that would have elevated the drink, and the refreshing Peter Cetera with lime juice, vanilla grapefruit, and club soda. Our server and host were both accommodating and took care of the adjustments we requested. We left with plans to return, noting how the menu looked much better online and the tempting specials they offer during the week - like the six dollar smash burgers and various dinner specials. Check it out!

I ordered from uber eats so I can’t comment on the service and atmosphere. Most of the food I ordered was great and the portion sizes matched what I paid for. However, tell me why I paid $12 for vegan chocolate coconut cake, expecting a normal sized slice of cake, and got this bite sized nonsense? I kid you not, it was smaller than the palm of my hand. It’s shameful that it was $12.
Probably one of the coolest, most affordable Bourbon bars I've been to. Great prices, food looked great but didn't eat. Highly recommend it for a bourbon stop.

Came for the vegan food- did NOT disappoint. Really beautiful old style bar inside with woo accents & tin ceiling. It really feels like a historic bar. Cozy & welcoming. All of our vegan food was amazing!

Seitan wings- super crispy but tender inside. Lathered in delicious BBQ sauce served with vegan ranch!

Vegan cheesesteak- the roll was fresh. Tons of seasoned seitan with vegan cheese sauce, onions & peppers. It was really delish! Ordered a side of onion rings because let’s be real- onion rings are the best part of bar food! The onion rings were delicious, crispy & so yummy!

They also have a IMPRESSIVE bar selection for bourbon/whiskey lovers. Like, an entire menu devoted to it.

Come for the cozy small bar vibes, good food & drinks. Enjoy the atmosphere !

document: Obao. cuisine: Vietnamese Thai Asian Fusion. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I had dinner with a group of four other friends today at this place. It's a busy establishment that requires the full party to be present before seating, but we were seated promptly once the time came. The atmosphere inside was warmly lit, quite welcoming, and the climate was very comfortable (though one friend had to put on a coat from sitting under the draft of the air conditioner). During our stay, there was upbeat music complimenting the entire experience.
The service was very swift, responsive, and reasonably respectful. We quickly ordered a couple of appetizers after sitting down, received drinking water, and were able to order our entrées shortly after. The appetizers arrived after minimal idling and the entrées arrived before the appetizers were finished, which was a welcome surprise. Massive thanks to Ken for providing the excellent service.
My entrée dish was the Drunken Noodles, which were without exaggeration, extremely delicious. The flat rice noodles had soaked up lots of flavor from the tomatoes and dried Thai basil, which was complimented by a well-balanced spiciness that made it hard to resist shoveling bite after bite (experience varies with spice tolerance). For the appetizers, the Kimchee Fries were moderately crispy and well seasoned while the Papaya Salad tasted fresh and surprisingly sweet.
Overall, I found this establishment to offer great food for reasonable prices and able to accommodate for individuals and small groups. I highly recommend giving this place a try.

I’ve been going here for years and it’s one of my favorite spots in the city. Everything is fresh and full of flavor, and if it says crispy, it’s actually crispy.
The tamarind glazed ribs are some of the best I’ve ever had, crispy outside and juicy inside. I also love their happy hour drinks. I wasn’t greeted right away once, but the service after that was totally fine. I’ll definitely be back soon.

Had a great experience at OBAO!

We started with Chamisul Original soju which is one of my favorite Korean sojus and was only $15. Surprised to see it on the menu but paired well (to me) with the Vietnamese dishes we ordered.

For dishes, we ordered the summer rolls, pho bo, and the ka prao kai khai dao. Everything was flavorful and well executed. The pho broth was clean and they gave a hearty amount of meat. The ka prao kai khai dao tasted like a comforting hug and was what I needed on a Sunday night before the work week.

The food was good, but the service made the experience even better. Jennie took great care of us and really elevated the whole night.

We will definitely be back!

Delicious Dumplings — Especially the Crab Soup Dumplings!

We had a very disappointing experience at this restaurant on December 25, 2025.
Three of us walked in after visiting a nearby cathedral and ordered three stir-fry dishes and three bowls of rice. The menu that servers showing to us clearly listed all stir-fry dishes at $15.95 each, and rice at $2.50 per bowl.

However, when the bill arrived near the end of the meal, we were surprised to see that two people were charged $22.95 each and one person was charged $23.95, with no notice of any price difference from the menu. No updated menu was shown.

One of the dishes (Beijing-style shredded pork with Garlic Sauce) also had a strong, unpleasant odor, possibly from the pork or the pickled bamboo shoots. The person who ordered it could only eat a few bites due to concerns about freshness and food safety.

At checkout, we were also forced to pay a mandatory gratuity, with only preset options of 18%, 20%, or 22%, with no option to decline or adjust. After tax and the mandatory tip, the total came to over $90 for three people, meaning over $30 per person. Based on the menu prices, even with tax and a reasonable tip, the total should have been around $22–$23 per person.

Update: The restaurant responded on another platform but blocked further communication. The dish in question was not edible due to a strong odor, regardless of the explanation provided.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Update on Jan first, 2026:

Dear Joe's Owner:

I want to clarify that this was not simply a “menu misunderstanding.”

We dined on Christmas Day. While the restaurant insists that everything was clearly stated on the menu, in practice the layout and communication made pricing easy to misunderstand, especially for visitors and first-time customers.

More importantly, one dish (the shredded pork with Spicy Garlic Sauce) was clearly not acceptable in quality. At the time of payment, I hesitated, but the server spoke in a commanding tone, telling me that I must leave a tip. Because it was a holiday and I was dining with others, I chose not to escalate the situation on the spot or ruin the atmosphere.

That does not mean the experience was acceptable.

Explanations about how ingredients are prepared or discarded behind the scenes are not something customers can verify. What customers can judge is what is served to them and how they are treated. From a customer’s perspective, the combination of confusing pricing, pressure at checkout, and food quality that did not match the price left a very poor impression.

This review reflects my real experience. I am sharing it so other diners can make an informed decision.

Regards

jane

I LOVED the French Onion soup. It was truly a standout in comparison to other French Onion soups I’ve had. The broccolini was very good! My drink was good!

My bartender was fine, but was hard to get ahold of and did not seem to be too interested in getting to me, despite the fact that I was one of two people at the long bar, and there were only a few tables who were seated. It wasn’t crowded, so this did surprise me a bit, but not the end of the world!

The ambience was simple and typical of what you expect from pubs, but still lovely! I really loved the building and its vibe! It managed to be cozy, as well as spacious and tidy! I liked it!

Overall, I’ll probably try a new place when I’m next in town rather than return, but I’m also glad I stopped in to The Elgin!

Great experience. The food was delicious, the Christmas decorations were brill. Very relaxed atmosphere and the service was excellent. The waiters were terrifically attentive. The portion sizes were generous. A starter with the mains left us stuffed. The fish and chips had an interesting chili tartar sauce and well worth it. The French onion burger was decedent and delicious.

Went with my boyfriend on a Saturday night on a whim since we were in the area .
The inside is really nice if you like old looking bars . The restaurant is two levels, with bars on each floor which you can sit at (and I’m not sure but it seems like they do prefer to offer that to parties of two). They do have a coat rack on the second floor (couldn’t note one on the first since just passed by). The food was good. I really liked their fries that came with the burger it was excellent. I had their expresó martini was fine. We got there around 4pm and it was full but not packed within a few minutes it definitely picked up. It does look like they had outdoor seating but not sure how many people are willing to sit outside now that it’s cold. Definitely a place to check out if you’re looking for a place to eat are in the area .

Awesome historic location and amazing staff. Our waiter was top notch and the food was incredible! The Wild Boar Chili, NY Strip, Rigatoni, pizza, Mac & cheese…all excellent. Also try the Golden Sunset (if you like mezcal) or the Hamilton (for gin lovers).

name: The Smith
document: The Smith. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Food here was really good. Stopped by with a friend on a random weekday and this place was packed. We ordered everything from the calamari, spicy salmon tartare, braised short rib mafaldine, bistro burger and the honeycrisp apple pie. The calamari had some surprising additions, but very delicious and a must order if you love calamari. The salmon tartare was really fresh and tasty. The mafaldine was cooked al dente and the short rib you could tell was slowly braised for hours.

My friend and I really enjoyed our experience here. The ambience is very warm, bright and definitely loud. If you want a private more intimate place this may not be it unless you have a private dining room. The servers were attentive and I loved how they bring out still water and sparkling. Highly recommend making reservations in advance.

My family and I visited The Smith on a busy Sunday around 5 pm. Thankfully we had reservations, otherwise it may have been a bit of a wait. The atmosphere was lively, and the food was solid across the board.

We ordered the calamari, kids cheeseburger, the Smith burger, and the braised short rib mafaldine. Everything was well prepared, with the short rib mafaldine standing out as rich and comforting.

A nice touch was the fresh bread service and the option of house still or sparkling water. Our server was friendly, though service slowed at times due to the crowd.

Overall, The Smith is a reliable choice for good food.

My wife and I had dinner here on Thursday and had a wonderful time. We had great service. Allyne took great care of us during our meal.
Our cocktails were excellent. I had a Whiskey Sour and My wife had the Yozu Gimlet. Both were well-made and perfect.
We started with the oyster sampler and it was fantastic. If you like oysters, you should give it a try.
We shared the ribeye and it was perfectly cooked, flavorful, and very tender.
Dessert was the Sticky Toffee Pudding, which was to-die-for. Rich, but not too sweet, it was a great way to end the meal.
Overall, it was a good experience and well worth the visit.

This feels like the place to go for business dinners and celebration occasions, yet it's comfortable enough for friends to meet or a nice date night.

The food is really good.   It's not a huge menu, but what is served is really good.

We had two vegetarians in our group and each person had something different, and our burger loving friend was super happy.   My husband really loved the muscles...so lots of options for everyone.

The drink menu is extensive a d we all tried something new.  The ladies tried the elegant cocktails, the gentlemen, the whiskeys and bourbon.  Everyone enjoyed their drinks.

I would definitely recommend trying The Smiths the next time you need a great restaurant and a really good cocktail!

After a day at the Mall, we went to The Smith for lunch. We were seated immediately, and our server greeted us as we sat down although it was busy. The sourdough bread was very good. I opted to get the veggie burger which was moist and flavorful. The fries were crisp. My friend had the Vanilla Bean French Toast. I ordered the Cucumber Mule mocktail which was delicious. We went during brunch but would have loved a few more options on the menu. Overall the food, staff and atmosphere were impressive. Definitely recommend.

A solid choice for Korean food. The wings are tasty and the japchae was also very good. Very friendly staff and reasonably priced (for NYC).  A good option if you want a decent but not over the top place

I had a wonderful experience at The Jin. The restaurant is beautiful, the service was amazing, and the fried chicken in the soy garlic sauce was the best fried chicken I've had in a long time. name: Giulietta
document: Giulietta. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars Mediterranean. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
From the team behind La Pecora Bianca, this new restaurant gives coastal Italy vibes with a fun 70s/80s soundtrack.

The food is delicious. The service was outstanding. The restaurant is gorgeous. Whipped ricotta toast, Orecchiette, Rigatoni with vodka sauce, and the spritz's were all fantastic. Now with all that said, having been to La Pecora Bianca a few times, this is nearly the same exact menu (especially when it comes to the pastas).

This is their 2nd day open and they are well staffed and the service and food were top notch!  It’s beautiful inside and the ambience is warm and inviting. I just happened to be walking past and the decor pulled me in. Can’t wait to come back in the spring and summer when it’s warm outside to dine Al fresco. It’s a French Riviera/Italian Coast dream.  I ordered a cocktail, Truffle Pizza, Linguini with Clams and Tagliatelle Bolognese. All 10/10.

Loved the food at Giuetta. I went with my mom and uncle, and we all enjoyed everything. My mom loved the fritto misto, tuna appetizer, and lobster spaghetti. My uncle loved the burrata and New York strip. My favorites were the pizza and ice cream sundae. Great vibe , we sat under the lemon tree.

My wife and I had diner at Giulietta and it was very good. We learned from our waiter that Giulietta has only been open for a couple of weeks. We arrived at 6:30 on a Friday night and were seated immediately, with plenty of seats at the bar and half the restaurant open. The restaurant has a French/Italian Riviera vibe and the menu reflected that. We ordered fried artichokes and meatballs for appetizers, which arrived quickly (almost too quickly). Both tasted great. Our main meals (linguine vongole and tagliatelle bolognese) also arrived quickly, and were very good, although the linguine was very “lemony”. Portions were fine, but smaller than other Italian restaurants we have been to (which was fine for us). For dessert we shared the Lemon Tart and Lemon Sorbet. The tart was more like a lemon meringue pie and less like a tart. All in all, we really enjoyed the service, atmosphere and of course our meals at Giulietta.

Simply excellent! The kale salad was fresh and delicious - I could eat that all day, everyday. The margherita pizza was so good & well balanced. The tagliatelle bolognese was full of flavor and the pasta was cooked to perfection (plus seasoned well!) topped it off with the baci sundae because why not! Also - compliments to the interior designer - I felt transported to a warm sunny beachside location!
Last but not least - the service was top notch. Cody & staff were incredibly attentive. Thank you!

name: Shukette
document: Shukette. cuisine: Middle Eastern. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
The food and service were 🔥!

We celebrated our anniversary at Shukette and had such a memorable experience. From the moment we arrived, the energy in the space was vibrant and welcoming. We were seated at the chef’s counter in the middle of the open kitchen, which made the night feel even more special. Watching the chefs prepare and plate the dishes added an interactive, immersive element that we truly enjoyed.

The food was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully presented. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, and you can really taste the quality of the ingredients. The atmosphere is lively and the playlist was everything!

What truly stood out was how the team acknowledged our anniversary. They surprised us with complimentary sides and desserts, which was such a generous and thoughtful gesture. It made the evening feel personalized and celebratory without being overdone.

Overall, Shukette delivered not just a great meal, but a full experience. We left feeling celebrated and well taken care of. Highly recommend for a special occasion or a fun, energetic night out in NYC.

Highly recommend!

I am a huge fan of Chef Ayesha, so we went for my birthday and had the best time and the best meal!

We were warmly greeted by the hostess and the restaurant manager (who happened to be at the host stand - very professional!). We had a great booth right next to the window, but I wish we had sat at the bar so I could watch Chef in action (next time!).

The meal was delicious, perfect for family-style sharing and noshing! Everything was fantastic, perfectly prepared, and beautifully presented. The flavors are so cool and unique, but also familiar and comforting.

Frena completely won me over from the very first bite. Soft and fluffy on top with a crispy, almost scorched bottom, the texture was incredibly satisfying. The seasoning looks simple, yet somehow it is deeply addictive. The only downside is that it is way too small and disappeared in seconds. I paired it with the labneh dip, which was also excellent. The chili powder sprinkled on top is the true star. It cuts through the richness perfectly and keeps everything from feeling heavy. The presentation is beautiful as well and instantly brightens your mood. The biggest surprise for me was the grilled fish. It carries a subtle Thai inspired touch, with wonderful seasoning and absolutely no fishy taste at all. The dipping sauce is quite spicy but pairs beautifully with the fish and brings everything together.

This was a meal that left me wanting more and I will definitely be back. The place is very popular, so it is best to arrive right around peak dining time or you will most likely have to wait in line.

Every bite = wow. Outstanding is an understatement. The Labneh, frena, ROASTED CAULIFLOWER, joojeh chicken were all amazingly good. The fish in a cage has a great presentation, it’s good, don’t get me wrong, it’s just I’ve had better whole fish. We also love the mic drop aka tahini soft serve, very interesting! And yummm.

Our server Oriella is wonderful, as well as other staffs, they were all super friendly and lovely. I absolutely adore the experience and would totally come back to try more dishes.

We ate at Shukette in Chelsea and even though we were seated in the outdoor section—which wasn’t the most comfortable—the food and service completely made up for it.

The standouts were incredible:

Shakshuka Braised Heirloom Butter Beans — rich, flavorful, and totally unique.

Grass-Fed Shish Kebab — perfectly seasoned and cooked.

Not Your Average Hummus and the Beet Tzatziki — fun, delicious, and definitely not average!

The staff was warm and on point, and the energy of the place is great. The indoor dining room looked amazing, but they were fully booked, so we’ll definitely try again for indoor seating next time.

Great location near the subway, delicious dishes across the board, and genuinely fantastic service. Highly recommend Shukette!

google_reviews.text:
I’ve been to many Korean BBQ spots in New York, but Nubiani is truly the best. From the atmosphere to the quality of the food, everything was exceptional. The banchan was fresh and beautifully prepared, and the meat quality was outstanding. Every dish exceeded my expectations.

If I have family visiting or an important gathering, Nubiani will definitely be my first choice.

A special thank you to our server, Michelle, who was incredibly kind and took the time to explain each item in detail. Her attentiveness made the entire dining experience even more enjoyable. We’ll absolutely be coming back.

Had dinner at Nubiani last weekend  and we loved everything about it. This Korean BBQ spot ranks among the best I’ve been to in the city. Stylish and modern, you can tell right away this isn’t just another Korean BBQ restaurant. Service throughout was exceptional, and we were really well taken care of by our tableside chef. The meat quality was outstanding and the portions were generous. We ordered the small beef set along with an order of pork belly, which we probably didn’t need, but it was really good so no regrets. The banchan was also a highlight, all very refined and full of flavor. All in all, an excellent experience and a place I’m really looking forward to coming back to. One note though: it’s highly recommended to bring cash. It’s not required, but you get a 10% discount if you pay in cash, which is considerable at  a place like this.

My family of four had the Nubiani package, their largest package.  The quality of meat and seasoning is very good.  We could rarely find this good Korean BBQ when we were in Korea.  And the side dishes are creative and good.  The side dishes are a little sweeter than our liking but we understand that Korean restaurants cater to broader tastes, both in U.S. and in Korea.  The portion was more than enough for 4 of us.
We had spicy cold buckwheat noodle, and the doneness of the noodle and the seasoning was very good, too.
The serves were attentive and knowledgeable.  However, they wind down the service after the kitchen closes at ~9:15.
One glitch during our visit was the coat check.  When a busy server retrieved our coat, she did not take off greasy poly gloves.  As a result, there are clearly visible grease stain on our coats.  I hope they could improve the coat retrieval procedure.

Truly a fantastic spot. It’s the best Korean BBQ I’ve tried so far. The lunch menu was excellent as well, and the staff were friendly and very professional. I’d definitely visit more often if it were closer to home.

My first time checking out this location and I’ve gotta say, I definitely prefer it over the K-Town one! The vibes here are way more chill and relaxed. Our server was super attentive and really fun to chat with. We ordered the large beef package, cold noodles, and hamachi. She grilled out meat perfectly and all the flavors hit just right. Plus, our banchan were refilled without us even asking. Loved the whole experience!

Already planning my next visit lol. Highly recommend 💯🍣✨

document: K'Far. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Bagels Middle Eastern. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
A Delightful Morning at K'Far Cafe Philly

I recently stopped by K'Far Cafe in Rittenhouse for a morning bite, and it was absolutely delightful. From the moment I walked in, I was struck by how inviting the space is. The pastel interior, with its bright, airy feel, creates such a warm and cheerful atmosphere.

I ordered the famous Egg and Cheese Jerusalem Bagel, and it did not disappoint. The egg was unbelievably fluffy, like a pillow, and combined with the melty cheese, it created the most perfect, soft texture in every bite. But the real star was the delightful, peppery aftertaste left by the schug. It added an incredible layer of flavor that lingered just long enough to make each bite exciting.

To wash it down, I tried one of their signature coffee drinks, which was perfectly rich and well-balanced. If you're looking for a gorgeous cafe with food that has complex and memorable flavors, K'Far is an absolute must-visit in Philly.

Great stopping in here on a freezing cold day. We got seated right away at the counter which has very cozy seating! We just had coffees, bagels and an apple-cranberry tart. All were great, enjoyed the Jerusalem style bagels and the scallion cream cheese was very good. Wish this was local to me, so many other items on the menu I wanted to try. Looking forward to a future visit!

We had a great breakfast in a freezing place. Each time (and it was often) that the door opens, all the cold weather was flowing into the whole place. I think there are enough solutions to prevent this and have a warmer place. Even the waiters complaining about this. In Philadelphia can't expect a warmer weather during the winter, therefore recommend to take care of this.

The Bagel Sandwich is big. Don’t worry about potion size 😉 It’s perfect. Staff was super friendly when I visited.

I had the egg and cheese sandwich. It’s a little spicy 🌶️ but I like the heat. Would definitely order it again. Coffe was good. The blondie pastry I got was good !

The only grief I had was I was next to the door and there is a lot of foot traffic coming in and out. Which is great for the company but not for the customer. Kept getting blasted with the cold air from outside. Ask for a table in the back or away from the door 🚪

Wish I lived in Philly, specifically across the street so that i can drop by anytime.  First time trying Jerusalem bagels and they were divine. The sticky buns were amazing as well as the rugelach. Actually everything is wonderful. Must visit if visiting Philly.
A little bit of a wait to get seated but there is plenty of seating so the wait was pretty quick.  Even if the wait was an hour it will be well worth the wait.

google_reviews.text:
I honestly wish I could give the service a 6/5, but I will make do with what I got! My fiance and I came here on NYE to do the pre-set menu of house favorites. The place was decorated so cute and they had little party favors everywhere for NYE. When we arrived, we got seated at the bar even though we made a reservation at the back patio on Resy. When I let the manager know, she was so apologetic about the Resy app incorrectly placing guests into the wrong areas of the restaurant and asked us if she could purchase our first round of drinks to make up for it. No problem! So we are eating dinner at the bar and she kept coming up to us after we were done with the cocktails offering us wine, refills, and even a great dessert wine that the bartender recommended with the babka. When I tell you this is some of the best food AND service i’ve ever experienced- what an incredible way to end 2025!!! At the end we expected to pay for the drinks completely and were told they were all on the house. Shocked and on cloud 9, beyond full, we left the restaurant so happy and a little tipsy.

As for the food, obsessed with the hummus and ricotta cheese, as well as the kofta was the best I’ve ever had. Babka was amazing and everything else was so yummy, my fiance never had Israeli food before and was cautiously optimistic going into the dinner I chose, and left saying that was his favorite meal from our NYC trip! name: Taqueria Milear
document: Taqueria Milear. cuisine: Mexican. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Excellent taco spot. Super authentic approach. The service was amazing and incredibly attentive. They have a 10 taco special with a pitcher of drinks for 25$. The pulled pork preparation was very authentic and the handmade tortillas were thick and yellow corn and delicious. The meal was terrific and we’re definitely going back for the Tuesday beer special. 100% recommending for a more authentic taco option.

As soon as you walk into Taqueria Milear, you immediately feel the warmth and the cozy, inviting vibe. I’m genuinely in love with this place — everything tastes homemade because it truly is.

They have amazing weekly specials, too:
•	Happy Hour on Mondays ALL DAY with classic margaritas for only $10 (so good!)
•	Tecate Tuesday, perfect if you love an easy, chilled beer
•	And my absolute favorite: the Carnitas Combo — tender, flavorful pulled pork that hits every time, available any day of the week.

If you’re vegetarian or avoid dairy, the Vegetable Burrito is incredible. It’s hearty, packed with flavor, and wrapped in their house-made corn tortilla, which makes all the difference. Don’t skip the chips it comes with a scoop of guacamole on top of the warm chips. Heaven.

Brunch here is another level:
•	Their chilaquiles are comforting and perfectly seasoned
•	And the eggs with steak is such a satisfying combo

The cocktails are unreal — especially their signature pineapple spicy cocktail. Truly one of the best I’ve had.

Overall, Taqueria Milear is one of those rare spots where everything feels thoughtful, homemade, and delicious. I can’t recommend it enough!

First time I came here was like a year ago, and I’ve always meant to make a review about Milear; so here we go : First of all , Manuel and Ryan provided wonderful service, always anticipating your need before you even asked, once I didn’t know what to order ; Therefore being opened to suggestions; Manuel Suggested the carnitas , and since then I’ve been in love with it and been coming back for more ; in addition to it , their consistency it’s unbelievable top notch food. Come try it out for yourself. Bottom line they’ve succeeded at making carnitas an Unforgettable Delicious experience.

Immediately upon entering the service was so warm and kind. Roberto was so welcoming and you could tell that he was so proud of the food and culture here. The owner even came and said hi to us at one point!

And they have a LOT to be proud of. The homemade tortillas were unlike anything I’ve had before. I’m usually not a fan of carnitas, but the ones they make here are incredible fresh and delicious.

If you’re not hungry, definitely come for the drinks. The spicy chipotle margarita is a whole meal in a drink - SO good. I was only able to get a picture of the drinks but look how beautiful they are! They also have a great happy hour deal where margaritas are $9-10.

Such a great hidden gem in crown heights. Highly recommend for atmosphere, drinks, food and service.
Fantastic place: the carnitas is so good, the margaritas are great too, made with agave syrup, great chips and guac, specials and happy hours (9$ margs during the week). Just a great spot.

google_reviews.text:
Soboku is such a cozy little neighborhood spot and was exactly what we needed on a freezing cold day. Everything we ordered hit. The crab cream korokke was hot, creamy, and perfectly crispy on the outside. The spicy tuna taco was fresh with just the right kick — a great lighter bite in between heavier dishes.

The curry omurice was pure comfort food: rich, savory curry, fluffy egg, and HUGE pieces of fried chicken that were insanely juicy and crunchy. We also got the sesame cucumber, which was refreshing and balanced everything out nicely. The ebi katsu burger was super satisfying, crispy, and slightly sweet, and the katsu on its own was unreal — so crispy and perfectly fried.

Overall, the food was warm, hearty, and incredibly comforting. The kind of meal that leaves you full, happy, and ready for a nap. Can’t wait to come back.

I had such a wonderful experience at Soboku! The moment I walked in, the cozy interior and warm lighting made the place feel so inviting. The rustic brick wall and simple Japanese-inspired decor created the perfect atmosphere for a relaxing meal.

I ordered several dishes, and everything was delicious.
- The Ebi Fry was perfectly crispy with juicy shrimp inside.
- The Katsu Curry was comforting and flavorful , the katsu stayed crispy even with the curry sauce.
- The Croquettes were creamy inside with a beautiful golden crust.
- The Spicy Salmon Crisps were such a fun bite, crunchy base with a creamy, slightly spicy topping.
- The Takoyaki was soft, savory, and topped with plenty of bonito flakes.

This is definitely a spot I would come back to for comforting Japanese fare. Highly recommend if you’re in the area!

Went exploring and found this nice little shop. Some of the best curry I’ve had around New York. The mackerel was great along with the salmon, very flavorful. Their menu had lots of pictures so it really helped to see what’s looks good and matches very well with what we got. They might be understaffed, very busy but was no wait line when we got there.

YUMMMMMMM
Probably the best curry I’ve had in Brooklyn yet. The chicken was crispy and had and good flavor in the breading. The curry was flavorful not plain at all, perfect to combat the wind beating at my window.

The avocado on the crisp was great and refreshing as well. Mashed avocado with a sort of chipotle aioli.

Must return!
Good food in a small setting. Friendly staff and food comes out quickly. The prices are a little high, but the portions are big for their entrees. Brunch is served on the weekends. The curry is good.

google_reviews.text:
The weather was nice today, so I took my dog out for a walk and coffee. Later in the evening I walked into Sukh for dinner without a reservation.

The host and staff were very welcoming and kindly seated both us and my dog inside. I highly recommend the fried chicken wings and the spicy Yum Pla Kapong. For mains, the Leng Zaab, Northern-style Larb, and especially the beef fat fried rice with marinated egg yolk were excellent. I love this so much. We ended the meal with dessert kanom tom with coconut ice cream. It was so good that I had to order another one to take home and The bartender also recommended a drink that paired perfectly with the meal.

This is the great spot in Fulton for dog owners and pets friendly too they even brought water for my dog 🤍

Thanks to the host, server Chase and PP for the warm service. I’ll definitely be back to try more dishes.

Lovely Thai spot in Fort Greene right off the G train. I mention that because the interior is modeled after an old locomotive carriage, it’s cute as hell. Really well executed Thai food with good to great dishes. The steamed branzino custard was delicious and interesting and we really enjoyed the larb nurh. They aren’t joking with the spice warnings FYI. The service is top notch and kept our water full while we labored through the overestimation of our Thai spice tolerance. Overall really enjoyed, Sukh and think it deserves the praise. If your looking for elevated Thai that explores all the region of Thailand, highly recommend Sukh!

Stumbled upon this restaurant through black bird, the ambiance is so adorable it’s almost like you walk into a train! We ordered the samosas and steak fried rice February special. The food is phenomenal, samosas were light and flaky while the steak was tender and seasoned perfectly. The Thai iced tea and pandas mojito mocktail were a nice addition. Will definitely be coming back! Looks like there’s yummy  vegan and gluten free options as well!

Thai on a Train experience, the atmosphere was wonderful and romantic. Lots of 50s songs and jazz playing. Service was amazing and faster than I expected, and the food was exquisite. I ordered the shrimp Kee Maow ($22), Jack's Kiss (limited time drink, $19), and the I-Tim Ruam Mitr (limited time desert, $14). The Kee Maow had the perfect level of heat and complimented the Jack's Kiss (Whiskey+honey+more) perfectly. The coconut ice cream desert is absolutely addicting as well, and I would definitely order it again if I had the money to spare. 10/10, highly recommend, definitely coming back again

Run here, to eat ASAP, you won’t be disappointed.

We went here for my friend’s birthday and coincidentally it was restaurant week. We initially thought of ordering from the regular menu, and we did order a couple things from there but then we decided to give the restaurant week menu a try - we didn’t regret it!
Our waitress was wonderful, the manager was so attentive and the atmosphere was great, it was one of the coldest nights in NYC so it was a little nippy, whenever the door opened (a nice thick curtain by the door might really help with that). That is literally the only complaint that we had, which wasn’t even their fault really because we haven’t had such cold winters in years.

The margaritas were perfect!!

The corn on the cob is truly the best that I’ve had. I used to love getting a pick up order of corn on the cob from Cafe Habana, that will not be happening again. Chela is my go to spot for the Elote from now on!!!

The New shrimp tacos with grilled shrimp were the bomb, all the ingredients complemented each other perfectly.

The meat tacos from the restaurant week menu (not sure what they are on the regular menu) were finger licking good!

The octopus appetizer from restaurant week had a nice kick to it, it refreshed your palette nicely.

The Chela ribs need to be in my belly on a monthly basis!

The Suiza enchiladas were so yummy and sauce was so creamy and on point!

Tres leches is my jam and so happy they had it on the restaurant week menu!
The tamarind Flan was delicious.

All the portions were very generous. We left completely stuffed and extremely satisfied. We plan to go back here to try everything on the menu and then keep on coming back to enjoy all the things that we loved best.

I highly recommend this restaurant for any occasion, big or small, or no reason at all. Come here if you want good food.

They have gluten free and vegetarian options and a kids menu!

Had Chela for lunch today (it was a company lunch) and it was really good. I got the enchiladas mole poblano with brisket and everything was super flavorful.

The mole sauce was rich and had a lot of depth without being too sweet or too heavy. The brisket was tender and paired really well with the sauce. The portion was filling and it definitely tasted like a solid, well-made meal (not just “okay takeout”).

Even though it was packed up for lunch, it still held up really well and tasted great. I’d definitely order this again and I want to come back to try more things on the menu.
Carnitas are a must on Sunday, amazing food every-time. I lost count how many times we’ve been to Chela, always superb service. It’s a gem, the flavors are thoughtfully crafted.

Such a great meal. The staff were wonderful. Brett, the manager went above and beyond to help us make sure we ordered all the right things. I will definitely be coming back to dine here, the next time I’m in Lancaster.

Held a surprise congratulations brunch for my best friend, and the staff at Chela were FANTASTIC. Every person was super cheery, helpful, excited for us, and accommodating. We all got different drinks and we ended up passing our drinks around the table because everyone kept saying "This is so good, you have to try this!" Our dishes were phenomenal and really generously portioned.

Staff brought us complimentary sparkling wine to toast my friend, which was so kind and so fun. (They also brought complimentary triceratops to the kids at a nearby table, so this type of attentive generosity applies to all types of customers!)

Perhaps most importantly: they let us just hang out for a while, sipping our drinks and catching up and laughing, which for Saturday brunch in Brooklyn feels like the height of generosity.

11/10 for Chela, and immense gratitude from me.

name: Cafe Mogador
document: Cafe Mogador. cuisine: Moroccan Breakfast & Brunch Mediterranean. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
I used to come to Café Mogador when I was in college nearby, so returning to the same spot almost 20 years later brought back wonderful memories and emotions. Needless to say, for any restaurant to survive more than two decades in a fast-paced foodie city like New York is no small feat.

The food was excellent then, and it’s still excellent now. The lamb tagine, salmon, and okra were all delicious. For appetizers, the labneh with za’atar, cauliflower, and grilled shrimp are especially tasty. And the baklava is truly to die for—in fact, you might as well order it first. Why not? Live a little.

Great staff, very reasonable prices, and a romantic atmosphere. It definitely deserves a visit from everyone—students, tourists, and old-school New Yorkers alike.

Amazing food, extremely attentive service and charming ambiance. LOVED the cardamom oatmeal and halloumi poached eggs. Dessert was amazing as well! Can’t wait to come back. Also everyone was helpful with accommodating gluten free restrictions 🫶🏻

Cafe Mogador was outstanding. The food was incredibly flavorful and beautifully prepared—everything tasted fresh and thoughtfully made. Service was friendly, attentive, and efficient without feeling rushed. The atmosphere was warm, lively, and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed meal. Easily one of those places that lives up to the hype and is worth coming back to. Highly recommend!

Host is quick & attentive. Servers are sweet & polite. Food portion & presentation is poor. I expected the lamb dish to have more starchy vegetables. All the meats were tender. The lamb taste was an 8/10. The skewers, sausage & salad were a 10/10. The “fresh” nonalcoholic drinks were questionable. Timing was also off from the kitchen (additional salad came 10 minutes later). The price for 2 people was $80 before tip. I would not come here again. Thank you for service.

I fell in love with Moroccan food the first time I ate at Café Mogador. The food is consistently  delicious, and the whole place has that warm, cozy, late-night vibe that I love. My must eats? The lamb shank with stewed apricots and prunes, the sautéed calamari, and for dessert, the knaffeh topped with roasted pistachios and rose water syrup. Reservations are highly recommended, as the restaurant is always bustling. Dinner at Café Mogador? Always a win.
