We ordered the shrimp tempura tacos. Well seasoned and tasty. I do recommend. The Burris tacos were good too. I got the fried rice with a sunny side egg and shrimp and scallOps. I enjoyed it and would order again. The chits do steak was beautiful and delicious as was the tostones. Highly recommend. The dessert was ok. Would order the tiramisu again as it’s housemade. The most beautiful views of nyc.

Making last minute reservations at The Lighthouse for dinner with some friends was such a good choice.
It was such a beautiful experience.
The ambience of this place is divine, the food was amazing and our server Mae was a sweetheart.
The views of Long Island City from the rooftop was just gorgeous.
I will definitely be back here and 100% recommend this spot!

name: Plaka
document: Plaka. cuisine: Greek. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This was the second time dining at Plaka, and my friend and I decided to come try out restaurant week. Between the both of us, we wanted to try the mussels and the dips (The tzatziki is fantastic!) and shared the moussaka and crabcake. Dessert was to die for. Everything exceeded our expectations, including the service! One of the best parts of the meal was having Lynn as the server, she was one of the best servers we’ve had and was attentive, knowledgeable, and personal - we hope to come back soon and have her as our server again!

My bride decided she wanted to check this place out for her birthday dinner and we went with our two daughters.
Parking is easy if the bank across the street is closed.  Nice corner spot for this relatively new addition to the area.  The atmosphere is delightful-> fresh and clean with a bakery section and restaurant/bar section.
Our server was a beautiful young Greek girl, (Ria?)  that was with us every step of the way.  We started with the Octopus, Calamari and Shrimp appetizers.   The presentation was beautiful.  The octopus was delicious, perhaps a bit on the tough side but the garnish was terrific.  We expected more from the calamari.. the breading was too thick for what we have come to expect from true Mediterranean calamari.  The shrimp was to die for with a sauce with whipped feta ! Yum...
The mixed grill entree is enough for three people of you have a couple of apps.  It too was scrumptious.   Then we had a desert there and a the girls wanted a couple to take home.
We had the one there with a sparkler and a Happy Birthday song.   A terrific evening!

This was the best dining experience that I've had in a long time in Baltimore. The food was impeccable! I had the short ribs bechamel with gemelli pasta. It could have fed two people! Generous portions of on beef, so tender and juicy. Usually I find this cut too fatty, but it was perfect! It had the creamiest bechamel sauce that melted well with the juices from the meat. The pasta was perfectly cooked too! They gave a delicious, warm bread basket with rosemary and olive oil when we arrived and it went very well with the haloumi cheese and tomatoes. Excellent wine list along with cocktails. My husband got the crab cake. The chef came by to see how we liked the food, and he shared that the recipe was from G&M. If you know the Baltimore crab cake scene, you know G&M has been the GOAT for a long time, so you won't be disappointed. Packed tight with jumbo lump - enough to please even the snobbiest of crab cake connoisseurs. We were going to skip dessert, but walking out passed a decadent wall of baked goods, we couldn't resist grabbing a few things. The hazelnut cake was so good it almost had me in tears. The baklava Gelato was the star, though. Huge portion and only $3!

The wait staff was friendly, fun, and knowledgeable, providing excellent service. We never had to wait for refills on drinks and the food courses were perfectly paced.

The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, but also felt modern and upscale. You truly felt like you had been transported to the Mediterranean.

Im truly looking forward to returning and trying something new!

Went last night for my birthday and it did not disappoint! The restaurant is beautifully lit, clean and comfortable. The service (I believe our servers name was Priya?) was fantastic. I have severe allergy to alcohol which usually drastically reduces my options because kitchens are not willing or are unable to accommodate but they said they can make anything safe so my parents and shared everything! We loved it all.

We ordered baked feta in phyllo with honey and sesame seeds, calamari with squid ink mayo, lamb chops (they did forget the side but so did we because we were too busy enjoying the rest of the food), seafood linguini and moussaka. Unfortunately we couldn’t try a dessert because we had a cake at home but easily in all of our top 5 favs.

We will DEFINITELY be back, especially for the bakery! Surpassed my birthday dinner dreams.

I was working with Estiatorio Plaka to plan a private dinner event. I do not have much experience but their catering director Antonia (Toni) and the entire team was incredibly patient, kind and professional with all of my questions throughout the process -- Toni really makes sure you are all good to go in terms of venue and food.

The venue itself is gorgeous with a lot of natural lighting even before decorations are all set up. They have two options for rooms upstairs depending on the size of your party. Parking is also free in a nearby lot just across the street. The bakery on the main floor which has a lot of delicious options as well. Highly recommend working with this team to plan a private event, reception, or gathering.

This team genuinely wants to see your events come to life and be successful! I will defnitely be working with them again in the future.

The Juqi Flushing offers great food and cozy atmosphere. The roasted duck is great, especially for a large party. Not only duck meat is served with a wrap, the duck bones can be served in soup or fried rice. All the other dishes are highly recommended, approved by traditional Peking citizen.

Hands down the best Peking duck I’ve had in a long time! The skin was perfectly golden and unbelievably crispy, with that rich, smoky aroma—flavorful without being greasy. The meat was tender and juicy, not dry at all. The pancakes were thin yet soft, and paired perfectly with the scallions, cucumber, and sweet bean sauce. The staff carved the duck tableside with great skill, and the presentation was super clean and impressive. Friendly service, great quality, and totally worth it. Will 100% come back!

document: Marathon Hong Kong Diner. cuisine: Chinese Diners Hong Kong Style Cafe. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Stopped by to try their NEW curry fish balls and they did not disappoint! The texture is perfect — bouncy and firm, just like the ones from the street stalls. The curry sauce is seriously addictive: thick with a little spicy kick that builds as you eat.

If you're a fan of Hong Kong street food, these fish balls are an absolute must-try. Already thinking about when I can go back for another fix!!!

I had an amazing time at Marathon Hong Kong Diner! Their black peppered beef noodles were so flavorful and their noodles were cooked to perfection. The pork cutlet was full of meat and was really good with their curry. The cheese on top was also the perfect combo. I love Hong Kong French Toast and they perfected this dish with the best ratio of bread, condensed milk, and peanut butter inside. I also loved their red bean milk tea. The food was also made so quick! Can’t wait to come back again~

Finally tried HK Marathon Diner and it's legit. The HK-style French toast was perfect — thick, golden, with that melty peanut butter center. Drenched in syrup just like it should be. Paired it with their milk tea: strong, silky, that proper bitter edge. Exactly what you want!

Love the "MADE IN HONG KONG" vibes — left way happier than I arrived. If you're craving authentic cha chaan tang food, this is your spot. Get the French toast and milk tea combo, you won't regret it!

Marathon Hong Kong Diner has become my favorite spot in Long Island City for real Hong Kong–style comfort food. The crispy chicken cutlet and pork cutlet over rice are huge, flavorful, and honestly some of the best in NYC. Their tomato macaroni soup tastes exactly like a classic HK café, and the HK-style milk tea is rich, smooth, and perfectly pulled.

Everything is made fresh, portions are generous, and the quality is consistent every time. I also love the bolo yau (pineapple bun with salted butter) and the French toast — both are must-tries.

If you’re looking for authentic Hong Kong food in LIC, especially inside the neighborhood’s food hall, this place is unbeatable. Marathon HK Diner is bringing true cha chaan teng flavors to NYC, and it’s quickly becoming a local favorite. Highly recommend stopping by!

My HK friends have been raving about their food, so I finally made the trip to check it out. You’ll spot their booth immediately when you walk into LIC Food Hall.

I met the owner, David, who’s born and raised in HK and very passionate about bringing true HK comfort flavors to NYC. A lot of their dishes remind me of Cafe de Coral (大家樂) or Fairwood (大快活), just even better. They exceeded even my high bar for HK food.

To be honest, the prices are higher than the HK cafes in Chinatown, Brooklyn, or Flushing, but you can really taste the difference in the quality of the meat. Since there aren’t any HK cafes in this area, this is a solid, legit option. Please support them! I’ll definitely come back with my HK friends.

The black pepper sauce was delicious, and the fried pork cutlet was tender. The portion was so huge that it was easily enough for two meals.

The pasta was super saucy with a peppery kick, while the sliced beef was tender and well-seasoned.

The 西多士 blew my mind. Crispy on the outside, moist on the inside, and packed with peanut butter. Add butter and condensed milk and it becomes peak comfort food. The pineapple bun with butter was quite pricey for what it was.

Their 紅豆冰 truly reminded me of the afternoon tea sets at Cafe de Coral. Both the milk tea and red bean ice tasted authentic and not too sweet (I did request for less sugar).

name: Marani
document: Marani. cuisine: Mediterranean Kosher Georgian. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
First time coming here yesterday as our friends keep Kosher. I lucked out with street metered parking right in front. There is a parking lot down the street that is fairly inexpensive.

Everything was absolutely delicious. The portions are large. We started with the Marani sampler and bread which was hot and fluffy.  The sampler dips were all flavorful. There is a big cilantro flavor pallet here so be mindful for those who don't like cilantro. We also ordered a version of soup dumplings which were hearty and warmed the soul. The sides were good too-rice, sweet potato fries (thick cut) and fried potatoes and mushrooms.

For entrees we for chicken breast skewers, salmon skewers-both grilled perfectly. Simple seasonings which enriched their natural flavors. We also got the lamb shanks which fell off the bone and did not have a gamey taste to it.

Overall a great dinner. Reservations good for a large group

Wow! Phenomenal restaurant with really unique traditional Georgian cuisine. We tried so many dishes we had never heard of and all of them were delicious! If I could remember the names of the dishes I'd recommend them, but honestly whatever you order you can't go wrong. Everything was served hot & fresh, had lots of flavor, was well spiced, and the portion sizes were very generous. Great service and patient staff as well. Truly an enjoyable experience!
Very delicious, they did a cute birthday thing for my friends birthday. A bit pricey but great vibes.

So I have really mixed views.
The food is absolutely delicious, and for that quality, it is really affordable. I love that.

However, the big issue is the customer service; the workers were talking crap behind our backs in Russian and Georgian, thinking that my group did not understand them, and the food kept arriving with an attitude. Even though we were really respectful and didn’t do anything to deserve that attitude?

The place was extremely noisy. Maybe we were just at the wrong time, but they had many kids running around the tables, pushing and screaming. I’m all for kids as long as they behave. Where were the parents or the manager, and why did I have to enjoy that soundtrack for an hour? I have no idea

But overall, I'm willing to give it another try, as the food was incredibly nostalgic and delicious, especially since I’m from Tbilisi myself

Not our first time visiting this restaurant, and just like prior times it was great. The food, the service, the atmosphere...
For appetizers we had roasted beet arugula salad and kubdari (Imeruli style beef pie), and even though they both are simple dishes, they were delicious. Khinkali were superb, and chashushuli (braised beef with spices) just melted in the mouth.
Monday night and the place is packed, so if you want to get a table you better call or go online and make a reservation.

name: GAN-HOO BBQ
document: GAN-HOO BBQ. cuisine: Barbeque Chinese Japanese. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: As the pescatarian friend would love to see more seafood options (at all KBBQ places) but shrimp was tasty and filling for me. We had just missed the ayce timing and did a la carte which honestly was probably the right move for us (nothing wasted). Service was meh even for DIY; every time we asked for napkins you’d think we were asking for cash…not sure what that’s about. Maybe BYO towel lol. I wouldn’t go out of my way to come here again but I’m also not a meat eater.

Gan Hoo in Flushing delivers consistently delicious food, with bold flavors and generous portions that make every meal satisfying. The dishes taste fresh and well-prepared, and you can tell the kitchen really knows what it’s doing. Whether you’re ordering classic favorites or trying something new, the quality is always impressive.

The one area where the experience falls short is the service. It’s efficient, but very impersonal — more transactional than welcoming. You get your food quickly and everything runs smoothly, but there’s little warmth or engagement from the staff, which takes away from the overall dining experience.

That said, the food alone makes it worth visiting. If you’re looking for great Chinese cuisine and don’t mind the lack of personal touch, Gan Hoo remains a reliable and tasty choice.

The beef combo portion is a good size. The Wagyu fried rice is even better than the one I had in Japan. My kids love the unlimited French fries and chicken nuggets. There’s a reason we still had to wait 20 minutes at 3 p.m. (not even rush hour).

This is one of the BBQ spots I find myself coming back to from time to time. The quality and flavor of the meat are well worth the price. Their watermelon juice and stair platter are must-orders, and there are plenty of other interesting menu items worth trying as well.

Gan Hoo BBQ in Flushing brings the art of Asian grilling to another level, combining Korean, Japanese, and Chinese barbecue techniques in a single, unforgettable experience. The space glows with energy the moment you walk in the sizzle of meat on the grill, the laughter from nearby tables, and the aroma of perfectly marbled wagyu filling the air. Every cut that hits the fire feels like a performance, with flavors that build as the fat melts and the edges char just enough to give that perfect bite. The meats are high quality and beautifully presented, from the delicate wagyu slices to the crowd-favorite “meat staircase,” a showpiece that always draws a few cameras.

It’s one of those places where you go not only to eat, but to experience the rhythm of the meal the sharing, the grilling, the excitement of each plate arriving. The team moves quickly, making sure your grill stays hot and your table full, while the energy in the room keeps the night flowing effortlessly. It’s lively, modern, and unapologetically fun, a perfect spot to come with friends, film a few sizzling shots for your feed, and lose yourself in the flavors.

Gan Hoo BBQ captures what makes New York’s dining scene so special that ability to transport you somewhere completely different while keeping its own bold personality. It’s the kind of place that turns dinner into an experience, where every bite reminds you why food is meant to be shared.

name: Chuan Bistro
document: Chuan Bistro. cuisine: Chinese Coffee & Tea Bubble Tea. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Last night, I had the most wonderful dining experience at Chuan Bistro in Flushing, NY. I came with a group of my dearest friends who truly feel like family to me. I originally made a reservation for 11
guests, but 14 of us ended up arriving. Even though it was a very busy night and the restaurant was completely packed, the staff graciously accommodated the additional three guests and managed to arrange our large table so we could all sit together. That level of hospitality immediately made us feel welcome.

We arrived early so we could take part in one of the most unique parts of the experience — changing into their beautiful traditional Hanfu outfits. The staff was incredibly kind and helpful, and one of our servers even assisted us with getting dressed properly.

From the moment you step inside, the restaurant’s décor transports you. The atmosphere is stunning, authentic, and immersive — it truly felt like we were somewhere in China rather than in Flushing, New York.

The food was excellent and surprisingly affordable. We ordered a wide variety of dishes, and despite ordering quite a lot, every plate was finished! Everything was flavorful, beautifully presented, and perfect for sharing with a big group.

Another highlight of the evening was the traditional dance performances that took place during dinner. The performances added such a fun and engaging cultural element to the evening and made the entire experience even more memorable.

Our servers, Cary and another wonderful lady whose name we unfortunately didn’t catch, were fantastic. They were attentive, efficient, and very friendly throughout the evening, even with how busy the restaurant was.

Overall, it was such a fun, unique, and enjoyable experience for our whole group. Between the immersive décor, delicious food, cultural performances, and excellent service, this is definitely a place I would recommend to anyone looking for something special and different.

I highly recommend Chuan Bistro and will absolutely return again.

Loved my experience here & it has easily became my favorite Chinese restaurant.
-Make reservations!
-multi floor experience
-Great atmosphere & ambience
-immersive experience : A Time travel to the Tang Dynasty
-Sichuan cuisine (flavors of Chengdu) so if you want spice in your life…This is it!
-loved the Hanfu experience (they truly dressed me up so incredibly, I felt like a princess and one of the dancers)
-incredible live performances! Definitely recommend
✨Every dish I tried was delicious—full of flavor and clearly made with care.
-Dry pot cauliflower was delicious
-cumin lamb chops were great
-hot tea for table
-green ice tea was good

-kung Pao chicken was good

I visited this Szechuan restaurant today, and while the interior decor is impressive, the overall experience was very disappointing due to poor service and food quality.
Service Issues:
• Drink Service: We asked for tea and cold water, but they served us "hot plain water" instead. We also requested ice for our Diet Coke, which didn't arrive until we were almost finished with our meal.
• Lack of Communication: We ordered several skewers, but only after finishing almost all our other dishes were we told that skewers are only available after 3:00 PM. This should have been mentioned when we placed the order.
• Missing Utensils: They served the soup but failed to provide any spoons or bowls.
Food Quality:
• Improper Holding Temperature: We sat on the second floor, and it seemed they waited to bring two dishes out at once. Consequently, the surface of the food was cold, and only the center was warm. It clearly sat out for too long before being served.
• Soggy Rice: The white rice was overcooked with too much water, resulting in a mushy texture.
• Flavor/Spice Level: We followed the recommendation to order "Medium Spicy," but it wasn't spicy at all. For a Szechuan restaurant, the heat was very underwhelming.

Absolutely loved this place. The vibes were warm, lively, and welcoming from the moment we walked in. Every dish I tried was delicious—full of flavor and clearly made with care. What truly made the experience unforgettable was the woman who performed a cultural dance during our visit. It added such a beautiful, authentic touch and made the night feel special and meaningful, not just like a meal but an experience. This is the kind of restaurant you leave already planning your next visit. Highly recommend.

Great portion! A bit salty overall for all dishes, but the Chongqing spicy chicken is among the BEST and it is HUGE. Generous. Performance 3 times at night starting at 7PM as of FEB 2026; dinner only I believe. 2 floors. I recommend the 1st floor for seeing performance, but 2nd floor for overall view.

document: Haidilao Hotpot Flushing. cuisine: Hot Pot Chinese. located in Queens. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
It was a fun and festive restaurant with great attentive service. They even gave us hair tie and eyeglass wipes, and scooped the oil from
the soup base during our meal to lessen the grease from cooking. Their dancing noodle performance was interesting and refreshing. They have a good variety of soup, sauce, meat, seafood and vegetable for you to choose from. Our favorite soup base was the spicy pork and bone soup.  The meal also includes a yummy scoop of ice cream cone!  Oh..:they have a cute robot strolling around to
collect plates 🤪

We had a reservation for 11 people on a Saturday at 12:30. We thought we might need two tables with such a large group, but everyone was able to fit into one square table, and even be able to hear each other talk! It's a cool experience for kids because they'll provide a (clean) high chair, a toy, and a kids meal consisting of dino nuggets, fruit, a bun, and a yogurt drink (unclear if we had to pay extra for this or not since I didn't handle the bill). For the adults, we ordered a bunch of items including fatty beef, razor clams, various meat/fish balls, udon, shrimp, kabocha, just to name a few items. My favorite was probably the beef tongue, and the smashed shrimp paste. Love a good freshly-made paste for hot pot. We went with two different broths, but you can pick as many as four. Everything seemed like your standard hot pot items. They did seem to have a few more sauces that other hot pot places, and they have a few cooked items - like spring rolls. We didn't opt for the fresh noodles this time but did catch a glimpse of the noodle dance at other tables.

It's of course pricier than the typical AYCE spot but with Haidilao, you get more unique menu items. It also feels cleaner than other hot pot places. It's like my Mama always says - "What you pay is what you get!"

Came in for my birthday - best dinner I had ever!! Yuna made the experience super amazing. She was attentive, kind, and really considerate. Checked in on us constantly and my family and I really enjoyed our time at haidilao😊🤩❤️ thank you so much!!!! We will definitely be back!! We got the golden and tomato broth, had really amazing flavor and all of the food tasted fresh.

I decided to have my birthday dinner here and it was the best decision! It was made so good because of our server Mengqi! They did a super nice birthday set up when I arrived and also sang me a birthday song! I saw that other servers didn’t really sing the birthday song with as much enthusiasm as Mengqi did, she kept laughing together with me and we had the best time! My husband honestly just informed them in the notes when I was waitlisting, he didn’t call or make very specific arrangements yet they were so well prepared! I’m so thankful and had a great experience! The great service aside, food was also so good! I couldn’t stop drinking the golden soup 😋 What a great birthday dinner! Thank you Mengqi 💖

Shout out to YiFan for such friendly, speedy, & attentive service! This spot never disappoints me & my bf whenever we come. The soup bases are always delicious and the meats are always good quality + fresh. We usually come for the AYCE menu option starting at 9PM which we love especially when we need our protein fix.

Overall, it was a really nice experience. Great food, great service, and definitely worth the hype. Would happily come back.

Elevated Southern Chinese restaurant with traditional interior and an expansive menu.

We ordered the following:

With high ceiling, cherry wood furniture, and touches red floral seating decorations, the atmosphere feels classically Chinese and elevated modern.

This is a great spot for both lunch and dinner, and I recommend coming in a group so you can order and share multiple dishes. Loved the vibe for both a date and a fun outing with friends.

I’ve lived in this neighborhood for a long time and have often heard that the food here is great but the service is terrible. After finally visiting, I can honestly say I don’t think the service is bad,  it’s more accurate to say there is no service at all.
Here’s what I experienced:
* There are no water refills because they leave one bottle of water on the table.
* There is no table check-in  no one comes by to ask how the food is or if everything is okay.
* If you have leftovers, there is no assistance packing your food. They bring you empty containers and you pack it yourself.
* When paying, the tip screen suggests 20%, 22%, and 25%. I genuinely wondered what level of service would justify a 25% tip, given that almost everything is self-service.
That said, there are strong positives:
* The environment is beautiful  it really elevates the experience above a typical neighborhood restaurant.
* The food is excellent.
* The drinks are also excellent.

Overall, it’s a great place for food, drinks, and atmosphere.
Just don’t come expecting traditional table service.

name: Na Rath Restaurant
document: Na Rath Restaurant. cuisine: Thai Buffets. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I recently dined at Na Rath Restaurant in Elmhurst, Queens, and overall it was a memorable experience with a few mixed notes.
The highlights of the meal were definitely the steamed fish and the tom yum soup. The steamed fish was fresh, delicate, and perfectly seasoned — tender and flavorful without being overpowering. The tom yum soup was outstanding: rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced with that signature spicy and tangy kick. Both dishes really showcased authentic flavors and were the stars of the table.
The service was amazing from start to finish. The staff was attentive, friendly, and quick to respond to anything we needed. They made us feel welcome and comfortable throughout the meal. The ambience was also great — clean, cozy, and lively without being too loud, making it a nice spot for both casual dinners and small gatherings.
The only downside was the crab salad. While it tasted fine at the time, I unfortunately felt unwell afterward and experienced some stomach issues. It may have just been an isolated incident, but it’s worth noting.
Overall, Na Rath Restaurant offers delicious dishes, excellent service, and a great atmosphere. I’d definitely return for the steamed fish and tom yum soup, but I might skip the crab salad next time.

As someone who deeply respects Thai cuisine, dining at Na Rath Thai Restaurant was truly special. Every dish was thoughtful and authentic. Knowing the head chef serves the Thai Consulate and has cooked for the King of Thailand’s sister makes this experience unforgettable. Highly recommend.

I had such a great experience at Na Rath Restaurant! The food was absolutely delicious — the larb tuna salad was so fresh and flavorful, and the crying tiger wagyu with garlic fried rice was out of this world! Their mocktail drinks were also really refreshing and tasty. The atmosphere was welcoming, and everything came together for a wonderful dining experience. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to!

3.5

For starters, Chive pancakes, roast veggies, Pad see ew and papaya salad (spicy!) were all ok. Fish cake and Breaded Chicken were dry. Food trays on warmers but don't think they kept them hot enough, like the fried rice which was cold.

Had to ask about the 6 curries - weren't labeled at first. From different regions. Some had proteins like chicken feet, pork, chicken. One was fish but only saw a few pcs of halved fishballs. The peanut curry was slightly sweet and was just the sauce. One was very spicy so just took the veggies and meat.
Instructions were finally posted on how to put together the curries with the noodles and toppings, which were set up on the table as well.
It was a good tasting.

Service was good. Preferred cash payment but accepted credit cards with added 3% fee.
Decor was bright with colorful flowers hanging from ceiling etc. Space is not that big. Restroom available.
Some street cleaning parking and the rest were metered along Whitney Ave.

My husband and our friends are there several nights a week and since I am often out of town, I'd never been, so I was eager to see what the draw is - and it's really simple. Exceptional food, an amazing and friendly team and an atmosphere that makes you feel as if you're eating and drinking with a group of friends, rather than with a restaurant full of strangers. google_reviews.text:
I came across Bistro Éloise while searching for a place nearby, and I’m really glad I did. It’s in a shopping area with plenty of parking, which made things easy. I loved the décor and the lively atmosphere.

The host was friendly and welcoming, and we were seated right away. I was definitely glad I made reservations because the place was packed. Service was a little slow, possibly because they were short-staffed, but it wasn’t a deal breaker. The escargot, French bread, and beef bourguignon were delicious and well worth it.

I’d happily go back.

The place while intimate is also open and airy.  The escargot and beef bourguignon is really good.  The portion sizes are New York sized which is great.  The bread was amazing as well.  We will be back to try the octopus, butternut squash soup, steak and frites,  and creme brulee.  Crowd is a mixture of families, couples, individuals, and friends.  The outdoor area is enclosed so there is room there as well.  For a Monday night the place was hopping so you should make reservations.
Such a cozy restaurant with a warm welcome. Everything we ate was delicious, and the staff's hospitality was outstanding. Can't wait to come back!
I loved everything about this place. The nicest service and most delicious food. Every bite of this delicious forestiere crepe made me more excited for my next visit.

We chose this place to celebrate our 3rd anniversary and, while the food was very good, the overall experience did not fully meet our expectations.

I made a reservation in advance and specifically mentioned that it was a special anniversary night, hoping for a bit of attention to detail. Unfortunately, when we arrived we were seated at a regular table with no special setup or decoration.

Service was slow at the beginning — it took around 10 minutes for someone to approach us, and an additional 10–15 minutes to receive the champagne we had ordered. The server also came across as a bit rude at first, which immediately lowered our expectations for the night.

That said, the food was genuinely good. We ordered the filet mignon, octopus with chorizo, onion soup, and shrimp. Everything tasted great, with the filet mignon being the standout dish of the night.

Overall, the food quality is there, but the service and attention to special occasions need improvement. With better hospitality, this place could easily offer a much better experience.

document: Rolo's. cuisine: Sandwiches New American Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Delicious delicious delicious. I’m so glad we decided to dine here on our trip. The food was phenomenal. I don’t think there is a bad thing on the menu. The tortellini and the lasagna were so good. The fish was fresh and so yummy. The polenta bread with the chili butter was so good and the mortadella was delish as well.

I went there earlier when it first opened and they had their fresh pasta market. But I recently came back for my birthday and was pleasantly surprised on how everything tasted. Definitely get each of the polenta bread as the appetizers are small portion sizes. I had the ravioli pasta dish and it was only like 8 pieces which was disappointing of a portion size. Food was however delicious. They also do not do complimentary dessert.

My best friend and I have been frequenting Rolos since we watched that one video about how their lasagna is made. It's been a special treat when we can manage to get a table (one that's well worth the wait).

The staff here is truly incredible. A lot of restaurants in the city can be condescending and rude, but the entire staff at Rolos is beyond kind and accommodating.

If you're able to snag a res, which we were today, you're in for a real treat. When I put in the res notes that this would be our last dinner together given my leaving NYC, the staff made it truly special!

Standout dishes: chili polenta bread, cheeseburger, skirt steak, and of course, the lasagna!

While we went back and forth about where to have our "last supper" as our server called it, we knew Rolo's was the only right choice. The food is always consistent, outstanding, and a memorable experience.

I couldn't have imagined a better way to close out my NY days. Thank you so much to the Rolos staff for such a considerate, caring, and extraordinary experience.

I highly highly recommend the leafy greens and herb salad, calabrian chili wood fired polenta bread combined with the house made mortadella, two sheet lasagna, and lastly, the littleneck clam pasta. I personally loved the crispy potatoes "war style" but do think the pungent lemongrass dip can be polarizing.
The fluke crudo was so unfresh that it made me lose my usually robust appetite (and taste-wise was very disappointing compared to other crudos), but the server was hospitable and took it off the cheque. The pork t-bone was tasty but not as remarkable as the other dishes.
Rolo's is very ingredient-forward and works with flavors in a unique way.

Minus the fluke crudo, 5/5 dining experience.

Made reservations walked in and was pleasantly surprised..this is a busy establishment reservations are recommended..Natalie who was our waitress was an absolute doll. So informative with a wealth of knowledge about the food. The food hands down was a ten out of ten. We ordered the crispy potatoes for the table, yum and yum. A second order was made immediately don't judge. I ordered the eggs with the polenta bread sooo good.my friend ordered the French toast which was to die for..need I say more. name: Blazin Chicken & Gyro
document: Blazin Chicken & Gyro. cuisine: Halal Chicken Shop Burgers. located in Bronx. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Blazin Chicken & Gyro in Ashburn absolutely exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, the service was welcoming, friendly, and genuinely attentive. You can tell they care about their customers and take pride in what they do.

The food? Incredible. Everything tasted fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The chicken was juicy and tender, the gyro meat was packed with authentic flavor, and the sauces tied everything together beautifully. Every bite was hot, fresh, and made to perfection.

The portions are extremely generous — you definitely get your money’s worth. They don’t cut corners on quality or quantity.

The restaurant itself is clean, organized, and has a great atmosphere. Whether you’re dining in or grabbing takeout, the overall experience is top-tier.

If you’re in Ashburn and craving halal food, this spot is a must-visit. Delicious food, amazing service, big portions, and consistent quality. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Everything here was amazing from the food to the customer service. The chicken platter is very delicious and was filled to the brim. We also tried their lemonade and strawberry/mango drink which was so refreshing. Highly recommend eating here!

We tried the spicy chicken sandwich, but honestly it wasn’t spicy at all. The good part though—it was very fresh and reminded me a lot of the KFC Pakistan style chicken sandwich. I just really wish it had more spice!

The rice mixed platter was fresh and filling as well, but compared to another branch we’ve been to, this one had noticeably fewer toppings.

Now the BEST part—they have a café section with shakes! We tried the Dubai chocolate shake, and if you like Dubai chocolate, you will love this. It was actually really good. It wasn’t super thick or heavy like most shakes; it was more on the milky side, which made it very easy to drink and still full of flavor.

Overall, we would definitely go again. Also, make sure to put in your phone number for rewards!

I had a great experience at Blazin! The food was really good everything tasted fresh and full of flavor. The workers were so nice and kept checking on us to see if we needed anything, which I really appreciated. The place itself is really big and very nice inside.

In my opinion, this is the best location even better than the Tyson’s and Fairfax ones. The overall vibe, the people, and the service just make it the best. I’ll definitely be coming back!
Much needed location after Fairfax best chicken and gyro ! Reasonable prices and best quality of food

This place was absolutely incredible. We will definitely be coming back here. They also have two other locations (which we haven’t been to, but will definitely go to).

First off, stepping into this restaurant was like stepping into an old world restaurant. There’s a really rustic, charming vibe that is absolutely transportive.  We went for dinner in the middle of the week, so we were the old table while we were there, but the staff was so lovely and attentive. They definitely have a lot of pride for the restaurant and food and I get why.

Now on to the food. Wow. The food was amazing and the price was so wildly reasonable. We started with the sausage dip, the pickled pepper, and the sesame baked cheese. The pickled pepper had the perfect bite to it and was a little spicy (think how a banana pepper is spicy) with great flavors for the veggies inside the pepper. The sausage dip was both familiar and interesting and so perfectly delicious. It came with these warm bread roll things that were steaming when we tore them open. The cheese was also nice, especially paired with the bread. We also had the Fli which is kind of like a baked layer pastry dish served with a feta cheese and was so good.

Then we had the fasule with suxhuk. It’s essentially a white bean stew/soup with a type of sausage in it. This was so hearty and comforting. I could eat a bowl of it in front of the fire on a winter day. It was simple with a depth of flavor that was on point. We also had the grilled octopus, which was cooked well and very delicious.

Overall, the meal was an absolute delight and we truly had a great time. Everything from the ambiance to the service to the food to the price point made this place an absolute must visit.

Cka ke Qellu gave us such a beautiful dining experience.

The food was incredible: deeply comforting, homemade, and full of love. Every bite tasted like tradition and care. We shared the meal with a delicious wine from Kosovo, which made the experience even more special.

This is the kind of place you leave with a full heart, not just a full stomach. We’re very grateful for the service, the food, and the beautiful energy. Highly recommended, and we will absolutely return.

Went back with my husband in August and it was a nice break before the Van Gogh show...but the food was gritty and unimpressive. The limeade was tasty. My husband enjoyed his burger. But the service was rushed and he seemed annoyed to be working, ha.

Visiting family in NY and we decided to stop off at the botanical gardens grill. Very disappointing food options. For a place that is meant to attract visitors and tourists of all ages, they really should offer more for all types of people. The atmosphere isn’t all that welcoming or friendly either. Clearly not meant for regular folks. Way over priced!

This was my first time visiting this restaurant, and I’m so glad we chose it for lunch! I came with my husband and was a bit nervous at first—it looked quite packed and I did not have a reservation.

The hostess was incredibly accommodating and managed to seat us at a large table right away. She even apologized for the size of the table, but we actually love to sit side by side, so it worked out perfectly!

We had initially asked to sit at the bar because it looked so cozy and had these beautiful orchids—definitely planning to sit there next time (and yes, this experience has already given me a reason to return!).

I wish I remembered everyone’s names, because every staff member we interacted with—or even observed—was so warm, friendly, and welcoming. The hospitality here is truly unmatched.

The menu had so many tempting options that I had a hard time deciding. I ended up ordering a vegan dish that sounded light and refreshing—but I have to admit, I ended up eating my husband’s cheeseburger and fries instead! It was absolutely delicious—100/10!

Our waiter noticed that I was enjoying my husband’s meal more than mine and kindly offered to bring me another dish, but I was already so happy and content that I didn’t feel the need. To top it off, he offered us cocktails from the bar, which was such a thoughtful gesture.

There also seemed to be a manager walking around constantly to check on guests and staff which I appreciated as going above and beyond. This gem provided a resort-like feel experience. Everything—from the service to the atmosphere—was simply amazing.

I can’t wait to come back!

Overall, I did enjoy myself and would love to give the restaurant another chance because the ambiance and some of the food were great. I just hope the service and cleanliness improve next time.

name: Trattoria Tra di Noi
document: Trattoria Tra di Noi. cuisine: Italian Seafood. located in Bronx. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We go down to Arthur Ave for dinner from time to time and always like to try a new place.
Tonight we decided on Tra Di Noi.
It's on 187th street around the corner from Arthur Ave.
The restaurant is small and cozy and has the old school Italian restaurant  red checkered table cloths.
We were greeted warmly by the hostess and seated at table against the wall in the dining Area. The table had salt, pepper, bread dishes, utensil set ups with a napkin and an olive oil bottle.
A waiter came over and explained the specials to us and took out drink order. The waiter then brought us bread and water to start. They only have beer and wine and I asked for a non alcoholic beer but they don't serve it.
The menu is small but has something for everyone and the specials more than make up for the smaller size menu.
We ordered fried calamari and a mussels special for the appetizers.
The calamari was ok. It was fried a little harder then I like but it was a nice size for 2 people and came with tubes and baby octopus. The Marinara with it was a little bland for my taste.
The mussels in white wine appetizer was fantastic and a great portion.
For the entree we had an order of the pork chop with vinegar peppers specials and a rigatoni special.
Both entrees were delicious and they came with a small plate of fingerling potatoes and string beans that were nicely sauteed with garlic and oil.
We split a piece of homemade Italian cheesecake and I had an espresso and both were absolutely delicious.
The staff was friendly and knowledgeable and attentive. The waiter came by and offered us more bread which a lot of places dont do.

This is a real Italian restaurant owned and operated by real Italians which is something that is hard to come by these days in the Italian restaurant business.
The food is as close to homemade as you can get.
It's not mass produced so you are not going to get heaping portions like you may get in other places but what you do get is a dish that is crafted with care to be as authentic as possible.
The restaurant is quiant and cozy and is staffed by friendly people.
We left the restaurant happy and you will as well.

Delicious and totally legit – I could eat here every day.  The waitstaff are extremely attentive and knowledgeable. The old-school tablecloths and classic tunes create the perfect nostalgic vibe. Easy to hold a conversation, and overall a great experience every time. Whether you’re popping in for a quick lunch or kicking back for a chill dinner, Tra Di Noi always hits the spot. Totally worth it.

Phenomenal, Exquisite, Delicous. The best Veal Limon I have experienced. Traditional home-cooking style meals. Quick service. Quaint but sophisticated. Very friendly staff. 10/10 reccomend this hidden gem.

We had an excellent lunch here, having found our way from the Botanical Garden’s orchid show (Mr Flower Fantastic this year.) We were given a lovely table by the window, and everything that followed was perfect—attentive waiter, interesting specials, good food.

Went here for the first time today to have a leisurely lunch with my parents. We sat by the window, so we got to take in Belmont’s street life while enjoying the best Italian-American food I’ve had since living in NYC. Everything was prepared simply and packed with flavor. The staff was very attentive, and the owners, who were both sitting in the dining room the whole time, were very welcoming.

This restaurant has been on my list to try for a while, and I’m glad I finally had the chance to come. As a Viet living on the East Coast, it’s hard to find truly authentic Vietnamese food. I went the traditional route and ordered the bún bò Huế, egg rolls, and fried tofu stuffed with shrimp.

The bún bò Huế lacked mắm tôm (iykyk), which made the broth pretty bland. The egg rolls were nice and crispy. The star of the meal, though, was definitely the fried tofu.

Definitely a hidden Gem in the Bronx! I haven’t explored much of the menu but the Pho is delicious! I go day’s craving it. I’ve had the wings, they’re very good too. The spring rolls were also so greasy.
Excellent Vegan Pho! Full of veggies! Broth is flavorful but light. Service was pleasant and helpful. We thoroughly enjoyed!

I’ve been coming to this place for a long time, and it used to be my favorite spot for pho and dining in. That’s why I was so disappointed by my recent experience four days ago.

My boyfriend ordered the rib pho, and I ordered the spicy pho. He mentioned that the meat in his bowl was very chewy and dry at the same time, and the broth tasted strange and oily—almost like it wasn’t fresh. I started enjoying my spicy pho at first, but while I was eating, I found a cockroach in my bowl. I immediately stopped eating and felt nauseous after seeing that.

That incident completely ruined the experience for me. It made me question the hygiene and cleanliness of the restaurant. The kitchen area looks very crowded, with everyone packed into one small space, which makes it seem difficult to keep things properly clean and organized.

Sadly, after this experience, I don’t think I’ll be coming back. I didn’t want to say this, but I feel like this place is overrated. There are definitely other pho restaurants that offer better quality and a cleaner environment.

An Unforgettable Vista - The Crown Jewel of Skyline Drive

I've been coming to Shenandoah National Park for years, and I have to say, Single Nob Overlook might just be my favorite stop on the entire Skyline Drive. We visited in mid-October, and the experience was nothing short of magical.

Let's start with the obvious: the view. It is absolutely breathtaking. The overlook provides a vast, panoramic vista that lets your eyes travel for what feels like forever. You're not just looking at a sliver of the valley; you're presented with a grand, sweeping canvas of the Shenandoah. On the day we went, the air was crisp and clear, and we could see the gentle roll of the mountains fading into a soft blue haze in the distance. But the real star of the show was the fall foliage. The valley was an incredible tapestry of color—fiery reds, brilliant oranges, and vibrant yellows, all woven together with the deep greens of the evergreens. It was like looking at a living painting. I must have taken a hundred photos, but none of them truly do it justice. You simply have to see it with your own eyes.

This is more than just a quick photo op; it's a destination. We saw several families with picnic blankets and groups of friends just sitting on the rock wall, chatting and soaking in the scenery. It's a fantastic, easy-access place to bring loved ones. The atmosphere is peaceful and communal, with everyone sharing in the quiet awe of nature's display. It’s the perfect spot to create lasting memories without a strenuous hike.

The drive to get here is also part of the adventure. Winding along Skyline Drive itself is a pleasure, with every turn offering a new, beautiful perspective of the park. The anticipation builds as you pass other overlooks, each lovely in its own right. But when you finally pull into Single Nob, you understand the hype. While there are many overlooks to choose from along the drive, this one truly defines what it means to have a "million-dollar view." It encapsulates the very essence and beauty of Shenandoah.

If you only have time for a few stops, make Single Nob one of them. It is, without a doubt, one of the best.

Today the fall foliage has reached its peak! And this overlook has the best views among the north most overlooks on Skyline Drive that you won't want to miss out! Check out my photos and videos taken from here and you will definitely agree with me!

google_reviews.text: I've always wanted to go to City Island, a far-flung neighborhood of the Bronx that's a schlep from most parts of the rest of the city, especially if you rely on public transport. But we had the opportunity to drive there, and decided to go to CIYC for dinner. The staff were wonderful and welcoming from the moment we called to make a reservation. One wasn't needed, it turned out, but in booking it, we did secure a table with beautiful views of Pelham Bay, and the city on the horizon. The food was wonderful, and we're happy we ordered the new Mac & Cheese recipe the chef tried. We even learned a little about the local life from our server who was a proud "clam digger". The restaurant is open to the public, attire is casual, and parking is available.

City Island Yacht Club is our favorite place to spend time from May to October (during the sailing season). We moved our boat here a few years ago and can't imagine sailing out of any other club. The convenience factor, incredible community of friends and affordability is hard to beat. Nothing better than enjoying sunset and a meal with friends either on your boat or on the club porch, overlooking Manhattan -- it never gets old.

Very nice yacht club, the location is ideally suited for mooring off vessels, with a hauling area, floating style docks, launch service to ferry vessel owners to and from their moored off vessels, restaurant and bar facilities and also young masters training school for young kids to acquire the skill and art of sailing.
Phenomenal, anyone can experience sailboat racing at this club. All age groups and levels of experience. ASA school on the premises as well. #nycsailing

I am a social CIYC  member, and go there frequently to Race on Eagle with Ernie Bivona, who used to be a club commodore few years back.  Club is very well managed and attentive to club members needs, most of the members are "old boys" with years of experience sailing and owning the boats. Dinners after regatas are great, with members commenting on the race and having fun.. Facilities are aged but well maintained and adequate for racers and day racers. Great atmosphere and very friendly club. Great mooring field with easy and protected access. Lots of restaurants on the Island if you need more dining options ( I don't) ,Only complain I haver is commuting from NJ. But I love it.
The restaurant is run by hired outside chefs, this year we have excellent one. Any issues with food are addressed right away and corrected. don't blame CIYC for chef having a bad day, if it repeats he will get replaced.

google_reviews.text: The food was excellent and the service wasn't too far behind! I ordered two thin Crust pizzas:  one was pepperoni and Italian sausage and the other was extra cheese. While in New York, my father in law suggested this place so my wife and I decided to give it a try for Lunch on a Saturday. We were first to arrive and had the restaurant to ourselves. The food was delicious, nice variety of food options from appetizers, to entrees and cocktails. Our server was polite and courteous. Strangely the service overall was slow but when food or drinks were brought to the table, they were delicious.   The skirt streaks were huge and cost about $35 dollars. Grilled chcken with sauce options of teriyaki, garlic were quite tasty. Yuca fries and tostones were crispy. I'd revisit this place if given the chance when back in NY since the food and drinks didn't disappoint. Maybe the kitchen was just having an off day.

I had 3 appetizers and 2 drinks my total was just over 32 dollars so rest assured that this deal is real, no hidden charges or hidden fees/taxes. Just thought it was odd that they accept all cards but you can only tip in cash (maybe this was just my case since I had such a small bill).

Beautiful exterior and very nice modern interior. Bathroom could use a little attention; otherwise, I enjoyed my time here and would definitely come back if in the area. document: Lena Trattoria. cuisine: Pizza Pasta Shops Italian. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: I came here yesterday to celebrate my birthday with my girls and we had such a wonderful time. The atmosphere was beautiful, classy, and the seating was very spacious. From the moment we walked in, we felt welcomed. Our waitress was so kind and patient, taking the time to answer our questions and make sure we were happy. I had the Japanese Kimchi Marinated NY Strip and it was cooked perfectly — I finished my whole plate lol. Overall it was a great experience and I’d recommend bringing around $100 for a nice meal. I’ll definitely be back. 😊

I had a wonderful experience at Lena. The restaurant is very cozy and the food is excellent. I tried the lasagna and it was absolutely delicious. I would definitely recommend it.

What I want to highlight the most is the service from our waitress, Inés. From the very beginning she was incredibly kind, attentive, and professional. She knew the menu very well and was not only there to serve us, but also to guide us with great recommendations.

I was there with my husband and my baby, and she made us feel truly welcomed and comfortable. That level of care makes a big difference. I would happily come back again and again, both for the food and for the wonderful service we received.

I found this restaurant while planning my 34th birthday dinner with my girls, and honestly, I’m so glad I did. Lena Trattoria is one of those hidden gems in the Bronx that gives you a little bit of everything elegance, great vibes, and amazing cocktails. From the moment you walk in, it feels upscale yet comfortable, with a modern, cozy atmosphere that’s perfect for a night out or a special celebration.
Let’s talk about the food everything is beautifully presented and thoughtfully made. One of my favorite appetizers has to be the Polipo, which is their Mediterranean seared octopus. It’s cooked perfectly tender, flavorful, and paired beautifully with its seasonings. The Clams Oreganata are another must-try; they’re so delicious, buttery, and seasoned just right. I also really enjoyed the PEI Mussels, which had that fresh ocean flavor and a nice garlicky touch that I loved.
Now, the cocktails deserve their own spotlight. Lena Trattoria knows how to craft a drink. My personal favorite was the Smoked Old Fashioned it’s bold, smooth, and beautifully presented with that smoky flair that makes you want to record it for your TikTok before even taking a sip.
What I really like about this spot is that it feels like a little piece of luxury right in the Bronx — you don’t have to go downtown to enjoy a sophisticated dining experience. The service was attentive and friendly, and everything came out in perfect timing.
If you’re looking for a modern Italian restaurant that’s perfect for date night, birthdays, or just a good meal with friends, I definitely recommend checking out Lena Trattoria. Whether you go for the cocktails, the seafood, or just the vibes, it’s worth the visit.

This place is amazing. Highly recommend.
I had my wedding reception there and my guests still talk about how wonderful the service, the space and the food were. I’ve had amazing experiences in both restaurant and event services.

We went to Lena Trattoria, an Italian restaurant in the East Tremont section of the Bronx, to celebrate my birthday, and it did not disappoint. The place was packed—nearly every table was booked, with only a few seats available at the bar. The bar area features TVs, and the ambiance throughout the restaurant is dim, cozy, and comfortable. A standout visual is the wood-fired pizza oven on display, along with a beautiful floor-to-ceiling glass wine case. The bathrooms were clean, and they also offer outdoor dining when the weather permits.

The service was top-notch: friendly, attentive, and consistent, with multiple staff members checking in even if they weren’t our assigned server.

The food was outstanding. We ordered the Pollo Scarpariello ($31.20), which featured tender chicken, cherry peppers, crumbled sweet sausage, char-grilled potatoes, and a rich white wine garlic butter sauce—absolutely delicious. We also had the Pollo Marsala ($28.08), served over linguine with a mushroom medley and Marsala wine sauce. The chicken was perfectly tender and juicy, and the sauce was excellent.

I will definitely be back.

The story of Jacob Soul Food Restaurant is a heartwarming tale of community, family dedication, and an immigrant's dream realized in the heart of Harlem.
​The restaurant, located at 373 Malcolm X Blvd (Lenox Avenue), was founded by Rachid Niang, an entrepreneur from Senegal who was educated in France before making Harlem his home. He named the restaurant after his late father, Jacob, and it quickly became a neighborhood favorite after opening in 2009.
​The Great Story: Giving Back on Thanksgiving
​The most enduring story of Jacob's is its commitment to giving back to the community, which started just months after its first location opened.
​Despite being a brand new business, Niang felt compelled to show gratitude to the community that was supporting his dream. On their first Thanksgiving, he opened the doors of his restaurant and invited anyone in Harlem—regular customers and those who couldn't afford a hearty holiday meal—to dine for free.
​This tradition has continued for over a decade. Every Thanksgiving Day, Rachid Niang and his wife, Kim Lum Chan Niang, mobilize dozens of volunteers to serve hundreds of free, traditional holiday and soul food meals. Guests can choose from classic Southern dishes like roast turkey, candied yams, and macaroni and cheese, along with Jacob's everyday Caribbean and soul food favorites.
​The restaurant, known for its buffet-style selection of Southern, Caribbean, and Continental fare, is not just a place to eat; it's a true community hub built on family heritage and a deep connection to Harlem.
​Note on Location: The restaurant you are referring to is located at 373 Lenox Avenue (which is also known as Malcolm X Boulevard) in Harlem, New York, NY 10027.

Imagine a simpler time. You’re at your Italian friend’s grandmother’s house, where dinner is made the slow way because there’s nowhere else to be. It’s a long weekend, time is generous. You’ve already had her signature tipple, the one she still argues about with her doctor, and a little wine she schlepped back from Napoli.
Her Trini friend drops by, bringing family recipes and big energy, sharing stories and food with her adopted New Yorker grandkids (you and your goober friends). This table is everything: cozy, welcoming, eclectic.
You eat a hearty meal. She teaches you how to eat lamb brains, how to get every last bit of meat from the head. When you finish, she tells you she’s proud of you.
Then the bill comes, and some of the magic slips away. You take a little home with you.
This is what the world is supposed to be: a place where people are welcomed in, where differences are shared, and where you leave more open, more curious, more human than when you arrived. There’s plenty for everyone. We just have to learn how to share.

Went to Raval Steakhouse for a birthday dinner and it was a great choice. The space has a dark, warm, intimate vibe that feels upscale but still comfortable. Came for a girls night with 3 of my friends. Phenomenal experience! Valet was available. The ambiance was perfect. It was dimly lit and very lively; every table was filled. The service was spectacular. We loved every dish and every cocktail. Coconut espresso martinis - to dieeee for. Our steaks were cooked to perfection. Honestly right up there with the best steakhouses in Manhattan. We stayed till closing - we were not rushed to leave whatsoever. Thanks for a great night..can’t wait to come back!

Raval is a charming little spot in Staten Island with a warm, romantic atmosphere. It’s on the pricier side, but absolutely worth it. The cocktails were fantastic—especially the coconut mojito, which was perfectly balanced and refreshing. The beet arugula salad was just okay and leaned a bit heavy on the vinaigrette. The filet mignon, however, was insanely tender, and the Wagyu skirt steak was incredibly juicy, paired with truly impeccable fries. We also ordered the creamed spinach and cauliflower as sides—great additions, even if not over-the-top. Overall, a wonderful dining experience and definitely a place we’ll return to. Thank you!

An elevated setting in Staten Island close to ferry and train, and it has a parking lot. We were motivated to try it out during restaurant week. Food was outstanding, especially the shrimp cocktail. Drinks were spectacular. Service was truly top notch. Definitely recommending!! I’m bringing everybody here even though it’s expensive- worth it!!!

If you love a great steak, this is definitely a place to check out. It’s a very cozy and charming spot. I thought it was really interesting that the restaurant was transformed from what used to be a body shop or storage space — they kept the fancy glass garage door, which I believe still opens up in the summertime. Such a cool touch.
You’ll definitely want to make a reservation. The menu is on the pricier side, but that’s pretty standard for a good steakhouse.
We ordered the aged porterhouse for two and the Australian skirt steak. One thing to note (and it’s not just here) — steaks don’t come with sides. We added mashed potatoes, spinach, and onion rings.
The spinach could use some improvement. It was cooked with cheese and a bit of sauce, but once it cooled down it became stiff and not very pleasant to eat. The mashed potatoes were just average. The onion rings, though — highly recommend! You get about four or five large, fluffy rings with sauce on the side. Perfectly crispy outside, slightly sweet inside — absolutely delicious.
I’m not usually a big beef person, but I was honestly impressed. We ordered the steaks medium rare, and they were cooked perfectly. The seasoning was just right, the doneness spot-on, and the meat incredibly tender. The porterhouse for two was definitely the star of the table — honestly, I think it could easily feed three people. The Australian skirt steak was excellent as well.
We also tried the beet and arugula salad, which was just okay. Most of the cheese was stuck to the bottom of the plate, and the dressing was a bit too sour for my taste. I probably wouldn’t order it again.
The staff was friendly, attentive, and provided great service. Some dishes and drinks even come with a little entertaining touch, which makes the experience more fun.
Overall, I’d definitely come back!

Out in plain sight is a hidden gem: Seabass Taverna. There you will feast on a wide variety of Mediterranean fare in a veritable smorgasbord that will leave you sated and satisfied. The abundance of food may well surprise you.

The feast is found in the family style meal, called the endless menu, and it’s a tremendous value, especially these days. Arrive hungry to savor each morsel, and there will be many.

The dishes arrive successively, and both the timing and the chef’s selections are just right. You needn’t do much thinking — let the chef do that for you, though you can ask for substitutes where desired (I am allergic to shrimp and swapped that for more of the hearty Greek salad).

You choose your fish, and I’ve found the branzino perfect every time, hot, seasoned, not too thick.

For dessert, you have your pick. My wife and I have leaned into the cheesecake and strawberry crème brûlée, though we probably should try some of the appealing Mediterranean selections on the menu, too.

The staff is lovely, quite attentive and welcoming, aiming to create a delectable dining experience from the moment you arrive. Their effort is a resounding success.

Everyone now and then you find a place that goes above and beyond. This is it. I visited Staten Island and stopped by here craving Greek food. They have a small parking lot that fits 4 cars and was a tight squeeze but the waiter literally came outside and helped me park my car. The inside is nice clean and has a great vibe/ambiance. I ordered cold apps. Eggplant salad and wild sea bass marine. Absolutely delicious. The seabass especially. Eggplant salad reminded me of home. Very good with the bread. Then I got the baby lamb chops and a gGenlivet double on the rocks. The pour was generous and the baby lamb chops are worth starting a war for. They may have invaded Troy for Helen but I would have invaded for these lamb chops. Thank you very much for such a pleasant experience while I was in Staten Island. You truly completed my day.

2026.01 sit in is definitely better, nice staff, appetizer is hot and fresh, fried calamari and oyster Rockefeller.  Lemon cod is fresh for sure and delicious .  Fried red snapper is a bit dry, hanger steak is a bit salty, seafood has good presentation, above average.  Dessert is really good, strawberry Creme brûlée, chocolate soufflés, and halva (to me it is a bit sweet).  Overall worth a five now.

2025.12 take out, sampler and a pasta.  Pasta lot of seafood, small portions of pasta, sampler has corn veggies, 1 fish fillet, clam, shrimp, etc.  we are sure sit in will taste a lot better, price so so

Since it opened, we’d been meaning to try Seabass Taverna—and it was a good idea.
The restaurant has a nice, authentic Greek feel. It’s a good spot for a relaxed, family-style meal in a comfortable setting. The staff were attentive and caring, but not pushy—which I appreciate.
We were served small bites of pita with a vegetable spread to start as a complement. For an appetizer, we ordered the fried saganaki. It came out with a small flame presentation. The cheese was crispy on the outside, firm inside (not overly soft like mozzarella), not too salty, and enjoyable with the side sauce.
We shared three main dishes. The Spanish seafood paella was a bit too watery for my taste and lacked flavor. However, the whole fried red snapper was fresh, crispy, and tender, as well as grilled octopus. I would recommend both. Each main dish came with a simple side that complemented the plate without overpowering it.
Overall, it was a good experience. They have a nice selection of drinks and cocktails, and we were served with a complementary small shot of Porto at the end of the meal.
Having traveled in Greece, I can honestly say this dinner brought back memories of eating in local tavernas there. It really felt authentic.
Definitely a great spot for a casual, heartwarming lunch or dinner with friends and family.

We dined at Seabass Taverna for their Thanksgiving pre-fixe menu. We had a large party of 14 people with impeccable service. The waitstaff were accommodating, patient, and efficient with taking all of our orders in a timely manner.

The seafood and steak dishes were cooked to perfection for a reasonable price. I highly recommend trying this restaurant!

google_reviews.text: My daughter and I ate tonight 2/18/26 as my Birthday dinner. We started with crab cakes which were good and French Onion soup which my daughter said was delicious.  For main course we had the  Tomahawk Steak special for 2 with mashed potato, brussel sprouts with bacon OMG  everything was delicious. No need for butter or sauces the steak was a star on its own. Service was outstanding and pleasurable. We ended the meal with the seasonal fruit crisp which was granny smith apples it was delicious only issue we had the apple skin was still on the apples which was cut very thin so the peel kind of was leathery. This place is a true old fashion steak restaurant. Highly recommend.

Stopped into the West Shore Inn during the week and it felt like one of those places you instantly know is a neighborhood staple. The bar was busy, mostly regulars, and had a great laid-back vibe.

I had the porterhouse for one and it was outstanding—cooked perfectly and full of flavor. My girlfriend ordered the cowboy steak, which was also very good, just a touch under her preferred temp (and honestly, that one’s on us for not asking for a little more fire).

I went here for Valentine’s day and I am so glad I did. The food was incredible. The porterhouse was cooked perfectly. It had so much flavor and was very juicy. We also got the volcanic steak tips, mashed potatoes, mac and cheese, onion rings, and garlic bread. Everything was so delicious. The service was great as well. Outstanding!! Brought a friend who went to culinary school before becoming a NYC Fireman, he’d never been to West Shore Inn and he LOVED it! He’s an amazing cook; he knows good food. I never had a bad meal or service here… i also ordered a Cosmopolitan and it was delicious. Sometimes it’s difficult to find a bartender who can make it properly and it was soooo good. Amazing!!!! Service was quick and always with a smile, and when it came to paying they were very accommodating as due to not being from the US they explained how the service charge/tipping worked.

Was so good we went twice in one week during our stay in New York.

Server was great, he sounded confident in all he was talking about and asked us questions to base on what he needed to tell us about. The "have you been here before" Question servers ask always feel awkward but our server did well in letting us know more info and went through it fast enough to not bother us. He gave us plenty of time to catch up and food came out in good timing. The sushi and short ribs were very good. My  boyfriend and I dined at Tommy’s Tavern and had an amazing experience. Our server, Cyanna, was absolutely wonderful—so sweet, attentive, and friendly. The drinks she suggested were fantastic, and the manager, Eduardo, was also very friendly and helpful, stopping by our table to ensure we were comfortable. I highly recommend it!
A beautiful and cozy place, very friendly and responsible staff, delicious food, and affordable prices. Special thanks for the fantastic birthday greetings for my son and the delicious pizza :) (From a table of 10 people:))

name: Siam Thai
document: Siam Thai. cuisine: Thai. located in Staten_Island. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Named best Thai in DC which is true, but there’s a lot of factors that make me want to choose a different place.

Food: even though it tastes great, I have noticed the quality has steadily decreased. The worst thing I’ve had was the Tom Kha soup. The most lime I have ever tasted in a broth, and I eat ceviche all the time. It was hard to eat, I couldn’t even finish the small serving.

Price: adding chicken as a protein costs 7 additional dollars…eating here is very pricey. My boyfriend and I alone will end up paying $80-$100 for one outing (appetizer, drink, 2 entrees). And they automatically include 20% gratuity on your bill.

Service: because the gratuity is already included, I’ve noticed service quality has gone down. Particularly from one individual. I believe she’s the daughter of this family-owned restaurant. She works almost all the time and has a very bland attitude towards serving. All other servers have been very pleasant.

Atmosphere: sitting outside is terrible, as you will get attacked by mosquitos (that will also come into the restaurant). Sitting inside is a little cramped. Worst thing that happened was a pipe burst in the ceiling in the middle of peak hours.

Nice to try once, but wouldn’t recommend as a repeat spot.

Warming up with hot and spicy food on a chilly day in DC. I got the lunch special with hot tea, tom yum mushroom soup (spicy level 5) and drunken noodles with chicken (spicy level 3). Both dishes tasted wonderful in flavors and heat!  🌶️ They don’t do spice tray anymore, but you can request mini seasonings like chili flakes, vinegar with peppers, or fish sauce.  I’ll def visit again for my next DC trip!  Aroi mak!

Cozy spot at the corner of the street. I stopped by for lunch and ended up enjoying tom yam mushroom while looking out the door and watching the snow trickle down. Their lunch special $18 for appetizer, entree and a drink is ideal for a sit down meal. I couldn’t finish everything and packed it up so I can enjoy it at home!

Visiting DC during Labor Day weekend and I had to stop in at The Siam House located on Connecticut Avenue in Cleveland Park. If you’re looking for a tasty meal in a great location, then Siam House is the place for you. I had the Tom Yum Noodle Soup with fried tofu. It has a zesty lemony flavor that deliciously complements hints of cilantro and spices. It was literally good to the last drop!  I finished my meal off with the Mango Sticky Rice which blends sweet mango with a rich coconut cream sauce sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds. Absolutely, divine. Keep in mind this is a seasonal dessert so don’t stay away too long if you want to partake. Overall, this is a fantastic restaurant for the family, friends, couples and anyone else that loves good Thai cuisine.

Siam House is the best Thai food in all of D.C. Every single time I go, the food is always up to par with the food I used to have in Thailand. Samantha and the rest of the staff are always so welcoming and warm when you go in and make you feel like you're eating at home in a loving community. The heaven pork is a dish I always recommend to whoever I bring, its so crispy and full of flavor it really does taste like you are having a bite of heaven. I have also loved the yellow curry with chicken as well as the Tom Yum soup. This establishment is definitely a place I have added to my frequently visits list and highly recommend anyone who hasn't been to go.

name: Pho 60
document: Pho 60. cuisine: Vietnamese. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I was seated immediately at around eight as just one person. The ambiance is bright and cozy. The service was pretty decent, and the pork rolls were good. The beef slices over white rice were thin and crispy, but they are overly salty.

Overall it was a good experience and worth a visit or few, but I don’t think I would return regularly! I might try out some other things on the menu some other day though. The dipping sauce was also subpar.

genuinely surprised, what is this Vietnamese restaurant that popped up in the neighborhood and also chained out to Staten Island, has a lot of interesting flavors representing the classic Vietnamese dishes that they serve, which include the ban cuon, bun bo hue, and pho dac biet, also ca phe sua da, but overall flavors are actually good and it's a great value as well. so will add this to my repertoire, fair warning. it's a lot of food so better off sharing if you can. tips, for bun bo hue it can get spicy so avoid adding too many jalapenos, I do respect that they provide different condiments between the bun bo hue and pho and the meat is really tender for both dishes, and the ban cuon is like a banh xeo without doing the additional work and it has that crisp and flavor, in the iced coffee is satisfying and huge

This is comfy Viet restaurant for me in NYC. Most authentic Viet restaurant around 8 avenue area. I’ve been going since 2018, and witnessed through many recipe changes. I gotta say, the soft shell crab 🦀 for the Bánh Canh Cua is really top notch 🫡 I wish they change back to the more chewy tapioca noodle though.

The BBH and the Bò lúc lắc here is also very good. Definitely their top 3 must try here imo. Plus the flan 🍮 the broken rice and rice crepe is okay, I only get them if I’m really craving (rice is not broken rice, rice crepe is a bit thick), but overall still very good 👍🏻

Pho 60 offers a solid Vietnamese takeout experience with thoughtful touches. The grilled beef roll with angel hair was familiar and satisfying, though not particularly standout. The Banh Khot, however, was a pleasant surprise—crispy, flavorful, and a rarity on most menus. What sets Pho 60 apart is the inclusion of all the classic accompaniments, especially the rice paper, which I always appreciate. A dependable spot with a few unexpected delights.

One of the most delicious pho broth I ever had. The grilled porkchop was juicy and freshly cooked.  I could tell they are popular too because the takeouts and food delivery men were consistently coming in.I highly recommend this place when craving for vietnamese cuisine when in the area!
