name: Pastavino
document: Pastavino. cuisine: Italian Wine Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Pastavino offers an energetic atmosphere, excellent service, authentic Italian dishes, and a good selection of drinks and wines. The prices are a bit high for Staten Island and for its distant location and challenging parking (there’s plenty but in a graveled lot, or via valet), yet that is the price for the many good things Pastavino has to offer.

You can quickly detect that the restaurant will move your meal along at a quick, although not too quick pace. I sensed they might do that when I saw a notice from the restaurant about the 90 minute limit for a two person table. I prefer it to be speedy so that’s OK with me. It is worse if it moved too slowly.

Many Staff members will be there to assist your meal along the way, seemingly well trained to pick up a dish, pour you some water, or tend to anything you might need.

The bread is fresh and crispy, and take a look at my photo of the olive oil – – green as olive oil should be. Burn your throat as it should – – perfect!

The pasta – – fresh – – is served hot as pasta should be. Perfect.

The desserts are pricey and though my wife and I got two desserts we probably would shift to one next time since, though good, we probably didn’t need to spend $40 (all in) for them. The gelato is really excellent by the way.

So keep Pastavino in your list of Italian restaurants to go to on Staten Island, even as you stick with your regulars for proximity and value.

We always enjoy our dinners at Pastavino!!
The food is always amazing and the service couldn’t be better. It’s always our favorite spot to celebrate our special occasions. We chose to celebrate Valentines Day dinner on Thursday and ordered  2 appetizers-Big Vic’s Meatballs, the fried calamari. For dinner we chose Linguini Vongole and the Pollo Alla Parmigiano. Everything was delicious. For desert we enjoyed the decadent Torta Di Nutella.
Already looking forward to our next visit!!!

5 stars for customer service, atmosphere and gluten free pasta quality!

This is my third time visiting Pastavino and it never fails to impress. The GF pasta is house made and they only charge $2 extra for it, which is extremely reasonable considering other local restaurants charge a lot more than that for premade GF pasta. The GF pasta is just the right texture, density and flavor.

The restaurant itself is beautiful and unique to the cookie cutter Italian decor you see around Staten Island. It is also adjacent to the water so has great views.

The employees were extremely attentive and hospitable and although it looks and feels like an upscale restaurant, the service made you feel comfortable, relaxed and at ease. Eg. I did not finish my salad and a manager immediately came over and asked what was wrong with it (nothing was, it was just a little lemony for my preference). I guarantee if I had any complaints they would have fixed it immediately.

Highly recommend I definitely plan on returning.

I ordered the Caesar salad to start and it was fresh, crisp, and perfectly dressed... not overdressed, not bland, just balanced the way it should be. It was completely different than any other ceaser salad I've had.

For my main, I had the eggplant with pasta in vodka sauce, and it was outstanding.

The eggplant was cooked perfectly — tender but not soggy — and the vodka sauce was rich, creamy, and full of flavor without being heavy.

The service was just as impressive as the food.

Attentive without hovering, friendly without being forced. Everything came out at the right pace, and you could tell they actually care about the experience.

The atmosphere was calm, clean, and relaxing... the kind of place where you can actually enjoy your meal and conversation without feeling rushed.

I’ll absolutely be back.

Highly recommend.

This was our third dining experience at Pastavino.  It did not disappoint.  Service is attentive without being overwhelming.  My salmon dish was superb.  My partner said his pasta with clams was the best he ever had. Salad was more than enough for two!   It is easy to see why they have a great rep.

Having loved this place for years, telling all my friends how good this place is and urging them to come, although it had only three square tables and a few window seats, at least I respected the old Malvern Buttery - they seemed to care about their pastries. The customers waited for a long time without seats, at least the customers were equally ignored - none was labeled.

Suddenly, either you changed your owner or your owner became ambitious - renovation, new menu and a whole lot more customers. New store opened in Ardmore. One is being prepared in Bryn Mawr. Nice, isn’t it?

Now things become interesting. Your new business move is to label your customers. As a loyal “laptop” customer, I am not welcomed anymore. Oh, “it’s just from 8am to 2pm”. You are pretending that you care about one group while casting out the other. What a beautiful business move. Ah, “back end of the coffee bar” - you mean the 3-4 seats at the doors of the restrooms?it makes me think of the old days when black passengers were only allowed at the back of a bus.

One day I was sitting at the big table, new customers came and squeezed in, what a magical moment! People started to talk to each other and I’ve heard strangers having long and meaningful conversations. I was thinking, wow, this is what a local pastry shop should look like - but now, seeing your new policy, I could only laugh at the naive me.

My advice? Mind your pastries. Let the customers figure out their seats. Then you are still the old good 4.8/5.0 Malvern Buttery not the new fancy Buttery - Malvern.

Don’t be so stupid to group your customers and treat them differently. Laptop users do buy food. Besides discrimination, there are many more better ways such as imposing a universal two-hour time limit for each order - if customers want to stay longer? They order more.

PS: one more thing I hated post-renovation is that you stopped making the coffee chocolate scone.

I can’t wait to come back and try the other menu items.

Now, for reference, I tip every time I’m here. I like to support small business. But TAKING the tip yourself out of someone’s change? It is egregious. Absolutely shameless. It’s unfortunate, because I really liked this place too.

I have no idea what maneuvering could've been happening in that tablet that was more important than the line of 10-15 guests building up in front of that hostess. My advice to her would be to look up every 60-90 seconds to greet people and help them get a table.

Finally, the restrooms could've used some tlc. The soap dispensers were nearly empty and one of the stalls had zero toilet tissue. This was at 7 PM, so they may want to have staff check them mid rush. Easier said than done, I know.

Short of those two things, the experience was great. Again, our server Amanda made the situation better through her diligent service with a smile.

We would visit again. 😊

This location in Fairfax actually seemed to have more selections of food than the one in Falls Church. Maybe we just came at a time when they had new things on the menu. The apple mango soju mule was really good. Dale was very friendly and charismatic. We wouldn’t have known this location was here because we never paid attention to the sign from the street. They should maybe put the sign in a more noticeable place. Other than that, loved it 🥰

For my first time having this experience , I would definitely come back. Awesome experience! Dale was our server and he was amazing. Actually, that’s an understatement. Extremely professional, personable and knowledgeable on his recommendations. Give that man a raise! (Lol) I enjoyed every part of it. The sauce selections and buffet was a great add on to this buffet. Ice cream was the cherry on top. Every worker was polite and working hard. Didn’t see one slacker. The music was even good (lol) Love love love this place. You’ll be seeing me again.

This spot offered a wider selection of meats compared to other Korean BBQ places I’ve been to, which was a nice plus. They also allow a 2-hour dining limit instead of the usual 90 minutes, so the experience felt more relaxed. Ordering was super convenient thanks to the tablet at the table. Once we submitted our selections, the food arrived within about five minutes, making it easy to pace the meal and keep the grilling going.

We stuck with the barbecue option, though they do require the entire table to choose hot pot if anyone opts for it, which seems pretty standard for places that offer both. Our server and the rest of the team were friendly, attentive, and quick to refill drinks, clear plates, and help with cooking the meat.

Every so often, they do a birthday celebration where the servers sing loudly and bring out a cake. It’s fun if you’re into that kind of energy, but it can be a bit loud or distracting if you’re not.

Overall, we had a good experience and enjoyed our time here.

document: HKS KITCHEN. cuisine: Hong Kong Style Cafe Chinese Japanese. located in Staten_Island. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: finally an authentic cantonese restaurant in staten island! they have a great menu of items with classic cantonese dishes. came for brunch and they had all of my family’s favorites. the hong kong milk tea is a must try and they also make it the traditional way!

My favorite local Hong Kong style restaurant. The food is always very good never over oily execution is always five stars. Most importantly it tastes amazing and the owners are always very friendly. Fried rice is smoky and superb wok skills are definitely present, fried fish with tofu and brown sauce is just wow.

The food is mostly pretty good but nothing spectacular. Now, I’m not sure if that is because I’m not into Hong Kong style cuisine or if the place is just okay. This was first time trying this cuisine.

Coming here on a rainy day is definitely a vibe.

The design and decor of the entire restaurant is unique, lots of popular musicians from Hong Kong and other posters all over the walls. The front counter is also decorated very nicely, with different items that make you feel as if you're really in Hong Kong.

There's a decent amount of seating, and the restaurant is very clean.

The staff is kind and considerate, and brought out the food very quickly from the time of ordering.

My personal favorite dishes were the beef chow fun and hot and sour soup. I paired it with a HK style iced milk tea and found it really complimented my food.

I tried the salmon rice ball, however, it was too over stuffed with rice and fell apart in my hand. I like that it was big and all, but I would've preferred it if it didn't fall apart while I was trying to eat it.

I felt the pricing vs the portion was okay... The food was very good, but paying $12 for half a plate worth of food felt unreasonable. I've tried HK style restaurants in Brooklyn, and I paid far less for twice the amount of food, so much in fact, that I couldn't finish it all, and had enough to bring home for leftovers. I feel if the prices matched the amount of portion you get, then sure, $12 would make sense. But not for half a plate of food ...

Overall, I found my first time experience quite enjoyable, but I think I will continue to travel to Brooklyn for HK style food in the near future.

Some of the best Chinese I have had on Staten Island. Hong Kong style food I would 1000% recommend. The food has flavor and spice. Not to mention the super sweet owner who I would give a million star rating to if I could. You must try to stir fry Hong Kong style and the French toast. I will be coming back. Thanks for your great food and service!

name: Lakruwana Restaurant
document: Lakruwana Restaurant. cuisine: Sri Lankan. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This is such a beautiful place with amazing traditional Sri Lankan décor that makes the dining experience feel special. The atmosphere is warm and unique.

I had the lumpice and kiri pani, and both were superb. The lumpice was very flavorful, not too spicy, and wrapped perfectly in a banana leaf. Everything tasted fresh and authentic. The kiri pani was creamy and lightly sweet, a perfect dessert.

Highly recommend Lakruwana if you want authentic Sri Lankan food in NYC

When I first saw the exterior of this restaurant, I was absolutely intrigued. The ornate carvings, majestic statues, and shimmering golden doors beckoned me to come in. The place was crowded and everyone seemed to be enjoying their meal.

Upon being seated in one of the elaborate chairs, I had to pause and take in the visual feast around me. The cozy interior was adorned with 360 degree of stunning ornate collectibles from Sri Lanka, exquisite tchotchkes adorning the walls and hanging from the ceilings, creating a continuous visual stimulus.

The hostess greeted me and explained that I could either scan the menu code or enjoy the wonderful lunch buffet for $21. (Since I visited during the weekend lunch hour, I'm unsure if the price changes at other times.) Noticing that everyone else was enjoying the buffet, I decided to follow suit, and I'm so glad I did.

I'm a huge fan of Sri Lankan cuisine, and the buffet was a delight. They have hot entrées in shallow cauldrons that are constantly being refilled. The spread consisted of many vegetarian delights alongside a few meat entrées, such as deviled chicken and pork curry. My personal favorites were the eggplant, dal lentils, and the kale and coconut salad. Their papadam was light and delicious, so definitely don't skip those! Along another wall, the dessert station featured sago, chocolate, caramel, mango, and gooseberry puddings. The latter two were my absolute favorites.
A pleasant Sri Lankan authentic spot on staten island.  Nicely decorated with delicious food and pleasant service. I suggest to visit. Enjoy!

An amazing exotic atmosphere adds to your dining experience. Food is presented well and almost like eating art. Friendly staff. It would have been better if the waitress could have explained the dishes. As a 1st time , it was tasty and well presented. I’d like to try the buffet to be able to experience a variety of options.

We had a great time here! We went for the buffet and got to try a bunch of different dishes — everything was super tasty. The coconut curry was definitely a highlight, so flavorful and comforting. Prices were really reasonable too, especially for the variety you get. Plus, the interior is beautiful — cozy, stylish, and full of character. We’ll definitely be coming back!

document: Chang Noi Thai. cuisine: Thai. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: AMAZING FOOD. 10/10 come here if you’re visiting Staten Island. Preston the bartender was so so nice made a delicious lychee martini and gave us great food recommendations. We got the beef pad Thai, curry puffs, the bean curd w/sticky rice. We left so stuffed and happy. The pad Thai “medium spice” is some serious spice so I recommend getting the chili oil on the side and that way you can control how spicy you want it. Genuinely such a great atmosphere and the decor is really cute too.

This Gem in St. George area of Staten Island (up the block from the ferry)  satisfied, we came for lunch on a Sunday (which they close fairly early like 5 but didn’t rush us. They have a seating and to go side. The decor is beautiful all wood with traditional Thailand carving. We ordered the vegetable dumpling which were tasty and the calamari which were thick but good. My friend and I shared a mean with sticky coconut rice (loved) garlic shrimp and veggies which was delicious. We will be back for more.

Very nice place to grab lunch in the area. They allow you to mix and match apps and entrees. Fried shrimp rolls were very good, but the Nam pla is a bit sweet. Curry has a lot of veggies in it, rather than chili, but it still tastes good. They adjusted authentic flavors for local diets and ingredient availability, I think.
Decor is very nice and lends to a feeling of a house built with wood from a jungle. Be careful with your step upon entering.
Staff are very friendly and quick to take orders and clear dirty plates. The kitchen is working very fast and quick.
Overall, a good introduction to Thai food!

Last night my fiancé and I headed to a show at the St. George Theatre in Staten Island and decided to take a stroll around the neighborhood to find a spot for dinner. We came across Chang Noi Thai and decided to give it a try — and we’re so glad we did!

From the moment we walked in, the bartender and our server were incredibly kind and welcoming. The restaurant was spotless, the atmosphere was cozy, and the food was absolutely delicious.

We were beyond pleased with our experience and will definitely be back the next time we’re in Staten Island. Highly recommend if you’re catching a show nearby!

I don’t like to write unfavorable reviews but as someone who has been eating there for years I think it’s time I write something. I really use to love this place. Honestly it had the best Thai food on the island and affordable! I tried to order on line for a pad Thai with chicken (no extra chicken which is a thing now apparently), and a basil chicken (no extra chicken), plus driver fee, plus taxes, plus tip was about $60!!! So I decided to order directly from them and it came out to the about the same. A few dollars less. We were hungry and exhausted from flying and thought this would be the best option despite the money. The food wasn’t its usual amazing taste instead it was oily/bland and the chicken didn’t really exist on either plate so I guess you have to order the extra chicken for $3 more per plate. Look I know prices have gotten higher and places are trying to conserve their portions but I can’t consider this place for my go to take out anymore. It’s too high of a risk to pay for and not know if it’s going to be good anymore. This was the second time I’ve eaten it within a few months and the quality isn’t what it use to be. Maybe I keep getting bad nights but it’s still not worth the price tag for take out. Hope things change.

I especially recommend the thick cut bacon. Pricing was definitely reasonable for the quality of the food. I would highly recommend this place!

If steakhouses had a hall of fame, this place would already have a gold-plated ribeye bust out front.
From the moment you walk in, you know you’re about to make excellent life decisions. The vibe is classy but not “I need a tie,” the service is confident without hovering, and the smell alone should be illegal without a warning label.
The ribs were perfection!!!
Let’s just say my knife did less work than I did chewing gum as a kid. Perfectly cooked, seasoned like the chef knows your ancestors, and so tender it basically apologized before melting in my mouth.

Sides are not “afterthoughts” here — they’re supporting actors stealing the scene. Everything arrived hot, fresh, and clearly prepared by people who care deeply about flavor and your happiness. I ordered the wedge saland and the blue cheese dressing was the best in the western hemisphere!
Also the macaroni and cheese was so good we ordered another bowl for desert!!

The woman that sat us and served us deserves a standing ovation. Friendly, knowledgeable, and somehow always there exactly when you need here — like steakhouse ninja.

name: Sapori Ristorante
document: Sapori Ristorante. cuisine: Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I’m not sure how I feel about this place. I had high hopes because of the reviews. It wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t great either.

To be fair, this was a Valentine’s Day dinner, so we didn’t get to try the regular menu. However, I do think the restaurant should inform guests when booking reservations that only a Valentine’s Day menu will be served. That wasn’t communicated to us. The portions were generous, and you definitely get a lot of food, but flavor-wise, it was just average. I’ve had much better Italian cuisine.

Starting with the appetizers, the octopus was a strong opener—nicely charred and a very large portion. The baked oysters and clams, however, were a hard pass for me. They were overly oily and heavily breaded, which completely masked the natural flavors of the shellfish.

For the main courses, we ordered scallops with squid ink spaghetti, a ribeye, and a surf and turf. It was a busy night, so perhaps the kitchen was rushed but that shouldn't be an excuse because it was about $80 per person. The spaghetti was just okay, but the scallops were cooked perfectly—tender, not rubbery, and done just right. The ribeye was my mistake; I should have known better than to order steak at an Italian restaurant. I asked for medium rare, but it came out closer to medium. The steak lacked flavor, not juicy and wasn’t particularly impressive, though that’s partly on me for the choice. The surf and turf wasn’t much better. The lobster was overcooked and rubbery, and the steak was well done even though we requested medium. Again, two strikes on the steak potions.

Unfortunately, the highlight of the evening was dessert. It was by far the best part of the meal, and I truly enjoyed it. It’s just disappointing that the rest of the dinner didn’t meet the same standard, especially for the price we paid. Again it isn't the money and it wasn't that bad, it could be a lot better knowing there are many Italian spot to dine out in but a friend wanted to try it.

That said, the service was excellent and the atmosphere was just right. Perhaps it was simply an off night. I would consider giving it another try if I’m in Staten Island again—just not on Valentine’s Day.

I was a little bit skeptical when I seen 370 reviews with a 4.9 rating until I actually went there. It is completely legit. The menu is small, but that’s because everything is done to perfection. I will most definitely be returning.

The pasta was made fresh but it stuck together and was a bit pasty. The staff was super friendly. It's a very romantic place.

Absolutely phenomenal!!

Went here with my wife and my in laws and it was amazing! For starters, the resturant has a great cozy vibe and the staff is so friendly and welcoming!

For appetizers, we got the special fried sweet and sour calamari, minestrone soup, and baked clams. All 3 of which I’d highly recommend! The clams had so much flavor and were in a delicious sauce. The calamari was perfectly crispy and sauced excellently!

For entrees we got the pollo scarpariello, lamb chops, risotto, and veal chop. I personally got the pollo and loved it! The chicken was off the bone which made it so easy to eat and the sauce it was in was perfect! Was light enough so you didn’t feel bogged down but was slammed full of flavor. The rest of my family all loved their meals and we would all happily get what we had again.

For dessert we got a spread of lava cake, cheese cake, carrot cake, panna cotta, and gelato. I thought I was full but I couldn’t stop myself from devouring the lava cake and carrot cake specially. The gelato was also fantastic!

Overall we had such an amazing dining experience! The resturant is family owned and it gives off the family oriented vibe! I cannot wait to go back!

Okay, so I see that this restaurant has great reviews and even the staff at our hotel lobby recomnended it.

Took photos of the food a bit late but I can say that it was tasteless, uninspiring, and not worth the pricey costs. Worst food on our holiday so far. Couldn't wait to be out of there. Lovely decor, though.

Perhaps it was a bad day for them.

name: Valla Table
document: Valla Table. cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Great restaurant for solid Thai food and a nice, intimate date. Amazing service and lovely ambiance. TK was the nicest and accommodated all of our requests.

My favorite dish was the Moo Krob Kra Pao and the Tom Yum Mor Fai soup was delicious. The Rak Bua Tod was so simple but good, and the mushroom dip it comes with is unreal.

The Thai Iced Tea is also great so don't miss out on it.

Valla Table is a gorgeous Michelin-recommended Thai spot in Midtown that’s perfect for date nights or small gatherings. The fine-dining vibe is elegant without feeling stiff, and every dish we tried was beautifully presented and full of flavor. Standouts included the Tod Mun Goong—crispy shrimp donuts with a bold black pepper kick—the rich and comforting Gao Lao Nuer hot pot, and the Khao Pad Pu with generous crab meat and great wok aroma. The Tom Yum Mama was a warming, upgraded take on classic tom yum, and the Kra Pao Kai with a perfectly runny egg was pure comfort food.

Absolutely loved our experience at this authentic Thai restaurant. The food was flavorful, fresh, and truly authentic; every dish was packed with incredible taste. What really stood out, though, was the outstanding service. The staff noticed we were seated near the cold entryway and kindly relocated us to a warmer, more comfortable table without us even asking. They were attentive, thoughtful, and made sure we were well taken care of throughout the meal. Great food, great atmosphere, and genuine hospitality. Highly recommend it, and we’ll definitely be back!

What a great find!

We had a 10/10 lunch experience. The food was absolutely delicious, and the service received by the team was super super good.

We tried 1 appetizer and 2 mains, but given how great they were, we feel any dish in the menu will be delicious too.

The atmosphere of the restaurant also aligns with the food quality.

100% recommended spot!

This is a great restaurant in Hell's Kitchen for Thai cuisine!
The food is great and they also have some great cocktails. In our case the food came out in separate intervals but in the end it was great... also, the staff is really friendly and knowledgeable about their dishes.
Great dining experience overall!

name: Odo East Village
document: Odo East Village. cuisine: Japanese. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
If you’re looking for a low-key but genuinely impressive night out in the East Village, Odo East Village deserves a spot on your list.

The food is the real draw. Their fried chicken is the kind you keep reaching for even when you’re full- crispy and well-seasoned. The raw fish was pristinely fresh, the kind that reminds you how much a good izakaya lives or dies by the quality of its sourcing. Every dish felt and tasted well considered. The staff was warm and attentive without hovering. We’ll definitely be back!

High end “Kaiseki Izakaya” (ala carte kaiseki) without the fuss of hour long commitment and price tag. Small, attentive and intimate. Every dish is bite size and sharable if you are willing. I had never had or heard of seaweed soy sauce and tofu sauce, its so good i had to ask for a spoon and the uni got me🤤

Exquisite meal of small beautifully crafted Japanese dishes designed to create a Kaiseki-style experience but customizable. Some unique flavors and sauces. Lovely room with a homey chili vibe and a soothing music soundtrack. Service was very attentive and warm.

I would recommend slightly larger portions for the price point, we ended up at almost $250 for 2 people including 1 glass of sake. Pet peeve:
Disappointed that the Toast payment device is configured to suggest tip amounts based on the total bill AFTER tax. This has never been the way that tips are calculated. It leaves a bad impression.
Every dish emphasized the ingredient's own flavor perfectly and they seasoned and flavored everything precisely. Beef tongue is really something. Service was also very attentive and caring.
Enjoyed everything we had and more. So hard to book a reso now but will highly recommend if you can get in

name: Vida Verde
document: Vida Verde. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Mexican Venues & Event Spaces. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This place went viral based off the drinks and the brunch atmosphere. I must say, everything you see that's viral take it with a grain of salt.

I will take ownership of the fact that, the birthday party seating amount was changed from 8 to 11 people. However, this was confirmed with the staff prior to arriving and they said they were okay with accommodating the large party. If they could not, they should have said so.

Food: Extremely small portions, overpriced and lacking flavor. We ordered tacos, and it was size of the bottom of a red solo cup, not even double tortilla, for a price point of $20 plus. I had steak over fries, I did not know they literally meant cut up steak over shoestring fries. What an absolute rip off for $27.00. Wings were ordered and they tasted like they were turning bad, we sent them back. Food is mediocre and lacking flavor, expensive for such small portions and just overall a disappointing experience. We had to get food after.

Tables/Seating: They squeezed in a table of 12 people on a tabletop of 3 tables. Absolutely ridiculous. I asked that they add a table or split the party to which the manager who appeared to be Irish kept saying he didn't have tables. I informed him they were getting paid regardless, so fix the problem, as we were sitting on top of each other. Sitting on stools with no backing, super uncomfortable, not to mention, we were by the door and the draft was cold, windy, coming through this heavy curtain that was useless.

Customer Service: Our server we had was rude, the manager was not polite, lacking customer service front of the house expertise, no sense of apologies for their shortcoming and the hostess is even more useless. I asked for a manager, she mentioned, she already addressed the issue with a guest from the party, I informed her this was not my question and my issue went above her pay grade. We had an issue with the bill and the server said she wasn't in "the mood" to deal with it. In addition to rushing us, walking away from the table when questions are asked, just overall disgusting with her attitude. We asked to remove her 20% automatic gratuity, as this is an option, so we could leave what we wanted.

Drinks: After 2 drinks, it becomes nauseating tasting the artificial flavor from the mimosas. I didn't understand why we paid for bottomless and instead of leaving the pitchers on the table with such a large party, server kept coming back, delayed. They tried forcing everyone to drink at the table, which how could you, if not everyone drinks and you have drivers? Nice little lawsuit on deck with this one.

Stay away from this location, they cram you into a small establishment, with tacky customer service and disgusting food for a price point which isn't reasonable at all. The manager, Irish male, dismissive, goes back and forth and I'm not really sure who's in charge of this puppet show. There are so many other locations in midtown and LES where you can get a better experience and bang for your buck.

We had a great time and lots of fun. We were a large group, and the drinks were strong and good. The appetizers were delicious. I really liked that they allowed us, and my group really enjoyed ourselves, and we didn't feel rushed. Also, the dessert was good

A high end contemporary atmosphere and the food was full of flavor. I like their salmon tacos and arrechera (skirt steak marinated in beer). The restaurant has a party vibe in the evening and a rooftop patio with taquila bar. The menu indicates options for vegan, gluten fee, and dairy free. Great drinks, cocktails, and service. They do have a dress code, so beware if you show up looking like riffraff.

The place was a good spot for a brunch, I wish the tables had a bit more space for two so we can fit the dishes. The wings and empanadas were really good, my favorite was the Al pastor tacos, Birria was a bit underwhelming so I recommend the fish/ shrimp options, Al pastor, or steak. The margaritas were good as well I got the passionfruit, overall not bad we came for a quick bite and they were able to seat us quickly which was nice! Very loud with the music so not a place to chill on the weekends, I am sure it is more relaxed on weekdays, deff a place to come for brunch to get lit and enjoy your time

This is one of my favorite restaurants or bars in the city. I love the food, the hospitality, the atmosphere, the music, the energy. It has it all. Unforgettable drinks, delicious food. I came with my family visiting for the first time and my cousin who love espresso martinis said. This is a real one. The bartenders (female) very kind and attentive. Please come here. I love the Latin community showing their culture in marvelous ways. I’ll be back again as usual.

name: Miriam
document: Miriam. cuisine: Mediterranean. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: We made a last minute reservation before a nets game and it was the best decision we ever made. There’s probably nothing bad in the menu, we loved everything we got. Specifically the Brussels sprouts and hummus as appetizers, I could’ve eaten 45 orders of those. The service was so freaking kind, they made suggestions for drinks and cocktails, everything loved them. I will def come back

Miriam is such a great spot. The food is delicious, the portions are generous (perfect for sharing between two), and the flavors are incredible. The pitas are honestly some of the best I’ve had.

We tried the chicken shawarma, which was wonderful. It comes with rice and a small Israeli salad, and everything was seasoned beautifully. The service was excellent, super attentive and kind.

They also offer special menus for Jewish holidays like Rosh Hashanah, which is a really nice touch.

Price-wise, it’s not cheap, but it’s absolutely worth it for the quality. Overall, just a really good restaurant, great food, great service, and one I’d happily come back to once they finish renovating their original location.

Popular brunch place we visited with friends. Our friends said the menu changed since they had last been. Overall several combinations offered for breakfast but it would be nice if there was one where you could mix and match the egg + simit/pita + side. I tried the avocado sandwich and really enjoyed it although could have used some more pickled onion and tomato could have been a nice addition. My friends had the popular breakfast and the smoked salmon latkes. Generally seemed like the chopped salad was left in varying amounts on everyone's plates, probably an indicator that another side might have been preferred. The kids enjoyed the challah French toast. Had to flag down our server for more coffee. Limited vegan or dairy free options. Menu skews savoury, only the challah French toast is on the sweeter side.

Come hungry! Seriously, the portions are generous and delicious. But that doesn’t mean the food isn’t wonderfully prepared and fresh tasting. For the price I’d describe it as a good value and most of the main entrees could be shared (especially with an appetizer). I really want to go back and try more of the dishes…next time I’ll come hungrier! It has a nice cozy ambiance, but not too cramped. Only complaint was the service was sometimes hard to track down (like to grab a new fork or get a water refill).

Came here for breakfast before going to Barclays and WOW. Everything we tried was phenomenal. I got the latkes Benedict and it was bangin.

Super cute interior as well lots of natural light and a big window to people watch out of.

name: Banh Anh Em
document: Banh Anh Em. cuisine: Vietnamese. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We really enjoyed our experience at Banh Anh Em. Even though we didn’t have a reservation, they were able to accommodate us within 10 minutes of our arrival, which we truly appreciated.

We ordered the Cha Gio, Grilled scallop with butter , Banh Beo, Banh Xeo pancake, and Banh Mi. Each dish was fabulous in its own way — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared.

The Banh Mi and Grilled scallop with butter were definitely our favorites. Highly recommend trying them!

The friendly service made the whole experience feel extra special and welcoming. We would absolutely come back again.

The BEST bánh mì I’ve ever had. The OG bánh mì was packed with flavor. It was savory, balanced, and the pork floss was such a nice touch, adding a light, airy texture with a subtly sweet-savory richness that complemented the fillings really well.

The grilled ribeye steak bánh mì was just as good. I don’t know what they put in that sauce, but it was insanely savory and umami. Every bite was bursting with flavor without being overwhelming. The steak itself was juicy, tender, and really well-charred, with a deep beefy flavor that paired so well with the freshness of the pickled vegetables and herbs.

Fun fact (from the server we talked to): the owner started this spot after working at Hanoi House, another popular Vietnamese restaurant nearby.

The best Vietnamese food in town I’ve ever had. This wasn’t my first visit,
if I remember correctly, it was already my fourth time here.

This time I came with friends, and we had to wait in line. When the restaurant opened, we put our names on the waitlist and waited at the bar nearby. After about an hour, we got a text that our table was ready. Totally worth the wait.

The food came out quickly and tasted amazing. We ordered Bánh Bèo, summer rolls with shrimp, scallops with scallion oil, Thịt Kho, Bánh Cuốn Hà Nội, and several other dishes I can’t even remember - there was a lot of food, and everything was phenomenal.

For drinks, I had the coconut cream coffee 🥥 and the egg cream iced coffee both were incredible. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and experience.

Great vibes, and the staff were so kind and friendly. I highly recommend this place and can’t wait to come back again.

We arrived at 5:15 PM and were 4th in line by 5:25 PM. This place is famous for its Banh Mi, and as a native of Hai Phong, I had to try the Banh Mi Pate Hai Phong. The dipping sauce was a great touch! We also tried the Heo Quay and OG Banh Mi—all very delicious, though I personally prefer a slightly chewier baguette over one that is crunchy all the way through.
The Bun Cha Ha Noi was nearly perfect; the sauce and sides were spot on, though the Cha Nem could have been fried a bit longer to get that deep golden brown shell. Skip the scallops with melted cheese if you don't like sweets—they were a bit too sugary for me.
The decor and vibe are stylish and authentic to Northern Vietnam. It is definitely worth trying for the food, but the long wait in the NYC cold makes it hard to justify a second trip during winter.

Lived up to the hype but our group’s wait time was minimal since we were the first round of seating at opening.

My personal favorites were:
1. OG banh mi (agree with other reviews that it is the best I’ve had in NYC… packed with pate!!)
2. Scallops (so diep sot trung muoi)

Had sample servings of the pho and bun bo hue which I thought were good too

name: CHADA
document: CHADA. cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Flavorful, elevated Thai food with romantic vibes for a date night! The heavy green curtains and booths create a beautiful and cozy vibe.

All the main dishes were delicious. We got Double Mushroom Spring Roll $14, Folded Dumpling $15,  Crab Curry $34, Wonton Tom Yum $24, Pad Thai $21, Goong Karee $25.

The only miss was the dessert - it was lacking the high quality execution from the main dishes.

I recommend making a reservation in advance because it’s pretty popular, even for a weeknight.

We recently hosted a private event for 35 people here, and it was a spectacular experience from start to finish. If you’re looking for a venue that combines authentic flavors with professional service, look no further.

The menu is incredibly diverse and every dish felt truly authentic. My personal favorites were the folded dumplings and the salted egg calamari. We finished the night with the coconut ice cream and chiffon cake, which were top-notch. In the best tradition of Asian desserts, they were "not too sweet," which was the perfect end to the meal.

The restaurant’s organizer was thoughtful and incredibly easy to coordinate with in advance. They were very accommodating with our various dietary restrictions, ensuring every guest had a delicious meal they could enjoy.

Our bartender and waitress were EXCEPTIONAL. They were attentive, polite, and very thoughtful throughout the entire evening, making sure no glass was empty and every guest felt welcome. Thank you again for the great evening!

Went to dinner on a Friday with two friends, the atmosphere, drinks and food were awesome.
I got three cocktails “Last Kiss of Summer”, “I’ll Wait for Yuzu” and “Ask for Jan”. Last kiss was definitely my favorite the Lychi flavor was light and delicious while “Ask for Jan” was punchy and strong.
For food we started with “Folded Dumpling” which were delicious and light. The coconut milk gave the dumplings and unexpected depth. We moved on to the “Fried chicken skin” and the “Sai Ua Croquettes” the chicken skin was delicious while the croquettes were spicy and a little refreshing.
The papaya salad was light and refreshing but packed a spicy punch at the end.
The “Pad Kee Mao” was good - flavor was strong but the dish overall was light - we ended the mains with the “Marinated Ribeye Steak” - which was solid but not our favorite dish.
The toast with Thai ice tea ice desert was sweet and delicious but the lychee yuzu sort was the perfect finish. Light yet refreshing.

Came here for dinner. Called in advance and was told no reservations were needed but when we showed up, there were no tables available so I had to wait a little bit. Waitress was nice, but Service felt a bit rushed. Appetizers were pretty good. The beef tartare was not your typical dish and was overpowered by the spice with no real flavor of the meat itself. We mentioned this to the waitress that we could not eat this and we’re just told OK and she took it away and still charged us. The Pad Se Ew  you was OK. The Pad Thai was good.  The duck breast was tender, however the curry was overpowering. Once we finished our entrées, we weren’t even offered any dessert, just the check came.  As we do like Thai food, there are better options in the city with larger portions at more fair prices.

This is easily one of the best Thai restaurants I’ve tried in New York. The overall quality is consistently high, and every dish we ordered was excellent — no misses at all ✨

Short Rib Curry:
The short ribs were incredibly tender and rich without being heavy. The spices were fragrant and well-balanced, and paired with the roasted vegetables, it was extremely satisfying and perfect with rice.

Beef Tallow Fried Rice:
Another standout dish. The portion of beef was generous, and the fried rice cooked in beef tallow had great depth of flavor. The addition of crispy fried garlic added extra texture and made every bite more interesting.

Coco Thai Tea:
Highly recommend this drink 🥥. The refreshing coconut water combined with Thai tea was amazing, and the chewy coconut meat on top added a fun texture. Super refreshing and memorable.

Overall, the food came out at a good pace, and the service was efficient. Definitely make a reservation in advance. 👍

google_reviews.text: Amazing food and staff! Very generous portions for a very reasonable price. It's really worth it! The atmosphere is very nice and pleasant. Bathrooms are located downstairs (for accessibility).

Good food. loved our server, very attentive.

There were great options available for all dietary lifestyles, which was much appreciated. The staff was friendly, the space was beautifully decorated and festive, and the overall experience was wonderful. Highly recommend. We’ll definitely be back!

Absolutely outstanding experience!
The food at Shuka was excellent — every dish was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. The service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere had a great energy without being too loud. Everything from the appetizers to the desserts was spot on. Highly recommend this place if you’re in SoHo and want a meal that’s both delicious and beautifully presented. I’ll definitely be coming back!

The cocktails were creative and perfectly balanced, and the portions were just right.
You can really taste the quality of the ingredients in every bite.
It’s rare to find a restaurant where everything — food, service, and vibe — comes together so perfectly.

I ordered the malawach and as someone Yemenite, I can honestly say—they nailed it. Perfect texture, perfect flavor, just the real deal.

We also had the fattoush salad, which wasn’t the traditional version you’d expect, but a fresher, more modern take—and it worked!

There was a delay with our order, so they sent us a complimentary muesli with pears, and it was honestly the best I’ve ever tasted.

Everything was excellent, full of flavor, and had a great kick. Highly recommended!

document: Mykonian House. cuisine: Bars Greek Seafood. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
We had a wonderful lunch at Mykonian House!
The atmosphere was warm, the service was friendly, and the absolute highlight of the menu was the lobster pasta — rich, fresh, and perfectly cooked.
Wish they could have added more pasta because the price is a little pricey.
Delicious. I had a Greek salad, sea bass, and Greek yogurt for dessert. My husband had calamari, chicken kabobs, and a fruit plate for dessert. Lovely!

Ate here several times since they opened. Food never disappoints and the place is very cozy. I’m not a huge lamb chop person and to hear me say that they are delicious, means something!!! Staff is friendly.

Mykonian House is a pleasant Greek dining experience carried notably by its warm and attentive service — the staff bring a genuine hospitality that feels true to the Greek spirit and makes you feel right at home. The food is decent but doesn't fully deliver on the 'authentic' promise in the name; the flavors are pleasant but lack the depth and boldness of truly great Greek cooking. The atmosphere is similarly understated and could use more Mediterranean warmth and character to transport you properly. A solid visit overall thanks to the excellent service.
The food, staff and atmosphere were all great. It's one of my new favorites...

name: Acadia
document: Acadia. cuisine: Mediterranean. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Came in February so expected it to be mostly closed. Still could navigate the perimeter of the park and catch some really cool and awesome views. Ranger was friendly and helpful. After October until May, everything in the area, to include towns inside the park and Bar Harbor are closed for the season, so prepare accordingly, especially food and drinks.

Fantastic weekend backpacking location. We did the full 22ish mile loop and it was stunningly beautiful. Due to slight altitude adjustments on the trail, there was a surprisingly large amount of biodiversity and that made traveling the trail super interesting the whole treck!

Despite the government being shut down at the time in October (or maybe because of it?), we had no trouble driving into the park and viewing a beautiful cove before driving back the way we came. It was quintessential Acadia with big breakers, lots of rocks and beautiful fall color! Definitely a spot not to be missed!

A friend and I took the Gorge Trail / Cadillac North trail and it took us 4.26 hours for a 5.4 mile hike. The gorge trail takes you to the Cadillac mountain summit. It is a serious hike that includes rock climbing. We then took the Cadillac trail north back down. We are 51/47 year old women. Be ready. It’s a work out. Have your knees ready. It is Beautful. All of it. Worth the hike. The reward is amazing.

The park is Awesome! We visited the 3rd week of October and it turned out great. The park was in peak season for Fall foliage. There was not heavy foot traffic on the trails. I would highly recommend Beehive Trail, Precipice Trail and Cadillac Mtn. There are many good trails to hike, those were just a few worth pointing out. For a change of Mountain scenery, take a ride to Schoodic Point for some awesome coastal views.

This place is a gem; if you’re exploring east 49th street don’t forget to stop here for some authentic Italian you won’t be disappointed. I celebrated my mothers birthday here we will certainly be returning again soon

I had a great experience here! I came here for just dessert and ended up having some drinks and a delicious margherita pizza! They also have happy hour exclusively at the bar from 3-6 pm. Service was fascinating,server will always check on us,we ordered an aperol spritz but it was a bit sour so they didn’t have a problem with redoing it,customer service is definitely given here. Food as I mentioned earlier was good,I also ordered a panacotta and we had a tiramisu! And that strawberry mule was pretty good too! I will be back for a full meal experience

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A True Italian Culinary Experience

From the very moment we walked in, the experience felt exceptional. We were greeted warmly by the host, whose genuine hospitality set the tone for the entire evening. There was no rush, only a sense of being truly welcomed, as if stepping into an elegant Italian home rather than just a restaurant.

The atmosphere was intimate and thoughtfully curated, but what truly elevated the night was the chef Alessandro. Rarely does one encounter a chef so deeply involved in the guest experience. He personally came to our table, not once but throughout the evening, taking the time to explain each dish with passion, precision, and pride. Every course felt like a story rooted in tradition, elevated by technique, and finished with unmistakable love for the craft.

Each plate arrived as a masterpiece. The balance of flavors, the quality of the ingredients, and the attention to detail were outstanding. Having the chef explain the inspiration, preparation, and origin of every dish transformed the meal into an unforgettable culinary journey.

The service was flawless from start to finish: attentive, seamless, and perfectly timed. Every need was anticipated without ever feeling intrusive, reinforcing the sense of personalized and full-service.
Without hesitation, a perfect score and a place I will enthusiastically recommend and return to again and again.

We had a party of 8 and were thrilled to get last minute reservations after our broadway play. The welcoming and cozy ambiance started as we walked in the door and were greeted by a lovely hostess. The waiter and manager were helpful, friendly and proficient. Our dinners were all delicious, including scrumptious Chicken Marsala and Margarita Pizza (just the best!) Two of us asked for a mocktail and were not disappointed by the bartender's yummy cherry and pineapple concoction. The deserts were large portions including a tiramisu and chocolate gelato (best to split one!) Our leisurely Venetian dining experience was  just perfect for our last night in New York City. Thank you La Piazza!

Stumbled on this amazing gem while going to the Saks light show.  Between the amazing greeting by the hostess and the staff it was our best overall experience after a week in NYC!  We had seafood pasta and tomato spaghetti and it was mouthwatering.  How good can pasta be?  Their chef figures out how to elevate the culinary experience. When we asked if they had a dessert we had experienced in Italy of lemon sorbet and prosecco they didn’t but then created it.  My black Manhattan was delicious and the overall space very cool and inviting!  Our only constructive advice?  If you sit near the door on a winter night prepare for frequent chill as the customers come and go.  One of those places that’s a must return next time we come to NY!

name: Angelo's Coal Oven Pizzeria
document: Angelo's Coal Oven Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We got the spaghetti pomodoro and a classic cheese pie. TLDR: worth a visit.

There was no wait and the server took us right upstairs to a two person table. Service was great and fast to attend to any needs.

The pizza was great. Crust had good leopard spotting and a tinge of yeasty flavor (which I like). Sauce was not overpowering and was very tomato-forward. Cheese was not too salty but provided the necessary fat that balanced out the acid.

Pricing: Decently good. Not like other places that overcharge for pies (cough trendy locations not to be named cough)
Overall: 4.3/5, an average experience

A classic pizza place that is always highly rated. We came around 12:30 and it was already packed. The guy who took our names down came out to check on all of us and give us updates frequently to make sure we knew we were not forgotten. Excellent service and a fantastic thin crust fresh pizza by the pie with fresh toppings. We did 3 pies, half meatball and half pepperoni, white with arugula and cheese with mushroom. The white with arugula was my personal favorite. But we left no slice behind. It is as good as they say it is, and with good service.

I didn't want pizza so I went with the Cesar salad with salmon as my protein. The croutons were too hard and not crunchy. Surprisingly the salad was very satisfying. The pepperoni pizza belonged to some one else.
We made what we thought were reservations for a party of ten students and ten parents. When we arrived it was something completely different. Not the best accommodation and management however we stayed. Students were cold and hungry. Overall the food was good!

I tried the Fettuccine Alfredo with chicken and the pepperoni pizza, and both were really good! The Fettuccine Alfredo was creamy, rich, and perfectly seasoned. The sauce had a smooth texture and just the right balance of flavor — not too heavy but still indulgent. The chicken was tender and cooked nicely, blending well with the pasta. The pepperoni pizza was also a hit — very thin crust, crispy on the edges, and topped with just the right amount of cheese and pepperoni. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients in both dishes.

The restaurant itself seems to have a bit of a historical background, which adds to its charm and cozy character. It’s one of those places that feels like it’s been loved by the community for a long time. Even at 2:30 p.m. on a Saturday, the restaurant was packed with people enjoying their meals, which says a lot about how popular it is.

The staff were very friendly, attentive, and welcoming. They made sure everything was good and checked in at the right times. The service felt genuine and professional.

Overall, it was an excellent experience — delicious food, warm atmosphere, and great service.

The service was amazing, thanks to our server Nathaniel. We walked in with 2 walkins of 30ish people each from our school. Nathaniel took care of our side and made sure we knew exactly what we were order by specifying that the white pizza had no sauce and that if we liked sauce then we should get the old school round. The pizzas were brought out really fast and tasted very well. The check was brought on time and there was nothing wrong with it. Thank you to the staff for taking us on such short notice. Great place with great pizza.

name: Izakaya Seasun
document: Izakaya Seasun. cuisine: Izakaya Gastropubs Korean. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Izakaya Seasun is a gem in New York. From the moment you walk in, it already feels warm like actually warm (maybe the heater was blasting 😅), but honestly I loved it since it was freezing outside. The vibe is cozy, intimate, and perfect for a chill after work hang or a fun dinner with friends.

The food was seriously on point. Everything we ordered was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully plated. The small plates are great for sharing, and you can really taste the quality and care in every bite. The skewers and hot dishes came out perfectly cooked, with flavors that were balanced and not overwhelming.

Service was friendly, attentive, and relaxed, which made the whole experience even better. You never feel rushed just genuinely taken care of. 👍

went to izakaya seasun for the 4th time, and it never misses! i had their matcha makgeolli and it was sooo gooddd, the matcha flavor was relatively strong. the waiter caleb was also very attentive as well! will def be back again for their amazing food and service

I understand how some diners might feel rushed for they definitely have a lot of traffic, but when we went right when it opened, we were told ahead of time we only had two hours to dine, but that was more than enough for the three of us. Service was also quite quick, with some waitress being more friendly and receptive than others. The aesthetics were nicely decorated and spacious clean, where each table also had a compartment to get utensils and napkins, which was very convenient!

The must-gets are the sukiyaki hotpot and the spicy crab cream pasta; the sukiyaki was so extremely flavorful with a perfect balance between sweet and savory! Some might find it a bit sweet, but sukiyaki is known to be at least somewhat sweet, which we found perfectly enjoyable! You can also add more meat and veggies for a fairly reasonable price, with the beef being quite tender and not overly thin. The spicy crab cream pasta was deliciously rich and spicy, which was a very fun and enjoyable balance that helps the richness of the dish to not be too overly intense. We loved those two dishes and can't recommend it enough! The pork jowl and tendon hotpot was on the blander side, so we just mixed it with the sukiyaki soup base to enhance the dish. The salmon sashimi and wagyu beef tartare was fresh, but didn't stand out too much with its mild flavor profile. The purple potato fries were just okay as well, but quite pricey for an appetizer dish.

Overall we had a great experience and we will definitely be back to try their many other dishes and relive the amazing time we had with both their sukiyaki and spicy crab cream pasta!

Thank you for reading and best of luck! (:

The food is decent and the atmosphere is nice. The 2 person table in the side are a little too small, but they'll usually let you sit at  a bigger table if you ask.

All of the food was decent, but none of it blew my mind. If I come back, I'd look forward to trying some of there other soups and noodles.

One comment is that the strawberries in the dessert were so cold and frozen that it was like biting into an ice cube.

Overall a really nice hangout spot for friends or dates. The matcha makgeolli was something I was looking forward to since there isnt many or any other places that really do that. And it didnt disappoint. The matcha makgeolli was on the sweeter side fyi, but otherwise it still tasted refreshing and the matcha tasted strong in a good way. The yuzu highball was good too.

I recommend getting the crab pasta and assorted skewers. Just a headsup that the pasta is somewhat spicy if you dont have any tolerance for spice.

Service was good too and the atmosphere was really chill.

name: Poppy
document: Poppy. cuisine: Bars Venues & Event Spaces Tapas/Small Plates. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Came in yesterday and there was some confusion about my order. They turn off the grill at 2. I ended up getting the hot pastrami and a taco salad. They were really good. Super friendly and helpful. I also got a dirty soda. The cherry coke is amazing 😍 I'll be back. Thanks ladies 😁

Stopped in for a sandwich. The staff is friendly and helpful. The meal was delicious. My wife got a Pop's Italian sandwich, and I had a Grown up Grilled Cheese sandwich. Great local spot that should be your local go-to restaurant list for a quick bite. Lots of daily fresh made baked goods as well.

Poppy's Place is a wonderful little cafe with fresh and healthy food options. We showed up with a party of 8 around lunchtime on a Saturday and they were able to handle our large party's order, had seating for all of us, and managed to bring our food out all at the same time (even though we ordered at 3 separate families).

For food, I picked the Seasoned Chicken Salad... Only to be told that they were out of chicken. Seemed odd to be out of chicken on a Saturday lunch situation, but no biggie, I asked for egg salad instead. But when my salad arrived, it was with hard boiled eggs instead of egg salad. No biggie with that either, the salad was delicious, fresh, and tasty (even with it being not what I expected).  Just a really good arrangement of healthy crisp ingredients.  My wife ordered one of the panini specials off the board and we were warned that it might take a while because they could only make 2 at a time and several people ordered paninis in front of us.  Our expectations in that were far exceeded because all the food came out together and in good time and the wife enjoyed her panini.  Our pescatarian teenager tied ordering tuna salad. Like the chicken salad, they were out of tuna as well, so our kid got a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, which was big but our kid didn't eat much. Sounded like the ratio of PB and J was off a bit, but our kid raved about the bread.

Other people in our group had similar challenges with ordering, and we figured out that 1pm on a Saturday must be towards the end of service for the day.  So just be aware of that if you go towards the end of lunch rush. Being out of chicken salad and tuna salad and some other things at 1pm on a Saturday just means more planning is required of the staff.  Other than that service snafu, we very much appreciated being told up front about what was out of stock and what would take extra time. Stuff happens, we get it! It's the communication and honesty that sets a place like this over others.

As for the atmosphere, it's a small place with one big family style counter (with a big pole in the middle, unfortunately) and several smaller tables.  They could get more space by moving the plasticware and condiments away and put another table or two there, and they would remove some of the things that remove from the atmosphere. The ambiance is fine, but nothing too special and it feels like getting food to go and eating somewhere else would be a better option.

Poppy's Place is a great gem of a restaurant in a cool little town. If you're looking for great food that makes you feel good to eat, you will love this place like we did! Poppy's Place is highly recommended!

Gem in Front Royal! Great food - love the grilled sandwiches, nourish bowls, breakfast burritos. Creative non-alcoholic beverages. Superb, friendly customer service.  Poppy's Place also invests in the local community needs through their Giving Board.  This establishment reminds me of a special treasure found in a college town.  A must visit!

Loved the vibes of this place. We went on a Saturday afternoon. Very homemade type of feel, as if my grandma was making hoagie sandwiches for my family. Food hit the spot, and you can't beat their big portion of Limeade - delicious 😋

name: L'Antagoniste
document: L'Antagoniste. cuisine: French Breakfast & Brunch Wine Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: I have to go at least once a month. Love the cheeseburger, the steak frites & the service. Haven’t had anything on the menu I didn’t like !

They had a filet mignon & fois gras special that may be my favorite entrée in all of Bed Stuy. The rest of the food was very good as well, but the frog legs could have been seasoned more liberally. That said, our waiter was kind and attentive, the interior was extremely welcoming, and I very much look forward to going back.

Cute spot with a warm atmosphere. Wasn’t blown away by the food and flavors in general. We had the mussels and tartar to start, which were both just alright. The fish of the day (cod) was tasty, however the steak was not cooked well - chewy and hard.  Chocolate mousse and hazelnut ice cream were also alright. Service was friendly.

Excellent, cozy restaurant.  Great for a date night.  Romantic.  Excellent wine selection and the food was divine!  And these were just the appetizers.  I forgot to photograph the actual meal. Service of course was great!  You can’t have great food and poor service.  They earned their stars!  You should rsvp though!

My boyfriend and I decided to drop in without a reservation, and we were fortunate to be seated just in time for the busy dinner rush. The restaurant was fully booked, but the service was exceptional. Our waitress was fantastic—she provided clear and concise descriptions of the menu items, making our choices easy.

I was starving so ordered the steak tartare since it would come to the table quickly since it’s raw. The presentation of it looks very pretty just when I scooped up some to put on a piece of bread the egg yolk popped and started dripping nice and evenly. I opted for the burger cooked medium rare, and it was incredibly tender, practically melting in my mouth. The burger looked substantial, a testament to its lack of added preservatives. My boyfriend chose the steak frites, and the steak was impressively thick and flavorful, showcasing the freshness of the ingredients. One wall proudly displays their local farm suppliers, which speaks to their commitment to quality.

The frites, a nod to their French inspiration, were perfectly crispy and absolutely lived up to my expectations. You can truly taste the freshness in every bite. Don’t hesitate—make a reservation and experience this gem for yourself!

name: Din Soup Dumplings
document: Din Soup Dumplings. cuisine: Dim Sum Noodles. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Delicious! Soup dumplings are amazing. 😍🤤I absolutely will be back!
Lunch menu was really affordable.
I highly recommend to make a reservation before you go.

Delicious dumplings!!! Always nice to find a great spot for soup dumplings and dim sum. They even had this dish that was so interesting- little tiny finger-bite sized dumplings in a cup/dish/lid situation with a straw through the middle and soda of your choice in the cup?! Seemed a little gimmicky like it was created for tik-tok, but hey I was thoroughly amused by it and impressed with the creativity so it's working. Holds up as a fun dining experiment even if you're not going for views online. I could just imagine popping in one day and ordering one to-go so I could walk around a park or something sipping my drink and snacking on dumplings - hah!

The little visible dumpling making cubicle was fun too, half of the magic of dumplings is knowing how much care goes into each bite and it's cool to be able to see them making them right there.

The taro tea was also delicious, maybe I'm wrong but it didn't taste like the standard powder/mix that you usually get with taro, not over sweetened. Was very yummy!

The deco had some nice art and ambiance, I like when lighting can be a little 'moodier' but I know they gotta keep it bright for the dumpling makers right there. Staff was very friendly and they had a great selection on the menu. Definitely worth a visit!!

It’s always very busy but this is a good thing! They have very flavorful food and everything is always delicious. The staff is amazing and work hard and they provide an excellent experience. I have eaten here twice and cannot wait to go back! I have been recommending this restaurant to everyone I know!

A friend of mine walked in and there was a waitlist so she signed herself up and it took around 10 to 15 minutes to be seated which isn't bad especially for no reservations. We enjoyed the drinks and the food was great! We started with the scallion pancakes, and the sautéed garlic green beans. For the main course we did have the beef tiny buns and the seafood shumai but for the drinks I ordered the passion fruit mango popping boba and my friend got jasmine green tea; the service was very attentive despite how busy it was. Would definitely return!

I wasn’t a huge fan of either dishes. The meat didn’t taste fresh for the pork soup dumplings and the noodles had a strange taste and lacked peanut butter flavor. Its was passable. I think if you’ve never had soup dumplings or peanut noodles before you would like it. I think their dishes are more catered to the western palette especially noting that the condiment sauce for the soup dumplings was very sweet when I just wanted vinegar.

google_reviews.text: We went for the first time on Friday night. They had valet and a coat check available. The hostess was welcoming and friendly. Wow, from the walk into the restaurant to the ambiance within. It is spectacular. But what really stands out is the service, drinks and the outstanding quality and deliciousness of the food served. Definitely added to our rotation list.
Get decked out, and get here to enjoy the amazing @olearestaurantnj

🍝💛

Had a fantastic dining experience last night. Morgan was a great server — knowledgeable about the menu and refreshingly down to earth with her recommendations. Evan, the manager, stopped by our table to check in, which was a great personal touch.

I’ve been a fan of Bud since his days at Butcher Block, and his newest spot absolutely didn’t disappoint. Highly recommend the Lobster Francese and the Chicken Fried Short Rib — excellent flavor profiles and a really unique appetizer approach. Definitely worth a visit.

document: Time Out Market New York. cuisine: Food Court. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I haven’t been to this area in a while, and I was blown away by the renovation! It’s an amazing spot with a massive variety of food vendors everything from matcha to pasta. I tried the pizza and it was incredible. The 5th-floor rooftop and outdoor decks are perfect for hanging out with a view. Definitely a must-visit in Dumbo!

Very busy but fun place to hang out, get some food and drinks with live music and amazing view of Brooklyn bridge and Hudson river, Manhattan bridge and Manhattan skyline! We ate at Bark barbecue. The food was amazing. If weather permits, you can sit outside as well! Worth a visit!!!

Some of my favourite food of the 10 days ive been here. I had Jacobs which is southern  comfort food and it was more than generous and certainly comforting. It was delicious and well worth the money.

Time out itself is huge with a massive variety of food. It's clean, and staff are friendly and helpful

After walking across the Brooklyn Bridge to the DUMBO (Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass) area of Brooklyn my wife and I decided to have lunch at the Timeout Market foodhall.
There were many wonderful indoor food stalls options on the ground floor together with the large Cecconi's restaurant with sitting outside next to the riverside with fantastic views of the Manhattan Bridge, as well as indoors.
After looking at all the food stalls options on the ground floor, we took the lift up to check out the open air seating area on the 5th floor rooftop, as I had downloaded the App that allowed me to look at all the food options from the stalls, order anything I wanted, pay for it online and have it delivered to our table on the rooftop.
When we got to the 5th floor we discovered there was a smaller foodhall with 5 food stalls and a bar. The Bark Barbeque stall immediately caught our attention as it was the only one with a queue and we love BBQ food. So I queued up for 15 minutes and I ordered some fantastic Dominican BBQ food (beef brisket, pulled pork sandwich, smoked conitas & cornbread with honey bitter), which we enjoyed with a couple of great IPA beers that my wife had purchased from the bar, sitting at a bench table.
There was also outside seating on the rooftop for diners, in addition to a public terrace with fantastic views of the Brooklyn Bridge, Manhattan Bridge & NYC skyline.
There are toilets on the first floor, which had big queues, and inside the 5th floor foodhall. The riverside with beautiful parks and Jane's Carousel can be accessed from the back of the mall.
Of the 3 food halls we visited on this trip to NYC (Chelsea Market & Market 57 being the others) this was by far our favourite and we would highly recommend it.

document: Doublé. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Comfort Food. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: This place is incredible. Not only is the service quick, even when busy. The drink menu is great, they have seasonal cocktails, the Coquito is sooo good. Every drink we’ve tried here is delicious. However, the real star of the show and the reason for this review is the food. We came here to get a quick bite one night and ended up ordering a chicken parm and a burger. “Chicken parm at a bar?” you say. It was INCREDIBLE. The sauce was delicious and the chicken was fried perfectly. The burger was great too, it was nice and moist despite being a smash burger and the cheese melted perfectly. We came back again and order the chicken tacos, chicken tenders, and nachos. The nachos were great with lots of toppings and nacho cheese which we all love. The chicken tenders were great and came with two sauces. The chicken tacos were fine, nothing wrong with them but they would likely be much better with a bit of salt. Overall this place is a must stop. Looking forward to coming back for drag brunch to try out their brunch menu.

A Bushwick Gem: Double's Delivers on All Fronts! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Double's Bar Restaurant on Halsey Street in Bushwick is an absolute standout, and it's quickly become one of my favorite spots in the neighborhood. From the moment you step inside, you're greeted with an inviting atmosphere that's both stylish and unpretentious – perfect for a casual drink, a delicious meal, or a fun night out with friends.

Let's talk about the food. The menu is thoughtfully curated, offering a fantastic selection of dishes that are both creative and comforting. Every single thing I've tried has been exceptional, from their perfectly cooked burgers to their inventive small plates. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and high-quality, and the kitchen clearly takes pride in every dish they send out. Portions are generous without being overwhelming, and the flavors are always on point.

The drinks program is equally impressive. Whether you're a craft beer enthusiast, a cocktail aficionado, or just looking for a well-made classic, Double's has you covered. The bartenders are skilled, friendly, and happy to offer recommendations. Their cocktails are truly something special – well-balanced and always a delight.

Beyond the food and drinks, the service at Double's is consistently top-notch. The staff are attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely seem to enjoy their work. They create a welcoming and comfortable environment that makes you want to linger.

And the ambiance? It's just right. The decor is chic but cozy, with a great energy that makes it suitable for various occasions. Whether you're looking for a lively weekend spot or a more laid-back weeknight dinner, Double's fits the bill.

In a neighborhood with plenty of dining options, Double's Bar Restaurant truly shines. It's a place where you can count on excellent food, fantastic drinks, and a wonderful overall experience. If you haven't been yet, you're truly missing out. Highly, highly recommend!

Feels like it should be on the establishment to control this… Won’t stop me from coming, but I really hate it when I want to sit in their outdoor space, and it’s taken over by people who aren’t even customers who are being loud and disrespectful to those who are. Whatever… maybe that makes me a jerk… I don’t know…

name: Alta Calidad
document: Alta Calidad. cuisine: Mexican. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Mexican spot that is featured on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list.

The list features restaurants that serve good food for reasonable prices and Alta Calidad delivered.

Must Try’s:

Yuca Fries + Chipotle sauce - out of the park delicious and salty

Alta Queso Fundido - probably the best thing we had. Make sure you order this. SO GOOD.

Churros - do yourself a favor and leave some room for dessert

Solid choices:

Carne Asada Tacos - would be on my must but the price point for tacos feels a little criminal. Very good but damn almost $10 per taco is rough

Pork Shoulder Carnitas - very good but again the other plates just put this to shame

Leave it:

Drinks - not a fan. Hot chocolate came out tepid and the mixed drink was just okay. Next time I’ll stick to water or coke

Verdict - solid choice for Mexican, would recommend, not in a rush to come back NYC just has too many other places to try

I visited Alta Calidad while on the hunt for a Mexican spot during NY Restaurant Week and it did not disappoint. I ordered the Snapper Tostaditas, Carne Asada, and Churros. My favorite of the bunch was the Carne Asada. I would order that again if I returned. The service was great. The waitress answered any questions we had and the drinks came out fast. This was great value for a price of $45 (because it was during restaurant week). The ambiance was great, with natural lighting and good music. I would recommend this place to someone looking for slightly upscale Mexican food.

We had a really good meal at this Mexican restaurant. We ordered chicken tacos, shrimp tacos, and a margarita, and everything was fresh and full of flavor. The sauce on the tacos was absolutely delicious, adding the perfect touch to each bite.

The presentation was neat, and the restaurant itself was clean and well-organized. The atmosphere was pleasant, and we especially enjoyed the music playing in the background, which added to the experience.

If you’re looking for tasty food, a nice ambiance, and good music, this place is definitely worth a visit.

Taste-wise, the food was delicious, and the drinks were very good. The service was amazing, and I really like the location of this place.

However, the portion sizes were quite small. If you’re coming here just to have a drink and a light bite, it’s perfect. But if you’re arriving hungry and expecting a full meal, even two plates might not be enough to fill you up.

Would highly recommend. Excellent food and service. They accommodated a kid request to simplify the tacos and a vegetarian request to make the queso meat-free. Margaritas were good. Tacos and short rib entree were great as was the rice and beans side. Portion sizes were perfect. Tres Leche dessert was delicious. The music wasn't too loud, so were were able to easily carry on a conversation. My only observation was that the music genre didn't really match the restaurant but that was hardly an issue. 5 stars!
