google_reviews.text:
This place is incredible. The service is amazing. The owner was so kind — he gifted my friend and me two mango lassis, which had a delicious touch of rose water. I was fascinated by how good it was

My friend and I also had the lamb curry — absolutely delicious. Everything was perfectly seasoned. The veggie samosas were wonderful too, very substantial and full of flavor inside. The tandoori was perfect as well, and we also ordered the garlic naan. Honestly, all the food was delicious.

The atmosphere is very warm and welcoming. We actually walked into this place by pure coincidence, and it turned out to be the most perfect coincidence.

Ate at the lunch buffet, all you can eat for $16.99.  It was delicious! Great variety and an amazing way to try other dishes. Staff was super kind and helpful. We ordered a side of garlic naan and it was the most fresh and best tasting naan I’ve ever had. Definitely worth a trip!

As someone who grew up in Kathmandu, I feel so at home and welcome. It was my first visit and definitely not my last! The jhol(sauce) of the momos was so perfectly tangy just like in Boudha and the momos were hella juiiiiicy.

THE ONLY INDIAN FOOD I'LL ORDER IN 8 YEARS. I've had probably 3/4 of their entire menu by now, and every single dish is amazing. I could not hype this place up more! I'll get 2 meals and naan/appetizer and it'll be my meal prep for the week. Absolutely the best Indian food in Brooklyn. (I've only ordered online via Seamless/GrubHub, never actually dined-in before.)

Absolutely the worst Indian buffet I’ve ever had. The food was worse than worst — cold, stale, and completely tasteless. Minimal variety and shockingly, breads aren’t even included. What kind of buffet does that?

Only saving grace was the server, who was polite and kind — but sadly, no good service can make up for food this bad.

Dhaba NYC is on a whole different level. Do yourself a favor and stay far away from this place.

document: Santa Fe BK. cuisine: New Mexican Cuisine. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: We’ve been looking for good breakfast burritos in the area and came across Santa Fe BK. They have a couple options for breakfast burritos, we went with the potato one. The hashbrowns inside were crispy and delicious. The green chile was a great add as well for flavor. I wish there was a sauce we could dip it in, but overall it was a solid burrito. It tastes very similar to these amazing breakfast burritos we used to have in Denver called Santiago’s. We’ve been trying to find a place that closely replicates that and this has been the closest we’ve come

A neighborhood restaurant offering unique southwest US mexican cuisine using local ingredients. The red, green sauced enchiladas, burritos and more. Also gotta come early to grab a billyburg breakfast burrito before they run out. Cozy space, a bit cramped, good drinks and fast service.

Perfect garden setting.
Waiter with the "Best Personality".
Refreshing cocktails.
Huge portions.
Delicious little "Pillows of Heaven" for dessert that are complimentary.
Recommend reservations.
Step aside, Shake Shack. Best burger and fries I’ve had since I moved to NYC. Best verde sauce I’ve EVER had. Love the light Santa Fe ambience. Super friendly staff. I’ll be back!

As a native New Mexican, I am always skeptical of any place on the east coast that claims to be authentic. However, SF BK is easily the closest thing to home I’ve found. In fact, calling it close to home undersells it, it IS home. The red sauce was perfect, the green sauce got the job done, and the sopapillas were the puffy pockets of heaven I remember. To be completely honest, if you put Monroe’s, Sadie’s, Los Cuates, Duran’s, and SF BK alongside each other, I would not be able to pick out which one was from NYC.

Now I need to make another trip for the breakfast burritos!

document: Bleu Nuk BK. cuisine: Caribbean Cocktail Bars Tacos. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Delicious food 😋 amazing, tasty drinks 🍸 and outstanding service! Me and my bf accidentally walked in into this restaurant, and for sure, we will be back. Fish 🐟 was mind-blowing!!! Pork was perfectly cooked and seasoned, so as my pasta 😋
The coffee was delicious, the food was on point, and the ambiance was supreme. The brunch menu was great. Prices are also reasonable. Let the Caribbean music ride out more through! Lol

My brother and I came here to toast our mother’s heavenly birthday, and I’m so glad we chose this place. The service was great, the iced coffee was amazing (made me wish I wasn’t lactose intolerant), and the bake and fish was so worth the wait. Will definitely come back again!

A fantastic new addition to the neighborhood!!!
I love everything about Bleu Nuk Bk.  For starters, it's simple, elegant style with great attention to the nuanced detail of comfort go a long way.  Minimalist yet padded bar stools are a key factor, gorgeous lighting,  beautiful wall design, and rustic chic bar shelving with excellent glassware are just a few of the things that immediately elevated your experience.
The staff is noticeably happy, which tells me it's well run by caring owners and  great management.
The menu is a beautifully curated mix of delicious local favors with a modern yet classic approach.
Everything we tried was a taste sensation, made with great love.
The mussels stood out in high regard for me. It was a nice appetizer portion, with full sized tender mussels which is a skill in itself,  but the great surprise was how well this heavily garlic broth stood out.  Garlic can be tricky,  and is often the gross, prechop, often rancid, kind, and when I saw how much garlic was in this dish I was ready to be disappointed but to my great surprise it was one of the BEST, most well prepared, garlic forward broths I have ever had!!! It has to be fresh and it has to be added to the mix at the right time, and this chef knew exactly how to handle every ingredient.  Just spectacular!  My coconut rice chick pea was comforting but still light. My anti pea, nut, legume husband absolutely LOVED my dish and much to my surprise,  he couldn't keep his fork out of my dish!.  That's high praise!!
His steak dish was so flavorful and expertly cooked, still soft, juicy med/rare which is rarely(see what I did there)  accomplished on the thinner cuts. We loved everything about it.
All the sides were bursting with flavors.   Nice quantity to feel satisfied without feeling too full.
The only suggestion would be a few additional wines to round out diverse pallets.
We're so excited to have another great walk to restaurants in our growing food destination neighborhood! Enjoy!

I can’t say enough about this wonderful new restaurant. The food is absolutely delicious! Omg, you have to go for Taco Thursdays. The best tacos you will ever eat. Everything on the menu that I’ve tried has been like a party in my mouth. Dionne, the best bartender in NYC, is just a delight. She makes the best and most beautiful cocktails/mocktails I’ve ever seen. She is welcoming and keeps me coming back for more. This is my new favorite neighborhood spot. People let’s support this wonderful addition to our neighborhood. Looking forward to many years of fun at this great establishment.

google_reviews.text: Nice day in Brooklyn. Went to Japan Village to walk around. Wasn't in the mood for Japanese food. IKEA was a planned destination but I didn't feel like swedish meatballs. Defontes!!!! I hadn't been there in a while. It was near lunch time so I want sure about the crowds. Usually it's packed on a Saturday lunch hour. Not today! Maybe people were out and about. Looked the wall of sandwich choices. Then it slapped me in the face. Chenzo 13 special. Prosciutto, sopressata, provolone, hot salad, broccoli rabe. I got the large. Went to my car and devoured 1/2 as soon as I cleared my car door. I saved the other 1/2 for dinner or tomorrow's lunch. It was awesome. The Red Hook Special has a great balance of meat and vegetables. As a result the lettuce and tomato work really well with the chicken cutlet and the turkey. That's two crunchy and two soft textures, well done. They don't put too much mayo either. The seeded bread is crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. A "1/2 sandwich" can feed two and is often cut in half for that reason.

Lovely spot, highly recommend, $20 for that sandwich is the right price and is an NYC steal.

Remember, cash only!!!!

DeFontes is one of those Brooklyn institutions that instantly reminds you why some places never need a refresh.

I went straight for the Signature Hot Roast Beef and, in a moment of well justified indulgence, added the Steak Pizzaiola. Zero regrets. These sandwiches are unapologetically stuffed. Meat, cheese, sauce, seasoning, all layered with confidence and generosity that feels almost defiant in today’s portion-controlled world.

And the bread matters here. It’s fresh, warm, and crisp in all the right places, sturdy enough to carry the weight of the fillings without stealing the spotlight. It’s the perfect vehicle for the kind of sandwich that requires both hands and lots of napkins.

Ordering at the counter may look intimidating at first, like there’s a secret rhythm you’re supposed to know and have rehearsed. Don’t stress it. The service is quick, efficient, and genuinely friendly. The staff are happy to guide you through it, even if it’s your first time staring at the menu trying to decide how hungry you actually are.

Just keep in mind that there’s no seating beyond a stand-up counter along the wall, so plan accordingly. This is very much a grab-and-go or eat-it-immediately experience.

DeFontes isn’t chasing trends. It doesn’t have to. This is classic, expertly executed deli cooking that delivers exactly what you want and then some.

I’ve been coming to Defonte’s for almost twenty years. I’ve tried a lot of their sandwiches, but the Nicky Special is still the one I go back to the most. Ham, provolone, salami, ham capicola, fried eggplant, hot salad, mushrooms, lettuce and tomato — everything fits together nicely and it’s always satisfying.

It’s a solid sandwich shop. Nothing fancy, just dependable and good. The reason it’s not five stars for me is simply that I’ve had a few sandwiches elsewhere that impressed me a bit more, but Defonte’s is still a place I keep returning to.

If you’re not sure what to order, go with the Nicky Special. It’s been my favorite here for a long time.

Got the special roast beef sandwich. The quality of the beef and cheese was very good, but I was honestly disappointed otherwise. It was cold and the bread was soggy. The flavors felt bland too. Could really use some vinegar or mustard at the least for being a special. I honestly felt sad because of the price I paid for it. Still, it was only one sandwich, their others might be better balanced.

name: Tabaré Williamsburg
document: Tabaré Williamsburg . cuisine: Latin American Bars Burgers. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A great little brunch spot with a meat-centric menu. Lots of Uruguayan beef, empanadas, steaks. The food was good, piping hot, and the the brunch service offers a cocktail and a coffee added to your meal for $8. Overall the prices were good, the food was delicious, and the atmosphere is very fun and welcoming. The service was slightly odd, a little slow for it being so quiet on a Saturday afternoon, but it’s a great place to relax.

Really enjoyed my dinner here! The service was really wonderful and the atmosphere is cozy. We had the beet salad and the octopus to start, both delicious. Then for entrees we got the burger, the ribeye, and the chicken milanesa. The food came out fairly quick and we had a great time. We spent $193 (including tip) for three people for the two appetizers, three entrees, a cocktail, and two soft drinks.

I recently went to Tabaré with three girlfriends and we had the most amazing time! We were lucky enough to catch the last half hour of happy hour, which was the perfect start to the evening.

For starters, we ordered the mussels with the most delicious brioche toast and the seafood casserole—both were absolutely divine. For our main course, we shared the skirt steak and ribeye, and I have to say, it was some of the best steak I’ve had in a very long time! To end on a sweet note, we split the chocolate cookie and flan, both of which were dreamy.

The service and ambience were a 10/10. Our waiter was attentive, welcoming, and made sure we had everything we needed.

Overall, I highly recommend Tabaré for a great night out with friends, delicious food, and an amazing atmosphere. I’ll definitely be returning soon!

One of my favorite local meat spot!
They do corkage fee, which I personally HIGHLY appreciate as I am a wine enthusiast and love enjoying some of my wines with dinner.
Their pricing is great, specifically for New York. They offer a limited menu which I personally like, that usually means they do whatever they have on the menu with fresh produce.
Typically they have 2 pieces of meat they offer, I always tend to go for the churrasco, the best option in my mind.
They do as well fresh pasta (usually different every time we've been there) and those are usually quite tasty as well!
In terms of appetizers, we've tried the blood sausage and their empanadas, both are great.
The atmosphere is simple, and nothing like a fancy steakhouse but for the price and the quality, I will definitely keep going there, specifically with their (relatively affordable) corkage fee!

We visited the Bushwick location first and after having such a great meal, we decided to try this one as well.
Unfortunately, they don’t offer the parrillada for one or two like in Bushwick, but the service, food, and overall experience were still excellent.

We ended up ordering the ribeye and the breaded chicken — both were outstanding and exactly what we were hoping for.

Our server really stood out with great attention and service.

name: Aunts et Uncles
document: Aunts et Uncles. cuisine: Vegan Cafes Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Scenic View of Little Haiti

Great outdoor space along with indoor nook space will plenty of books for decoration.

Well diversed menu with plenty, plenty of vegan options. Diverse menu with West Indian options to American to Spanish options. Like Wow. What don’t they have.

I fell in love with the music the clean, immaculate, professional space. Perfect for Solo dates, Couple dates and even quick bites before certain locations with Drinks only.

The drinks are also exquisite from hot drinks to cold wine and other options. Go check it out for yourselves. And let me know how it goes.

Such a beautiful & cozy all vegan spot serving up some of the best vegan comfort food in Brooklyn! I love dining local small business while visiting NYC & stopped in for the first time after hearing about it online. From entering, the vibe is cozy & welcoming. Beautiful decor. Staff was friendly. Their menu has so much to pick from but I tried their famous vegan Mac n cheese & the smash burger. Both delicious!

The smash burger had so many flavors all at once & worked so well! A vegan burger that’s not bland. The pretzel bun was amazingly fresh, burger cooked to perfection & loaded with vegan cheese, a little bit of spiced sauce & veggies. It was really filling & dense but so fresh & perfect. Mac & cheese was also very flavorful! Everything came out beautifully presented.

This is such a wonderful spot to grab a vegan bite! Really enjoyed myself & would love to return one day! The vibes here are everything I want in a vegan place! Cozy, beautiful, welcoming & just fresh, amazing food!

Stopped in w/ my vegan/fluent intolerant friend who is a regular here. I am neither so this was a task for me lol. The food was Amazing, the atmosphere, and the service were top tier. Makyla was sooo sweet and patient. We shared several laughs and she had amazing recommendations. Will def be back

I found this restaurant by coincidence when I was looking for a place to treat myself to a vegan breakfast on my birthday, and I’m so glad I ended up here! Absolutely everything about Aunts et Uncles is on point!

First of all, the food! I‘m vegan, and I love breakfast sandwiches. So I’ve made and eaten my fair share of them over the years. The one I had here was one of the best ones I’ve ever had: the textures, the flavors, and to top it all off, a delicious sauce. For dessert, I had the pudding cake, which was also all around delicious.

Next, the service: Amazing! Super friendly staff, lots of attention to detail. They even put birthday candles on my cake.

Finally, I loved the overall vibe. Aunts et Uncles manages to create an environment that feels cozy and hip at the same time. I spent a chill weekday morning on the couch reading and sipping tea, but I’ll definitely be back for dinner and drinks. (Their cocktail menu looks spectacular!) Bonus points for the art installations & book displays!

Absolutely love this restaurant! The owners are very friendly and interact with costumers every time they are present. The food brings me back home as I’m half Trini. Who would’ve thought, I can get a nice vegan meal that tastes so good and reminds me of Trinidad right in Brooklyn? I absolutely adore the staff as well. Just be patient as all orders are made to order and made fresh in the kitchen. I promise it’s worth the wait!

name: Antidote
document: Antidote. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Dim Sum Szechuan. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’ve been here twice with friends. Staff were nice, normal space. Food was good but definitely you pay for the experience in the prices. If you are familiar with Chinese food, then this might not be a place to visit necessarily, but if you r not, worth once.

🌿💚Veggie dishes for vegan were surprisingly delicious! I highly recommend them. Especially the one in my pic (green slices)

Dandan noodles were ok. Classic flavor.

Same did the chive pancakes.

Tea-smoked duck was a little buttery and expensive.

No notes on this place. Simply outstanding food, great ambiance, perfect for coming with friends so you get to try a lot of the menu items. They were all fantastic. Would come back to keep on trying stuff for sure. Our favourtie dish was the crab tofu!
Highly recommend coming here! Thanks for the great experience

Just adding to the rave reviews: do not miss the cucumber salad, fei-hong fries, tea smoked duck, or caramelized eggplant. These were genuinely mind-blowing.

Also liked the crab tofu and the sautéed green beans, but the list above cannot be missed.

everything was absolutely delicious and there are tons n tons of vegetarian friendly options. mapo tofu was mouth numbingly good w the schezuan peppers and the cucumber salad and green beans are also a must try. I loved the storm cloud cocktail!! Great spot for a birthday and it’s very spacious and beautiful!! Portion sizes are also substantial

Wow. I’ve been wanting to try this place for a while, and this went above and beyond my expectations. I eat a lot of Szechuan food so my standards are pretty high and I’d have to say that this place has shot up to the near top of my list. Probably the best take on Chungking style fried chicken I’ve had yet and the sliced fish stew dish was unreal. We also had the woodear mushroom salad and pork soup dumplings as starters. Everything was packed with flavor but I’d have to say that fish dish was the highlight. Cannot wait to order that again. On top of the amazing food (not to mention the incredible cocktails), the service was impeccable , and the live jazz was sublime; a very pleasant surprise. A 10/10 experience. Would love to see their take on 3-pepper chicken on the menu someday 😉 but needless to say, I’ll be back soon.

document: Sweet Catch . cuisine: Seafood. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Sweet catch caught us! Excellent food! We had the Plain Deviled Eggs, shrimp and grits, catfish and grits and fried chicken. Delicious! Get it all! The Amazing Owner Ka-Wana was very hands on and welcoming. The thoughtful Chef Jay came over and greeted us personally. He said I tried to put my foot in it and I told him I didn’t know how he was still walking! Lol our server Michael was great and quick. We ordered, ate, meditated on the goodness of the food, came back down to earth and was out of the door with a hug from the owner in less than an hour, with good vibes poured over us that will stay with us always. The sweetest catch!

Stumbled upon this place for restaurant week. Tim greeted & seated us very politely. Took our orders & made our drinks which were amazing. He recommended the food which was also top tier. Literally everything was flavorful and delicious. Entire staff was so attentive and polite. Shoutout to Nicomy, Prince && Brandon.
Loved the atmosphere, music choices, and the food was great! Very calm and inviting. The stand-out of my meal was definitely the fried okra. As someone from the south it reminded me of home

My second experience wasn't great as the first. The food and decor nice. I went on a Sunday evening to celebrate my friend's birthday.  There was a large party and us.  I didn't understand why the hostess/manager seemed to be pressing me when she asked if we had a reservation.  She was slow to take our food and cocktail orders but was quick to clear them away before asking if we wanted or needed anything else. Thank goodness the gratuity was included because I wasn't planning to tip any further.  She wore a Bob haircut and acted as the host server and manager. I barely finished my crab cake.  It was a weird experience and decided not to stay away.

Everything was amazing! The food,  the service,  the people,  the vibe, was simply amazing! Order anything it willy be good,  any waiter will be great,  a truly amazing experience. Don't worry the patio is covered and heated so go ahead and book!

name: La Ñapa
document: La Ñapa. cuisine: Tapas Bars Seafood Venezuelan. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This place is amazing! I was expecting some good eats but they absolutely surpassed that. I’m already planning to go back. The lovely server Roxanna recommended the arepitas as it’s easier to share than the full arepa, we got it with brisket and it was so shockingly amazing. The chicharron was possibly the best I ever tried, the bed of sauce (kinda like a buffalo sauce) it comes on is perfect. Also shout out the Brussels sprouts, cooked perfectly and the sauce was nicely tangy. The passionfruit margarita was also insanely good and made with all fresh stuff, you could tell! I literally can’t wait to come back here with a group, everything was so beyond good :)

One of my favorite Nieghborhood spots, you can’t go wrong.  The chicken empanada is my favorite but the ceviche is also top tier, great drinks and happy hour during the week. Truly a gem of a spot with so many different options.

Was excited to try La Napa, based on its photos and reviews. Unfortunately it does not live up to either. For the most part our meal was fine. Not good, not horrible, just fine. We tried the jamon croquettes, the pan con tomato and two empanadas, one chicken and one chorizo. Everything tasted bland and lacked any crunch or texture beyond wet soggy bread. I think they are afraid of salt. Overall, disappointing experience and will not be returning.

A favorite go to for when I want a nice sit down place to dine or order for take out. I have been a customer since 2020, a lot of great meals and memories. And many more for the future. I love everything on the menu. (I have ordered the pork arepa, pastor taco, and shishito peppers many a time). I returned today with a friend who has a food allergy and our server Roxanna was excellent and accommodated us to ensure we had a flawless dining experience. Many thanks to the always thoughtful staff.

My New Favorite restaurant love love love their Shrimp and Fish tacos. the empanadas are also on point. Thank u to my waitress Rossana she is very polite and made the welcoming even better on the walk in . This Will be my go to spot especially for the Passion fruit Margaritas ..ask for Rossana ,Thank me later .

name: Bonafini
document: Bonafini. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Dropped in this past Sunday for breakfast/brunch. Picked it out randomly from Google Maps. Had a wonderful meal in a bright, cheerful atmosphere. Service was great. Shown is the Montrealer breakfast sandwich. Deeelicious😁!  Glad we stopped in!

This is a small Italian restaurant in Brooklyn, but personally, it’s not a place I would visit again. I went on a date and didn’t have a chance to look at the menu beforehand, and my date didn’t ask about any dietary restrictions, so there were a lot of items I couldn’t eat. Most of the dishes were tomato-based, which I can’t consume.

I ordered the calamari and zucchini, which were extremely oily and lacked flavor. The oil definitely affected my stomach later on that night. It felt like they were simply battered, fried, and served—no seasoning at all. My date had the pizza and seemed to enjoy it, but I wasn’t able to try it, so I can’t comment on it.

Bread was offered to the table, and the drink options were pretty standard. The beer selection consisted of Italian beers. On a positive note, the waitress was very nice, and the restaurant itself was clean. They also serve I believe ice cream at the front.

Overall, it just wasn’t the right fit for me. Maybe brunch would have been a different experience.

Visiting Brooklyn, we were in the mood for brunch and stopped by Bonafini, an Italian spot.

Even though it's primarily Italian, that didn't matter -- we went straight for American brunch classics.

I had the pancakes, which came with blueberry compote, Greek yogurt, and hazelnut spread. My dining partner went for what I believe was the Sicilian Shakshuka -- tomato and vegetable stew, olives, bread, and eggs.

The pancakes were solid: just the right amount of maple syrup. They were a little on the dry side, but still tasty, helped along by what seemed like Nutella or another chocolate-hazelnut sauce. Not mind-blowing, but satisfying and definitely hit the spot.

Overall, a pleasant brunch -- we left full and happy. I'd be glad to come back the next time I'm in Brooklyn.

Last visited: August 23, 2025

We came to support our local friend from the neighborhood, we really enjoyed our lunch. We ordered the Prosciutto Pizza and the bolognese lasagna, they were both delicious! I had a sparkling lemon water which was super refreshing. We also tried the salted caramel and chocolate ice cream. The waiter was super attentive and friendly. The space was well designed, cozy and welcoming.

Came for brunch and it was pretty good. Will definitely come back. The ginger cocktail was really good. Loved the hash browns. The shakshuka was okay - felt like it could have been a bit richer in flavor and thicker in consistency but it was still enjoyable. Best brunch I've had in this neighborhood. The server was incredibly friendly and helpful.

name: Gage & Tollner
document: Gage & Tollner. cuisine: American. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text: I took my girlfriend to Gage & Tollner for her birthday. The service overall was fantastic, your water glass is constantly being filled up and you never feel forgotten (especially for how busy the place was on a Thursday night). We had a reservation and were seated immediately, and our drink orders were taken after our water preference. To start we had the Caesar salad and the hot rolls and both were delicious, our server even brought extra butter when we used all of ours. The croutons in the Caesar salad were delicious. For dinner we had the T-Bone for 2 which can be ordered pre-sliced. It was a very good cut of meat with a little too much fat but still amazing. For dessert we had the Brooklyn Blackout Cake which was also very good and not too rich for a completely chocolate cake. Finally, since I indicated on OpenTable that we had a birthday in our party there was a Happy Birthday card waiting at our table when we sat down and a candle in our cake complete with Happy Birthday written on the plate! (All a surprise). Overall, a great spot for steak dinner and especially a special occasion!

In a landmarked building in Brooklyn, this remarkable, Victorian- design restaurant harkens back to 1879. We invited friends for brunch there and enjoyed a first class experience. First, the decor is exquisite (see photos) and their wait staff couldn't be friendlier. Then the food and drinks came! Their cocktails were well crafted (the Bloody Mary is a brunch favorite). We then enjoyed their poached eggs and sprouting broccoli on toast (so good!), fried chicken w/hush puppies & sriracha honey (to die for!), G&T steak and eggs (perfectly cooked steak & eggs) and finished the meal with their Brooklyn blackout cake (amazing!!) and fresh brewed delicious coffee. All this while surrounded by wonderful furniture, wall decor and lighting that transports you to an earlier, more civilized era. We have to return there for dinner!

Visited on 11/16 in the morning and had a reservation for one. I got seated quickly and the service started off well. The food was good overall, I had the House Rolls, steak with eggs, and fries. The fries were too salty and the rolls were average, but the steak with eggs was excellent with the sauce. The only downside was the constant check-ins; two different servers came by about every 15 minutes. I know they’re trying to be attentive, but it felt a bit rushed for someone who likes to eat slowly.

What an incredibly special place! Perfect for our anniversary celebration, although it's also the type of place you could go regularly without needing a special reason. Beautiful space where you just feel the history of it. Service was top notch from start to finish and the food was fantastic! Highly recommend the devila on horseback (bacon wrapped dates stuffed with cheese and almond), bone-in rib eye for two, and the baked Alaska. I already want to go back!

I found myself at the bar enjoying a drink and a meal with my friend on February 12 around 9 PM. The bartender by the window, wearing snake earrings, appeared somewhat neutral and professional, but came across as quite cold and unwelcoming. It felt as though they didn’t fully understand what true hospitality means, and I didn’t feel valued, which made the experience awkward.

We spent nearly $300 on a quick meal, which isn’t much given the atmosphere, but it felt like we weren’t welcome despite or consumptions  . While the bartender wasn’t rude in her words, the way she looked at people felt condescending. Their demeanor seemed entitled and disengaged, lacking both personality and warmth.

On a positive note, the food was excellent, and the hosting team was friendly and attentive. However, the bartender's lack of engagement really stood out. A simple smile or a warm sentiment like, "Thank you for visiting, have a great night," would have made a significant difference. This establishment has a lot of potential; I noticed many great servers who were engaging, smiling, and professional. With so many patrons, it’s clear this is a wonderful place, and it deserves a bartender who embodies a more welcoming spirit and better hospitality. I hope the bartender was just having a bad day and that this isn’t the usual way they interact with guests. We’re all human and not perfect. While my experience with that person wasn’t the best, I still want to give a 5-star rating because the food was fantastic. At the end of the day, we don’t know what someone might be going through, and I hope their demeanor isn’t typical, as it really lacked the warmth of good hospitality.

name: Runner Up
document: Runner Up. cuisine: French New American. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Mili’s pop up here was outstanding. Truly a great experience. The rating should go to Jose and Alexis. The dishes were simple but beautifully balanced and every detail accounted for. We loved them all. I think the cheese dish was one of my favourite things I ate all year. The pork was expertly cooked and so flavourful. Would love to come again to any popup here because the space is also lovely and intimate. Thanks for a great meal!

This place is stellar. We went for Valentine's Day, and the tasting menu was legitimately some of the best food I've had in New York. The food was inventive and delicious. It's small and intimate, which gives it a lovely atmosphere. Perfect for date night or when you want a damn good meal. I will be going back regularly.

runner up is SUCH a wonderful place. snagged a last minute resy after eating winner sandwiches for a year, and WOW. food was outstanding — a nice meal, without being too stuffy / over fancy. love the intimacy of the space & the experience of sitting at the counter while everything is being fired. super accommodating to allergies, too. we ordered the focaccia+whipped ricotta, meats & cheeses, the bitter greens salad, and the short rib. short rib came with a bowl of baby purple lettuce, pickled radishes and cucumbers to wrap the meat into. Loni & Freddie were so welcoming and passionate, we had a lovely time!

Today I visited this cafe with my colleagues (a group of about 20 people). We sat on the second floor, it’s a converted apartment, but the atmosphere is simply unique and authentic, which I’m delighted with. Service at the highest level. The food is incredibly tasty, I liked the salads, especially the yellow beet salads. It should be noted that I ate it for the first time and was pleasantly surprised at how tasty it was. My colleagues were delighted with the pork and even took extra. The chicken is definitely delicious. In general, this is an ideal place for a company to have a great lunch or dinner.

Exceptional dining experience. Wonderful food served in a beautifully lit and intimate environment. The chef prepared a  well sourced  and seasonally appropriate menu, show casing marvelous flavors through simplicity that allowed for a natural pop of colors. Each dish excites the visual mind and palate. A wine list that stands up to the food  is rare to find at this price point and setting, runner up exceeded expectations, thoughtful curations that only amplified the experience. Having incredible options means nothing if you don't have the service aptitude to bring it all together in  a meaningful way, the team here handled each step with care representative of all the fantastic facets of this fantastic evening.

My friend and I dine in with our kids and we had a great time. The food was amazing. The drinks were great. The atmosphere was a breath of fresh air. We enjoyed our stay. name: St. Anselm
document: St. Anselm. cuisine: New American Wine Bars Steakhouses. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Love St. Anselm! The ambiance is very relaxed, a good place to go for any occasion.

Those biscuits with pimento cheese, the crab deviled eggs, and steaks - I dream about them.

Went with a friend on a Friday afternoon; we were immediately seated (we did have reservations). The restaurant did get incredibly busy at one point, and our server apologized for it, but to be honest, I never felt neglected. I also saw that everyone worked as a team to help one another.

We started with the Buttermilk Biscuits and Pimento Cheese, Blue Crab Deviled Eggs, and the Beet & Ricotta salad. All of these were incredibly tasty; I had to be careful not to finish them all so I could save room for the steak.

For our steaks, we ordered the Butcher Steak (hangar steak) and Ribeye. Both were amazing and cooked perfectly. I enjoyed the hangar steak the most.

For dessert, we ordered the Carrot Cake and Chocolate Cake. We shared a bite of each. Both were phenomenal and perfectly balanced.

I highly recommend!

St. Anselm is an American steakhouse/tavern that serves delicious steaks and comforting dishes in a relaxed setting.

THE MEAL
🥮 Biscuits & Pimento: These were amazing. The biscuits have a crisp, crunchy crust protecting a decadent, soft crumb. The pimento cheese adds great creaminess, but, the side of salted Vermont butter elevated them even further.

🥩 The Steaks:
• Butcher's Cut (Hanger Steak): Served medium rare with an excellent sear. Tender, juicy, and full of flavor.
• New York Strip: Robust beef flavor with perfectly seared fat.
• Lamb Leg: Cooked nicely to medium rare, though the pickled pepper relish was a bit overpowering. Tip: We used the onion cream sauce from the Baby Carrots dish to balance the relish.

SIDES & SWEETS
• Savory: The Baby Carrots (on that tasty onion cream) and the Thick-Cut Grilled Bacon were standouts. The bacon had a nice richness without being too heavy.
• Sweet: Do not skip dessert. The Carrot Cake was incredibly moist, and the Toasted Marshmallow Ice Cream was a memorable finish.

SERVICE
⭐ Special thanks to Abi for the warm, professional service. She understood the food and wine menu inside and out.

OVERALL
A great place for a business dinner or special date night. St. Anselm shares high-quality food and service at a reasonable price.

This place was packed on a Thursday night with good reason— the steaks were superb. We ordered the 32-oz Prime T-Bone, the 16-oz Ribeye, and the Pork Porterhouse and they were beautiful— perfectly grilled and succulent and flavorful. You’ll also be glad to get the Baby Iceberg salad for starters as it came with heritage bacon that’s so good, as well as the especially tasty Crispy Pig Head Croquette. Overall a most happy meal.

Food was delicious. Salmon was delicious, the Brussels were the best I’ve ever had. The crab deviled eggs were good. Oh and definitely the biscuits with the pimento spread is one that friends ordered before and love, we got some I was stuffed and wasn’t going to have one, but I had to try it, and yes I probably would not had ordered biscuits but they were of course good. My only complaint was not getting any refills on my iced tea. That’s a pet peeve of mine.

Sorry for the length but I was so impressed, I wanted to take my time and write a thoughtful review to let everyone know.  I went to St. Anselm because my guest picked it, so I showed up not really knowing what to expect. I left wondering how I hadn’t been there sooner.

Every single dish impressed me.

I started with the Baby Iceberg salad, and I’m not exaggerating when I say it’s the best wedge salad I’ve ever had. Instead of that traditional massive wedge that crumbles the second you try to cut it, this one is actually constructed in a way that’s easy to eat. It’s generous enough to split, but I’m glad I didn’t. I finished the whole thing without regret. :-)

They’re known for the buttermilk biscuits with pimento cheese spread (pictured), and now I understand why. If they decided to serve only those and nothing else, I’d still come back. They’re that good.

As for the NY Strip, I hate to keep saying “best I’ve ever had,” but here we are. It was cooked perfectly, exactly as ordered, and the au poivre sauce added this creamy, peppery depth that elevated the steak without overpowering it. Just outstanding.

We shared the ice cream cake for dessert, and I’m glad we did. It’s big, and by that point I had already cleaned every plate put in front of me. Worth it.

The place was at full capacity on a Thursday night, but you wouldn’t have known it from the service. And I really do mean team. Our waiter was clearly busy, yet drinks were refilled, plates appeared and disappeared, and everything moved seamlessly. It felt coordinated, not chaotic.

One thing that really stood out was the acoustics. The dining room was completely full, but I had no trouble hearing my guest or the staff. It never felt loud or overwhelming. Someone clearly put thought into the design because it struck that rare balance of lively-fun without being noisy.

This is officially my go-to for steak in DC. I know they serve other proteins, but after that strip, I may never branch out.

name: Syko
document: Syko. cuisine: Syrian Korean. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Really dope place! Super friendly owners helped walk me through the menu because admittedly, I was overwhelmed by the options. I don’t live near here and the vast menu made me to go a tiny bit overboard. I started with the kimchi soup, superb! I got the 3 baked goods for $9.99: sfiha, za’atar, muhammara. All great and reheated well. Probably the only thing I didn’t love was the fatboy sandwich. It’s held together by a Korean pancake that was charred in some parts and undercooked in other parts. If you just want something to stuff your belly, this is for you. I also wish it was wrapped with foil only; the paper wrapping was impossible to peel off. Leftovers were better because I was able to deconstruct it and cook the pancake more. Now my absolute favorite item was from the fusion menu. The beef shawarma hotteok was chef’s kiss! Holy hell, I can’t stop thinking about each crispy and flavor packed bite. I will definitely be back for this! Such a beautiful marriage of cuisines.

SYKO is an all around worth-it foodie experience. The food is split into 3 menus: Syrian, Fusion, Korean. I was interested in the fusion food, so the co-owner's wife recommended we try the Labandu (pork dumplings covered in crispy chili oil over labne) and the Half Falafel Half Shawarma pizza (the pizza dough is actually a scallion pancake). Amazing recommendations - that Labandu dish is making us want to relocate to Brooklyn lol. The fusion flavors work so well together. You can pinpoint the Middle Eastern flavors from the Korean flavors - the fresh labne from the spicy chili - and somehow they come together in a way that makes SO much sense.

We walked in on a Saturday afternoon and were immediately immersed in what felt like a Middle Eastern and Korean grocery store. The walls are lined with items you'd only see if you were in a predominately Syrian or Korean populated area. There are 10 indoor seating spots and when it's nice out, 8 outdoor spots. Despite how busy the restaurant was, we were able to find a spot for our group with ease because a lot of people were getting take out.

Can’t wait to return!

Amazing! The food is Michelin guide level. The amount of fusionary flavor that explodes with each bite is phenomenal.

You need to close your eyes while eating to truly indulge all your senses in the explosion of flavor.

Different,  yet familiar.  Highly recommended. The staff are also very friendly and hospitable.will be back very soon.

Interesting take on a fusion of both Syrian and Korean culture. The flavors of both blend well with each other and the menu design is rather thoughtful. I've gotten the falafel pizza and the flavors are so fresh and herbaceous the portion was rather large too so it was price appropriate. The vegetarian Hotteck Japchae is so flavorful as well, easily one of my favorite on the menu now.

Amazing.

name: Ikigai
document: Ikigai. cuisine: Japanese Asian Fusion. located in Brooklyn. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Ikigai Arcade is an absolute gem. I was visiting from out of town and the staff were incredibly welcoming! It’s affordable and the games all felt great. In fact, they were some of the best I have played on. Sound Voltex in particular was the best feeling 60hz cab I have played. The community is lucky to have such a place with owners who care!

I had an absolute blast at Ikigai, staff was very friendly, helpful and answered all of my questions! I was able to play Kancolle Arcade and was helped by another player, they were also very nice!

I can't wait to visit when I come into town again!

At long last, Pittsburgh has its very own rhythm arcade! I can’t compare to any game centers in Japan, but I’ve been to a number of arcades across the US, both small/privately owned and big chains. Ikigai Arcade is hands down the nicest I have ever visited. There is more for rhythm & fighting game fans than any other American arcade I’ve been to; the owners know their audience and don’t waste space with random stuff aimed to satisfy your average Dave & Buster’s visitor 😛 the cabs (including but not limited to: Ongeki, maimai finale and dx, chunithm, sound voltex, wacca, pop’n music, groove coaster, beatmania iidx, pump it up, nostalgia) are very well maintained. I was also impressed with their selection of imported Japanese merch (figurines, apparel, cute accessories) and mythical sports drink Pocari Sweat.

The arcade is quite easy to navigate and does a good job of creating pockets with lower noise where you can rest or even hold a conversation—if you are a regular arcade goer, you know how big of a deal this is! Null & Taka are very approachable, friendly, helpful, and responsive to customers in person and via Discord. I expect to lose a lot of my disposable income to this place in the future.
I knew nothing about this subculture before going and had such a blast! Very beginner friendly- all the games I played had tutorials and were in English and the staff was very helpful and welcoming.

Not just a local rhythm game landmark - Ikigai is at the forefront of bringing rare cabinets to the states.

Cab maintenance is sublime here, and the owners rule. Lots of hard-to-find cabs -or outright impossible-to-find cabs outside of Japan, including both the newest cabs and some discontinued ones. Community is also really friendly and I was finally able to get into rhythm games thanks to this place.

name: Pangat
document: Pangat. cuisine: Indian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I ordered takeout because I live a bit out of the way, and as soon as I heard about this spot, I couldn’t wait to try it. I ordered the vada pav, spicy butter chicken, and a mango lassi — and overall, the food was fantastic.

As someone born in Mumbai, I’m constantly chasing good vada pav, my all-time favorite food — and they absolutely nailed it. The pav was soft and buttery, the batata vada was incredibly flavorful, and the gunpowder chutney had the perfect kick. A total flavor bomb and easily the standout of my order.

The main reason for the 4 stars is the butter chicken not coming with rice. This is the first time I’ve ever ordered curry from an Indian restaurant and not received rice with it. Since the dish wasn’t cheap and I wasn’t prepared to make rice at home, it was disappointing. I’m not sure if they forgot, but I’d strongly suggest including at least a small portion of rice with curry in the future.

That said, the butter chicken itself was excellent — probably the best I’ve had in a long time. Tangy, well-spiced, perfectly balanced, and not overly creamy the way many places make it.

The mango lassi was also yummy, pretty standard, though it didn’t come with a straw, which is another small detail worth improving for takeout orders.

Overall, the flavors were incredible, and I’d definitely order again — especially for that vada pav.

Fantastic Indian food. In my opinion, in the conversation for best in Park Slope. Thw owners are so nice and the service was attentive and friendly. The menu is short which allows them to mix it up with the daily specials, which have all been outstanding. The Vada Pav is crushable, I could eat a small platter. The butter chicken is wonderful, the curry is rich and silky and the chicken melts in your mouth. The chili paneer is lightly fried cubes of their pillowy paneer covered in a deep and complex chili sauce. They make the paneer in house daily and it shows. Overall, highly recommend Pangat. They are doing some wonderful things in the kitchen and deserve the praise and attention.

This recently opened Indian food joint in Brooklyn, NYC checks all the boxes. They serve authentic Indian food along with the best Vadapav in town. This is a must visit place if you are looking for authentic Maharashtrian cuisine. They do have Sunday sit-outs where they serve fish, chicken & goat thalis. The menu is small but they do not compromise on quality and taste.
10/10 recommended !

We were visiting NYC and tried this authentic Marathi style indian restaurant and we loved it so much. The food was absolutely delicious and matched our expectations really well. I had fried pompret and garlic chicken with some parathas, rotis and vada paav on side. Everything was fabulous, must try the chicken and fired fish if you are a paaplet(pomfret) lover.

Hopeful this spot will build on its potential for being a great Indian restaurant in the ‘hood.
We a started with Crispy puris, Sprouts Bhel and Pav Bhaji, which was the stand out of the three and I’d order again. The other two dishes had a suspicious egg like aroma to them (although no eggy taste) - not sure what that was about.
For mains we shared a selection of the breads with butter chicken, the cauliflower and some rice. The two main dishes were excellent and the cauliflower delightfully spicy. The paratha’s, whilst tasty, were a bit stodgy and wet, which I wasn’t expecting. We also ordered a special, a chill paneer, which felt like it belonged in a different restaurant altogether, and wasn’t really enjoyed. I’d love to see a daal on the menu, and a more traditional paneer dish. The mango lassi was needed after the mains. Service was friendly and efficient. I will definitely return for the Sunday thali.

google_reviews.text:
"Great Food and Cozy Vibes, but Prepare for a Wait"

If you’re looking for fresh sashimi in the heart of Chinatown, Tora is a solid choice. This small, basement-level gem has a very cozy and warm atmosphere, though it stays quite busy.

The Experience

Wait Time: Expect a bit of a wait. I waited about 15-30 minutes for a table, and the food itself took a fair amount of time to arrive after ordering.

Atmosphere: The vibe inside is lovely and intimate. I particularly enjoyed watching the chef work—very calm, focused, and professional.

Service: The staff are polite, though the service felt more functional, almost like a "fast food" pace rather than a personalized dining experience. It wasn’t particularly memorable, but they get the job done.

The Food

The quality is where Tora shines.

Freshness: Everything was incredibly fresh and delicious.

Pricing: The prices are on the higher side, but considering the quality of the ingredients, it’s reasonable and acceptable.

Pro-Tips

Parking: Finding a parking spot near Chinatown is quite a challenge. I’d recommend using public transport or a ride-share service if possible.

Perfect for: A casual but high-quality meal when you aren't in a rush.

Went here from a tiktok recommendation, this place seems to be more for aesthetics rather than service. We did manage to get seating fast, however it took 15-20 minutes to get our order taken after we asked how to order. We over heard two guest ordering at the front, so we wanted to ask if we order at the front and then sit back down.The hostess got rather upset we asked, but we really didn’t know who was a server and who was a guest. None of the servers were wearing uniform only the people behind the sushi bar. They had hoodies on with no company logo. The servers did not refill waters and it was pretty difficult to get their attention. One of the male servers was actually very attentive he sat us down and had given us an extra item we ordered. Other than that, the service was extremely lacking.

Presentation of the food was nice. The sushi quality was decent at best. There is a 90 minute dine in time restriction probably due to the small size of the restaurant.

The bathroom was in unpleasant condition, someone had left blood on the floor; it was rather gross.

Overall, a sub-standard experience to the average recommendation, that we saw online.

It’s rare that a Sushi restaurant in the US surprises me, but this was truly special. I was seated quickly and the food came in just a few minutes!
I ordered the “Sake Aisuru Don” which in English is translated to “Salmon Love Bowl.” Trust me when I say that this dish was made with great quality Salmon, and even better quality Love.
The atmosphere was great, and transported me right back to my days traveling all over Japan.
I will be back to eat here again.

I had a delicious salmon bowl and our roll was so good. Servers were nice! My only thing is that the bench against the wall is not the same height as the chairs across from it and it was a little too high compared to the table so it was uncomfortable. That being said it didn’t bother me that much. I’d definitely come back. Our food was great and a good price

I got off at the South Station and wandered over here. The restaurant is located in a basement with limited space, and mainly serves seafood donburi, making it more suitable for a quick meal for 1-2 .

Itadori Don虎杖丼: Sea urchin, salmon, tuna, salmon roe, scallops, octopus, crab sticks, avocado, tamago玉子, and cucumber – a mixed dish, perfect for first-timers wanting to try everything. The sashimi was indeed quite fresh, with a firm yet tender texture, and the open display on the counter showed the restaurant's confidence in its freshness; however, I personally felt the quality could be improved. The sea urchin wasn't smooth enough, and the salmon and tuna were too lean, lacking in fat aroma. The rice itself was also lightly seasoned, becoming dry and less smooth towards the end, and ultimately uninteresting. Finally, I couldn't resist drizzling some shoyu醤油 on top, which instantly elevated the experience.

Matcha Cheesecake: Absolutely not recommended. The cheese was too heavy and hard, the matcha flavor was very weak, and the accompanying cream had a very weird foamy texture.

Curry goat, curry chicken, rice and peas, macaroni salad, coleslaw slaw and fruit punch.

Fruit lunch was loaded with fresh ginger. Wowza!!!!

Really enjoyed the curried meat. Staff and customers very nice. Music is loud. Cash or credit same price. Long line to order but moved quickly.

Grab a seat if dining in first. Can't wait to go back!

Cost us $20. Inflation buster.

Stopped by here this morning. Really bright and clean place. Food looks good but I only stopped in to grab a beef patty. It had a lot of meat, the right amount of spice and the crust was on point. I’d give the patty about a 7.5/10. It’s good to have in the area, but I wouldn’t drive across town just to have it. The staff members were blah, not rude but they weren’t very welcoming either.  I really wanted to try their oxtail, but it was still early and it wasn’t ready yet. Id highly recommend the “This is it” all natural juice. I had the strawberry lemon lime flavor, one of the best I’ve had. I’d give it a 9.5/10

I came to CC’s earlier today really looking forward to getting some stew peas. I traveled all the way from Queens and arrived around 11:30 a.m. When I got there, I greeted the cashier and asked if the stew peas were ready. She didn’t look up or acknowledge me, and when I asked if she knew about what time it would be ready ,  whether in an hour or two , she just shook her head without saying a word.

What stood out to me was that shortly after, a Jamaican gentleman came in and asked her when the jerk chicken would be ready, and she immediately gave him an answer. I couldn’t help but wonder if it was because I don’t have an accent, which made me feel a bit dismissed and unwelcome.

I ended up waiting in my car for about 20 minutes, planning to stay an hour if needed, until I realized I could just order on DoorDash. As soon as I placed the order, the food was ready within 5 minutes — which was confusing since I had been told (or rather, not told) that it wasn’t ready.

Her attitude was honestly disappointing and could turn customers away. If I hadn’t thought to check DoorDash, I probably would’ve left without getting any food. I really enjoy your food, but I hope the staff can be more attentive and polite to everyone who walks in. Her name is CHANEL ! Or Chantel either or !

I used to like CC’s bc of its pricing and decent portions but after today, I won’t be visiting again! Not only did they forget my plantain that I paid for, there was hair in my food.. not one, not two, but three pieces of hair!! This is unsanitary and disappointing to say the least.

I was walking by here the other night and the aroma coming out the door was so good I had to stop in. There were already closed. They were cleaning up. And still the restaurant just smelled so wonderful, I just had to come in the next day.

Oh my goodness, I'm so glad I did. The jerk chicken was fabulous! Chicken was moist and tender, oxtail gravy very flavorful, and the jerk sauce was nice and spicy without being overpowering. I had some of their ginger fruit punch as well, and the ginger just made the flavor pop -- and it does a great job of easing back the heat from the jerk chicken as well.

As others have said, the restaurant itself it very clean and well kept, and the staff are very friendly, welcoming, and helpful. There's just a vibe here of a warm family restaurant and you can see the other customers pick up on it as well.

I know there are a lot of Jamaican restaurants in the neighborhood and I'm new here ... so I should try some others ... but it will be hard going anywhere else.

name: Miriam
document: Miriam. cuisine: Wine Bars Mediterranean Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We made a last minute reservation before a nets game and it was the best decision we ever made. There’s probably nothing bad in the menu, we loved everything we got. Specifically the Brussels sprouts and hummus as appetizers, I could’ve eaten 45 orders of those. The service was so freaking kind, they made suggestions for drinks and cocktails, everything loved them. I will def come back

Miriam is such a great spot. The food is delicious, the portions are generous (perfect for sharing between two), and the flavors are incredible. The pitas are honestly some of the best I’ve had.

We tried the chicken shawarma, which was wonderful. It comes with rice and a small Israeli salad, and everything was seasoned beautifully. The service was excellent, super attentive and kind.

They also offer special menus for Jewish holidays like Rosh Hashanah, which is a really nice touch.

Price-wise, it’s not cheap, but it’s absolutely worth it for the quality. Overall, just a really good restaurant, great food, great service, and one I’d happily come back to once they finish renovating their original location.

Popular brunch place we visited with friends. Our friends said the menu changed since they had last been. Overall several combinations offered for breakfast but it would be nice if there was one where you could mix and match the egg + simit/pita + side. I tried the avocado sandwich and really enjoyed it although could have used some more pickled onion and tomato could have been a nice addition. My friends had the popular breakfast and the smoked salmon latkes. Generally seemed like the chopped salad was left in varying amounts on everyone's plates, probably an indicator that another side might have been preferred. The kids enjoyed the challah French toast. Had to flag down our server for more coffee. Limited vegan or dairy free options. Menu skews savoury, only the challah French toast is on the sweeter side.

Come hungry! Seriously, the portions are generous and delicious. But that doesn’t mean the food isn’t wonderfully prepared and fresh tasting. For the price I’d describe it as a good value and most of the main entrees could be shared (especially with an appetizer). I really want to go back and try more of the dishes…next time I’ll come hungrier! It has a nice cozy ambiance, but not too cramped. Only complaint was the service was sometimes hard to track down (like to grab a new fork or get a water refill).

Came here for breakfast before going to Barclays and WOW. Everything we tried was phenomenal. I got the latkes Benedict and it was bangin.

Super cute interior as well lots of natural light and a big window to people watch out of.

name: Bijan's
document: Bijan's. cuisine: Persian/Iranian Cocktail Bars Mediterranean. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Very lovely place and friendly service, the appetizers were tasty , and they had a good selection of drinks ; maybe it would be nicer and tastier of they use a different bread for appetizer.
The main course was a creative mix , and well served.
I would recommend their sumac chicken and lamb stew for main course and grilled eggplant for appetizer.

Happy hour is the way to go. Great selection to go with it.
Monday - Friday from 4 pm - 7 pm

The Dim lights are a plus. Definitely recommend for a date night or late vibes before parties closing at 12 am depending on the night.
Be sure to inquire with server for timeframe.

Drinks are made expediently and with expertise in consideration of your palette.

The salad & sandwich menu is a grand plus to choices. I gotta try the shaved cucumber salad with the pomegranate vinigarette it’s tempting.

Turn any quick bite into a full meal with varied add ons.

Baby green with added salmon to make a dinner.
Such a great choice, the sherry shallot vinaigrette was divine with the balance of savory taste without too much other ingredients.

I really enjoyed my meal. I got the calamari for an appetizer and the Rosemary Lime Sumac Chicken for the entree . The mashed potatoes were soft and delicious and the chicken was cooked beautifully and juicy. The atmosphere was so beautiful. I would definitely recommend!

Food was three stars as the chicken kebab I got was average and kind pricey for what it is. The service two stars because it was INCREDIBLY SLOW. It was a weeknight dinner and everyone’s gotta work tomorrow, so expected an efficient dinner, but it took forever for the waitress to come take our order and deliver food and even get water. In terms of ambiance — hard to describe as at the end of the night it turned out into open mic which we were not aware of. On the one hand it was kinda spontaneously cool, on the other hand it was unexpected and we couldn’t continue our conversation at the table.

There are a lot of things wrong here, I'll make a list so its easier to read

First and foremost this is not Persian food, it's a disgrace to call it Persian food the closest thing they have is a kebab and its only ground meat, where are the rest of the options? The menu is small and primarily American centered, I went there during dinner time but if you look at the other times you'll see what I mean as well.

The service was mediocre, my table was never checked on, mind you there's 5 people here so they immediately add a 20% gratuity uncharge.

The waitress pushed alcoholic drinks on us and once we declined she left and never came back. What I will say is she knew what was good and what wasnt on the menu.

Now moving to the prices and what we got we spent about $30 a person for a very mediocre meal. The pasta bolognese was terrible, all the sandwiches were alright but the meals did not justify the price in the slightest.

I'd avoid this place going forward.

name: French Louie
document: French Louie. cuisine: French. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Joined for dinner on a Thursday night. The restaurant has a modern-bistro sensibility with subtle rustic touches and a nice balance between elegance and comfortable warmth. We sat in the back section of the main dining area with the leather banquettes. Tables did feel too cramped, and the it wasn’t a busy night but it would be difficult to get out from your seat on a busy one. Service was okay, not the most friendly and warm. Food was very good. The escargot was delicious, the piece of sausage added to each shell elevates the flavor. The grilled whole dorade was very fresh, meat was tender with a subtle sweetness. But the charred broccolini was very bitter for some reason. House steak was okay. Would love to try the lamb next time. Overall a cute bistro with great food.

I tried to get a healthy dish so ordered the socca with multi grains and fried egg, but unfortunately it wasn’t that great. Also someone else in my party got a French toast but it was basically a large shared dessert instead of a brunch entree and he could really eat it, would not recommend getting that as an entree. The bread was hard and crusty!
The service and ambiance were nice though.

Had a spontaneous date night here and it turned out to be the perfect spot. The food was great and I especially appreciated the portions considering the affordable price point. The highlight for me were the fried artichokes, they were so delicious and memorable and so was the salad verte!

Came for lunch on a date! It’s a cute and elevated spot.

Get the Trout Po’ Boy- you won’t regret it. The dressing on it is so delicious, I’d love to know how they make it. The French bread is thick so if you’re looking for a lighter meal, then maybe skip.

They have a very nice outdoor patio in the back! Very nice to sit under the sky / in the sunlight, but there are only 2 tables in the direct sun. The other “backyard” seating is actually under a big awning.
Cute and cozy, Great service, great food. Sardines and slow roasted lamb ribs are my favorite. If you like dessert, Do not miss the Banana Foster Profiterole!

name: White Maize
document: White Maize. cuisine: Venezuelan Empanadas. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I just ordered food to go from this restaurant through Uber Eats, and I have to say — wow! It was my first time ordering from here, and this was honestly one of the best lunches I’ve had in a long time using Uber Eats. The portion size was just right, the salmon was perfectly cooked and full of flavor, and the maduros were spot on. Everything in this order was simply excellent. I highly recommend giving this restaurant a try — you won’t be disappointed!

I visited this Venezuelan restaurant for the first time today with a friend, and I absolutely loved it! The food was delicious — full of authentic flavors and made with care. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, making it a perfect place to relax and enjoy a great meal.
A special shout-out to Alexa for her amazing service — she was super friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home. It’s not easy to find places where both the food and the service stand out like this.
Highly recommend this spot if you’re looking to enjoy real Venezuelan food and a great dining experience!
Amazing place to eat! The food is delicious and tastes just like home-cooked meals. The portions are generous, and the place is super cozy and welcoming. Highly recommend!

You know how when you live in a place you find the local spots that completely answer your craving for a certain flavor that you need right now, at a great price, that's always perfectly consistent? White Maize is one of those places. I get the pulled chicken bowl with an extra side of plantains and I'm the happiest of happy puppies. The menu is pretty simple, good food done fast and right. The staff is lovely, friendly and accommodating. It's a bit of a hole in the wall so the atmosphere is definitely "fast food" (though we have eaten in with friends on occasion), so our typical MO is take out. If you like the ingredients, you should enjoy White Maize.

So torn here. Used to love their food but my experience was so bad I'll never go back.

Food 4/5
Honestly the food is pretty good. The empanadas are really great (particularly the beef one) and the pabellon arepa is pretty good. The tostitos are not as good imo, using a plantanos base instead of the traditional tortilla is interesting. Gives it a thicker crunch and more heft, but I think I prefer the traditional style more?

Service/experience 1/5
They mixed up my order (online). I have the receipt and everything. I called to ask them about it and the woman realized and admitted her mistake, and said they'd send the rest of the order over in 20 minutes. 40 minutes later, nothing. Called again a few times, and no one picked up.

Horrible experience. Used to go out of my way to visit/order from this place. Never again. Horrible experience. I ordered 18 empanadas and had some friends over, talking up the food, and was really disappointed when the only 3 came. Called to try and get it fixed, and they said they'd take care of it (after admitting the mistake) but one hour later, my guests were still hungry and I got us Thai instead. Go to Luck Thai. Pretty good and pretty reliable.

name: Velvet Brooklyn
document: Velvet Brooklyn. cuisine: Venues & Event Spaces Cocktail Bars Mediterranean. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This past weekend the Velvet Brooklyn staff hosted my 32nd Mean Girls themed birthday party in their private lounge. Jose the event coordinator & GM, plus the rest of the Velvet Brooklyn staff were all very attentive & just AMAZINGGG with helping make my celebration such a special night!!!! From helping me set up a laptop to stream the movie on their screen behind the bar while the party was in motion, to just being so friendly & consistent with checking in. The lounge was perfect for my party. I had private catering come in before I arrived to set up the food and again the venue was so accommodating in assisting my caterer with whatever she needed. The night was so much fun, all of my guests were having a great time. I had a great time & would definitely recommend Velvet Brooklyn to anyone who is looking for a fabulous space to host their special events. Also I would like to shout out the owner, Phil for also being so wonderful throughout the whole booking process. Thank you Phil, you have a great staff behind you - keep up the great work & I will be stopping by soon to enjoy some cocktails!!!

My fiancé and I recently had our engagement party at Velvet and it was better than we could have ever expected!

We cannot recommend Jose and the Velvet team enough! From the beginning, Jose was so personable and felt excited about our party. It was super easy to communicate with him and every interaction was so genuine!

Our party was so much fun and we received many compliments from our friends and family about the venue and the service. We felt like everything was taken care of and knew we were in good hands that entire night.

Even though our party is over, we now consider ourselves regulars! We would definitely recommend Jose, his team, and this venue for any private party or just for a night of cocktails! You can’t go wrong!

Jose and his team were incredibly hospitable and friendly throughout the entire process from initial contact till the very last minute of the event. Our private event was well organized and Jose frequently checked in with me and my guests to make sure everything was going smoothly. Not to mention the food and cocktails were all delicious! I highly recommend Velvet Brooklyn for any private event!

Came to this establishment on Saturday night with some friends. We sat at the bar. There are only 3 tables in this place: one by the window that seats about 6 people that was occupied, and another in the back, and one off to the side, also both occupied. I asked the waiter if I could get the table by the window when they leave. He said no, it's reserved. I said, "Okay, how about the one in the back?" He replied, "That's also reserved." "Okay, how about the one to the side?" "Nope, that's also reserved, and by the way, this bar is also reserved, so we have about 40 minutes until we have to leave." I've never felt more uncomfortable in my life. We are definitely not wanted here We are here, quiet, enjoying ordering ourselves having cocktails and food. He just smiled.Wont be back

there ever again

Velvet Brooklyn is incredible. I just had my Halloween / bday party in their private lounge last weekend and couldn't have asked for a better experience. The space is beautiful, and every aspect of the planning and hosting process was an absolute joy thanks to Phil (owner), Jose (GM/event coordinator), and the rest of the super kind, professional staff. I received a speedy response to every email, accommodation of all my requests, and the most fun, attentive day-of team ever. Thank you for a spectacular night!

name: Lucali
document: Lucali. cuisine: Pizza. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Every bit worth the wait! The pasta and pizza are both incredibly delicious. Some of the best I’ve ever had. The food comes out so quickly, it will catch you off guard. The service was so friendly and accommodating. BYOB, so bring your own drinks, no charge. People usually start getting in line a couple hours before they open.

Cool place with excellent pizza, calzone, and an off menu pasta dish. All very good - recommend keeping it relatively simple with the toppings. A bit hard to get a table here, you need to wait in line to get put on the list later in the day, so it’s a commitment. BYOB and cash only. Worth visiting if you have time in Carroll Gardens!

Finally was able to try Lucali thanks to Dorsia members night. Loved the cozy environment and the staff was so friendly, really good local neighborhood vibes. The special for members night included pasta which was spectacular, a salad, a meatball (also incredible) and then still followed by a full pizza, calzone and rainbow cookies. Plenty of food for 2 full meals for the days after. The pizza is a thin crust style that you don’t find in too many places. The sauce and ingredients all delicious. Enjoyed everything about my experience.

We got there around 3 pm and they started taking reservations around 4pm. The earliest time available was 6pm. We got seated at 6pm. We got the cheese pie which was very thin and airy. I did not have high expectations based on some comments but I was surprised. It was vey good and worth the wait. The wood fire oven always produces the best pizzas.

Wish it was easier for me to get here because the food was spectacular. Thought it lived up to the hype. Don’t know how often I will make it here, especially in the winter, but it’s definitely worth a trip at least once. pasta, meatballs, pizza, and calzone all delicious.

name: 5ive Spice
document: 5ive Spice. cuisine: Vietnamese Coffee & Tea Tacos. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Fantastic place for comforting Vietnamese food. We tried the Pho as well as some of their fried chicken appetizers. Highly recommend any of the pho dishes, as well as the Yuca Chips. I'm a fan of strong coffee and the Vietnamese Coffee was just right. I'd go back just for the coffee, indeed. Lots of space for big parties indoors.

A moderately priced restaurant on the West Village that caters to students and weekend tourists on a budget.
Not for discerning palates or first timers to Vietnamese fare.
The unappetizing gray color dough on the steam vegetable dumplings was way too thick and chewy, overwhelming the filling.
The grilled shrimp on the main entree were on the smallish side, the salad abundant in iceberg lettuce, and the fried rolls too greasy.
The bathroom well hidden behind a bookshelf, before 6:00 p.m. on a Saturday looked like it had not been cleaned since Friday night.
Once was more than enough.

Had such a great lunch at 5ive Spice.

Had the crispy chicken Bahn Mi and some spring rolls. Set my hangover right. Needed the greasy filling food, caffeine, and light beer.

Did a lot of liquid, Vietnamese coffee, Sapporo, and their home lager Ho Chi Min.

Love the bookshelf hiding the bathroom. Was a classy way of disguising it.
The 5ive spice pho was well worth it, a very generous portion of meat — all juicy and full of flavor. The short rib was especially tender. Broth was also very good with plenty of herbs. Recommended!

GET THE WINGS!! I didn’t take a picture but you won’t regret them.

Service is quick and direct. The pho is clean, well seasoned and served. Had both the beef and lemongrass chicken pho, both had plenty of protein!! So far the best pho in SoHo 😍

name: Mr Bao
document: Mr Bao. cuisine: Shanghainese Asian Fusion Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: We had all this food and drinks and we’re in an out in an hour. Can’t recommend this place enough. Every single item was beyond delicious, but personal fav has to be the mushroom bao. Very reasonable pricing: we ordered slightly more than recommended and both had a cocktail and dessert and we paid £40 each including service. Easy on public transport. Lovely lovely staff, and they popped a candle on my dessert for my bday. Already planning my next trip back

The fact that this is our GO TO place for every special family occasion says a lot . The ambiance is very Peckham cool, the service is always friendly and the food is most delicious. The umami flavours are epic. And the Specials. And the cocktails..And the fluffiness of the bao buns…And you need to book to avoid disappointment…And I could go on forever.

Wonderful place, I came here for an anniversary for the first time, and was not disappointed. Delicious food, lovely atmosphere and fantastic service. Our waitress was Jess, who I have to give a special shoutout to for her incredibly warm and friendly service which made our night even more special. (Her colleagues were also lovely). Everything was top-notch, what else could you want?

Went to Mr Bao with a large group for a birthday and the whole experience was perfect from start to finish. The staff were incredibly friendly and attentive, especially considering how big our table was. Everything ran smoothly and we never felt rushed.

The pork belly and brisket baos were absolutely next level, but special shoutout to the sticky BBQ corn ribs and the handmade dumplings which were unreal. The flavoured sake is also a must. So good.

Will definitely be going back. Highly recommend.

Always a delight! The prawn and tamarind bao specials are incredible. I also had the special cocktail, the Szchuan Spritz - one of the best cocktails I've had in a while! Ask for a taster of the cocktails to help you decide which one to get!
