We were here years ago and said no to a second visit but it's been years so we gave it another go. The experience was better. It wasn't busy at all for a Friday night and the service was excellent. It's not inexpensive, I got spaghetti and meatballs, the least expensive thing on the entre menu at $22. Not a huge portion but decent size, $22 felt high but food costs and labor are what they are. My wife got a bowl of minestrone soup for $9. Bread basket with 4 rolls comes with dinner, I'm a sucker for bread. Food was good though. We also got a carrot cake and a Carmel something, cake. I liked the carrot cake, my wife thought the Carmel one was just ok but they had a nice selection of desserts for around $8 each, a decent portion though so no complaints. They have their own parking lot and the dining area was clean and quiet. I say you try it and it looks to be a family business.

name: Malecon Restaurant
document: Malecon Restaurant. cuisine: Dominican. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We took the subway to Washington Heights to explore the neighborhoods and worked up an appetite.  I picked out the Malecon restaurant in advance after reviewing the menu and the many good reviews.    We were seated quickly and spent a few minutes looking over the substantial menu.    I chose one of the daily specials and my wife selected what she thought would be lighter a bowl of their Sopa De Pollo.

A server brought a plate of warm bread and after a few minutes our food arrived - it was plentiful!
I enjoyed the Pernil which was slow-roasted marinated pork, served with a side of Moro Gandules (mixed rice with pigeon peas).  The pork was so very tender and flavorful - would definitely order again.  Honestly, I was not a fan of the mixed rice (I do not love peas) but that’s my fault for ordering.

My dining partner enjoyed her bowl of Sopa De Pollo, flavorful broth with lots of big chunks of Chicken.  We shared a plate of Maduros (sweet fried plantains).  So tasty.

The prices were very affordable and the serving plentiful.  Although I thoroughly enjoyed my Pork, next time I would order one of the dishes with the roast chicken (you can see the rotisserie in the front window and an employee cutting up the freshly roasted chicken as you enter the restaurant.

Worst mofongo I’ve ever had. Not sure if it was just mine, but it seems like the garlic was burned. Taste was horrifyingly bitter. Will not be coming back. Churrasco was very delicious—along with the yuca fries.

Brought my mother-in-law from DR to eat here during 6:00pm rush hour. Medium frame 30's Latino fella with short dark hair approached me and directed us to sit where we like. Nice fella, professional, great customer service skills & well groomed. He should be in charge of reception, training and directing wait staff. Our waiter was taller thin older Latino. Upon seating noticed tables being properly cleaned. We Both ordered baked salmon, avocado, mashed potatoes, broccoli. Had to get up and speak to waiter because we decided to order salads. He had never come back to our table to see if we needed anything, except to deliver the food. I used the bathroom and it was very clean and cleaned with bleach. This is very important. The same fella that met us at the entrance also came to our table to give us a pan to take leftover food home and took my credit card to pay $75 bill. Super reasonable. Upon departure I gave tip to the guy that met us door, seated us, took care of bill , and gave us food tray and told him split with the other guy. Our waiter was very nice fella but needs a little training to make him the perfect waiter and he would get better tips. The food was good, didnt have to go to the bathroom in an hour, so this tells us kitchen must be clean. One drawback was the music was way too loud for us senior citizens. I felt like I was eating at bodega in Barrio where the 20 year olds are drinking all the time.  Music needs to be turned down 2 notches. The crowd was respectable at the restaurant.

Excellent service, best cubano ever. The sancochado was delicious. And their jugo de piña and batido de guanabana. Literally loved everything here, would prioritize eating here again next time in New York. Me encantó :)
I truly enjoyed the food. Ordered the shrimp mofongo and roasted chicken. VERY good. The Malacon drinks were sooooo good! And great service.

document: Emilia's Restaurant. cuisine: Italian. located in Bronx. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Phenomenal experience! Food, atmosphere, service & vibes were all perfect! I wish I knew the names of everyone that tended to our table, but you all were fantastic! Also and more importantly, thank you Gloria for recommending us this restaurant. I will be back soon!

Amazing. Amazing. Amazing. VERNICK does it again. All of the dishes were special but not too fancy. Apps, entrees and desert were all memorable. Atmosphere was perfect, energetic but not too loud.. the space is beautiful, built by a developer who knows what they are doing.  I’m going back for a second visit this month

The long wait for Emilia to open was certainly worth it. Really great service and excellent food all around. Tried a little bit of everything on our first visit and already have reservations to go back multiple times. An excellent addition to the neighborhood.

Emilia is Vernick’s newest addition to the Fishtown neighborhood!

The ambiance was stunning, loved the bar area and all the ambient lighting. Service was stellar and cocktails were great. The food fell a bit flat.

The standouts were the basil roma tomatoes, small but bursting with flavor. The pesto capellini was executed perfectly - nutty, garlicky and al dente. Dip the free bread in the pesto. The braised rabbit was tender and juicy.

The misses were the king salmon bruschetta and potatoes on the fire. The salmon bruschetta toast was burnt, you can see from the photo. Some bites were ok, but others we tasted the char too much. The potatoes on the fire was just one singular potato, also burnt. Our server told us these were smashed potatoes, I wouldn’t consider that true. $16 for a potato is crazy.

Overall, I can see this becoming a great spot for a date night or celebration. Just be aware that the prices are high for how small the portions are.

Top notch service and tasty dishes. Tried the Emilia Spritz cocktail which was quite pleasant. The Summer Breeze also received high praise. Our group of four shared a number of small plates and three pastas- all were delightful with the salmon brushetta and the mushroom radiatore being the standouts. The dark chocolate sorbeto was fantastic! Tiramisu was fluffy and sweet. All in all a great meal!

document: Peking. cuisine: New American. located in Bronx. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Once upon a time you came here for a good meal at a reasonable price. You arrived and the walls, adorn with portraits of politicians and Hollywood elites, welcomed you into the hallowed main dinning room. They elevated the atmosphere, but the overall retro feel balanced the scale, good food, fair price, strip mall, next to a convenience store or two selling malt liquor and 40ozs.

Fast forward to today. $18 cocktails, $80 duck, $49 Leek Spouts with Shrimp. The portraits have yellowed with age, the staff is still very helpful, but balance it once had is off kilter now. It's still next to a convenience store, in a strip mall, is fine overall food, but the prices are higher than downtown DC. In my opinion, the prices are just too high for the level of food.

You can tell by the ambiance that you've stepped into a place that had served famous people.  There is an old time classic Chinese restaurant vibe here.
The ambiance is gorgeous, the decor is history, with pictures of patrons from wall to wall.

The servers and staff are professionally dressed, I felt underdressed

Walked into the place around 2:50pm, as i read through the menu, and decide on the lunch special, the waiter says, sorry but it's after 3pm (3:02pm) no more lunch special.  Bummed, as now the prices from lunch to dinner are a 3-4 dollar amount difference, portion might be larger, but for one person, I didn't need more of just one dish, I wanted variety.

Everything was just basic, and the fried calamari's funnel cake like batter was quite sweet and greasy for me.

The wonton soup had a thick wrapper, well stuffed, not bad

Fried Rice was delicious, loaded with meat and shrimp, worth the value

Will go back to try the famous Duck when I have enough people to share it with, as it is at least $100 for the table service.

This place is one of the most famous Peking duck restaurants in the area, so it was incredibly crowded when we visited. The duck itself was delicious, and the other dishes were all above average as well. The service wasn’t unfriendly, but it wasn’t particularly warm either—pretty much what you’d expect from a typical busy Chinese restaurant.

Peking Gourmet Inn is an absolute legend in Falls Church. This place has been a community staple for decades, and it shows everyone from local families to politicians and celebrities has eaten here, and for good reason.

Their signature Peking Duck is the star of the show. It comes out perfectly roasted, and the staff slices it right in front of you with the kind of precision that turns dinner into a performance. The crispy skin, the warm homemade pancakes, the fresh scallions grown on their own farm every detail is next-level.

The restaurant itself is spacious and classic, but don’t let that fool you it gets busy fast. Reservations are definitely recommended. Parking can be tough (the lot is small and always packed), but once you’re inside and tasting that duck, you’ll realize it was absolutely worth the effort.

The Peking Gourmet Inn 🇨🇳 clearly has had better days…also prices are severely inflated and quality/price ratio is not there (xtip $222 for 2 adults + 2 kids).

Probably in a large group setting cost will get diluted, but still found prices too high for the experience and the food itself. Happy to have a second go to try other dishes, but I was not impressed.

Food wise the Snow peas with roasted garlic were very good, the ribs appetizer was ok, the rice and lo mein were also ok, and the famous Peking duck was a 7 out of 10 (the pancakes were dry & flour forward).

🦆 🍜 🫛

Avenue Gyro offers a fantastic experience for anyone craving authentic Greek flavors in a cozy, casual setting. The standout item on the menu is, of course, the gyro itself—packed with tender, flavorful meat, fresh veggies, and a generous drizzle of creamy tzatziki sauce. The pita is perfectly soft yet sturdy enough to hold everything together. If you're in the mood for variety, the restaurant also serves up delicious salads, falafel, and baklava for dessert, all crafted with quality ingredients.

The atmosphere is welcoming, and the service is friendly, with staff making an effort to ensure you have a great meal. The portions are generous, offering excellent value for money, especially considering the high quality of the ingredients. Whether you're stopping by for a quick lunch or enjoying a laid-back dinner, Avenue Gyro is a great choice for satisfying your Mediterranean cravings.

google_reviews.text:
One of the best ramen places in Vilnius. I went to Sakai two days in a row.
I ordered the special ramen; it was very rich in flavor.

Service 5/5. They managed to find me a spot when I called 30 min before, even though the booking system showed they were full.

This cozy and delightful ramen restaurant is precisely what one needs to combat the chilly -13 degree weather in Vilnius. My wife thoroughly enjoyed her ramen, noting that the soy meat was wonderfully juicy and the mushroom topping was exceptionally flavorful. The broth was perfectly balanced, not at all overpowering, and the noodles had an ideal texture. As for my ramen, I believe it had the most tender pork I have ever had the pleasure of tasting. This establishment is an absolute must-try for all ramen enthusiasts.

It was my first time visiting this ramen place. The atmosphere was cozy, and the staff were very friendly, which made a great first impression.

Unfortunately, I was slightly disappointed with the ramen itself. We were offered a spice sauce to add to it, and I tried a few times, but I couldn’t really feel any spice. The ramen turned out a bit too salty for my taste. When I asked what the sauce was made from, I was told it contained soybeans — that probably explains the saltiness.

The egg wasn’t marinated enough in my opinion, and the pork was just a bit too fatty for my taste. However, the noodles were absolutely perfect, and the cocktail I had was amazing!

Overall, it was a good experience — just a few small things that could be improved.

The best ramen I have had in Lithuania, definitely recommend if you are craving ramen. I visited Japan this year and this ramen is a very solid recreation. I would just like the menu to be expanded a bit, maybe in time. The noodles were very nice. The broth is very flavorful, maybe a touch on the salty and oily side. The meat was quality cuts, especially the chicken. For some reason the egg was whole instead of halved but perfectly cooked.
I have never understood why so few places invest in real chopsticks especially when the restaurant capacity is on the smaller side (even in Japan).

A Five-Star Slurp: Reviewing Sakai Ramen in Vilnius

​In a city filled with excellent dining options, Sakai Ramen manages to stand out in a spectacular way. My expectations were high walking through the door, and for good reason: this isn't just a popular spot, it’s a verified Vilnius favourite, boasting an almost unbelievable 4.9 stars across 500 reviews on Google. That kind of consensus is truly exceptional and set the stage for what turned out to be a perfect evening.

​However, a word of caution to fellow diners: do not just turn up without booking. This small, highly sought-after spot fills up quickly. Luckily, fate smiled upon us. Despite failing to secure a reservation in advance, we were graciously offered a seat right by the window, which offered a great view and a perfect, cozy atmosphere for our dinner.

​If you are thinking of visiting Sakai Ramen, be prepared for a singular experience. The menu is beautifully simple and focused, making it clear that the mastery here lies in one discipline: ramen. Do not come here expecting anything other than spectacular ramen; it is the entire star of the show, and rightly so.

​We kicked things off with the pickled and spiced cucumber, a starter that was crisp, cool, and offered a fantastic palate-opener with a hint of heat. For the main event, I chose the classic miso ramen with pork, while my wife opted for the aromatic garlic ramen. Both bowls were, simply put, amazing. The broth was rich, complex, and deeply satisfying, and the noodles were perfectly chewy. A great touch was the small dish of chili sauce provided on the side, ensuring we could dial up the heat exactly to our liking.

​To wash it down, I enjoyed a glass of the recommended red rice beer—a unique and refreshing pairing—and my wife chose a traditional sake.

​The overall service was excellent, moving with impressive efficiency without ever feeling rushed. From the moment we were seated to when our order was taken and the food delivered, barely 15 minutes had passed. Our waitress, Patritzia, was particularly accommodating and attentive, making the experience feel personal and seamless. Sakai Ramen is a genuine culinary treat and a must-visit destination in Vilnius.

If You find yourself in a charming Great Kills neighborhood of Staten Island, a world away from the city's frenzy, don't shy away from Da Damaso on Amboy Road. The charming atmosphere and aroma of home cooking with the  scent of family welcome greets you at the door, pulling you into a cozy space that feels less like a restaurant and more like a family's gathering.

​The menu is a love letter to the owner's hometown of Salerno, with dishes you won't find at your typical Italian-American joint. Each plate is a masterpiece of authentic, high-quality ingredients. Every dish we have tried so far tasted like it was  made with a secret family recipe passed down through generations.

​What truly sets Da Damaso apart is the warmth of the family who runs it. They treat every guest not just as a customer, but as a long-lost relative returning home. The owner’s son, who served us shared stories about the dishes. This isn't just a meal; it's a full-on cultural experience. You leave feeling not only incredibly satisfied but also like you've been adopted into a new Italian family. The owner/chef, his wife (that cooks as well) and the oldest son who always greets you with the smile are incredibly charming people.

​If you're looking for an authentic taste of Southern Italy without the plane ticket, Da Damaso  is the place. It’s an unforgettable experience that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of Salerno.

google_reviews.text: I loved Alkoefeia! This was our second time here and we will definitely be coming back! We ordered the kabseh lamb which was perfect for 2 and labneh which paired perfectly. The food is so flavorful and meat is so tender. It’s a small restaurant and can get busy pretty quickly. The service is great; the first time we came with some friends and stayed until closing and were not pushed to leave early.

First time ordering from here. I really like their online website, makes ordering super easy. And I like how you can get delivery through them rather than going through a third party app. There are coupons on the website too for pickup and delivery. We were able to get 15% off.

Our food was delivered a half hour later but the delivery person was very nice and found our apartment quickly and dropped the food off at the door which was great.

We tried the snapper and vegan platter ($30). The snapper was huge ($30)! Enough to share with another person. Was on a huge tray of rice. The flavor was good but part of the fish was overcooked and dry and tasted a little fishy. The rice was excellent. I enjoyed the vegan platter, the cauliflower was standout. I also liked the falafel, which had a good consistency, flavor and wasn’t too dry. Their garlic sauce is good too, and we ordered extra. Our friend’s chicken and meat shawarma platters looked really good and I would try a chicken platter next time (~$17 each). They also got the mint lemonade ($7) which they say is really good, I would try that next time as well. It looked super green and healthy, and like a slushie. They make the pita there and the pita was warm still and had a flavor! Didn’t taste just bland and doughy. It tasted a bit buttery and kind of like pizza dough. Only $1 extra for pita and they gave us a bunch.

This place definitely gives big portions for a good price. I would try some other food again!

Very authentic Middle Eastern food! We’ve tried several Middle Eastern–style restaurants in Jersey City and decided to try this one in Bayonne since it’s near a playground where my daughter was playing. It turned out to be so good! Much better than the places we’ve tried in Jersey City.

We ordered the chicken kebab platter and the lamb and chicken shawarma platter, and both were delicious. Highly recommend the mint lemonade as well. it’s incredibly refreshing!

Food and service were amazing and everything was super great. People there were amazing and I had such a good time while eating there. The employees came up to us multiple times to speak and it felt real and welcoming and not for show. They were very try easy to talk to and the atmosphere was amazing as well, It felt very homey and cozy and there was many authentic Palestinian decor on the walls and in the restaurant. Volume in the restaurant was also good, everyone was enjoying time with family and friends without being too loud. Before we knew it the food was out and it was very quick for a restaurant, time passed so quick while we were talking to the employees and having a good time that we didn’t even notice, Food was amazing. Would definitely recommend, this was my first time but I will be revisiting when I’m back in this city.

Hands down the best food in Hudson County. From the Arabic Chicken Shawarma to the Kunafah , everything is perfectly seasoned and incredibly fresh. The portions are huge, and the staff makes you feel like family. If you’re in North Jersey and haven't been to Alkofia yet, you’re missing out

document: Don Cheech. cuisine: Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
This place was such a great experience from start to finish. The dining room is beautiful with warm lighting, a chandelier, and that classic upscale Italian feel. It’s elegant but still comfortable, the kind of place where you can actually relax and enjoy your night.

We started with the burrata and it was incredibly fresh and creamy, perfectly balanced with the tomatoes and basil. You can tell they focus on quality ingredients. The fried croquettes were crispy and flavorful with a great dipping sauce. Both appetizers set the tone right away.

For dinner, the braised short rib pasta was rich and comforting with tender, flavorful meat. The veal with mushrooms was cooked perfectly and the sauce was smooth and balanced without being too heavy. Even the sides were done right, especially the Brussels sprouts which had a great caramelized finish. Every dish felt thoughtful and well executed.

Service was attentive without hovering and the pacing of the meal felt just right. Overall, it was one of those dinners where everything came together. Great food, great atmosphere, and a place I’d definitely come back to.

First time here!  The service was outstanding,  the food spectacular.   We came for the restaurant week special lunch.  We will DEFINITELY be returning.   Presentation and taste were amazing.  Loved it ll.
SECOND TIME:  Even better than the first time.  This time we came for the Prix Fix dinner.  Large selection to choose from.  Included appetizers, salad, main course and dessert for $39 per person.   Service was spectacular and food was AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS.

Adrian, was our waiter for my Birthday dinner. He treated us with royalty and respect. The food was impeccable. My husband is from Brooklyn and he said this is the best restaurant he’s ever tried on Staten Island. We will be back. Thank you Don Cheech for being so awesome!

I see why everyone raves about this place! I wasn’t sure how much I was going to like it because I like Italian but I’m not obsessed like some people are. It’s hard to find homemade pasta and a pasta that even outshines the fresh seafood it came with. The tripe is the silent appetizer that wins my heart. It was soothing and clean. I want this every time I come here. Our server Adrian was incredible and very kind. I will recommend this place to anyone who asks! Please come and support, I want this place to be here forever!

Amazing! Molto bene. Highly recommend if and when you are in the Staten Island area. Calamari was perfectly cooked. Burrata hit the spot and the black squid ink pasta entrée knocked it completely out of the park. Thank you Cheech and Don.

google_reviews.text: Came in for brunch and ordered the steak and eggs with potatoes and it exceeded expectations across the board. My girlfriend and I decided to dine at Violette's last night for an early Valentine's Day dinner.
As we have been in the past, we were extremely satisfied with our experience.
We've been coming here since it was La Botte and have always enjoyed the attentive service and delicious food. As a starter, we opted for the Focaccia and it was heavenly. The dipping sauces were exquisite and the bread delicious. For an entree, we opted for the Tomahawk steak for two and it was bursting with flavor. Cooked perfectly and sliced well, it's hard to beat and complimented our wine selection perfectly.
Our very polite and attentive waiter, John, offered to decant the wine (which I would recommend to anyone else who appreciates the steak/wine pairing).
The zucchini side was delicious, the roasted cauliflower underwhelming but passable.
For dessert, we chose the warm chocolate cake and it was positively delightful.
Overall, Violettes delivered as it usually does and we'll be back.
The check was a bit high, but you get what you pay for and it was worth every penny!

google_reviews.text:
Richmond Republic offers a mediocre dining experience where nothing particularly stands out. The food, service, and atmosphere are all just average, creating an overall experience that's neither impressive nor disappointing - simply adequate.
The menu delivers standard fare that's acceptable but not memorable. While the food is edible and will satisfy basic hunger, don't expect any standout dishes or exceptional flavors. Everything feels middle-of-the-road, neither excelling nor failing in any particular way.

Do not eat here.  I was served the worst meal I ever had.  Not edible.
I got a bad vibe when we walked in and no one was there. Not one patron.  It was late on a Monday so I thought maybe that was the reason. It wasn’t. The food is absolutely vile.
We were a party of six and were seated at a tiny table with the most uncomfortable metal chairs. We ordered 2 appetizers to share, and we all ordered burgers as our entrée.  The pretzel was more like soft bread than a pretzel and the cheese sauce tasted nothing like cheese.  The chicken wings were dry and cold.  Definitely sitting around for a couple of days.
Everyone got the smash burger and I got the Richmond burger. I asked for it to be well done.  It arrived pink and cold.  I sent it back.  When it came back it was on a new bun.  But when I cut it in half I noticed it was still pink and cold but it was very thin and falling apart.  What they did was they cut the top off and left the bottom of the burger that was cooked a little bit more.  They never put it back on the grill. It was ice cold and when they cut the top off they also cut the cheese off so all that was left was a thin layer of beef. When I called the waiter over to show him he said he couldn’t do anything about it because the kitchen staff left already.  That tells me that they never put it back on the grill, all they did was cut it in half and send it back. It was a shred of beef masked in a lot of lettuce.  Wish I took a pic.  Won’t ever return here.

I get there with a reservation for two. They seat us at a table for 6 and in the uncomfortable chairs they have. night.

name: Pho plus Vietnamese Noodles
document: Pho plus Vietnamese Noodles. cuisine: Vietnamese Noodles Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I ordered the tofu and mushroom noodles. In this cold winter day of February, where snow is still dripping from the roof of the building, I expected it to be hot in the restaurant. I walked into an igloo with winds fiercer than a boat out at sea when I stepped foot into the restaurant.

As for the food: don’t be fooled by the delectable description. It was two pieces of tofu cut up into 8 thin pieces. As for the mushrooms? CANNED. Canned mushrooms in an established restaurant. I won’t be returning, and I wouldn’t recommend it either unless you and your food enjoy hypothermia.

About the food

To any vegans/vegetarians, I would not recommend this place. While they have the option of vegetable broth with tofu and mushrooms, it is disappointing. The mushrooms were very obviously canned, and it seemed like they just cut small pieces of tofu from a bigger piece. Tofu and mushrooms are very cheap, so I don’t understand this idea of charging the same as the chicken option and not giving a decent portion. The broth was pretty good, but other than that, it’s not worth it.

I stopped in on one of the hottest, most humid days of the year after walking about 8 miles. It felt so absolutely refreshing to step into this restaurant, which was so cool and clean. The environment was completely relaxing and gave customers plenty of space to enjoy their meal. There is a restroom that was also clean and well kept. Then when the food came I continued to be pleasantly surprised. It was served so quickly and beautifully presented, while also being full of flavor. The crispy tofu bahn mi, summer roll, and pineapple mango iced green tea all continued with the absolutely refreshing theme of this visit. Best of all, was that the staff was just as amazing as the food. Brenda was so quick to help, answered all my questions and gave such useful advice. She was bubbly and sweet, making the visit even better! I look forward to returning, as it was an absolute pleasure!

If you're craving pho I highly recommend Pho Plus Vietnamese Noodle. Their broth is aromatic and packed with flavor, and the rice noodles are cooked to perfection. Plus, they serve it with all the traditional toppings like bean sprouts, basil, and lime. It's a cozy spot with great service. I really enjoyed the drinks menu they had multiple juice combinations that were multi colored.

If someone is following me they know I like Vietnamis PHO. So we went to try it on Staten Island. Place is lovely. So many exiting details such as sticks with restaurant name on them, call button with different options ( call, pay, cancel), gold spoons, plenty of decorations which makes this place cozy and comfortable. Start with drinks. There are a good amount to choose from. Mine with real fresh passion fruit was packed in clear plastic can and was sparkling and delicious. Summer rolls were ok. A lot of vermicelli, few shrimps, no any added vegetables. A peanut sauce wasn’t bad but wasn’t really good either. The star dish was beef Pho. Delicious rich broth, vermicelli and variation of different meat: ribeye, filet mignon, beef tripe and beef balls. To call this Pho great, one thing should be improved. Beef tripe was too chewy. You actually cannot bite it, you have to swallow whole piece. Overall you will enjoy Pho and will come for it back. I didn’t mentioned that as a compliment to Pho comes plate of bean sprouts, lime and basil. Volcano Wings sauce was basically more on sweet side than spicy, not too flavorful and I didn’t like the crunch on the top. It didn’t taste as somewhat connected to dish. But the meat was juicy and tender. Grilled chicken is one more dish we ordered. Chicken thighs were overdone, dry, salty with cold vermicelli. I will recommend to take a rice instead of vermicelli. Pickled radish and carrots gave some nice flavor and texture but honestly I don’t think I would order this dish again. Boring and the sauce that was served with it didn’t make any difference. In conclusion this place is a good choice for lunch especially if you like soups and fancy nonalcoholic drinks. Service was quick and helpful and as a bonus you can find a parking right by the restaurant.

name: YaYa Roasted
document: YaYa Roasted. cuisine: Chinese. located in Staten_Island. with 3.6 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Roast Duck
•	The roast duck is fragrant, with perfectly crispy skin and tender meat. The cooking is spot-on, and the slight char on the skin is incredibly satisfying. The flavor is rich but not greasy, with a well-balanced level of seasoning. A highly recommended dish.
•	The duck has crispy skin and juicy meat, with a deep roasted aroma that isn’t heavy or oily. It pairs well with both the dipping sauce and the sweet-and-sour sauce, and the portion size is generous.

Stir-Fried Beef Ho Fun
•	This dish has excellent wok hei. The rice noodles are nicely separated without breaking or sticking together; the beef is tender and flavorful. The aroma is strong and authentic—an outstanding example of classic Hong Kong–style stir-fried beef ho fun.
•	The rice noodles are smooth, aromatic, and well-fried, and the beef stays tender. The ingredients and seasoning are well balanced, not too oily, making it a very solid version of this classic noodle dish.

I always come here for the 3 meat rice dish 🙏 this place is better than King’s Kitchen 100% - the roast pork actually has crispy skin and has hoisin sauce, the chicken is smooth, and the cha siu doesn’t have excess fat and is marinated well. Rice also is like a jasmine/glutinous rice blend, very satisfying to eat :^)

Good staple in the community. Have been going here since the beginning and they have slowly expanded the menu to include more items. The service is fast and attentive and prices are fair.

Parking is limited so try street parking especially if you’re coming during a weekend lunch rush.

Ate hear twice this week, favorites hands down are the clay pot rice with eal & the fish / tofu entree. Also loved their rice rolls, made fresh not frozen. Super clean but owners make you feel like you're in Golden Unicorn but on Staten Island.
Yummy, authentic, bang for your buck. I recommend the duck or chicken over rice, and definitely get the lemon tea or HK milk tea

document: Yemen Cafe & Restaurant. cuisine: Middle Eastern Cafes. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: The food was good overall, though not exactly to my taste. I ordered Fahsa Laham, which was excellent and truly authentic, just like the ones I’ve had in the Middle East. The charcoal-grilled chicken and chicken haneeth were decent but a bit bland; they could’ve used more spice. The atmosphere was really nice, and they offered complimentary black tea, which was a great touch. The food was a little pricey, understandable for Brooklyn.. but I felt the taste didn’t quite match the cost.

TLDR: I haven't even eaten there but wow was it good. Definitely will be returning, the baba ghanoush and both the lamb leg/stews were insane.

Had this delivery at a friend's place and wow - everything was so tasty. Each order comes with this huge toasty pita that's perfect to mop up the sauces and plates.

The baba ghanoush was the first thing I tried and I loved the texture. Not overly whipped or too smokey. Kinda of like rice pudding without the grains, that's just how it felt as I dragged the pita through it.

The fahsah was this incredibly tender lamb stew that was my favorite. It's got a decent kick to it and that rich deep flavor. The lamb leg was also delicious, the edges are crispy but the meat literally falls off the bone.

The chicken curry was tasty too along with the grilled fish. I can see why this place is popular, definitely will visit one of their locations again in-person.

The level of hospitality these people offer is -to my experience- unmatched! They serve the guests free (yes free!) fresh baked bread with beef broth soup and some amazing side of pickled vegetables and lemons once you sit at your table, and the tea is also charge free and self serve! They also bring a free dish of side salad topped with the same yummy pickled chopped vegetables. The food is AMAZING, specifically the rice, which I could just continue eating forever! We were mainly surprised by how kind, generous and welcoming these people are. Will definitely go back!

We thought we would have leftovers- nope. So good! Unlimited bread refills too :D lamb fahsah was def the highlight

We were so shook bc so many things came out at first that we didn't order (bread, salad, soup).

Once Great, Now Deeply Disappointing 👎🏼 !

As a Yemeni who knows how real Yemeni food should taste, it honestly hurts to say this, but this restaurant is no longer what it used to be. It used to be one of the best and first Yemeni restaurants in NYC, but the quality has dropped so much that it barely resembles authentic Yemeni cuisine anymore.
I went recently with my cousins, and we all felt so bad about the experience. Some of us couldn’t even eat the food, including me. For the high prices they are still charging, the flavors, freshness, and overall quality are just not acceptable. It really feels like they are living off their old name and reputation, especially with customers who don’t know what true Yemeni food is supposed to taste like.
I’m not writing this to advertise anything, just to be honest and to protect the reputation of Yemeni cuisine, because this direction only harms it. I will do my best to reach out to the owners directly, because many of us would love to see this place return to its old standard. If you really want to experience authentic Yemeni food at this price point, I highly recommend Yemenat, the only Yemeni restaurant added to the Michelin list as one of the best in New York.

document: Joe's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
I just had to share my amazing experience at Joe’s Pizza — it truly exceeded all my expectations!

From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm, lively, and welcoming. The staff greeted me with genuine smiles and were incredibly friendly and attentive throughout my visit. It’s clear they take pride not just in their food but in making customers feel valued and comfortable.

Now let’s talk about the pizza — absolutely phenomenal. The crust was perfectly crisp on the outside while staying soft and chewy inside. The sauce had that rich, balanced flavor that tastes fresh and homemade, and the cheese was melted to perfection with just the right stretch in every bite. Every slice was packed with flavor, and you can really tell they use high-quality ingredients.

Service was fast and efficient even though the place was busy, which says a lot about how well the team works together. The staff were patient, helpful with recommendations, and made the whole experience even better.

If you’re looking for authentic, delicious pizza served by a team that genuinely cares, Joe’s Pizza is a must-visit. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly recommend

Joe’s Pizza (Broadway) is undeniably one of New York’s classic pizza institutions and often one of the first recommendations for anyone visiting the city. Whether you’re grabbing a quick slice or ordering a whole pie, it’s a convenient and iconic stop.

The prices remain reasonable, especially considering the location and popularity. However, be prepared for long queues—waiting times can easily range from 30 to 45 minutes, and sometimes even up to an hour. The line does move, but occasionally slower than expected.

Their classic cheese, Margherita, and pepperoni slices are the clear favorites—simple, well-executed, and consistently satisfying. Inside, you’ll also find plenty of photos featuring celebrities and famous visitors, which adds to the nostalgic charm and history of the place.

While there are certainly other pizza spots in New York that may offer more innovative or elevated flavors, Joe’s stands out for its legacy, convenience, and reliability. It’s less about being the absolute “best” and more about experiencing a true NYC staple.

Definitely worth adding to your to-do list when visiting New York—especially if you want a taste of pizza history.

FANTASTIC low cost pizza!!! This it's my one must hit place in new york and I'm so glad I did. The pizza is affordable and it's light, crispy and delicious. There is definitely a wait to get in, but it's all part of the New York experience!!! I will say that their deep dish pizza was not my favorite and I would not get that again. However, if I return to New York I would definitely, make it a point to go here again.  The staff is friendly and the amount of pizza that they turn out is unreal!!! There is limited seating, so don't be upset if you don't get a seat.

A Simple but Outstanding Classic New York Slice.
One of NYC’s most popular pizza spots, known for its thin, crispy crust topped with rich tomato sauce and plenty of cheese. Slices start at around $4.50, making it an easy and satisfying choice.

Just steps from Times Square and open from morning until late night, it’s a perfect stop anytime you’re craving real New York pizza!

This was my first time in NYC and the pizza was FABULOUS! Our driver recommended this place and stopped here at 3am. I was surprised how crowded it was during that time but that goes to show how great the pizza is! They say the pizza is great in NJ and NY because of the water. Whatever the reason, I wasn’t disappointed! Definitely recommend!!

document: Pommes Frites. cuisine: Belgian Specialty Food Poutineries. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Pomme Frites had a really cool atmosphere. It really gave like a little Belgian tavern vibe. It was a total hole in the wall but the fries were so good! They were super hot and fresh. Three of us shared the double order and that was plenty. Definitely worth the trip. We got the fries with the garlic aioli and it was creamier than expected. We were split on whether we liked it or not.

For many people this will be FIVE STARS. I want to make that really clear because if you like a thick cut fry that’s golden on the outside with a high “fuffly potato” ratio on the inside, you’ll enjoy it thoroughly because they’ve executed amazingly on that kind of fry. The problem in this case is me: I like a thin cut fry with more of the crunchy / crispy golden exterior and less of the interior of a fry. And they really are two different categories of fry. As far as execution on the former is concerned, it’s done well. I just don’t like that kind of fry. The black truffle mayo we got sounded great but fell very short of our expectations. Barely any truffle flavour and you have to buy truffle oil separately. The place does feel like a rendezvous for Diagon Alley’s shadiest wizards so that’s actually really cool especially because it feels like you’ve entered an olden times tavern restaurant in 18th century England. All in all if you like the thick cut fry scene they guys have executed beautifully, but if you’re like me I wouldn’t choose to come back here simply because of my preference for cut fries. I’m sure these guys would do an amazing job making those.

If you’re a fan of fries, this is the place to be! Pommes Frites truly specializes in what they do. The fries are perfectly crispy, and the variety of sauces is incredible—each one is delicious and unique. On top of that, the service was excellent and very friendly. Highly recommended! 🍟

I have been running a traditional Belgian frituur “Oma’s Frit” for 15 years 🇧🇪. I walked in here out of pure curiosity, because Belgian fries are not just food — they’re a network of tradition and perfection, built over generations.
The secret to real Belgian fries lies in the quality and variety of the potatoes, the type of fat used, and precise control of temperature and frying time. Even how many potatoes are added to the fryer at once makes a difference: if you add too many, the temperature suddenly drops, which immediately affects the texture.
A powerful fryer, the right fat, and especially the double-frying method with correct temperatures and timings are absolutely crucial.
In Belgium, potatoes are delivered fresh every day, and we mostly use Bintje potatoes because of their unique flavor and structure. Occasionally we switch to Agria, but nothing truly compares to good Bintjes.
With all that in mind, I was curious to give this place a try. I walked in… and honestly, I walked back out rather quickly. The bar for fries in Belgium is simply very high, and what I saw here didn’t reach that level.

This is not meant as negative criticism, just an honest observation: real fries… that’s something truly Belgian. 🇧🇪🍟

Cute and cozy shop great for a quick snack. Love the Belgium fry culture but these could have just been a *tad* more crispy to be perfect. Of course they have an insane amount of delicious dipping sauces!

google_reviews.text:
Fumo: A Must-Visit Italian Gem in Harlem
​Fumo on Amsterdam Ave and 137th Street is, without a doubt, a must-visit culinary destination in Harlem. My recent dinner here with my wife was nothing short of exceptional, offering a perfect blend of great atmosphere, attentive service, and truly amazing food.
​From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was vibrant yet cozy, setting the ideal stage for a memorable night out. The energy is fantastic without being overwhelming, making it a perfect spot for either a special occasion or a casual weeknight treat. The service was equally good—our server was helpful, prompt, and genuinely friendly, ensuring we felt welcomed and well-cared for throughout the meal.
​The true highlight, however, was the food. I ordered the classic Spaghetti Carbonara and it was sublime. The sauce was rich and creamy, coated the perfectly al dente pasta, and was exactly the comforting, authentic dish I was craving. The Garlic Bread served alongside was crisp, buttery, and the ideal accompaniment.
​My wife opted for the Penne alla Vodka and was equally impressed. The sauce achieved that perfect balance—tangy from the tomato and decadent from the cream—a clear testament to high-quality ingredients and skillful preparation.
​Fumo offers a complete and unforgettable dining package. If you’re in the area and looking for high-quality Italian cuisine that backs up its reputation, stop searching. This place is an absolute gem.
​Highly, highly recommended!

Great experience. Sat at the bar and our server Arturo was great. We got the spicy calimari, the arugula salad and the baked ziti all were really good. Wing bottles were also 50% off so that was great

I dined here tonight at about 5:45pm to celebrate my friend and her daughter's birthday along with my mom.

We were promptly seated inside and served shortly after. The first server, Steven, took our drink orders and gave us a little time to peruse the menu. We ultimately chose a rigatoni bolognese (friend's daughter), a penne vodka with meatballs (friend), a naked penne vodka for my mom and I had a spaghetti vongole. For drinks, my mom and I each had a raspberry lemonade and my friend and her daughter had a Fumo mocktail and a coke, respectively.

Now after enjoying our meals, two other servers came and we requested extra bread from one and he never brought it, even after asking an additional time. Steven immediately brought it right after we were able to get his attention. Also while busting the table, the other server from the two mentioned earlier, reached across without asking for clearance which rubbed us all the wrong way because he passed really close to my face.
This turned us off from tipping extra because the service was not great and I just thought I should make a note of it but other than that, everything else was good to go. I'll be back to try the brunch and other menu items.

I visited the restaurant on February 4, 2026, around 4:00 PM, and unfortunately my experience was very disappointing. The host was not welcoming and appeared disengaged, as though she did not want to be at work. My date and I were seated near a large crowd despite there being available seating on the other side of the restaurant. When I asked if we could change seats, the host responded with an attitude that made us uncomfortable.

After being seated, we waited approximately seven minutes without being acknowledged—no water, no greeting, nothing. Meanwhile, a guest who arrived after us and was seated next to us was immediately attended to. She received her wine before we received our drinks and her food before we received our appetizer, even though we were clearly there first.

When I politely addressed this with the server, she appeared frustrated that I spoke up about the lack of service. The situation made me feel unwelcome, especially given that this occurred during Black History Month. My waiter never came back. Fortunately, another waiter, Miguel, completely turned the experience around. He was attentive, professional, and ensured that the remainder of our visit was pleasant. His service was greatly appreciated.

While the food was excellent and the drinks were good, the overall experience left a lasting negative impression. Due to how we were treated, I would not return. I strongly encourage management to ensure staff are properly trained to provide respectful and equitable service to all guests, regardless of race.

name: Le Café Louis Vuitton
document: Le Café Louis Vuitton. cuisine: Cafes French. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Had the chance to visit Le Café Louis Vuitton, and it was honestly something I’ve had on my restaurant bucket list for a while. I was lucky enough to grab same day reservations, although we did have to wait a few hours but for a spot like this, I expected that. We kept it simple and ordered a couple of coffees and a dessert. Everything was beautifully presented, very polished, and felt luxurious without being over the top. You’re definitely paying for the experience and the setting as much as the food, but that’s kind of the point here. It’s inside a luxury store, so the whole vibe feels elevated and curated. Service was attentive, and it felt special just being there. Overall, I’m glad I went it’s one of those “try it once” experiences that’s fun to check off the list.

Beautiful restaurant. The layout is designed like a library, that may sound strange but you have to visit to understand. It’s very chic and inviting. Walking to the restaurant on the 4th floor of the store can be a bit challenging if you like Louis Vuitton, there plenty of it and the temptation to whip out that credit card may over come you so be aware. Gorgeous to say the least. However LeCafe was an exceptional experience in French cuisine. The meal I had was called the Afternoon Tea, it includes an assortment of small sandwiches and small desserts and your choice of tea or cafe. The sandwiches were all different and all packed with flavor. One of my favorite was the little cucumber sandwich, tiny but refreshing like a cucumber. The lobster roll was surprisingly packed with lobster all though the sandwich was tiny, the salmon sandwich has just the right amount of caviar on top to make the sandwich pop. I really enjoyed the taste of France in every bite. The dessert where to die for but my favorite was a little crispy number that taste like pound cake in a French way and it has this little yellow sauce that goes over it and really brings the flavor out. Most of the food and drinks have the Louis Vuitton stamp on them which is very exciting and fun, it’s like your literally eating Louis Vuitton. I really enjoyed it. By the way they sell chocolates also. It’s hard to get a reservation, but I definitely would recommend and return.

My experience at Le Café Louis Vuitton was truly unforgettable. I had the LV Culinary Experience, and it was hands down one of the best dining experiences I’ve ever had.

Our server was exceptional and made thoughtful recommendations — the ravioli, the steak, and the chocolate entremet — and every single dish exceeded expectations. The steak was cooked perfectly medium-well, exactly as I ordered, and it was incredibly tender and flavorful. The ravioli was beautifully prepared, and the chocolate entremet was the perfect elegant finish to the meal.

From the impeccable service to the refined atmosphere and outstanding cuisine, everything felt luxurious and thoughtfully curated.

A truly beautiful experience.
The atmosphere is elegant, calm, and very refined — exactly what you would expect from Louis Vuitton.
We ordered lattes and desserts, and everything was absolutely delicious. The chocolate mousse was outstanding, rich and perfectly balanced. My friend chose a vanilla-based dessert with hazelnuts and a delicate floral touch — both desserts were beautifully presented, with around five dessert options available, each looking like a small piece of art.
The service was exceptional. The barista took the time to explain how the dessert is meant to be served and even suggested the best way to enjoy it, which made the experience feel very personal and thoughtful.
The latte was excellent as well.
Expect to spend around $40 per person for a latte and a dessert, which feels fair for the quality, service, and overall experience.
The only small downside is that the café is very popular, so it can be difficult to get a spot. Other than that, everything was simply perfect. Highly recommend.

My husband scored this reservation perfectly. He traditionally takes the girls out for Valentine’s Day and I get to go too ! It’s very pretty inside. Yes the portions are small, but delicious. My lavender latte was delicious. All the food was delicious. The little dessert square they gave us at the end was delicious as well. It was a great way to celebrate, and in style.

name: Naks
document: Naks. cuisine: Filipino Wine Bars Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
The food and drinks were delicious!!!! Staff was quick and helpful. Decor was lively and chic. Restrooms were nicely designed and clean.

The Calamansi Spritz was so nice, lightly sweet and refreshing. Every thing I had was amazing, but my favorite parts of the meal this time (1st time) were the Kanton Fried Chicken (KFC), Pork Bbq and the grilled pampano. A new favorite spot!

Brunch food and service was wonderful I recommend. Omelet had wonderful flavors it came with toast and dried shrimp paste I would get again. The platter also great flavors nice portion. Pancakes delicious crispy edges and lovely sauce. Sampler cocktails really enjoyed the calamasi and ube smooth to drink the peach bellini were very strong. Server was friendly, sweet and fun.
Went for dinner service not a great experience idk if the server was new but she added things to our order that we didnt order,we ordered the pork belly platter for 2 it wasn't available and didnt find out for a while after ordering. The same calamasi drink wasn't as refreshing. The chicken app was good and the pork belly app was good. The server also got the placements of food and drinks wrong and was very out of it. Not sure if I would return for dinner considering how expensive it is it didnt live up to the pricing but brunch was pleasant and I recommend.

Went to restauraunt week Jan20-Feb12. Price was solid and the food was flavorful and distinct. Portion size was good and accurate to Filipino food according to the person I was dining with. The service, staff, and atmosphere were all exceptional. The restauraunt gets packed very quickly from opening, so reservations are probably recommended.

Had a great dinner at Naks in the East Village. The food was flavorful, well-executed, and portions were solid. Definitely a place where ordering a few dishes and sharing really pays off. Just make sure you book ahead because it fills up fast.

Starters:
The grilled pork belly was excellent. Nicely charred, juicy, and packed with flavor. Easy 9/10.
The fried chicken was also a standout. Super crispy on the outside, very juicy inside, and seasoned well. Another 9/10.

Noodles:
The stir-fried egg noodles with pork were comforting and well-balanced. Savory, satisfying, and easy to keep going back for. 8.5/10.

Entrée:
The dungeness crab completely stole the show. Rich, deeply flavorful, and honestly the kind of dish you wish you could eat all the time. A clear 10/10 and the highlight of the meal.

We added white rice and water spinach on the side, which were perfect to soak up all the sauces and round everything out.

Drinks:
The Ambaboy was solid but didn’t stand out as much compared to the food. 7.6/10.
The Ooh-Bae! was much better. Balanced, interesting, and paired nicely with the meal. 8.9/10.

Overall, the portion sizes felt fair, the food was consistently tasty, and the service moved well. It is a bit on the pricier side, but that was mostly due to cocktails. I’d definitely come back and would love to try brunch next time.

Naks delivers bold flavors and some truly memorable dishes, especially that crab. Worth the visit if you enjoy Filipino food done with care and confidence.

Tried Nak’s New Year special with the wine pairing and I’m still thinking about that sopas. The salpicao dry-aged beef with rice and bone marrow rice was crazy umami. Sinuglaw was chef’s kiss! The mango float was also a hit. I’ve been here before and the ube cheesecake and leche flan from the regular menu was the best I tasted in my life lol. Also, kudos to the crew, super friendly and really knows their stuff. Been telling my friends and coworkers to try it.

name: The Polo Bar
document: The Polo Bar. cuisine: American Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Ralph Lauren built The Polo Bar underneath his flagship store on East 55th Street and it is exactly what you would expect from the man who turned American style into a global brand. Dark wood leather banquettes equestrian art and a menu that reads like the greatest hits of American comfort food elevated to a level that justifies the price tag. The burger is one of the best in New York full stop. The crab cake is lump meat minimal filler perfectly seared. The wedge salad is classic and generous. Everything on this menu says we know what you want and we are going to give it to you done right. The crowd is a mix of Upper East Side regulars tourists who know what they are looking for and celebrities who come because nobody bothers them here. The bar area is always full and the cocktails are strong and well-made. What Lauren understood that most restaurateurs miss is that atmosphere is not decoration it is identity. Every detail in this room from the napkins to the light fixtures tells the same story and that consistency is what makes great brands and great restaurants. The service is warm and attentive they treat a couple on a date night the same as a table of executives. That democracy of experience is rare and valuable. The Polo Bar does not need to be trendy. It is timeless. And timeless always wins.

Great experience overall. The only negative thing to say is the ambient sound downstairs is very loud during dinner service. Hard to hear your own party at times as it feels like everyone at every table is collectively talking loudly. Great hot spot and celeb sighting joint. Hugh Jackman’s ex-wife Deb was there. Scott Caan was also dining the night I went. Food was very tasty. A touch pricey but it’s a near impossible reservation to get, so you pay it. Service was pretty good. The bar upstairs is the real winner for me. Elegant. Outstanding service. Fantastic drinks. In terms of food downstairs, the burger was solid and the dish of the night was Ralph’s Corned Beef Sandwich.

Difficult to get a reservation, but we finally managed to get one on NYE, and we had a wonderful festive dinner.

The entire staff was kind and welcoming, we were greeted by a nice man at the door and at coat check and our server was attentive and professional.

The decor is classic Ralph Lauren, elegant wooden moldings and polo motifs.

The cocktail menu is fabulous, so many great martinis to choose from.

The food is classic American fare, we ordered several dishes and everything was excellent. The steak was a quality cut and the burger is one of the best in the city, the biscuits and crab cake pair well together as starters.

Save room for dessert, we opted for the chocolate cake and childcare brownie with sambuca.

Nice spot for a date or a classy evening with friends and family. Hope to visit again soon.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Getting a reservation was not easy, but it was well worth it. The Polo Bar is a gorgeous restaurant with a classic New York feel. Service was attentive throughout the meal and the cocktails were excellent. The crab cakes were fantastic and the burger was great. Overall a great experience and definitely worth visiting.

unfortunately the hype is real. i thoroughly enjoyed my meal and would happily go again. one of the best burgers i’ve ever eaten. and the pastrami starter is a MUST order - truly such a rich and beautiful dish. the meal felt very decadent in general and if you can snag a reservation, you should definitely go

document: Kame. cuisine: Ramen Japanese Curry Salad. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The Spicy Tonkatsu Ramen had pork belly that were large pieces, meaty and tasty. With so so many ramen places in the City it is hard at times to know which one is worth checking out. Jeni and I had lunch here a few days ago. She likes bao and ordered the pork bun. This version had lots of creamy sauces on top which made it messy to eat. She still prefers the one at Ippoudo. With it she chose the Shoyu Ramen which she enjoyed. My ramen had an unusual flavor of the broth and it was spicy. Kame has been here for about six years and resembles a railroad apartment. The walls are grey and the atmosphere seems dark. Service was fine. Both cash and card are accepted. Two restrooms are in the back.

The #1 place for ramen 🏅

The ramen had an incredible depth of flavor but at the same time felt surprisingly light, so it didn't leave that heavy feeling you sometimes get after a big bowl. Everything tasted fresh and perfectly balanced, and the broth was so good I honestly didn't want it to end. The service was great, friendly and welcoming. If I had more days in New York, I would definitely come back again and again just for another bowl. Highly recommended for anyone who loves good ramen!

What an unforgettable experience! From the very moment we walked in, we were greeted with such a warm and genuine welcome that instantly made us feel at home. The service is truly top-notch—every staff member we interacted with was incredibly friendly, kind, and attentive. The level of hospitality here goes far beyond expectations and really sets the tone for the entire dining experience.

The food was absolutely outstanding. Ribs are crazy good! The Tonkotsu ramen was rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced—every bite was comforting yet full of depth. It’s easily one of the best bowls of ramen we’ve had. To finish, the pudding dessert was unbelievably fluffy, silky, and bursting with flavor, a perfect sweet ending to the meal.

Overall, the experience was nothing short of amazing. The combination of warm hospitality, exceptional service, and outstanding food makes this place truly special. Without a doubt, this is a 10/10 experience that we would recommend to anyone looking for not just a meal, but a memorable and heartwarming dining experience.

Rich and flavorful, savory tonkotsu ramen! Creamy onsen egg! Delicious takoyaki! Wonderful matcha pana cotta!

Attentive and friendly server staff. Chill vibes!

Highly recommend for a chill and delicious ramen spot.

Perfect spot to get a quick meal during a cold day! Walked in at 3:20 on a Sunday and were lucky to find a table. They close at 4 pm to reopen for evening service.

As expected, quick service, flavorful food, and surprisingly quiet ambiance. The place was at 90% occupancy when we were there.

They have a good amount of Vegan options thanks to their dedicated Vegan menu. Order anything that is labeled Spicy and for spice food lovers, it'll definitely hit the spot!

Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen ($20), and Spicy shrimp ($23) is what we got. Very flavorful and good portion size.

Highly recommended if you enjoy a hot bowl of Ramen!

name: The Tyger
document: The Tyger. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Noodles Pan Asian. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Tyger is an absolute gem and one of my go-to Thai restaurants. The food is consistently delicious, and I love how the menu evolves with creative and seasonal dishes. Their rotating cocktails are always beautifully balanced and pair perfectly with the food.

Standouts include the lobster noodles (when available), the fried snapper, crab fried rice, and gem salad. I’m also a big fan of the wok beans, house-made noodles, octopus salad, and fried chicken—each dish full of vibrant flavor and texture. If you have a little room left, don’t skip the tart for dessert; it’s the perfect finish to a wonderful meal.

Great food, welcoming energy, and thoughtful details make Tyger a place I always look forward to returning to.

I went to this moderately fancy, pretty popular Pan-Asian spot with one of my groups a while back, where, as usual, we split a lot of main dishes. They are a sister restaurant to the even fancier Chinese Tuxedo, with a menu that leans primarily towards ASEAN/Southeast Asian countries. The place was slightly loud and somewhat dim for photos, but thankfully, we were in a separate room, so the noise was muffled. The food was overall pretty good, though I prefer some other spots. This is especially given the price point, but it is nice to have solid representations of food from many different countries. To drink, I remember not being in the mood for a cocktail, so I went for the $14 Fiery Forge with Pathfinder hemp spirit, Lyre's Italian orange, pineapple, five spice, and pomelo soda. It had mild spices and a lot of citrus, and it was decent.

The first dish that arrived happened to be the best, the $38 Crispy Lamb Ribs with a Cambodian sweet & sour sauce. The ribs were crispy on the outside while remaining very tender inside, with the fat properly cooked as well. I was also happy that they weren't overly sweet either. This was very tasty and one of our easy favorites.

The Roasted Duck Breast for $32 with Chinese celery, Thai basil, dragon eye fruit, and plum dressing was also solid. The duck was cooked nicely, being tender with a mildly fatty texture, and the dressing was thankfully not overly sweet. I do wish there was a bit more dragon eye fruit/longan, but it was solid.

Also tasty, but the most expensive, was the 'Crying Tiger' Grilled Sirloin Steak for $46 with aromatic herbs, spicy tamarind dressing, and toasted rice. I have had this dish, also known as Suea rong hai, in many Isan/northeastern Thai spots, and this was solid. The steak was cooked nicely, and the dressing had a mild kick, with some roasted chilis for those who want a bit more heat. My only complaint is that I wish this were also served, as per usual, with sticky rice, as it's already a pricey version of this dish, and even cheaper places serve this traditional accompaniment.

The Newton Circus Sambal Stingray, for $28, with roasted skate and sambal belachan, was alright. It was comparable to most Malaysian and Singaporean spots serving this dish, though I preferred a slightly stronger sambal at some spots, and the fish was cooked better at others. The portion size was also daintier, although at least we didn't have to deal with the fish bones. For a better version at a reasonable price, I highly recommend Wok Wok nearby, on Mott Street near Confucius Square.

Last and least was the Singaporean Chili Crab Fried Rice for $28 with hand-picked Jonah crab and lobster oil. This is famous here, and I don't really see it. I liked the fried rice's seasoning and crunch. However, the sweet chili sauce overpowered whatever little crab there was. For a similar price, I would recommend the nearby Phoenix Palace, which had more crab flavor and was more balanced.

The food overall was good. If this were in another neighborhood, I would probably recommend it more, but there are other spots for ASEAN food that are a bit more reasonably priced and of better quality. It's still good, though, and certainly better than many other Pan-Asian places. This would be another 3.5, but that doesn't exist, so I'll round up.

🐅The dishes here are all very authentic and generously portioned. I highly recommend the sweet & sour lamb ribs, as well as the fried rice and water spinach — these are also some of the most popular items. That said, the drinks are honestly pretty mediocre, even hard to finish. But the service is great, and although the food takes a bit of time to come out, the staff are very friendly and attentive.

Many restaurants in NYC have the vibe and aesthetic but the food is subpar. Not the case with The Tyger. We went for NYE and the food was so good.

We had the:
Shiitake Mushroom & Glass Noodle Spring Rolls
Charred Octopus
Salt & Pepper Crispy Snapper Tempura
‘Pad See Ew’ Rice Noodles
Singaporean Chili Crab Fried Rice
Wok Tossed Heirloom String Beans
Morning Glory' Stir Fried Water Spinach
Good Morrow
Strawberry Serenade
Fiery Forge
Little Wren

Top 3 Dishes:
Singaporean Chili Crab Fried Rice
Charred Octopus
Salt & Pepper Crispy Snapper Tempura

Want to shoutout their amazing and accommodating staff as well. Will definitely be back!

Great Foody experience, went there with 5 of my friends, one of them is a French food tour guide we all loved the food.
Pan Asian kitchen very flavorful and well designed on the plate which really open our appetite. we started with chicken skewers , Fried chicken Papaya salad  and beef tartare, we had lamb chops, Roasted duck , noodles with mushrooms, fried rice and green beans , each dish was better than the other , Great service. We also had tropical cocktails which are also tasty perhaps on the sweet side of the map. The nonalcoholic cocktails were extraordinary tasty. Almost forgot we have tried all 3 deserts on the menu.. Go !!

We visited The Landmark Tavern on 11th Avenue. The steak was flavorful and well prepared, and the beer – especially the dark Guinness – was excellent. The burger, on the other hand, was nothing remarkable. The fried chicken fingers were decent, but very simple, and the fries came overcooked. What really disappointed me was the side dish: the menu listed “steamed vegetables,” which normally suggests peppers, tomatoes, corn, or maybe eggplant. Instead, I was served a full plate of broccoli. Since I cannot tolerate broccoli, this should have been clarified on the menu. A more accurate name would be Steak with mashed potatoes and broccoli.

Foods service and atmosphere were all great! The waitress and the bartender were super friendly and attentive; my hamburger (sirloin and Swiss cheese) was delicious as well as the French fries! I also had an Aperol spritz which was also very good. The place is very clean and there are tables suitable for all size of groups.

Incredibly friendly staff. Good portioned food with an excellent patio to dog-watch. Will be back! And yes, the mac and cheese is as good as it looks. 😋

Easily a recent favorite spot for sure. Love how the vibes are low-key. The lamb shank was incredible and really hearty. The shishito peppers were excellent too. A strong recommend for anyone in the neighborhood, ideally for 1-2 people.

This restaurant has such a lovely, intimate vibe and the food is even better than the ambiance. We ordered a bunch of things to share and nothing disappointed. It’s been a while since I’ve been but I feel like their prices have raised significantly since the last time I’ve been. Dead slow at 6pm on a Thursday. Food and service was great.

name: Osteria Delbianco Bryant Park
document: Osteria Delbianco Bryant Park. cuisine: Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Two weeks after a trip to Italy, my wife and I wanted to dine at an Italian restaurant where we can relive that authentic Italian dining experience. With Yelp's assist we stumbled upon Osteria Delbianco.
Located in a prime spot within earshot of Bryant Park, OD checks all the boxes for diners seeking a pleasantly satisfying Italian dining experience. A grand old-world exterior and restrained but stylish interior hint at the attention to detail with which OD prepares its meals. For appetizers, we had a burrata salad and beef carpaccio. Both were delicious but it's important to note that the carpaccio serving was minuscule and did not merit It's $22 price tag. We ordered a perfect bottle of red Mondavi wine for $70. For entries, we chose oven roasted sea bream, linguine al vongole and risotto with mushrooms and porcini. All were delicious, generously portioned and fairly priced. Service staff were attentive and pleasant - no small feat on a very busy Wednesday evening. Despite the large space, the noise level was quite high as we struggled to carry on a conversation without leaning forward and speaking loudly. Because the portions were large, we skipped dessert altogether.
I strongly recommend OD to those who expect first-rate Italian cuisine and don't mind a sometimes noisy and boisterous atmosphere. Mangia bene!
Great food, classy atmosphere, and an attentive staff. Healthy proportions, tasty deserts, and reasonably priced drinks. Highly reccomend it you are looking for great Italian.

Very disappointing experience. My aunt shared a small portion of her dish with a friend, and the server accused us of “ruining the plating” even after we apologized. For the rest of the meal, he kept glaring at her, which felt unprofessional and hostile.

At the end, they automatically added a 20% service charge without telling us beforehand, supposedly because we had a “large party.”

As an Asian family, we felt unwelcome and unfairly targeted. We don't know what we did wrong.
（Is this the new invisible racism, lol?）
Would not recommend.

I and 7 others came here to celebrate a friend's birthday. We had high expectations and they still exceeded them. I inquired about a spicy sauce for the complimentary bread, and the chef took initiative to make our table a fresh impromptu spicy sauce. The food was exceptional. All the pasta was fresh and delicious, the steak was perfectly cooked, and all the appetizers were served in good portions. The service was incredible. Staff was fun, helpful and nice. The prices were also very affordable. I plan to go back as often as I'm in the area.

I came to Osteria Delbianco on a recommendation from my hotel concierge after specifically asking for family-friendly restaurant options. Unfortunately, this place was anything but.
I was visiting NYC with my young child while my husband was traveling, and from the moment we were seated, the experience felt uncomfortable and unwelcoming. We were placed next to unfriendly couples (not entirely the restaurant’s fault), but the overall atmosphere clearly wasn’t suited for families with children.
The service made things worse. The waitstaff appeared annoyed when asked for menu recommendations and couldn’t offer suggestions without a grimace. Even more frustrating, no one checked on us during the entire 1.5 hours we were there — no follow-ups, no concern, nothing.
The food itself was decent, but nothing memorable, and certainly not worth the price. In a city like Manhattan, you can easily find much better Italian food with far better service.
Despite the lack of attention and overall poor experience, the bill came to $140 including tip, which honestly felt undeserved.
This was by far the worst dining experience I’ve had in NYC so far. If you’re traveling with children or looking for warm, attentive service, I strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

name: Hudson Local
document: Hudson Local. cuisine: Wine Bars American Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️🤩Major vibe! From the moment I walked in, I felt welcomed — every staff member was friendly, organized, and genuinely attentive. The energy of the restaurant is chic and inviting, with beautiful art and photography displayed throughout.

I started with the mushroom ravioli, which was perfectly flavorful and served hot. Then came the steak with broccoli and potato hash browns — absolutely top notch. The sauce that came with this dish was so delicious I could’ve eaten it by itself. I went with the wine pairing, and every pour was high-quality and perfectly matched to each course.

The presentation of every dish was creative and thoughtful — truly picture-worthy. Even with a packed house, the service stayed smooth and attentive all night.

Dessert was the perfect finish — a cornbread-inspired dish that hit that ideal balance of sweet and savory, and another vanilla and raspberry delight that was light, refreshing, and full of flavor. Both felt comforting yet elevated.

What made the evening even more special was learning that the menu was inspired by the chef’s childhood, paying tribute to his late parents who encouraged his love for cooking. You could really feel the heart behind every dish.

This is the kind of place I’d celebrate my birthday or bring friends to make memories. There’s even a grand piano in the dining area, so I’m sure live music will be a vibe on some nights too.

Highly recommend — 5/5, amazing food, amazing service, and full of soul.

What a great place in Hell’s Kitchen to have dinner. Excellent food ! We had the grilled cabbage - I don’t remember ever having such an amazing vegan dish.
We also had the hunger steak which was delicious.

Chef came over to check in and make sure everything  was to our liking.

Finally, Lacey recommended outstanding delicious and perfect wine pairing to our selected dishes.

Will definitely be back !

Amazing night!! Great location, wonderful atmosphere. No complaints, I am very satisfied. The staff was extremely accommodating. Especially enjoyed the sommeliers insight on wine pairings. The food is some of the best I have had in the city, everything was really amazing. The summer medley vinaigrette I could DRINK! And by far the chicken tartine is a must try. Can’t get over how juicy it was!! My favorite of the night was dessert with the Eton Mess. To die for. Highly recommend this place, you won’t regret it!

Even if I could give the folks at Vu 10 stars, that wouldn’t be enough. They went above and beyond for our anniversary dinner, from complimentary bottled water to the chef bringing our meals out and explaining them. The wait staff was friendly and genuine, and the surprise free champagne was the best nightcap ever (until we went upstairs to their sister property, Vu, for sunset cocktails and more unexpected VIP treatment)!

The menu is so much more accessible under the new ownership. Our meals were very different but each nailed it on every level. We WILL be back!

This amazing place has quickly risen to the top of my favorite spots in NYC. The menu is phenomenal, I’m a huge fan of the burger and hanger steak. It was my second time dining there and the General Manager Lacey remembered me from my first visit which was a great personal touch. Lacey is always so friendly, warm and welcoming, she is beyond knowledgeable when offering great wine pairing suggestions. The cocktail selection is also incredible, I recommend the Cucumber Gimlet its beyond refreshing and delicious. This is definitely a place you have to experience.

google_reviews.text: This classic New York burger joint is a small, well-known spot right in the heart of the city — easy to find and something of a local legend. The beef wasn’t quite what I expected — to be honest, I think the big burger chains taste a bit better. But the loaded fries were really good, and the service and atmosphere were decent. Overall, a fair spot for the price!

Best Experience Ever Mariah is the best!!!!. Ive seen this going viral on social media and decided to give it a shot!. Mariah helped me pick the best options , was all so very kind A1 Customer service Make sure to ask for her and leave a tip shes so sweet!
