Place is a little crammed when crowded could be a little difficult to find parking but overall 10/10 experience.

I definitely recommend giving 7th street burger a try make sure to check it out thanks 7th burger & mariah for making my experience!!! as great and welcoming as possible I WILL BE BACK!

(Not my finest pictures, but I was cold and hungry)

A really nice smash burger, you definitely taste the beef. Honestly, it’s the perfect burgerfication of “beauty in simplicity”. Fries were ok, the burger is why we’re all here.

Only downside is it’s a bit of a wait, but definitely worth it. Consider getting two as you will get hungrier as you wait.

Not many seats inside. Could be cleaner.

OK, so this is the place that’s been blowing up on TikTok? Super overrated. Glad I tried it, but there are so many other better burger chains. (The cheeseburger is the size of my palm.) The spicy jalapeno loaded beef fries are pretty good, though.

Jacob is a fantastic person. I was hungover and really hungry, heard about this spot online, and was the first customer at 11am. He was very friendly and offered a free drink since I was the first customer. Fantastic burger and fries, and then just as I'm getting too full to eat another bite, he gives me a second burger for free. I mean, unreal customer service and great food. Can't ask for more. Thank you Jacob.

name: Gramercy Tavern
document: Gramercy Tavern. cuisine: New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
If I had to become a regular anywhere, this would be my pick. You can tell how impressive this restaurant is by the way they execute American cuisine—which, as you know, is usually my least favorite. But they absolutely nailed it.

I was genuinely so pleased with everything. The farm chicken with the onion rings were standouts. Crispy, perfectly fried. The beef steak sandwich looked incredible, but I was way too full to even take a bite—so I’ll definitely be back and will keep you posted. The beef carpaccio was delicious, and while the mushrooms pasta were slightly salty, the creamy, flavorful sauce paired perfectly with the sweet potato bun. (This is their restaurant week menu!)

And let me just say—the desserts are a must. You have to get the apple pie. It was amazing, especially with the hint of balsamic vinegar and Parmesan—holy moly!! The chocolate cake came with a woodside-flavored ice cream that I had never tried before, and I absolutely fell in love.

The back room is stunning, and the service is easily the kind to deserve 30% tip—attentive, polished, and welcoming. This is also an amazing spot to bring your partner to meet the family!

We had lunch at Gramercy Tavern on Sunday with a group of four, seated in the Tavern area rather than the formal dining room. The cocktails were a fantastic start—absolutely 5 out of 5. The staff was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was lively and welcoming.

The flatbread was excellent, one of the highlights of the meal. But overall, I was hoping for a bit more from the rest of the food. We tried the burger, pork shoulder, swordfish, tomato salad, and liver mousse. While some dishes were fine, the burger and pork shoulder in particular were disappointing and just didn’t hit the mark. The salad and mousse also felt a little ordinary.

For a place with such a strong reputation—and at this price point—I expected the dishes to shine more. Still, the service and vibe were wonderful, which made the experience enjoyable overall.

If I had to rate it: 5 stars for service and ambiance, but about 3 stars for the food, so overall a solid 3 stars.

Excellent dinner from start to finish.
The seasonal menu was thoughtful and well executed, with great balance and high-quality ingredients. The lamb main was cooked perfectly and full of flavor, and the overall pacing of the meal felt just right. Desserts were refined and not overly sweet. Professional service and a relaxed, elegant atmosphere. Would definitely return.

First off; special shout outs to Kamor and Morgan for exceptional service and for an exquisite experience. My daughter brother and I went out for my brothers birthday and had a phenomenal time. Thank you to the whole staff for their fluidity and expertise on every single dish that was presented. We shall return soon

Really lovely place to dine! Food is delicious and staff is amazing. Host staff is one of the best in the city! The burger is divine, but don’t miss out on the seasonal pastas either! And you can’t miss the chocolate chip cookie with milk. They have a coat check as well which is really nice.

Would definitely recommend you have a reservation or look for seating at the bar.

name: Lin & Daughters
document: Lin & Daughters. cuisine: Noodles Chinese Bubble Tea. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I nominate this place for Bib Gourmand!
Yes, seriously- this is one of the best Asian food I had in a while outside of what I have eaten in China. This is a tiny place with huge taste! Unpretentious little hole in wall place, you are there to eat, it’s not about the tables or decor. One of my pet peeves is kitchen smoke and smells - and given the size of the place I was expecting that we would be smoked like fish by the time we finished eating. But incredibly not even a bit of kitchen smoke or anything. We enjoyed the dishes so much we were speechless! I am still thinking about the broth, the crunch on the noodles dish, the unique cumin potstickers.. and so on. If I lived in the area I would become a regular. The quality of food and taste this place is serving out is incredible - so in my book it’s worthy of Bib Gourmand designation!  Thank you, owners, cooks, and every person that contributes to this magical food spot - your food fed our eyes, stomachs, and souls - doesn’t get better than that!

Tiny little restaurant in the west village serving up familiar Chinese cuisine, not the classic NY takeout with neon sign, more regional and homemade stuff here.

We got the Brother Lin’s Beef Noodle Soup and Sister Lin’s Chicken Noodle Soup. Both, in my opinion, were very good. I found the Beef soup to be more flavorful and savory, the broth was had a more punch, not to mention the very tolerable spice level too. The Chicken soup would be perfect on a cold or sick day and felt a bit healthier / simpler.

The prices are a bit higher than those spots in Chinatown serving up similar fare, but, this is obviously catering to the neighborhood and with that, convenience is at a price.

The food is good and I would recommend! There’s about 3 tables inside and also 4 bar seats, so keep that in mind.

food here is amazing!! we got the beef soup & the chili lime dumplings as well as the milk tea & it was all 10/10. customer service was also great, love the atmosphere in here, i had trouble choosing food because it all looked so good!! definitely recommend & will come here again! we left empty plates & with our bellies full

I know West Village rents are crazy, but this is basically the same food as any of the Fujianese noodle/dumpling shops in Chinatown at 3x the price.

The ingredients are a notch or two higher, and everything is made fresh (no batched and lukewarm fried dumplings). And you get a top 40 Spotify playlist too, I guess, and signature "sauces" that are for sale.

I can't fault the business sense to be honest, but $15 for dumplings I guess is something I'm just not ready for.

This is such a cute and cozy place 💙 the kind of place you can go as a party of one, two or three and enjoy good food. The menu is on the wall when you walk in, the sake offerings and food and the server was very friendly and helpful. This is your little romantic restaurant to get close, or go with your bestie to hear good news or take your kids for one on one dinner and listening time. We really enjoyed the ambiance. The food was good, I had the shrimp dumplings, he had the beef noodles. What I loved - the dumplings had a fat, juicy full shrimp inside. What he loved - his dish was just the right level of spicy. We both loved the sake. I want to go back and try the peanut butter noodles and just enjoy the vibe, relaxing, romantic, sweet and lovely place to dine.

name: Coppelia
document: Coppelia. cuisine: Cuban Latin American Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Rating: 9.5/10
Date Last Visited: 1/25/2026

We ordered the Lomo Saltado ($30), Shrimp and Grits ($28), Mofongo Con Constilla ($30), Churrasco ($29), Steak Frites ($32), Ceviche ($17), and Dulce De Leche Pancakes ($17). Almost every dish was amazing, but the lomo saltado is the star of the show. The combination of the beef short rib, onions, tomato, and fries along with the sauces is perfect. The beef is extremely tender and the dish is super flavorful. It’s worth going to Coppelia just to eat the lomo. For brunch, the shrimp and grits is really solid too, but a bit pricey for just four shrimps. The pancake was amazing too. For the dinner entrees, the churrasco and steak frites are also really good. Coppelia does a good job on all their dishes and I’m a huge pan. Overall, I would 100% recommend this place.

Had a gift certificate so decided to try brunch here. Sat at the bar easily on a Sunday morning around 10am, no wait. Food is fine - could be hotter. Had to flag waiter down a few times for more coffee and check. Definitely some character customers in here since they are open 24 hours (people ending their night here - still drunk). Not blown away, don’t think I’ll come back.

AMAZING EXPERIENCE, i am absolutely coming back here again. we ordered the shrimp and grits, oxtail empanada, mofongo w the beef, and the dulce de leche milkshake. the shrimp and grits was out of this world, so creamy and delicious, the grits reminded me a little of mashed potatoes. the oxtail empanada was much smaller than i thought, but really nice flavors and the crispy plantain on the bottom was to die for. the beef in the mofongo was so so tender and delightful, it basically melted in my mouth, I would highly recommend. the mofongo also was so flavorful and had a nice kick to it! the milkshake was nice, not my favorite idk what i was expecting but it was lovely and sweet. they also only have fufu and oxtail during dinnertime so keep that in mind, i definitely got to come back to try that next time!! also the service was outstanding, very kind and welcoming staff. when i went in for a table, they originally only had seating at the bar and a table would be a 15 min wait so we just decided to sit at the bar, but later the kind gentleman notified us that a table had just opened up and they helped us get acquainted. it got a bit loud at some point but thats to be expected in such an amazing restaurant where people come to enjoy some good food. overall an outstanding experience and i am so excited to come again soon

It is one of the only places in the city that opens 24 zh hours. I love that convenience.
I usually get chicken for the main course , Arroz con Pollo is delicious as well as the pollo a la plancha if you like the spicy kale.

Service is always great, but this time,staff went the extra mile. Thank you very much Sandro for the great experience, as well as Pedro for your great work being our waiter.

This took me back to early New York. It’s set is the beautiful Cuban diner, with a classic diner touch and a Cuban flare. The food was perfection. I had the Salmon with purple mashed potatoes. My date had the Lomo Saltado. I had a wonderful Dulce De Leche milkshake and my date had the Sangria. I also had an oxtail empanada that was made like I landed in Cuba. The atmosphere alone would make you stay, but the food will make you linger. The Mojito is one of the best that I’ve had in the city. My new favorite spot.

name: Roberta's
document: Roberta's. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Buzzy/noisey atmosphere at the entrance, good host and reception with drinks at the bar before table was ready. Waiters not really alert, they messed up with my order, still smiley at least.
The pizza is very good/authentic Italian, average price 20 dollars each, but the service is very slow(and I mean it). Can’t say I loved the dessert as I left most of the pancake. Will still be definitely back as the it’s probably best pizza in Brooklyn.

A very local place, which creates an excellent atmosphere. Their pizza oven looks and smells incredible, but in the end, the result isn't anything amazing. I ordered a pasta dish with guanciale, which had more pepper than guanciale flavor, and the pizza, even though I ordered the "most popular" one, wasn't bad, but it wasn't anything special either, considering the incredible oven they have.

Kitchen cool Brooklyn vibe. Indoor and outside seating.  2 bars. The one we were at you could get food from, but every time you went back up for anything such as a drink or anything like that you had to stand on an enormously long line and wait quite a while, which wasn't great. The meatballs were very good, and the regular and Margherita pies were very tasty. Crust was soft, not crispy and thin.

Note, only gave 4 stars for atmos as we were cold, though they had just opened.  We visited Bushwick as my boy is a huge fan of DIIV who use to live and play in the area.  I wanted to try one of the Roberta’s and when my boy pointed out the small sign we thought that surely can’t be it. It was 11.30am and I opened the door to see quite a fair sized restaurant. A chef came out and told us they open at noon. He then kindly brushed the snow off a nearby bench and said why not wait. We ordered 3 Margherita pizza’s and four drinks. The pizzas were very good and my son wished he hadn’t shared with his mum, so I gave hime some of mine. The house red wine was a little rough but enjoyable! We paid by card and it came to about $103. More than we’d pay in Sheffield at our local joint “Porter Pizza”. For us though it was a unique and enjoyable experience and we enjoyed our day in Bushwick and my son would like to live there. Oh and the staff were lovely and I was surprised that no tip was asked for on the card machine, so I gave a cash tip.
By the time we left at 1pm the restaurant was full.

A cozy atmosphere and delicious food. We ordered Fesenjoon and Koobideh Kabob. The kabob was good, the fesenjoon was amazing! The interior had beautiful Persian-style details. name: Walter's
document: Walter's. cuisine: New American Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
It is a good bar for sports enthusiasts in front of Nats Park! This place is big, with indoor and outdoor seating, a massive beer wall, and 16-screen TVs that are perfect for catching all the action, not only for baseball. The atmosphere is lively, with friendly and attentive staff.
The food is good and the service is fast.
The menu's got something for everyone, from classic bar favorites like wings and burgers to elevated options like pork belly bites. The drinks are also great, and their craft selection is on point.
Located near Nationals Park, it's the perfect spot to grab a bite before or after a game. Just be prepared for crowds on game days! As in any place in DC, parking is hard, but it is within walking distance of the Metro station. They also have some special events.

Walter’s is a perfect place to grab a bite before or after a Washington Spirit game at Audi Field. The food was good, the menu appropriately varied, service was fine (a little slow given how empty it was), and the atmosphere was classic sports bar but there’s plenty of outdoor seating and only a 10 minute walk to Audi. We plan to make this our regular pre-game spot. Why mess with what works!  I would recommend a reservation normally though - we’ve been by here before and it’s been packed before Nats games.

Stopped here on my way home from D.C. and the food was delicious! The steak in the steak salad was seasoned so well and my burger was cooked perfectly. The old bay on the spinach and artichoke dip was the best. Can’t wait to go back.

The location is perfect for pre-game or post-game gatherings at Nationals Park, or catching other sports with good company. Lively but not overwhelming; perfect for group banter without shouting. The outdoor patio offers a relaxed vibe for all ages. Our server was wonderful, she was very attentive and friendly even though it was a busy time for her. The food was great and reasonably priced.

I love everything about Walters! Great dinner options! Wonderful staff! And tons of TVs!

The bartenders are amazing everyone is so attentive and friendly.

It’s great for a family dinner too.

name: L'industrie Pizzeria
document: L'industrie Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
A New York staple that everyone needs to try at least once when visiting. Get in line before opening because this place gets busy fast.

Their pizza is classic, cooked to perfection with fresh ingredients. The pesto slice is a standout. Bright green sauce layered over bubbling mozzarella, finished with fresh basil and creamy dollops of ricotta. The crust is thin but sturdy, with that perfect balance of crisp bottom and chewy interior.

Definitely want to come back try more

It was our third time in NYC and we had always been pretty disappointed in the pizza there. We decided to give l'industrie a try since we were staying in Brooklyn, and are so glad we did. Our expectations were not high due to the previous sub-par experiences eating pizza in NYC, but this place has changed our minds.

We did half Fig Jam & Bacon and half Burrata. The pizza tasted fresh, and the flavours were a great combination (especially the Fig Jam & Bacon). They offer free hot chili oil as a condiment, which really complemented the pizza. There is no seating, but some standing tables if you wanted to eat in the resto.

In terms of wait, there was a decent queue even for the Williamsburg location. We waited around 20 minutes in the queue, then another 15 minutes after ordering. Staff was friendly and helpful. We would definitely come back on future trips to NYC.

Delicious pizza! I’m very happy we got to try. Super thin crust, but not crunchy, which I love. The toppings were delicious as well. Def recommend the fig and bacon, pepperoni, pesto mushroom and the pesto sausage. Get the olive oil cake as well, it was the perfect dessert.

Finally!!!!!

I am usually not the biggest fan of American pizza - it is too greasy, too thick, has a little too much going on but wow this was a perfect slice.

a burrata pizza is a must. I got also New Yorker and omg it was so so good. The price are higher but so worth it. And they have beer which is a plus.

Pizza with a side of Perroni - incredible!

This was a must visit while my daughter and I were in the area. Especially with all the rave reviews and people saying this is the best pizza in all of NY. Is it good?? Hell yeah!! With how popular the place is it does get a little cramped inside (especially on a rainy day), however, there is a constant flow of people coming in and out so you can find a spot to hover over as you ingest these delectable slices. Ordering process is straightforward and quick and once you pay you find a spot and then they bring the slices out to you. We ordered 3 slices even though 2 would suffice however this isnt some place thats convenient for us being on West Coast so had to just walk a little bit more to work it off! All the slices were fantastic in their own way though the Sausage and Pesto was my favorite, followed by the Margherita and then the L'Industrie. I think I would have enjoyed the last slice more but I was getting full. Ingredients are all top notch and I just wish I could try some of their other offerings. Another time perhaps!

name: Cecconi's Dumbo
document: Cecconi's Dumbo. cuisine: Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 3.5 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: We were here for a Friday night dinner with our toddler. This is a nice and warm place tucked inside a building same as the time out market. This place felt effortlessly cozy the moment we walked in - perfect place for a date night. The service is attentive and the staff genuinely makes you feel welcome. We ordered whipped ricotta- truffle honey, eggplant parmigiana, a side of roasted potatoes and a wood fried pizza. Everything tasted good. Whipped ricotta is my personal favorite. Ask for free focaccia bread which tastes amazing with the whipped ricotta.

We celebrated our anniversary here and couldn’t have picked a better spot. The team was incredibly kind and attentive and they set us up with an amazing view of the Brooklyn Bridge that made the night feel even more special. The food was outstanding. The pastas were perfectly prepared, tasting truly authentic and homemade, and the salmon was cooked to perfection, moist and flavorful with no dryness at all. An unforgettable experience from start to finish.

Went for an early birthday celebration to Cecconi’s in Dumbo and had a wonderful time. The food was good, service was great, and the views were beautiful. One thing to note is that it is located in the same building as the Time Out Market, so we were walking around looking for a separate building for a few minutes until we realized. We appreciated the fact that they were timely, our reservation was set for 7:15 pm and we were outside seated by 7:25 pm. We sat outside in the middle of October and it was not cold, they had heaters set up all around.
Our favorite dish was the truffle honey whipped ricotta, incredible! Order their free focaccia bread basket and it goes great with it. Food was good, not excellent but the ambience and the service made up for it. Wonderful date spot / somewhere to celebrate a special occasion! Recommending coming after sunset go get a beautiful view of the bridge.

I visited Cecconi’s with my friend and left feeling a little mixed. The space itself is undeniably beautiful, and the view of the Brooklyn Bridge is really something. It looks like the kind of place where the food should blow you away, but it didn’t quite match the vibe.

We ordered the Orechiette Arrabbiata, Eggplant Parmigiana, and two Tea Amo desserts. The pasta was alright, but the eggplant parm felt underwhelming, especially for the price. I also wish they had more vegetarian options on the menu. For such an impressive restaurant, the selection felt limited. The drinks were good I enjoyed that for sure.

Parking in the area is rough, so plan for extra time if you’re driving.

The highlight of the night was the service. Our host, Juan, was genuinely kind and attentive. When I mentioned I didn’t love the eggplant parm, he surprised us with cookies on the house, which I really appreciated.

Overall, amazing ambiance and great service, but the food didn’t fully deliver for me.

Cecconi’s in DUMBO delivered an exceptional dining experience from start to finish. The food was absolutely amazing—beautifully prepared, full of flavor, and clearly made with care. The service was genuinely untouchable; every staff member was attentive, warm, and perfectly timed without ever feeling intrusive.
The atmosphere alone is worth the visit, but the view is what makes this place unforgettable. Looking out over both the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges is stunning, and it’s the kind of backdrop that makes any meal feel special. I can’t wait to come back in the summer to enjoy that view again with the warm weather.
If you’re in DUMBO and want a combination of great food, exceptional service, and iconic NYC scenery, Cecconi’s is a must-visit.

document: Vera's. cuisine: Southern. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Great food, drinks, and atmosphere!  Cocktails are creative and well balanced -- we had the Three Dollar Bill and the MUSTAAAAARD (which should not work, but does).  For food we got the shrimp and broccoli rabe flatbread special, the meatballs with polenta, the garlic cheese bread, and for dessert the tiramisu.  Everything was fantastic.  Probably one of the best tiramisus I've ever had.  This worked out to about $40/person.  We will definitely be back!

This place... Mama Mia!! This is an awesome cocktail bar 🍸 with an Italian 🇮🇹 flare and modern entertainment. They have a seasonal menu, so my husband Michael and I weren't able to order what we were craving since the last time we were here (a little over four months ago; we live in South Bend, Indiana); however, their current menu didn't fail to impress. The Chicken 🍗 Piccata 🍝 was delightful and mouthwatering, while their signature drinks definitely wet our proverbial whistles. We ended our experience with their great canoli coffee, and tea. And the service... Jason and the entire staff was friendly and welcoming and put smiles on our faces. If you're in the Somerville area, this is a must dine. We strongly recommend it.

We had an outstanding experience hosting a private graduation party at Vera’s! We worked with Meghan, who responded to us promptly and provided a clear outline of costs, which we thought were very fair. The appetizer and dessert platters were delicious, fresh, and plentiful, easily feeding our group of 50. The bar crew was outstanding and very attentive. The venue provides everything you need to play your own music playlist, but we also had DJ L’Duke play the last hour—she was wonderful and was scheduled to play there later that evening. At the end of the night, the staff thoughtfully packed up the extra food in neatly labeled boxes. Many of our guests stayed well after the party ended, enjoying the lounge once it opened to the public. If you’re looking for a place to host your next gathering, look no further than Vera’s!

I think the dj said his name as DJ panda? anyway, avoid if he’s dj-ing. we left after he yelled at me. Drinks and bartenders are cool though!

In the front it's a cozy bar with side tables to sit for more comfortable eating. In the back is a spacious Lounge area with table games on one side lounge chairs on another a bar and a little open space to dance. Our old neighborhood spots, and this time I remembered to take pictures. Amazing latin American cuisine with nice collection of drinks. Beautiful and lovely space. It always Leaves you fulfilled!

name: Ix Restaurant
document: Ix Restaurant. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Latin American Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
TL;DR version- Some high highs and some very low lows. Hot Figs was a fun app. By a mile, the soups were the favorites, so I would recommend the Pepián or Caldo Tlalpeño Rojo. Nice happy hour and a large chocolate drink selection. As per usual, removed some of the extra things in this review from the start due to space

There were a few nice hot sauces on the table, with the red one reminding me of salsa macha as it had a smoky kick and a spicier green sauce reminiscent of ají verde. They gave us some complimentary blue corn chips and a very mild black bean dip, which was tasty enough and hard to complain about, as it was free.

From the appetizers, we got the Hot Figs for $15.95, consisting of honey goat cheese, corn tortilla chips, and plum + pumpkin seeds. This was a unique and fun blend and reminded me more of something you would find in a wine bar. The mix of sweet and salty, with a bit of crunch from the seeds, was nice. This was good, and I would recommend it for a table rather than for a solo diner. There was also The Zingy Salad for $21.95, featuring zucchini spirals, yuzu, tomato, onion, cilantro, pumpkin seeds, and a jalapeño infusion. $18.95. The salad was fine with a bit of crunch and a mild spiciness. It was fine, though a bit wet, for lack of a better word.

The best dishes of the night were the soups, which each had its own distinct flavor profile. My sight presence went to the Pepián for $21.95, consisting of chicken, pumpkin/sesame seeds, green tomatillo, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper, carrots, chili coban/pasta/guaque, and potato + rice. There was plenty of tender chicken inside, with the soup having a nice roasted flavor with some spice and a bit of sourness. The potatoes and rice on the bottom added more sustenance to this dish.

Almost equally delicious was the Caldo Tlalpeño Rojo for a dollar more with shredded chicken, tomato, black pepper, garlic, onions, peas, chickpeas, corn, achiote, chipotle, Monterey jack cheese, and crunchy blue corn tortilla chips. By comparison, this was a bit heartier, with the melted cheese and shredded tortilla chips inside, similar to soups found in Mexican cuisine. While I also liked the mix of veggies a bit more in this one, as it added a bit more texture, I still slightly preferred the flavor of the other soup, as I usually prefer a bit more spice.

The rest of the food was fine. The TPC sandwich for $19.95 with chicken, peanut butter, coconut cream, ginger, cilantro, pickled carrots, and lime was fine.  For the number of ingredients, I found it a bit sweet, likely from the cream and the peanut butter mix. The bread was nice, but it also fell apart. It came with a nice side salad with a good vinaigrette. The most expensive at $24.95 were the Slow Cooked BBQ Ribs, consisting of baby back ribs with rice and beans. The ribs were almost a bit too tender as they lacked any bite, which was nice, but the sauce was a bit too generic tasting, reminding me of Sweet Baby Ray's or something similar. The rice and beans were standard. This was also OK.

Next came some dessert. There was first the $12.95 Rosemary Churros served with dulce de leche & chocolate dips. While I'm not sure if it worked, the rosemary did add a unique smell and a bit of flavor, and at least it wasn't generic. The churros themselves were hot, and the sauces were standard, with my preference being the dulce de leche. I also ordered a Champurrado for $7.95, which was fine. It wasn't as thick as I expected, though perhaps the style is a bit different than the champurrados I rarely buy from Mexican street carts. The chocolate flavor was very nice, though, and I like that it wasn't too sweet. Another person got a $4 Alfajor, which I got a bite of, which was standard.

This place is a bit hard to rate. The two soups were wonderful, I liked the appetizers, and I found a couple of the other dishes just OK. Overall, it was a good meal, but I'm not craving to go back. This would be the perfect 3.5, but I'll round up as that doesn't exist.

If you’ve always wanted to travel to Guatemala, IX Restaurant serves truly authentic Guatemalan food that will make you feel like you teleported to Guatemala with every bite.

As soon as I walked in the vibes, music, and energy put me in a good mood.

What really sets IX apart, though, is the service. The staff is incredibly warm, attentive, and welcoming. In just my second visit they truly make you feel like part of the family. Between the authentic food, the energetic atmosphere, and the top-notch hospitality, [and the fact my food arrived quickly - I prdered El Patron Burrito] IX Restaurant is a place that inspires you to come back to try every dish. I'm already scanning the menu to plan my third visit.

I’ve been coming here for years and it’s one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. 🙂 I recommend the queso derritido, caldo ix and jocon. Oh, and don’t forget the hot chocolate! Cocktails are great too 😄 If you’re lucky there will be live music.

Ix brings Guatemalan flavors to NY. The chef does a great job on the stew dishes that have great flavor. I had the pepian stew and the shrimp sliders. Both were delicious.

The place is a little small. But you can often see artists perform here in weekend nights.

Cozy spot for this winter days. However, ai have passed by during summer days and they have their door and windows open. Nice atmosphere.
Tasty and colorful food.

name: Brennan & Carr
document: Brennan & Carr. cuisine: American. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Brennan & Carr is one of those old-school New York spots that has stood the test of time. From the outside, it has that authentic neighborhood charm — simple, traditional, and full of history. Step inside, and you immediately feel the classic diner-style atmosphere that makes it so special.

The roast beef sandwich is the star of the show. Thinly sliced, tender, and incredibly flavorful, served on a soft roll that perfectly absorbs their famous house gravy. The dipping sauce takes it to another level — rich, savory, and unforgettable. It’s comfort food at its absolute best.

Portions are generous, prices are reasonable, and the quality remains consistent. It’s not about fancy presentation here — it’s about bold flavors and tradition done right.

The staff is efficient and straightforward, keeping the line moving while maintaining that friendly Brooklyn energy. It’s the kind of place locals love and visitors are lucky to discover.

If you want an authentic, no-frills New York food experience with serious flavor, Brennan & Carr is a must. Classic, satisfying, and iconic. Highly recommended

I hadn’t been in the Marine Park area in ages & decided to stop here for lunch yesterday. It was a cold day so I decided to have a soup & a sandwich. I had the clam chowder to start, which was pretty good. Then had the roast beef sandwich which they’re known for dipping the bread in the beef’s juice. I added cheese & onions & practically inhaled the sandwich it was so good. The service was quick & the server polite. The restaurant is quite old & though that adds to the atmosphere the table I was seated at needs to be refinished. There was a huge chunk of lacquer or varnish missing & if you’re not careful you could end up spilling your drink if you slide it across the table. Though I’m sure not all tables were like that. Still a great place to have a reasonably priced & delicious meal if you’re in the area. They also have a takeout window.

Iconic and absolutely worth the trip out. It can get busy and there was a bit of a wait, but after trying the food, I can see why. I started with a cup of their New England clam chowder, and it was easily one of the most flavorful I’ve had in a long time. But the real star is their signature roast beef sandwich, served soaking in jus. So tender, so flavorful, and exactly what you hope for from a place like this. I can see why it’s such an institution. And on top of that, it’s a great value too.

Finally got to visit this Brooklyn institution. It was alright to be honest. I do like the other famous competitor more better as there is pizza after a certain amount spent. The roast beef sandwich was alright, the  Manhattan clam chowder was good. Sweet potato fries were nice! Big fan of the service and atmosphere! Be ready with your cash and it is pricey in my opinion.

What an awesome place. Feels like going back in time. I came here on a cold Monday night with two friends. They sat me before my friends arrived which I appreciated. We had 3 sandwiches, 2 cups of NE clam chowder, a few sides to share, 2 rounds of beer all around and 2 desserts a la mode. The total came out to $98. Unbeatable. The beef sandwich is incredible. I recommend getting it rare with cheese and double dipped. If you don't like too much au jus and are scared of soggy bread, maybe get it on the side. But I liked it! Also the desserts are not to be missed, we got the blueberry pie and chocolate lava cake. I think the pies ala mode are definitely the way to go here.

name: Inkaico
document: Inkaico. cuisine: Seafood Breakfast & Brunch Peruvian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Delicious food and drink, amazing staff and beautiful ambience. Came here to celebrate a friend’s birthday. Everything we ordered was so good, to the point someone in our group even ended up ordering food to go. The music was the cherry on top. We will definitely be back!

We had a perfect experience! We happened to be in around happy hour and made the most of the pisco sours. To start we had the mango salad (delicious, lightly dressed), the oyster ceviche (beautiful presentation, beautiful flavors, steep cost to size ratio but understanding these are luxury ingredients), classic ceviche (oh how I’ve missed you). For mains we had the lamb chorrillana (perfectly cooked, balanced with a beautiful puree and delicious sauces worth cleaning your plate) and the arroz con mariscos which was truly a showstopper (loaded with seafood, rice perfectly cooked, bursting with flavor that draws you in for just one more bite), and to end the chirimoya panna cotta - I don’t know who presented the idea but it was beautiful- chirimoya flavor was rich, the panna cotta was light and perfectly set! We left full and happy, looking forward to our next visit.
My favorite Peruvian restaurant! Love to come and try a new ceviche and the Arroz con Pollo. The panna cotta was also a great way to end the meal.

From the moment you walk into this new Peruvian restaurant, you can feel the warmth—not just from the décor, but from the staff who greet you like family. The atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between modern elegance and authentic Peruvian charm, setting the stage for an unforgettable dining experience.

Every dish feels like a celebration of flavor and tradition. The ceviche is bright, fresh, and perfectly balanced with just the right amount of heat and citrus. The lomo saltado melts in your mouth, full of rich, smoky flavor, and the aji de gallina is pure comfort food.

Estefania was the cherry on top of our experience there with immaculate customer service.
Definitely will be coming again!!!

Was so excited to try this place, and was well worth the wait! The ceviche was so fresh, so many different textures and layers of flavors, so well balanced. The drinks were incredible, the bartender, Alejandro, was super attentive and answered all our questions. I really appreciated that he paid attention to small details and was so kind. The entire experience was great, everyone was so welcoming and made us feel like family. Everything about the service and ambiance and generous portions of food made this night memorable. Can't wait to come back and experience this new restaurant again!

name: Mama Kitchen
document: Mama Kitchen. cuisine: Kosher Middle Eastern. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We lived here 4 years. I've seen this place ms Amy times and told myself I'm coming here. 4 years later I made it.  WOWWWWWW. Hands down best empanada I've had in years. Tastes homemade. Verry full empanadas. I got beef with cheese and a pineapple sauce.  Definitely recommend a stop in for deliciousness. Worth a stop. Ill be back often
😁👍🏼👍🏼

I'm back already lol. Had to try the chicken and cheese.  WOW again. Delicious.  Im telling ya its a 20/10. Look at how full they are. Definitely go in for the greatness. 😁👍🏼👍🏼

Back at it!!! My wife brought me a breakfast wrap today.  😵😵😵 no joke with the Piña sauce (or without) 20/10. Sooooooo Delicious.  Y'all need to stop in for some great food. 😁👍🏼👍🏼

This quesadilla hat has to be one of the best quesadillas ever!!! She makes this homemade mango, Pineapple and habanero sauce, baby I can eat that on everything!!! Not only was the food amazing it's all made fresh and they were super super super amazing. Amazing customer service,  if you haven't tried them It's a mess.

Drove an hour to try this place after seeing it on Tiktok, very much worth the trip. Extremely friendly and welcoming staff, didn't make me feel rushed. I got the breakfast Quesadilla with that signature pineapple habanero salsa and I'm more disappointed I didn't go back for more or go on Tuesday when they sell the jars. For the price I paid I definitely was fed and then some. I would absolutely make the trip back out here again. 11/10

As I was cruising through the 208 intersection at Hardee’s, something hit my senses like a telenovela/soap opera plot twist — the smell of pure happiness. It led me straight to Mama’s Kitchen. I didn’t even plan it. My car just… turned on its own.

I walked in, and immediately, the smell of fresh empanadas hugged me like a long-lost relative. I looked at the menu, tried to keep my composure, but my stomach was like, “Bro, you know what time it is.” I ordered the empanadas, the tacos, and a fried burrito because self-control is overrated.

When that first bite hit… I swear my soul briefly exited my body and did a little salsa dance in the air. I looked at Nina and said, “If I keep eating, I’m gonna fall asleep right here.” She said, “That’s fine, — this is Mama’s Kitchen.” I knew right then I was home.

The food was so good I ordered another round to go before I even finished my plate. And when I left… not gonna lie… I shed a single tear. Because leaving Mama’s Kitchen felt like saying goodbye to a summer love.

Five stars, 10/10 — would risk a food coma again.

I am currently resting in my hammock.

Wow wow wow!
Such incredible and welcoming service. The food is made to order so it's always fresh and absolutely delicious! You can tell everything is homemade. If you're from Puerto Rico and missing home, head to Mama's Kitchen it'll feel like you traveled back to the island.
Mama's Kitchen really has the world's best empanadas!

document: Ayat. cuisine: Comfort Food Soul Food. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Very friendly and accommodating service. Best knafeh I’ve had, made fresh to order. Notably this location does not have a wood fire stove as they are not allowed to — so the marketing there is a tad confusing.

How can people eat such plain bland dishes here. Sorry to say but not worth it at all. Don’t get me wrong, staff was kind, atmosphere was great but the foods not it. Extremely bland flavors and the rice was cold. The pita which was fresh was fresh but would be nice if they served it was something. Got the mixed grilled platter, Arabic chicken shawarma, chicken kebab platter and the mixed shawarma platter. Tasteless food. Ayat is definitely a great place to visit!! The cauliflower was the best thing we ate, along with Baklava, and the olive oil and pita!!! Igor was such an amazing waiter, thank you for making our experience fantastic!!

The food was all wonderful; however, I was a little disappointed with the service. I felt a bit uneasy noticing that a server handled food right after cleaning without washing their hands.
​It’s a popular restaurant that gets quite busy, and they don't accept reservations. That said, it is very reasonably priced—especially since you can bring your own drinks without a cover charge. Plus, the freshly baked pita is delicious and complimentary.

Excellent food and great service. The flavors were rich and fresh, and the portion size was very generous. The place was clean and welcoming. Definitely coming back again!
Thank you Daniela 🤍 such a nice girl 😘
very friendly and respectful .

name: Petisco Brazuca
document: Petisco Brazuca. cuisine: Brazilian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Very cute window service restaurant!! There is no seating, it’s take out only. A friend and I split a medium portion of chicken coxinhas and a guaraná, the perfect combination and it really hit the spot as a Brazilian. Great service. Matheus, behind the counter was so nice. I can’t wait to come back.

Growing up with this, my godmother & sister always treated me to these amazing treats, I first found them a few years ago at the smorgasburg so I was so happy to see something I grew up eating.
The empanadas were so crunchy and flavorful, we got half cheese and half spinach coxinha, and OfCourse the churros!

Delicious, fresh Coxinhas. The spinach had an amazing cheese pull, the pic doesn’t do it justice! I had spinach and chicken, and I will be back to try all the other flavors. The staff was very friendly and was happy to answer all my questions and give recommendations for my first time there. Also I don’t know what the green sauce was but it was amazing😋

I really enjoyed the cheese pastel cheese coxinha. They are the authentic and tasty pastries.
Just a little disappointed about brigadeiro, which is my favorite treat. I’ve tried the tradicional, coconut and both texture were a kind of hard. Brigadeiro usually has a softy texture.
Also did not like the fact that everything must be to go since you don’t have acess to the store 🤷🏻‍♀️Order through the window. Since we are not at the pandemic it make no sense.
I recommend the pastries.

I tried this place at the Bryant Park Winter Village. I had the chicken coxinha, it was so good! It brought a sauce that took the dish to another level. Now that I’ve seen there are multiple locations here in Brooklyn definitely visiting. The starts for atmosphere were because the winter village was crowded insanely! I’ve tried this dish before from an authentic Brazilian home, and the ones I tried here lived up to it. You should give it a try!

name: Footprints Cafe
document: Footprints Cafe. cuisine: Caribbean Desserts Vegetarian. located in Brooklyn. with 2.9 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A coworker had recommended Footprints to me & I’ll have to thank him tomorrow. I went there for lunch & enjoyed their Rasta Pasta dish which it is known for. I meant to order the jerk shrimp as an appetizer but it topped the Rasta Pasta & to my surprise it was amazing. I wasn’t sure how the spices from the shrimp would taste with the mild cheesy sauce but it was delicious. The waitress taking care of me was very polite & helpful. I choose to dine outdoors since it was a gorgeous day & had the pleasure of conversing with one of the chefs who stepped outside for a moment. They had a nice variety of nonalcoholic beverages & since I was driving I decided to try one the waitress recommended: pineapple passion & it was very good. For dessert I went with the Red Velvet Cake & though it may look small it was rich & extremely filling, not to mention delicious. I can’t wait to go back.

Great to have Uber eats deliver. The cheesecake looks and taste like regular cake with pineapple pieces or something else. Perhaps a mixup. Delicious creamy rasta pasta but the BBQ chicken was hard rough and next day was papery. Please cook that chicken some other way! Absolutely love the Caribbean salad with fresh fruits like mango and veggies.

Not giving a low review because of the food or the vibes. But I ordered for pick up online and the confirmation said my order would be ready 8:30-8:40, gave them the grace of not checking until 8:40, they didn’t even start on our order. Order wasn’t ready at 9:24pm. Spoke to manager she talking about grub hub doesn’t always tell them when they accept orders. Ok give you a pass for technical glitch but not even a cup of soup was offered and when asked it was denied. Like come on. You guys clearly busy enough to be 40 minutes behind orders you can give costumer a freakin cup of soup when your system messed up on the order and couldn’t deliver as promised. It’s really simple. Either don’t sign up for so many online options or be prepared to repair the damage from a mess up.  Hope the food is worth the wait 🤞🏾

I had the roti and I got sick badly the same night and into the next day. However, the service and fish fingers were great! The vibe in there is cozy and casual for a date night. Overall, if I didn't get sick from the food from that night and the allergic reactions from other foods in there I would have given it a great review.

We showed up just as Footprint Café was about to close, but instead of turning us away they welcomed our party of six with open arms. The staff went out of their way to make us feel comfortable, and the service was excellent from start to finish. The food was fresh and flavorful the Rasta Pasta was absolutely to die for! Big thanks to the team for taking care of us when they didn’t have to. This spot has heart, flavor, and great vibes. Highly recommend! I’ll make sure my Arizona family knows about this place. I’ll will definitely let my Arizona people know about this place when they visit Brooklyn.

name: Le Crocodile
document: Le Crocodile. cuisine: French Wine Bars Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Really good food, with the highlights being the mushroom pate and the duck confit. Service was top notch and I loved the dessert. Great place for a date, book club meeting, or business meeting based on the people around us. The menu changes seasonally so the stuff we got might not be what you get. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible.

Me and my hubby were looking for a French dining around Williamsburg and chatgpt recommended this spot, i couldn’t really find it via my google searches before that. The food was amazing in general. It was our first time trying Barbajuans and it was soo tasty. The onion soup and the complimentary bread and butter were delicious. The steak had a salty and overpowering sauce so it’s not my favorite but still we devoured everything. The last star of the show was a crème brulee which was just 💋👨‍🍳 Service was very calm and good they were very attentive. Pricing is normal for a place like that. (Maybe the steak is a bit pricey for the portion?)

Very cute French spot, love the decor.
Bar seats suit for low number parties, also comfortable seats for party of more.
I had the burger and it was great, love the brioche bun, patty was well cooked and juicy, very guilty pleasure (for me)
Banana pudding taste like a very moist banana bread (I guess that’s what a pudding supposed to taste like 🤣🤣)
The profiteroles were delicious as well!
Great place for couples and friends.

Le Crocodile was fantastic. I wasn’t sure what to expect but I pleasantly surprised with how good the food was. The menu is unique. I tried certain dishes I’ve never had before like steak tartare & mushroom pate. Both were incredible. Entree I got the bistro steak frites, it was good not great but tried the roast chicken from my friend it was delicious. My other friends got the duck breast and really liked it. The sticky banana date pudding was so good didn’t last more than 30 seconds on our table hahah. Will definitely be returning to this spot! Great place for a date or dinner with friends

Went in for dinner last night with some friends, I was really looking forward to dining at this restaurant. I had heard so much about it, but I was very underwhelmed. They were already out the two items on the menu we wanted since they were busy and then we ordered steak frites, which I assumed a French restaurant absolutely cannot go wrong with, and we were so disappointed that the temperature came out extremely wrong, we asked for medium rare and got a beyond well done steak. So verdict, I’m unhappy that my first experience of a restaurant I heard so much about turned out like this.

name: The Ten Bells
document: The Ten Bells. cuisine: Wine Bars Cocktail Bars Tapas Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Solid pub experience with great history. A little dark history but I love the authenticity keeping it real. Staff was spot on ordered at the bar. I know cheeseburgers and the crunch was unexpected. Like a smashburger vibe and tasty. Had a cider on a quick stop very local bar. A good option after walking the market..

We really enjoyed our stop in!! The Ten Bells Pub is where multiple victims of Jack the Ripper visited before being killed, and they have done a great job of maintaining the historic atmosphere of the place, as well as putting little pieces of information around the building.

My family and I hung out here for quite a while one evening and had a lovely time. Our bartender was busy, but super helpful and fast whenever possible. She was also super friendly and great to chat with!

The space is just a super neat looking spot and worth checking out and stopping in for a few drinks!!

Went here following a visit to the Jack the Ripper Museum. A couple of the victims were reputed to have drank here prior to being murdered, which thankfully did not happen to us (obviously as I wouldn't be writing a review). The pub itself was very atmospheric with many original features. Staff were friendly and attentive. We only went in for a quick drink but would definitely go back. Food coming out the kitchen looked excellent.

The Ten Bells, a historic pub near Spitalfields dating back to the mid-18th century and linked to the Jack the Ripper case, disappointed with cold, dismissive service and no basic courtesies like a “thank you,” making me unlikely to return despite its decent beer selection. The lack of toilet paper in the toilets was an extra letdown for such a storied venue.

My partner and I booked a dinner here which we presumed would be in the upstairs resturant as part of my birthday celebration. It seemed that way when we booked at least. Unfortunately they'd booked two events over this and we had to eat downstairs in the pub area. Normally this would be fine but we wanted to have a quieter experience. Staff were helpful on site and were apologetic, the food was good but the experience in this case was not quite what we wanted.

name: Leitao
document: Leitao. cuisine: Portuguese Cocktail Bars Beer, Wine & Spirits. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Flavorful, delicious dishes! We very much enjoyed our dinner at Leitao. Everything had a delicious sauce. We loved the little neck clams, the peppers and the sirloin steak in garlic sauce. Portuguese bread was amazing. The piri piri chicken was good but the drumstick was a bit dry. Fries were fresh and crispy. Overall would recommend. Good, attentive service. Note they got rid of tipping and automatically charge 20%.

I had an order of clams and chorizo and an order of shrimp in lobster sauce. The clams were just ok. They could've used more seasoning. The shrimp in lobster sauce was great. The menu is really interesting and extensive. I have to go back to try more dishes. Service was fantastic. I love the cozy atmosphere here.

We were very grateful to get a table as a walk-in around 5pm without a reservation. The appetizers were much better than the main courses. The polvo was the best dish of the meal, the clams were extremely fresh, though the sausage was a bit salty. The Mediterranean white bread with olive oil was amazing; my mom even ordered an extra one.

For mains, we ordered the grilled chicken and the seafood rice, and both were quite underwhelming. The chicken lacked flavor and was mostly just covered in chili oil. Surprisingly, the seafood rice was less flavorful than the clam appetizer and also tasted bland.

We finished with a Portuguese egg tart, which we expected to be a specialty of a Portuguese restaurant, but it wasn’t really to our taste. It felt like flour was added to the custard, giving it a slightly sticky texture, and the flavor was just okay.

The service, however, was excellent! Special thanks to the gentleman who took great care of us.

On Christmas Eve, I went out for dinner at Restaurante Leitão in New York. We started with an octopus salad as an appetizer, served with an incredible little bread. For the main dishes, we had codfish and a francesinha — honestly, one of the best francesinhas I’ve ever had in my life, absolutely amazing.

We were warmly welcomed by the owner, Nuno, who quickly realized we were Portuguese and made us feel right at home. We were served by Juliana, who was extremely kind and recommended the octopus salad, which turned out to be an excellent choice.

To make the night even more special, they surprised us with two incredible desserts: a chocolate mousse with crumble and CRF Reserva, and a cinnamon-infused pear dessert that was absolutely delicious. I was also offered a glass of CRF Reserva, which was a fantastic touch and perfectly complemented the experience.

A truly memorable dining experience and a place I would highly recommend.

An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. The atmosphere is incredibly cozy and inviting, and the staff go above and beyond to make you feel truly at home. Every dish was outstanding, showcasing authentic flavors and impeccable quality. Without a doubt, this is the number one Portuguese restaurant in the tri-state area. I’ll be very happy to consider myself a regular moving forward.

name: Chez Moi
document: Chez Moi. cuisine: French Desserts Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
They roped me in when I saw foie gras on the menu.  It was so good that I had to go back a second night for another portion.
Had the snails, short ribs, duck, and salmon.  All were perfectly cooked.
Don’t forget the dessert.  For me crème brûlée or, if you are into chocolate, the mousse.  Certainly leave room for dessert
Wish they had a better, more extensive wine list but they did have some good French champagne at a reasonable price.
Definitely worth the price of admission.
Make a reservation.

A cute, cozy restaurant with (mostly) French food that was delicious!
Portions were perfect for sharing-- it was 4 of us for my mom's birthday dinner.
We actually got all the specials that the server listed (which I *never* do!) because they all sounded so good, and we were not disappointed!
The carrot ginger soup (a special) was amazing and the French onion soup was great, too. Escargot was good, slightly too chewy for my taste. The branzino with mushrooms and bok choy in dashi broth was phenomenal! (Another special)
And the last special, the pistachio risotto was amazing!
Duck breast with barley was very good, as per my brother.
And for the dessert, we got the floating meringue with almonds, salted caramel sauce, and a cream sauce. It was divine!
Would definitely come back here and try the other food and desserts!

Holy cow this place surprised us with their delicious brunch specials. We split the croque monsieur and the very special Lobster 🦞 BLT which blew our minds.  Definitely would recommend for a delicious meal in the city’s largest borough.

We went to Chez Moi for Sunday brunch the day after Valentine’s Day as a group of five, including a one-year-old. The staff was incredibly welcoming and accommodating, especially in arranging our table with a high chair for the baby, which we truly appreciated.

The brunch selections were excellent overall. Two of us ordered the steak and eggs, one had the lobster eggs Benedict (the day’s special), another chose the grits, and I ordered the savory crepe. Everyone was very satisfied with their meals.

Unfortunately, my crepe fell short—it was a bit dry (which is unusual) and lacked flavor. I’m hoping this was just a one-off, as the overall experience and service were lovely. I would certainly return for another brunch soon.

This place is hands down one of my favorite spots in downtown Brooklyn. Not only has it always been so consistent and delicious, but the warm environment always makes me feel like I’m at home.  Whether it’s brunch, where you are given a comforting, energizing welcome and experience, or dinner which gives the best balance of date night or group dinner energy, you just can’t go wrong. The ambiance tells enough of the story, and if you’re looking for a cool person to talk to - T is there most nights behind the bar and really just makes the evening even better. 10/10

google_reviews.text: What a great restaurant we really enjoyed dinner here.  The service and food were amazing.   They don’t take reservations and are cash only which is kind of a pain especially at this price point.  There’s an ATM 1/2 a block away which you can get charged $3 to do a withdrawal.

Things you need to know before you feast here: 1. Cash only, 2. No reservations and 3. You’ll wait and it could be 20 minutes like us tonight or 45. But I must said is worth it, Brooklyn Heights is charming enough to take a nice walk while you bide one’s time. Andy was quite the star tonight, he faces some great recommendations, from the Rigatoni allá norma to the Grilled octopus which is one of the best I’ve had in some time. Just simple but delicious, was one of those dishes that on its simplicity didn’t lack any depth of flavour or character. Another favourite for me was something my husband had years ago and all this time after was still mouthwatering, the Garlic bread with Calabrian chilli get it and have it with the Meatballs. Also amazing and worth mentioning the Tre colore salad and the Hanger steak. For dessert we took home the Chocolate espresso cake order it and have a night cap or a coffee with it. So come in, share some food, listen to your server, bring the cash and enjoy a tasty cozy meal. Will be back soon!
Great experience - very cozy spot with delicious Italian food and wonderful appetizers.. 5 star 🌟

Actually this is my first time maybe i rank restaurant 1 star, for many reasons.

The experience was disappointed, the food look like already made before order just but it in microwave, many items in the menu not available, I can’t finish my plate actually.

They only accept cash!!.

This is the worst Italian food i ever had.

Tony does it Best ! All the freshest ingredients and the best fish and seafood in Brooklyn try the homemade wine too take a walk after dinner on Brooklyn promenade you will thank me great way to walk offf dinner

name: Nita Fish And Fry
document: Nita Fish And Fry. cuisine: Fish & Chips. located in Brooklyn. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Wow, this is some good soul food. The fish was fishy in a good way- indicating that it was fresh like it was recently caught, seasoned to perfection along with the shrimp, which I’ve never seen uniquely filleted this way. This will make someone who doesn’t like shrimp like shrimp. Definitely want to come back and try the Mac and cheese!

Let me start out by saying , I’m a big on reading reviews before trying a spot. I can see why Nita has a 4.9.

Last night was my first time trying this spot. Ive been looking to get a place where I can get some good late night eats on my break and luckily I found them. I was greeted with attentiveness and southern hospitality which made the atmosphere easy to relax. I got three platters ( Fried fish, BBQ Wings , Fried Fish & Shrimp W/ seasoned fries ). The fish was fresh , seasoned and cooked to perfection. The fries were also seasoned with care. Let’s just say the food and vibe was so good that here I am writing a review on my way to get 4 more platters. Best fried fish I’ve had !.

Regular wait time expected due to getting everything fresh.

5/5

Mac n Cheeze Stickyyyyyy !!! 10/10 Make you want to smack yo grandma foreal ! The best recipe !! Everything well seasoned! Not overly seasoned but seasoned with love! Stop by for good late night eats and cravings! They also serve drinks and have a cozy lounge area with good music !!
PS: Chef , Plsss Add Yams To The Menu! my taste buds say it would pair so well !!!! lol Keep up the good work !!

I just want to thank Sun God for such an experience. Today was my first time here and I will definitely come back. The food was immaculate!  I haven’t had fried fish so good in such a long time. The drinks were also bomb! We dined in and the music and conversation kept us there for hours. We even got to play games like connect 4 and tic tac toe along with cards. I felt like I was at a house party and the nostalgia just warmed my heart. Truly felt the love in the space. Sun God and his son will truly make you feel loved and like you are visiting family. When I say a time was had, a time was truly had 🫶🏾

I'm born and raising bedstop, Brooklyn, but I came all the way to Brownsville. For the fish and shrimp, I must tell you is a small little place.You'll miss it.But that fish was very, very nicely.Seasoned and flavorful as well as I got aside out of mac and cheese very good. Just note is in the heart of brownsville. The food is delicious

name: Bar Birba
document: Bar Birba. cuisine: Pizza Wine Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I ordered delivery so can’t vouch for the ambiance of the place itself.

I got the arancini (which were good) and the don’t tell nonna bar pie (which was not). I don’t like to post negative reviews, but I have to say I’m shocked that a restaurant would send me a clearly burnt pizza. There was another review that mentioned this, but I thought it was an honest mistake or might be similar to Neapolitan pizza—it was not.

This pizza was full stop burned and clearly overcooked in the crust and in the middle of the pizza itself making it hard and charred. The flavor in the non-burnt places seemed like it could be good, but the char and flavor of burnt food completely overpowered everything. I had to pick off those spots to taste anything else which was hard since it was a lot of the pizza.

I’m very disappointed to say the least, since I was looking forward to trying this place and I should have not ordered from here.

Always love this spot. Had my birthday dinner here for ~22 people and they were awesome start to finish. Super helpful picking out menu, drinks, etc. The staff and space are both amazing. All of the food is delicious and the drinks are fun. The boozy affogatos are out of this world. Everyone is still talking about how much fun they had and how good the pizza was. Can never go wrong with Bar Birba! Perfect date night spot as well.

A really nice, intimate spot for a glass/bottle of wine and some surprisingly killer pizza. The Don't Tell Nonna pie was awesomeee—like, I was not expecting it to be that good, but the sesame crust with the jalepeño + everything else was a great combo. We also had an all-veggie pizza that was really solid too, plus the gigantic beans appetizer which was complex but definitely worth the order.

Staff was wonderful and attentive, atmosphere was welcoming and cozy, crowd was lively but not too loud. And the generous drink menu (wine and beer) had something for everyone. So glad I stopped in!

Amazing. Would give 10 stars if I could. Food delicious and I just went to Italy and did a food tour. Arancini stands out. And their wine selection is top notch. Servers are really knowledgeable about everything. Small place and newly opened and I expect them to be packed and reservation only very soon. Serving pizza in NYC is a bold move since literally there are so many places that do that well like Roberta’s and Union Pizza etc. But the prices here are very reasonable considering what they are at other places. Small menu of small plates. Unique offerings of appertifs and digestivs that I’d like to try next time. Could use more dessert options considering the digestiv selection. Please do a killer Tiramisu. Food felt very Tuscan or Sicily region. No pasta I don’t believe. Only thing I didn’t love was the Caponata. It was a lot of onion and pepper. I was expecting more eggplant chunks. The bread with it was amazing and my friend really loved it though so what do I know. I’m always a sucker for Lambrusco.
I forgot what kind of pizza this was but sesame crust and toppings were sick. Recommended. My friend got the spicy soppressata. Also good .satisfies my pizza craving

name: Siren Restaurant & Bar
document: Siren Restaurant & Bar. cuisine: Seafood Cocktail Bars Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
My boyfriend & I were looking for Happy Hour Oyster spots to treat ourselves and came across this beautiful location. We also use the ‘Seated’ app and this location specifically had 17% back for the week.

We arrived 6:15pm on Wednesday with 45 mins to spare for HH and we got to order 2 dozen House Oysters (sourced from Virginia) they were very good,  a selection of small to medium sized oysters (as pictured) and I loved that they came with various topping, where some restaurants lack.

Also on the HH menu there were bar snacks and we picked Fritto Misto, the Calamari was perfect, the white fish was fresh and the shrimp was good, all of it paired great with the lemon aioli.

The entrees of choice were Linguine Clams, Lobster Roll. The Linguine was perfectly al dente, the sauce was rich and the amount of clams they offered was more than enough. The Lobster roll was good but not amazing.

Dessert we ordered the Tiramisu and if you are thinking one slice is enough, no you’re going to want seconds. You’re also going to want to remember the last time you had a great slice of tiramisu, it won’t matter because this will be on your mind until the next morning. I say get it if you’re not going to order anything else on the menu.

Overall experience was good, they accidentally charged me for two club sodas but offered a refund for the $6 that was charged. No issues - there may be a wait to get your food but honestly it’s worth it.

Oh my God, please listen to me! This place is absolutely amazing. I have close to 13 million views on my Google restaurant contributions and trust me when I tell you, this place is 100% worth it. I cannot express enough how wonderful the staff is, nice Brooklyn style atmosphere, and the food is absolutely AMAZING!

Please look in my pictures and you get an idea on why I tell you you should rush to this place, don't walk, rush!

The owner, Diego, is absolutely incredible. You could tell this man really truly cares about what he does and the love he puts into his restaurant.

We visited this restaurant with a large group and had a pleasant overall experience. The wine selection was good, and the oysters were very fresh and flavorful — definitely a highlight of the evening. However, some of the other dishes didn’t quite live up to expectations. We tried the biscuit soup and lobster roll, and while they were decent, they weren’t particularly memorable.

The atmosphere was quite nice — comfortable and inviting, making it a good spot for a gathering. Prices were average for the area, so it felt fairly reasonable. Overall, it’s a good place if you’re looking for a nice setting and great oysters, but the rest of the menu could use a bit more refinement.

We visited during Restaurant Week about two weeks ago and, unfortunately, left feeling very underwhelmed.
As seafood lovers who live in the neighborhood, we were excited to finally try this spot. We started with the tuna crudo and crab cakes, followed by the rack of lamb and branzino. Disappointingly, each dish fell flat—lacking the flavor, freshness, and execution we had hoped for. The dessert ended up being the highlight of the evening, which says a lot, considering I typically skip dessert and only ordered it because I assumed it would be difficult to get wrong.
Service was another letdown. While we were greeted upon arrival and promptly seated, our waiter seemed to forget about us—even though we were the only couple in his section at the time. To make matters worse, the restaurant automatically adds gratuity to the bill, which feels unjustified given the level of service provided.
The cocktails were equally underwhelming, so much so that we ended up going elsewhere afterward for drinks to salvage the night. Overall, the experience was lackluster and forgettable, and we will not be returning.

We have a tradition to meet with girls and to choose the best restaurant in ares, this one was so pretty on a pictures. We were excited to come here and so disappointed to leave.

Staff is nice, food is pretty but absolutely not delicious. And absolutely overpriced for the quality.

I’ve got pieces of shells in a lobster roll.
Burata is my favorite salad and I never thought it could be so destroyed.

Maybe someone will like it more, but I won’t come back for sure. Sorry. I can only be honest.

name: Big Tiny
document: Big Tiny. cuisine: Wine Bars French Tapas/Small Plates. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Oysters were so fresh and the service was good!They had a happy hour for $11 of a glass of wine and $20 of a choice of an appetizer with a glass of wine. I thought the food was a reasonable price and I would definitely come again. The atmosphere is great too, when we came it was still empty, but when it hit 6:30 there were more people.

We recently had brunch at this location and ordered the Big Tiny veggie omelette, the savory crepe, and the Benedict hollandaise. Unfortunately, the brunch dishes were underwhelming and fell a bit short for all of us—we found ourselves asking for extra salt and hot sauce to add flavor.

That said, their regular lunch menu is much stronger. I’ve had the steak tartare before and it was simply delicious. The space itself is very charming, as the name suggests—a cozy little corner spot—and it really shines as an appetizer and cheese bar with an excellent wine selection.

While brunch wasn’t a hit for us, I’d still recommend visiting for lunch, wine, and small plates rather than brunch.

Amazing service + amazing food = best combination! Big Tiny goes above and beyond to reassure and satisfy their customers. It’s hard to find restaurants that truly are passionate, but their love shines through especially with the plating and the quality of their food. There were many picky eaters at this table, and yet those plates were wiped clean!! Would recommend and definitely coming back 😇👏

This one is a hidden gem that we found while Googling good foods nearby. We ordered the Steak & Eggs, a Nachos with Chicken. Curry Mussels, Guava Mimosa, and an Escargot. Everything was fantastic, especially the curry mussels. We'll be back soon!

The presentation and taste of the food was A+. I ordered a bunch of apps and they came out in a timely matter and were delicious. The restaurant had inside/outside seating. I wish the waiter was a bit more attentive but very friendly

google_reviews.text: The Chicken Korma Was pretty good for $17, huge chunks of quality white meat chicken in a delicious curry

The staff were friendly and welcoming.
If you’re into Indian food, I’d definitely recommend checking this spot out. I’ll be going back soon to try more dishes for sure.

If there is any option that I can rate 0/10 I would do that. Food is disgusting. World will definitely loose respect towards Indian Food if this is served. This is not at the authentic Indian Food. name: Bar Mario
document: Bar Mario. cuisine: Italian Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
5 stars to food, service and atmosphere!!!! Cozy and “moody.” They’ve got oldies playing with vibey lighting. I was really drawn by light fixtures at the bar and the overall design of the bar. Portions were perfectly sized, flavors were SPOT ON.

Pictures really don’t do it justice but the brussel sprouts with arugula were really nice and cronchy. Beets tasted like a balanced appetizer dessert, not too sweet, the honey nor the Gorgonzola overpowered and the walnuts were a nice addition for texture. Focaccia was soft but also perfectly toasted with olive oil and fresh rosemary. Our pasta dishes were cooked perfectly in terms of al dente, and richness in sauce. We got the hazelnut cookie cake that just a big mic drop lol

Anyways, highly recommend as their service was lovely as well

Our second time here, because we loved it so much last year we needed to come back.
This visit was again well worth it. We were greeted promptly and cheerfully ( I didn't catch the name of our hostess but she was great!)
The food and cocktails are exceptional.  Risotto croquettes with sausage and gorgonzola as a starter, agnolotti ragu ( the Bolognese was velvety smooth and amazingly flavorful) and Conghiglie Cenere ( house made shells with a gorgonzola sauce and chopped olives) as our mains. We had to try the Tuscan Fries and are now addicted.   Gran Madre and the Vanchiglia for our dinner cocktails, with a negroni with dessert. Everything was fantastic. Dessert was also lovely, a butter cake base with hazelnut spread and a whipped topping . (Gianduiotto)
-I am taking the names from the receipt, there is no chance I could remember the spelling.-
Our server, Natalie, was wonderful. She was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, gave great recommendations and overall helped make our night amazing.

Drove an hour and a half to meet friends and try this spot and it was totally worth it! Great cocktails, food, wine, and service! Enjoyable atmosphere, jazzy vibe. Alessandro and other staff friendly, helpful, and professional. Loved the carciofi, squid ink pasta, fritto misto, chicken milanese. All delish! Would have loved to try the vitello tonnato but didn't see it on the menu. Very good Barbera d-Alba (would like to see more bottles in that  price range). Great Vanchiglia martini! Looking forward to returning!

Looking for a good restaurant in the area for Christmas Eve and we found this awesome Italian restaurant. Very very good and authentic, and the pici pasta is something that you can’t find easily in the US. Alessandro is the best host .. highly highly recommended.

We arrived earlier than the reservation time and received a warm welcome, along with excellent service. Feel like home.
We ordered two appetizers, two pastas, and three drinks.
The 3rd drink, we wanted something mezcal, and the bartender made the one beyond our expectations, five stars plus!
Spaghetti hangover I love it!
My bf got cacio e pepe, too good, he didnt want to share with me, haha.
Definitely, we will come back!!!
