name: Birria Landia
document: Birria Landia. cuisine: Food Trucks Mexican. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Birria-Landia’s famous birria tacos loaded with tender beef and vibrant salsa. Birria-Landia deserves a special shoutout for delivering a masterclass in birria tacos, consomé, tostadas, and mulitas. As a taco enthusiast, I was blown away by the exceptional quality and depth of flavor in each of these offerings. This Queens-born taco truck (now a multi-location NYC icon) has rightly earned a cult following for its authentic Tijuana-style birria ￼. It’s even been credited with “changing the taco landscape” in the city ￼ – and after tasting their food, I completely agree.

Birria-Landia keeps the menu simple – just four items – and each one is outstanding. The secret is the succulent birria itself: beef slow-simmered for hours in a rich, brick-red chili adobo ￼ that infuses every bite with incredible depth of flavor. Bite into a birria taco and you’ll get juicy, fall-apart beef in a tortilla that’s been dipped in the savory consomé and crisped on the griddle for extra flavor ￼ – an explosion of savory goodness. That consomé (the coveted broth) is the soul of the meal, packing a bold, tangy richness that elevates everything it touches ￼. Even the tostada – a crispy tortilla piled high with birria – comes drizzled with that copper-hued broth (liquid gold you won’t want to waste) ￼, and the mulita (a cheese-filled birria “sandwich”) reaches its full indulgent potential when you dunk it into the consomé for a next-level flavor boost ￼.

In short, Birria-Landia has set the bar for birria in NYC, and I’m beyond impressed. Consider this my personal thank-you to the team – you’ve won a loyal fan, and I’ll be eagerly back for more. Highly recommended for anyone who loves bold, authentic flavors!

Ordered delivery from here, probably would’ve been better if I got it myself fresh.

Overall wasn’t bad. If you’re looking for solid birria I’d recommend. Not the best birria I’ve had, but I love the addition of the picked red onions and spicy sauce on the side. I also had the cheese tostada birria ‘sandwich’ known as the multida which was tasty and had cheese. The birria itself isn’t the most flavorful but it does have a nice flavor and isn’t too fatty which I was glad about. The taco shell was great, tastes like it soaked in soaked in consume or toasted with achote oil.

Nicely packaged and overall not a bad value at 5 dollars a taco and a bit more for the tostada.

It's an incredible dining experience. Their birria tacos are simply delicious, and the broth that accompanies them is the best. My daughter really enjoyed her meal. Don't miss out on visiting this place, 100% recommended.

If you’re looking for high-quality Mexican street food, Birria-Landia is definitely worth the visit. It’s a classic food truck setup, so keep in mind there is no indoor or dedicated outside seating—you’ll likely be eating standing up or snagging one of the very few limited tables nearby.

The food is incredibly good for the price. I ordered the Mulita, the Birria de Res Tacos, and the Tostada, and every item was packed with flavor. They also have a good selection of traditional Mexican drinks to wash it all down.

This could easily become my go-to Mexican food truck. It’s simple, authentic, and hits the spot every time.
Best beef tacos ever... Worth every penny! 👌🏽😋 Its a must try spot! You won't be disappointed.

Chez Messy is the definition of a neighborhood hidden gem—unassuming from the outside, yet delivering an experience that easily justifies traveling across the city. There’s an immediate sense of care the moment you walk in, from the warm welcome to the thoughtfully curated atmosphere. It’s the kind of place that feels rooted in its community while still offering a level of quality and execution that stands out well beyond the neighborhood.

The food is where Chez Messy truly shines. The octopus is a standout, expertly cooked to achieve that perfect balance of tenderness and char, bringing out deep, savory flavors in every bite. The salmon is equally impressive—rich, delicate, and cooked with precision—while the steak and egg is indulgent, satisfying, and beautifully balanced, showcasing both comfort and refinement on a single plate. Each dish reflects a clear respect for ingredients and technique without unnecessary embellishment.

Equally memorable is the cocktail program. The drinks are creative yet approachable, thoughtfully balanced, and crafted with the same attention to detail as the food. Whether you’re starting the evening with a cocktail or lingering over one at the end of the meal, the bar program elevates the overall experience and complements the menu seamlessly rather than competing with it.

What truly sets Chez Messy apart is the hospitality. The team is passionate, attentive, and remarkably detail-oriented, striking that perfect balance between professionalism and genuine warmth. It’s clear they care deeply about both the food and the people they’re serving, creating an atmosphere that feels personal and welcoming. Chez Messy isn’t just a great neighborhood spot—it’s a destination worth seeking out.

name: La Cuchara
document: La Cuchara. cuisine: Spanish. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: My wife found this place to celebrate my birthday here and it was super special. The ambiance is great. The service very attentive. The food is very special, a combination of tapas, charcuterie, and other Spanish specialties. They also brought a sorbet for my birthday. The duck, croquetas, empanadas, and the crudo were the highlights of the night. The churros could've been better.

We scored on a Sunday evening after the Steelers beat the Ravens. Truly a destination meal as you drove through a myriad of bridges, train tracks and warehouses. The Basque flavors were popping on all our tapas especially the Pan Con Tomate, Spinach / Gruyere croquettes, shrimp and oysters. The potatoes were phenominal and the bread is baked in house and take a loaf home!

Don’t seem to recall how this made it to my hit list. I’m glad it was. Since we were not as hungry, we ordered small plates like croquetas, small empanadas, candy bar dessert, and fried oysters to share. The only disappointment was not having jamon iberico on the menu. Will certainly go again to try the wines and anything grilled. They have the grill I’ve seen in Spain. Service was attentive.

La Cuchara is definitely worth a visit. Parking is directly out font and there were plenty of spaces on a Saturday evening. We made a reservation in advance, but they also gave a large bar area.

The menu includes small bites, tapas, entrees, and tinned seafood options. Once seated, they give you a few slices of their fresh baked bread, and you can order a loaf to take home! We loved the onion and garlic bread.

There is quite a lot to choose from on the main menu and they have a large wine list. We ordered the 12-month aged Jamon (to die for), the shrimp, oyster fritters, and lobster broth mushrooms.

Our service was great- thanks to Amanda for some bread to take home after they ran out of the onion/garlic bread. Attentive service and friendly staff.

Great servers polite, knowledgeable, and very nice. Kudos to them. The craziness for the evening - you have a set menu and first they run out of the main entree then they substitute it for another type of fish and right when all the entrees were due to come, they tell us they ran out of the substitute! Wow!
Don’t recommend to come here for special events. Otherwise, this is a good restaurant.

We haven't met the owner yet, but Tim and the waitresses are great! Friendly, attentive and knowledgeable of the menu. We're looking forward to bringing more friends and family here.

document: Roppongi Robata & Sushi. cuisine: Japanese Sushi Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I came for our anniversary and loved their omakase!! The fish was fresh, each piece was unique and delicious. The service was also top-notch, super attentive without being overbearing.

I ended up taking off two stars because they allowed vaping indoors. I saw a guy smoke throughout his meal. I know some might not agree on this take but this was something that mattered to me. In such a cozy environment where you’re supposed to savor your meal, the last thing you want is the risk of second hand smoking. Honestly, I wish I hadn’t docked those stars because it really could’ve been a full 5-star experience.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Easily the Best Omakase Experience on Staten Island

I had an absolutely amazing experience here. I tried the Omakase, and every single course was on another level — super fresh, beautifully presented, and made with real skill. The chefs were incredibly attentive and didn’t rush anything. They waited for me to fully finish each piece before preparing the next one, which made the whole experience feel personal and authentic.

They also offer more than just Omakase. The carne salad was fantastic, and the sushi rolls were honestly some of the best I’ve ever had. You can really taste the quality in everything they serve.

The staff was friendly, professional, and made me feel right at home. This was without a doubt the best sushi experience I’ve ever had on Staten Island, and I’m already planning to come back regularly. Highly recommend this spot to anyone who loves sushi or wants a true Omakase experience.

Omakase is great! They import top quality ingredients from Japan. The Uni is excellent. Spicy crispy rice from omakase is excellent. Food is inventive and fresh. Service is lovely from everyone, including Vincent.

My family and I had the absolute pleasure of attending the tuna cutting event at Roppongi Robata, and it was truly an unforgettable experience from start to finish. The atmosphere was electric, filled with excitement, curiosity, and an incredible appreciation for Japanese culinary artistry.

Watching the chef expertly break down an entire bluefin tuna right in front of us was nothing short of mesmerizing. Every movement was precise, skillful, and educational. The team took the time to explain each cut, the texture differences, and how each one would be prepared turning the whole event into both a show and a masterclass.

And then came the sushi. Every bite was fresh, buttery, and bursting with flavor. The toro was melt-in-your-mouth amazing, and the presentation was just as beautiful as the taste. You could feel the care and craftsmanship behind every single piece.

A special shoutout to Vincent, our host for the evening, who made the entire experience even better. He was warm, engaging, and made everyone feel welcome. His energy and attention to detail elevated the event and made it truly memorable.

If you’re a sushi lover or even if you’re new to Japanese cuisine, Roppongi Robata is an absolute must-visit. The tuna cutting event is an experience you won’t forget. Exceptional food, outstanding service, and a team that genuinely loves what they do.

They recommended I get the tuna omakase since they bought fresh blue tuna. We’ve had tuna in various forms, grilled, sashimi, sushi, along side a deep flavored yet slightly sweetened matcha ice cream dessert and I felt this place was one of the better sushi spots in Staten Island and Brooklyn. Pricing was relatively high but the freshness and taste was worth it.

I saw other people’s food beside us and didn’t really see frozen sashimi but I’ll test that out later when we go back.

After dinner, we got a personal tour from Jennifer, their membership director. She was awesome! Showed us around the whole club, including the swanky members-only dining & bar. And the live Jazz Band? Perfect touch!

Honestly, I'm seriously thinking about joining up with my friend. It's close to home, and I have even some clients in SI & Brooklyn. I can totally see myself hanging out here with friends, treating my clients & even taking my wife for another amazing night out. Definitely a top notch experience 👍

Well. Here it is. The BEST neighborhood bar in Providence. Im not kidding. There are dozens of excellent bars and restaurants in Providence. And I will tell you about all of them in good time- but Point Tavern is where you go when you want to be in good company and have a good time.
Im not originally from Rhode Island and I have struggled to understand the lack of bar culture here. But Point Tavern has restored my belief that… everyone loves a good bar.
A bar is a sacred place where you go to feel good, feel familiar and amongst friends.
That’s what Point Tavern has to offer. The LOVELIEST, most wonderful bartender Derrick, an excellent (way above average) bar fare made lovingly (yes I can taste the love).
The dry rub wings are excellent. Truly. I also want to give a shout out to the hummus dish- this is clearly homemade and has pickled collard greens on the side… just sayin.
I cannot say enough about what a warm and inviting space this is. The music is always good- the backyard is lovely for summer evening drinks and dogs, the bar is always cozy with gentle banter and excellent hosting by the staff. I love this place.

Ten thousand stars.
Oh yeah- I almost forgot. So, they serve breakfast sandwiches here after 10 pm until close.

Besides that this is necessary- It is brilliant, and quite frankly and important public service.

Let me Preface this with, I am not from RI but know that RI has some really good food, for my personal preference, this was not one of them. So when arriving, you have to find street parking, for a Saturday night approx 800pm in the city it was a breeze. When you walk in, its seat yourself and someone will greet you eventually. Our server came around after approx 5mins. I wasn’t too impressed with the drink menu, not sure if it was b/c of  seasonal cocktails being featured, but when in doubt.. go with tequila. ;)  when we got our drinks they were pretty tasty but seemed to be alcohol lacking, nonetheless we scoured the menu to find some food. We decided on the creole crab cakes, wings, and cornbread. The latter was the star of the show, it came with a honey butter and tomato jam on the side. The tomato jam was ok but the honey butter over the cornbread was divine. It was soft with crispy edges and moist. The wings, we could have done without. We ordered the buffalo lemon pepper and they came out with a dry rub and lemon pepper sauce in a condiment cup on the side. -_- they were tender but definitely lacking in flavor. A huge disappointment as the pictures and reviews really bigged them up. Lastly, the creole crab cakes. They had a nice texture but idk where the crab was. I definitely got some bites of the chopped shrimp and sausage but the flaky crab I was looking for seemed to be missing. Our second round of drinks (not pictured) were a margarita and tequila lemon drop. Both were bleh, lacking in taste/flavor. Overall I probs wouldn’t return unfortunately but the music was jumping, the good tunes were the saving grace of the evening.

This is by far my favorite bar in providence! The ambiance is amazing and cozy. The bartender is so friendly and makes you feel like home. The food is yummy with so many options to pick from. Definitely will keep coming here.

The Point Tavern is bar far my favorite bar in Providence! They have incredible food, my favorites are the chopped cheese and Mac and cheese-both are delicious! They also have great specials throughout the week and are an amazing neighborhood bar who often shows fun movies on Mondays! Derrick the bar manger is amazing!

Listen if your looking for a great relaxing night out great food The point tavern is the place to be. Either if it's on the weekend or during the week you can't go wrong. From the drinks to the food one of the best places I have been to in a long time. Service is beyond amazing. The bartenders are amazing it's just very welcoming very clean I highly recommend this place to all. There are a lot of restaurants and bars in RI but The point tavern is my go to. I love Wednesday nights very relaxing from great drinks and service from the bartender Ahmad just one of the best he's very welcoming, once you walk in until you walk out they also have trivia on Wednesday which I love as well. If you go tell them Dwayne sent you. Enjoy Thank me later.

google_reviews.text: Great restaurant at the jersey shore. Recommend getting reservations unless you want to sit watching drew and chefs cook at a bar top for 6 first come….  It was my dads first time here so I said Hey it’s the chefs table where you can sit and watch drew prepare your meal right in front of you.  Special seating lol it’s a BYOB as well.  Food was amazing especially the pork chop was delicious and one of my favorites.  We received piping hot bread rolls and 2 complementary raviolis which were great.  Another favorite which I didn’t get this time the braised short ribs.   Anyway always great food and don’t forget the voodoo shrimp..  will be back

We had the pleasure of dining at Drew’s Bayshore Bistro in Keyport during their special Valentine’s Day event, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. The atmosphere was cozy and romantic — perfect for a holiday dinner — and the service was warm and attentive from start to finish. This is also a BYOB restaurant.

We enjoyed a four-course meal, and every single dish was a standout. Some of the highlights included the incredibly flavorful pulled pork mac and cheese, packed with smoky richness and creamy perfection, and the jumbo Cajun shrimp, which were perfectly seasoned and cooked just right.

For the entrées, the French onion pork was a total surprise — tender and savory with that classic, comforting French onion flavor. The braised beef was equally impressive, melt-in-your-mouth tender and deeply flavorful.

And then came dessert, which was the perfect sweet ending to an already amazing night. The beignets were served hot and fresh, with chocolate and caramel sauces for dipping — absolutely heavenly. The chocolate tart was not only delicious but also beautifully presented, making it feel extra special for the occasion.

Overall, Drew’s Bistro delivered an incredible dining experience that felt both upscale and heartfelt. The food, the ambiance, and the little Valentine’s Day touches made it a night to remember. We’ll definitely be back!

We have dined at Drew's a bunch of times over the years and it never disappoints. It has been some time since we were there last, and overall a great dining experience. The Shrimp and Grits is by go-to and my husband ordered the surf and turf. He said it was the best flavor he has had on a steak in a long time. Plus it was cooked exactly as he likes it. The jalapeno cornbread was good and plentiful. The Banana Foster's bread pudding was a perfect seasonal dessert and we had to take home the homemade "Funny Bone".  Too nostalgic not to try but haven't had it yet. The only few things which led to me not givig a full 5 stars is that it was very cold in the restaurant. Granted we are in an artic freeze but it became so uncomfortable we had to leave before we wantrd. One last thing, and maybe it was a fluke, but the amount of cornbread we had with the Voodoo shrimp seems to have shrunk.

Another terrific meal from chef Drew and all. Food delicious servers knowledgeable didn't feel pushed to turn table. Had appetizer voodoo shrimp. Oysters. And pork rind. All perfect. Pork chop special for entree was tasty and just as good next day leftovers. Leave room for dessert beignet. And it's BYOB. Prices are extremely fair for quality and quantity.
Always delicious! Drew makes tremendous food and a delicious pork chop! The voodoo shrimp is fantastic and the desserts are always to notch. Been coming here for years and it never disappoints!

google_reviews.text:
Great little place in C-Ville. The food is terrific, you can’t go wrong with anything on the menu. We had the cheese board and cauliflower/Brussel sprout appetizer. The appetizer was really good, strongly recommend. The mushroom pasta and the fried chicken breast were well cooked. A ton of mushrooms in the pasta. Very good wine list thats not overpriced or overwhelming.
Very worth the visit.

We picked The Local based on the menu options.  We were traveling and didn't want anything fast, so we looked up food near me.  The Local popped up, was rated high and we always enjoy seeing fresh food options and unique entrees, so decided to give them a try.    When we arrived, the ambience appeared to be casual and comfortable. Our focus is always the food, service, and ambiance.  All areas met my expectations.  I was excited about the crab soup, but unfortunately sold out.  My other appetizer options were crispy shrimp and fried cauliflower & Brussel sprouts.  The flavor of the aioli and seaweed salad on the crispy shrimp was top notch flavorful as well as Sriracha aioli on cauliflower dish.  I would have been happy with both as my main dish.  Our entree was Crispy Fried Trout, a unique twist on fish.  I've never had fish with okra.  It made the dish a bit heavy, but I enjoyed it.  The fish was perfectly cooked and fresh, it was the rice and sauce that made it heavy.  Not sure if I would order again as I prefer my fish with light flavors.  Overall, we enjoyed dining here and our server was pleasant, attentive and personable.  Give it a try, I'm sure you will enjoy your experience.

We hosted a rehearsal dinner Friday night and I cannot thank The Local team enough for such a fantastic event. Our guests loved the food and the service - it was a true celebration. We hosted the rehearsal dinner and then a welcome party in the Opal Lounge and all had a fantastic time!  Thank you all for creating such a memorable celebration for our family!

Wow wow wow this place is excellent. From start to finish the service, food and drinks were phenomenal. They have lots of nice specials, an extensive wine menu and fun cocktails. We got the ribs and sirloin and they were both cooked perfectly.

This tiny spot is a hole in the wall in the best way — serving the best food we had in Charlottesville. The dishes were fresh and fantastic, highlighting locally sourced ingredients and thoughtful seasonal flavors that stand out from the usual tourist fare. The atmosphere was cozy and authentic, making you feel like you’re truly experiencing something unique. If you want a memorable meal that showcases Charlottesville’s farm-to-table scene, this should be at the top of your list.

Overall, Ariana’s Cucina is off to a strong start. Amazing food, good drinks, and a really welcoming ambience. I’m definitely looking forward to going back and seeing how they grow.

The food came out fresh and hot. I had the Caprese Chicken Sandwich — crispy breaded chicken topped with mozzarella, tomato, fresh basil, and a drizzle of pesto and balsamic on a hoagie roll. So good! It came with seasoned fries. My guest got the Mushroom Swiss Burger with caramelized onions, roasted garlic aioli, and portobello mushrooms — another winner.

They’ve got a bunch of appetizers that sound great, so I’ll definitely be back to try more. And true to its name, Mule Barn Tavern has a big selection of mule cocktails — highly recommend trying one!

If you’re in the area, it’s the perfect place to grab a bite, enjoy a drink, and take in the sights.

The summertime vibes here are amazing. Plenty of parking, and right on the water. The drive in and out is really nice too, however at night it can be a bit spooky! So when you get to the Sandy Hook toll gate, you just tell them where you are going; visiting the lighthouse, going to this restaurant, etc.

10/1/2025: The chipotle chicken pasta is the best pasta dish I’ve ever had in my life. The sauce is absolutely incredible. You must try this dish. And the fish & chips too!

NOTE: 10/5/2025, I’ve lost the last 3-4 days of my life to major digestive distress. I’m just now feeling normal again. That pasta dish was the last food I ate that had any sort of substance outside of my home. Do with that information as you may. I have just stopped eating anything outside my home for the time being. I do not know if we will ever return.

We've been planning a visit to the Mule Barn, and coordinated with a day at the beach. It was a beautiful day to sit outside and enjoy the patio. We enjoyed the outdoor area, and the food was great! Amazing food and drinks, even more amazing that they’re dog friendly! As soon as me, my husband and dog came up the host stand the hostess offered us a table that is best for our dog and brought him water! Will be returning when we go back down the shore.

A part of Brooklyn (little pakistan NYC) right here in Springfield, VA.  It's a small world.   So much food for 1 platter I had to take leftovers to go.

A welcomed addition to the neighborhood with very good quality coffee. The interior aesthetics were pleasant and their pricing is quite reasonable. The feta and spinach pastry, tuna salad and egg salad croissant were all very flavorful, but they overly light with the filling, where the ratio between the pastry and the filling were way too imbalanced (which you can easily see in the photos). For how much potential they have, if they add just a bit more filling to them they can easily become one of the top cafes in all of Staten Island.

I hope they take this to heart for I really want them to do well and continue to become successful!

I wish them much luck and I’m very happy to be able to go to a family owned coffee shop right near my job! I’ll be telling everyone to give them a visit! :)
I love all these new cafés opening around Staten Island. We deserve Bunn cafe like this to open up, share their culture and most importantly, coffee, pastries. Very impressed with their service.

name: Marina Cafe
document: Marina Cafe. cuisine: Italian Seafood Lounges. located in Staten_Island. with 3.3 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This was my first visit to the marina several weeks ago and I was very impressed. The floor to ceiling windows offer an incredible view of the marina from everywhere in the restaurant and gives the place a feeling of serenity. Some of the food I tried would rival some of the best Manhattan steakhouse and seafood restaurants. The food was perfectly prepared and plated beautifully
The seafood tower as an appetizer was very impressive with right off the boat fresh tasting clams, oysters, very large shrimp and lobster. The tuna tartare had a very unique and delicious sauce and was mounded on an absolutely delicious fried disk. My other two stand out appetizers were the seafood salad and, a surprise, what they call an Italian eggroll With really delicious Italian red sauce. If you are a lobster bisque lover this lobster bisque was to die for. The Châteaubriand was cooked exactly as ordered, medium rare with house made barbecue sauce and Demi glace which were both excellent with a roasted garlic bulb creamed spinach and mashed potatoes.
The very fresh angry red snapper came on top of broccoli rabe and was topped with very fresh premium crab meat. The best part of this dish for me was the ring of gnocchi around the fish that were like little pillows of softness. The variety of desserts are homemade and all were delicious. If you happen to be there on a nice day and the tiki bar is still open, it is definitely worth sitting out there for a cocktail and a dessert and coffee. I can’t wait to go back there in several weeks for my birthday.

Haven’t been at the marina since 2012. Thought it would be a nice place to catch up with a friend I hadn’t seen.
The appetizer was shared , crab meat, artichoke and spinach dip with tortilla was good. Our main course wasn’t seasoned, very bland, the chicken was raw and pasta soaking in a mixture of water and tomato sauce.
Reservations were for 2:15-2:30. We were feeling pushed out due to a party coming in that needed that area. We learned of this upon arrival. No advance notice was given otherwise we would have changed the date. We decided to leave asap taking our dinners with us. I cooked the chicken at home, pasta was drained but beyond repair, the soaking caused it to become gummy. Our bill with tip came to $162.00. Staff were kind, view calming. Very frustrating how our afternoon turned out.

One of the best Italian spots on the island AND good views ? It's hard to find a place that does both but this one hits the mark. Growing up on SI there have been so many parties and dinners here especially during the summer for the tiki bar, the drinks are well made for the price! I would definitely recommend if you haven't been !

Food was mediocre. We ordered the dry aged rib eye steaks but the meat was more chewy/ striated than rib eye cuts should be. Minimal marbling. Mashed potato was lumpy and looked microwaved. Broccoli was bland and seemed like it was simply steamed. The service was also mediocre- it is apparent they’re not bothered about hospitality and “wooing” customers as the location is the main attraction.

In summary, the price tag is literally for the beautiful waterside view and location. The restaurant has large glass windows so no matter where you sit you get a great view and feel of the natural sunlight.

We started with the dragon shrimp and meatballs. Both were great! The shrimp was our favorite but meatballs were really tasty as well. They also gave us bread with the sesame crackers I love. Then we got the pasta di vincenzo and the short rib. The eggplant pasta wasnt our favorite but not bad. The short rib was very good but tasted a bit like stew meat not what i expect from short rib. Would still get it again just know to expect a more stewy short rib. For dessert we got the creme brule and apple tart. The creme brulle was really good but the apple tart crust wasnt our favorite

name: El Sabor Peruano
document: El Sabor Peruano. cuisine: Peruvian. located in Staten_Island. with 3.3 stars (decent).

google_reviews.text: The food here is phenomenal. We stumbled upon here Wanting something different oh, and we were not disappointed. We've been coming back ever since. The food is fresh and hot and service is always very good. Most of the time the server is barely speak English, so you know the food is very authentic. Many of the dishes accompany rice, french fries, and egg at some point the steak is good and the green spaghetti is great
Honestly a great place we’ve eaten here twice, can be pretty pricey but that being said the food is good, the people are nice. Love being able to eat peruvian food in Ohio.

The food was amazing. The service was excellent. The Cau Cau was juicy and soft, with subtle umami flavors from the peas. The jalapeño in the in-house hot sauce paired well with the coconut they added to it.
Food is Amazing!  Never a bad experience!  A little pricey, but ALWAYS worth it!!!  The quality is top notch!  I eat here, or get a to go order at least once a week!

This was our first Peruvian experience. It was a good time. If we had gotten there earlier we would have had more time to look at the menu. They have a menu that has many many items on it. It is not a hard menu but never having eaten here we did a fair amount of reading to find out what was what. It was a fun atmosphere. People were spread out pretty far from each other giving everyone kind of their own privacy to talk without having to shout over other tables. I had the seafood and steamed rice. I opted not to have the french fries. Fries, steamed rice comes with a lot of the meals. You are able to change them out for other items though. We definitely like that we were not charged to swap out side dishes. They have a sauce made up of Habaneros and jalapenos that you mix with mayo and ketchup. Well we didn't know and thought it was mustard. There was no mistaking that it was hot. My dad and I fought through the heat with quivering lips and a numb tongue. Once we asked about it and it was explained how to eat it, it tasted really good. The burning went away once we started eating our entrées. I'm looking forward to going back again. They have all kinds of live music lined up and its posted on the front doors and in the bathrooms. The place is big enough to dance here as well. As big as it is i cannot call it a hidden gem. But I will say if you like trying new foods please swing by and try this place. Our waiter didn't speak much English but it was good enough to understand what he was saying. If you speak Spanish then you are good to go. Enjoy another culture and sit back and embrace something new. I love looking at places from the eyes of a tourist. It truly opens me up to an entitle new world without having to travel across the globe. That will be coming soon I hope!!!!!!

name: Boriken Restaurant & Bar
document: Boriken Restaurant & Bar. cuisine: Puerto Rican Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
I had to come on here and write a review because this place completely exceeded my expectations. I actually ended up coming here twice in the same week  once with a small group, and then again today (3/7/2026)  for a birthday dinner with a reservation for eight people.

Both experiences were incredible.

First off, the service was outstanding. We had a reservation for 8:00 PM and they seated our entire party right at 8:00 with no wait, which I really appreciated since we were celebrating a birthday. The staff was so attentive, friendly, and made the whole night feel special.

Now the food… absolutely amazing. Every single person in my party was raving about their meal. There wasn’t a single dish that disappointed. Everything was flavorful, perfectly cooked, and clearly made with care.

As someone who is Puerto Rican, I can honestly say the food tasted incredibly authentic. It truly reminded me of the way my grandma used to cook comforting, rich, and full of flavor. I actually just came back from Puerto Rico recently and had been craving that real, authentic Puerto Rican taste, and this place delivered even better than some of the food I had on the island.

That says a lot.

If you’re looking for authentic Puerto Rican food, amazing service, and a great atmosphere, this place is a must. I will 1000% be coming back and already can’t wait for my next visit.

Highly, highly recommend!

The food was good and the drinks were good too!
We got sat right at the entrance which was cute for date night.

Service could have been better, it took about 10 mins to get the menu and some water which is kind of insane since it was literally just two tables in that area and our waitress was only handling our area. I guess they noticed we were getting annoyed so the gave us complimentary soup. We ordered and got the food fairly quickly so no complaints from that. The drinks were good but when it was time to pay, again, had to wait like 15 mins for our waitress to notice we needed the check. She was too busy on the phone (literally on her phone sitting down at a table across the bar not even looking up at her one table at this point). The bartender noticed again we were getting annoyed and she said something. This got us “complimentary shots”.

Again, food was good just wish the service would have been better. I would have 10000x preferred good service over complimentary shots.

Ok, why 5 stars?. The food and drinks were phenomenal. The Staff! Amazing! I’m Puerto Rican , grew up with my grandmother and I barely like going to “Spanish” restaurants because you expect the food to be the same way you grew up eating. This place is it! I felt like I was home with my grandmother again , listening to Salsa and enjoying the ambiance. Thank you for letting me re-live my childhood memories.

I wanted to love this place but it’s mediocre.
The drink I had was great - the Old San Juan .
But unfortunately that was the one highlight.
In short, the food was cold.

Apps:
Beef Alcapurria - lack seasoning
Bacalaitos - too greasy. As someone who is 100% Puerto Rican, and visit multiple times a year, I can 100% confirm these are too greasy.

Mains:
Bistec encebollado with arroz con gandules and maduros - the maduros were good and hot, everything else was barely room temp

Mofongo with Garlic Shrimp - again barely room temp

Salmon Al coco - the rice was hard and again the food was barely room temp

Absolutely delicious and authentic Puerto Rican food! From the start, they serve a comforting sopa de platano that tastes like it came straight from your abuela’s kitchen, instantly transporting you to La Casita Blanca in San Juan. The alcapurrias were perfectly made—crispy on the outside, tender and flavorful inside. The mofongo and arroz con gandules were seasoned beautifully, but the standout was the pulpo a la parrilla—easily one of the best you’ll find in NYC. Don’t miss their homemade pique for an extra kick! Beyond the food, the warm decor and lively salsa music set the perfect vibe. Finally, a true Puerto Rican destination in Staten Island—I’ll definitely be back!

Overall, a great dining experience with excellent ambiance, solid food, and portions that definitely satisfy. I would gladly go back!

I had the best anniversary dinner here. The staff is attentive, the food is amazing and the drinks are out of this world. Hoping for many more years of success for your team! This was the best service I’ve received in all of New York City! Highly recommend the wings and of course the burger. Ordered a light salad and it was the perfect compliment.
10/10 experience! Burgers were absolutely amazing, super tasty! Salad was great as well. The chocolate cake really topped the entire night. Great service as well! Will definitely be back again!!

Lovely restaurant with a cute speakeasy below. Both serve full menu which has great options. I had the steak frites which was a tender, very flavorful ribeye with fries and a delicious garlic aioli. 10/10!

For appetizer, we had the chicken liver which was served chopped and chilled like chicken salad. It came with the best toast I've ever had... so crisp and buttery.

Caesar salad was also pretty good, and cocktails were great!

Absolutely incredible experience. I am a snob when it comes to service and Scott really impressed me!! A big shout out for making our dinner that much more phenomenal. We love their restaurants but in our opinion this one hits the hardest! The burger was by far the best execution with the perfect amount of peppercorn. I was highly impressed with the salad Scott recommend along with the steak tartare. My partner went to heaven with the bone marrow. Overall our experience was a 10/10 and we will definitely be back on our next trip to the city. We never felt rushed, the place was buzzing and the food was outstanding.

This place was super cute. The atmosphere mimics Greece and the food was delish.
The drinks were tasty, but not very strong and the servers were amazing.
The food here was super delicious, I loved the spicy feta and pita

​Greek Island Vibes (Without the $1,200 Flight)!
If you're tired of that New York Winter, duck into Souvlaki GR. It’s basically a Greek teleportation device—one minute you’re dodging icy slush, the next you’re surrounded by blue walls and staff so authentically Greek I expected someone to start breaking plates.
The food is awesome, and the cocktail I "treated" myself to was the perfect Sunday lunch companion (read: it made me forget my toes were numb). 10/10 would hide from the wind here again.

Great place for Korean Bbq. They mainly serve pork options, but they do have one beef option. My friends and I passed by this restaurant, and we didn’t have a reservation. There was no waiting time.

name: Little Ruby's West Village
document: Little Ruby's West Village. cuisine: Australian Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We walked in on a Friday evening at 6:30. Service was fast and amazing. Me and my friends had an amazing time and the atmosphere is something you would expect from a lovely crowd.
We ordered their appetizer:
salt&pepper calamari
I ordered their spicy vodka pasta which was to die for. I would recommend this if this is your first time!

The food at Little Ruby’s is fantastic — the crispy brussel sprouts were a standout and the truffle fries were equally delicious. Everything we ordered was really well done. Would absolutely come back for the menu alone.

The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is the experience. Throughout dinner, staff kept coming by to clear dishes and rush us along. Then the moment we paid the check, someone came over to let us know a reservation needed our table — basically telling us to get up and leave. It took away from what was otherwise a really great meal. A little more tact would go a long way.

This was a delightful spot for a light lunch. The roasted chicken avocado salad tossed in lemony vinaigrette was flavorful with balanced acidity. The fresh pineapple mint juice was a light and refreshing blended mocktail that felt like an energy boost. I also enjoyed the truffle fries and seasonal drink (cinnamon, maple latte). No wait when we walked in at 2 pm on a winter Saturday.

Halloween in the West Village is an experience! Made reservations at Little  Ruby's...thank goodness bc the city of course was packed.  Wait wasn't long and we were seated away from the front but with a window view so we can watch costumed pedestrians walk by. Our Pirate server was amazing! She checked on us often and offered perfect dining suggestions. I had gluten-free Ragu and loved the taste & texture of the pasta (wasn't spongey or gritty).  For appetizers we had the french fries with truffle aoili and the sweet potato fries,  both had the perfect crunch.  The aoili fries was the winner. The other dishes included a huge burger and shrimp pasta. Everyone finished their dishes with no leftovers! For dessert,  we had the chocolate cake with vanilla ice-cream. And to my luck, it was flourless...divine decadence! Great ambience with dim lighting, modern music playing in the background, and diners in their costumed best!

Little Ruby’s West Village never disappoints! The food is always fresh and full of flavor, the pasta was rich and comforting, and the burger with fries hit the perfect balance of juicy and crispy. Their iced latte was smooth and refreshing, easily one of the best in the area. The space feels cozy yet modern, with great natural light and a relaxed vibe. Perfect spot for a casual lunch or weekend brunch. Highly recommend!

document: Bolzot. cuisine: Bars Mongolian. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
The first ever Mongolian bar serving homemade dumplings and beef stew with mantuu — and the food was so good 🥲.
I hope they add more mocktail options that are a little less sweet for those of us who don’t drink much alcohol.
The two ladies did an amazing job with the interior design. The details really stood out — especially serving shimiin arhi in a traditional copper cup.
I really appreciate the effort and thought they put into everything.

I’m so glad a Mongolian inspired spot opened on the Lower East Side. The space is beautifully decorated with Mongolian themes and has such a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The Mongolian dumplings, “Buuz”, are made perfectly, juicy, authentic, and full of flavor💗

TLDR: New, local Mongolian-inspired bar with solid cocktails and great service.

Happened upon the bar while roaming around Chinatown, waiting for Golden Diner. Great service and solid drinks - so sick seeing a bar that’s paying homage to Mongolian culture.
I'm so excited for this new spot! The ambience is lovely and I love the owners of the place! The dumplings are to die for and I'd love to come back again 🥰

Wow wow wow! It was an honor to be at an authentic Mongolian bar / restaurant! It is the only one in NYC. And to see actual Mongolian relics & culture plastered on the wall & shown via items placed in various areas, all while hearing actual Mongolian being spoken is quite the treat! I even got to try Vodka made from Yaks. Definitely not something you can find easily. The dumplings were so good I ordered 2 orders of them and even thought about ordering a 3rd one for the ride home. They sometimes have special meals like beef stew too. Their cocktails are fascinating and the ambiance is great. I highly recommend it!

google_reviews.text:
favorite burger I’ve had in UWS to date. wowow you ever get the feeling when you walk-in somewhere and EVERYTHING hits right? couple irish coffees + pornstar martini. very quality cocktails

nobody’s burger (def add bacon) walks a fully-loaded fine line & nails it. indulgent, but never messy. perfect meat-sauce-toppings proportions where the first bite is as good as the last (EVEN ON A GLUTEN-FREE BUN). french toast sticks are out of this world + one helluva breakfast burrito

if I lived in the neighborhood this would be my go-to “let’s meet up” spot. day or night

So, I really do like this cute spot on the UWS, and would customarily give it 5 stars. The food is always good, and prices reasonable . Their cocktails are interesting and delicious.  The service depends on whose on that day, but it's usually ok. And I love the design of the place. Today, however,  a customer bought a dog and a cat inside the restaurant.  Who the hell brings a cat INSIDE of a restaurant?? Aren't there sanitary rules about this? The creature was adorable,  so much so, that the waitress cuddled it before going back to the bar, surely covering herself with cat dander.  It's really not cool to allow people to bring pets into an  establishment that sells food.  I was shocked  at how some folks are so entitled to think it's ok to bring a dog and a cat to a restaurant not caring that the other patrons might be allergic or afraid of them. Stopped into Nobody Told Me and really enjoyed it! The rosé I had was refreshing, and the Porn Star Martini was extremely tasty. Food-wise, the wings and mac & cheese both hit the spot. Service was quick, the vibe was relaxed, and overall it made for a really good experience.

I’d definitely stop back in again!

Angel and Justin were the absolute best! The two made our night such a great experience from start to finish. document: Golden Diner. cuisine: Diners Breakfast & Brunch Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Came for the pancakes. Stayed for the salad with chicken katsu which was seasoned well and cooked well (juicy). Their kimchi soup was good with the grilled cheese, and sando. Desserts were great too. Would highly recommend. Definitely get a resy or come here and put yourself on waitlist. On lunar new year aka a Tuesday at 2:30pm, still had to wait close to an hour.

On a Saturday morning after getting there early (about 9:10) we checked in with the hostess staff at Golden Diner a little after 10 and were told we had secured a table for 4 which would be ready in approximately 50 minutes. Our group was ELATED. After about 30 minutes we received a text indicating our table was ready. After hurrying back we were promptly seated and greeted by our server. We ordered a double order of plain pancakes, a single blueberry pancake and an order of the fried chicken wings. Everything we ate was as delicious (if not more) than the hype had led us to believe. The chicken was seasoned and fried to crispy perfection with a slightly sweet and slightly spicy flavor. The pancakes were easily the fluffiest I’ve ever eaten and the flavor was pleasantly sweet. Every staff member we encountered was helpful and pleasant and our food arrived hot and fast. My only regret is that I didn’t order more from the menu. Oh well, until next time.

We came here based on the recommendation  of our daughter for "best pancakes" and the Golden Diner did not disappoint. The pancakes were indeed fluffy and delicious. They were so good that I forgot to take a picture of them before eating... Located in a lively and artsy neighborhood on the southern edge of Chinatown, the Golden Diner has a great vibe. Friendly and efficient service. Breakfast items are served until 5 pm which is great. Reasonable prices. But be prepared to wait for a table since the place is small and very popular. If you have some time to pass before your table becomes available, I can recommend a visit to the nearby Management art gallery on East Broadway.

I was finally able to snag a reservation here, and I now understand why the wait times are so long lol. The honey butter pancakes are absolutely divine and by far live up to the hype, I’ve never had a pancake melt in my mouth like these did - they’re somehow both fluffy and creamy, and the honey butter syrup isn’t overly sweet, balanced with just a little citrus from the yuzu. I also got the chicken katsu sando to save for lunch the next day, the red cabbage slaw was perfection and balanced out the saltiness of the katsu and sweetness of the sauce so well. I’m so glad I finally got to try this place and enjoyed it so much that I had to write an actual review, Golden Diner exceeded my expectations and is well worth the commute and wait times. Highly recommend!

We haven’t tried their other dishes yet, but we ordered the pancakes with berry compote, and they were honestly the best pancakes we’ve ever had!
My boyfriend is extremely picky when it comes to food, and even he couldn’t stop saying this place is the best pancake spot.
We’re definitely planning to come back soon just for the pancakes :) ❤️
It feels perfect for brunch, breakfast, or even a light dinner!

This was just what I needed after a long day of working. It was a short walk from my hotel.  I was sat at the bar. The bartender was attentive but not pushy. I order a Cosmo that was perfection. Best in Class in a world-class neighborhood. Not that this place needs any more props, they’ve been here a while and…

Beautiful experience, very knowledgeable and kind staff. We had stopped by for brunch and got their steak & potatoes with their beautiful butter pancakes 🥞. It was so fluffy, it melts in your mouth, perfection. The steak was cooked beautifully and seasoned to perfection.
I’m looking forward to joining them for their dinner service.

Very warm and cozy space; perfect for the fall and winter. We got the specials, clam chowder, rabbit stew, and their take of the Sunday roast. The rabbit stew was probably the best out of the specials; nice flaky pastry with a flavorful and filling stew. The carrots and kale were good side dishes. My fiancé and I’s favorite was definitely the beef steak tartare as well as the cheesy tteok-bokki. The flavors were great and the service was excellent. Would definitely come back here to try their other tartares! (The white chocolate matcha pudding was also really good!)

Absolutely amazing experience at 8282. Every single dish we ordered was incredibly delicious — not one miss. The flavors were thoughtful, well-balanced, and memorable from start to finish.

This is the kind of place where you’re already planning your next visit before you even leave. Definitely coming back again. Highly recommend!

Absolutely amazing Korean food—every dish was on point and full of flavor.
The customer service was exceptional: attentive, friendly, and professional.
The vibe and mood are perfect—stylish, lively, and great for drinks as well.
Ideal spot for both dinner and a night out. Highly recommend.

This modern Korean spot in LES is truly a gem, and I absolutely loved it. The interior is cozy but tables are a bit small, so I recommend reservations if you are come with a group. Service was absolutely stellar—they were so kind to talk to, attentive, and patient.

We got their chestnut makgeoli to drink and for food we got their: grilled octopus, ebi ikura uni tartare, clam sujaebi, scallop jjajjang boribap, 8282 steak, and yuzu panna cotta. Everything was phenomenal. Their chestnut makgeoli was creamy and a delightful pair to the meal. Their grilled octopus was probably the favorite of the night as it was flavorful, amazing texture, and had great sauces. The ebi ikura uni tartare was also good and came with seaweed, but there was nothing super crazy/different about it (compared to other restaurants). I also loved the broth for the clam sujaebi but I felt like this leaned on the more modern side—the sujaebi was a bit different than traditionally, and the broth was also more seafood forward. The scallop jjajjangboribap was good but I wish the jjajjang sauce was a bit stronger/more saucey. And, the steak was amazing. The yuzu matcha panna cotta was the perfect way to wrap up the meal, and by the end of this I was stuffed. Absolutely loved this dinner and I highly recommend.

Overall- I loved this place. It’s also part of InKind. The tuna tar tar was one of those dishes where once you have it u almost want to eat a second. It’s a must.

Food - once we order the tuna tartare it was so good. We almost over a second however, the table next to us had the Uni tartare so he said we’ll take that and it didn’t impress me as much as the tuna I loved it still.

We also ordered the KFC chicken, which was good a little relied to heavily on sauce and we got the Wellington, which was pretty impressive. Lastly, we got the butter chicken, which was delicious with the rice however, the rice could be cooked. There was also a cold onion in it, but the dish wasn’t cold

Atmosphere – The place is full. It’s cute. Nothing too crazy or over the top. Dim it everything is back in a red light, which makes it really hard to take pictures of the food, but that’s OK. Please excuse my pictures.

I love this place but people next to us get the kimchi cheese rice with chicken and it looks so good. I wanna go back and get it and of course get the tar tower again.

document: White Olive. cuisine: Mediterranean Seafood Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Me and my wife had our first date here and eventually the most amazing wedding reception too. All of the food is amazing and our compliments to the chef. Our go-to is the grilled octopus, octopus salad, the branzino and the lamb ribs. If I could give 10 stars for the service, I would. Everyone from Lucille (the event coordinator) and our waitress Saniya treated us like family and the feeling is mutual. The restaurant plays very calming/classy music, such a nice ambience to eat at. I can’t recommend this place more.

It was our second time dining at White Olive and it was just as good as we remembered! We made a reservation just in case, but walk-in would have been fine too. Front of house greeted us warmly, took our coats, and brought us to our table. Full bar, but unfortunately it wasn’t that kind of night for us. We stuck to the dinner menu which offered what I like to call an “essentials”—the menu had everything, yet was simple to focus more on quality rather than quantity. google_reviews.text: Thought I had already eaten my way through K-Town, but this place was a really nice surprise. We started with a few fried dishes since it was freezing outside and we were starving. The soft shell crab was easily the highlight, super crispy and packed with flavor. The fried calamari was also interesting because it had nuts mixed in, which gave it a really nice crunchy texture. We also tried the vegan pancake and it was full of vegetables and surprisingly crispy, almost thought it would be soft inside but it had great bite. The galbi jjim was the main event, with really tender beef, soft rice cakes, and glass noodles soaking up the slightly sweet sauce. We also ordered the Harmony cocktail set which comes with four light fruity drinks that actually glow in the glass, which was a fun touch. Finished with a huge bingsoo topped with ice cream, almonds, berries, and chewy rice cake balls, definitely sweet but perfect to share.

We snagged a reservation for a Wednesday evening and got a table up top in the corner. Our waitress was fantastic and had great recommendations. We split the soju flight, pork dumplings, chicken steamed buns, a Bulgoki bowl and a seafood pancake. Good and service was top notch. Great experience for my first dinner in NYC!

Came here for a team dinner. Service was great, food was amazing, drinks even better. Love the Korean style tapas, get to try everything. Will definitely recommend to anyone looking for a chill place to have dinner.

We went to Barn Joe 35 on a Tuesday around 6 p.m. without a reservation and got seated right away at a table for two. The place is small but cozy — it feels welcoming and not overcrowded, which I really liked.

The menu has a good amount of options — enough to choose from without feeling overwhelming. We started with the chicken bites, which were super good: crispy, came out hot, and had a nice spicy sauce. For the mains, we had beef bibimbap and bulgogi — both were delicious and really hit the spot. I also tried one of their drinks, which was tasty and a bit unique.

They do have a happy hour, but it ends early (around 5 p.m.), so we missed it. Prices are pretty typical for Manhattan: appetizers around $15-$20, mains around $24-$30, and drinks about $20.

The vibe is relaxed and pleasant, the service was friendly and quick, and everything we ordered tasted great.

Overall, I’d give Barn Joe 35 a solid 5/5 — cozy spot with good food, good service, and a nice atmosphere. Would definitely recommend!

name: Wah Fung No 1
document: Wah Fung No 1. cuisine: Fast Food Cantonese. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Wah Fung is the definition of a no-frills Chinatown institution. A true hole-in-the-wall spot where the focus is squarely on the food, not the ambiance.

Service is fast and efficient, but depending on the time of day (and season), expect a line that can stretch to 30 minutes. It moves quickly, though, and the payoff is worth it.

The move here is simple: roast pork over rice. The pork is beautifully caramelized with crisp edges and tender, juicy meat beneath. It’s served over rice with a side of cabbage The roast duck is also solid, though be prepared to navigate bones throughout.

At around $6 for a generous plate (as of my last visit), it remains one of the best value meals in Manhattan.

Cash only!  come prepared.

We did a cheap-eats food crawl through the historically rich streets of NYC’s Chinatown, and Wah Fung No. 1 Fast Food absolutely earned its name. This is a cash-only spot, and you should expect to wait at least 20 minutes in line, but the payoff is worth every second. The roast pork and duck are incredibly flavorful, tender, and satisfying. We asked for extra sauce, and that was the right decision. Do not skip that step.

The value here is unmatched. You can get a small lunch plate for just $6, which comes with a generous portion of rice, steamed cabbage, and your choice of roast pork, duck, or chicken. We ordered the large plate with all three meats, shared it between the two of us, and still had leftovers for later that evening.

One important note: if you order the roast duck, eat carefully. The duck is chopped into bite-sized pieces with the bone still inside, so be sure to eat slowly and stay aware.

If you’re anywhere near Chinatown or doing a historic food crawl of NYC’s best cheap eats, Wah Fung should absolutely be on your list. Incredible food, unbeatable prices, and a true New York experience.

What a wait but for the price and food quality, it was well worth it. Definitely go early to avoid longer queues. That would probably mean opening time 🤣. Ordered the 2 meat for $9 nett. Generous serving of BBQ pork (Char siew) and Roast Duck (that was not just bones and meats which some of the other restaurants serve in Chinatown). If you feel in the mood for some pastries as after meal snacks, you can check out the shop on the right of it.

The strong points are the extremely affordable price and good taste. Personally, I think the roast duck rice is better than the pork and chicken. Also, since the sauce served with the rice is a bit limited, if you want it to taste better, you should ask for extra sauce. The only things I didn’t like were that they only accept cash and that you have to wait over 30 minutes to get your food. However, the price is so good and the food quality is solid, so I think it’s definitely worth coming back, just make sure to factor in the waiting time if you’re in a hurry.

It's exactly what it says it is. We were in town for the weekend and had to check it out since it was near by. It was freezing that day and we waited in line outside for about 20 mins. I could tell there were a lot of locals so I knew it was going to be good.
We were so full from just eating so we got a small pork and duck bowl just to try, it was the perfect portion. It comes over rice and cabbage. The pork, was tender and flavorful, the duck was alright. All that for less than $7.00 was unbelievable. I can totally see why people were lined up to get that pork and they ordered the big boxes.

name: Loi Estiatorio
document: Loi Estiatorio. cuisine: Greek Mediterranean. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
I have been to this Greek restaurant twice, though I seem to have forgotten to write my first review from several years ago. My second time was about 2 months ago, and it was a late-birthday meal with two others. The first time we were sat outside, and while comfortable, I would recommend the inside as part of the lovely experience here, as the staff inside are friendly, and the inside is charming. This is especially true of Chef Loi herself, who is a character and makes everyone there feel special. To drink, for the first time, I am pretty sure I got the Xios Spritz which was enjoyable, refreshing, slightly sweet, and with a good anise flavor from the mastiha. The last time I had a glass of white wine. Both times, we were served nice, warm pita bread, which pairs well with their good-quality olive oil, which they sell alongside mezze and other Greek items.

First time- Bone Marrow Soup (excellent) and Lamb Shank (very tasty.)

The second time, I was with some others, and we shared a bunch of appetizers (honestly, too many, but they always order too much.) Their most unique appetizer was their take on Stuffed Eggplant for $28 with baby eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, onion, tomato, and Anthotyro cheese. The cheese almost served as a semi-soft crust on top of the warm eggplant, with a lightly salty flavor, and the remaining ingredients were soft and earthy. This was good and easily shareable, and I think it could work as a main dish for a vegetarian.

Their Spreads/mixed mezze for $27, which consisted of tzatziki, tyrokafteri, melitzanosalata, and hummus, were of pretty good quality. My preference of the bunch was their version of tyrokafteri, a spicy feta dip, which wasn't too salty compared to some other places. The melitzanosalata was also good, with a nice eggplant texture. The tzatziki was good, and the hummus was fine, though I generally prefer hummus from Middle Eastern spots, as the texture is thicker and the flavor is stronger. The toasted pita pieces went well with the dips.

There was finally an alright Village Salad/Horiatiki for $26 with tomato, red onion, green pepper, cucumber, kalamata olives, feta, and olive oil. I prefer a bit less green pepper, and other spots have had better quality feta, but the vegetables were fresh, and the portion was large enough for the price point. This was standard, and there are better versions at similarly fancy spots such as Nerai nearby, among others.

My main dish was the Seafood Pasta for $49, with the chef's seafood selection, tomato, onion, garlic, and feta over Greek pasta. I ordered this after confirming it didn't contain my usual allergens. The seafood consisted of many mussels, along with shrimp and scallops. The mussels were all open, which is a good sign, though one had a bit of sand. The shrimp were plump, while the scallops were large and tasty. The dish was savory with a bit of sweetness from the seafood and a bit of saltiness from the feta, and was overall pretty good. I believe the other two had the Branzino for $49 with seasonal greens (or horta,) lemon, and olive oil, which they gave me a bit of, which was also great.

They had asked us upon arrival whether this was someone's special occasion, and as it was my birthday recently, they brought over a nice little dessert sampler at the end. The desserts included a baklava, yogurt with honey, and a chocolate cake. The baklava was very cinnamon-forward, which was a bit unique and was a tad dry. The yogurt with honey helped with the dryness, with the chocolate cake being dense, rich, and very mildly sweet. This was a kind gesture at the end of the meal, and we appreciate it.

While not my favorite fancy Greek place, the food here is still tasty, and there is a certain charm that many of the other spots lack, thanks to the particularly friendly hospitality. I would definitely go back here for another dinner.

Loi is unbelievable!!! When it comes to food, friendliness and flexibility. Myself and my wife were having a micro-wedding in Central Park and wanted something amazing that was close by so we could all walk, following our ceremony at the Ladies Pavilion. Alex and Maria (Loi Estiatorio) could not have been more accommodating and flexible to make our wedding day and reception so amazing and so memorable.

First of all, the food is a delight. Greek food that blows Gyro's or kabobs away (those are great too, but Loi is a whole different levl of great). The Octopus appetizer (which we loved having eaten at Loi in the past) was a favorite by all. Branzino and Lamb Shanks were popular dinner options, and the menu had something for everybody.

Great shared appetizers to start, beautiful entrees to choose from, and a all encompassing desert with a little of everything (try the Baklava!!). We also like to drink and the wine was amazing, beer crisp, and the cocktails exceptional (try the espresso martini!).

We had a few late changes to who was arriving, we also wanted to work with a decor person as well as have a wedding cake dropped off, and Loi couldn't have been happier to work with us and our vendors to pull off the most special day on 10/25/25. I've put a few photos of the ambiance, decor and food in the review.

We cannot wait to come back for our 1st wedding anniversary and hope you take the time to read this and give Loi a try on your visit to NYC or if you're looking for something delicious in a beautiful setting.

Thank you Alex and Maria for making our day a dream come true. We will be back and can't tell enough people about you!

- Colin & Debby

My dining experience at Loi Estiatorio, was perfect. Soon as I walked in, I was greeted warmly by Chef Loi and her staff and felt welcomed before I even sat down.

The atmosphere was sophisticated and friendly, the staff were knowledgeable and attentive, and the food was exquisite. I ordered the shrimp pasta and it was amazing. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the shrimp was bursting with flavor.

I had zero complaints throughout the night, but it was comforting to see Chef Loi always circulating around the tables, making sure everything was to our expectation, and it most certainly was. She was so caring and consistent. She made us feel at home, and we were very appreciative of that.

With so many restaurants in New York City, choosing the right place for a meal is always a hard decision. Loi Estiatorio makes that decision very easy. This restaurant is 1000% worth your time.

Incredible food and outstanding products, full of flavor and authentic taste, made with ultra-fresh ingredients. And above all, a smiling chef and a genuinely welcoming team. We had a wonderful evening tonight. Thank you to the entire team !

Had a really great experience here! The staff was super friendly and made great suggestions. The lamb was so delicious! Cooked perfectly and melts in your mouth. The food is organic with nothing fried or use of butter. Although the food was delicious, I could not fully give this place 5 stars because it just lacked full flavor. The food tasted very simple and very lightly seasoned, if at all. It was also pretty expensive which I understand because of the location, the services the dining space and so on. However, as someone who comes from ethnic background where things like flavor and spice are such a huge part of my culture, my taste buds left wanting something more so take my review with a much needed grain of salt. On the flip side, if you’re someone looking for food made simply but done extremely well with a more upscale atmosphere and impeccable service, you have to try this place! I’m not very familiar with Greek food so I can not say how authentic this is but based on Maria, (the owner) story, background and how some of the ingredients are directly flown in from Greece, I do believe it is. If you got the money, want to have a cool experience and love Greek food, I would highly recommend!

Looking forward to trying their entrees...the fried chicken and gouda Mac caught my attention.

By far the best experience I’ve had at a restaurant in months! I’m talking establishments ranging from fast food to fine dining. To begin, this restaurant is situated in quaint Old Town Manassas so you can escape the hustle and bustle. Absolutely enjoyed finding outside. Then there’s the food…great selection, good portions at a fantastic price and OMG, so flavorful down to the last bite! And finally, I’d be remiss to not mention Evan and Steven! These gentlemen were knowledgeable not only about the menu but the history behind the restaurant. They were impressively attentive, and so I never found myself searching for them to request a refill, napkins, or anything else for that matter. If you haven’t visited do yourself a favor and head over ASAP!

Went for lunch here today for the first time in a while. It was fabulous. We had the Club and the Reuben. Both were amazing with excellent, fresh ingredients. The marble rye bread is superb. The ranch we got for our fries was nice and thick, very tasty. Bryant took great care of us, had excellent knowledge of the beers on tap, and made us feel like regulars. We will definitely be back.
Outstanding food at a great price. Fantastic drinks. The best deviled eggs we have ever had. Excellent service. Destiny took great care of us, made great recommendations, and was very friendly.

Wow what a great find!

After a long walk around the battlefield me, my partner and his two brothers were all super hungry!

When I happened upon public house kitchen, my group can be quite particular when it comes to food and we all left happy, satisfied and full!

Danyelle was our server and was super friendly and patient as she happily guided us through the menu making great suggestions along the way! She also mentioned what a great place it is to work and how active the owner is in the restaurant helping out in every department as needed and wow does it show.

We will definitely be back soon and highly recommend them to everyone looking for a great bite and a drink in the area!!

google_reviews.text: While the vibes was nice, the food was mediocre. I would only get their ramyun since you can’t really go wrong with instant noodles. But wow, they used the cheapest quality squid and pork, both were as hard as bricks. Kinda a shame since the sauce was really good. ☠️😅

Not the best place to go. Food was mediocre. Drinks were the standard and was typical NY pricey - 16-17 dollars for soju  service was slow. Not friendly but it was Christmas Eve.

I’d skip here.

I went there with my friends for Sunday dinner to have a good time. The food was okay. Also I like the vibe and decoration.
However the waiter doesn’t seem enjoy working with a service mind or we might did something that make he feel upset.
So the other waitress took care of us and she was very nice.
Our bill was included the tips already (party of 4) fyi
And the bottle of water was not cleaned well…

Came in on a Tuesday night with my friends. It was a group of 4 including myself.  Unfortunately the experience was very disappointing. We were seated in a corner directly under strong AC even though it was around 30 degrees outside. We politely asked if it could be turned down, they unplugged something but the whole section remained cold the entire time, even with our jackets on.

We only ordered soju, beer, and a soda. Once they came around, we asked to move to another table. We were then told to wait, but ended up standing for another 5 mins, only to watch the newly opened table be given to another couple who had just arrived. (It wasn’t a busy night and there were plenty of tables opened). When we were eventually moved to a slightly warmer spot, we had to relocate all our drinks and water ourselves without any assistance.

The biggest surprise was the bill: a 20% automatic gratuity was added, supposedly for parties of 5 or more or after 10 PM which neither of which applied to us. Even the receipt wording was confusing, mentioning automatic gratuity for “parties of 0 or more,” which essentially means everyone gets charged. Considering the level of service we received - basic requests weren’t met, and much of the experience felt self serve. This was incredibly frustrating.
Overall, this place has really declined since pre COVID times, and we left extremely disappointed.

Korean drink bar on the second floor. Not super crowded but still a small crowd of bargoers occupying tables. Decent selection of drinks, courteous staff, and festive decor all around. It’s a nice place to check out for a group wanting to grab a few drinks.

name: Suki Desu
document: Suki Desu. cuisine: Sushi Bars Japanese. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
A cute corridor of a sushi spot. I LOVE THIS PLACE. I have been now both to the UES and the Chelsea location and they are fantastic.
The fish is fresh, the ambiance is cozy, and the service is stellar. I will say, this location is exceptionally tight inside, but it has a nice ambiance nonetheless.
They were even able to accommodate my Celiac disease, with gluten-free soy sauce. The menu is simple and fulfilling. You can't go wrong with anything here!

I went shortly after opening and grabbed a counter seating. Ordered the basic bowl and had the broth added midway. The sashimi was super fresh and I did not need to add any soy sauce to my bowl. The broth is so rich in flavor but light and refreshing at the same time. It's an intimate spot where its mainly bar seating. There is one table in the back that can seat a group of 4

This spot had just what I needed: a giant seafood mountain. I ordered the $28 option with uni. It came with two slices of sashimi with goma sauce, uni and Ikura on top of the kaisendon, and it was everything. After you eat about half of it, you can have broth put in and have the rest as a soup. A++++ 10/10 Will absolutely come back here. Great service and vibes.

$28 Kaisen don was so satisfying. It comes with two yellowtail sashimis on the side. They serve broth in your bowl in the end, I recommend leaving some rice before they pour and eat them together.

The restaurant has only counters, I recommend for people who wants a quick yet high quality food. It was also easy to visit alone.

I ordered the “Fresh From the Sea” ($28). It’s worth the price. The ingredients are fresh and the flavors are well balanced. When you have just a few spoonfuls left, the chef pours soup into your bowl, and it becomes another delicious experience. I will definitely come here again soon because the service is really, really nice.

document: Pio Pio 8. cuisine: Latin American Peruvian. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Love love loveeeee this place! Had a great experience tonight 🥰 food was delicious as usual. I’ve had their food for the past 10+ years but first time trying this location and it was great. We got the calamari, limeneo cebiche for starters and for entrees the Lomo soltado is a must. We also got the corvina a lo macho. The sauce was AMAZING for the seafood. 🍤 great for date night, amazing vibes. If you go in bigger group the seating is even better because of the booth/tables.

My family, friends and i decided to see an off Broadway play and afterwards we were all hungry and we all agree to go to this. We were escorted down these steps into a  large room. They were accommodating since we were a large group with no reservation. Everyone enjoyed their food.

10 of us went to PioPio 8 on Valentine’s Day before we attended a concert at Madison Square Garden. First we were running late due to traffic, we had to postpone the reservation to 6:30. We got there around 6:45 due to parking issues and the staff welcomed us graciously. Not only they expedited our orders because we were running late but they were very patient and professional!
Now the food was a surprise, huge portion and delicious. Every single dish was tasty. We had the sea bass, the shrimp in some creamy sauce, the steak and the chicken; not a single complaint. Everyone of us was happy with the service, the food and the price. We are planning to go back and cannot wait this time. Thank you for a job well done! Kudos to the staff!

Hearty portions and a large and nice restaurant makes for a really solid dining experience in the area.

The two of us shared the chicken empanadas, half a rotisserie chicken and the arroz chaufa with shrimp. By the way, let me get out of the way that the green sauce is so delectable that I could have eaten it by the spoonful.

The empanadas were ok. I've had much better in NYC and I would probably pass on these next time. The chicken was DELICIOUS. They are rightly known for this and I think it's a must get. The arroz chaufa was solid - flavorful and plentiful. It came in what felt like a bucket and is clearly a sharing portion.

We also had chicha moradas. I love chicha morada and have had it in several restaurants in NYC. This version is a little watered down, but still good.

Service was fine - efficient, but not very friendly. Nothing negative, just not anything special.

Came here for lunch twice this week while working nearby. Weekdays around lunchtime (noon to 4) they have a special that's a quarter rotisserie chicken with side and a drink for $15. A great bargain for delicious food! 2nd day was a Saturday, still spent around $30 per person which was reasonable for the portion sizes and how delicious the food was. Service was fast and courteous, everyone was nice. Manager checked in on how we were enjoying our meal. Would definitely recommend and will be coming back!
