name: Malii Gramercy
document: Malii Gramercy. cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Malii Gramercy was such a great experience. The CHO MUANG was absolutely amazing—so unique and beautifully made, nothing like I’ve had anywhere else. The crab fried rice was loaded with crab meat and tasted so fresh and flavorful. We ended with the sizzling roti for dessert and it was incredible—the perfect sweet finish to the meal. Everything was so good and well executed. Definitely coming back!

It was my first time coming here after being recommended on social media and it did not disappoint! Of all the Thai restaurants I’ve tried,  this one probably takes a top spot. The flavors were well-balanced from start to finish. Highly recommend the papaya salad, steamed sea bass, and crab fried rice. For dessert, the Thai tea sizzling roti was a unique mix of savory and sweet. 10/10 recommend!!

Malii Gramercy lived up to its 4.8 rating with a beautiful ambiance and impeccable food. We tried the $119 Lovebirds set and every dish impressed—the Tom Yum wings were crispy and perfectly spiced, the Lemongrass Sea Bass was flaky and flavorful, and the Pad Thai Boran wrapped in an egg net was both stunning and delicious. Added the minced beef basil rice (a must-try). Cocktails were lovely too. Cozy, aesthetic, and ideal for a date night. Highly recommend!

Had dinner at Malii Thai Kitchen in Gramercy and honestly everything we ordered was solid — not a single miss. The restaurant itself has a cozy but modern vibe, perfect for dinner with friends or a date night. Service was attentive and the pacing of dishes was great.
Definitely one of the better Thai meals I’ve had in NYC. Would come back again.

Malii Gramercy is a great spot for Thai food in Manhattan.

We ordered several dishes and everything was well executed with bold, balanced flavors. The Shrimp Pumpkin Curry was rich and comforting, with tender shrimp and creamy pumpkin in a fragrant red curry. The Tom Yum soup was bright and refreshing — properly sour and spicy, not watered down.

The Lychee Duck Curry was a standout: crispy roasted duck paired surprisingly well with lychee and pineapple, giving a nice sweet-savory contrast. The Crispy Sea Bass was perfectly fried with a crunchy exterior, topped with a fresh and spicy mango salad.

The Pad Thai Boran felt more traditional than most — not overly sweet, great wok flavor, and wrapped in a delicate egg net. For dessert, the Thai Tea Sizzling Roti was a fun and satisfying finish.

name: The Brazen Tavern
document: The Brazen Tavern. cuisine: New American Sports Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We ate here prior to heading over to Broadway for a play and it was a great find. The food was good and the staff tag teamed our table so we didn’t have just one server. That was nice because we were able to get anyone to help us, but a little challenging to know who to ask for help. The seating and atmosphere was great. It was just loud enough for ambience, but still quiet enough to have a nice conversation with my friends.
Everything was Delicious.  The Pear & Bleu cheese salad had me in a choke hold. The drinks were perfect and refreshing.  I look forward to going back ASAP.

My visit to The Brazen Tavern was… lackluster.  Liked the exterior and the interior (inside was redecorated while working to maintain a vintage vibe), but the experience was underwhelming. Sparse crowd, and the server told us when we came in that they were about to close (online said they were there 2 hours from closing). Last call was 40 minutes before the server’s closing time, and the server was definitely trying to get us out ASAP. The drinks were fine, but the overall experience felt lacking. Lots of other options in the area; maybe try somewhere else for a better experience.

I made reservations for the Brazen Tavern on a Monday at 3:00 PM—only to realize afterward that they *open* at 3:00 PM. No problem at all though, because Ryan welcomed us right on time and made us feel immediately at home.

The space itself is an adorable, cozy pub—exactly the kind of place you want to relax in before the Times Square chaos. We went specifically for the 3–6 PM happy hour and tried the chicken dumplings, sliders, steak quesadillas, and a couple of cocktails. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and well prepared.

The bathrooms were clean and fully stocked (always appreciated), and the service Ryan provided was truly exceptional—attentive, friendly, and never rushed.

The only reason I didn’t give a full 5-star rating is because the prices felt a bit high for a “happy hour” menu. That said, the quality and atmosphere definitely make it worth a visit. I would absolutely come back again when I’m in the Times Square area.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

A quaint spot my daughter and two grandchildren found after we visited the Madame Tussauds Museum. Atmosphere was great and service excellent. Considering we arrived when they first opened we were the only ones there, so service was attentive. Food was excellent!! I would have given 5 stars but for two adults and 2 children during Happy Hour our bill was $140 without tip and I thought that was a bit pricy for Happy Hour.

name: Bird Dog
document: Bird Dog. cuisine: Southern Tuscan. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
For context, I live in the south and have dined in the gulf coast US

The ambiance is quaint and intimate without taking itself too seriously which I enjoyed. The menu is a prefixe or chefs selection which was also was a welcome to explore a lot of the items on the menu. Portions were pretty significant for two and will leave you feeling plenty full.

I had the hush puppies, Campanella, gnocchi, steak, and fried chicken. All were very good - the rock stars were the fried chicken and Campanelle. Both absolute 10/10 fantastic. The hush puppies were nice and crisp but a bit bland and dry, and the gnocchi was also a bit bland. The steak was very tender, fire grilled, and nicely seasoned, but not sure it was worth the $30 markup over other entrees.

Staff was extremely friendly and helpful, though at a rush period service times were extended so plan on a good ~2hrs.

Overall would visit again for the atmosphere, and to try some other stuff.

A definite 10/10 West Village restaurant. Bird Dog was the perfect double date night spot and everyone in our party opted for the 3 course meal. The table was unanimous in our opinion of the food: every single dish was perfect; the cook on the pasta, the seasonings, the portions, the plating, everything.

The decor was hilarious and adorable - Puppy renaissance. The service was top tier and our server has charisma fitting for the acting industry. The atmosphere was balanced and cozy. The food was so good I forgot to get a good picture of everything before going in!

Food highlights: hush puppies, collard greens w/peanut dressing, baby back ribs, ravioli, fried chicken.

Wow the fried chicken saved my life for sure. This was a great experience. Our waitress was so helpful in deciding our entrees and pairing a wine with them as well. We got the fried chicken which is an absolute must. Okay I lied we got TWO fried chickens. We also got their hush puppies (honey butter was divine) burrata and the pimento cheese. All fantastic choices! I will say we enjoyed the pasta but it was a tiny earthy for my taste. However the vibes made up for it all. Perfect cozy meal with good friends!

Visited here with my 2 gfs and had an incredible time! We came during pasta happy hour and shared the pimento cheese, tagliatelle, the bolognese, and the fried chicken. It was the perfect order and everything was SO GOOD! Antonie was such a fun server and gave great recommendations. 10/10 would recommend!

Was very pleasantly surprised by this place! Not that I was expecting it to be bad, but we came for the pasta happy hour (50% off, 4-6, walk-in only) for a quick dinner before gallery hopping and it definitely exceeded expectations. We shared the orecchiette and tagliatelle and both were delicious - the orecchiette had a generous serving of lamb and the tagliatelle was mixed tableside and super decadent. Each had its own subtle twist of flavor with the mint in the orecchiette and the citrus in the tagliatelle. With the happy hour, it came out to $19 before tip, which was a great deal.

Also want to mention that the (I believe) owner is very kind, and the restaurant itself is so cute and homey with all the on-theme dog photos and moody romantic lighting. We came a little after 5pm and were easily able to grab a table. Will be back someday to try more pastas and apps!

Hands down the best seafood in the city!

A beloved seafood destination that feels like a New England fishing village, fresh, high-quality seafood, lively yet comfortable atmosphere, and excellent service. Key highlights their generous happy hour with discounted oysters and cocktails and a popular lobster roll.

Perfectly cooked cod with a crispy skin and buttery finish. Great happy hour menu for food and drinks. Nice seafood selection. I would definitely return to try other menu options. Attentive staff. Clean restaurant with an elevated nautical motif.

The Mermaid Inn in Chelsea is an exceptional destination for anyone craving fresh and delectable seafood. As soon as you step inside, you’re transported to a charming seaside atmosphere reminiscent of San Francisco, all while being situated in the heart of New York City. The ambiance of the restaurant is lively and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a casual meal or special occasion.

The dining area is spacious, so while making a reservation is recommended to secure your preferred time, it’s often not essential. The staff is attentive and delivers service with remarkable speed, ensuring that your experience is both enjoyable and efficient.

When it comes to the menu, the standout items are truly unforgettable. The lobster roll is a must-try—a generous portion of succulent lobster meat nestled in a perfectly toasted roll, seasoned just right. The tacos are equally impressive, featuring fresh ingredients that create a wonderful burst of flavor in every bite. On the day of my visit, the chef's special was exceptional, showcasing seasonal produce and expertly cooked seafood that delighted the palate.

To cap off the wonderful meal, be sure to indulge in dessert, which, delightfully, is often on the house. Whether it’s a rich chocolate cake or a refreshing sorbet, it’s the perfect sweet ending to an already fantastic dining experience.

google_reviews.text: The Smokey miso noodles was SO GOOD! The dipping noodles was also excellent. Love the thick noodles. Both noodles had a nice texture and chew while the broth popped with flavor. I used to work in the offices above over 20 years ago. It would have been great to have a noodle shop here back then. This is definitely in my top 10 ramen spots in NYC. Don’t need to fly to Japan for an excellent bowl of noodles. Come here.

Lunch special for me, $28. Started with the tsukune (chicken “meatball” bun) very tasty. I got the spicy Dan Dan Ramen, which was flavorful and delicious, the noodles were cooked to perfection, and the broth had just the right amount of spice. The place has a kind of basic/funky vibe, servers were very nice and efficient and the place was quite busy at lunchtime.

Great tonkotsu broth - I am a big fan but tan tan was alright. I was a bit underwhelmed with it. Good selection of drinks and the service is quick and very friendly. Would go back again 100%. Definitely need a reservation unless you want to wait 30mins to an hour for a table.

This place has a Michelin star for a reason. Got the classic tonkatsu ramen and one of the Chashu Tokyo rice balls. The rice ball was fire. Ramen I’ve had a lot of good ramen in my life so this wasn’t the best I’ve had but very good anyway. Great vibe. And one person seating is much faster than a group :)

definitely make a reservation! we tried to walk in at 5pm and it was a 1.5 hour wait, so we made a resy for the next day!

the front gets congested & a bit chaotic as the restaurant is quite busy! but once seated, service is quick and friendly. ramen noodles had a nice bite to it, but the broth wasn’t as complex as i’d like. the baos were unique but overall, everything was a bit too fusion-y despite the great presentation.

document: Cross Road. cuisine: Caribbean New American. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
My husband and I have been going here for years now. We’ve always experienced great customer service, until about two weeks ago.
We usually order food from their deli counter or get prepared sandwiches out of the window. In the past we’ve asked for toppings either put on the sandwiches or on the side and there has been no problem.
A gentleman has even gone above and beyond for us to make delicious food when they’re out of other items we’ve wanted! Ensuring us to come back because of how well they treated their customers.
Today the lady behind the counter was not only extremely rude, but refused to give us any toppings for our sandwiches; claiming they’ve never done that before.
I’m not sure if there are new people working or new management. But as a family who works in customer service, our treatment today was completely uncalled for and exceedingly ridiculous.

We stopped for gas yesterday and when we went inside we found a wonderful place. It was clean, appealing with a vast variety of items and fresh home cooked foods. There's a beautiful place to sit and eat. I found bacon ketchup, and local specialty items. We bought Christmas soda, Butterscotch Beer and Butterscotch Cream soda. Very friendly staff. It's too bad we live an hour away, I would make it my regular place to go. Coming from the deli business in NY, this is a place I would be very proud to work or even own. We'll be coming back whenever we are in the area. Love it. ❤

Bbq sandwiches are amazing, the Italian Sausage was also very good!
We ordered the fried chicken and it was very crispy and big pieces but it does have a little kick to it so it wasn’t my favorite.
We also got some of their made in house fudge and that was 10/10 !!!
I’m so glad we decided to stop and use the restroom otherwise we wouldn’t of known of the Deli/Bakery :)
Try their cheesecake, you won’t regret it!
Great customer service!

I love this place. I can't count how many times I've stopped here, even if it was just to pee.

2. I love the food counter with it's fried chicken and Southern sides and especially, especially, especially, the desserts: cannoli and cheesecake, carrot cake and something called unicorn cake. It's always fun and so hard to choose.

3. I love the local wine and beer selection.

4. I love the dry little grocery area with the quirky dry goods.

5. I love that it's a cozy place to stop to eat and rest on your travels along 29.

6. I love the cute hats and other gifts and the random antiques that adorn the store.

7. I love the boot scrape outside.

8. I love that it feels like it's been there forever and it always will be.

9. I love always wondering what's upstairs.

I live seeing the "wall of shame" inside the front door that features people who are no longer welcome at the store. I appreciate the clean restroom. I like the local merchandise and the assortment of lunch options. Prices tend to be high so I generally limit my purchases.

name: Lert Ros Thai food
document: Lert Ros Thai food. cuisine: Thai. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Had been here for lunch. We ordered curry puffs which were nice and flaky and delicious. We then got 2 lunch specials with drunken noodles and red curry with a side of soup and chive pancakes. We asked it to be made spicy and the food was absolutely delectable. Soup and pancakes were also full of flavor. Service was quick and friendly, decor was welcoming and restroom was clean. Will surely be back.

Totally weird experience here. I have to say. It really comes down to the service. First of all, it took me 25 minutes to get the cocktail I ordered. Which is like insane. I honestly didn’t want it by the time they brought it to me. By the time I did get it, I was impressed with the presentation and taste of the drink. The Siam Mule. It’s good, but it doesn’t really make up for waiting more than 20 minutes, though. The calamari was fine but underseasoned. Our entrees, however, my drunken noodles with crispy pork, came out fine;in fact, there was a clear attention to detail evident in the presentation. My date, however, was never served her rice with her meal. Which is like wild. We made an effort to flag down our server multiple times, only to be told, “It’s gonna take five or ten minutes for jasmine rice.” She offered us sticky rice, which sounded like a better idea than letting our food get cold. Anyway, she returns with this bag of sticky rice, which looked just stupid, honestly, in the context of the rest of the meal. It’s kind of hard for me to trust a restaurant to be operating correctly if they can’t manage to get rice of all things sorted out. I felt like a clown paying full price for my date’s meal.

I visited this place twice for lunch special and for my lunch for a birthday dinner I would go back again. Food is so authentic and spices are so yummy. I traveled to Bangkok, Thailand and food  in this restaurant is so much authentic. !! Highly recommend !
I wish this place to continue to grow. Thank you so much for the amazing service.

google_reviews.text:
Review: Blue Line Fry Plantains – Flatlands, Brooklyn
Rating: 10/10

If you're in Flatlands, Brooklyn, do not sleep on Blue Line Fry Plantains—this place is a whole vibe! It's a small, super clean storefront with big energy. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by the sound of Afrobeats playing on a big screen, and the ambiance instantly set the tone for a great experience.

The menu is stacked—so many tempting options that I didn’t even know where to start. I ended up ordering the fish sandwich made with plantains as the bread (yes, plantains as bread—so good!), with sides of extra plantains, mac and cheese, fried goat, French fries, and some refreshing drinks. Every single item was flavorful and cooked to perfection.

What truly took this experience over the top was the hospitality. The customer service was superb. Despite limited seating, the staff made sure we were comfortable and personally brought the food to our table. The manager—who is also the owner—came over to greet us, check in on our experience, and even offered us a taste of their signature Haitian soup, free of charge. Let me tell you—that soup was on point. I had never tried Haitian food before, but that soup alone made me a fan. It was so flavorful, I honestly wish I had known about it sooner!

From the food to the service to the atmosphere, Blue Line Fry Plantains gets a 10 out of 10 from me. I’ll definitely be back—and next time, I’m ordering a full bowl of that soup!

It wasn't a bad experience. I was looking for somewhere to get some food and decided to try it. I liked the plantain sandwich with avocado and chicken. I'd have to try more meals to give higher reviews

I love Haitian food and couldn't wait to try. When I arrived I parked on the street nearby. I walked into a cute restaurant. The owner greeted and helped me order at the kiosk. I ordered:

Plantain Soup
Turkey and black rice
Chicken and rice and beans
Fried red snapper and mac and cheese
Rara Bowl
Passion fruit and lemonade

All the dishes honestly were really good and the favorite for me was the fried red snapper. So so tasty! I also really liked the juice. All in all was a good experience!

A must try!!! We stumbled here after a nice holiday walk. Seeking to eat a nice dinner at a place we hadn't tried. This was our first time trying Haitian food and it was delicious. From the start they try to make you feel welcomed with a door bell that says this to each patron. No loud music. We decided to eat there but from the looks of it lots of people place orders to go. If you are seeking a hardy home meal I recommend you try this spot.

One of the best haitian food in the entire New York State. Griot is tender, juicy and flavorful. Don’t get me started on the rice and salad russe. Everything is to perfection. Under $20 you can eat a nice plate. The people serving your food are clean, unlike other places where ppl are missing front teeth with nasty attitude

google_reviews.text: Chef's kisses for this beautiful restaurant! From the moment that we walked in we felt like family. This is what quality food is about. The smells, the sounds and the atmosphere is so beautiful. Trust me when I say you will not be disappointed. These meals are prepared with the utmost care. The lamb was out of this world. They do offer gluten free options. Make sure that you ask the waiter. My favorite dessert is the lemon one. I get it every time we go. They can make this gluten free as well. The prices are great for the quality and amount of food that you get. They spare no expense with making sure that you are fed well. The wine pairings are perfect! and the cocktails are great as well. Sociale also offers a private dining space if you want to host a private party.

Wow! René is super attentive and friendly. The bartender was also very attentive and really knows his cocktails. The drinks were amazing, and the pizza was perfectly cooked. The service was more than excellent. Thank you so much! Highly recommend — we’ll definitely be back soon!

We had dinner at Sociale Celler and really enjoyed the experience. The basement private room is small but very cozy, comfortably fitting around 20–30 people, and being next to the wine cellar creates a warm, intimate atmosphere that works well for a group dinner.

Starters were served family-style. The Napoli-style Pizza Fritta was a highlight—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside—and the meatballs were flavorful and well balanced.

For the pasta course, I chose the Carbonara, which was rich, well executed, and made with very fresh ingredients. The Branzino was extremely fresh and simply prepared, allowing the quality of the fish to shine.

Desserts were shared and included the Tortino al Cioccolato, a classic Tiramisu, and the Meyer Lemon Catalana, which was bright and refreshing. The family-style setup for the desserts worked well overall; however, slightly larger portions or individual servings could make it even better, given the no double dipping rule.

Overall, Sociale Celler offers a cozy setting with thoughtfully prepared food and a relaxed, enjoyable dining experience, especially well suited for group dinners and private events.

Calamari was delicious and not too fried, the Eggplant was a small portion but good. Branzino was delectable. I want to go get another bite. The two cocktails were delicious. My Piccante Margarita was perfectly spicy. The Sato Project was fresh and the right amount of sweet.

Overall, this is a great restaurant to try in Brooklyn if you’re looking for an upscale atmosphere. There’s also a bar area if you’d like to just stop in for a drink.

10/10 recommend. The food flavorful the atmosphere a vibe not too loud, the service A1. Server/waiters were attentive. Loved this place will go back. And the drinks were good with cute mocktail selections. The bartender held us down!

name: De Hot Pot
document: De Hot Pot. cuisine: Trinidadian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
I visited KPOT Korean BBQ & Hot Pot in Sterling, VA and had a great experience overall. The employees were very nice and welcoming, and the décor was modern and inviting.
This was my first time trying Korean BBQ, and there was so much to choose from on the menu. Our server kindly offered to cook the meats for us, but my daughter wanted to do the cooking herself, which made it fun and interactive.
The meats were well seasoned and flavorful. I initially chose the spicy soup base, but it was a bit too spicy for me, so I switched to the mushroom soup base instead--and I'm glad I did. I added vermicelli, sweet potato, onion, corn, chicken, and bok choy, and it was delicious and comforting.
The buffet bar was really nice. I enjoyed being able to make my own dipping sauces based on what I like. They also had fried shrimp on the bar--the shrimp were fried nicely, but they still had the full shell on them. I almost choked on a shell, which was a little concerning and honestly my only complaint so far.
The steamed crabs were good, but I think they would be even better if there was a sauce or drawn butter available on the bar. The crawfish and corn were yummy, and the three free juices available at the buffet were a nice touch.
Overall, I had a very good experience and will definitely be back.

Great selection of meat and seafood. All were very tasty. They also have buffet bar where you can get more food, side dishes, sauces, and desserts. Lunch price is a bargain but dinner price is pretty good also. You can get meat buffet or Hot Pot or both for $5 more per person which is still a great price.

The recently opened KPOT Korean BBQ & Hot Pot is located in Sugarland Crossing, Sterling, where another all-you-can-eat BBQ and hot pot restaurant, Running Dish, used to be. This restaurant offers all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ and hot pot options. When we visited, they still displayed Running Dish signage outside, which caused some confusion.

The interior resembles that of the previous venue, with large tables and booth seating throughout. The space is spacious and equipped with sauce stands and self-serve stations offering side dishes like pickled radish, shrimp tempura, onion rings, kimchi, desserts, and fruits. There is an extensive selection of hot pot ingredients and BBQ meats, which is impressive; however, some meats, such as garlic pork, were heavily sauced and had unusual flavors. Service was adequate but could be improved. Overall, the prices are pretty reasonable, especially considering the current rise in food costs.

We went for dinner on grand opening day and had a blast! They were offering $1 mimosas in celebration so I couldn’t pass up… but the food and service made it memorable and I will definitely be back in the future. Everything was fresh and they have a nice sauce bar with a range of options. It was very busy, which I expected for grand opening day, but despite that, they were attentive and timely. Nicole was our server and she was excellent! Definitely ask for her when you come in. 😁
The food 100/10 service 10000/10 everything was so good. iKa made me a hot sauce it was super yummy!!

name: Tom's
document: Tom's. cuisine: Diners American Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: If I could give Tom's Auto Repair higher than five stars, I would! Their team really helped our family out in a tight pickle and saved our spring break vacation in March 2025! It all started on our longest stretch driving between an attraction in Kentucky to our cabin rental outside Shenandoah National Park's Thornton Gap entrance in Luray, VA. Our minivan started making concerning sounds, then started shaking, and eventually threatening to break down as we were pulling up the mountain into Luray in the dark. Here we were hundreds of miles from home and in the middle of our national parks road trip with our rescue dog and two young kids - and our car was done! By God's grace, we made it safely to our cabin and got some sleep. Our nerves were shot! First thing in the morning we were calling nearby  mechanics and saw these great reviews for Tom's Auto Repair. We called them the minute their office hours supposedly started and they immediately answered and helped us make a plan. The Lord helped our van make it to their shop and then they efficiently evaluated what the issue was. Their quick attention helped this not become a full-day waiting event that could have ruined a day of our vacation. Their expert assessment quickly determined that the passenger CV axel that had been replaced the previous year was what was causing the van's problems. And guess what? It was still under warranty! Sherri (Tom's daughter who runs the office) was such a big help as we tracked down the warranty info and arranged a temporary rental car. Their mechanics put us to ease that the repair wouldn't take longer than a day or so. Within about 24 hours, they got our van completely fixed up and we were able to still enjoy our Luray Caverns and Shenandoah National Park hikes as a family. We'll be forever grateful!

I was driving up the steep, winding hill to the north entrance of Skyline Drive when my 2007 Honda Accord started smoking. Panicking, I frantically drove to Tom’s Auto Repair. They took us in immediately, without any wait. The mechanics quickly identified a steering fluid leak as the issue and had us back on the road in less than an hour. Thanks to Tom’s Auto Repair, our friends' hiking trip was saved! They were incredibly nice and respectful, and the check-up price was surprisingly affordable. Tom's Auto Repair truly saved the day with their prompt, caring service.

I've always gone to Tom's for help but recently I had a tire removed and they jacked up the wheel so bad there were gauges on the barrel of the wheel where there shouldn't have been any contact, the duckbill is there for a reason. Getting my own tools and doing it myself from now on, ASE certification and proper equipment isn't part of good business practices apparently. Definitely a place to maintain a low value vehicle.

I was passing through Luray on my way back to Georgia and my check engine light came on. I stopped by two other places in Luray, but they were full and they directed me to Tom’s. The lady in the office was delightful and was willing to check what was going on immediately, even though there were other customers and they were clearly busy. The mechanic was also incredibly nice. They quickly discovered what was needed to get me back on the road. They could have easily gouged me or told me anything, but instead they were honest and I was on my way for $57 and about 30 minutes of waiting. I made it all the way back to GA with no problems at all. When you don’t know a lot about vehicles, it’s easy to get taken advantage of, but the wonderful people at Tom’s are honest and do good work. Thank you for your help.

Best repair shop experience I’ve ever had! The service team was able to replace our alternator within two hours on a Saturday morning, New Year’s Eve. If it wasn’t for Tom’s, we would have been stranded in town until the following Tuesday. Not only was their work great, but the staff was super friendly and welcoming. We now have a favorite shop whenever we’re in town. We are so impressed. If you need anything for your car or truck, this is the place to go.

document: Casa Azul. cuisine: Mexican Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Visiting the Frida Kahlo Museum was truly eye-opening. I’ll be honest — before coming, I didn’t know much about her life beyond the fact that she was an artist and married to Diego Rivera. But walking through her actual home, learning her story, and seeing where she lived completely changed my perspective.

Being in that space makes her life feel very real. You really begin to understand how much pain and hardship she endured, yet how deeply creative, resilient, and influential she was. Even during times when she was sick or confined to her home, she still maintained a powerful circle of influential friends and continued to shape culture in a meaningful way.

The museum does a beautiful job of showing how much Frida contributed not only to art, but to Mexican culture as a whole — and how her impact continues even today. It gave me a much deeper appreciation for who she was beyond the paintings.

Definitely worth the visit. If you’re even slightly curious about her life or legacy, this museum is a must-see.

Buy tickets weeks in advance. We could only get a 19:15 slot and were somewhat disappointed by the lack of lighting in the courtyard: the garden and its plants where in pitch darkness & the blue of the blue house was barely visible. Also, the souvenir shop was closed since 17:30.
The website advertised Thursday nights as a special event with music and a special atmosphere, though during our visit it was silent and we didn't notice any special effort being made.
All in all, we feel a bit cheated because we paid to see the Casa Azúl but everything was dark.

This museum was everything I hoped for. Frida has been my favorite artist for over a decade and I was so excited to visit. It definitely didn’t disappoint. Her home was lovely and felt so much like her. I only wish there was even more information, but I left feeling like I was on cloud nine.

I was honestly a little disappointed with this museum, I was hoping to see a little more of her artwork. Granted this museum was mostly about her life, which was nice to learn about, but frankly quite repetitive about her story.... I must have read the same history about her life as a student/being handicap/love affairs 3 or 4 times throughout the museum during the 1.5 hours I was there. The garden was colorful and nice, but was not personally worth the cost/time in my opinion. Also don't worry about purchasing merchandise in their shop because you will find better options on the street with vendors at a cheaper cost.

Really interesting museum, stunning both inside and out. I especially loved how each room tells the story of Frida and her influence. Would recommend buying tickets in advance, and unfortunately the best way to do that is through overpriced places such as GetYourGuide as it’s sold out months in advance.

google_reviews.text: Mannie has Jedi mind powers. Idk where he gets his magic. 2 work buddies and myself walked in hungry and only knowing they had great reviews. We arrived and  Mannie took awesome care of us. This guy is next level. He could be a maitre d' in a Michelin restaurant. Having eaten at that level, you get to appreciate the dedication to the craft. Food was as good as any I had in Mexico, which is saying something. You will not be disappointed unless you really hate mexican food or can't stand great service.

Outstanding service! We are regulars, and they  remember our drinks and food.
After moving here from Honolulu, we spent some time looking for a great Mexican restaurant to our liking. We found it here and have visited multiple times and it always proves to be a great choice.

I booked a part of 16 two days in advance, knowing our group would have delicious food, great service, and delicious margaritas. We weren't disappointed! This is my go-to Tex Mex spot in Alexandria, and I always recommend it to friends. Absolutely love it.

I live in Texas and eat a lot of Tex Mex.  I don’t know if this qualifies as Tex Mex but it is very good.  I like the salsas that come with the chips.  The green chili salsa is tangy and just a little spicy. I ordered the chorizo enchiladas that comes with fruit and your choice of potatoes or refried beans. Other members of my party ordered the  vegatable enchilada lunch with salsa verde, refried beans, and sour cream and an egg and cheese enchilada with refried beans and fruit.  The brunch menu items come with fruit. All were delicious and a lot of food. Our server was Manfredi and he was awesome.

Dos Hermanos is certainly deserving of its 4.6 rating on Google. I dined 🍽 here with a friend right at opening time this past Tuesday. It was my very first visit here. Teresa was our server, and a delightful young lady. I ordered chicken enchiladas with tomatillo sauce and refried beans and it was delicious 😋. You could tell from the nice presentation this entrée was the real deal. The thick, crunchy chips and chunky salsa were great, too! Beautiful dining room, pleasant service and nice ambiance...I'll definitely be back!

This cozy and inviting coffee shop, with plenty of seating, great place and friendly service

name: Karasu
document: Karasu. cuisine: Japanese Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Hidden within another restaurant, this speakeasy izakaya offers a thoughtful, seasonal menu crafted by a superstar chef who began his career in Tokyo. Each dish is beautifully and deliciously prepared, complemented perfectly by cocktails mixed by their amazing bartender. The experience of おもてなし(omotenashi; Japanese hospitality) at this spot is so apparent that by the time we left, my two dinner companions had already declared they’d become regulars, eager to bring their clients next time. I cannot wait to be back next time.

Really cool space behind the restaurant Walters. Dark, vibey interior which really complimented the food and drinks.

Drinks were delicious, creative, and well organized. They had a wide offering of drinks and cocktails which work perfectly with the menu.

The food was so very delicious. Prepared perfectly with authentic Japanese flavors. Really enjoyed the Wagyu tartar and the winter bean salad. The unagi don was also outstanding.

Perfect for an intimate date, will be back when the occasion calls for it.

Tucked behind Walter’s, this moody little Japanese spot is seriously special. The interior is stylish and intimate, with a gorgeous bar and super friendly staff that make you feel right at home.

We sat at the bar and watched the magic happen, the sashimi was fresh and beautifully presented, and everything had that quiet confidence of a place that knows it’s good.

Grab the perched booth and enjoy a lovely view of the bar and rest of the place. The scallops, hamachi, ikura don, & black cod are works of art and taste. The sake & Japanese whiskey options rank some of the best in the area. Go, relax and enjoy the view!

Celebrated our anniversary here. Was perfect for us. We were looking for a place that had some elegant food without the pomp of an overly serious stuffy tasting menu place and this was exactly it. The service was great- pleasant without being overbearing. I have no idea what the negative reviews were talking about regarding service. Atmosphere wasn’t loud and overwhelming like many nyc restaurants. The food was great and cocktails were absolutely delicious. Highly recommended. Absolutely will go again!!

name: Radio Kwara
document: Radio Kwara. cuisine: African. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: An excellent experience from start to end. We ordered every dish on the menu for a group of 5, and the flavors were so bold and unique. Everything was great, but some personal favorites were the goat pepper soup, the toast with mushrooms, the cabbage and the beef short rib. The staff was exceptional and very attentive. Loved the simple and minimalist atmosphere too. A strong recommend without a doubt.

Ordered the entire menu with no regrets. To be specific with the absolute bangers: the mushroom bread, the pepper soup, and the puff puffs. The bread and mushroom has so much flavor and should be your first stop to start your palette. The soup is POW flavor with a delicious spice. The puff puffs are lighter than they seem and the guava will have you digging at the bowl for every drop.

If you’ve never enjoyed the delights of Nigerian cooking - welcome to Radio Kwara, an absolute gem that brings traditional Nigerian dishes, BYOB, and a beautiful setting together for a tremendous treat.

If you are well versed in the enjoyment, you will chop life well at Radio Kwara.

We tried just about everything on the menu and spent about $500 - not necessary by any means but 100% worth every penny for such a feast!

Can’t wait to go back - highly recommend!

Wanted to love this place so badly! Loved the record player playing old school African music and that there was a wine store next door as the restaurant is BYOB. The vibe and service were 100/10. However, the food is good..... but in no way shape or form does it taste like West African food. I felt that for the price, the portions were small and lacked pepper- pivotal for West African cuisine.  (It wasn't even available as a condiment).

A group of us had the opportunity to dine at this restaurant as part of Tasting Collective, where a pre-set menu was created to showcase the cuisine. While I understand that a tasting experience may not fully represent the regular menu, it provided a glimpse of what might be expected.

One area of concern was the spacing of the restaurant. It is quite compact, which made it challenging to be comfortable throughout the meal. Despite my petite stature at 5’1”, I found it difficult to stretch my legs.

We began our meal with the goat pepper soup, which was enjoyable and had a bold flavor profile, though it was quite spicy and may not have been the most suitable choice as the first dish for all guests.

The subsequent dishes featured minimal meat, leading to the perception that we were enjoying a primarily vegetarian experience, which may not have aligned with everyone’s expectations given the higher price point of the tasting menu.

Before dessert, we were informed that the planned “Nigerian Sweet Dough” was unavailable, and we would instead be served ice cream and caramelized plantain. It was a bit surprising that a restaurant would run out of key ingredients for a tasting menu, especially since we were the first seating of the evening and had provided an exact count in advance.

While I appreciate the effort put into the dining experience, I must admit that it may not be on my list for a return visit to Brooklyn for a redo.

google_reviews.text: I love a dive and this place provided! Aisling was phenomenal; she was constantly busy, yet consistently on top of everyone’s drink orders. She’s incredible!! We had a chicken Sandwich and a Burger + a little birthday drink for my boyfriend -> thanks a lot for this ♡

It was very delicious and a nice evening.
Great service!  The locals know where to go.  This is the place.  We had the Icehouse Burger and Fries.  Generous side of thin, hot fries and a loaded up cheeseburger.  Glad we discovered this place!

Rated high for the overall atmosphere and dive bar vibes. The food is broadly average at really good prices. Solid enough food if you’re having beers and enjoying the evening but not good enough to come for on its own. The 7.5 burger was a little soggy bun with little in the way of flavour. The 7.5 wings were a good size but a little dry. The fries and onion rings were 6.5 at best, far too over crisped. The best dish was the 8.5 tater tots, great fresh fry and salt combo!

This place is so awesome, that I proposed to my girlfriend there this past Saturday night. Our friend Liz brought us last year and we had such a great time and everyone was so nice and real, that it is now a special place for us. Such a great place with great people. name: Westville Dumbo
document: Westville Dumbo. cuisine: Comfort Food American Salad. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We picked this at random and it ended up being our favorite meal on our first trip to NY! The staff was super friendly. The pork shoulder with au poivre was incredible. I could eat a bowl of the sauce on those mashed potatoes. The beets were incredible. It’s simple stuff, but it’s made very well.

Shout out to the cooking staff. The food was awesome turkey sausage egg and cheese with arugula salad. I also had the French toast . I could only eat one bite I had to take it to go. Service was excellent Roberto was professional and gave great recommendations. Atmosphere is cozy and friendly. Also can't forget the bartender whom brought us the drinks. Last but not least the host for the warm welcome. Your team did an exceptional job

I visit my son in New York and we always try a new place.  I will definitely be coming back the food was so good so fresh perfectly cooked.  Service was excellent and I love the atmosphere.   I recommend the salmon plate I got the asparagus with Parmesan cheese and the kale with caramelized onions.  My son got the kale salad. We also ordered the empanadas for an appetizer everything was excellent. I can't wait to come back

Randomly chose this place after walking the bridge. Host and waitress were very friendly. Ordered the Beyond Burger with a side of the Pesto Mashed Potatoes (can I say i have never thought of this mix but it was superb👌) cant recall what husband ordered (steak pictured) but he enjoyed his food as well. He ordered some kind of tea as well but it wasnt his favorite - he's not a herbal tea drinker and was trying something new since it was cold! I got a passion fruit margarita with sugar rim and it was delicious (and strong!)  Wouldn't mind eating here again in the future.

I love going to Westville in DUMBO — it’s such a trendy, farm-to-table spot, and their brunch is definitely my favorite.

The space is super aesthetic, with both indoor and outdoor seating, plus a really cute indoor patio situation that makes it feel open and airy. It’s a great vibe whether you’re meeting friends or just want a relaxed but stylish brunch setting.

The food comes out fast, and the staff is nice and attentive without being over the top. I really enjoyed my brunch salmon salad — the portion was large and absolutely worth the price. Everything tasted incredibly fresh, especially the vegetables, and I loved all the toppings. You can really tell they focus on quality ingredients.

I also ordered the Blueberry Spritz mocktail, which wasn’t too sweet and still felt classy and elevated without alcohol. If you prefer, you can add prosecco to turn it into a cocktail.

I’ve gone back multiple times and definitely will again. Westville is always a solid brunch choice in DUMBO.

google_reviews.text: Went with my wife after church service, instead of take out, we dined in. The food is great, service is impeccable. While we were there, they attended to almost 20 orders. The jollof rice is solid.
The meat pie was dry, like cracker dry.
The chicken, well see for yourself never have seen wings so thin and rock hard like some of the other reviewers mentioned. There were some feathers still visible on there too. Thus I will not chance eating the chicken. I ordered via Ubereats and the food was still nice and hot which was a plus.

I’ve ordered food from them plenty of times, the food is flavorful but you do not get a lot of meat at all, plus the cow foot is always very hard. Maybe that’s how they cook there meats traditionally but I had to put mine in a pot and cook it some more when I got it home. The jollof rice is good.

I stopped by after the lunch crowd left and had a great meal. Both the meal and atmosphere contributed to satisfaction. The team's service approach deserves praise. The yelp community knows about this restaurant. This place creates a lovely environment.

The food here is very promising! I do not think the ponmo is worth $18 at all. But the $4 meats are usually one big piece in a little bit of stew which is fair.
I have not tried their soups just stew and plantain.

name: Montesacro Pinseria Brooklyn
document: Montesacro Pinseria Brooklyn. cuisine: Italian Pizza Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Walked in on a Friday night and was seated immediately. The people after us were offered seats at the bar while they waited for a table, so I would say get there earlier if you don’t set a reservation.

My friends and I ordered a bowl of cacio e pepe and each got a pizza to split. The casal bertone was everyone’s favorite! The perfect combo of flavors combined with that crispy guanciale (don’t let this scare you away if you’re not used to it) had us all wanting more. The infernetto was okay, nothing spectacular honestly but still good to me. A tougher sauce critic at the table rated it lower. We didn’t really enjoy the Tufello. It felt like it was missing something, so that one we didn’t finish.

If you’re drinking, the Caligola was great and I could see myself ordering that every time. Our Arnold Palmer critic said “it was all Arnold and No Palmer…1/10”. Our waitress was kind enough to remove it from the bill.

I would recommend this place to others. It’s a nice vibe inside for sure and overall you’ll enjoy the food

Montesacro was a great place to have a solo dinner.  I sat at the bar. The staff is friendly and service is quick. I ordered the Carbonara and Tiramisu, both were amazing. I also had a glass of Pinot Noir. I’ve had better, but it was fine overall. When I dine alone, I like to read a book. The noise volume was conducive to doing so.

Came here for thanksgiving and was so impressed! The restaurant was full of people and energy. They had a wonderful menu along with Thanksgiving options but it wasn’t a pre fix like so many other places were trying to do. Had a wonderful meal and would definitely return again!

I absolutely loved this Mezze Maniche alla carbonara. From the first bite, it was pure comfort. This is the kind of dish I could happily order again and again. Simple, comforting, and done so well. Definitely one of my favorites.

One of the best vegan pizzas ever be ever had. The dough was 11/10, and the toppings were all amazing. Large sizes and very homemade tasting. No non dairy cheese, just red sauce and toppings. Other group members liked their traditional pizza and carbonara pasta. Great drinks, cozy atmosphere during a blizzard. Overall perfect experience

document: Omar's Indian Fine Cuisine. cuisine: Indian Pizza Bagels. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and lamb vindaloo lunch box. Good amount of food for $15.95, came with rice, dahl, meat and naan. Lamb vindaloo is spicy! Chicken was ok.

We got take out and it was excellent, great Indian flavors, nice portions. I am vegetarian so all of the veggie dishes we have ordered have been delicious.   The food is fresh and not oily. Great Indian spice.  Highly recommend!
Also Omar and staff are generous kind people.

I was in the neighborhood around 1:30pm on a Friday, and I saw that Omar's had decent reviews. There was only one other party aside from me inside, and they have a decently sized space. The interior has a nice ambiance if you do decide to sit down.

I thought the special was a steal for $17.95! I ordered the vegetable samosas, naan, and chicken saagwala. The samosas were the hugest I have ever eaten, and the filling was very tasty. There was a bit of a kick to the curry filling if that's something you are sensitive to. The naan could have used a touch more moisture, but I liked that it wasn't charred and had some fluff. Regarding the saag, the chicken was MOIST, which is such a rarity in curry. The saag is also more on the pureed side, which I don't mind. Flavors were on point, and I only had to spit out one cardamom pod.

When I sat down, they brought me a large bottle of water, so nothing needed to be refilled. Service was more impersonal, but maybe would be better if it was busier. The one complaint I had was that one of their employees came back from a smoke break, and the cigarette smell was so strong and disgusting.

Overall, this will be going down as one of my new favorites, and I will be back to try the unique pizza and some of the other dishes.

Omar’s is always great

Family run, inexpensive

Tikka masala pizza all day every day :)

Not a drop of food left

I love Omar’s. I’ve been here several times—even though it’s a bit of a hike from my apartment—and I’ve also ordered delivery. The food is consistently outstanding: simple, classic Indian dishes that are fresh, flavorful, and an incredible value.

Their prices have stayed remarkably reasonable over the years, and they haven’t cut corners on portion sizes. The dinner combination (entrée, side, and bread) is my go-to, and it’s always enough for two meals.

The service is friendly and welcoming every time. Highly recommend.

name: Blackbird
document: Blackbird. cuisine: American Lounges. located in Brooklyn. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: My name is Rowles Adams, I’m a current resident of the Blackbird DC and have been since September. I expressed to Bertha how I was looking for a new home in a short amount of time and she worked diligently to make it happen, her bright and kind personality eased my stressful situation. Angel does an amazing job with keeping the relationships of the building team strong, everyone does an amazing job working together at keeping a positive and peaceful environment. Also shout out to Isaac and Jose whenever I have a problem with my apartment they are always there the next day and if they can’t they work around my schedule and I’m grateful, I love my new home.

Great apartment complex — I truly enjoyed my time living here. Josue and Isaac from maintenance were always wonderful, and Bertha and Angel in the front office were equally great. I would have loved to stay longer, but life had other plans.

I adored my time at blackbird. Amazing walkability, as well as accessibility to metro across the street. Bertha and Angel took care of me! They took my concerns seriously, and addressed them promptly. Maintenance was always performed the day of the request, and I loved having peloton treadmills in the gym! Having the roost downstairs provided an amazing social element as well that was really fun, and the security at the roost is great so I don’t feel it raised any safety concerns.  If you’re considering blackbird, I suggest it!

Unprepared, uncommunicative, and unprofessional — that’s been my entire experience with Blackbird. As I write this, today was supposed to be my move-in day. Instead, I showed up to find that the unit they assigned me was not the one I agreed to lease.

Bertha, one of the leasing staff, told me the apartment I was shown was “identical,” just with a slightly different closet and balcony. That was completely untrue. Not only was this a completely different unit but it they tried to move me into an ADA (or a unit tailored to accommodate people living with disabilities) which no one ever mentioned, and to make matters worse, it was unprepared to which I only found out because there was no dryer installed. When I pointed it out, Bertha seemed surprised, like they hadn’t even realized it themselves.

After haphazardly admitting the mistake, Bertha said she’d reach out to the property manager. It took TWO HOURS for him to respond because there’s no leasing office or on-site staff at this property. Mind you I was, fresh off a flight, standing outside with all of my belongings, waiting.

And honestly, this lack of communication and disorganization didn’t start today. Throughout my entire application process, I constantly had to follow up because my emails and calls would often go unanswered until the next day and even then it was me having to call back. I can’t count how many times I was told “Bertha will call you back,” and she just never did.

On move-in day, I even had to wait 20 minutes for someone to show up to the building just to let me in. That alone tells you how inconvenient it is to rent in a so-called luxury building with no leasing office, no concierge, and no real support. I was never informed of where the loading doc was let alone if there was one at all. If something goes wrong — or even if you just have a question — you’re basically on your own.

After hours of waiting, confusion, and zero urgency from their team. Angel, the other shadow manager, finally called to inform me they would not provide me with a unit . I ended up having to scramble to find a place to stay for the night because they completely dropped the ball.

If you’re thinking about moving here, please take this as a warning:

1. Leasing staff are only reachable by phone or email and rarely respond promptly. Expect to chase them for updates.

2.There is no concierge, no on-site office, and no security staff despite the building being marketed as “luxury.” Anyone with a fob can easily slip in and out especially since the bottom floor is a public food court.

3.Communication breakdowns are common. Accountability is nonexistent.

As frustrating as this entire experience has been, I’m actually relieved it didn’t work out because the more I saw, the more it became clear that living here would’ve been a huge MISTAKE.

I strongly DO NOT recommend the BlackBird Apartment property in DC.

The best apartment building I have lived in Washington, DC by far! The size is perfect, the entire staff from management to concierge and custodial, are all super friendly and helpful, the residents I've encountered have been courteous, considerate, and respectful, and you cannot beat the location. Really appreciative of finding this community.

**Updated**

I've been living at Blackbird for about 8 months now and couldn't be happier with my decision to move here. It's the perfect-sized apartment complex with great amenities and a convenient location - shopping, restaurants, public transit, are all right at your fingertips in this capital hill/eastern market neighborhood. The Blackbird team are all very welcoming and attentive -  quickly responding to inquiries, maintenance requests, and are friendly staples to the community.  Angel has done a brilliant job engaging with residents, listening to feedback, and creating fun and exciting events like live music on the rooftop, wine/beer tastings, free meals from The Roost (located just below us), Salsa dance lessons, among a host of other things. I would highly recommend moving here particularly if you are a young professional or creative person looking for a unique, smaller apartment community, that has a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere.

4.5/5!

name: Landmark Cevicheria
document: Landmark Cevicheria. cuisine: Bars Latin American Venues & Event Spaces. located in Brooklyn. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: I visited Landmark Cevichería with a friend, and it truly surpassed my expectations. The restaurant is absolutely beautiful, spotless, and spacious, creating a welcoming atmosphere. The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming. We initially sat at the bar for drinks, but once we saw their delicious plates, we decided to dine in as well — and we're so glad we did! We enjoyed the mini lobster tacos, chicken skewers, and tuna & seafood ceviche, all of which were absolutely delicious. The drinks were fantastic, especially thanks to our bartender Douglas, who expertly prepared our cocktails and customized drinks to our liking. He really did an amazing job. We loved this place so much that I can't wait to return. I definitely recommend it if you're looking to try something new and exciting!

Landmark Cevicheria in Brooklyn, NY is an absolute gem! The moment you walk in, the décor sets the tone beautiful, inviting, and full of charm. The service is excellent, and the food… truly outstanding.

We started with the freshly made guacamole, and from there everything just kept getting better. The ceviche was the star of the night—perfectly balanced with a bright citrus touch and just the right amount of ginger. For drinks, I enjoyed a delicious chicha morada pisco sour, while my husband had a classic Pilsen Callao.
Our waitress, Lady, was wonderful—attentive, friendly, and very knowledgeable. Even more impressive, the owner, Petro, personally came to our table to explain the concept of his restaurant. He is incredibly kind and clearly passionate, with a deep understanding of the industry.
We also tried the tacos al pastor, the rib-eye tacos, and the seafood soup—all flavorful and highly recommended.
If you’re looking for a place with amazing food, great service, and a warm atmosphere, Landmark Cevichería is a must-visit! Highly recommended.

Landmark Ceviches — Park Slope
Such a great vibe from start to finish. I had the Everything Ceviche, fish tacos, and the Landmark Old Fashioned—all 🔥. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully done.

Shoutout to Douglas the bartender—super friendly, great energy, and really made the experience. The drinks were especially impressive: well-crafted, balanced, and so many options to choose from.

If you’re craving ceviche in Park Slope, this is the spot.

YOU MUST GO.
The food was fantastic, the drinks were fantastic, and the service was fantastic. We were visiting from out of state and stumbled upon this place by chance, and now we’ll be recommending it to every person we know who visits Brooklyn. I have no idea why it’s not already impossible to get a table here — it deserves to be one of the most popular spots around.

First off, the atmosphere is lovely — the decor, the lighting, the vibe — everything feels intentionally designed and effortlessly cool. It would be a perfect spot for a date night or an evening out with friends. The whole space has this moody, European charm that makes you want to linger for hours (which we did).

The staff were absolutely incredible. Every single person we interacted with was genuinely kind, warm, and knowledgeable — not in a forced way, but in that “we love what we do” kind of way. They knew everything about the mezcals and the food, and their recommendations were spot-on. We ended up staying several hours simply because we were enjoying the experience so much.

We started with the watermelon tuna ceviche, and it was phenomenal — such a unique, refreshing flavor combination. The shrimp ceviche was also fantastic, with lots of interesting textures, but the watermelon ceviche was our favorite overall. Then came the lobster taquitos, which were not what we expected — in the best way. Instead of rolled tortillas, they were these tiny, perfectly crisp little tacos with fresh, flavorful lobster and a squeeze of lime that made them perfection.

For drinks, I had the passion fruit pisco sour — sweet, tart, and just phenomenal. We also tried a few mezcals and a mezcal margarita, and every cocktail was balanced and beautifully made.

This is all just my opinion.

Please please please rethink your branding. The name reads generic upscale lounge and isn't inviting or suiting for the neighborhood. The logo is milquetoast and can't be read from distance. I've spoken to at least 6 or 7 others who have all shared the same exact sentiment. I would lean into a fun, vibrant Peruvian vibe. I understand the need to include Mexican menu options but that also is a little weird to me since there is a lot more competition in the neighborhood for Mexican

Now that I got that out of the way, overall good food. The lomo saltado was solid but coating was a little too saucy. Very nice service. Food can be improved a bit, but I'd really like to see you guys succeed

document: For All Things Good. cuisine: Cafes Mexican. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This is hands down my favorite neighborhood spot. Everything I’ve tried has been consistently delicious, but their tortillas truly stand out. The birria & consomé tacos are my top pick, though the mushroom tacos and flautas encabronadas are also a must-try. Pair your meal with a nixtarita, or go for the horchata if you’re skipping alcohol — you can’t go wrong either way.

I ordered two tacos here to spend some time with a friend who I hadn’t seen in a long time. The cashier got my order completely wrong, but I was so wrapped up in the conversation I didn’t really realize until I’d eaten one.

(I'd had few options as a vegetarian so the "vegetarian option" I was given didn't register as wrong until it was almost too late.)

I returned the other taco and asked if they could just charge me the difference (in *addition* to what I already paid) and give me what I actually ordered. The cashier refused to do this and walked away from me.

The taco I had was pretty terrible so I insisted something be done (any good restaurant would fix the issue right away and not even charge extra).

The cashier finally offered to give me one of the tacos I originally ordered (remember, originally the order was for 2) and charged me $4 to add avocado to it.

So, I ended up paying almost $15 for a terrible taco I didn’t order and one decent taco that I did order.

Never again.

name: Flora
document: Flora. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars Wine Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Stopped by for brunch on a Saturday afternoon. Flora Flora had good food, great drinks and a great view in a beautiful space. Here are some of my takeaways:

Environment
Flora Flora is located on the second floor of the Pendry Hotel in the Wharf. It's a beautiful space with a great view of the river with inside and outside dining space. No matter where you seat the view and space is amazing. Wonderful and beautiful ambiance great for friends or for date night.

Service
Our server and the staff were great with a lot of energy. Very welcoming and friendly and made sure we had everything we needed. Accommodating and ver easy to engage. Great experience.

Food and Drinks
They have a pretty good brunch deal for DC.  For about 60 dollars you get bottomless sangria, an appetizer and a main dish. The food was really tasty. I had the wharf benedict which was poached eggs, crab cakes instead of a biscuit and, old bay hollandaise with home fries. It was very good and not too heavy which was pretty refreshing. My friends had the blueberry pancake and the truffle spinach quesadilla. My friend enjoyed the pancake - it does present more like a muffin so be mindful of that. The quesadilla was fine but not a favorite at the table. And the guacamole was good too! The drinks were pretty good and plentiful. I would definitely come back for this brunch special and especially for the benedict.

Overall
Overall we had a great time here - we even stayed past the closing time. The space was quiet, beautiful and welcoming, the service was great and you can't beat the views. Definitely try this place out.

Located within the Pendry Hotel, we stopped down for breakfast at Flora Flora and had an excellent experience. The restaurant is beautiful, the service was great, and the breakfast, while expensive, was amazing. We all loved our dishes and will definitely be returning each morning of our stay!

The vibe for this place is outstanding, located on the second floor of Pendry hotel. The view from the hotel is simply amazing! The staff is very nice and professional. I headed to this place for a weekend breakfast, and enjoyed my time here. I had almond latte and huevos rancheros, fresh, delicious and rightly portion sized.

On a Saturday afternoon, Kishore and I went to Flora Flora, which is located on the second floor of The Pendry at the Wharf. Since we came for drinks, we sat at the bar. They had lamp lights on the bar that didn't move and were nailed down. They serve as a seat divider. I'm not sure what beer my friend had. I enjoyed the Mayan Mango Pisco Sour, which consisted of Pisco, Mango, Lime, Simple Syrup, and Egg White. It was sweet, fruity, refreshing, but strong! I hope to return soon to try their other Pisco Sours and Grilled Squash Caesar Salad!

The food is terrific. It is positively evident- Everything on the menu is deliberately curated. The scallops were my favorite, so sweet and succulent. The filet was delicious.

Opportunity for improvement:  the service could be a bit more timely.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Review by Vanessa Caballero
Date: Saturday, October 18, 2025

I was born and raised right here in Jackson Heights, and I’ve visited many diners in the area over the years—but Florence Prime Diner truly stands out as one of the very best.

We visited on Saturday, October 18, to celebrate both my birthday and my daughter’s 11th birthday, and everything about our experience was absolutely wonderful.

The chicken soup was outstanding—rich, flavorful, and full of fresh vegetables. It tasted exactly like homemade chicken soup, the kind your mom would make when you were little. The broth was perfectly concentrated, and for that delicious soup alone, I give five stars without hesitation.

The coffee was excellent—fresh, smooth, and never bitter. The staff offered refills generously, which made our breakfast even more enjoyable. I would easily give the coffee a 10 out of 10.

We also tried the mini waffles with berries, which were light, fluffy, and perfect for sharing. My daughter had the green chilaquiles, and they were exactly as we requested—not spicy, since she doesn’t eat spicy food. They came beautifully served with rice and beans, and she loved every bite.

For my birthday meal, I ordered the carne asada, cooked exactly the way I asked—tender, juicy, and full of flavor. It was served with two over-medium eggs, potatoes, and a fresh salad. The meat was so soft that it was a pleasure to eat and enjoy every bite.

To make the celebration even more special, the waiters kindly sang “Happy Birthday” to both my daughter and me, bringing a cheesecake topped with fresh berries. Everything was so fresh, delicious, and made with care.

Our server was incredibly kind, polite, and attentive, always checking in to make sure we had everything we needed. We truly appreciated his warmth and professionalism.

It was a lovely family moment—especially since my son, who is currently away at college, joined us to celebrate. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, making our birthday celebration truly unforgettable.

We’ve often walked past Florence Prime Diner, but this time we decided to stop in—and I’m so glad we did. From now on, this will be one of our favorite places in Jackson Heights.

Ten out of ten for this beautiful diner—thank you, Florence Prime Diner, for making our birthdays so special!

— Vanessa Caballero

name: Phayul
document: Phayul. cuisine: Himalayan/Nepalese. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We visited here following the 13th annual momo crawl in Jackson Heights which this establishment did not participate in in 2025. Looking forTibetan cuisine on Yelp, this place came up.  There are actually 2 locations on the same street, right across from each other. One location upstairs and the other on ground level. This is for the newer ground level spot.
Small dining area, but 1 or 2  tables for groups available.
Full bar and bottled bear selection.
This are some tradional Tibetan dishes,and they do have momo,  but dishes seem more a fusion of the Himalayan regions and and other fare.
I really wanted to try the laphing appetizer, a spicy, cold noodle dish. I liked the texture of the noodles. The filling was super hot! I am not sure if chili oil was the only thing inside, but seemed like it was.
We also had the stirred fried beef with radish which did have a nice flavor,  although some of the meat slices were chewy. The chicken lollipops, which were originally ordered dry, came to the table with sauce and were not dry. The owner seemed perturbed with us, asking us if we were sure we ordered it dry. They took it back. The other main dish came out and the correct chicken dish took a good amount of time to arrive.
Service was cold. There were no checks ins and we did feel a little ignored and had to ask for drink refills and the check when someone walked by. We were told the check had to be paid at the bar (it was never brought to our table) but when going to pay, no one was at the bar. Little confusing.
I did not look carefully enough at the check to see if the automatic 18% tip was charged as other reviews pointed out. We left a generous cash tip.
Cozy atmosphere and the restroom was relatively clean.

First of all people need to understand food and culture. There isn’t a “maitre d” here this is a homely hole in the wall with great food. If you sant to be waited on hand and food this isn’t the place for you. If you appreciate good food and culture this is a perfect representation of such.
Authentic to it’s theme and the amazing food speaks for itself
Momo’s are amazing and juicy and bok choy and beef stir fry top tier.
Visit Eat Enjoy

Hello everyone,
I want to share one of the worst experiences I’ve had this year. I’ve been to many restaurants in my life, with both good and bad experiences, but I have never encountered service this terrible before.
•	The ordering process was a complete disaster. They didn’t even bother to listen properly, brought the wrong order twice.
•	The waiting time was ridiculous. It felt like they forgot about us, and we had to remind them multiple times.
•	The staff were extremely rude and careless. Even to simple questions, they gave cold or disrespectful answers. A smile? Forget about it.
•	The place was messy and poorly maintained. Tables were dirty and the overall atmosphere felt neglected.
•	The food quality didn’t match the price at all. The dishes were tasteless, and the portions were surprisingly small.

Honestly, this place was nothing but a waste of time and money. When you go to a restaurant, you at least expect basic respect and decent service—here, you get neither.

So my advice is: if you’re looking to enjoy a nice meal or a pleasant evening, do yourself a favor and stay away from this place. For me, it will always remain the restaurant with the worst service I have ever experienced

It’s a very simple yet pretty place. Has minimum decoration but it looks neat n clean. Service is fast n good momos we’re really good. They were with potato and Veges. A very different combo but would just slither in the mouth

Phayul Restaurant offers a cozy, albeit compact, dining experience with a lively and constantly bustling atmosphere. The space is small, and it’s common to find yourself waiting for a table, which is a good sign for their business but may cause some inconvenience for guests looking for a more relaxed experience.

The service was satisfactory, considering there was only one server handling all the tables. This may be due to the restaurant’s limited serving area, but the staff remained efficient despite the busy environment.

As for the food, it was a mixed but generally positive experience. The Chicken Shapta was delicious and cooked to perfection, while the Lhasa Chicken stood out with its rich flavors. The fried rice, while decent, didn’t particularly shine. The Momos were enjoyable, though not remarkably different from others in the city. However, the Mokthuk and shredded potato was somewhat disappointing compared to the other dishes.

Overall, Phayul Restaurant delivers on flavor with its standout dishes, but could improve on the dining experience, both in service and space. A great spot for flavorful Tibetan cuisine, especially if you’re not in a rush.

This was my first time here, and I’ve already decided I want to come back for my birthday next year🥹 Honestly, I wanted to order almost everything on the menu.

The clams were incredibly fresh and plump, huge clams, super juicy, and perfect with a beer🍺

Both the lamb skewers and lamb kidney skewers were delicious, cooked just right with great flavor.
We also ordered the frog ($58), the portion was huge and definitely worth it, the 🐸 was very tender and clearly not frozen.

The lamb and beef skewers are over-marinated and lose their natural taste. I do not recommend the lamb leg since it is about 200 dollars, takes a long time to cook, and often ends up overcooked. Their dumplings and stir-fried dishes are quite good and worth trying. The biggest downside is the service. 9/20/25

Amazing breakfast spot. The lamb innerds soup or lamb soup are one size only, giant bowl like a mini bucket. The innerds are a few slices of lamb and tons of tripe, there’s no lungs or other organs. Soup comes with a free bread (shao bing). Amazing for $10.

There’s 3 parking spots available in front of the restaurant.

You can tell everything is made fresh, and the flavors taste like something straight out of China.
