Overall, the experience was fun, smooth, and well-organized. I left feeling happy and well taken care of, and I’d definitely return.

Umi Hotpot is such a fun spot to eat at. There’s a wide selection of food, including sushi, seafood, hot dishes, desserts, and more, and everything we tried was fresh and tasty. The ramen surprised me in the best way… super comforting and really good for a buffet. The place is clean, the staff is attentive, and you definitely get your money’s worth. A perfect pick if you’re craving variety and want to leave full and happy! 🍣🥢🍜

I came here for weekend lunch with my dad and overall had a really good experience. The food quality was solid and there’s a huge selection, especially if you love seafood. Tons of options across the buffet — although I was a little sad there weren’t any scallops.

One thing to note: many of the buffet items aren’t labeled, so it can be hard to tell exactly what you’re picking up. Also, not every tray has its own serving tongs, so sometimes you have to borrow from another dish. That could be a downside if you have food allergies or strict dietary preferences.

The atmosphere is really cool — lots of Asian-themed decor and calming music that makes the space feel relaxed rather than chaotic. The restaurant and bathrooms were both clean, which I always appreciate.

Service was adequate. The staff were polite, just not especially warm or chatty. They charge a 12% service fee and tips are not expected.

It is on the pricier side (and even more expensive during dinner and weekends), but honestly, I think it’s worth it for the amount of selection and quality. If you want to try it at a lower price point, I’d recommend going during weekday lunch first.

And side note: they include unlimited boba tea with the buffet, which is kind of amazing. At other places, that alone can cost close to $10 each. Here, it’s included — and yes, I had multiple.

Overall, I’d come back. If you go in knowing what to expect price-wise, it’s a fun experience with a lot of options.

Honestly the best buffet around. But of course, like with every buffet, there are hit and miss dishes but most of them are very good. Only down side is the wait time. Just be prepare to wait 1-2+ hrs depending on day and time you go. You can use a kiosk upon entering to add your party to the queue and they text you when it’s ready. Highly recommend to pay attention to where you are in line so you can come back if you do decide to leave.

**Now I decided to add this part in but just know it’s not part of the buffet food.** They had this Facebook promotional event where they’ll ask you to post their flyer on your Facebook page and each person who post will get steak and lobster for free. They didn’t seem to be opening advertising it in the restaurant, seems to be an ask to know basis. We only found out about it after another table personally told/show us. Now, that was fun and all, steak was good but lobster was RAW. We notified the server, he told us to cook the lobster in the hot pot broth if we need it more cooked. Not the response we expected but it’s free so I won’t complain. I figured these would be helpful for others to know.

UMI Hot Pot & Seafood in Rockville, MD is amazing! 😋🔥
They have fresh seafood, sashimi, sushi, hot pot, fried rice, and so many options to choose from. 🦐🐟🍣

The seafood tastes super fresh and high quality — you can tell right away when you take the first bite. The sashimi and sushi are delicious, and the hot pot broth has a lot of flavor. 🍲✨ The fried rice is also really tasty and pairs well with everything.

The place is clean, service is fast, and the food comes out quickly. ✅
Perfect restaurant for family, friends, or group hangouts — you will leave full and happy. 😄

document: Caleta 111 Cevicheria. cuisine: Seafood Latin American Peruvian. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Food was phenomenal. Portions were kinda small for the price (everything is pricey ) I recommend the ceviche appetizer and the rice with seafood was amazing.

Pisco sours are very solid. The ambiance feels like being transported to a different realm, forgetting one is in queens and not lima, peru.

Caleta 111 is a culinary gem in Richmond Hill!

This place NEVER disappoints. My husband and I have dined here a few times, and have ordered takeout just as much. Honestly, if I could eat this every day, I would.

The menu offers a journey through vibrant, sometimes unexpected, yet surprising flavors and thoughtful dishes. My personal favorites are the Tiger's Milk, Lomo Saltado, Chica Morada, and cancha - which is a perfect snack on its own! The Tiger' Milk is an explosion of fresh, tangy and savory flavors that excite the palate, while the Lomo Saltado is the ultimate comfort food - perfectly seasoned, tender, and packed with bold flavors.

If you're looking for something different, order the Chaufa de Mariscos. From the very first bite, we got instant dopamine hits - the unexpected flavors were a sensory experience that left us saying "ooh!" with each bite.

Don't leave without ordering the Chicha Morada. Its a definite must-have. This refreshing, cold Peruvian purple corn drink is lightly sweet with hints of cinnamon and clove that make you feel at home. It's like a non-alcoholic mulled wine, but better - comforting and reminiscent of Christmas, pure perfection in a glass.

[I think they rotate desserts, but if the Peruvian ice cream is on the menu, definitely try it. I'll be back to try the others.]

The staff is always attentive and friendly. Whether it's your first time or 10th time, they'll ensure you have a great experience. If you're unfamiliar with something on the menu, ask and they're more than happy to explain and recommend dishes that suit your tastes. This definitely adds to the cozy vibes of the restaurant.

The decor is another standout feature, most of it seemingly handmade - I think I've seen them working on a few pieces in the past (I live in the neighborhood). Every detail feels intentional, with a personal touch that perfectly complements the amazing food.

From the appetizers, to the desserts, you can taste the quality and care that the chefs put into every item on the menu. Whether you're dining in or ordering takeout, Caleta 111 is more than a meal - it's a flavorful adventure I know I'll return to  time and time again.

google_reviews.text: Stumbled on this spot on a busy Sunday morning. The menu is packed with great dishes and they have just about anything you can think of to customize any dish. name: Stanley's Pierogi
document: Stanley's Pierogi. cuisine: Specialty Food International Grocery Polish. located in Queens. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: This place is about fresh pierogi.  That's it.  You walk in, there a counter to the right and a poster in front showing you all the varieties of pierogi they make.  Some are dessert pieroysuch as strawberry, strawberry and cheese, blueberry, blueberry and cheese, chocolate and then there's the varieties of savory pierogi.  It's a filled dumpling inside unleavened dough that's boiled and then baked with butter or fried before serving.  It's a food eaten from Eastern Germany all the way through Russia, meaning Romanians, Ukrainians and most famously in America, the Poles.  In the heart of a traditional Polish neighborhood lies Stanley's Pierogi. Their pierogi are made without eggs though some contain meat, and are fresh and delicious.  Every time I'm in the neighborhood, I can't help but stop by.  This place is just to pick up pierogi to go.  There's a counter and a refrigerator behind.  You walk in and wait for someone to walk up and hand you what you ask for.  They're pleasant enough, but they're not very gabby.  The prices are beyond reasonable, especially given the freshness and quality of the product.  Come in, look at the chart and figure out what you want and ask for it after a quick greeting.  If you need help, they will help without going into too much talk.  There's nothing short or rude about it, they have to get back to work in the back.  There's nothing to the decor, it's all spartan and that's it.  Just perfect for what you came for in the first place.

I felt the tension leave my shoulders when I sat down. Their dishes showed no special care. Staff members maintained excellent attention. They provide a broad selection of dishes. The employees maintain high standards consistently.

Stanley's Pierogi shines brighter than others. The staff was incredibly kind - completely sincere. Their drinks program shines and their food holds its own. The people working here are as good as the food. As a newcomer to the area, I'm thankful to have found this place.

The environment here is as good as the menu. The kitchen earns highest possible ratings. The experience here stands out. Staff members combine efficiency with genuine interest. The restaurant maintains standards across the board.

Stanley's Pierogi is a hidden gem - a small shop that packs big flavor. Their handcrafted pierogies are simply irresistible, especially when fried.

My top picks? The sauerkraut & mushroom, and the creamy spinach & cheese. Each bite is a delightful explosion of flavors and textures.

What sets Stanley's apart is their versatility. You can enjoy these Polish dumplings piping hot at the shop, or grab some premade to cook at home for a quick, delicious meal. With a variety of unique fillings to choose from, there's always something new to try.

The price surprisingly doesn't raise considerably, but of course comparing to the portion size 4 years ago, the dishes become a bit fewer. As long as they could maintain the food quality, the size doesn't really bother me.

If you are craving for outstanding authentic taiwanese food in NYC, this is certainly a place you shouldn't miss.

name: Tong
document: Tong. cuisine: Bangladeshi Food Trucks. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Tong in Bushwick is where you go to experience authentic Thai small plates known as kub klaem. The sleek dining room wrapped in rustic metal walls captures that raw NYC energy while still feeling clean and cozy with lighting that mirrors how vibrant the food tastes. Tong does not hold back on spice and a simple medium Thai spicy is no joke, definitely not for first timers and even seasoned spice lovers might find it daring but that heat brings out the true and unapologetic deliciousness of Thailand. From cocktails to small plates everything is thoughtfully crafted and plated like edible art. If you love Thai cuisine or crave bold spicy flavors, Tong is the perfect spot for incredible food creative drinks and warm hospitality with genuine smiles that go the extra mile.

Came here to say with my brother and his finance. Pretty nice restaurant. The prices were decent. Large portion sizes. The tom yum soup was amazing. It was spicy but full of flavor and texture. I had the green curry with tofu and it was one of the best I have ever had. The curry was smooth and the rice was fresh and not sticky. I’m he tofu was the perfect texture for the broth. My brother and his fiancé got the drunken noodles and I know they loved it because they finished the bowl.

Went on a date night to Tong, a Thai restaurant in Bushwick recognized by the Michelin Guide. Because of how popular it has become, it’s definitely best to make a reservation ahead of time since the space fills up quickly and many people come specifically for the food.

The atmosphere makes it a really nice date spot. Dim lighting, warm wooden tables, and thoughtful plating give it an intimate feel without being overly formal, and the staff were warm and welcoming from the moment we walked in.

To start, I ordered the Jolean cocktail made with gin, lychee, butterfly pea flower, orange blossom water, lime, and egg white. It was light, floral, and well balanced, with the egg white giving it that silky foam texture. My boyfriend kept it classic with a Thai iced tea, served in a mason jar with the familiar gradient of dark tea and creamy milk that gives it that rich sweetness and deep caramel color.

For appetizers we started with the Som Tum Thai, one of Thailand’s most iconic salads. Traditionally from the Isan region in northeastern Thailand, som tum is all about balancing the four core Thai flavor elements: sour, spicy, sweet, and salty. The dish came with long strands of shredded green papaya piled high with peanuts, cherry tomatoes, long beans, dried shrimp, fresh chili, and a wedge of lime on the side. The green papaya itself is mild and crunchy, almost like a vegetable version of a green apple, which makes it perfect for soaking up the lime heavy dressing. The dried shrimp added a deep umami note while the peanuts gave it texture. It was refreshing but still packed with flavor, with the dressing lightly pooling at the bottom so everything could be tossed together.

We also ordered the Truffle Spring Rolls, filled with glass noodles, shiitake mushrooms, and oyster mushrooms. Glass noodles, made from mung bean starch, absorb flavor really well and give that slightly chewy texture that works perfectly inside crispy spring rolls. The mushroom filling was earthy and rich, and the truffle added an aromatic depth that made it feel slightly more elevated than a typical vegetable roll. The fry was clean and crisp without feeling greasy, which made them really enjoyable.

For mains, I ordered the Pad Cha Talay, a seafood stir fry known for being bold and aromatic. Pad cha refers to a style of stir fry loaded with herbs and spices that create a fragrant, slightly spicy dish. This one had shrimp, squid, and mussels with bamboo shoots, eggplant, long beans, kaffir lime leaf, fresh green peppercorn clusters, and krachai, also known as fingerroot, a traditional Thai herb with a peppery, ginger like aroma. The seafood was cooked well and the vegetables still had a nice bite to them. The bamboo shoots and eggplant absorbed the sauce nicely, while the fresh peppercorns added small bursts of spice throughout the dish. It was served with a dome of fluffy jasmine rice that paired perfectly with the aromatic sauce.

My boyfriend ordered the Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup from the Chiang Mai region known for its rich coconut curry broth and the contrast between soft noodles and crispy noodles on top. Flavor wise, the broth was really delicious, warm, creamy, and comforting. However, the presentation and balance could definitely be improved. The chicken was mostly hidden under the broth and noodles, and the portion leaned heavily toward noodles compared to the bean sprouts and other components. If the ingredients were distributed more evenly, visually showing the chicken, noodles, and bean sprouts, it would elevate both the presentation and the overall balance of the dish.

Service overall was great, though water refills could have been a little more attentive.

For a restaurant recognized by Michelin, the food here is already strong in terms of flavor and execution, but there are small areas where things could be elevated further, particularly presentation and balance in certain dishes. With a few refinements, it could better match the level that the pricing suggests. I would definitely come back to try more of the menu.

name: Casa Enrique
document: Casa Enrique. cuisine: Mexican. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The place has a modern feel, the service was excellent, very attentive. The sauce and the tortilla work is very impressive. We got the shrimp ceviche that was a special of the day and it had an interesting fusion sauce, with Asian notes to it. The sopecitos were outstanding. I thought the carne asada lacked flavor a bit. But the tortillas were some of the best I have had. The flautas were disappointing. The entire filling was super crispy and over fried so there was no texture contrasts in the dish.

We had brunch on a Sunday and it was great. We had reservations, but it wasn't too busy at about noon.

Here are the positives: the service was really wonderful - perfect mix of attentive and leave you alone; the table hot sauces are FANTASTIC; the guacamole was really delicious and the pan frances (french toast) was phenomenal. Okay, I don't really have negatives...but the other dishes were just good (nothing spectacular). The fish tacos and albondigas were tasty, but not standouts.

Overall a lovely brunch, but I definitely want to return for dinner.

Food was AWESOME! Everything tastes homemade and packed with tons of flavors and spice. We had the special shrimp ceviche, the enchiladas, branzino, the cheese ice cream was out of this world and the tres leches was the best. Cocktails were delicious and made with fresh juices not that sugary bottled stuff. Can’t wait to return, I highly recommend.

Casa Enrique continues to be one of the best restaurants in Long Island City and it fully deserves its reputation. Every time we visit, the food is consistent, fresh, and full of bold flavor. You can taste the care in the cooking, whether it’s the guacamole, ceviche, enchiladas, or their signature mole. The dishes are beautifully balanced without being overly complicated, which makes the experience feel both comforting and special.

The service is another reason we keep returning. The staff is warm, patient, and genuinely welcoming. Even on busy nights, they make you feel taken care of and always offer thoughtful recommendations. It is clear they care about creating a positive experience for every guest.

The atmosphere is relaxed but polished, making it a great spot for a casual dinner or celebrating something meaningful. It has become one of those rare neighborhood restaurants where you want to bring friends and family just to share how good it is. We also love that the quality has never slipped no matter how popular it gets.

Casa Enrique is a true gem in Queens. If you are in LIC and want an amazing meal with great service, this should be at the top of your list.

My cousin from the Philippines were visiting NY and invited me with others to have dinner at this restaurant. I have to start something totally unrelated to this topic, was finding a parking on the street like, Manassas Virginia where I live finding a parking is never an issue no matter where you go to here in this town. I was little late but dinner was ready and preciously placed on the table with rest of the side dishes. I hade a probably a 6oz steak as a main course with other sides as you can see in the picture. Since I spent decades with Mexican family in California, I really do know the taste of assorted salsas and sauces, it was to the perfection. Steak was medium rare tender and was easy to chew on. I loved the masa tortilla, reminded me of someone especial who use to make it from the scratch. Our Host Andres and the rest of the host was wonderful,friendly and attentive to our needs. Definitely will go back next time I’m in New York. Thank You!

document: Sugar Factory - Queens. cuisine: Desserts Candy Stores American. located in Queens. with 3.4 stars (decent).

google_reviews.text:
We had such a fantastic time at Sugar Factory – Queens! The highlight for me was definitely the S’mores Brownie Insane Milkshake — it was absolutely massive, insanely delicious, and honestly impossible to finish without sharing. Even though they were short-staffed due to a last-minute callout, he took incredible care of us, stayed so friendly and upbeat, and you could tell he genuinely cares about the guests and the experience they’re having. He made everything feel smooth and special.

Highly recommend Sugar Factory – Queens for birthdays, celebrations, or just an unforgettable dessert outing!

The place and the food look nice, but that's where the good part stops. Service is meh, food is warmed up tv dinner quality. Drinks are fun to look at, but taste like nothing special. Strange. It could be so good, but it's all for show and no substance. It's like the food is prepared to be in a commercial instead of to be actually eaten and enjoyed. My eyes were happy, my mouth was not. document: The Brewery Bar & Kitchen. cuisine: Sports Bars American Irish Pub. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I was working in Queens for a month and saw this place when I was looking for a new spot to try. My visit surely didn’t disappoint. I had a drink and wing, and the wings had me wanting more. Great size and flavor (sweet Thai chili), crispy and juicy. Everything you could want from good wings. If I’m ever in the area, definitely will going back to explore their menu.

Nice neighborhood bar-eatery, good  selection of tap beers, including cider and they’re own lager and ale.
Menu has upgraded, and quality choices are available.
Always ask if there’s a special, you may be surprised, such as meatball hero and fries.
Plenty of bar and table seating with good views of large TV’s .
I usually visit in the pm hours so I can’t speak for brunch and lunch.
Staff is friendly and experienced with a dash of patience for the undecided patron.
The owner is open and pleasant and can be caught mingling and busting out service.

How have I lived so close by and never been to this place??? Definitely a great neighborhood spot for drinks, food! Decent options for vegetarians..our server was so nice!!! We made it 10 minutes before the happy hour was ending and she was so kind and doubled our drink order. Seems like very family oriented, even though its a bar..all in all, I will be back!!

For an extremely slow night (I was with a party of 4 and there was one gentleman at the bar) the service could've been better, as in they could've been more attentive. The food didn't take super long to be served but we were never offered refills for the hour that we were there and we were never checked in on (asked if we were enjoying our food or needed anything else). It also took super long to pay for the check. As for the food, my partner found the fries undercooked and the chicken tenders were crispy but underseasoned. I ordered the BBQ ribs and there was hardly any meat on those bones (it would've been better to order them at an applebees tbh) and they ended up not agreeing with my stomach. My friend ordered the salmon with mashed potatoes and veggies. The salmon was the only excellent thing I tried. The mashed potatoes and veggies were super bland. Honestly, I wouldn't give this spot another try :/

Had a great time at The Brewery Bar & Kitchen.  We chose outside dining which they have several tables and a covered canopy for.

We ordered the brunch specials, Steak & Eggs, Irish Breakfast & Homemade Corned Beef Hash.  Delicious all around!
The steak was perfectly cooked.  The Irish breakfast was authentic (the beans!). The hash was plentiful and not greasy.

This is a great spot for catching live sports events or a late night mac & cheese.

The staff is great and doesn't hurry you out.

Seriously… get the Irish Breakfast!

document: Awang Kitchen. cuisine: Indonesian. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I vote this restaurant as Indonesian restaurant with the best service and atmosphere. Not only Awang that sometimes greet the customers, both waiters are very friendly and accommodating. The restaurant seems to always filled with Indonesian that make us feel like home. For the food, just like other restaurants, there are some that are very delicious and some that are ok. You got to know their specialty (based on Awang’s explanation, it is for Jakarta food). In my personal preference, I like their Bebek Madura, Ayam Geprek, Mie Ayam, Bubur Ayam and Gado-Gado. For appetizer, their Sate Ayam is delicious, Tahu isi is good, Tempe mendoan is too thick to be called mendoan (should be just Tempe goreng) but it’s delicious. Some food that I feel need improvement (doesn’t mean they’re not good) are Rendang, Iga Bakar, Nasi Goreng and Mie Goreng Tek Tek. I always come here for the food. A lot of Indonesian variety of food. Grill chicken is always great. The es campur is wonderful. Some of the food taste more inferior than the last time I ate, but still this is the best choice for Indonesian food in Queens

Good food, authentic indonesian food. My fave goes to Kwetiao (we tried Bun version), Nasi bungkus Padang is nice too, and Bakso is nice during cold/winter season. Portion is ok, price is ok too for NYC i guess. Recommended if you're in area.

I went to this place with my Indonesian Friend and ordered Pregnant meat ball Soup & spinach sauté & finally a dessert &
O.LORD did I fall in love with  it !!! It amazing and will go back in a heart beat. Definitely endorse this place. Must check it out. ❤️

We were recommended this place by an Indonesian, and it surely did deliver! The food was also super affordable, costing less than what we typically spend for lunch even with appetizer, two entreés, and dessert.

Recommend getting the combo for the chicken meat and the liver, so good. The ginger scallion sauce pulls the dish together.

We also got extra chicken, photo shows the portion for 3 with $7 of extra chicken.

name: Winnie Said
document: Winnie Said. cuisine: Beer Bar Chicken Wings Cocktail Bars. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A touch of the Adirondacks in Sugar Hill, Harlem. Winnie Said, a part of the extended Harlem Public family, is a delightful departure from the standard sports bar one finds in this area. There is ample space to kick back on a coach and relax in this charming and family friendly spot. The decor is distinctly ‘mountain lodge’ and while there are tv screens through out (creating a chill spot for sports), they do not dominate or overwhelm. The food is exact right ‘step up’ from bar food without loosing the homey yet indulgent vibes of their sister spots on Broadway. One dish not to miss: The double smash burger. Decked out for ‘burger of the month’, the ‘cabin melt’ rocked double smash patties with the right mix of char and juice, spot on caramelized onions, bbq ranch(!) and upside down buns. I was not sure about this last bit, but getting this inside of the bun onto the grill did, in fact, add to the texture and the flavor. I had mine with maple bacon and a runny egg. It was soul satisfying. The sub’d in kale Caesar was a nod to my cardiovascular health and was very nicely dressed. 12 beers on tap, un-fussy cocktails and a warm welcoming staff pull the experience together. Great place to take family, groups and out of towners.

Love this place! We came in Saturday at 6 and were able to find a table immediately. The food was amazing! We got the burger of the month (elote smash burger) and it was incredible. I was pleasantly surprised by the cheesy grits with short ribs. SO GOOD. I am going to be coming back just for those to be quite honest.

They have a front dining area and back dining area and can accommodate larger parties with advanced notice. The drinks were strong so it makes the price worth it. Overall I really have no critics. Check out their funky wallpaper in the bathrooms, it made me laugh.

I had a nice first visit here. It took a while for us to get serviced, but besides that, it was a great visit overall. I love the vibe of the restaurant and really enjoyed the food and drinks! Great happy hour and our margaritas were strong. Will definitely come back!

Love this place! We came in Saturday at 6 and were able to find a table immediately. The food was amazing! We got the burger of the month (elote smash burger) and it was incredible. The portion sizes for the entrées here are very very small. I ordered the shrimp roll, and it was about a four inch sandwich. The roll itself was unusually thick, which made the amount of shrimp inside feel minimal. For the first time at a restaurant, I felt like the fries-to-main ratio was around 75/25. That dish was $21.

The other person in my party ordered the steak dish, and the proportions were similarly unbalanced. Flavor-wise, everything was just okay and the shrimp had a Cajun-style seasoning, and the steak came with a chimichurri-style sauce.

On the positive side, the space is interesting and unique. The cabin theme is nicely done and gives the restaurant a distinctive atmosphere.

name: Nana's Dim Sum & Dumplings
document: Nana's Dim Sum & Dumplings. cuisine: Dim Sum Noodles Soup. located in Bronx. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: First off, the restaurant is decorated really nicely. The music they play is very cool, not too loud though. I got the hot and sour soup, which was amazing. And I got the firecrackers as an appetizer. They are fried jalapeño with cream cheese and imitation crab topped with I believe eel sauce and spicy mayo. They were pretty good. Then I got the regular Xiao Long Bao (Pork soup dumplings) and the Spicy Chicken soup dumplings. The xia long boa were great, but the spicy chicken ones were OUT OF THIS WORLD GOOD. Service was extremely helpful on how everything works, ordering wise, and very nice. I'll definitely be back if I'm in the area...if not tomorrow!

So happy there's a location in Longmont now. Stopped in for lunch and was not dissapointed. I tried the lunch special and although it say "lunch portions" it's still a lot of food all together for a lunch portion. You fill out your options with a marker on the menu, similar to what you do at some sushi locations with the roll selections.
Everything I tried was very tasty. I did the $25 lunch combo which gives you 4 options, 1 item from 4 sections. The egg drop soup was thick and well seasoned. The fried rice had a decent amount of chicken and veggies. The dim sum & crispy shrimp were delicious as well. The shrimp was super crispy. I also ordered the dumpling roulette and soup buns. The soup buns were decent. They were not as full as some others that I've had, but the broth was super flavorful. The dumpling roulette is a great option you want to try their different dumplings. You get one of each. The pan fried thumblings are sooo cute. Delicious mini bites of dumplings. The Thai tea was good, not overly sweet like most.
Everyone was very helpful with menu recommendations and super nice as well. The ambiance is nice, not too loud. The music playing is mellow and just the right volume.
Loved the creative decor, such as the dragon that wraps throughout the restaurant space above head and the dim sum steamers used as decor above the entrance. There are also some ramen/soup bowls used as decor towards the back of the restaurant. Overall, it has PF Chang sort of vibe to me, but toned down and it feels more homey, cozy, and less commercialized. I'll definitely be back and bringing the Fam. Glad they accept reservations. Recommend them for weekends and large groups as they get busy on weekends.

Nana’s is a great spot for dim sum and dumplings. The food is excellent across the board , fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care. Everything we tried hit the mark.

The decor really stands out. It’s thoughtfully done, warm, and fun without feeling over the top. The atmosphere feels intentional and inviting.

Customer service was friendly and welcoming throughout the visit. Everyone we interacted with was polite and helpful.

One small detail I really appreciated was the background music. It’s set at the perfect level, easy to hear and adds to the vibe, but still quiet enough to have a normal conversation at the table.

Overall, great food, great atmosphere, and a place I’d happily come back to.

What a wonderful new addition to Longmont. Saturday night was busy but we never felt rushed or like we waited too long for anything! Our server helped us make delicious choices. Cant wait to go back and try more of the menu!

Food: There was a lot of options, too many to choose from! Everything we had though was delicious. The cucumber salad was so refreshing, with it being flavorful and a little spicy from the chili oil. The soup dumplings were good, nice broth. I really enjoyed the pork and shrimp Shao Mai, the filling was delicious and the wrapping was soft and flavorful. I liked the crab rangoons and the extra crab they added on the side. The creamy walnut dessert buns were amazing!! They weren’t overly sweet and were just satisfying to eat.

Service: They had a good system worked out here! We just marked what we wanted on the menu with a dry erase marker, and then as everything was brought out the servers would put an x on it. Everything came out as it was ready, so not everything was given to us at the same time which I enjoyed. The waiter was nice and helped us figure out a few things!

Atmosphere: From the outside, this building looks small, but when you enter it somehow looks a lot larger. It feels spacious inside with still plenty of seating.

Overall: Delicious, haven’t really had a good dim sum place here in Colorado, but now there is one. Would come back here happily and I can’t wait to enjoy another meal here!

google_reviews.text: World-renowned, most romantic, iconic blue-domed churches, spectacular sunsets destination everyone has to visit 😍

Santorini is a crescent-shaped volcanic island in the southern Aegean Sea, famous for its dramatic caldera views, whitewashed cliffside villages, and unique multi-coloured beaches. Formed by a massive volcanic eruption roughly 3,600 years ago, it remains one of the few places where you can dine and stay on the rim of an active volcano.

Top Experiences
Caldera Hike: A scenic 10.5km trail from Fira to Oia that follows the ridge of the volcanic crater.
Volcanic Beaches: Visit the striking Red Beach near Akrotiri or the black sand beaches of Perissa and Kamari.
Ancient Akrotiri: Often called the "Minoan Pompeii," this prehistoric city was preserved in volcanic ash and offers a look into Bronze Age life.
Wine Tasting: Sample the island's unique volcanic wines, particularly the crisp white Assyrtiko, at cliffside vineyards like Santo Wines.
Volcano Tours: Take a boat from the Old Port of Fira to explore the active volcanic islets of Nea Kameni and swim in the nearby hot springs.

name: Denino's Pizzeria & Tavern
document: Denino's Pizzeria & Tavern. cuisine: Pizza Italian Chicken Wings. located in Staten_Island. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Simply put, the trip to Staten Island is worth it for Denino’s.

The regular cheese pie alone is outstanding. Perfect crust with that slight crisp underneath, great char on the bubbles, fresh mozzarella, balanced sauce, and just the right amount of basil. It’s simple, but when it’s done this well, that’s all you need.

The vodka pie was unreal. The sauce is creamy, rich, and packed with flavor without feeling heavy. It coats the mozzarella perfectly and the crust still holds up slice after slice. That sweet, slightly tangy vodka sauce with the char from the oven is a combination that’s hard to beat.

The buffalo wings were excellent. Crispy outside, juicy inside, and the sauce had real flavor, not just heat. The fried zucchini was a sleeper hit. Perfectly breaded, crunchy, and great dipped in marinara. Even the sautéed spinach with garlic was fresh and done right.

Denino’s feels old school in the best way. Big menu, generous portions, and food that’s consistent and confident. Nothing trendy. Just really good Italian food and pizza that delivers. The service was amazing too. They were very attentive to us and shook everyone’s hand at the end of the meal. What a great experience!

Food and service perfect! Best fried calamari and red mussels I've had in decades. The 'garbage' pie is fantastic, loaded with meat, great crust!
Our server was cordial and did a great job.

Been going to this place for years never a bad time. Always has a good crowd and good food. Bar area had a good crowd.
Service today so so.
That would Never stop me from going back.
Enjoy

Do not miss out on the fried calamari & other appetizers...  consistently high quality and generous portions.  Great pies as always.  Service is efficient even when busy... many of the servers have been there for ages.

Denino's is a Staten Island classic for a reason! We've been coming here for years, and it never disappoints when you want that perfect thin-crust bar pie. We got the garbage pie (loaded with sausage, meatballs, pepperoni, mushrooms, onions – pure chaos in the best way) and a garlic pie on the side, both were killer. The clam pie is also a standout if you're into that.

document: Wonderland. cuisine: New American. located in Staten_Island. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Whether it’s for an event or a random summer day- Dutch Wonderland has always been a fun experience for our family. The park is clean, the lines move fairly quickly, and there is a variety of food options to pick from. Our two kids 6 years old (48 inches tall) and 3 years old (42 inches tall) find a wide range of attractions to enjoy and shows to watch as a family. The water park is always a nice spot to cool off on hot summer days too. The park also does a really nice job for different holidays/ events too- Eggs in the spring time, trick or treating during Halloween (when we went they had Hershey’s chocolate), and the lights around the winter holidays. In our experience, Dutch Wonderland truly is a perfect park for families with younger kids. We absolutely recommend a trip to check it out!

Dutch Wonderland Family Amusement Park

2249 Lincoln Hwy E, Lancaster, PA 17602

So I’m not gonna lie I wasn’t sure what to think when my wife said let’s go to Dutch Wonderland in Lancaster, PA. Doesn’t really seem like there’s anything there as a quick roadtrip destination, but the fact that this amusement park is geared towards 12 and under and we needed some long overdue family fun we decided to hit the road.

Once we arrived, the checking process was super easy because we bought our tickets online. People that were purchasing tickets on site were waiting forever in line 😩. Shout out to my wife for making the arrangements online.

We got in and began riding all the kid friendly rides we could fit. First we went on a boat ride and had to identify different characters along the way. We rode the skylift across the park which was relaxing. Once we got off the skylift we went to a BBQ stand to eat and unfortunately that was the only bad part about the park. The burgers weren’t real ground beef, they didn’t have any of their sides like, and the smoked sausage wasn’t very good either. They also ran out of drinks so we had to get kiddie cups of water. After the dissster that was lunch we allowed the girls to ride a bunch of rides that parents couldn’t ride with them on. We watched a water show with an evil sorcerer, a king who’s princess daughter needed to be saved by the prince that was turned into a frog by the sorcerer because he wanted to marry the princess himself. We were able to finish off the park with a couple of family rides and rollercoasters as well as taking the girls to the gift shop and grabbing some souvenirs. If we ever go again we’ll stick to your traditional amusement park food like chicken tenders, pizza, hot dogs, pretzels, popcorn, etc, but all in all it was a great experience and most importantly the girls had lots of fun!

My 4 year old really enjoyed this theme park! We went on awesome rides with our kid, checked out lots of stuff with our kid, and basically loved this theme park! Perfect for your kid child any age. Would most definitely recommend.

Our 6 and 4 year old grandchildren love it here.  Their favorite rides are the Whip It, Old Fashioned Car, the small roller coaster, the Bee.  They were disappointed this last visit because none of the dinosaurs in explore Island were working.  A fun amusement park.

A quaint little amusement/water park in Lancaster, PA.  There are a few rides for the older crowd, but I think this park is geared mainly to the younger kids.  My boyfriend and I took his 9 year old daughter and we all had a great time.  You could actually spend the entire day at the water park if you wanted to.  We didn't get to see any of the shows as we were only in Lancaster for a few days. It's interesting to see this park right along the main roadway.  I believe the park was open in 1963, so I do not know if that highway was there at that time. There is also an area where you can walk through and learn about dinosaurs.

The decorators and musicians we hired were fantastic and really made the night beautiful. I especially want to thank Felix, the manager, he was incredibly helpful and handled issues quickly the night of the event.
That said, there were several problems that really took away from the experience. The biggest issue was the food. We added sushi at $135 per platter and were promised it would be a large platter for each table with more than enough to feed the table. It was a small plate of basic rolls ( about 5 or 6 rolls) that couldn’t feed a table of 10–14. I complained immediately and they brought out more, but it shouldn’t have happened in the first place and there should have been a larger variety of sushi.
I also heard from multiple guests that the kids were starving and ended up going to adult tables to eat. Apparently the kids were served last, only once the hot food came out—several hours after the event started. My daughter told me they were asking the waiters for bread constantly because they were so hungry. We had over 45 kids, so this was disappointing. The food overall was a hit or miss, but the family style portions were definitely not big enough for the table and we had to ask for more frequently. Some guests also sent me pictures of fruit that wasn’t fresh.
There were other small but frustrating issues: some kids’ tables didn’t have the correct number of seats, so we were scrambling to rearrange chairs, and the waitstaff kept dropping plates and bottles throughout the night. After the event, I called about picking up the remains of our $600 cake, only to find out it had already been thrown out—no call, no heads-up, nothing.
I did reach out afterward to share my feedback and was told management would call me back, but I never heard back.

Angelina’s is a beautiful venue but the food problems and multiple oversights fell short of what I expected for such an important and expensive event. I hope they take this feedback seriously for future clients.

name: Deluca's Italian Restaurant
document: Deluca's Italian Restaurant. cuisine: Italian Seafood Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: From the moment I entered Deluca's Italian Restaurant, I sensed I was about to enjoy an exceptional meal. The ambiance immediately sets the perfect tone for a memorable experience. The highlight of my visit was definitely the Calamari Oreganato - a first for me and a revelation that changed how I perceive Calamari. Now, their preparation is the only way I recommend enjoying this dish. The Fried Calamari was perfect, with a crispy texture and well-balanced seasoning that truly enhances the appetizer. The Meatballs evoke a nostalgic, authentic Italian flavor, made with evident passion and skill. However, the real star was the Salmon, cooked flawlessly with a delicate blend of flavors that left me savoring every bite. The service at Deluca's matched the quality of the food — attentive, friendly, and highly knowledgeable. Every staff recommendation was spot-on, greatly improving the overall experience. In summary, Deluca's Italian Restaurant is a true gem in Staten Island. Its superb cuisine and excellent service make it a must-visit for anyone seeking authentic Italian dining. I give it five stars without reservation.

A friend & myself flew in from Charlotte NC for lunch. We came to try the lobster pesca tore. Rita was our waiter and she was pleasant & she took very good care of us. The atmosphere was excellent. We enjoyed the decor and the music. The food was truly amazing. It was worth the trip!

DeLuca’s is the definition of a classic Italian dining experience done right.

From the moment we sat down, everything was exceptional. The food was absolutely outstanding. The seafood was incredibly fresh and perfectly prepared. The calamari was light and crisp. The pasta overflowing with lobster, mussels, clams, and shrimp was rich, flavorful, and generous. The salmon was cooked beautifully with a sauce that elevated every bite. Portions were plentiful, presentation was on point, and every dish tasted like it came straight from an old school Italian kitchen.

The atmosphere was warm, elegant, and inviting, perfect for a special night out or a celebration. What truly made the evening unforgettable was the live entertainment. Charlie Romo delivered an incredible performance that brought true Sinatra style class and energy to the room. Since it is Christmas time, he also performed classic holiday songs that added a festive and joyful touch to the entire evening. It truly felt like dinner and a show.

The service was attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming throughout the night. You can tell this place takes pride in what they do.

If you are looking for phenomenal Italian food, a beautiful atmosphere, and outstanding live music, DeLuca’s is an absolute must. We will definitely be back.

Highly recommended.

This was my first time to go at Deluca’s restaurant with my family and let me tell you something everything was excellent !!!! Food comes in big portions! We went there to have our New Year’s Eve dinner and we picked à la carte option. Little pricey but we were very happy with food and atmosphere. We definitely going back there again!! Also service was excellent!!!

First time here. Loved the atmosphere. Decor is slightly old world. Dark wood, crystal chandeliers. Besutiful. Very friendly staff. Ordered their special 2 lb lobster and seafood platter for two. Came with spaghetti. Presentation A+. Unfortunately the taste was not there. We ordered white sauce. It tasted like all the seafood was just steamed. There was juice but not much else. No garlic, no olive oil, no wine, no seasoning, no parsley. Just watery juice. No flavor. We took it home to make a sauce for the leftovers. For $160,such a shame. I might give it another chance and try something else on the menu. Don't like to judge a place by just one dish.

name: Don Udon
document: Don Udon. cuisine: Noodles Japanese. located in Brooklyn. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: I am a huge fan of raku so my expectations were high but Don Udon exceeded them all. The environment is so cozy just like a local spot in Japan and the udon noodles are bouncy while sitting in the flavorful rich but clean broth. The Niku beef is incredible and soooo thin but so so tasty. Just warms your soul. Also got a side of the cucumber unagi and highly rec. unagi quality is like that of an omakase. You order and pay through your phone so very fast and efficient!! Support local 🥹

I have never been to Japan and I have always wanted to go, but I feel like walking into this beautiful little gem gave me a small taste of it. We were instantly greeted and seated at the bar as soon as we walked in. Seriously, it's like one moment you're in the streets of Brooklyn and the next you're in a cute little Japanese udon noodle shop. They did a stellar job at creating the atmosphere with the decoration and their hospitality.

It doesn't stop there though. Literally, your sense of taste is also transported with their high quality food infused with the very spirit of their hospitality. The beef udon here was the best I've ever had and is what I would imagine it would taste like in Japan. It is so comforting. It's like someone giving your taste buds a hug and praying over it. The flavors are so homey and the texture of the udon is perfectly al dente. The beef was tender and the ratio of everything was balanced just right.

We also got the unagi don, and the server offered a small bottle of shishio pepper powder which complimented the dish perfectly. It added a nice layer of flavor to the already smokey and delicious unagi. The pickled veggies on the side were so well done and went right along with the whole meal.

This meal was probably the most satisfying to have and experience during our stay in NY, and we will be sure to come back next time we're in town! Bless!

The place is small and cozy feels like a local restaurant in Japan. You can scan Qr code for order and the food comes out in few minutes. We ordered Kitsune Udon-Curry rice set and Cold Ddon - Gyu Don set. The food here was deliciously and so reasonable priced with great portion sizes.

Such a cute place!!! We tried the kitsune udon and the beef udon which were both great! We also did the curry rice add-on which as just as amazing. You scan using a Qr and the food comes out in about 5 minutes which I felt was super efficient! The place is small and cozy and they also have plenty of outdoor space! Highly recommend for a great dinner!!🩷

Was looking for a quick and hot meal to warm up from the cold, hit the mark perfectly. Ordering is done through a QR code and every menu item has a clear photo attached, makes it very easy to pick and choose your meal and add-ons. Owner is a nice Japanese man, and the interior is decorated in a very Showa Japan era style, feels incredibly homey. Udon itself was slightly chewy just the way I like, and the broth leans a little sweet but nice and light, perfect.

name: Red Hook Tavern
document: Red Hook Tavern. cuisine: American Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Red Hook Tavern feels like one of those neighborhood spots that’s been there forever. It’s warm and a little dim, with candles on the tables. Simple and comfortable.

We had a reservation, so we didn’t have to wait, but outdoor seating looked nice too, and the wait seemed around 30 minutes on a Tuesday night.

The burger was the reason we came, and it really was great. It’s dry-aged, so the flavor is strong and a little different, in a good way, but definitely something to know before you order. The potato chips were thick and fresh, the cheese was melted perfectly, and the pickle was honestly one of my favorite parts. I never thought I’d say that about a pickle, but it was that good.

It’s not a cheap meal, and you can tell part of what you’re paying for is the place’s reputation. The food’s solid, the space feels genuine, and the whole experience just fits together nicely.

Great joint. Their burger is delicious, cooked rare as requested, and ranks high in my personal list of all time great burgers globally.

Note to self: I should have avoided the unnecessary shrimp cocktail, that was bland at best (and probably recently defrosted)

The young team running the show is dynamic and friendly, not to mention very efficient, and the vibe is neighbourhood-ish.

I was there 30 minutes before their lunch opening and joined a small queue which grew much bigger by the time they flung the doors opened. Reservation is therefore highly recommended.

Didn't know how popular this place was but found out very quickly. Got a lucky open reservation that opened up and was sat down by 8pm. When I say this burger ranks up there with the best in NYC, not hyperbole. Got to try it yourself. Otherwise everything else we got, the wedge with thick bacon, the squid ink pasta, and the mussels were amazing. Will definitely come back.

A+

Came on a Monday without a reservation at 5pm and sat at the bar. Ordered the Dukes martini, croquettes, wedge salad, oxtail cavatelli and the burger. The place filled up after about 20 mins. Wedge salad was delicious and large! The sauce on the croquettes was delectable. The burger was buttery and big. Brought the cavatelli home as I was stuffed (the sauce was lovely, a hint of sweetness). They were playing 60s and 70s tunes 🥳

The burger was a moist thick patty so for those who are secretly anti-smash come here. I suggest sitting outside where the environment is calmer. Inside is warm but a bit too cramped compared to the lovely crisp air.

Also highly recommend the romaine wedge. It's a full romaine heart layered with a great dressing and crumbs.

The French onion soup was deep and hearty, for those who want a light meal consider just the soup and an appetizer.

The waitstaff were excellent and the tavern captures the vibe of the local community. Highly recommend.

I have come here several times for dates and family dinners out to celebrate. I believe on one family celebration we meet the owner who was absolutely hilarious. He is a character in himself. FOOD:
I am always looking out for their specials. I believe their menu rotates seasonally which I love because it takes advantage of what's in season. My husband's go to is the Pappardelle alla Bolognese (housemade ribbon pasta, meat sauce) For a lighter pasta I like to get Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe from their specials. document: The Kettle Black. cuisine: Burgers Chicken Wings Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 3.5 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The Kettle Black is pretty so it hurts, in a dazzling combination of heritage and contemporaneity. Different rooms and outdoor sections offer diverse seating options, from solo to communal. The food is pretty, too. I had scrambled eggs and was impressed by the freshness and depth of flavour, although the sweet intensity of sambal was a bit hard to reconcile with shrimp and eggs in some more sambal-heavy bites. The coffee was good, the service friendly and efficient. It may not have been anything extraordinary, but the setting made it feel satisfyingly indulgent nevertheless; I left happy. A cool spot!

Sitting outdoors with a light breeze, excellent coffee, and a great atmosphere was the ideal way to begin the day before heading to the circuit🏎️

🐮Beef Brisket Pastrami Benedict (AUD 26)
🐔Bang Bang Chicken Salad (AUD 26)
🧊Ice Long Black (AUD 5)

The Beef Brisket Pastrami Benedict was a standout, and the drinks were exceptional😌The Iced Long Black was particularly unique, using light roast beans that delivered a distinct, nutty flavor profile🌰 The Bang Bang Chicken Salad was flavorful, though the dressing was a bit heavy-handed😅 Toward the end, the saltiness became a little overpowering, so it might be worth asking for the sauce on the side if you prefer a lighter touch🤓

Highly recommend stopping by for a high-quality coffee or a relaxed brunch if you’re making your way to the Grand Prix 🏁

The Kettle Black never disappoints. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, with excellent service that makes you feel looked after from the moment you arrive. The food is consistently amazing—beautifully presented, fresh, and full of flavour.

Coffee is absolutely on point, and the soulful background music perfectly complements the experience, giving the whole place a laid-back but premium vibe. A standout spot for brunch or coffee in South Melbourne. Highly recommended.

The event staff were very responsive from day one and the staff on the day were very organised and lovely! The set menu was great and they even catered for dietries! We can't thank the staff enough for letting us host the perfect event here! Look forward to visiting again soon!

google_reviews.text: The Smokey miso noodles was SO GOOD! The dipping noodles was also excellent. Love the thick noodles. Both noodles had a nice texture and chew while the broth popped with flavor. name: Twin Tails
document: Twin Tails. cuisine: Thai Vietnamese Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We had a girls' day with my friend, and we both chose this place to go. Nobody asked me to write this review - I'm doing it because I believe this place deserves to be known for its service, food, and ambiance.
The staff, especially our waitress, was welcoming and helpful. We ordered grilled branzino, coconut rice, and twin lobster noodles, and as someone who grew up eating seafood most of my life, this place nailed it! My stomach felt perfectly fine after our lunch.
*For the dessert: I told our waitress I was allergic to coffee, and she kindly took the extra time to keep everything separate for me and my friend (who loves coffee).

Beautiful restaurant on the third floor of The Shops at Columbus Circle.  We were not seated near a window but if you can try to sit there, beautiful views. We had a few appetizers and all were good. Beef satay was tender and not overpowered with the marinade.  Pancakes were different than expected but had slightly crispy edges and tender inside and the crab (probably wrong term but I thought of it as crab salad) was bright and a refreshing counterpoint to the pancake.  Black sticky rice lived up to its name.  Mild flavor but good. Crispy pork rolls were good but least favorite for us.  Very nice crunch but not much flavor.   The only slight downside was the service. We were served water as soon as we were seated but waited more than 10 minutes to have a server come over and ask if we wanted a cocktail.  Definitely busy lively restaurant worth trying for good Thai food jn an upscale atmosphere.

Absolutely loved the food! The greed goddess salad was incredible. I loved the mushroom buns. The lemongrass ribs were so tender it just fell off the bone. The pad kra chicken was also so good! I wish they had a Thai iced tea but other than that amazing experience. And for sure get the pistachio soufflé

Great food and good vibe. The set menu was a great deal, I liked all the food and the portions were generous. My favorites were the appetizers, the fish, the coconut rice, and the flan. The flan was very dark and caramelized. The meat in the drunken noodles was a bit hard.

The servers were on one hand present, on the other regularly tried to get us to leave. It gets pretty loud as it fills up.

Service was impeccable. Food was to die for. Drinks were strong. Please don’t second guess it, just go! The ambiance and restaurant itself is simply gorgeous and beautifully crafted. I chose to celebrate my birthday here and was met with a handwritten birthday card. We were also given free apps and desserts. It was definitely one of the best birthday dinners I’ve ever been to and it was mine; so it was perfect!

name: Kaoru
document: Kaoru. cuisine: Japanese. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Came with a friend just after they opened at 11:30am on a weekday for a quick lunch. The smiling woman greeted us kindly and we did to-go orders. We ordered the 3 amigos donburi bowl for $24 and the Uni bowl with tuna & fluke for $35. We took a to-go order and it was ready in about 5 minutes. The place is most definitely family run, I think it's the owners husband and wife and son. The place has a vintage feel from the wood and the accessories, definitely well loved by local the local Japanese. When we opened our to-go packages we noticed the 3 Amigos bowl was stacked with fish but the uni bowl was a bit sparse. The salmon was my favorite cut of fish, super fatty and fresh.  Well, we figured out what was missing, the uni! Haha. When we finished our meal, we walked back and they already had a table of Japanese businessmen. We showed them the photo of our obligatory shot before we ate and they apologized and gave us the small box of uni that was missing. Would recommend for the salmon and spicy salmon portion, tuna was pretty standard. Rice was nicely seasoned and fresh. Decent price and portion for the city.

Visiting NYC, wanted to have some sushi, I stumbled on this restaurant on Google Maps, decide to try it because the reviews rated it 4.5. I had shrimp avocado and spicy tuna roll, and the beef tataki. The sushi was meh, I had better before. But I did enjoy the beef tataki, I would order that again. The service was a little less than average.

Kaoru Sushi is one of those hidden gems that you’re grateful to discover and even happier to return to. It’s a cozy, inviting spot that immediately makes you feel comfortable the moment you step inside. The atmosphere is warm and relaxed, making it the kind of place you can visit not just for special occasions but as an everyday go-to for great sushi and Japanese comfort food.

The food is excellent. I tried both a roll and a donburi, and both were absolutely delicious. The sushi roll was fresh, perfectly prepared, and balanced in flavor — you can really taste the quality of the fish and the care that goes into each bite. The donburi was equally satisfying, hearty yet delicate, with flavors that felt authentic and thoughtfully put together. It’s the kind of food that keeps you coming back, not just because it’s good, but because it feels consistent and reliable.

What also stood out was the atmosphere. It’s small enough to feel personal but with enough seating that you don’t feel cramped. Service was warm and friendly, adding to the overall charm of the place.

In short, Kaoru Sushi is a true hidden gem — cozy, authentic, and consistently excellent. Definitely worth checking out if you’re in the neighborhood.

This is probably the most authentic Japanese place I’ve been to for sashimi. So fresh. Rolls are fresh as well. Their eel is amazing, absolutely the best I’ve ever had. However, it is $30 a bowl, so it’s quite expensive, but it is worth it. I recommended it. Three amigos is a great dish. I think people should give it a try.

Updated review (7/11): What the....how did they up their came on presentation in a week?! Take a look at the second 3 amigos bowl pic posted -nice!

Original review (7/2):What a great find! Had lunch with some colleagues here and while it’s not cheap, it’s reasonably priced for what you’re getting. I got the 3 amigos bowl (regular, $24) which was a good variety of sushi, and came with a bowl of miso soup. We were seated at the counter and the counter staff was friendly, and let us have our conversations without interruption. Would definitely come back again.

Our server took time to help us pick a wine to our taste, and it was perfection of course! Kind energy, warm space, n-frills perfect food that would heal me any day.

The half a roast chicken knocked my socks off, tender and perfectly cooked, delicious skin and a glossy pan juice reduction which nailed it, rich and perfect. It was like gravy if gravy wasn't playing around. The chicken looked fabulous too, It caught the light and was a beautiful deep color. The roasted potatoes which came with it were perfect, tender and tasting like they'd actually grown someplace outdoors, and the roasted half garlic bulb hidden in the potatoes was a knockout - delicious on its own and beautiful spread on the potatoes. The potatos au gratin were great, what I always hope I'm going to get but never do. The cheese was perfect. The tender parts were perfect. The super thin delicate crisp part was perfect. The cream sauce with rosemary was delicious. I went in alone just before closing on a cold night and was welcomed as though I had a reservation and fed a delicious meal that made me so, so happy. I walked home in the cold afterwards feeling incredibly lucky. Thank you everybody!

What a delightful dinner experience with food, wine and atmosphere.  The host was super friendly and informative. I was pleasantly surprised with all the flavor that every dish brought. I have been meaning to come to this neighborhood sport for a while now and it did not disappoint.
We were celebrating my mother’s birthday and wanted to try a local restaurant with fine fare.  We ordered the whole chicken and it was so delicious, we paired with the beet dish and charred salad special and Mac and cheese.  We also had the suggested  white wine pairing that went really well with our dinner.
Overall a really lovely evening with food and ambiance.  Highly recommended and will def be back!

Low blue ceilings, open kitchen, and dim lights. The moment you step into Badaboom, their Parisian rotisserie chicken locks eyes with you as it slowly rotates on the spit. Seating is cozy and tight, with unique furniture and accent pieces. Some of the art on the walls is from the chef himself; it seems every French person is artistic, huh?

Both the carrots and ratatouille were exceptional and complemented all of the mains very well. I highly recommend splitting a large ratatouille for the table to add tomato and roasted vegetable flavors to your palate. Before we get into the 7 oz steak frites, let me tell you about the Potatoes au Gratin. This is probably one of my new favorite potato dishes in NYC. The texture was unreal, with the layers of potatoes merging together, blanketed in butter and cream, and salted perfectly. You could tell they spent the extra time needed to bring this coveted French dish to life in Bed-Stuy.

The steak au poivre came as hunks of medium-rare beef dressed in pan sauce. Crusted and peppered well, it wasn’t too tough to cut, and there was zero meat left behind. Through and through, an excellent steak. The fries were big, classic, freshly fried potato chunks that absorbed the leftover sauce and were dunked into one of the few delicious additional sauces you can order.

As always, dining is elevated through experience. From the service to the music, it is nothing short of an experience at Badaboom.

Great space, loved all the details.

Salad and bread & butter.  A simple salad with the light dressing. It was a good way to get greens and couldn’t go wrong.

The seasoning in the chicken was amazing. A perfect amount of salt an herbs.

The steak frites I would honestly skip, something the flavor that I didn’t necessarily enjoy. And the fries were light on salt and crisp.

name: Corner 28
document: Corner 28. cuisine: Chinese. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
When a place like this has roast ducks hanging in the window, especially in the heart of Flushing's Chinatown, you know it's going to be good.
However, I didn't expect how good this was going to be

After the initially confusing ordering process (you order with one person, pay with another, and pick up your order at a third person), I got my food - which was Three Meats over Rice - in my case I picked roast pork, crispy pork, and roast duck over rice

This was a pretty simple meal. It's just a bed of rice, with three types of meat over it, partitioned into sections. there's also a small amount of lettuce off to the side. It's not the type of dish that goes viral for any sort of aesthetic preparation or presentation. How good could it really be?
The answer is, absolutely incredible

The meats were all-time good. I could write for paragraphs about each of the three meats I got in detail, but for brevity I'll keep it shorter than that.
The roast duck was so juicy. When I've had duck in the past, it's tasted tough and gamey, but that was the absolute opposite here. It felt so fresh.
The roast pork was also exceptional - it had a exterior that took on a red color which gave a slightly-sweet, slightly-smoky flavor that was just perfect.
My absolute favorite, though, has to be the crispy pork. I noticed how crispy the skin was when I lightly touched the meat with my fork after opening the dish, but eating it was truly another level. It has to be the crispiest skin on meat I've ever had in my life. It's impossible to accurately describe how wonderful the skin on this pork was.

The rice was also so good - it was cooked to the perfect level, and not dry at all.
This dish spent over 30 minutes from when I picked it up to when I ate it, and didn't lose quality whatsoever.

If I had one minor complaint, it would be that it didn't come with sauce. I realized later you had to ask separately for a ginger scallion sauce, but it would be nice if it were included. This would give even the plain rice that much more flavor.

The portion size, for the money, might be the most incredible part of this dish. I think it's the most 'worth it' meal I've ever seen. For a total of $11, including a water bottle, you get this gargantuan plate of rice and meat. There's so much rice and meat here it could be two or three meals in a blink - and for less than the price of a Chipotle bowl, with even more expensive meats involved! It's such a low price for the amount of food you get it's unreal. This hits especially hard when you compare it to all the other food options around the US Open.

Overall, this is just ridiculously good food at an all-time value. 9.75/10

Affordable char siu and all roasted meat in NYC, 20% off all day and without a line!

Corner 28, a Hong Kong style roasted meat spot in the heart of Flushing, sparked my interest as its chinese name “旺角燒臘” refers to a distinct in HK (“Mongkok”).

Their roast bbq pork (叉燒), roast pork belly (燒肉), and roast spare ribs (排骨) are only $12 per pound after discount. They also sell char siu rice for just $10. CASH ONLY!!

＊Roast Pork 叉燒 $12/lb (after 20% off)
I got about 1.8 pounds of their char siu this time, and it was enough to feed a family for two meals. The meat was well-seasoned, not overly salty or sweet, so we didn’t even add additional soy sauce.

Remember to ask for ginger scallion sauce (薑蓉) as it really elevates the flavor and tastes delicious with rice.

While I wouldn’t say it blew my mind, it is a pretty good deal for what you pay for as it’s cheaper than most Chinatown spots. It’s worth a try if you are in the area.

Stopped in here at around 4 PM on a Saturday. I love a good Cantonese BBQ meat spot where it's easy to order. All the prices and menu items are listed out, as well as the prices so you don't have to guess if they are overcharging you or not. I ordered a pound of the roast pork, and half a pound of the char siu and I have no complaints. You order at the front, and pay in the back - no frills, no thrills, quick and easy.

Tip - cash only

The three meat over rice is this place's claim to fame. The bbq pork is my favorite. The chicken is okay and the duck is a little bit meager but it is overall fine. For 11 bucks it's phenomenal value.

This stall right off main street has one of the best roast meat platters that you can get! Walking by the stall, you can see all of their meats on display, looking fresh and juicy. I got the 3 meats platter here, which came with rice, cabbage, water, and your 3 choice of meats (I chose the classic chicken, duck, and pork). The portion was so generous for $10, and all of the meat was delicious. The cuts were thick, they were juicy, and so full of flavor. One of the best deals I've seen. Highly recommend.

Car & Carriage Caravan Museum is a charming and surprisingly interesting stop, especially if you enjoy history, classic vehicles, or unique museums.
The collection of vintage cars, carriages, and early transportation pieces is well curated and gives a clear picture of how travel evolved over time. Everything is clean, well maintained, and thoughtfully displayed, making it easy to enjoy at your own pace.
The atmosphere is relaxed and family-friendly, and it works well for both adults and kids. Even if you’re not a hardcore car enthusiast, there’s plenty here to catch your attention and spark curiosity.
Overall, it’s a nice add-on to a visit in the Luray area and pairs well with nearby attractions. A pleasant, educational experience that’s worth stopping by.

This place is very cool outside of Lou ray caverns. They have a lot of old cars. Some really vintage pieces. Some million dollar cars, lots of old schools from the beginning, and some pretty cool stuff to see around this museum. A lot of stuff. I didn't know about very interesting. I must go.

This is a fantastic opportunity to see cars and other forms of transportation used over a hundred years ago—beautifully preserved and maintained. The vintage cars are truly classy and timeless; I was amazed by their design, quality, and the fact that they still look so flawless.

Who wouldn’t want a car that has aged so gracefully? I absolutely loved seeing them. If you’re a vintage car enthusiast, this is a place you should definitely visit at least once.

The Car and Carriage Caravan Museum was an unexpected highlight of our visit to Luray Caverns! The collection of vintage vehicles is truly impressive—beautifully preserved and displayed, with everything from elegant horse-drawn carriages to early automobiles and classic cars. You can really appreciate the craftsmanship and history behind each one.

It was a pleasant surprise that admission to the museum is included with the Luray Caverns ticket. It made the experience feel like even better value. One of the coolest facts we learned was that all but two of the vehicles are still fully operational! It would be amazing if they held a parade or special event once a year to get them out on display in motion—that would take the experience to the next level.

Whether you’re a car enthusiast or just enjoy a glimpse into the past, this museum is well worth the visit. Definitely don’t skip it while you’re at the caverns!

The staff is friendly. The cars are beautiful. It’s amazing to see how far cars have come. I think I would honestly prefer to actually still drive some of the cars they have there. Rolls Royce, Bugatti, Dodge, Ford, Chevrolet. After walking thru the caverns. You can head into the car museum from the gift shop.

document: Wabi Nori. cuisine: Sushi Bars Japanese Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
5 stars for the stunning ambiance; the atmosphere alone makes a visit worthwhile.

While the service was impeccable and the rock shrimp was a standout, the sushi was a bit of a mixed bag. The salmon nigiri was fresh and enjoyable, but the hand rolls were just average. The enoki, miso cod, salmon, and scallop hand rolls lacked a seasoning - fish roe, jalapeño, bonito flakes -  or a textural contrast needed to make them truly memorable.

On the bright side, the edamame was served warm, perfectly charred, and generously portioned. I also highly recommend the Kesseler Riesling, which paired beautifully with the meal. I’d definitely return to explore more of the menu.

Coming from someone who is a huge KazuNori fan, I didn’t think another hand roll spot could truly impress me but Wabi Nori is literally in a hand roll league of its own.

What really sets Wabi Nori apart is the appetizers. For a hand roll restaurant, the appetizer selection is exceptional and honestly one of a kind. We started with the soft shell crab, yellowtail jalapeño sashimi, rock shrimp, and Kumamoto oysters, and oh my gosh… every single bite was packed with flavor. Everything was fresh, well-balanced, and beautifully executed.

For the hand rolls, I ordered the five hand roll set from Restaurant Week, which included the spicy tuna, salmon, yellowtail, bay scallop, and EB mushroom hand rolls. My absolute favorites were the spicy tuna and the bay scallop; both were outstanding. While the other hand rolls were still very delicious, if I’m being honest and comparing the two, they didn’t quite beat KazuNori for me personally. That said, they were still excellent and absolutely worth ordering.

For dessert, I had the house-made cheesecake, which was the perfect ending to the meal. To drink, I ordered the strawberry matcha, but instead of coconut rum, I swapped it for whiskey… and if you’re a whiskey drinker, trust me, this swap is elite. The sweetness of the matcha and strawberry really accentuates the whiskey and takes the drink to a whole new level.

We also had an espresso martini and a dirty martini, and I can confidently say this: even though they don’t have blue cheese olives, the dirty martini here was the best dirty martini I’ve had in my entire life and I’ve had a lot of dirty martinis.

Overall, Wabi Nori is 100% a spot I would come back to and enthusiastically recommend to others. From the appetizers to the cocktails to the overall experience, it’s truly something special.

Let me start by saying the only reason i gave this place a 2 and not a 1 is because the service was incredibly kind and fast.
We were seated fast and all the servers were very polite. We came for restaurant week menu -45$ preset, seemed promising. 2 people eating.
We ordered for starters ; the rock shrimp and soft crab - both were deep fried and very mildly flavored. Mostly just tasted the oil.
The main was a preset 5 set hand roll ; fried enoki mushroom, spicy tuna, salmon, yellow tale, crab meat salad. The sushi was just really not great. name: Le Grin African American Restaurant
document: Le Grin African American Restaurant. cuisine: African. located in Bronx. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
I recently purchased a bottle of natural milk from Le Grin African Restaurant, expecting a fresh and high-quality product. Unfortunately, my experience was nothing short of disappointing and concerning.

When I opened the bottle and took a sip, the milk tasted absolutely terrible—clearly spoiled. Trying to understand what went wrong, I checked the expiration date on the label, only to find something shocking. The original expiration date was clearly January 20, 2025, but someone had manually altered it to March 20, 2025, using handwriting. It was obvious that the date had been tampered with in an attempt to make it seem like the product was still good.

This is completely unethical and dangerous. Selling expired dairy products by simply changing the expiration date is not only deceptive but also a serious health hazard. Consuming spoiled milk can cause food poisoning, and I find it unacceptable that a business would risk the health of its customers like this.

I am beyond disappointed. This is a serious food safety issue that should not be ignored. If a business cannot ensure the quality and freshness of the products they sell, they should not be selling them at all. I strongly urge other customers to double-check expiration dates on perishable products from this restaurant before purchasing.

Le Grin African Restaurant needs to immediately address this issue. Selling expired food with falsified expiration dates is unacceptable and a major violation of customer trust. I will not be buying from here again unless they take full responsibility and make sure this never happens again
