name: Muteki Udon
document: Muteki Udon. cuisine: Japanese. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Trying to give six stars. Best seaweed salad I’ve ever had, which was a surprise because I ordered it on a whim and didn’t expect a whole plate of seaweed I’d never had before excellently seasoned with shredded daikon radish in a crisp yuzu dressing with cucumber and tomato. The textures and refreshing flavor were something I’m going to dream about. And then we were served complimentary matcha udon sticks which were addictive and I would regularly buy them in a large bag for snacking if such a thing existed. And then what we came for - the udon. Served in monster-sized-but-beautiful pottery bowls, the udon impressed on visual alone. I ordered the mushroom vegetable udon in which I was served more mushrooms and more kinds of mushrooms than I’d ever seen. The broth was somehow delicate and hearty at the same time and the noodles were plentiful, thick, and springy. I’ve determined after this meal that udon is my favorite noodle. My partner got the curry udon which came in another beyond belly-filling portion with as much meat as I had bounty of mushrooms. We both had enough to take home for lunch the next day and it was so delicious we went through with carrying it back with us instead of just leaving it behind. A patron near us ordered the karaage fried chicken which was also a very big portion and looked incredible. And all this food for what I would say is a very good price! A much less exciting and much smaller udon bowl I had recently in Brooklyn cost $10 more than the one I had at Muteki. Some of the best food I’ve had all year, great sake selection, cozy atmosphere, excellent decor makes you think you might be at an Izakaya not in Brooklyn, wonderful service. Can’t wait to return and try the whole rest of the menu which also includes ramen, donburi, and some raw/cold options as well.

The restaurant is nicely decorated and lit, and I love the unique bowls that the udon comes in!

I got a mentaiko cream udon, which has a great portion size and tasted good (though it is unusually tangy/sweet compared to mentaiko cream udons that I'm used to eating... it says it on the menu that it will be tangy so if it's not your thing, don't get this.) My friends got soup/curry udons and they all were great in portion size as well! The curry udon is more broth-ish than curry-sauce-ish.

Unfortunately, I can't recommend the muteki pudding. My friends and I were all not fond of the taste. The staff explained that the flavor came from the toppings on it, but I'm almost certain that the milk pudding itself was sour. Service was also not great, there seemed to be only one waiter struggling to help all the tables. The cost of drinks, appetizers, and desserts are also very pricey despite the smaller portions ($9 for a matcha and $8 for a pudding).

Overall, it's hard to recommend this place when there are other udon spots that will provide the same or better value for a lower price.

This was one of the best Ramen places I've ever had the honor of discovering in the city! The atmosphere screamed authenticity with the amazing Japanese designs and coloring all around. I was able to have a seat at the bar and it is a much better experience than a regular table. The Karaage that was served was extremely well made and authentic with an exceptional sauce covering the meat. It was so wonderful I just had to get more of it in my Ramen. Id like to thank the server Eileen for her amazing service and positive drive when serving me.

We came here for the first time. We started with salmon tartare, fried chicken, tofu salad and seaweed salad.

The salmon tartare was very nice. The salmon was plated on a thinly sliced, fried lotus root. It also had some fried matcha udon bits. The flavor was nice and it was fun to eat.

The fried chicken was very delicious! Crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. The spicy mayo paired with it.

The tofu salad was a bit different from what I expected. It had cubed tofu, and cucumbers. It also had some cooked spinach, fresh cherry tomatoes, fresh baby spinach, and fried crispy matcha udon. The dressing was nice, but I would ask for more.

The seaweed salad was nice and refreshing. It had a good variety of different seaweed. It also had some cherry tomatoes and lettuce. In my opinion, it could use more vinegar.

For entree, we got a curry udon and a salmon udon.

The curry udon was served hot. The broth was nice and pungent. It was mildly spicy, and very flavorful. The pork bits were nice but a bit too sweet. It also had some cooked spinach, a soft boil egg, snd some spring onion. It was perfect for winter time.

The salmon ikura udon was served cold. It was covered with slice salmon. It also came with some fresh seaweed, dried seaweed and shredded white radish. It was nice and refreshing. The udon was the special matcha udon.

The udon was cooked perfectly. It was bouncy and chewy. I loved it!

The space was organized and cute.

Solid spot right by Barclays Center! I highly recommend their udon, since that's what they're known for. I DONT recommend the Salmon Don. It was very plain and it came with flavorless seaweed. It comes with a small dish of dipping soy sauce. While the portion size was plentiful, it was mostly tasteless.

On the other hand, I enjoyed the apps! The Yakitori Skewers, especially, were soft and melted in my mouth! The Salmon Tartare and Vegetable Tempura were also good.

Attentive + kind staff. Plenty of seating. Overall, great, convenient spot for a pre-Barclays meal.

google_reviews.text: Found this place looking for sushi in the area and read through some reviews. I had family in town and wanted to have a nice dinner somewhere close. The experience lived up to the reviews! It is a tee tiny place with maybe seating for 25. Service was excellent and intentional. Everything we had to eat and drink was phenomenal! The fish was so fresh and the sashimi melted like butter. I will absolutely be back and I'm so happy to have found this gem!

Uotora is a true hidden gem in Brooklyn. Sushi is incredibly fresh and expertly prepared - each bite melts in your mouth. The ambiance is cozy and intimate, making it perfect for a quiet dinner. Easily one of the best sushi experiences I’ve had in the Brooklyn. Highly recommended!

The fish was super fresh. The sushi chef was warm and welcoming. If I had to nitpick, the service was a little slow, but I didn’t mind it too much. It gave you time to digest the sushi. I would come back!

Great casual omakase experience

Bae surprised me with dinner- I thought we were just gonna pop into a place that had oysters bc I was craving them.

Got the sushi omakase, 2 different sake carafes, and an extra oyster

The oysters were 15/10. So creamy and flavorful. Not super cold as most Western style oysters, which allowed the flavor really shine. The soft shell crab was also perfect.

As others have shared, the omakase arrives in flights, which isn't horrible but I see what people mean about not getting the freshest piece of each round. I think a bit of wasabi was added between the fish and rice of some pieces, which took away from the experience of the fish in my opinion. Still, it was very delicious.

The miso soup service at the end of the meal arrived in a perfect cup for sipping. The tiny clams were a pleasant surprise that elevated the mild soup. Now I want all my miso soup with clams!

The staff was all very friendly, professional, and knowledgeable about the menu.

Would return to try their other non-omakase menu items.

Excellent sushi at a reasonable price.
The quality is high and the service is friendly and welcoming.
It's essentially half the price of what you'd pay for the same top quality fish in Manhattan. It's delicious!

document: Manhatta. cuisine: New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text: We had an absolutely incredible experience at Manhatta for my friend’s birthday! From the moment we walked in, the entire staff made her feel so special—everyone went out of their way to congratulate her. We were lucky enough to get a stunning window seat with a breathtaking view of the city. There was even a thoughtful birthday card waiting for us on the table! The food was of the highest quality and the service was flawless. They truly know how to make an occasion feel grand. Highly recommend!

We had dinner at Manhatta, located on the 60th floor of a skyscraper in the Wall Street district, and the experience was impressive overall.

From the moment you arrive, the welcome is highly professional. The hostess team, maître d’, and sommelier all contribute to a very polished and well-organized atmosphere. The service is attentive, refined, and genuinely professional throughout the evening.

The view is truly spectacular. One side overlooks the Brooklyn Bridge and Brooklyn, while the main façade faces Uptown Manhattan, showcasing the iconic, glittering skyline in all its glory. At the entrance, there is a stylish and functional bar area with a stunning backdrop view. Walking to the right, the restaurant opens into an L-shaped dining room with approximately 30 tables. The staff-to-guest ratio is excellent, and service flows smoothly.

They offer a 3- or 4-course prix fixe menu. Each course (starter, main, dessert) includes about five options, which keeps the selection focused and prevents the menu from feeling overwhelming. The concept feels standardized, elegant, and based on quality ingredients rather than excessive variety.

My wife and I both chose the four-course menu.

I started with the raw shrimp, which was excellent — easily the highlight of my meal. I then had scallops, followed by a vegan main course that, unfortunately, felt underdeveloped and barely cooked — surprisingly so, to the point that it felt almost unfinished. I ended with a chocolate mousse. I paired my meal with a mezcal-based spicy cocktail, which was well balanced and enjoyable.

My wife chose burrata as a starter, a lentil-based dish, tagliatelle, sea bass as her main course, and sorbet for dessert. She paired her meal with a Blanc de Blancs champagne, which complemented her dishes beautifully.

Overall, the food was good but somewhat mediocre in execution, with a few highlights (especially the raw shrimp). I would rate the food 4 out of 5. However, the atmosphere, views, and the professionalism and friendliness of the staff easily deserve 5 out of 5.

A unique and charming touch: the restaurant provides binoculars placed around the space for guests to enjoy the skyline up close — a thoughtful and memorable detail. Additionally, the small “bites” served between courses were delightful and well executed.

In summary: go for the view, the ambiance, and the impeccable service. The food is good, but the overall experience is what truly stands out.

Visiting Little Italy in New York City with my family was like stepping into a small slice of Europe right in the heart of Manhattan. The moment we walked down Mulberry Street, the atmosphere felt lively, colorful, and full of character. Italian flags hanging across the street, outdoor seating areas, and the aroma of garlic and fresh tomato sauce instantly made us hungry.

What I loved most was simply strolling together and exploring the many snack outlets and restaurants lined up one after another. Small bakeries displayed cannoli, biscotti, and pastries that looked too good to resist. We stopped to try fresh cannoli filled on the spot — crispy shells with sweet, creamy ricotta inside. It was absolutely delicious.

The restaurants offered everything from classic pasta dishes and wood-fired pizzas to seafood and rich lasagna. Many places had outdoor seating, which made the experience even more enjoyable. Sitting there with my family, enjoying authentic Italian food while watching the crowd pass by, felt special and relaxed. The drinks were just as enjoyable — refreshing mocktails, Italian sodas, espresso, and cappuccino that completed the meal perfectly.

There were also small souvenir shops and specialty stores selling Italian sauces, olive oils, and sweets, adding to the cultural charm of the neighborhood. The entire area had a warm, welcoming vibe that made us slow down and truly enjoy the moment.

Little Italy is not just about food — it’s about culture, tradition, and togetherness. Visiting with my family made it even more memorable.

document: Take31. cuisine: Korean Gastropubs Soul Food. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Went with some friends and it was great! Complimentary tteokbokki and all the food were very tasty. Service was ok but busy, we asked for a side of rice but didn't get any. The atmosphere is comfortable.

A little pricey for the meal overall and I wish there were banchan or a side of rice for the meat entrees, but overall good food. Would definitely recommend getting the pong flurry (crereal milkshake) for dessert too!

Bathroom review: very clean and nice-smelling bathroom with individual stalls. Soap smells good 🧼

Take 31 Korean Food genuinely surprised me in the best way. The space is small, but it has a cozy, welcoming vibe that immediately sets the tone for a great meal.

We started with the pork belly, and it was outstanding. The pork was well-seasoned with a very natural, clean flavor—tender, soft, and cooked perfectly. Paired with the kimchi underneath, which had a slightly tangy, lightly sour note, it helped cut through the richness of the pork belly. Without that balance, the dish could’ve felt heavy on the palate, but instead, the entire flavor profile came together beautifully. The plating was also impressive; everything looked absolutely stunning when it came out.

The Korean fried chicken was easily one of the best I’ve had—and I don’t say that lightly. I’ve been to many Korean spots and tried plenty of Korean fried chicken, and this one truly nailed it. Perfectly fried, incredibly crispy on the outside, and immensely juicy and tender on the inside. The texture, seasoning, and sauce were all spot on. Extremely well done.

We also tried the beef ramen noodle dish. While it didn’t taste bad, it lacked seasoning and depth of flavor compared to the other dishes. Because of that, I wouldn’t recommend this particular item.

Overall, Take 31 delivers excellent food with great execution, especially when it comes to their pork belly and fried chicken. Definitely worth a visit if you’re a fan of Korean cuisine.

Food is very comforting and the perfect place for a cold winter day trying to find a place to eat at ktown when everywhere is fully booked (including this place, but the wait time was reasonable and they gave us complementary handwarmers when we had to wait outside which was so nice).

The stew was very comforting and the pork belly with rice crepe and pickled radish was very creative and special. Loved how the radish was sliced to exactly the size of the pork belly, in perfect bite sized slices. The attention to detail was impressive.

Service was amazing, servers were very attentive and they give complementary tteokbokki! We got our food and orders in very quickly. The atmosphere was very nice, intentional and warm, not cramped or stuffy.

Take31 serves up comforting Korean food in a lively Koreatown setting. The sliced pork belly looks amazing and tastes even better. It’s rich, a little sweet, and super easy to keep eating. Korean fried chicken is also a real crowd-pleaser, with a crispy outside, juicy inside, and a sticky, spicy glaze topped with crunchy garlic and chili flakes. Every bite is full of flavor. The creamy seafood udon is a nice surprise, with udon and a sauce that feel extra indulgent. Altogether, these dishes show how Take31 does a great job mixing Korean flavors with fun modern comfort food.
The environment was pretty good for friends gathering. They are small plates which are good to share. Would come got the nice, but the food is heavily seasoned which can be too much and oily…

Not great. I was a tad annoyed.

We ordered seared tuna as an appetiser. The price was very reasonable. But it was over seared and tasted average.

The ramen, very pea-nutty. My husband didn’t mind because he enjoys peanut, again not authentic.

The salmon maki, average also. Presented well. But the rice was not sushi rice and was soggy.

They charge a 10% service fee, which I was surprised by. We haven’t had this in Boracay, so we queried.

The staff who looked after our table was unenthused and gave the sense she didn’t enjoy her job.

google_reviews.text: A cultural enrichment type restaurant.  It's a quaint restaurant that gives you the feeling of being in Albania.  You can tell the owners have pride in their culture.  Truly a hug from Albania that makes you feel like you’re there.  The authentic flavors did not disappoint. The staff is courteous and professional and super accommodating.  The food over exceeded our expectations.  Best dining experience I’ve had this week in NYC.

My first time trying Albanian food. It was very delicious and wholesome. The restaurant itself feels like you’re entering someone’s home. It felt very warm and cozy. The dishes tasted home cooked too. The flavors were full without feeling too heavy. The lamb was super tender and not gamey. Service was excellent and our waitress gave great recommendations! Id love to come back to try more of the dishes.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Absolutely amazing experience at Ça Ka Qëllue in Manhattan! The food was outstanding—rich flavors, beautifully prepared, and truly authentic. Every dish on the table was delicious and comforting.
The service was top-notch as well. John was incredibly attentive, friendly, and made sure we were taken care of the entire time. You can really feel the passion for both food and hospitality here.
Highly recommend this place if you’re in NYC—can’t wait to come back!

Albanian food is completely underrated and doesn't get nearly the attention it deserves.  This was my first time trying this cuisine and I wasn't disappointed.  I had the pepper dip appetizer which reminded me of a mildly spicy and perfectly balanced fondue served with fresh baked bread similar to a pita or puffy Naan.  For the entrée, I had the Tava Kosi, which is braised lamb served over an egg custard.  The custard reminded me of the inside of a quiche but with a much softer texture.  I went for Christmas dinner while visiting New York and the atmosphere and ambiance inside the restaurant could not have been better.  The interior looks like an old European tavern with rustic brick walls.  Cannot recommend this restaurant highly enough.  Extremely tasty food at an amazingly low price point.

First time trying Albanian food and really didn't know what to expect, but wow! This did not disappoint.

My group of 4 ordered a few things to share:

- Sausage dip
- Sesame baked cheese
- Fli
- Mantia (Tava)
- Qofte Shari
- Mixed meat combo (excluding the liver and qofte)

Everything was absolutely delicious, it's really hard to choose a favorite. The bread was so soft and fluffy, I dipped it in everything that I could.

The inside was super cozy, staff was great, will definitely be coming back to try more of the menu!

document: See No Evil Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: This is pizza done right 👍 I wanted to try the Johnny Peppers since it seems like it would be the most packed flavor pie. And I was right. Bell peppers, hot cherry peppers, onions, garlic, sausage all incorporated with gooey cheese and tomatoey sauce. Dispite all those toppings this pizza manages to taste light. I didn't feel heavy after eating. The location is on the smaller size and the day that owner it was a little too warm inside the restaurant. Staff wasn't that great. But definitely go for the pizza 🍕

Nothing scream more New York than a hidden pizza shop in a subway entrance.

Have being passing this little hidden spot every time we are taking the 1 train home on 50th street after a show nearby and we finally sat foot in.

One pie is good for sharing. The pie came out fast, love the doughy crust although a little sloppy just be careful not to burn your tongue because you just want to gaucho it down once you start.

The space reminds me of a 80’ vibe, a little small but they have many tables and can be joined together to sit a large group. For those big group who wants to get a late night snack after a show all together, head there asap it gets filled up quickly as many others are thinking of the same.

What a cool experience! This is more of a casual pizza spot in downtown 1 subway at 50th Street. It's a retro kind of feel, the place was popping! It was definitely a mix of tourists and locals. It felt like a unique but authentic experience in NYC, which is rare, usually 'unique' experiences can end up being kitschy/overpriced.

The pizza was SO delicious- Neapolitan style. We were actually struggling with all of the choices, because everything sounded so good. We went to their bar next door afterwards, Nothing Really Matters, and it was super lively at around 10 pm, and was actually going to get even livelier, according to the host. Oh! And there was an awesome dj.
The staff was super kind and very prompt. The food was amazing, and the vibes were vibing. I loved having the smaller dining area, makes NYC feel a little less crowded
Had an incredible experience at See No Evil Pizza. The pizza, appetizers, and desserts were absolutely delicious. Service was excellent. Definitely will be back.

document: Leonetta. cuisine: Mediterranean Seafood Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Had an early dinner on Valentine’s Day with friends. We had a reservation but were seated once our entire party was present at the restaurant. Staff were very friendly and pleasant! Our server was attentive and provided great service. The spacing between tables upstairs was adequate as well. The downstairs area is perfect for taking pics/videos to spice up your social media. Now to the quality of the food - the appetizers were good. Highly recommend the hummus! The drinks were impressive as well. However, the menu did not provide enticing entrees, main meals were underwhelming, and overpriced for its portion size. This would not be my first or second choice when selecting a Mediterranean restaurant in the city. While it has a great ambience and atmosphere, it does not justify the entree prices or subpar quality of their main entrees.

Amazing drinks, oysters, and pasta. The vibes were amazing. My only negative comment is we had a 530 res and when we showed up restaurant was empty (as expected) but they refused to let us sit down until the full party was there. The lack of flexibility was a bit uptight given the place was empty, But our waitress was absolute amazing - very fast and friendly 10/10. Def coming back

I had an absolutely amazing experience here! The food, the atmosphere, and the service are all incredible! They had some unique drink options which we all definitely enjoyed but the real star was the food! I tried both the rigatoni and the filet mignon & mushroom kebab. The rigatoni was really good but the kebab was one of the best things I’ve ever eaten. It was seasoned and cooked to perfection! The tiramisu for dessert was also amazing! An amazing experience and definitely recommend!

Dining at Leonetta felt like discovering a hidden gem in Murray Hill that elevates Mediterranean cuisine with creativity, color, and fearless flavor (see my photos). Every dish my wife and I tasted was a masterclass in balance and imagination...from bold small plates to beautifully composed mains that celebrated seasonal ingredients with a modern twist. Vibrant flavors in each "mezze" dish that were special and memorable. Inside, the space is stunning, warm, and inviting, with lush design details and an ambience that instantly made us feel welcome. The combination of inventive food and gorgeous interior made for a truly unforgettable meal, one we keep thinking about long after leaving the table.

I really hate to do this, but had to leave this review. The service itself was fine, but it was the manager forcing us out of our table before we were done that just ruined this restaurant for me.

We had been at the restaurant for 2 1/2 hours, still ordering drinks and planning to order dessert. But the manager stopped by and told us they needed the table. I understand the need to turnover, but it was closer to closing, there were a 4-top and 6-top empty and open for at least the past hour we were there and still empty when we left.

The food was okay, highlight was porkshank - seemed decent value for food to price ratio. The beetroot and baba ghanoush were solid, octopus salad with good flavor. Just be aware very small portions for the price

name: Chalong
document: Chalong. cuisine: Thai. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Chalong brings the ไฟ!!... This is the real deal, and is the best Thai I’ve had outside of Phuket!!

I started with the Lumpu Salad, built around pristine scallops that were bright, citrusy, and layered with that classic Thai balance of heat, acidity, and herbs. The scallops were incredibly fresh and the dish had a punchy vibrance that woke up the palate immediately.

Next up were the Baerng Golae shrimp tacos…juicy shrimp with deep, smoky southern Thai spices wrapped in a soft bite that delivered savory, slightly sweet, and the right amount of heat.
The steamed fish was beautifully executed. Clean, delicate, and perfectly cooked, with aromatic herbs and broth that made every bite feel light but deeply flavorful.

To finish, the mango sticky rice hit the spot..nothing standout about this dish but after getting hit with all that flavor, I didn’t mind.

I washed all that down with a Surat Thani “After School” cocktail which was dangerously easy to drink so I just sipped on it rather than drank!

Across the board, the taste profiles at Chalong were dialed in and dialed up! The service, perfect!  It’s the kind of spot that reminds you how exciting Thai food can be when the kitchen leans all the way into its roots. A seriously impressive meal.

I recently visited Chalong NYC for dinner with friends, and overall it was a solid experience worth sharing! Located in the heart of Hell’s Kitchen, this Thai restaurant blends modern Southern Thai flavors with a lively atmosphere that’s perfect for dinners out, pre-theater meals, or casual nights with friends.

The space feels warm and welcoming, with thoughtful décor and an inviting vibe that made our group feel comfortable right away. The restaurant tends to be popular, so reservations are definitely recommended — it can get busy, especially on weekend evenings. The service throughout the night was friendly and attentive; staff were happy to explain the menu and adjust spice levels based on our preferences.

We tried several standout dishes that left a great impression. The Green Curry Brisket was rich and flavorful, perfectly tender and aromatic. The Mee Pum Riang had a unique, savory taste that paired beautifully with the noodles. Khao Pad Mun Goong was comforting and well-seasoned, while the special Baerng Golae offered a bold, complex flavor that really showcased Southern Thai cuisine. Each dish was generous in portion and carefully prepared, making the meal very satisfying.

The vibe inside Chalong is energetic and vibrant — lively enough for a fun night out, though it might be a bit loud if you’re hoping for a quiet, intimate dinner.

In summary, Chalong NYC offers flavorful, well-prepared Southern Thai food, attentive service, and a buzz-worthy setting. While some dishes might feel a bit pricey for what you get, the quality and creativity make it worth trying. I would definitely go back to explore more of the menu and enjoy another night of great Thai flavors!

Every time I visit NYC, having Thai food is a must. This trip, a fellow Thai recommended that I try Chalong, especially because they specialize in Southern Thai cuisine and as someone from the South of Thailand, I had to see if it lived up to the hype.

Let me just say: 200/10.

The flavors were absolutely incredible, it truly felt like I was enjoying a proper, high-quality meal back home in Thailand. I went with my husband, and we both agreed that every dish was beautifully executed and packed with authentic flavor. You can really taste the freshness of the ingredients.

What impressed me even more is that their curry pastes are made fresh in-house,  not from a can. That makes such a difference, and you can tell they take pride in doing things the right way.

The service was also outstanding. Mr. Mung Korn was our server , so polite, attentive, and genuinely warm. He made the whole experience even more memorable.

I sincerely hope Chalong opens a location in DC one day! Until then, I will definitely be back whenever I’m in NYC. Highly, highly recommend.

Visited Chalong and overall it was decent but not particularly memorable. The squid ink seafood fried rice was flavorful and had squid and crab that tasted fairly fresh, with balanced seasoning. I’ve been ordering delivery from this place for a long time, but this was my first time actually visiting the restaurant. We went on a busy Friday night and had a reservation for four. name: Lundy Bros
document: Lundy Bros. cuisine: Seafood Bars American. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Nothing beats Lundy’s on a cold day! We’ve been here a few times at this point, and it’s just got this wonderful old school feel; both in the portion size and the quality and offerings of dishes, but also in the warmth of the atmosphere and service. This time we got the arugula salad (the dressing actually reminded me a lot of the lemon curd in lemon meringue pie! In a really good sweet, savory way) and the calamari as appetizers. We also got the Milanese (spectacular portion, and the collaboration chili sauce that comes with it. It’s such a good touch) and the famous chicken and obviously finished with the huckleberry pie. This restaurant is a continuous series of hits, and we will continue to come here for as long as possible!

It’s been a few months since I’ve been to a place as special as Lundy’s. I wish I came here sooner! First off, the vibe inside is cozy and old school. Really feels like you’re thrown back a bit in time to old Brooklyn. Everything we had during the evening was delicious but some highlights are the French onion soup and the calamari. I loved my burger as well but I was just so full by the end of the meal. The crab cake was also delicious and fresh, probably the meatiest crab cake I had to date. I’d 100% come back to Lundy’s soon to try out a few more options on their menu and get some of the classics. I actually think I might become a regular here! I wish we took down our waiters name since he was so helpful picking out some items on the menu and was very attentive. If you’re reading this, definitely come and visit Lundy’s, you won’t regret it!

I celebrated my son’s bday dinner last night. I was running a little behind due to traffic. I called  to let them know. A really nice lady answered and was so sweet. When we walked in, we got the warmest welcome from her. Her name is Debbie. I have a 10yrs old also and she immediately started having a conversation with her.
When she sat us in the dinning room, she let us know there were 2 servers for the night with a 1 bus boy. She mentioned them by name and I loved that. We were attended to by Keith. He was such a gem. He recommended so really great choices for us. This is what we had. For drinks, my husband and my son had the Red Hook which they loved. I don’t drink so I had the Captain Jack Mocktail.
Appetizers- Seafood Tower and Rhode Island Calamari. OMG the calamari is a must try. It has a little kick but you will thank me later. I little heat never hurt nobody.
Dinner- we all shared the Gala Apple Salad, Porter House, Linguini and Clams, Lundy’s Potatoes, and  Mac and Cheese.
Dessert- The Butterscotch Sundae my daughter hogged, and the Lundy’s Huckleberry Pie. Now let me tell you. I do not eat huckleberry pie, but that one, I could not believe how tasty. The crust was hard and sweet and the filling had the right flavor. Not too sweet or tart. All throughout dinner my husband and my son kept saying how great the food was. It was truly amazing and the service was great, with only 3 working and staying attentive to several tables.
I would definitely come back. Maybe for a girls night next time.

Dined here for my birthday. Everything was excellent. My mom had the calamari, flounder special that day, mashed potatoes and creamed spinach. I had the fried mozzarella, fish and chips, and a side of mac & cheese. Everything was amazing. The biscuits given in the beginning of dinner were a but salty but still good. Our waiter was excellent! I do wish that the menu stated that sides are shareable. We had sooo much food to go home with. Will definitely return!

My fiancé and I had an absolutely wonderful time at Lundy Bros,  and a huge part of that was thanks to our amazing hostess and server, Corey. From the moment we sat down, Corey made us feel welcome and taken care of. He was warm, attentive, and incredibly knowledgeable about the menu offering great recommendations that turned out to be spot-on.

The food was outstanding, the atmosphere was comfortable and inviting, and the service was truly exceptional. Corey checked in at all the right times, anticipated what we needed before we even had to ask, and added such a genuine, friendly energy to the whole evening.

If you’re thinking about visiting Lundy Bros, do it and if you’re lucky enough to have Corey as your server, you’re in for a fantastic experience. We’ll definitely be back!

google_reviews.text: I love this spot so much. The congee is consistently incredible-I am so grateful to have them in the neighborhood. The pork banh mi was good with tender and nicely seasoned pork, along a delicious turmeric salsa. Definitely not the most traditional but they mention that on the menu. Delicious bread.

Will be coming back for more !

This might be my favorite lowkey spot in the neighborhood. I’ve always walked past but never had the time to come in. I’ve only eaten congee that my friend has made, so I was skeptical to try another!

But I was not disappointed! It was truly deliciously and hearty! I’ve been craving a nice home cooked meal and this is exactly what this felt like. I will be back!

Highly recommend! Maya Congee catered my daughter’s 100 day celebration with chicken banh mi, veggie banh mi, and chicken & ginger soup. Everyone who attended raved about the food!

name: Burke’s Tavern
document: Burke’s Tavern. cuisine: New American Burgers Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Great food and service.

Nice atmosphere, reasonable prices.

The pizza was great and the wings were outstanding.

Also had the fish and chips which was killer too!

You won’t be disappointed!

What a pleasant surprise — it’s honestly surreal to visit places you once frequented as a curious youth. I’m talking about what once was HELL’S KITCHEN, a hipster neighborhood bar that is now a posh, beautifully curated lounge / restaurant — which is now BURKE’S TAVERN. This was an impromptu visit during a snowy Saturday — from beginning to end the experience was very overwhelming in the most positive way. From entrance to seating to the bar — from the subway tile and very carefully curated wood accents / furniture, to vintage tchotchkes and so much more — once you enter the locale, it really engulfs you with the ambiance and experience.

Here is where it goes from great to magic… Luisa our bartender made us some of the BEST COCKTAILS I’ve had in a really long time! I had the Paper Plane which was a whisky based cocktail with amaretto and aperol - it was HEAVEN in a glass. Followed by a French liqueur cocktail of which the name escapes me… honestly — paradise on a cold snowy day! Thank you Luisa! Made our day!!!

Here is where the establishment misses the mark keeping them from 5 Stars from my perspective. Wait time for food… We ordered something pretty simple, but it took almost 45min to get our food — luckily we were so distracted by the delicious cocktails, time escaped us - but yeah, it took quite some time, and we had to remind them in efforts to finally get the dishes.

Okay… The dishes… I got a Steak & Eggs for $23 dolllars — shell steak I believe with house fries, eggs, and a slice of toast - pretty reasonable for what I was expecting and fair. BUT - the flavor was lacking that umphhh - presentation was more like an $18 dish, due to receiving a sliced steak that was well done vs medium; home fries were just 2-3 full potatoes sliced in half — not really home fries, but not complaining for the giant pieces of potatoes lol - I don’t mind potatoes but if you are a lover, that style of home fries is for you lol. Eggs were not over easy as requested, but the sliced toast tasted like a buttered artisan sourdough which was amazing! Steak was tender but tasted slightly gamey… like maybe it wasn’t fresh from the butcher that day? Overall it was nice but NOT AMAZING!

Second dish was a CHIKIN sandwich (that’s how it’s spelled) that has what feels like an Asian or some kind of exotic name attached to the sandwich. $18 bucks… just the sandwich , this was recommended by the bartender. The sandwich in burger style form, was small, for $18 we were expected a diner sized sandwich in burger form. Flavors were decent, but the chicken was not crispy, and some parts were chewy and others crispy and soft…. It had to be returned, after 2 bites it was just  no-go. Ok so we said let’s just get some fries while we drink…. Fries were tasty but tasted and resembled the fries you get at a chicken shack (aka crown fried chicken) — those fries that emulate the McDonald’s fries that you buy at Costco or restaurant depot.

Now… based on this we did not want to explore anything else on the menu, but we remained happy with our cocktails and craft beers and wine. We felt ultimately that this location was built with cocktails and libations in mind - that was the primary it feels like, and that food was secondary — could be 1000% wrong, but that’s what it felt like for us, and after speaking with friends who also agreed, the consensus is, go for the amazing cocktails but avoid the food…

In the end, it was still a happy impromptu visit, will definitely be back for the cocktails, and for food there is always the Ironbound for authentic Brazilian and European cuisine — and so much more.

CHEERS!!! 🍻

Ordered the sliders… so good. Also ordered the espresso martini. Perfect. Highly recommend. Service was on point. No waiting .. was greeted right away. Will definitely come back when im in the area. Atmosphere was lively. Lots of chatter, music but super relaxed.

Burke's is a gem to say thr least.  Obviously those who were in the know didn't let me in on what amazing food and ambiance.   The shrimp with sauce...tasty. My chicken sandwich with slaw was flavorful and last but not least that blueberry cheesecake... My words will not due it justice!  Definitely will be back great staff and treated us like we home.

Outstanding experience from start to finish. The service felt genuine and welcoming, the European inspired ambiance created a cozy vibe, and the Moroccan lamb meatballs were bursting with rich, unforgettable flavor. Easily one of the best spots in Newark’s Ironbound area.

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3 stars)

I had a mixed experience at this restaurant, primarily due to some food issues and less-than-stellar service.

We were seated promptly and had ample time to review the menu. However, the service quickly became overwhelming. The waitstaff frequently approached us, almost rushing us, and came over right as we finished our last bites to ask if we wanted the check. It felt like they were anticipating a large table and wanted us to clear out. Considering that a large group beside us was moved to the bar and staff were rapidly rearranging tables around us, I’m unsure why we were seated just 30 minutes before their arrival when there were plenty of other available tables.

Regarding the food, we both ordered the NUEVAyol drink, which was decent but not worth the $17 price tag. The chicken and waffles were enjoyable, although the chicken itself was unseasoned; only the breading had flavor, and unfortunately, some parts of it were burnt. The steak and eggs, however, were disappointing. I ordered the steak medium-rare, but it arrived well done, with crispy edges and essentially folded in half from overcooking.

Additionally, I was disappointed to see an automatic 18% gratuity added to our bill for just two people. I understand this might be standard for larger parties, but it felt excessive in this case. I certainly wouldn’t have tipped $15 for the rushed service we received.

On a positive note, the atmosphere was delightful. A live DJ played Hip Hop tracks, and the decor featured nice art along with a faux speaker wall, which contributed to a vibrant vibe!

google_reviews.text: I was here for a wedding. The Valet parking isn't really good parking. It was a cold night and we had to walk a bridge and a courtyard to the location. Pedro was our main waiter on this very special day and tended to our every need. He made sure I knew each step and when each course was ready to be served. name: Maison Passerelle
document: Maison Passerelle. cuisine: French. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I am such a huge fan of this place! My boyfriend found this restaurant online, and once we saw that most of the menu was gluten free and dairy free, I got so excited! I was even more excited that the head chef and creator was Black. We made a reservation for the same night. We really enjoyed our meal. Walking in, the restaurant was elegant, and I loved the open kitchen. The 2 seater tables were a bit tight, similar to most restaurants, but the seats were comfortable. Our server was nice and the other staff were great. It was also great to see so many Black chefs, and I loved the RnB and soul music. We ordered off the restaurant week menu as well as the regular menu. Looking at the both menus, it’s evident that a talented chef created these dishes. My boyfriend is Haitian, so we appreciated seeing some Haitian staples being converted to fine dining. Our favorites were the lobster pasta, which had plenty of lobster, but we wanted more noodles and more of the entire dish. The gumbo was interesting, but really good. The Sòs Pwa Nwa with the
Pickled red onions was next level. The light coconut cake with the sorbet was fantastic. The only disappointment was the cornbread. I was so excited to try to gluten-free bread. It seems like some nights they have mini muffins and some nights they have the bigger loaf. We were only given 1 mini muffin for two people, so I asked for more and was charged $12. I was annoyed since the mini loaf is clearly much bigger than the mini muffin. Even if it was only 1 mini muffin per person who ordered off the regular menu, we spent so much money, it feels like it’s ridiculous to charge for an extra mini muffin on a $350 bill. That made me a bit upset. Otherwise, I’m a huge fan and highly recommend. Thank you for offering delicious Haitian food that’s gf/df. We will be back.

Ate here for a birthday lunch.
I was not disappointed.  I loved the hand cut tile mosaic floor and the open kitchen.  The staff were attentive and  enthusiastic.  Excellent cocktails. Every dish was a wonderful melange of flavor combining French,  Asian and African influences.  Even the French fries were notable. .My wife described them as like a good baguette...crusty on the outside and fluffy on the inside.  My favorite was the the Duck Confit Curry.

The most marvelous dining experience in Manhattan—I find myself returning over and over again. Every dish showcases a blend of exciting flavors, drawing from Caribbean and southeast Asian cuisine. The food is as visually stunning and luxurious as the beautifully designed interior. The prix fixe format may seem pricey initially—but is very reasonable when considering the portions are more substantial and the cooking technique more refined than many modern restaurants that have opened in the last years.

This is the cool new restaurant inside the beautiful Printemps building downtown. The restaurant is eclectic with bright colored tiles and stand out chandeliers, a great spot for striking conversations over a small dinner.
We visited for restaurant week - and apparently got some new testers on the menu. Food is inspired by French colonial cuisines - lots of Thai, south east asian, New Orleans, etc.
The dishes were tasty. Some flavours were a bit boring compared to other places in NY but overall pretty good.
Service still working out some kinks.

An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. This  restaurant offers a thoughtfully crafted prix fixe menu that showcases both creativity and precision. The duck was outstanding—perfectly cooked, rich, and deeply flavorful, with a balance that felt refined rather than heavy. The cod was equally impressive: delicate, fresh, and expertly prepared, allowing the quality of the fish to truly shine. Each course was beautifully presented and timed perfectly, and the overall menu felt cohesive and intentional. Attentive service and an elegant atmosphere elevated the evening, making it ideal for a special occasion or a memorable night out. Highly recommended for those who appreciate fine dining done right.

I can't wait to try their other items on the menu.

Fair prices! Fresh, juicy fish and other products. Good choice of rolls and drinks! This time I ordered vegan set - sweet potato roll pleasantly surprised me. My friends had sashimi and kani salad, the portion was formidable!

Overall Muzi is affordable value in sushi was pretty fresh for rolls. Would recommend.

Order the party platter A and some additional pieces which was over $50. Because of that we got a free tiramisu and bubble tea. Just note the bubble tea is very sweet.

I have been getting Muzi for any gathering or occasion. It's always a good, solid choice for affordable sushi that is well presented and has a good amount of filling. Other places might cheap out on the amount of fish and ingredients, but I haven't had that issue with Muzi. Their special rolls are quite special. The fire roll is quite fire. Torched tuna on top really makes it quite special. On holidays, they're open. Close at 5. Although they're extremely busy on holidays, they've been able to get my order in and ready for pickup. Just make sure to call in or order at least an hour and thirty minutes before 5 pm (on holidays). Their rolls are very good, and they have incentives for spending more. An order of hundred dollars brings in an extra special roll for free. A special roll, if bought individually, is listed for around 12-15 dollars. That's pretty cool. I think 30 dollars brings in a free drink. Also, I really like their spicy scallop roll. Tastes great and has good texture. Great staff. Great service. Thank you.

A truly excellent Peruvian rotisserie chicken with two large sides! It's my first time here, and it's one of the best chickens in town. I love a good Peruvian chicken, but haven't found a favorite in Manassas till now, it's legit! Plump, juicy and spiced right. So good!

We used to love this place but they recently started adding MSG (monoglutamato de sodio) in the recipe and this got my family sick. Sad because they used to be one of the only places in Manassas that didn’t use it.

This place is delicious! This is our go-to spot whenever we want peruvian chicken. Chicken is nicely flavored and the sides are always delicious. Price is worth it and quantity is great.

We also decided to try something other than the chicken and got the lomos saltados, which was also delicious! Steak is nice and tender and flavorful and one of the few places I can get this dish.

And of course, they have the green and yellow sauces, which they give a lot of without having to ask for more.

Great service and great food.

document: Moss Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Kosher New American. located in Bronx. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Great spot to come to especially in the morning as they have a great selection of breakfast pastries such as their seasonal apple danish (with or without cream), rhubarb danish (warmer months), muffins, scones and a good selection of coffees. They don’t have coffee syrups as everything they make is homemade but they do have other sweeteners. For lunch or dinner, you can grab a yummy salmon fried rice bowl or a generous greek salad.

Fantastic food and great vibes. Food was great we had the shakshuka and the moss egg sandwich (out of this 🌎). The coffees were great especially the pistachio latte. And last but not least after a lot of back and forth we picked from the bakery items a delicious curry/scallion cheese croissant and a. Nice buttery pistachio chocolate chip cookie.

Im so happy to write this review. Moss is a delight to go to. Everything is fresh, healthy portions and so delicious. Smooth no bitterness to their coffee, an impressive tea selection and cool beverages. It’s a kosher farm to table eatery filled with an array of food choices to satisfy your palate. I love the kale salad. Some may say it’s slightly overprice, but I see it as I pay the price and receive back so much more. Im happy they are here in Riverdale.

Delicious amazing vibes cafe. Went there on a Wednesday morning, was packed! The food is generally great and they have a super unique and healthy main menu. Also very yummy pastries. document: Panda Restaurant. cuisine: Chinese. located in Bronx. with 3.3 stars (decent). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Panda Express is my first American Chinese fast food chain (I just recently moved from Bali, Indonesia). What can I say? I’ve been here almost once every week, they always stuff your box to the fullest, great food and always have limited menu which I like to try everytime I come here. Beijing beef, honey walnut shrimp and orange chicken are definitely my trio go-to (and when they have the spicy orange chicken)

Our young grandson introduced us to Panda. Since then I'm we go on a regular basis when we want quick service and good food. Good variety of choices, freshly cooked. A change of pace from fast food burgers. You won't be disappointed.

The sign inside reads " American Chinese Quisine." That it is, so don't look for authentic Chinese food. To me, everything was too sweet, hiding the veggie and meat flavors. But it was fast, inexpensive,  and filling. Typical American cuisine.  The staff was accommodating.  This is not a buffet. Pick your main entrée and side. There is not a lot of vegan choice, just the sides. Dishes were beef, chicken, or shrimp based. Perhaps tables need to be cleaned more often as most are large and you may share a table with others. If you want fast, cheap, and filling, it's a good place.
Got lunch here to go, very delicious orange chicken and noodles. Friendly staff, easy accessibility, plenty of parking, clean restrooms.  Not far off of I-66.

Ordered the family style meal. Got home to find the boxes weren’t even filled up all the way. For what you pay you’d think you’d get your money’s worth. Complained online to Panda Express and still haven’t heard from anyone in management.

name: Alessa Cucina & Bar
document: Alessa Cucina & Bar. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars Venues & Event Spaces. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Alessa Cucina E Bar in Midtown was a great spot for a relaxed night out. We ordered the marinated olives, which came in a generous portion and were well seasoned and delicious. The Fritto Misto, a mix of calamari, shrimp, and zucchini, was lightly battered and served with chili aioli. It was good, though not particularly memorable. We also tried the housemade focaccia; the bread itself was very good, but I wasn’t a fan of the butter it came with. The fries were tasty, but I would have preferred a crispier bite.

For drinks, I ordered the Flower Martini made with rosebud-infused vodka, and I would definitely recommend it. It was pretty, flavorful, and strong in a good way. My friend enjoyed her Ravello Spritz.

Service was friendly and attentive. We were walk-ins on a Thursday at 10:00pm. They let us know the kitchen would be closing soon, though we were told it closed at 10:20 when it actually closed at 11. They still made sure to check in before last call. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, with plenty of space between tables and a comfortable, spacious layout. It was a great place for girl chat and an easy, relaxed evening.

I’m honestly very disappointed, especially since this restaurant has a 4.7 rating.

It started with the hostess. I had a reservation specifically for the dining area, but she seated us in the high-top room instead. When I asked if there was a table available in the dining area, she said no. Meanwhile, there were two empty two-person tables the entire time we were there. If I made a reservation for the dining area, I expect to be seated there.

Service was very slow. Our waitress, Pam, was very nice and polite, but the restaurant was packed on a Sunday evening and they only had three waitresses working. Unfortunately, all of our food arrived cold.

We were seated next to the pizza station since it’s an open kitchen, and we clearly saw the pizza cook eating mushrooms directly from the container. That was very unprofessional and uncomfortable to witness.

The rice balls were probably the best thing we had that night — but even those were cold. The rest of the food was a disaster. The cheeseburger was extremely spicy (I assume from a spicy mayo), and no one informed us that it would be that spicy.

Overall, a very bad experience and not what we expected based on the high rating. Very disappointing.

Went for an early dinner with some colleagues on a Thursday evening and the place was absolutely buzzing! Super packed and a little loud by the bar, but thankfully we were seated in the back where conversation was much easier. Bonus points for the happy hour that runs until 8pm—such a win.

We shared a few apps and some pizzas for the table, and everything was delicious. Our waiter was an absolute vibe—fun, attentive, and really made the night. The only downside was the cocktails, which tasted more like juice than a proper drink, so I switched to wine after that (definitely the safer bet).

Overall, great energy, tasty food, and I’m already looking forward to coming back to try more of the menu.

I had a fantastic time at the restaurant and enjoyed the service and restaurant atmosphere. I took home some leftover pizza. The Bianca pizza was delightful and had roasted garlic pieces underneath the cheese.

Unfortunately, halfway through eating the pizza slice I bit into this plastic piece. Thankfully I didn’t come close to swallowing it. I guess, be careful eating the pizzas and chew thoroughly.

Wow. So glad this opened up near my home. Beautiful inside with fantastic misern italian fare. The best drinks in the city. Alexis makes a mean drink. Nice has such knowledge about drinks and food. He gave us a wonderful experience. My birthday was outstanding. The martini parm was fun. Light, interesting and great blue cheese stuffed olives. So fun. The ravello spritz was like itslian lemon candies. Delicious. The expresso martini fantastic. Light n frothy. The clarified ny sour blew my mind. May be the best drink ever. Frito mistook was like naples. The beet salad fantastic and refreshing. The interesting part was the dehydrated squid ink olive oil.  Just wanted more, all mixed with the marscapone. The pizza here fantastic. Memorable.  The pesto was like moms and the mozzarella tasted farm fresh.  The cantalope and prossuto  fresh. The coconut Verde drink outrageous.  It was a frothy tropical coconut, green juice gone margarita. The chicken park was huge, delicious and seasoned. The best i ever ate out. Fun cheese pull. The broccoli nuggets with fried hot peppers yes please. Good buccatini n clam. (They have gluten free options). The house made tiramisu,  with homeade lady fingers and caramel brittle was delicious. Outstanding meal and service.

name: Sophra Grill
document: Sophra Grill. cuisine: Mediterranean Turkish Halal. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We recently visited Sophra Grill in Murray Hill and really enjoyed the experience overall. This place feels like a true neighborhood gem, warm, family-run, and focused on authentic Turkish and Mediterranean flavors rather than fancy presentation or trendy gimmicks.

The atmosphere is cozy and casual, with only a handful of tables and a welcoming vibe that instantly makes you feel at home. The staff were friendly, helpful, and patient in explaining the menu. It’s the kind of place where you can sit back, relax, and enjoy a comforting meal without feeling rushed.

We decided to share a few dishes, the mixed grill platter (which included lamb, chicken, and beef kebabs), a red lentil soup, and a few vegetarian sides. They also brought out complimentary Turkish bread, which was a nice touch, though it wasn’t particularly fresh that day. Everything else arrived hot and nicely presented. The chicken adana kebab stood out, flavorful, juicy, and perfectly seasoned, while the chicken kebab was tender and well-grilled. The red lentil soup was smooth, hearty, and well-balanced in flavor.

For dessert, we tried the baklava, which was excellent, light, flaky, and not overly sweet, just the way it should be. Portions here are generous, and prices are quite reasonable for the quality and portion size, making it a great value overall.
If there’s one small note, it’s that the restaurant can feel a bit tight during peak hours since it’s a compact space. But honestly, that adds to its charm, it feels personal, genuine, and homey, which is hard to find these days.

Overall, Sophra Grill is an excellent spot for authentic Turkish cuisine served with care and consistency. Whether you’re craving kebabs, grilled meats, or vegetarian dishes, you’ll find something delicious here. Definitely worth visiting, and I’d happily come back again for the mixed grill platter and baklava!

Perfect ambience, friendly staff and amazing dishes. Peaceful atmosphere with warm light and calm music. Staff is friendly and they do pay attention to whatever you request. We had Iskander and chicken gyro. Iskander we had was well balanced and delicious, but I won’t be able to say the same for chicken gyro. If you like good seasoning and delicious chicken i would say pass it on this time. But meat is 100% way to go here . Amazing stuff. It also could be preference with chicken( you may like your chicken unseasoned or plain ish) . Thank you for having us today here everyone ❤️

This was a delicious, authentic Turkish experience - the food was fresh, phenomenal and filling - if anything the photos don't do it justice.

Ask for oil over the Iskender for the full experience, and the lahmacun is the real deal. They homemake their own ayran as well.

They were also unbelievably attentive and lovely to us.

One of the best Turkish meals I've ever had, including in Turkey.

Absolutely amazing spot for Turkish food in Murray Hill. It was close to my hotel, so I figured to stop in. I’m so glad I did. I got to try a variety of different items, inducing: ayran, chicken Adana sandwich on home bread, Turkish tea, and rice pudding.

The ayran was probably the best I’ve ever had in my life. It was so refreshing, the perfect amount of salt, so good. And it’s homemade. I would highly recommend you try this drink regardless of what you order, it’s that good.

The chicken Adana sandwich was also quite nice. The chicken was fresh and well seasoned in a good portion with some lettuce, onions, tomatoes as well. The bread was great. It’s served with two wonderful, flavorful sauces: hot sauce and yogurt sauce (I much prefer the latter). Portion is incredible for the price.

Then, I was initially interested in trying the fig pudding for dessert but they were out of it, so I went with the rice pudding. Again, a huge portion that is well worth the price. So creamy, so good. And, they brought out 2 Turkish teas for free to make up for not having the fig! The people are just very nice here, and the tea was also lovely, piping hot and just perfect.

It’s a pretty small restaurant but doesn’t get crowded early on. They were playing some Turkish music while I ate, and I really enjoyed it. The people are very kind and attentive and the food is just incredible. Must try!

Probably my favorite Turkish spot from recent discoveries. Get the mixed grill from the lamb section, it's excellent. You get different types of meat and they are each so flavorful. The staff is very hospitable and kind too. Hands down a fantastic neighborhood spot. Love the casual and inviting atmosphere.

document: Yezo Thai Isankaya. cuisine: Thai Izakaya Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: omg this needs to be the best Thai food I’ve had this year so far!!! If you get one thing from the menu, please let it be the short rib massaman, the short rib literally melts in your mouth and the sauce is so good I think I can eat three bowls of rice with it. The mango parfait was also the best way to end the meal, the mango were so sweet.

Lowkey underrated Thai spot. Came around on a Thursday at 6:30 pm, and it was empty besides one table. We made a res but you prob don’t need to. Interior is so cute!

- Short rib massaman w/ roti ($34.95): 8/10, pretty good, and it came w/ roti, which the menu didn’t mention! The roti was so crispy and flakey (11/10 stars wow). The actually massaman curry was okay. Thought it would be thicker, but it was lowkey watery, and the potatoes were still kinda hard. Overall flavor was really yummy, and the meat was very tender. Wish there was more meat tho. This same dish at Pranakhon is a LOT better
- Pad Thai Yezo w/ chicken ($17.95): 9/10, I actually really liked this! I’m usually not a huge fan of pad Thai, but this one had really good flavor. The chicken wasn’t tough

Fantastic Thai restaurant in midtown east. The interior is so cozy and aesthetic and service was attentive. We had a great meal here and would absolutely come back!

Crying Tiger: Grilled NY strip that was flavorful and tender. Also loved the sauce that it came with. I personally prefer my steak a bit more rare, but the flavors delivered

Keaw Tod: Crispy fried wontons with a delicious chicken and shrimp filling. Super snackable and great to share

Short Rib Massaman: Rich and comforting with tender short rib. Loved the roti to dip into the curry too!

Larb Salmon: From the winter seasonal menu. Fresh, citrusy, and tangy in the best way. Definitely balanced out the other dishes

Mango Parfait: I didn’t know what to expect but loved this. Think mango sticky rice meets ice cream parfait

Drinks:
My Summer (mango mocktail): Super refreshing!
Melon Lar (melon mocktail): More syrupy than I expected, but still tasty if you like sweeter drinks

Yezo Thai Isankaya is an absolute gem! From the moment you walk in, the ambiance feels warm and inviting. The flavors are incredible—authentic Thai dishes with that perfect balance of spice, sweetness, and freshness. The presentation of each dish is beautiful, and the service is attentive without being overbearing. Whether you’re a fan of classic curries, fresh seafood, or signature cocktails, everything here hits the mark. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a top-notch Thai dining experience in the city!

Cozy place with great service & delicious food. We ordered crying tiger, spring rolls, chicken satay & massaman curry with roti for appetizers. Mains was chicken basil, drunken noodles, steak basil & salmon bowl. Everything was super delicious & Molly, our server was very friendly, helpful & efficient. Would definitely recommend this restaurant as must try.

Everything was very tasty, the portions were generous, and the prices were reasonable. The service was very friendly and welcoming. A perfect place for a satisfying and authentic Polish meal. We would definitely recommend it and would be happy to come back again in the future.

My favorite Polish restaurant in NY. Warm atmosphere, friendly staff, and great food and value even after all these years. I couldn't get over how reasonable the prices still are especially considering the generous portions. This could easily qualify as a NY essential. The white borscht in a bread bowl is one of my favorite things to eat in the city.

Karczma never lets me down. It’s one of the last true Polish spots left in Greenpoint, and it honestly feels like a little piece of home. Whenever I’m feeling homesick or just need some comfort, this is where I go for food that warms my soul. The meals are always tasty, portions are generous, and there’s always something good on the menu. Love this place!

I’m Polish so I know what means good quality Polish food ! And this is what you would find in Karczma ! I’m really impressed! Sour rye soup aka Zurek in a bread is to die for! We came back next day for more food . Highly recommend for everyone! Do zobaczenia next time !

document: Blu Ember. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 3.8 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Great experience overall, smaller space than expected which becomes loud when the table next to you is drunk and borderline screaming. Atmosphere was great aside from that. I wish we visited on a calmer night or that the staff was able to do something for us. Otherwise, the place was classy and dimly lit. The food was quite delightful. Portion sizes were perfect for us but there was way too much ice in the drinks.

The ambiance is undeniably appealing, making it a suitable choice for dates or special occasions. Among restaurants in Flushing, this type of refined and elegant interior is relatively uncommon. Service is attentive, with staff offering thoughtful recommendations and guidance throughout the meal.

The food itself, however, is fairly average. After multiple courses, none stood out in particular. The dry-aged T-bone steak was especially underwhelming, lacking depth of flavor and slightly overcooked, resulting in a tougher texture. The plates used to serve the steak also felt impractical, as they cooled too quickly and were not ideal for maintaining temperature. In comparison, the ribeye was noticeably better, with more consistent execution and a stronger sense of value.

If the visit is primarily for the atmosphere, the restaurant is worth considering. If the focus is on the food alone, the experience may vary depending on personal taste.

Blu Ember was a good experience. We went for my daughter's birthday 🎂. The service was outstanding. The food was amazing. The burgers was juicy and delicious. My mom had the seafood medley and the french onion soup and she didnt have anything left. My daughter had pasta and sushi and was delicious. Please go and support this place delicious.

I picked Blu Ember at the Westin LGA simply because it was convenient before our flight—but it ended up being one of the best pre-airport meals I’ve ever had. Everything exceeded expectations: the food, the service, and the ambiance.

We ordered a mix of dishes and every single one was beautifully presented and packed with flavor. The oysters were incredibly fresh, the burrata with heirloom tomatoes was bright and delicious, and the toro/uni bites with caviar were a true standout. Our entrées—from the seafood to the steak—were cooked perfectly and tasted even better than they looked.

Service was friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. For a restaurant this close to the airport, the atmosphere is surprisingly upscale and relaxing—perfect for a calm meal before flying out.

Whether you’re staying nearby or just want a great dining experience before heading to LGA, Blu Ember is absolutely worth it. I’d come back even if I wasn’t flying.

Had higher expectations for this place. The food wasn’t that good. The spot is cute it’s located in the hotel. The service was friendly. For starters I had the Kumamoto oysters, toro caviar Monaka, tuna crispy rice, salmon hand roll, waygu hand roll. I didn’t like the oysters it had a really weird after taste and I’m a big raw oyster fan. The toro and crispy rice were underwhelming. The hand rolls were probably the best thing out of all the appetizers. You can’t go wrong with salmon hand rolls haha. but I will say their prime ribeye was really good. It was juicy I liked it. So definitely recommend that! Overall not a bad date night spot !

name: Friendship Foods BBQ
document: Friendship Foods BBQ. cuisine: Barbeque Hot Pot. located in Queens. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This was our first time at Friendship BBQ in Shoreline and overall it was a cool experience. The skewers were fun to try and the atmosphere was lively. We did order wagyu, but it honestly didn’t taste like wagyu and was pretty tough, so the quality could definitely be better there. The chicken feet was another level. Ordered but could not finish it.  Still, we enjoyed trying the place and would come back to try other items.

The Lamb Skewers were on the saltier side. The Xinjiang Lamb Skewer was chunky, which made it hard to eat. The Spicy Rice Noodle Pot was also a bit salty. We tried a variety of other items, including Enoki Mushroom, Gizzards, Beef Skewers, Pork Belly, Lotus Root, Squid, Lamb Kidney, Pork Belly with Enoki Mushroom, and Chicken Heart. None of these stood out, but I also don’t have anything negative to say about them. There’s also a free order of Shrimp in Chili Sauce if you spend over $88.

I liked the free Yakult we received after our meal. The vibe is very relaxed. Overall, it’s a wonderful spot if you’re craving Chinese-style skewers, though I think the seasoning could use a little work.

We came on a Saturday afternoon without a reservation, specifically craving the lamb and beef with tərdan spices, both were our top picks. The pork intestine were also surprisingly good, especially if you’re into offal. The service was exceptionally friendly, and overall, it was a solid dining experience.
Tasty and better price than other 2 Chinese bbq here. They offered their homemade 牛轧糖🍬 that’s super super soft and milky

This place is amazing if you visit in person! We ordered once during the pandemic and wasn’t impressed, but decided to give it another try. We were not disappointed! The menu is pretty extensive. We ordered an assortment of skewers (our favorites were the pork belly, beef and fat, and chicken gristle) which were all nicely cooked and had great flavor. We also got a side of cold cucumbers which were refreshing and slightly tart / sweet and the spicy rice noodles. My husband loved the noodles which were very comforting to eat alongside the skewers. Everything tasted very fresh, was served quickly, and decent in portion. We hit $88 and the waitstaff gifted us with a shrimp dish, which was also very yummy. After the meal, staff also gave us two yakult drinks to wash it all down. The service was also great - water and napkins were provided without us having to ask. So glad we decided to stop by! We will definitely be back to try more things!

name: Jing Li
document: Jing Li. cuisine: Shanghainese Cantonese Szechuan. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We stopped in in he middle of the week for a bite. The drinks definitely were enjoyble. E perfect balance of sweet and potent. The shrimp tempura was very light with a slightly sweet aoili. We had the duck mins one braised, and crispy both were delicious. We had to try the truffle fried rice although our dishes came with a side of white rice. It is light, and not salty at all. We thoroughly enjoyed all out dish. We will be back.

We got the pre-fixe menu for $39/person!

So worth it. The food was really good and the portions were solid! Three of us shared our meals and enjoyed our meals. My favorite entree was the braised beef clay pot! The drinks were also really delicious. I got a Lychee Martini.

Tony was a great server and so attentive! Will definitely come back :)

The interior design and the whole environment was the most memorable part of the visit, but unfortunately, the food does not leave any strong remarks. Avoid the chicken wings — they were oily and very heavily flavored, but didn't leave a very satisfactory feeling. The fried rice was also surprisingly plain, as if they forgot to add salt. While the flavor of the steamed fish was acceptable, the portion was disappointing (check the photo for reference). It’s a beautiful space, but the kitchen needs more consistency and better portions.

After seeing so many reels on Instagram, I have been curious to try it out. Lucky for me, an opportunity came up the other day! So, Jing Li is a modern Chinese fusion restaurant that is inspired by Szechuan, Shanghai, and Cantonese cuisine. The restaurant brings a unique twist to global flavors, creating delicious dishes.

I highly recommend the Dinner 4 Course Prix Fixe. You can choose one of three soups (Hot & Sour Soup, Wonton Soup, or Tom Yum Soup), an appetizer or dim sum (except the Dim Sum Tasting), an entree (except MaLa Day Hot Pot), and a dessert (Crème Brûlée or Mochi Ice Cream).

I would suggest ordering the Royal Style Barbeque Beef. The beef was tender and delicious! The spices and peppers give it a nice kick, but do not make the overall dish too spicy. The fire underneath kept the dish warm and made an appealing dish to watch!

One of the appetizers that I enjoyed was the Lychee Prawn Cake. Prawns are shaped and lightly fried to this beautifully, lychee-looking cake pop. The prawn cake is very light and tasty, even better if you use the sauce provided too, although not necessarily needed!

While the Crème Brûlée was small, it was still tasty. The caramel top was hard enough for the audible crack without the need to apply too much pressure. The custard underneath was not overly sweet!

Service is perfect too! The staff are attentive and frequently walk around, checking in on the table. The dishes come in a timely manner that does not make you wait for long! I will be returning soon to try the other dishes. There are still a ton of appetizers and entrees that I have been meaning to try!

My new favorite place in LIC! The food, the portions, the ambiance, the price-can’t beat it. They have a prefix dinner menu for only $39! My family and I were stuffed. The food was absolutely mouth watering. The staff were so nice and attentive, going to come back with friends!

name: Coco Hotpot
document: Coco Hotpot. cuisine: Hot Pot Chinese Asian Fusion. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
One of my go-to winter comfort meals in New York.

The reason is simple: the chicken is consistently tender and fresh, and the portions are generous for the price. On this visit, I noticed they’ve expanded their soup base options beyond the classic herbal and pork stomach broths, now offering flavors like curry and pomegranate as well.

We ordered the coconut chicken set for two, which includes half a free-range chicken, a main carb, and a vegetable platter. The pot is served with two fresh coconuts, and you can ask the staff to scrape the coconut meat directly into the broth, which makes the soup even sweeter and more fragrant. It’s best to remove the chicken slightly early to keep the texture tender.

For an additional $15, you can add clay pot rice, which is well worth it. We chose the salted fish and pork patty clay pot rice. The pork patty was juicy and bouncy, with crispy water chestnuts inside for added texture. The salted fish bits hidden in the rice provide a savory depth, and the lightly crispy golden rice crust at the bottom is a highlight.

We also added sliced beef, which stays tender even after cooking, and radish, which absorbs the coconut broth beautifully. Portion-wise, it was more than enough for two people.

Overall, a solid, satisfying choice for cold weather, especially if you’re looking for something warming, comforting, and reasonably priced in Queens.

This is my go to place for coconut chicken hot pot!! Ingredients are always fresh and high quality. We ordered the chicken combo for 2, that’s a lot of food!!! We were really satisfied with the sweet coconut broth, and the sauce bar has great options to go with the chicken. 100% recommend!!!

My first time trying coconut hot pot and I’ve clearly been missing out! The coconut broth was light and sweet, and way easier on the stomach than a regular hot pot.

We visited on one of the coldest days, and the restaurant was PACKED. It’s located in Downtown Flushing, literally right next to Tangram. It’s also more affordable than other coconut hot pot spots in the city, with a heartier portion too.

Shoutout to the impeccable service — our server even helped skim off the floating oil from the broth (and made me want to buy that ladle lol).

＊Coconut Chicken (for two) 皇椰雞套餐 $75.95
They use cage-free chicken, and the pieces were generously sized with not too much bone. This portion was already enough to feed four. The set also comes with vegetables, plus your choice of rice or noodles. The coconut broth wasn’t heavy at all that we were basically sipping it nonstop.

＊Poached Egg & Beef Clay Pot Rice 窩蛋牛肉煲仔飯 +$15
You get a discounted price if you add their claypot rice to your hot pot order. It looked very promising and delicious, especially with the runny poached egg. But I thought the rice needed a few more minutes in the clay pot to crisp up the base a bit more.

＊Maxi’s Noodle Wonton 雲吞妹雲吞 $9.95
The price is pretty steep for just three wontons, but I love Maxi’s so much that I still went for it. The shrimp wontons were so plump and meaty.

＊Handmade Battered Shrimp 極品鮮蝦滑 $12.95
SOOOO GOOD I am a fan of shrimp paste in a hot pot.

Really enjoyed the coconut chicken hotpot here. The chicken was fresh and tender, and the coconut broth was flavorful and comforting. The combo set came with plenty of food, and everything tasted great. Cozy atmosphere and friendly service. Would definitely come back!
The ingredients are fresh, the taste is great, and the environment is clean and hygienic. I've been a customer many times, and today I had dinner with my son and wanted to leave a five-star review.
