name: Let's Do Brunch
document: Let's Do Brunch. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Salad Sandwiches. located in Queens. with 3.8 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
I loved this place. The atmosphere is cozy, and the attention from the waitress was also the best. She was really attentive.

Regarding the food, it came out fresh and warm. The omellete is delicious! We also had the hangover burger and the chicken skeewers. Personally, both great, but, I would have love the french fries to be a bit more seasoned. Not a big deal though, since you can add salt to it.

I'm definetely coming back to this hidden gem!

Had such an amazing experience here. The staff were so kind, welcoming, and helpful. The food and drinks both came out extremely fast. The food was top notch. The chicken and waffles I got were so soft and flavored well. The chicken was seasoned and fried perfect. The mimosas are amazing. Best of all the meal was well priced. Wholeheartedly recommend this.

Let's do brunch was amazing. One of the things that I really admire is the fact that they serve brunch every day. It is located in Queens and parking was not too bad. It is a residential area so keep that in mind. We were seated right away during the midday hour. There were other people there but it wasn't overly crowded which was really relaxing and comfortable. The service was exceptional. To put a cherry on top of this review, I would like to add that we asked for the manager and she came over to our table sat with us, had coffee, and we had a really great conversation about so many different topics. That  really was impressive because it's so important for managers to know their customers, and to know the community that they are doing business in.

One to the food, the jerk salmon was well seasoned, and well prepared. It was cooked to a great temperature and tasted really good.   The chicken and waffles were well seasoned and the waffle was so fluffy and warm and nice. I really appreciated the fact that although it was chicken tenders, the batter was seasoned really well and you could taste something other than just chicken. lol.

I would definitely return because I saw so many things on the menu that I would want to try.  they also serve mimosas, wine, and lots of hot drinks and I want to try their mimosa flight.

Let’s Do Brunch is my favorite brunch spot ever! The inside has such a cozy, welcoming vibe, the waiters are always so friendly and the owner is so sweet! The food tastes amazing, my go-tos are the chicken and waffles, the seasoned fries, and the buffalo chicken rolls.

The presentation of the food is also worth noting, the chefs really take their time to make everything look good! It’s become my go-to spot whenever I have something to celebrate. I honestly recommend this place to anyone. You’ll leave full and happy every single time.

We had such a lovely experience at Let’s Do Brunch! The food was prepared fresh and very flavorful, and the service was absolutely excellent — warm, friendly, and attentive from start to finish. The restaurant was clean, and the vibe struck the perfect balance between vintage charm and chic, modern comfort.

It’s always so inspiring to see persons of Guyanese heritage doing amazing things and creating cultured establishments like this. You can truly feel the pride, passion, and authenticity in every detail. Highly recommend this gem and look forward to my next visit.

The service was good as I remember years ago.

The food is very good. The food did not disappoint and I was happy with my choice.

Prices are acceptable.

The music was too loud for me. I have hearing problems, and speaking was a challenge. That’s the reason of the four stars.

I recommend this place and I will be back when I visit The Bronx.

DISGUSTING FOUND A ROACH IN MY SOUP !!

I’ve never left a review like this before, but my experience here was truly disappointing. While having seafood soup, I found a roach inside my bowl  yes, an actual roach, which I have a photo of. When I brought it to the attention of the staff and manager, they were completely dismissive about it.
We politely asked if they could at least cover our second round of drinks since we clearly didn’t want to continue eating after finding a roach in our food.

The waiter responded casually, almost as if this was something that “just happens,” and said they would cover the drinks we had.

Moments later, another waiter came over to say we would still need to pay for them.

The manager showed no concern, no apology, and no sense of responsibility he acted as if this was a normal restaurant situation. It was unprofessional and honestly unsettling.
I would never recommend this place to anyone after this experience. Cleanliness, accountability, and basic customer service were completely missing.

Everything about this establishment was appreciated and customer centered! The location, food, portions, service, servers, drinks, decor, music, price - bravo 👏🏾. We frequent often when in the area, and it helps that we catch the happy hour. Accessible by the parking garage on one side and the pedestrian street side, on the opposite side of the mall.

name: Honey's Thai Pavilion
document: Honey's Thai Pavilion. cuisine: Thai Noodles Beer Bar. located in Bronx. with 3.5 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This was our first time here as a date night option.  We came early around 7pm and there was plenty of seats.  The staff and manager were very attentive, friendly, and were very helpful with the menu suggestions.  The restaurant has a nice cozy atmosphere.  Despite being by the train station, it's quiet enough to have a nice evening on a date.  The food came out quickly and was very fresh.  The drinks were a good "strength" and tasty. By mid dinner, the restaurant was packed.  Come early for dinner is my recommendation.  If you're a repeat customer, I've noticed that the manager remembers you, your likes and dislikes, and your usual order.  That's amazing and shows that every customer matters.  We got good portions for our meal and the prices were reasonable.  They also offer delivery if you choose to order in.  Also, you can ask them to tweak the spiciness level of your food - mild, medium, Thai hot.  I asked for the Thai hot and it was very spicy (which I love) without compromising the taste of the food.  I will definitely come back here again and try the rest of the menu!

The worst Thai Food I have ever tasted! I initially ordered Pad Thai(picture not taken) it was so disgusting I sent it back and replaced with Basil Fried Rice. The fried rice wasn’t any better. I ordered fries and nuggets for my son, the nuggets were literally fried chicken skin. Never going back!

What kind of a restaurant forgets to remove the shells off the shrimp soup?

A restaurant that is spiraling downwards!

I could understand if they forgot to remove one or two shells, but they left all the shells on the shrimp. It’s soup!

Additionally, the serving size soup was so tiny that it doesn’t qualify as a side dish.

Rather the container size is the size of a sauce container and they charged $12.95! What nerve!

I contacted the restaurant to send me a replacement but not only did they refuse to do so, they were unwilling to refund me.

We are disputing the charge with our credit card company.

This is the last time I will ever order from this place.

Do yourself favor go elsewhere!

Also, The pad Thai was mediocre at best.  You can get better pad thai from a food court at the mall.

I provided pics with the shells. Couldn’t finish this soup! Shame on them for serving subpar food.

Visited on a Sunday afternoon for thai cuisine. My hostess and waitress was pleasant and courteous in making suggestions. She was very nice and I was happy with her service.
She suggests the pad thai noodles with beef, she did say it was regular noodles. But she boasted about how good it was.
The plate was less than par, first impressions was a plate of angel hair pasta with sweet ketchup, with overdone beef pieces and what I think was microwaved. I heard the microwave beep, I'm sure of it.
What was delicious was the crispy shrimp appetizer and sweet tea.
I was not impressed with the hot sauces stationed by the entrance.
I was not impressed with all their cleaning supplies lined up outside the bathroom. It's not what I want to see to see as part of the decor.
I would not visit again.

Very nice Thai spot in the Bronx. Very convenient to get to either from the train or from the highway. I've ordered here many times, the food is always great. My go-to meals are the pad see ew and the basil fried rice. A nice side of crab Rangoon or the wings always hits the spot as well.

name: Campania Coal Fired Pizza
document: Campania Coal Fired Pizza. cuisine: Bars Pizza Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Came for lunch. Food is mediocre. Service stinks. Ambiance is good.

Service:  Waiter took our order. Runner brought out the food. No one came to check in after the food was delivered. Our glasses were empty, my wife had to get up and find the staff congregated by the kitchen chatting to ask someone for drinks.  I get the feeling that owners are absent during the day and management does a poor job keeping staff accountable. Poorly run establishment that has potential.

Food: ordered the Milanese and veal Francese.  Breading on Milanese was too thick and soggy. I like my Milanese to have a thin crispy breaded crust and tender chicken within - this wasn’t that. Ironically francese had the same thick breading but was dry in the sense that it didn’t have enough sauce.

It’s a shame because the owners/investors clearly put a lot of money into the actual building. If they focused on properly managing the kitchen and front of house, this place could be so much more.
both our main courses and appetizers (not pictured) were very fresh and tasted homemade! I really enjoyed the service from the kind staff Ermal and Elian. The drinks were also good!

Campania on Hylan Blvd is the kind of spot that instantly makes you feel comfortable. The atmosphere is warm and lively, with a perfect balance between casual and upscale. Whether you’re meeting friends, having a family gathering, or just looking for a place to unwind, it never disappoints.

I spent some time here doing remote work, and even with the energy of the restaurant, it never felt overwhelming. The staff was attentive without being intrusive, making sure I had everything I needed. The seating is comfortable, and the overall ambiance makes it a great place to settle in for a while.

What really stands out is the consistency. Every visit feels just as welcoming as the last, and the service is always on point. If you’re looking for a place with a great vibe and a welcoming atmosphere, Campania is definitely Helwa Approved.

name: L'Artusi
document: L'Artusi. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
I’ll start with the appetizers. I’m not usually a kale fan, but the kale Caesar was a standout. The Caesar dressing and croutons were so good—they really made the dish. I wouldn’t necessarily order it myself, but if someone at the table gets it, definitely try it.

The hamachi with Granny Smith apples, cucumber, and horseradish was solid. It was fresh, light, and had a nice balance from the apples and horseradish. Nothing that completely blew me away, but definitely good.

The focaccia was also really good—thick, soft, and just great bread overall. It paired well with the Wagyu carpaccio. This was my first time having carpaccio, and it was interesting. It didn’t have a huge flavor at first, but the aftertaste was nice. If you’re curious, try it, but it wasn’t something that stood out enough for me to order again. I didn’t try the roasted beets, but I heard they were great.

For the main dishes, I think the rigatoni was possibly the best thing on the menu at L’Artusi. The pesto really stood out, and you could clearly taste the soppressata. I usually think pesto can be a little bland, but this one was really flavorful and balanced well with the rest of the dish.

The braised short ribs were the only thing I was really disappointed by. As someone who loves meat, it just didn’t hit for me. The polenta was good, but polenta only really works if the meat carries the dish, and this didn’t. Honestly, it reminded me of something I’d expect from a fast-casual place like Wonder. After seeing the hanger steak in person, I’d definitely recommend going with that instead.

For dessert, we had the olive oil cake, the pear napoleon, and the coffee sprout torta. The torta was very chocolatey—almost too much for me. I like chocolate, but when the whole dessert tastes like chocolate it can be a bit much, so I probably wouldn’t get that again. The olive oil cake is the one everyone raves about, but honestly I thought it was pretty basic. The pear napoleon, though, was really good and probably the best dessert we had.

The service was phenomenal. Our waitress was really nice, gave us good suggestions, and made the whole experience smooth. I’d give the service a 10/10.

Overall, I’d rate the restaurant a 4 out of 5. I probably wouldn’t go again on my own, but if someone asked me to go, I’d say yes—it’s definitely solid. 👍

Had L’Artusi on my list to try — it’s a must! Grabbed a reservation for 2 @ the bar on a Friday at 12:15 for 12:45pm. The garganelli pasta was incredible - I was hesitant about the mushroom ragu but it was so delicious and perfectly done. The olive oil cake was my favorite thing we ate — unbelievable flavor. A spoonful of cake w / the raisin marmelleta and mousse was absolute perfection. Highly recommend L’Artusi. Spent $150 including tip for 2 people - no alcohol.

Definitely one of the best Italian restaurants in New York City. I’m honestly not a big fan of Italian food outside of Italy but this one left a mark.

The place gets very crowded so book in advance and be ready to sit pretty close to other tables with quite a bit of noise.

The food is very good. We got the rigatoni the perciatelli and the branzino. All of them tasted very good and the portions were also appropriate. It’s hard to find pasta dishes in New York under $30 that make you full these days. For dessert we got the olive oil cake which I personally think is overhyped. It tasted good but a bit dry and just not special enough to have everybody ordering it according to the pics.

Overall main dishes were excellent and felt like good value for money. I’d love to come back.

One of my favorite pasta places in NYC! I’ve historically tasted most of the pastas and all hit a perfect flavor! My favorite would be mushroom pasta. Super aromatic with truffle and cheese. Their burrata appetizer is also amazing!

We chose L’Artusi for brunch and it was a great experience. From the server walking us through several vegetarian items in the menu and explaining possible modifications, to the timeliness of the food coming out, and the delicious flavors, we felt taken care of and enjoyed our meal!

I would recommend the house focaccia (it comes with this delectable pepper olive oil with a kick) and the spaghetti dish (it has a parm base and feels refreshing/light). For a sweeter choice we liked the honey ricotta lemon pancakes, they were airy and not overpoweringly sweet.

google_reviews.text: I really like the concept of combining revolving sushi with bubble tea. My friends and I enjoyed the food. There was a lot of good selection of sashimi, rolls, and nigiri, and everything tasted pretty good. It was a fun and unique experience overall. The drinks were great too. For a soft opening, it wasn’t bad at all and staff were friendly

We stopped by for the last day of their soft opening. It was a snow day but the restaurant was still quite lively and filled. The restaurant was clean and spacious, and the staff were friendly and attentive. It's rare to find revolving sushi restaurants outside of Japan. The concept is always cool.

There was a good variety of sushi on the belt; my favorites were the salmon-topped shrimp tempura roll and the scallop nigiri. 3.95 a plate is very fair especially for things like scallop and special rolls. Everything tasted fresh and high quality. Since it was the soft opening, the ordering tablet was partially limited, but I assume the full menu will be available soon. They are still working out a few minor kinks, but the place has lots of potential!

The bubble tea was also a highlight. Even though the tea shop has a separate entrance, we could conveniently order from our table. They gave out samples of different drinks to try, I ended up ordering the mango yakult green tea; it had a nice, strong tea flavor and was delicious.

Highly recommend! I will definitely be back after the grand opening to see what else they have to offer.

I came here on New Year’s Day and can I say WOW! I love Japan so much that I travel to Japan every year and of course I need something in between the trips to satisfy my sushi craving and I can say this place is it! this place is spacious, clean and the variety of sushi on the belt is endless. I love being able to see what I’m getting rather than ordering from the menu like typical restaurants. i also got to try the grilled yellowtail neck, which I haven’t seen in other restaurant, the owner said they only serve one to two plates per day, I feel so lucky to be able to try it. it is very buttery and melt in your mouth, cant wait to eat it again next time. the rolls on the belt I see are 3 to 4 pieces per plate, which is great because I am not getting full from just one dish. you can also order your own food on the tablet as some items are more appropriate to be ordered as fried tempura or fried chicken. They also have bubble tea and cheesecake, I feel like I can stay here for hours to try every item! The price per plate from the belt is $3.95, which is a steal for sashimi like scallops, red clams, tuna, salmon belly and much more!!! Most restaurants charge $4 PER PIECE, so this is very reasonable price. I don’t understand why people give bad review about the price, obviously you haven’t been to a good sushi restaurant because you get what you pay for. someone also mentioned that the staff is not chatty, which I think it’s personal preference because I prefer where I don’t have to talk to the staff, I grab what I want, and I order what I want from the tablet, I do not want any interaction.

Honestly, not bad to have in the area. There's definitely room for improvement.  The plates on the belt should be labeled. As an experienced sushi eater, some pieces even I can't identify. name: Daesung Korean Noodle
document: Daesung Korean Noodle. cuisine: Korean Soup Noodles. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Atmosphere was clean, fast pace, but loud! Had to wait to be seated but Saturday lunch time is to be expected.  It was quick, 7 before me on the wait list for 2/3 people... only waited less than 15min before we were seated as well!  Service was spots on... A call button if needed but waitress was always around for anything.  Food wise ... Came very fast... Banchan were fresh kimchi (was amazing... Not overly spicy and still have a nice crunch.  Soy sauce marinated daikon... A bit sweet to me but mom loved it. Seafood pancake was soooo good with their hot soy sauce... Pack with squid, shrimp and the batter was so light!  Fishcake kalguksu spicy broth (level spicy)... To me had a nice kick but next time will definitely get extra spicy... Different type of fishcakes... Plenty to make you full and that's before the noodle... Lots of not too chewy noodle that blends well with the soup.  Beef bulgogi soft tofu stew (level spicy) also would get extra spicy for me but spicy had a nice kick also.  The beef bulgogi was so tender and sweet, tofu was nice and soft (and not overly soft were it would crumble when trying to spoon it), the raw egg added a touch of creaminess to the broth.  Stew came with 3 other banchan... Fishcakes, cucumber kimchi, beansprouts.  Also all were great and refillable.  Definitely will come back again and again!

Hearty noodle soup meals here. The tofu stew was a bit bland - probably because it's not their specialty however their seafood pancake was delicious. Very crispy. Recommend trying the pancakes. The service is quick and responsive. Food also came out very quick.

I love everything about this place! The noodle is top notch! It has a soft but chewy texture. The tofu is always so silky. The amount of ingredients they give is very generous. The staff is so sweet and attentive! They would ask if we want more side dishes. Highly recommended!
Hot chewy noodles were the best texture, not too salty or oily. Seafood pancake with just the right amount of crisp. Good barley tea to start. Service was very efficient and place was really clean.

Truly authentic Korean food!
The pajeon and kalguksu tasted exactly like what you’d find in Korea. The kimchi, made fresh every day, was honestly the best kimchi I’ve ever had. After our first visit, we ended up coming back three weeks in a row.

They even serve sujebi, which is hard to find these days. The owner mentioned that it requires a lot of labor, but he is committed to making it as long as there are customers who appreciate it. That level of craftsmanship and dedication was deeply moving.

As a multi-generational Korean restaurant, this place is truly rare, it has both a strong philosophy and outstanding flavors.

The staff were very friendly, everything was extremely clean and hygienic, and the portions were generous enough that we could enjoy the food again at home. Considering the quality, portions, and care that go into each dish, the prices were very reasonable, they could honestly charge more.

If we ever return to New York, this will be the very first place we visit.
Thanks to this restaurant, we had a wonderfully relaxing and healing vacation. Thank you!

document: Katabaru. cuisine: Japanese Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Very unique and delicious dishes! The anchovy potato was out of this world! The scallops were so fresh, as well as the sushi. The reason I have 4 stars for the food is because my husband wasn’t satisfy enough with the beef steak. Compared to other dishes, this one was quite average. It could have been just not to his taste, unfortunately I couldn’t try it bc I’m a pescatarian.

The cocktails were extremely yummy. If you love matcha, you must try the matcha low alcohol thing, I don’t usually order alcohol at a restaurant but this one seemed different. And I was right!

Beautiful space, perfect for dates and hang out. The bathroom was one of the best, I took pic of it 😅

A fun Japanese restaurant in east Billyburg 3 stops from L Montrose stop. Good happy hour selection, $drinks, $5 sapporo, $karaage till 7. Good ambiance, service a bit slow as they were packed, one of the entrees came out very late after others but was taken off the bill. Nanban chicken burger tender with crispy fries. Katsu and Una don both delicious and filling. Soft shell crab & squid apps came out nicely, not a big fan of the pork belly.

Katabaru was a great dinner spot. We enjoyed delicious cocktails, soft shell crab, gobu sticks, sushi, and flavorful rice bowls (pork cutlet and popcorn chicken ones) all capped off with sake. The space is cute and inviting, the food was consistently excellent, and the servers were very nice and quick. Would definitely recommend.

Burdock Root: This was prepared perfectly. It was a highlight of the meal—very good flavor and texture.
Chicken Karasge:  was impressively juicy on the inside while maintaining a great crisp on the outside.
Una-tama Don: Absolutely delicious. The balance of flavors here was spot on.

Where the meal lost its momentum was with the sides (pickled radish, seasoned vegetables, and miso soup). Calling the side "seasoned vegetables" felt a bit misleading. It was actually just hijiki (seaweed). While technically a vegetable in some contexts, it’s much more accurate to just list it as hijiki so diners know what to expect.
Miso Soup: This was the biggest disappointment. I am a huge fan of miso soup and I can’t remember a time I haven’t finished a bowl—until now. They seemed to use a dark miso, which is already quite bold,it tasted so bitter. After two sips, I had to stop.

Fresh, well-balanced, and absolutely delicious Japanese food at an incredibly reasonable price. Easily one of my favorite dining experiences in Brooklyn—better than many Michelin-rated spots in the city that cost far more. The unagi don, chicken, and pork belly were standouts, and the drinks and matcha tiramisu were just as impressive. No wait, fast service, and a cozy atmosphere made the whole experience even better.

document: Ler Lers. cuisine: Thai Noodles Salad. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
A new spot to go to in the hood located in beautiful Bed Stuy! We booked an early dinner here for Valentine’s Day via Resy. The restaurant is beautiful and has two entrances one for the main dining room and one for the bar. We were greeted and sat right away. However, as we were walking to the table the host reminded us that there was a 90 minute time limit for today’s reservation. I get it because of the lovers day holiday but dang he should’ve let me take my coat off first or at least order! 😂
The food was amazing and we even had dessert! My partner enjoyed her cocktail. She just wish it had less ice so she can enjoy the flavors of the Mezcal more. My Thai iced tea was perfect in all ways, I could’ve drank three of them! On the way out, I stopped at the bathroom and I’ll tell you this. They have to do something about the heating in there, as it felt like it was an outhouse. It was so cold in there. All that aside, we’ll
definitely be back with friends because those wolves can definitely accommodate large parties. Go here!

Stumbled upon this place and so glad that I did. It’s unique, authentic and absolutely delicious! I really enjoyed the crispy wings and crab fried rice with soft shell crab that I ordered for delivery. The soft shell crab was a nice touch. I’ll definitely be ordering again and highly recommend.

I am so so happy with the food and service here. Came here last minute for valentines days with my husband. I was doing the happy dance the entire time. IMPECCABLE!! VIBE, FOOD EVERYTHING! Will be back! (Everything was delicious but the corn salad made my mouth water!!)

So happy to have a delicious Thai place nearby! I’m a big fan of this place, it’s a beautiful restaurant very well organized, always with a pretty stunning display of fresh cut flowers. The food features fresh ingredients, bold flavors, lots of herbs 10/10. The service has been consistently friendly and welcoming. And as an added bonus the lunch special is incredibly affordable and delicious. One of my favorite dishes is the Pla Rad Prik (whole fried fish) the technique they use to fry the fish results in an impeccable crispy but not oily flavorful fish with sauce that I readily drink up by the spoonful! Highly recomend.

Finally had dinner at Ler Lers! We didn’t have a res so waited about 45 mins, but for a Friday it wasn’t bad at all -  it was worth the wait.

The lychee style cocktail I got was perfect cause it wasn’t too sweet (and as an Asian iykyk).

Let’s talk food. We started with the chicken wings and tom kha soup. Wings were a flavor bomb of tang, garlic, and umam-iness from the fish sauce but most importantly it was crispy a f. The tom kha had a nice rounded out flavor. Som tum salad is a must.

Pad Kee Mao with beef is always a table favorite. It wasn’t spicy enough for me but the side of chili powder they gave, did the trick!

The Pak Boong Moo Krob is the pork belly over sauteed morning glory. This would’ve been in the top 3 but the pork was a bit cold, however the crisp on the skin was great!

To finish, we got the Thai coconut ice cream dessert and asked if we could add a scoop of the black sesame also :) they were nice enough to accommodate.

All in all, dinner was delicious. Vibes were intimate and cute. Service throughout, from the host to our server Alex, were 100. Thank you Ler Lers! We’ll be back

google_reviews.text: Calling all ice cream lovers, “this is a “ Must Go”place!”  If you love, love, great ice cream, friendly service, and a super atmosphere 🍨 you will love this place. You have three choices: 1. Uncle’s Ray’s specialty ice cream 2. Yogurt, Or 3. Soft serve 🍦. The owner “meet and greet” U as you enter the ice cream parlor. Wonderful experience. Family friendly.

I love the personable friendly staff and the ice cream & frozen yogurt is fantastic.
Such a pleasant surprise to the day!

Some friends and I went to Uncle Ray’s back in the summer and it was a great time! While most of us were still standing in line to order our ice cream, one of our buddies already ordered and was waiting in the other line for his ice cream. We noticed gentleman  with an apron came over to talk with him. After we ordered we came over to see what was going on and we quickly found it out was Dave, the son of the Uncle Ray. He quickly introduced himself to each of us and you could immediately tell that he had a very bright light about him and did his best to impact and let his light shine to all of us. We talked for the next few hours till closing time, and it was the best ice cream experience I’ve ever had. Beyond having great ice cream, amazing customer service, and several years of amazing community and relationships built, they also have a nice mini golf area that, if someone gets a hole-in-one at a specific hole, they could win anything from a free scoop of icecream to a giant sub from the nearest sub shop. I would definitely recommend going to Uncle Ray’s Dairyland, don’t leave before meeting Dave for a time you will never forget.

This is usually the only place we go to for ice cream but we’re done now. We’ve ordered the same sizes every time and they just get smaller and smaller. A medium cone now is the same size as a small and it certainly hasn’t gotten cheaper in fact it’s gotten more expensive. Not to mention the numerous times they’ve given us completely different flavors than what we’ve ordered in the bottom of the cones or cups. Very disappointing since we make a special trip to go here, not anymore they’ve lost us as customers.

Other people may complain about the cost or the portions but for me and my girlfriend's money they hit the ball out of the park every time. We went in there to order on a Saturday and ended up getting a long conversation with Dave about customer service. He was kind enough to take us in the back of the restaurant and show us how he ran the store and how much pride he took in customer service and product quality. Sadly, we have not had a chance to go back as my girlfriend spends much time taking care of her mother at assisted care but please be assured that we will be back when time permits.

We also got to see the full set up of their Kamayan table for a big birthday party (keeping this in mind for our own future plans).

Overall, we are excited to go back. Word has it brunch should be available soon (and some mahjong?!), and I can’t wait to bring my family here, especially with my sisters!

Thank you so much to the team for a wonderful experience especially during times of despair and uncertainties in our personal lives.

So happy we made reservations at the newest and hottest Filipino-Spanish restaurant in the city! The food was incredible and the vibes were top tier. Every dish was packed with flavor, comforting and nostalgic but elevated in the best way. You have to try the Lobster Palabok, Dinuguan Tacos, and Short Rib Kare Kare. The Pinya cocktail was a favorite too! The team was so warm and welcoming, and we even got to meet one of the owners. Loved our experience and can’t wait to come back!

An absolute gem - a traditional Philippine restaurant with a beautiful Spanish soul woven throughout the experience. From the moment we walked in, the ambiance set the tone: stunning, tasteful wallpaper, elegant light fixtures, and a warm, romantic glow that makes it perfect for a date night or special dinner.

The food was exceptional. The Dinuguan Tacos were truly to die for - rich, bold, and perfectly balanced with deep, comforting flavors. The Sizzling Short Rib, slow-braised in savory gravy with shiitake mushrooms and chives, was incredibly tender and packed with umami. Every bite was indulgent. And the garlic fried rice, absolutely amazing - fragrant, flavorful, and the perfect complement to the dishes.

The bartender elevated the entire experience by expertly pairing wines with our meal. Each recommendation enhanced the flavors beautifully and showed real knowledge and care.

Outstanding food, impeccable atmosphere, and thoughtful service. Highly recommend - we’ll definitely be back!

I've been always wanting to come here. I'm Filipino and I think it's rare to have an upscale Filipino restaurant in NYC. We came during new year very excited to try all the food. We got off 23st PATH and walk around 10 minutes. The space was smaller than I thought. Maybe cause I think Filipino restaurant are usually packed with large party? I was surprised none of the staff were Filipino. We ordered two cocktail, sisig, Kare kare, and dinuguan tacos. I love dinuguan so that was exciting. The food is on the pricier side (see receipt pic) Kare kare for $47 😭 I just came back from the Philippines and thought take me back lol the food was overall good. To be honest, I was expecting more considering the high price 🥹 it was nice but probably won't come back again. There was no spark 🙈 The staff was nice tho! Hope the restaurant can improve the food quality because I'm proud that there was an upscale Filipino restaurant in NYC.

name: Tessa
document: Tessa. cuisine: New American Bars Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Absolutely loved my experience at this restaurant! The grilled octopus was a standout dish—10/10 for sure! The flavors were incredible, and it was cooked to perfection. The fried cauliflower was  equally impressive, also a 10/10; they had the perfect crunch and flavor. The romesco salmon was spot on, beautifully balanced and delicious.

The ambiance was just what we needed for a chilly evening—gloomy and moody with candlelit tables that created a cozy atmosphere. Perfect for a date night or a special occasion!

And let’s not forget the drinks! The Grey Goose martinis were amazing—smooth and refreshing. Overall, a fantastic dining experience that I can't wait to repeat! Highly recommend!

Usually busy. I’ve sat at the bar mostly, a couple times at a table. I prefer the bar. Sal and the woman bartender are awesome! I like their cabs and the garden martini. The cauliflower app is so good. I love their bread rolls. The happy hour has food and drink specials. I’ve been many times, it’s a neighborhood favorite.

We had an early dinner here on a Saturday with a reservation, but there were plenty of open tables. The space has a cool ambiance but a bit on the darker side.

The service was mostly attentive throughout the meal, and the pacing between courses felt just right. Presentation across the board was excellent. Every dish came out looking like there was thought put into them. The standout for me was the cacio e pepe. Super rich flavor, and the foam layering the sauce on both sides was a nice touch.

We also had the octopus appetizer, which was really well-cooked and flavorful.

Prices are definitely on the higher side, but there’s clearly thought behind everything from the visuals to the taste.

The bathrooms are clean. There’s one upstairs and three downstairs.

Enjoyed the food and atmosphere. It does get really hard to hear even though there isn’t music blasting. The pork chop was good but I wish the eggplant rigatoni had more eggplant in it. I thought it only had tomatoes at first. I got the small plate which is good for a single serving, I think the large would be great for sharing.

For dessert we got the baked Alaska and it was delicious! Wish we had more room to try out the other desserts. Server was super nice and friendly.

Stepping into Tessa, you're immediately struck by the wonderful ambiance – The flavorful Meatball is an absolute must-try. If you are keen on healthier starter, I recommend “house dips” which come with 3  dips; garlic hummus, whipped ricotta, spinach-artichoke, with veggie sticks. And if you're looking for a satisfying main, don't miss the juicy and flavorful pork chop – cooked to perfection! You can tell the ingredients are fresh and carefully chosen, and the dishes are prepared with obvious care. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

name: Pho Thai
document: Pho Thai. cuisine: Vietnamese Thai. located in Queens. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Our new favorite spot in Warrenton! Easily the best pho in the area.  Very fast and friendly service with a relaxed atmosphere.  This will be a usual spot for us from now on. The owner told us the menu is smaller right now but will be expanding after they get settled in. Can't wait to try everything!

I’ve wanted a Pho restaurant in Warrenton since 2002. My brother in law is Vietnamese and made authentic Vietnamese Pho and other dishes since I was married 30 years ago and it was from scratch and delicious. My wife and I have tried many Vietnamese restaurants all throughout Northern Va and in DC including Eden Center in 7 Corners.

It’s a small corner restaurant behind Carousel with light furnishings and seats 26 people. Arrive early and expect a wait because they are currently light staffed and busy.

Today we started with Autumn Rolls which are similar to Summer Rolls but have warm crispy pork, fresh basil lettuce and noodles served with a sweet dish sauce for dipping. I will never go back to summer rolls! Delicious! We ordered two more orders to go!

For our main lunch entree we ordered Beef Pho and vermicelli with shrimp as well as a lychee boba and a mango smoothie with boba. The Pho is at least a 9/10, crushing Faangs Thai version and the Vermicelli was a little over cooked and needed a request for additional sauce but the shrimp rocked!

This will be a staple for us moving forward weekly!

Highly recommended!

Sorry the only pic I got was half way through the meal but this place is really close to a four star experience. The service was amazing, super friendly staff. The marinated beef skewers were also DELICIOUS. Everything else needs a bit of work before this can compete with places in Manassas or Centerville/Chantilly. The prices for the entrees are fair. If you live in Warrenton it's a good, local, convenient option but don't expect your mind to be blown if you've eaten lots of Vietnamese before.

I found the new pho restaurant, Pho le, in Warrenton's Waterloo Station
today. I had a small bowl of their beef pho with fresh bean sprouts, basil and hot pepper slices. It was all very good.
Trang (the owner?) and the other staff were very friendly and did a great job taking care of me. I will definitely go back there. Very satisfying.

It’s a new spot, they have some wrinkles to iron out, however, the food was well worth the extended wait. I had the beef pho and hubby had the chicken pho. Both bowls were amazing, broth was delicious. We also ordered their crispy spring rolls and Thai tea - delicious! Definitely recommend but again, new spot so be patient.

document: Old Sport Food. cuisine: Noodles Halal Uzbek. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: 1st of all. Halal menu and best thing is the noodle are freshly made. You will taste the freshness in every bite. Broth was super tasty. I liked the lamb burger. Overall taste and experience was really good. Worth the try.

As one of the earliest customers of this restaurant—and someone who has visited more than 20 times—I won’t be coming back, and I wouldn’t recommend it to others either.

Over the past year, prices have increased by more than 50% while portions have been significantly reduced. I clearly remember my first visit: my partner and I ordered Lanzhou noodles and the big plate braised chicken. The portion was so large that we couldn’t even finish the braised chicken and had to take the noodles home for another meal. At the time, the Lanzhou noodles were only $10.99, and with their free membership, you could get an additional 20% off. It was an amazing deal.

About a year later, after they opened two more locations in the city and brought in all their chefs, prices at this original location went up. Initially, I thought that was understandable—the discounted price was still reasonable, and the portions were fair.

However, my most recent visit was extremely disappointing. The food quality has dropped dramatically. There was barely any braised chicken or beef in the dish, and the chicken was even served cold. It’s embarrassing to see such a steep decline in quality in just over a year. It’s no surprise that fewer neighborhood customers are coming anymore, given the high prices and poor taste.

name: Bukas Cafe
document: Bukas Cafe. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Filipino Desserts. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
When I saw Bukas popped up on Instagram and saw how close it is to my home, I knew I had to try it with my boyfriend eventually. I waited a few weeks, maybe a month after opened to try it.

We lined up on around 10:30AM on a Sunday morning when there was already a line out the door. We had at least 10-12 people ahead of us. I believe we waited outside for at least 1/2 hour or so. When we finally got in and waited by the register, we waited another 10-15 minutes for an employee to tend to us and take our orders.

My boyfriend ordered the Champarado & I got the Ube Eclipse. I also picked up the last piece of Ube Flan. Both drinks were good, I truly enjoyed the Ube Eclipse, good flavor! The ube flan was amazing and one of the best I’ve had so far.

The decor is super cute and feels very homey. Overall, I think this is a true gem and a special addition to the neighborhood. I do wished there were more food options on their menu, maybe later down the lines. I’m not sure what I’d like to try but I can’t wait to see how busy it gets in the warm weather

Amazing little Filipino cafe in a residential area of Elmhurst; limited hours but amazing service and food and drinks! The adobo jalepeno melt has the perfect flavor from the original adobo dish and the melted cheese and toasted bread just makes for such a special sandwich. The Tultul salt adds a nice touch to the latte, and the Hey Jovy is such a perfect warm, comforting drink for the current weather. The pastries from Arellano are great, so happy they’re being sold here! Overall, a cafe I will be a regular at!

This is a Filipino cafe that serves drinks and foods that are all Filipino-flavor inspired! My partner and I ordered the two signature lattes: the ube latte and the bukas na latte. The latter comes with grated salt on the top, which the staff grates directly on for us, which was cool!

We tried the adobo chicken jalapeño sandwich, which is a hit here. I’m a big fan of adobo chicken, so this really hit the spot. The jus that comes on the side for dipping is so so good. It’s nice to know it’s a good spot for breakfast/coffee break or lunch!

The pastries selection is small but mighty here- everything is delicious and is also sourced from local Filipino bakers. This is a great add to the neighborhood and they really highlight Filipino cuisine and flavors!!

There’s ample seating indoors, most of the tables have 1-2 seats. While it wasn’t too crowded at 10am, by 11am it was filling up!

Be prepared for a line. Be prepared to chat with the people around you while you wait, snd be prepared for amazing customer service.

On top of that — limited-edition Filipino pastries and artisan coffee that are absolutely worth it.

This place was so good I got back in line just to grab a to-go container and try my third drink.
Some spots are worth the wait. This is definitely one of them.

PS: There’s a laundry spot next door for anyone who appreciates the art of multitasking —feed your self and do your chores all in one stop. 😄

Waited 25 min on a Saturday morning, which wasn't too bad! The staff is very friendly and everything was delicious.

They only had 2 paninis choices that day and the jalapeño one was not as spicy luckily!
I ordered a espresso drink by mistake but it was so smooth that I didn't mind it.
The flan with Uber dessert was also so fluffy and yummy. Would def come back, but maybe once the lines die down a bit more (since they've only been open for 1 month)

name: B2J Tasty Pot
document: B2J Tasty Pot. cuisine: Comfort Food Szechuan. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
There are so many places selling suancai fish (pickled mustard fish) in New York now, but B2J Tasty Pot in Bayside really stands out with its unique flavor. The soup is flavorful but not overly salty or heavy, and most importantly, it doesn’t leave you feeling extremely thirsty afterward, which I really appreciate.

If you order their combo meal, it comes with a variety of side dishes, and the selection is surprisingly generous. Even though the sides are included with the set, most of them are actually very tasty.

The Spiced Chicken with Chili Sauce was quite good, and the Fried Fish Skin was crispy and enjoyable. The Fried Milk Custard was soft and sweet. The Pickled Chicken Gizzard was tender and flavorful. The only two sides that could be improved a bit were the Crispy Fried Pork Belly, which felt slightly less impressive compared to the others, and the Fried Chicken Wings, which were a bit on the small side.

One more thing worth mentioning — their rice is surprisingly amazing. It’s honestly one of the few places where I actually felt the rice was good enough that I wanted to take some home. It pairs perfectly with the suancai fish.

✨ Also, the waitresses were extremely friendly and welcoming, and they all had bright smiles throughout our visit, which is something you don’t see very often these days. That made the whole dining experience even better.

Overall, this is a place I would definitely come back to, especially for their suancai fish, the great combo sides, and the excellent service.

Great food and generous portions. Not too oily, and the fish was very fresh and tender. The noodles were also excellent, chewy noodles with a clean, comforting broth. Everything tasted authentic. Will definitely come back.

Tomato broth bliss with beef and fish!!
We ordered the tomato soup base combo for two at B2J Tasty Pot—and it fed three of us easily! The portion was generous, with two sides and two rice included, making it a fantastic value. The tomato broth was rich and flavorful, and the combo of beef and fish was surprisingly perfect—hearty, fresh, and super satisfying. Every bite felt comforting and well-balanced. Definitely one of the best hot pot experiences we’ve had in a while. We’ll be back for sure!

This place hits all the marks! The Three-in-One noodles (get the extra wide!) are my perfect comfort food, and the Chinese Beef Burger is so good. Plus, the vibe is clean and modern, and the staff is genuinely friendly. A fantastic spot for a satisfying, no-fuss meal. Highly recommend!

This was our first visit here. We tried to come on a weekend but you need a reservation because it is not a very large restaurant and is busy,  which is good! One of the best meals my fiancé and I have had in a long time. The pizza was incredible and so was the eggplant and pasta we ordered. Everything came out piping hot and fast - excellent and attentive wait staff. Friendly service behind the bar welcomed us inside too. Can’t say enough good things about our dinner .. we left and texted family that they have to go try the food themselves. Think my mother is going tomorrow lol. Will be back soon!

WarrenPeace is one of my favorite hidden gems in Tribeca — a cozy, stylish cocktail bar and restaurant with a lively but intimate vibe that works for everything from date night to happy hour with friends. The decor feels warm and a little speakeasy-ish, which makes it really fun to hang out and sip drinks even before the food arrives.

The menu mixes Mediterranean-inspired small plates with standout dishes like duck confit, a juicy black & blue burger, and crispy duck-fat fries that are perfect for sharing. The cocktails are creative and well-crafted — I loved trying a few of the house signatures — and the service is friendly and attentive.

It can get pretty busy, especially on weekend evenings, so booking ahead is a good idea, but that buzz just adds to the energy. Overall, it’s a fun, memorable spot with great drinks, tasty food, and a vibe that keeps me going back.
Stopped by with some friends after karaoke for a night cap. Good snack, tasty cocktails and cool atmosphere to chill for a while.

We discovered this place by accident. We were looking to step outside the SoHo bubble and find our Tribeca third-space. And lo-and-behold… WarrenPeace. Everyone and every drink was unexpected. The duck fries snatch my soul and the Albanian Raki was a gem. I’d recommend this for intimate date nights - cutesty birthdays - and corporate dinners… and for the gentlemen, if you know you know….

Cool bar, good vibes, delicious drinks and friendly service. Great overall bar. Didnt try any of the food but it sounded good as well. There are some good happy hour prices...drinks are a little expensive in normal hours. Was pretty empty on a Tuesday but imagine it's busier on a weekend. Would definitely go back again.

google_reviews.text:
Came as a party of 7 on a Saturday night. It was packed, per usual. We made a reservation for 7pm and still had to wait ~35 min for an available table! We got seated at a large table upstairs. Everyone here gets individual pots, however if you're a party 6+, the extra folks are likely sharing a pot with someone.

We order our hotpot items off iPads + beverages are an additional charge. Servers are prompt and clear finished plates efficiently. Their dessert was a yummy mango jelly pudding. If it's someone's birthday, that person eats free, as long as there's a party of 4+. If there are 2 bday people, the party must be 8+.

Standard + reliable hotpot spot in the neighborhood that's always packed for a reason. Great AYCE price with plenty of standard hotpot options. Lots of neighborhood regulars!
We had the best time and the food was delicious. Service was fast and friendly. The servers are extremely attentive. They accommodated a last minute reservation. The decor inside is beautiful.

We really enjoyed our visit to this BBQ place. The atmosphere was great, and the food was excellent — we especially liked the way the grilling was done right in front of us, which made the experience even more interesting.

However, one thing we didn’t enjoy as much was being told there was a 2-hour limit for staying, and then being asked to leave, even though there were still plenty of free tables. That part felt a bit unnecessary and took away from the otherwise pleasant experience.
Had my b-day there. 8 people. Private room. All was good. Just wish there was waiter service for each table. Not like all food goes to 1 table and I have to redistribute it after myself

This was at the 86th St location and it was honestly the worst experience I’ve had.

Everything was fine at first, but then a server moved my belongings without saying anything. I had placed my things next to the connected booth table, and one of the servers just picked them up and moved them back to my seat without letting me know. Later, we noticed that one of the lamb meat platters looked greenish. We told them about it, and they just took it away with no apology. After that, no one checked on us or came back to take our order. The service the whole time was horrible.

Very disappointing experience. Please do better.

name: Sunday In Brooklyn
document: Sunday In Brooklyn. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
What a great spot!! We came here for a lovely dinner that most certainly did NOT disappoint!

Sunday in Brooklyn is a delightful little corner spot that seems small initially, but actually has plenty of seating throughout - including in an upstairs space.
Regardless, we were promptly seated (without a reservation) in a table downstairs, and had very friendly, hospitable service throughout our visit.

While dining, we ordered a few of the cocktails, and I found each one I tried to be a good amount of strength while also creative in the flavors and heat.
My personal favorite was the Ski Lift, which is a hot cocktail with bourbon, coffee, and other ingredients - soooo soothing, STRONG, and flavorful!

Now on to main event - the food!
My wood-fired lasagna was INCREDIBLE - so much flavor, texture, and uniqueness to each bite.
My partner's chicken pot pie was similarly unique and yet familiar in its excellent textures and taste!

Sunday in Brooklyn had a wonderful ambiance, lovely food, and great service - I highly recommend!

The service amazing. For 2 people they offered a 2 person table, outside or inside, they sat us right away. The food was Fast and tasted fresh. Eggs were done perfectly, soft scrambled, bacon crispy, potatoes were a little too salty, and the shakshuka was a little disappointing, like salsa with pouched eggs, but the bread was crisp and yummy when dipped into the bowl. However, the Sunday pancake was amazing. It’s was like a mini fluffy yellow cake with delicious buttered maple all over. not a maple taste but like a chocolaty buttery nutty flavor. “It was like a reward”. We enjoyed it the most. Overall we understand the hype and definitely recommend to try it for yourself.

Visited Sunday in Brooklyn for brunch and honestly, wow. We got the pistachio hummus with wood-fired flatbread — probably the richest, most flavorful meze I’ve ever had. A total must-try (and so generous we couldn’t even finish it!).

Also ordered the warm grain bowl, and it arrived in what felt like 5 minutes — unbelievably fast service. The bowl itself was pure comfort: warm, rich, and beautifully balanced. The eggs were cooked like a soufflé — soft and melting — topped with a gigantic half avocado and a generous handful of pepitas (which I love and rarely see done this well). The rice underneath was so delicious.

Finished with a cappuccino, served instantly in a lovely porcelain cup — the perfect touch to end brunch.

Our server was incredibly kind and attentive, checking in often to make sure everything was perfect. Honestly, one of the best brunch experiences we’ve had in

I've been to Sunday in Brooklyn several times for both brunch and dinner. Brunch certainly gets busy but its a fun time - make a reservation. The food, service and drinks are always lovely - Thomas the bartender is incredible!
I recommend trying the Sage Fright brunch cocktail, the Wood Roasted Half Chicken for dinner and the S'mores soft serve for dessert. The S'mores latte is fun too for all the s'mores fans.

The food was a bit hit-or-miss. The burger was good, but the fries were overly salty. I felt pretty indifferent about the pancake, and the French toast wasn’t great. Both the latte and coffee were served lukewarm, which was disappointing. That said, the service really stood out our party arrived late for our reservation, and the staff was very accommodating. Server was great. The inside was also nicely decorated for the holidays, creating a warm atmosphere.

Overall, I wouldn’t be reluctant to go back, but it wouldn’t be my first choice either.

I really wish we could give 1/2 stars. Food was more of a 3.5.

name: Peaches HotHouse
document: Peaches HotHouse. cuisine: Southern American Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Went with my sister and was exactly what I needed for a soul food fix. It does the job that it needs to do let me tell you. I got the mikes hot honey fried chicken sandwich the chicken was perfectly fried the bun was perfect the slaw on it was the right balance. We also ordered a side of greens, Mac and cheese, and grits. All side were exactly how they should be if you ask me, proper comfort in each bite

This is a review of Peaches Hot House take out. I ordered through Grubhub and the order was ready promptly. I am in the neighborhood so the food was still warm when eaten. Obviously the presentation of takeout isn’t going to be as pretty as dining in so I will not critique that. The flavors were definitely present and pleasant. I had the fried chicken sandwich and had crispy grits as a side.

The fried chicken was juicy with a crispy, hearty breading. This is not some “lightly fried” chicken and thank goodness because that’s how I like it. The standard chicken is seasoned well but I wanted it spicy so I paid a dollar extra for “very spicy.” I’m assuming the spice is provided by the salsa situation served on the side. In all honesty, it’s not that spicy so having a warning when ordering that it’s VERY SPICY is a bit dramatic. I wish it was spicer. Also the salsa/sauce is very runny and doesn’t feel like it makes sense with the sandwich. It looks and tastes like something that would be wicked good on some tacos but for a chicken sandwich is was a bit of a mismatch. Thankfully the sandwich is served with a spicy mayo that worked great with the meal and cole slaw that was ACTUALLY GOOD. The slaw was light and crisp with the perfect amount of tangy dressing. Unfortunately the bun was stale so that knocked my opinion down a bit.

The crispy grits I ordered as a side (a dollar extra) were great. I am not familiar with this variation of grits but I definitely would order them again. They are like hush puppies but soft and cheesy on the inside with a crisp exterior. Really great stuff.

If the meal was perfect I probably wouldn’t feel this way but with the stale bun and mismatched sauce I do think the price is steep. If I am paying $20 for a chicken sandwich meal, it should be a restaurants best work. If the meal can not be made consistently fresh and hot then it feels negative to pay premium prices for it.

I know the hothouse location is designed for more quick, simple meals compared to the other Peaches locations so I will be trying the other locations out and hopefully have a 5 star experience there.

I am giving grace as I presume they were busy due to the Juneteenth holiday/celebrations in the area. It was VERY packed—reminded me of a pack sardines. They had the a/c going but with the constant opening of the door and the amount of people inside the story didn’t really matter. We waited about 30-minutes after placing our name on the list. Wish they did reservations or a pay system; but I understand with the size of the place most people might not even bother. The food was mid lowkey just okay. I’ve heard lot of great things about Peaches in the NYC circuit as it pertains to food but as a table of 4 and everyone consensus being “it’s okay” don’t know if we’ll try again. For a soul food place I would say I expected better. However, I know Southern soul food and the east coast version of soul food don’t always translate. It’s like the transplants that not live in New York majority of the time it won’t work! I have one good note: the kale salad was delicious! It was fresh, had the best amounts of grated cheese and dressing just need more kale in my opinion since the salad name is named kale salad.

My recent visit to the restaurant was a mixed experience. While some dishes were enjoyable, others fell short of expectations, especially for a place that appears to specialize in soul food.

The fried chicken and cornbread stood out as the highlights of the meal—flavorful and well-prepared. The mac and cheese, however, was just average, lacking the rich, creamy depth that makes it memorable. The collard greens were particularly disappointing; they lacked seasoning and soul, and we ultimately left them uneaten. On a more positive note, the 1/2 & 1/2 tea (half sweet tea, half lemonade) was delicious and refreshing.

Service was standard but could have been more attentive. No one came by to check in on our table during the meal, which would have enhanced the overall experience.

Finding the restaurant initially proved difficult, as there was no visible signage outside—just red umbrellas with "Bacardi" printed on them, which offered no clear indication of the restaurant's identity.

Additionally, we noticed ants crawling on the table near the window, which raised concerns about cleanliness and maintenance.

Overall, while there were some enjoyable aspects to the meal, the restaurant has room for improvement in both its food offerings and customer service.

name: Celestine
document: Celestine. cuisine: Mediterranean Diners Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Absolutely amazing location for this restaurant.  Started off with the grilled octopus and burrata and was not disappointed.  For my main, I went with the ribeye with a side of brussel sprouts...both were delicious.   But, saved the best for last with a piece of Basque cheesecake with berry compote and chocolate sorbet.  The flavors and creaminess of that dessert was spectacular.   Great place to bring a date and walk around afterwards.

Pleasantly surprised how large the eggs were and runny for the arugula on the lox benedict. I got the orange wine and it was a very dark orange interestingly enough and had an after taste familiar to something but not my cup of tea. Beautiful view if the bridges in dumbo and very well lit area from all the wall to ceiling windows. The public can access outside the restaurant for a nice path to catch the view for photos.

We recently celebrated our anniversary here and have no words for the incredible team who took care of us. They accommodated us with a table that had a beautiful view and even surprised us with a complimentary wine to celebrate.

The food was 11/10. We ordered the mezze platter, Spanish octopus, and the short rib, and finished with the most delicious Basque cheesecake I have ever tried.

Thank you for making this day so special.

Very moody setting, excellent service, phenomenal food. I wont even speak about the breathtaking view. Husband and I ordered their Mezze platter, Miso caesar and pork chop. Everything was a hit. Beware the portions are generous so come with an appetite.

We went to Celestine to celebrate my brother’s birthday and it turned out to be a great choice in terms of food and location. The setting is stunning — right by the water with an amazing view of the Manhattan Bridge. It creates a beautiful and memorable backdrop, especially for a special occasion. The atmosphere is modern, airy, and cozy at the same time, which makes dining here feel unique and relaxing.

For the food, everything we ordered was excellent. From Eggs Norwegian, Chicken Breast, Branzino, Golden Beets, Miso Caesar, Burrata, Hamachi Crudo, Buttermilk Pancakes, and Fries, to the desserts like Chocolate Tart, Lemon Cake, Basque Cheesecake, and Salted Caramel Ice Cream — each dish was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully presented. The highlights for us were the seafood and desserts, which were prepared with great balance and taste.

The only weak point was the drinks, which looked nice but lacked flavor compared to the high standard of the food. Unfortunately, another downside was the service. While some staff were polite, the overall experience was disappointing. We were rushed off our table even though there were still plenty of empty tables around. On top of that, when we tried to move a chair slightly to take a photo, a staff member came over and told us, rather rudely, to put it back — something we already intended to do anyway. It felt unnecessary and left a bad impression, especially since we were celebrating a special occasion.

Overall, Celestine is a restaurant with an unbeatable location and delicious food, but the service could be improved to match the quality of the kitchen. The setting and dishes make it worth a visit, but I hope the staff can be more considerate to ensure that guests leave with a truly positive experience.

document: The Horny Ram. cuisine: New American Bars Venues & Event Spaces. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This past weekend I went on a girls trip to NYC for my and my friend’s birthdays. We went to The Horny Ram and it was such a great vibe!

I loved the industrial and wood looks and tasteful style.

We had the bottomless brunch and I had the m&m pancakes. Those hotcakes were slapping and our server Ashley was top-tier. I never saw the bottom of my glass, and when she found out that it was our birthdays we had an entire spotlight song and cheers and special complimentary “mini beer” shots that were incredibly cute and tasty.

We had an amazing time and Ashley was so warm and friendly and really made our day unforgettable.

100% would do this again. Thanks Horny Ram and Ashley!

We made reservations for Valentine morning. An hour prior to leaving for this reservation we received a text message confirming that we are coming. We get to the restaurant and there’s a sign saying that there was a water outage, but they never communicated that with the customers as there was other people waiting outside reading the same poster. Everyone wasn’t sure if we could leave because we would get charged a $25 fee per person.

There was no communication. There were servers inside. However, instead of communicating to us that there would be a late opening. They just stared and didn’t want to open the door when we wanted to ask what would happen next or if they would be open for the day.

After 20 minutes of waiting with no answers, the manager finally went in and let us know that they would probably be opening in like five minutes. It really turned out to be another 15 minutes. We didn’t get in there until around 11:40.

We decided to still give it a try because we were excited about trying the restaurant however it probably wasn’t the best sanitary decision and that was our fault.

We ordered the croissant sandwich, it was okay. We also had the waffle sandwich. We ordered one of their cold brew coffee however we didn’t finish it because it tasted off. Instead, we decided to just order mimosas which were good. We did their bottomless mimosas deal.

It was not worth the price. We also didn’t get any discount or apologies from the restaurant, not disclosing that they were having a water outage at all. We found that very displeasing and unprofessional because they didn’t let us know about the issue and on top of that they didn’t offer anything complementary, given the issue at hand.

Best Brunch NYC! Have always wanted to try this spot in the neighborhood and finally had a chance to try their brunch. Their pancake burger was amazing. The burger is done so well and the pancake with syrup compliments the flavor so well. The group I went with also tried a few other items on the menu and they were all great! Highly recommend!

This place was nice. 1st time visiting and I have to say the food was deeeelicious. Great staff with great manners & customer service. I will be going back again. I had the double smash burger with those amazing fries /buffalo style wings & pretty in pink tequila drink. 🙌🏽

Had a great experience here. First time going. The person who took our order (I wanna say his name was Salvador) was extraordinarily amazing. We called my mean the “kids meal with the pink lemonade” aka the bottomless pink pony drink. Everyone was super friendly and welcoming. Definitely taking some friends back here and asking for him!

name: Cachapas Brooklyn
document: Cachapas Brooklyn. cuisine: Venezuelan. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
A random showing on my Instagram algorithm tipped me to this place and I have been curious about Venezuelan and Colombian cuisine so I made the trip to this location.

Off the bat, the exterior seems kinda plain but the inside the area is themed just like how it would be coming into a brick and mortar South American restaurant. Latin music, treats and snacks from their country. Service was swift, steady and courteous as it took no longer than 5 minutes for my food to reach my table.

My lunch for the day was the Grilled Chicken Pabellon Lunch Special, Chicken Empanada, Tequequava and Tamarind juice. When the pabellon got to my table I thought it was a little on the small side but it was surprisingly filling. The Grilled chicken, a bit on the salty side still had taste to it and it was a good mix to go with the rice and beans. I loved the texture of the Empanada I had and the Tequequava (Cheeze & Guava stick) was actually superb. Never thought Mozzarella cheese could mix well with Guava fruit, but it was a solid blend. The Tamarind juice was sweet and savory. That was quite a meal I've ordered yet came just under $30 so everything was reasonably priced.

The place is on a seemingly sketchy area of Cypress Hills but it's worth a second visit because the food is good and the menu has a bevy of choices there.

I wanted to try something new and decided to go with this Venezuelan restaurant. First and foremost, I ordered delivery. I thoroughly enjoyed that they delivered it themselves, as opposed to a third party service. Secondly, I ordered two days in a row back to back.

In total with both days combined, I ordered Shredded Beef Pabellon, a 9" Venezuelan Grilled Steak Sandwhich, a Dominican Chicken Empanada, a Dominican Beef Empanada, a YOYO sweet plantain sandwich with shredded beef, a sweet plantain sandwich with shredded chicken, and a tequeguava. I really wanted to immerse myself in the items they sold and the different flavors.

The Shredded Beef Pabellon 🍚came with white rice, black beans, shredded beef, and 3 sweet plantains - every bite a delight 10/10
Dominican Chicken Empanada was very flavourful and juicy. 🥐 Most chicken empanadas I've tried are usually dry 8/10 and not because it was lacking anything, just because of my own tastebuds.
Dominican Beef Empanada 🥐if you like olives 🫒 you will love this. It is very flavorful and well seasoned.
Sweet plantain 🍌 with shredded beef and the chicken sandwich 9/10 it was really good. I had to eat it with a spoon because the mix of the condiments with the lettuce and tomato had it falling apart, but that was not an issue!
9" Venezuelan 🇻🇪 Steak Sandwhich was amazing! Every bite packed a punch 11/10
Tequeguave- 11/10 i adored this. The flavor profile was delightful. The guava, fried cheese, and fried dough fully complimented one another.

This is definitely a place my family and I will continue to order from.

We live far from here but was nearby and wanted to experience some good neighborhood food.   You get a very decent portion of food for the price you pay.  We ordered the lunch special pabellon carne mechada with beef.  I took off a star bc the rice was slightly undercooked and it was bland... Maybe that was how it's supposed to taste?  The platter was full with some plantains, black beans, and beef for $13.75.  The burger was salty but delicious with bacon, beef patty, roast pork, cheese, lettuce and super crunchy potato sticks.  Definitely a good choice.  Also tried the tequeyoyo.  I liked that a lot too.  It was a stick like dough with ham and cheese inside.  The passion fruit drink was very tasty too. As more and more customers entered we noticed almost everyone buying empanadas to eat.  That definitely creates a FOMO moment for us ... So we ordered some for dinner.  The service was impeccable with the owner/worker giving us extra garlic/green sauce- that was so yummy. It was super clean inside.  They accepted cash and cc though with a 4% charge.  If I lived close by I would definitely come by again to try their other selections.  Thank you for a wonderful introduction to Venezuelen food!
Honestly feel tricked. Our personal favorite Venezuelan spot wasn’t available so we thought to give this place a try and never again.

The food was flavorful and well‑prepared, with plenty of options that feel fresh and authentic. Service was excellent—friendly, quick, and attentive throughout the visit. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it a comfortable spot to enjoy a meal. Overall, a satisfying experience with great service and solid food.

document: The Monkey King. cuisine: Chinese Asian Fusion Bangladeshi. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Asian-fusion restaurant in the Bushwick neighborhood of Brooklyn, NY. They are a blend between Chinese and Bengali influences. Came here for a pre-show dinner.

For starters, we ordered the scallion pancakes and the chicken dumplings. We also ordered a side of Szechuan marinated cucumbers. All the small plates were fantastic - we particularly enjoyed the scallion pancakes which came with a very nice dipping sauce.

For mains, we ordered the cumin lamb ribs, double garlic eggplant, and a side of crab fried rice. I have never had a lamb dish cooked so well and seasoned perfectly. The double garlic eggplant was also delicious and the sauce that it was in was perfect for dipping pieces of lamb as well as the fried rice. The crab fried rice was awesome, the crab meat was perfectly blended in so you weren’t eating a big chunks of crab.

This has definitely been one of the best Asian fusion restaurants I have been to.

Overall: 9/10

First time being at this restaurant, and it was incredible. The staff was super attentive and nice. The vibes were very chill but comfortable. Their drinks and cocktails were from a select menu, and you can tell everything was curated. All the food was seasoned and cooked to perfection; the peking duck was the crown jewel and a must-have, but the roasted duck-fat fried rice came in a close second. We were celebrating our anniversary, and they made it extra special. This is a high recommend, and we will be back!

Took my daughter here for dinner. Very nice ambiance however the seating area was very tight where other ppl butt was touching me. The food was ok the shrimp pancake thingy was tasty we ordered 2 the crab rice was on the dryer side and as well as the ribs. The drinks was way too pricey to be filled with so much ice. Two sip and it finished no exaggeration. Tasty just too much ice.

We came here to celebrate my friend’s birthday and it turned out to be such a lovely experience. The food was flavorful and beautifully presented-every dish had that perfect Asian-fusion balance of comfort and creativity.

The ambiance is where this place really shines. The lighting is warm and moody, giving it that intimate, modern-lounge feel without being too dark. The brick accent wall, emerald-green booths, and gold fixtures make the space feel cozy yet upscale-perfect for date nights or small gatherings.

Our waiter Jonathan was excellent, attentive, kind, and made us feel welcome from the moment we sat down. Service really can make or break a dining experience, and he nailed it.

My only wish is that the cocktail list was a bit more extensive, because the drink I had was okay, and I would’ve loved to explore more options. The wine list was impressive I’ll admit, but I wasn’t in the mood for wine lol

Overall, it was a beautiful night-great food, beautiful setting, and wonderful company. I’ll definitely be back!

Service here is amazing! Thank you Manasi! Very friendly and attentive. Ambiance is beautiful.

We tried many dishes from the menu and almost everything was truly a 10/10; very flavorful. We got Char Siu, Tea Smoked BBQ Ribs, Crispy Garlic Fried Chicken, and Roasted Duck-Fat Fried Rice. The Crabcake Shumai was a disappointment, 5/10. Drinks were okay, tasty and not strong.

For all these dishes and two drinks, party of two, the bill came out to $190.
