name: L&B Spumoni Gardens
document: L&B Spumoni Gardens. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
L&B Spumoni Gardens is a true New York institution and a must-visit spot in Brooklyn. From the moment you arrive, you feel that old-school, authentic neighborhood vibe that makes the place so special.

The square Sicilian pizza is legendary. The thick, airy crust is perfectly baked, the tomato sauce is rich and slightly sweet, and the cheese sits beautifully underneath the sauce — a unique and delicious twist that makes it stand out from any other slice in NYC. Every bite is comforting and full of flavor.

And of course, you can’t leave without trying their famous spumoni. Creamy, colorful, and refreshing, it’s the perfect way to end your meal. It adds that nostalgic Italian-American touch that defines the place.

The outdoor seating area creates a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. It’s lively, casual, and feels like a true Brooklyn gathering spot. Despite being popular, the service remains efficient and well organized.

If you want authentic, classic New York pizza with history and personality, L&B Spumoni Gardens is non-negotiable. Iconic, flavorful, and unforgettable. Highly recommended

Classic Brooklyn vibes! Came here Sunday around 7:30 PM. It was packed, but we were seated in just 15 mins! Very family-oriented and lively.

Pro-tip: Don't even bother with the parking lot; go for street parking.

Must-orders:
• Sicilian Pizza (The best!)
• Baked calms & Shrimp Cocktai
• Chicken Bolognese

Not a fan of
• potato croquettes
• chicken Parmigiana

Overall experience was great, will come back again!

As a man who grew up in Coney Island and Brooklyn boy, this place brings you back to the old school Italian deli feel.

The food tastes like the heroes you get from the best pizzerias and they obviously focus on the sauce the way it's intended like real Italians would.

I only had the tomato Sicilian with vodka sauce, meatball hero with fresh mozzarella, and shared a chicken parm with vodka sauce. Each bite was delicious and the service was great despite being busy.

On the way out, the guy remembered my name and asked how was the food. I said, it was amazing and it definitely was. Come try this place out. There is also pasta as well.

Parking is a bit crazy and people were double parked down the block, waiting to get in. You must try it if in the area!!

Sorry as i didn't get the usual photos I typically don't when trying places out but trust me, it's good. They also have this ice cream boat that people order for special occasions. It's a mix between pistachio, chocolate, and creamoso ice creams with cones and piled high. You can find pictures of it in other reviews.

Great space, and even in the garden space — it was toasty warm on a frigid day. Great service and vibe. Plenty of people and clearly super popular.

Ok - to the point: the pizza was really good! The 6 of us got a 12 slice rectangular pie, and it was crispy where it was supposed to be and the sauce was fresh and just so good. Recommend.

Wonderful doesn't come close. We were a party of 10 including 3 kids, and we couldn't have had a more perfect afternoon. The food!! Yes of course the pizza but everything we ate was delicious -- mozzarella tomato salad, calamari, baked clams (to die for), soft and delicious chicken parm, the eggplant Sicilian ziti, the spaghetti marinara... Great inexpensive house chianti. And of course an incredible dessert platter. Thanks to the entire team - we will definitely be back!

name: Di An Di
document: Di An Di. cuisine: Vietnamese Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Spectacular dinner.

Very authentic and much more to the menu than just Pho.

We ordered the sizzling fish for two, and it was perfect. The very fresh tasting fish and herbs complimented each other very well. Also a fun experience of putting the ingredients together and eating it in your own bowl.

The rice cake omelette was also amazing. A little small, but amazing texture.

Really average food with extremely small portion for upscale prices. Realistically the only thing upscale about this place are the prices.

3 pieces of spring roll is a joke and tastes the same as most authentic pho places in the city.

Grilled pork was too burnt and bit flavorless. Pho had not much flavor with few slices of overcooked beef. The only thing good / special was papaya salad had a crispy thing on the side.

Suggested tip was on top of taxes too.

I visited Di an Di on a Saturday afternoon for lunch after hearing many great recommendations, and it absolutely lived up to the hype. The food was excellent and a great value. We started with the spring rolls, which were fresh and flavorful, then shared the fish for two—truly outstanding. We also ordered the papaya salad, which I highly recommend; it was crunchy and refreshing without the overwhelming spice you often find in Thai versions.

The atmosphere was pleasant and inviting, with plenty of seating and a few high tables. We arrived without a reservation and were seated right away. Overall, it was a wonderful lunch experience, and I’ll definitely be back.

Great service, decent atmosphere, but yeah.. if you're viet you know how I feel.

name: Ajo y Oregano
document: Ajo y Oregano. cuisine: Dominican. located in Bronx. with 3.5 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Real, honest review from a first-time customer.

I stay in NJ but was in the area and decided to try this place on a friend’s recommendation. We ordered takeout — 4 items — and with tip the total came to about $100.

What we ordered:
•	Shrimp Mofongo – $24 (10/10)
•	Shrimp in Garlic Sauce w/ Tostones – $26 (5/10)
•	Chicharrón de Pollo w/ Rice & Beans – $24 (5/10)
•	Tres Leches – $9 (?/10… more on that below)

We waited about 45 minutes for the food. The bag was stapled shut, so we left assuming everything was inside. My gut actually told me to check before leaving… I should’ve listened.

When we got home, the Tres Leches cake was missing. On top of that, the Chicharrón de Pollo looked exactly like chicken tenders. I immediately called the restaurant to let them know they forgot the cake and that the chicken didn’t look like traditional chicharrón. I was told that’s “how they make it” and that I could come back anytime to pick up the Tres Leches.

Here’s the issue… I stay in NJ. Going back means paying another $16 toll to cross the George Washington Bridge just to pick up a $9 cake that was forgotten. That part was frustrating.

Food breakdown:
•	The Mofongo was amazing. Honestly 10/10. Perfect flavor, perfectly cooked. If they only served mofongo and called themselves “Mofongo House,” they’d probably crush it.
•	The Shrimp in Garlic Sauce lacked flavor. I had to add quite a bit of salt to bring it to life.
•	The Chicharrón de Pollo — while it tasted flavorful — was essentially a chicken tender. So yes, it was seasoned well for what it was, but it wasn’t what I expected when ordering chicharrón de pollo.
•	The Rice & Beans were delicious and very flavorful.
•	The Tostones were fine.
•	The Tres Leches… well, I can’t rate it because I never got it.

Overall, this place is Overpriced but the mofongo is worth trying. The missing item and the response to it, along with the chicken tenders pretending to be Chicharron de Pollo left a bad taste in my mouth. I’ll probably only come back if I’m already in the area — for the Tres Leches I paid for… and maybe for a mofongo.

Pro tip: skip the Chicken Tenders .. I mean Chicharrón de Pollo. And check your take out order before leaving.
I really love this spot. The staff is pleasant and easy to deal with. They also have very large portions.  They are just a bit slow depending on the time a day!

The atmosphere was okay nothing bad, nothing that really stood out.
The food was also just okay. It wasn’t terrible, but it wasn’t memorable either.

Where the experience really fell apart was the service. Our waiter barely checked on us. We weren’t asked how the food was, if we needed water refills, another drink, or even if we wanted dessert. After finishing our meal, we waited an unreasonably long time just to get the check, which was frustrating and unnecessary.

Overall, it’s a place with potential, but the lack of attentive service seriously hurts the experience. Service matters, and unfortunately, it missed the mark here.
Had a great time! The servers were very welcoming and attentive. The food was absolutely delicious, and the presentation of the mofongo was beautiful. We’ll definitely be coming back!

I quite enjoyed eating here. Especially the mofongo de chicharron de cerdo. Also got the churrasco and the chimi tostones. Wish the meat on the chimi tostones was a little bit thinner but still good. The atmosphere was great, I felt like family members were asking me how everything was etc.

document: Yia Yia's Taverna. cuisine: Greek. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Great food and great service! We stopped in for dinner and had such a nice time, everyone was so kind and the food came to the table quick. The Spanakopita was probably my favorite, but the lamb was also cooked perfectly. We will be back!

For 5 years now, I’ve willingly have traveled over an hour to dine at Yia Yia’s and it still remains as the best Greek culinary experience in all of NYC. As someone who travels back and forth to Greece, I know my Greek food and this is one of the best there is. Not only is the food amazing, the service here is unlike anything you’ll experience elsewhere. The warm and caring hospitality from the owners and staff is truly exceptional, making every visit feel like home. From the perfectly grilled octopus to the hearty chicken souvlaki platter and the comforting moussaka, each dish is fantastic. This place is one of my favorite eateries in all of NYC because they have it all - food, drink and service, which keeps me coming back, again and again. Trust me, make the trip. You won't regret it.

Must try: Home Made Sangria, Grilled Octopus, Afelia, Chicken Souvlaki Platter, Moussaka

We stopped in for a quick dinner - first time for all 5 of us and we were NOT disappointed! Everything was amazing! Grilled octopus was so delicious!! Service was also great! Highly recommend and will definitely be returning!

google_reviews.text: Went for a lunch hang out and I loved it. I can’t wait to go back. Service was attentive but also we didn’t feel rushed. I got Brooklyn sushi combo and it was delicious cuts. I can’t wait to go back

I usually order takeout from this establishment; however, yesterday's pleasant weather prompted a change of plans.  The restaurant, while compact, offers comfortable dining and bar seating.  The menu is extensive, featuring a diverse selection of dishes, including sushi and soups. I enjoyed my dining experience and will certainly return.

Ordered delivery and decided to go with the new menu item Bul Go Gi fried rice. It took a while for us to get our good so I thought that's good made to order. Once it arrived it look horrible. Immediately I thought of day old reheated beef and rice. That was all that was in the dish. Old fried rice and beef with an egg on top. No carrots, scallions, peppers, chicken, shrimp or sesame as the description states. We tried to power through eating it but after reheating again it was inedible. Customers who order delivery and take out trust that they will get quality food that they pay for upfront. We have eaten from here at the restaurant in the past once but unfortunately this experience was so bad we will not order from here again.

I’ve been to Slow Loris a few times before writing this review, and overall, I’d give it three stars. The food is decent but uneven. The bibimbap is pretty good, fresh and well-balanced, but nothing exceptional. The miso soup, however, is horrible. It always tastes metallic, like metal leached into it, and is quite diluted, lacking the depth and richness you’d expect. It could be over-boiled or the result of bad/toxic cookware.

Flavors overall are average; not bad, but not amazing either. Another issue is the wait time. Service is friendly but consistently slow, and both seating and food take longer than they should. Maybe that’s part of the branding with “Slow” in their name, after all. Slow Loris has a few strong dishes but needs improvement in both execution and service to reach its full potential.

After getting my hair did, I traypsed over to Win Son. It was brick out so the only remedy would be hot cup of tea! I also wanted something to fill me up, so I ordered their signature double patty Smash Burger. I like that their sandwiches are paired with a hefty salad. The mixed greens are a nice edition to the cheesy, rich Burger. I especially like the citrus dressing on the mixed greens. It's always a vibe when I have a meal here. Folks are sitting by the bar ordering cocktails, others are with family or friends for a quick bite and relaxed conversation. The music is nice and this time the Christmas tree was still displayed and it gave a really great indoor/outdoor ambiance to the icy patches along Graham Avenue...Nice!

That made me uncomfortable but also, not a deal breaker.

The martini was delicious 😋. The buffalo wings were not 🚫 good. The Tres leches cake 🍰 was tasty but no coffee was available at 11pm, bummer.

There was a person named Marquis, I hope that's how you spell the name, who was an amazing spirit. I summoned them for extra plates (they quickly attended to me), they checked on me and my friend several times and when I got up to go to the bar to pay, they offered to assist and was just absolutely and completely the height of my night ( great energy and conversation) I can tell they work really hard, as I saw them doing a little bit of everything besides cook.

We were told to sit anywhere we wanted, given menus and then we just sat there. Eventually after waiting for about 15min or more I decided to go to the counter and ask if we had to wait for a waiter to order and that is when I was told that I had to order at the counter. Apparently, according to the staff she had informed us at arrival but neither myself or my wife heard it. I was asked to leave my credit card if wanted to keep the bill open which made me feel extremely uncomfortable considering I thought I was going to a restaurant and sitting at a table and not at the bar. The coffee arrived and it was fantastic, but I almost cut my lip on the cracked cup they served me. In short. I won’t be coming back, but do think the place is beautiful, food is good and reasonably priced so it got potential. The tall short hair bartender was actually super nice and came to check on us afterwards which was nice.

Edie Jo's has such a cute vibe!  They do not take accept reservations and it appears they get busy in Saturday afternoons.

The staff (bartenders, wait staff and everyone else) was so friendly.   A bit more attention to detail would be great (there were a few drinks mixups and forgotten biscuits).  I imagine mistakes happen often since you place your order at the bar and it is brought to your table.   You present your credit card to open a tab.

My niece and I arrived just after 11 AM on the last Saturday in March.   It was not very crowded at that time.  We sat at a booth inside, but did see some people dining outside.

I can personally recommend the French toast and the EJ rum punch (please note... this is NOT Jamaican rum punch...  but it's delicious).

My niece enjoyed her chicken sandwich with fries.  She also highly recommends the Moscow mule.

With tax and tip, we paid approximately $135.

Bathrooms were fine.

Even at 11 PM, everything was fresh, and the place was buzzing with energy. I wasn’t surprised—it had been on my oldest’s list for a while now. He remembered eating here as a youngster. We came as a family of five, and it exceeded all expectations.

The variety was incredible—fragrant rice, tender braised meat, perfectly fried whole fish, and an array of chicken dishes, each more flavorful than the last. Every bite was absolutely mouthwatering. The boys were so impressed that they insisted on packing extra for lunch the next day!

On the car ride home, the conversation was unanimous: it’s not about the decor or ambiance—it’s the food that truly matters. And Hadja Marley delivers on all fronts. We’re already counting down the days until we can go back!

We brought many people, but the restaurant seated us quickly and served us attentively. I shared this dish with my friend. The proprietor and workers make guests feel welcome. Servers make you feel special and the meals are too. This spot calls for your prompt attention!

I feel like I have to go there bc they have a particular meat i like that nearby african restaurants don't have. The problem is the service is HORRIBLE. Every time I go, there's always some silliness with their prices. Basically, they have different prices for Guinea and Senegalese people vs the rest. Today, the cashier charged me $8 for less than a pound, but charged some man $4.10 for DOUBLE THE FOOD I HAD. She and the man tried to gaslight and get an attitude with me when I mentioned the discrepancy. But trust,  wasnt having it.  Always nonsense with them, i tell you. Not a good look when there's so many competing restaurants like right next door. Don't think I'll be returning. I'll wait until I can make the meat myself.

This place was truly enjoyable. The inside setup of this place caught me off guard. The cooking satisfied while service excelled. Restaurant workers notice when assistance is needed. This place has an exceptional nature.

So I called in to inquire about a specific african dish and the people who answered the phone were so rude. I was going try this restaurant for the first time, I quickly changed my mind. Remember without  customers you will have no business. It cost nothing to be polite

name: La Chacra
document: La Chacra. cuisine: Peruvian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
If you're craving bold, authentic Peruvian flavors in Brooklyn, this place is an absolute must. We came around golden hour and were lucky enough to grab a table outdoors - the patio seating was super cozy and gave us the perfect view of the sunset while we ate.
We ordered the rotisserie chicken and it was insanely juicy and flavorful -- perfectly seasoned with that crispy skin you dream about. The lomo saltado was tender and full of that rich, savory stir-fry flavor you'd expect. For sides, we had both the yuca fries and regular fries --honestly couldn't pick a favorite. The yuca fries were crispy on the outside and soft inside, and the papas fritas were classic perfection.
The cocktails were another standout -- super refreshing with unique flavor combos (and you can feel them, too).
Definitely not watered down.
Service was amazing also!

A cute little gem, looks like unassuming and gives kind of of hole in the wall vibes, but it was nothing short of spectacular!! Went with a bunch of friends so we were able to try a variety of options. I am a steak person and the skirt steak to me was SOOO good. It was perfectly cooked for me (I'm a medium rare girl) and it was PERFECT!! Everything was seasoned well and the green sauce. The green sauce needs its own review. I would get the skirt steak and the octopus dish again. The ceviche was also good and the meal sticks were also cooked to perfection in my opinion. Super tender 👌 😍 ❤️

Really great neighborhood spot.   The service is excellent and the food is really delicious.   We especially love the ceviche, chicken empanadas, and rotisserie chicken.    All that and very reasonably priced.   Definitely worth checking them out.

Food is great, but you have got to work on that customer service. Stood there at your "please wait to be seated" front door, only experience a silent treatment and no recognition. No hello. No welcome. No acknowledgment at all. I waited there for like 10 minutes just and letting me stand there. The waiters at the back seem free too, just watching me wait no acknowledgment. Bartender just stood there watching me. I get it. Maybe it's because I ordered pickup, but really, are you going to just like pretend I don't exist for like a 10 whole minutes and just ignore me.

Came here twice and I like their drinks and ambience but the chicken is a bit dry. Hard to find parking but not a bad service. I like their tostones and green sauce, lomo saltado has flavor but missing a piece of something.

Loved the chicken empanadas w chicken. Cool bathroom.

name: Wheated
document: Wheated. cuisine: Pizza Cocktail Bars Whiskey Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Wheated probably takes the crown for some of the best specialty pizzas in Brooklyn. We absolutely loved our dinner here. The space has a fast, lively energy that makes it feel like you’re in on a neighborhood favorite, and the food completely lives up to the buzz.

One of the coolest touches is that every pizza is named after a Brooklyn neighborhood, which makes the menu fun to explore. I ordered the Flatbush and it honestly surprised me in the best way. I had never tried eggplant on pizza before, but it worked incredibly well. It added a rich, savory depth without feeling heavy, and the crust had that perfect balance of chewy and crisp.

The cocktails were also a pleasant surprise. It’s not always expected at a pizza spot, but they were thoughtfully made and paired perfectly with the meal.

Everything about Wheated just clicked, from the energy of the room to the quality of the food. This is the kind of place you leave already planning what you’ll order next time. I cannot wait to come back. 🍕🔥

Definitely one of the TOP Pie spots in Brooklyn!

Love the aesthetics! The bathroom door blending into the wall is cool! I don’t remember that last time I was here to dine-in but that was a while ago. I’ve done both take-out & dine-in here.

There were a couple tables available but they do fill up fast! I found a seat by the bar right away!
I ordered a drink while I waited I don’t remember the name but it was good.

The Pizza came after like 15min or so it wasn’t a long wait.  I was really happy with its presentation, flavor & texture etc…

The cheese was perfectly melted, the crust was crispy & sauce was great!  They definitely didn’t disappoint & piled high the toppings for the supreme part of the pie. I would definitely get the supreme again though next time I wanna try a white pie maybe the New Haven rosemary potato pie sounds good as a next try.  I would also highly recommend the Flatbush for all the Eggplant lovers out there!

The service was good, the staff was attentive to my needs & were friendly.

First Impressions & Vibe:

We popped in on a Saturday with no reservation and were seated within 10 minutes. The place was busy, or “bumping,” as you said. The atmosphere is cool, casual, lively, neighborhood pizza spot energy.

⸻

🥗 Salad + Starters

We tried the Tuscan Kale salad. The cheese was nice and nutty, and the walnuts added a good texture. But the dressing was too acidic — the moment you bite in, the tang hits first and lingers. It overpowered the greens instead of complementing them.

⸻

🍕 Pizza & Side

We went with a classic New York style pie, 12-inch split between two people. Served correctly, satisfying size — we didn’t leave hungry. It’s the kind of pizza you expect from a pizza place: decent cheese, but teg crust was BURNT , but overall “good.”

But I have to call out a few details:
1. The bacon side was disappointing. It tasted more like honey ham than bacon. It lacked the fattiness, crispiness, texture contrast you want from bacon.
2. They even served it with a side of ketchup, which felt odd
3. The execution of the pizza was fine, but nothing popped. The food didn’t “wow” me.

I will say that their menu offers a wide range of “sourdough pizzas” and “special pizzas” in different styles which I found interesting!

🍹 Drinks & Service

We didn’t try any cocktails this time, so can’t speak much on that front. The service was average — nothing bad, nothing that stood out. Exactly what you’d expect: professional, steady, no major slip-ups.

⸻

🔍 Final Thoughts

Wheated is a solid neighborhood pizza spot. It has thoughtful craft behind its dough and menu concepts. Its strengths lie in variety, ambition, and decent pricing. But on this visit, the food didn’t fully deliver — the salad was overpowered, the bacon was off, and the pizza was good but not memorable.

Would I go back? Yes — probably more for drinks next time, and maybe experimenting with other pizzas, or to see if another visit hits harder.

I just moved over to the Flatbush area from the city and I was looking for a solid local pizza spot you can dine it at. This is the one! Been twice and both times the pizza was phenomenal (top 10 in all of NYC good). The atmosphere and ambiance is great and it is good for families or just a date night. I highly recommend this spot and I will become a regular soon!

We popped in and it was busy. Luckily they had 3 seats at the bar. 10/10 would recommend. We got 2 12" pizzas and it was perfect for 3 people. We took home a few slices. Both pizzas were delicious.

The ceasar salad was also outstanding

google_reviews.text: Such a fabulous spot - the perfect place to warm up and settle in for a good time. We visited recently to try their fondue for two on a freezing day and it was such a winter warming treat! Super tasty and moreish :)

Great neighborhood spot for a Sunday brunch ! Tried the Nashville shrimp sandwich as well as it was delicious. The lemon ricotta pancakes were outstanding and desert - a chocolate pie with caramelized warm marshmallow on top was delicious as well. We will be back to check out dinner!

This restaurant was a delightful surprise.
The double lamb burger was imaginative and rich in flavor, with a well-balanced sauce that complemented the distinct taste of lamb beautifully. The texture of the lamb itself was unique and refined, making this burger absolutely worth trying.

The fried baby potatoes, recommended by our waitress, were another highlight. Trust me — they were far more interesting and satisfying than ordinary fries, with a wonderfully crispy exterior and a hearty bite. Truly excellent.

The dessert provided a perfect finish to the meal — a wonderful combination of chocolate, peanut butter, and marshmallow, offering layers of flavor without being overly sweet or overwhelming the ingredients.

The service was attentive, thoughtful, and perfectly paced — never rushed, never dragging.
All in all, it was a thoroughly satisfying dining experience.

When we have company we always take them to Krupa, it's our go-to for special occasions or to celebrate having survived the week. Great brunch great dinner great coffees and pastry, cocktails, etc. The outdoor patio is fantastic in good weather and has heaters and a retractable covering for bad weather. My meat-eating spouse is always very happy with the seasonal variations in the burgers and steak, and I enjoy the vegetarian/vegan options. I've never seen anyone less than thrilled with anything on the menu. IIRC there are several gluten-free options and substitutions. We arranged to bring a group of ~10 and had a great experience, and while we didn't end up using their wedding reception-sized options they looked good too. Very popular so make a reservation.

GREAT FOOD, GREAT DRINKS, GREAT ATMOSPHERE 👨‍🍳  Been coming to Krupa for many years and it’s a very versatile restaurant bar that does not disappoint in any way. Whether you’re meeting someone for morning coffee ☕️ with breakfast in the backyard or a larger group at night for cocktails 🍹 and small plates to share; Krupa is a solid choice. document: Pomo. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Mexican. located in Brooklyn. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Pomo Pizzeria Napoletana, and I can honestly say it was an outstanding experience from start to finish.

The food was absolutely incredible. I fell in love with the parmigiana—rich, comforting, and perfectly balanced. The Neapolitan-style pizza was everything you hope for: light, flavorful, and beautifully crafted. And the gnocchi… simply unforgettable—soft, delicate, and full of flavor.

What truly made the evening special, though, was the service. Stefano, the owner, went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. His warmth and attention made us feel right at home, like we were sharing a meal with family. It genuinely felt like bringing a little piece of Italy to Scottsdale.

Amazing food, exceptional service, and a memorable atmosphere. I will definitely be coming back—no doubt about it. 🍝🇮🇹

Pomo Pizzeria Napoletana truly delivered one of the most authentic pizza experiences I’ve had. Everything we ordered was delicious and thoughtfully prepared. We started with the Fritto Misto — chula seafood squid and shrimp lightly fried and served with bell pepper aioli — and it was absolutely perfect. Light, crispy, and full of flavor.

For our main, we ordered the Pizza Napoletana Margherita (veg) with tomato sauce, fior di latte mozzarella, parmigiano, and basil. It was absolute perfection — simple, fresh, and done exactly right. You can really taste the quality and authenticity in every bite.

For dessert, we had the profiteroles: choux pastry filled with Luna’s vanilla gelato, topped with chocolate and crushed pistachio. While it was good, it didn’t quite stand out, and I wish I had chosen a different dessert.

Overall, the food was excellent, especially the pizza and appetizers, and I would definitely come back again.

Pomo Pizzeria is a place we keep coming back to, and it never disappoints. We’ve tried quite a bit of the menu over multiple visits, and every experience has been fantastic.
Our absolute favorite pizza is the Burratella — hands down. The combination of creamy burrata, hot soppressata, a touch of honey, and a perfectly baked crust is just unreal. It’s the kind of pizza you crave long after you leave. We’ve also tried other pizzas and dishes, all made with high-quality ingredients and true attention to detail.
The salad was amazing as well — fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. It didn’t feel like an afterthought at all, which we really appreciated.
And the spritz flight deserves a special mention — such a fun and delicious experience. Every spritz was refreshing and well made, and it’s a great way to try multiple flavors in one visit.
Great atmosphere, friendly and attentive service, and consistently excellent food. If you’re looking for authentic pizza, great drinks, and a place you’ll want to return to again and again, Pomo Pizzeria is a must. Highly recommended.

Pomo Pizzeria Napoletana in Scottsdale is a great spot if you want authentic Italian food while staying nearby. It is within easy walking distance of several hotels, which made it really convenient. The pizza tastes truly authentic, with quality ingredients and a classic Naples style. The atmosphere has a traditional Italian vibe that feels warm and relaxed. I would recommend it to anyone visiting the area who wants a solid pizza and a comfortable place to eat.

Perfect Sunday family lunch at Pomo! Came with my vegetarian wife and toddler — everyone was happy.
Started with the Italian Bread, then our little one crushed a cheese pizza with OJ (that Neapolitan crust is impossibly soft and melts in your mouth!). Wife loved the Nerano, I had the Burratella — sweet, spicy, creamy perfection. Washed it down with a Falanghina white wine.
David was a fantastic server — mention this review for extra smiles! 😄
10/10, will be back! 🍕🍷

google_reviews.text: We arrived at 1pm on a Saturday. There was a 1-2 hour wait. We decided to sit in the front desk area and review the menu. It was a crowded space and very cold but you can go to nearby bar for a cocktail. They will text you when your table is ready. We were seated within an hour. Hao, our server, was friendly, helpful, and attentive. The decor is delightful. The food is delicious except the beef tongue was too chewy. The variety on the menu is plentiful. Great selection of drinks. The music is relaxing. All the staff were professional. We will definitely return.

I came in by myself for dinner and Shawn gave me the best service I’ve ever experienced. He was an incredible waiter from start to finish — kind, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

He took the time to explain how hot pot works and made great menu recommendations that were spot on. His knowledge, patience, and positive energy made the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. Shawn has a rare ability to make you feel completely comfortable while also delivering top-tier service.

Truly the best waiter I’ve ever had. He made the night memorable, and I’ll absolutely be back because of him.

The place is famous of long waiting line for a good reason, it is best hot pot spot in New York City, tastes real authentic as you were in China.

They offer a good selection of items on their menu, all fresh and high quality, which is important for hot pot. Few different types of soup base, even you don't eat spicy you can choose mushroom or herb one, both were tasty and good.

My favorite dish is the beef with milk, it's fun to watch the waitress preparing it and the meat so tender and fresh after putting into the hot pot.

This place is my No.1 choice when it comes to hot pot.

Decent but slightly pricey hotpot place with lots of unique items on the menu. Everything was fresh quality and tasted good, except for the Milky Beef (6/10). They pour milk to marinate the beef, which supposedly makes it more tender, but I didn’t think it was that special. What I really liked though was the Fresh Bamboo Shoot (10/10) because of the distinct texture. You don’t find this on the menu of a lot of hotpot places so it felt particularly special.

The wait can be long but you can add yourself to their online waitlist. Also they charge per person for dipping sauce, which is why I docked one star off. It’s not uncommon for hotpot places that are not AYCE, but I still don’t like it.

Lao Zao Chongqing Hot Pot has this beautiful store front. As you enter the wooden doors, you are transported to a traditional village setting of stone and bamboo architecture, hanging lanterns and a water-wheel that separates the higher floor from the lower floor. Even before you sit at your table to savour the food offering, the setting of the restaurant really sets the mood. Service was very efficient and super friendly. The staff were very helpful and provided wonderful recommendations and suggested portions. We opted for the Triple Flavor Pot which consisted of a mushroom soup base, a tomato soup base and mild beef broth soup base. The beef broth was my favourite but a note of caution, the “mild” is fairly spicy especially as the dried chilies continue to infuse in your pot. Would recommend taking out the dried chilies if it gets too spicy. The complimentary starter of spicy pickled vegetables was also amazing so much so that we asked for extra. Some of the standout dishes that we ordered; Milky Beef - when severed, the milk would be poured over the beef and this supposedly helped tenderise the meat. Either way, the beef was delicious, tender and succulent. The Shrimp Paste was served in a hollowed out bamboo, in a crushed ice bucket with its own unique serving spoon. This was fresh and tasty and definitely worth trying. The Stir-Fried Bean Curd Rolls was another favourite. Cooking time for this was a few seconds as it would soak up the soup and inflate very quickly when cooked. We also tried the Thick Sliced Tender Beef, Marbled Beef and Beef Ball which were all amazing. Definitely great to go with a group so you can try the variety of meats, seafoods and vegetables.

google_reviews.text: I Visited this Thai food spot in Sunnyside and I had a great experience. The service was excellent and the food was delicious. We tried the funnel cake fries dessert, and they were really good. Prices are very affordable, and the portions are generous with great flavor. The place is small, so sometimes you may have to share a large table or sit at smaller tables, but it’s totally worth it.

Truly some of the best ramen i’ve had in the city! I’m so lucky to be living so close to this place the last 3 years, but have been coming here before the move.

I HIGHLY recommend any of their ramens, and their soft shell crab bao bun is one of the best buns i’ve had period.

Lovely staff and atmosphere! You will not regret stopping by😊

I came to Fuyu Ramen for the ramen, but I discovered the absolute perfect beer-pairing strategy! If you are grabbing a Kirin Ichiban, you have to order these two side dishes: the Kara-age and the Smashed Cucumber Salad.

They are deliciously contradictory. The Kara-age is that classic, perfectly crispy Japanese fried chicken that everyone loves with a beer. But then you have the Smashed Cucumber—it’s pickled in a spicy oil and topped with fresh sprouts, giving you a sharp, refreshing kick. I found that rotating between the two—one savory and hot, one spicy and cold—was the best way to enjoy the crisp, light lager. Truly a perfect meal!

Huge relief to leave the madness of Manhattan and find this cozy spot. The food was amazing, and there were plenty of veggie options. Curious to go back and try more! The veggie dupbab was very satisfying and a great meal.

Cute place, always busy but moving. We went for ramen on a very cold NYC day and it was good but the broth lacked depth. This is compared to the best ramen restaurents out there - it is a 3/5 in terms of flavor but with atmostpher and the kind staff make it a comfortable spot if you really need some ramen!

name: Laser Wolf
document: Laser Wolf. cuisine: Middle Eastern Desserts Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️ (3/5)

We really wanted to like Laser Wolf. With a new baby at home, nights out are rare, so we hoped this would be a special one.

The setup overlooking the kitchen seemed fun at first, but the fixed chairs made it awkward to get in and out. The menu also isn’t as straightforward as it looks — “Salatim included” is confusing, and even after dining, it’s not 100% clear how it all works. Our server Eddy was helpful in explaining, but overall it feels like you’re paying for a bundle of food, much of which you may not want.

We ordered the sirloin shishlik ($52 for ~8oz) and the merguez. The meats were good but not worth the price. The salatim spread is plentiful, but I only took a few home (hummus, Lebanese potato salad, lutenitsa). Fries were easily the best dish of the night, the wings were tasty but messy with no wet nap provided, and the halloumi was very good. Dessert is included — we got both soft serve and sorbet — but again, it felt like cost buried in the mains rather than a bonus.

Eddy was kind and attentive, but the overall value just isn’t there. $50+ entrees paired with forced sides and dessert doesn’t add up, especially in a city with so many options. Glad we tried it, but unlikely to return.

Pros
•	Attentive and kind service (thanks, Eddy)
•	Fries and tehina ketchup were excellent
•	Halloumi and wings were solid
•	Dessert included (soft serve + sorbet, thanks again Eddy)

Cons
•	Confusing menu structure
•	Overpriced mains ($50+ for 8oz steak)
•	Too many “included” sides you may not want
•	No wet nap for messy wings
•	Overall poor value compared to other Philly spots

So much food. So delicious. This was another amazing experience. It wasn’t just about the food. We sat at the Chefs counter, we loved the view of the kitchen while we ate. The hummus was a real stand out. They had a rack of lamb special for two that was decadent as well. Would go again.

Riley K was the best server we’ve had at a restaurant in a while, we basically let him order for us and he hit it out of the park.  It would be wise to request him if you can.  His knowledge and passion for the food is exceptional.  He certainly made the experience one to remember.  The Dorade was amazing, the skirt steak also incredible.  The brown sugar ice cream is 10/10.  Not a single thing hit our table that we weren’t 100% impressed with.  The after dinner drink he suggested was perfect.  Monte negro or something I can’t remember but it’s wonderful.  He will take care of you.

Here's the deal - just order the salatin with pita and the desert. There are 12 small dishes with the pita that fill a party of 2 easily. The charcoal grill items are good, but you'll satisfy that flavor craving with the salatin alone. The tahina ice cream is scrumptious.
FYI - the door blends into the background.

I’ve come out of my Google review slumber, just so that I can spread the message about how amazing Laser Wolf is (although I’m sure you already know that). I’ve heard so many good things about Laser Wolf… to the point where I started questioning if it was overhyped - I was terribly mistaken.

I decided to make the trek out to Philly (unknowingly on the worst day, due to all the political protests). However, I didn’t let that keep me down. I was on a mission - Laser Wolf.

As a quick prelude, I do want to mention that reservations here are hard to get. So be sure to book out weeks in advance … I was actually on the waitlist, until a 5PM dinner spot opened up. A bit early for me, but beggars can’t be choosers.

I get to Laser Wolf around 4:45PM, eagerly (and awkwardly) pacing around the building until the doors opened. Once 5PM hit, I was surprised by the volume of the people that showed up at the opening. Upon entry, I was greeted by warm smells and spices and a cool/casual interior. Plenty of space, comfortable seating, and nice decor.

The service was phenomenal. Our waiter was super kind and knowledgeable - explained how the whole process worked in perfect detail. For those who don’t know, when you come to Laser Wolf, you are just paying for the entrees, the salatim and the desserts are included. The salatim is basically a huge plate (with 10 smaller bowls) with different types of spreads, bites, appetizers. It also comes with hummus. The salatim by itself is already incredible. So fresh, so flavorful, and the hummus is by far the best hummus I’ve ever had. Also, don’t sleep on the fries… they are amazing - apparently they are brined and flash frozen to make them super crispy - so good! Our waiter actually hooked us up with a free order of fries, since we said we heard good things about them! What a legend! And then on to the meats, I got the chicken shishlik and the steak shishlik, both cooked to perfection. The juiciest kebab style meat I’ve ever had - and a great portion size, not too much, not too little, perfectly balanced with the salatim.

I really can’t express how much I enjoyed the entire experience. From the vibes to the service to the food, everything was on point. They even had specifically designed take away containers with 4 compartments for the salatim - they really thought through everything!

A quick heads up that a 20% service charge is already included on the bill. You don’t normally see that in US restaurants, but honestly the staff deserves every penny, and even some.

An absolute MUST try. There’s also a location in Brooklyn, but Philly is the OG. 10 out of 5 stars.

The Little Pig is such a gem and is a true neighborhood favorite. It has that perfect blend of cozy and lively that makes you want to linger. The backyard patio is absolutely charming, with string lights and a relaxed vibe that feels like a little escape right in Brooklyn.

The food and drinks are both fantastic. The arancini is especially good- perfectly crisp on the outside and delicious inside. And the cocktails are creative, well-balanced, and full of flavor. The espresso martinis are a definite standout!

Service was excellent, too. Our server, Sofia (with an F!), was incredibly attentive, friendly, and made sure everything ran smoothly throughout our meal. I also love the small touches, like the self-serve water setup- simple but convenient and thoughtful!

Overall, The Little Pig is the kind of place you can go for a light dinner, some appetizers, or just great drinks with friends. It’s got everything you want in a neighborhood spot: great food, great atmosphere, and genuinely kind service. Highly recommend!

google_reviews.text:
My favorite fine dining restaurant in NYC. Ive been to the shops outside of this restaurant but I never knew this restaurant existed. Its private, homey, and so welcoming. Our hostess was fantastic. She provided the best service I have ever received and her knowledge about food and alcohol pairings is so good.

The food was fantastic. It was just the right amount and they combined french and japanese very well. This restaurant is also listed in the michelin guide as “hidden gem” and I couldnt agree more. There were so many times I had my jaw open because the food was so good.

I had the best sake of my life here too. Just ask the hostess for her recommendations and you wont regret it.

The entire staff spoke w us during the dinner and we had some nice interactions w the people next to us as well.

What a fantastic dining experience!

Came with my family and had some dietary restrictions, so they called in advance. The team was so accommodating and helped tailor the menu for us — we really appreciated the extra care💕

The food was outstanding, and they took the time to walk us through each dish. The sake tasting was perfectly paired with the meal and made the experience even better.

Can’t wait to come back and try the spring menu!

I had been wanting to try HOUSE for a while now, being a regular shopper at Dashi Okume. However, had been wary of fine dining experiences in Greenpoint after trying 2 so-so places that privileged novelty over flavor. Well let me tell you, HOUSE did not disappoint.

Picture this. You arrive in a quiet street in Greenpoint, with the typical warehouse-y yet clean, modern and minimalist vibe. You see the interior through giant bay windows of a dimly lit store with Japanese products and ceramics. You see people waiting inside and other patrons dining at the café. By then the store is closed, so you ring the intercom  to get in. You wait to be called to the HOUSE, in the back of the store. It feels like you are at your friend's house, and your friend is a sophisticated person with a beautiful house and he cooks for you. The atmosphere is quiet but elevated. There are 10 seats. And you are hosted by 4-5 people. It feels luxurious. You may start the dinner as perfect strangers, but you certainly make friends along the experience.

And the food is incredible. Your friend is an amazing cook. From start to finish, the story is coherent, with subtle development and transitions that never miss a beat or take you somewhere uncomfortable. Flavors are predominantly Japanese forward with some international ingredients and techniques. Noting for example the Monaka filled with ricotta and corn or the french tuile on top of a burrata with berries, reminiscent of Scandinavian flavors.

The highlight of the menu for me was the noodles. With a fragrant Dashi and rich egg noodles covered in egg yolk and fish roe, the final dish on the meal is an unmistakably Japanese grand finale, with an explosion of flavors.

Fantastic experience. Thank you team.

Beautiful space. Lovely intimate dining experience. We snagged a last minute reservation and were blown away. Every dish was meticulously prepared. Each bite highlighting a perfect blend of French technique with Japanese flavors. The craft sake pairing was phenomenal and must be experienced.

The hostess was knowledgeable and welcoming - made us felt absolutely at home, which is their philosophy. You truly felt as if you’re at a friend’s home, albeit a friend who is an incredible chef.

Thank you HOUSE brooklyn for such a special evening. Loved every minute of it.

Exquisite experience. The chef cooks right in front of you, serving a series of creative and tasty dishes inspired by Japanese and French cuisine. The food is high-end, but the vibe is relaxed since you sit at the counter.

name: Crispy Burger
document: Crispy Burger. cuisine: Burgers Fast Food. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Not sure what happened with that first one star review 😅 but I had a decent experience dining here and trying their fried chicken. First off, their grand opening is on 12/29 so maybe they were still getting things together before that? 🫣
.
Anyways, their fried chicken is just as good as this other location of Crispy Burger in east village that I have tried before 👌. I tried their regular fried chicken, tenders, spicy chicken sandwich combo, skewers, new Orleans style whole chicken leg and tried a few of their sides like onion rings, fries, biscuit and mash potato. Overall, I want to say its good fried chicken. The chicken is nicely fried and crispy with good flavor to them. Their tenders weren't bad either but you really need to get their sauces to pair with them (a little dry if you dont 😅). The chicken sandwich wasnt the best looking but it was a big sandwich with a big chunk of crispy chicken, lettuce, tomato and mayo. There was also a little kick to it since i got the spicy version👌👌. The chicken leg was massive too. (If only they provided gloves tho... 🙈). Their fries are the good kind with a nice crisp but still soft-ish center 👍. Onion rings on the other hand was just okay... didnt find actual onion rings inside it but still decently onion flavored. The mash potato was also okay... just mash potato 🙃. Other than food, they also have a few tea and bubble tea options too, which to my surprise was actually decent tea and very refreshing paired with all the chicken 👌. I tried their jasmine lemon bubble tea.
Portion-wise, everything was generously portioned for its price. They have some spicy seasoning and cumin seasoning available too  for dine in (Not sure if theres any to-go), if you want to add some more flavor to any of the chicken. Again, overall, I had a decent experience dining here and recommend it for anyone looking for fried chicken in the area. They're having grand opening promos starting 12/29 including free merch with purchases so more the reason to try them out if you have the chance (and crave fried chicken).
It's delicious! I often bring my kids here late at night to enjoy this treat. They especially love the grilled chicken skewers and all sorts of fried food—it's fantastic!
The crispy chicken is tasty! The source for cheese burger is good. And they have these little cute bag charms!! Love this place!

The food was amazing—hot, fresh, and perfectly crispy. I placed my order and my sandwich came out within minutes, which was impressive. The staff was incredibly friendly and welcoming, making the whole experience even better. Highly recommend this place and will definitely be back!

We ordered food to go. The chicken was super crispy and perfectly cooked. The wrap was big, juicy, and filled with fresh, tasty salad. They also gave our child a little toy, which was really sweet of them. We’ll definitely come back again! 😊

name: Ok Canaan
document: Ok Canaan. cuisine: Taiwanese Soup. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This location of OK Canaan Taiwanese Gourmet is inside the  ***99 Ranch Market food court*** and is one of several locations they have in Flushing. We ordered the Pork Chop Lunchbox and the Spicy Stinky Tofu with Duck Blood.

When we arrived, it was around 11 AM, which is their listed opening time, but the chef had not arrived yet. Because of this, things felt a bit unorganized at the beginning.

The Pork Chop Lunchbox was quite good and enjoyable overall. The Spicy Stinky Tofu with Duck Blood, however, was a bit underwhelming — not because it wasn’t stinky enough, but because the broth tasted very light, almost like plain water, and lacked the bold flavor that this dish usually has.

Overall, the pork chop was the stronger item we tried. The experience felt a bit uneven due to the opening preparation and the mild flavor of the stinky tofu.
If the operation becomes more stable and the flavors improve in the future, I would be happy to come back and give it another try.

Had lunch here today and enjoyed the food a lot! We tried the pork bun and the ba wan appetizer… I thought the pork bun was good but did not enjoy the gelatinous texture of the ba wan, my dad however did! I thought the hot and sour soup was really good. I had the eggplant vermicelli dish which was tasty and not too spicy. My dad had the Taiwanese lo mein with chicken which was garlicky and good. Service was great! Would visit again and try more of their dishes.

Authentic Taiwanese food! We got the oyster pancakes and four god soup (literal translation). Meat is off the bone tender, and feels like home food. Will be back for their breakfast menu as it’s only Sat/Sun.

Great food! I ordered the stinky tofu along with a few other traditional Taiwanese dishes, and everything was delicious. Authentic flavors and really well prepared—definitely recommend for anyone craving Taiwanese cuisine!

Went with a friend during lunch time on a weekday. No other customers but couple of delivery orders. Quality of dishes vary, but staff was friendly. Still worth a visit!

🥤🥤Taiwanese drinks in the fridge were great! I highly recommend trying them (especially if u go with Taiwanese, ask them what them are lol)

💜💜Taro cake was my favorite that day. They were fried smashed taro. Kinda moist, and mochi with great flavor.

(Deep fried) Sticky tofu was classic. White kimchi was a highlight.

Sesame oil kidney was not the style I had in Taiwan, but my friend liked it.

Braised pork rice was delicious too, pretty classic, especially with a flavored egg. But pork was in big chunks which was not ideal.. Traditionally we use grounded pork and it should almost melt in mouth.

Soft shell crab was also average. Delicious but I won’t say it’s a must or signature Taiwanese dish.

name: Reyna Restaurant
document: Reyna Restaurant. cuisine: Dominican Mexican Latin American. located in Bronx. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
I went here with my friends for Valentine’s Day around 10:30 PM (looked like the last seating). The place itself is beautiful — the ambiance, decor, and vibe were honestly fantastic and exactly what you’d want for a night out.

Unfortunately, the service didn’t match how nice the restaurant looks.

Our waitress came to take our drink order, but the drinks took a very long time to arrive even though the restaurant was already pretty empty. We asked if they were coming soon and she said yes… but then our appetizer was delivered to the table next to us. They told the runner it wasn’t theirs, and we literally watched him stand there unsure where to take it until the waitress came over and said it was ours. By then the food was already a bit cold, but we didn’t complain.

After that, another set of appetizers was brought to our table — except those actually belonged to the table next to us. At that point it just felt really disorganized. We understood it was Valentine’s Day and everyone was probably tired after a busy shift, but when you’re going out and spending money you still expect decent service.

We tried ordering more food, but the waitress told us the kitchen was closed — even though no one came beforehand to ask if we wanted to add anything before closing. The same thing happened to the table next to us, and we didn’t even get the chance to order dessert.

Overall, the restaurant is genuinely beautiful and has great potential. I’d probably give it another chance and hope for better service next time, because the atmosphere really is worth it — but the experience definitely needs improvement!

Decent Mediterranean food in a great space. I loved the high ceiling and the room was dim lit and intimate, though I fear it was because most tables were empty. The tables are so close to each other than in a busy evening it must get quite loud.

The food was hit or miss. I got the Taste of Reyna sampler and the muhamarra. I loved the intense flavors of the lamb baklava and I liked its originality, but the muhamarra was very thin and the falafel dry. The rest of the Taste of Reyna was somewhere in between. Nothing stood out besides the lamb baklava.

Most of the dishes in the tapas section of the menu were not available, which is where I wanted to order from. The waiter said at least one had been removed from the menu and the others were just not available at the time. A bit disappointing.

This is hands down my favorite go-to restaurant! The food is absolutely delicious — everything on the menu is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. The drinks are just as amazing — creative, refreshing, and always perfectly made.
What really sets this place apart is the service. The staff are all so friendly, attentive, and professional. I always feel welcomed and well taken care of every time I visit. The hostess is truly wonderful — warm, kind, and always makes me feel like a valued guest.
If you’re looking for a spot with incredible food, top-notch drinks, and personal attention that makes you feel at home, this is it. Highly recommend!

I had a fantastic experience at Reyna near Union Square! The drinks were well-crafted and flavorful—definitely a highlight to kick off the evening. I tried a variety of dishes including the oysters, croquettes, hanger steak, and ricotta bites, and everything was absolutely delicious. The hanger steak in particular was perfectly cooked and full of flavor.

What really stood out was the attentive and friendly service. The staff made sure everything ran smoothly without being overbearing, which made the evening feel relaxed and enjoyable.

Highly recommend Reyna for a night out with great food, drinks, and a welcoming atmosphere. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Reyna is my absolute favorite! I only got to try the cocktails last time (which brought me back again... my favorite is the Spagliato!), so I was really looking forward to my get-together with friends this time. All the dishes we had were flavorful and perfectly seasoned.
Our highlight was the Gambas A La Plancha (grilled shrimp with different sauces that came alongside)—so good. If you like shrimp, this is a must-try. The croquettes were very nice, and my friends who don’t usually eat lamb loved the Lamb Baklava!
Bringing all of this together is the wonderful team at Reyna. Kudos to Tima, Chrissy, Emmy—they make sure every guest has a great time here.

name: The Eighty Six
document: The Eighty Six. cuisine: Seafood Steakhouses American. located in Manhattan. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We had the nicest date night at The Eighty Six! We were so happy to be able to experience this incredible dining journey. Our waiter, Kevin, was so nice and explained the details of the menu wonderfully. We wanted a specific cocktail that wasn’t on the menu and he sent the bartender over to ensure we got exactly what we wanted. Jermaine at the door was so kind in making sure we got into the restaurant and settled in nicely. He continued checking on us throughout the evening making sure everything was up to par. We’re so thankful for his hospitality! Mario, Don and Chris were absolutely delightful entertaining us throughout our meal and providing context on how The Eighty Six came to be. Chris even treated us to a complimentary dessert/palette cleanser that was delicious. We absolutely loved The Eighty Six and hope we have the chance to dine there again!

Here’s everything we ordered:

Food:
The Eighty Six Waldorf salad
Caviar butter pasta (off-menu)
Maine lobster spaghetti a la scampi
The Eighty Six Cheesesteak
Truffle fries with house malt aioli
Corn pot pie

Desserts:
Pineapple (rum infused) - the Hemingway
Banana pudding (ode to Magnolia’s Bakery)
Lemon sorbet

Cocktails:
Champagne Pornstar
Fluffy Margarita
Mezcal Infante

10/10 across the board. This is the quintessential NYC restaurant experience. Cool speakeasy vibes, incredible cocktails, impeccable service and the food across the board beat my expectations.

Let me start by saying Sherief brought everything to another level. Superb recommendations and great vibes. Everything was paced out well with an attention to detail that really makes a difference.

We started with the croquettes and caviar, and the madai. Great light starters with tons of flavor. The 86 salad was really differentiated and an incredible salad like no other.

We had the 86 cheesesteak and the Wagyu steak with creamed corn and mashed potatoes. Plenty to take home and enjoy a 2nd meal tomorrow for lunch.

Will absolutely be back. Had a wonderful experience.

Came here at 4:15pm as a walk in. Don was at the door and helped us get a seat instantly(VERY RARE THIS HAPPENS BTW). Jermaine took down our info and proceeded to get us seated. Let me describe this experience as if you were here with me:

- walking through the curtains and you see the atmosphere; calm vibe, dimmed lights and semi-quiet. Everything is meticulously organized.

- We got the booth all the way at the end next to the kitchen(honestly, best seat in the house) in which we were extremely grateful for.

- As soon as we sat down, our waiter “Claude” properly introduced himself and made us feel at home. Charming, funny & very charismatic. He was well versed with everything on and off the menu.

FOOD & DRINKS:

- I ordered the whiskey sour with McAllen 12 alongside egg whites, a MUST have for whiskey drinkers. & Refreshingly delicious strawberry vesper(must have for the girlies).

- Ordered the famously delicious 86 Waldorf Salad to start off. Full of flavor and was instantly blown away by the ingredients. Then went on to order the Minolette Potato Croquettes(absolutely will recommend) & their famous cheesesteak for starters. 10/10 on all of it

- Entree was Bone in Wagyu NY Strip(mouthwatering delicious!!) alongside the corn pot pie 🤤.

DESSERT:

- Best Cheesecake in all of NYC(as a native New Yorker who’s been here for 26yrs i can say that!)

Thank you to Chef Randy & Nat. & to the rest of the team: Francisco, Matteo, Emily, Jermaine, Claude & the others… you guys were amazing in every aspect!

Final rating: 100/10 on every single dish & customer service!!!

Everything about this is NYC. No sign on the door and it looks a like an if you know you know kinda place from the outside. Stepping inside is old school vibes with art deco. A real fireplace really set the ambiance. To go with the cool vibes is some great food. Everything we had was fantastic. Some really unique items on the menu that are executed flawlessly like the French onion croquettes, cheesesteak and all the desserts. Would definitely recommend.

CHRISTOPHER THE MANAGER IS AMAZING. Nicest guy, so welcoming, kept checking in on us. He truly made the experience amazing and was such a pleasure to talk to. Jermaine and Dom gave us the warmest welcome, they were so sweet. Can’t get over how nice all the staff are. Claude, Mario, Yanick, Kaitlin, Sean all came over to say hello and take care of us! Can’t wait to go back. They really made this the best experience possible. Excellent food. The desserts were incredible.

google_reviews.text: Second time visiting Tara Rose on a Friday night. Came here for happy hour the other night with a few friends and loved it! Oddly enough, despite working in the area this was my first time here. The service was great and the food was too! We tried a smattering of things from the happy hour menu as well as some of the main dishes. I would definitely recommend the smoked salmon and rice cake appetizer as well as the chicken tenders, hummus, and fig+ricotta toast. A note, they can make many things gluten free! Great cocktail drinks and appetizers options. We tried the fries, sprouts (a bit honey sweet, i like it), crispy rice with salmon, fish and chips. Clean bathroom.

What a fun and eclectic place!  Savanah at the bar killed it with her cocktail skills!  She made great suggestions and with such a lovely Irish accent I knew she knew her craft! The food was great and the staff including a super friendly and knowledgeable Manager, McKenna, made my first visit such a great one, I can't was to go back!

A huge shout-out to McKenna, who truly went above and beyond. She helped with setup, made sure the bar and dinner areas were perfect, and checked in throughout the night to ensure everything ran smoothly. Her energy, professionalism, and willingness to jump in made a huge difference.

The entire staff was warm, attentive, and extremely professional. The complimentary bottle of Prosecco was such a special touch, and every single guest commented on how delicious the food was, how great the drinks were, and how beautiful the venue is. Several people even mentioned how well they were served and how welcoming the staff felt.

The evening went off without a hitch—truly seamless from start to finish. I’m so grateful to Tara Rose for making this engagement celebration unforgettable. I highly, highly recommend this restaurant for any event or special occasion. Outstanding in every way!

name: wagamama - midtown
document: wagamama - midtown. cuisine: Asian Fusion. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Absolutely loved Wagamama for its Asian fusion restaurant. They recently put out a new bar menu with a wonderful lychee martini and I can only imagine how great all the other drinks taste came here during restaurant week and was greeted by a lovely hostess and server and Freda that atmosphere was wonderful as we had by the bar seating . The food was lovely straight. I was able to help me make a substitution for my  pork allergy. which you made me feel welcomed on a cold winter day the chicken gyoza Ramen hit the spot with the crispy rice as my appetizer and a nice Yuzu to wash it all down. It was a wonderful experience. And although unfortunately, this time there was no banana Katsu I will be back.

I thought this place was really good! I’ve been wanting to try like a Asian inspired restraunt and this checked the box. We had reservations at 6 but we came early and not many people were there so we got seated right away. The servers were nice and very quick. I liked the vibe of this place. It was modern and clean. They had ramen, bowls, noodles, rice, and so many drinks to choose from. I got the spicy salmon noodle bowl snd it was delicious and not to heavy. The bang bang cauliflower was very flavorful and a little spicy to. The Tokyo fries were ingesting but crunchy and flavored nicely.

Surprised to find this evolved Wagamama in midtown NYC compared to the simpler noodle bar I first tried in London over a decade ago. This place has a more extensive menu and table service. We were a party of 2 and tried the pork gyoza, the tuna tataki and the bang bang cauliflower from the shareables menu. Of these 3 dishes we enjoyed the last one the best. The other 2 were good but not outstanding. We also ordered the chicken mandarin salad which we found very good. Lastly we had the grilled duck ramen. This was good but not comparable to ramen from the great ramen shops in the city. Overall, the restaurant serves good Asian fusion food, the service is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is lively and festive for a Saturday evening.

Great food, convenient location and great service. We stopped in for a quick meal before attending a performance at the New York City Center. Service was friendly, polite and very attentive. My ramen bowl was filled with flavor, and the tuna was an excellent piece of fish that was seared to perfection. Extremely satisfied with our dining experience here.

We’ve been coming to this ramen restaurant for about 3–4 years now, and it’s been consistently good the entire time. The quality of the food and the level of service have stayed the same, which is something we really appreciate. You know what to expect every visit, and it never disappoints.

We’re big fans of the shrimp ramen — it’s flavorful, comforting, and always hits the spot. The staff are friendly and efficient, and the overall atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming.

It’s a solid go-to place for ramen, especially if you’re looking for consistency and a dish you can keep coming back for. Definitely worth a visit if you enjoy good ramen done right.

name: Miriam
document: Miriam. cuisine: Mediterranean Cocktail Bars Middle Eastern. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: We made a last minute reservation before a nets game and it was the best decision we ever made. There’s probably nothing bad in the menu, we loved everything we got. Specifically the Brussels sprouts and hummus as appetizers, I could’ve eaten 45 orders of those. The service was so freaking kind, they made suggestions for drinks and cocktails, everything loved them. I will def come back

Miriam is such a great spot. The food is delicious, the portions are generous (perfect for sharing between two), and the flavors are incredible. The pitas are honestly some of the best I’ve had.

We tried the chicken shawarma, which was wonderful. It comes with rice and a small Israeli salad, and everything was seasoned beautifully. The service was excellent, super attentive and kind.

They also offer special menus for Jewish holidays like Rosh Hashanah, which is a really nice touch.

Price-wise, it’s not cheap, but it’s absolutely worth it for the quality. Overall, just a really good restaurant, great food, great service, and one I’d happily come back to once they finish renovating their original location.

Popular brunch place we visited with friends. Our friends said the menu changed since they had last been. Overall several combinations offered for breakfast but it would be nice if there was one where you could mix and match the egg + simit/pita + side. I tried the avocado sandwich and really enjoyed it although could have used some more pickled onion and tomato could have been a nice addition. My friends had the popular breakfast and the smoked salmon latkes. Generally seemed like the chopped salad was left in varying amounts on everyone's plates, probably an indicator that another side might have been preferred. The kids enjoyed the challah French toast. Had to flag down our server for more coffee. Limited vegan or dairy free options. Menu skews savoury, only the challah French toast is on the sweeter side.

Come hungry! Seriously, the portions are generous and delicious. But that doesn’t mean the food isn’t wonderfully prepared and fresh tasting. For the price I’d describe it as a good value and most of the main entrees could be shared (especially with an appetizer). I really want to go back and try more of the dishes…next time I’ll come hungrier! It has a nice cozy ambiance, but not too cramped. Only complaint was the service was sometimes hard to track down (like to grab a new fork or get a water refill).

Came here for breakfast before going to Barclays and WOW. Everything we tried was phenomenal. I got the latkes Benedict and it was bangin.

Super cute interior as well lots of natural light and a big window to people watch out of.

name: Theodora
document: Theodora. cuisine: Mediterranean Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Finally snagged a reservation! And yes, it was worth the hype. The atmosphere is amazing and warm. Our server was wonderful and kind. Love the sourdough with whipped ricotta. The mackerel toast was delicious. Red snapper ceviche excellent. And the whole dry-aged branzino, so good. The server also helped debone the fish and he did a great job. Would definitely come back again!

100/10. The culinary highlight of our NYC trip.

We ordered a bunch from the menu, and there wasn’t a dish we didn’t love.

We loved the Hiramsa to start, fresh and had a tang to it. The grilled mackerel is a must and comes on beautiful sourdough made fresh. It may not be visually appealing for some, but I recommend you try it!

The black cod was perfectly cooked, covered in an amazing sauce and salad. The whole butterflied trout was the standout item, packed full of Smokey flavour and different experiences you get switching from one side of the fish to the other is unique and delicious. This dish was what brought Theodora to my attention and it did not disappoint.

The service was fantastic and the waiters were tentative but we loved the chefs table experience. Eating in front of the grill and watching the food go through different stages if cooking so much fun. The chef was very friendly and made time to talk to us over the course of our dinner. If you are a small part, book the countertop table.

We spent about $200 for 2 people, we didn’t have alcoholic drinks.

Theodora is fully booked out weeks ahead, a reservation is a must, good luck getting one. I absolutely recommend this place and will be back the next time I’m in NY.

We absolutely LOVED this place! The hype is real!!
We were lucky to be sat at the chefs counter right next to the expo. We got to watch everyone work and they are a well oiled machine.
This is the best Mediterranean food we’ve had in NYC. All the dishes benefit from the wood firing even if they aren’t directly prepared on the grill which was a beautiful surprise. For example the oil on the hummus. Mind blown

Favorite bite of the night…the tilefish ceviche with wood fired pineapple. Wow!

Also and most importantly, the service was elite. Our server Zoe was just so great, friendly knowledgeable, attentive, all the things!
We also got to meet and chat a bit with the GM, Katie. So nice!

We can’t wait to go back and try everything we don’t get to try this time.

Theodora Restaurant absolutely lives up to the hype—even if getting a reservation feels like winning the lottery. Every dish is bold, flavorful, and confidently executed, especially the seafood-focused menu. The appetizers were flawless across the board, and the fish dishes truly shine. Don’t miss the sourdough (elite), yellowfin tuna, salmon king crudo, and the ceviche—standout bites that justify the buzz. The lamb was a bit too strong on aroma for my taste, and while the octopus was good, it wasn’t the star. Still, an exceptional meal overall and 100% worth the chase.

The team behind Theodora has truly captured the intimate Brooklyn-aesthetic. I loved the open kitchen layout and curated seating. We were in a curved booth right in the middle of it all (best for people watching) but would so come back to experience the chefs counter or alcove or front seats by the window.

Now the food is sublime. The Middle Eastern, Brazilian, Mexican flavors blend together so nicely for an exceptional taste in each bite. We started with the Hiramasa and Seeded Laffa. Holy I would eat five plates of the Hiramasa if that were socially acceptable… the dip with the warm Laffa is also really tasty. For mains, we got the Octopus and Whole Butterflied Trout which were both yum. I’d say the potato chips and brussel sprouts added a unique dimension to the octopus dish. To end the meal we got the chocolate cake, which as the reviews mention, was perfectly sweet and paired well with the mascarpone and olive oil on top. Bliss.

The cocktails are also noteworthy. We enjoyed the La Cigua and Mayahuel and would recommend the former for a smoky cucumber flavor and the latter for a savory mezcal martini.

A last note on service – the staff is really friendly and knows the menu well. Our dishes were paced out in multiple courses and were brought out fresh. You can tell the chef team enjoys their work and it was exciting to watch!

Highly recommend a visit, or two!
