google_reviews.text:
My friends and I (party of 5) had such a great experience here! The drinks were one of my favorite parts, they come served in either a pineapple 🍍 or a watermelon 🍉, and as a pineapple lover, I was obsessed! I also ordered the rice and seafood mix served inside a pineapple, and it was absolutely delicious.

If you love seafood, this place has tons of great options, but they also offer wings and plenty of non-seafood dishes, so there’s something for everyone. The service was amazing, our waiter was super attentive, friendly, and really made sure we were taken care of.

The decor is phenomenal! The whole place is beautiful, and with the holiday decorations it looked extra cute, perfect for photos, date nights, or a fun outing with friends or family. The space is a little narrow, but it honestly didn’t bother me much because everything was so clean (even the bathrooms!).

For a group of 5, our total was around $520 including tip. We each ordered an appetizer, a main dish, and a fruit-served drink, plus we all got a second drink 🍹. With the quality, presentation, and overall experience, I can’t complain at all, I loved it! 🥰 definitely make reservations ahead!

Definitely recommend!

Tried Thai Lemongrass and it was such a nice surprise. The whole experience felt easy and genuine: good food, great drinks, and a really pleasant space.

The Crab Rangoon were incredible, definitely a must. We also ordered the Shrimp Dumplings, BBQ Beef Short Ribs, and Bae-Mee Pok Pok, and everything was delicious. You can tell they really care about the presentation too — every dish came out looking delicate and beautifully plated, which made it feel a bit more special without being over the top.

We finished with Mango Sticky Rice (we can never skip it) and loved it. Cocktails were also a highlight — the Watermelon Margarita and Piña Colada were both amazing.

The décor is stunning and adds a lot to the atmosphere. Overall, a place I’d happily come back to.

This charming restaurant has made the best impression.
The ambiance was warm and lively, featuring a perfect mix of background decorations for Valentine's Day, including traditional Tai lanterns adorned with flowers and hundreds of balloons, making it ideal for the celebration.
The team were attentive without being intrusive, always ready with a smile and great recommendations.
For our drinks, we have ordered a Coconut Mojito and a Watermelon Margarita, both of which look fantastic, and taste delicious.
For the main course, we ordered the duck Basil mild and the Whole Red Snapper Fried with goddess Garlic Sauce, which was cooked to perfection—flaky, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The side of roasted vegetables was fresh and seasoned perfectly.
For dessert, the chocolate mousse was rich, silky, and the perfect sweet ending. I’ll definitely be coming back and recommending this place to friends!

Lemongrass Brooklyn is such a cute spot! The atmosphere was so nice and welcoming, the food was absolutely amazing, and everything came out perfectly. The drinks were so pretty and tasted just as good as they looked. The service was great got seated quickly as a walk in, the lady helping us was super kind and made the experience even better. Honestly, everything about this place was just so nice. Definitely coming back!

This place is absolutely amazing. Not only is the food great but it comes out so fast and hot. The SAKE does the job lol the place itself is beautiful and to the customer service to die for. We got the garlic chicken, tai fried rice, shrimp pad see eww and the fried banana as a desert. The complementary pea flower lemonade omg! This place did not miss.

I’ve been to Red Hook Lobster Pound twice now, and both visits were consistently excellent. The seafood was incredibly fresh, the dishes were flavorful, and the happy hour was genuinely worth it. The lobster was clearly fresh, well prepared, and fairly priced—which is always appreciated.

The happy hour oysters and drinks were a highlight and made the experience even better without feeling gimmicky. Everything tasted high quality and thoughtfully done.

A big shout-out to Aissa, Mason, and Luke, who were fantastic hosts and servers. Their recommendations were spot-on, and their service went above and beyond without being overbearing. They really made the experience enjoyable.

I would absolutely recommend Red Hook Lobster Pound to any seafood lover looking for great food, a fun happy hour, and excellent service. Definitely a place I’ll be returning to!

Love the food! Everything here is so fresh and delicious. The Lobster Mac & Cheese is my absolute favorite, but the Lobster Roll, Fish & Chips are all tasty and S’mores is delicious! The atmosphere is great, with plenty of indoor and outdoor seating. The staff is super friendly and helpful, making the dining experience even better. If you’re in the area, you won’t regret stopping by!

Delicious lobsters and appetizers.
We had the Maine lobster and Connecticut lobster roll. It was delicious. I’d recommend getting the lime ranch on the side as a dip.
Loved the calamari too.
It’s a little pricey, but I think it’s worth it.

I came to see what all the hype was about, but left wondering what I missed. The Connecticut lobster roll, which cost over $50, didn’t deliver the buttery punch I expected. If I’m paying that kind of price, I want flavor that grabs me; not something forgettable.

The oysters were okay, but I’ve had better. Calamari was heavy on the batter and lacked the crispiness I like. Tacos? Meh—just so-so. And the lobster bisque came out lukewarm, which really dulled the richness it should’ve had.

Service didn’t help either. It wasn’t busy, yet I had to wave down our server multiple times just to get basic attention. That kind of inattentiveness really takes away from the experience.

Honestly, I’d rather track down a Cousins Maine Lobster truck and call it a day. Better flavor and no need to play hide-and-seek with the staff.

Was looking for lobster roll in Brooklyn after key lime pie. The lobster could have been sweeter, and with more melted butter.

name: Chama Mama
document: Chama Mama . cuisine: Georgian Wine Bars Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
🇬🇪 A Georgian Culinary Journey in Chelsea

If you’re looking to break away from the usual dinner routine, Chama Mama is an absolute must. We came here for a work dinner of four, and it was the perfect blend of a professional atmosphere and a genuinely fun, unique vibe.

The Highlights:
• The Food: Traditional Georgian flavors that feel both adventurous and comforting. Every dish was a conversation starter.

• The Service: Truly top-tier. Our server was originally from Georgia and treated us like guests in their own home. They were incredibly patient, helping us navigate the menu and giving us "the whole 9 yards" on the proper way to eat the traditional dishes.

• The Drinks & Vibe: Relaxed yet polished. The environment is pleasant, the drinks are great, and it’s a fantastic spot for groups.

🍰 Don't Skip Dessert:
You have to order the Napoleon cake. It is quite literally to die for—it has the perfect amount of crunch and flavor without being overly sweet. It was the highlight of the night!

Verdict: 5/5 stars. Great food, even better service. Highly recommended for team dinners or anyone wanting a delicious "culinary trip" to Tbilisi without leaving Manhattan. 🥂

We absolutely loved Chama Mama! First time having Georgian food. So much to love. Flavorful food, honest craftsmanship, stunning drinks, incredibly friendly staff, beautiful design of the space. While I've seen and understand criticisms of the steep pricepoint for "homey" food, the investment in a meal at Chama Mama is worth the authentic experience, and most of all the DELECTABLE food. Stars of the show were the Beef Kharcho Soup (delicious tomato flavor, hint of spice, stewed beef, wheat), the Khinkali (excellently spiced beef & pork in our case, bathing in a wonderful meat broth inside the dumpling wrapper), and the Khachapuri (cheesy, delicious bread, a must-try food experience), and don't sleep on the mocktails and lemonades. Fantastic restaurant, from the food all the way to the branding.

Absolutely incredible experience at Chama Mama!
The food was rich, flavorful, and truly felt like a journey into Georgian cuisine. The khachapuri was perfection — crispy on the outside, warm and cheesy on the inside — and the khinkali were juicy and full of flavor. Every dish tasted homemade and cooked with real care.

The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, and the staff made us feel right at home from the moment we walked in. It’s the perfect place to share plates, enjoy amazing wine, and discover something new and delicious.

Hands down one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. Can’t wait to come back!

Our server, she was very kind and professional, wine tastings, cocktails, were all above expectations and quite delicious. The food though? Excellent, phenomenal, superb! We enjoyed our meal quite a bit. Easily a place we’d come back to. Georgian food is a must try, and Chama Mama does it justice!

This was our second visit, and it was just as amazing as the first!

We ordered the Adjaruli khachapuri, chicken mtsvadi, honey cake ice cream, and chocolate cloud cake, along with the drinks (passionfruit caramel lemonade and Château Buera – Rkatsiteli). Every single item was absolutely delicious.

The service was also top-notch! Truly outstanding. Easily a 10 out of 10. We can’t wait to come back! ❤️❤️❤️

document: Izzy's Brooklyn Smokehouse. cuisine: Barbeque Kosher Smokehouse. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Absolutely Outstanding BBQ Experience!

I had lunch today at Izzy’s Smokehouse, and it was nothing short of phenomenal. We ordered a spread that included the brisket, pulled beef, burger, and chicken, and every single item was cooked to perfection.

The brisket was melt-in-your-mouth tender with just the right amount of smoky flavor. The pulled beef was rich, juicy, and packed with flavor — easily one of the best I’ve had anywhere. The burger was perfectly cooked, incredibly juicy, and bursting with bold, smoky notes that made every bite unforgettable. Even the chicken, which can sometimes be tricky at BBQ spots, was juicy, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned.

On top of the incredible food, the service was attentive and friendly, making the whole experience even better. The atmosphere was relaxed and inviting — the perfect spot for lunch, whether you’re a BBQ enthusiast or just looking for an amazing meal.

I highly recommend Izzy’s Smokehouse to anyone looking for top-notch BBQ. It’s clear they take pride in what they do, and it shows in every bite. Can’t wait to come back!

Great kosher BBQ! I had the brisket sandwich and I was barely able to walk out on my own. Should've eaten 1/2 and take the other half home in a box. The place is small, just a couple of tables. Highly recommend all the meat. We ordered the lamb ribs, burned ends, wings, and pastrami. Every entree comes with pickles and red cabbage. Everything was ready in ten minutes. It was all licking my fingers delicious!! The best in my opinion was the lamb ribs. Interesting options for local beer. I added a photo of what i got, it had a tropical flavor that i enjoyed greatly. The place is small, only 4 tables (seats 18) and a few outdoor as well. We came at 4:30 and by 5 the line was almost out the door and no seating available. Definitely go early if you want to sit down. Husbands favorite was the pastrami, which came with a horseradish mayo and mustard! We definitely will eat here again! Great food!

Definitely lives up to the hype!

Been following for a long time and always wanted to come, so when I was in NY this week I had to go.

The food and portions were excellent and something you definitely cannot get elsewhere. Highly recommend the smoked chicken sandwich and the tacos! Service was great and the food was fresh with amazing flavour.

Would love to see a location in London 😉

Definitely take the time to visit and enjoy!

document: Ganblaze. cuisine: Barbeque. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
The food here is really good and the vibe is fun. They even have live singing—someone at the table next to us had a birthday and the staff sang for them, which made the whole place feel lively.
The skewers are solid: beef tongue, chicken cartilage, and chicken skin were all tasty. The new items are worth trying—lychee beef short rib was surprisingly sweet and flavorful, and the plum beef was a nice balance. Salmon skewers were also good.The cheesy beef fried rice was unexpectedly one of our favorites.
Overall, great spot for hanging out with friends or celebrating something casual.

Great spot for late-night skewers and Xinjiang-style BBQ! The lamb skewers were juicy and full of flavor with the perfect cumin spice. I also loved the variety of skewers—everything from lamb, beef, and chicken to veggies.

The setup is fun because you can pick your skewers and watch them grill right in front of you. The atmosphere is lively with cool lighting and music, making it a great place to hang out with friends.

Prices are reasonable and the skewers are super fresh. Definitely a must-try if you’re craving authentic Chinese BBQ in the area. I’ll definitely be back!

I am a big fan of bbq, so this place really hits my comfort zone. The lamb was wonderfully fatty and incredibly fragrant after grilling, exactly the kind of flavor I love. They offer a wide variety of dipping sauces, so it is easy to find one that suits your taste. One of the female servers treated us like babies, in the best way possible. She was extremely friendly, attentive, and made the whole experience feel warm and welcoming. During dinner, there were also a lot of interactive moments, and the entire restaurant got involved, creating a lively and energetic atmosphere. It is a great spot to come with friends on the weekend, enjoy drinks together, and soak in the fun vibe. The experience was genuinely enjoyable. The only downside is the waiting time, which feels endless, so make sure to arrive early to put your name down.

Tried this place for the first time. This is a great place to eat and hang out. Pretty unique with the spinning skewers. Personal favorite was the pepper beef skewer. There are also a lot of seafood options. The price is decent and it’s pretty much the same as the carts outside. They also have a raffle at the end. 10 skewers for one raffle for a chance to win a plushie.

the concept is definitely unique where you cook your own skewers on a rotating grill right at your table. You grab whatever items you want, and they scan a wristband with a barcode to keep track of everything you pick, which is pretty convenient. They also offer cooked entrees like rice and noodles if you want something more filling.

That said, the experience didn’t fully justify the price. It’s very expensive for what you get, and the taste was just okay. The meat quality was average, nothing memorable, and even with the dry seasoning powders they provide, it still didn’t compare to regular Chinese BBQ that comes properly grilled.

They gave us cheese on the house, but honestly… that thing was diabolical… it didn’t even melt. Service was decent though as the staff member kept checking in on us and made sure we were okay.

Overall, it was interesting to try once for the experience but I wouldn’t be back.

name: Eaterniti
document: Eaterniti . cuisine: Burmese Salad Noodles. located in Queens. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Downtown Queens… this tiny, 1-year old Burmese eatery shines !!  I was raised in Burma (now Myanmar) ~ and granted, that  was a looooooong time ago, but our family still cooks Burmese for many special occasions, as my wife loves it too.  Of course, our favorite dishes are dredged up from the depths of years of old memories and associations, and different family members have subtly altered these memories to where the resultant dish is not always something that I like.

Eaterniti is located off Queens Boulevard, in a small parking strip and adjacent to Popeye’s Louisiana Kitchen (yuck !) so access is usually easy.  They opened just over a year ago, and provide a small selection of generally authentic-tasting Burmese street food, snacks, salads, sweet tea, sugary and icy treats and a few actual entrée items using noodles, rice, etc., including the ubiquitous Khow Suey, which to me is the star of the show.  There is no real table seating – just a small counter with some 4 stools along one storefront.  Everything is clean and well maintained, so one feels good walking in.  The service is cheerful and fairly quick.  Though, many food delivery services frequent the place, so it can get hectic.

Discovering Burmese cuisine is always a must-check-it-out for us.  It was early for dinner, so we ordered a couple of snacks to try while waiting for out take-out order of khow suey for dinner later.  The Spring Rolls ($4.99) were crisp, wonderfully herbed, and fresh - this dish is something that is universal to all Far-eastern cuisines.  The Gin Thoke – ginger salad ($10.99) was also incredibly, fresh, very gingery and hot.  If you can’t handle hot foods, be careful.  Ask.

The garlic flavored Chicken & Noodle Khow Suey ($12.99) was eaten later for dinner when we got home.  Had to re-heat, so the noodles lost some of their freshness, but overall, the dish still tasted very authentic ~ probably one of the best we have eaten outside our own klitchen – so I don’t say that lightly.

I hope this establishment will thrive and spawn some more like it ~ the cuisine of Burma is varied though it’s a small country.  It offers a wide variety, like in neighboring Thailand, and must have more exposure in New York.

Highly recommended !  Will probably go back to try some more.  Thank you, folks.

This was my first time trying Burmese food and it was amazing!!  The tea leaf salad was so flavorful and I enjoyed the fried crunchy peanuts and pieces in it.  The potato pancake was fried perfectly and the sauce was tasty - very unique flavor, I can’t quite describe it but it paired well.  We ordered the chicken rice noodle dish and I have never had this type of noodle before; again super flavorful.  The chicken biryani was also good.  I will definitely come back again!

I am trying this hidden gem on Facebook reels and stopped by for a noodle dish before heading to the airport.
The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the free parking was a huge plus.
I couldn’t ask for more. I really wish we had more restaurants offering authentic Burmese flavors at such reasonable prices.
Keep up the great work!

Very good food and friendly people! Would recommend the Burmese pancake, which was   even better than it looked. Also the ginger salad. Very refreshing! The seating is fairly limited but people are in and out fast so we were able to sit and eat.

I’m officially a fan of Myanmar food…the tea leaf salad was so good!! Never knew it could be that crunchy.

The vermicili noodle also tastes good. Burmese food feels like a mix of Thai and Indonesian cuisine

document: Okay Noodle. cuisine: Noodles Comfort Food Hong Kong Style Cafe. located in Queens. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: A cozy and welcoming little place with a warm, down-to-earth vibe. The handmade noodles and fresh soup dumplings are delicious, and the BBQ skewers are excellent—especially the lamb. Definitely a spot worth coming back to.

I was very excited to see a Hong Kong style & authentic Chinese restaurant opened up in my area. Finding good & authentic Chinese food spots is a bit of a challenge here.

I’ve done take-out here 2x and ate there for dinner recently. I’ve eaten here before it was Okay Noodle so I knew the restaurant wasn’t too big to begin with. Last time I went my friend and I shared a steamed rice roll and a Chinese sausage clay pot rice.

The steamed rice roll was good, perfectly made. The clay pot rice could have been better. I felt like there wasn’t enough toppings or the ratio of rice to meat was limited.

The service was mediocre. I felt like we were rushed by one of the waiters after we were done eating when the restaurant wasn’t even crowded.

I think I prefer ordering take-out instead since I live close. Food was okay so far. I did wish they had dim sum dishes and congee too, maybe later on.

If you’ve been wondering where E Noodle in Flushing has gone, it’s here. The same owner of E Noodle opened Okay Noodle! (I asked the staff and the manager and cashier confirmed). Same good tastes and menu (and phone number), just in Elmhurst. Wonton noodle soup came with 4 dumplings, the soup tasted like a sweet dashi broth? Their noodles were crisp! We appreciated that the soup and noodles/wontons were separated since we got it to go. The beef chow fun was flavorful. It had a heavy oyster sauce taste that we liked. The chicken fried rice was pretty standard. The kids like it so we ordered it (note to parents: it does have onions in it but we pick it up for the kids and they happily eat it). Looking forward to coming by for their clay pot rice when we have more time.

Food is delicious and very authentic Hong Kong style. The handmade rice noodles have great texture, and the dumplings are fresh and flavorful. Small place but clean and cozy, and service was friendly. Definitely a great spot in Elmhurst. Will come back again.

I tried their curry dish and it was amazing. The curry flavor is rich, deep, and very aromatic. You can tell it’s made with a special, house-style blend of ingredients that you don’t find everywhere. The sauce is bold, comforting, and honestly a bit addictive. Definitely one of the best curry dishes I’ve had in Elmhurst.And the pearl noodle is really good and fresh also, I’ll be coming back for this again.

name: Hudson Smokehouse
document: Hudson Smokehouse. cuisine: Barbeque Steakhouses. located in Bronx. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: My brutha told me about this spot near 138th and the Bruckner Blvd that has good smoked foods. He's practically a meat connoisseur so I was curious to see what this place was about. The inside definitely gives me cozy, barbecue house vibes; the wooden furniture and bar was a nice touch. Kinda like how you would order at a fast food spot, you go up to the counter and order what you want and a waiter/waitress will bring you your order. They have a 5% off discount if you pay with cash 🫡 They have brunch and happy happy hour menus too, as well as catering. I had the 6 piece smoked jerk chicken wings with two sides, the mac and cheese and seasoned french fries. Everything tasted good to me 😋 I'm a big foodie so I'm content so long as I enjoy the meal. The jerk sauce was authentic, made me have a glass of water on standby. The meat was tender and cooked through and through. The Mac and cheese was flavorful and was made with a different noodle than the usual macaroni noodle (I forgot the name, but it's one of those spiral ones). The fries were seasoned well and not overpowering either 👌🏾 I also drank the Bacardi punch, it was sweet and refreshing in my opinion. I can definitely see myself coming back to this corner spot, I'm thankful for my brutha for inviting me out last night 😎🍗 He loved his food too 😁

I recently stopped by Hudson Smokehouse in the Bronx and ordered the brisket, turkey, mac & cheese, and baked beans.

The brisket was the standout: tender, properly smoked, and sliced thick enough to hold its structure without drying out. It had a deep, smoky flavor without being overpowered by sauce. The smoked turkey was equally impressive—juicy, well-seasoned, and a great lighter counterpoint to the brisket.

On the sides, the mac & cheese was rich and comforting with a solid balance of creaminess and bite, while the baked beans had good depth—slightly sweet, slightly savory, and clearly simmered with care rather than treated as an afterthought.

Service was friendly and efficient, and the overall atmosphere felt casual and unpretentious—exactly what you want when the focus is on the food. If you’re looking for reliable, well-executed barbecue in the Bronx, Hudson Smokehouse is absolutely worth a visit.

You will love this place. I thought I might not like ordering at the counter but our meal was at out table before I had a chance to take off my coat. Everything was very good moist and flavorful. Our drinks also arrived in a timely fashion and we had a great time it's a 10 outta 10 from me. Couldn't take a picture of the food because it was gone that fast.

We ate here with a large group of more than 50 people and the staff did a great job of keeping up with great service. Eight course meal including breads, cheese, pasta, greens, ravioli, chicken and more. Looking forward to my next visit. Thanks!

Pasquale’s Rigoletto – An Authentic Italian Gem in the Bronx

Pasquale’s Rigoletto is hands down one of my absolute favorite Italian restaurants. From the moment you step inside, you’re transported straight to Italy. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with pristine white linen tablecloths, elegantly contrasted by dark napkins, and a beautifully designed bar area that sets the perfect mood for a memorable dining experience. The staff is incredibly polite and attentive, making you feel right at home. Nicki, in particular, is the epitome of hospitality—welcoming, engaging, and ensuring that every guest feels special.

Let’s talk about the food—because that’s where Pasquale’s Rigoletto truly shines.

As soon as you’re seated, you’re presented with an authentic Italian dish that immediately sets the tone for the evening—roasted red peppers paired with sharp provolone cheese, all drizzled with high-quality olive oil. Enjoying this with a glass of perfectly paired Cabernet Sauvignon is the ideal way to begin your Italian culinary adventure.

Mozzarella in Carrozza – I couldn’t resist this classic dish, and I’m so glad I didn’t! This perfectly fried mozzarella sandwich was golden and crispy, reminiscent of an Italian sunset. The mozzarella stretched for miles, and the marinara sauce was fresh, aromatic, and bursting with balanced flavors. It was so delicious that I devoured it before I could even take a picture—a true testament to how amazing it was.

Ravioli with Pesto and Shrimp – This dish was pure perfection. The ravioli was fresh and delicate, enveloped in a creamy, nutty pesto sauce that was vibrant and packed with flavor. The generous portion of shrimp was cooked to perfection, adding a delightful seafood touch. My husband couldn’t resist scraping the plate to get every last drop of the pesto—it was that good!

Pollo e Gamberoni Alla Francese – The balance of lemon and white wine in this dish was flawless. The chicken was tender, flavorful, and cooked to perfection, while the shrimp added a delightful twist. The portion was so generous that I had enough for a late-night snack—always a win! Served with perfectly cooked penne, al dente and seasoned just right, it was a dish that left me completely satisfied.

To end the evening on a sweet note, the homemade Tiramisu was the perfect conclusion. Creamy, with the perfect balance of ladyfingers, mascarpone, and espresso, it was a true dolce delizioso. Not overly sweet, just the right finish to an exceptional meal.

Pasquale’s Rigoletto captures the essence of authentic Italian cuisine, delivering a dining experience that feels like a journey through Italy. Whether you’re a local or visiting from out of town, this restaurant is a must-visit. If you’re looking for top-notch Italian dishes, attentive service, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere, look no further. I can’t recommend Pasquale’s Rigoletto highly enough—you’ll leave with a full heart and an even fuller stomach.

Buon Appetito 🇮🇹

google_reviews.text:
I had 1 concern out of my entire experience! There is a fee to use a card, which is abnormal for the guest to pay unless it's a small charge. $9 card fee on top of a $300 bill didnt really make sense..

Aside from that..
I had a great experience at Umi Seafood Buffet and chose to celebrate my birthday here with my family.
We came as a table of 10, and everything from start to finish was smooth and enjoyable.

The host, a young male, was very kind and accommodating, which made arriving with a large group easy and stress-free. Our server — a friendly woman with short hair — was especially great: attentive, efficient, and welcoming without being overbearing. She handled our table really well and made sure everything stayed on track.

The restaurant itself is very easy to navigate and self-explanatory, which I appreciated. Everything was clearly laid out, accessible, and simple to move through, even with a big group. The space felt comfortable and relaxed, making it a great place for a family outing or celebration.

Overall, the experience was fun, smooth, and well-organized. I left feeling happy and well taken care of, and I’d definitely return.

Umi Hotpot is such a fun spot to eat at. There’s a wide selection of food, including sushi, seafood, hot dishes, desserts, and more, and everything we tried was fresh and tasty. The ramen surprised me in the best way… super comforting and really good for a buffet. The place is clean, the staff is attentive, and you definitely get your money’s worth. A perfect pick if you’re craving variety and want to leave full and happy! 🍣🥢🍜

I came here for weekend lunch with my dad and overall had a really good experience. The food quality was solid and there’s a huge selection, especially if you love seafood. Tons of options across the buffet — although I was a little sad there weren’t any scallops.

One thing to note: many of the buffet items aren’t labeled, so it can be hard to tell exactly what you’re picking up. Also, not every tray has its own serving tongs, so sometimes you have to borrow from another dish. That could be a downside if you have food allergies or strict dietary preferences.

The atmosphere is really cool — lots of Asian-themed decor and calming music that makes the space feel relaxed rather than chaotic. The restaurant and bathrooms were both clean, which I always appreciate.

Service was adequate. The staff were polite, just not especially warm or chatty. They charge a 12% service fee and tips are not expected.

It is on the pricier side (and even more expensive during dinner and weekends), but honestly, I think it’s worth it for the amount of selection and quality. If you want to try it at a lower price point, I’d recommend going during weekday lunch first.

And side note: they include unlimited boba tea with the buffet, which is kind of amazing. At other places, that alone can cost close to $10 each. Here, it’s included — and yes, I had multiple.

Overall, I’d come back. If you go in knowing what to expect price-wise, it’s a fun experience with a lot of options.

Honestly the best buffet around. But of course, like with every buffet, there are hit and miss dishes but most of them are very good. Only down side is the wait time. Just be prepare to wait 1-2+ hrs depending on day and time you go. You can use a kiosk upon entering to add your party to the queue and they text you when it’s ready. Highly recommend to pay attention to where you are in line so you can come back if you do decide to leave.

**Now I decided to add this part in but just know it’s not part of the buffet food.** They had this Facebook promotional event where they’ll ask you to post their flyer on your Facebook page and each person who post will get steak and lobster for free. They didn’t seem to be opening advertising it in the restaurant, seems to be an ask to know basis. We only found out about it after another table personally told/show us. Now, that was fun and all, steak was good but lobster was RAW. We notified the server, he told us to cook the lobster in the hot pot broth if we need it more cooked. Not the response we expected but it’s free so I won’t complain. I figured these would be helpful for others to know.

Lee’s Tavern is a staple on Staten Island, and for good reason. The pizzas are among the crown jewels of Staten Island, and the bar itself is just a classic, cozy, hole in the wall kind of place.

We had fried calamari, an Italian shredded pork hero, a white clam pie, and a regular pie (half with sweet peppers). The calamari was great. It was fried perfectly and the hot marinara sauce was really good with a nice kick. The pork hero was very basic, and though it lacked a bit in flavor, the ingredients all tasted very fresh and the cheese was melted very nicely, I enjoyed it quite a bit. The pies at Lee’s speak for themselves. The white clam pie is delicious, it’s a perfect balance of garlic, cheese, and that classic Italian clam taste. document: Bar Mexicana. cuisine: Mexican Cocktail Bars Beer Bar. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We randomly walked by and heard the music, and it immediately caught our attention. We originally stopped in for a couple of drinks,but ended up trying some tacos too. Their happy hour selections are great,every day from 4pm–6pm with select cocktails and $3 mini tacos.

The drinks were solid, especially for happy hour. From the food menu, I tried the Calabaza Crema taco (zucchini) and loved it ,such an amazing vegetarian option! The guacamole was also great, though the tortilla chips were a bit too salty.

Overall, we had a good experience and would come back again!

I was honestly shocked at how affordable this place is, especially for being right in the heart of Manhattan. The prices are incredibly reasonable, and the food tastes amazing. I ordered a margarita and the chef’s tower everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The food was so good that I ended up ordering tacos and quesadillas to take home, plus their street corn, which is a must try. The restaurant itself is clean and has a nice, casual atmosphere. My only small complaint is that after my order was taken, I didn’t see my waiter again and had to flag down another server for help. Other than that, I have zero complaints. Overall, if you’re in Manhattan and looking for a budget friendly spot with great food and generous portions, I’d definitely recommend this place. You’ll be pleasantly surprised

I was excited to try Bar Mexicana, the new sister restaurant to Mermaid Oyster Bar, which is one of my longtime local favorites. Naturally, I was delighted to see this spot open right next door to Mermaid’s Times Square location.

Bar Mexicana’s menu is concise, featuring staple, authentic Mexican dishes and classic cocktails. As expected, every item is made with simple, fresh ingredients, and the quality really shines through.

For our first visit, we ordered quite a spread: Birria Empanadas, Pozole, Guacamole, Pollo Asado, Carne Asado, Birria Tacos, and the Carne Asado Burrito. We also tried the Cadillac Margarita and Mojitorita.
•	The Birria Empanadas were incredibly flavorful, and the consommé was perfection.
•	The Pozole was light, refreshing, and comforting—especially nice after coming in from the cold.
•	The tacos were generously filled, and the meats were tender and delicious.
•	The drinks were well-made, tasty, and refreshing.

We genuinely enjoyed every dish. The staff was attentive, friendly, and accommodating. They even moved us to a larger table to ensure we had enough room for all the food we ordered.

That said, the overall maintenance and cleanliness of the restaurant could use some attention.
•	Our first table was wobbly, and although the staff quickly fixed it with a coaster, it wasn’t the most comfortable start.
•	When we moved to the new table, the chair I sat on was noticeably wobbly as well, which made the furniture feel a bit cheap for a new establishment.
•	The biggest disappointment was discovering gum stuck underneath the table, which is very off-putting, especially just as you’re settling in to eat.

These issues didn’t overshadow the excellent food and service, but they’re worth noting. With better attention to cleanliness and sturdier furniture, Bar Mexicana has the potential to be just as beloved as its sister restaurant.

Overall, I’d definitely give it another try. The food is authentic, fresh, and flavorful, and the staff is wonderful so I’m hopeful they’ll tighten up the maintenance as they get settled in.

This authentic Mexican gem right in the heart of Times Square! The food is incredibly flavorful and clearly made with care, the atmosphere is lively and welcoming, and the service is truly superior. On top of that, the value is outstanding for such a prime location. A must-visit especially if you are a large family!!!!

The Cantina Nachos were soooo good. We got it with steak. The sauces and steak were incredible. The steak quesadilla was also 10/10. Very cheesy and lots of steak pieces. Very nice atmosphere. Kind staff. Reasonably priced.

document: Saperavi. cuisine: Georgian Soup Wine Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We’ve visited Supra twice already this month, and every time the experience has been amazing. The food is incredibly flavorful, satisfying, and beautifully presented you can truly feel the care in every detail.
I especially want to recognize Ana for her outstanding service. She is attentive to every detail and always there exactly when you need her. Supra has officially become our favorite restaurant again. Thank you for such a wonderful experience.

This was my first time trying out Georgian cuisine, and boy did it live up to my expectations! The restaurant was pretty packed for a Sunday night, but we were seated within ten minutes of our arrival. We were served complimentary champagne while we perused the menu.

We started off with some chicken croquettes that were crispy and mildly flavoured to begin with. Then, we had their ajaruli khachapuri — this was sooooo good. The combination of the cheese mixed with the butter and egg tasted delicious. The khachapuri was pretty big and can easily be started between four people. Then came the pork and beef khinkali which basically consists of three/five huge dumplings(you can choose the amount) — the mincemeat stuffing is mildly spiced and the whole dumpling is kinda soupy but it tastes great.

After all these dishes we were sorta full, but still decided to order the mixed grill platter which came with three kinds of meat (pork, chicken, and lamb), roasted potatoes, roasted bell peppers and three kinds of dips. The kebab pieces were again quite generously sized and we were unable to finish them all so we decided to pack them up.
I don’t know where we had the space after all this to think about dessert but we did!! 😅 We ended up getting their honey cake which tasted great and was totally worth it!

All in all, the whole experience — service, food, ambience — was simply superb. Loved it absolutely. :)

Went for a Galentines celebration brunch. Every dish was delicious and fresh! Only one server for the main area so service was slow but once we ordered the food came out fast! Would recommend: pancakes, mushroom omelette, cheese/potato dumpings, sokos khachapuri, and Lobio kotanshi.

FANTASTIC!! Everything was phenomenal! Service was friendly & attentive. The lamb chops were especially delicious and the khachapuri will satisfy any cheese lovers palate. An excellent choice for medium to large groups so you can share as much as possible!

Also, I noticed the separate bar area which was spacious and tucked away from the rest of the bustling restaurant which looks like a great date spot!

Staff is friendly and diverse. Very fast service and the restaurant itself does feel
georgian.

Food was horrible though. Maybe for an untrained american tastebud it would be different and full of flavors but in reality the food was, to say the most, edible.

They do not have anything actually authentic outside of sauces and lemonade.

Pork Mtsvadi (bbq) came absolutely raw. The inside was dripping blood and not in a way that’s actually tasty.
I sliced one and they replaced only one slice after that, I sliced all of it and discovered all of them were raw. Again, not in a way that was actually tasty or on purpose. They just plain undercooked it. Gladly, it was taken out of the check. Staff was friendly.

Khinkali dough was not machine kneaded it was hand knead so it was uneven and unprofessional, in my opinion. The beef in Khinkali was dense. It was like biting into a meatball rather than what it actually should have been.

Potatos with tarragon sauce were mildly good.

I would not recommend to go here because it didn’t taste Georgian at all. I am Georgian so I would know.
They do not have actual unique or authentic Georgian tastes.

Went there hoping to taste home for a minute. Ended up angry.

The tuk trey koh kong wasn't as potent as I expected it to be, but the oysters were good. The meekatang had a lot of woodear mushrooms and lacked some flavor. The wings were pretty good. Overall, it just didn't taste very authentically Khmer. 😕 Maybe I have to try it again.

Unfortunately the short rib was unavailable but overall the meal was good.

Fried chicken and the duck were great mains and the morning glory was very flavorful. I think the crab fried rice was a slight miss because it lacked flavor and the fried rice noodles was interesting but definitely too saucey.

Overall cute restaurant and would recommend.

google_reviews.text:
I happened to be in the area on some errands and felt like having Thai food. I searched on Google for a Thai restaurant that looked appealing and reasonably priced. This place immediately caught my attention due to its excellent reviews and the fact that it had opened fairly recently. Most importantly, the prices were mid-range and very reasonable for me.

Once we were seated and ordered our drinks and food, I was impressed from the very beginning by the warm welcome. The restaurant atmosphere was comfortable, clean, and inviting. The waiting time for each dish was short, which was another pleasant surprise. As for the taste, it was outstanding—well-balanced, rich in flavor, and made with fresh ingredients. The overall experience felt like dining at a high-quality Thai restaurant in a five-star hotel I once stayed at in Bangkok.

Yep, the hype is real. The coconut beverage was delish! The wings were crispy and flavorful, the crab curry and brown rice was divine, and the coconut pudding was one of the best desserts I’ve had (not overly sweet)!!
I will definitely be back!

Absolutely loved this place! The food was incredibly authentic, flavorful, and clearly made with high-quality ingredients. Every dish we tried was well-balanced and full of rich, bold Thai flavors. You can tell they really care about getting it right. The atmosphere was welcoming and the service was great too. Highly recommend if you’re craving real Thai food that tastes just like it should!

It is always comforting to come across an authentic Thai restaurant amidst the bustling of NYC. Every dish we ordered at Samyan was perfectly cooked. Drinks were exceptionally delicious. And the presentation was just wow! Samyan serves authentic Thai food that is outstanding like no others. Strongly recommend and will definitely come back with friends and family.
Incredible meal, immaculate service. Recommend the curry chicken - divine - and the basil friend rice - to die for. Great for dine in and take out!

name: Fish Bone
document: Fish Bone. cuisine: Fish & Chips. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We had a wonderful dinner at the Flying Fishbone. The fish cakes, seafood pasta with white wine cream sauce and grilles shrimp were all delicious. Rommell was an excellent server who went above and beyond to make my husband's birthday special.

We arrived at 5:30 and didn't not have a reservation. We were sat promptly at a table with a great view.

We will return when we come back to Aruba.

Food:
The food was great—tasty and flavorful all around. I ordered the grilled shrimp and swapped the sides for fried rice instead of what was listed on the menu, and they were very flexible with substitutions, which I appreciated. Everyone at the table enjoyed their meals. For 6 people, the bill came out to around $500… and somehow everyone managed to order about two drinks each 😅.

Atmosphere:
Absolutely beautiful and romantic. The setting is scenic, right by the water, and the sound of the calm waves is peaceful and relaxing. This is definitely a dress-up kind of place. We all wore dresses with flats since you’re walking in the sand—they have an area where you can leave your shoes, which is a nice touch.

Service:
This is where it fell a bit short. The service was average to below average. Our server checked on us maybe once or twice, and the first time was only because I asked the bus boy to get her so we could order another round of drinks. Compared to other tables around us, we weren’t checked on very often. I’d rate the service a 3 out of 5 stars. That said, we still left an $80 tip.

Overall:
Great food and an amazing atmosphere—worth it for the experience and setting alone. Just wish the service matched the level of the rest of the restaurant.

Loved this place. Great unique location but requires better taste in ambiance and decor. It has HUGE potential. The food is absolutely delicious.  Food to remember.  Well presented.  Great options. Amazing deserts.  The service over all lacked a lot of attention & simple common wait services. Very distracted and forgetful and not on topic the tables. Our waiter was better than the rest of the staff but was not great either. Other than that I highly recommend it.

Very nice place.  You must make reservations.  If you want to get seated with feet in water,  there is only 1 seating at 4pm.

We sat with get in the water and ended up with a table near the edge.

There is a shelf to leave your shoes and also a very nice foot Washing station to clean your feet on the way out.

We started with the oysters New Orleans style.   It was really good.

Then came the Roasted Artichoke & Goat Cheese Salad.   So good.

I got the Chicken Portobello.  It was delicious and it was a huge portion. It can actually be shared with 2 people.

My husband got the seafood pasta.   He enjoyed it.

For desert we hot the Baked Alaska which is set on fire at the table. The ice cream and sponge cake part was good. I didn't love the merengue and sambuca part of it.  I thought the merengue would be a little harder but it was soft.  The sambuca was a bit strong.  But after we mixed it all together,  it was fine

Excellent food! Very cool vibe and view!! Some tables even were partially in the water! All 4 of us were happy with our food and highly recommend! The view is awesome, so try to go before the sunsets! We had a reservation at 6:30p in January and the sun was just setting so we almost missed it.

name: Nourish
document: Nourish. cuisine: Thai Asian Fusion. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: *UPDATE* The last time I went here I was given food that was incompatible with my dietary needs, even after I explained the medical/health necessity. I am Muslim, so I also have religious preferences which were completely ignored (no pork). It's unfortunate that this happened because the service was pretty good at first, but the quality is obviously declining.** I have been going here to get food for a few months now, so I can give an unbiased review. We have been relying on Nourish Now to help us get through the month because my Saudi prince husband works in the US Army and he isn't here right now, so we're basically living in poverty. One of the best things about Nourish Now is that they do their best to accommodate food allergies and other dietary restrictions. That's important for me because I'm Muslim, diabetic, and I have a couple of food sensitivities. There was only one time where I had an issue with the food because they gave me several items containing pork and there were several gluten containing items, but I called and spoke to Paisley who  was apologetic, agreeable, and helped me arrange another appointment. They give a good mix of fresh and nonperishable items, with sweets included (which I literally need to live! 🎂🍬🍭🍪😆).Our interactions are always pleasant when we visit and I must say that they're probably the best food pantry in the area. 💯
Great people and a great cause what else could you want for your community.

I love Nourish Now! Not only do they give you good quality foods, plus catered items from restaurants, they give you fresh flowers from Trader Joe's!!!  I always come home and make the most beautiful flower arrangements and I have at least a week's worth of food for the family.  Keep up the good work!!!

A large cake was delivered to us by mistake - free and unopened. We called the bakery to correct the error and they told us to keep it.  I guess if we had a large family this would be a great thing but my husband and I were a bit bewildered.  The last thing we wanted was to waste this cake. We were desperately searching Google, looking for a place on a Friday night that was open for donation.  We found and cold-called Nourish Now - the only food pantry we could find with an off-hours phone number.  Thanks to the founder (who personally answered the phone, and drove over to pick up the cake) this beautiful cake will find its way to people who can enjoy it.  I will sleep better tonight knowing that this wonderful organization exists trying to bridge the gap between food waste and hunger.  A HUGE THANK YOU to you and your team!

Everyone is so very nice and it's welcoming to see a smiling face. Unlike Manna where you have to wait in line when you call for a food pickup they give you an available appointment. This allows them to concentrate totally on you and you're in and out after filling out a monthly form which takes all of 2-3minutes. The food is always good and I noticed donated by Trader Joe's Wegmans. There are plenty of snacks, cookies and cakes to choose from and you can take as many as you need. This month I received 2 steaks, chicken drumsticks, Angus beef hotdogs and a small roast. I also got eggs.fruit, potatoes, bagels etc.and and though I still go to Manna I prefer them so much more!

name: Holic Thai Bistro
document: Holic Thai Bistro. cuisine: Thai. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
They had me at $14 Lunch Special!
And the food is actually Good!
Holic is a great spot, it's cozy, and beautifully designed. The ladies running the front end are very good, I've never had an issue. My family has been here several times on Saturday and has tried different dishes, the food is consistently good. This might be my new favorite Thai Spot!

I chose Holic Thai Bistro for a lunch meet up with a friend because of the location. I was delighted that I chose this beautiful restaurant when I walked in! The decor and atmosphere was great. It's a small restaurant but typical for NYC/BK and the layout flowed perfectly! I wanted to try so many things on the menu but decided to get the dumpling soup and a side a fried rice because it was 20 degrees outside! The food was great just the right amount of wontons and bok choy to fill me all the way up! The staff was very attentive gave great feedback and information on menu items. I had a lychee Thai iced tea for the first time which was great and included 2 sweet lychee fruits. My friend has the chive pancakes they were crispy and different from other chive pancakes but the flavor was on point. The green curry was also delicious! Overall I'll definitely go back great staff, very good food and beautiful atmosphere!

We visited this Thai restaurant for dinner around 5 p.m. It was already quite busy, but luckily we were seated right away. The interior was cozy and slightly dimly lit, with nice décor and a lively atmosphere. Even the restroom was clean and well-maintained, which I always appreciate.

For my entrée, I ordered a stir-fried minced pork dish cooked with basil, garlic, and Thai green chili, served with rice and topped with a fried egg — a classic Thai street-style meal. It was incredibly flavorful, made with fresh ingredients, and perfectly balanced in spice and aroma. The portion size was generous — I couldn’t finish it all and ended up taking the leftovers home for another meal.

Overall, the food quality was excellent, the service smooth, and the atmosphere pleasant. Definitely a great spot for authentic, flavorful Thai food — highly recommended, and I’d gladly return!
My go to Thai place when I was living in Crown Heights. The food tasted close to what I had in Bangkok. Highly recommend the crab curry, drunken noodles and green curry!
Mini is the best waitress and bartender! Fantastic service, friendly and super helpful staff, food is AMAZING, cocktails are great & strong. Highly recommend

name: Barbuto Brooklyn
document: Barbuto Brooklyn. cuisine: Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: We really enjoyed the atmosphere here! The restaurant is located inside 1 Hotel, and the decor is super nice. Plus, the views of the NYC skyline are nice. The food was delicious, with generous portions. We ordered the focaccia as a starter, but my only critique is that they brought it out with the main courses instead of before. We didn't really get to enjoy it as an appetizer, which was a bummer. That said, the portions are a great size. Chiken & Mahi Mahi (dorado) super recommended.

This was our first visit to Barbuto in Brooklyn. Everything was perfect. Vibe is great: beautiful, elegant and casual at the same time, a nice mix of locals coming in for a pizza, and maybe some folks who had traveled there staying at hotel, and people who may have been there for a celebration (us!). Josh took care of our table and did not miss a beat, and the rest of the team seamlessly made things appear(and disappear as needed) from our table. Everything from being greeted upon arrival until we walked out into the chilly night was lovely. We were there to celebrate the 95th birthday of my partner's mother who had recently moved from Manhattan to (assisted living in) Brooklyn Heights. We did not know that Barbuto had a Brooklyn location until we searched for places not far from her new home; we've always loved Barbuto in Manhattan, so we knew we could trust this for our celebration and it was even better than expected. We had: champagne toast; focaccia and breadsticks; burrata and proscuitto; polpettone (meatballs); pasta bambini; pasta with wild boar ragu x2; chocolate budino x2; red wine by the glass (both Italian, wonderful -- Josh checked with the sommelier about which glass of red I should have with my dinner, which, coincidentally, was also wonderful with my chocolate dessert, I was happy I had a couple of sips left). All of the food was divine. When the meatballs arrived, the fragrance of basil was so welcoming on freezing cold night. (I shared this as an appetizer with my partner, but I honestly could've had this as my main course!). The three of us loved every bite of what each of us ordered. The chocolate budino arrived with a candle for my partner's mother, which lit up her face with a smile, and that smile got a lot wider after her first bite. I was glad that we also got a second budino for my partner and I to share, but there were other desserts that looked incredibly wonderful, everything from tiramisu to pistachio cake to a blood orange sorbet -- next time (there will be a next time!).

We visited Barbuto for our company holiday dinner, which is close enough to Barclay’s (for a Nets game afterwards). I walked in the door and felt like I got the vibe of the place immediately. That isn’t always the case at places to eat, as sometimes a place doesn’t really know its own vibe. Cool and chill, and every person I encountered on the short walk to the table was inviting and friendly. The menu is kind of funky and somewhat hard to read but full of grey options. We started with tuna, salad, focaccia bread and the carpaccio. We were 5 and this was plenty to share and whet the appetite. I had the sea bass, which was very good (on a bed of squash) but the chicken appeared to be the winner; just make sure you are hungry if you order the yard bird. It comes as a roasted half. The gnocchi was also ordered and was a similar large portion. Desserts were equally varied and sounded amazing although we did not order any. Our server knew the menu inside and out and could not have been more friendly and fun. Add all of this up and then check the view outside of the Freedom Tower, Brooklyn Bridge and lower Manhattan and you get a dynamite spot for a date or lively get together. If you end up having to wait for a table, no worries bc the lobby for the hotel that is opposite the entrance to the restaurant is a very cool space on it’s own.

Tarren was our server and truly made our brunch a special occasion.  She's funny and friendly.  Best of all she knows the menu quite well with great recommendations.  Food arrived in a timely manner and the rest of the staff was great!  Thank you for a memorable experience!

The place itself feels relaxing and very pleasant — lots of live green plants, soft sunlight that makes it feel like a greenhouse, and great background music. The service is attentive and calm.

The food is average. The fish tartare wasn’t marinated enough for my taste — it lacked a bit of salt and spice. Other dishes were fine but nothing memorable.

Around 4–5 pm it’s pretty quiet, which makes it perfect for an early dinner.

name: Bites of Xi'an
document: Bites of Xi'an. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Burgers. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
During our trip to New York, it was very cold and rainy. As we were walking by Bites of Xi’an, we decided to step inside to warm up and grab something to eat — and we were pleasantly surprised.

Since it was our first time there, the staff kindly helped us choose. You can simply tell them what you like, and they’ll take care of the rest. The food was outstanding — incredible flavor, generous portions, and handmade noodles. The soup was packed with meat and tasted absolutely amazing. It was exactly what we needed on a cold, rainy day.

The moment you step inside, the atmosphere makes you feel like you’re somewhere in Asia — the artwork, the staff, the food — everything creates a very authentic experience.

Highly recommended!

I was pleasantly surprised eating the spicy hot oil seared hand-ripped noodles from this restaurant.  The noodles were springy and had the unique texture that comes from hand-pulling.  The dish does carry a kick, and there’s a deceptive amount of pork in the dish, even more than can be seen in the photo.  The food was pretty good, but the restaurant is slightly unclean.  I came right when they opened, and there was still food and litter on the floor from the day before.  Also, the restaurant only accepted cash on the day I ate there, which was a slight inconvenience.  I would definitely check with the cashier in advance before ordering.  Overall, the food was tasty, but the atmosphere inside left a little to be desired.

Excellent Xian food. Very authentic.
It is a small shop as part of a small chain. But excellent  food. The beef noodle  is very good and tasty.  They hand make the noodle here. Exactly as I expected.  The Rou Jia Mo (Chinese sandwich) is also great. The bread is fresh, flaky and soft. Highly recommend.
Good noodles, not too gluteny. Stewed beef noodle soup broth is a little watery and salty. But the dry noodles with meat sauce are very good. Great prices!

This is my 2nd time coming here. Albeit 3rd try. The first time coming it was delicious! The 2nd try, I was with a friend. We walked two hours looking for this place as I couldn't remember the name of it. After buying a zipper in the fashion distract and being late for a comedy class (broken leg/navigating New York in a wheelchair and faulty public transportation/elevators). I had just left the fabric store and was looking to have a meal at Bites of X'ian and low and behold! It was across the street, no need to google! (Though O had just pulled out the phone to google a location).

Ordered the cripsy sandwich (later snack) and the spicy beef noodle soup. Nothing like good comfort food on an otherwise failed day! Was sitting in the restaurant somewhat stressed as I finished the soup and a smile came over my face. It was at that moment, I set the bowl down and wrote the review. With a satisfied smile on the face.

If you don't like American Chinese, prefer healthier good tasting food, and are in NYC, definitely take the time to stop and have a bite. You will not be disappointed!

From the jerk chicken plantain pizza to the turkey or snapper Tiboush platter to the exquisite djon djon rice, it was all amazing, well seasoned amd balanced food. Don't even get me started on the smoked herring!!!!!!  That right there was just too much!  It was so good, I can't even articulate how good it was. To top it off, we had a passion fruit lemonade that was a perfect accompaniment to a meal. When I come back to NYC again, this is defo my spot!  Fantastic place.

This is hands down one of my favorite spots to eat. The Bunnan sandwiches are packed with flavor and they offer a great variety of options. I love that the menu goes beyond the usual, where else can you find plantain pizza. The plantain pizza especially is so unique and delicious. If you're looking to experience authentic Haitian flavors, this is definitely the place to go. The staff is super friendly and welcoming, which makes the whole experience even better.

This place is a hit! I absolutely love the green plantain griot (pork) sandwich.  The meat was tender and flavorful.  I also had the passion fruit juice which was a nice pairing.  The sandwich had caramelized onion and shredded red cabbage.  There was a small container of sauce on the side - could have been a vinaigrette (not sure).  Whatever it was, it all went together really well together.

This was my first time here and the customer service from heidi & tanhny was amazing.  Heidi was extremely patient with answering any questions I had. Food was so flavorful and reasonable regarding pricing. I will definitely be back !

BUNNANBK! The BK is for Brooklyn… when I say I’ve seen this on TikTok and specifically came to NY to try this I’m not kidding. Nothing is better than sweet plantain with juicy/tender meat. I had to give the sandwiches and the sampler a go. I tried one sandwich with the goat tassot, the jerk chicken and for the sampler one mushroom, one red snapper and two goats. Highly highly recommend the goat, it was extremely flavorful, juicy and tender. Hands down the best out of the others. Paired with the sandwiches was the passion fruit lemonade, absolutely refreshing. This quick service is located in a small town hall with a ton of different shops, food places and vendors. You can shop around for other island favorites whether it’s food or merchandise while you wait on your food to be completed.

name: Makan House
document: Makan House. cuisine: Malaysian Chinese Singaporean. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I came to this restaurant with my friends for the first time and we simply ordered three appetizers.
We didn’t expect them to be so tasty and delicious. The staff were very friendly, especially our server, Tingting. Her service was excellent, and her sunny smile made the dining experience even more enjoyable. And the atmosphere was great.
My friends and I will definitely come back next time! 😄

Shortened version of my much, much longer Yelp review- I went to this Malaysian place a couple of weeks ago with a large group. I have had Malaysian food from many different restaurants, and this was excellent across the board with a couple of definite highlights. The place was crowded and the staff was friendly, though a bit overwhelmed, so it took a while for the food to come out. This was also likely the reason why they forgot about one of our dishes (the Hainanese Chicken,) which was unfortunate, but we were full enough anyway. You can see below what we ordered and what my recommendations are-

Beef Rendang- Excellent. Semi-dry style. Could use a tad more heat but very flavorful with tender beef
Crispy Rice- Excellent. Excellent wok hei and texture. Plenty of scallion oil for flavor and a good amount of shrimp
Kangkung Belachan- Very good. Nicely cooked water spinach and a good amount of funk.
Trengganu Duck- Very good. Nice curry. Tender duck though there were bones. Plenty of veggies.
Chow Zhou Tilapia Fish- Good. Reminded me of some Canto fish dishes but a bit sweeter.
Kajang Beef Satay- Good/standard. Good beef. Standard satay
Coconut Butter Chicken- Alright. A bit light in flavor.
Ice Kacang- Alright. Not sweet enough. A bit bland

Would recommend. The rendang over rice is also a tasty reasonably priced option for takeout

Ordered the lunch special and received an unrequested extra special portion of rice. The Cheng Mai chicken was alright and dry. The general Tso was a bit bland (not enough sauce) had way too much rice not enough protein and left me hungry. Will just head over to Wing Hing Seafood restaurant next time for their lunch- they have better portions for the price.

I'm so glad I ignored the negative reviews. If you want delicious Malaysian food be sure to try Makan House. We had the beef rendang, drunken noodle, Malaysian pork chop, and roti canai.  Every dish was delicious.  The beef was tender and flavorful.  The deep-fried Malaysian pork chop was crispy and delicious.  The staff was friendly and made us feel at home.

There are several large round tables. The owner is friendly and works fast. The staffs might be a little overwhelmed with the owner’s fast pace. The owner needed to remind staffs several times to get rices or drinks to the table.

The food is a hit and missed. The roti tasted like store bought. The chicken and beef were ok. The sweet and sour fish is a winner. It’s not printed on the menu but it was written on the wall as special.

google_reviews.text: If you love sushi or specialty rolls you should try here. We came here on Thursday lunch AYCE. Weekday lunch buffet is about 28 or 29 per person. The food is fresh and made to order. Try their specialty rolls. It was delicious. You order thru a ipad. The kitchen items I like shrimp tempura, Kani salad and fried squid. I try their pork katsu it was too thin and dry. The space is small but the service was good. If you pay cash you get small discount.

With regular and holiday pricing, absolutely not worth spending $60 per person (with tip) because you get full way faster than you realize and don’t get your moneys worth! But lunching pricing? $28 for that much good sushi? I’ve been going back extra early just to get that lunch menu.

The fish are so fresh, everything just melts in your mouth. Everything is flavorful and I just wish I could keep ordering if only my stomach would allow it. I don’t think there was a single bad menu item. Even if I didn’t like the flavor, it was never because of their culinary skills but my personal taste. You can tell everything is made professionally. The place is much smaller than the Flushing location however, with a lot of workers running around and kind of hovering over you, but if that doesn’t bother you, go!

Best AYCE sushi (during lunch!)

The Dragon Balls are absolutely delicious deff a standout! Overall, this was a fantastic experience. The sushi was super fresh and the rice to fish ratio is honestly one of the best I’ve come across perfectly balanced in every bite. All you can eat for $45 is perfect. I’d definitely recommend this spot to anyone craving quality sushi!!

Small tip: Keep an eye on your orders and stay on top of the staff since you only get 2 hours for the unlimited menu.

Really delicious food as always! The fish is the freshest and the flavor of everything we ordered was amazing. The only complaint we had was how cold the restaurant was. Not sure why the heat wasn’t turned on as it is the middle of winter. Other than that, our experience was lovely.

name: Wong Kwong Hop
document: Wong Kwong Hop. cuisine: Chinese. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
The steamed rice rolls at Wong Kwong Hop are BACK starting this weekend 9/28/24! (They had a labor shortage these past few years). This is where you get the best steamed rice rolls in Elmhurst, Queens. These fresh cheung fun are currently available only on the weekends. They’re steamy, pillowy, and piping hot - all starting at just $3. Definitely recommend adding an egg in for an extra 50 cents. For the sauces, we get them all - hot sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and peanut sauce. Come earlier in the day, before 2/3pm, I’d say, before they run out for the day. Don’t forget to bring cash to pay!

While you’re here, this spot also makes fresh soy milk and tofu in-house daily. Love their springy, cold, and refreshing grass jelly as well. This is a true tofu factory where you can just walk in and get fresh tofu, directly from the source. They distribute tofu to many businesses throughout Elmhurst, Flushing, and Chinatown.

Pricing as of Sept 2024:
$2 tofu pudding/bean curd dessert
$2.75 grass jelly
$1.75 soy milk
$3 beef rice rolls
$3 pork rice rolls
+ $0.50 egg
Great soy and rice noodle products at reasonable prices. They have fresh rice rolls with toppings on the weekend. Their grass jelly and tofu fa are great too! Cash only.
They have the best soy bean milk around, and us much cheaper than grocery stores. The soy flavor is super strong and is made fresh everyday. The fried tofu and soy bean tofu are also really good.

Workers, Please don’t smoke inside the shop where all the food is being processed. It’s unsanitary and would you like it if someone smokes and then there’s a chance that ash from the cigarette can land on the food? Not cool right. Despite all that , overall great rice noodles.

I saw somebody mentionned this on IG and decided to give it a try.
My first time visiting, the place was crowded. There was a line. I ordered rice roll with egg. They are somewhat chewy. Better than other street vendors, can't compare to with dim sum restaurant.
Small size of soy milk was good. Not too sweet. Tofu ho is not too sweet.
Overall the flavor is on the blended size but the food itself is good.

document: Mrs Georgia. cuisine: Georgian Bakeries Soup. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Wow! What a great evening visiting Mrs. Georgia. This was my first time having Georgian food and I was very pleased about it. From the moment we walked in we were greeting with friendly smiles and great service. The khachapuri and the khinkali dumplings were so good, you must try. The meal was filling but also not that expensive. I will definitely be back!

I visited a Georgian restaurant in Astoria, which is a beautiful country I'd visited on a trip. I ordered traditional Georgian Kvebri wine, khachapuri, ojakhuri, and eggplant rolls, and they were all hands down. Definitely, I'll try other dishes next time. The staff was friendly and attentive. If you've never tried Georgian cuisine, I highly recommend giving it a try.

Mrs. Georgia is the best kept secret in New York City! The adjaruli khachapuri and imeruli khachapuri are must trys. They are rich, creamy homemade cheese and the bread is perfectly baked and yeasty. The khinkal are juicy, gigantic soup dumplings that are incredibly savory and delicious—I especially appreciated their vegetarian options. We ordered two plates at first and ended up getting two more because they were so good! The mushroom and cheese are so satisfying for vegetarians and unlike anything you can order elsewhere. Their pumpkin soup is divinely velvety resembling a creamy butternut squash. We also loved their double fried fries and arepa cornbread, which pairs well with salad or soup. Their selection of Georgian wine is also not to be missed!

As amazing as the food is the ambiance, it is cozy, clean, and incredibly inviting. We spent hours just leisurely chatting and eating. Even the bathroom was remarkably decorated, with little details like Parisian perfume sprays in the handwashing station. I really appreciate how much thought they put into everything! For a large meal for five, it came out to just over $35 per person, which was a steal for how much food we got.

I make the trip to Brighton Beach every time I miss Georgian food, but I’m so excited that Mrs. Georgia has brought the best Georgian food to Astoria, Queens!

What a fabulous find!  Had the best meal starting with lovely red wine 🍷 .  The meal was fantastic as well starting with Khinkali ( dumplings) With Beef - than Adjaruli Khachapuri (Boat-shaped bread with melted cheese and egg) it was out of this world! Definitely my new go-to for an amazing Georgian cuisine meal.

I recently had a memorable dining experience at Art of Grill in Queens a cozy and vibrant Glatt kosher Mediterranean-style grill restaurant known for its generous portions and quality dishes. ￼

Food

The food at Art of Grill is one of its strongest points. The menu offers a variety of grilled meats, juicy kebabs, and flavorful salads, all prepared with fresh ingredients. Many guests highlight the tender steak and lamb kebabs, as well as delicious sides like garlic fries and dumpling soup. ￼

What really stood out to me was how well the dishes were seasoned and cooked full of flavor and served in generous portions. The mix of Central Asian and Mediterranean influences gives the place a unique culinary identity. ￼

Service

The service here was warm and attentive. Staff made sure we felt welcome, explaining the menu and checking in regularly to ensure our meals were enjoyable. Despite being busy at times, the team stayed friendly and responsive, contributing to a comfortable dining experience. ￼

Manager Anel

A key highlight of my visit was the exceptional hospitality from the restaurant manager, Anel. She greeted us personally, offered thoughtful menu suggestions, and monitored every detail of our visit to ensure everything was perfect. Anel’s professionalism and genuine care made the experience feel more personal and welcoming than typical restaurant service. Her leadership clearly influences the upbeat energy and smooth operation of the restaurant.

Final Thoughts

Overall, Art of Grill impressed with its delicious food, lively atmosphere, and outstanding service especially thanks to the warm and attentive management by Anel. I’d highly recommend it for a casual lunch or dinner with friends and family.

This place has been on my "want to try" list for a while. It was kind of close to closing time when I visited so I was happy to still be able to order and take my soup to go. A+ for service already 😄 I love that they have a vegetarian/vegan broth option for soups so that's what I got. I highly recommend the duck egg noodles! Great texture and they went so well with the well seasoned broth. The mushroom was an add-on item and was interesting. Thick, chewy, and semi sweet. I've never tasted a mushroom like that before. Lowkey, the star of the soup for me were the big leafy green vegetables! They were cooked absolutely perfectly and weren't bitter! They provided welcomed crunch and balance to the soup. I added the included chili oil and it did not disappoint 🥵 I see what the hype is about and I will absolutely be back to try more. Maxi's Noodle is valid.

Possibly my most favorite noodle soup in all of New York City right now! Lately life has introduced me to some really good businesses worth the trek to Flushing (for the love of all things beauty!) and whenever I go do these appointments, I’m comforted by the fact that I can enjoy my favorite Beef + Wonton Noodle soup after. I go for the 2-topping option and add extra noodles and it’s always so satisfying! It’s a small and no frills place so I just order pick-up to go and get in the car and get back home. The wontons are huge and the beef is delicious, they just need to be a little more generous with the beef stew sauce a bit. Add some chili oil and voila. Trust that you’ll crave it in just a matter of days! Thanks Maxi’s, will be back again soon! :)

Absolutely deliciousa I had a craving. Maxi's noodles hit the spot and then some. This soup with more than I expected very filling. It felt like your grandmother made it or something lol. I will be back someday maybe to try something else or maybe not 😋

Best noodles I have had in a while! The options were great and very customizable to your liking. The dumplings were delicious. I was out of state and hope to come back again soon. Might make the trip just to eat here. There was a little bit of a wait as it is very small and very busy but very well worth the wait!

name: Seichou Ramen
document: Seichou Ramen. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Finally found a hidden gem nearby! 🍜 After the snow today, I was craving a warm bowl of ramen and Seichou delivered. I ordered the Steak Ramen and it was delicious. We started with the fried squid legs, which were super crispy and flavorful. To drink, the Iced Matcha Latte was a pleasant surprise—not too milky, just the way a real matcha should be. They have a massive menu, so I’ll definitely be back to try more!

This is my go-to Japanese restaurant in Elmhurst. I’ve tried many of their dishes and they consistently meet my expectations. I highly recommend the Takoyaki and ikageso —the Takoyaki comes in a generous portion and is full of flavor, while the ikageso is tasty and perfectly crispy.

The Niku Udon and Gyudon are quite similar (one with noodles, the other with rice), and both are enjoyable. I’ve also tried the Steak Ramen and Chashu Don, which were decent, though not my top picks. For the Ebi Fried, I personally wish the shrimp were a bit larger.

Overall, I really enjoy this restaurant, which is why I keep coming back to try more of their dishes. The Takoyaki alone makes every visit worthwhile.
Cozy ramen place with a cozy atmosphere. I love their green tea and the ramen and udon noodle soup was so good and needed after a cold day.
my new favorite restaurant at elmhurst, portions are big and the server Ja is so sweet and nice. Their spicy tonkotsu is similar to ichiran.

So happy our neighborhood finally has its own ramen spot! They have a nice selection of ramen and other dishes. We really like the shoyu ramen and steak ramen, which have a rich, comforting broth and perfectly tender noodles. The chicken katsu curry is another go-to for us. The curry is full of flavor, and the chicken katsu is cooked perfectly. The gyoza was also great. The staff are always friendly and welcoming. Highly recommend checking them out!!
