name: Jora
document: Jora. cuisine: Peruvian Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Hidden gem in LIC where the food is amazing, staff is accommodating and the ambiance makes you feel like you’re on vacation! This spot is located on the corner of 47th street so you can miss it. One of the best things about this restaurant is directly across the street. There is free parking for about four cars. The rest is regular street parking. But coming here for lunch. It was easy to park for free in one of those spots. I asked for recommendations from the waitress and what she recommended did not fail. My guest and I left here fully satisfied, and will be returning for dinner to see what the nighttime vibes are all about. I’m interested in trying one of the dishes. The bartender stated that he makes with Budweiser beer!?! Can’t wait to go bake. Go here!!!

Jora offers excellent Peruvian dishes. Ceviche carretilla has a prefect blend of flavor and texture with fresh ingredients; tangy and savory, tender and crunchy. Grilled octopus was smoky, not chewy, served over a bed of creamy yukon mille fueille. Salmon was exactly how I like it; crunchy skin with juicy and tender meat, melts in my mouth. Aji amarillo curry was a great addition to the flavor profile with a touch of creaminess. Aji de gallina is a beautiful dish with shredded chicken, I like the addition of quail eggs.
The restaurant is spacious, offers both indoor and outdoor seating options. The bar area is quite nice. We were seated immediately without a reservation on a Saturday afternoon. Service is good, although server forgot to deliver my drink even though the restaurant was not crowded at the time.
I would recommend this restaurant for the food itself. It's a great place to try if you are looking for Peruvian dishes.

Came here for holiday work dinner and we had an Incredible fine dining experience!
The pisco sours are divine and the authentic Peruvian food is delicious 😋
I highly recommend the jalea appetizer it’s a fried seafood mix with calamari shrimp fish and yucca with red onion and some amazing sauces. I ordered the pastel de choclo which was flavorful with plenty of truffle and cheese 🧀
The lomo saltado came with fries which were such a delight!
The pisco shots at the end of the meal were a nice touch too and this place is overall phenomenal ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We had an absolutely fantastic experience at Jora. From the moment we arrived, the staff went above and beyond to make the evening memorable.

Miguel was exceptional; he was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Our waitress, Lorena, was equally outstanding. Their care, professionalism, and kindness truly stood out, making us feel exceptionally well taken care of.

The food was nothing short of amazing. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared, beautifully presented, and absolutely delicious. It was one of those meals where every bite feels memorable. The Lomo Saltado was a standout, but honestly, all the dishes were incredible.

What made the night truly unforgettable was how the team helped us celebrate my mother’s birthday. They made a special day even more meaningful, surprising her with a celebratory birthday dessert that she absolutely loved. She had an incredible time and was so grateful for the attention and service, and honestly, so were we.

Everything was perfect from start to finish. Jora delivered not just an amazing meal, but a genuine experience filled with care and hospitality. We will absolutely be returning and can’t recommend it highly enough.

Food was absolutely delicious! We had the mixto ceviche, octopus, chicken dish and paella dish. Everything was awesome, the chicken fell off the bone and was so tender. The ceviche was so flavorful, the octopus was tender and so good. The cocktails were great. Will definitely return!

name: Khao Nom
document: Khao Nom. cuisine: Desserts Thai. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
If you’re around Elmhurst, Queens, this is a Thai spot you don’t want to miss 🇹🇭✨
Khao Nom delivers the true taste of Thai street food with bold, authentic flavors in every bite. From comforting rice dishes and slurp-worthy noodles to vegetarian options, fresh salads, and smoky BBQ, the menu has something for everyone.

And save room for dessert — they have so many dessert options to choose from. The adorable fruit-shaped mung bean sweets are almost too cute to eat, made with smooth and lightly sweet mung bean paste 🍡🍓

Everything here is packed with flavor, making Khao Nom a true hidden gem for Thai street food lovers.

Cafe style Thai restaurant serving Thai street food and beverages. Was expecting authentic Thai style food but found dishes to be mediocre in taste and authenticity. Homemade hot Thai tea is perfect for these very cold days. Desserts are ok. I think there are better Thai restaurants in little Thailand.

Khao Nom is such a hidden gem in Thaitown! I ordered the stir-fried minced pork with basil and fried egg, and the deep-fried shrimp cakes — both dishes were packed with flavor, cooked perfectly, and reminded me of the authentic tastes you’d find in Thailand. The basil pork had the right balance of savory and spicy, and the fried egg was perfectly crispy on the edges. The shrimp cakes were golden, juicy inside, and came with a tasty dipping sauce that paired so well.

What really makes this place stand out is the variety of traditional Thai desserts they offer — it’s like stepping into a Thai dessert shop back home. There’s so much to choose from, and everything looks freshly made. On top of that, they also serve classic Thai-style dishes you’d find at local street-side eateries, which is such a treat if you’re craving true home-style flavors.

The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, and the staff are friendly and attentive. Whether you’re coming for a meal or just to pick up some desserts, it’s a great spot to experience real Thai flavors. If you’re visiting Thaitown, make sure to stop by and try it for yourself — I’ll definitely be coming back!

not the worst but i won’t be back again. food wise was okay, not much flavor but dishes were solid and cooked well. had some vegetarian options too. i got the KAO MOK KAI (Steamed marinated curry chicken with curry turmeric rice) and the curry chicken didn’t feel like it was marinated well and paired oddly with the rice. i don’t remember the exact dish my friend got, but she felt like the meat tasted artificial. service was non existent and we even had to walk up to the counter for them to take our order. there is a mandatory 18% tip automatically added for you despite the lack of service and overall comprehension going across the restaurant. a bit of a disappointment bc i love thai food but i think ill be giving other places a try.

I’ve been to this restaurant twice. The first time, I tried the Hainanese chicken rice. As a big fan of the dish, I’d say they did a really good job. The rice texture is a bit different—in a good way—and you can really taste the ginger.

The second time, I tried their khao mok gai (Thai chicken biryani). It was so good—honestly, it tasted just like the version I’ve had in Thailand. I also love their condiments.

Overall, I’m giving them 4 stars. The staff are friendly, too. It can get packed, especially when groups of tourists come in to buy Thai desserts, so please be patient.

name: Dallas BBQ
document: Dallas BBQ. cuisine: Barbeque Salad Seafood. located in Bronx. with 2.6 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Round-em up and come on in for a delicious feast of authentic southwestern food. They are very welcoming and my waiter was very attentive. Looking around me, I could tell that the portions were really big. I had the brisket burger and it was mouthwatering.

Dallas BBQ is a gorgeous restaurant with a great atmosphere. The staff were fantastic—friendly, attentive, and welcoming from start to finish. We started with the chicken wings, which were absolutely amazing and full of flavor. For our main meal, we had burgers, and they were delicious, cooked perfectly, and very satisfying. Overall, a great dining experience with excellent food and service. Highly recommended

Good place for dinner. It was extremely busy the day before New Year’s Eve, but we were seated right away and only took a moment to get our food.
We sat on the second floor with a nice view outside.
The food tasted great.

We went to Dallas BBQ in NYC around Thanksgiving, and overall it was a pretty good experience.

The place was packed, like, really packed, but they still found a table for us almost right away, which was impressive. The restaurant is huge and lively, and despite the crowd, the service was quick and friendly. 👍

I ordered the Smokehouse Special with an extra beef rib, and the portions were absolutely massive:
• Cornbread was honestly amazing. Soft, warm, and one of the best parts of the meal. 🌽
• The meat itself was good, but the sauce was way too salty, and it kind of took over the whole plate. A bit disappointing because you could tell the meat was well-cooked, but the sauce just overshadowed everything.
• The fries were solid, but I really missed something fresh on the plate. Even a little salad or some veggies would’ve helped balance things out. For a dish that’s around $30–40, it would’ve been nice to have something green on the side. 🥗

Portions are huge, so you definitely get a lot of food for the price.

Despite the salty sauce, Dallas BBQ is still a good spot if you’re craving big BBQ plates in a fun, busy atmosphere.

The place has a fun atmosphere, especially with all the Halloween decorations. The food and service were both okay — just as expected from a busy Times Square restaurant. Fried chicken, steak, and burgers were decent and portions were generous. A solid spot if you’re in the area and want a casual meal in a lively setting.

name: Emiliano's Market
document: Emiliano's Market. cuisine: Italian Delis Sandwiches. located in Bronx. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I ordered a few sandwiches from Emilio’s Market, and they were absolutely delicious—a mandatory stop for anyone serious about what goes on between two slices of bread.

The ingredients were so fresh and noticeably high-quality…piled on with an impressive, honest generosity.
If you are looking for a top-tier sandwich for lunch, Emilio's is legit.

This is authentic, delicious Italian food that perfectly delivers on the simple promise of a great NY deli.

Great neighborhood family owned deli and coffee shop. The place is beautiful and the employees are very friendly. Great assortment of goods: specialty coffee, bakery items, spices and much more. The store is vibrant and colorful.
I very highly recommend this place.

Awesome vibe and good food. We drove off the beaten path to check this place out and I'm glad we did. The menu we saw only showed paninis, though... I kind of wish we could have seen the local menu :)

Emiliano’s Market Italian Deli is an absolute gem! From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with the warm, inviting atmosphere of a true neighborhood Italian market. The quality of the ingredients is outstanding — everything tastes fresh.

The sandwiches are next level. Perfectly baked bread, generous portions of premium meats and cheeses, and flavors that transport you straight to Italy. Their deli selection, specialty items, and imported goods make it hard to leave without grabbing a few extra treats.

The staff is friendly, welcoming, and always happy to offer recommendations. It’s the kind of place that makes you feel like family.

Went in for the first time and I loved it. The people there are so nice and helpful. I got the Belgium waffles with fruits. It was delicious! And the hot chocolate was the best I've ever had. I had a wonderful experience and will definitely be back!

name: Jerk House
document: Jerk House. cuisine: Caribbean. located in Bronx. with 3.2 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: 2.22.26/approx 2pm - I called in our order about 1.5 hours before arriving. We found this place on Google and drove from Sterling, VA to try. The vibe inside and the two guys were very pleasant and welcoming. We didnt get to eat until 7.35p. However, we can tell that the escovitch snapper was freshly prepared and it was flavorful, as well. We're happy that we ordered 2 plates and a medley of sides: collards (🤢 & way too salty), cabbage, plantain, & rice/peas. When next we're in the area we will definitely return!

1. Stir fry shrimp w/ white rice: is amazing! As a veggie lover it was the perfect amount of flavor and veggie
2. Shrimp curry w/ Mac & cheese, rice & peas: the peppers and onions are cooked perfectly they are not soggy or undercooked, the shrimp is also cooked perfectly, they are large and perfectly cooked.
3. Brown stew chicken w/ veggies, rice and peas; WOW! So tender and delicious.

I go back and will always go back
Jerk chicken Rasta pasta and oxtail Rasta pasta was hot, made to order and very delicious. Parking was convenient behind the building. Atmosphere was a vibe and people were nice and friendly.
First time trying jerk house. I ordered curry shrimp but my order got mixed up and i got jerk shrimp instead. I must say I’m not disappointed. The food is super good. I will definitely be back,

My husband and I were craving something truly satisfying, so we decided to visit Jerk House—and what an incredible choice it turned out to be! From the moment we walked in, the gentleman at the front greeted us with warmth and was wonderfully informative, setting the tone for a fantastic dining experience.

We ordered the beef patties, oxtail, and jerk shrimp, along with the cucumber ginger juice, and WOW—every bite was an explosion of rich, bold flavors. The seasoning was spot-on, creating dishes that were nothing short of perfection.

Beyond the food, the atmosphere was welcoming and inviting, making us feel right at home. Jerk House has truly mastered the art of delivering an exceptional experience through both service and taste. Highly recommend!

name: El Nuevo Bohio Lechonera
document: El Nuevo Bohio Lechonera. cuisine: Dominican Sandwiches Seafood. located in Bronx. with 3.3 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The food itself is great. The service is hit or miss depending on date/time/crowdedness.

They are a bit messy with serving plates don’t always practice the best and cleanest methods of serving but if you can get past the old school mentality the food is awesome. I recommend freshly made plates over Food under heat lights. The fritura is good but not the best they have to offer. Their Morcilla is probably the best in the northeast hands down. Authenticity at its best.

Prices are extremely HIGH . so many other Latin restaurants within walking distance don’t go here . The service is also sub par a they are rude .  Last but not least how is a side of beef stew in a little cup 14 $ YET A LUNCH SPECIAL OF BEEF STEW WITH RICE AND BEANS 12$ make it make sense !

Don’t waste your time coming here. This was my first visit, and the service was terrible. I was charged $16 for a lunch special that was advertised as $10, and to top it off, I was given the wrong order. I asked for chicken, but they gave me pork. When I went back, they gave me the chicken, but it wasn’t even a proper portion—barely any chicken with a whole bowl of rice. The staff was rude and did nothing to improve the situation.

Since I don’t speak Spanish, I felt like they purposely took advantage of that, which made the experience even worse. I would not recommend this place to anyone—paying $16 for what I got is unacceptable, and being misled about the price makes it clear that this is very bad business.

Should of listened to the previous reviews. There seems to be a salt shortage at Bohio. The pork had no flavor, just dense dry pork, that seem to be overcooked by a lot. I tried to eat the skin and my teeth hurt afterwards. The pasteles were flavorless. For people who eat this style of food, you will be sadly disappointed.

We thank El Bohio restaurant and their delivery guys for sending us an excellent one, accepting our suggestion of the pork chop portion. Combo #2 and Chicharron de Cerdo. They took us there the first time we ordered, finally perfectly cooked food, congratulations to that new cook! Delicious, just the right flavor, fresh and well made food, thank you! No more salty, burnt, tasteless or half cooked food.
🥇👏🏻

They don't cook well all the time, nor are they surprising when everything is fresh and with the authentic taste of PR and RD food. It's sad that they dare to send poorly prepared food. I placed the order through Uber Eat and it didn't take more than 30 minutes to arrive. The bad thing is that the Pernil, the most desired protein, arrived cold, dry and with hard skin, the meat was white as if it were chicken. The truth is, it's not what it used to be. The food in general was very well cooked and delicious. They really are bad at making excuses about everything now. And they dare to say that one is the only one who has problems with food and no one else complains to them, yes of course!

name: Donjito
document: Donjito. cuisine: Latin American Cocktail Bars Asian Fusion. located in Bronx. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
To celebrate my friend's birthday tonight, we tried DonJito for the first time, and it was fantastic! The food was delicious, the service was friendly, and the atmosphere was lively. Plus, they have an amazing cocktail selection! 🍸

We had a fantastic time and look forward to visiting again soon. Thanks again, DonJito fam!

I read all the great reviews on this place but we had such a subpar experience. The worst part had to be the service. To start, parking in the area is a little tight (which we had accounted for) and just as we sat down my husband realized he had left his phone in the car, a pretty decent walk away. As the server had not come to us yet, he asked me to order him a beer in the meantime when they did come around. To his surprise, when he came back to the restaurant after being gone about 15 minutes, no one had taken our drink orders or greeted me, despite me flagging someone down a few minutes in. That should have been a sign to us how the evening would go. When our server finally did arrive, her approach was cold and she simply asked what we wanted, no greeting, nothing. We made the mistake of only putting our drink orders in, and again didn’t see our server for another extended period of time. I will say my drink was good, but a bit on the juice-side. Finally, she came back for our orders; we got empanadas, stuffed plantains and a sushi roll for apps. For dinner, the city island special for my husband and the shrimp trifongo for me. From there we waited….and waited….and waited. And then waited some more. Then the silliest thing happened (in retrospect). Our server came over to us and asked if we wanted dessert? We were so confused and had to remind her our food had not come out yet. She had no urgency, just a simple “oh” and left again. So odd she would’ve been asking us for dessert, because even if our food had come out, she hadn’t checked on us once. It actually made us think she may have forgotten to put in the order because about 10 mins after that interaction our apps came out. Empanadas are 2 small ones to an order, cut in half, the stuffed plantain had an odd taste and we couldn’t finish (it looked very pretty though) and the sushi was good. My husband enjoyed the city island but I could not get through the Trifongo, a dish I normally love. This had zero flavor an was completely bland with rubbery shrimp. When the server finally came back well over 30 minutes later and asked if I wanted to wrap my untouched food and I said no, she didn’t blink twice. Normally my husband and I would have brought our concerns to the attention of management but honestly we were so ready to get out of there and salvage what was left of date night. Total disappointment. Also, despite the name and menu, Donjito played almost no Spanish music. Instead the night was mostly alternative and pop which added a confusing vibe to the atmosphere. Water was never refilled. Overall super disappointing and will not return.

It was really a great meal & experience. The hardest part was picking what to eat. Great options. I ordered mojito delicious. Also had their Ropa Vieja beautiful presentation and truly flavorful. The black beans could have been more seasoned but honestly still tasty. The molten lava cake was yummy but not very warm in the middle to molten. My friend had the mofongo with lobster and said it was amazing. I still give it 5 stars because the staff added to a satisfying meal. I will be returning.

The outdoor patio was so nice and comfortable, and I even got a parking spot right in front of the restaurant—couldn’t ask for better. The frozen mango piña colada was delicious and strong, just the way I like it.

We shared the coconut shrimp, which were fried perfectly—crispy with a great crunch and paired with a tasty chipotle mayo. For my meal, I ordered the bento box. There are three options, and I chose the one with sliced skirt steak mofongo, shrimp mofongo, a dragon roll, and a tropical salad. The mofongo is a hearty dish, so I took some home, but it was packed with flavor. The skirt steak was especially amazing—tender, melt-in-your-mouth, and served with a rich, flavorful sauce. Even though I was full, I did manage a taste of the shrimp in a coconut sauce, and it was absolutely delicious. Can’t wait to reheat it and enjoy the rest tonight.

Good food, relaxing atmosphere, and overall a nice experience!

Returned for a second visit during the winter month so he dined inside still comfortable our waiter. Gabrielle was very friendly a good server. Both entrees were very good. I just wasn’t crazy about the cappuccino. It’s a Latin fusion restaurant so probably shouldn’t have ordered that. Coconut flan was very good although a small portion.  The cake for tres leche was a little dry, still tasty.

Just had my bday dinner in this place and the food waa amazing! The service from Eury was top notch! Will definitely come back very soon! My favorite dish was the Trifongo with churrasco and we tried a couple differenr sushis and they were all really good! My sister in law had a vegan mofongo and she loved it!

A Fundação Instituto Tecnológico de Osasco (FITO) é um verdadeiro patrimônio educacional da cidade, referência em ensino, inovação e formação de cidadãos preparados para o futuro.
Com uma trajetória sólida, a FITO se destaca pela excelência de seus cursos, pela dedicação dos profissionais e pelo compromisso em oferecer educação de qualidade, unindo conhecimento, tecnologia e valores humanos.
Mais do que uma instituição de ensino, a FITO é um espaço de transformação, onde ideias se tornam projetos, sonhos se tornam metas e o aprendizado se transforma em oportunidades reais.
Seu nome carrega credibilidade, tradição e um olhar constante para o avanço científico e tecnológico, mantendo-se como um dos grandes orgulhos de Osasco.

Consultem: Fito Jusbrasil
Uma escola tentar me prejudicar, me trazendo tantos transtornos emocionais e financeiro. Isso não esperava na minha vida. Estudei nesta fundação em 2014, na qual a estrutura e qualidade de ensino é horrível. Passei um constrangimento com um professor na qual abandonei esse lugar me causando transtornos psicológicos. Passaram a me cobrar 6 mensalidades com juros abusivos em mais de 3.000,00 reais. Estive na escola em 2022 propondo o valor de 1.500,00 reais não aceitaram. Agora em 2025 bloquearam minhas contas bancária me causando mais problemas descontado 1,333 00 com bloqueio judicial e colocaram um saldo devedor de 3.355,00. Comecei a trabalhar no final de fevereiro, estava cuidando de uma cachorrinha doente. Estou com aluguel, conta de água atrasados e sem poder comprar alimentação e não tenho ajuda de ninguém. Além de ter um péssimo ensino é desrespeitosa e desumana. Foi feito um acordo na justiça, porém eles demoram pra responder e ainda me cobram juros. O valor está em 5.264 Covardes, vocês são covardes! São abusivos, abusados e injustos! Algo vai acontecer com essa escola... Uma instituição com mais de 5 mil processos, tem mais processos do que alunos. A direção dessa escola estudam maneiras de prejudicar alunos para obter ganhos abusivos ao invés de educar com coerência e consertar tantas irregularidades.

google_reviews.text:
The Bronx Public — Brunch Done Right

The Bronx Public is a fantastic local bar with a strong brunch offering. The staff is attentive, portions are generous, and the experience feels relaxed not rushed.

Standouts:
•	Homemade biscuits, served warm with raspberry or strawberry butter are absolutely delicious.
•	$50 brunch menu includes your brunch entrée plus 1.5 hours of unlimited drinks (sangria, mimosas, or tequila sunrise).
•	I ordered a coconut martini on top of that smooth and so good.
•	DJ kept the energy up, playing all the jams without overpowering conversation.

Operational notes (the practical stuff):
•	They don’t rush you, which is a huge win for brunch.
•	The restaurant doesn’t split checks, but the handheld machine makes it easy to split payments yourselves by card.
•	Tax and tip are included, so no surprises at the end.
•	Drinks were flowing consistently throughout the brunch window.

Bottom line: Great food, solid value, lively vibe, and a smooth payment process. I’d definitely go back again.

Friendly attentive service. Extensive food & drink menu with variety. I liked the sangria. Pesto pasta was good but had too much sauce. Also wish the happy hr menu had more food choices and lower prices.

My wife took me here for my birthday, she knows how much the Bronx and hip hop means to me.  this establishment is a must if your looking for a glimpse of hip hop culture and some of the greatest food/drinks the Bronx has to offer.

If you are looking for somewhere with atmosphere to catch a game and grab brunch (or something to eat), look no further. The Bronx Public is a comfortable, familiar sports bar/restaurant with bottomless drink options at brunch on weekends.

They offer a variety of 90 min bottomless flavoured mimosas, sangrias and a few other cocktails.

After getting word that its gets super crowded once it’s game time, my cousin and I got to the spot early because we didn’t have a reservation! Luckily it was super quick getting us seated, and we were told we had to wrap up before the next reservation time; which worked out great.

Overall it was a good experience. The food and drinks were okay/good… And most importantly you can tell that this is a spot which is a regular for people living nearby.

Bronx Public is my favorite go-to spot for burgers,wings and drinks! Randy our server was great providing amazing service for our lunch celebrating my grandfather's 84th birthday. Thank you guys for always providing the music and vibes ❤️

​From the friendly service to the exciting cooking show at the hibachi tables and, of course, those phenomenal, big, and delicious boneless chicken wings, Flame Japanese Hibachi is a must-visit spot in Falls Church. Highly recommended!

google_reviews.text:
My mom chose Tony’s Pier for her birthday because she wanted a wide variety of seafood in a casual setting. While I originally leaned toward something more formal, she was absolutely right to pick this spot!
​We ordered the steamed and fried combos so she could sample a bit of everything, and she loved the variety. She also enjoyed the Manhattan Clam Chowder, though she mentioned it could have been served a bit hotter. The only real misses were the baked clams, which were over-seasoned and slightly bitter, and the tostones, which were unfortunately soggy.
​The atmosphere, however, was 10/10. The staff was friendly, and the whole restaurant even joined in to sing "Happy Birthday" to my mom and another lady celebrating her birthday too. Despite the couple of side-dish hiccups, the seafood was fresh and the experience was memorable!

The food was fried and full

I did not like this place and will not return.

document: Szechuan Mountain House. cuisine: Szechuan. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Had an incredible dinner at Sichuan Mountain House! We started with the cold noodles, which were the perfect refreshing kick-off to the meal.
The highlights were definitely the Mala Prawns (loved the fun gloves they provided to keep things clean!) and the Mapo Tofu, which had the perfect balance of spice and numbness. We also ordered the eggplant and green beans, which were cooked to perfection.
A huge shoutout to our server, Emma. She was amazing. super friendly and gave us some fantastic recommendations that really made our night. We’ll definitely be back!

Great restaurant with large portions!

We visited on a Thursday evening and waited about 15 minutes for a table. One quick heads-up: the food here is authentically spicy, so definitely be prepared for that Sichuan heat!

We ordered a few different dishes to share. I personally didn't love the cold chicken, as it was a bit too sour for my taste. The Sichuan chicken, on the other hand, was easily my favorite! We also really enjoyed the peppercorn beef and the steamed fish. While the flavors were great, the fish was almost too spicy at times—even for someone used to some heat.

Overall, the portion sizes are very generous, which I really appreciated. It's a great spot as long as you can handle the spice!

I’ve been wanting to try Mountain House in the East Village for a long time since it’s often mentioned as one of the best Chinese restaurants in NYC. While the food was good and the portions were very generous, none of the dishes we tried stood out as significantly better than other Szechuan restaurants I’ve had in the city.
That said, the portion sizes are great for sharing, especially if you go with a group, and the staff was very kind and accommodating. The menu is also extensive and has a lot of interesting options.
The atmosphere was honestly the most underwhelming part for me. Online photos make the space look quaint but spacious, but in reality it’s quite small and can feel cramped. Luckily we sat in a booth, but I imagine the middle tables might feel a bit chaotic when it’s busy.
Overall, I still really enjoyed dining here and would definitely come back to try more dishes.

Mountain House is one of those places I wish I had tried sooner. The food here is outstanding, with bold flavors and the perfect level of spice in every dish we tried. Each plate was deeply seasoned and full of character without being overwhelming. The proteins were especially impressive, from the tender fish to the flavorful beef and perfectly cooked chicken. Everything tasted high quality and thoughtfully prepared. The menu offers a wide range of options, so there is something for every preference. You can really fill up here and leave feeling like you had some truly excellent Chinese food. I would absolutely come back again.

Szechuan Mountain House is truly one of the most exciting and consistently delicious restaurants in the East Village. Every time I come here, I’m blown away by how flavorful, vibrant, and perfectly executed the dishes are. The moment you step inside, the ambiance sets the tone — dim, stylish, and buzzing with energy, but still comfortable enough to settle in and really enjoy your meal.

The food here is the real star. The heat level is bold without ever sacrificing flavor, and every dish feels thoughtfully crafted. The spices are aromatic, the textures are on point, and even classics taste elevated. Whether it’s a noodle dish, something braised, or one of their signature appetizers, everything arrives hot, beautifully presented, and absolutely packed with flavor.

Service is quick and efficient, even when the restaurant is packed (which is almost always). The staff knows the menu well and is great about offering suggestions if you’re stuck between dishes.

Portions are generous, prices are fair for the quality, and it’s the kind of place you finish your meal at already thinking about what you want to order next time.

If you’re craving authentic, spicy, and deeply satisfying Szechuan food, Szechuan Mountain House never disappoints. Highly recommend!

google_reviews.text: We came to Del Frisco for a special occasion, a milestone at work. and we had such a great food and an amazing experience, largely thanks to our waiter, Titus. He was incredibly attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming from start to finish. He made us feel comfortable, checked in at just the right moments, and ensured everything was perfect without ever being intrusive. Service like his really elevates the entire dining experience. The ambiance was perfect and we couldn’t ask for a better waiter. Management should absolutely know how much of an asset he is. We’ll definitely be back—and hope to be seated in his section again.

Reservations were for 4:30pm. We arrived a little early and we were seated as soon as we checked in with the hostess. We ordered the calamari and Caesar salad to start. The bread for the table was so delicious- better than a lot of other places. I enjoyed the field mignon and, ordered medium rare, and the lobster with truffle butter. The fried rice served with the sea bass was perfectly cooked. We also ordered the cream corn, broccolini, and the start of the show- the lobster Mac and cheese. Ambience, in my opinion, could have been better. I prefer a more dim-lit scene.

Was a little busy when we went. Server was very friendly, I think her name was Catarina? Tried the strawberry martini and it was quite good. I think it was a special drink for February. Had a wedge salad - enjoyed that a lot! For entrees we had the chicken and the sea bass. Both were excellent! We didn't have dessert, but overall we enjoyed everything and we would go back again.

Our evening out for dinner was fantastic.  The ambiance was perfect with a low hum of patrons without any unruly and unnecessary noise. The precisely aimed accent lights gave each table enough glow to admire the company and food. The waiters and support staff were quietly and effortlessly efficient. Our evening began with freshly baked butter bread, followed by an exquisite lobster bisque for me and a charred octopus with chorizo for my wife, both made to perfection.  Our main course was a prime ribeye and prime strip, just as we ordered and delicious as were our broccolini and whipped potato sides. Our decadent desserts consisted of chocolate mousse cake and a tiramisu crème brûlée. We chased all this down with our favorite Albariño wine which was chilled with precision. We cannot say enough about our server Markus and his support Herberth, who ensured everything was to our satisfaction. All our questions regarding the menu were answered with confidence and without hesitation.

Stopped by Del Frisco’s on Saturday for a birthday dinner. The ambiance was great—low, intimate vibes. We were seated on the second floor with a beautiful view of the Conrad and the CityCenter tree, which set the tone nicely.

Unfortunately, the service and food fell far short of expectations. We started with a round of drinks, which ended with the server spilling someone else’s drink down the back of my outfit and onto the floor. There was no apology, no cleanup, and no replacement—he simply looked back and walked away.

I ordered a medium-rare steak and was served what can only be described as a hockey puck: dry, overcooked, and completely unseasoned. It didn’t melt in my mouth at all. When I notified the server, I was told the kitchen was closing. My friend attempted to order food as well and was met with the same response, so she opted for another drink instead—a lemon drop. The drink never arrived, yet it appeared on the bill. When we pointed this out, the waiter giggled and removed the billfold.

The moral of the story: an apology or simple acknowledgment of poor service goes a long way, especially at a restaurant where there are certain expectations for service and quality. While my friend still enjoyed celebrating her birthday, it’s the small details that truly matter.

Isiah later called to follow up and worked to resolve the situation, which I genuinely appreciate. Thank you for the follow-up—it did not go unnoticed

name: Nin Hao
document: Nin Hao. cuisine: Chinese. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Vibey restaurant with fujianese fusion food.

We liked the mains - the steamed fish was great and so was the lamb chops (must get!)

The dan dan noodles had good texture but probably needed some more toppings and the razor clams were good but a little tough.

Would skip the string beans (felt undercooked) and the braised eggplants (just was not impressed by the flavor).

Would totally come back here for dinner again if in the area!

I didn’t expect to find a restaurant that brings Fujian culture to life so beautifully outside of China — but this place truly does.

Unlike many “Asian” restaurants that blend regional flavors together, this one is proudly city-specific. It focuses on authentic Fujian cuisine, and you can feel that intention in every dish. This isn’t generic Chinese food — it’s deeply rooted in local tradition and identity.

The shrimp appetizer was absolutely killing it — fresh, perfectly seasoned, and incredibly addictive. My kid finished the entire plate by himself, so we immediately ordered it again. That rarely happens. The cold chicken was just as impressive — tender, clean in flavor, and very true to Fujian-style preparation.

The steamed fish was excellent and noticeably different from the more common Cantonese-style steamed fish. The seasoning felt lighter yet more layered, highlighting freshness in a uniquely Fujian way.

The rice cake tasted exactly like the ones I had when visiting Fujian, China — soft, chewy, and nostalgic. The noodles and fried dumplings are true Fujian snack staples, not the usual Americanized versions. It really felt like eating local street food from a specific city, not a broad “Asian” menu.

The Wellington beef was incredibly tender — it literally melted in the mouth. What really stood out was the way they served it. It came with bun bread, which traditionally is paired with condensed milk for dipping. But here, instead of condensed milk, they paired the bun bread with rich crab sauce from the dish. That creative twist completely elevated it. The savory crab sauce soaking into the soft bun created a perfect balance — indulgent, unexpected, and so well thought out.

This restaurant isn’t just serving food — it’s promoting Fujian culinary culture to the world. It celebrates a city’s identity through its flavors. If you’re looking for something truly different from the usual Asian restaurant experience, this is it.

Authentic, nostalgic, creative — and unforgettable.

I walked in because the decor was beautiful. I stayed because the food felt like home.

As someone who immigrated from Fuzhou at a young age, authentic Fuzhou dishes are rare treasures — usually found only in small neighborhood spots. Seeing so many childhood favorites on the menu honestly surprised me.

The drunken chicken, dragon head fish, shrimp, and dumplings were all incredible. Every bite brought back memories I didn’t even realize I missed.

After talking with the owner and learning he’s also from Fuzhou, I felt even more connected to this place. There’s real heart here — a genuine desire to share traditional Fuzhou cuisine with more people.

Truly special. Highly recommend.

Service was excellent all around, food was bright and well done, no dishes we didn’t like or would skip. Loved the mahjong tiles as chopstick holders, such a cute touch.

google_reviews.text: Once upon a time this place used to be the spot!! I’m not sure what’s happening there but after my third disappointing order they deserve a review. Firstly I waited almost 3 hours for the delivery. I ordered pork and chicken. I got 2 pieces of pork bones and 3 pieces of pork skin that was charred and too burnt to be eaten. The packaging was a disgrace. By the time I got the food all the sauce was already in the bag. I’m keeping my distance. I’M DISAPPOINTED!! But I bet the owners don’t care.

Pros
Overall I saw this place from a chime time review I got the Rasta Pasta which is different then regular more on the sweet side than salty or spicy. Was not bad I actually liked it! Chicken was fall off the bone and smoked very well.

Cons
However my ribs I was for sure disappointed although it was smoked well. I never in my life had my ribs but in squares. There should be an option on if you want them cut never thought I would have to give directions because I never had that happened. When you cut ribs into squares it dries out quicker. That’s why you keep it intact so it stay juicy wrapped around the fat.

Other than that I give it a solid 4 👍🏾

But I will be coming in next time for sure!

First Review 04/03/2024

Was recommended to try the food here, so I decided to get large Ribs only for $16, large Jerk Pork only $16, 3 festivals and a chicken soup.

The Ribs flavor was good, however it was really dry. The jerk pork also was properly seasoned but was too dry. The dryness from the meat could be from being overcooked or possibly being left in the oven where it is being stored to keep it warm. I went a little before 2pm on a Wednesday with high expectations but the food did not match this expectation.

This is a second review. 06/06/2024

The jerk chicken was great, it was cooked properly and it was tasty and juicy. I would highly recommend it.

The jerk pork was also great, it had the same amazing flavor and it was moist and tender. I also would highly recommend this.

The Ribs was also great, could be a little more juicy, with a lower heat, or taken off slightly sooner, but I truely enjoyed and would also recommend it.

Big up the jerk man who was friendly and multi tasking to help out when a crowd built up in the shop, and to Nelson the owner who reached out to me on my first review to make things right.

Yaad man thing or tings lol😂. It’s labor day weekend and I wanted some Caribbean food .  So I found yaad man things and it was my first time trying them . I had the jerk chicken with bbq sauce . Honestly it was decent , very flavorful and the chicken was tender . I’ll be back when I’m in the neighborhood . 👍🏾.

So today is actually not my first time coming to Yaad Man Thing. I came last month but it was super crowded and took at least 30 mins to get my food.

I came today on my lunch break. The lady who took my order was nice. The two people, man and women who put my order together were nice, especially the man.

I ordered jerk pork, jerk chicken, curried goat meal, festival, baked Mac and cheese and a Ginger Beer soda.

Jerk chicken 5/5. It taste so good. Cooked to perfection and seasoned well. The sauce complemented the meal well and it wasn’t doused in barbecue sauce like other Jamaican restaurants like to do.

Jerk pork 10/5. If you want it; get this. It’s sooo good! It is cooked well and it’s not greasy or oily like other Jamaican restaurants. It’s grilled perfectly and it has the nice bit of kick to it.

Curried goat 4.5/5. It’s good, I like it but a bit much bone in it and the pieces of goat are small. The gravy was good and I did get a nice serving! I would order it again.

Festival 4/5. It’s good, but small. It was fresh and I did like the taste of it; but I’ve had better festival at Peppa’s. I would still order it again.

Mac and cheese 4/5. It’s better than most Jamaican restaurants I’ve gone to and it’s seasoned, but I had the last slice and it was a bit “old”. I’d wait next time for a fresher batch.

They usually have lo mein on weekends, so I’ll have to stop by for it.

All in all, good service, nice people and delicious food. I did not have to wait either on this Tuesday, so give them a chance.

name: Xi'an Famous Foods
document: Xi'an Famous Foods. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Burgers. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Take out on August 31, 2025.

Stop complaining about the noodles being cold when you bring them home. Just warm them up for 1 minute in the microwave or eat it in the car. It’s not a big deal, not sure why this has become a point of conversation in these reviews. Food was delicious. This is special food from Xi’an, China. Thank you for bringing this chain to the DMV. Hope to see a proper sit down restaurant soon.
谢谢!

First of all, it is not DoorDash Only, I don’t know why the title says that. You can order from the official Xi’an Famous food website or the Four Mile website. I have visited this restaurant many times before in NYC, including the flagship Flushing location. Happy this one opened in the DMV. The good: the burgers are on point, the cold noodles are yum. The bad: the flat wide noodles do not travel well. I had to drive 30 mins home after the pick up, and the chew in the noodles probably lasted maybe 3 mins after I started eating. The taste is good. They need to open a spot with seats so the noodles can be enjoyed immediately. I heard they are actively looking for a Maryland location with sit-down options. Can’t wait!

So glad Xi’an Famous Foods has finally made it to the DMV! I took my parents to their NYC location many years ago, driven by homesickness after weeks of traveling in the U.S. The chewy, hand ripped noodles instantly transported us back to northern China, where wheat noodles are widely loved and celebrated. They still remember that meal to this day.

Fast forward to now, I ordered via DoorDash after doing some research. Since it’s a shared space with other vendors, there’s no dine in option, and the parking and pickup process can be a bit confusing, as others have mentioned. But nothing you can’t figure out.

We ordered the lamb and pork noodles, cold gluten salad, pork dumplings, and pork burgers. We reheated the noodles after the car ride, which softened them slightly, but the flavor was exactly how I remembered - bold, savory, and spicy. The noodles were well ripped, with a wide, smooth surface. The gluten salad was tangy and refreshing, and the pork burgers were packed with juicy braised meat in firm bread.

The dumplings are real surprise. I usually make dumplings at home and don’t often order them out, but Xi’an Famous Foods is an exception. Their spicy and sour pork dumplings are actually regional specialties and definitely worth trying.

For drinks, I recommend the Sour Hawberry and Chrysanthemum Tea. The hawberry is fruity and refreshing, while the chrysanthemum is cooling and calming, both perfect to balance out the richness of the food.

If you’re a first-timer, I highly recommend the lamb hand ripped noodles + spicy & sour pork dumplings + sour hawberry tea.

Hope I can enjoy those perfectly chewy noodles fresh out of the pot soon! Will be on the lookout for their full service location.

Drove over for pick up(only option) on a Sunday afternoon around 2:30.  Be aware the pickup location is behind the 7-Eleven.

Parking is difficult and very tight when busy. There is no where close to sit and eat. Also when you ask for cutlery they don't include in your order they put it in a basket for you to grab. No napkins.  Forks were grab and go and not wrapped separately. You walk in find your order in the website based on text and a locker opens with your food. Pretty straight forward interesting concept.

We ordered 3 different dumplings. These were probably our favorite.   Cucumber salad was very good.  We also ordered 3 different kinds of noodles. Lamb, pork, and beef. All were good though we were hoping for more. One friend who goes often to New York mentioned the noodles weren't as good here.

For us the food wasn't good enough to deal with the hassle of the location. If they moved though we would definitely give it another try or when we go to New York.

An honest review from a longtime New Yorker who used to walk 10+ blocks every week just to get my Xi’an Famous Foods fix: the taste here is exactly as I remembered from the NYC locations, so that’s a big win. I highly recommend the spicy lamb hand-ripped noodles and the stewed pork burger. My favorite dish back in New York was the cold noodles, and while I didn’t realize this location’s version comes without noodles, no problem—I just cooked some at home and added them in.

The sour hawberry tea was the perfect palate cleanser after the rich, spicy meal.

This location is a bit far for us, and since there’s no dine-in option, the food had to sit through a long car ride - unfortunately the noodles got a bit soggy. But I was happy to read in other reviews that the ghost kitchen setup is temporary and that they’re opening full locations closer to my home. When that happens, I’ll definitely be back to my weekly visits.

name: Nurish
document: Nurish. cuisine: Salad Breakfast & Brunch Cafes. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Super fresh, high quality ingredients, super satisfying & so so yummy. Love this place, I order for delivery often. Feels like you’re indulging but it’s so healthy. 100% would recommend. Favorites are Chef K Salad, Acai Bowl, Nurish Breakfast Sandwhich.

Healthy and nourishing food that is excellently sourced. Nurish is a vital staple in BK and New Jersey; it offers a vast menu of food that is simple, fresh and tasty. I usually get the brioche and egg sandwich and a latte. Also, I occasionally get the chicken sausage added into my egg and cheese. A tad on the pricey side but you know it’s going to who works at Nurish and the ingredients cannot be topped. Truly a treasure - the owner does great work

Health food cafe with plenty of options and dietary accommodations. There’s a laidback, neighborhood feel and staff have always been friendly. For someone that’s trying to eat clean, this spot uses fresh ingredients that work really well together. The prices are hefty but the portions make up for it on most of the items. Great spot in the Prospect Heights area! Below is a breakdown of what I ordered, along with my thoughts. Asterisks (*) indicate items I especially enjoyed and would recommend ordering again.

*The Nurrita Breakfast Burrito ($16) - One of favorites here. It’s packed with veggies, eggs, and potatoes. You can forget the hot sauce since this burrito does not miss!

Queen Caesar Wrap ($17) - As caesar wraps go, I’m not mad about this one. It’s pretty one-dimensional with a decent amount of chicken. Some citrus and croutons would level it up.

I really hope this place uses clean ingredients because boy oh boy one of the best bowls I ever had. I have a new favorite and that jerk sauce my gosh! 🔥 I had Jerk chicken, quinoa, Brussel sprouts, cauliflower, and zucchini’s. Only down fall cheap on the amount of protein i literally got 3 slices of chicken.

I’m on my fourth bite and already planning my next visit here. I literally googled “quinoa bowl” while walking through Prospect Park and decided to try this spot. It’s immaculate. Warm vibes. Happy hearts. Peaceful energy.

I ordered the cleansing tonic juice (10/10) and the farro & veg bowl with egg and salmon added (11/10!). (Note: The salmon is a generous fillet!)

The atmosphere gives hanging at your favorite cousin’s house. Cleo Sol playing on a cold fall day. I love it. Fully recommend.

name: Abc kitchens
document: Abc kitchens. cuisine: Venues & Event Spaces Italian Tacos. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Lovely ambiance for both lunch and dinner. The restaurant feels lively and family-friendly during the lunch hour, while dinner has a warmer, more romantic feel. I’ve genuinely enjoyed the atmosphere on both visits; the ambiance alone makes it a standout.

The food offers an interesting blend of flavors and was very enjoyable. Service was polite and attentive, though understandably a bit harder to flag down once the restaurant got busy. Overall, I’d definitely recommend stopping by if you’re in the area.

This new location is so beautiful, right by the water, with delicious food and good service! I’ve already visited twice for dinner and brunch, and both were great experiences!

I wish they can add dietary labels to the menu so we don’t have to keep asking questions, but there are many dishes that are vegetarian or can be made vegan! (paccheri pasta, dosa, etc.)

We encountered two surprising problems and ended up with good results: 1. Reservation made for 8:00pm but did not get table until 8:40pm. 2. Ordered more dishes but was told that kitchen stopped serving food at 9:00pm. We were definitely not happy. However, manager Paul was very helpful and turned problems into opportunities. He offered free drinks and desserts for us. The food was great, the atmosphere was very nice. As we are newly moved into Dumbo neighborhood, we like to see the success of this local restaurant. Of course, we would love to have a place that we can enjoy and keep coming back. Thanks to Paul and his hospitality that made us feel special.

abc kitchens feels like a natural continuation of the original, but lighter and more open to the water and sky. After years of associating abc with Union Square, seeing it set against the Brooklyn Bridge and the East River gives the whole experience a different kind of light. You walk in and everything feels airy and quietly buzzing.

Ordering the crab toast again felt almost ceremonial. It was such a marker of my early life in New York, one of those dishes I tied to date nights, weekend brunches, and the feeling of discovering the city through its restaurants. Tasting it here brought all of that back, but in a softer, more spacious setting. The menu still follows that market-driven philosophy Jean-Georges is known for, where vegetables lead and everything tastes clean and intentional, food that nourishes rather than weighs you down.

What I loved most was how naturally it fits into DUMBO. It carries the polish of abc, but the room feels more relaxed, almost like a daytime restaurant that slowly becomes dinner. I left with that familiar abc feeling, full but light, and a little nostalgic in the best way.

Favorites:
Razor clams
Peekytoe crab toast
Grilled avocado
Gruyere cheeseburger
Turmeric tonic

The Restaurant is really colorful and energetic!  The stain glass-esque windows towards the kitchen were very cool to look at from the bar.  The bar had sort of a glowing pastel pink underneath the counter top.

The Gruyere burger was so flavorful, one of the best burgers I've ever had.  The fries were solid as well.

The drink I ordered, would taste familiar if you've had limoncello. It was called yuzu drop and refreshing is the best way to describe it.

Last but far from least the staff. They were so attentive and friendly! Everyone from the bartender to both host.  Can't wait to come back in the summer.

P. S. Mind my pictures, the restaurant was very well lit.

we had a wonderful dinner at Botte Italian. Our server Anderson was extremely attentive to us the moment we sat down. The Chicken Milanese was delish and paired nicely with the Rigatoni à la vodka. Highly recommend as a go-to for late night dinner, and thank you Anderson for being so kind. Great service!

I had a great time at Botte BK . A Friend brought me out for my birthday.

The aesthetic was beautiful, i wish more people were dressed up but there was no dress code so casual wear i guess is the norm. The place is self was beautiful with wine shelves and a clear view of the brick pizza oven.

I lived my meal, i had the steak with roasted potatoes and spinach and the camamari for an appetizer.

I was in town with my friends & we found this gem. Henderson was spectacular & made sure we had a great experience! Food was amazing i highly recommend trying the Burrata & the rigatoni alla vodka.

BOMB! The food, wine list, service, atmosphere. Hazel, Vicente, and Sarah were all amazing. First time here and will definitely return. I had the rigatoni alla vodka with shrimp and a Caesar salad. Both were great. This would be a great date night spot or perfect for group dinners.

name: David's Brisket House and Deli
document: David's Brisket House and Deli. cuisine: Delis Sandwiches Burgers. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Such a great lunch at this local institution with a storied history dating back to the 1960’s. I went with their lunch combo, which came with a nice, warming Moroccan soup that really hit the spot. The brisket was super tender and outstanding, especially with that flavorful jus. Exactly what you want from a place like this. I’ll definitely be back next time to try the pastrami.

Visited on a Friday night in the winter, was not very busy. The food however was amazing. Had the pastrami sandwich, Reuben and brisket cheesesteak. Really happy tried in that order but have to say for me the Reuben stole the show with the condiments and cheese as well as toasted bread. The cheesesteak was a little spicier but also a bit salty , still very good but had we started with that could not have finished it all. Will be back!

Had the lunch combo of pastrami on rye, knish, and Moroccan Harira.

Soup was better than I expected (took a few spoonfuls before realizing I forgot the picture)…knish was flavorful but a bit difficult to eat since it was cut in half horizontally and only had a fork to attempt to cut it into bite size pieces. Sandwich was good, with a good portion of pastrami.

Bathroom was out of order so couldn’t review that. They can seat a good amount of customers, with booth style seating, and the location looked clean. Customer service was great, with a staff member bringing the food over to the table (just didn’t expect that).

100% HALAL, and absolutely worth trying!
I ordered both the corned beef and the pastrami sandwich.
The corned beef was tasty, but the pastrami was truly AMAZING. It was bursting with flavor, had the perfect amount of fat, and was so tender.
Fries were solid, too! I’ll definitely be back soon.

This is hands down the best brisket we have tried in Brooklyn! We had a fantastic experience and will definitely be coming back. One of the best parts was that there were no lines and no crowds, making for a very relaxed meal.
The staff was incredibly helpful and welcoming from the moment we walked in. Also, a special shoutout to the gravy they serve on the side—it is absolutely delicious and brings the whole meal together. If you're looking for top-tier brisket without the typical NYC wait times, this is the spot!

google_reviews.text: The flowers they always have in this place are beautiful, fresh and at a good price. They have different types of flowers, that's why I'm always going to buy there. Their attention is very pleasant, they are quiet people and the place also has a quiet atmosphere.
One of my favorite spots in the neighborhood. The kimbap is so good. The flowers are beautiful. There’s always a treat worth getting in the snacks. So thankful to have this place near my train stop.

I walked in, and the lady at the register kept staring at me as if she expected me to take something and walk off. It's frustrating how people often make assumptions based on skin color. Was excited to stop in for mochi donuts but when I arrived at 9:18am on a Thursday, I was disappointed to see the shop was not open :(

Great selection of flowers and bouquets, nicer ones up to $30. Staff very friendly, the flower guy offered to wrap it nicely although it wasn’t necessary. There is a huge void of Korean spots in the area, so happy I don’t have to go all the way to ktown!

google_reviews.text:
⭐ 5-Star Review for Yawdie Restaurant – Brooklyn

I had an amazing experience at Yawdie Restaurant in Brooklyn. I’ve known the owner for a long time, and watching his growth and passion come to life in this new chapter truly made me proud. When I stopped by, he greeted me with nothing but class and hospitality and immediately made me feel at home.

He brought out a variety of dishes perfectly seasoned french fries, juicy shrimp, and the most delicious sliders. Every single thing I tasted was fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with love. The presentation was on point, and the service from his staff was just as warm and welcoming.

Seeing him step boldly into the restaurant world and excel the way he is? That’s a beautiful thing. He’s always been a gentleman with impeccable quality, and now his food reflects that same standard.

If you’re in Brooklyn, make sure you stop by Yawdie Restaurant. The food is excellent, the energy is right, and you will definitely leave satisfied.

10/10!  I seen this place pop up on my social media twice and I just had to come. Everything was amazing! Literally everything I ordered was a hit! Definitely get that 6 pack lemonade! Now the vegan ice cream chef Damien gave us at the end… CRAZY! I just left and I already want more 🤣
I literally never leave reviews, but for this, I just had too!

Hands down the best sliders I’ve had in the Flatbush area. The coconut shrimp is a hit as well as the jerk chicken slider. I had high hopes for the Jerk Lemonade and it definitely lived up to expectation!
I am of Jamaican descent so this was a really good meal for my date and myself

Vegan options!! Wow, you must come here. The owner and chef is super friendly and the food is absolutely delicious.

I got the jerk beyond meat slider and the breaded sweet plantain fries. They were so crispy! The sauce it comes with is bommmbbbb. They need to bottle up their sauces and sell them bc I would legit buy it every month. So yummy.

Will def be coming back here again when I’m in the area. They also had a sample of ice cream that was vegan - it was a rum flavored one which I normally don’t like rum but it was really tasty.

Highly recommend coming here!

The food here is absolutely delicious and the chef and cashier are so friendly. The atmosphere and music here is also so calming and welcoming. This is my 8th time back here, and is my go to food spot. The food is cheap too!! It’s group friendly aswell, I always come with some friends. I ❤️ Yawdie

document: Sisters. cuisine: Music Venues New American. located in Brooklyn. with 3.4 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
It was Christmas Eve and we were looking for somewhere in Old Town Alexandria to get food. So glad our search led us to Sisters Thai🌟!!

I was super impressed and dare I say blown away by just about everything! From the Tom Ka soup right through to the Drunken Noodles - each dish we had was packed with flavours that were bold, authentic, and beautifully balanced.

The service was great! Despite it being super busy - our sever was very attentive (especially on a holiday evening), and even came to let us know the kitchen was closing and if we wanted desserts, we had 10-15 mins to place the order/s.

The venue itself is really unique/trendy - I would describe it as a fun, unexpected blend of a cozy French bistro aesthetic with a Thai twist—warm, stylish, and welcoming. A total gem in Old Town & I can’t wait to go back!

Had an amazing meal. The service was friendly and knowledgeable.

Their cocktails were perfectly mixed.

We got a couple of dishes and every single one of them tasted great and full of flavors. The sisters fries rice was one of the best fried rices I’ve had so far.

Sisters Thai is truly a charming spot — the décor alone makes the visit worthwhile. The floral entrance is stunning, the interior stylish and modern, and the chandeliers add a touch of elegance you don’t usually expect from a casual Thai restaurant.

I had a beautifully presented cocktail that was refreshing and delicious, and the curry was rich, creamy, and full of fresh shrimp and vegetables. Everything tasted vibrant and comforting.

Service was friendly, and the overall vibe makes it a lovely choice for a relaxed dinner or a cute night out. The only reason I’m giving 4 instead of 5 stars is because the experience felt a bit rushed, and at 10 PM they turned on the bright lights as if signaling guests to wrap up — which felt too early and slightly disruptive especially being on a date.

Other than that, it was a delicious and visually beautiful dining experience — definitely worth visiting! 🌸🍜🍹

Lunch was a bit disappointing. My pad kra pow was admittedly really good. My friend’s green curry was lackluster at best.
Water was always empty and the restaurant was almost empty as well. I can tell why: the “lunch specials” are $20. And a minimum suggested tip is 20% and goes all the way to 30% is so crazy to me. Sadly I don’t think it’s worth it anymore for me for a $30 lackluster lunch

FOOD SAFETY issues. They actually delivered me ROTTEN mango! And I don’t know what’s in the thai iced tea latte, but there certainly isn’t any thai iced tea flavoring or coffee. It’s just some weird kind of milk with a bit of coloring. Tiny portions - the pad thai is mostly bean sprouts, and check out the size of the “Oreo” ice cream. The crepe is soggy and inedible.

document: Don Neo Fusion Japanese Izakaya. cuisine: Izakaya Asian Fusion. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Visited Don Neo Fusion Restaurant and it was such a cute spot. All the food tasted delicious.
The staff were amazing—very friendly & attentive, which made the whole experience even better. I posted photos of what I ordered and everything was great. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to.

Came over after the snow storm. I honestly love Gyudon so much. This one that never disappoints. Blending perfectly with the juicy beef and creating that comforting, slightly sweet soy-based sauce seep into the warm bowl of rice underneath. Very Comforting!

The chiken katsudon portion was not too big. The sauce is a bit sweet (like honey mustard), not the kind of sauce I often got on Japanese food. But the yakitori (I got the beef one) was great. Perfectly grilled and seasoned. The scallion noodle was delicious, simple yet strong taste. Although more scallion would make it better I think— to emphasize on the scallion taste.
Great ambience, sit next to the huge window overlooking the streets, calming yet exciting experience. Offers discount for NYU students!

Words can’t describe how fresh and tasty the food is here. We ordered the mini don which was good for two people and super flavorful. Do NOT sleep on the shrimp tempura, normally tempura in American restaurants is too greasy but it was fried to perfection here. This spot is truly a gem, the vibes felt really warm and you know it’s an authentic Japanese spot when they play 90’s Japanese music

I didn’t catch the waiters name but he was so kind and attentive, he gave us a refreshing strawberry limeade which was the perfect end to the meal

I’ve eaten here with my family about 4-5 times now and the food is always perfect!! Gyu don, chicken katsu don, karaage are all so delicious and cooked to perfection. The atmosphere, service, and music are S tier. This is one of the best Japanese restaurants in Brooklyn in my option.

google_reviews.text:
Don Pollo is a hidden gem that offers authentic flavors and a delightful atmosphere. The enticing aroma of their perfectly grilled chicken and colorful sides is sure to tantalize your taste buds.

Each bite of comfort food is a symphony of flavors, from the tangy sauces to the cozy ambiance. Whether you’re dining with friends or treating yourself to a solo culinary adventure, Don Pollo promises a memorable meal that you’ll cherish for days to come.

Don Pollo is a hidden gem that delivers big on flavor and comfort. From the moment you walk in, the aroma of rotisserie chicken  sets the tone for a satisfying meal. The chicken is  juicy on the inside with a perfectly crisped skin, and the sides—especially the, black beans & rice, and the pico de gallo garden salad—are flavorful and generously portioned. I even had to splurge for a beef empanada appetizer and it was crispy on the outside with a very savory season filling that hit the right spot!

The space is clean and welcoming, with a casual vibe that’s great for families or a quick solo bite like I had. Service is fast and friendly, and even though they were busy, the staff kept things moving smoothly. I especially appreciated the variety of sauces—each one adds a unique kick to the meal.

Whether you're grabbing takeout or dining in, Don Pollo hits the mark for quality, value, and taste. Highly recommend if you're craving Latin-inspired comfort food done right!

document: Chef Papa Vietnamese Kitchen. cuisine: Vietnamese Sandwiches Soup. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The entrance makes the place feel smaller than it actually is. Everything is well laid out and the staff is very attentive. Since I came alone without a reservation, I sat at the bar. Service was quick and my signature pho arrived almost immediately. Water and green tea to drink, and mochi ice cream for dessert. Everything was well executed, though not particularly outstanding. I’d come back.

To start, I love the Chef Papa location in Flushing, it’s my go-to spot for Vietnamese food. So when I saw the LIC location had opened with such positive reviews, I was excited to give it a try.

As two people, we ordered truffle fries, the signature pho, pork chops over rice, and a daily special of pork belly bao buns.

I’ll start with the good: the ambiance is nice, the staff were friendly and attentive, the bathrooms were clean, and the fries were crispy and tasty.

Now the bad. The pork belly bao buns would have been good, but the buns were so stale they broke apart while eating, ruining the entire plate. The pho was smaller than the Flushing location and nowhere near as flavorful. The pork chops were dry as well, saved only by the nước chấm. And I’m not a fan of restaurants that make 20% the lowest default tip option.

Overall, I was disappointed. The food is not up to par with the Flushing location and isn’t worth the price point. You’re better off going to Flushing, or skipping Chef Papa LIC entirely.

As a native Vietnamese and grown up in hospitality industry, I am always looking for the Vietnamese gem. It’s still not the case here.

The staff is really friendly, welcoming and caring. The atmosphere is nice and light. The music is not too loud which is great.

For the dinner I tried the Nem nuong (grilled pork skewers), Banh khot (mini savory pancakes) and the Chao tom (sugar cane shrimp). I was a little bit disappointed by the cuisine. In general, I was expecting more fresh herbs and salad as in Vietnam we eat those dishes with a lot of herbs. Just few mint leaves ? The pork skewers were original with the shape but a little bit too dry. The shrimp skewers were surprising as they made them with dried shrimp. It was the first time I saw this recipe. They were somehow too skinny but as an appetizer it is fine. And the pancakes were ok for the taste but a little bit too greasy.

Bathrooms were clean.

Happy to have been here but will probably not come back. Especially I don’t live in the area.

Perfect for date night. Good drinks beautiful atmosphere.(Long Island City location) But the food here is the star of the show. The shrimp and pork egg rolls were delicious. The calamari was exceptional and I do not like calamari usually but I like this one. The signature pho was absolutely delicious rich and flavorful broth. I brought my girlfriend here for Valentine's Day and they didn't disappoint. My girlfriend had the grilled pork over rice and she loved it as well. I will be back to try to lemongrass chicken and more pho. 😋

Chef Papa is my favorite Viet spot in LIC!

I visited back in July and had the crispiest and well flavored calamari along with cocktails and pork chop vermicelli and other dishes with my friend. I loved this spot so much that since that first visit, I’ve ordered delivery to even a few blocks away, and hosted parties with their food! (Sometimes I order multiple portions of calamari just to snack on 😅😅) Their back area seating is a stunning sun room and was a great spot to catch up and chat. Nothing beats good food with good chats with a great ambiance!

It’s sad to see an honestly delicious mom and pop restaurant face defamation by self proclaimed influencers displaying clear micro aggressions against certain ethnic foods, and I hope anyone who sees this review gives this place a try before believing an influencer trying to get out of a dinner bill.

I absolutely love this place and will continue to come back and continue to order from them!

document: Boon Dee Moo Ka Ta. cuisine: Thai Barbeque. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
This Thai restaurant is an amazing spot for AYCE BBQ AND hotpot. Located in Flushing, it is a bit far from the city, but if you're in the area, I highly recommend. Everything here is self-serve but the staff is super attentive with water and quick with drinks and changing grills.

They have a good variety of meats, fresh veggies, and a hot bar here (with a diverse array of Thai hot foods, such as pad kra pao, tom yum, and fried foods). I loved their hot bar and everything was pretty good quality. I got multiple bowls of their tom yum as it was full of mushroom and shrimps, which I loved. Their wide selection of meats and seafood was great. While I did feel that some meat quality was so-so, everything was (overall) pretty solid. They also have a dessert section at the end where you can get shaved ice and smores (for your grill). Great meals and I had such a good time!

We’d been wanting to try Boon Dee Moo Ka Ta Thai BBQ for a while, and finally went for lunch the other day. There are a lot of food options — a salad/veggie section, a raw meat area, and a cooked food section. The staff were super nice and kept changing the grill pan really frequently, which we appreciated. The setup is mainly Thai BBQ, but there’s also broth around the grill so you can do hotpot at the same time.

Most of the food was pretty good, but we did notice that some cuts of meat weren’t the best quality and got really tough once grilled. Not a huge deal, just something to keep in mind. When we were about to leave, the staff told us there was a dessert section we totally missed. We ended up trying the Thai shaved ice, and you can adjust the sweetness yourself, which was fun.

Overall, it was a nice experience — lots of choices, friendly service, and worth trying if you’re into Thai-style BBQ.

We had a very good experience here. There were variety of choices, and the meat had nice quality.

The Thai milk tea was very tasty and a must try!!!

The staff were friendly. P’Pui seated us and always asked if we needed anything. She was very kind.

The place has a nice atmosphere and feels comfortable.
Overall, I really recommend it.

NYC’s best Thai AYCE BBQ and hotpot!!
As a huge fan of Thai food, I think I just found my new favorite spot. This place is a dream for AYCE lovers — from premium meats and fresh seafood to hot cooked dishes.

What makes it even better? You get 2-in-1 right at your table — grill AND hotpot at the same time. Sizzle your meats while your soup bubbles next to it

Don’t skip the sauce bar — so many different flavors that take your grilled meats to the next level.

Then comes the sweet finale… endless cakes, DIY shaved ice with jackfruit and jelly, plus a marshmallow sandwich torched right in front of you.

Thai food lovers, this one is a must!

Follow me @foodie.elite on IG and Tiktok for more!

Boon Dee BBQ is such a fun and delicious Thai BBQ and hot pot experience. The $40 all-you-can-eat option is definitely worth it, with endless meats, noodles, appetizers, and dessert. I love that you can grab your own food so there's no waiting and no pressure.
The hot pot comes with a flavorful chicken broth where you can even make ramen while your BBQ cooks. Service was friendly and always ready to help with anything we needed. Everything tasted fresh, and the appetizer station had great options like wings and crab rangoon. I highly recommend this spot for a casual night out with friends or anyone who loves to eat well!

80-07 Broadway, Elmhurst, NY 11373

Initially, I was confused and let it go, convincing myself it was an accident.

When I found the hair in my dish, I attempted to get the server’s attention from my seat. She was sitting at the register about 10 feet away. I politely raised my hand and asked if she could assist me; she remained seated and tried to address me from there. Even after asking again, she continued to stay at the register instead of coming over. It was only after I gestured and asked her directly to come to the table that she finally got up. It was extremely clear she did not want to assist, despite multiple requests for help.

When I pointed out the hair, the server showed **no interest in resolving a clear food safety issue**. She offered no apology and no solution, and displayed **no concern regarding potential food contamination**. She literally just stood there with no reaction.

I also want to note that I felt targeted by both the server and the kitchen staff. The combination of the deliberate-feeling table bump, the lack of engagement from the server, and the absence of any attempt to address a **sanitation concern** created an uncomfortable and unprofessional environment that went beyond standard poor service. These actions suggested **retaliatory behavior** and a **concerning pattern of conduct**.

Given the sequence of events and the behavior from both the server and the kitchen staff, I am concerned not only about the hair in my own dish but also about what may have been done to my daughter’s food. The timing, the placement of the hair, and the interactions leading up to the meal raise reasonable questions about whether the **contamination may have been deliberate**, which is a serious **health and safety concern**.

My table was fully visible on your surveillance system, the cameras should clearly show the staff interactions, the timing, and the events I described. I arrived around 2.45pm.

I have shared this experience with the appropriate authorities to ensure the matter receives proper attention.
