google_reviews.text: Sami is so warm and welcoming, he puts care into his costumers experience! I highly recommend  the mix grill for 2. It has EVERYTHING! Lamb, lamb chops, beef kafta, chicken kebab, beef kebab, falafel, hummus, fried and pita. Everything was well seasoned and delicious.  My new favorite  place!

El Toum in New York is truly a special place. From the moment you walk in, the décor and atmosphere immediately transport you to the Middle East, with an authentic and welcoming vibe that makes the experience even better.

The restaurant is run and attended by its owner, who is very friendly and takes the time to give recommendations. That personal touch really makes a difference.

I ordered a chicken shawarma with hummus, but they served me a lamb shawarma with hummus instead. Normally, I never eat lamb and in the past I’ve never really liked it. But I decided to try it, and it was a complete surprise — absolutely spectacular. The lamb was tender and full of flavor, the salad was fresh, and the hummus was outstanding, definitely some of the best I’ve had.

This is without a doubt a great spot if you’re looking to enjoy an excellent hummus and a flavorful shawarma. A place worth visiting and repeating.

I had tried El Toum a few times shortly after they opened and wasn’t impressed — the food wasn’t good and the interior felt a bit grimey. I never understood all the rave reviews this place seemed to get. Since I live down the block and the restaurant is always bustling (and constantly written up by sites like Gothamist and Eater), I decided to give it another try.

We asked to sit outside and were told menus would be brought over. After about ten minutes of waiting, my husband had to go in and ask for them. The staff apologized, but it wasn’t a great start.

We ordered the artichoke appetizer, hummus with cauliflower, and the chicken mushrooms. The artichoke dish was disappointing — it seemed like jarred artichoke hearts tossed with walnuts and golden raisins, microwaved, and served with a thin, over-toasted pita. The hummus was creamy and the roasted cauliflower and tomatoes on top were nicely seasoned, but again, served with that same unpleasant pita. Of the three dishes, this was the best, but not enough to make me want to return.

The chicken mushrooms entrée was underwhelming. The chicken lacked seasoning, the balsamic tasted harsh rather than smooth, and the sweet potatoes were just dry, unseasoned chunks on the plate. The zucchini and carrots were fine, but nothing memorable.

On top of that, the wine glass I was given had dried food crusted on it, the interior still feels skeevy, and even the table we sat at was sticky.

Overall, I can’t understand the hype. While the hummus was solid, the rest of the food, atmosphere, and attention to detail fell short — again.

An outstanding meal in every way, I’ll definitely be returning.

google_reviews.text:
I have been an avid fan of Jollibee since I was in the Philippines. Even after moving to the United States, I made sure to live near a Jollibee location because I truly enjoy your food. I frequently order takeout from your Chantilly branch almost four times a week and usually order a 6-piece Chickenjoy bucket with sides.

Throughout my visits, most of the crew members have been very kind and professional. However, during my most recent visit, I encountered a crew member named Jon whose behavior was disappointing.

I politely asked for a small extra gravy because the gravy included with my 6-piece Chickenjoy was not full and was not enough for all the pieces. In the past, other staff members have kindly provided a small extra gravy upon request. However, Jon responded in a rude tone, stating, “We are not giving free gravy.” When I explained that I had previously received extra gravy from other staff, he immediately said, “Do you want me to call our manager so they can be in trouble? We are not giving free gravy.”

I felt that this response was unprofessional and unnecessary. I was simply asking politely, not demanding anything. As someone who has worked as a crew member and currently works as a restaurant server, I understand policies must be followed but there is always a respectful way to communicate with customers.

This is the first time I have experienced this kind of treatment at your Chantilly location, and I hope this feedback helps improve customer service moving forward.

Also for dessert, they have a peach mango pie to die for.

Jollibee never disappoints! The Chickenjoy is always crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, and the gravy is chef’s kiss. The Jolly Spaghetti is perfectly sweet and nostalgic—such a comfort food. Service was fast and friendly, and the place was clean and welcoming. Every visit feels like a little taste of home. Will definitely keep coming back!

We came to visit my sister, and we ate lunch here at Jollibee in Chantilly. We ordered a 10-piece bucket with spaghetti, rice, and pie. It was delicious! The chicken was crunchy and fresh. Checked out the new Jollibee in Ashburn and it definitely lived up to the hype. The restaurant was clean and the staff were friendly and patient while I figured out what to order. The Chickenjoy came out hot, crispy, and well seasoned, not overly salty. The gravy was on point too. I also tried the peach mango pie and it was fresh and flaky—not overly sweet.

It was busy when I came in, but the line moved faster than expected and the order was accurate. Overall, a solid first visit. I’ll definitely be back.

name: Rice Thief
document: Rice Thief. cuisine: Korean Seafood. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Korean marinated crabs, shrimp, abalone and other more tradition dishes as well as a seafood tower. The bagged drinks were good, but preferred the simple sweet rice drink. The place is packed and smells great, but pretty loud. Gloves are provided to handle the marinated items, also ordered pork stew, rice chirashi and pancakes. Ok service, a bit lagging to get the bill and pay.

I was at this rather unique Korean restaurant a couple of months ago with a large group. They specialize in gejang/게장, or in other words, raw marinated seafood Korean style, which is marinated in either soy sauce or gochujang. The staff was pretty friendly, and the place inside was quite casual and slightly loud, but not too overbearing. To drink, I had a sikhye/식혜, which is either available in the traditional style with just fermented rice for $6, or also with pumpkin for $8. It was less sweet than the canned variety I have had before, and it was a nice touch to top it with a little piece of jujube/red date and some pine nuts. A few others ordered their cocktail pouches, with a couple of people liking the Open Sesame for $15, and another person or two also enjoying the $14 Pear with Me. They gave us some banchan consisting of broccoli with a bit of sesame as well as a slightly fermented kimchi, which was decent.

The first thing that arrived was something I can't eat, which was the Seafood Pancake/Haemul Pajeon/해물파전 for $24 listed as our classic Korean Style seafood pancake, crispy fried batter, squid, shrimp, clam & scallion and paired with our home style soy sauce dip. It was cut up into eight pieces, and it seemed like there was plenty of seafood inside. I unfortunately have a cephalopod allergy, so squid is a no-go, but the rest enjoyed it.

The next to arrive was one of their signatures, the Soy Platter for $89 with 6 soy crabs, 6 white shrimp, 4 red shrimp, and 3 abalone, with the host ordering extra of the blue crabs so everyone could have one. The platters come with rice and seaweed, but we upgraded to the Rice Thief Bowl, which is $5 with the platters or $8 normally, which has some masago, wakame, daikon, roasted seaweed & sesame seed along with the rice, which was very tasty, from the bit I could taste. The platter was as per the price point, quite massive, and I think two or three people could eat it as a main and leave comfortably full with another appetizer or something. The crabs had a good amount of roe and were soft enough in most places to bite and eat the delicious slightly sweet and salty meat inside. However, my preference was surprisingly the shrimp as I liked the texture more, and it was less of a hassle with the red shrimp being stronger flavored. The abalone had good texture as well, and overall, we all enjoyed this a lot.

As this is a raw seafood place primarily, the other two $25 dishes were fine. The better of the two was the Beef Brisket DwenJang Jigae with thinly sliced beef brisket, fermented soybean miso soup, tofu, slightly spicy anchovy broth, assorted mushrooms, jalapeno, and squash. The broth had a nice fermented flavor with some funk and plenty of pretty tender beef. The portion size was also adequate for the price point. The Spicy Pork Belly for $25 with sauteed spicy pork, Korean sweet & spicy sauce, onion, rice cake, and jalapeno was alright. It was well portioned, though I found the meat not as tender as some other spots. However, the sauce was solid, and I can imagine the spicy crabs having a good kick of flavor as well, and I wouldn't mind having that instead of the soy version next time.

I wouldn't mind going back here at all, as overall, I liked the food a lot. The platter also sounds excellent for a group, though likely, I'd try their abalone jook and/or the spicy marinated crabs next time.

google_reviews.text: My husband and I tried this place for lunch today because our usual place closed due to snowy weather. Tikka Masala is going into our regular lunch spot lineup! Everything was DELICIOUS and the wait staff was wonderful. We ordered samosas to start, Chicken Tikka and Chicken Curry for the meal. The meal was served with rice, seasoned potatoes and delicious naan. It was hard to stop eating, but we finally surrendered and brought the leftovers home to our teen. The curry was described as tomato gravy and it fully lived up to that description! I can’t wait to go back and have it again!

The Village at Waterford has two very popular restaurants. Tikka Masala is a newcomer that should be an option, especially when there's waiting lines at the others.  We were quite surprised how nice this place turned out to be.  The bright colored marque sign, promoting "bar and grill" is a bit misleading.   Once you are through the foyer, you will find a very pleasant and attractive decor.  The tables and booths are set with quality dinner and glassware, including cloth napkins.  The vibe is casual, yet provides an elevated restaurant experience.  Certainly not a grill, nor a bar.  There's  only a counter with two stools.  Mixed drinks & beers are available and brought to your table.  The wait-staff were very attentive, courteous, and unobtrusive.   My wife and I split an entree.  We ordered Makhani, which is  Butter Chicken. The chicken was in a rich and creamy tomato based curry; mildly spiced.  It was delicious!  With it was served naan, basmati rice, and seasoned potatoes.  The shared order was more than sufficient for each of us, and consequently, economical. Pye Boat Noodle
Star Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)

Pye Boat Noodle is one of those places where the wait feels less like an inconvenience and more like a quiet reassurance that something good is coming. And it is. What you’re rewarded with is Thai comfort food that’s confident, deeply satisfying, and absolutely worth your time.

The beef boat noodle soup is the clear standout. Its dark, aromatic broth carries a gentle sweetness balanced by rich, savory depth—comforting, soulful, and endlessly slurpable. Each bowl feels thoughtfully composed, the kind of dish that stays with you long after the table is cleared.

Don’t skip the crispy chive pancakes. Golden and crackling at the edges, tender within, they offer a perfect contrast to the richness of the noodles. Savory, fragrant, and addictive, they’re the kind of side that quickly becomes essential rather than optional.

Prices are refreshingly reasonable, especially for food this satisfying, and the service is genuinely warm—friendly, efficient, and unpretentious even during busy hours. There’s a natural rhythm to the place that makes everything feel easy once you’re seated.

Pye Boat Noodle doesn’t rely on trends or spectacle. It delivers honest Thai flavors, executed with care and consistency. Worth the wait, worth the return visit, and unquestionably deserving of five stars.

Pye Boat is a really great place. The atmosphere is nice and welcoming, and the servers are genuinely attentive and caring. They always greet me warmly, which makes every visit feel special.

Most importantly, the food is really good and consistently satisfying. Everything I’ve tried has been well prepared and flavorful.

Highly recommend this spot. Everyone should come check it out.

name: Salsa
document: Salsa. cuisine: Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I have not been to this place since before COVID, when they were in a different location. First things first, I had a good time but not a great time. I went on a Saturday and they had two bachata classes, not salsa as they used to do before and what you would expect from a dancing establishment that calls itself 'The SALSA Room.' I don't know if they do it differently on other days of the week, so you may want to check on that.

I stayed there for almost three hours and I heard only 5 salsa songs; most of the music was modern, urban Latin beats. I would say that 70% of the songs were in that genre, the rest being bachata and a couple of merengue songs. I would have understood that if the crowd was mostly young people, but it wasn't.

Yes, it was a very diverse crowd in terms of age, but that's the usual in clubs that cater to people who like to dance to tropical Latin music. What united us is a love for social partner dancing — the kind where you connect with someone, move together to the music, and create something beautiful in the moment. That's what salsa and bachata are about, and that style of dancing calls for a certain kind of rhythm and feel.

The modern, urban Latin music is welcome in small doses, but that's not what you would expect to dance to in a venue with that name.  Like I said, I had fun, but it's not what I was expecting, and I'm not inclined to go back or recommend the place. It is a shame because the facilities are first class, the staff was courteous and professional, and the prices are reasonable (cover $20.00).

For about 45min to an hour the music turned into jumpy-jumpy non-salsa, non-bachata. I have heard it used to be a lot better for dancing before the pandemic. The crowd is mixed level-dancers from very beginner to advanced dancers. Ladies get in free before 11pm which is great because the drinks start at $7 for a bottle of water and $20 for a mixed drink.

My experience is based around Friday night lessons. We came to celebrate a friend for her birthday. Arrived at 8pm. Free for ladies, $20 cover for me. We ended up talking to the host to get seating which at that time came with no cost. The mentioned lessons around 820 but people slowly came to the dance floor for warm up around 840. Beginners lessons were first after warm up. You get in a big circle and pair up. The choice is yours to switch partners which can be an advantage with different styles of leads and follows. You also can stay more on the outskirts with your partner if you don't want to switch. More people come the later it gets so more attended the intermediate class. It transitions well into open floor dancing. I enjoyed the energy and can be easy to dance the night away. At midnight they do birthday circle where those celebrating their birthday dance with multiple people for 30 seconds each. Ordered the BBQ chicken quesadilla which was pretty tasty. We ended up leaving around 1245. It's a good place to try.

My favorite salsa club for years. A lot of space and older people, no underaged, a lot of great security, never saw any incidents or fights. Security constantly circles around and is very attentive. The music is great, they have two floors and free salsa and bachata classes starting at 9. Ladies enter for free until 11. Enough parking around, there is a parking lot in the back. People are nice and friendly, we all come there to dance and have fun. The hookah is bad, tried it multiple times, and the service is slow, so I usually order at the bar, they have enough bartenders and two bars, so no long waits, you will be served quickly with delicious drinks. The bartenders are very friendly and accommodating. Highly recommend this place, love it!

I was at TSL on Friday and witnessed an incident that could have been entirely avoided with proper de-escalation.

A patron was sold a drink moments before security began enforcing a “no drinking” directive. When the issue was brought up, security initially handled it reasonably by allowing him to finish the drink immediately. While the patron was understandably frustrated, he was not aggressive, threatening, or physical.

The situation escalated when a security guard who was not directly engaged became visibly agitated. As the patron attempted to move away to speak with friends, this guard interpreted it as “pushing,” which further increased tension instead of calming the situation. Despite the patron ultimately complying and finishing the drink, he was later taken down forcefully and removed.

Outside the venue, while I was recording from a distance without interfering, my phone was struck by security — twice — despite no engagement or instruction to stop recording. This interaction occurred outside the bar.

The entire incident appeared driven by poor communication and unnecessary escalation rather than any real threat. This reflects a serious lapse in crowd management and de-escalation training. I hope management reviews their security footage and policies, as this was not handled appropriately and creates liability for the venue.

I’m sharing this to provide honest feedback, not to provoke — this could and should have been handled better.

Also, eight dollars for a draft beer is insane! And of course, they’re one of those places that don’t let you look at the receipt before you pay. Always a red flag!

The service wasn’t that great- I asked for ice water and got cold water with two ice cubes that were melted 80%. lol the waitress seemed irritated.

None of these things by themselves would’ve been a dealbreaker, but when you add up all of the less than favorable aspects of this visit, I likely won’t go back, especially when there’s so many great restaurants right there in Davis that you could choose instead.

NOTE- I heard they just opened back up. Maybe it’s new owners who just aren’t getting it right because this place used to be really good from what I’ve heard, and even the pictures of the queso were very different before.

google_reviews.text: The entrance makes the place feel smaller than it actually is. Everything is well laid out and the staff is very attentive. Since I came alone without a reservation, I sat at the bar. Service was quick and my signature pho arrived almost immediately. Water and green tea to drink, and mochi ice cream for dessert. To start, I love the Chef Papa location in Flushing, it’s my go-to spot for Vietnamese food. So when I saw the LIC location had opened with such positive reviews, I was excited to give it a try.

As two people, we ordered truffle fries, the signature pho, pork chops over rice, and a daily special of pork belly bao buns.

I’ll start with the good: the ambiance is nice, the staff were friendly and attentive, the bathrooms were clean, and the fries were crispy and tasty.

Now the bad. The pork belly bao buns would have been good, but the buns were so stale they broke apart while eating, ruining the entire plate. The pho was smaller than the Flushing location and nowhere near as flavorful. The pork chops were dry as well, saved only by the nước chấm. And I’m not a fan of restaurants that make 20% the lowest default tip option.

Overall, I was disappointed. The food is not up to par with the Flushing location and isn’t worth the price point. You’re better off going to Flushing, or skipping Chef Papa LIC entirely.

As a native Vietnamese and grown up in hospitality industry, I am always looking for the Vietnamese gem. It’s still not the case here.

The staff is really friendly, welcoming and caring. The atmosphere is nice and light. The music is not too loud which is great.

For the dinner I tried the Nem nuong (grilled pork skewers), Banh khot (mini savory pancakes) and the Chao tom (sugar cane shrimp). I was a little bit disappointed by the cuisine. In general, I was expecting more fresh herbs and salad as in Vietnam we eat those dishes with a lot of herbs. Just few mint leaves ? The pork skewers were original with the shape but a little bit too dry. The shrimp skewers were surprising as they made them with dried shrimp. It was the first time I saw this recipe. They were somehow too skinny but as an appetizer it is fine. And the pancakes were ok for the taste but a little bit too greasy.

Bathrooms were clean.

Happy to have been here but will probably not come back. Especially I don’t live in the area.

Perfect for date night. Good drinks beautiful atmosphere.(Long Island City location) But the food here is the star of the show. The shrimp and pork egg rolls were delicious. The calamari was exceptional and I do not like calamari usually but I like this one. The signature pho was absolutely delicious rich and flavorful broth. I brought my girlfriend here for Valentine's Day and they didn't disappoint. My girlfriend had the grilled pork over rice and she loved it as well. I will be back to try to lemongrass chicken and more pho. 😋

Chef Papa is my favorite Viet spot in LIC!

I visited back in July and had the crispiest and well flavored calamari along with cocktails and pork chop vermicelli and other dishes with my friend. I loved this spot so much that since that first visit, I’ve ordered delivery to even a few blocks away, and hosted parties with their food! (Sometimes I order multiple portions of calamari just to snack on 😅😅) Their back area seating is a stunning sun room and was a great spot to catch up and chat. Nothing beats good food with good chats with a great ambiance!

It’s sad to see an honestly delicious mom and pop restaurant face defamation by self proclaimed influencers displaying clear micro aggressions against certain ethnic foods, and I hope anyone who sees this review gives this place a try before believing an influencer trying to get out of a dinner bill.

I absolutely love this place and will continue to come back and continue to order from them!

google_reviews.text: Perfect place to eat during these cold winter days. The ramen is very flavorful, fried oysters have a soft crunch and the spicy dumplings are just right ! The Experience:
We had a 7 PM reservation, but after hitting some brutal traffic, we ended up ditching the car and walking. The location is very unassuming—keep your eyes peeled, because we literally walked right past it!

The Atmosphere:
Once inside, the space was smaller than expected, but in a very nice way. We were seated in a private closed-in booth with a curtain, which was a nice touch. It felt very secluded and cozy. They also have a convenient call button in the booth for ordering and service, so you never have to hunt down a server.

The Food:
We ordered the Honeycomb Appetizer Platter and two "C" Combo Chicken Ramen Platters.

The Ramen:
Absolutely delicious and surprisingly filling.

The Sides/Drinks:
The iced tea was excellent, and the bulk of the  appetizers were good as well. I'm not a big edime fan, but I was told they were good.

Price:
Prices were reasonable. Complete meal for two (appetizers, entree, drinks, dessert) was just under $90. I can't complain.

Verdict:
Altogether, every piece of the meal complemented each other perfectly. It was a great experience from start to finish. From the food, to the privacy and atmosphere. I will definitely be going back!

There’s nothing wrong with the food itself, but the management, cleanliness, and service at this Flushing location are detrimental to the Kyuramen brand. This location seriously needs better front-of-house coordination and attention to basic restaurant standards.

google_reviews.text: My wife and I dined here for lunch with another couple. The restaurant has a high ceiling (which I like) and an upscale interior with Korean themes. The overall atmosphere was excellent. We were quite impressed by the great variety of authentic Korean dishes on the menu. We ordered three appetizers - Haemul Pajeon, Cold Sliced Pork, and Fried Eggplant & Shrimp. All of them were high quality in both presentation and taste. We were pleased to learn the pork was from a barley-fed pig. Among the side dishes, I especially liked the kimchi, which was properly fermented. We had grilled sirloin (prime grade) and naengmyeon (cold noodles), which was an ideal combination as usual. The service was very attentive. I enjoyed the Italian coffee after the meal. We would like to come back soon to try other dishes on the menu. The restaurant seems like a great place for a date, a business meeting, or a family gathering.

High end Korean BBQ dining experience at Fort Lee. The interior is grand and luxury vibes. Everyone is friendly and welcoming. The host offering to take my coat made it a nice touch of service.

We had a combo with 3 meats, miso halibut, seafood pancake and spicy squid (to me it was VERY spicy). Meat quality is good. The staff cooked it beautifully. Seafood pancake was full of ingredients and the sauce brought it to another level. Miso halibut and vegetables were seared nicely.

The staff were all attentive. The main grill chef/waiter did a great job on the meat. The manager came couple times to check on us. There were at least 2 more staff helping them to serve our table. They were a great team.

Highly recommend Hanwoori for a unique Korean BBQ experience.

This place truly stands out in New Jersey’s crowded and competitive Korean food scene. Every dish strikes a delicate balance with perfect seasoning that feels thoughtful and refined without being overdone. The standout for me was the black cod in a pot. The space itself is spotless and edgy with a modern vibe that still feels welcoming. You can tell there is real care behind both the food and the overall experience. Highly recommend.

The side dishes weren’t salty at all—lightly seasoned, yet each ingredient’s natural flavor really stood out. I especially loved the spicy stir-fried octpus.

We celebrated my wife’s 60th birthday here with a group of 20 people, and the entire evening was absolutely perfect. From the moment we arrived, the staff was attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming. Everything was seamless

The food was outstanding—beautifully prepared, and consistently excellent across the table. Everyone in our group was impressed. The service struck the perfect balance, attentive without ever feeling rushed or intrusive.

The restaurant itself is stunning, creating a warm, elegant atmosphere that made the celebration feel truly special. It was exactly the kind of place you hope for when marking an important milestone.

Thank you for helping make my wife’s 60th birthday such a memorable and joyful occasion. We couldn’t have asked for a better experience.

name: The Taste of Brazil
document: The Taste of Brazil. cuisine: Brazilian. located in Staten_Island. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Decent First Visit, Some Highs and Lows

We stopped by Taste of Brazil around 4:30 PM on a weekend—nice timing since it wasn’t too crowded. I had called ahead and was told the all-you-can-eat option was $40 per adult and $20 for kids under 12. Thankfully, our server was honest and helpful, letting us know that paying by the pound would be a better value for our group, and it definitely was.

The meat selection was impressive, though I couldn’t try everything. The beef was tasty—definitely best enjoyed fresh out of the oven. Unfortunately, the chicken was overly salty. A highlight was the bar in the middle with sides—don’t miss the pickled garlic, it pairs perfectly with the meats.

Service was mixed. We were seated but had to get up and ask for guidance since no one came back to explain the process. It’s mostly self-serve, so keep that in mind. Also, they don’t serve alcohol, but it’s BYOB if you want to bring your own drinks. Another thing to note: gratuity is automatically included in the bill.

Overall, it was a decent first experience—great meats, casual atmosphere, and some room for improvement on service.

I ordered via uber eat today for the first time from this place. I ordered combo CHICKEN, which should have chicken obviously with rice, beans and fries. When I received my order, I opened the box and instead of chicken I found PORK! I was about to throw up from the smell. I called them more than 10 times to let them know they mixed up my order and ask if they can take it back, they never replied and I had to toss the food. First and last time ordering from this place 👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻
Real authentic taste from Brazil. Top grade meat grilled by extraordinary Brazilian chef. Price is very reasonable. I live in university city but I'd rather drive 35min to this restaurant.

Their food is amazing and way better and more authentic than any of the chains around within the city. If you want to support small business and get better food and a more authentic experience give them a shot you will be glad you did.

The price does not match the vibe in there, I’d say they definitely need to either lower their prices or up the fancy. It felt like I was in a random burger spot but I’m paying Brazilian steakhouse prices because that’s what it’s supposed to be, their food tasted good but honestly wasn’t worth it. I got the rodizio experience that was supposed to be like the churrasco thing where they bring the meat to you continuously until you flip your card to red, they didn’t come by nearly enough with not enough options. 100% just going to fogo next time because although it’ll be crowded I know the food and service is well worth the price i pay (and they actually have lamb at fogo and other spots) if this place had lamb it was not brought out

google_reviews.text: Me and my husband recently stayed for our second stay- this time in winter (so very breathtaking in the snow!). Our experience was perfection! We stayed in the briargate room which was an absolutely lovely modern room enclosed within the main building- a 30 second walk to a 6 course dinner that was delicious with perfectly crafted martinis. My previous stay we stayed in an end unit in a larger room with a walk up entry, which was a short walk to the main property. Both stays were perfectly quiet, we slept like a dream and the beds and showers and robes are *chef’s kiss*. The first stay we came to Glen Gordon during my pregnancy and they made me delicious mocktails and mods to the menu for the night at my request. The fireplace in the lodge is gorgeous. I adored everything about my stay and will definitely be back!

Everything stood out! From the moment we checked in we felt so welcome. The tour of the house with a glass of champagne in hand was top notch. Our room was so comfortable and had everything we needed. The dinner was 5 star and so was the service. We couldn’t recommend Glen Gordon more. I have already recommended it to multiple others.

Dinner was amazing! The potato leek soup probably one of the best  dishes I've ever had in my life! Could have a large bowl of it! Wine pairings were fantastic! If you like bourbon, they have a great selection. Enjoyed Weller Single Barrel for the first time in my life, which was fantastic! The room, Windsor suite, was beautiful and my wife and I enjoyed soaking in the double tub together. Highly recommend this place! Landscaping is scenic, spacious, and very restfull!

Glen Gordon Manor is an absolute gem! Luxurious, historical, well-maintained property; picturesque inside and out. ALL staff are amazing, helpful, kind. Dinner and breakfast Our second annual stay in the Windsor suite. It was as grand as the first time. I hope we can continue to make it there again and again although it may become more difficult as more people learn about and experience Glen Gordon Manor.

Spent an amazing and relaxing weekend here! Booked the Indulgence Package as a birthday gift for my boyfriend, and everything was lovely from the champagne tour, cheese plate + chocolate roses + champagne welcome, massage to breakfast and dinner.

Service was exceptional - Matthew was great giving suggestions, helping us around, starting a fire for us. It snowed Saturday night, and we were happily surprised that the Glen Gordon team put our windshield wipers up! The horses and pony on the property were super friendly and sweet, and we loved seeing the chickens run around.

Dinner was well thought out across the five courses, and the pairings were on point. The servers also exuded the passion of the chefs.

Additionally, they had lots of suggestions of things to do in the area and we ended up doing the Linden Vineyard Vintage wine tasting as per their recommendation. We wanted to go for a hike but unfortunately couldn't walk as well since we had ultramarathons the weekend before + it was super duper windy. We'll be back to enjoy more of what Glen Gordon and the area has to offer!

google_reviews.text:
Absolutely delicious food! The ingredients were fresh and high quality. Flavors with so much depth you couldn't quite remember the entire experience of tasting it, and wanted to keep having more. They could be vibrant and delightfully surprising as well. I wish I knew how they pulled it off, but I didn't think I'd get away with sneaking into the kitchen to watch! The dishes were a treat for the eye as well. The best items we got were the Enchiladas De Camaron, Cob Seafood Caesar, and best of all, the Brochetas De Salmon Kung Pao. The only thing that was disappointing was the Chilaquiles. My party shared everything so we all got to experience more of their cooking.

The salmon in the Brochetas De Salmon Kung Pao was perfectly cooked and amazingly fresh. It easily flaked under a fork, the texture was almost creamy. The creamy Mexican rice was good on its own, but came with a caramel-colored sauce with a light zing that made it hard to stop eating it!

The Cob Seafood Caesar had a wonderful interplay of flavors and textures. Tomatoes and avocado were so fresh they shone on their own. The gentle vinegar on the tomatoes helped make the flavor pop without overwhelming the tomato. Fun chewy pieces of savory meat.

The Enchiladas De Camaron came drenched in a beautiful orange sauce. Perfectly uniform coloration that's hard to achieve at home. The enchiladas were soft with a lovely bite to the (shredded?) shrimp inside. Wonderful depth of flavor.

It's like they put all the effort into the food and none into the advertising. This might be the second time I've ever written a review, but the food was so amazing it's a pity no one knows about this place. The outside of the restaurant is nondescript, with a small sign saying "El Fish" far above eye level. You just see the large window with mostly empty tables and an indoor plant inside.

The ambiance was wonderful. It was quiet and calm. We could talk easily. Lots of natural sunlight, airy open space, soft tones on the walls.

We came here to celebrate my mom’s birthday but imagine the first impression upon entering is to be greeted by someone with a disgusting attitude and zero manners. He pretended not to hear me when I told him I had a reservation and instead of saying “I’m sorry I can’t hear you” he says "huh." It’s clear that I’m not the only person who has felt this way about this individual and you can see other reviews pointing out his horrendous attitude. It's the male manager with the hat that is mentioned in multiple other reviews. I’m surprised he’s still employed, it's incredibly surprising that an individual with such a terrible attitude holds a position where you interact with paying customers. I will echo that the rest of the wait staff was incredibly friendly and I am sorry that they need to work alongside this individual. You can see their discomfort when he is around and I'm sure it is a toxic work environment that should be investigated. The food itself was subpar and though creative lacks flavor. My recommendation is to stay away from this place. We will not be coming back.

Elevated Mexican dishes on the upper west side. Food is a little slow to come out but the service and atmosphere are lovely. The Cob Caesar salad is very generously portioned and filled with seafood - highly recommended!

The food in this restaurant is pretty good. the atmosphere is pretty good, but keep in mind. You are in the upper west, so the crowd was mostly older people, but still with good vibe. Overall, at dinner, the restaurant was almost full. I wish that you would have more privacy. many tables are just 2 people, one next to the other. So you hear Everyone's conversation, so some lack of privacy, the cocktail where good the Margarita, the chef's Margarita, it was good. The mule was just okay, and the service was okay as well. Nothing too exciting. I wish they would pay more attention to our requests. Also they suggested more food than we could consume. So we had a lot of leftovers are on the table.

Simply outstanding.  On the expensive side but is worth every $.  Service is quite attentive. Clearly staff is well trained.  We had Yucan fish chip which is fresh and flavorful. The best chip we had as they seem to be just coming out kitchen frier.  Tuna tartar was creative when they came out like taco. For main, we shared fried black bass over corn tomato-egg rice which is fried just right, seasoned just right.  The fired fish bone was justly lightly prepared and crispy, I finished all the bones! Definitely very happy an UWS restaurant that offers food with love ( which is quite rare these days IMO)

name: Tomi Jazz
document: Tomi Jazz. cuisine: Japanese Jazz & Blues. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We arrived on a Wednesday night around 5:45 pm and managed to get in just before 7:30 pm.  With only about 20 people ahead of us, the wait was definitely worth it. They play jazz every 30 minutes at 6:30, 7:30 and 8 pm.

The atmosphere is lovely, though it can get quite packed. It’s a great spot for a romantic date night rather than a large get-together.

The food was fantastic. I highly recommend the cod roe udon – it’s creamy and fishy but the kick of spice cuts through the fishy aftertaste.  The croquettes are also delicious, and the ominiyaki was very good, especially considering what I had in Japan.

The service was incredibly good. The food arrived quickly and the dishes were served right after each other without feeling rushed.

Overall, it was a very good experience. They accept cash and offer a 5% discount.

The atmosphere was amazing, the service was excellent, and the food was great. The drinks weren’t mind-blowing, but still nice and enjoyable.

As for the music, we saw two brilliant groups. The acoustics were great and the volume was perfect — loud enough to enjoy the performance but still low enough to hold a conversation.

Overall, a great spot with very reasonable prices compared to other jazz bars in the city. Would definitely come back.

One of my favorite places in New York to go out for a night, despite its long wait-times. Waiting in line can take more than an hour or two depending on the day.

Food:
Affordable and tasty food overall! I’ve had a lot of their menu selection and I have enjoyed every one of them. My favorite would be the hamburger steak and cod roe spaghetti.

Atmosphere:
Very cozy ambience with the candle-lot lighting and the chill live jazz. Feels very intimate!

Service:
The service is wonderful. Many times I’ve been here, when there was a seat closer to the live jazz the servers would offer if my party would like to sit closer. The staff are very friendly and attentive!

The atmosphere was phenomenal. The wait time was not because over 2 hrs waiting in line is insane granted we started waiting at 8pm on a Thursday night. We were so hungry, but some dishes are skips (Champon noodles and maybe the spam rice balls). I really enjoyed the Omurice and the cod roe udon. The popular dishes are popular for a reason!

I do have to say that the layout of this place is a bit awkward. There are tables where you cannot see the jazz band at all, so just be wary.

Not mad honestly at the 1hour 15minute wait. It felt like part of the experience but I wouldn’t have been happy if I had to wait closer to 2 hours. The food was pretty good and I agree with others that it’s not actually “intimate”, it really is just small and cramped. But it’s unique and an experience that I wouldn’t probably do again just for the vibe. You don’t get on a waiting list or have any idea of the wait time. It’s just a waiting game and many people ahead of us gave up. I wouldn’t say the food is ABOVE average but i have no complaints.

name: Maison Pickle
document: Maison Pickle. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Comfort Food Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Amazing Food and Outstanding Service – Highly Recommended

We visited as a party of two without a reservation and were seated immediately. From the moment we walked in, the staff greeted us warmly with eye contact and smiles. Even during busy moments, they continued to smile and acknowledge us whenever our eyes met, which made us feel very welcome and comfortable.

We ordered the steak & eggs and the chicken toast, and the food arrived quickly while we were chatting. The sweet and savory combination of the chicken toast was absolutely delicious, and the steak and eggs were cooked perfectly. It was a truly satisfying and enjoyable meal.

We paid in cash and weren’t able to leave a large tip, but the staff never made us feel uncomfortable or awkward about it. Every employee was incredibly kind and attentive, and we genuinely felt well taken care of. Even though we arrived without a reservation, the place filled up very quickly, which clearly showed how popular this restaurant is.

An excellent restaurant in every way—food, service, and atmosphere. Highly recommended!! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

American comfort food at it's best! Amazing setup, easy reservations, excellent and quick service is what our experience was all about.

Sasha, our server was friendly and was quick to take our order. We started off with drip coffees which were warm, Grilled Asparagus ($14) which was tasty and well cooked, Crab Cake Sandwich ($24), Mac and Cheese ($21), and Texas Toast Egg and Cheese Sandwich ($18). Food overall was pretty good, and tasty!

Service was quick, food arrived within 15-mins of ordering. Noise levels were on the average end and it was easy to have conversations. This will be one of our go-to options for brunch!

We came here to eat and OMG… everything was so good. The bread alone had me ready to come back soft, warm, buttery, literally perfect. I’m still thinking about it.

The portions here are HUGE in the best way. We didn’t get to try the cake, but when I tell you the slices were humongous… like the size of a whole birthday cake 😭😂 Just watching it go to another table had us in shock. Next time I’m 100% getting one.

The food overall was amazing. The chicken, the mac and cheese, the breakfast dishes everything was cooked perfectly, seasoned well, and super flavorful. You can tell they actually take their time with the food. The plates come out looking like something you see on TikTok.

The vibe inside is really nice too warm lighting, cute setup, and the service was great. Our food came out quick and hot.

I honestly recommend this place to everybody. If you love good food and big portions, this is the spot. I’m definitely coming back to try more stuff on the menu because everything looked too good.

We’ve been here before, and each time it’s great. It’s classic American comfort food - big portions, friendly staff, comfortable seating and tables. The French dips are their specialty, and they’re great - messy, yes, but satiating and impossible not to enjoy yourself while eating. The patty melt was great also - huge, almost impossible to eat, but the meat was great and it was nice with jus. We weren’t overly impressed with the deviled eggs or French onion soup as they were just a touch plain, but the restaurant week deal was excellent value and there really was nothing we didn’t enjoy!

Me and my bf went here 2 times, and gotta say this is affordable and they were generous with the portion size. I love love their bread butter pan. We always ordered their French dip. First time, we went we went overboard with it. We thought it was small portion but the portion were huge! At the end, we have a lot of left over. Second time, we went with my brothers and we ordered the same thing again everything taste great. The server were nice and attentive. During the summer it can be hot especially down stairs  would suggest like ac? Fan weren’t enough for us. Everything came out to be below $100!!

document: Liberty Bagels Midtown. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Bagels Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Liberty Bagels Midtown is absolute chaos in the best possible way. Place was packed—standing room only—like a bagel-themed subway car at rush hour. But honestly? Worth it.

The bagels are so good they should come with a warning label. Chewy, fresh, and clearly the reason everyone in Midtown decided to be in the same square footage at the same time. Staff somehow kept things moving despite the crowd, which felt like an Olympic-level achievement.

If you’re looking for a quiet, meditative breakfast… this ain’t it. If you want a top-tier bagel and a story to tell afterward, get in line and embrace the madness. 🥯👏

The best bagels in midtown in my opinion. I got the bacon egg and cheese on a garlic bagel, so good. The shop is extremely crowded every time I'm in, but the service is quick and you're in and out very fast. I also got a dozen bagels which was quick and easy.

Colorful and fun experience. Expect to wait in line about 15-20 mins tops but very worth it. Once you get inside be ready with your order, would recommend to research before going lots of bagels and schmear to choose from. I am a somewhat purist so plain bagel and cream cheese for me but make it colorful please. Can't rate service higher since it's basically : what's your order, here's your bagel and get out from all the noise and standing shoulder to shoulder to the 30 people that are inside quite a small amount of space. Overall would recommend.

Unbelievable bagels and great service!

I stopped by Liberty Bagels Midtown during a mother–daughter weekend in NYC, and it did not disappoint! It’s an easy walk from 5th Avenue, and even though the line forms outside, it moves quickly thanks to the nice gentleman managing the flow of traffic.

Orders are handled super efficiently—pickups are brought right to the door for fast access. Inside there’s a small standing bar, and outside you’ll find a few tables on the patio if you want to enjoy your food there.

The staff was friendly, the service was quick, and the food was incredible. I had a blueberry bagel with egg, sausage, and cheese—honestly one of the best bagels I’ve ever had. And don’t skip the hash browns—they’re worth it!

Highly recommend this spot for anyone craving a true New York bagel experience.

Go for the Rainbow bagel. You know you want to. We did and enjoyed it along with some other bagel options. Bonus: you can also get a red white and blue Liberty bagel. Plenty of cream cheese choices too. The crowds were wild but manageable. Started outside and they let you in one group at a time. Then you wait inside in a split line to order. Then you wait again in the pickup line once it’s ready. Whole process took about 20 min or so. Limited seating/standing outside. Share if you need to or take to go. Must try spot if in the area.

name: Locanda Verde
document: Locanda Verde. cuisine: Italian Desserts Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: What an amazing evening! I’ve had the pleasure of dining at this old New York gem a couple of times over the last few months, and Caiden at the bar has made it an extraordinary experience, even feel at home. I first came to Laconda with my family in 2012 for a birthday and had an amazing dinner. Now over 10 years later they still have some of the best Italian food, service, and drinks in the city. Caiden got me up to speed on the menu changes, and helped make this celebration unforgettable. Starting off with the champagne coutier and sheep’s milk ricotta— this combo will leave you dreaming about it for weeks to come. Other apps worth recommending are the exquisite (melt in your mouth) wagyu steak tartare and the perfectly balanced insalata Andrea. All of the mains are great, but Locanda prepares pasta like it’s Italy. Grandmas ravioli are delightful, although I wish it came with more sauce, and the lamb ragu papardelle is my favorite. Rich, delightful, creamy, I thought I was already full but devoured the whole plate. The prime NY Strip steak is fine but I’d recommend apps and pastas route to get the most out of the experience. I also must commend Caiden the bartender, we had the best espresso martinis of our lives with their home style creamy tiramisu for dessert. Thank you Locanda for holding what feels like golden age New York, with delicious food, amazing drinks, and undeniable service. Be back soon!

Walking into Locanda Verde in 2025 feels a bit like attending a high school reunion for the Cool Kids of 2009. The volume is still turned up to eleven, the room is still packed with the sort of energetic, golden-hued crowd that suggests something important is happening, and the ghost of Robert De Niro’s patronage still hovers in the rafters like a guardian angel of reservations.

But if the ambiance is still partying like it’s the Obama administration, the food seems to be suffering from a bit of a hangover.
We arrived ready to worship at the altar of Chef Andrew Carmellini’s urban Italian temple. And to be fair, the Sheep’s Milk Ricotta remains the restaurant’s security blanket. Served with that burnt orange toast, it is creamy, fluffy, and reliable—a reminder of why this place became a landmark to begin with. The Lamb Meatball Sliders also did their job: bite-sized punches of flavor that pair perfectly with a loud conversation and a glass of Nebbiolo.

However, once we moved past the "greatest hits" appetizers, the cracks in the veneer began to show.

The Lamb Chops Scottadito were the culinary equivalent of a shrug. For a dish whose name translates to "burned fingers" (implying they are so delicious you can't wait to grab them), these were safely fork-and-knife territory. They arrived looking uninspired, accompanied by a small, lonely triangle of what the menu calls "chickpea panelle" but what the palate registers as "sad, dry polenta." It felt like a dish going through the motions.

Similarly, the Black Shells Frutti di Mare—squid ink pasta that should smell like the ocean in the best way—missed the mark. You want "briny and bright"; we got "tired and murky." When seafood doesn't feel 100% fresh in a place charging Tribeca rents, the illusion of luxury dissolves pretty quickly.
We rounded things out with the Fire-Roasted Garlic Chicken and the Gnocchi, both of which were… fine. And that’s the problem. In a city where Italian dining is a blood sport, "fine" is the first step toward irrelevance.

The Verdict:

Locanda Verde has undeniably lost some of its luster. It is currently a restaurant coasting on its location and its legacy. If you want to feel the pulse of the city, drink good wine, and shout over the din in a beautiful room, it’s still a contender. But if you’re looking for a meal that haunts your dreams? You might be a decade too late.
The food and service were outstanding.  The dining room was a little loud but will definitely go back. Great mix of sweet and savory dishes. Didn’t try the pasta, but it looked delicious.

great and fresh pasta perfect for a business lunch or a date night in fidi. we got a few apps to share and the salmon and trout to share for the mains. wine is fab and service is very good. lots of space so you have a great meal with your party.

At first I thought with the name it would be Spanish, but turns out it's an Italian spot in Greenwich. The appetizers were solid - the toasted bread with what looked like eggplant or wild mushroom (I'll ask the guy who ordered) was fantastic, tasty and a good treat.

The lamb meatball sliders were top heavy and ok. Regular sliders probably would've been the way to go. Steak tartare was good. Gabagool and grana was capicola and and a hard cheese which was ok, but not easy to eat - heavy/oily.

The pappardelle with lamb bolognese was ok, overly salty - ended up eating most of the pasta (some of the sheets stuck together, though, so that wasn't edible), and leaving much of the lamb bolognese (greasy, but better than the meatball sliders).

Good thing - service was quick and efficient and knowing the business nearby (Citi) they asked us how fast we needed to be out - and they kept us mostly on-time, nicely enough.

Decor inside was dark woods and bottles all over of liquor and wine. Bathrooms downstairs. They have some private dining spaces and they were packed at lunchtime on a Wednesday.

name: Le Rock
document: Le Rock. cuisine: French Cocktail Bars Brasseries. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Last Saturday we went for dinner at LeRock. Our experience was wonderful. The food, the atmosphere, the staff… From the first to the last minute, everything felt special, and every person in my party had an awesome time.

We had Christmas Eve dinner here and it was a wonderful experience! There was a partial view of the tree from our seat but it was still very special. The dining room isn’t super large and feels cozy and festive. It wasnt too noisy either. Service was great, very professional. There was a moment when they cleared crumbs off the table and accidentally brushed some onto my dads lap😅

The food was wonderful! The flavors were delicious and filled us up. I read other reviews that the portions were small but I wouldn’t agree. Only the lobster was “small” as the serving was only half a lobster. I had the Dover sole and got very full. The starter burrata pasta was so delicious I almost wished it was my main!

Exceptional dining experience I had for my birthday.

We particularly enjoyed the snails, steak, and the traditional French dessert, as well as the table with a view of the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree.

Our waiter’s suggestion regarding the excellent fries was also correct. He is also very helpful with recommending the menu items and super friendly to the children.

A wonderful evening, we look forward to dining again.

A perfect restaurant in a prime touristy location if you want to see Xmas tree or a skating ring. Elevated enough buy not pretentious and decently priced for the area. The cheeseburger is a bit underwhelming with not much flavors but the quality of meat was very good. My friend's tuna tartar was ok, on a  smaller side. The bread basket use to be much better, now it is just 5 pieces of a baguette.

Had an amazing lunch experience at Le Rock today, this is the quintessential French Bistro located within in heart of Rockefeller center in Midtown Manhattan. The restaurant was crowded and noisy but the food and service were fantastic today. We will definitely be returning to this fine establishment!

name: Hey Yuet
document: Hey Yuet. cuisine: Dim Sum Cantonese. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Probably the Top 1 Dim Sum place I have ever tried in the U.S. Fabulous vibe instantly brings you back to the Republican Era. They not only make authentic dim sum but also offer a few special ones that I haven’t seen in other places. Plus, you will be shocked by their price!!! Highly recommend!

A friend of mine who is Cantonese wanted Chinese food but he did not want us to travel to  Flushing. We read the review on Trip Advisor. Three gave it excellent ratings  and 1 gave it average or in other words 4 reviews and not much of a sampling. Actually the reviews had no detail just the basic reviews of food, the space etc Nothing that gave you much to go on. We went. There is no WOW factor and nothing memorable but it’s in the neighborhood and I do want them to succeed.

The service is ok and maybe a tad chaotic. I think the young men are nice and try to do well but there is no congeniality and I think part of the problem might be lack of staff. Maybe a staff member called in sick or it’s lack of training which means that’s a managerial issue. We still have no idea why things were served in the order that they were served and why plates weren’t offered at the right time.
But I will say the staff  seemed to overwhelmed.

THE DRINKS- I would stick to beer and wine or simple drinks on the rocks. What was impressive MACALLAN was on the drink list.

Food- the shumai was probably the best item. The white rice was moist and NOT OVERCOOKED most Americans just think it’s a filler and they do not pay much attention to it but my Chinese grandsons if were there would have gobbled omit down. The dish with rice where you pick 2 meats: duck, chicken or pork. I would not pick the duck. The green bean dish was good but the beans were chopped into too small of pieces. The cooked cabbage with one dish was simply bland but cooked appropriately (al dente). My Cantonese guest thought we should atleast come back but try other dishes. But my POV was food in NYC is not cheap but their prices here were solid. I eat out over 300 meals a year and I love discovering little jewels. Sadly this was not a little jewel but maybe my Cantonese guest saw something that I didn’t. Therefore, I will give it another chance and hope to find out that it is a little jewel. I will share a Happy Chinese New Year and RAMADAN MUBARAK since both holidays are back to back this year. Xie Xie

This place has great reviews, so since I was in the neighborhood, I decided to check it out.

The food was just okay. The soup dumplings were mediocre, and the chicken chow fun was fine but a bit bland. Ironically, the best thing I had was the jasmine tea.

The most disappointing part, however, was the service — or rather, the lack of it. The restaurant was nearly empty, yet it took a long time to get a waiter’s attention just to place my order. Dirty dishes were left piling up and were only cleared after I finished eating and paid. There was no one around to even ask for a napkin.

I dislike leaving a small tip, but the staff’s attitude felt as though they were doing customers a favor by being there. Given the service, it was hard to justify tipping at all.

The food here is okay. None of the food we ordered came hot.  Most of it was slightly warm or room temp. Portions are small for the prices.
The pan fried dumplings here are good.  Well filled and not too doughy. I would come here and just order a few serving of the pan fried dumplings. They are superior to the soup dumplings, which you can skip. I like that they serve both steamed and crispy roast pork buns but they weren't hot.
The beef chow fun is tasty.  I would recommend it. And the Chinese broccoli is delicious.
This restaurant can randomly get very busy.  Make a reservation if you can.

Walking into HEY YUET feels like stepping through a time capsule straight to 1950s Hong Kong warm lights, vintage décor, and the comforting aroma of freshly steamed dim sum.
Great aesthetic and an extensive menu featuring authentic Cantonese cuisine.

name: Kashkaval Garden
document: Kashkaval Garden. cuisine: Mediterranean Fondue Tapas Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Post-theatre dinner at Kashkaval Gardens, a true hidden gem in Hell’s Kitchen.

They have a wonderful Mediterranean menu (+ happy hour from 3-6). We feasted on an assortment of kabobs and squash caponata.

Make sure you have a reservation! It was empty when we arrived, but by the time we left, there wasn’t an empty table in the entire restaurant.

A shout out to David, THE most entertaining bartender in NYC!

Such a lovely experience having dinner here. The back room was so cozy but overall the entire place is very nice and cozy. Food was delicious and the mocktails were tasty. They also have a prixe fix that looked great but didn’t have the stomach space for it. Service was awesome and everyone working there is extremely nice and on top of it. We will definitely be coming back!

We visited Kashkaval Garden two weeks in a row, and both times were absolutely amazing.
Last week, we enjoyed a delicious truffle cheese fondue paired with a Lambrusco, and our server truly made the evening complete.

This week, we were back in New York and couldn’t resist returning to this restaurant. We ended up spending four hours at the table, enjoying cheese boards, pitas, everything was perfect. I was even surprised with a prosecco for my birthday, which made the night extra special.

Another top evening, with a special thanks to Hayden.
Can’t wait to come back soon!

Loved the borek. The atmosphere was really classic and homey and the bartender B was so attentive and friendly. She made everyone at the bar feel so comfortable. I had a winter in Manhattan and it was the perfect winter drink. Highly recommend. Want to come back to get the old fashioned cold brew when I need to stay up later.

We happened upon this little gem our last visit to NYC. Very cool atmosphere with an open air front. We were able to get seats at the bar as all the tables were full. It was happy hour and we started with the Four Mezze platter. We chose: babaganoush, Tzaziki, hummus and Turkish Bean Salad which came with 4 warm pitas. This turned out to be our meal as we were pleasantly full and indulged in the chocolate torte for dessert. We would love to go back next time we visit NYC.

name: Black Iron Burger
document: Black Iron Burger. cuisine: Burgers Beer, Wine & Spirits Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Visited 2/3/26
Went in at lunchtime on a Tuesday and it was not packed at all so we got a table super quick. My wife and I both got the smash burger but she had her's on a gluten free bun as she has an allergy to gluten. Burgers were amazing! We love when we can find a place that serves grass fed beef. It really makes a difference in the flavor of the burger. Her gluten free bun was great too! Fries were like McDonald's size, which we love since they are usually crunchier, and they were. I also got a chocolate milkshake and it was very tasty as well. We did try and come back on a Friday night around 6pm and it was paaaacked! There was a 20 min wait and we had to go meet friends so bummer this place isn't a little bit bigger, but honestly that's more of a compliment than a downside! Would highly recommend this spot if you're in this area! 💯👍

I just ordered 2 turkey burgers, onion rings, two extra sauces and a gingerale for almost 60 bucks.... I received everything but the gingerale and who want food with no drink? The burgers was good but could use more seasonings and the onion rings were good  as well but didnt taste like much without the sauce it came with. I got the spicy mayo and I guess it was spicy for a child but I felt no heat and the espresso BBQ sauce was really good. I which I got 2... and sadly this food is delivered from the restaurant and they forgot my drink which is silly when you work there and know to read everything before you pack it but they didnt. Oh well. Good but its not good enough to spend that much money and not get everything... also they dont offer regular mayo... you have to buy mayo with this and that but nothing regular.  I mean sometimes you need and want regular mayo especially when you are getting something with the works..

Fast-paced, buzzing burger joint with a mix of Latin apps and flavors at the edges. Nice dark style with a bar in back and sports on tv throughout. Midtown prices play to tourists and families, but the service and quality are built for New York standards.

I had the mushroom truffle cheeseburger with fries and coleslaw; I was hungry and it was good. Portions were thankfully right-sized and not bulging. Moscow Mule cocktails were on point and not syrupy. Service was kind and sustained.

I recommend making reservations. The place is narrow and they push table tops, but it was jammed the whole time I was there (5-6pm on a Saturday). Also, be aware there are *two* and I came here to the 38th location after booking at the other one. Google Maps didn’t show the other location when I searched. The host was kind enough to call the other place.

Love the vibes, the food, the  drinks, the music & most importantly,….. the food!!!! Burgers come out quick and delicious. We finished our meal in less then 40 mins from be seated to last bite. Servers are very pleasant and helpful. Definitely going back

A Place who find the best match between burger and food quality. I'm italian, I know what good food is and this Place Is the best One in NY.
The meat quality Is Amazing, the bread so tasty. Comfortable and clean Place with identity Is a must to do in NY.
Reservation Is Better

name: Monkey Thief
document: Monkey Thief. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 4.9 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Brunch at Monkey Thief did not come to play. The space is small and cozy, but the design is beautiful and gives off Southeast Asian vibes that really set the tone. The food was packed with flavor and felt like a fun twist on brunch favorites.

Everything we ordered hit the spot, especially the creativity behind each dish. That said, the lamb burger could’ve been better for the price. At $21, the patty was a lot smaller than expected, and there was more bun than burger. It looked great but just didn’t deliver on portion. Also, one of our dishes didn’t make it to the kitchen due to a mix-up, but we were fine skipping it and still left full and satisfied.

It’s the kind of spot that feels like a hidden gem. I’d definitely come back next time I’m visiting.

This trendy spot offers a brief menu from raw bar to fried chicken.  In line with their positioning as a cocktail bar, it is a rather loud space.  So I wouldn’t recommend for a quiet meal.  However, if you don’t mind the buzz the food is absolutely delicious.  Given the menu is largely small plates, we had an assortment of dishes and enjoyed every single one of them.

The Beef Koi was very good.  Diced and in a spicy sauce, it was a unique plating that packed a good spice.  The mash up of flavors in the croquettes was impressive.  Delicious cheesiness while also a mix of flavors from the chutneys.  The calamari was a big hit.  Not your typical calamari at all, this was proper pieces that had been lightly breaded and dashed with seasoning.  The sauce it came with added a kick.  Definitely worth trying.

We also had the Chicken Satay, Dumplings and Chicken Bao.  The chicken skewer was tender with a pretty standard peanut sauce, the dumplings packed a lot of flavor in their filling and the Chicken Bao had such good chicken on it, we ended up adding the Fried Chicken to our order.  And that was perhaps the best plate of all.  This bowl of boneless fried chicken, we ordered the large, was filled with taste.  The chicken was juicy and tender and the breading had a little spice to it with cumin and a mix of others.  This is the dish not to miss served along side of a cucumber salad.

From a drink perspective, we tried an assortment and you really can’t go wrong.  An upside for a crafted cocktail space, they were quite swift.  We had two rounds and at no point did it seem like we were waiting long for drinks.  The wait staff was also very quick to clear empty plates and bring water which was helpful given we ordered so much.

Helpful reviews? Check us out on IG @jjluxtravel

Stopped in on a busy night hoping they could squeeze us in for a table and fortunately they could! The atmosphere was very chill and there was vibrant conversation at the tables, but not so loud we couldn’t chat amongst ourselves. The tables were small, parties larger than 2 or 4 may struggle walking in and getting a table easily.

Great drink menu with a good variety of unique hand crafted cocktails. Food was delicious and there were quite a few dish options. The waitstaff gave us great advice on what to order and how to choose between cocktails and dishes. We came back for brunch on a different day and the menu was a bit more limited, but still delicious. My only negative feedback was we felt a bit “nickeled and dimed” when we needed additional sauce for a dish when we ran out - they charged us for the additional (which was less than a tablespoon portion size). We had spent plenty on other food and multiple cocktails, so it would have been nice if they “threw it in” without the extra charge. We plan to come back and bring friends the next time we’re in NYC.

Amazing food and cocktails, in this beautiful place! I loved the sesame inspired 7 Long Years cocktail, and the food was all amazing! The fries packed a flavorful punch, the croquettes were delicious, and the fried rice was perfectly crispy. Will definitely revisit to try out more from the menu, and would highly recommend the place!

Don’t get the bok choi—it’s too charred and it’s like a mouth of ashes. Ask for the bao to be warm—it’s not as good when the bao is kinda chilly… the temp and size makes it feel more like a happy hour appetizer. Drinks are fun, but on the sweet side and there’s not too many spirit forward options. Coconut salad nice but small. The rice was good, but wouldn’t have been notable without the egg. Server was super nice with a great smile.

name: Ye's Apothecary
document: Ye's Apothecary. cuisine: Szechuan Speakeasies. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This place was absolutely gorgeous! My girlfriend and I visited to celebrate our anniversary and they were sure to make it special for the both of us. The whole speakeasy vibe was definitely selling as there was a lot of antique decor littering the walls and the ceiling. The waiter was very attentive and visited us every once in a while to check in and made sure we enjoyed the food and drinks. Speaking of which, the cocktails were expertly made and were the absolute selling point of the company. Also a great spot for photography. Thank you guys for making our night spectacular!!!

Amazing food and experience here. We only came for apps and drinks but I will definitely be returning to try more of the menu. We had the spicy yellow beef and potstickers, highly recommend. The nude and noble cocktail was also delish. The atmosphere is great, service was 10/10. The host and everyone was so professional and service was quick.

The worst part of our experience at Ye’s Apothecary was definitely the service. Our server seemed completely uninterested in working, she spent most of the time on her phone and chatting with the bartender instead of paying attention to the tables.

She brought a bottle of tap water to the table but didn’t even serve it; we had to pour it ourselves the entire night. She never came back to check on us, ask how the food was, or see if we wanted another drink. It honestly felt like we were a burden.

Drinks arrived almost 10 minutes after the food, which is unacceptable, especially considering the restaurant was not full. The bar was extremely slow for the amount of people there, although I have to say the cocktails themselves were delicious.

The food was really good and the atmosphere is nice, but unfortunately the service completely ruined what could have been a great experience. We ended up leaving the place very quickly.

American-style Chinese cuisine cannot be compared with the traditional authentic Chinese cuisine. The prices are a bit on the high side.
The environment is actually quite good.

Ye's Apothecary，Appetizers? Sichuan Wontons exploded with flavor, Chili Filet O' Fish was "I'll-have-two, please" good, and Changsha Spiced Chicken surprisingly paired well with pineapple (who knew?). Friendly staff, perfect sound levels, and lounge vibes make Ye's ideal for dates or small gatherings. Love the place! We'll be back – with a paper reservation confirmation 😂  a must try guys!

name: Ocean Prime
document: Ocean Prime. cuisine: Seafood Steakhouses Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
We spent an afternoon in DC and decided to stay for dinner.

Our waitress, Angelica, was incredible. The entire staff was very attentive. The service was exceptional to match the food. Many items were either GF or could be modified if requested.

It was busy with evening crowds, boasting many there for work meetings.

The ambiance was perfect for a couple, to celebrate a special occasion, or to have  dinner while working.

It was not overly crowded and during the week we were able to get seated right away. Bonus is there is a Parking Garage a few doors down, so no need to stress about that.

For me to give all 5 stars it has to be fantastic Ocean Prime Seafood is fantastic! The service, the ambiance and how about the food and dessert? Yummy! I had the Blackened Red Snapper, Warm Butter Cake for dessert, Berries & Bubbles cocktail & lime mojito (so good I forgot to take a pic).
Excellent food and drinks. Very impressive and expensive. Definitely will be going again. Hit the happy hour if you want to save money. Reservations need for dinner bit has a large bar area.

There's not enough stars to measure the unmatched experience we had on Valentine's Day! We were escorted to a beautifully decorated VIP Room that sat four couples intimately at tables. The appetizers (oysters, bread basket and salad) were great starters. Then the entrees were superb (waygu steak, sirloin, garlic jalapeño au gratin potatoes, asparagus & hollandaise). For dessert I had Creme Brulee with the most delectable caramelized top!!! The wine was delicious, the cocktail was impeccable. The service was top tier!! Dazhai was so attentive, personable and informative! She knew the menu and brought forth such a beautiful air and lightness to the space. Wonderful time for a first time....the bar has been set! Thank you, Ocean Prime!

Ocean Prime DC is a true gem! We booked our reservation through OpenTable, which made everything easy and seamless. I started with the Berries and Bubbles, which had a stunning presentation with dry ice smoke swirling around the glass. For appetizers, my husband and I absolutely loved the Asian Thai styled calamari and the crab cakes. Both were flavorful and perfectly prepared. We then shared the lobster linguine with shrimp scampi, which was rich, fresh, and a perfect dish for two.

For dessert, we enjoyed the complimentary butter cake with berry sauce and ice cream, which was the perfect sweet ending to an incredible meal.

The highlight of the evening, though, was the outstanding service. Do yourself a favor and ask to be seated in Jiya’s section. She went above and beyond to make our dining experience special.

Highly recommend Ocean Prime for an elevated dining experience in DC!

name: The Gyro Project
address1: MIDTOWN CONVENTION CENTER HOTEL, 505 W 37th St
document: The Gyro Project. cuisine: Mediterranean Greek. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: This place was absolutely delicious. It was easily one of the best gyros I have had in New Jersey. I ordered the gyro fries as well, and they were just as impressive. The portions were generous, especially for the price, and everything was packed with flavor. The interior is beautifully designed with a great vibe, making it a comfortable spot for lunch, dinner, or even getting some work done. It was my first time visiting, and I will definitely be coming back with my family. I highly recommend it.

They deserve to market themselves as “fine-fast food” - it’s the best Greek fast food we’ve had in the US. The gyro is authentic, they use quality ingredients, the staff was friendly, it’s clean, the atmosphere is cozy & inviting, and the shop with imported Greek products was very nostalgic for us Greeks! 100/10 recommend. Delicious.

Such a great Greek spot! The vibe is beautiful and super inviting. The girls who helped us were so sweet and friendly. I had the spanakopita and baklava—both were absolutely delicious. We also got the Greek club sandwich, which was fresh and really tasty, and the fries were cooked perfectly. Highly recommend and will definitely be back to try more desserts!

Last night, I had the pleasure of dining at the Gyro Project in Fort Lee, NJ, and it was a delightful experience. Having moved to New Jersey years ago, I’ve struggled to find gyros that compare to those from my hometown. When a childhood friend visited, we decided to give this place a shot.

Nestled among a variety of eateries, the Gyro Project stood out with its bright, colorful decor and ample parking. The ambiance felt reminiscent of a traditional Grecian courtyard, making it quite inviting. Despite walking in on the tail end of a busy evening, the staff managed to maintain a well-organized atmosphere. I appreciated the selection of Greek products available for purchase, adding to the authenticity.

The girl at the counter was incredibly sweet as I placed my order. I opted for the classic gyro (sans fries), lentil soup, and chicken skewers, while my friend chose a gyro bowl with lemon herb potatoes. Everything was fresh and full of flavor. We couldn’t resist trying the mini spanakopita, which was a fantastic choice.

There was a slight hiccup when they forgot to bring my friend’s dinner out, but the staff handled it graciously. They remade my gyro to ensure it was warm and even offered us dessert on the house. Their attentive service truly made a difference.

Overall, my first visit to the Gyro Project was enjoyable, and we all agreed it’s worth a return trip. While it may not fully match the expectations set by the two gyro spots I grew up with, it certainly comes close.

This Greek restaurant has a really nice ambiance and spacious decor which makes it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. The service is fast and friendly. The food is delicious. The dip sampler was amazing and we got the gyro platter which was also really tasty. Overall, it’s a great spot for good food, a comfortable atmosphere, and efficient service—I’d definitely come back.
