name: Cantina Cubana
document: Cantina Cubana. cuisine: Cuban Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
My friends and I came on a Sunday and did the 3 hour bottomless brunch. The music was amazing, vibes in the air, drinks were flowing and food was delicious. The place is small but perfect because it allows the staff to cater to you without long wait times in between. The staff was friendly and attentive. I don't usually drink mojitos, but theirs was definitely yummy.
If you're looking for a Cuban style bottomless brunch, this is the place to be.

This place is definitely a bang for your buck! A lot of food for the normal entree price in NYC. The place is small and kind of tucked away in the East Village. The service was quick and tables were intimate. Pretty casual joint as well. Food is good! The food was delicious and very authentically Cuban. I had the Cuban sandwich which was crispy, buttery and soft. My family loved both the oxtail soup and the avocado relleno which  were both great.

Came here with my husband and two young kids for lunch on Sunday. The server was lovely and warm, the food was fresh and delicious (we had a bunch of starters a Cuban sandwich and roasted pork) and very authentic. Really enjoyed it here!!

Great Latin restaurant, not only serving Cuban food, but many traditional Latin dishes!
Worth trying, good quality/value

name: Shinjuku Ramen
document: Shinjuku Ramen. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I was drawn in by the interior, it really feels like a ramen shop in Japan.
The staff were very efficient, and the food came out quickly, which really stood out to me since many other restaurants take much longer. The tonkotsu ramen was delicious, and the portion was more than enough.
It’s also a great place for photos. I came with my Japanese friend, who told me that many Japanese celebrities have visited this place.

Great food, this is my first ramen in New York… and I’m surprised that they serve really good ramen.
Fantastic soup, pork was really tasty and soft, noodles cooked at perfect firmness.
Love it.

Just my table was very close to the toilet, so sometimes the smell of the cleaning liquid was pretty strong and it definitely makes me want to finish the bowl and go. Otherwise, I’m very satisfied with the ramen.

First off, I recommend you make reservations for this Ramen spot. My cousin made reservations for five people for 2pm. I came here with my family for our reservation and this place was packed. So I recommend a reservation because there was a small wait even with a reservation. Also this restaurant is small and a bit cramped so it isn’t very spacious. The service at this ramen spot was okay and could have been a little better. As for the food it also wasn’t too bad. I got the Mapo Don with extra udon and miso soup. I feel like the Mapo Don would have been better with a side of rice instead of the udon.

The black ink tonkotsu was pretty amazing. I hadn't had that type of ramen before and I really enjoyed it. Loved the crispy garlic too. The pork slices could have been more "melt in your mouth", but it was still fantastic.

The $17 tonkotsu ramen lunch set (with chashu pork rice and hijiki salad) was a comforting meal, perfect for cold weather. The black king ramen with squid ink is another great option, highlighting Shinjuku’s mastery of the broth and the noodle texture. Dining would have been a near-perfect experience had service been more welcoming. Even during the busy lunch period, there is no place for being curt and snappish,

name: Friedman's
document: Friedman's. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Gluten-Free New American. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: My absolute favorite restaurant in New York City! Beautiful interior, modern yet cosy American flair and food. The service is really friendly, well informed and super fast. The food has exceptional quality, a lot of gluten free options are available, including pancakes, fried chicken, waffles, bread and toast. The fryer is completely gluten free, something like this does not happen often. The servers are well informed about gluten and can provide additional information. Pancakes, fried chicken and co are also available as a side dish, allowing you to try more food. Everything is reasonably priced and the food arrives super fast. 12/10 would recommend again.
I’ve been here several times and always received the best food, the best service! Their chicken waffle is amazing!!!! But this place is always crowded. Better reserve a seat before you come.

Definitely recommend to try this place .  We had a great time here. Our breakfast was good.  People are nice and friendly.  Atmosphere was great.  My meal was OK. I got myself shakshuka. It was good but little bit too much bitterness/sour tomatoes.  Omelet was great.  One more thing  coffee was not good.  But overall great place,  good service and friendly atmosphere.

We chose this restaurant for Thanksgiving because I have Celiac. We started with the Mac & cheese bites which were amazing! My sister ordered the prefix Thanksgiving dinner which she really enjoyed. I took advantage of the chance to have gluten-free fried chicken, mac & cheese, and roasted Brussel sprouts. Everything was delicious. The only thing that could have been better was the apple pie crumble. It was served cold even though the waitress said it was a warm dish. When I let her know that it actually wasn’t warm,  she did not  offer to heat it up.

Perfect pre-MSG concert spot! Walked in during their Happy Hour, which is daily from 2-6pm! FYl, their HH bevs are always avail, but their HH small bites are only avail on the weekdays. We shared everything as a party of 3 and it was just right:
- Sweet Potato Fries (HH): Plentiful and the perfect finger food to pick on
- Buffalo Wings (HH): Standardly coated with the right level of spice
- Korean BBQ Wings (HH): Reminds me of a soy garlic flavor, YUM!
- Classic BLAT (Reg item): Shared this w my sister and it came with fries too! This was the right amt to share with all the HH items we got

Overall, would return for a reliable, decent American bite if I have another concert nearby. Spacious restaurant, clean restrooms, and helpful staff.

name: Ernesto’s
document: Ernesto’s. cuisine: Basque. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Ernesto’s has been a long time favorite.

Our server, Alex, was incredibly attentive but not overbearing.

We started with their complimentary chips and delicious salsa. I ordered a frozen margarita, unfortunately there was way too much sour mix for my tastes and I couldn’t drink it. We ordered the chicken quesadilla, kids mozzarella sticks with fries, and carnitas tacos. The quesadilla was humongous with a generous helping of chicken. The mozzarella sticks and fries were perfectly crisp and tasty. The carnitas were soaked in a tomatillo sauce and were divine complimented by the fresh avocado. The tacos were served with refried beans and rice, not were underwhelming. The rice was dry and the beans were very under seasoned.

The restaurant itself is very clean with plenty of seating. We came between the lunch and dinner rush so it wasn’t very busy.

Overall, I’d recommend Ernesto’s.

Had dinner here last night with family and had a wonderful experience. Despite the restaurant being very busy, the service was excellent, friendly, attentive, and never rushed. Every dish was cooked perfectly and full of flavor, especially the Pescado Alex I ordered, which was outstanding. We also noticed a table nearby enjoying the Ernesto’s Especial Parrillada, and it looked absolutely delicious. I’ll definitely be back and plan to try that next time.

We tried this place again.  It had been some time since we last visited.  The mole was OK, but a bit sweet and not ve.ry spicy.  The chicken it covered a bit overdone.  The chimichanga was mostly tortilla wrap, and not very fried.  And, what is with orange cheese?  The chips were light and the roasted salsa good.  Overall, though, not a very inspired meal.

Nice local place for good Mexican food. We loved the super friendly service and the atmosphere. Not a lot of veg options, but the one they have is a hit - Spinach Enchiladas with tomatillo sauce, killer. Definitely much better than the usual red sauce enchiladas. We loved the Fajitas and the drink selection. We got Tacos to go for my son, the food packaging was excellent 😊

This is a great local spot for some delicious Mexican food. Tasty guacamole without lime juice (just the way we like it); creamy queso; fresh made chips; yummy steak; delicious top shelf margarita!

Service was very friendly and attentive, which matches the inviting and comfortable atmosphere.

Menu items are reasonably priced with ample parking in the shopping center.

Highly recommended by @WineDinenVacay

document: Sentir. cuisine: Mexican Kosher. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I just had the most incredible meal and I can honestly say it’s the best vegan Mexican food I’ve ever had. Every dish was packed with flavor, fresh ingredients, and the service was amazing.
The quesadillas were hands down the best I’ve ever had — perfectly crispy on the outside, melty and savory inside, and so satisfying you’d never guess they’re plant-based. And whatever you do, don’t skip the chocolate chili tart. It’s rich, slightly spicy, and

I had an amazing experience at Sentir Vegan Mexican Restaurant in Manhattan! The fully vegan Mexican menu is incredibly flavorful - the tacos and plant-based chorizo quesadillas really stood out and tasted like dishes you’d expect from a traditional Mexican kitchen. Don’t forget about churros and citrus tres leches for dessert! 🍮 The vibe is stylish yet cozy, with thoughtful presentation and a great cocktail selection to match. Sentir is a true experience. I’m not vegetarian, and I absolutely love Mexican food — and this place delivers on flavor in a big way. The dishes are vibrant, satisfying, and surprisingly authentic for being fully vegan. The atmosphere is fantastic, with a warm, lively energy that makes the whole meal even better. A must-try spot, whether you’re vegan or just love great Mexican food. We try the plantains, the birriatacos and the flautas 😋

hands down the best meal i had on my trip to nyc. i have had this place saved for a while and decided to visit for dinner and was so impressed. the ambience of the restaurant is lovely and it was pretty full on a saturday night. our server was very attentive (even gave us a light when one of us was struggling to read the menu) and the menu was extensive. we ordered the salsa, the caesar salad, carne asada tacos, and pesca tacos. all were amazing - i especially loved the carne asada tacos and their fake meat was incredible. i was dining with a non vegan who said this was the best vegan meal she has ever had. i also ordered the oaxacan hot chocalate which was super decadent and delicious. portions are quite large and it is definitely worth the price - we left feeling incredibly full. i cant wait to come back again!

The food was so good. It does not taste like vegan food. It is well seasoned and authentic 🌮😍 the food and atmosphere were amazing. Other than that it’s nice for an intimate date night or celebrating an event.

name: Hatsuhana
document: Hatsuhana. cuisine: Japanese Sushi Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
The food is ok for American standards but the service is rushed and rude! I made a 7pm reservation for 2 at the sushi bar last night and I arrived 30 mins earlier while my friend is running late due to work. However the host made me wait way beyond my reservation time while letting few walk ins in first because they won’t seat people unless all parties are there. Even when I told him I will order drinks. I approached him again after losing my patience and finally got seated as if he was doing me a ‘favor’ that is the exact term he used.

Long story short, my friend and I both ordered the 15pc omakase and a bottle of sake with a bill of total ~$400. I had to start the course first because the server was rushing me and the chefs were doing small talks behind the counter. Sure my friend was late, but I did ordered a bottle of sake and a starter, it was not like I am taking up 2 seats for nothing. My friend joined later near 8pm and we both felt the entire course was rushed, the chef was serving us 2-3 sushi’s at the same time so he can finish the job asap!  What’s the point for omakase ?

At the end, the server neglected that there were 2 cards to split the bill and charged everything on one card because he wanted to kick us out asap so he had no time to do the math!

Worst service in NYC, even McDonald and burger kings have superior level of hospitality.

i tried hatsuhana and the sushi was not the freshest. thought it was a fluke and tried again, but again it was not the freshest. i was surprised that they chose to garnish the salmon sushi with lemon--it not only cured the fish but also seemed to mask the subpar freshness. tried some sushi a la carte and some where hits some were misses. they provide matcha tea (not just green tea) that is a lovely accompaniment to the meal.

It's been a very long time since I've eaten here and the place has hardly changed. The sushi is still very good, the service still excellent, but the atmosphere feels a bit duller; the space definitely needs some updating.

The sushi was still very good, although the rice was a bit inconsistent; some parts of my sushi rice was a bit al dente. Excellent freshness, the ikura was nicely seasoned, the scallops and shrimp were incredibly tasty, as was the rest. The tuna was a bit less memorable, normally otoro is a bit more oily and buttery, but this cut wasn't quite what I'd hoped.

Our waiter was very attentive, loved that he spoke Japanese; helped keep my dad using his native tongue which he hardly gets to do outside of home.

Overall this will always be a special place for me, memories of when I was a kid and my dad would bring back home sushi after long work days in the city. Still lives up to those memories and hopefully next time will be just as good if not better.

This is an outstanding sushi place. Everything is fresh with our choices. The green tea was refreshing and delicious. Great service, lovely place and good overall experience. Tip: upstairs is much nicer to sit. Make reservation.
Everything was fantastic! The chef was very friendly, but the staff seemed a bit rude, possibly because they were too busy. However, the sushi was the best I’ve ever had!

name: Side Door
document: Side Door. cuisine: Gastropubs Sports Bars New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Very fun experience, makes you feel like you're hanging out in a cool basement from the late 70s / early 80s, with vinyl adorning the walls and a little corner bar offsetting the vinyl wraparound bench seating and small tables. Playlist was on brand too.

The cocktails are fun and creative, if not altogether well made. They tended to steer towards the tooty-fruity sweet side and pretty imbalanced.

Bartender / host seemed a bit overwhelmed, but did the best he could but the experience could have been better if he had some help. As a result, service was spotty and we were left stranded for long stretches as the place filled up and our glasses went empty.

Food was very good, really solid modern gastropub offerings. We enjoyed the following dishes:

Creamy Rigatoni "Mac" & Cheese
Yellow Cheddar, Sharp White Cheddar, Creamy Bechamel Sauce and Crispy Bread Crumbs

Buttermilk Scallion Hush Puppies
Sweet and Heat Green Tomato Jams to Dip

Deviled Eggs
Four to an order. Pickled and served with Jalapeno Lime Slaw, and Bacon Sticks.

"The Heidi" Sandwich
Crispy Chicken Breast, Cheddar, Bacon, Smoked Guacamole & Chipotle Aioli. Served with Fries.

Chef's Bowl
Cubed Pepperoni, Tamari, Toasted Panko, Shaozing Wine, Crispy Shallots, Fried Garlic, Sesame, Banana Peppers, Parmesean, Herbs & Thai Basil Aioli over Chinese Fried Rice.

The only thing I would pass on are the chicken wings, they were quite ordinary.

Great experience. Definitely would return, especially if the bartender had some help.

The bartender set 10/10 vibes. Cool music, movies and vinyls all around. Those drinks were AWESOME. I hope the baby yoda drink becomes a permanent menu item. Food was pretty good but ive had better. Too salty.

11/22/2025 10:45. Walked in, stayed for maybe 10 min, and the bartender made it seem like why am I in this establishment. Asked for a drink in the nicest way and got an attitude for asking for a drink. I was looking forward to an interesting drink and good time but quite the opposite. Hope who ever reads this has a better experience than myself.

So glad we finally made it over to Side Door for drinks. They definitely nail the "grandpa's basement" vibe, and it's hard not to chuckle a bit when you first enter. If you have the time, take a moment to walk around in the space a bit to appreciate the decor - you might find some amusing additions to shelves/bottles.
It's kind of impressive how little attention this place has gotten since opening - it's very much one of those "if you know, you know" types of places at the moment. I'm guessing this is partly due to the area formerly being a bit of a cocktail desert, and the limited hours (just Fri/Sat during the summer).

After spending several hours here on a rainy Saturday, I understand why those in the know keep coming back. The menu is expansive for a one-man show, and the drinks are creative to boot. Don't see something you like, talk to Ulf to figure out if there's something else that he can whip up for you that fits the flavor profile you're looking for.

Some logistical tips for your first time in: 1) you can make reservations on Resy ahead of time (located on The Pub & The People's Resy page), 2) to access Side door, you have to walk through the patio that runs along North Capitol. Look for the retro stripe running down the ivy-covered wall, and you will see a set of stairs. Your destination awaits you at the bottom! If you want to scope it out ahead of time, you can actually walk through the patio area on Street View within Google Maps!, and 3) you can order food from TP&TP downstairs, so don't worry about scrambling to figure out food beforehand if you arrive hungry (or when you realize you need to order some snacks halfway through your third drink).

Vibes here are unreal. Drinks are to die for. One of the only places I have ever been where the bartenders are real cocktail snobs in a way that isn't pretentious and annoying. Rotating short list of cocktails that are really fun and usually have a good theme. Love this place

name: Birley Bakery
document: Birley Bakery. cuisine: Bakeries Breakfast & Brunch Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Oh wow, I don't know if these are special croissants or if no one else knows how to make them. I love how crunchy, fluffy, and layered their croissants are, and the cinnamon flavor was next level amazing. The Thai salad was tasty; with the smoked chicken it was quite a nice snack for fueling up. Our service felt a little slow, but we were treated with lots of kindness. The whole spot it artful and a delight for the senses! Yes, it is on the pricier side. Dare I say, it's worth it.

Such a chic patisserie in the Upper East Side! Close to Central Park and museums, it’s a great stop after a nice walk in the neighborhood. Very large offer of viennoiseries, cakes, ice cream, chocolates and more - home made, of course. I tried the apple pie and it was just amazing - delicate, crunchy, flavorful. The chocolate section would make a perfect gift for a loved one. There is a tea room upstairs, which I didn’t get to check out. Staff is lovely and patient - great service!

This small bakery/restaurant is a little hidden jewel tucked between brownstones on the Upper East side.  It's a  perfect "New York neighborhood experience" for anyone  who wants to feel like a local.
The upstairs restaurant is small, but beautifully decorated, and very Parisian. The staff were all  attentive and friendly.
I loved the power bowl with fresh fruit, nuts and passionfruit sauce. The Croissant was warm and flaky,  paired with a cappuccino tasting straight out of Italy.
The atmosphere is cozy and chic.  I felt perfectly comfortable dining solo.  I will visit again.

I have been to this fancy French bakery twice since it opened, with the first time being a day or so after the grand opening, and the other time being more recent. Their initial location is in Britain, with two locations in London, with this being the first location outside of the UK. The design inside is chic, with a fancy space upstairs for breakfast, brunch, and lunch, as well as a selection of pastries, viennoiseries, chocolates, breads, ice cream, and other goodies. The prices range from moderate to overpriced, with most of the general pastries and viennoiseries ranging from $6 to $12, and the chocolates being much more than that, with the fancy packaging matching the prices. The staff was pretty friendly both times I was here.

The first time, they were pretty empty, and as I wanted a small snack. I got their summer berry brioche for $7.50, which included hazelnuts as one of their ingredients, which was a bit surprising (perhaps it was the slight crumble on top, though I couldn't taste said filberts,) which was alright. The top, consisting of blueberries and raspberries, was fresh tasting with a bit of sourness, but not too much. There were also some sugar crystals, which helped with the general sourness of the berries. However, even for a brioche base, the bread was a tad too dry for my liking, and it likely needed to be dipped in coffee or tea. It may be because it was dry or a bit old, as I was there in the late afternoon, but if this is the usual case, I would not recommend this pastry.

For the second time, they were much more crowded with many people inside on multiple lines, including some people trying to go upstairs, as well as a line for takeout, which converged with someone behind the pastry counter taking my order eventually. I asked the person working there his preference between my usual favorite French pastry, the Paris Brest, which was $11 there, and their Tarte Tropézienne, which was $10. He said that he liked both, but their signature is the latter and slightly better, so I went with that. Said Tarte Tropezienne consisted of a brioche soaked with orange blossom, filled with crème madame (or in other words, a lighter French pastry cream,) and topped with pearl sugar, with them selling it by the slice or the whole tart. The slice was pretty large for the price, with the brioche in this case being much better, which I presume was at least partially since it was soaked in the pastry cream. The orange flavor was subtle, which is good, as orange blossom can be somewhat overpowering if overused. The pearl sugar added a bit more sweetness as well as some crunch. This was a very tasty version of this cake, and I would go back and get that again.

The first pastry probably got a low three at most, with the brioche's price point and texture subpar. However, the tart I got was delicious. Mid/upper 3.

Oh, that hot chocolate! The best. Thick, silky, smooth, rich and so good! Did I already say the best? Mhmm. I only wish we had places like this in the Boston area... If you’re a true chocolate lover, this is the destination!

They have shops in London and New York. The space in their NYC location is a bit too tight and often crowded with guests, especially now, during the holidays. A sign of just how good this place is. Will certainly return. Cheers!

She was chomping down in a red checkered cafeteria, in some kind of nasty basement, the crisp of the chicken loud in my ears. Oh boy I want that!, i shout upon waking, shooting straight up in bed, licking my lips! And so the search began. We wander and wander, in the cold, until we find the warm tunnels of Time Out market. Pulsing and throbbing with the noises of slurping and lip smacking! Inside we go and there we hit gold! Aka, Jacob’s Pickles. Jacob with his big big pickle…. He made me happy. In more ways than one. (Hey, ask the guy at the front about the glory hole in the kitchen… you’re welcome. And by that I mean mouth hole of glory- party on the tongue!)  Thank you for a lovely meal, Jacob, my man. We got two chicken sandwiches, they were Huge! And you know I like em huge (and juicy). Bravo. A great meal for tonight, as we pad ourselves in multiple diapers for the Times Sq ball drop. We needed all that chicken and buttermilk biscuits for our crispy time in the crowd! Woo! Happy new year everyone! Cheers to more delicious chicken sandwiches and big pickle times in 2026! You’re a big dill! 💚
Amazing flavors and huge portion sizes. Their waffle fries were delicious and the fried chicken was crunchy and satisfying.

The mac and cheese is decadent, and the crunchy and tasty buttermilk fried chicken with soft biscuits is incredible, waffle fries quite good too. The only thing I didn't like was the hot honey, cause it was very hot but not sweet at all. The restaurant is inside the Time Out market, which is a great location right on the waterfront, with lots of good restaurants and seats, even though they weren't very clean, but the table service is very convenient.

First of all, this location with all the restaurants is awesome. So many options and easy to order from anywhere.

Second, Jacobs Pickles is unreal. Sandwich is enormous so you may even want to share one with someone. Honey Hot Sandwich was so flavorful and delicious. Little spicy but not bad. Great meal.

document: Chef Quang Guyanese Chinese Express. cuisine: Caribbean Chinese. located in Brooklyn. with 3.4 stars (decent). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: I ordered from Uber eats I paid 19 dollars for the duck and roti and 18.50 for the goat. I gave my dad the goat he was so mad the portion size is so minute. Had I ordered from the other roti shops in queens I would not have been disappointed as I am here. The food taste good but how can you charge so much for next to nothing. I have added a photo hope this helps.

Some places just don’t miss and this Guyanese Chinese spot is one of them.

The flavor is always consistent. Every single time. The noodles hit the same. The fried rice tastes like it’s supposed to taste. No guessing, no “maybe it was an off night.” Just reliable, seasoned-to-perfection comfort food that understands its roots.

What I appreciate most is introducing it to friends outside the culture. There’s always that moment first bite, pause, raised eyebrows and then: “Wait… this is different.” Different in the best way. The seasoning, the depth, that unmistakable Guyanese Chinese flavor profile that blends Caribbean soul with Chinese technique. It’s familiar but elevated. Comforting but bold.

I’m simple when I go any of the noodles or fried rice dishes. That’s it. And they never disappoint. When a place can master the basics and keep them consistent, you don’t need a long order.

Be forewarned, order by phone before going in for takeout.  Check your food delivery app to see if the store participates.  The staff is young and spend more time talking instead of focusing on the customer in the store.  In terms of ambiance, it’s nonexistent!  The place is clean, the food is fresh, and the refreshments are limited.  The chicken is barely seasoned, and the shrimps are decent, but nothing much to write home about.  The taste lacks the tantalizing favor you get from Chinese restaurants.  I suggest ordering the small items, in case you don’t like the main course they set up for you.  Parking is in front of the store

google_reviews.text: Cash only!  We walked in on Sunday late afternoon without a reservation. There was no wait and were seated promptly.  This is a very popular spot so plan accordingly.  We observed that almost every table had pancakes.  I had intended on getting the pancakes after reading the online reviews.  Seeing pancakes everywhere solidified my decision.  Everyone enjoyed their food!  Our table ordered the avocado toast, burger with fries, French toast with apple compote and berries with bacon & eggs. Unfortunately I had to trade a portion of my glorious pancakes for a taste of the French toast.  Everyone at the table kept coming for my delicious pancakes. The savory options on the table were seasoned well.  How do I know? 😉 We plan on trying their dinner specials and course meals on future visits.

The best pancakes I’ve ever had in my life - perfectly crispy on the edges and soft in the middle with fresh fruits and great syrup. French omelette with bacon was also tasty! Really good cappuccino! Must try if you’re nearby or visiting
I had the Pancakes, and they were amazing! Very nice french-inspired spot with friendly staff and not too long of a wait. Cash only, and I recommend coming with cash because their ATM fee is $$$

document: Zhongzhong Noodles - Brooklyn. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Ramen. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This place is absolutely fantastic! My friend and I came here after doing pottery and had no idea what we were walking into. The menu is short, sweet and to the point, with a little bit of everything for everyone. We opted to share the Marinated Fried Chicken and the Shrimp and Corn Dumplings, while my friend got the Braised Pork Rice Bowl, and I got the Szechuan Braised Beef Noodle. Everything we had was fantastic; excellent portions and flavors all around. My friend wasn't a big fan of the chicken, but I personally loved it. Of all the items we had, both of us agreed that the braised pork was top tier. Everything else was good, but there was something that stood out with the flavors, textures, and just overall satisfaction you get from that dish. That one is HIGHLY recommended. I also opted to try the sour plum juice, which I don't think will be everyone's cup of tea, but I enjoyed it.

All of these items were portioned generously, and didn't cost as much as you would think. We did get a discount as part of a promotion they were doing that was buy one get one 50% off for the bowls, but even at full price I would say that everything was worth it. The customer service here was also excellent. The gentleman at the front was very friendly and clear, and helped us to make our decisions. The interior of the restaurant was also very clean. If I had one criticism, it would be that the place is a bit small for anyone looking to dine in, as seating is limited. But that doesn't detract from the overall experience. I highly recommend this hidden gem to anyone in the area.
This place is conveniently placed in Fort Green, Brooklyn. They have the best prices. Food is fresh, tasty and clean. Location is quiet and cozy. Staff helpful and friendly.

Ordered Chicken noodles from HungryPanda. After I poured in the soup, stirred for ten seconds and ready to take a bite, I saw those dirt and took the pictures. There were still so many dirt after I stirred the vege in soap. THIS RESTAURANT DOES NOT WASH VEGETABLES.😅

Overall rating: 4.5

I didn’t realize this was a chain when I visited. Clean area and nice service. Not a place to sit down, but rather to go. I had the Szechuan braised beef and it is SPICY. I wasn’t prepared how spicy.

On the first day, the broth just tasted like hot water. It was missing the flavor or fullness of broth. But on the second day, I added some soy and a few other Asian spices & it got so much better. Surprisingly day 2 was better than day 1. I could come back to try another, less spicy dish, if I’m in the area.

Definitely more a lunch to-go spot, than anything else. Recommend giving it a try.

This is the worst meal I have had in a very long time. I usually don't bother to leave bad reviews because I have worked in the service industry, and I know this can affect a business's rating, but I'm honestly APPALLED at the quality of this meal. I ordered the marinated beef bowl, pork & chive dumplings and chicken appetizer.

The chicken was 100% undercooked. I took a bite into the first nugget, and it was cold and pink. The dumplings were tough but edible and slightly flavorful. The bowl, however, was the most horrendous thing I've ever encountered.  The "beef" seems like low low low quality meat. Very stringy, fatty, and chewy. For a moment, I thought I'd mistakenly order chitlins or tripe because of how rubbery it was. I've had authentic chinese cuisine many times before, and i am an adventurous eater, so it's not that I'm unfamiliar with this style cuisine. This is just low quality and poorly executed food.  I was excited to have this style food in the neighborhood and pumped to give it a try.  I was sorely disappointed.

I'm upset because I wanted to treat myself to a nice meal, and I feel like I fully wasted my money. Literally, no part of this meal was worth the money spent. I've had better food on the street in flushing. I will not be returning and would honestly like a refund.

If you do choose to patronize this restaurant, please just steer clear of the items I ordered, and maybe you'll be fine. I literally attempted to pan fry the meat to salvage some part of this meal, and the meat wouldn't even brown or firm up in any way. I seriously don't understand what's going on here.

To be clear, I gave the service and atmosphere an average of 3 stars because I ordered delivery and didn't interact with the staff or go in the store. They are all probably fine, kind people, and my review is only about the food.

The atmosphere is quiet and pleasant for a conversation. The service was kind and super friendly.

My favorite Korean place. I've been going here for more than a decade. Food is always consistent, and they have the best side dishes! If you're looking for home-cooked flavor at a very reasonable price, this is the place.

First off, I want to state that I am Korean. I can speak, write, read, and am from the Northern Virginia area where there are plenty of Korean restaurants. I understand it is busy in lunch time . But I waited sooooo long to order. The worse thing is the food I order not good 😭😭😭 tastes so weird. I ordered pork rice. $19. It is not worthy at all. The rice so stinky and sticky. I probably don’t come again.

name: Hometown Bar-B-Que
document: Hometown Bar-B-Que. cuisine: Barbeque Sandwiches. located in Brooklyn. with 3.5 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This was easily one of the best steaks I’ve tried. I’ve had similar preparations in many places, but this one truly stood out.
From the moment I walked in, the aroma of smoke and perfectly cooked meat immediately caught my attention and set the tone for the experience.

The atmosphere is very pleasant and comfortable, making the whole visit even more enjoyable.
I left very satisfied and will definitely be coming back again.🥩❤️

WHAT DO THEY DO TO THIS NACHO CHEESE DIP TO MAKE IT SO PERFECT?! It’s perfect. I’d never order this of my own will but my friend ordered it and what a great decision that was.
The cornbread is great.
All the meat is great.

A 1/2 lb of meat per person is definitely enough, especially if you get 1-2 sides.

This isn’t the cheapest spot. 2 sides and 2 1/2 lbs of meat was $75 (fed 2 people and was a lot of food).

I LOVE that they have Stiegl! And they have special really great mugs for the radlers.

Lots of seating. There was a long line on a Saturday at 7pm and it moved slow.

Absolute hands down best BBQ joint in NY and perhaps best I’ve ever had. All the hype about Hometown is on point. Super casual and super friendly staff. You have the choice of both indoor and outdoor seating.

Every item on their menu is to die but the ultimate is the pastrami sandwich. YES you heard me right! This sandwich is even better than Katz’s. More bark, more tender, juicier and let’s not forget the buttered rye bread.

Bottom line, there is not a single item on their menu that is not worth devouring.

10/10 experience. Food, drinks and service, seriously all outstanding. I like the laid-back atmosphere and the fact that they have good quality napkins. Meat was beautifully cooked and so flavorful. The sides? Perfection. As a  southwestern girl I could dream of nothing better. And they were playing steely dan 💯

The brisket and ribs are melt-in-your-mouth and fall-off-the-bone and juicy. Perfect American BBQ. The pastrami bacon is worth it and full of char flavor. We loved the cornbread and the mac and cheese. Atmosphere is very southern. A bit pricey but definitely the best BBQ you can find anywhere in and near the city.

name: Rogers Burgers
document: Rogers Burgers. cuisine: Chicken Wings Burgers Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I stopped by Rogers Burger and tried the Creole Burger, which came topped with pikliz. It had just the right kick, mildly spicy but not overwhelming and the burger itself was juicy and full of flavor due to the pikliz and sauce.

The wait time was only about 8 minutes. The spot itself is small, but they have seating by the window to look at the outside view, as well as some outdoor seating if you prefer.

For about $16, I got the burger, fries, and a drink. The fries were decent, some were a bit oily but I ate most of them.

All in all, this is a solid burger spot. I'd definitely come back when I'm craving a good, flavorful burger.

Delicious yard burger with spicyyyyy jerk flavor!! Hits so gooood and juicy wud order again. Wings were amazing as well seasoned before frying i  can taste it idk tho. But yummmmy and economically friendly! There's no combo but the fries are good if you get cajun  and the chicken burger has good outer crust flavor. Our all time fav is the yard burger!!!

Visited 3 times so far. Go for the burgers. So juicy, good sauce, and the bread was soft. Classic smash is pretty good.
Jerk wings were fantastic. Lots of sauce but they cheaped out on the jalapeños my second run here. Barely any on top, disappointing.
Sadly the fries are very dry even with ketchup. Ive tried the curly and paprika fries. Idk you can skip it. Will visit again later to try their normal fries.
Love a burger & fries combo and I want to give this place a genuine chance.
75 cents for the tiniest cup ever for suace 😭(as seen next to the wings).
Lastly, service is hit or miss here.

I love to see our Haitians thinking outside of the box and expanding horizons when it comes to food. When I saw this restaurant highlighted by an influencer, I rushed over so I could support them. I ordered the creole burger which was topped with pikliz. The burger was so good, I'm upset that was the only thing I ordered. I will definitely be back to try everything else they have.

The burger was very juicy and they definitely didn’t skimp on flavor. The fries were fresh and crispy. And whatever Ranch that they are using is better than every other ranch I’ve had. The service was great as well! The guy in the front was a class act. Will definitely be back.

name: Simply Greek
document: Simply Greek. cuisine: Greek. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: One of the best Greek food I’ve eaten. The food was flavorful and delicious, and service was quick and thoughtful despite the fact that the place was packed. We tried the spanakopita and the falafel bowl, both of which were scrumptious! Highly recommend, especially for vegetarians!

Our experience at Simply Greek was absolutely incredible! From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with warm hospitality and an atmosphere that instantly made us feel at home. Every single dish we tried was truly amazing — full of authentic flavor, freshness, and care that brought my wife and me right back to our days living in New York, enjoying the incredible food of Little Greece.

The standout of the evening had to be the baklava cheesecake — it was so delicious that I didn’t even get the chance to take a picture before it was gone! Each bite of our meal reminded us why we love great Greek cuisine, and Simply Greek absolutely nailed it.

Thank you to the entire team for giving us such a memorable dining experience. Our meal here honestly made our trip worthwhile. We’ll definitely be back, just to eat here again!

9.5/10

You can taste it, every ingredient and every sauce is made from scratch. Rivals with the great Greek restaurants in Astoria, NYC.

Mixed grill combo is 10/10. The pita bread is amazingly fresh, taste like it just came out of the oven just for you. The tzatziki sauce is amazing, truly from scratch. All the meats are seasoned and cooked perfectly. Careful if you’re doing family style, we ordered our individual dishes and this combo, we couldn’t finish the combo.

Mousaka - 9/10. Wish portions was 30% more. The Greek salad is amazing fresh, that’s 10/10.

Calamari is the only disappointing dish. 8/10. It was cooked correct temp, juicy, not chewy. The issue is the batter, it falls off and very soggy.

Greek wings was fried perfectly. Very juicy and great batter. 9.5/10.

Baklava cheesecake. 9.5/10. Very good.

The special cake which waitress couldn’t pronounce. 9/10. Less sweet than the baklava.

Too bad we live 4hrs away. Would love to come back here. Very impressed with a high caliber restaurant. They should get a Michelin star.

This highly raved Greek join was originally delivery only and it wasn't until 2020 that it started the dine-in option. Then obvious due to its success, it moved to the current location for the larger space.

The interior decor and vibe are pleasant and inviting.  The menu is organized and easy to navigate.  Items are fairly priced and affordable.

As you enter, you see a big station with cashier counters on both ends, and the desserts proudly displayed in the middle.  To the right is the dine-in area, and to the left for the takeout.

We had the Lamb Souvlaki Pita ($12) and Pork Souvlaki Bowl ($12) which came with cut-up pita bread on the side.  Both were fantastic as I had wished.

We're definitely stopping by again next time we're in Hershey.

By far the best food we had in Hershey. This is a gem of a place. We walked in as a party of 7 in a busy holiday weekend and were greeted warmly by the hostess and seated promptly. Our server Saul took our order and the food came out within 10 minutes and was some of the freshest we’ve had anywhere. We ordered Lamb and Chicken Souvlakis, Kabab skewers and Tabouleh Salad. The desserts were the cherry on top. We ordered a few off the menu (including a special) and they were all truly amazing! Trust me, you will not be disappointed. Can’t wait to come back for more. Thanks guys!

document: Patsy's Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Everything was delicious!! We had the crab and shrimp fritters, the calamari, the Ozzie rolls, blackened prime rib (12oz) and the drunken ribeye. I had an Arnold Palmer. He has sprite. They did not disappoint. It’s a very busy restaurant but well organized, clean and they have friendly staff. Definitely recommend!

Patsy's is always a great choice for lunch or dinner. Their consistency is one of the best things about them, being one of the GAR's, you know to expect quality food, service, and environment. We showed up for lunch after an appointment and it wasn't long before the place filled up. For appetizers we got the blue crab and shrimp fritters, and today went with the pulled pork sandwich and the goat cheese and pecan salad with grilled chicken. Any GAR is one of my go tos and our 1 year old loved the kids smoked salmon!

Great restaurant and an excellent solo dining experience on a business trip. I ordered the drunken ribeye, which came with a house salad—absolutely phenomenal. The ribeye itself was juicy, tender, and cooked to perfection.
For dessert, I had the bread pudding with white chocolate, and it was honestly out of this world.
Top-tier customer service from start to finish. Strong execution across food, service, and overall experience.
10/10 — would absolutely recommend.

I visited this wonderful location on New Year’s Eve for a solo dinner date, and they did not disappoint. The parking lot was very clean with plenty of available parking. Upon entering, I was seated immediately. Since it was my first visit, I ordered several items to get a feel for the menu—10 out of 10, no notes. I would highly recommend.

Justin was my waiter, and even though I arrived during a shift change, his service truly made a difference. He was attentive and welcoming. The manager, Shelley, was also very kind—extremely helpful and polite. I absolutely enjoyed this experience and will definitely be returning.

We had such a fantastic experience at Patsy’s. It’s a very welcoming atmosphere with quick and friendly service. The food was also very tasty. I was also surprised at the prices, especially for the cocktails as everything was relatively very affordable.
Can’t wait to come back!

document: Cheryl's Global Soul. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Comfort Food Caribbean. located in Brooklyn. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Might’ve found my new breakfast/ brunch spot and I will be back for dinner to confirm that this is my new spot all around. My food was delicious and my wife was pleased with her meal as well. The drinks were great as well. It was small inside but not too cramped. I like the homey feel. Our server, Sage, was amazing. Really attentive and explained a lot about the restaurant and how they cook their food. I took his suggestion on my meal and was very happy. I will definitely be back and refer this place to everyone who’ll listen!

Saw the reviews and thought to give this place a try. I honestly felt the food was underwhelming.

Two of us ordered the pancakes with fried chicken and my vegetarian friend ordered a side of eggs, potatoes and pancakes.

All of the food was severely under seasoned, all of us were adding lots of salt and pepper on everything. The fried chicken wasn’t crispy but it was juicy and I felt it was a good portion size, one nicely sized boneless piece of chicken for each pancake. The creme that came with the pancake was very tasty as was the mustard syrup. The pancakes were fluffy. Two if us had the house cocktail rum punch, which I felt was on the weaker side, overpriced at 14 dollars. Would’ve tried another drink had they come to our table and ask before we all were fully done with our meals.

The service was okay. Friendly as we entered and were seated but they don’t check on you after the food is delivered. Food came fast which was nice, the restaurant overall was pretty empty.

Outdoor and indoor seating available as well as a patio I believe.

Fish and chips and fried chicken sandwich was delicious as well as the mango margarita. Great portion sizes. Staff was friendly and attentive. Cute vibes and yummy food. If you’re in the area check it out me and my boyfriend loved it (:

The food and service was amazing! The server recommended the pancakes and they literally taste homemade. Everything was flavorful and filling. I was also recommended a ginger drink and that was great too. I recommend everything that was recommended to me.

Cute brunch spot. It’s very crowded on the weekends. Food was pretty good - I liked my pancakes and waffles but friends gave mixed reviews on the other dishes. They were a bit understaffed and didn’t bring out our drinks until after we had received our entrees.

name: Nai Brother
document: Nai Brother. cuisine: Chinese. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Great food and service, it’s authentic mala Xiang guo that’s not overly salty or anything. Also, great portion! I literally have been craving this place for so long and I’m happy to come back over and over again! Definitely recommend! I got their spicy shrimp pot w fatty beef added.

A no frills joint and bare bones interior, but the kitchen rocks! So who cares. Had the special sauerkraut soup and it lived up to the hype. The stock was excellent, the heat just when chewing n the sprinkled dry pepper bits, the sole fish portion generous and the taste like nothing I had tasted here or overseas.
The cucumber side dish was enough for three people, and I suggested they offer a half portion for solo diners but that fell on deaf ears. They have a formula and are sticking with it.
Not fond of plastic utensils, and the fact that they do not serve warm Chinese tea is a puzzle.
Not a place to linger after the meal is over, but every bite and slurp totally worth it.
I had lunch around 2:00 p.m. and the place was empty. Which is never a good sign, but this time not at all.

We came to Nai Brother Sauerkraut Fish Times Square location and were really impressed with the value. We ordered the sliced fish spicy pot and the sliced fish with green pepper soup. It was only $30 ($15 for each dish) and enough to serve four people. Both were flavorful, generous with fish, and came loaded with veggies and toppings.
The broth had that perfect sour-spicy kick, and it felt like such a good deal compared to other spots in the area. I'm not sure if it is because this location opened recently but we got complimentary matcha crepe cake as dessert which was also delicious!

Delicious and affordable. We tried the sauerkraut fish, hot & sour fish, and a spicy beef dry pot. All of which were delicious, and great value. The staff was very chill and the venue was well lit and chill as well.

I came back a week later to try the kim chi fish, just as delicious as the first two. Highly recommended!

So delicious! Great price for a sit down restaurant in Hell’s Kitchen. We got the signature sauerkraut dish, bok choy, rice, and a Thai ice tea. This was perfect for two hungry people on a cold day. Would definitely come again.

document: Fu Shen Restaurant. cuisine: Taiwanese. located in Brooklyn. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This is a great spot for a date night or a meal with family. The complimentary appetizers are amazing. The fruit salad is sweet and juicy. The toasted butter bread is crispy, crunchy and full of buttery flavor. The drinks are sweet and fun and even come with a tiny ice animal on top.

The ribeye steak was so juicy, tender and full of flavor for a $30 price point. To add on the fine dining service, the waiter brings steak is brought out in display full of steam that my party go WOW every time we go. Outback Steakhouse has nothing on this place. I tried a runny sunny side up egg with spaghetti and it was creamy, comforting and delicious. At the end, little lollipops are given with the bill, which is perfect for kids. The restaurant feels cozy and fancy at the same time, even in the bathroom.

If you love delicious, affordable food, fun drinks, and a classy atmosphere, you have to try this place!
Tried multiple rice dishes and a noodle dish. Their beef is tender and well seasoned. Beef and egg pancake was tasty as well
4.7/5 Black Pepper Sirloin Steak ($29)-- perfectly tender steak, flavorful black pepper sauce! Comes with a salad and warm toast as well!

Excellent food for the price. Lots of variety and items to try. They have little ice sculptures as well when you order the drinks. Steak is good, onions are good and the soups are good well. I think the pastas need a little bit of work though.
Surprised this place only has 3.9 stars. Food tastes good every single time. Wait time is short and the steaks are soooo good and yummy. Food is always hot and fresh and delicious!!

name: Brooklyn Residency
document: Brooklyn Residency. cuisine: Cafes. located in Brooklyn. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
If you looking for a vibe and good food this the place to come. We went on a Sunday the DJ and service was amazing. The food was excellent. We left Beso Brooklyn 😫 to come here and were not disappointed. My girlfriend and her friend were waiting outside for the rest of the party and was greeted by a hostess who asked if they were ok, needed anything or wanted to come inside….so sweet. The drinks were bomb and the food was well seasoned and tasty even the fries which they seasoned with Cajun seasoning. I ordered the shrimp, fish and grits it was creamy like grits should be but not runny. The fish was crispy and fried to perfection. The shrimp did what it needed in every bite. We also had the shrimp tacos (best I have had in a long time), and chicken nachos. I don’t eat meat but the party enjoyed it.

I would highly recommend this establishment❤️ and it’s black owned.

I visited The Brooklyn Residency and ordered the shrimp tacos—no chipotle sauce or cheese—and they were still absolutely excellent. The shrimp was cooked to perfection, juicy and flavorful with a perfect seasoning. The tortilla was toasted just right—a balance of crunchy edges and a soft, chewy bite. The pico de gallo was fresh, mixed well, and evenly distributed, adding the perfect pop of brightness to every bite.
Highly recommend these tacos whether you customize them or get them as is. Delicious and worth every bite!

I also had the Brooklyn Blue cocktail crafted by Petrice, and it was outstanding. Petrice is an amazing bartender who really knows how to balance flavors. The drink is vibrant and refreshing, with all the fruity notes blending together beautifully for a smooth, flavorful sip every time.
The food was so good I wish i was able to try more of the menu in one sitting. the service was alright could’ve been better but could’ve been worse! i’ll be back for those fish and grits 😋😋

The food here is DELICIOUS. Everything is cooked well and very well seasoned. These may just be the best fries in Brooklyn. We ordered wings and sliders, both came with fries. One of my favorite things about this place, is they open their kitchen to other chefs so they can pop up. You can see who's coming via the businesses instagram. It's a cool way to get introduced to new chefs and also help them get exposure. It's also quite enough in the day time to work from home here even though they don't have coffee. Will continue to come back here.

Absolutely loved my experience at Brooklyn Residency! The D'Usse Berry cocktail was smooth and delicious, and kudos to the talented bartender. The Rate R Shrimp with Grits was incredibly tasty, prompting me to also try the Honey Jerk Wings with Waffles – both were packed with flavor. I'll definitely be returning for more!

name: Gersi
document: Gersi. cuisine: Italian Wine Bars Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Gersi is at the top of the pack if you are looking for a fantastic Italian restaurant in Richmond.  Cozy and crowded.  Great vibe. There are a few outdoor tables.  Definitely make a reservation. The service was excellent and very responsive - extra shout out to Dan, behind the bar, who took care of our every need.  The wine list is modest, and perhaps at the top end of pricing, but they do have a selection of some nice Italian reds.  Every dish was delicious - and the portions are generous.  Their burrata was perfect consistency with great taste.  Don’t miss  trying some of their homemade pasta dishes - the rigatoni was amazing, and the calamari with black fettucini out of this world!!  We will definitely be back!  Save us seats at the bar, Dan!

Tremendous experience overall. Bread service was sort of needed as the restaurant was quite busy but was enjoyed quite a bit. Both the ravioli and the lamb ragú were incredible. Wine and drinks were great and our server was more than willing to offer suggestions or pairings with our meal.

I enjoyed the environment quite a bit inside as it definitely harkened back to a time in the past. I would absolutely return here during my next trip to Richmond.

As someone who was brought up italian, this was as good as it gets.  The lamb ragu with homade tagliatelle was as good as I've ever had. The wife had the rigatoni rage which was also fantastic.  In true Italian tradition both servings were more than we could finish. And to end the meal, the best tiramisu ever.  Service was fast, friendly and efficient. I absolutely love Gersi! This family owned establishment is perfect for a date night or dinner with friends. The food is impeccable and the staff makes you feel like you’re at home. name: Rua Thai Restaurant
document: Rua Thai Restaurant. cuisine: Thai Noodles Soup. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Tried Rua Thai for the first time and had a great experience overall. One dish that really stood out was Pad Sa Tor (stink bean stir-fry). I had never tried stink beans before, and the server kindly explained what it was. It’s definitely a unique flavor — a little funky but surprisingly fragrant and very savory. The pork was stir-fried with shrimp paste, which added a lot of depth, and it paired extremely well with rice. Different from what I usually order, but I’m really glad I tried it.

We also ordered the shrimp donut as an appetizer, which was crispy and delicious when dipped in the sweet chili sauce. The yaowarat duck was flavorful with crispy skin, and the pad see yu had great wok flavor. Everything tasted fresh and well prepared.

Overall, the food felt authentic, the service was friendly, and the menu had a lot of interesting options beyond the typical Thai dishes. Definitely a place I’d come back to if I’m craving Thai food with bold flavors.

We love the interior environment of this restaurant!! It’s so pretty and elegant. Our favorite dish is the Gra-Praw Over Rice. I recommend everyone to try it! The Tom Yum Soup is creamy and super flavorful! The mama instant noodle and crab curry are okay. Overall we had a great experience. The waitresses are all very nice!

Came here for a fun night out and RUA Thai delivered great atmosphere and food. The vibe is lively and really does feel like a Bangkok street stall. We loved the Mama Tom Yum Grilled River Prawns—the instant noodle cup presentation was as tasty as it was fun, and the prawns were juicy. The Pineapple Fried Rice with Softshell Crab was also a standout, with the crispy crab adding a fantastic texture. The Appetizer Sampler is perfect for trying a bit of everything, and the Duck Crepe was a flavorful start. A solid choice for a casual, flavorful meal with friends!

Decor is super cute- traditional elements and lots of color and florals
Staff is very friendly and attentive
Food is delicious. Thai iced tea was great. Green curry with chicken very tasty. I had as is, so spice was a little more than medium. Spring rolls had nice crunch and the sauce had great flavor. The peanut dressing for the salad was light and tasty.
Overall, great lunch experience. Would come again if I'm in the area.

Finally found the Thai spot we’ve been craving in BK! Rua Thai’s vibe is cozy and fun (floating market inspo is so cool), and the food is next-level fresh. Shrimp donuts were crispy perfection, Mama Tom Yum Grilled River Prawns had insane flavor and spice, and the drunken noodles were loaded and wok-tossed just right. Friendly service, great portions. We’ll be regulars now. 🌶️🍤 Highly recommend to anyone hunting for authentic Thai in Brooklyn!

document: Brooklyn Roots Italian. cuisine: Italian Salad Desserts. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
What a gem in Bayridge!!! Just know you can feel the ITALIAN pride in this place. We did not have a reservation but went in when they  first opened around 430pm. They sat us right away.

Its very comforting, warm ambiance. I love the servers who was bringing the garlic pan around the establishment and making it smell delicious.

Our server was so nice. Well, two of them. A shorter woman and a taller young man.
The woman explained the specials and also suggested a pasta and sauce with a couple of meatballs. I ordered the eggplant parm and he ordered the chicken Francese.

Everything was very very good. Portions: so big. The only thing I was not too fond of was the way over eggy taste of the francese sauce. Otherwise the pasta was fresh and aldente to perfection, sauce delicious and chicken in the francese was very good!
I am excited to go again and try something else! Get two or three plates and share all around!!!

HUGE portion sizes was what our server warned us from the start, and boy was that an understatement! What we ordered for dinner was enough for lunch and dinner the next day! Hats off to this place for serving such a delicious menu, from meatballs to their selection of seafood, we were very impressed by how great everything tasted! Service was beyond amazing—very warm and inviting, just amazing people here! Will be coming back now that we know Brooklyn Roots lives up to their reputation. Must try!

IMMACULATE. Literally the only word I can use to describe my experience tonight. We were debating all day what to order. (My best friend lives here) we asked what the specials were - so we could narrow down the choices. When he said “Sunday sauce (sawce)” we KNEW that was the choice to make. For a brief moment in my life I had an Italian stepmom who would make Sunday sauce, and I knew immediately nothing else mattered. Give me the sauce, extra cheese, extra bread and a big bottle of red wine. If you’re coming to Brooklyn Roots, and you need to feed your soul (and a small army) get the Sunday sauce. Obviously only available on Sunday. First and only runner up was the chicken Marsala. Damn it Bobby that dish was AMAZING also. Since we aren’t professional eaters we only managed those 2 dishes plus some cookies. The octopus looked amazing, the chicken parm was HUGE, and some seafood pasta dish also was looking prettyyyy good. Long story short “if you’re not getting the Sunday sauce what are you even doing??”

I was there on a busy night. Not only was I surprised how fast my food came, it was absolutely delicious. The orange sorbet was a great finish. My manhattan was full and just potent enough to make me have a second.

What could I possibly say. Our children gave us a Christmas gift card to this restaurant. We, finally were able to go. Parking wasn’t bad at all . Was able to find a spot right away. Going into Brooklyn Roots brought back memories of the old days. Small but prefect. So we were greeted by the one of the workers that sat down right away. The server promptly came to us asking the usual. What would you like to drink and what the special’s were. I will definitely say the food was ABSOLUTELY Delicious……the amount of food was incredible. Most restaurants give you small portions but not Brooklyn Roots. I definitely would recommend this restaurant to everyone. If you want great food and a good amount definitely go and try it. You will not be disappointed. To the owner and cook don’t stop what you’re doing. You have something special here.

document: Village Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Mediterranean Kebab. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I came in for breakfast with my daughter, a student at VCU. The place was warm with personality and charm and the temperature quickly warmed up, too! Service was friendly, polite and our orders came quickly. We asked our server for a third plate so we could share since there were so many great things on the menu (for vegetarians, too)! Not an issue.

Ok… the care shown by staff was top notch and it also came through in their food. I ordered the veggie omelet. This is my first time having the veggies omelet where the vegetables are caramelized. The flavor was awesome, fresh and tasty. My daughter was feeling like chocolate chip pancakes and they were the best. Coffee was great, too!

I highly recommend!
We will return. Next time I want to try lunch or dinner!

Absolutely loved this stop during our Richmond visit! The vintage booths were cute and service were excellent. The pancakes were delicious and eggs and bacon were high quality. I tried my boyfriend’s burrito that was smothered in gravy and I kept stealing more bites it was that good.

This staple of downtown dining in Richmond has been around since the 1950's. This used to be my weekend haunt when going to punk rock shows in the 80s and 90s in the Grace Street area. While VCU has unfortunately swallowed up a lot of historic Richmond, it is good to see that this piece of history is still intact and just as i remember it. It has a very friendly atmosphere, full of friendly staff, and a decent size menu. It is a small establishment, so it is not really friendly for people with wheelchairs or other pieces of disabilty equipment. There is a parking lot on the side of the building, but please don't use that one. That is for the convenience store next door and they do tow. There is plenty of paid parking along Grace Street. My wife and went there for lunch. Two entrees, two drinks, plus tip was $60.
Not a bad place here in Virginia. Service was great, atmosphere is pretty cool, but the food is alright. Loads of different options at least.

Cozy cafe with perfect booths for two. Very Art Deco. They had generous portions and daily specials. I had the shrimp and corn chowder—excellent! I also had the feta and spinach croissant which was tasty and very filling. In spite of that, we shared the churro dessert! It was plenty for two, served with ice cream, whipped cream, nuts, and chocolate chips. I really enjoyed our lunch.

name: UnTable
document: UnTable. cuisine: Thai. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Already decided to come back with friends.

Dinner for 2. We had the crab fried rice, the crab croquettes, and the branzino. I had the Mean Girl to drink.

Everything was fantastic. Especially liked the spicy sauce on the crab fried rice and how it was easy to add your own heat level to the dish since we were sharing courses.

Dined in on 12.04, Waitress was really sweet and attentive. We were late for our resy and she still sat us quickly which was so appreciated.

We had dinner here as a party of four. The interior was quite nice and had a pleasant atmosphere, but unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to the setting. We ordered two appetizers and four main dishes, and none of us left feeling satisfied. The portions were small, and overall the dishes were very average—nothing particularly flavorful or memorable. The only dish worth recommending would be the Khao Soi, which stood out as the highlight of the evening. Otherwise, the experience was rather disappointing for the price and expectations.

My partner and I had our wedding dinner here. Before deciding on this venue, we had dined here a couple of times. We were always impressed by the food but were deciding between other restaurants. We were already engaged but I wanted to surprise my partner with her own ring and propose during our visit, and in the end, the staff’s warmth and willingness to make it a special moment sealed the deal.

For our wedding, we chose Beef Khao Soi and Veggie Duck Dry Green Curry as our main dishes, with Yum Samgler, Crab Croquette, and Evergreen Roll as appetizers. Almost all of our guests said they’d return again!

The restaurant supported us throughout every step of the planning process. I would also like to sincerely thank the team — Jessie, Meen, and two members of the kitchen team whose names I unfortunately don’t remember — for their kindness, warm support, and constant smiles.

I wholeheartedly recommend everyone to come here.

Came on a Friday night to celebrate my birthday and managed to get a seat at the bar w/o a reservation.

I got the midnight train to Georgia which was like an old fashioned and my husband got the I’m walking on sunshine. Both were true to their descriptions. My husband’s was slightly sweeter, but more citrusy and interesting in flavor. Both were enjoyable!

For appetizers we got the seasonal Thai pancake which was a slurry of pork and veg on a fried thin pancake, kind of reminding me of a giant nacho. We also got the baby corn fritters. The fritters came with a sauce that I could drink out of the plate, it was that delicious. Both appetizers knocked it out of the park.

The entree is where I felt a twinge of disappointment. I was unsure of what to get, I told the waiter I liked spice but didn’t want to cry into my food. He recommended the crab fried rice which had a spicy sauce on the side. There was no chili pepper next to the dish to give it a heat level. He steered me away from another option which had 4 chili peppers next to it, telling me “it’s gonna be too spicy.” Sometimes I don’t understand why Thai restaurants offer spicy options but feel the need to gatekeep what they think you can tolerate. After trying the crab fried rice, it was good, but not exactly what I was looking for. I really came ready to feel the heat, but this was a dish I felt like I could have ordered at any Thai restaurant without a Michelin star. The “spicy” sauce on the side was sweet/sour, delicious, but without a twinge of heat. I regret not ordering something spicier or even being brave and ordering the “what the hell?!!!! fried rice”

Dessert is where they really lost me - I ordered the truffle honey ice cream pie. Maybe this is on me; but I assumed the truffle flavor would be chocolate truffle. Or if it was the earthy dirty pig truffle, that it would be just a whisper of the odious flavor. I was wrong. First of all, the pie was inedible because it was more structurally similar to a block of ice than ice cream. They served it with a spoon. I think I’d be more successful carving out a bite if it was served with a knife or an ice pick. By the time I managed to sever off a piece, I was taken aback by the pungent truffle flavor. I felt like I was eating icy dirt. Thankfully they took it off the bill.

Overall, id come back for the drinks and some appetizers, and maybe to be steered more in the right direction regarding spice. There is a wide spectrum of spice tolerance, and I’d like to think I can handle it!

That being said, staff were incredibly polite and friendly! Service was stellar.
Excellent. The What the Hell Fried Rice, their signature dish, is super delicious - but warning - it is extremely (really) spicy. Very cool place and nice atmosphere and service, recommended!

document: Kowloon Cafe. cuisine: Hong Kong Style Cafe Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 3.2 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Stereotypical Hong Kong style place with reasonable prices in today’s economy. Place is decent sized but packs quickly during lunch and dinner service. We ordered:
1) chicken gizzard- decent but lacking flavor and chewy. I’ve had better
2) fried chicken skin- not bad oily
3) Kowloon fried rice- very good and kind of spicy
4) stir string beans- decent
5) peanut butter toast with condense milk- okay
6) pork belly with preserved veggies- really good and done well
7) Chinese cheng fan assortment- nice and bouncy noodles
8) beef and egg chow fun- good “wok hei” on the noodles and good flavor. Best dish
9) oyster pancake- oyster didn’t taste fresh and pancake could have been cooked longer
10) sautéed eggplant garlic sauce- flavorful and not too salty
11) Portuguese chicken spaghetti- second best dish with authentic flavor

Will definitely stop by again to try out the rest of the menu. The servers were typical HK waiters- so don’t expect exceptional customer service just above being rude- but it’s understandable.
Childhood comfort food. Breakfast combos are always hot, tasty, and fresh. Recommend their noodles with mix sauce and french toast!

So good! So many of these Hong Kong places popping up but this one is very authentic, great variety menu and great prices. Staff is also wonderful, bartender gave my daughter a handmade horse, so kind. Will be back soon!

First time, love the vibe and food. French toast was delicious, fake shark fin soup was also on point. Their red bean ube is the best I’ve tried!
Will come back to try other food!

Service was fast, food was hot!

I was really expecting my usual Hong Kong authentic cafe (茶餐廳/Cha Chang Tang) but it was a bit disappointing.

The afternoon tea set was reasonably priced with a drink - red bean ice drink (it’s included in one of the set and you can’t change it to other drinks). I ordered the chicken leg w fries and red bean ice. The chicken leg was huge but the meat quality was not what I was looking for. I would rather choose a smaller leg with nice dark meat than a large one. The red bean was too milky without much red bean taste.

The satay beef noodle was soso. The beef was cut too thick and we normally don’t add green leaves (gai lan) on top but I guess it’s a local American style to add veg. The taste is half way there, but I wish the sauce and beef can improve.

The Portuguese chicken was ok. I just feel like the cheese was somehow different and perhaps too much.

name: Yummy Noodle House 粥麵之家
document: Yummy Noodle House 粥麵之家. cuisine: Noodles Cantonese Hong Kong Style Cafe. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The spareribs clay pot rice was hot, crispy and flavorful. The you choy was nicely cooked and the lemon tea tasted nostalgic.

We were excited to find a Hong Kong style restaurant with great reviews so the 3 of us traveled from Brooklyn and 1 from Forest Hills to meet up at 8pm Saturday to give Yummy Noodle House a try.   Once we were seated we ordered the HK milk tea, lemon tea, & 2 clay pot rice (pork & salted fish and Chinese sausage) with the female server then asked for a few minutes so we could discuss what other dishes we wanted to try.   A few minutes pass and the male server approaches with a bit of an unfriendly demeanor asking if we were ready to order we finalized our selections in front of him while he grimaced - HK pan fried rice roll, HK pan fried noodle w soy, shrimp wonton noodle soup, deep fried fish skin noodle soup, fried chive dumplings, salt & pepper fish, and steamed Shanghai soup dumplings.  The drinks and the dishes started to come out relatively quickly considering the house was semi full of patrons 1 hour prior to closing time.   HK milk tea was average at best compared to what many HK cafe's in the east coast present as HK milk tea - there was no depth in flavors, not much condense milk flavor, and too bitter.   Onto the food - we were really excited also to see they offered HK style clay pot rice which is becoming rarer to find these days.   One of our excitements of the dinner to try, yet it was similar to the HK teas - just average at best compared to the others in the NY/NJ area.   Lacking favor and quality in the rice base, proteins added to the clay pot were average nothing impressive, and even the flavored soy for the clay pot rice was eh.   One of our litmus test items for a HK cafe or restaurant besides the HK Milk Tea is the HK pan fried noodle with soy and Yummy's version isn't exactly authentic in all its ingredients but it was tasty, had some wok hay, and noodles were proper - a decent dish here.  The other stardard HK dish we rate a HK eatery on is their HK wonton noodle soup and Yummy's is another eh.   The wontons were lacking shrimp and the mostly pork filling was overly salty, the soup base was lacking flavor or that umami/shrimp/seafood flavor, and the noodles weren't exactly amazing being a bit limp as well a bit soft and missing true HK noodles having that "ghan sui" flavor.   The pan fried chive dumplings were very decent with flavor, fresh chives, and filled nicely.  The salt & pepper fish dish was eh - nothing for us to order again.  The Shanghai XLB were eh - another nothing for us to order again.  So for the drink and food I would say Yummy is what it claims "HK Style" and not authentic HK food.   Portions are decent but if you are looking for authentic HK food and excellent prep/flavors then it's worth a try but it's not the place.
Now, the biggest issue we had with Yummy is that at 8:20pm while we were eating and still a few other parties eating - the staff started sweeping all around us, spraying cleaners around us, and the male server asked us if we wanted to order anything else.  Then at 8:30pm the male server printed out the checks for all eating patrons and placed checks on everyone's tables without saying anything.  Then he proceeded to sit at a empty table across from us playing with his phone while seemingly eyeing us with another staff standing at the rear of the restaurant also eyeing us.   We all felt the pressure of the staff wanting us to finish, pay up, and leave yet we were half done with our food.  At 8:35pm the female server comes over to ask us if there is anything else we would need and one of us says - oh no but we know you want us to finish up and leave.  The server then says - oh no thats not the case.  I then ask her what time do you close?   She responds with a "ummmm, well the kitchen usually closes at 8:30pm"  and I ask her - but your listed closing time is 9pm isn't it?  There was no confirm or response.  I mean I get it - there are 2 parties left and you want to go home but the whole night we felt some unfriendliness from 1 or 2 of the staff and a lot of pressure from all staff 40 minutes before closing time.   This isn't how you should treat customers.

The whole set-up is an interesting-cool food truck eatery.  You order from a well decorated converted short bus.  Attached to the bus is a whole separate smoker that is open so you can see the variety of meats that are available on the menu (whole pig rotating on a spit, Ribs, whole chickens, sausage).  They also provide 4 folding picnic tables set under a tent in the parking lot, with Puerto Rican music playing on their speakers.  Considering it's a parking lot, they've done a great job offering an option to sit and eat.

We ordered two of the bowls which come with rice & beans, Yucca (not fried, which is how we're used to getting yucca), plantains.  The sausage has a great mix of different flavors, with pork, seasoning, and either peas or lentils.  We had differing thoughts on the lechon as one person at the table thought it was a bit too salty, but others thought it was still good and tasty.  We also ordered a half rack of ribs.  These were not fall off the bone, but they were still very tasty with its smoky flavor, seasoning and bbq sauce, plus they were also very meaty.

I also have to give mention to the team that works there.  They were all very friendly and welcoming.  They took the time to explain everything on the menu.  Came to our table a couple of times to bring some sauces, make sure everything was okay, and to tell us when they're open (Fri, Sat, and Sun).  He explained Fri was a smaller menu that varies with what they have, then Sat & Sun is their full menu.

I highly suggest a stop here!
