I’d have to say, the place itself is lovely and the staff members were very nice but the food itself was horrible. We ordered the ribs and fried cheese as appetizers. The ribs tasted old and they weren’t hot. They seemed to be warmed up and the meat itself had a weird flavor. The fried cheese was good. It had a crunchy outer texture as the inside was cheesy and gooey. On to the food, I had the buffalo Mac n cheese with bacon. My chicken was extra slimy and had a gray color. It actually disgusted me. I tried eating just the noodles and bacon but I couldn’t. My friend had the chicken pot pie. She enjoyed! Our server, Mateo was very nice and helpful as was the buser and host. The place itself is nicely decorated. I’d like to try their brunch but as for food, I’m good. I had a stomach ache all day after visiting.

We are so happy to have Caroline’s in the neighborhood! The place is beautiful and the service was spot on. The server put a delicious bag of seasoned popcorn on the table after we were seated, yummy!! I had the short ribs the first time and the double burger on an English muffin another time !! The best burger ever! I highly recommend this place!

The food here is good,  but ridiculously over priced for the portion sizes. I got 2 chicken Caesar salads and 2 soups for $66. The Caesar salad had no croutons, and one salad had bottom of the bag lettuce. I could bypass these issues any other time, but not after paying $66 for a meal not big enough to have as leftovers. I think the prices should be adjusted a bit on certain things, or increase the portion sizes.

This spot is new across from the Avenel NJ train stop, Next to the Avenel Performing Arts theatre ; just within the newly built (appx. Yr and a half) housing, but can be seen from the streets.  There is ample parking and the perimeter of the restaurant is floor to ceiling doors and windows… a perfect view of cleanliness where ever you sit.  The little touch lamps gives a nice aura to the eating area but with over head domed hanging lights it’s good enough to see the menu ( no eye strain due to dim lighting) .  A patio in the front and on the side (side walk entry if walking) the fire pit area with the red outdoor furniture catches your eye, and a perfect area for a friendly gathering for drinks or after eating your meal.  The waiters are professional, and have good conversation when engaged ( 🙌🏽 to Nathan, ( should be head waiter, talk about engaging!!!!)  who made sure we learned everything about his place of employment, loved him, talk about up sale, he is smooth with it, and we enjoyed him.) Yes we liked the aura so much we were shocked it wasn’t crowded for a Saturday, but they’ve been open for only 2 months!!! This place is go king to be THAT treasure for the area, I’m speaking it into existence!!!
Now the food.  The menu is simple and easy to read. On a board that’s easy to handle as well as the bar menu which is a little smaller.  I skipped drinking as I was driving tonight.  Our waiter was Mateo, also professional but quiet and handsome ( you too Nathan!) He explained the dishes well, we ordered chicken pot pie which came in a shallow bowl , served with a large puff pastry  and OMG the chunks of chicken, not one bite without having chicken. The sauce was a tad bit thin but it was tasty.  Skirt steak and fries was ordered.. I admit I would have like some Jasmine or basmati Rice, but this is my error because I did not look at side dishes.  The steak cut was very good and the way I ordered the steak was perfect, well done but not dry, the sauce was just enough for flavor and not splattered all over my steak, the fries were seasoned well, loved the dish.  We finished off with the bread pudding with ice cream!!! Let me tell you the slice can be shared! Tasty and full of flavor not dry at all..  we ordered the peach drink, sweet but good, ending with coffee.  Oh and yes there was a lady that kept your dining area clear and clean!!!
The best thing….. upon being seated you are given a medium bag of seasoned popcorn (while you wait)  that will have you conversing about what flavors you taste… we even asked for another bag.
Definitely coming back and obtained a planning menu for my Bday in December.  Price range is good $$-$$$ .  Wow this was long, but I meant every word…  I wish them the BEST!!!

name: Shaw-naé’s House
document: Shaw-naé’s House. cuisine: Soul Food Personal Chefs. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: You know that saying "when you're here, you're family", they don't play around at Shaw-nae's. From the moment you walk in, till you pay your check, you're family. Our waitress Jennifer was amazing, explained the menu very well and was extremely attentive. We ordered the catfish tenders and the sugar daddy wings for appetizers. Amazing. How she was able to capture the waffle in a wing is beyond me. For dinner, we got the ribs and jerk chicken with rice. Amazing. Everything was delicious. We even met Shaw-nae herself! We were too full for dessert. We will definitely be back. You need to come here!

Tried Shaw-naé’s House after a long wait and the food lived up to the hype. The fried chicken wings were the highlight. The batter is very thin, and even after being coated in sauce, the skin stayed crispy instead of turning soggy. It’s not crunchy because of a thick crust, but because it’s fried really well. The sauce leans sweet, with notes that reminded me of maple syrup and cinnamon, which may be a bit sweet for some, but the texture and technique were excellent.
The oxtail rice was also very well done. The meat was tender and flavorful, with just a slight black pepper kick that balanced it nicely. The BBQ pork ribs were soft and cooked properly, though the sauce again leaned sweet. Service was friendly, and everything felt carefully made. Definitely a place worth trying if you appreciate well-executed soul food.

We had the BEST night out here in Staten Island!! Shaw-nae’s House not only had mouth watering food just but also the cozy atmosphere with VIBEY music made the whole experience a 10/10. The Sweet Potato Cheesecake is by far the best cheesecake I’ve ever had and it had such a perfect balance that just absolutely melted in your mouth. The oxtail fell off the bone and the flavors were just absolutely incredible. If you need a comfy, delicious night out COME TO SHAW-NAE’S!!!! A special shoutout to Jennifer for taking such wonderful care of us. The staff were so friendly, and gave incredible recommendations. We also had the opportunity to meet Shaw-nae in the flesh!!! Thank you to everyone working tonight and THANK YOU SHAW-NAE.

We trekked from Brooklyn to SI on the coldest night of the year so far and omg it was worth it!
The restaurant was chilly on the inside but I ended up taking my jacket off after having a bite of the food because I just felt my soul warming up. I guess that’s what good soul food is supposed to do!
We got the jerk chicken with rice, ribs & fries, and a side of collard greens and Mac n cheese.

The pork ribs and Mac n cheese were MEMORABLE. If you like a sticky sweet sauce with ribs that fall off the bone, order this. I included a photo so you can see the chiaroscuro happening with the glaze. The Mac n cheese was gooey and crispy in the right places. If you enjoy macaroni pie vs the Kraft Mac n cheese, you’ll enjoy this.

The complimentary corn bread was a really nice touch. I almost wish we got savory cornbread as an appetizer and sweet corn bread as a dessert chaser (we had strawberry cornbread, sweet potato cornbread, and strawberry cornbread).

Jerk chicken was just ok. It was tender and well cooked, but I wanted more of that smoke/spice. Collard greens are a must order, just to have a little greenery on the plate.

Staff was warm and polite Ms. Shaw-nae made an appearance and hugged me and my husband! I was star struck

Overall, worth a hop, skip, and a jump!

I mean, I truly do not know where to start as I have no words to describe this experience. From the moment we walked in, we felt like we were right at home. And!! one of the young gentleman had called us earlier to let us know our table was ready, very nice! Jennifer was our amazing host and off the bat she came through with some amazing complimentary cornbread that was out of this world!!! We were so excited about trying the food that it took us a while to settle on something but thankfully Jennifer explained the whole menu and had some great recommendations. We had the sugar daddy wings and on my goodness, I will be dreaming about those! For entrees, we had the oxtail and the chicken sandwich, both were incredibly fresh and had amazing flavors. We were then blessed with Shawnae’s presence as she checked in on us. What an amazing woman, it was beautiful to see how connected she is to her roots of staten island and how much she pours back into the community. She also prayed over us and it brought me to tears but I had to hold it in. I mean when I say we felt like family and i’ve known them for years is an understatement. This place makes you realize we are all here on earth together, why not pass time with beautiful people?! Shawnae, you are doing something incredible and I can see God’s work moving through you, God bless you all at the restaurant. Truly a one of a kind experience

document: Ho'Brah. cuisine: Mexican Hawaiian. located in Staten_Island. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Love this place! It’s small but fun! Love the music, the atmosphere is pretty chill. The fish tacos are amazing and OMG, you gotta try the pulled pork empanadas (sorry I don’t have a picture). If you’ve never been, that drink in the pic is a Bulldog. Very good, especially on a hot day!

Mid-morning on a Friday. To our delight, there wasn't anyone around except the obliging barkeep.

We ordered the calamari, and two tacos – Korean BBQ and Captain Jack. It’s always nice when calamari – quite possibly the most ubiquitous app there is out there – comes adorned with something a little extra: zippy lime-soaked red onions, charred corn and a creamy, piquant chipotle mayo. We polished off the tacos, which were a tad pricey, but no complaints!

It’s not surprising that Ho’Brah’s is a local beloved; if you’re looking for a brunch snack, or a place to just kick back, this is the place for you. The only thing missing are some oceanfront vistas.

The service sucks.  There are signs that say “ see hostess to be seated “ I waited around for a while, couldn’t tell who worked there.  I eventually asked the bartender and he seemed clueless.  We sat ourselves outside; then went inside to ask how do we order.  After about 15-20 mins someone came.  The drinks are good, and nachos, def recommend.  Not sure about the tacos. We had some Long Beach all star and bohemian tacos.  The meat was bland.  The Long Beach all star was a little too wet for my liking and the steak pieces were cut big and thick for a small tortilla.  Next time I’ll just stick to drinks and nachos.

Great taco joint and have eaten there many times. Never disappointed. Tacos are top notch as is the service. Consuela's pork empanadas are delish, actually all their empanadas are delish. They make a mean Margarita as well. Kid friendly since they have a children's menu. A small place and fills up quickly so keep that in mind if you are thinking about going there. Also keep in mind it has a bar right next to many of the tables and it can get loud. This is mostly after 6pm, lunch and anywhere up to 4pm it is fairly quiet with no wait for a table. Not a pure Mexican style restaurant, but more of California style.  Menu is varied and very reasonably priced.

When we first arrived there was a couple looking in through the window.  One said, 'there's only two people seated, let's go somewhere else.'. That was their mistake.  We had read the reviews, we knew where we were going.  Probably seats 30 with a nice vibe and decor for a taco bar. Birria tacos were amazing.  A thin shell that was sturdy and tasty too.  The beef great, the sauce too.  By the time we left our late lunch there were 10 inside.   Great food, we'll be back.

name: The Anchor Fish & Chips
document: The Anchor Fish & Chips. cuisine: Seafood Tacos Fish & Chips. located in Staten_Island. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The food itself was definitely enjoyable and worth recommending. We went with the classic fish and chips and added a curry dip for the chips, which paired really well. The fish was nicely done, and the curry dip in particular stood out.

The only downside was the service. We did not tip prior to being served, unfortunately the experience afterward felt a bit underwhelming. Tip should come AFTER the service, not before.

Overall, the quality of the food would bring us back, and we’d be open to visiting again at a different time in hopes of a better service experience.

This is such a cute place! It was big enough to sit 6 people but still cozy. The fish and chips were SO good, but what I really loved the most was the meat pastie. I will dream about it. We also got poutine, a ham toastie, and a burger. The toastie was the best grilled sandwich we had ever had! And the poutine made our taste buds dance and sing.

Stopped by since I was in NE running errands. I am NOT a fan of Fish and Chips but I saw they had Sheppards pie on the menu.

I added Irish cheddar and man, this thing was de-lush-iius! The cheese was bubbling and a perfect compliment to the meaty innards and mashed potatoes.

Just what I wanted o n a brisk December winter afternoon here in Minnesota.

HUGE fish portions perfectly fried. The best chips and house-made tartar sauce, excellent poutine, shepherd's pie and bangers. Ordering and seating is a bit unconventional but it makes sense because they are a small operation but wildly popular. When you walk in, you check in at the station to your left. You can also grab a pint of beer or a glass of wine to wait for a table. The workers watch for tables to open up. Once a table starts to vacate, you order and pay at the station while they clean up your table. Once seated, your food is out rather quickly. Believe me, it's worth the wait.

The Anchor sets a very high bar! I have yet to find Fish and Chips that tops The Anchor. Very generous portions with the fish being the obvious attraction. We marveled at the light, crispy, batter, perfectly golden brown! How do they do that? It doesn't just fall off at the first bite. The wild Alaskan Cod was flakey and perfectly done, almost sweet. Even the hand cut chips were done to perfection. Do try the house tarter sauce, it is the perfect compliment to the fish, just as the malt vinegar compliments the chips. Exemplary job, keep it up!

name: Kimchi Kooks Kate's Kitchen
document: Kimchi Kooks Kate's Kitchen. cuisine: Korean Specialty Food International Grocery. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Kimchi Kooks ruined store-bought kimchi for me. There’s no going back.

This is the kind of kimchi that’s alive in the best way: perfectly fermented, punchy but balanced, spicy without bullying, and somehow gets better every day it sits in your fridge. You eat it straight from the jar, then start putting it on everything.

Two things I love (besides the kimchi itself):

🥬 The jar return program — bring back an empty jar and get $1 back. Sustainable and satisfying.
🥬 The giant jar — yes, it’s $26, but it’s enormous and absolutely worth it if kimchi is a staple in your house (it will be).

Heads up: their store hours are a little finicky, very “small, excellent business” energy. But! You can reliably find them at the Park Slope Farmers Market on Sundays and at the Park Slope Food Coop, so no excuses.

This is neighborhood kimchi with serious standards. Once you try it, you’ll start quietly judging other kimchis — and you won’t be wrong.

As a new resident to the neighborhood, this place gives me a little piece of home cooking. Good kimchi is hard to find, and most are poor imitations. Kate’s Kimchi is one of the best I’ve tried in a long time, and having it so close is brilliant. I’ve tried their Bibimbap and the Dubu Bokkum—both fantastic. If you’re like me and miss home cooking, but find it a hassle to drive into the city or to Queens, Kate’s Kitchen is a time saver. What a gem! Highly recommended. I just hope this place doesn’t get too popular.

The kimchi is soooo good. Handcrafted, fresh, raw, and gluten-free. Believe me or not when I had a crazy diarrhea week it actually cured me (LOL) because it’s full of probiotics. It’s so flavorful, so tasty, I can eat one jar a day! I also love their dubu jorim (tofu). Highly recommend this small local business in Brooklyn!

Some of the freshest Korean food I’ve ever had in NYC! I absolutely love the new weekly menu approach this research has. In my experience, it’s kept the food interesting and appealing and has a quality that is hard to beat. Additionally, they have a wonderful selection of cold take-out meals available daily & a variety of different kimchi options. The staff is also incredibly kind. My friend and I went to Safta for their Valentine’s Day buffet brunch, and it was outstanding. The spread featured a wide variety of Israeli dishes, and every dip we tried was packed with flavor.

The in-house pita was soft, warm, and incredibly satisfying. The focaccia was just as impressive. Honestly, all of their breads were exceptional.

Service matched the quality of the food. The staff was attentive without being intrusive, promptly clearing plates and keeping our water glasses filled.

Their Cortado coffee was smooth and well-balanced too.

Overall, it was absolutely worth it. I’d happily go back again.

Honestly, probably the best food I’ve had in Denver! Could’ve kept eating that fresh pita all night. In fact if anything, I think we filled up too much on the bread and dips…but the entrees were also fantastic.

The whipped feta and hummus were standouts, along with the super moist harissa chicken! The cocktails were also really unique takes on classics and were delicious.

A bit on the pricey side, but worth it for the quality! Definitely recommend checking this place out and definitely book a resy - it was nearly at capacity on a Tuesday.

As absolute foodies, Safta has been on our list for a while. We have monitored over the years but never made the time to go. Recently we saw the reviews being a bit critical or non-sensical. At this point we decided to just try it and we were not disappointed. We ordered a combination of 7 dishes overall and yes it was a random Thursday, but the kitchen timed coursing perfectly for everything. Our server Duncan really made the experience for us. Attentive and proactive in our needs, great suggestions to maximize how we paired our meal, and overall just a fun person to have as a server! Really they made the experience and the food was the cherry on top. I did not book as a birthday but I did mention it was in fact my Fiancé’s birthday and Duncan had small touches to make her feel special on her special day. Everything tasted spectacular from the NA mocktails/soda to all of the small shared plates and main entrees. I think the star for us was their Persian rice, what an absolute playground of flavors. If you’re open to new flavors, you can’t really go wrong with anything in my humble opinion.

I’d give 4.5 stars if I could. TLDR it’s a bit overpriced but the food is excellent. The pita is perfect, the servers are super friendly, the space is beautiful, and super fun to order a lot of the different dishes to share! Must tries are the lamb hummus, mushroom hummus, muhammara, and the Bulgarian lamb meatballs. Skip the babaganoush and the Persian rice, they were pretty mid. We had 3 different cocktails and all were amazing, but very very pricey.

One of our favorite restaurants in Denver! The mushroom hummus and muhamarra are our favorite dishes. The fried eggplant is also great but could do with a thinner layer of goat cheese. One reason why we love this restaurant is because the servers are fantastic. Many restaurants have great food but poor service because the restaurants get too cocky. But Safta has remained humble and we appreciate that.

document: Sushi On Me. cuisine: Japanese Sushi Bars Speakeasies. located in Queens. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Excellent dining experience with a very entertaining staff. If you love sushi you'll love dining at Sushi On Me.
This is a semi-private and cozy (not cramped) dining experience. The staff caters to a small group as you dine right at the bar. Get ready for 15 rounds of sushi paired with good saké.
Each round of sushi was more delicious than the last and the staff really puts on a show as you eat.

Love...love...loved this place! Delicious food, great music, fun and interactive chef's and servers. I just wish it kept going. I went with a group of friends. We had an amazing time. The surprise of it all and the presentation of the dishes were so unique and elevated the meal.  If you're planning on going, pick a fun group of friends to join you. The vibe at the bar is lively, upbeat and fun.  IF you choose the right group to join in on this experience it'll be even better. Its a dark speakeasy atmosphere.  One of the servers even did karaoke - and we sang along (not corny). My coworker set this all up and strategically invited the max amount of people to reserve the bar table so that it would be exclusive for us and we all had a great time...it helps that we're a vibrant group and had unlimited sake 😀

Best Japanese food in NYC!! I was surprised Japanese have that fun, wow I had a blast there complementary sake and the food feels just healthy and good, you have the chef so close to you that feels part of your family! Would love to go back💝

Great experience with lively staff that keeps the sake flowing.
The plates are presented beautifully.
Wish there was a little more time between plates so you have time to really enjoy the unique flavors.
Reservations required.

What a luxury to be able to have this in my neighborhood. I’ve been here three times now and each time I leave feeling like I had just gone to an underground party and enjoyed some great sushi!

The AYCD sake is a plus. They are super attentive in refilling your cup. The omakase is far from the traditional omakase however I like how they incorporate Thai flavors into their dishes. The Penang curry with eel over rice is the perfect amount of spicy and sweet. They serve a good amount of appetizers before preparing the sushi pieces and ending with a dessert.

If you have a birthday person in your group, prepare to sing! It’s so fun to see a group of strangers coming together enjoying sushi and just having a good time. The chefs are hilarious and I always enjoy coming!!

name: Margot
document: Margot. cuisine: New American. located in Brooklyn. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: Overall, enjoyed the food and ambience here. It’s an open concept kitchen, which is always fun to watch and in my opinion, enhances the experience. The roasted artichoke was hands-down my favorite thing we ordered. The verte salad was also really yummy, the added crunch from the breadcrumbs was nice and the dressing was fresh and flavorful. We also ordered the aglio & olio pasta which was yummy and the bucatini was cooked really well. The seabass was unique thanks to the addition of bacon and we enjoyed it. The reason I took a star off is because the chicken didn’t taste fresh. You could tell that it was prepped much earlier in the day because it had that sort of stale taste. Otherwise, the side of panzanella salad was delicious.

We enjoyed our dinner at Margot. We grabbed a late reservation on a Saturday and were happily seated before the time on a busy evening. Really liked the salad verte. It was very large and had a really nice dressing on it. I did questioned the peas on it. We ordered it because of the peas and it being summer, but when it turned out they were cooked peas and may have been frozen peas which seemed incongruent with the rest of the very fresh salad. Another thing that I asked the waiter about was a little bit of grittiness that turned out to be bread crumbs. I would have preferred them to be noted and larger in size. But we made all gone with the salad.

The tomato salad was also very good! I love a bit of purslane.

We enjoy the artichokes with salsa verde.

With both the tomato salad and the artichokes that would have been good to have some bread.

Bread is offered on the menu in conjunction with prosciutto for $22.00. We didn't ask about getting just bread and that may be our bad.

We also ordered the french fries which turned out not to be quite french fries but more like potato sticks. They were a trip down memory lane but not quite what I would describe as french fries.

The Zuni style Chicken itself was tasty and a good size portion With a nice panzanella salad.

The salmon was fine. There were more of those peas in the otherwise unflavored couscous.

The dessert offerings were not compelling enough but we did enjoy our dinner.

When we look back at the photos on Google it seemed like certain dishes like the pasta or more interesting in the past. That's why we didn't order any pasta. The descriptions seemed kind of plain for the price.

We miss the old diner but glad it’s open again for American comfort food. We had the beets and artichokes to start that were both simply done but delicious. The limone pasta was the least liked plate. Branzino with beans and steak were also tasty. Their version of Zuni cafe’s chicken was also flavorful. (I ate that chicken at least 1x/month with oysters and a Bloody Mary in SF!) Ultra thin shoestring fries were a hit. If you want bread, ask them for it plain. The toasted one was greasy with oil. Pleasant comforting winter meal. And you get $50 off for $150 on the inKind app if it’s the first time using it.

We’ve been wanting to try Margot but tonight was a perfect surprise - couldn’t get into a restaurant nearby, got lucky with Margot. Food was delicious and the wine was so refreshing and lovely. Service was great, too. The focaccia was amazing and the spring vegetables were over the top. Must try. Glad that our neighborhood has one more lovely new spot. Can’t wait to come back again.

My friends and I had a celebratory birthday dinner at Margot and it was exceptional. The staff were so warm and welcoming, they didn’t rush us along, and they truly cared about our experience. The food and drinks were perfection. What a gem Margot is.

I finally tried Baht and we loved it. Fantastic flavors all around. The cocktails are a great price and happy hour is even better. We will be back!

name: Siam Thai
document: Siam Thai. cuisine: Thai. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Named best Thai in DC which is true, but there’s a lot of factors that make me want to choose a different place.

Food: even though it tastes great, I have noticed the quality has steadily decreased. The worst thing I’ve had was the Tom Kha soup. The most lime I have ever tasted in a broth, and I eat ceviche all the time. It was hard to eat, I couldn’t even finish the small serving.

Price: adding chicken as a protein costs 7 additional dollars…eating here is very pricey. My boyfriend and I alone will end up paying $80-$100 for one outing (appetizer, drink, 2 entrees). And they automatically include 20% gratuity on your bill.

Service: because the gratuity is already included, I’ve noticed service quality has gone down. Particularly from one individual. I believe she’s the daughter of this family-owned restaurant. She works almost all the time and has a very bland attitude towards serving. All other servers have been very pleasant.

Atmosphere: sitting outside is terrible, as you will get attacked by mosquitos (that will also come into the restaurant). Sitting inside is a little cramped. Worst thing that happened was a pipe burst in the ceiling in the middle of peak hours.

Nice to try once, but wouldn’t recommend as a repeat spot.

Warming up with hot and spicy food on a chilly day in DC. I got the lunch special with hot tea, tom yum mushroom soup (spicy level 5) and drunken noodles with chicken (spicy level 3). Both dishes tasted wonderful in flavors and heat!  🌶️ They don’t do spice tray anymore, but you can request mini seasonings like chili flakes, vinegar with peppers, or fish sauce.  I’ll def visit again for my next DC trip!  Aroi mak!

Cozy spot at the corner of the street. I stopped by for lunch and ended up enjoying tom yam mushroom while looking out the door and watching the snow trickle down. Their lunch special $18 for appetizer, entree and a drink is ideal for a sit down meal. I couldn’t finish everything and packed it up so I can enjoy it at home!

Visiting DC during Labor Day weekend and I had to stop in at The Siam House located on Connecticut Avenue in Cleveland Park. If you’re looking for a tasty meal in a great location, then Siam House is the place for you. I had the Tom Yum Noodle Soup with fried tofu. It has a zesty lemony flavor that deliciously complements hints of cilantro and spices. It was literally good to the last drop!  I finished my meal off with the Mango Sticky Rice which blends sweet mango with a rich coconut cream sauce sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds. Absolutely, divine. Keep in mind this is a seasonal dessert so don’t stay away too long if you want to partake. Overall, this is a fantastic restaurant for the family, friends, couples and anyone else that loves good Thai cuisine.

Siam House is the best Thai food in all of D.C. Every single time I go, the food is always up to par with the food I used to have in Thailand. Samantha and the rest of the staff are always so welcoming and warm when you go in and make you feel like you're eating at home in a loving community. The heaven pork is a dish I always recommend to whoever I bring, its so crispy and full of flavor it really does taste like you are having a bite of heaven. I have also loved the yellow curry with chicken as well as the Tom Yum soup. This establishment is definitely a place I have added to my frequently visits list and highly recommend anyone who hasn't been to go.

name: Lao Fu Zhou
document: Lao Fu Zhou. cuisine: Chinese. located in Queens. with 2.3 stars (decent).

google_reviews.text:
When we walked in, there was a long line, but it moved quickly. I only waited about 5–7 minutes to order. They have signs on the wall saying you should know your order before stepping up and clean up after yourself, but I noticed a lot of people don’t really pay attention to that — so just be prepared.

What I ordered:

Wheat Noodles with Peanut Sauce (#5) – It was good, but I wish the sauce was thicker and more buttery so it would coat the noodles better. It was a bit watery, so the sauce kept sliding off when I picked up the noodles. Adding the chili oil from the table definitely helped improve the flavor.

Small Pork-Filled Fish Ball Soup (#11) – Pretty good overall. The broth was clean and hot (though it cooled down quickly). The fish balls tasted like real fish paste, not the powdery hotpot-style.

Overall, it was a good experience — two dishes for under $10 is hard to beat. Service was quick and efficient as long as you’re ready to order without hesitation. Also, it’s cash only.

We got our food to go, but would have sat inside if we didn’t need to be someplace shortly after our stop in. We got the wheat noodles with peanut butter sauce and the pork and chive dumplings and with tip it was $10 for two people for lunch! What a bargain. The noodles were delightful and we added the leftover dumpling sauce, had we ate there I would have added Sriracha to it and it would have been perfect. The dumplings were crisp and steaming hot and delicious, though they did short us one so we only got seven instead of the eight we ordered. Make sure you count before you leave! We will be back and dine in to enhance our experience.

We tried to go here a couple of weeks ago, but the line was long and we were very hungry, so we left. Good news was that today the line was short, but ended up pretty long by the time we left. It seemed to move quickly though. They also have plenty of tables, so by the time you order one is usually available before your food is ready. Given the lines, I was expecting the food to be better. We got a #1a and a #11. The noodles and meat in 1a were ok, but not great. The broth wasn’t super flavorful. I’m not sure if it’s what we ordered, but this was probably the first place from the infatuation best noodles in nyc place where we said we don’t need to come back. Note, I love spicy food. Like really, really spicy. They didn’t really have anything spicy, minus the chili oil, which isn’t even spicy. It also was one of the most unappetizing things I have seen in a while. I am not sure how long it was been there, but I think it has more nastiness in it than bob Marley’s hair. I am not sure what the red sauce is, but it isn’t sriracha.

Absolutely delicious food and quick service. BRING CASH! It’s very busy inside but it’s common for you to ask to sit at a table with other people if seats are open. I got the wheat noodles with peanut butter sauce and vegetable dumplings for $8.25! Wow such a steal. I’m vegetarian and with my two dishes I left full and satisfied. My friend recommended the wheat noodles vs the thick rice noodles because she thinks they soak up the sauce more and I was happy with them! I’m sure personal preference factors into preferred noodle type. No frills place, but can’t beat the price or the flavor here. I think it’s worth the hype

I came here for lunch with a few friends who have never tried Fuzhounese food before. We ordered fried dumplings, steamed dumplings, peanut butter noodles, wonton soup, and fish ball soup. We all enjoyed the food and left super full. The prices are very affordable, we only spent $35 for a total of 4 people. There are a good amount of tables and also a bathroom for customers. I definitely will be coming back here soon!

google_reviews.text: What an amazing experience we had at Izakaya Nori Restaurant ! An amazing tranquil environment with a lot of natural light and beautiful ambiance filled with traditional Japanese cherry blossoms at the entrance and greenery decorations everywhere. The tables have very nice ornaments that truly give off the Japanese culture vibes. Now the food was incredible ! Started off with some edamame on the house ! (They serve it to us before we placed our order) We ordered the 3 roll special and I ordered the Tokyo Ice Tea. In the pictures you can see the drink looks refreshing and was actually very tasty. Please take notice of the presentation of the plates and why I want to give this place 6 stars!  The Philadelphia, California, Boston, Salmon, Eel Avocado, and Shrimp rolls were all amazing! Ended the dinner with two Sapporo beers and gave a nice tip! Would come again and again and again!

The ribeye yakitori was pretty good, tender and a good amount of sauce to pair it quite well. The chicken skin yakitori was very crispy and delicious, with just a tad too much sauce which made some pieces overly salty, but no biggie. The salmon tartar was just okay, with the yuzu sauce being very sour. I think if the amount of avocado being increased a bit, it would have helped equalize its sourness with the creaminess of the avocado. The three rolls lunch special is very fresh and had more ingredients than rice, just like the special dancing lobster roll which had so much lobster (as evident in the pictures)! The rock shrimp lunch bento was also just mediocre, potentially due to it being overly battered and pieces were combined together. Overall, we really loved the freshness and generosity of the fishes in their normal and special sushi rolls! The restaurant also looks very pretty with beautiful floral decorations and is incredibly spacious and clean. The staff were all very friendly and quick with their service, with pretty plates and utensils. Will definitely be back and I'm sure with a little adjustment, the quality of their food will only continue to enhance!

Thank you for reading and best of luck! (:

google_reviews.text:
The server asked us immediately if we understood the menu was vegan and whether we were seeing a show. Between 2 people, we split the Smoked Tofu Spinach Salad and Sweet Potato Fries with a side of BBQ sauce.

Hands down the most flavorful tofu we had ever had. We wished we hadn’t ordered the fries—not because they weren’t delicious—but because we couldn’t finish.

If I had any negative — the lighting was so low that I almost felt sleepy.

They made sure we received the food promptly with time to eat and pay the bill before making it to our evening show on time.

As we paid, we noticed that the bill indicated the restaurant operates as a nonprofit. What a pleasant surprise!

Amazing and phenomenal. Fresh ingredients, upscale vibe with casual staff, tasty food. I got the sweet chilli Maitake Wings and truffle fries. The prices match the portions in my opinion. Don’t be afraid to splurge a bit if cash is tight, you might even have leftovers.

A group of 5 of us traveled into NYC to see a show and being a mix of vegans and vegetarians, we decided to try P.S. Kitchen for lunch before the show, great choice and great food.

I ordered the P.S. Burger which consisted of a Beyond Burger, queso, lettuce, tomato and red onion, Thousand Island dressing on a pretzel bun, with a side of fries.  The burger was fantastic, loved all the flavors.  The fries were not hot, so thumbs down for that.

My partner ordered the Thai Chicken Sandwich with Crispy Chicken glazed in Sweet Thai Chili Sauce, lettuce, tomato, red onion, mayo on a pretzel bun, with fries.  He loved the crispy chicken sandwich.

Our friends ordered the Smoked Tofu Spinach Salad, the Crispy Caesar Wrap and the Thai Chicken Sandwich loving all the food.

For desert two of us ordered the Tiramisu and the Carmel Apple Cheesecake.  Both deserts were a hit.

Service is attentive and a large help with the menu.

Overall, great plant based food.

Great vegan spot in the Theater District. I had been here a couple of years ago and ate at the bar before checking out a show.
This time I went after seeing a show. The restaurant wasn’t busy so we were seated right away. The waitress was friendly and explained the menu to us. We ordered the Smokey bbq burger, Chicken caeser wrap and sweet potato french fries. We also ordered the hummingbird cake and peach cobbler to go.

The burger was delicious. It was a little messy, with the bbq sauce but it had great flavor. My Mom is not vegan and she loved the wrap. She was only able to eat half and took the rest to go. We shared the sweet potato fries. I was happy they were shoestring and not steak fries. They had a good crispness to them on the outside but still soft inside.

We got our desserts to go. The peach cobbler was yummy. The peaches were seasoned well and the crumble was tasty.  My mom is still talking about the hummingbird cake so it was delicious.

I definitely recommend this spot if you are in Times Square.

Great vegan spot in NYC's Theatre District with a wide range of vegan food to choose from.

Mostly focused on American classics, the menu caters for a variety of palates. We opted for:

-Crabby Cakes
-Black-N-Bleu Burger
-Chicken Pot Pie
-French Fries
-Mashed Potatoes
-Tiramisu

All of them were faithful vegan recreations of the traditional dishes they're based on – although the tiramisu and the crab cakes were absolutely the highlight.

We were seated and served quickly by friendly staff – certainly a great option for vegan food if you're attending a show nearby.

google_reviews.text:
Shenandoah National Park is a beautiful place to visit, especially if you enjoy nature and scenic views. Skyline Drive offers incredible overlooks of the Blue Ridge Mountains, and there are plenty of spots to stop and take photos or just enjoy the scenery. The park feels peaceful and is a great escape from busy city life.

There are many well maintained hiking trails for all skill levels, from short walks to more challenging hikes. The waterfalls are a highlight and definitely worth the effort to reach. Wildlife sightings are common, which adds to the overall experience, and the park is clean and well cared for.

Overall, Shenandoah National Park is a great destination for hiking, relaxing, and spending time outdoors. It’s a place I’d recommend to anyone looking for fresh air, great views, and a calm, natural setting.

Skyline drive, in Shenandoah National Park, is a well maintained road along the mountain. There is a lodge, gift shops, and supplies for backpacking on the Appalachian Trail.  There are many turnouts with exceptional views of the valleys and vistas below. Many opportunities to see wildlife.  But while driving, please obey the speed limit and be aware & courteous of wildlife.  This is their home…you are a guest!

Although it was a short trip, it was packed with fun adventures and great views. Skyline Drive offers plenty of great areas to pull off and take in the breathtaking views, but I suggest taking more time and exploring the parks trails. There are a wide range of trails that are suitable for all skill levels.

Definitely must visit,.especially during the changes of the fall foliage. It was such a beautiful peaceful drive. There are many view point stops. Must take a moment to pull over at least once to look over the Mountains. My husband and I loved Hawksbill Loop area during the Skyline Drive. It is breathtaking. Highly recommend. 🥰

We make the couple hour trip here every fall.  The views are spectacular, the air is clean and there is abundant wildlife, especially at night.  On a clear sky night, the star gazing is exceptional. Lots of trails to hike, places to camp, and very cool stuff in the surrounding towns.  If you live within a 6 hour drive of this park, you should regularly visit.

document: Ji Bei Chuan Noodles. cuisine: Noodles Chinese. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This is one of my favorite fast-casual eateries on 86th st! I’ve dined here about 4 or 5 times now and the food is always great. We love the cooling cucumber salad which contrasts nicely against the HOT (and I mean HOT!) bowls of steaming silky rice noodles served in a stoneware style bowl which helps retain the optimum serving temperature. The ingredients are fresh and the soup broths are delicious. The original bone broth is so flavorful and comforting but they also have a range of different broths for when you want something spicy. In addition to their main menu which is already good value, they offer 3 options of dine-in only set menus which get you an appetiser, a main course and a drink for no more than $19.95! The service is always friendly and the food comes out lightening fast.  It’s a clean and well presented restaurant with minimalist decor apart from a cute animae style wall decoration on one side.  We’ve also had this delivered and it will was still excellent. We’ll continue to be regulars here!

Had the soup thai golden fatty beef and bestie had the tomato soup with beef. Pipping hot broth on a rotatable stand and friendly service with a single bathroom. Sweet corn in soup and one quail egg, wood ear mushrooms and big batch of lettuce and some enoki mushroom.
Lots of noodle and big portions but the thai style golden soup was gingery but not spicy.

Pretty good and flavorful noodle spot. There’s multiple specials they offer here. You can get a stamp card and get a free bowl for every 10th. You can load up a prepaid card for bonus credits. We did $300 and got $50 bonus. There’s also 2 different special menu options that offer a bowl of noodles, small appetizer, and a drink for $17.95 option. All in all, they try really hard to promote their business and find value for their customers which is a major plus. I ordered the beef tomato soup base, which came out piping hot! So be careful to not burn your tongue/ mouth. The place itself feels super well organized and clean, albeit not that big, so expect a long wait during dinner rush hours. Friendly staff is also a plus here!

Love their Sauerkraut version and Fish Rice Noodles and also Tom Yum Noodle soup. The soup base is very flavorful and great mix of ingredients combination. This is one of our go to spots on 86th Street.

The restaurant is located in the Bensonhurst section of Brooklyn.  They prepare Chinese cuisine.  They have tables and servers for dining in.  Various noodle soups, cold dishes, appetizers and beverages are available.  They have additional locations in Chinatown in  Manhattan and Flushing, Queens.  I ordered the dumplings in spicy oil and crispy coconut lava balls as appetizers.  The seafood tom yum soup with rice noodles had a nice variety of seafood.  The silken tofu with fish slices was a smooth and light soup with rice noodles.  The food was well-prepared and packaged well in an insulated reusable bag.  Friendly and helpful staff.

name: Tara Kitchen - Tribeca New York
document: Tara Kitchen - Tribeca New York. cuisine: Moroccan Mediterranean Seafood. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Amazing restaurant with excellent food and I'm excited to come here again. We came here as a group of 5 and loved every single dish we ordered.

Our apps included the (1) Spicy Chickpea Bowl, Ras Fries, Spinach Briouats and Spicy Shawarma Hummus.

The briouats filling' was a lovingly creamy texture due to the spinach and cheese with an amazing and complex garlic flavor, all wrapped in flaky phyllo. It also came with a spicy sauce which I even used with the pita I thought was brilliant. The spicy shawarma hummus was also delightfully creamy and served with pita. It wasn't grainy at all and I'd even describe the taste as delicate and nuanced- not too spicy at all.

The chickpeas and fries were simple but great- I'd like the fries to come with a little more seasoning or mix the seasoning more evenly, but there was another spicy harissa-based sauce it came with that was great.

Our entrees were the (1) Chicken a l'Orange, (2) White Fish and Bouillabaisse, (3) Shepherd's Pie, and the (4) Lamb Tagine Makfoul.

Overall, the portions of all the entrees were huge! Almost all of us took our meals home, and that's not because they were loaded with carbs. The orange chicken dishes had an amazing natural-tasting orange sauce that had a nice amount of heat with tender on-the-bone chicken and couscous. The shepherd's pie was also amazing with smooth potatoes and a very complex sauce which had a similar super warming heat to it. The lamb tagine had so much meat and the cinnamon and honey were perfectly balanced to the dish and came with a bowl of rice.

I've eaten many different cuisines in Manhattan and this restaurant is among the best.

I was looking for an authentic Moroccan experience after our trip to Morocco earlier this year and Tara Kitchen was a great choice. I was specifically looking for appetizers and entrees I tried on our vacation which led me to order Shrimp pil pil and lamb meatballs with poached eggs. Everything was delicious. I would visit again. We had the vegan chocolate cake dessert with pistachio mousse and a mango cheesecake.

We visited this Moroccan gem as a group of 8 coworkers to celebrate a birthday, and it was such a lovely experience from start to finish. We made a reservation two days in advance, and when we arrived, they were ready and waiting for us, such a great first impression!

We ordered a variety of dishes: rice chicken bowl, boneless chicken, golden chicken, shrimp pil pil, Moroccan shepherd’s pie, and lamb kebab. Every single dish was flavorful and satisfying. I personally had the shrimp pil pil, and it was perfectly spicy with a rich, bold flavor, just the way I like it. The portions were generous, and we didn’t have to wait long for our food, which made the whole experience even better.

After such a hearty meal, we were hesitant to order tea, but we’re so glad we did! We shared two pots of Moroccan tea, and it was the perfect way to end the meal—refreshing, great for digestion, and served in the cutest little glasses.

The ambiance was authentic and full of charm, with a warm, welcoming vibe. The staff were incredibly attentive and kind, even surprising the birthday guest with a beautiful slice of cake, a candle, and a sweet gesture involving singing, such a thoughtful touch!

We’re already planning to come back and try more dishes. Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for delicious Moroccan food and a genuinely lovely dining experience.
This place is SO GOOD!! Service is so fast and everything is delicious! The broth the tikka masala comes in is so good I could eat it like soup! Lovely atmosphere and gorgeous decorations.

Wow, what an experience this was! This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants in NY, I wish I had discovered it earlier. The food was so delicious, I can’t quite name my favorite because all of them were favorite! We got some pita bread with dips, carrots with hummus (which was far from the ordinary), egg rolls (wow! maybe my favorite?), chicken sandwich, orange salad, mango dessert, and more. And I shouldn’t forget the cocktails! Go for the salt and pepper martini if you like non-sweet drinks. The service was also outstanding. Omar really made us feel welcomed and took great care of us. Will be counting days to my next visit…

name: Fishmarket II
document: Fishmarket II. cuisine: Malaysian. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
The food here was good. Interesting flavors and good variety in dishes. Pretty spicy too. Very reasonably priced.

The ambience is just okay - it feels like a sport bar that’s somehow also a Malaysian restaurant. If they invested in designing a nice interior this could be a popular restaurant.

Excellent Malaysian food. And a surprisingly wonderful American bar food menu too, the fried fish fingers were freshly fried, crispy outside juicy inside, paired with a perfect tartar sauce, not the typical frozen bar food stuff. Whoever in the kitchen really knew how to make crispy fried food. Highly recommend the food here!
The ambiance was interesting... They were playing Midwest country music and football games on the TVs when I was there around 10pm. No one was around and it was quick to get seated. The games and excellent bar food would make a great choice for night bar gatherings, in theory. An interesting choice in NYC though, where I don't imagine the demographic to be as prominent as other more conservative states.

This place is so awesome and I don't want anyone else finding out about it because I hate waiting in lines for things...but I am not actually living in Manhattan right now, so I sadly won't be coming back anytime soon, and I want this place to be open and thriving for next time I come back; therefore, I think everyone should know about this. The place is a little dive-y but not in a bad way at all, very clean, with a long bar, a wall full of TVs showing various sportsball,  and country music of my Midwest college days playing in the background. The bartender is super cool and kind and chill and I kinda want to be her friend if that wouldn't be weird (sorry, bartender if you are reading this and I made it weird).

We ordered the beef rendang because we love rendang and where I live now I can't reliably access it, as well as the crispy rice. IT. WAS. INCREDIBLE. Like, seriously, I will probably randomly think about this meal and have a slight tear in my eye as I do because it is so damn delicious and I will be far, far away.

So, locals, please come to this place and eat all the food because it is so good and you will not be sorry and that way when I do come back it will still be here.  Anyway, 10/10, no notes.

My husband and I came here for an early dinner get together with my brother, sis in law and their 6mo old. Kim, the bartender/server was amazing; attentive without being overbearing. Food was savory, very flavorful, and had the right amount of kick. We all had a great time and finished off all the food we ordered. I recommend the scallion pancakes, the curry laksa, the crispy fried rice, the curried chicken, and nasi lemak. We will definitely be going back!
Loved the Malaysian offerings here. Came with a big group and they were very accommodating to us, service was excellent. Definitely will be coming back here for more of that laksa.

name: 4 Charles Prime Rib
document: 4 Charles Prime Rib. cuisine: Steakhouses Seafood Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text: Went for a private event and sat in the private dining room.  The food was out of this world!!  If and that is a BIG IF, you can get a reservation you must eat here.  There are only 9 tables in this spot.  We had the crabcakes, sizzling shrimp appetizers. Ceaser salad with salmon.  Menu courses were the wagyu cheese burger, prime rib and wagyu porterhouse.  The sides we had were Elote Style Corn and Truffle Mac and Cheese.  You are not going to have a better meal anywhere in Manhattan nor the entire country!!  Highly recommend you do what you can to go here and enjoy as much of the menu as you can!!!

My review is slightly biased by the “untouchable” reputation this restaurant has built and the pure joy that came with just being able to eat here.

Overall the food is good. It’s not the most incredible restaurant in NYC for the price, but you will have a good meal. Loved the bacon, steak, and truffle mac. The burger was also good and I appreciate that they make it a show with the glove and egg cutting. Only thing I was meh on was the French dip but I think that’s just because it was served cold.

The ambience is great. Very institutional feeling. I like that it’s an intimate dining space, well decorated, dimly lit - you feel like you’re dining among NYC’s elite.

Service was great. Very personable staff and clearly they can recruit the best of the best.

I just wish I was on their list so I could eat here more regularly but alas. Well worth

Very hard to get a res but this place absolutely lived up to the hype for me. Prime rib was the best I’ve ever had. Burger was amazing (maybe top 2 in nyc) and so was the chocolate cream pie. French dip and truffle mac and cheese were also good but not must-gets.

Finally managed to get into 4 Charles Prime and it was worth it.

How to do it:  If you are a walk-in, the restaurant opens at 4pm, if you are a party of 2 or 4 (any larger is not worth trying) I suggest someone be in line by 230/3pm. We arrived at 3pm and were the 4th party in line (party of 2) and just before opening, the host accepted the first two parties and we were entered into a lottery slot for any potential openings before 8pm and we managed to get a 630 slot.

Onto the experience… the decor is intimate and dark/rustic and all of the staff were very kind,  accommodating and professional.

The wine and cocktail lists are extensive and offer many delicious options.

We ordered a lot of food, since it may be our only visit. Be prepared to take some home, as the portions are large and rich.

The sizzling shrimp scampi starter was excellent, filled with flavor and accompanied by crispy garlic bread. The cheeseburger was also excellent, though adding the bacon and egg makes for a rich and filling experience, if we return I would skip the bacon and egg.

The star of the night was the French dip sandwich, which we shared. The meat was so flavorful and the roll had a perfect crisp. The dip and horseradish together made for a perfect dish.
I also recommend the truffle Mac & Cheese. We took most of it home, and it heats up well the next day.

If you have room for dessert, the chocolate cream pie is a must.

It’s a rough place to get in, but it made for a nice experience, and worth the hype.

All around wonderful experience. Four of us had quite the amazing dinner. One of us waited for them to open and we luckily got a table. The staff were extraordinarily pleasant and friendly. They immediately made us feel comfortable. They helped us understand the menu and home in on our choices. All of the food was out of this world.

We started with the gem salad. Incredibly fresh, dressed perfectly with delicious avocado in the center. They then brought out the cheeseburger and the French dip sandwich. They cut the burger and sandwiches in four and we shared everything.

Our second course was the Wagyu strip steak and the 4 Charles cut prime rib. The Wagyu was absolutely extraordinary! Probably the best piece of steak ever. Prime rib was also delicious. Both were served with sauces, one Bernaise and one horseradish. We also tried the shrimp scampi, which was the best I’ve ever had. We had the cream spinach and the mac and cheese as sides. Both quite decadent.

We finished with a table full of desserts. Way too much food, but it was an important birthday and the staff were very kind. We took home the leftovers, lol.

This place is tough to get in. This place is quite expensive. But, for a special meal it’s worth it. Really a step beyond other places with similar menus. Intimate. Attentive, informative and friendly staff.

google_reviews.text:
A quote from my boyfriend after our appetizers: "ill never be a mother, but i imagine this feeling is the equivalent of holding your child for the first time"

My new fav spot, how this place isn't packed out is actually beyond me because it was easily one of the best meals I've ever had in New York and I've eaten a lottttt.
Everything I could hope for from an NYC seafood restaurant comes alive here.
Ambience is so nice lighting is perfect doesn't get too noisy but still feels alive, service is excellent, cozy but cool.

The food is just outstanding, I literally recommend everything like truly. Each dish was like wow I've never had something like that before and I need it again and again. In fact, I went two days in a row because I just had to get some appetizers again and try some more mains. I'm actually obsessed. I would be here much more often if I lived somewhat closer, but I will with no hesitation make the trek from Manhattan anytime I start craving it.

I honestly recommend every single dish that I have posted in this review (it's also every single dish that I've ordered in my times coming here) , but I think for me (i really love raw seafood) I can't go here without ordering the wild shrimp appetizer and the lobster tostada. The lobster tostada is one of the craziest things I've ever had I don't know how they made it taste like that and the textures (im salivating as i write) and they give you so much lobster i was swooning. Not that everything else isn't also perfection because it all really is in their own ways, but as a lobster lover this just tickled me.
Love their drink menu, non alcoholic list is pretty limited but what they do offer is tasty, for low ABV they have a lot of options featuring sherry, sweet wines, and amaros etc
Dessert was great im forgetting what it is called atm, but alongside the creamy looking one is their italian ice and flavors rotate.

This is our second time coming back to this restaurant. It’s a small cozy spot where I love sitting by the bar to see the action. The food was still amazing.

It’s our first time trying the violet hour though. We should have totally done that the first time. $45 PP - we can choose 3 dishes each. It was a tasing menu where dishes were supposed to come in half portion. It’s definitely bigger than half portion, we feel it’s almost like 2/3 of a real portion. The 2 of us with 6 dishes to share - we were full! Great value! Will definitely do this again if we come back between 5-6.

One star deducted to the service was because it seems we didn’t have a dedicated server. No one told us about violet hour nor special of the day x 2. We had to keep asking about it. Imagine if we didn’t overhead about the violet hour from the table next to us, we’d have totally missed it. So does the special of the day

The lighting is not photo friendly,  so don't judge the dishes by my pics.   The food was excellent.   Don't skip the anchovies or the iberico steaklette.   Cocktails were just as good and they even served me something off menu that turned out to be my favorite drink of the night. Excellent find in the neighborhood.

Incredible meal, no- experience. We got the chefs counter and were greeted by Winnie. She was helpful with an amazing drink recommendation. Then came the scallop tacos which I hear are only available on Friday/Saturday and Sunday if you’re feeling lucky (they run out)! The stars of the show were the seafood sausage and the squid. Can’t wait to go back!

I’ve been eating in NYC and similar establishments all over Europe for 40 years. I enjoyed the owners other places especially Txikito.  I don’t remember the last time I felt like having a slice of pizza after a meal.

Hushpuppies had a nice flavor. No complaints there.
Amberjack was good, appreciated the tomato water especially.  But when sharing with another, jute a couple of small pieces each.  One of the smallest “crudo” dishes I’ve seen.
A special of polenta fritters with babaganoush and salmon was delectable, but it’s more like a $20+ amuse bouche.
Rissotto was flavor packed and smoky. But again, poor value and a dish that felt like an excellent side dish midway.  Would have loved to pair this with some fish or something. This is a fisherie with zero cooked fish on the menu other than a very expensive whole fish special.
Squid a la Plancha - not as good as I hoped. Overly sweet and one-note until you mix all the sauces.

5 dishes, one drink - $170.  We could have easily ordered two more dishes but simply didn’t feel like paying more for such poor value.

document: Ayy Chihuahua. cuisine: Mexican Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Been here 2 times on Saturday. Their brunch is until 4pm, 30$ for an entree, a cocktail and coffee and tea, great deal! I chose the steak and eggs and believe me, one of the best dishes in Queens! Their margaritas are delicious as well, highly recommend the Hibiscus one! Me and my bros got chicken nachos as well, very delicious! Best Mexican restaurant in Astoria and the atmosphere is amazing as well!

tonight was my first time coming to Ayy Chihuahua and I will definitely be coming back! i have absolutely nothing bad to say about this restaurant. the service was excellent, the food was amazing, and the overall vibe is great too. we ordered the grilled shrimp tacos, the chicken soup, and the chicken fajitas. everything was delicious! i also recommend the classic margarita, but they have other good flavors too. our server was so attentive and kind. he even packed up our leftovers for us. i will 100% be eating here again!

It was a great evening celebrating my mom's birthday.  The appetizers, entree, and dessert were great. The service was attentive, friendly and informative. The only thing I would change is that all the entrees should be served with the sides of rice and beans.

I felt rushed during my meal. I was asked several times if they could take my plate before I had finished, which was frustrating. The Mexican michelada wasn’t very good. The food is okay for the price, but the overall experience could have been better.

Decided to come here one day after work with a friend of mine the service is really good. The drinks are good. The food is good.
I didn’t care too much for the Ají tuna tacos and the Elote should be perfected. my favorite was the steak shrimp fajita, guacamole rice and beans

name: Secret Kitchen
document: Secret Kitchen. cuisine: Cantonese Seafood Noodles. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Impeccable suit & tie service - high quality ingredients like the fish is fresh in the tank at the point of ordering.
Probably the only place in Melbourne that serves goose, it's good but not HK style or quality #IYKYK.
The duck was amazing, cooked to perfection. perfect crispy skin, nice render on the fat and importantly juicey on the meat.
Definitely a place to take someone to impress. The decor has that old world charm & several different types of seating & booths and rooms make up for a very cozy and memorable experience.
Have previously had their yum-cha too, which is probably my fav go-to place in Melb.

The food at this restaurant was really delicious — everything we tried tasted fresh and full of flavor. However, the service could definitely improve. We were served by three or four different staff members. The only person who stood out was a lady in black (possibly the manager) — she was professional, friendly, and had great customer service skills. Overall, I’d come back for the food, but I hope the service becomes more consistent next time.

An authentic dim sum restaurant with a wide variety of dishes to choose from. The food tastes great and feels traditional. Prices are slightly above average. Service could be improved, but the environment is clean and comfortable.
Everything was perfect. We came here for our anniversary dinner and the food was delicious. The service was great. We’ll definitely be back to try the Yum cha for lunch.

It’s been a while since I last ate here.
Today’s standouts were the Mango mochi (only in the weekend), BBQ pork rice rolls — generous meat filling wrapped in delicate sheets — and the roasted duck with lean meat and crispy skin. 😂 I was even tempted to order a bowl of steamed rice, hahaa.

The scallop truffle rice rolls didn’t really suit my taste; the flavor combination felt a bit odd.
The har gow and xiaolongbao weren’t very impressive either as I found their wrappers were kinda thick 🥲
The black bean chicken feet were a bit too soft for my liking, though my friend really enjoyed them.
Black bean pork ribs were standard, nothing much to complain.
The sweet bean curd lacked the fragrant ginger note although the bean curd itself was smooth & tasty.
The mango pudding was a little too sweet for me, but it was very fragrant — probably even better if served chilled!
__________

Overall, I think it was better a few years ago. However, considering the limited options for yum cha in the CBD that still serve in the traditional style, this place isn’t too bad.

name: District Saigon
document: District Saigon. cuisine: Vietnamese Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Wow!!

What an extremely amazing establishment for a Vietnamese food in Astoria Queens.

Everything we had was absolutely delicious.

I highly recommend the dumplings and the piña colada. The banh mi was out of this world. Best chicken banh mi i’ve ever had.

I will say the service was a little lackluster that night no hate on the staff. There were only three people working that night and it was extremely busy. I give kudos to them and they definitely deserve the tip. But the restaurant ownership definitely needs to do more hiring or better staffing for weekend nights.

The atmosphere also was extremely good. We had a community table as the restaurant was packed and I will say it was absolutely lovely.

I highly recommend you to go to this restaurant and it was not too expensive.

Went here for dinner with 9 of us and they were able to fit us no problem. The curry chicken was very flavorful and would get again. The bun lemon grass chicken dish was very light and refreshing. The pho was full and flavorful. The bah mi sandwich was just the right size for a meal. The steak and eggs the meat was a little tough but the seasoning was good. Drinks too a minute to come out but it was just one person making and bringing them out so that made sense. The food came fast and the service was good. Overall would come back

Overall really liked this spot. It’s not very traditional but still yum. The bun bo hue is a cleaner beef broth instead of pork and has beef toppings instead of pork kunckle and blood. It also didn’t have shrimp paste instead it was a strong lemongrass flavor. So not traditional at all but I liked it. The smoked brisket pho broth was good but the brisket was just a little too smoky for me. The viet crepe aka bun Xeo was really good they use ground pork in it and it’s very flavorful. I really liked their fish sauce it’s a sweeter one.

I like this little place. Conveniently located on Broadway in Queens between the R and  the N/W lines, it has a festive atmosphere and friendly service. My daughter loves the pho and the summer rolls. Today I tried the catfish bun, and though the vermicelli noodles were a little plain, the fish was tender and delicious.
food was delicious!! it was my first time trying pho with my friend and we were not disappointed. The broth was good, the meat was good, everything was a 10/10. I will definitely come back here again

google_reviews.text:
Aesthetic of the place: 7/10
Price: 10/10
Quality: 10/10
Quantity: 10/10

Waiter: Very attentive, great personality. Loved that he took the time to explain everything as dishes come out. 10/10

Starter 1: No picture. Tomato, mozzarella, and arugula were all very fresh. 9/10

Starter 2:. Basically a charcuterie board picked apart. Very fresh and creative. 8.5/10

Starter 3: You could taste the freshness in the sauce. Garlic bread had the perfect crunch to softness ratio. Meatball very moist. 9/10

Seasonal drink: 9/10 Crazy to say but it taste like fall. The grapes were a nice addition to the drink.

Entree 1: Ravioli was a little chewy, but the sauce made up for it. 8.5/10. The almond pasta was delicious. T the perfect consistency & the texture was a perfect al dente. 9.5/10.

Dessert: Unique, never had fig jam inside of a crepe with ice cream. Wasn’t the best combination. 5/10

The food came out at the perfect rate. The Parmesan was delicious and fresh. I loved that I got to choose what I wanted to get for dessert. I loved that my waiter, Jude, went out of his way to assist a pair of elderly females who needed a little extra help ordering due to a language and vision barrier.

I came at 3pm on a Saturday, sat down with my problem. I had not ate anything for the day… I left beyond full. Truly a hidden gem in the heart of queens.

Chef Franco never fails to impress me. 🫶🏼
With every dish made to perfection.
Highly recommend the 11375 Mushrooms and Classic Rigatoni with pesto sauce! Don’t forget to add chicken we also got the chance to enjoy the Lemon Shrimp pappardelle.

Exquisite dishes as always! Will be back for another date night!

FYI:
Sunday is BYOB 😉

Delicious pasta, great service, cozy atmosphere!

I really enjoy coming here for both dine in and take out. Their pasta is always made fresh, and their dishes are flavored well with good texture.

The servers are very nice and accommodating. Their restaurant is nice and cozy. But they can still host larger parties by rearranging the tables.

Price is reasonable for the amount and quality of food that you get. Highly recommended!

Delicious Food & Amazing Atmosphere!
This place is an absolute treasure! From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with such a warm, homey vibe that makes you feel instantly comfortable. The service is top-notch—everyone is so kind, attentive, and genuinely cares about your experience.
The food? Incredible. The penne alla vodka is easily one of the best I’ve ever had—perfectly cooked pasta, rich and creamy sauce, and bursting with flavor. You have to save room for dessert—the chocolate dessert is out of this world. Rich, decadent, and the perfect sweet ending to a great meal.
One of the best parts of dining here is the owner. He personally comes around to check on customers, chats with the tables, and makes sure everyone is having a great time. It’s that kind of personal touch that makes this place so special.
If you're looking for amazing food, great service, and a welcoming, cozy atmosphere—this is the spot. Can’t recommend it enough!

The homemade pasta was delicious and I definitely recommend ordering it to go. The wine and beer was good as well. We started with zucchini flowers and a Caesar salad. The sauce was delicious but the stuffed flowers were too cold, like just pulled from the fridge. Our main course pastas were all Al dente and tasty…would consider coming back for more. Serving sizes were comparable to the price. Servers could have been more personable and welcoming, I’ve seen friendlier service at a fast food restaurant. We would have stayed for dessert but the party of 8 next to us were quite loud and it ruined the end of our evening.

google_reviews.text: Quite honestly the best meal I’ve ever had at an airport. The vibes are good, the service is great, and the food is simply delicious. Thanks to my server Paola for curating an excellent dining experience. I’ll be back the next time I connect via LGA. 5/5 stars

document: Bestia Kitchen. cuisine: Tapas Bars. located in Bronx. with 2.8 stars (decent).

google_reviews.text:
Bastia in Los Angeles is an absolute standout and easily one of the best Italian dining experiences we’ve had. We called the same day on a whim and were thrilled to score seats at the chef’s counter, front row to the wood-fired pizza oven, the magic happening in the kitchen, and the chefs in action while dining, which added an unforgettable layer to the evening.

Our server was exceptional, knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and full of great recommendations. We started with the Charred Spanish Octopus, which was perfectly tender and beautifully smoky. The Herb Caesar salad was fresh, vibrant, and beautifully balanced, but the real star of the night was the Grilled Branzino, absolutely DIVINE. Light, flaky, and full of flavor, it was cooked to perfection.

Sitting so close to the pizza ovens made it impossible to resist ordering a pizza, so we went with the ’Nduja, bold, perfectly spicy, and so satisfying that we happily boxed half to enjoy later. No regrets.

The setting itself is stylish and artsy, tucked into a cool warehouse-like space in a vibrant neighborhood. Valet parking is available for $13, which is a bonus in LA and makes the experience even easier.

From the food to the service to the atmosphere, Bastia exceeded every expectation. This is now one of our go-to Italian spots in LA, and we will absolutely be back every time we’re in town.

I heard some mix reviews but I’m so glad I came! My fav dishes of the night were the snap peas, octopus, spicy prawns, branzino and squid ink pasta 🤤🤤 The only reason I didn’t give a 5 star is cause they don’t have mainstream liquor and their tequila and vodka were not ittt.

Picked up my husband and headed straight to Bestia for our late reservation, and the night did not disappoint. They offer valet, but we lucked out and found street parking right in front — already a win in LA.

From the moment we sat down, our server was warm, attentive, and paced the meal perfectly. Service truly elevated the whole experience.

Drinks
•	Riesling – crisp, clean, and paired well with seafood.
•	Seven Faces – a passion-fruit-forward pisco cocktail. Bright, tropical, and so easy to sip.

Apps
•	Bone Marrow – rich, buttery, and a great start.
•	Scallops – absolutely incredible. Perfectly seared and full of flavor. One of our favorites of the night.

Mains
•	Lobster Squid Ink Spaghetti – good, but probably the least memorable compared to the rest of the meal.
•	Branzino – standout entrée. Perfectly cooked, beautifully deboned, and just delicious.

We skipped dessert since our reservation was at 9pm, but honestly, the savory courses alone made the visit worth it. We can see exactly why Bestia is one of the top-rated spots in LA — the quality, flavors, and service all live up to the hype. We’ll definitely be back to try more!

Bestia delivers an unforgettable Italian dining experience in an industrial-chic setting. Our meal was a masterclass in execution and flavor, beginning with the stunning Scallops Crudo, which was impeccably fresh and bright, paired perfectly with the savory, tangy Marinated Olives.

The pasta course was the true highlight: the dramatic Ink Squid Spaghetti with Lobster offered intense seafood depth, while the Cream Sauce Pasta with Truffle was pure, aromatic indulgence, generously shaved with fresh black truffle. For the main event, the Lamb Neck was a triumph of slow cooking- fall-off-the-bone tender with a robust, charred crust.

Every dish demonstrated a commitment to high-quality ingredients and flawless technique. Bestia remains essential dining for a truly exceptional meal in Los Angeles.
