name: Tong
document: Tong. cuisine: Thai Bars Tapas/Small Plates. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Tong in Bushwick is where you go to experience authentic Thai small plates known as kub klaem. The sleek dining room wrapped in rustic metal walls captures that raw NYC energy while still feeling clean and cozy with lighting that mirrors how vibrant the food tastes. Tong does not hold back on spice and a simple medium Thai spicy is no joke, definitely not for first timers and even seasoned spice lovers might find it daring but that heat brings out the true and unapologetic deliciousness of Thailand. From cocktails to small plates everything is thoughtfully crafted and plated like edible art. If you love Thai cuisine or crave bold spicy flavors, Tong is the perfect spot for incredible food creative drinks and warm hospitality with genuine smiles that go the extra mile.

Came here to say with my brother and his finance. Pretty nice restaurant. The prices were decent. Large portion sizes. The tom yum soup was amazing. It was spicy but full of flavor and texture. I had the green curry with tofu and it was one of the best I have ever had. The curry was smooth and the rice was fresh and not sticky. I’m he tofu was the perfect texture for the broth. My brother and his fiancé got the drunken noodles and I know they loved it because they finished the bowl.

Went on a date night to Tong, a Thai restaurant in Bushwick recognized by the Michelin Guide. Because of how popular it has become, it’s definitely best to make a reservation ahead of time since the space fills up quickly and many people come specifically for the food.

The atmosphere makes it a really nice date spot. Dim lighting, warm wooden tables, and thoughtful plating give it an intimate feel without being overly formal, and the staff were warm and welcoming from the moment we walked in.

To start, I ordered the Jolean cocktail made with gin, lychee, butterfly pea flower, orange blossom water, lime, and egg white. It was light, floral, and well balanced, with the egg white giving it that silky foam texture. My boyfriend kept it classic with a Thai iced tea, served in a mason jar with the familiar gradient of dark tea and creamy milk that gives it that rich sweetness and deep caramel color.

For appetizers we started with the Som Tum Thai, one of Thailand’s most iconic salads. Traditionally from the Isan region in northeastern Thailand, som tum is all about balancing the four core Thai flavor elements: sour, spicy, sweet, and salty. The dish came with long strands of shredded green papaya piled high with peanuts, cherry tomatoes, long beans, dried shrimp, fresh chili, and a wedge of lime on the side. The green papaya itself is mild and crunchy, almost like a vegetable version of a green apple, which makes it perfect for soaking up the lime heavy dressing. The dried shrimp added a deep umami note while the peanuts gave it texture. It was refreshing but still packed with flavor, with the dressing lightly pooling at the bottom so everything could be tossed together.

We also ordered the Truffle Spring Rolls, filled with glass noodles, shiitake mushrooms, and oyster mushrooms. Glass noodles, made from mung bean starch, absorb flavor really well and give that slightly chewy texture that works perfectly inside crispy spring rolls. The mushroom filling was earthy and rich, and the truffle added an aromatic depth that made it feel slightly more elevated than a typical vegetable roll. The fry was clean and crisp without feeling greasy, which made them really enjoyable.

For mains, I ordered the Pad Cha Talay, a seafood stir fry known for being bold and aromatic. Pad cha refers to a style of stir fry loaded with herbs and spices that create a fragrant, slightly spicy dish. This one had shrimp, squid, and mussels with bamboo shoots, eggplant, long beans, kaffir lime leaf, fresh green peppercorn clusters, and krachai, also known as fingerroot, a traditional Thai herb with a peppery, ginger like aroma. The seafood was cooked well and the vegetables still had a nice bite to them. The bamboo shoots and eggplant absorbed the sauce nicely, while the fresh peppercorns added small bursts of spice throughout the dish. It was served with a dome of fluffy jasmine rice that paired perfectly with the aromatic sauce.

My boyfriend ordered the Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup from the Chiang Mai region known for its rich coconut curry broth and the contrast between soft noodles and crispy noodles on top. Flavor wise, the broth was really delicious, warm, creamy, and comforting. However, the presentation and balance could definitely be improved. The chicken was mostly hidden under the broth and noodles, and the portion leaned heavily toward noodles compared to the bean sprouts and other components. If the ingredients were distributed more evenly, visually showing the chicken, noodles, and bean sprouts, it would elevate both the presentation and the overall balance of the dish.

Service overall was great, though water refills could have been a little more attentive.

For a restaurant recognized by Michelin, the food here is already strong in terms of flavor and execution, but there are small areas where things could be elevated further, particularly presentation and balance in certain dishes. With a few refinements, it could better match the level that the pricing suggests. I would definitely come back to try more of the menu.

document: Blue. cuisine: Mediterranean Seafood Desserts. located in Staten_Island. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Highly recommend! We enjoyed an amazing meal here for the second time, and the flavor profile and overall quality truly surpass the Ashby Inn in Paris, VA. The food, drinks, and desserts were all phenomenal—a memorable treat from start to finish. Just note that reservations are usually needed to get a seat on most nights.

Service was excellent indoors. Some of the negative reviews seem tied to outdoor seating, and honestly, it’s understandable—staff have quite a distance to cover between the kitchen and the outdoor tables, so a little grace goes a long way.

Our only suggestion would be to rotate the main entrées a bit more or perhaps introduce a weekend specialty dish. Everything is fantastic, but the variety can feel limited if you’re a frequent visitor since the entrée list is fairly small.

We had a lovely experience at the Blue Door Kitchen and Inn. The property and grounds are beautiful and you can tell owners Reem Arbid and chef Andrea Pac put a lot of love into the project. We stayed in the Washington Suite and it was cozy and a great size room for 2 people. What's nice is being able to walk to dinner downstairs when the evening comes. The restaurant is fantastic with delicious food (the gnocchi is incredible!) and a great wine list. We enjoyed a Italian wine recommended by Reem and it paired well with the appetizers and mains that we ordered. Reem was a lovely host and chatted with us throughout the dinner and evening, where we headed to the bar for a nightcap after dinner. We plan on staying here when we go hiking in Shenandoah and highly recommend them for your stay.

Our Thanksgiving lunch at Blue Door Kitchen and Inn was delicious and perfect. The place already has that cozy, tucked-away charm, but today it felt even warmer. Paige took care of us, and she was fantastic. Friendly, genuine, and totally on top of things without ever rushing us. She made the whole experience feel easy.

The Thanksgiving menu was delicious. Every dish tasted fresh and thoughtful, like someone actually cared about what they were sending out of the kitchen. It was comforting without being heavy, which is exactly what you want in the middle of the day.

The whole afternoon felt calm, relaxed, and special. If you’re looking for a spot that makes a holiday meal feel both elevated and homey, this is it. We’ll definitely be back.

Compliments to the chef!  I enjoyed the rockfish, perfectly cooked, seasoned and paired with delicious sides.  It's worth ordering dessert also.  I will suggest that management and staff might attend more courteously to every guest, even if cocktails and starters are not ordered.  Worth mentioning, the branzino at Osteria Maria runs a very close race.

The restaurant is perfect. Each item in the menu is a jewel. I usually have the fish offering and there is always a lovely sauce and something surprising. As a GF, DF person, I adore that they keep dark chocolate sorbet in the menu. The husband and wife team are warm and professional.

google_reviews.text: Me and my honey loves this establishment!!! Every time we come it’s always delicious fresh food. Joey is the man! As a private chef in the city, he has the best seafood and the best customer service. Always a smile on his face. His seafood is always fresh and at great prices.  His knowledge about where he gets his seafood always amazes me.  If you aren’t getting your seafood from here then are you really eating right?!?! I THINK NOT. Go get yourself a sandwich or some raw fish, NOW.

We stopped by last weekend on a whim as we were walking through Brooklyn and I have to say that we got extremely lucky - Shipwreck is the best seafood spot! name: Kyuramen - Forest Hills
document: Kyuramen - Forest Hills. cuisine: Ramen. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I needed a Ramen spot that met specific paramers. Good ramen. Good service. Good price. All these will appeal to anyone, but for me personally, it's close to home AND work. This place is perfect. Ivan and his staff have time and again provided excellent service and ramen that has me coming back at least weekly, something I don't do anywhere else. Look at my attached pics. None are duplicate bowls. All of them were delicious. I'd say Ichiran has slightly better ramen, but considering all other factors (starting with Ichiran being almost double the price), this is my #1 spot in NYC, no question.

Very cute and cozy place, very clean and ramen bowl was amazing taste 10/10. Service was quite fast there’s a button you can press on each table to order, pay or just call them someone showed up every time in under 10 seconds that was amazing. I got vegetable miso ramen bowl and it was so amazing.

I thought I was in a Japan! The atmosphere was so aesthetic. We ordered the noodle combo and mango crepe cake which is a pretty great deal. It comes with a Ramen, a pork bun, Cold coffee, and a matcha pudding. I specially loved the pork buns and the cake. Definitely recommend!

I stopped by Kyuramen and ordered the Curry Ramen and an Iced Thai Tea, and both really hit the spot. The curry ramen had a rich, flavorful broth and savory with just the right amount of spice. The noodles were perfectly chewy, and the tender slices of pork soaked up the curry flavor nicely. It’s a comforting bowl that balances warmth and spice without being overwhelming. The Iced Thai Tea was creamy and refreshing, with that signature sweet, slightly earthy flavor that pairs perfectly with a salty, savory dish. The atmosphere was cozy with a modern Japanese feel which is great for solo dining or a casual hangout. Service was quick and friendly, and everything came out fresh and hot. Overall, Kyuramen delivered a satisfying, flavorful meal that I’d definitely order again especially on a cold day!

I’ve been to all four Kyuramen locations in Queens, and one thing I truly appreciate is the consistency — the service is always warm, the atmosphere inviting, and the quality never disappoints. Whether it’s Flushing, Bayside, Long Island City, or Forest Hills, each visit feels like coming home to a familiar, comforting meal.

My staple order is always the Yin Yang Ramen Bowl, which beautifully combines two different broths in one — one spicy, one mild. It’s the best of both worlds. Each side is deeply flavorful, rich, and balanced, and the portions of meat and veggies are generous. The presentation is always on point, but it’s the taste that keeps me coming back.

I unfortunately suffered a loss today and grieving - honestly, there’s nothing quite like a hot, savory bowl of ramen from Kyuramen to soothe an aching heart. There’s comfort in the routine of that first sip of broth — it’s like being wrapped in warmth and familiarity.

Kyuramen isn’t just a place to eat; it’s a small reminder that even in hard times, simple pleasures like good ramen can make things a tiny bit better.

document: Ayada Thai. cuisine: Thai. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Ayada in Elmhurst is easily one of the best Thai spots you can visit, and it’s a fantastic choice for groups. We went as a party of 6 with a reservation and ordered a variety of dishes, but the portions were so generous that we couldn't even finish everything. I’d definitely say that all the orders are perfect for sharing if you want to taste a bit of everything with your friends.

The absolute highlight for me was the creamy tom kha gai soup—it was incredible, and I’d recommend it to anyone. Just a heads-up: whether you love the heat or prefer things mild, make sure to let them know your spice preference when you order!

Every dish we ordered was packed with bold, authentic flavors and executed perfectly.

The drunken noodles were smoky, spicy, and beautifully balanced, great wok char and just the right kick. The larb was fresh, vibrant, and full of herbs, with that perfect tangy heat that keeps you going back for another bite.

The curry duck was the standout: incredibly tender, rich, and deeply flavorful, with a curry that was complex without being overwhelming. And the Thai sausage? Juicy, aromatic, and addictive, the perfect appetizer to kick things off.

Everything tasted intentional and true to Thai cuisine. Add friendly service and a cozy, no-frills atmosphere, and AYADA easily earns its reputation as one of the best Thai spots around. Can’t wait to come back and try more of the menu.

Wow - this place was fabulous. Excellent service and what we had was absolutely delicious. We started off with the dumplings as an appetizer and then we split a few items, including drunken noodles with beef – medium rare – with basil fried rice and Chinese broccoli. document: Louie's Pizza. cuisine: Italian Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
We had been seeing this place pop up on my feed for a while, so when my friend group and I were in Detroit we wanted authentic Detroit style pizza, so this was the obvious choice. We made sure to get there right when they opened and there were already people trickling in and the waitress mentioned the locals come so regularly it's basically a habit at this point.
We ordered three different pizzas for 4 people. They have premade options but you can also build your own with toppings. Everything was delicious and exactly what we expected from Detroit pizza. The inside has this really fun retro vibe with wine bottles decorations. It is a great place for any occasion, families, date night, a big friend group, or even coming alone for a bite. Would recommend if you're in the area and want the real deal.

I visited Loui's yesterday with my preschool-age daughter. We were in town from Indiana so I wanted to get her the most authentic old-school Detroit style pizza possible and Loui's came highly reccomended. It was our first time ever eating here. The food was awesome and my waitress was pretty great too. She was friendly to me and my daughter, made great suggestions, and gave all-around great service. I reccomend this place based off my experience and will personally go back when I'm in Detroit again.

Have been wanting to try this place for a while and glad the parking and long wait for a table did not deter us. The ambience was great — noisy but not so loud that you had to shout across the table for your party to hear you — and the waitress was friendly and attentive despite it being a busy Saturday night. She was helpful when we asked about the sizes of the dishes and we were glad she talked us into sizing down for the salad and pizza.  We ordered antipasto for the famous dressing, a small Detroit style pizza (my husband and I were barely able to finish 1 1/2 squares), and my daughters ordered a small ravioli with meat sauce and a spaghetti with meat sauce each. The crust in the pizza was crispy and the cheese pull for the stuffing was 10/10.  We are normally thin crust/NY style pizza fans but this was definitely tasty. The crust dipped in the homemade ranch was also delicious.  For us the stars of the show were the salad (perfectly dressed) and the spaghetti.  The spaghetti sauce was slightly sweet which is how we like our sauce and they were generous with the meat.  I would come back and endure the wait just for the pasta dishes!  We had no room for dessert but will be fighting over who gets to eat the leftovers over the next couple of days.

Very busy and crowed.  No chicken tenders or wings or  potato wedges. Food was fine. No romaine lettuce.  No ranch dressing. I ordered  a medium antipasto  salad which was smaller than i normally get. It  had alot of cheese, not enough ham and Salami. The  Pizza was good i just did not like  the  green peppers on it were raw. I enjoy the things I ordered  much more at the original buddys location.

This is the original Detroit style pizza and restaurant.

Pizza is delicious with crispy cheese crust and balanced sauce.  Crust is fluffy.

Get the bottle of canti that you can decorate yourself. Fun

Greek salad was great. Fresh crispy and packed with black olives beats and feta

Throw in some cheese bread sticks.....you have to order these. and you have a perfect evening of fun and great food.

name: Lin & Daughters
document: Lin & Daughters. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Bubble Tea. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I nominate this place for Bib Gourmand!
Yes, seriously- this is one of the best Asian food I had in a while outside of what I have eaten in China. This is a tiny place with huge taste! Unpretentious little hole in wall place, you are there to eat, it’s not about the tables or decor. One of my pet peeves is kitchen smoke and smells - and given the size of the place I was expecting that we would be smoked like fish by the time we finished eating. But incredibly not even a bit of kitchen smoke or anything. We enjoyed the dishes so much we were speechless! I am still thinking about the broth, the crunch on the noodles dish, the unique cumin potstickers.. and so on. If I lived in the area I would become a regular. The quality of food and taste this place is serving out is incredible - so in my book it’s worthy of Bib Gourmand designation!  Thank you, owners, cooks, and every person that contributes to this magical food spot - your food fed our eyes, stomachs, and souls - doesn’t get better than that!

Tiny little restaurant in the west village serving up familiar Chinese cuisine, not the classic NY takeout with neon sign, more regional and homemade stuff here.

We got the Brother Lin’s Beef Noodle Soup and Sister Lin’s Chicken Noodle Soup. Both, in my opinion, were very good. I found the Beef soup to be more flavorful and savory, the broth was had a more punch, not to mention the very tolerable spice level too. The Chicken soup would be perfect on a cold or sick day and felt a bit healthier / simpler.

The prices are a bit higher than those spots in Chinatown serving up similar fare, but, this is obviously catering to the neighborhood and with that, convenience is at a price.

The food is good and I would recommend! There’s about 3 tables inside and also 4 bar seats, so keep that in mind.

food here is amazing!! we got the beef soup & the chili lime dumplings as well as the milk tea & it was all 10/10. customer service was also great, love the atmosphere in here, i had trouble choosing food because it all looked so good!! definitely recommend & will come here again! we left empty plates & with our bellies full

I know West Village rents are crazy, but this is basically the same food as any of the Fujianese noodle/dumpling shops in Chinatown at 3x the price.

The ingredients are a notch or two higher, and everything is made fresh (no batched and lukewarm fried dumplings). And you get a top 40 Spotify playlist too, I guess, and signature "sauces" that are for sale.

I can't fault the business sense to be honest, but $15 for dumplings I guess is something I'm just not ready for.

This is such a cute and cozy place 💙 the kind of place you can go as a party of one, two or three and enjoy good food. The menu is on the wall when you walk in, the sake offerings and food and the server was very friendly and helpful. This is your little romantic restaurant to get close, or go with your bestie to hear good news or take your kids for one on one dinner and listening time. We really enjoyed the ambiance. The food was good, I had the shrimp dumplings, he had the beef noodles. What I loved - the dumplings had a fat, juicy full shrimp inside. What he loved - his dish was just the right level of spicy. We both loved the sake. I want to go back and try the peanut butter noodles and just enjoy the vibe, relaxing, romantic, sweet and lovely place to dine.

This no-frills dumpling spot is tucked into a busy strip on Sutphin Boulevard. The interior is compact and casual. Just grab a seat at one of the few tables tucked in the back, and expect a friendly, laid-back vibe.

My friend once told me they serve “the best dumplings of the world but located in the kind of street whispered of trouble.” That comment alone made me curious enough to visit. I ordered every type of dumpling they had, all cooked by frying and I have to say, I already agree with my friend’s assessment. Crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, they were packed with flavor. According to my friend, the boiled dumplings would be even better, so that’s definitely on my list for next time.

The portions are generous, and the prices are friendly to your wallet. Service is straightforward and warm, adding to the charm. It’s not fancy, but if you’re here for dumplings that punch far above their setting, this place is worth the trip.

I have not had Chinese dumplings since I was 10 years old, so when I went to Jamaica, I decided to stop by this place. The dumplings are already decent by themselves, but once you put that chili oil, it hits different.

Just trying to figure out why there is imitation crab meat in the shrimp dumplings?
It's not listed as "seafood dumplings" or "shrimp &". I get that this place is affordable and to keep their prices low they may need to take certain measures but it should be disclosed.
Overall the dumplings did not have much flavor and a super weird texture because of the imitation crab meat. Also the wrapper is very thick, doughy. It's a convenient dumpling spot however taste wise, it just doesn't hit.

Also paid extra for spicy, garlic . Asked for no cilantro. Check the photos.

name: Sammy’s Smoke House
document: Sammy’s Smoke House. cuisine: Steakhouses. located in Bronx. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
This place was a 5 outta 5!!!
I've never been to any of the Sammy's places on City Island so I'm happy we started with this one.
We came here for my momxs birthday dinner and the food was huge and delicious. They greeted us as soon as we walked in. The service reminded me of me at work, joking with the customers and just making u feel so welcomed.
When I was reading up on the menu i was skeptical about the sizes for the prices but I must say it exceeded my expectations.
I ordered the Pit Master Feast for 2 (for mom and I) and it came with Ribs (we picked Baby Back), Pulled Pork, Brisket, BBQ Chicken and Smoked Sausage, it also came with 3 sides so we did the Collard Greens, Mac n Cheese and corn on the cob.
My sister had the Fried Seafood Combo. Came w/ Jumbo Shrimp, Scallop, Cod Fish, Calamari and a Baby Lobster Tail.
My niece had the Large Snow Crab Legs (2 clusters).
When I tell you I was shocked as everything came out.
Everything was delicious perfectly seasoned and more then we could finish lol.
Only downside is the pulled pork was a little dry for my liking but it was still tasty.
I will definitely be returning here to try out more stuff on the menu.

Exceptional experience at Sammy’s Smokehouse! My friend and I had outstanding customer service from start to finish, and the food was absolutely delicious. The ribs were fall-off-the-bone perfection, the salmon was cooked beautifully, and everything we tried from the rice to the nachos and crispy onion rings was full of flavor. Portions were generous, presentation was on point, and every bite was truly chef’s kiss. We left full, happy, and already talking about our next visit. Definitely going back highly recommend!

My fiancé and I came here to celebrate his birthday and we were not at all disappointed. The food was amazing, everything was bursting with freshness and flavor. The value for the money is acceptable. The service was also incredible. The atmosphere was relaxing and clean. 10/10 recommend and we will definitely be back! The ease of parking is also a huge plus and the location.

One of my cousins suggested this restaurant and let me say I’m so glad he did. Our party of 7 dined here on a rainy sunday in October, with coastal flood warnings still we made it out to city island for our family reunion meeting.
The service is top-notch even the restaurant owners wife (Sammy’s wife) came and visited our table and had a conversation, with us for a few minutes before our dinner arrived. I ordered the boneless rib sandwich with onion rings and it came with coleslaw. We also ordered two appetizers of the barbecue wings. The food is so tender and delicious. My family ordered different food combos. Everyone enjoyed their meals some had mixed views on the side dishes, the collard greens had too much vinegar. We asked for another batch and they accommodated us with no extra charge. Other than that, we enjoyed our meals and our waiter even offered us the pumpkin centerpiece.
I highly recommend this restaurant.
It’s been a long time since I was able to go out and have such a great experience at a restaurant with my family. If you’re looking to go out to eat a nice lunch or dinner with a very accommodating staff, I highly suggest Sammy’s Smoke House.

One of the best BBQ spots in NYC.  Not only can you enjoy amazing BBQ, but you can also savor Sammy’s famous classic seafood.  This time I only grabbed the BBQ and it was so delicious.  We started with their complimentary bread basket.  I  recommend you try the garlic bread and biscuits.  I ordered the 3-meat BBQ platter.  I chose Baby Back Ribs, Beiscket, and Pulled  Pork. The brisket was so tender and juicy that it melted in your mouth.  The Ribs were equally as tender, and the pork was wonderful.  We had so much food and had to take some home but I just loved it.

document: Hapag Filipino Cuisine. cuisine: Filipino. located in Bronx. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: As one of the only Filipino restaurants I’ve eaten at, Hapag was phenomenal! The authenticity shines through in both the menu offerings & the ambiance. The veggie pork stew I ordered was delicious, full of various Filipino ingredients & seasonings. The calamansi juice is also worth a try. Yum!

I went here twice.

The first time I went, I had kare kare, palabok, and halo halo. I had dinuguan and taho when I came back.

The food is so incredibly comforting and it tastes so unbelievably good! The flavors are very well balanced. The first time I came, I was so eager to eat that I forgot to take photos of the kare kare! 😅 It almost happened again during my second visit had I not consciously stopped myself to take a photo.

Another thing I especially like about this place is the service. The staff always welcome you with a smile on their face and are willing to give suggestions if you're lost or undecided.

The prices are reasonable and you will not leave hungry. I'm definitely coming here more often.

Food is served quickly & the staff are very friendly. I appreciated the fact that they serve tofu as an alternative for those who don't eat meat (ME). The Ukoy became an instant favorite of ours! My husband enjoyed the menudo. It's very small space & fills up quickly over the weekend. We enjoyed our experience & will definitely be back.

What a treat Hapag! The aroma from arriving food made the mouth water straight away, and the service top notch. Great ambiance, great service, great food. Clean and unpretentious place serving delicious food. During my most recent visit, I was able to order the kare-kare oxtail stew which I was told is their most popular dish.

name: Marea
document: Marea. cuisine: Italian Seafood Wine Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Second time visiting Marea during my New York trip and it was even better than the first!

The service was excellent — attentive, professional, and warm from start to finish.

The pasta here is 100/100! Highly recommend the Pappardelle Granchio Reale — the king crab was sweet and generous, perfectly balanced with garlic butter.

For appetizers, the Polipo (grilled octopus) and Scampi on “Scampi” were both phenomenal. Every dish was fresh, beautifully presented, and packed with flavor.

A true NYC fine-dining highlight.

Must recommend to all my friends traveling to New York — you can’t miss it!

Excellent meal, excellent service! My husband and I were celebrating our anniversary and a couple of other milestones and the entire staff was welcoming and warm. All of our dishes were delicious and we can’t wait to go back on our next trip. Our server Robert was delightful and friendly. He had excellent wine pairing suggestions! Everything on the menu is delectable, you cannot go wrong. Definitely make room for dessert!

We came on Christmas Eve and it was extremely crowded. The restaurant previously held a Michelin star, and after this visit, I can see why it might have lost it. Perhaps it was due to the holiday rush, but the service that night was fairly mediocre.

We ordered the white truffle pasta, $110 for 4g. While the presentation was fine, it definitely did not feel Michelin-level. The risotto was more enjoyable than the tagliatelle and had a much richer flavor.

For the starter, the Cannolicchio was quite creative, and the Astice was excellent!! The lobster was very bouncy, fresh, and sweet, and the burrata was rich and milky. Unfortunately, the Ricci was a big disappointment; the uni had a strong fishy taste and the quality was poor.

For the primi, we tried the Capellini, which I was really excited about but ended up disappointed. It was overly acidic, and the butter was not well incorporated. We also ordered half portions of the Pappardelle Granchio Reale and Fusilli, and surprisingly, these simpler pasta dishes were more enjoyable than the so-called signature ones.

For the main course, we chose the Anatra. It was already portioned when served, and the duck skin was beautifully crispy, one of the best dishes of the night.

We ordered two desserts and both were very good; I especially liked the tiramisu.

Overall, the portions here are quite generous. Some shortcomings help explain the lost star, but I would still recommend coming when it’s less crowded.

We chose here to celebrate Chinese New Year and had a really lovely experience. I’m allergic to olive oil, and to be honest, many restaurants either can’t accommodate that or simply say no, which makes dining out pretty stressful.

The staff at Marea were incredibly understanding and accommodating. They were able to adjust the dishes so I could enjoy the meal without olive oil, and everything was still absolutely delicious. It felt great to be able to relax and actually enjoy our celebration without worrying about my allergy.

Great food, thoughtful service, and a memorable way to celebrate the New Year. Really glad we picked this spot！

We had an extremely disappointing experience here as a group of four. Our bill was almost $900 including bottles of wine, so this was not a casual or low-spend visit.

Despite that, we were made to feel unwelcome towards the end of the evening. Staff began clearing our table without asking or receiving permission, while we were still seated. Shortly after, we were explicitly asked to leave because we had “overstayed,” even though no time limit had been communicated in advance. Also, they took forever to take our orders.

If there is a strict seating policy, it should be made clear upfront — not enforced abruptly and rudely after guests have spent a significant amount of money. The way this was handled felt disrespectful. Being the only four brown people at the restaurant it totally felt discriminatory.

For a restaurant positioning itself at this price point, the service and hospitality fell far below expectations. We won’t be returning and would not recommend this place to others looking for a welcoming dining experience. We did bring this up to the management and they seemed more interested in getting the credit card charged right away and did not offer any significant apologies. Our server ( Robert) was actually nice but his service could not make up for how the evening turned out overall.

Kings of Kobe is still a solid spot, but things have changed. I used to come mainly for their burgers, which were incredible, but the quality has dropped noticeably over time. They’re still good, just not at the standout level they once were.

That said, the new all-you-can-eat Wagyu steak option is a nice addition. It’s actually quite decent — flavorful, tender, and definitely good value if you’re hungry. The sides and overall atmosphere remain enjoyable, and the service is generally friendly and efficient.

Overall, Kings of Kobe is still worth visiting, especially for the Wagyu experience, but I do hope they bring the burger quality back to what it used to be.

We had the most wonderful Valentine’s dinner tonight at Kings of Kobe!

My husband ordered the 10oz ribeye with garlic mashed potatoes, and it was cooked perfectly — tender, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. I had the salmon with asparagus and coconut rice, and it was just as amazing. The salmon was perfectly cooked and paired so well with the coconut rice.

The drinks were also a 10/10 — perfectly made and the perfect touch to our special night.

Everything from the food to the atmosphere made our Valentine’s dinner date as busy parents so special. We’ll definitely be back!

I had one of the most unforgettable dining experiences at this Wagyu Japanese restaurant. From start to finish, everything was executed with perfection.

The pork belly was melt-in-your-mouth tender, perfectly balanced between richness and flavor, while the steak was nothing short of spectacular—juicy, buttery, and bursting with umami in every bite. It was, without question, among the very best steaks I’ve ever had.

The real surprise, though, was the truffle fries. Crispy on the outside, fluffy inside, and infused with truffle aroma, they were simply addictive—the best I have ever tried anywhere.

On top of the outstanding food, the presentation and service were equally impressive. Each dish felt thoughtfully prepared, and the staff made sure the whole evening felt special.

If you’re looking for a place where every bite is an experience, this restaurant delivers in every way. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates authentic Japanese Wagyu and unforgettable flavors.

I finally got to come here after wanting to come here for ages. We had booked a reservation a few days in advance for the all you can eat waygu but given that there seemed to be a decent amount of available tables when we came in, I imagine that we could've got a table without a reservation. The waygu itself was cooked good and around the cook that we wanted (medium rare). The waygu is American waygu, not as famous as Japanese waygu and to my basic and uncultured taste buds, I found the waygu to taste similar to normal steak. For the fries, we opted for all 3 versions; the regular fries, Parmesan truffle fries and onion rings. All three of these were tasty so no complaints in that regard. The two sauces that they gave, butter sauce and chimmichuri, were both good, especially the chimmichuri. My buddies and I came here with the intentions of going through at least 8 rounds of steak but after 5 rounds, we just couldn't eat anymore. To the restaurant's credit, they were attentive with the rounds. After we got the first round of steak, it was about 5 minutes later when we were asked if we were ready for the next round. After receiving the second round, it would be about another 5 or so minutes before you were asked about the next round. The service was great, we were constantly getting checked up on and consistently had our water refilled which I loved. Our server was very friendly, although I don't know his name. Overall, it was a great experience and honestly not a bad deal for the money, especially in Manhattan. Don't come here expecting Gallaghers level of food and you'll be more than satisfied. The dress code itself seemed to be casual, sneakers and jeans and such. A lady near me had a winter hat on and I myself had a ball cap on the entire time I was there. I myself appreciate the casual dress code, since normal people don't like wearing dress shoes/heels when there's snow and ice on the pavement.

name: Dubu Haus
document: Dubu Haus. cuisine: Korean Hot Pot. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Came in at a random Saturday afternoon because I’ve seen this place online but I didn’t have very high expectations.
Started us off with a house made soy milk— unexpectedly creamy and slightly sweet unlike store bought ones that are more watery

We ordered short rib and bossam that came with different vegetable bonchons. Both of the dishes were pretty good.

The short ribs were nice and tender fell off the bone easily while the thick sauce coated the meat beautifully.

Bossam was very good as well, the tofu was a crumbly texture that kind of reminded me of feta cheese.

I know koreans like their rice on the stickier side but I think the rice was a little too sticky and moist?
Ended the meal with a yummy injeolmi soft serve.
Overall, flavors were good and comforting, nothing too mind-blowing. I’d come back again but their service can definitely improve.

Amazing comforting Korean cuisine. Great quick service and delicious food. The tofu is the main attraction as you can see them making it in the kitchen through the dining area. Ask for a soy milk sample if you want to try very fresh raw soy bean flavor! Food was packed with flavor and very satisfying textures.

I don’t normally leave reviews but my visit did not meet any of my expectations, the experience overall felt underwhelming.
We arrived around noon and were looking to get a table for three but were told that the next available seating would be in two hours. We had no issue with that seeing as we didn’t have a reservation prior but was disappointed when we were told that my birthday cake (“outside food”) wouldn’t be allowed inside. I don’t think I’ve ever been to a place that didn’t allow this, especially if parties wanted to come and celebrate any type of milestone. In my head I thought, maybe they have their own desserts that we could order instead but upon seeing the menu that wasn’t the case either.
As for the food, it wasn’t anything stellar. We ordered the soondubu, the kongbiji, and the spicy braised dubu. Upon arriving to our table, the braised tofu left us a little disappointed as we had hoped it would look as good as it did in the picture. Flavor-wise it was alright, nothing mind blowing. The best thing we tasted ended up being the complimentary tofu soft serve they give at the end of the meal.
As for service, I could tell they were doing their best, no remarks there. The interior and atmosphere was really nice and dim, it just didn’t help since we were already not enjoying ourselves. Can’t say that we would come back again.

Honestly, the food itself wasn’t bad. However, despite not being a very old restaurant, there were several issues that really affected the experience. The table had visible stains, some dish was chipped, and there was red sauce residue left on the side-dish bowls.

During the entire meal, no staff member checked on us even once. We had to pour our own water and take and set up our own utensils, so I don’t understand why 20% tip is expected.

In addition, the noodles contained vegetable ends that clearly should have been trimmed and discarded. Overall, for the price, there are many aspects that need improvement.

This is a tofu specialty restaurant, yet the tofu itself was dry and not very good. The tofu lab area was especially concerning—after making tofu, the tools were left out without being properly cleaned, which gave a very unhygienic impression. The rice was somewhat dry and lacked moisture. The photos clearly show what I’m talking about.

We dined at this Korean restaurant specializing in tofu on Saturday evening and were immediately impressed by its modern, upscale ambiance- especially considering how reasonable the prices were. We were welcomed with complimentary soy milk, which was rich and flavorful.
We ordered the kalbi beef soondubu, perilla oil buckwheat noodles, and tteokgalbi, and each dish was truly enjoyable. The banchan was fresh and delicious, and the complimentary soft serve at the end of the meal was the perfect finishing touch. Additionally, our server was attentive and provided excellent service throughout our meal. I would gladly return and highly recommend this spot.

document: Aqua Boil. cuisine: Seafood Cajun/Creole Comfort Food. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We shared the Mad Ocean Combo and chose shrimp, snow crab legs, crawfish, mussels, and a whole lobster with the Cajun Mix sauce at medium spice—everything came out dumped straight on the table with corn and potatoes underneath, classic style. Portions were generous (we couldn’t finish), the seafood was fresh, and the sauce was flavorful without being overly salty. The snow crab was easy to peel, the lobster claw meat was pretty full, and the corn soaked up the sauce nicely. We also ordered the Aqua Roll, which was more filling than expected with a good amount of shrimp and lobster, plus two cocktails—Beach Bum was more fruit-forward than the Piña Colada.

The food was beyond expectation, we had the lobster and the crab by the pound with lemon garlic and cajun spice sauces respectively. Great portions, the sauces were amazing. You might need to dip the meat well into the meat to get all flavors as initially they just have the seafood boiled and kept on top of the sauce. I would go there again whenever I am in NY next.

Hands down the most satisfying seafood boil I’ve had in NYC! 🦀🔥 The Cajun mix was insanely flavorful, perfectly coating the fresh lobster, snow crab legs, shrimp, crawfish, and clams — every bite was messy in the best way. The fun, hands-on experience and coastal vibe at Aqua Boil make it a must-visit in Hell’s Kitchen!

Came here with my mom during restaurant week and had such an amazing experience!! The food was delicious and service was exceptional! Our server Zom was so sweet and took the time to explain the menu to us. I will definitely be coming back here!

document: Rosticceria Evelina. cuisine: Italian Pizza Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We had such a wonderful experience dining here! From the moment we walked in, everyone made us feel genuinely welcomed and taken care of.

Daniel was attentive and professional, making sure everything was perfect throughout our meal. Andres brought such a warm, positive energy that truly elevated our experience. Nicole was incredibly kind and thoughtful — you can tell she truly cares about the guests.

It’s rare to find a team where everyone works together so seamlessly and treats you like more than just another table. The service was just as impressive as the food. They all deserve recognition for going above and beyond.

We’ll absolutely be back — thank you for such a great night!

Rosticceria Evelina — cozy Italian comfort done right

On a freezing night, Rosticceria Evelina felt like a warm hug. Intimate, softly lit, and effortlessly romantic—the kind of place where you slow down and let the food do the talking.

We started strong with the Polipetti in Purgatorio—tender petit octopus swimming in a spicy, deeply savory tomato sauce al purgatorio, finished with fresh parsley and fett’unta for that rich olive-oil finish. Bold, comforting, and easily my favorite bite of the night.

The Foraged Mushrooms were earthy and elegant, tossed with thyme and paired with a punchy black garlic aioli, then balanced by salty aged ricotta. Every forkful had layers—umami, creaminess, and herbaceous depth.

The Sourdough Onion Focaccia came out warm and pillowy, topped with whipped ricotta, roasted tomatoes, and olives. Rustic, comforting, and dangerously easy to keep reaching for.

For mains, the Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe was textbook—perfectly al dente pasta, glossy pecorino sauce, and just the right hit of cracked black pepper. Simple, balanced, and executed beautifully.
The Burrata Ravioli was rich without being heavy, creamy on the inside with a delicate pasta bite that let the filling shine.
The fish dish (fresh, expertly cooked) brought brightness and balance to the table—clean flavors, beautifully seasoned, and clearly high-quality seafood.

We ended with an affogato, because obviously. Hot espresso melting into cold, creamy gelato—simple, indulgent, and the perfect finale.

Service was warm, attentive, and unpretentious—knowledgeable without hovering, making the entire experience feel relaxed and genuinely welcoming. Everything tasted fresh, thoughtfully seasoned, and intentionally composed, with flavors that complemented rather than competed.

A cozy Italian gem that knows exactly what it’s doing—comforting, soulful, and quietly impressive. ✨🍝

Great dinner. We had the onion focaccia and meatballs to start. We then had the broccoli rabe pizza, lasagna, funghi pizza and the burrata ravioli. Everyone loved their dishes. The pizzas were amazing and the lasagna was light. The tiramisu was amazing for dessert. Highly recommend!

Went last night for St. Valentine’s day, I must confess I ended up here by mistake, my reservation was in another restaurant across the street, but for some unknown reason I came here and it was amazing, my only regret was not being here before… Food was beyond amazing, the lasagna is a MUST! I have never had something like that before, would love to go back again.

I would think that on a busy day like this, service/food might not be the best, but they proved me wrong, staff was very nice,they didn’t take forever with our food, music was nice too.

Can’t wait to go and try the brunch one of these days…

PS: I tried the cucumber drink, which is alcohol free and it was also very good, the olive oil cake since the tiramisu had finished,it wasn’t bad but I bet they have better options for desserts.

We were just walking around the neighborhood when we stumbled upon this cute little restaurant with great reviews, so we decided to stop by. At first, I wasn’t sure what to order but on the way to the restroom, I passed by the open kitchen and spotted someone being served the Eggs Benedict and a pizza. We ended up trying the eggs Benedict and the lasagna, and both were absolutely delicious highly recommend! The cozy covered outdoor seating area added such a nice touch to the whole experience, we loved the vibe and felt so relaxed just sitting there.

We’re really glad we decided to check this place out. The food was amazing, the atmosphere was warm and inviting, and we’d love to come back to try more dishes next time.

name: Salt + Charcoal
document: Salt + Charcoal. cuisine: Japanese Steakhouses Wine Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
My recent visit to Salt + Charcoal was absolutely incredible for my birthday experience, from the moment we walked in, the ambiance was perfect cozy, intimate, and ideal for a special occasion.

The food, a unique fusion of a Japanese steakhouse and grill, was sensational. We started with the tuna tartare which was incredibly fresh and beautifully prepared by our waiter. The diced avocado and wasabi provided the perfect amount of creaminess and kick, and rolling it ourselves in the crispy nori sheets added a fun, interactive touch to the Japanese style preparation. The oysters were an absolute amazing. They arrived sizzling, bathed in a rich, flavorful soy butter garlic sauce with a pop of fresh cilantro and lime zest. The balance of the smoky grill and the savory butter was perfect, and the texture was plump and crunchy.

For the star of the show was the NY strip steak. The New York Strip, cooked medium-rare, and it was perfect. The unique charcoal grilling method gave it an incredible, smoky char on the outside, while the inside remained juicy, tender, and robustly flavored with a satisfying bite.

Beyond the exquisite cuisine, what truly made the night memorable was the outstanding service. My waiter, Patrick was attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely friendly throughout the entire meal even when it came down to making the payment hint hint Whitney Houston debit card 🙂. Patrick explained each dish with enthusiasm, offered brilliant recommendations, and ensured our glasses were never empty, timing each course perfectly so our never felt rushed.

Salt + Charcoal offers a truly refined yet welcoming experience. It's on the pricier side, but for the quality of food and the impeccable service, it's well worth the splurge for a memorable evening. I can't recommend it enough and will definitely be back!

Food was Amazing. For the Appetizer we had the Crunchy Oyster which was tasty. We followed that up with the 30 day Dry aged porterhouse steak for 2 with a sides of S+C baked potatoes. For drinks we had the Pineapple Express. Food and drinks was a 5 outta 5! Will recommend

This completely exceeded my expectations. The Wagyu was rich but balanced, cooked beautifully, and served in a way that let the quality speak for itself. You can tell a lot of intention went into every detail. I’d happily come back just for this.

document: Angel Indian Restaurant. cuisine: Indian Halal. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Food is heavily authentic, tasty, spices are really appropriate - fit for desi and Americans.

We asked for kid friendly masala food and they really made it to cater.

Angel Indian Restaurant in Jackson Heights absolutely lives up to the hype—and the Michelin-star chef recommendation by Vikas Khanna feels well deserved. From the moment the food hit the table, it was clear this is a place that takes traditional Indian flavors seriously while executing them with precision and heart.

Amritsari Lassi
The meal started on a high note with the Amritsari lassi—thick, creamy, and perfectly balanced. Not overly sweet, not too tangy, just deeply refreshing and indulgent. It felt authentic, like something you’d get in Punjab, and was the perfect companion to the bold flavors that followed.

Samosa Chaat
The samosa chaat was a flavor bomb. Crispy samosas broken down and layered with chickpeas, yogurt, chutneys, and spices—sweet, tangy, spicy, and crunchy all at once. Each bite had contrast and depth, and it never felt soggy or heavy. Street food comfort elevated to restaurant-level execution.

Chicken Tandoori Starter
The chicken tandoori was beautifully cooked—juicy on the inside with a smoky, charred exterior. The marinade penetrated deeply, giving the chicken layers of flavor rather than just surface spice. The fresh herbs and chutney on the side added brightness and balance.

Goat Dum Biryani
The star of the meal. The goat dum biryani was rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. Long-grain rice infused with whole spices, tender goat that fell apart effortlessly, and that unmistakable dum-cooked aroma when you dig in. This is slow-cooked comfort food done right—robust, soulful, and memorable.

Amazing food

One of the best Indian restaurants in NYC. Each dish we had topped the previous ones. We had a great samosa chaat and dahi batata puri. The dahi in the dahi batata puri was perfectly thick too. The lotus kofta and kadhai paneer then came out alongside the amritsari kulcha. Each item was incredibly flavorful. The piece de resistance was the dum biryani. The vegetables were perfectly cooked and felt tender.

The service was amazing too! I strongly recommend getting a reservation here as seating is a bit limited.

I was so impressed by this restaurant! The food is delicious and the service is exceptional. There were tons of vegetarian and vegan options which is exactly what I was looking for. I am definitely coming back to this super cute place. I totally recommend!

I had an amazing experience at Angel with my family. The paneer was incredible and imo the best paneer in nyc. The service was also great and they were really accommodating. Our server Prathamesh was super kind and knowledgeable. We also had the amazing experience of meeting the chef and owner himself, Amritpal Singh, who happened to sit down next to us and eat with his family! We had a lovely conversation with him about his experiences and passion for cooking.

It was extra special because we were celebrating my dad’s birthday and they really made sure we had the best experience possible and also sang happy birthday and gave us some complimentary kheer.

Highly recommend the fresh lime soda, pani puri, samosa chaat, kadai paneer, and paneer kulcha! Will definitely be back soon.

Food, calamari was good, the baked clams tasted a little fishy. We ordered the chicken and shrimp scampi and I'm so happy we ordered 1 dish to share. The dish lacked flavor, felt soupy and the pasta was definitely not al dente. This pasta was short of being in a soup, just completely underwhelming and soft.They gave us 3 pieces of shrimp and more chicken than anything. I make better pasta than this at home. After eating the food, definitely felt a bit nauseated.

I'd pass on this location for a meal. Between the underwhelming food and lackluster serve, it left a bad taste in my mouth.

Before addressing the food, I want to acknowledge that the front-of-house staff is doing a great job—they were helpful, attentive, and professional throughout our visit.

Unfortunately, the dining experience itself was deeply disappointing. Cafe Baci is a forgettable yet unforgettable experience—forgettable in flavor, unforgettable in how low-quality and tasteless the food was. As someone who is Italian, I had far higher expectations. Calling this “Italian cuisine” is honestly a stretch.

I lowered my usual dining standards to try something local, and that decision was a mistake. Every dish was bland and borderline inedible. My entire party lost their appetite—we left three full entrées untouched. To their credit, the manager removed them from the bill, which we appreciated.

If you enjoy low-quality food, excessively large portions, and overpriced plates, this may be the place for you.

Ambience: Confusing at best. At one point, I genuinely felt like I was in Texas. Nothing about the space reflects Italian culture or cuisine—it’s heavily Americanized. If you own cowboy boots, you might feel more at home than someone looking for an Italian café experience.

Overall: I will not be returning. This was a disappointing experience across the board, and there is significant room for improvement

Be warned, the wait can be long. Why? Because they don’t take reservations BUT if you time it right, you can be seated right away like we did when we went.

document: Yop City Resturant. cuisine: African. located in Bronx. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Had to try this spot for lunch after seeing numerous reviews on Instagram. We arrived around 2pm mid-week, so it was not during the height of the lunch crowd. Luckily we found street parking right near the place, but I imagine during busy times, finding parking could be difficult.
The place was empty, so we were seated immediately. The server came over quickly with menus, but offered little information or suggestions. I ordered based on what I had seen in online reviews. We had hoped for some fresh juices to go with our meal, but we're told they were all sold out.
We ordered the fried fish, chicken, and a side of plantains. The food was fresh and made to order.  The chicken came out on a sizzling platter, and the smell immediately filled the air. The sides could have been hotter, but perhaps they are just served warm because many people choose to eat with their hands.
They had a bathroom with a small sink outside of it so that patrons could wash hands prior to eating.
The restaurant was clean, the decor was simple with some african themed art on the walls. The staff were friendly but could have been more engaging, especially since we were novice to their cuisine.
The fish and chicken were very good. The sides were OK.
Portions were large, and we had plenty of leftovers to take home.
If you are in the area, and you can find parking, check this place out.

Another great food adventure with my sister friends. I'm so glad we decided to try this place as our 1st African restaurant. I have been here 3x with family. I haven't had a bad dish here. There's so much food you will get a doggie bag. Bring your plastic containers to avoid a charge. I'm a fish lover & you will slap your mama over the fried croaker. The lamb is tender and can't say enough of their country chicken. Very good sorrel & ginger juice. We made an Africian AlDonald Palmer juice by mixing them. Definitely a place I will go to monthly. Large good food and Ivory Coast food seasoned to perfection. Please check them out, you will not be disappointed 😋😋😋

I’ve got to give a shout out to the content creator who did a blog about this restaurant. Got to also give a shout out to the waitress that served us Fanta. Now to the food; OMG it was amazing! My friend got the Big Sosso and I got the Dibi Mouton and we enjoyed the flavors was on point. For the first time trying Attieke it was amazing.
The only downside was the wait time to get our food it was however worth the wait. We will definitely be going back to this restaurant and we will be bringing friends to enjoy the experience. Yop City 10/10!

I went to Yopcity on a late night cause they dont close until 2 am, had the fried Crocker and rice, the Crocker was seasoned to perfection, and the rice was delicious.  Will definitely be going back, tho i didnt stay the atmosphere looked great i would definitely sit and eat, staff were very welcoming.

I had a really great experience at this restaurant. The customer service stood out right away. I was seated promptly without having to wait, and the waitress was very kind, attentive, and checked on us often to make sure everything was okay. I’m usually not a fan of tilapia, but theirs was so good well seasoned, fresh, and paired perfectly with the pepper sauce. I also tried attieke for the first time and, although I was hesitant, it surprised me with how delicious it was, especially when I sprinkled a little Maggi cube over it. The plantains were cooked just the way I like them, slightly overripe and sweet. I wanted to try the sorrel juice, but since they were out, I went with the ginger juice instead, which was refreshing and full of flavor. The atmosphere was lively with great music, and the prices were very reasonable for the quality of the food. Overall, the food, service, and vibe were excellent, and I’ll definitely be returning to try the lamb and the sorrel juice next time.

Lastly to make matters worse gratuity was included in the bill—which baffled me. I’ll never be back to this establishment. Please do not believe their hyped up instagram page.

This was the first time in a long time eating out where I felt that the entire meal  and experience was truly worth the price.

How this place has anything less than a perfect 5 stars is beyond me. The food-exquisite, the service-perfect, the atmosphere - inviting. Our waitress, Katrina went above and beyond to make sure our "out of towners" table felt welcome beyond measure. We ordered a wide selection of food and EVERY SINGLE THING WE TRIED WAS DIVINE! The truffle fries were a 100/10!! If you are in the area, please do yourself a favor and stop in and ask for Katrina. I'm sure the rest of the servers are just as kind and hospitable but we hit a home run with Katrina.

Absolutely fabulous - once again. The Black Whale is over an hour drive from our home, but well worth it. This time we tried the sashimi. The yellowtail was like butter. For entrees we had the Sesame-Crusted Seared Tuna with Jicama Slaw and Black Forbidden Rice (don’t miss this one!) and the Blackened Swordfish with Crispy Polenta and Roasted Broccolini. Both very well created, cooked and presented with very generous portions. Especially impressed with the thick cut of swordfish. The tuna entrée was especially good with the soy sauce and wasabi from our sashimi appetizer. One of the best meals out we’ve had in quite a while - and service was excellent thanks to our server. Thank you, Paul!
Appetizers were amazing, main course was super and the coffee was outstanding. Wished we'd saved room for dessert.

document: Barolo East. cuisine: Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: We came here for dinner after a Rockettes show. It is just off the beaten path of the holiday tourist crowds, but what sets Barolo East apart is the phenomenal staff and food!!! I will dream about this meal!

Authentic Italian in an understated, elegant, old-world spot. Delicious food - - the Gorgonzola gnocchi sauce was heavenly smooth and decadent. The tiramisu was consumed in 3 solid minutes. I went by myself and did not feel rushed, the pacing was very good and all the staff and management were very attentive and courteous. Timeless and classic place.

Everything about this restaurant is perfect.   The atmosphere is warm and inviting and the table placement allows for quiet conversation which is difficult to find these days.. The portions are very generous.     The pasta selection is huge and we settled on the special cavatelli made in house with a wonderful beef ragu sauce followed by the perfect Branzino opting for a lemon preparation which kept the fish moist and flakey.    We ended the night sharing a delicious profiterole.   The meal was paced perfectly and inspite of being crowded that night we were never rushed or hurried.    One of the best Italian spots in the city and we are going to be regulars for sure.

name: Carbone
document: Carbone. cuisine: Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text: Carbone brought Italian-American dining back to the center of New York and did it with style that nobody else has been able to touch. The spicy rigatoni vodka is the dish that launched a thousand imitations and none of them come close. The veal parmesan is a two-person commitment and worth every bite. Walking into the dining room feels like stepping into a 1950s supper club dark leather tuxedoed waiters Frank Sinatra energy without the costume. Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi understood something that most chefs miss entirely you do not need to reinvent Italian food you need to perfect it. Every dish on this menu is a love letter to the red sauce joints that built this city and every bite proves they studied the originals until they could do it better. The Caesar salad is prepared tableside and it is theater and substance in equal measure. The wine list is Italian-heavy with deep cuts from regions most people have never heard of. Getting a reservation requires either patience or connections and the fact that the waiting list is months long tells you everything. I have eaten here multiple times and I have never once been disappointed. New York is full of Italian restaurants claiming to be the best. Carbone does not claim anything. It just proves it every single night. Go hungry and bring someone you want to impress.

EPIC. INCREDIBLE. BEST MEAL IN NYC! I’ve been wanting to come here for years! Bucket list experience ACHIEVED! I will be trying to find spicy vodka rigatoni that good for the rest of my life. Lemon cheesecake was the best I’ve ever had as well. Start to finish, the meal was indulgent and the service was unparalleled!

Carbone absolutely lives up to the hype. The spicy rigatoni is perfect—rich, decadent sauce with just the right kick. The chicken Massimo was surprisingly good: sweet, beautifully charred on the outside, tender on the inside, and finished with a deliciously creamy sauce. It came with shallots which were cooked perfectly!

The baked clams were excellent (loved that you can substitute bacon for breadcrumbs), and the Caesar salad was a generous portion made tableside with anchovies—classic and delicious. The bread was good with a solid assortment and one that was cheesy and a bit oily. There was no fresh mozzarella available that day, but they made up for it with olive oil and pickled cauliflower.

Some folks say the place is cramped, but we were seated at a round table so we thought it was more than enough space for us to enjoy a nice meal.

Finished with a delicious raspberry sorbet, which was solid. Overall, a flawless meal and a true 10/10 experience. Would absolutely return.

We were there for an early lunch. Couldn’t believe that we had a table. It was so hard to get a reservation. We were greeted by really nice professional staffs. The bread with salami and fresh mozzarella served at the beginning of our meal was yummy! We ordered a Caesar salad that was prepared on a cart for our table specifically. The pasta vodka sauce was amazing not so much about the meatballs ( a little bit undercooked for our tasting and a bit fatty) I’ve had better but the marinara sauce was good. And then deserts oh boy! The display was mesmerizing and it tasted even better. The whole experience was Definitely worth the wait and the vibe!

I had high hopes and expectations going into my meal at Carbone. It’s highly regarded as one of, if not the toughest reservation to get in the city.

Once you get inside, you see why. The place is TINY with maybe 15 tables all nestled inside the front area and larger back. The service and staff are some of the best in NYC, able to take your order, course it out and make suggestions where necessary. Thankfully I went with a friend who is a regular and knew exactly what to order.

We ended up feasting like kings with a full flight of courses, starting off with the spectacular complimentary meats, breads and cheeses, the burrata, caesar salad (prepared table-side), beef carpaccio, spicy rigatoni (a MUST), meatballs (which were a delicious blend of beef and I believe bison), veal parmesan and brocollini. Got the carrot cake to try it even though I was well at my limit and it was worth it for the sugar rush to come back to life over an espresso.

Washed it all down with a Manhattan and an awesome red wine my friend recommended. The servers made sure our table was always taken care of and water was filled. A+++ service and will definitely be back the next time one of my friends with pull lets me tag along. Worth every penny!

Thank you for sharing your shop with me today.

Breeze has always been one of my favorite bakeries; from their paninis, to the fresh fruit cream cake to their ginger tea.
When I first started looking for wedding cakes I mostly focused on specialized wedding cake bakeries. However, I unfortunately didn’t realize how far in advanced they get booked. But then I realized all I really wanted was a fresh fruit cream cake and it really didn’t need to stress me out. Which led us to working with Peter, who was so helpful and very clear in communicating to us all the options and pricing of the cake. We got to try a couple different cakes during our tasting and he had given a lot of wonderful suggestions and we ended up deciding on a fresh yogurt cream and strawberry sponge cake with diced fresh strawberries inbtwn the layers. For a guest count of approx 135, we got a two tier cake along with a sheet cake. Pricing was reasonable and fair.
Peter and the team were very dedicated to making sure our wedding cake was our “dream cake”, down to asking for a color pallet to make sure they created the right blues! The design was a moshposh of inspos, even I didn’t have a clear vision. We didn’t have a dream cake per se but they took what we gave them and made it feel like a dream come true.
Not only did we LOVE the cake but we still have family and friends raving about it too. It had honorable mentions in our guest book and we had some guest hanging out by the cake table for seconds (or fourths but who’s really counting).

I didn’t have a dream cake but I am dreaming about this cake every now and then. I have not had a cake as good as my wedding cake since. I can’t wait for our 1 year anniversary to come around so we can do a personal order of our wedding cake. Until then though, I look forward to trying that coconut pandan cake I spied for my upcoming birthday.

If you’re looking for a stress free customized cake experience, this would be the spot, they have so many flavor options to work with and the quality is great it would be hard to go wrong. And even if it isn’t for a big event, the cakes they typically sell are great too. I get all my work event cakes from Breeze and they’re always a crowd pleasure.

Highly recommend their basil chicken pesto panini, yogurt soft serve and a new favorite is the pandan macaron.

Much thanks to Peter and his team for doing such an amazing job!

name: Brooklyn's Best Eats
document: Brooklyn's Best Eats. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Sandwiches Salad. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Nicely located in the closed loop in Flatbush area, this corner deli serves up a variety of hot/cold sandwiches.

Go checkout the creative sandwiches with plenty of options like the Steph Curry, omelettes and breakfast burritos. I got the healthy breakfast burritos (egg whites, Turkey bacon, Swiss and home fries w/ ketchup). It was good and definitely some extra napkins as you devour it.

Will go back to try a different sandwich for sure. Make sure to check prices, they may have some incentives if using cash and watch out for addictives to pricing.

Definitely worth a check out if you’re in the area and just want a lot of options to choose from.

Just to preface this deli has always been overly expensive. Today I purchased a chicken ceasar wrap and it said $10.95 on their menu (which is already really expensive) the cashier told me 11.92?? Then I paid a total of 12.40. Whatever tax they gave us ridiculous. And on top of all that my wrap was the size of my palm. It wasn’t even worth it. Same thing with the Philly cheese steak and it wasn’t always like that. My entire 13.00 Philly cheesesteak was literally the size of a sushi roll. And the music was obnoxiously loud. $25 dollars spent at that place today and I’m still hungry and now I’m broke.

This place is really convenient to go to during breaks after class. The space is small so it gets preety overwhelming waiting for your food. There a bit on the pricier side but their portions are good. All I get is the chicken chipotle.

The food is always fresh, the staff are super friendly, and it’s just steps away from Brooklyn College, perfect for a quick bite between classes. Their sandwiches and wraps are packed with flavor, and the prices are great for the quality. It’s become my go to spot whenever I’m around campus. Highly recommend to anyone nearby!

I am not sure what other people are talking about, but this is one of the best places to eat. Coffee is delicious, food is top notch, and the workers are friendly. The chicken chipotle is my good to here.

name: Vera's Soulfood
document: Vera's Soulfood. cuisine: Soul Food Desserts Seafood. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Vera's is a much needed fresh food spot on Sutter ave in Brownsville/E. NY. I arrived at opening and most of the options were not ready. I did get the $6  platter with chili barbecue chicken mac and cheese and a drink. The food was tasty and I must come back around noon.

So this year Thanksgiving I went out to eat and I am so grateful I went to this restaurant!! In addition to the portions being generous the flavor reminded me of my deceased grandmother greens❤️ the location was farther than the one I normally go to but it was well worth it! Get the peach cobbler for dessert! The manager also gave me another side of the peach cobbler too!!! Everything from the service to a peaceful Thanksgiving was all due to Vera’s Restaurant!

Guys, you know I don't play when it comes to my taste buds—so let me give you the real on this Southern spot called Vera’s. When I say I almost passed out from how good the food was? I mean that! Picture this: I was ready to strip down just to enjoy the meal in peace—nothing was getting in my way.

I started with the beef ribs, mac & cheese, and mixed veggies—and baby, that first bite of rib melted in my mouth. The mac? A solid 20 out of 10, and the veggies were seasoned just right. I was calling myself Big Back by the end because everything I tasted was fire: meatloaf, marshmallow candied yams (yes, marshmallow!), turkey wings falling off the bone, fried chicken, potato salad, and don’t even get me started on that homemade strawberry and regular lemonade—it had me thinking somebody’s grandma put her soul (and toes) in it!

Vera’s is officially my new favorite soul food spot. The food? Unmatched. The customer service? On point. Do yourself a favor and try the $6 soul food platter, and when you bite into that cornbread, remember who put you on.

And whoever the chef is—holla at me!

So I took the drive from Long Island to Vera’s because of the amazing food.The service was very attentive and everything was explained in detail. Tilla was so kind and made us feel like family. I will be back for sure! Thank you

I lowered my review because it said they’re open once a week on Wednesday and I went and they’re closed. Why are they closed the one day it says they’re open? Two other reviews were interesting. One said they’re only opened when they wanna be. And another review left a review a day ago and they’re supposed to be closed on Tuesdays…

Change your hours Vera’s!! The other location on Stanley Ave is open. Go there don’t waste your time.

name: Zatar Cafe & Bistro
document: Zatar Cafe & Bistro. cuisine: Sandwiches Falafel Halal. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Actually outstanding. The dips are world-class. Best mahumarrah and hummus I’ve had in nyc. The tomato-egg brunch thing was phenomenal. The pita is fluffy and delicious and perfect.
Our server was SO kind and awesome.
The coffee is good. The yemini tea was delish.
The prices are great. Brunch starts at ~$13 which is so fair.
Desserts look great.
My only complaint is that it’s a bit cold inside when it’s cold outside. The cold seeps in.

This was my first time coming here and wow — the food was absolutely delicious. Every single dish we tried was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully prepared.

I came with my friend, who is a true professional degustatore with a very refined palate, and even he was genuinely impressed. He enjoyed every bite of the dishes they served us. When Saba says something is delicious, his whole family and friends trust his judgment — and they always try whatever he recommends.

That alone says everything. We’ll definitely be back!

Always a great option for warm and comforting eats! Looking at the menu, you really can’t go wrong with anything—the flatbread pizza is a MUST, the bowls are so deliciously filling, and the appetizers will fill you up because you won’t stop until you finish. Great staff and vibe—a very relaxed and inviting vibe for friends, family, or couples. You’ll definitely get seating during the day, but it’s very popular in the evening. It’s the kind of place where you eat at once and you’ll be coming back time and again! Neighborhood gem!

We came with a party of four for brunch on a beautiful fall Saturday and though it was busy they were able to seat us outside right away. We had the Yemeni Soufflé which was quite good, the Eggs Benzatar which was very good, the Eggs Baladi which was good and spicy, and the chicken kebab which was very good. The pita is also very good. We tried three desserts which were all respectable, not very sweet. Very reasonable prices!

Amazing food and great service. I loved the flavors and quality of the food. Everything tasted fresh and delicious. I got the salmon kabob and the Mediterranean salad. It comes with the rice and salad on the side. I also got the mint lemonade and a few drinks and desserts from the little cafe section. Everything was great but I’ll be coming back for the dinner more than the desserts.

They have indoor and outdoor seating with lots of room and a cute windowsill seating. The staff were attentive and friendly and quick to serve. I really enjoyed it!
