name: Al Badawi
document: Al Badawi. cuisine: Middle Eastern Soup Sandwiches. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: As an arab woman, I’m ashamed that they’re serving these dishes to people who want authentic palestinian food. My husband (also arab) and I walked in after passing this place a bunch of times. It looked very beautiful inside, but there’s where the amusement ended. We ordered labna as an appetizer which was pretty decent, however the pita bread was severely undercooked. We ordered the maskhan dish, and we waited probably close to an hour waiting for it. I understand things are freshly prepped and made, but when we received it, it did not look like a meal that needed almost an hour. It had bread that was also undercooked, burnt not caramelized onions, and very bland and under seasoned chicken. The presentation was nice but it truly was not a good experience for my taste buds. The service was okay, I felt bad for the workers it seemed like it was only like 2-3 of them serving tables so of course I dont mind them checking in once in a while due to how busy they were. But overall, disappointment. Only way I’d come back is if i’m deathly craving some arab food and this is the only restaurant open in a 5 mile radius.

DELICIOUS food and excellent service. enjoyed everything we ordered: the lamb was tender and fell off the bone, with nicely spiced rice; a generous portion of tasty meat with our hummus shawarma; and a classic rendition of muhammara.

no wonder this place is always full! will definitely be coming back.

Excellent middle eastern restaurant.
With all the classic dishes like hummus and tabuleh, and good quality shawarma.   They don’t have lamb but chicken and beef.
Beet salad was excellent.
Combination appetizer platter was excellent too - recommend it highly.
Overall, a nice experience and great food.

Solid Palestinian food on Atlantic Ave! We got the Ouzi Lamb and Mixed platter kebabs with the lamb chop; and ended with the knafe. Lamb was falling off the bone- the Ouzi Lamb tasted like it was cooked in a Palestinian’s grandmothers home and served fresh - flavors were warm and fragrant!! Kebabs had a ton of flavor; rice was fluffy and the knafe was probably one of the best I’ve had in the city. Service is slow but they are extremely busy! Would love to be back - if you can get a seat, def try it out!

This restaurant came to my attention through a strong recommendation from a devoted fan, so I made it a point to visit while in New York/Brooklyn. It was fairly busy for a late Sunday lunch or early dinner, which initially seemed promising.

Unfortunately, my experience was somewhat disappointing. The first item we attempted to order, laham ajun, was unavailable. The menu felt a bit cluttered and slightly overpriced for what was offered. While the restaurant appeared well-staffed, a noticeable language barrier made communication somewhat difficult.

The food itself carried good flavor, though I am uncertain whether it truly represents Palestinian cuisine as advertised—it didn’t quite evoke the familiar tastes I associate with authentic Mediterranean dining. Portion sizes were generous, which was appreciated.

The most surprising—and frankly disheartening—moment was when hot tea was served in a Turkish-style china cup poured from a coffee pot. It felt inconsistent with the restaurant’s cultural presentation.

Overall, while the visit was underwhelming, I do believe the place deserves a second chance.

name: Ralphs Sports Bar
document: Ralphs Sports Bar. cuisine: Sports Bars Burgers Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Our experience at Ralph’s Sports Bar was superb; great vibe, very cozy  and charming. The service is spectacular.  Raffaele and Luisa were very attentive and professional. They were both exceptional on every level. We dined on delicious Smash Burgers, baked clams, Italian Egg Rolls were divine! The wine selection is vast, as well as the beer and cocktail menus- Ralph’s is a great family place or just a cozy dinner for two and everything in between. Great place to watch a sporting event too! Price point is exceptional. Don’t miss out on this great dining experience. Thank you Ralph for a great experience, we will be back soon!

Ralph’s Sports Bar kills it on all levels, food was amazing. Had a burger with onion rings and it blew my mind. Ralph himself was involved in everything and made my experience unforgettable. Everything you want from a sports bar is here. Make sure you stop by when you’re in Staten Island.

Delish.  Get those mozzarella sticks. they are soooo good. the sauce to dip is amazing. french onion soup was awesome. the filet mignon tips were excellent. and we had fun singing karaoke! great night. will be back

Food pretty good, moderately priced. Staff kind and attentive, BUT this place following three separate visits for dinner is always freezing ? I don't know if they can't afford heating or not, or if this is a money saving tactic ? There's only maybe 2 restaurants on the Island that I find with the same deficiency, and it's either that they're being cheap and don't really care about their customers comfort and/or their staff is warm because they're going back and forth from the kitchen and they're dropping the thermostat for their own Gen-Z comfort ? Likely both in today's society. Our young daughter came back from the ladies room literally shivering ? There's really no excuse for this in a business that hinges itself on pleasing customers with a relaxed, comfortable dining experience so that they might return again. We'll Sadly not return again unless this condition is corrected. 😒

Came up from DC to Staten Island to get tattooed. I spent my first night at Ralph's - had a delicious burger. Really enjoyed the atmosphere at this place - everyone made me feel very welcome (including Ralph, who I met and had a great conversation with!). My only regret is that I couldn't make it back out on my last night because my tattoo session went so long! Would come back for sure!!

name: Meet The Meat
document: Meet The Meat. cuisine: Steakhouses Seafood. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: We dined here on 12/31/25, our 2nd NYE dinner with the MTM family. Our reservation was made for 9:00P, same as the year prior, knowing it was likely one of the business evenings (if not the most) of the year for them. We had a wait of about 20-25 min, but we expected a wait and we were all good. One the staff (really sweet blonde woman) was great about acknowledging us and keeping us updated about our seating time, and I bet other diners may have not been as patient, but we were all good and appreciative of her pleasantness. We were seated by the owner I believe, who was also kind, and since we knew our order (same as last year), we promptly provided our order to our server staff, the porterhouse for two, mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus. Once we ordered, we enjoyed a cherry blossom martini and Texas mule while we waited and not even 20-25 min later, all of our meal components arrived….that was a short wait! The porterhouse steak was cooked perfectly to our preference, and the perfect portion for us. Didn’t leave us overly full! Delicious mashed potatoes and fresh asparagus. We had a discrepancy with our bill of an overcharge, but the owner was kind and handled it swiftly. Last year we didn’t have room for dessert, but this time we took the walnut pecan pie to go, it was just ok. This is our new tradition for NYE, we enjoy it’s in our neighborhood walking distance, warm and cozy, food is delicious and feel welcome here.

Came here for an anniversary dinner and was so worried that the steak wouldn’t be good. I was incredibly wrong and the steak was absolutely delicious. The sides were a little bland so we added salt and pepper. The service was really attentive and the bathrooms are so clean. Highly recommend this gem in Astoria and there’s plenty of street parking. Reasonable prices as well, considering the times we’re living in.

Delicious. Came for restaurant week. Ordered. The ny strip steak medium and it was delicious. The salad dressing felt like it had a little too much oil. The tiramisu was soft and fluffy and full of flavor.  Also got the lemon drop martini and it was so good!

A delightful dinning experience, attentive, friendly service, chill ambiance, relaxed atmosphere. Good price point & range, satisfying, delicious portions. Obviously, it is not a coffee shop with $13.99 dinner special, one needs to know this is on a different level. This is a great spot, for those who seek a steakhouse experience in the area. Will drop by again in opportune time.

Went for restaurant week with a few friends. Was expecting good things based from reviews for the food. Unfortunately that wasn't the case. 2 x salmon bland. So was steak and also undercooked. Broccoli just tasted like garlic. Friends burger was best thing on the table but he didn't even eat it. Only 1 person actually finished their meal.
The service was very good though. Just wish they had of asked how everything was as we would have spoken up. They gave us a free dessert which was very kind of them

name: Zoralie Restaurant
document: Zoralie Restaurant. cuisine: Dominican Spanish Puerto Rican. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Was craving some good Dominican food & found this gem. If its a hole in the wall i just know the food is gonna be amazing, and it was! The service is even better, cozy space but you feel right at home. The Morir sonando really had me soñando. The portions are perfect!

Delicious food in a little hole in the wall. Cash only !

I wasn’t sure what to get so asked the server what was good and she made me up a delicious plate of rice/beans/chicken. Massive plate of food for $12 - I shared with my boyfriend !

They were very friendly and as we sat and eat, we saw many many people come and go for takeaway - a cute little find in the city
Love this spot. The lunch special was so hearty and flavorful. The roast pork and the yellow rice were great. The staff were so kind and friendly too. Definitely a strong neighborhood spot.

The staff are very warm and friendly.  It's a small place with only two tables inside and two tables outside.  They are CASH ONLY!   I ordered the baked chicken, arroz con dules, tostones, plaintains and morir sonando.  The ONLY tasty morsel was the chicken. I am a huge arroz con dules fan and have yet to find a place calling itself authentic puerto rican or dominican restaurant that serves up good, abuelita style arroz con dules.  The arroz con dules here was EXTREMELY dry and tasteless.  I could tell by the sort of greyish appearance it wasnt going to be good.  The tostones were very dry inside, the plaintains instead of being a little crunchy outside and sweet and soft inside, was completely dry.  Very disappointed especially after reading the positive reviews, which I'm now convinced were written by people who dont know authentic puerto rican/dominican food.

We found this gem in the middle of the city while wandering around. The staff were super nice and they helped us ask for a good combination of dishes to try as many things as possible. Don't forget to try their juices as well! It seemed like a family-owned business with a great atmosphere. 100% recommended!

name: Nobu Fifty Seven
document: Nobu Fifty Seven. cuisine: Sushi Bars Japanese. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Nobu Fifty Seven was absolutely beautiful in every way. We booked our Valentine’s Day reservation two to three weeks in advance, and it was still the last seating of the night at 10:45 PM. Although they were running slightly behind, we were seated about 30 minutes after our reservation.

We ordered the Valentine’s Day special bundle, and every course was outstanding. The variety of dishes was incredible, and everything we tried was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. You truly cannot go wrong with any selection here.

From the moment we arrived, the staff provided exceptional service, hospitality, and attention to detail. The entire experience felt special and memorable. We will definitely be returning.

Been here long time ago before covid...

Overheard prices skyrocketed... then... co-worker ordered takeout.

Totally impressed with bento.
Surf and turf. Mero exquisite. Steak not bad. Sushi excellent as well.
Nicely packed as well as utensils.

Bit overpriced for appetizer, tuna tartar.
Guess no plating and all... bit not worth it.

I reserved Nobu for my wife’s birthday and it exceeded expectations. The yellowtail was incredibly fresh, the sushi was perfectly done, and the wagyu tacos were a standout. Dessert was just as impressive and the perfect way to end the night. The service really made the experience special. Our waitress was amazing, kind, attentive, and made my wife feel celebrated.

Great atmosphere, great food, and an overall unforgettable night. We will definitely be back.

Two story Nobu on 57th, they have a lot of classic Nobu dishes (wagyu dumplings, firecracker shrimp, and the miso cod are examples) - miso cod was great. Sushi was ok, and the yellowtail jalepeno (spicy!) was good to start. Get the hot dishes here!

Went on a Friday night and it was busy but the staff was very attentive . Great vibe .
I had the lychee martini and they were great. To eat I had the lobster tacos, shrimp tempura, the rice cake, tiradito and Toro roll. It was so delicious and I want to go again. Dishes are shareable. Very nice for a date night or just a night out with your girls/friends.

**went again 10/24** amazing service !  I love how they tell you how to eat the dish  and what’s part of each dish. Very clean and efficient service! Got sat at the counter but enjoyed watching the amazing chefs at work. Had the tiradito again and crispy rice. Lobster taco and wagyu taco, rock shrimp and the ribeye were all delicious. My bf loved the old fashion . Had the banana pudding for desert! Amazing

name: 3 Times
document: 3 Times. cuisine: Dim Sum Shanghainese Noodles. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Went here last week and loved how quick and delicious the food was! We got the pan fired dumplings with the rice and beef that came with scallions.

I got to this gem by accident , and it’s an excellent place for lunch or a simple dinner.

I ordered the shrimp and pork steamed dumplings and seaweed shrimp soup. The dumplings were absolutely delicious—well-cooked, fresh, and bursting with flavor. The soup, on the other hand, was more like a broth and a bit too salty for my taste, but it was still enjoyable. Overall, I had a wonderful time at this cafe.

Drawn in by the enticing sign advertising soup dumplings for $6.95, I couldn't resist venturing inside to confirm the price with the server. Upon their confirmation, I eagerly ordered two portions and was delighted by the quality and value of these delectable little parcels. Each dumpling was generously filled with a flavorful broth and tender, fatty, well-seasoned pork. The flavors were well-balanced, and the textures were complementary, with the soft dumpling skin contrasting nicely with the savory filling. The dumplings were well-executed, with the ingredients tasting fresh and cooked just right. The portion size was also appropriate for the price, making it an excellent value. While the service was a bit brusque, it didn't detract from the overall enjoyment of the meal. The ambiance was casual and unassuming, providing a comfortable setting for a quick bite. There was no wait time, which was a plus. Overall, I would recommend this place for their delicious and affordable soup dumplings, despite the slightly curt service.
So good! I came here with my brother and we got the bbq pork buns, orange chicken, and xiaolongbao. It was really good and the portions are amazing.

One of the best soup dumplings you will find in the city. The service is nice, good dining vibes, not too busy for Sunday morning.

The crab soup dumplings and pork soup dumplings are both phenomenal. Wraps are not too thick and juice is flavorful.

Also recommend fried buns (pork + cabbage), braise beef, nanjin duck (brined flavor), and beef pancake.

name: Liberty Diner
document: Liberty Diner. cuisine: Donuts Diners Coffee & Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: On our way back from NYC, we stopped by this lovely diner. The food was fresh and delicious. The portions were enormous! The service was quick. Our waitress was extremely nice and very accommodating. We had a great meal and an excellent time there.

Ordered a greek chicken salad and it came out underseasoned, watery, and gummy. Still better than another guest's burger, which he asked for medium-well but ended up overcooked to death. To top it off, staff was unfriendly and inattentive.

2/10 - Never again

As our family was leaving the Catskills we wanted to stop for breakfast.

Liberty diner was the perfect stop that was enroute to NYC.

The diner is very festive, upbeat, and lively. Loved that they are one of the very few places in the Catskills opened late hours.

Large variety of choices on the menu, the food is very good, coffee was great. Service was excellent.

Loved that they serve cocktails if your in the mood for a glass of wine after a long road trip, or other spirits.

When visiting the area this will definitely be a place I visit for a sit down, bite to eat.

They make very good scrambled eggs with ham. The egg sandwich was good. Good eggs Benedict. The hot chocolate is amazing.  Clean restaurant and great service.  Food was hot and fresh. Everything was good and food came quickly.

After two disappointing encounters with Diners on the trip, I have to say we were third time, lucky. Although this is a diner, the food here is a notch above your typical diner food.   The space itself is huge with a lot of different seating areas. as you enter you are welcome by shelf full of cakes and pastries, and it was very hard for me to resist ordering a couple of them, but I had no space after the breakfast. We ordered a bunch of breakfast item, and I got the eggs. Benedict over crabcakes while my friends got the French toast and the omelettes. Everything tasted great. Although the crabcake was not very crabby, and I am sure they used some form of imitation crab, but given the price, it was still pretty good. The only let down was the coffee and it was a very bad quality of coffee. I wish they invested in better coffee beans. Overall, a really good breakfast place.

document: Bibble & Sip. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Bakeries Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We tried the hot chocolate, matcha cream puff, matcha croissant, and lavender latte at Bibble & Sip.
The matcha croissant was the standout—flaky, buttery, and filled with a rich matcha cream that wasn’t overly sweet. The matcha cream puff was also delicious, light, and well balanced. The hot chocolate was comforting and satisfying, perfect for a cozy break.
The only miss for us was the lavender latte—the floral notes were a bit too strong for our taste. Everything else, though, was beautifully made and clearly high quality. It does get busy and seating is limited, but it’s still a great stop if you love matcha-forward desserts. We’d definitely come back to try more from the menu.

The best cream puffs in NYC! 🧁 The Earl Grey flavor is a game-changer—crispy on the outside and overflowing with silky cream inside. Their specialty lattes are also fantastic and beautifully crafted. Super cute vibe and great for anyone with a sweet tooth. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re near the Theater District!

Will be revisiting this dessert shop after 2-3years which was about 3years ago. Love to drop by and have a piece of heaven whenever I visit NYC. Bought the matcha cream puff and it exceeded my expectations! Crusty on the outside and generous with the fillings! Super yummy for dessert lovers like me 😍 (pic were taken during my first visit).

Bibble & Sip is easily one of the best little café gems in NYC. Everything here feels thoughtful—from the beautiful pastries to the perfectly crafted coffee. The cream puffs are absolutely outstanding: light, airy, and filled with rich, flavorful cream that isn’t overly sweet. You can really tell the ingredients are high quality and made with care.

The coffee was just as impressive. Smooth, balanced, and expertly prepared, making it the perfect pairing with their pastries. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, and the staff is friendly and efficient even when it’s busy.

If you’re anywhere near Midtown and love great coffee and unique pastries, Bibble & Sip is a must-stop. Definitely a place I’ll keep coming back to whenever I’m in the city

A lot is for the visual appeal and adding elements that do not need to be there. I had the everything croissant, panda cake and black sesame cream puff. I also ordered a peachy lechee tea and asked for less sugar. That translated to less flavor, not just less sugar, was like  drinking a lightly flavored water. But the woman at the front was very helpful at accommodating - cannot fault the service. Kind and attentive.

name: Ralph's Coffee
document: Ralph's Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Ralph Lauren's coffee shop is undeniably a stunning space, beautifully designed and embodying the elegance of the brand. The atmosphere contributes to a lovely experience.
However, after ordering a cappuccino and a flat white on two occasions, I can't extend the same praise to their coffee drinks. It's clear that this place primarily serves as a Ralph Lauren store, with a coffee shop that complements the retail experience. The coffee is actually quite good; however, the exquisite design and prestige of the brand set high expectations.
While I'm sure they use high-quality coffee beans, the cappuccino and similar drinks fall short of the standards one would expect from such a chic and stylish venue.

We went to have breakfast at Ralph’s Coffee at my girlfriend’s request. We are both big fans of the Ralph Lauren brand and really identify with its style, so visiting this café, which we had seen many times on social media, was something we were genuinely excited about.

We arrived quite early, knowing that if you go later you usually have to queue to get in. Luckily, we were seated straight away. The staff was very polite, friendly, and welcoming, and the overall atmosphere was exactly what you would expect from Ralph Lauren: elegant, classic, and very well curated.

We ordered a coffee, an orange juice, and for food a croissant, a wrap, and a sandwich. The coffee was good, not the best I’ve ever had, but definitely more than acceptable. It’s served in a beautiful branded cup that perfectly matches the company’s iconic colors, white and bottle green, which adds a lot to the experience.

However, the food was a big disappointment. Both the wraps and the sandwiches were served cold and felt like pre-packaged, vending-machine-style food. They don’t even heat them up, and the quality compared to the price is completely disproportionate. We understand that you are paying for the location, the ambiance, and the brand, but the food offering should be much better and more carefully curated.

Inside the café there is also a shop where you can buy mugs, coffee, teas, hoodies, textiles, tableware, and many other products, all following the same green-and-white aesthetic with the iconic teddy bear logo. This part is very well done and definitely worth it if you want to take home a souvenir from such an iconic place.

It’s also worth mentioning that this is the only Ralph’s Coffee where you can actually sit down, located in the Upper East Side of Manhattan. Other Ralph’s Coffee locations are more like take-away spots or food trucks.

Overall, it’s an iconic place with an amazing atmosphere and strong brand identity, but the food offering is something they should seriously reconsider.

There was a line wrapped around the place, but it moved fairly well. You can grab coffee to go or wait in a separate line for a table. After a great workout in Central Park, a friend and I chose to sit down. The coffee was excellent, and the chocolate cake was so good. Would definitely return.
No reservation needed. We just walked in and got on the line.

First off, it must be a rule that you are stunning and dress to impress to even work here. Every single person is gorgeous. Men and women. And honestly…..they are all so nice! We waited in line this afternoon for a table and it was worth the wait. The coffee….soooooo good. The line wasn’t bad. We may have waited about 40 minutes total between inside and out. We went around 2 in the afternoon on a weekday.

Ralph’s Coffee is an absolute gem — a perfect blend of style, quality, and classic New York charm. The moment you step inside, you’re greeted by the inviting aroma of freshly brewed coffee and the elegant Ralph Lauren aesthetic that makes the space feel both timeless and cozy.

The coffee is exceptional, rich and perfectly balanced, whether you choose a cappuccino, espresso, or their signature cold brew. Their pastries and light bites complement the drinks beautifully, with fresh ingredients and impeccable presentation.

The staff is friendly and professional, always welcoming and attentive, making every visit a pleasant experience. The atmosphere is calm yet sophisticated — ideal for a quick coffee break, a casual meeting, or just people-watching in style.

Located in some of the city’s most iconic spots, Ralph’s Coffee captures the essence of refined simplicity. Every detail, from the green cups to the classic decor, reflects the brand’s dedication to quality and elegance.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
A must-visit for coffee lovers who appreciate good taste and timeless design.

Its a mound of pistachio cream and kataifi wrapped in marshmallow and coated in cocoa powder. I found it to be quite delicious, with the contrasting textures of the soft, stretchy marshmallow and the crunchy, sticky filling. Flavor is not too sweet, and nutty from that pistachio cream.

Definitely recommend visiting to try this and their many other treats like their shaved snow, basque cheesecake, new chocolate beignets, and more.

The pastries were fine, not amazing, so I had low expectations for our meals, but the food was surprisingly delicious!

The menu is somewhat limited, but what they make they make very well.

google_reviews.text:
Super cute and trendy onigiri spot! Everything felt very nice and clean, and the space is thoughtfully designed. I really liked that it’s a sit-down place, since most onigiri spots are usually more grab-and-go — it makes the experience feel more relaxed and enjoyable.

BUT!! Sweet potato cheesecake was the most delicious one!! Out of all them I will come back to eat that again!!!! 💕✨

Stopped in for a snack and this cafe is very cute with tasty options.  I love ume and wanted to try the ume onigiri but it was sold out so my other vegan option was the  kinoko (5 kinds of japanese mushroom, scallion).  It was so tasty! The perfect bite.

I wanted to love this place more than I actually did. We each got the set meal. I was really disappointed in the shrimp tempura onigiri, which was the monthly special. The rice could have used some seasoning as the shrimp itself was quite small, so it was mostly just eating plain rice. The highlight of the meal was the mentaiko onigiri. If I went back, it would only be for that.

I can see the social media appeal of this kind of food, but honestly it just seems messier and more complicated than a sushi roll. I stopped here for a quick lunch this past Thursday around 1pm. There were a few people in line in front of me and throughout the small restaurant, but once I sat down it got pretty busy - clearly a popular midday destination. As an aside, 90% of the clientele seems to be Asian Gen Zers, which I guess makes sense. Like a lot of the smaller NYC restaurants, the ceilings are super high but the space is pretty narrow. They have very modern tables/chairs (kind of gave off a higher-end Ikea vibe), which I think works well with the more limited square footage, and it doesn't feel too claustrophobic even when the place is jumping.

I decided to aggressively hit up the onigiri section of the menu, ordering three different ones. They were bigger than I thought they would be, so unless you have a pretty hardcore appetite, their $16 two-onigiri combo that comes with soup/sides is probably the way to go. Mine cost around $18, so not a big deal, especially since I'm not a huge miso soup fan.

My three were the Salmon, Inari and Karaage. The Salmon was a giant miss for me, though a lot of that is palate preference. The obvious comp/not-so-distant cousin to these items is a sushi roll, and I think it's weird to have seared salmon rather than raw salmon in a roll with rice. It always tastes like the fish is off, even though it isn't. Coupled with the pickled radish it was just not my thing at all. The Inari was pretty good - basically the equivalent of a very small, almost breakfast burrito. The problem with it for me (and all of these onigiri) is that it's hard to eat and get all of the ingredients in one bite, if that makes sense. Maybe there's a sophisticated technique to eating these that I'm unaware of (100% a possibility), but I'd end up getting a bite of just rice, or just the beef. All of the ingredients were good, but it was hard for me to get them to play together.

The Karaage for sure was my favorite. Unsurprisingly, it's also the naughtiest one I had, featuring fried chicken and spicy mayo, but very tasty. The primary issue with that is it was super messy - one side of the onigiri is doused in the mayo, and from what I could see, they didn't have napkins (maybe I missed it, but I even went up to the counter to check). As a result? A spicy mayo-drenched paw that I tried to subtly wipe on the tray a lot. Again, if I had more practice with using the chopsticks on these, maybe it's a moot issue. I would suggest though that they provide napkins and more Americanized utensils for Neanderthals like me.

This was an interesting lunch, I'll at least give them that. It's not really my thing, but I could easily see this being a go-to destination for someone who's more versatile with a pair of chopsticks.

google_reviews.text: This is the first place we stopped when arriving in town and it was amazing. The restaurant has a beautiful country farmhouse atmosphere. We walked into Charlotte's Cafe and received a friendly greeting. It's a very casual, unassuming, and small restaurant.

The pastries were fine, not amazing, so I had low expectations for our meals, but the food was surprisingly delicious!

The menu is somewhat limited, but what they make they make very well.

It was also beyond plentiful for the prices being charged.

Our server was very friendly and quick, which we greatly appreciated.

The apple cider margarita was tasty. This has a very homey/family run feel and feels genuine, and they're doing good food. We'd definitely stop in again.

Walking out of Chelsea Market, I wanted a cup of coffee so I instinctively turned toward Starbucks Reserve next door where they have fantastic selections from countries all over the world.  But wait...I thought to myself as I stopped...I should support the local businesses, support the neighborhood. So I turned up instead to Stone Street Coffee.  When I walked in, there was already one customer but strangely he is sitting and chilling on the stool by the cash register...I thought this was weird bc normally at this place without seating, ppl just stand at the counter, order, get coffee, pay and leave.  I should have known this was a red flag.  Turns out the barista was on the first of 3 lattes and this customer must have known how long it takes this guy to make a drink so he probably sat down to get comfortable. I just wanted a cup of coffee but I watched this barista go through the motions of making *3* lattes like he was heavily sedated or if he was recovering from a stroke as every movement was made at a glacial pace.  This barista was totally unbothered and in no hurry despite me standing there awkwardly waiting in silence.  He even paused what he was doing at one point to change his rap music!  Even after waiting the eternity for him to finally get to my simple cup of coffee, he misheard the type of milk I asked for and had to make it again. Look, I'm all for supporting local businesses but there has to be something worthwhile supporting. They have to understand the competition they're up against and if this is the level of effort and service I'm going to get here, why am I going to choose it over Starbucks?

Coffee is not great. Over-burnt espresso. My latte tasted so bitter that no milk could cover it. Also I don't trust that ancient La Marzocco... Not sure if that's a specialty coffee roasters but maybe train your baristas better. If I wanted to get bad coffee I'd go to Starbucks

document: Strangelove. cuisine: Dive Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Nice relax bar, rock vibe with local people! So why 3 stars ? The bartender added the 20% tip and gave me a non-itemized bill, so I added an additional 20% thinking the tip wasn’t included. Don’t do that if you want people to come again. I don’t mind giving an extra tip if is a good service, but I Do Not appreciate when bartenders play that game with me. Will I come back? Probably yes, but will pay more attention.

Strangelove is where Midtown goes to forget it’s Midtown. You duck off 53rd between Second and Third, slide past the neon, and the place hits you like a brick of noise and cheap salvation. Whole room is a shotgun. Narrow, red glow, walls cooked over with graffiti like a teenager’s notebook that learned to drink. You sit, you breathe marker fumes and rock sweat, and you remember why bars exist.

The deal is simple. Beer and a shot. Six bucks. Bud, Genesee, cream ale if you feel civilized, plus a well kick to follow. You are not here to swirl or sniff. You are here to get honest. Order the special, let the room tune your brain to punk standard, and watch your shoulders drop.  ￼

It opens at two every day and runs late enough that you lose track of your better ideas. That is the point. Midtown tells you to be a person who hustles for a living. Strangelove tells you to be a person who sits still for once and lets the jukebox and the bartender do the talking.  ￼

The front bar is short, seats are few, so you learn to lean like a pro. Past the first stretch there is a quiet kink to the right, a little rear alcove where the graffiti gets louder and the tables get low enough to make saints slouch. If you get parked back there, time melts. You will leave a better version of your worst self.

Strangelove Bar has been my go-to spot since 2018, and it hasn’t changed a bit—and that’s exactly why it’s my favorite bar in the city. If you’re looking for a true dive, this is it.

Graffiti-covered walls, cheap beer, and a $6 beer-and-shot combo set the tone, but it’s the people that make this place special. No pretension, no judgment—just a solid crowd that’s as real as the bar itself. Strangelove is proof that a great dive doesn’t need gimmicks, just good vibes and good people.

document: Thyme Bar. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Speakeasies. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Thyme used to be a fun, charming spot that I genuinely enjoyed visiting and bringing out-of-town friends to. I was warmly greeted by the gentleman at the door (5⭐️ service there), which set a great first impression.

However, as soon as I walked downstairs, it felt like the space had lost its speakeasy vibe. I was seated right near the stairs and could feel cold air from outside every time the door opened, which made the experience uncomfortable.

I was also surprised to see how much the cocktail menu had been reduced. When I asked about it, the response was that “the place changed a lot.” That’s fair — places evolve — but instead of highlighting the improvements or new strengths, the explanation focused negatively on what the bar used to be. As someone who really enjoyed the former version, that wasn’t reassuring.

Unfortunately, the drinks themselves didn’t make up for it. One of the two cocktails was simply not good. No one came back to check on the drinks, and when I asked for the check after about 20 minutes, there was no acknowledgment that I had barely touched mine or any inquiry about my experience.

Overall, a place I once enjoyed and recommended now feels more like a standard dive bar, the complex fun drink in crazy glasses with beautiful presentation are gone… and the fun talk with mixologist are gone as well. It was just lacking the warmth and attention to detail that once made it special.

TLDR: Had a great time at Thyme! Unique cocktails (including customized ones) and very interesting, tasty bites.

Came here with some friends and ended up staying for a while! Had a great time ordering cocktails and hanging out - service was great (shout out Cody, was very patient and explained some of his and the team’s thought process on the drinks well), and really enjoyed the gin drinks (ordered birth mark and a custom drink based on my palette which I really enjoyed) and bites (especially the potato churros). Some of the other drinks were interesting to watch get made as well (e.g., the What Ales You which if I remember correctly involved a very hot rod). Definitely worth checking out!

Thyme Bar was underwhelming. Let’s start with the positives… The service was friendly, the space was stylish and the food was good.

The olives were really very good. The potato churros were great as well. Unfortunately the drinks were underwhelming. We had 4 in our party and we all tried different drinks the first round. None were fans, so we tried each others drinks and were equally disappointed.

We ordered different drinks the second round, and were each underwhelmed again.

There are so many great spots for cocktails in NYC. I think Thyme bar misses the mark with quality and execution of cocktails.

Great bar! Some of the best drinks I’ve had in the City. The bar crew was so friendly too. The drinks and the presentation itself was amazing. Our first cocktails were so tasty and we initially didn’t even think they were strong, but boy, the way they felt in a bit haha. Honestly I’d definitely be back here for their tasting menu. We really enjoyed our night!

Just visited Thyme Bar today and I was really impressed by the creative sesonal cocktails they have! The bites were amazing the staff was so kind and the cocktails were some of the best i’ve tried! Definitely stop by to have a drink cheers

Amazing, tasty, drinks in a very upscale venue. Our service was lacking (which made the 20% default tip on the $30 drinks seem excessive) but I absolutely recommend this bar for a drink and a bite.

The Gold Room is another classic Manhattan cocktail lounge, the kind of place where you automatically sit up straighter because the walls look like they’ve seen things.

Pro tip: check in with the host, even if you’re just aiming for a spot at the bar. This is Manhattan — even the bar stools have a waitlist.

The dirty vodka martini is excellent, the kind that makes you remember why this drink survived every cocktail trend of the last century. Drinks arrived quickly, service was friendly with a smile, and everyone seemed genuinely happy to be working in a room this pretty.

Yes, it’s pricey — but you’re paying for the atmosphere, and the atmosphere delivers. Think golden glow, quiet sophistication, and the sense that you’ve stumbled into a very tasteful time capsule.

A lovely spot for a cocktail and a reminder that Manhattan still does these lounges better than anywhere else.

I’ve been taking people here for years! The Gold Room is one of my favorite places to take friends when they visit the city.

As a huge fan of New York's history, the entire experience is very special from entering the courtyard of the Villard Houses (built in 1884 and originally called Cathedral Court because it faces the back of St. Patrick’s Cathedral), which any Gossip Girl fan will recognize as the residence of the Van der Woodsen family, to ascending the stairs inside to the right and entering The Gold Room itself, which is located in the southern wing of the Villard Houses.

Walking into The Gold Room is like stepping into a gilded jewel of New York’s architectural past. Its shimmering surfaces, classical artistry, and hidden musical balcony create an unforgettable, timeless atmosphere, perfectly blending history with modern elegance. It’s one of the most iconic settings in the city, both visually and experientially.

They have a wide variety of drinks, many with names calling back to New York's past and pop culture such as The Commodore (referring to Cornelius Vanderbilt), The Carnegie, The Mrs. Astor (referring to Caroline "Lina" Astor, who led the Four Hundred, New York City's high society during the Gilded Age of the 1870's - 1900), and Gossip Girl.

Whether you're enjoying a cocktail in the evening or just admiring the space during a quiet moment, The Gold Room is a rare gem. It’s like stepping into another era of opulent, elegant, and unforgettable grandeur. Every detail, from the gilded ceilings to the finely crafted cocktails, feels thoughtfully preserved and beautifully reimagined.

Also to note: The courtyard often has great decorations year-round that are great for photos. If you visit during the holidays, there is a beautiful Christmas tree and other lights and decorations which make the courtyard one of the best areas to visit during the holidays if you love that time of year.

While the beverages and food were satisfactory, individuals who value minimal wait times or prefer a more relaxed atmosphere may consider visiting at less busy hours.

The Owl Tail is such a cozy gem, just a quick and easy stroll from the 72nd Street Station (1, 2, and 3 lines). The inside is beautiful, but since the October weather was perfect, we grabbed a table outside and soaked up the vibe. The menu might be small, but it’s packed with great seasonal options and they’ve got a happy hour from 4:30 to 6:30!!! Definitely worth catching.

Our servers, Emily and Cynthia, were absolute stars: super friendly, honest, and knew the menu inside out. We went with their suggestions and loved everything. The deviled egg platter (half-off during happy hour!) and the butternut squash crostini were both winners. I ordered the Owltumnal Daiquiri, and wow, it tasted like fall in a glass. The drinks all sounded tempting, so I’m already planning my next visit to try more. Clean bathrooms, good vibes, and a place I’ll definitely be back to check out indoors next time.

Found this place in a book called Drink Like a Local and with its location and vibe I can see why the locals like it. LOVED the wine, the food, the vibes! Highly recommend sitting outside if the weather is nice.

I have been hearing about this place for a while now and decided to give it a try. After a long walk on the Upper West Side, I was lucky enough to get a seat at the bar, since it is quite small. Service was welcoming; I liked the design of the menu. A great selection of cocktails that caters to a vast clientele with different tastes. My cocktails were pretty tasty and well-balanced. The bartender was friendly and seemed knowledgeable. I had the shrimp dumplings, and they were tasty as well. Overall, this place did not disappoint. I had a great time and will likely come back with a date.

Staying at the Artezen Hotel, but regardless of where we stay we will always come here!!  What a hidden Jewel!  Everyone so nice, the atmosphere perfect, the view, you will not be disappointed!!

The food is a great quality and comes out quick and the drinks are incredible. The bartenders are masters at their crafts and make delicious drinks. This is a great space with an amazing view of the city and amazing service highly recommended. One of my top 3 locations ever.

document: The Rum House. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Piano Bars. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Didn't eat here, came for a cocktail (an Escape) and to listen to some live Jazz whilst I drank it. This place has history and ambience. Drinks are not cheap but it has over 180 different Rum's and the bartenders make mean cocktails. The Jazz was good too. Will definitely return one day.

Such a cosy place to visit with friendly staff and amazing drinks. Loved the Christmas decorations. Wish they didn’t cram as many people in to make it more comfortable, but it’s fine if you have a reservation and get there early. The live music when we visited was amazing. Would recommend!

I went to The Rum House the other night and had very mixed feelings. The live music was absolutely fantastic — trumpet, contrabajo, piano — more 40s/50s style than modern jazz, but the musicians were incredibly talented, friendly, and cheerful. Honestly, they were the highlight of the evening.

That said, everything else was disappointing. A bottle of wine was $60 (just checked, you can get the same bottle for $13.99 online) and honestly not very good. The food menu was extremely limited — the most “serious” option was a $10 hot dog, which took half an hour to arrive (though, to be fair, it was decent once it came).

The real dealbreaker came at the end: when the bill arrived, there was a 20% service charge automatically added. This wasn’t presented upfront, and it wasn’t a tip — it was just baked into the bill with no choice. I get that the musicians need to be paid, and I’d happily contribute or buy a ticket at the door. But sneaking in a hidden fee after you’ve already ordered feels shady, especially since most of the crowd are tourists.

It’s a shame, because the music really was wonderful, but this left such a bad taste that I wouldn’t come back, even if they booked the best musicians in the world.

We were looking for something to do on our overnight trip to New York, we popped in around 11 PM and unfortunately couldn’t find a spot to sit. After waiting a few minutes outside, we noticed that a table had cleared up so we made our way back in and we were seated. Our server was attentive and kind, the drinks were spot on. I had an amaretto sour, it was one of the best I’ve had. We did not try any of the food on the menu as we just come from dinner.

The live music was a vibe. The atmosphere was perfect. As someone who has never been to New York before now, this place is exactly what I was hoping for. It feels, authentic New York. It was the exclamation to our night as we had just left the Broadway Theatre watching the Great Gatsby. Definitely worth the wait. Will be back!

A rum lover’s dream but an absolute NYC staple. Where else can people go out to a swanky dimly lit cocktail bar and be serenaded by luxurious cocktails and funk jazz beats?

The vibe is immaculate and this place lives up the classic Manhattan cocktail lounge reputation. The drinks are bold, exciting, and rum-forward. Have to give a shout out to the best doorman in the biz, Gino, who not only made us feel welcome like VIP’s, but did his best to bestow the same feelings to everyone else who walked through the door. His energy matched the brand the drinks and decor worked so hard to cement. We will be back

Vanguard is an absolute gem just steps away from the chaos of Times Square. Tucked on a quiet corner, it feels like slipping into a little dream world — warm, cozy, and instantly welcoming. The atmosphere is intimate without being stuffy, the kind of place where you can actually hear the person you’re with, relax, and just enjoy your glass of wine.

The service was truly outstanding: kind, attentive, and genuinely thoughtful without ever feeling pushy. You can tell they care about what they’re pouring and about making you feel at home. It’s the perfect spot to escape the noise, sip something delicious, and slow down for a moment in the middle of NYC. I’d come back in a heartbeat — Vanguard is the kind of place you almost don’t want to share so it stays your little secret.

Vanguard is such a gem in the neighborhood! It has great vibes, music, and (most importantly) the best staff! Isabel, Jacob, Manny, and David are fantastic. We’ve discovered so many new wines, and love bringing friends & family from out of town.

What a great spot to spend a Saturday evening! Isabel greeted us warmly when we arrived and helped us discover a new favorite white wine. She is very knowledgeable about the wines on the menu and gave us great recommendations and even shared some trivia about the towns in France where the wines come from! We met her colleague Jacob later in the evening and he also made sure that we had a great experience…will definitely be back!

Such a cozy, welcoming atmosphere. My friend and I came here on Saturday night and ended up spending hours here because it was so lovely. Both of the bartenders were kind, accommodating, and had great recommendations. They were very attentive, checked on us throughout the night, and always made sure we had enough wine. They were personable and easy to talk to. It never felt like we had to go out of our way to get their attention, like it often does at bars in the city.

We sat at the bar and were greeted by two of their regular customers. The four of us had great conversation and it felt like a home away from home. This place has all the charm of a small neighborhood bar, where everyone greets you with a smile, only steps away from Lincoln Center. This place seems truly perfect for any occasion. Casual enough you can come in for a drink at the end of the work day, while also elegant enough to impress your friends after the symphony, ballet, or opera.
Locals - this should be your go-to wine bar in the city. Tourists - vanguard is a “can’t-miss” stop on your itinerary. I can’t speak highly enough about my experience here! Stop reading this review and go see for yourself!

google_reviews.text:
Located below Judam (formerly Rib No 7), Barbam is a cozy and smaller bar serving up Korean cocktails. you walk down the stairs to this small and cozy area. There’s both bar seating and a table seating, but we chose to sit at the bar.

Cocktails are a bit on the pricy side (around $24 per each one) but the presentation is quality throughout. We got a Hulu punch and a JMT.

The JMT came with a little show of lighting steel wool that added a smoky flavor to the drink. The alcohol was on the stronger side, but it tasted good and the lime juice went well with the bourbon.

The Hulu punch was also on the strong side, but the alcohol taste wasn’t as strong. The strawberry went well with the drink as well.

We also got fried chicken on the side, which was lightly battered and soft and juicy. It came with a wasabi mayo that paired well with the dish, as well as a chili sauce.

Came by on a weekday evening after a friend’s recommendation. We each got a cocktail that came with a strawberry tanghulu (totally forgot the name though 😅). The interior was beautiful, the cocktails looked amazing, and the fire show was such a nice touch. It tasted so good I didn’t even realize how strong it was until later, got tipsy faster than expected! Definitely coming back to try other cocktails next time.

Had a great time here! The atmosphere is cozy and relaxing, perfect for a night out.
The highlight for me was definitely the bartender — you can really feel how passionate and focused he is. Watching him make drinks is like watching someone truly enjoy their craft. Loved that energy!

I hope more people get to experience this place.
Just one small tip: I personally wouldn’t recommend the oysters — not really my taste. But everything else was great.

everything runs on the sweet side and is pretty pricey. seating was tight but they let us sit and yap. i got the milk kiss and my friend got the hulu punch. hers was more alcohol forward versus mine was like drinking the real thing!

i don't know that i'll come back because of how tight the bar seating was. it was difficult to orient myself in a comfortable position because the seats were so close together. i didn't even want to take a trip to the bathroom because it was such a squeeze. i would've hated being on a date here.

The spot was a bit small but not too crowded. Cocktails were delicious—we got the naengmyeon and the hulu punch. Presentation was A+. I would love to come back and try more of their signature menu! Great for date night.

google_reviews.text: I’ve lived in New York for years and been to the BG cafe on the 7th floor but the Goodman bar is a recent discovery for me. The bar is located on the second floor of the men’s store and I’ve thoroughly enjoyed both of my visits here. The lobster BLAT, their tuna crudo, homemade potato chips, and warm parker house rolls and madeleines are all really delicious as well as the soup of the day that I tried, their coffee, and drinks. Feels very upscale but still casual. Food is great and I loved everything that I tried but the service is even better. Everyone was very friendly and charming especially one of the hosts/servers I believe his name was Andrew. I was really impressed by the level of service he provided even when every seat at the bar and tables were full. Will definitely be back even if I’m not shopping at BG, it was that good!

This is a nice little hidden gym in the midst of the store. I find it very comfortable and relaxing for a cocktail and a snack. Not a ton of tables so you have to hit it at the right time and get lucky but I will certainly make it a habit of grabbing lunch here.

Hidden gem. Came for a quick drink and bite. Quiet escape from the city with a comfy and welcoming atmosphere. Loved the caviar chips and made to order madeleines.

Special thanks to our bartender (tall gentleman, regretfully I did not catch his name), a class above. Attentive and kind.

This is such a nice little bar and you’d never expect much from a spot inside a men’s clothing store. Although it’s a bar, there are still a good selection or restaurant quality dishes to enjoy. I was able to try several drinks and dishes and all were great. Both Eric and Victoria provided lovely service and recommendations as well. My favorite dish was one of the small plates, the Parker house rolls. Trust me, just get them. The tacos were a very close second, but omg those rolls. Would highly recommend stopping by this little spot if you’re in the area, even if you’re not shopping there.

Pure class, deliciously done.  Aysa, Eva, and Eric were sublime and we had a decadently good time.  We especially love the martinis, the caviar, but their soup was the surprise hit.

Update:  Goodman’s Café is a masterclass in elegance and class. This was our fifth visit, and it remains a true secret gem of NYC.
We were served by Eva, who was an absolute delight—her suggestions were spot-on and her service was impeccable, as always. We enjoyed the caviar and two orders of the crudo; both were exquisite.
For a sophisticated sanctuary with top-tier service, there is no better spot. Looking forward to our next return!

google_reviews.text:
This was my first time at Bar Orai, and I really loved the atmosphere, they even had a DJ playing vinyl, which added a great vibe to the space.

One downside is that they don’t accept reservations for groups larger than four, and if you show up with more than four people, they won’t seat you, even if you’re willing to split into two groups. That was a bit disappointing. However, we do respect that.

Overall, though, the ambiance is lovely, the food is decent, and the cocktails are well-crafted. They’re not ultra high-end, but the flavors are fresh and appealing. I only had two drinks, which felt a bit rushed, especially since they also have a time limit. Sad.

That said, the service was good, the staff was friendly, and the space is small but cozy. I’d definitely come back again.

Bar Orai is a gem!!! The food is amazing (kimbap and mac and cheese), and the cocktails are insane — everything was so good.
Every server was chill and friendly, and their cocktail and whiskey recommendations were perfect.
Considering how great my overall experience was, the prices felt more than fair.
I will definitely be visiting again soon. 😋

Cool vibe, I like the music and ambiance. Good music and interesting books. Server wasn’t too friendly. I tried the octopus dish and it was weird. It wasn’t bad but it’s not for everyone. I made comment to the server that it was weird, as a joke, and it seemed like he took it offensively. I also wasn’t drinking and I could tell his attitude changed when I ordered a club soda. Definitely didn’t get warm friendly vibes from him. The fried shrimp sandwich was interesting but idk if it’s worth $20. Don’t think it’s a place I need to come back to

I love a listening room! We need more places that play vinyls where I live, this one is top 3 on my list. Perfect for a date night drink, I recommend the Penicillin. The ambiance is everything! So cozy! And can we talk about the matches? How creative!

I have visited this place countless times, which speaks volumes about how much I appreciate it. If you enjoy good music and quality drinks, this venue truly feels like a little piece of heaven.
What sets it apart, however, is the consistently excellent food — every dish is thoughtfully prepared and full of flavor.
I personally recommend the kimbap, yuzu tomatoes, and mac and cheese; they have become staples for me. Each pairs beautifully with a well-crafted whiskey or cocktail, elevating the entire dining experience.
If you’re considering a visit, I highly encourage it — you’re in for a memorable time ❤️🫶🏻

name: L’industrie Pizzeria
document: L’industrie Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
A New York staple that everyone needs to try at least once when visiting. Get in line before opening because this place gets busy fast.

Their pizza is classic, cooked to perfection with fresh ingredients. The pesto slice is a standout. Bright green sauce layered over bubbling mozzarella, finished with fresh basil and creamy dollops of ricotta. The crust is thin but sturdy, with that perfect balance of crisp bottom and chewy interior.

Definitely want to come back try more

It was our third time in NYC and we had always been pretty disappointed in the pizza there. We decided to give l'industrie a try since we were staying in Brooklyn, and are so glad we did. Our expectations were not high due to the previous sub-par experiences eating pizza in NYC, but this place has changed our minds.

We did half Fig Jam & Bacon and half Burrata. The pizza tasted fresh, and the flavours were a great combination (especially the Fig Jam & Bacon). They offer free hot chili oil as a condiment, which really complemented the pizza. There is no seating, but some standing tables if you wanted to eat in the resto.

In terms of wait, there was a decent queue even for the Williamsburg location. We waited around 20 minutes in the queue, then another 15 minutes after ordering. Staff was friendly and helpful. We would definitely come back on future trips to NYC.

Delicious pizza! I’m very happy we got to try. Super thin crust, but not crunchy, which I love. The toppings were delicious as well. Def recommend the fig and bacon, pepperoni, pesto mushroom and the pesto sausage. Get the olive oil cake as well, it was the perfect dessert.

Finally!!!!!

I am usually not the biggest fan of American pizza - it is too greasy, too thick, has a little too much going on but wow this was a perfect slice.

a burrata pizza is a must. I got also New Yorker and omg it was so so good. The price are higher but so worth it. And they have beer which is a plus.

Pizza with a side of Perroni - incredible!

This was a must visit while my daughter and I were in the area. Especially with all the rave reviews and people saying this is the best pizza in all of NY. Is it good?? Hell yeah!! With how popular the place is it does get a little cramped inside (especially on a rainy day), however, there is a constant flow of people coming in and out so you can find a spot to hover over as you ingest these delectable slices. Ordering process is straightforward and quick and once you pay you find a spot and then they bring the slices out to you. We ordered 3 slices even though 2 would suffice however this isnt some place thats convenient for us being on West Coast so had to just walk a little bit more to work it off! All the slices were fantastic in their own way though the Sausage and Pesto was my favorite, followed by the Margherita and then the L'Industrie. I think I would have enjoyed the last slice more but I was getting full. Ingredients are all top notch and I just wish I could try some of their other offerings. Another time perhaps!

name: NY Pizza Suprema
document: NY Pizza Suprema. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
NY Pizza Suprema is one of those rare places that doesn’t just serve food — it serves memories. I still remember the first time I walked in, carried by the warm smell of fresh dough and melted cheese drifting out onto the street. It felt like stepping into a pocket of New York where time slows down just long enough for you to breathe.
I was tired that day — the kind of tired that settles deep in your bones after hours of rushing through the city. But the moment I stepped inside, something softened. The staff greeted me with that unmistakable New York mix of warmth and confidence, like they already knew I was about to have a great slice.
When I took my first bite, everything else faded away. The crust — perfectly crisp; the cheese — rich and comforting; the sauce — bright, warm, almost familiar. It tasted like care, like tradition, like someone put a little heart into it.
Sitting there with my slice, I felt a small moment of peace in a city that never stops moving. NY Pizza Suprema isn’t just a pizzeria — it’s a place where you feel grounded, welcomed, and reminded of how simple joys can turn a day around.
I’m genuinely grateful for every visit — for the flavor, the kindness, the feeling of home tucked inside a perfect New York slice.

I was looking for some good New York pizza, and this place absolutely SLAPS! Very glad I found this place. There can be a long line, but it moves quickly. Also mind that seating can be limited and tables can be left dirty. However, everyone there was very friendly and had some nice accents.

Now onto the pizza itself: This is exactly what I’m looking for in New York. The dough was at a great texture, it can be greasy at times, but I absolutely love the sauce. Overall, I really enjoyed this place and would come back again.

Best Pizza when you get off the train at Madison Square garden!
Great crispy thin crust. Balance of sauce and cheese. We've tried almost every type over the past year. Hands down favorite spot for a quick slice before hitting the town.

Superb family owned pizza restaurant with excellent food at great prices. Handbags a slice and enjoy, its amazing.

Lots of different options and lots of classics.

A must do NY restaurant and a great place to grab a slice and a break.

Very close to madisson square garden if you are visiting there.

Amazing slice of pizza — truly a quintessential New York experience. The moment you walk in, you’re greeted by a lineup of pies like they’re auditioning for your stomach, and yes, you can even go wild and add extra cheese.

The slice itself? Chef’s kiss. Crispy, balanced, and just the right ratio of everything. Was it the best pizza I’ve had in my entire life? Honestly, no — Canadian pizza still has my heart (they flavor the crust at my go-to spot, and that’s hard to beat).

But this? This is officially the best slice I’ve had in the U.S.

name: Pop's Pizza
document: Pop's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Stopped by Pop’s Pizza in the East Village and was really impressed. The pizza was very flavorful and clearly made with care. I had the burrata slice, which came with hot honey and freshly grated Parmesan, and it was excellent. The crust was perfect crispy on the outside with a nice chew and the sauce had a great, well balanced flavor.
What really stood out was the burrata. A lot of places serve burrata and it ends up being room temperature or just kind of blended in by the time it hits the table, but here the burrata was cold, and that contrast in temperature with the hot pizza really elevated the whole experience. It made each bite feel intentional and well thought out.
On top of that, everything here is fairly affordable, which is always a plus for the area, and the staff was very friendly and welcoming. Definitely a solid spot I’d come back to.

I ordered two slices of pizza, one with mushrooms and another with burrata and they were absolutely incredible. The tomato sauce’s intense flavor combined with the burrata and honey was sublime. The mushroom one came with caramelized onion, ricotta and rúcula. A spectacular combination.
The people that work there are so friendly and kind. Definitely a place I will visit again soon.

The pepperoni pizza slice is amazing. The white slice and the mushroom slice are also unreal. Best slice I’ve had so far in NYC. I always ask for fresh jalapeños on top of the pepperoni slice and they added ricotta + hot honey to every slice. Incredible and such great people!

Pop's Pizza is a pizzeria serving up a menu of slices and pies on Avenue B. super small space -- clean modern decor that has that casual classiness. there's very little seating, but I'd say it's more of a grab-n-go place since there is a steady stream of hungry locals, during the day and night.

been here quite a few times to grab a slice and the quality of the pizza is very good. it's evident that a lot of thought and time goes into the pizza at Pop's and it shows in each bite. as a pizza purist (mostly plain slices and hardly anything else), the plain cheese slice hits the spot each time because the slice has a mix of satisfying flavors coming from the crust, sauce, and cheese. the crust is a thin one -- with enough  firmness to make each bite firm with a chew...but also light and airy enough that you don't feel weighed down by a slice or two. the sauce is flavorful layers of tomato and garlic & herbs that you can actual taste without it being soupy...it's a great balanced sauce. the mozzarella cheese is a thin sheet of melty-ness. and add the finishing of fresh basil, grated Parmesan, and olive oil drizzle to lift an already enjoyable pizza slice's taste, scent, and texture to new heights. all that said, the pizza is very satisfying and you can't go wrong with this classic pizza slice served up hot. as a test i got a slice without the finishers of basil, grated cheese, and olive oil, it's a mighty fine slice, BUT always get them, regardless,

the staff + the owner operator are friendly. never got to chat with them about the pizza-making, but hopefully at some point i will when i have a minute. anyway, this another welcome addition to Avenue B and already has established as a legit slice spot.

Classic NYC slice shop with a friendly, no-frills atmosphere. The pizza was super fresh, with that perfect thin crust and just the right amount of cheese and sauce. You can really taste the quality. Great spot to grab a quick bite in the East Village.

document: Mimi's Pizza - East 86th. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: A tight but great place. Line was very quick and staff were straightforward and efficient. Flavors of pizza were varied and good quality overall. Highly recommend any of their square slices as had nice crisp to the dough and flavors were on point. Seating is counter style against the side wall which felt a bit cramped but adds to the vibe in a way.

Fantastic UES pizza! We stopped in for a snack after visiting the Guggenheim and it did not disappoint. We just grabbed a few slices of what was already made: a sausage and pepperoni slice and a pepperoni deep dish square slice.

It can be hard to figure out what pizza in New York is actually good but this place is the real deal. Perfect crunch, perfect sauce to cheese ratio. The price was right and so was the wait! Give them a try

Whenever I think of New York, pizza is always at the top of my list, and Mimi’s Pizza is one of those spots that absolutely stands out. I stumbled upon it not expecting much, but after trying it once, I can confidently say this is a place I’ll always make a stop at whenever I’m back in the city. The pizza here is just that good memorable in every sense of the word.

The crust strikes the perfect balance: crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside, and sturdy enough to hold the toppings without feeling too heavy. You can tell the dough is made with care because it has that subtle flavor that only comes from a well fermented base. The sauce is another highlight tangy, flavorful, and seasoned just right without being overly salty. Paired with the fresh cheese that melts beautifully over the top, every bite feels like the kind of New York pizza experience people rave about.

What I really love is that Mimi’s doesn’t try to do too much or reinvent the wheel. It’s classic pizza done right, with the kind of execution that leaves a lasting impression. I’ve had countless slices around the city, and while New York is packed with good options, Mimi’s has this way of sticking with you. It’s the kind of slice that you think about later and crave again.

The place itself is unpretentious and welcoming, making it easy to grab a quick slice or sit down for a whole pie. Service is straightforward and friendly, which matches the casual, no-frills vibe.

All in all, Mimi’s Pizza is a gem that deserves the praise it gets. Delicious, memorable, and the kind of pizza that makes you want to come back to NYC just to have it again.

I was visiting Manhattan, NYC, and ended up having the third best pizza I’ve ever had in my life at Mimi’s Pizza — and I’ve had a lot of pizza.

As a pizza connoisseur with very high standards, this place honestly exceeded expectations across the board. The crust, the balance, the flavor — everything just worked. The pizza was shockingly good.

HUGE shoutout to DJ and Franklin, who served me and made my pizza. The service was absolutely amazing, and somehow the pizza itself was even better. You can tell there’s real pride and consistency behind what they’re doing here.

If you’re anywhere near 3rd Avenue and 86th, do yourself a favor and stop in. Mimi’s isn’t just good NYC pizza — it’s elite.

P.s. Ask for what they recommend

They have a great sales tactic of opening their door and as you walk by … you’ll need to exercise utmost self-control to not follow your nose and try a slice. I am not strong so I had to stop and see if the pizza tastes as good as it smells… and thank GOD I did because it was the absolute best grandma marg slice of pie I’ve ever had. I cannot wait to bring my family here to have them try.

When a place says they’re “delivering happiness one slice at a time,” you hope it’s true and this spot absolutely lives up to it.

We ordered a slice of the Naughty Pie (spicy vodka sauce, pepperoni, ricotta, and hot honey), and let me just say… I went to heaven and came right back down just to grab another slice. The balance of spicy, creamy, and sweet was unreal. Every bite was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly crisp. It’s the kind of pizza that makes you pause mid-bite because it’s that good.

This is definitely more of a grab-your-slice-and-go kind of place. They do have a few high-top tables, but it gets crowded quickly because it’s so popular. That said, the line moves fast, so don’t let it scare you away.

Pizza was slamming good with plenty of pepperoni and burned the top of my mouth. As it should. Well Worth the trip. What I really liked, as the original site of Ray’s pizza, the prices aren’t gougy and the staff totally unpretentious. This is a real pizza joint delivering delicious slices for their neighbors.

Tried the naughty pie slice and it was amazing!! The flavor and the crunch were perfect! Definitely different than a regular pepperoni pizza. Would highly recommend and would definitely come back. No inside seating available. There are a few standing tables outside the store but they may or may not be available immediately. Definitely try it fresh.

The pepperoni square pizza was as delicious as it looks, the service was ok but the gentleman that spoke to me was hard to understand. Great place to grab a slice. Quality pizza, quick, buzzing place. Small and busy but you have a standing area inside or standing tables outside.
The plain cheese pizza was a bit sloppy on top making it difficult to eat, but still had a crispy base and tasty.

First stop in NY you have to get pizza right ?!? Exactly just a few streets over we ended up at John’s. Starting with a healthy portion of  Caeser salad which was great fresh shavings of Parmesan and crisp lettuce. A Beautiful Pizzeria Renovated from a Historic Church

John’s Pizzeria is set inside a beautifully renovated former church. The spacious, multi-level dining room features a striking Manhattan mural and original stained-glass ceilings, creating a great atmosphere.

They serve classic New York–style pizza with a slightly thicker crust, topped simply with cheese and tomato sauce. Hearty, satisfying, and nicely chewy around the crust. Appetizers, pasta, and sides are also available, making it a solid spot for a relaxed meal or date.

I’ve ordered 3 different pizza to insure I give my absolute honest feedback. I’ve also ordered one pasta with meatballs, for the quality of the pizza I must say I was expecting something little more premium, the crust was little hard and the topping though it was packed felt like it was coming direct from the freezer to the pizza and then placed into the fire pit, the chicken was little hard, the pepperoni was little to oily with less cheese and the margarita I was expecting more cheese they covered it with some greenry which is a first for me on a margarita pizza. While the location is fabulous and the architecture is beautiful the place missed the soul which is the music that will greate the vibe. If you are not an expert pizza lover then you won’t find my comments valid as the food is still tasty just not as perfect as when visiting other pizzeria in the same area

What a fantastic find while in the city for the day!  Staff was nice, attentive, and informative.  Place was clean, nostalgic, and warm.  We placed our order and it arrived so quick to our table!  Plenty of seating, which was a great find because so many restaurants have very limited seating in NYC.  Would definitely come back here!  For a group of 4, our bill was less than 70.00 before tip.

We had to grab a quick bite before our 1pm show.

You need to wait in line as they don’t do reservations. This doesn’t bother me. It’s actually quite interesting. It’s part of the experience.

We along with quite a few others were swiftly seated. I can tell they do this regularly. It’s efficient and pleasant.

Our waitress was extremely nice and friendly and efficient.

The ambience is nice. The food super tasty. I highly recommend John’s even though the name is boring. :D

We know we will come back again!

document: Stretch Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
​This spot offers delicious pies at a good price. ​The crust is the star of the show on both their round and square pies! We tried the Classic Cheese, Al Pastor, and the Buffalo Chicken Square.

​My favorite was the Buffalo Chicken Square the crust had a crispy undercarriage, soft and fluffy middle. The blue cheese was the perfect complement.

​The Classic Cheese and Al Pastor were also delicious, featuring an extra crispy crust that had no flop. Highly recommend

Stretch Pizza has very flavorful pizzas. This is the work of the celebrated Chef Wylie DuFresne. Some time ago, the restaurant started serving slices all week till 5 pm. Having had a tasty slice at their branch in The Hugh, I came here to see the variety. Now this is the first time that I ordered two slices. The first was the plain which was top notch. Restaurant Review: Patzeria Pizza, Times Square NYC

Patzeria Pizza became my go-to spot during my week-long stay in Times Square—literally just a one-minute walk from my hotel, which made it incredibly convenient. I ended up stopping by five times in seven days!

They offer a huge variety of pizza slices, and every time you order, they pop your slice into the oven to warm it up. While most of the time the result was delicious, a couple of slices came out slightly overcooked with a hard, dark crust. Still, the flavors kept me coming back.

My favorites were the pepperoni, beef, sausage, and bacon slice—loaded with meat and great flavor. I also tried the sausage with peppers and onions, which was generously piled with sausage and made for a hearty bite. Their cheese pizza was another standout—simple, classic, and satisfying.

My granddaughter ordered the fettuccine Alfredo one night, and she raved about it, calling it the best she’s ever had. It came with a side of garlic bread that hit the spot.

Prices were reasonable: a cheese slice ran about $4–$5, and my combo of a meat-heavy slice with a can of Coke was around $9–$10. They also offer a full Italian menu, which we only began to explore.

Seating is limited, with a small indoor counter and a few tables outside under a covered sidewalk space. Unfortunately, the tables weren’t always the cleanest, and garbage sometimes piled up—definitely something they could improve.

All that said, the fast service, solid food, and unbeatable location made this a reliable and tasty option. Not perfect, but definitely worth a visit if you're staying nearby.
