name: Joe's Pizza
document: Joe's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
I just had to share my amazing experience at Joe’s Pizza — it truly exceeded all my expectations!

From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm, lively, and welcoming. The staff greeted me with genuine smiles and were incredibly friendly and attentive throughout my visit. It’s clear they take pride not just in their food but in making customers feel valued and comfortable.

Now let’s talk about the pizza — absolutely phenomenal. The crust was perfectly crisp on the outside while staying soft and chewy inside. The sauce had that rich, balanced flavor that tastes fresh and homemade, and the cheese was melted to perfection with just the right stretch in every bite. Every slice was packed with flavor, and you can really tell they use high-quality ingredients.

Service was fast and efficient even though the place was busy, which says a lot about how well the team works together. The staff were patient, helpful with recommendations, and made the whole experience even better.

If you’re looking for authentic, delicious pizza served by a team that genuinely cares, Joe’s Pizza is a must-visit. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly recommend

Joe’s Pizza (Broadway) is undeniably one of New York’s classic pizza institutions and often one of the first recommendations for anyone visiting the city. Whether you’re grabbing a quick slice or ordering a whole pie, it’s a convenient and iconic stop.

The prices remain reasonable, especially considering the location and popularity. However, be prepared for long queues—waiting times can easily range from 30 to 45 minutes, and sometimes even up to an hour. The line does move, but occasionally slower than expected.

Their classic cheese, Margherita, and pepperoni slices are the clear favorites—simple, well-executed, and consistently satisfying. Inside, you’ll also find plenty of photos featuring celebrities and famous visitors, which adds to the nostalgic charm and history of the place.

While there are certainly other pizza spots in New York that may offer more innovative or elevated flavors, Joe’s stands out for its legacy, convenience, and reliability. It’s less about being the absolute “best” and more about experiencing a true NYC staple.

Definitely worth adding to your to-do list when visiting New York—especially if you want a taste of pizza history.

FANTASTIC low cost pizza!!! This it's my one must hit place in new york and I'm so glad I did. The pizza is affordable and it's light, crispy and delicious. There is definitely a wait to get in, but it's all part of the New York experience!!! I will say that their deep dish pizza was not my favorite and I would not get that again. However, if I return to New York I would definitely, make it a point to go here again.  The staff is friendly and the amount of pizza that they turn out is unreal!!! There is limited seating, so don't be upset if you don't get a seat.

A Simple but Outstanding Classic New York Slice.
One of NYC’s most popular pizza spots, known for its thin, crispy crust topped with rich tomato sauce and plenty of cheese. Slices start at around $4.50, making it an easy and satisfying choice.

Just steps from Times Square and open from morning until late night, it’s a perfect stop anytime you’re craving real New York pizza!

name: Nolita Pizza
document: Nolita Pizza. cuisine: Pizza Gluten-Free Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
I stopped by this little slice of heaven on a weeknight after an event, around 8:30 or 9 p.m. The place wasn’t too crowded, which was perfect. I ordered at the counter, and the staff was incredibly friendly — she told me to grab a seat, and she’d bring the pizza over once it was ready.

The menu had several tempting options, but I went with two slices: a deep-dish square spicy pepperoni and a burrata with basil slice. The burrata came out first, and it was absolutely divine — the thin, crispy crust topped generously with fresh burrata, olive oil, and basil. The ingredients tasted so fresh that it truly elevated the whole experience. I’d highly recommend this one — you don’t often find burrata pizza done this well.

Next came the deep-dish spicy pepperoni, which was massive and indulgent. The slice was thick, heavy, and loaded with spicy, flavorful pepperoni — they definitely didn’t skimp on toppings. One slice alone would’ve been enough, but it was so good I couldn’t resist finishing both.

By the end, I was stuffed but completely satisfied. The best part? The whole meal cost just $11 including tax, which felt like a steal for the quality. It’s a cozy, affordable, and genuinely delicious spot — highly recommend it, and I’ll definitely be back!

Thin crust perfection with a smile!
It’s a fantastic spot for thin crust pizza lovers. The pizzas are light, crispy, and full of flavour, easily among the best in Little Italy. What makes the experience even better is the friendly and welcoming customer service. Staff are warm, quick, and genuinely caring. A must-visit for great pizza and good vibes.

I’ve walked by this place so many times and never went in. Today I was nearby, just wanted one slice, so I finally tried it — and I’m so glad I did.

The owner was incredibly friendly and proud of his craft. He showed me how he treats the dough — three full days of work, not your quick mix-and-bake. You can taste the effort in every bite. The sauce, the texture, everything was just right.

Yeah, the slice is a little small and the price a bit high, but it was totally worth it. One slice was enough for lunch, and honestly, one of the best I’ve had this year.

I tried the honey pizza and added vodka sauce on top — unreal combo. The dough was airy and crisp, cooked with love, and the homemade honey gave it that perfect sweet-spicy kick. The cheese and burrata tied it all together.

It’s a real celebration of flavor — bold, balanced, and addictive in the best way.
Go try it and tell me what you think.

EVERYONE needs to try this. It’s fantastic. Shout out to Elizabeth our server she was incredible, 10/10 service, 10/10 dinner, please go eat here.

Great dinner. Had the crab dip as a starter and then the baked Tuscany. Both were delicious. The mango berry sangria was savory as well. Will try the pizza next time I go back. Friendly service. Pink Squirrel cocktail is very refreshing and smooth. The pizza was very good too. Definitely fresh. Had the lasagna and bada bing shrimp, both were absolutely delicious. Weekly specials are a hit as well.

Perfect lunch spot during a hot midweek walkabout. Dropped in for the pizza and salad lunch special - which can't be beat for $10...and ended up ordering some of the very best, crunchiest onion rings I've ever eaten. Michaela provided excellent, attentive service, rounding out an overall great lunch. Couldn't have chosen better today.

The waiters here are incredibly friendly and helpful, they always checked in to see if we needed anything. They have dinner specials that sounded appetizing, and I was indecisive on what to get because everything seemed good to try. I don’t usually eat pizza because I don’t like the taste, but these ones blew me away! I could not stop stealing a slice or two from my friends, They are so delicious!

name: Song E Napule
document: Song E Napule. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Food was not great. The Caprese salad was not salted, so it was difficult to appreciate umami flavor of the tomatoes. The buffalo milk mozzarella had a sour taste, and I suspect it has gone bad, though our server explained it is supposed to have a tang. The basil leaves were added on top as a decorative bunch and not torn, so there was no basil flavor in the salad. Arugula seemed out of place in a Caprese.

The octopus in tomato sauce with capers and olives was flavorful, though it had a fishy smell and may not be the most fresh.

The two pizzas had large black burnt areas  that were bitter.

The fancy-looking olive oil on the table smells like paint thinner.
Finally find some authentic Napoli pizza in the city. It brings me back to Italy and London when good pizza is served hot and fresh. Definitely recommend it if you are a big fan of thin pizza.

A bustling spot for Neapolitan style pizza with energetic service and a huge menu that offers tons of options. We tried four pizzas: a calzone, a pistachio pizza, a truffle pizza, and a burrata pizza. The truffle pizza was the standout with its rich, umami flavor, and the burrata pizza was also very enjoyable, even if a bit tricky to share. The pistachio and calzone were decent, just not as memorable.
Great Neapolitan pizza and the gnocchi were also really good. The ambiance isn't bad, but the side is very tight so people bump into your table and chair, and it's very loud.

When we ask for the bill and waiting someone to take the payment, the guy ( I believe was the owner’s son ) he came at the table clapping hands like are you paying and give me the table back or what? So disrespectful. Pizza was amazing

name: Upside Pizza
document: Upside Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Decent pizza, maybe a little overpriced but not that much. If you're a cheese slice kind of person, try their spicy vodka, it's mellow and more fun. I also had the olive pie which could have used more acid somehow.

Quick and easy slice of NYC pizza. Their Spicy Vodka slice might be the best in the city. Crust is on the heavier and drier side.

Priced same as most other NYC pizza slices. Must go for their Vodka slice but you can skip the others

Grabbed a slice from this location as a snack. Location is pretty small (this is NYC), so you'll likely be getting this to go and eat elsewhere.
Plenty of different types of pies to try, so you do have options for even a picky eater. Staff was pretty nice on a rainy Sunday when i stopped in.
The Sicilian Pepperoni was a bit spicy (to me); may have been due to all the other pizza I was eating. I'd go back to try some of their other pies to see what I might like.
If you're in the area totally worth stopping in for a bite.

I went here on a whim looking for a quick slice of pizza. Turned out to be one of the best I’ve ever had. I tried the square pepperoni slice which was a thick square with crispy pepperoni on top. Along the edges of the slice were crispy cheese edges from the pan that melted in your mouth as you took a bite. The real star of the show was the spicy vodka pizza. Not only was your classic thin crispy New York slice executed perfectly but the sauce on top was out of this world. The sweetness of the sauce was enough to get you going and the spice was not too overpowering but just enough to give you that tang. The dough was super thin, not floppy, and a crispy but chewy crust. I would eat this pizza everyday if I could. Did I mention it only took them around 15 minutes for them to make a whole pie. Upside pizza was the most pleasant surprise of my evening and I would honestly choose this place over any sit down restaurant.

I work across the street, and have been coming to upside pizza for a long time. It's a true New York slice, thin, crispy and tasty. Their pepperoni Sicilian is amazing, but the belle of the ball to me is mushroom slice. The mushroom slice is thin, with a good  ratio of different cheeses, sauce and crust. They place a few small tables on the sidewalk, for patrons to dine at. Upside is good spot for the tourists, locals and the people that work in the city

name: Lombardi's Pizza
document: Lombardi's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Had Lombardi's suggested to me, as a place worth visiting while in the Big Apple. So we headed over there for a bite to eat, stepped in and it was like stepping back in time! The interior decor and vibe of the whole place, was brilliant and gave off such an oldy-worldy feel. As it states, it's been going since 1905 and was America's first pizzeria. With visiting during the week, and earlier on during the day, there were plenty of seats available. We were served by a very pleasant gentleman, ordered a root beer that tasted super and we decided on the 'Meatball, Ricotta, Garlic' pizza. When it arrived, it had a lovely crunchy crust all the way around, with plenty of ricotta and meatballs on top. Super hot and super tasty, a pizza that was delicious from the first bite, right down to the very last. If I remember right, it came to a little over $30 - maybe a bit more, including the tip - but was more than worth it without a doubt!

To be able to visit the America's first pizzeria was experience my fiance and I would never forget. We were seated right away and the service was quick. The meatballs and pizza was fantastic! I wish we had Lombardi's in Georgia!

Apparently this is the first pizza place in America, so we had to try the dish they’re famous for. We ordered half of their signature pizza and half of a different one so we could sample both.

I personally wasn’t a big fan of the signature pizza as the flavor was a bit too sour for my taste but the “regular” cheese and pepperoni was really good. I also loved how crunchy the crust was. Overall, a cool spot to try for the history and the variety.

Lombardi’s Pizza absolutely lives up to its legendary reputation. From the moment you walk in, you feel the history—this place is pure New York. The coal-fired brick oven gives the pizza that perfect balance of a crisp, slightly charred crust with a soft, chewy center that’s hard to beat.
The margherita pizza is outstanding: fresh mozzarella, bright tomato sauce, fragrant basil, and just the right amount of olive oil. Every bite tastes simple, intentional, and perfectly executed. The clam pie is also a must-try—savory, garlicky, and loaded with flavor without being heavy.
The pizza are a bit small, but great to eat. The only small complaint was we did not finish our pizzas and had to ask 4 times to get them to-go.
Service is friendly and efficient, even when it’s busy, and the atmosphere feels authentic and unpretentious—exactly what you want from an iconic NYC pizzeria. This isn’t trendy pizza; it’s timeless pizza.
If you want to experience real New York pizza history done right, Lombardi’s is a must-visit. I’d come back again and again.

Lombardi’s is a classic New York City spot that’s definitely worth the visit. The pizza has a great old-school feel with a solid crust, rich sauce, and quality cheese. You can really taste the history and tradition in every slice. The atmosphere is lively and authentic, making it a great place to sit down and enjoy a real NYC pizza experience. I’d absolutely come back again.

name: Lucia Pizza
document: Lucia Pizza. cuisine: Pizza Salad Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Blackened chicken fettuccine Alfredo was the best I ever had. Asked them to add blackened chicken to the fettuccine Alfredo and I loved it! Wife and children enjoyed the pizza and ziti. Highly recommend! Called and placed order. It was ready when we arrived. Pickup and tap to pay was quick and easy too.

We had a great experience at this local Italian restaurant in Herndon. The place was clean and cozy, and our waitress was very nice and attentive. The food was delicious—especially the pasta, which is always our first choice. Everything was well prepared and tasted fresh, definitely a step above what you'd get at a chain restaurant.

They also have a good selection of beverages, from non-alcoholic drinks to wines and cocktails. And the desserts? Amazing! Plenty of great options to end the meal on a sweet note. It's not the cheapest place around, but it's also not fancy expensive—just a solid spot for a nice Italian meal.

I absolutely had to leave a review to give this family-owned business the credit it deserves. For those in search of an authentic Italian restaurant that brings community charm and modesty, look no further. I have been in search of a local quality cheese pie for YEARS. I prefer a robust sauce above all else. This did NOT disappoint. I don't know what tomatoes/sauce they use but it legitimately brought me back to tomato flavors when visiting Sicily. My entire family (3 generations worth) said this made their weekend, and I couldn't agree more. I cannot wait to come back and try their other offerings. Please show this place some more love.

Absolutely LOVED. We stopped by when we were in town for a work trip, absolutely the best food we had in Herndon. We ordered the Linguine con Gamberi and the Tortellini al Tino. They were so flavorful and creamy! Highly recommend. We will definitely be coming back!!!

Our first visit to Lucia’s Italian Ristorante in Herndon was a great experience. We tried the meatball sandwich and the turkey sandwich, and both were fresh, flavorful. The atmosphere was welcoming and the service was friendly. We really enjoyed it and definitely recommend it.

google_reviews.text:

Dipping sauce was cold for the garlic knots.

Perfect pizza and incredibly tasty vodka penne pasta. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and cooked just right. The portions were great and the overall experience was excellent. Highly recommend this place

Best I've had on Manhattan.  Definitely up there with Joe's.  Ordered a slice and it was so good, I had to go back and order another!

Margherita slice was also great!

Was in Manhattan for several days attending to the passing of my sister and having relocated from NY to Florida I was in desperate need for a NY slice. I'm a plain cheese guy so I ordered one slice to start as a test. I knew after one bite a second slice was in order. Great balance of tasty sauce and cheese cooked to perfection, nice crisp crust, great undercarriage, no flop. The following day I brought my two grown kids with me, they ordered the Pepperoni/Ricotta/Hot Honey slice which they said was excellent. All the pies on display looked delicious and picture perfect in every way. My only regret was I didn't have time to get back there one more time before I had to head back home. And kudos to the pizza maker, a master and culinary artist. The best Pizza I've had in several years. Outstanding!

I was awaiting a scrumptious slice of pizza on my way home from work. So I stopped at Pizza Masters, a brilliant name for a pizza place. However, I was greeted by a long wait with employees who were overtired. The pizza was like cardboard, however, the Anacini’s were incredible!
If you like the 67 meme then you should oil up this pizza place’s floor.
Follow up, why is this place called Brooklyn Pizza Masters when it is located in the Manhatta?

name: MAMA'S TOO!
document: MAMA'S TOO!. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Manhattan. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We were looking for some comforting pizza and went here - the lines were long- not sure coz it was a Saturday? though it moved fast. The service was fast. Ordered 3 slices of pizza, the thin crust being the best. The cacio e Pepe was way too salty which rendered it inedible! The vodka sauce pizza was flavorful. Overall did not enjoy the place much, as not a fan of thick crust pizza - personal preference and the crust was not very yummy.

Mama’s Too near Christopher Street subway stop was absolutely packed to standing room only because of the holiday rush, so we grabbed our slices to go. Even with the crowd, the pizza was hot, tasty and perfect for a quick bite. Thick, crispy square slices with strong flavors and great textures held up really well on the walk. Busy spot, but totally worth it if you are nearby and want excellent pizza fast (we still had to wait 20-25mins)

No line, decent number of guests inside. All but two tables taken. The crust was good, crispy, but most places in NY do a good crust. Rarely is that their downfall. The sauce was mediocre. The angry nona, which claims to have multiple spicy ingredients was a bit to sweet (hot honey) and had no kick. The house vodka slice was cold…and too heavy on the sauce. Maybe that would have been better if it were hot though? Unclear. Handfuls of better pizza in the city. I wouldn’t waste my time or dollar here. They also don’t have chili flakes which is just strange. The service was fine, nothing bad, nothing great.

We went around 9ish, place had line out the door.  Earlier in the day they had good lunch crowd.  Timing is everything.  After 9, wanted some sandwiches.  We had they were really good.  Unfortunately after standing in line and getting to the counter to order, we tried to order and informed us they were out of sandwiches.  That was  disappointing,  but we quickly ordered the square pizzas. Glad we did.  They aren't your New York style thin but are thicker crisp crust with great toppings.  It was challenging to get a table,  limited seating.  Place your order and you hope someone is finishing up and about to leave and swoop in to get a table. We will go back for the sandwiches,  but if they are out the pizza are delicious alternatives.

Best. Pizza. Slice. I’ve. Had.

I’ve been dreaming of going to this place since the wife and I planned a NYC stop on our trip. I’ve seen it everywhere and knowing we both love Detroit style, this was a must visit.

We were shocked to see the line didn’t go outside on this Saturday night. Maybe it was because the Bills were playing the Broncos and it went to overtime? Either way, we were lucky to not have to wait that long.

The server actually approached us before we got to the counter and we ordered 2 Angry Nonna & 1 Upside Down slices. We waited about 10-15 minutes.

Once we received the slices we knew this was going to not disappoint. The perfect textured crust and the aesthetics alone were enough to set a very high bar. Now onto the taste.

Phenomenal execution of the crust. The crunch could be heard throughout the entire restaurant.

Each of the three slices we had were consistently great with the crunch & abundantly flavorful sauce. The sauce is my favorite part and the bread/crust is my wife’s favorite. To see that this pizza married those two favorites of ours perfectly - made this experience unforgettable.

I’m now making it a tradition to go to Mama Too’s every time I’m in NYC.

name: BarDough
document: BarDough. cuisine: Bars Pizza New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: BarDough was a fantastic first-time experience. The pizza was excellent — great flavor, perfectly crisp crust, and really fresh toppings. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, with a friendly vibe that made it easy to relax and enjoy the meal. The staff were just as great — super nice and attentive without being overbearing. Overall, an awesome spot for pizza and a place I’d definitely come back to.

We couldn’t decide where to eat but then found BarDough, and we are so glad we did! It was decorated for spooky season which we absolutely loved! We started with five garlic knots on happy hour ($1 per) which were so good! I ordered a pepperoni pizza and loved it. My wife ordered the penne alla vodka with grilled chicken which was delicious!

Great food and fantastic service with a playlist that was vibes. I highly recommend paying them a visit!

Update: October 2025
I went back and the pizza was just as good. This time I had a garden Grove pizza and my friend had the truffle pie. They're pizza here is incredible!!!

I went before seeing Operation Mincemeat on Broadway. I met up with my friend and we sat at the bar. I was too late, but I recommend their happy hour for $1 garlic knots and cheap drinks. The interior is more high end than I expected. Our bartender was new, but you'd never know. She was super sweet and helpful.

We got the garlic knots to start and I can't shutup about the cacio pepe dipping sauce. Our pizza made in the on-site brick oven was incredible. Crunchy crust, herby pesto, stretchy cheese, and tangy sauce.

The downstairs bathroom was adorably wholesome covered in cute stickers. It looked like a clean dive bar bathroom in a kid's TV show.

I found my new spot before shows. I need to come back!! 😀

We were so lucky to find this incredible restaurant in an unassuming location in restaurant row. We have three family members with dietary restrictions, and they were able to easily and knowledgeably accommodate both gluten and dairy allergies. The pizza was incredible, and the happy hour deals were great. I really enjoyed the sauce and the inferno pizza with dairy-free cheese. My partner loved a gluten-free version of the ricotta sauce pizza, and my kids both enjoyed a margherita pizza (one gluten-free, one regular crust). The 12-in pizza was much larger than expected, I should have taken leftovers but it was too delicious to stop. Highly recommend, if we lived in the city, we would be here often. Very reasonable price for the high level of quality, service, and really well crafted atmosphere.

Super recommended pizza spot! First of all, the overall ambience and vibe of the place are super nice. The pizzas are big, and most important: they are DELICIOUS! Service was very attentive and friendly. A must visit spot!

name: Scarr's Pizza
document: Scarr's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza Beer Bar Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Get here early! We arrived a few minutes before they opened and there was already a line.

The people who work here are superhuman. They move so quickly and efficiently even though there isn’t much room. It’s dazzling to watch them make pies, throw things in the oven, and cut slices.

We got the vodka pesto, original, and Sicilian hotboi slices. The original was simple and just right. Good sauce-to-cheese ratio, thickness, and taste. The other slices were also amazing. No regrets, no notes. One of the best slices I’ve had in the city.

Saw some reviews say that you can only sit if you order a full pie. We were able to sit at the bar with just slices, so YMMV.

Pizzas were delicious and what I expected from NY pizza with the nice crust. The plain slice was perfect but the hot slice was a bit greasy/soggy that the dough tore apart a bit when I lifted it.

Service was quick since I went for lunch. However, they assumed I wanted a medium size beer when I wanted the small glass.

Also, this restaurant has changed since the last time I went. It's been a while. Now, you either order takeout or dine in with waiter service. Back then, you can just order at the counter and eat it inside without waiter service. It is awkward that to dine in a pizza joint that comes with waiter service, though it is also unfeasible to do takeout during the winter, yet they serve the pizza slices on paper plates. Some restaurants should not be waiter service. Feels like they just want to make a few extra dollars making it waiter service so that more people will give tip money. It should be the old format: order standing up, get your slices of pizza, sit at a table without waiter service, finish in 5 minutes and leave. It's so awkward to have this kind of environment at a pizza joint.

This pizza was pretty excellent, and the classic embodiment of what you think of as a 'New York slice'
I got the beef pepperoni as my NY-style slice, and the mushroom as the Sicilian-style slice here

They were both very good, but I'll start with the NY slice first
What was the most noticeable here was how good the crust was. It was very cracker-like, maybe the most cooked undercarriage I've seen on pizza, without being burnt. It perfectly exemplifies the term "well-charred". I thought I preferred softer crusts to harder ones, but after having had this slice, it's definitely the opposite for me - once I realized how good a crust like this could be.

Aside from the crust, the rest of this slice was also fantastic. The blend of cheese and sauce on the top tastes great, especially those bits where you see the browned cheese on top. The pepperoni was also super consistent; basically every piece was able to curl up into a cup on top

The Sicilian style pizza was also nice. The dough was way more airy and softer here, but it worked as a different type of pizza. The part that I liked slightly less was that it was a bit sloppy as not all the toppings stayed on throughout, and I preferred the level of cook in the other slice, but the softer taste was a nice change of pace.

For the price, each slice cost me around $5, which is not *super* cheap, but when you consider that these are a) meat/special slices and b) quite large, I will take that deal

Overall, if people ask me where to find a great New York-style slice, this will be the first place I point to. 9/10

We were in town Super Bowl Sunday, there was a decent crowd in there. But I loved that we were still able to get a table.
We shared a slice of the hotboi pizza because we were already going around trying all kinds of food that day. But that pizza was amazing and it was actually spicy which I loved. They also have cocktails and I got the canned cocktail which was pretty good too.
The music and the vibes were fun, I'd definitely go back when I'm in NYC.

Scarr’s Pizza in the Lower East Side definitely lives up to the hype. The pizza has a really nice char on the crust  not too soggy, not too firm  just that perfect NYC balance. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients in every bite.
There can be a bit of a wait, but the line moves quickly and is worth it once you get your slice. The only small downside is that they don’t have fountain soda, which is kind of a New York pizzeria staple. The seating area looks nice, but I chose not to sit because there was quite a bit of smoke in the dining room coming from the ovens.
Overall, great pizza and worth the stop if you’re in the area  just maybe grab your slice to go.

document: Mimi’s Pizza - Broadway. cuisine: Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: I’ve been on the hunt for the best cheese slice in NYC and came across this place on the way home one day. Great crust, delicious flavors, classic and original topping combinations with friendly quick service, and good prices. This has become my go-to spot when heading out of town as it is a quick stop off of the west side highway with easy parking right on broadway.

Pizza was awesome. Thin crispy crust. Perfect blend of sauce and cheese just how I like my pizza. Service was quick even with a line. They keep everything moving like a well oiled machine. Definitely coming back when im in the area. No flop jalops over here.

We stopped by this Pizza place for the first time. We ordered a mushroom pizza with truffle oil and a square buffalo chicken. it was crunchy & delicious! The prices are also fairly reasonable. The gentleman who took our order explained what they have in the menu very well and it was excellent. We highly recommend this Pizza place!

Mimi’s Pizza on Broadway is a true NYC gem. The pizza is classic New York style—thin crust, perfectly crispy, and full of flavor. I tried a slice of pepperoni and one of margherita, and both were excellent. You can tell they use fresh ingredients, and the sauce has just the right balance of sweetness and spice.

The place has a cozy, no-frills vibe, exactly what you’d expect from a good local pizzeria. Service was quick and friendly, even during a busy lunch hour. Prices are reasonable, especially for the quality you get.

Whether you’re grabbing a quick slice or sitting down for a casual meal, Mimi’s delivers the kind of pizza experience that reminds you why New York is famous for it. Highly recommended if you’re in the area!

Stopped in here tonight for a couple of slices. Solid choice.  Pizza was good.  Crispy thin crust with a nice sauce and cheese.  The Sicilian slices looked good too and I’ll be back to try a few of those. Service was friendly and fast.  Could have sat inside but chose to take it to go.    Definitely one of the better pizza places on the UWS.

document: Rosa's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Stumbled upon this spot four years ago in Brooklyn after a comedy show and it was so amazing that we came back after all this time on our most recent trip to New York. Just as great as I remembered! Vodka Mozarella and margarita were both killer—get a side of vodka sauce to dip your slice in if you’re feeling saucy.

Note: limited seating inside, so be prepared if it’s cold to eat outside or take it to go!

Funny how serendipity works…a flat bike tire landed me right by Rosa’s, a pizzeria I’d only been to once before but remembered fondly.

This time, over a Vodka slice and a Buffalo Chicken slice (with a little help from the busy but friendly crew behind the counter), I finally put my finger on it: the pizza here is just plain delicious. Fresh cheese, generous toppings, and slices that practically melt in your mouth.

Definitely not the paper-thin New York style…these slices fill you up, and then some.

Thanks Rosa’s… already looking forward to the next visit. 💗
Very nice people and cozy atmosphere. 2 vegan slice options. So tasty!! Best slice I’ve had in NYC. Great pricing too!

One of the best slices I’ve ever had
The cheese, the sauce, the olive oil everything is on the spot
This is the pizza to go
Don’t go to the overrated spot the serve you dry pizza with a little bit of cheese
This is the spot to go!!!
Excellent top notch pizza, sauce is like crack. I got the pepperoni sicilian square. Wow. Just do it, go there without hesitation, even if the line is out the door. Line goes quick yo!

name: Sweet Rehab
document: Sweet Rehab. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Desserts Patisserie/Cake Shop. located in Manhattan. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Sweet Rehab just recently opened in my neighborhood.  It is a French patisserie.  I ordered a cappuccino with natural honey and took home a vanilla eclair.  C'était absolument agréable!

So happy the second location is finally open! Sweet Rehab has been a favorite for years — always perfect for an after-meal dessert and tea. Tina and Ismail are the sweetest hosts. Truly, the night wouldn’t have been the same without this place!

This is the second Sweet Rehab location (original is in SoHo). It has a ramp with railing outside if the step is too high. There are maybe 4 seats in the back. We had the le miel with orange blossom, pistachio, and praline. The staff are very friendly. Many are from France, which comes through in the viennoiserie. I’d recommend this bakery if you’re looking for something really special, fresh, and possibly large enough to share with a few people for a special occasion. I might skip the chocolate chip cookies but I’ll need to return for the brownie croissant.

This is Sweet Rehab’s second location, fresh on the upper east side! Located on 87th, it’s a luxurious and delicious pastry and tea bar. I love Paris in Blue, all fruit pastries like the signature raspberry and pistachio tart, plus the chocolate chip cookies. Most of all, John Vasquez is an absolute sweetheart :)

If you live uptown you already know that Sweet Rehab on 87th Street is a destination. The pastries are delicious, stunning, and decorated like little works of art. Everything tastes unbelievable. The price point is on the higher side but completely worth it. Choosing a favorite is almost impossible because I genuinely love them all.

name: AlimamaTea
document: AlimamaTea. cuisine: Desserts Donuts Coffee & Tea. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I waited to try a mochi donut until I could get one from Alimama Tea because I heard they were really good. They’re also naturally gluten-free because mochi is derived from rice flour. If you’re used to a more conventional NY donut, this will take you by surprise in the best way: it’s chewy, not too sweet, and pairs well with the very aesthetic teas. I had the brûlée donut, which was delish but very gently flavored, and I think my NY instincts still wanted something a little sweeter—but that’s on me because I actually wanted the frosted strawberry mochi donut or the crumbly topped cereal donut, but I was trying to be sophisticated when I know I am not. Next time I’ll get a donut with a little something extra on the top and I think that will hit the perfect balance of sweetness for me!

I was floored and amazed at the flavor, freshness and quality of the mochi donut; this was absolutely delicious.  Alimama is a MUST try.  We did the six pack of mochi donuts and the brown sugar boba cream puff all of it a 10/10!!!

Hokkaido milk cream puff for only $1, and black sesame mochi donut that tastes like 芝麻糊 (black sesame paste)… this tiny store in Chinatown has totally won me over.

I’ve tasted a lot of cream puffs around NYC, but Alimama Tea wins for their perfect choux and flavor lineup. Their cream puffs were huge irl, and the custard-to-choux pastry ratio was done right.

＊Cream Puff $4.50 - 5.50
I couldn’t stop munching on the yuzu one, so tart and refreshing with a yuzu curd filling. The boba flavor was not too sweet and packed with mini boba. Matcha was the winner (as always).

＊Mochi Donut  $4.50 - 5.50
The roasted black sesame glaze was rich, nutty, and pleasantly grainy. It reminded me of chinese black sesame paste dessert which I loved.

What surprised me most was the strawberry flavor. It didn’t taste artificial at all, unlike the ones I’ve had at other donut spots.

The brulee donut was coated in a caramelized sugar glaze that left a gold shimmer on my lips. Their mochi donuts had a dense yet chewy texture.

＊Hokkaido Custard Mini Cream Puff $1 each (min. 6 pcs)
Despite their small size, they didn’t skimp on the filling! Each one was packed with luscious, creamy custard made from Hokkaido milk, all wrapped in a crispy shell.

＊Lychee Rose $7
While I had higher expectations for their sweets, this lychee rose drink actually blew me away! I didn’t even ask for less sugar, but the sweetness level was just right. It was made with lychee purée, coconut water, rose, and topped with real lychee. The boba scene is competitive in Chinatown, but I’d come back just for this drink.

Yuzu cream puff was such a tasty treat! The tart citrus cream filling inside was a great contrast with the sweet and crisp outside crust. Service was quick and friendly. Shop is tiny, maybe 5 or so seats lined up against the wall.

I’ve been wanting to come here for some time. Everything was delicious. I got the Vietnamese cold brew, the Hokkaido brûlée mini cream puffs, and taro munchkins. This place is must visit. I’ll come back. I want to try some other things.

name: Mojo Desserts
document: Mojo Desserts. cuisine: Desserts Chocolatiers & Shops. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This was my first time going to a mousse shop. My husband & I are chocolate lovers so this was a decadent treat. I purchase the white chocolate mousse with salted caramel pearls. While my husband stuck to the fan favorite dark chocolate 70. Our server was awesome as he talked with us about  the history of the  restaurant.  We even discussed recommendations for us to visit Belgium.

Super cute ambiance, delicious dessert! It’s a unique spot and really wonderful. I love that it has mousse as the focus (can’t wait to also try the hot cocoa!) — it’s something different than the “same old” for dessert. Connected to a bar, but I didn’t try that this go around. Really worth the visit! I had the hazelnut praline and it was incredible! Light, fluffy and full of flavor. They also have various sizes of Mousse, so you could pick up a big one to serve at home for a dinner party. Also, the founder’s story is really cool (American Dream!!!). Loved it & we will be back!

Finally ! A place where I can get my mousse au chocolat fix.. I am very exigent when it comes to desserts, especially that I am used to French desserts that are one of the finest in the world.
I took the dark chocolate mousse and that was exactly what would heaven desserts taste like. The balance of cocoa flavor was perfect, and the main ingredients are imported from Belgium obviously.
The chocolate mousse was VERY light and has perfect airy consistency.
Will visit again soon !

Mousse lover paradise! Felt like I’m in Belgium again with their mousses! So good and delicious!

Location: It is located in Upper East Side 100th St. near Mt Sinai Hospital. Due to covid, I can’t come inside the store, but they will re-open soon. I ordered by the door with the owner.

Service: the owner was super nice, the store wasn’t open yet but he took my order.

Food: I bought all the 5 flavors and everything was good. Their mousses are velvety, silky smooth and perfect amount of sweetness. My FAVE FLAVORS are: DARK CHOCOLATE, HAZELNUT PRALINE, WHITE CHOCO and MATCHA. Least favorite: PASSION FRUIT: not a fan, taste like chemical and grainy. Just get the other flavors!

Price rating: 8/10, a little pricey, really small cup for $4.

Definitely will come back to get the 4 flavors I ordered but not passion fruit! Lol

Stopped by MOJO today with my kids. Oliver gave us an amazing experience. He was incredibly kind and professional. Also sweet with my kids. The dark chocolate and passion fruit were my faves. Though the kids liked white chocolate. Thanks for the great service, Oliver.

name: Yingtao
document: Yingtao. cuisine: Chinese Wine Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Yingtao continues to be the crown jewel of Chinese fine dining in NYC. The new menu by Chef Emily Yuen is phenomenal.
Each dish in the Tasting Menu was thoughtfully balanced. The Black Cod with fermented bean and pickled greens was a masterclass in texture and savory depth. I also loved the Plum Duck—the kumquat and red dates added a refreshing sweetness that rounded out the dish perfectly. For dessert, the Nian Gao with walnut and lime was a creative and delightful ending.
If you are looking for an elevated take on traditional flavors, this is the place. The optional wine pairing ($100) was also very well-curated and enhanced the meal significantly. Truly a 1-star experience that lives up to the hype!

From the moment I walked into Yingtao, I knew this experience was going to be special. I loved being greeted by the entire staff when I entered, and the service and hospitality were genuinely some of the best I have experienced anywhere in the city.

I came in feeling curious and a little unsure of what to expect, but I have been wanting to try Yingtao for a while and I am so glad I finally did. Every single dish was thoughtfully curated with unique flavors that paired and blended together beautifully. The progression of the courses was incredible. Each dish somehow got better than the last, which I honestly did not think was possible. Every course had me finishing the plate completely, which says everything about how good the food was.

The atmosphere truly sets the tone for the entire experience. It is moody, cozy, and effortlessly cool, perfectly preparing you for the incredible flavors to come. Watching the chefs work in the open kitchen was also a highlight. It was calm, precise, and impressively quiet, unlike other open kitchens I have experienced. You could hardly hear anything, and it was clear the team was working in perfect sync to have dishes come out smoothly and on time.

We opted for the non-alcoholic pairing with the courses and were completely blown away. You can tell an incredible amount of thought and energy went into crafting those drinks. Each one was carefully designed to balance and complement the dish it was paired with, which elevated the entire meal.

I was also told that the menu changes quite frequently, which makes me even more excited to come back and try their other creations. The bar area looks amazing as well, and they mentioned you can order some of the same dishes à la carte there. I will definitely be back for a more casual night out with drinks.

I completely understand how Yingtao earned its Michelin star in 2024. This place is absolutely worth experiencing, and I highly recommend it. Do not hesitate to book. It will be well worth it.

One of the best dinners I’ve ever had in the city. My family loved it and can’t stop talking about the food. Definitely bringing others back. Chef Emily’s new menu is impeccable and went above and beyond my expectations.

If you’re dairy allergic, think twice—surprisingly, this Michelin one-star Chinese restaurant couldn’t adjust anything, even though most Chinese main dishes rarely use dairy.
The replacement beef was really tasty.
The plating looked amazing!
The staff seem unhappy after I told them beef was too salty.
Service:poor
Food:good

Please note that this was entirely my personal experience. I do hope Yingtao continues refining and improving - there’s potential.

Service:
Two tables that arrived after us were seated first, which made me wonder whether the table settings hadn’t been properly prepared in advance.

There were small handoff issues - we were asked twice what water we wanted, and it took about 15 minutes for someone to confirm our wine order/add-ons. Including the wait to be seated, we didn’t receive our first course until 7:30pm.

The course component introductions felt stiff, almost like they weren’t fully memorized yet, and there was no guidance on how the chef suggested each dish be enjoyed😅

The space itself felt slightly at odds with the food - an odd smell near the entrance, and a constant draft blowing directly at us from the far-right counter seat. Not sure if this was a kitchen design issue or overall layout problem. There was also a physical discomfort element: the server brushed into my shoulder multiple times throughout the meal, which made the counter seating arrangement feel even worse.

Food:
Overall, it felt like there was too much time between plating and serving. Other than the cold dishes and the wonton broth, most of the hot courses lacked actual heat. A few plates were also noticeably inconsistent in presentation.

Hamachi: Fresh. Paired with watermelon radish, pear shreds, and sweet bean sauce - a fairly interesting combination.

Lo Mai Gai: The stuffed wing format is a full score visually - beautifully presented. I liked the sticky rice and Chinese sausage filling. It’s actually not easy to make a hand-held course look refined instead of messy.

Wonton: Major disappointment. I love soup, but the broth was overwhelmingly salty, almost undrinkable. The filling tasted like ground pork and tiger shrimp blended together - I couldn’t actually taste any shrimp presence, and the texture wasn’t great either.

Fried Chicken add-on: Basically the Peking Duck wrapper swapped for a taco and roast duck replaced with fried chicken. My partner asked, “How is the chicken different from Popeyes?” I honestly didn’t know how to answer.

Black Cod: One of the dishes I liked more. I loved the plating and structure - cod layered over soft tofu with a mildly spicy fermented bean sauce. Unfortunately, the cod felt slightly overcooked.

Plum Duck: Two preparations. The “pure” version had uneven doneness - cooked on the sides, under in the center. The crispy version was better and paired nicely with kumquat and honey glaze.

Dessert 1 – Mandarin: A mandarin that I’m still not sure what it was trying to do…The jelly topping had no flavor, and beyond the not-sweet fruit, there was even bitterness from the pith.

Dessert 2 – Nian Gao: The dessert was placed in front of me an hour and a half before we actually ate it. By the time we got to it, the rice cake had completely hardened. It unfortunately exposed staffing and pacing issues pretty clearly. We finished all seven courses at around 9:00pm.

We came to support it under the Michelin Chinese fine dining name, but left feeling there’s still a long way to go. Compared horizontally with other one-star restaurants, there are noticeable gaps.

name: Lady M Cake Boutique
document: Lady M Cake Boutique. cuisine: Desserts Bakeries Custom Cakes. located in Manhattan. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
They are truly beautiful cafe located inside the Galleria mall.

1. Expensive spot and bright, instagrammable decor. 2 cakes and 1 drink and 1 chocolate will cost you $60!

2. Cakes: I have always liked crepe cake and they at least taste decent now but still very expensive for a very small slice: $12.

3. Drinks: tea and coffee selection is good.

4. Service: 1 star at best. We have been there 30 mins and he wouldn't bring our water! like wth! How are we to eat cakes without even a drop of water.

5. Stand in line to order but they will bring it to you to your table and has the audacity to demand tips!

Again, i like this place but their service and business practice is truly not right.

Our family ordered a cake from Lady M online. When it arrived, the cake box was slightly open, the inner plastic wrap was torn, the cake was exposed inside the paper box, and crumbs were spilled along the side. I reported this to customer support.
Nina, the Assistant Manager, responded quickly but simply issued a $15 partial refund and filed a report with FedEx—without discussing or confirming anything with us first. It has now been five days, and we still have not received the refund.
I am very disappointed with how this was handled. The cakes are delicious, but their customer service does not match the quality of their brand.

Very disappointing experience. The cake we purchased was clearly not fresh and tasted like it had been sitting out for days. The texture was dry and the flavor was off. For the price they charge, I expected much better quality. Definitely won’t be coming back.

When you only make one thing it has to be good.  These crepe cakes are absolutely beautiful and taste as good as they look.  They do just make the one thing but they have a range of different flavors available by the slice, or the whole cake.  I had the Dubai Chocolate version and was fantastic.  They do have coffee and hot tea to go with the cakes as well.  I was only in town for 4 days and may have come back and had the pistachio version as well.  That may have also been amazing.  Trip to this mall is worth it even if you only had a slice of cake from Lady M.

Lady M at Tysons Corner is a must-try dessert spot! 🍰✨ Their mille crêpe cakes are super light, creamy, and taste amazing. The shop is clean, elegant, and the service is polite and quick. Prices are a bit higher, but the quality and presentation make it worth it. Perfect for a sweet treat or special occasion! 😍💯

name: Messy Donuts
document: Messy Donuts. cuisine: Donuts Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Messy Donuts is a mini donut shop located in a little pop up section right on the same street as K-Town. The store has no indoor seating, but uses its space effectively to advertise.

The staff was friendly and able to explain how their store works. It is a bit loud due to it being right off the street, but staff were friendly and understanding.

We got a mix of donuts, with toppings like strawberries and other things. They were fluffy and not too overwhelming, and overall tasted quite good with a mix of toppings.

Overall, a nice spot to visit if you want a quick treat.

These mini donuts are unreal. I could use these for snack during work hours, except I don't work around here, so that's a disappointment.

Anyways, one order of the mini donuts, they are super customizable and if you need help picking and choosing flavors and toppings, the staff member can provide suggestions and pairings. I got the Ube and Pistachio and they both taste great, especially when they're freshly made and warm.

I've also tried the Strawberry Covered Chocolates and those strawberries were massive. The problem with massive strawberries is eating them. If I had a knife, I could cut them into smaller pieces as eating them on a skewer stick got really messy. Also the strawberry itself overpowered any of the chocolate taste, so it didn't balance well in terms of taste. For sure favored the milk chocolate over the dark chocolate.
Such a great time time loved the desserts and would definitely recommend anyone coming to enjoy great donuts and shaved ice cream! Check out my video on IG with them @JadaExploresAll!!!

document: La Maison du Chocolat - Rockefeller. cuisine: Chocolatiers & Shops. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
This was our first time visiting this French chocolate shop and we were blown away by the beautiful interior, the divine looking chocolates, and the attentive and knowledgeable staff. The variety of chocolates and other items available are impressive. Edible works of art and extremely high quality. You taste it with just that one small bite.
We left with some praline sticks and a praline assortment, and much more.
How great to know I can place an order online for our now favorite chocolates!
We liked everything we purchased and cannot wait to try more. Anything here would make a wonderful gift for any chocolate lover.
I highly recommend a stop in and the staff was wonderful and helpful.

It is a small indulgence that’s absolutely worth it. Yes, it’s a bit pricey, but the quality and balance of flavors justify every bite. The chocolates are elegant and not overly sweet, letting the cacao shine. My favorite is the plain truffle—simple, rich, and perfectly smooth, with no distractions. It’s the kind of treat you savor slowly rather than rush through.

I’m usually a fan of the hot chocolate here, but this time it tasted a bit burned and slightly bitter

That said, I’ll still keep coming back because the service is wonderful. The gentleman here is incredibly polite and takes such great care of us
it honestly reminds me of Parisian hospitality

The King Bread (Galette des Rois) at Patisserie Vanessa is absolutely delightful. The pastry is beautifully flaky and buttery, with perfectly crisp layers that give way to a rich, smooth almond filling. It’s not overly sweet, which makes it feel refined and authentically French.

You can really taste the quality of the ingredients and the care in the baking. It pairs perfectly with coffee and makes for such a special seasonal treat.

If you’re a fan of classic French pastries, this one is definitely worth trying — I’ll be coming back for it again next season. 🇫🇷👑🥐

Every year for my partner’s birthday, I search for weeks to find a cake that feels special—authentic, artisan, and far from big industrial chains. This year, I discovered La Charlotte at Pâtisserie Vanessa, and it was worth it. Looks elegant and the taste is amazing. Deep, rich chocolate without being too sweet, a crispy heart, and a light, airy texture from the ladyfingers boudoir. I highly recommend pairing it with a scoop of whipped cream or vanilla ice cream to balance the intensity of the chocolate fondant. Professional staff, cozy space, and fair pricing. A satisfying experience.

Just okay overall. I stopped in on my way to the 4 train to try a few sweet treats and left feeling a bit underwhelmed. The woman at the counter recommended the raspberry pastry — it was very soft, but the filling had a flavor and texture that felt a bit off to me. I also tried the marble loaf, which was dense and tasted somewhat artificial; I usually prefer a lighter, more moist cake with a larger crumb.

That said, the interior is lovely — very Parisian café vibes with a charming upstairs seating area that makes it a nice place to sit for a few minutes. Overall, cute spot but the pastries didn’t quite live up to the look.

A Parisian vibe. The pastries were delicious. And beautiful. Very classic and clean. Quiche was good but the salad wasn’t that good. It’s a lovely place. Staff could be more friendly. I know it’s hard to work in this industry, but  you’re dealing with people. But I want to go back and try different things.

document: Rosetta Bakery. cuisine: Bakeries Coffee & Tea Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 3.6 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Fantastic Find: Great Coffee, Food, and Vibe!
​We had such a wonderful visit here. The location is incredibly convenient, but the true standout is the overall quality. From the moment you walk in, the ambiance is great—cozy yet lively. I highly recommend the pastries (freshly baked and delicious!) and the main food menu is just as good. Coupled with expertly made coffee, this place offers everything you need for a perfect morning or afternoon break. Five stars!

Staff was great but personally I feel it overpriced. I got the Margherita flatbread and spicy Prosciutto. Flavor was there but wish the dough would've been more crispy. Got a connoli which was enjoyable and a mini Nutella cup looking thing which was $4 and was not worth it. Cappucino was designed with a 🐻 and tasted amazing. Lots of pastries on display that looked incredible. Maybe I'll come back and try those

From the moment you walk into Rosetta Bakery, you can tell it’s more than just another café—it’s a vibrant New York stop that brings authentic Italian bakery vibes straight to the Upper West Side. Whether you’re grabbing breakfast before work, meeting a friend for coffee, or stopping by for a savory lunch, this place consistently delivers delicious food, great drinks, and a welcoming atmosphere.  ￼

First things first: the menu here is wonderfully varied. On the sweet side, the pastries are the real stars. Their pistachio croissant and pistachio donut are standouts that strike the perfect balance between buttery flakiness and rich flavor—ideal with a morning espresso or cappuccino. Fruit tarts, raspberry and pistachio combinations, and almond croissants round out a selection that feels both traditional and exciting.  ￼

But this bakery isn’t all sweets. Rosetta also serves hearty breakfast and lunch options that are genuinely satisfying. The egg dishes are fresh and flavorful, perfect fuel for a busy day. On the lunch side, the turkey and prosciutto sandwiches are generous and well-made, and their breakfast/lunch pizzas hit just the right savory notes when you want something a bit heartier.  ￼

The coffee program here deserves its own mention. The espresso and cappuccinos are expertly brewed—smooth but bold enough to stand up to a sweet pastry. It’s the kind of coffee that feels as good lingering over a table with a friend as it does in your hand while you’re walking out the door.  ￼

One of my favorite things about Rosetta is the atmosphere. Natural light fills the space, bouncing off clean white surfaces and making it feel airy and bright. The seating areas are comfortable and well-laid-out, giving you plenty of room whether you’re working on a laptop, enjoying a casual meal, or catching up with friends. Even during peak times, the vibe stays relaxed and pleasant.  ￼

The staff here are friendly and efficient. While it can get busy—especially during morning rushes and weekend afternoons—the team keeps things moving and is always happy to help with recommendations or questions about the menu.  ￼

If there’s one thing to note, it’s that some items can feel a bit pricey compared to your average bakery or café. But for the quality of the ingredients, the presentation of the food, and the overall experience, most visitors find it well worth the cost.  ￼

All in all, Rosetta Bakery is a gem in the city. Whether you live nearby or are just passing through, it’s worth stopping in for a coffee and pastry or a full meal. Warm, welcoming, and undeniably delicious—this bakery has quickly become one of my go-to spots in NYC. Highly recommended!

Rosetta Bakery is a wonderful place! It’s very clean, the staff are friendly, and there’s a wide variety of delicious sweets and sandwiches. The cappuccino was fantastic — they use Julius Meinl coffee, which adds a great touch. Prices are quite affordable — we paid about $30 for one cappuccino and three sweets, which is very reasonable for the area. I wish I could have stayed inside to enjoy it, but we had to head home since it was getting late. I’ll definitely come back next time I’m around Times Square!

A true European bakery! Everything was incredibly fresh, delicious, and beautifully presented. It was a feast for both the eyes and the palate. From the pastries to the coffee, every detail reflects quality and authenticity.

The atmosphere is cozy and elegant, and the staff is always warm and welcoming. It truly feels like stepping into a small bakery somewhere in Europe. We would be so happy if Rosetta Bakery opened in our city as well — these amazing flavors deserve to reach more people! 👏💫

Tried the small Aztec hot chocolate, flavor was good, though $8 for a small cup feels a bit pricey. Dine-in requires a reservation. The store itself is very cute, they sell a nice variety of chocolates, and the staff friendly. Would like to come back and try other hot chocolate flavors.

Such a lovely spot! I had their Aztec-style hot chocolate, and it was absolutely delicious — rich, smooth, and comforting. The service is sincere and kind, and I really appreciate that they let you take your time to enjoy without any rush or pressure to leave. The decor is classy and elegant, especially during the Christmas season — so festive and cozy! I came here solo and felt completely comfortable and relaxed. A perfect place to unwind in SoHo.

This wasn't my first time visiting this delightful cafe. It's a kingdom of chocolate and cocoa! You feel like you're inside a jewel box. A friendly waiter immediately brings you a tiny glass of cocoa, which you can sample while you read the menu. Everything was delicious – the cocoa, the quiche, and the pastries. The waiters are very polite and efficient. You can buy chocolate and candies in the front part of the establishment.

I must say the experience was amazing here . Johnny the trouble maker was knowledgeable about chocolate and gave recommendations on what to order .  Most of the chocolate drinks are 66% -68% of real cacao . Did you know that they import chocolate from Honduras , Columbia and Ecuador .The dark chocolate drink I ordered wasn’t sweet but the whipped cream balanced the flavor . You can definitely taste the richness of the cacao. We ordered the chocolate lava cake . The richness of the chocolate dessert went well with the vanilla cream and strawberries, the flavors complemented well with each other . I’m going to come here again with my mother next time .

name: Té Company
document: Té Company. cuisine: Tea Rooms. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Loved this little spot with a fantastic tea selection. The interior is clean and sophisticated, and despite the small size, it feels cozy and comfortable.
The staff are friendly and attentive.
I especially enjoyed the tea flight, which lets you sample several varieties, and they offer a similar option for small bites.
A really enjoyable experience.

Long overdue review! The service is always super friendly and thoughtful, whether you’re dining in or grabbing something to go. Today was a great example—there were no seats available so I ordered to-go, and one of the tea baristas remembered something I had asked about earlier and even wrote it down for me. Such a sweet and thoughtful touch! And of course, the bite-size snacks are a must 😄

My favorite tea shop in the city, the tea selection is great and the biscuits and pastries are perfect for pairing with them. It’s a bit expensive but the quality is there. The ambiance is calming and decor is nice too.

It’s our pleasure to be here at Té Company! A small but lovely Taiwanese tea house located in the West Village. Taiwanese high mountain oolong tea, is well known as the best tea in the world. All products of Té Company come from Taiwan, a high-quality tea producing country. It is a pleasure to taste high-quality tea in this lovely space on weekends. We waited for more than an hour to get a seat, but it was worth it. The traditional Taiwanese dessert egg yolk cake is delicious with tea. A staff, he is very friendly, kindly helped us pour tea and answer the  questions of the tea. We will definitely come back!

I enjoy the tea flight, it’s a good way to try new tea. We often buy one of the teas if we really like it.

However, the brewing time for the second and third steeping is not precise, so these are usually over steeped and bitter. Regardless of how much they try to be precise with time, inevitably the staff gets held up by other tasks, and the flight is ruined. This is the only thing that stops us from coming back more often.

I suggest getting small timers and strainers so customers can pour their own steeps to ensure that the time is precise and the tea is not ruined.

google_reviews.text: Hands down the BEST chocolate chip cookies you will EVER eat! Gooey, soft in the middle, melts in your mouth. The perfect Chocolate Chip cookies. Recommend getting the smaller chipper one for the best cookie. Will definitely keep coming back for any occasion.

I came here for the very first time and thought the place was the cutest.

When we entered the place, the gentleman did not greet us, no pleasantries by any means. I was taking pictures and videos of the place and stated to my mother which cookie I would like. We decided to get 3 cookies, which we  split them with each other. We ordered the Chocolate Chip, the Smores cookie, and the Cookie Butter Cookie. They smelled absolutely heavenly.

Once it was time to pay the cashier who was given money in their hand, he thought it was a great idea to place the money on top of the box instead of my mother's hand the same way she gave it to him. I observed the transaction and stated never again would I come to an establishment where we did not feel welcomed, no pleasantries, and money given on a box and not your hand.

In my opinion, the 3 cookies we ordered were absolutely delicious. I love how they were hard on the outside but soft on the inside. The cookies themselves weren't hard as bricks but hard in a sense of freshness and soft and gooey on the inside. Again, the cookies smelled heavenly, and I definitely thought these are some of the best cookies I've had in a long while.

I would visit again if the customer service was better. The cookies are delicious but a little on the pricier end.

This place is very unassuming but their cookies are really good. Super thick and gooey with just the right amount of crunch. My girlfriend and I came in and got the Brookie and it was amazing! I wholeheartedly recommend checking this place out if you like cookies.

Discovered this location and stopped ina do I must say it was a pleasant experience! The two you ladies both greeted me and walked me through the different variety of cookies they had to offer —also shared their personal favorites and why, my cookie selection was a great one - I enjoyed my cranberry white chocolate cookie! They also have weekly features! The establishment was very clean and welcoming and definitely worth a visit next time you are in the area or just to come by and grab a delicious cookie or two! The cookies are very moist and filled with delicious types of chocolates - they even have an oatmeal cookie!

We heard about their cookies several years ago but it was not easy for us to go to New York for the cookies especially during the pandemic, so we ordered on line to give them a try and really liked them.
Recently we found out that they have a new branch around DC, so we wanted to see if they were as good as we remembered, or was it the $100 price tag for overnight shipping.
We already knew how delicious their cookies were so we grabbed 6 cookies.
The fresh cookies are much better than the frozen ones and you can eat them immediately.
We are so glad to have this store much closer to us now.
We would highly recommend going and getting some especially as they have weekly cookies coming out. So there should always be a new one out to try. We love the cookie butter one.

name: HARBS SoHo
document: HARBS SoHo. cuisine: Bakeries Coffee & Tea Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A bakery that stays true to its Japanese roots, delivering light, fluffy cakes with just the right touch of sweetness. Every flavor shines, and the variety of textures makes each bite enjoyable and thoughtfully crafted. The cappuccino is impressively done as well—smooth, aromatic, and the perfect companion to the cakes. Staff very friendly and helpful.

I just love Harbs! I am a Japan style fan and they do it like that. The price fixe set comes with salad, main dish (either pasta or sandwich) today’s cake (strawberry cake is delicious & a must have if you like strawberries) it also includes a cup of coffee or black tea for $28-30.
My kids and I usually get the lemon & Parmigiano pasta with the prix fixe. A La carte is also available, fresh cake, a quiet enough environment for a good conversation or a date.

Food was excellent.  Prices were a little high but not too bad.  Portions were great even the prix fixe that we had came with a good size, and very tasty, salad, plentiful main course and a reasonable size of cake.  Tea was lovely, disappointing to me the tea was not a refill but the water was free flowing and never allowed to get empty!  The Japanese washlets in the bathrooms are fantastic and I still cannot believe they are not everywhere!

This was my first time trying Korean pastries, and overall it was a nice discovery. While it’s not necessarily my favorite type of pastry, I did enjoy what I tried and found the flavors interesting and well executed.

That said, the experience felt a bit restrictive. If you choose to eat on site, each person is required to order something, and considering the relatively high prices, that felt a bit disappointing. The pastries were good, but not exceptional enough to fully justify the price point in my opinion.

The atmosphere was rather cold and not very cozy, but the biggest positive was definitely the kindness of the staff, who were very pleasant and welcoming.

Overall, a decent experience for discovering Korean pastries, but not a must-visit for me.

Must try!! Expensive spot, for a cake and a tea you pay around 30$ including tip. However!! Well worth it!
If you hesitate, I can assure you, go try it! It is delicious!! Try the fresh fruit cake, Mille crepe or just anything really. My fav is the grape jasmine tea in a pot

google_reviews.text: Very clean, well maintained space. We had a wonderful time with calm and adorable furry friends. We wish we had more time to get to know each of them! As a cat parent myself, I was kind of hoping to get more information on how to adopt them during our visit, but they all seem to be very comfortable living there as a while family and made us think that maybe it’s better for them to stay with each other…there’s a little dilemma! But it’s definitely a happy place for both kitties and cat lovers and we are happy for them too.

Had an amazing time! The staff members wwre very friendly, and very knowledgeable about each cat and their needs. The snacks sold were great, and the drinks were all delicious. The true draw was definitely the cats. (If it wasn’t for allergies and already having multiple pets at home I would have certainly come home with a few new family members). Looking forward to an opportunity to go back!

It was super easy to get a Cattery reservation here! The cafe has delicious food, cute merch, and the staff is very kind. You can tell that they are very knowledgeable about cats and care about what they do.
There are three separate spaces where you can interact with the cats, including an outdoor space, and the cats move between those freely.

It’s a really nice space, there are two levels and the kitties are free to travel to both places. It was a little crowded however , so there wasn’t much opportunity to play with the kitties and they were sleeping so peacefully . But they are sweet cats and I will definitely go back maybe at a different time and day.

Clean, well-managed gem on the LES. Cats are docile and expertly cared for. I love that they have the option to migrate to the back room if they get tired of mingling. Matcha was very good too. Note it's a $3 upcharge for matcha drinks if you get the $25 hour + free drink package.

The menu has a number of sweets like crepes and bubble waffles, where you can pick the drizzles and toppings like icecream or chocolate sauce. We got the waffle stick because honestly my friend was already too full but we just wanted to feel something inside.

document: Ddobar. cuisine: Bars Korean. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Dining at Ddobar was a delightful experience, elevated by warm hospitality and thoughtful service. The overall menu was well-executed, though the standout for me was the trio of Yubu Tarts, which offered a refined and elegant progression of flavors. 😋The Earl Grey ice cream was an inventive concept, yet the salt tended to overshadow the subtle yet prominent tea notes. The sake pairing recommended by the sous chef was exceptional and complemented the dishes beautifully, adding depth to the overall experience. The complimentary macarons were a gracious and memorable finishing touch. While the cuisine itself may not redefine expectations, it is best appreciated alongside their excellent sake selection and impeccable service!!

9/10

DDOBAR NYC is an absolute knockout. Chef Jiho Kim's spot turned our large party of nearly 20 into a seamless celebration

They accommodated us like pros, rolling out an outstanding set menu that had everyone raving

Flavors were incredible, layered and bold. Had some surprise specials that blew us away (that duck pastrami/sushi piece? Phenomenal)

Everything tasted so damn good, fresh and precise

The ice cream finale was outstanding.. creamy, perfectly balanced, light yet so refreshing

Service was warm and on point the whole night. Highly recommend this spot. Excited to go back!

DDOBAR is the definition of a hidden gem! Tucked away inside Olly Olly Market, this concept comes from the talented team behind the Michelin-starred Joomak Banjum. The $55 set menu is an unbelievable steal, offering value that far surpasses the price point. It’s a massive bargain and worth far more than what’s cost. The food quality was superb, with thoughtful seasoning and presentation that truly hit the spot.

Charcoal 🐶 also enjoyed here since olly olly market is dog friendly! We’ll definitely be back for the main chef tasting set

Really great experience.  Took care of a big group like we were VIPs and made it feel very special.  The food was fantastic with really creative choices.  Definitely on the list to head back there the next time in NYC.

This is not your typical omakase experience – inspired by korean yubu (fried tofu pockets), Michelin-starred chef Jiho Kim brings a fresh perspective to the format with two inventive tasting menus at DDO BAR, all centered around yubu tarts.

We chose the 13-course yubu tasting menu at $75. From the creativity and attention to detail to the use of premium ingredients, every course felt thoughtful and refined that it was hard to pick a favorite. The menu also had a good ratio of raw and cooked toppings.

Most importantly, the pacing was just right—we never felt rushed, which made the whole experience even more enjoyable. It’s a great spot for a casual date night or a relaxed catch-up with friends.

As a bagel lover, I was impressed to see their reimagined Smoked Salmon with Everything Bagel into yubu!

The Hiramasa was an indulgent bite, generously crowned with caviar for that extra touch of luxury.

My friend couldn’t stop raving about the Scallop, finished with a drizzle of brown butter dashi.

Moving forward to some special and unexpected toppings: The Duck Pastrami was a standout with its smoky and peppery taste. The sweet Korean Beef Tartare reminded me of bulgogi. While the Pork Belly with Mushroom Pickle, served with a piece of lettuce, felt like a playful nod to kbbq.

But what really caught us off guard in the best way were the desserts. The Earl Grey Soft Serve sprinkled with sea salt might just be the BEST dessert I’ve ever had, and the portion was generous. It was rich with tea flavor even by my standard, subtly savory.

Our server also surprised us with mini coconut treats. At that point, we both agreed they’ve truly mastered the art of dessert.
