Food: I ordered classic tea and taro.. both of them taste like water to be honest. I don’t taste any taro or milk tea. It was so sad. The boba was okay. Little bit hard already.

Price rating: I paid 17 bucks for 2 large bubble teas with mount sinai discount.

1.0 ★☆☆☆☆ An Absolute Scam - The Worst Bubble Tea I've Ever Had

I rarely write reviews this scathing, but this establishment deserves every single critical word. This wasn't just a bad experience; it was a complete and utter scam that insults the very idea of what bubble tea should be.

My wife and I, avid bubble tea lovers, were looking for a treat. Google Maps, in its infinite wisdom, suggested this dump with a seemingly impressive 4.3-star rating. I now believe those stars are as artificial as the ingredients in their so-called "drinks."

My wife ordered a strawberry tea that tasted like the runoff from a cheap fruit yogurt mixed with tap water. I got the mango tea, and it was as if they emptied a packet of discount "fruit drink" powder into a cup and called it a day. There was no trace of milk, creaminess, or any natural flavor—everything we love about good boba was completely absent. This wasn't subpar; it was a concentrated, watery GARBAGE.

The "tapioca" pearls were the final insult. They weren't the soft, chewy, sweet balls we know. They were stale, rubbery, flavorless blobs that felt like they'd been sitting in a vat for a week.

For this chemical assault on our taste buds, we were robbed of TWENTY DOLLARS. This isn't a price point; it's daylight robbery.

To crown this circus of incompetence, the staff member decided our transaction was the perfect time for a personal phone call on speakerphone. We had to stand there and wait while she finished her conversation, with zero acknowledgment or apology. The sheer disrespect and unprofessionalism were the perfect cherry on top of this disgusting sundae.

Verdict: The absolute WORST BUBBLE TEA EXPERIENCE OF MY LIFE. A place that murders any love for the drink, poisons you with chemicals, and spits in your face with their service. One star is infinitely too generous. AVOID THIS TRAP FOR FOOLS AT ALL COSTS.

9/10. The mango milk tea and strawberry milk tea were amazing. I prefer the strawberry over mango but both were good. Very fast and great service. There are only three tables and there weren't many people when we were there. There isn't a bathroom so it's a little inconvenient for people who want to sit and drink and stay there for a while.

The boba teas are entirely customizable in terms of flavor, level of sweetness and choice of toppings.
Because the cups have a snap-on cover (and not a plastic seal as in other boba shops), contents may leak if taking things to go.

I got a milk tea with boba, and idk what in the world they did, but it had the nastiest bitter flavor I’ve ever had half way through every sip. I couldn’t even drink it and tossed it. I truly can’t imagine what ingredient could be causing this. I’ve had bubble tea hundreds of times, and the milk teas a classic. Such a bummer. I fully rated it as my worst drink on Beli, you couldn’t pay me to drink it.

Spot is my favorite dessert place!

They consistently serve delicious desserts, and the variety is impressive. Everything I’ve tried has been great so far. The items that come with the ice cream are especially good — the combinations are always creative and flavorful.

Every time I visit, choosing what to order is part of the fun because there are so many tempting options. The coffee drinks are excellent as well and pair perfectly with the desserts.

It’s also a great spot for a weekend evening date.
Highly recommended.

I wasn’t sure what to expect at Spot Dessert Bar East Village, but it turned into one of my favorite dessert stops. I tried a few of their signature items like the Matcha Lava Cake, Mango Sticky Rice Crepe, and a Thai Tea Boba Float, and everything was fun and delicious. The Matcha Lava Cake was warm with a gooey green tea center that wasn’t too sweet, and the flavors really popped. The Mango Sticky Rice Crepe had fresh mango with creamy coconut and soft sticky rice wrapped neatly inside, which felt unique and comforting at the same time. The Thai Tea Boba Float was refreshing and creamy with chewy boba that made it feel like dessert and drink combined. The vibe inside was colorful and lively with upbeat music, which made it feel more exciting than a typical dessert shop. The staff were friendly and helped explain the menu when I was deciding what to order. Portions were generous enough to share, and I left feeling satisfied and already thinking about what to try next time. The place also felt clean and well maintained even when a few people were waiting. It is one of those dessert spots that makes you want to come back just to try another item on the menu.

I think this place is a bit overrated. It gets busy quick and the desserts are okay. Out of all of them the matcha lava was by farrr my favorite. Very rich and the perfect amount of matcha. The harvest was not that great in my opinion and the golden toast was a little dry for my taste. Maybe I would come back for the other items but its a bit pricey.

This place has absolutely unique desserts — we’ve never tried anything like this before! We ordered two different desserts, and both were very unusual in flavor and presentation, yet incredibly delicious.

A great spot for anyone with a sweet tooth or those who enjoy trying something new. Definitely recommend!

My husband and I had the most unforgettable experience at Cannelle Patisserie on Sunday, February 1. We brought in the gender results for our future baby, and from the moment we walked in, the staff treated our little secret with so much warmth, excitement, and genuine joy.

They were thrilled to be part of our surprise and went completely above and beyond—creating the yummiest box of pastries in the color of our baby’s gender for us to open later at home. They even included the sweetest handwritten note and, to our absolute delight, a precious little pink cake. (It was a girl! 💕)

The kindness, enthusiasm, and care they showed us turned a simple bakery visit into a once-in-a-lifetime memory. We will truly never forget how special they made us feel, or how magical and delicious our gender reveal was because of them.

Thank you to the amazing team at Cannelle Patisserie for being such a joyful part of our story—we’ll be back forever and recommending you to everyone we know!

The bread is exceptional—crispy crusts, airy interiors, and full of flavor.
Their pastries and sweets are just as impressive: buttery croissants, delicate tarts, and rich, perfectly balanced desserts.

google_reviews.text: Abuelita's Desserts are True Puerto Rican desserts and pastries made by the Amazing Aizek Santiago, using his grandmother's recipes with his own spin on them! He makes the most delicious Coquito Hot Chocolate, Coquito Flan, ALL of his Guava pastries, Pan Sobao breakfast sandwich....all are Chef's Kiss!! I've tried them All and speak from experience!! He also makes Farina, Flan Cocho, in flavors reminiscent of Good Humor bars as well as other delectable flavors, also ChoCoQuito Café, and Tembleque. Just to name a few!!  You HAVE to stop in and try one of his amazing treats and transport yourself to Puerto Rico, you Won't regret it!!

I stopped for a breakfast treat. Love this place. I must come back.
I had the coquito hot chocolate. It was too sweet for me, but it tasted soooo good. The flan was perfect and so was the sandwich. I felt like a little girl eating with my Mami. They open at 7am and are not to be confused with La Fonda who they rent the space from.
Also get the guava brownie.
Just do it.

Stopped by Abuelita’s Desserts in Harlem recently and left seriously impressed. As someone who grew up in a Puerto Rican household, the food here felt like being back in my grandma’s kitchen. I had the café con leche, coquito farina, and a pan sobao sandwich.

The café con leche was exceptional — the coffee beans are imported from Puerto Rico, and it makes a huge difference. The flavor is smooth and rich, and the milk is perfectly foamy and blended so evenly that every sip hits just right. The coquito farina tasted like holiday coquito combined with the warm farina many of us woke up to as kids. The pan sobao sandwich was soft, slightly sweet, and very comforting.

As a Puerto Rican, I’m proud and grateful a place like this exists to keep our flavors, memories, and traditions going.

We heard about Abuelita’s Desserts through a mutual friend and previously tried their Strawberry Shortcake Flan Cocho and Guava cornbread. They were both amazing! So when me and my husband planned our New York trip this year, we made sure to stop by their location in Harlem. We were not disappointed!! The restaurant is inviting and has a cozy atmosphere. We ordered the Classic Farina and the Pan Sobao. The food was absolutely delicious! But my favorite was the Coquito Hot Chocolate! Heaven in a cup! We also took a Guava Brownie for the ride home. I highly recommend visiting this Puerto Rican treasure. Everything from the food to the overall experience was excellent!

I LOVE it here! Feels like home. Isaac is such a warm and humble person. The vibe alone is amazing. Every time is a great time and his food is ALWAYS delicious. He adds a nice twist to some of the dishes but all of them make you feel like your back on the island. The Coquito hot chocolate is addicting. Literally my favorite drink in the world.

I love bringing desserts back to my Grandma's. They love everything I bring them. One of my Grandma's just moved here from PR and it's nice to comfort her with food she can relate to. It's gives her that homemade feeling.

If you have a big palate, order blind! You'll enjoy everything. If your palate is small, order with confidence. Literally everything is delicious. Even if you think you might not like it.

Ordering to go is always an option but if you have time, stay for a warm conversation. My visits are therapeutic.

Membership through CashApp and/or phone offers numerous discounts, and you'll be impressed by the comfortable seating inside and outside the cafe, as well as the friendly services.

name: ICHIRAN - Times Square
document: ICHIRAN - Times Square. cuisine: Ramen Noodles Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This is always one of my go to spots to enjoy the perfect bowl of ramen. Perfect to eat at solo, but I've also visited with friends and family as well! This is a no tipping establishment and the service is as attentive as you want it to be.

Upon entry you place an order on one of the kiosks. You're given a ticket and then they assign a booth seat to you.  When you sit down you give them your ticket, they confirm your order and then they bring it to you when it's ready.  Water is self serve.

I like the have purse/bag hooks under your booth and place to hang up your jacket on the walls. Food is always consistent! I usually go with the recommendations notated on the kiosk for levels of heat, garlic, firmness of noodles. Love a jammy soft boiled egg, be aware you have to peel this when you receive it.

They do a pretty brisk take out service as well.  Join the rewards program if you plan to frequent. I'm a fan!!!

Great spot if you’re craving a focused, no-frills ramen experience in the middle of Times Square. The tonkotsu broth is rich, smooth, and consistently flavorful, and the customization sheet makes it easy to get the bowl exactly how you like it. Noodles had a great texture, and everything came out hot and well-prepared.

The individual booths are perfect if you want a quick, quiet meal despite the busy location. Service is efficient and streamlined. It can get crowded, especially at peak hours, and prices are a bit higher than some other ramen spots—but that’s expected for Times Square. Overall, a reliable choice for quality ramen when you’re in the area.

Exceptional ramen that tastes like the authentic version in Japan, located in the heart of city. Had the opportunity to taste Ichiran numerous times in Japan, and to the best of my taste bud ability, it’s almost identical. Even though they have around 65 seats available, be sure to wait a little bit if you come dine after 12:30 as there was a long line while we left. You order and pay ahead at the kiosk before being sitting at your very own tiny seating. When the shades open up, provide the server your ticket and your meal be be ready soon. Everything felt so fast and efficient, compared to the traditional sit down experience. No tipping required as they follow the Japan culture. The broth is super flavorful and pure liquid joy! Can’t go wrong dining here during the cold brutal winter months in NYC!

I have been to the original in Japan and this is spot on to what I had there! Rich, creamy broth with incredible noodles. You can build it how you like, adding in your favorite toppings and even order extra noodles right from your seat. The line was out the door but their system was so smooth we waited maybe 15 to 20 minutes (we were a larger group) after ordering. If you are in the area, definitely go! You won't regret it!!

One of the BEST tasting ramen I've ever had! The experience was also unmatched, I loved the authentic solo dining experience I received here. You can remove the dividers if you are sitting next to someone though. Also worth the price- this bowl was $25 after tax. It was nice to customize your bowl to your liking (you can adjust the salt, garlic, onion, spice levels, etc). It was totally worth the 30 minute wait in the snow!

document: Teppen Ramen. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Not cheap. But maybe because they’re good and authentic. We ordered chicken ramen and shoyu ramen, both of which were DELICIOUS! The chicken meat had some ginger in it and it tasted so smooth. The soya-based broth was clear and comforting. The shoyu pork ramen broth was different but also great. You can taste the meat and the bones but not too rich or overpowering. Sometimes you have a couple of slurps and you already feel full. You know what I mean? But this one is refreshing and mixed with the noodle you want to keep slurping. You can tell the high quality of meal they serve here. Service was ok. Just taking your order, bringing your meal to your table, cleaning it up, and closing it out. Not rude. But not warm either, which we didn’t mind.

Casual restaurant slightly below ground level. Clean.

The cabbage salad was super fresh and crunchy with a nice dressing. The Kyuri ipponzuke was super simple. Cucumber, sesame oil, peppers. Yum.

We also had the Char Siu Don and it was generous with the pork. Also had the Maji Teppen. Great broth and nice grilled char siu. Lots of ingredients and a ton of bean sprouts. So of you like simpler brothy ramen, this might not be for you.

I have tried Ramen spots all over NYC and Queens. I decided to try this place since I just recently relocated my work place to midtown. Nice small cozy restaurant if you plan to dine in. I walked in and ordered for lunch the Teppen Shio Ramen and it was ready in 5 minutes. The taste was very good and serving size was enough to fill you up until dinner time. Will definitely come back again for lunch.

I’ve enjoyed dining at Teppen Ramen through the years. The cold  noodle ($19.49, tax included), a seasonal offering during summer, combines mildly spicy ground pork and fresh vegetables with the noodles. The only real disappointment is that their suggested tip amounts are calculated from the taxed total.

I had dinner at Teppen with my family and we're seated right away. We ordered Ramen and some appetizers. The waitress Ploy was very nice and resourceful. She explained the dishes and what was included in our orders.The waitress Sara was also very attentive and checked in on us. The food was great especially on this cold day. We will come again and had a great experience thanks to the staff.

name: ICHIRAN Midtown
document: ICHIRAN Midtown. cuisine: Ramen Noodles Soup. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Ramen in separate seating spots where you don't have to worry about tipping - they do the order upfront and you print out, leave for your server and you don't really see anything other than hands delivering your food and you have hard fixed dividers between diners and hooks on the wall behind you - does remind me of a Tokyo Ramen shop with more people... US not ready for no staff upfront yet. The one in Times Square at least has the foldable wall so you can eat more shared with friends.

One style of ramen with varying levels of spice. 1/2 (0.5) spicy is already a bit for me and 3 is already too hot for many 10 - I can't imagine. The pork didn't really have much flavor and was too lean.

Water in the back wall you can get yourself. The matcha pudding was very heavy bitter on the matcha.

More expensive general set with the ramen and would probably pass next time here. Lines can grow quickly. The board will have green and red seats so you can tell which ones are busy and not, similar to the parking lights.

Ichiran—A Peep Show for a Noodle Fiend

Getting ready for a massive New York blizzard, I thought it prudent to fill up on some spicy ramen before this mean Nor’easter touched down.

I’d actually never heard of Ichiran (don’t judge me), but as often is the case, my stomach found this gem. I went inside and was greeted by the host/technician/ramen ambassador who walked me through the process like I was about to defuse a bomb.

I went with the Classic Tonkotsu Ramen with all the fixings—a little heavy on the broth, a bit spicy.

Then I was escorted to what can only be described as a g-rated peep show window for frisky broth.

The setup goes down like this: you sit in a tiny cubicle about the width of a small go-kart, then a bamboo half-window opens, puppeteer hands reach through to grab your ticket (a bit odd), and about five minutes later those same creepy hands deliver what I imagine eating clouds would taste like if clouds were made of noodles—piping hot and ready to be devoured.

Let me tell you about this bad boy:
pork and fixings? Legit.
Noodles? Fantastic.
Broth? What devils probably eat on their lunch breaks.

The overall experience is almost like being a perverted noodle fiend hiding in a closet with a bowl of liquid sin.

If you can get past the vaguely dystopian solo dining setup, Ichiran delivers the goods.

Highly recommended.

Hands down the best ramen I’ve had in the city. The fact that it can be personalized is a game changer.
The broth was exquisite, the noodles just right and the amount was just perfect.
In a cold day there’s nothing better than to get a ramen bowl and this place will be my go to when I’m not in a hurry.
There is always a line at all times I’ve passed by. A 15 min wait was my experience but definitely depends on how busy they are.
Honestly the whole experience is simply great.
Must try!

I was never really a fan of ramen—maybe I just never had it at the right place. But the tonkotsu ramen here was very rich and full of flavor. I actually finished the entire bowl, which I’ve never done before. Usually, noodles make me feel too heavy, but these noodles were thin and served in just the right amount, so it felt easy to eat.

The menu itself is pretty limited, with not many options or much variety in ramen. It was also a bit on the pricier side for the portion, especially since it came with only two pieces of meat. I ended up ordering extra meat on the side, but honestly, it was worth it.

I went on a rainy day, and luckily there was no line—I was seated within five minutes. I really enjoyed the experience and would definitely go back.

Ichiran was a very structured and unique experience from the moment we arrived. The process starts with waiting in line to order at the counter, and if you are buying alcohol, you are asked to show ID before placing your order. After ordering, you are assigned a booth and asked to leave your receipt on the table, and the food is then brought directly to you. Everything felt organized and efficient, even though we waited about 45 minutes to get in. Ordering itself was easy and straightforward using the iPad, which made customization simple.

The seating setup is very distinctive, with single booths designed for one person per booth. It creates a quiet, focused environment where you can really enjoy the meal without distractions. We ordered the veg ramen along with soft boiled eggs, and the food was absolutely worth the wait. The veg ramen had a deep, comforting flavor, with a well balanced broth and perfectly cooked noodles. The soft boiled eggs were cooked just right, with creamy yolks that added richness to every bite.

Overall, the experience at Ichiran felt intentional and thoughtfully designed. From the clear ordering process to the calm, private booths and even the availability of clean toilets inside, everything was convenient and well planned. It is a great place if you enjoy structure, efficiency, and high quality ramen served exactly the way you ordered it.

document: Toribro Ramen. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Had been here on a snowy evening and the ramen did complete justice. We started with chicken bao bun and kimchi as appetizers. The taste was yum but the portion was quite small for $5 each. We then got 2 spicy toribro ramen and a chicken paitan curry and rice with an additional side of spicy sauce. Both the dishes were delicious and flavorful. Due to less quantity, we had to share 3 dishes amongst 2 people for us to be full. The space is quite small and would need waiting as they don’t take reservations. Would recommend adding the spicy sauce to the broth to make it more flavorful.

Had a subpar experience for lunch on Toribro. I recognize that I came as the lunch rush was starting and maybe they were understaffed, but the service and food was lacking.

Upon entering, I was told that the only seat available was the at the bar counter closest to the door. This was during a deep freeze in NY. I understand that solo diners get bad seats, but since they were seating groups of two communally at tables inside, I was at least hoping to maybe sit communally or maybe to get moved down the bar further away from the door. Instead just got a cold attitude and sat through lunch freezing even with my down parka on.

I also was really disappointed with my gyoza order. The chef was multitasking when he flipped the gyoza from the pan to the plate. The gyoza was way off center, and he made no effort to try to center it. Moreover, the left side of the gyoza were burnt. See photo. The order already took 15-20 minutes, so I did not bother trying to ask them to remake it.

The ramen was fairly tasty. My only quibble was the sparse toppings. Really seemed like too little for the price of the dish.

Anyway, I probably should have gone to nearby EAK Ramen instead.

Solid ramen. Ordered the paitan and the deluxe mega - same signature chicken broth but the deluxe mega just has more toppings. All the main components - broth, noodles, and pork - were great. Nothing that blew me away, but all very good quality!

Arrived right at open at 530pm and glad we were the last to make the first seating because the line immediately started building up. Took 45 min for us to get our food because it’s just one guy cooking. Service was very friendly.

Really small dining area so best to finish up your meal and make way for other diners. Their chicken broth is very good and perfect during the colder months. Menu is not huge but what they do they do quite well. Food comes quite quickly and service is quick and efficient. Worth a visit if you’re in the area.

Tucked below street level, this cozy ramen spot feels like one of New York City’s hidden treasures. The space is small, with only a few tables and mostly bar seating, creating an intimate, authentic atmosphere that’s perfect for a quick pre-show meal. We went around 5 p.m. before a Broadway performance, and by the time we left an hour later, a line was already forming out the door—a clear sign of its popularity. The ramen was fantastic, with rich, flavorful broth and perfectly cooked noodles that hit all the right notes of comfort and depth. A delicious, no-frills gem that’s well worth seeking out.

The spicy tuna roll was excellent, the tuna itself was very fresh and high quality, and the roll did not have too thick of a layer of rice. We came with our 1 and 3 year old, and the staff was kind and accommodating, but they had no high chairs and the booster seats offered had no straps. If you come with a wiggly baby or toddler, expect to hold them with your arms.

New favorite ramen spot!
Ambiance (5/5): Sleek dining room with high top seating facing the windows or bar seating, or regular low seated tables. The establishment was only a third full on a random weeknight at 6:30p so it was very quiet and peaceful.
Service (5/5): Our server was manning the bar and also attending to a few tables. Since we sat at the bar, we were serviced quickly and often! She was very friendly and checked in with us at the perfect cadence. She even suggested using their special hot sauce when we were eating and it definitely elevated the meal.
There’s a dinner special of 1 ramen and 1 app for $30 (some of the options were extra $) so it only makes sense for some of the combination orders.
Pork Bao Buns (5/5): WOW, the pieces of pork were generous, thick but also super super tender. The sauce was creamy and the bun was soft/fresh. It has to be one of the best pork buns that I’ve had!
Tan Tan Ramen (5/5): Holy smokes, this is one of the best ramen I’ve had in the city!! The ramen noodles were a perfect chew and bounce which soaked up the rich sesame broth. The broth is so savory and packed with tons of flavors at once. Half soft boiled egg.
Spicy Tonkatsu (5/5): I liked my tan tan more but this ramen was equally good. Half soft boiled egg.
Second visit: The waitress remembered me!!
Tsukemen Ramen (4/5): This was a bit of a letdown compared to my first visit because: the soup was not hot enough and the thin slice of meat in the bowl was less impressive. The noodles were superb (cold as supposed to be). There's chunks of meat in the broth that were tender! Half soft boiled egg.

I am brought up with ramen being fast food so it feels a bit crazy to be paying almost $100 (incl tips) for a starter, the ramen, and a beer each for two people, but it's NYC, it is tasty, and conveniently close to my accommodation. The ribs might be my favourite.
I would consider this a treat.
Delicious! Had the lunch set Tan Tan Ramen + Spicy Tuna Roll + Gyoza. Value for money. Great ambience and service. Walk-in alone. Sat at the bar. Table for one.

name: Nishida Sho-ten
document: Nishida Sho-ten. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’ve been coming to Nishida Sho-ten on 49th Street between 1st and 2nd Avenue for the past 13 years, and it’s still one of my absolute favorite spots in New York City. I’ve been to a lot of ramen places over the years, but this one easily ranks in my top three. It has that cozy, comforting vibe that feels like home, and the food is consistently amazing.
The portions are generous, the flavors are rich, and the broths — whether you go with pork, chicken, or one of their specialties — are always deep, hearty, and full of soul. Everything on the menu is great, but a few of my personal favorites are the Black Kakuni Ramen - is one of my long-time favorites — the pork is melt-in-your-mouth tender, the black garlic oil adds such incredible depth, and the broth is so flavorful you’ll want to drink every drop. You can choose between wavy or straight noodles, but I’m partial to the wavy ones — they hold the broth perfectly. Sometimes, I even order an extra serving of noodles because it’s just that good!
The White Kakuni Ramen, the Miso Ramen! ( love it!) and Tan-tan Ramen are also fantastic! Tan-tan Ramen, which has the perfect spicy kick and that yummy ground pork with the bean sprouts.
My latest obsession is their seasonal special, the Mole Miso Ramen. I’ll admit, I was a little skeptical at first, but after the first few bites — I was hooked. The flavors are bold, rich, and unique — it’s a surprising but perfect blend that works beautifully in a ramen bowl.
The service is just as wonderful as the food. Beverly, one of the longtime servers, is incredibly friendly and always makes everyone feel welcome. She’s been there for years, and her recommendations never miss.
Over the years, I’ve met people from all over — Queens, Brooklyn, Staten Island, even visitors from other cities and
countries — who make the trip just to eat here. Once you try it, you’ll understand why. Nishida Sho-ten has a loyal community of regulars for a reason — this place is comforting, consistent, and absolutely delicious. Hands down, one of the best ramen restaurants in NYC. Highly, highly recommended!

Great ramen spot 🍜
A small, cozy, and authentic place — be ready that it’s quite tiny, but that’s exactly what creates its charm and vibe. We got lucky to find a table on a Sunday evening, which says a lot.

The service was very welcoming, and the ramen was excellent. I’m not a fan of spicy food, so I asked to tone it down and they happily adjusted it without any fuss.
Highly enjoyable experience — thank you! 😊

This little whole in the wall was amazing. I got the spicy red ramen, pork onigiri and a coke. All the food was delicious and the service was great. It was cramped inside but that is ok because the food was worth it! I would definitely return!

Fine ramen, think the 4.4 rating here is very generous. Ordered the white and black ramen, broth on each was ok but didn’t stand out in any way. The pork was unfortunately tough, and I personally didn’t enjoy so much raw diced onion as a topping. Karaage was average as well. Service is very nice though, and I loved the vibe inside.

A good ramen spot that's open nice and late! I was there at 1am on a Thursday night and the restaurant was pretty lively! The atmosphere is warm and cozy (I sat at the bar), and the service was great too.

As for the food, I got the black garlic ramen with thin noodles. The broth was definitely the star of the show. It was rich and creamy, and the distinct flavors of garlic and pork melded together to create a wonderful synergy. I really liked the broth! The noodles were good too, with the signature chew that good ramen noodles are known for. Unfortunately the pork chashu was tougher to chew than I would've liked, but at least it had great flavor. I do also wish they put another piece of bok choy in the bowl, as I thought it was a great addition. The price of the bowl wasn't bad either relative to other ramen spots in nyc ($17 for the black ramen as of this review).

Also, as someone who LOVES bidets, I was really surprised to see one in the bathroom, they're super rare in nyc!

I would recommend this spot if you love late night food. Also, If you're like me and have zero self control there's a pizza place around the corner open late where you can satisfy a completely different craving afterwards... (and then I got Popeyes even after the pizza... my cardiologist is gonna kill me! 😭)

name: Izakaya MEW
document: Izakaya MEW. cuisine: Tapas Bars Sushi Bars Izakaya. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Izakaya MEW is a cozy and lively spot that’s perfect for casual Japanese comfort food in the heart of the city. The atmosphere feels authentic and energetic, making it a great place to grab dinner with friends.

We ordered the kimchi udon, okonomiyaki, and karaage. The kimchi udon was flavorful and comforting, with a nice balance of spice and savory broth. The okonomiyaki was cooked well, topped with rich sauce and plenty of flavor in every bite. The karaage was crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, making it a standout dish at the table.

Overall, the food was satisfying and well-prepared, and the variety on the menu makes it easy to find something for everyone. Izakaya MEW is definitely worth visiting if you’re craving casual Japanese dishes in NYC.

My son and I had an enjoyable dinner here this past weekend. The ambiance and service was nice. We got there at 5pm on Saturday and the place was already packed. Luckily we had a reservation.
The food was delicious! We ordered Kimchi Cream udon, Katsu Don(not pictured), Kushiyaki Set and Toro Taku Crispy Rice. We loved the Kimchi cream udon!!! So good!
We'd definitely go back again next time when we're in NYC.

Excellent doesn't even come close.  Every thing I tried was among the best, if not the best I have had.  Couple this with a vibrant atmosphere and exceptional service make this a place where the wait is worth it!

Of note are the following: Uni Nigiri Sushi, Black Dragon Roll, Nigiri Set (an excellent choice for the less adventurous), Tan Shio, Kani Oshixushi, and the Homemade Tiramisu.

The Homemade Tiramisu is the best I have ever had, and that was the opinion of the other 6 people in our group.

A friend of mine suggested this place since he's already been before. He made a reservation for six on a Friday night. I loved the vibes and atmosphere. Everything we ordered was fantastic. They also offer some pretty fun, mocktails, perfect since many of us do not drink. Service was fast and efficient. I would definitely come back.

Really delicious food , amazing flavours. The prices were also really good for the quality of the food. If you’re looking for a fantastic Japanese restaurant that doesn’t break the bank definitely check this place out . It’s a lively atmosphere, very full and chatty in a good way .

name: Shuya
document: Shuya. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Amazing food, service as we remember when they had the restaurant in Astoria. We missed them so much so we had to go to the city and try them out. And yes, food is so delicious, fresh and on point as always! It was so good that we order another ramen to go. I wish they have the tantan dry ramen but it was not on the menu. We had the yellowtail sashimi, Brussels sprouts tempura (which is always one of my favorite), fried chicken, spicy miso ramen and shoyu ramen. All were so delicious and fresh. Keep up the amazing work. We will definitely be back again.

Update: 3.4.26- I got to try the classic shoyu ramen. It doesn’t come with corn and nori so I added them. The broth is nice but missing some flavor that the nori and corn definitely added. My chasu was fatty and slightly gummy. I wish it were more tender. The noodles were thin and tasty though. Overall a good bowl of ramen.

Party of five and the food and service was great. The fried wings were so juice and crispy. The duck tsukemen was delicious. That duck was tender. The sake was smooth and dangerously good.

great food & really nice atmosphere! The servers weren’t the nicest because they were eager for us to rush, immediately giving the check and hurriedly asking if we were done with our plates. But, we were there at 9pm which was was close to their closing time which is understandable..! I got a clam based ramen and it was alright, I would definitely recommend the spicy miso ramen instead!! The wings were also delicious

A very fantastic experience. The most impressive parts are the yuzu ramen and hand roll. The yuzu broth is quite novel (my first time tasting it!) and its freshness is very compatible with the tender chicken breast and shellfish. The hand roll is both tasty and aesthetic just like an art collection. Will definitely recommend to friends who'd like to try ramen in New York!

After my first time at Shuya, I immediately wanted to go back!  The food was phenomenal, including some of the best fried chicken and ramen I’ve had in the city.  The space is very aesthetically pleasing- with the owner supposedly handcrafting much of the furniture!  The plates, bowls and cups are also handmade and they sell them there.  Overall, a great experience and will be back!

name: IPPUDO NY
document: IPPUDO NY. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We first ordered takoyaki, edamame, and aioli chips to share, and they were honestly amazing. Everything we ordered for the table was really delicious. We tried calling to make a reservation but couldn’t get through, and if you’re a large group without a reservation, they make you wait until all your friends arrive.

My friends ordered ramen and really liked it. The portions were very generous. We also ordered buns. I tried the chicken bun and absolutely loved it. I had the Manhattan Bridge sushi. It was good, but I wish I had ordered the spicy shrimp tempura instead.

Overall, the food was tasty and enjoyable. A great spot, especially for sharing plates with friends.

Absolutely loved the food! It was amazing all of it. We got some of bao buns i had the pork and the veggie one and both was absolutely amazing! I have to highlight the veggie bao bun because it was a light crunch with the soft bun that was flavorful and delicious that i honestly would go back to NY just for this bun. Sushi was delicious and so was the ramen. the peppers we got for an appetizer were also very yummy! Everything we ate was incredible. The atmosphere was a really incredible vibe and you got to watch them make the ramen too! Definitely would go back.

Ambient ramen experience in LES! Right off Union Sq, great place for a big group of friends.

Have to say the experience of eating here is quite pleasing, but for me the food is so so. I got a pork bun, which was quite good, and the spicy miso ramen.

Though it photographed beautifully, the ramen was just okay, I found it a bit too oily and just texturally off. Wasn’t super impressed with the other flavors. Also, kind of wild to me that the soft boiled egg was an extra topping and didn’t come with it automatically. I’ve come here a few times now for the vibe and convenient location but left a bit unsatisfied.

not bad, but not as impressive as I expected. The ramen had good flavor, but the broth felt a bit lighter than the original in Japan. The noodles were nice, though the portion felt small for the price.

Service was friendly and the restaurant has a nice atmosphere, but overall, it didn’t quite capture that “wow” factor. Still, it’s a decent spot if you’re craving ramen in the city.

What can I tell you…. One of my fav ramen places. Took my kids out for a meal… had a GREAT time.

I got a special ramen that came in extra large. Apparently I was one of 2 ppl to order extra large in the past 2 - 3 months lol… I had no idea how big it was. It was frigggin enormous. I could not finish even with the help of my 16 yr old. Had to pack for home.

But good lord was it tasty. The food was on point with broth rich with flavor and melty meats. Garlic toppings, spicy flakes and  extra sauces galore. This meal was everything my boys and I needed at the end of a great day in the city.

document: Kogane Ramen-Manhattan. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Ambiance (5/5): The establishment was empty around 6p but by 7p, it was pretty filled up. I loved the decorations with the overhead flowers which were cute, welcoming, and spacious. The tables are set out with enough space between. The
Service (5/5): The staff was very friendly and welcoming. We definitely were taking our time ordering and eating, and loitering post-meal and the staff never came to rush us! We felt like we were attended to the whole experience.
Jowl Buns (5/5): Super moist and tender pieces of pork. The creaminess of the sauce blended well with the bite.
Tonkotsu Ramen (5/5): The broth was super rich and delicious, with the black garlic oil flavor in the background. The half soft boiled egg was nicely seasoned. The two large pieces of charsiu pork was a great blend of fat and meat, which gave it a really tender bite. The noodles are thin straight noodles. The mix of wood ear, scallions, seaweed for a price point of under $20.
I observed my friend eating the lobster ramen but be warned that the lobster pieces required manual maneuvering and thus a very messy experience!

My experience every time I come here is superb. The vegetable ramen has the perfect combination of veggies with just the right amount of kick. The Chicken katsu curry rice has a perfectly fried crispy chicken that is majestically paired with the curry. The Orion beer is one of my favorite beers to date. It's a smooth, non-bitter lite beer that pairs great with this food. Complimentary warm tea is usually served after the meal. Overall affordable place with great food.

We happened across this quaint little Ramen place in March of 2020, right before the city shut down for the pandemic. We loved it so much that we’ve been back to the city (from Florida) twice more and visited both times. The ramen is made fresh daily and you can tell. The service is amazing and the ramen is amazing. You can’t go wrong if you even remotely like ramen!

Literally walked by the sign and my daughter said, "Let's get Ramen!" So, I did a quick search of the reviews and bang!! We enjoyed every bite. Fair warning on the octopus 🐙 balls... they are served fresh & piping hot!! Excellent flavors all around. See pics for our choices and trust that they know how to deliver. Even the green tea 🍵 was steeped perfectly and capped off the meal perfectly. Great food & service. #LocalGem #GoodEats #theresthatfoodie #AVTeats

Just a random place to snack at after the halloween parade, it turned out to be the best ramen I've had for a long time. So surprising to drop in and this place beats all the japanese places I've been to at St Marks Pl. Ramen was not salty and very flavorful, yakitori had really good char flavor for chicken, pork belly, and also short rib. Really give this place a try. Hoping to hit this place up again next time in the city.

name: Okiboru House of Tsukemen
document: Okiboru House of Tsukemen. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We were in town for Super Bowl Sunday and basically went on a food tour. It was freezing cold so I wanted ramen.
This place was small, you can see them cooking in front of you. It reminded me of Japan.
Because we just ate, we just ordered the bao bun which was really good. The bread was light and the meat was tender. We got the fish and chicken dipping noodle and that was delicious. We got tired of dipping so we just poured the broth over the bowl. The lime & pepper made every bite perfect.
Can't wait to go back.

One of the best tsukemen spots in the city. The noodles are thick, chewy, and clearly handmade, while the dipping broth is rich, savory, and perfectly concentrated, comfort in every bite. The squeeze of lime adds a bright, surprising touch that balances the flavor beautifully.

The space is small and minimalist, more focused on the food than atmosphere, but service is quick and efficient. It’s best for solo diners or a quiet meal for two.

If you love ramen and haven’t tried tsukemen yet, start here, Okiboru sets the bar high!

Very high quality tsukemen in a small counter space. The tsukemen broth has a very strong smoked dashi with lots of concentrated katsuobushi bonito flavor. Noodles were perfectly chewy, and the lime was nice to break up the fattiness. The chasu was a little dry and could have been hotter. Also highly recommend the shrimp katsu pops to start.

Tried the tsukemen here today.
The broth is flavorful but noticeably salty, so dip lightly if you’re sensitive.
Noodles are chewy and good.
Chashu was just okay, but the fried croquette skewers were surprisingly nice.
Fast service, busy open kitchen.
Good for a quick tsukemen fix, just keep the saltiness in mind.

Incredibly delicious classic and dipping ramen. Nothing too oily, fatty, or salty. Every element cooked perfectly and all made in-house. Mimi makes the experience unforgettable with her warm personality and efficient service to keep the line moving but not make you feel rushed. Will be going back again soon!

document: Kyuramen - Union Square. cuisine: Ramen Japanese Curry. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Ordered their happy combo $30.99 today. It came with an appetizer, a bowl of ramen, a dessert and a soft drink.

I got a chicken popcorn. It was not hot enough. The chicken inside was nice, but some of them were a bit dry.

I got a bowl of Katsubushi pork ramen. The broth was a bit salty and garlicky. The flavor was nice. The pork belly is tender, but a bit fatty with skin attached. The marinated soft boiled egg was nice. The texture of the noodles was nice. It was a nice bowl of ramen.

I got lemonade, and it was a bit too sweet. It had some shredded cucumber in it. It was a bit weird in the beginning, but it was actually quite nice and refreshing.

I also got a match pudding with red beans. It was very good! It was not too sweet. I love the texture of it as well. It was dense and packed with matcha flavor.

Overall, the meal was nice. The restaurant smells a bit funky when I first walked in. The staff were nice, but I felt a bit rushed. The restaurant was like 30% capacity when I got there, but they were constantly cruising around, and take the bowl and plate away the second you rest your chopsticks.

Great spot to grab ramen. We were seated quickly and our food came out fast as well. Highly recommend the shrimp tempura for a starter, the breading was super crispy. The spicy option ordered "hot" wasn't overwhelmingly hot either, which I appreciated.

I gave kyuramen a second chance & it was a good decision. The food was absolutely amazing, I went with a group this time so we all ordered a combo b supreme combo with Thai iced tea (My favorite 😍) $54.99 for 2 bowls of ramen, drinks & dessert! We also ordered the yakitori sticks plus popcorn chicken so freaking good!! The sweet potato fries were so crunchy! I reccomend getting the ramen mild/spicy if you'd like to enhance the flavor. As someone who usually don't choose spicy the mild spice makes it taste better.  I'm still craving it. I'll defintely better back soon

Came here for lunch with a friend. We both got the $23 combo. We enjoyed the sides that came with the ramen, such as the pork bun and dumplings, but we weren’t a huge fan of the ramen itself. The meat was okay, but that was really it. The noodles and the broth didn’t have that much flavor. Even the egg tasted weird. The deserts were okay, but they also didn’t taste like anything. We honestly preferred the $1 microwave noodles. The service was okay. It took them a while to realize we were done with our food. We most likely wouldn’t come here again, or at the very least, try a different meal.

Wow! This place is amazing! My sister is visiting and I decide to choose this place. Best decision ever! The food was delicious and they even have Taiwan Beer!!! I’ve missed Taiwan so much so having it was nostalgic! Service was very nice and our server comes to our table right away!

name: Kyuramen - Times Square
document: Kyuramen - Times Square. cuisine: Ramen Desserts Soup. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Great decor with even better food! The popcorn chicken was fantastic! Fried nice and crispy with amazing spices. The ramen was full of rich flavors and a nice portion of noodles. Dessert was incredible! Not very sweet but full of flavor!

Came here on my own and got seated right away as a walk-in. I ordered a combo. The presentation of everything was really lovely. The ramen looked a bit on the smaller side but was still quite filling; the flavor was alright. The Thai tea was a little different from what I had in mind. The shrimp tempura wasn’t like the traditional Japanese style, but it was still pretty tasty in its own way. The matcha crepe cake was nice, and the matcha aroma was really pleasant. The service was warm and attentive enough. Overall, I had a nice experience, even though the ramen itself wasn’t particularly standout.

Long line but you really don’t wait very long on the line, a lot of food options and the food tasted so good with spices in front of you in case you want to add more flavor. My boyfriend got the #2 ramen which was really good but looked nothing like the pictures. I got the diced braised pork don which was extremely good and $14.99! Has a lot of food my boyfriend even wished he ordered it too! Although this took a very long time to come out. Originally my boyfriend wanted to eat with my but after 5 minutes of his ramen coming out the pork don wasn’t out yet and so he started eating without me. By the time he was almost done with his ramen the don finally came out. The Thai tea was really yummy but I wish it came with tapioca. Servers remember what u ordered and bring out the desert you ordered as soon as you finish your food. Overall I would love to come back here.

This was a late night dinner after the Broadway show. We got there on time before it got crowded. They closed late until 1:30am (Sunday). We were seated at a booth towards the back. The booth have a Japanese decor that includes a  noren at the door. They also have a call button when you are ready to order.  The food came in fast and hot. The ramen broth we ordered was savory and light. Yakitori was okay. The tonkatsu was crispy and well cooked.Banmih pork belly was just enough which was  included in the A1 combo. Overall, it was a pleasant and filling late night dinner from the Broadway. Will be one of our go to places when visit Rheather district again.  I recommend this place.

I read about the good reviews on this restaurant so I came. I went for the classic tokantsu combo. The flavors were great. My only complaint was that the ramen bowl had only two small pieces of pork. I didn't think this was sufficient.
The atmosphere is very casual.
Overall , the food was good , but not great. I would still come back here and eat again.

document: Meijin Ramen. cuisine: Ramen Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Beautiful atmosphere and delicious food! Came across this place and was not disappointed at all! Super good. Everything was a bit more expensive than my go-to place in Kips Bay but 100% worth it. The ramen was so good. Broth tasted amazing. Everything we got was perfect! Calamari, sushi all great.

I was a big fan of the seating area too. The paper cranes on the ceiling were a cool addition! Staff was also very nice. For a Saturday Lunch, there was no wait.

LOVE this place! This is my go to for great ramen and Japanese dishes. My boyfriend and I come here all the time and its one of our date night spots. Great food, great staff and amazing ambiance. Definitely come here!

One of the best ramen spots in New York 🍜. Meijin delivers rich, flavorful broth, perfectly cooked noodles, and generous portions every time. Cozy atmosphere, friendly service, and consistently amazing quality. A must-visit for ramen lovers.

Waiters camped my table of three. Usually I appreciate when a restaurant takes the time to check in on me, but for some reason today, three different waiters came to my table to ask if we were doing okay. These three did it on rotation as well, but only to our table or so it seemed. My friends and I (three girls in total) were coming to celebrate a birthday, and this happened after a long day of classes. As you can imagine, we weren’t the most dressed up. Otherwise, I don’t think we stood out too much, but it felt like we were being extra watched by the servers.

This constant attention and our conversation repeatedly being interrupted by the waiters made the meal slightly unnerving. Hence, the low score on service. Otherwise, they did a good job ensuring our time was nice with constant supply of water. To be honest, if they simply asked how we were doing while refilling the waters, I wouldn’t have minded. But it felt strange having multiple waiters go out of their way to ask us “is everything okay?” every 20 minutes. Imagine being constantly checked up on to the point where I was asking myself, should something not be okay?

Okay onto food review, I got the chicken chashu ramen, my friends got the salmon poké and spicy chicken ramen. Soup was very good! Not too salty, which is something I worry about when ordering ramen. Ramen noodle, mushroom (especially the mushroom), egg, and corn on my ramen bowl hit hard! Unfortunately, the main element, the chicken chashu was disappointing. The chicken was dry, lacked flavor, and felt a little rubbery. Portion size was amazing though.

Last miscellaneous detail service tip was set to 20%, but that might be the norm for upper east side.

Apparently the restaurant is celebrating their 10th year anniversary, so congratulations to them. Overall, nice restaurant but nothing extraordinary.
Went here for some lunch and I absolutely loved it, I got a salmon poke bowl and was t expecting anything too crazy but it was really good! It’s super cute and cozy inside too!

document: Bua Thai Ramen & Robata Grill. cuisine: Thai Ramen Vegetarian. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Had such a great experience at Bua Thai Ramen & Robata Grill on the Upper East Side. The space is really cozy and perfect for a relaxed dinner with friends.

We started with the crab rangoon and veggie dumplings, both delicious and flavorful. For drinks we tried the Pomelo Mai Thai and Berry Margarita, which were refreshing and well balanced.

For mains we had the miso veggie ramen and pineapple fried rice with shrimp, and both were excellent. The pineapple fried rice especially had great flavor and generous portions.

We finished with mango sticky rice, which was the perfect dessert.

Also worth noting — they have a huge vegetarian menu, which makes it a great spot if you’re dining with friends who have different dietary preferences.

Overall everything from the food to the atmosphere was a 10/10. Definitely a great Thai spot on the Upper East Side.

Me & my husband tried BUA Thai Ramen & Robata Grill and we fell in love. I checked YELP, google reviews and TripAdvisor before trying it and the reviews don’t lie. The location is perfect, the interior made me feel as if I were in a restaurant in Thailand and the best part was the utensils kept my food warm.   About the taste, we started with an appetizer, Vegetarian Crispy Roll (perfectly crisp on the outside and so well cooked it almost melted with every bite), and Crab Rangoon was golden, crunchy pockets filled with a rich and savory crab mixture.

For the main course, we tried Gai Tod Hat Yai which has a beautifully crisp exterior fried in oyster sauce and juicy meat, bua Thai has mastered the art of fryering ). Their Pad See-Ew was good too. They have a MASSIVE menu to choose from, ranging from seafood to chicken and beef, rice, all kinds of noodles, and cocktails and mocktails. It also happens to have Halal, gluten-free, and vegan options.   The drinks were so good, the aesthetic was just 😍 very Instagram-able. For dessert, we ordered Crepe Cake, and for drinks, we had an organic Thai mojito served in a literal coconut and a piña colada in a fresh pineapple.
They also had a statue of Ganesha & Duma and their bathrooms were too cute.

I was so impressed with the wonderful food and service at Bua Thai Ramen & Robata Grill. The food was exceptional, and I absolutely loved how fresh and flavorful everything was.
Their Tropical Cocktails were excellent, and the presentation of the food and drinks were simply stunning!
The desert tasted divine, and the staff was so friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable.
The atmosphere was so aesthetic and romantic.
I highly recommend the Pineapple Fried Rice with Shrimp and the Clay Pot Fried Rice. I absolutely loved our drinks: Bua Sangria and the Pina Colada!
I had a wonderful time, and I’d love to come back soon.

Amazing experience from the beautiful atmosphere, great hospitality to the delicious food and drinks!
I was invited to try Bua Thai Ramen & Robata Grill and this was a great opportunity to celebrate one of my good friend’s birthdays as well!

this was a a great experience, would definitely return. I was so amazed at how delicious the drinks were and how flavorful the entrees were. HIGHLY recommend trying the clay pot fried rice, i’m still thinking about it!

we got two appetizers, two entree, two drinks & 1 dessert!

appetizers- Chicken Curry Puffs (FAV) & Fried Chicken Dumplings 🥟

drinks- Pina Colada 🍍 & Melon Berry Satho 🍉(WOW)

entrees- Sweet chili salmon w/ Forbidden Brown Rice
& Clay Pot Fried Rice (I was amazed) 🍚

Just came back from Thailand a few months ago. This place really hit the spot. The flavors were so good and had the right amount of spice. Good price for the city. Appetizers drinks, main course and dessert. Was still about 150ish and we had extra toppings in the ramen. Definitely recommended.

name: Tabata Japanese Restaurant & Yakitori Bar
document: Tabata Japanese Restaurant & Yakitori Bar. cuisine: Japanese Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Ambiance (5/5): (I think some of the vibe pictures are outdated as there is no longer a bar seating that overlooks the kitchen) It is a cozy atmosphere with the wooden wall panels and brick. The space was fairly open.
Service (5/5): It was not very busy during the lunch hours so we were serviced quickly and often.
Food: There was a couple of seasonal specials posted on the wall.
Chicken Bun (5/5): The chicken came out piping hot with a classic chicken katsu breading that was flakey and seasoned wonderfully. The soft buns with the creamy sauce was very very good!
Lava Men (5/5): There was a lot of flavor and depth to the broth. The charsiu pork pieces were perfect, a great thickness with fat to meat ratio that gave it a juicy bite.
Note the soft boiled egg was actually poached and not boiled whole
Tan Tan Men (5/5) (award winning): The broth was very creamy and the noodles were perfection—chewy and thick. The chicken chunks were tender as well (Although I wish I had charsiu instead or ground pork in it). Ever so slight preference for the spicy tonkotsu ramen.

My family and I stumbled in here the other night not realizing they were closing in 30 minutes. They still sat us down and got our food out pretty quick. Not only was the service amazing, but the food was so freaking good. I’m still thinking about the pork katsu curry and my apple saketini. The pork was cooked perfectly and was so juicy, along with the very flavorful curry. My sister and cousin both ordered the BBQ beef short ribs and left no crumbs. We also tried the spicy miso ramen, which was super yummy and filling.

I highly recommend their fun drinks, like the apple saketini, strawberry saketini, lychee sake, and the yuzu sake. This is a great spot to go out with your family and friends, or even for a night out. I don’t even care that I’m based in Queens, I will come out of my way for this place. I swear I am not exaggerating it! Everything was sooooo good!!!

I used to work in the area, and this was one of my favorite spots. I came back today just for the ramen, because I’ve tried to find another one as good as this and haven’t been successful. I usually get the edamame and any of the ramen options, and they’re always amazing. It’s a hidden gem on the UES — you should definitely check it out!

Love Tabata! I use to go to their previous locations for years. My fav is their Sutamina Ramen! You just cant get this ramen anywhere else. This is the best place to get authentic Japanese Ramen. Also their hospitality has always been top tier. This new location is beautiful and the food is great as always. I can't wait to pass by again.

So happy to find this place since the other location wasn't available! I actually cried because I loved the ramen there but now no more sad tears. I can finally slurp noodles and drink that amazing yuzu soda in peace. The food’s amazing as it always has been. The tonkotsu ramen was perfectly filling and the karaage was very good, especially since it was first time eating it. The staff were lovely and accommodating, made my bestie and I feel very welcomed. Plus, there was no wait to be seated. Just walked in and were instantly ushered to a table and offered water with menus. Absolutely will be coming back no doubt about it. Hopefully, I’ll learn how to use chopsticks by then, who knows?

google_reviews.text: We were seated and waited on very quickly. Ordered some Chashu Buns as our app,which were decent, but we've had better. They serve it with some shredded fresh cabbage - - not our fave. We prefer more Chashu and more sauce. I ordered the Black Jack Ramen while hubs got the Spicy Tonkatsu. We were pleasantly surprised that the Chashu was not too fatty. Loved that they were so tender that they fell apart easily using chopsticks. Overall flavors were good with ample amounts of ramen and broth. They have a good selection of canned and bottled drinks. Hubs enjoyed his fruity ales.

Funny enough I saw this place rated on a msn article while bored at work. I was surprised to see it was one of the top ramen joints on the east coast. Had to see for myself... and the hype seems to be real. Ramen was on point, rich and flavorful with al dente medium small thickness noodles. Bowls were priced moderately well, $9 to $16.5 which is okay. I didn't find any of the "spicy" Ramen even remotely spicy so i wouldn't have that stop you from choosing something hot. Definitely worth checking out. Service was friendly and fast and noodles came out hot.

We finally got over to this Ramen location to give it a try. It  also made the top 100 Ramen on Yelp in the US. For me the ramen was okay and my husband liked his. This review is based on both of our experiences. We waited  over 30 minutes to be seated and when we finally sat down it took awhile for someone to wait on us. The restaurant was very busy and the staff was really hustling to get to everyone. The menu itself doesn't tell you anything about their ramen. It list names but not what type of broth they have, spice level, and meat that is in it. For anyone going to the restaurant looking for ramen and you don't eat pork, your only ramen option is the vegetarian which is what I had to get. I did get an extra egg and asked to make it spicy which helped. We both enjoyed the fresh noodles. I was not a fan of the red onion in the vegetarian. The onion was not cooked and very strong. My husband thought the blackjack broth was flavorful and not that spicy. Overall the experience was okay but I would not say top ramen in Maryland.

The best Ramen hands down.  The broth is very flavorful and the noodles have a great texture. I believe all the Ramen broth outside of the vegetable Ramen is pork based.  It's about 40 minutes away from me, but if I want Ramen I will drive there every time! The service is good as well, but be prepared to wait. The restaurant is quaint and has minimal seating but the wait is worth it!

10/10 quality is persistent and delicious, never have had bad customer service ever one that works there is amazing. The pork buns are the most amazing creation ever made. The noodles are amazing and fresh the eggs are delicious for the tonkotsu. I highly recommend this place for authentic Ramen.❤️❤️

They really made our Valentine’s dinner feel special, and we left happy and grateful. Highly recommend!

google_reviews.text:
Got there at Noon on a Friday. One of the first table so no wait, service fantastic, food magnificent.

I got the tsukemen with the egg.

The broth is so rich and garlicky it’s something I never had before. The noodle were delicious and I usually can eat well and I did not finish my meal. The egg was also really good. I got brought a hot stone half way through to heat up the broth.

Fun experience for a really decent pricing. Will go again

First time having tsukemen before.  It was delicious.  Noodles are served separately with the tonkotsu broth.  The broth was very flavorful and great texture to the palate.  Noodles were perfect for doing into the broth. The perfect amount of sides and Noodles.   The experience was great,  the service was great.  Very attentive, did the hot stone to reheat the soup.  Did the soup warm to soften the thickness and concentration of the broth and it was perfect at the end.  I will be back, and recommend this place for everyone.

Great little ramen joint. Service was fast and friendly. Food was delicious.

Got there around 8pm on a Tuesday night. Put your name on the strip of paper on the wall. Got seated at the bar in about 20 minutes.

Tsukemen both was savory and rich and loaded with veggies and pork. The splash of vinegar was perfect. Noodles were pleasantly chewy. Highly recommend.

Super rich and filling portions of ramen and tsukemen are the main draw of this popular spot! Personally, it was too heavy for my taste. I prefer a more classic/lighter style of broth with less fattiness. My friend liked it though and finished the whole bowl (I could only finish half). I do like how thick and chewy the noodles are!

The restaurant is pretty cozy with a few tables and bar seating. There was a wait around 30-40 minutes for dinner on a Saturday-- you put your name on the list and wait for it to be called. Service was lovely, staff were all super nice. Overall everything was great, but the food just wasn't my favorite. I'm glad I tried it once though!

COME HERE - if you want the most full bodied, rich, and flavorful bowl of warm ramen. I ordered the seared mackerel appetizer and the tonkotsu chashu tsukemen. The fish was flavorful, satisfying and refreshing. Plus you get the added bonus of the torch at the table. The people next to us ordered the megamori tsukemen challenge. It was MASSIVE and gave everyone quite a good piece of entertainment for the night! No reservations, so prepare to wait OR get there on the earlier side. It was a Saturday at 5:30p and we waited about 15 mins! Enjoy !!!

google_reviews.text: There are no words to describe how truly wonderful this place is. The staff alone are so amazing! The kitties were adorable. I didnt want to leave. We did a 70 minute visit there and that still wasn't enough time for me! The cafe is so beautiful and comfortable inside. So many places to lounge and play or snuggle with the cats. I cant wait to go back! We got  coffee and cookies from Levain bakery while we were there as well. They deliver it to you! ♥️

Incredible!!!  *Dog owner/lover review*. This place was incredible.  From the various places to sit and interact with the cats to the large assortment of cats to play with, everything was top notch.  The inside was VERY clean and fresh.  All of the cats looked very healthy and clean as well.  The cats ranged from kittens up to older adults.  All of the cats are adoptable which is amazing.  The staff was also a very pleasant surprise.  They were extremely knowledgeable, friendly, and helpful.  I visited with an appointment on a weekday around noon and we had the place to ourselves.  The cost is 25 dollars per person per 30 min time slot and you are required to remove your shoes once you enter.  There are also gifts for sale and the cafe does provide drinks and sweet treats from the levain bakery next door ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️.  Such a soothing and relaxing experience that I will def do again.

I liked this place. I absolutely love cats. Having recently experienced a loss of a beloved fur baby, this was therapeutic for my healing.

My takeaways:

1.  The staff required visitors to remove their shoes, however, they do not remove theirs. I've noticed one employee walking all over the floor pillows.

2.  The staff were nice, went through the rules quickly, and allowed people to move about freely.

3.  As a person sensitive to smells, I could smell the litter boxes needed to be changed. It wasn't overpowering, however, I personally could smell it as could one of my friends that attended with me. In an establishment such as this, you'd think they would invest in automatic self cleaning litter boxes to be sure the boxes are always tidy, keeps the odor down, and keeps cats safe from picking up germs from uncleaned litter.

4.  I noticed while petting one of the white cats, that the cats have fleas. It would be wise to give these cats flea baths before introducing them to the general public so that people who have other pets at home don't risk bringing fleas back into their household.

5.  We ordered some snacks from the Levine Bakery next door. The sourdough crumb cake was absolutely delicious and the unsweetened tea was really good to me.

Overall, aside from the few aforementioned things, I'd visit again. 4 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Stars

This was our first time visiting Devoción, and while the space itself is trendy and modern, the experience left us with a bad impression. For context, when I try a place for the first time, I usually don’t tip upfront so I can keep the experience as unbiased as possible.

When we walked in, the staff didn’t greet us with a smile or even a simple “welcome.” We ordered two lattes and one aromatic iced tea. The total came to $19.87, and I paid $20 in cash, telling them to keep the change. As I walked away, I overheard the woman at the counter mocking the “no change” part to her coworker in a snarky tone. Since we were celebrating my mom’s birthday, that moment really soured the visit. It also left us uneasy about the tea, since it was made after that interaction.

On the positive side, the drinks themselves looked good — the lattes had nice designs and the tea presentation matched the $5.25 price. The service was quick, and they let us know the tea would take a few minutes, which was fine. But the way we were treated overshadowed everything else.

Because of that, I wouldn’t come back or recommend this place. The drinks alone don’t make up for being treated poorly.

google_reviews.text: I had a great experience at Passionfruit Coffee! The atmosphere, coffee, and customer service is 11/10. I have been wanting to visit this coffee shop for a long time and today I finally made it. Everything I expected and more. The passion fruit matcha is so good and we also tried the seasonal matcha with salted caramel, and wow! It was perfect! The pumpkin cake was also delicious! I loved it 💛

I first discovered this local treasure back in its 2023 infancy when it was still a well-kept secret. While I am genuinely thrilled to see their success, they have transitioned from a "hidden gem" to a "standing room only" phenomenon.
The coffee remains peerless and the pastries are as divine as ever, but securing a table has become an Olympic sport. It appears the shop has fallen victim to the "wifi-hoarding" demographic—those nomadic office workers who treat a single espresso as a three-hour lease on a 2-person table.
I’m a loyalist at heart, but it is disheartening to see genuine patrons deterred by a sea of glowing laptops. I would love to see management implement a polite residency limit for the "one-latte-per-workday" crowd, if only to ensure the rest of us can enjoy a seat with our caffeine. This is more of a gripe with these type of customers and not the shop lol. You guys are still the best in Brooklyn! My suggestion, the small window bench section should be reserved for the laptop folks and the rest of the seating for the others.

Cute coffee shop with lots of interesting pelicans and dragonflies all over the wall. The service is very friendly, and the passionfruit pound cake is delicious. And they have a lot of interesting seasonal specials like the raspberry pandan iced Matcha latte. Lots of seating, but it’s popular, so it gets crowded fast! Lots of outdoor seating is also available on good weather days. Gratuity included!
i love this place. great coffee, great vibes, great natural light in the morning, and the passionfruit things are all delicious 😋

google_reviews.text:
Padmores is hands down my favorite coffee shop in the neighborhood. The staff are genuinely some of the nicest people you’ll meet. Not fake nice — real, warm, remember-your-order type of nice. They’re attentive without hovering, and every drink is made fresh from scratch and always hits. The menu is just right — no fluff, just solid options.

I love the different seating setups too — cozy bench vibes, round tables for catching up, long shared tables when I need to cowork. There’s always a spot that fits my mood.

And the music? That’s my favorite part. As a Bed-Stuy native, it’s easy to feel out of place in a neighborhood you grew up in because of how much gentrification has changed things. But Padmores blends old and new Brooklyn so well. On certain days they’re playing real throwback Hip-Hop, R&B, and Soul — the classics. It feels familiar. It feels like home. I really hope they never lose that vibe. There are plenty of cafés around here, but I’ll choose Padmores every time.

document: Rita & Maria. cuisine: Cafes. located in Brooklyn. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: I will go the distance for excellent coffee and pastries and Rita & Maria has both!! I’ve been coming to this quaint cafe for the past 2 years or more. The cafe is a 20 min walk from my place and it’s well worth the trek. I would typically walk over with my dog, so it gave him a chance to sniff along the way. Each of the many visits have been a good experience. The staff is always welcoming and friendly, no matter how busy they are and there is typically a bit of a line. I’ve had my fair share of delicious pastries—maybe to my own detriment (working on discipline)! Rita & Maria’s never fails to impress, always offering a unique twist on their pastries and changing them for the seasons. Their baker creates some wonderful creations. The most recent tasty, perfect pastry was their citrus olive oil fennel cake. Soo soo good and moist. The fennel gave it a nice twist. The sizable piece was perfect and once I finished I wanted to have another! Of course, it’s all about moderation. I’ll be back for a slice another day!

I don’t think I’ve ever visited a single other establishment with as much devotion as this one. name: L'Appartement 4F
document: L'Appartement 4F. cuisine: Bakeries. located in Brooklyn. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: French cafe in Brooklyn! Croissant is good! Other bake gods looks good too. I try pistachio croissant and it was amazing. Lots of sitting space at second floor, window side table is so lovely. But our chair is sticky, so we use a paper on it to cover. The bathroom is clean.

My first experience with this incredible bakery was this: I went on a 5K run beginning and ending at High Street in the morning summer heat. I was dehydrated, exhausted, and hungry. I found a bakery that had bagels on Montague and walked about 10 minutes there. When I arrived, I saw a line outside L'Appartement across the street. I was curious, and ditched my original plans to find out what was so great about this place that it deserved a line that long at 9am on a Friday morning.

Had the most incredible pistachio rose croissant and cappuccino. The croissant was lightly sweet yet massively flavorful. The cappuccino was mild and smooth and not bitter at all. Not only was my stomach filled, my soul was too. I loved the upper level seating looking over the bustle of orders below. The place is decorated tastefully, white walls, dark wooden chairs, assorted portraits with gold frames and accents.

I'm back in NYC again 6 months later and had to stop by the Brooklyn location again. Same order and just as delicious. I want to box this feeling and take it home. But I can't, so can't wait until I visit again!

Very cute bakery in a fun area of Brooklyn, be prepared for the line outside that moves quickly. We tried the raspberry croissant and a cinnamon roll. I liked the cinnamon roll more than the croissant. The croissant was too sweet for my taste, it had a heavier topping and was different than what I've had in other bakeries. Their bread and other items looked great, I'd opt for something less sweet next time. There is quite a bit of seating inside and it's super cute, plus there's a restroom. The staff moves quickly to serve customers.

You know what we say in New York: a long line is a good sign. Luckily, I can affirm what others are saying about the line moving quickly. And it’s a worthwhile wait—the croissant selection is amazing, and it was so hard to make a choice! I set my heart on an almond croissant, but then I panic switched to a pumpkin croissant at the counter. I figured it was a seasonal flavor since I didn’t see it on the permanent menu and wanted to try. Amazing decision, past self. In a world where very few pumpkin-flavored things actually taste like pumpkin, this croissant had all the flavors of your favorite pumpkin pie packed inside courtesy of a creamy filling. It was next topped with delicately toasted (and perhaps caramelized) pecans and powdered sugar. Heaven. I’m coming back for you, almond croissant. I also tried the tahini chocolate chip. In all fairness, this is a Parisian bakery (one of the founders is literally French), and I think the tahini chocolate chip cookie might just be a little too high brow for me, but I see why people love it. It’s very creamy, gooey and has a nice umami flair from the tahini. If you could score a table upstairs, I think that would be just the cutest little date spot.

These pastries were incredibly good. We didn’t have too much of a long line but we waited around 10 minutes. We got the chocolate chip cookie, butter, croissant, raspberry, almond croissant, cinnamon roll, and regular almond croissant. We also got an almond milk cappuccino.

There is very limited seating upstairs, we waited around 10 minutes to get a table. Overall, there are a lot of options for bread and sandwiches, as well as pastries. Highly recommend coming here on a weekday when it’s not super busy. Overall, very cute, bakery and café!

google_reviews.text:
Best babka I’ve ever had, ohhhh my goodness. Best bakery I’ve been to in a long time, and I am bakery-obsessed. I ordered a regular coffee with milk, but unfortunately, the milk curdled right after being poured into the cup. I’m not sure if it was the milk or the acidity of the coffee, but it clearly wasn’t right. To their credit, the barista was kind about it, tossed it out immediately, and I switched to a plain black coffee instead. I’m not usually a black coffee fan, but it was fine. I also grabbed a plain croissant, which was simple and decent, nothing special.

Overall, it’s an okay spot. If you’re in the neighborhood and want a quiet place to enjoy your coffee or get some work done, this café fits the bill—even if the food and drinks themselves are pretty average.
