google_reviews.text: The coffee tasted really good and the service was great. I’m pretty picky with my lattes, but I actually enjoyed this one!

I’m writing to share a very disappointing experience I had at your coffee shop.

I ordered an iced matcha latte that cost $8.70 which is already on the expensive side. Unfortunately, it was genuinely undrinkable — extremely bitter and unpleasant. I took one sip and knew I couldn’t finish it.

I politely asked if it was possible to switch to a different drink. The barista handled the situation professionally and kindly agreed to make another drink. I appreciated that and thought the issue was resolved.

However, about a minute later, the female owner came out and confronted me, saying that if the matcha latte tasted bad, I should have “added more syrup to make it sweeter,” and that switching to a different drink meant I had to pay again.

I was honestly shocked.
Telling a customer that it’s their responsibility to fix a poorly made $8 drink by adding syrup is unacceptable. Even worse, reversing your own employee’s reasonable decision and putting the blame on the customer shows a serious lack of professionalism.

At that point, I was too uncomfortable to argue further, so I paid and left — but I will never return.

Bad drinks can happen. What matters is how a business handles them. In this case, poor management completely ruined what could have been a simple, fair resolution.

I hope you reconsider how you treat customers in situations like this, because this experience alone is enough to make sure I won’t recommend this place to anyone.

Regards,
E.Bae

We visited Roast & Co Café on a sunny afternoon while waiting for my daughter to finish work, and it turned out to be such a pleasant surprise.
The moment we stepped in, we were struck by how beautifully decorated and cozy the place is. It has a warm, welcoming atmosphere that immediately makes you want to sit down, relax, and enjoy your coffee. The décor is charming and full of thoughtful details, it actually reminded us of the small Parisian brasseries in France, with its tasteful design and inviting energy.

The café offers both indoor seating and a lovely outdoor terrace. Since it was a gorgeous day, the terrace was full, so we decided to sit inside. The indoor space was lively but comfortable, filled with regulars chatting or working quietly on their laptops.
We ordered two cappuccinos, one regular and one made with unsweetened almond milk, which they had available. The coffees were prepared with care and attention to detail, and you could tell they use high-quality beans. The aroma alone was wonderful.

The barista behind the counter was friendly, cheerful, and clearly knew many of the customers by name. It gave the café a genuine neighborhood feel that’s hard to find.

We enjoyed sitting there, sipping our cappuccinos, and just soaking in the atmosphere. Even though we didn’t try the food this time, we took a look at the menu, there’s a great selection of light dishes, cookies, and pastries, and everything we saw being served looked fresh and delicious. You could tell people were enjoying their meals.
Before leaving, we had a nice chat with the owner, who was very friendly and clearly passionate about the place. It’s always nice to see a business where hospitality feels genuine and effortless.
Overall, Roast & Co Café is a delightful spot, beautifully designed, welcoming, and full of good energy.

The coffee is excellent, the service is warm, and it’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back. We’ll definitely return soon, maybe next time to try their food as well!

name: Pleasant Ave Café
document: Pleasant Ave Café. cuisine: Cafes Pizza Bakeries. located in Queens. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
My wife and I stumbled onto this location one day when passing through Queens. She just wanted to grab a quick cup of coffee, but what we got was so much better than expected. We had a “flat white” which was amazing high-quality coffee. And a piece of homemade baklava. I have to say this was hands-down, The absolute BEST baklava I’ve ever had in my life and if you’re a fan of this dessert, you absolutely need to go try it for yourself. I myself, have grown-up eating plenty of baklava. In my hometown, we have one of the highest Middle Eastern populations in the country so we have plenty of great baklava but I’ve still never had it this good. It was Perfect!✨ A large quantity, but not too filling, well-defined layers, very light & flaky but still moist, and just the right amount of nuts. when you bite into it, no part of the dessert gets lost or covered up. You can taste every element standing out with prominent flavor; from the freshness of the walnuts to the sweetness of the syrup and quality of the dough. After talking to the owner for a while, she explained to us how she bakes everything herself and how she refuses to buy her desserts from bakeries or skimp out on quality even if it makes her job easier. Let me tell you, it shows! I highly respect the integrity she brings to her baking and her café. She also gave us some cookies that were amazing as well.

Now let me tell you a bit about the owners of this establishment. They’re a dedicated hard working family from Montenegro and were some of the nicest people I’ve ever met in my travels. They were VERY kind warmhearted people who opened their business up to us as if it was their home and we were long time friends, stopping by for a visit. It was honestly surreal how comfortable they made us feel. We spoke for over an hour and enjoyed their beautifully designed and well kept Café/Bar. Whenever I go to a new location, I really pay close attention to how much the owners care about their business and the customers they serve. It is by far the most important criteria. With these owners, you can tell they really put their all into the business and it is truly a family affair. I loved how the husband and wife were both there working together and even their daughter pitches in. The daughter even drew this amazing Halloween picture on the board by the entrance and you can tell how proud her parents are of her skills. I truly admire the love and attention this family puts into their business, and I can confidently say they’re the American dream in action!🇺🇸 Please go pay these guys a visit I promise you won’t be disappointed. I know for us, It will be worth it to make the trip from New Jersey to visit again soon.

I stopped by here, once I landed. The owners were amazing! I had the Freddo Espresso ( Iced Espresso) with oatmeal milk. It was one of the best Espresso I ever had. No sugar was needed. The atmosphere was welcoming and funky. This is definitely one of my places to frequent, while in New York.

name: Deploy Coffee
document: Deploy Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Food Trucks. located in Queens. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
hidden gem for an amazing brew! Been a regular for about 2 years now, the quality, service and kindness is unmatched. don’t be fooled by the stigma of coffee from a cart, delicious and worth the wait.

Pro tip: follow their socials for hours, some days may sell out earlier than others. don’t miss out

Deploy Coffee is a solid choice. The setup is clean and well-organized, and the barista is friendly and welcoming.

I ordered an oat milk cappuccino, which was made to perfection - great balance of flavors and a smooth texture. The coffee is clearly brewed with care.

Considering the quality, the price is very reasonable, especially for a cart setup.

Overall, I'm impressed with Deploy Coffee and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a well-made cup of coffee on-the-go. It’s located right outside the hunters point queens public library on Vernon LIC.

Visiting on a 30 degree windy day, and this beautiful matcha latte really warms my heart💚 It's good quality matcha that is smooth and subtly sweet without any sweetener added.

The two baristas were both kind and really poured their hearts into each cup they made. I will definitely come back when the weather is warmer so I can enjoy my drink and stroll by the riverside.

Side note is that they only have one size and it's on the smaller size compared to most of other coffee shops.

Jimmy, Danny, and the rest of the Deploy team did an amazing job catering our post wedding brunch at the Culture Lab earlier this Fall! Everyone was very happy, one of our coffee snob friends even commented that he loved the choice of roaster Deploy used for their beans (Onyx in case anyone was wondering). Thanks again, be sure to see you in the neighborhood soon!

Nice to see a van-style coffee set up in New York, definitely has good potential (good location, right on the river, busy passing trade). The coffee was slightly better than average for the area. I got a 7.8 cortado, some nice roasting but everything else was quite average.

name: Taste of Paris
document: Taste of Paris. cuisine: Desserts Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
This ranks up there with one of the BEST experiences we have ever had at a restaurant!  It was our granddaughter's 12th birthday and she's been talking about wanting to go to Paris.  So I found Taste of Paris in Mundelein, and thought that would be perfect (for now).  She invited her 11 year old cousin (BFF) and the four of us headed to the restaurant - it was a surprise and we told them to pretend we were flying somewhere.

When we got there, they were in complete amazement throughout the entire experience.  We met Chef Claude when we walked in as the girls were wide eyed looking at the Eifel Tower in the restaurant - he knew it was our first trip there.  We got to sit under the Eifel tower.  The food was AMAZING, and the service was the BEST.  We brought some sweets home from the bakery, and the girls had their dessert at home.

We can't wait to get back here for Breakfast and Lunch!  Thank you Chef Claude and your amazing staff for a birthday that will be remembered forever!  Ann, Rick, Hollie & Riley

Bar none, the best espresso I have had in decades. Of course that blend can only be purchased in France!  I had the spinach mushroom quiche and it was absolute perfection. If I ever come back to this area, it is on the top of my list. The macaroons are perfection as well! This is true French café at its best!

We stopped in for the first time and had a wonderful experience!
We had really great food, I ordered a savory and very flavorful mushroom and spinach crepe with Swiss cheese, and my husband ordered eggs Benedict, on a croissant, light and fluffy eggs, with a light and flavorful hollandaise sauce, clearly the owner knows what he is doing in the kitchen. I mentioned it was my birthday and the owned gave me macrons for my birthday! I even left with a beautiful cake!

Food here is very good, and it is very reasonably priced.  The servers are friendly and helpful. The omelets and quiches are delicious. The bakery area has a wide assortment of beautiful French pastries and breads, and I can never leave without purchasing a baked good to take home!

Stopped in for a quick brunch. I ordered eggs Benedict. The prices were higher than what is posted on their website by a few dollars per item. For $13.50 I got two poached eggs, one slice of ham, sauce and a croissant. Nothing came with the meal. I left still hungry. The dish was very good and I enjoyed it but felt that the price was too high. But so is everything everywhere. $21 for a very small breakfast which included coffee. The breads and pastries looked fabulous on the way out and I would have loved to buy a couple of items but that would have been another $20. Pass. Cute place. Good service.

document: Qahwah Valley Cafe. cuisine: Desserts Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 3.8 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: I had such a wonderful experience at Qahwah Valley today. From the moment I walked in, everything just felt luxury - the decor is beautiful, the ambience is warm and inviting, and the overall energy of the place makes you want to slow down and truly enjoy your time there. I received high class and warm service from the crew and it genuinely elevated the entire experience for me. Their attention to detail, warmth, and professionalism made me feel welcomed rather than just served - something that’s rare and deeply appreciated. I ordered for a Caramel Macchiato and it was truly the most flavorful and satisfying one I’ve had in a while. Perfectly balanced and rich. I’ll absolutely be coming back!

I visited this cozy Middle Eastern-inspired café and was pleasantly surprised. I ordered the traditional Yemeni coffee and the Dubai Chocolate Cheesecake — both were excellent.

The Yemeni coffee has a rich, aromatic flavor with warm spice notes; every sip feels unique and comforting. The Dubai Chocolate Cheesecake was wonderfully smooth, with deep chocolate notes and a balanced sweetness — not overly sugary, just perfect.

The atmosphere is calm and inviting, great for relaxing, working, or meeting with friends. Staff is kind, welcoming, and happy to help.

A wonderful spot I’d happily return to. Highly recommend!

This cafe is located at a peaceful and posh neighborhood of Manhattan and they offer one of the best adeni chai (just like masala or karak chai that we have here in Pakistan). I also tried their honeycomb which is a good unique dessert (serving size is good too). Their pizza bites were not something special but the quality of Adeni Chai surpassed everything. Will come back I.A

Wonderful Yemeni cafe in the Manhattan/Murray Hill area. The staff is quite friendly, and if you are unfamiliar with some of the items, they will even offer suggestions. There is also free Wi-Fi! I got to try the basbusa cake and the Adeni chai.

The chai was amazing. It is hard to describe what I liked so much about it, but it’s definitely up there as one of my favorite variations of chai. Not too sweet, not too spicy, just perfect. A nice sort of silkiness to it without it heavy. Would highly recommend it, and the portion is fantastic! The glasses they have are marvelous too.

The basbusa cake was pretty good as well, although I would probably try something else next time I am there. It was like a cheesecake-type item sandwiches between 2 classic basbusa pieces. Surprisingly, not overly sweet. But, it had a tad of that refrigerator flavor to it. Still, very good and a cool concept.

The inside is also just so pretty. There’s more than enough space to study or work, and it’s so open with lots of light and nice decorations. Highly recommend!

I would come here again even though I don't particularly liked the food I got to try with my friends. Just the atmosphere, service, and new cuisine entices me to come again, try something new; maybe I'll find something I'll like. This place has a bathroom. I got to try the Dubai Chocolate Bar from this place and it was ✨️amazing.✨️

The Dubai Chocolate Cake however, was too rich. The other cake shown in the photo, was too bland. The Honeycomb pastry was LARGE; it was pretty much perfect except as we progressed towards the end, there tended to be a lot more honey left and became too sweet. The Sahlep is a cinnamon-topped porridge that successfully made me sleepy. If I lived around this cafe and needed to get drowsy, I would order this. Porridge is thick and heavy.

google_reviews.text: I stopped by on my way to the airport. It looked like a great place to get some work done. The latte I got was tasty.

Anne had the Mango Refresher which was needed during the scorching weather in New York City. I opted for a small Iced Latte and a toasted Everything Bagel with  cream cheese as I hadn’t had lunch. We sat at a large table with grooves. While there were some customers the cafe wasn’t crowded or noisy. However, the music was a touch too loud which made it hard for me to hear my friend. We sat there for quite a while. Service here is friendly and efficient. There is a variety of seating including comfortable armchairs which is unusual. I recently visited a coffee shop with a few friends and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The service was fast and the staff was friendly and helpful. The inside was clean and wide open with plenty of seating spread out, which allowed us to easily socialize with each other. Additionally, there was plenty of space to get work done with lots of tables and open areas.

The coffee was great; they had several different beans and flavors to choose from. My friends and I all found something that we liked. The pastries were also delicious. I had a muffin that was freshly baked and had a wonderful flavor.

Overall, my friends and I had a great time at the coffee shop. It had a great atmosphere with lots of space to hang out and get work done. The coffee was excellent and the pastries were delicious. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a great place to hang out and get some work done.

I highly encourage every customer who pays with their credit card to check their credit cards statement. I’ve been to this cafe multiple times since last fall, sometime alone sometime with friends. I always paid with my credit card and added a tip. But when I received my credit card statements, I realized that they added extra tip on top of what I paid every single time.
They rely on customers not noticing $ amount difference between what they actually paid at the time of checkout and what actually is charged to their credit cards.
There are multiple other Google/Yelp reviews by customers who noticed the same issue. Some reviews were written one year or so back. So I assume this cafe is running this scam for quite sometime. Shameful and dishonest business practice!
This cafe seems to be owned by a mother/daughter duo and I would have loved to continue supporting their business. But I will not be back - there are many other good, honest businesses/cafes around the same neighborhood.

There really is something about their coffee, I only drink black coffee and it was the best tasting coffee I really have ever had! google_reviews.text: Stumbled across this place by searching ‘Coffee Shops’ on Google Maps. It was nice to sit, drink an espresso, eat a pastry and keep going on my walk. Gave me nostalgia from one of my Europe trips. Was a nice experience and if I’m town, would come again :)

I love going to Elly’s for coffee whenever I can! The coffee is excellent and the owner Elizabeth is so nice, and remembers my order when I go, even though I’m not in daily. It’s a very cute and whimsical cafe, not super large or meant for long-term laptop work but perfect for a grab and go, or a chat with friends. The smoothies also look great and there’s a new ceramics space in the back that has affordable events and classes/painting. There are also some unique items for sale and some of my favorite coffee roasters - Joe and Intelligentsia! Definitely one of my favorites in the area!

I held a family birthday party here for a small group (adults and one 11yr old). Elizabeth was a great hostess and instructor for our clay shaping class. People had the option to create many different objects which I *loved* -- everyone was able to choose to make something they would really enjoy. She provided helpful instructions and ensured everyone was able to complete their project and have a fun time! We are looking forward to picking up our creations next week. You do have to wait some weeks to pick up your items - this is typical with any pottery as it needs to be fired - just something you should know if you've never done this before.

After we finished our class we had some coffees and iced drinks. A few ppl had some pastries and everyone enjoyed what they chose.

It's great to have this local, small business in our neighborhood. I'm so excited to go back!
Elly’s is the perfect spot for date nights, casual hangouts with friends, or even solo adventures. The atmosphere is amazing, and I’m so happy with how my art turned out!

name: First Cup Cafe
document: First Cup Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Cozy and bright coffee shop on a busy corner of little Bangladesh. Decided to check them out with bae after yoga class. The shop is nicely decorated with a flower motif, giving heavy date spot vibes. Pastries looked very delicious and almost museum like in the display. I went with a cocunut sandosh latte. As explained to me, sandosh is a Bangali dessert. The latte was smooth with a cocunut flavor base and a hint of floral notes.  I treated bae to a mango matcha latte, iced. Was also delicious.  We sat by the window and enjoyed our conversation, while we watched the second major snowstorm of the year, a blizzard this time, start to fall on the street. It was very calming. I noticed they didn’t have any music playing in the background and although there were several people in the shop it was quiet as a mouse inside.
Interesting note, they rent board games for 3 bucks (e.g., UNO)

I stumbled upon First Cup Cafe during a weekend walk and I'm so glad I did. This isn't just another coffee shop—it's a uniquely wonderful experience that seamlessly blends a cozy cafe vibe with incredible, authentic Bengali-Indian street food. I'll be thinking about their fuchka for days!

Let's start with the service: fast, genuinely friendly, and helpful. The staff seemed proud of their menu and were happy to explain their offerings. The atmosphere is a huge plus. It's spacious, airy, and filled with interesting decor that makes it perfect for everything from a solo work session with a laptop to a casual catch-up with friends. You never feel cramped, which is rare in city cafes.

Now, the most important part—the food and drink. Their unique menu is what truly sets them apart. The fuchka and chaat were an explosion of flavor—perfectly balanced between tangy, spicy, sweet, and crisp. An absolute must-try. I also ordered one of their special teas, and it was fantastic: robust, aromatic, and deeply authentic. It’s clear they care about the quality and tradition behind their beverages.

A practical note: I found street parking without too much trouble, which is always a win in Astoria.

The most exciting news? I overheard the owner mentioning they are planning to introduce special Flavors latte on upcoming days. I cannot wait!

Overall, First Cup Cafe has won me over completely. It delivers on all fronts: exceptional and unique food, great drinks, warm service, and a comfortable, inviting space. Do yourself a favor and visit. You’ll leave planning your next trip back.

Small and beautiful cafe with a good mix of authentic Bengali vibe and classic cafe drinks. Really liked their strawberry matcha latte. Service was great and friendly. They have a good selection of standard drinks but also some refreshers and savory snacks. Happy to have another halal spot in Astoria!

Bangali family owned. Really original flavours with bangali fusion dishes.
Very reasonably priced.
We got the malai chaa which is just plain Dhaka Chaa, rosh malai latte, chopped cheese and doi fuchka

Welcome to this family-owned cafe, a true "mom and pop" destination where every dish tells a story. They specialize in elevating traditional Bengali street food, infusing classic flavors with a contemporary, unique twist. From their hand-crafted snacks to their daily selection of fresh-baked pastries, every item on the menu is made to order with the highest quality ingredients.
Their hot drinks are exceptionally flavorful, offering a signature taste that is truly one-of-a-kind and cannot be found elsewhere. At the heart of their kitchen is a passion for authentic hospitality; their friendly team is dedicated to ensuring every meal and beverage is prepared exactly to the customer's liking.

document: Cafe Mocha. cuisine: Cafes. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I went on a Sunday early afternoon to get a mixed special and jambon pizza to-go. It took only about 20 mins tops for them to be prepared, although the place wasn't busy. The staff were also very nice.

The pizzas were smaller than I expected, but extremely filling to the point we were full and had leftovers. The sauce is really good, too. My husband says they taste exactly like the pizza back home in Iran. He was very happy!

My favorite was the jambon pizza. I would love to order more pizzas in the future. I'm very happy to see that they're available to order on Uber Eats now and will probably try to order using that in the future.

The mixed special pizza was amazing.  it instantly took me back to the days of getting pizza from Chaman Pizza in Niavaran, Tehran. The taste was exactly what we expect from a true traditional Persian pizza. If you’re craving authentic Persian-style pizza, this is definitely the go-to spot in the DMV area.

Absolutely love this place! If you’re Persian, the flavors will instantly take you back home — the pizza and hotdogs taste exactly like the ones we grew up with, full of comfort and nostalgia. If you’re not Persian, you’ll be surprised to find one of the healthiest and freshest takes on fast food out there. On top of that, the people here are incredibly warm and welcoming, which makes the whole experience even better. Highly recommend!

Update - expect super delayed service. Unfortunately the kitchen doesn’t seem to be able to handle more than couple of orders at a time.

This place is a true gem! Rob had amazing customer service. Wonderful food, service and atmosphere. Definitely a good place to go to study or hang out with friends. Food is make to order and fresh. Coffee and pastries are delicious! We will definitely be back.

The pizza is amazing! Tastes exactly like the pizzas in Iran. Super crunchy crust and fluffy on the inside. Highly recommend the mixed style. Instead, we get our receipt and we get charged $25 which is the price of the original platter with the cutlet replacement. We ask if this is a mistake and he comes back to tell us it’s right and that he already told us this when we ordered. You can just go to Gulp and get the Lu Rou Fan PLUS the same amount of chicken cutlet for only $15. google_reviews.text: Love the atmosphere! And the drinks! Greatt selection. Had the Islay Sour, spot on. The mixoligists are fantastic. Prices good.

The food and drinks were amazing. Each of my friends and I loved our various cocktails and our waitress recommended the roast carrots to rave reviews. The pumpkin creme brulee was so good that we all started scheming to add it to our thanksgiving menus. HOWEVER, the music was absolutely disastrous. It was poundingly loud and with genre swings that were both disruptive and at odds with the aesthetic of the space. At one point the Titanic theme song started and then, was abruptly replaced with a thumoing bass track. It felt like conversation was fighting uphill which was a huge detraction to the enjoyable food and delightful drinks along with soothing cozy lighting. Another point the music got so loud that when we finally pled with the staff to turn it down other tables clapped as it got quieter. Despite the amazing food, we agreed the noise was so uncomfortable we wouldn't want to return.

On a snowy February evening, there was absolutely no shortage of superb food, inventive cocktails, and excellent service at The Last Word. This is a polished and designed experience that demonstrates real thought and commitment to high quality. Yet, it also somehow avoids feeling snobby, pretentious, stuffy, and imposing. Instead, the cozy, welcoming, accessible, and warm atmosphere allowed cocktail beginners and cocktail connoisseurs to both feel like their expectations were met and even exceeded. I could not recommend this bar enough and look forward to returning as soon as possible.

If you are a speakeasy and/or cocktail enthusiast, this is a must. Sat at the bar for dinner and was recommended a phenomenal cocktail by the bartender. Food and ambiance were equally impressive, but the service was undoubtedly the best part of my experience. Because I was on the way to Detroit for a work conference, the staff wrote a list of restaurant recommendations for the city that did not disappoint. 10/10

You ever find yourself moseying into The Last Word on a night when you’re looking for a proper cocktail and a place that’s got a little class but still lets you breathe easy? Well pitter patter, let’s get at ’er.
First thing you notice walking in is the atmosphere. Speakeasy style, dark and cozy, but not the kind of dark where you’re holding your phone flashlight over the menu like a caveman discovering fire. No sir. Just the right amount of dim so everything feels cool and relaxed without feeling like you’ve stumbled into a bat cave.
The cocktails? Absolute beauts. Real craftsmanship. None of that “splash of this, glug of that, shake it twice and charge ya 18 bucks” nonsense. These are thoughtful drinks. Balanced. Tasty. The kind where you take a sip and give a little nod like, “Well alright then.” And if you’ve got a few of ’em you might start thinking you’re funnier than you actually are, but that’s a risk worth taking.
And let’s talk about the service. Sara was our waitress and she was an absolute beauty. Friendly, attentive, quick with recommendations, and never once hovering around the table like a seagull at a chip truck. She checked in when she should, gave us space when we needed it, and kept the whole thing running smoother than a fresh sheet of ice.
Noise level was perfect too. You couldn’t clearly hear the folks at the next table—which is ideal, because nobody needs to hear a stranger’s entire hinge date play-by-play—but you could still chat easy with your crew. That perfect middle ground a lot of places try for and miss by a country mile.
So if you’re in the mood for great cocktails, solid vibes, and service that’s top shelf, you could do a whole lot worse than The Last Word.
And that’s what I appreciates about it.

document: Philomena's. cuisine: Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Filomena’s is an institution in Georgetown! It’s such a special place for all the right reasons: great ambiance, amazing decor for every holiday, attentive service and delicious and hearty food!
The menu can be overwhelming with options, but you can’t go wrong with anything in here.
One of my go to dishes here is the short rib ragú pappardelle. It’s a rustic dish that’s hearty and will stick to your bones. Wish there was a better meat to noodle ratio as it’s chock full of meat. But then again I love me my pasta!
The seafood carbonara is rich and creamy.
Another one of my faves is the ravioli chiacchieri. Ravioli is tender and cheesy in a creamy rose sauce with shrimp and scallops.
There’s a rich history of celebrities, politicians, musicians, and athletes that have been through Filomena’s, and I can see why.

An unforgettable meal and a beautiful atmosphere. My linguine and clams (not on menu) were incredible, the bread was absolutely delicious, and my Tiramesu was fantastic. Our server Gennaro aka Edgar was outstanding, warm, attentive, and made the night feel special.

This place means so much to us. My husband brought me here 8 years ago when we first started dating, and coming back all the way from Texas was pure magic. Still just as amazing. ❤️

The food was delicious, the service great, and the restaurant has outstanding stylish décor, the only downside was not being able to capture photos of the food with the real color because of the lighting. The place was beautifully decorated for Christmas,  the food was delicious (and enough for 2 meals). I personally recommend the ravioli and meatballs, as you can see we 3 agree! Desserts were over the top. We all ordered a different dessert and then shared with each other, after thought was we should have done that with dinner as well. Next time I guess, as we will definitely be back.
Oh a service was excellent! You felt welcomed!

Filomena is truly my favorite restaurant! Their homemade pastas are out of this world incredibly fresh, rich, and full of authentic flavor. You can really taste the love and tradition in every bite.

The atmosphere is super classy and very high elegant, yet warm and welcoming at the same time. It feels like stepping into a place full of history, comfort, and charm. The service is always amazing, very special place for special occasions.

I highly recommend Filomena to anyone who loves real Italian food made with heart!

name: Sal's Pizzeria
document: Sal's Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Excessive 25% "Service Charge" for Counter-Style Service

I recently visited with a group of 9 seniors, and while we enjoyed the food, the service policy was extremely disappointing. Even though we were a large party, there was no table-side  payment service; instead, our entire group (of SENIORS) was required to stand in a long line to pay our checks separately at the counter.

Despite this 'self-service' payment experience, the restaurant automatically added a 25% gratuity to every bill. While I understand automatic gratuity for large groups is common, 25% is well above the standard 18-20% industry average—especially when customers are doing the administrative work of standing in line to pay.

If you are coming with a large group, be aware that you will be charged a premium service fee regardless of the actual level of service provided. Check your receipts carefully!

We came to Sal’s Pizzeria in Stanardsville originally just planning to grab some pizza after a hike—but the menu looked so good, we ended up ordering everything else! The owner was incredibly kind and welcoming, which made us feel right at home.

There were great options for everyone in our group, and everything we tried was delicious. Our favorites were the chicken cutlet parmigiana and the fried pickles, which were a super tasty surprise. We finished with a tiramisu that was the perfect sweet ending to an amazing meal. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re in the area!

Sal's is affordable with huge portions. The calamari was a bit overcooked, the meat lovers pizza had a ton of toppings but a bit underdone. Sal's uses a screen to bake their pizza instead of using just the stone in the pizza oven. If they used more than 1 screen it would allow the dough to fully cook and add more caramelization of the under carriage of the pizza.
The antipasto salad was good (the quality olive oil served on the side was a nice touch). The veal Parmesan was very tender. The sauce on the pasta was good but the pasta was overcooked. Veal prices are expensive so for the price it was a good deal.
The cannoli and cheesecake very good. (Actually the best part of the meal).
The service was attentive and efficient.
The atmosphere was pleasant but missing something. Background music is an industry norm so when a restaurant is not jam packed it doesn't sound like a library.
Sal's overall is good but could be much better.

Came hungry after long hike in Shenandoah. Affordable, large portions, great taste. Chicken parm and fried pickles were awesome - would definitely recommend. Beyond they food, they had $4 beers and really nice staff. We had a very enjoyable time.

Also a bonus… gum-ball machine.

We were just passing through Stanardsville while driving the Skyline drive.  We order a large Calzone,  fried pickles, and a Greek salad.  The calzone was huge, cooked well, and filled. The salad was large, fresh, and filled. Fried pickles were on point.  Staff was amazing and provided plenty of sauces and dressing without me having to ask.  Very pleasantly surprised. I'd go back if I were ever in the area again.  There are few options in this town and this place would stand out in any other large town.

With all honesty, at New York Margherita, as soon we walk in every time we smell the olive oil the garlic the basil the oregano, so we already know what we’re eating.

The staff is extremely friendly and the service is excellent just sometimes a little slow 7/10 but not all the time. We understand the rush hours could be a major factor, but It could improve a notch 9/10.  The restaurant is always sparkling clean.

I have gone to Pizza NY Margherita for over 10 years and there's really no one else that has consistently great food and atmosphere than their restaurant. Joe and Maria treat you like family and make it a memorable experience. I can't recommend it enough (order the steak and cheese it's amazing!!!!).

The food here is so so SO good!  We have been patrons here for about 4 years.

Their grilled chicken Caesar salad is my go to here.  My husband gets the steak & cheese with sweet peppers.  We get the large NY style pepperoni pizza.  Pleasant, comfortable atmosphere with booths, high-top tables, regular flat top tables.

You place your order at the counter and they give you a number if you are sitting down and they will bring it to your table or you can order takeout and go.  There seem to be issues with ordering through Grubhub+ so I still needed to go inside to place our order.

Was looking to grab a few slices for lunch and chose Pizza Margherita because the website said family owned and they're not a chain.
Lots of parking, don't be discouraged by the strip mall. Was warmly greeted in the large, open entryway. The entryway is perfectly appointed to serve the lunch crowd with pizza slices and  calzones and the evening dinner crowd for a full sit down dinner.
Seating is mixed and open to accommodate lunch and dinner crowds.
The plan was to have 2 slices of pizza but the calzones looked too good to pass up.
Pizza slice was thin, good crispy undercarriage, no flop, great cheese and the sauce balanced out. 8 5/10
The meat lover calzone was good, cooked well and not soggy. A little heavy on the ricotta side, would have liked more dry mozzarella instead of ricotta. 8/10
Overall, Can't wait to go back and try more fr9m the menu!

google_reviews.text: I recently moved into the neighborhood and ordered here for the first time. I had high expectations since a friend recommended it. Unfortunately, the pizza dough was very thick and overcooked, leaving it completely dry and lacking any moisture. The crust was inedible, and the rest of the pizza was also dry and crumbly. I can’t say enough good things about this pizzeria! From the moment you walk in, the warm and inviting atmosphere makes you feel right at home. The staff is incredibly friendly, attentive, and genuinely passionate about what they do.

The pizza itself is next-level — perfectly crisp crust with just the right amount of chew, a flavorful sauce that tastes fresh and balanced, and generous, high-quality toppings that never feel overdone. You can tell every pie is crafted with care.

We tried a few different options, and every single one was excellent. The classic Margherita was light yet flavorful, the specialty pies were creative without being gimmicky, and even the garlic knots and appetizers were outstanding.

What really sets this place apart is consistency — every visit feels like a guaranteed great meal. Whether you’re grabbing a quick slice or sitting down with family and friends, you’ll leave happy (and full!).

If you’re a pizza lover, this spot is an absolute must-try. Easily one of the best pizzerias in the neighborhood

name: Milkflower
document: Milkflower. cuisine: Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Hidden gem in Astoria, NY. Walked in on a Friday night and seated immediately. Rustic vibes, felt like you were in a cabin of sorts, cool art and taxidermy on the walls.

For starters we ordered the ricotta cheese with fig and honey served with a warm fruit & nut bread as well as some oven roasted vegetables (eggplant and zucchini). Both were awesome, I liked the veggies more - they were served over a bed of crème fresh & this lemon dressing.

For pizza, we ordered the Queen (margherita) and the Stun Dunn (caramelized onions, scallions, gruyere cheese). Both were wood-fired and cooked to perfection. Wood fired pizza > any other style in my opinion.

To close out our meal we ordered a Basque cheesecake topped with a blueberry compote and it was a 10/10 dessert 😮‍💨

Overall: 8/10

Astoria for the win again. Milkflower was absolutely delicious and the service was immaculate. Staff was so attentive, despite it being extremely busy and the food came out so quickly. Don't sleep on that grilled octopus because it will change your life. And the squid ink pasta is a can't miss as well. Leftovers barely even make it into the fridge.

The pizza here is AMAZING!  The pizza dough is to die for!  The dough is soft and chewy!  We all loved it!  We had the Stun Dunn, The Ghost, and The Queen with extra cheese.  Our favorite was The Queen probably because we added extra cheese to that pie.  All of them were delicious though.  For dessert we had the basque cheesecake, chocolate budino and chocolate gelato.  The basque cheesecake was FANTASTIC!  I’d definitely order that again!  The chocolate budino and chocolate gelato were good, but not good enough for me to order more than once.  I highly recommend Milkfower in Astoria!

I love this restaurant in our community. It’s cozy, warm, and inviting. Every dish we’ve tried are delicious. The margarita pizza stands out with its fresh tomato flavor, and the small plates are just as impressive, both in presentation and taste. Recommend! If the pasta could be fresh made then it would be perfect!

Easily one of my top pizza places at the moment! We got the Stun Dunn with sausage, and it was the perfect combination of sweet and savory. Solid ingredients, solid chef, and solid recipes. Definitely recommend if you’re in the area!

document: Vinny's Pizzeria. cuisine: Pizza Italian. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
My family picked up Vinny's for the first time today and WOW is it good!

I got classic cheese and was thoroughly impressed, great cheese/sauce/crust ratios. My husband got the meat lover's and it was absolutely jam packed with meat. Their cannoli is also super good and HUGE! Everything is also very reasonably priced.

The employee at the front was very kind and welcoming, and the store itself reminds me of pizza places I went to with my mum as a kid.

They also have highchairs, so I think next time my family wants to eat here, we'll eat inside!

Was in the mood for pizza and had to skip all the chain places. Vinny's has plenty of seating, with a walk-up counter and old school "call your number" and pickup at the counter system. A few slices at lunchtime only took a few minutes.  The pepperoni slice had just the right amount of pepperoni to nice and spicy but not greasy. Same with the buffalo chicken slice, just enough buffalo sauce with plenty of nicely diced chicken. Undercarriage was thin and crisp with a super light crust that has to be finished before grabbing another slice!
Can't wait to stop in again and try the pepperoni rolls and stromboli!
Plus, bottles of wine for $20 will make this our next dinner stop too!

We enjoyed a wonderful family dinner at Vinny’s this past weekend. The food is truly heartwarming and delicious, with plenty of options to satisfy both kids and adults. There’s a little something for every taste, and if you’re craving something specific, the kitchen is usually happy to accommodate. The atmosphere is welcoming and friendly, making it an easy place to relax and enjoy a meal together. Highly recommend.

I just want to give a big shout-out to Vinnie’s New York Pizza! We’ve been loyal customers for years, and they continue to impress us every time. Recently, they went above and beyond when I needed a pizza replaced—no hassle, just warm, friendly help. The pizza is always delicious, the service is genuinely caring, and the whole team makes you feel like family. I absolutely recommend everyone bring their friends and enjoy it here!

I grew up coming here when it was Tony’s and recently revisited it. Happy to report that it’s as good as I remember 😊. Vinny was there to serve us, working along his employees. The pizza was great, nothing mind-blowing but if you’re in the area, yiu really should stop by.

I accidentally ordered from Bellucci Pizza instead of Andrew Bellucci’s but figured I’d use this as an opportunity to compare the gluten free pizza; I ordered the trifecta-roni, which is what I usually get at AB. The Bellucci Pizza version is essentially the same price as AB’s, but nowhere near as good. The crust is thinner and less flavorful. The vodka sauce isn’t very creamy (which is my preference) and the pesto is only lightly drizzled. It’s still a good gluten free pizza; if you’re in the area and can’t make the walk to AB’s, I’d recommend it…But by comparison, knowing how much better the same pie at AB’s is, it’s disappointing.

Lovely pizza for children and adults alike. Everything is made in house- from the dough to the sauce, which makes a huge difference in taste and freshness. I highly recommend the white and plain slices.

Delicious food. I've never had a bad experience while dining in. Normally I do not have a problem when ordering takeout either. Except recently I placed an online order before leaving work at 4:25 p.m. on a Friday. The online system said that the order would be ready by 4:48 p.m. they were very busy so it is understandable that the online system wasn't accurate. However, I waited there until 6:05 p.m, over an hour past. I asked several times about my order while I was waiting, and just kept being told by the young girls that "I'm sorry they are still working on it". By this time, of course I was tired and couldn't stand it anymore it was only one pizza and an order of wings. The wings had long been ready but the pizza never came up, So I was told that it seemed to have been lost and they were remaking it. I ended up asking for a refund I couldn't spend my whole Friday night in that tiny takeout area. I'm still giving a five-star because I really love the restaurant, and I'm not going to give a low rating over one single experience. I will also add that the manager who issued the refund was very kind, and even gave me the wings with the full refund. I just hope you will find a better solution to keeping track of your takeout orders so that the situation doesn't happen again.

This is a very quality pizza.  I prefer a thin crust these days and Leonardo’s is perfection to me.  This review is for the veggie pie.  Sauce and ingredients are superb. Nice flavor from the oven.  I picked it up but atmosphere inside was very nice . Probably a nice place to dine in and have a nice beer or cocktail.

I had high hopes for VIP Pizza, especially after seeing the change in management and the mouthwatering photos online—but unfortunately, the experience didn’t live up to the expectation. The pizza tasted almost identical to what you’d get at Cici’s, and not in a good way. It was overcooked, lacking freshness, and the desserts had a slightly stale taste that was disappointing.

My biggest issue was the overall cleanliness of the restaurant. The bathroom was dirty and the toilet barely flushed. The kitchen looked clean as far as I could see from the dining area.

I would give the pizza 4/5. I would give the cleanliness 1/5.

The pizza is fresh and hot. They have some amazing wings crispy and juicy.  The staff is friendlyand very helpful. My favorite lunch place with a salad bar. Great price for the pizza and salad bar buffet.

name: Pizzeria Panina
document: Pizzeria Panina. cuisine: Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Incredible spot for our first night in town from Boston! Shout out my girl Victoria for reserving us the table, and to the whole staff for being lovely and kind and treating us like family. The service is really very good which made the experience so fun. The food was incredible. We genuinely left stuffed after sharing salad, meatballs, pizza, and pasta. The sticky date cake was truly the star though…..so good I forgot to get a picture 😂😭

For a place focused on pizza, the pizza missed badly. We ordered three pies. All arrived soggy and wet. The crust was overly thick. The slices collapsed due to a soaked center. The date cake stood out and tasted excellent. The pistachio tiramisu was acceptable. Service was fine overall, though one server with glasses came across as unfriendly. She might have been having a rough day. The experience was average, but the pizza was a major disappointment.

Place really blew me away. They also were real accommodating of me being a vegetarian which is always nice. Sat in that one sneaky corner table which makes for real cute intimate vibes. Great for a date 😌 oh speaking of dates; they have like a date dessert bread thing that is next level shiiii.

We pulled up to Pizzeria Panina right at 7PM, and the vibe was exactly what you’d want on a laid-back summer night in Ridgewood. It was casual, cozy, and well-designed. It’s a small, intimate space, but it doesn’t feel cramped. You can tell they pay attention to the little details.

I didn’t order any drinks this time, but I loved that they didn’t charge extra for sparkling water! My homies did get a few drinks.

The service was incredible. Friendly, attentive, but never overbearing. Everyone was on point from the second we walked in.

The special ravioli they had tonight was absolutely incredible. Perfectly cooked, balanced flavors. Who knew corn and ravioli would work so well together. The pizza was great too—high-quality dough and toppings—but the pies run a bit small, just something to keep in mind if you’re rolling in hungry.

For dessert, we got the sticky toffee cake with gelato! Amazing. The olive oil on the ice cream was crazy good and the sea salt flakes on the cake was AMAZING! The watermelon sorbet was also AMAZING! It was refreshing, fresh, and the perfect way to close out the meal.

Overall, I’d give them a strong 4.5 out of 5. The pastas and desserts really shine. Pies are tasty, just on the smaller side. But between the service, flavor, and thoughtful touches, Panina’s 100% worth the trip.

From the moment we stepped into this place, we were impressed by the staff, the food, and the overall atmosphere. Every dish that arrived exceeded our expectations. We tried the Calabrese Pizza, the Agnolotti Pasta, and the Sticky Date Cake.

The pizza was decent but very burnt at the bottom such that our fingers were black just from holding it. The sauce wasn’t that spicy, it’s just the jalapeños that add the kick. I wouldn’t necessarily go back for it.

12/23/24 it is no longer a cozy eatery as it is only take away and delivery. Thought we would sit for lunch today and found out that isn’t an option. Also they have no restroom. I’ll try again next time in the neighborhood.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Update 2/23/25:

name: Picciotto
document: Picciotto. cuisine: Cafes Sicilian Pizza. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We went to Picciotto a couple of times already, and the quality of the food and service were superb!

The pizza is a gem. Every pizza lover should make this place a destination. Located in a charming street in Douglaston, the first thing you’ll see in the window is the chef making the pizzas.
This is not your typical fast-paced fast food pizzeria. Everything is done with precision, attention, care and love. You will wait for your food, but it absolutely worth it.

Service is great and kind, and prices are fair.

Highly recommended.

In Douglaston there is a hidden gem, you feel just like you are in Italy 🇮🇹. I am a foodie to put it lightly!!! Alessandro is a wonderful host, he does it all. Everything is made to order, delicious 😋!!! We started with the spinach salad, then we had Gamberetti all’aglio an amazing tapas shrimp with garlic and cherry tomatoes. We had an Ian Special panini a margarita pizza and topped it off with an affogoto and gelato. We have been here 4 times in 3 weeks. I was almost afraid to spread the word of how delicious everything is here. We will most definitely be back to try more!!!

Authentic Italian cuisine in a warm and inviting atmosphere. While you may wait a little longer for your meal, this is actually part of the charm—every dish is prepared fresh, and you can even watch Chef Alessandro in action. A truly worthwhile experience. Highly recommended!

If you’re looking for an authentic taste of Sicily in Queens, Picciotto Restaurant in Douglaston is an absolute gem. From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with warmth and hospitality—especially by Alessandro, the owner, whose generosity and passion for Sicilian cuisine truly elevate the entire dining experience.

The dishes are rich in traditional flavours and made with incredibly fresh ingredients that you can taste in every bite. You can tell each recipe is deeply rooted in tradition and has a story that Alessandro is more than happy to share it.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Queens—this is not just a meal, it’s a true cultural experience. Bravo, Picciotto!

Everything was deelish. Don't come here for a slice or a salad. He will get mad i heard. Lolol. This dude is straight up Sicilian and so is his food!  you must try the coal fired pizzas. Any of them are great! Everything on the Tapas menu is def worth it. And just everything. First time there but ive ordered from grub hub which prompted me to go check it out. It was THAT good.

And of course the service. 👏The place can use a little ‘juhjing” up aesthetically but its still a nice quiet little hidden gem off the LIRR IN Douglaston. Plus, big parking lot next door for 7.50.

Think I might go there for my birthday. 🥳🎂

I ordered the cake on Thursday and tell them exactly when you will pick it up and they will have it ready for you! $65 for this 10 inch cake and totally worth it. Bring cash to pay as they are a small business.

The best bakery I’ve ever visited!!!

The lemon bar was a particular favourite!
I absolutely recommend visiting here.

I’ve lived in this neighborhood for over 25 years and finally visited this bakery for the first time. I purchased a pound of assorted cookies, and each one was a delight—handmade, fresh, and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. They only accept cash, so come prepared.

Small and quaint, but packed with flavor and homemade goodness! I stumbled upon this charming little pastry shop tucked away off Austin St. and was instantly drawn in by the irresistible aroma of freshly baked treats. Every bite tasted like it was made with passion and tradition. I ended up trying four different pastries—and I don’t regret a single one! The owners shared that they’ve been doing this for 33 years, and I can only hope they continue for at least 33 more. They are cash only and no indoor seating so be prepared .

I must have tried each item here and there has never been a miss. It’s a small, intimate operation, which means there is a high level of care and simplicity to the recipes. The walnut raspberry bars and the almond tart are highlights. Best small bakery in Queens

google_reviews.text: THE BEST FILIPINO FOOD IVE EVER HAD IN THE US. Anw, will try the takeout laing later.

I stopped by this Filipino restaurant for lunch today and was really impressed! The food was flavorful and tasted authentic. They have a wide selection on the menu, and everything I tried was delicious. I dined in and also ordered some food to go because I wanted to try more dishes later. I also tried their dessert called halo-halo — it was refreshing, colorful, and the perfect sweet treat to end the meal. The staff were friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Taste of the Philippines is the place if you’re nostalgic for Filipino home cooking. The turo-turo/carinderia vibe is just like being in the Philippines. Limited seating is available. The best values are the combo meals (2 or 3 dishes plus rice, $13 and $17, respectively). The flavors are authentic; some dishes more successful than others. The laing and chop suey were good, but the meat dishes like adobo and bistek could be more tender. There is a 3.25% surcharge if you pay by credit card. Julie, behind the counter, is the epitome of Filipino hospitality.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
We finally tried this new Filipino restaurant and it did not disappoint! We ordered the tocilog, beef caldereta, fried bangus, chicken adobo, and bistek —  The flavors were authentic and the portions were generous:
The place itself is clean, cozy, and truly a little gem in Northern Virginia. The staff was so warm and welcoming, and Humphrey took especially great care of us and explained their menu enthusiastically

Would recommend if you’re craving real Filipino comfort food in the Hybla Valley area.  We’ll definitely be back! 🍽🇵🇭

The seats outside make it really comfortable in warm days. Makes you go like “wow I really am in Astoria”

Nice place for a date

I come here often for Italian pastries and breads. And the one thing I look forward to every year is their Saint Joseph's pastries which are both only available around the holiday of patron Saint Joseph. The Saint Joseph is a puff pastry filled inside with cannoli cream and topped with a dollop of cannoli cream on top and the Saint Joseph sfingy is a puff pastry filled with custard and topped with a dollop of custard and some candied orange peels and cherry. Yesterday I went to pickup some of each and when I got home and opened the cake box the Saint Joseph looked like they forgot to put the cannoli cream inside and when I lifted off the top half of the puff pastry I saw a small low profile swirl of cannoli cream only in the very center not even covering the whole width of the bottom half of the puff pastry, and the same for the same for the Saint Joseph sfingy. I'm not sure if it has to do with the high prices of eggs but they could have at least put on enough filling in a single layer to cover the whole pastry base so you won't bite into a completely dry rim of pastry before actually getting to the filling that makes it worth the once a year wait. And for 3 of each version totaling 6 pastries little over $31.00. It was disappointing.

A bakery that excels on every level 🥇🥇

Authentic Italian breads, pastries, & cookies. Walking in gives you the aura of being outside NYC. Warm hospitality with a smile 😊.

I was ecstatic with all the goodies on display. Took me a while to decide what to indulge in. The apple tart was outstanding and so were the lemon eclairs.

Love the outdoor seating with church bells tolling from the corner.

BEST of the BEST 🙏🏻🙏🏻

I’ve been coming to this place for a couple years. It’s been consistent with the flavors and the people that work there are very kind and polite.

I understand the price of the cookies because you need to weigh those by pound. That makes sense.

What doesn’t make sense is that you’re now charging by pound for your pastries. I don’t see any other bake shop in Astoria doing that. My most recent purchases of the pastries have been charged by weight and it’s now more than double the price. That’s just greedy.

Strict checking is done at every step, in the process of production, to ensure that the desired quality is achieved. name: Hokkaido Cheese Tart
document: Hokkaido Cheese Tart. cuisine: Desserts. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: This is a takeout place - there isn’t seating to eat there, but if you’re staying (or live or work) nearby, it’s a great place to grab breakfast or a snack!! The custard pastries are so good!! There’s a good variety, and they are always willing to heat things up if you want them warm.

The tarts are delicious! I think that's the only justifiable thing for the price. They are a bit small but you get more for your dollar by getting a bundle. I got three tarts; Original, Matcha and Ube. The tarts appear to be baked through, like what you would expect a cheesecake's texture to be like but actually it's the opposite. The tarts are very creamy inside. Almost like biting into a pudding. Out of the three flavors I got, I really enjoyed Ube and Matcha the most. On a previous visit I enjoyed a Sakura blossom one but it has been retired unfortunately. I definitely think these are  perfect to gift to someone or even to just enjoy by yourself.

Hokkaido Baked Cheese Cafe. 315 5th ave Manhattan n.y. Cute Cafe where they offer delicious matcha drinks and delicious taiyaki ( Japanese fish shape pastry filled with delicious creamy light black bean paste) as well as cheese tart, Ube, matcha chocolate chip cookie,hojicha,Sakura orange tart, egg brulee,yuzu tart. Outside seats available. If your palette craving Japanese desserts this place won't disappoint.

Thought I’d stop by after dinner. I was greeted by a super friendly and patient guy and selected an Ube croissant and original/classic tart. The Ube croissant had a very slippery and light filling and a sweet and savory chocolate shell. The outside is flaky and fragrant, but the inside gives rather strong notes of yeast. The tart, however, is perfection. The shell is like a more crumbly version of a vanilla shortbread cookie, and the custard is like a cross between a non-bake cheesecake and pudding. Next time, I will still get the croissant, but I might just eat the top part.

The Ube croissant never fails to disappoint — it’s absolutely delicious! 🔥
However, I decided to try the blueberry square croissant this time, and both my partner and I unfortunately ended up with excruciating migraines. It might sound like a coincidence, but it honestly felt like a sugar overload — probably the most concentrated amount of sugar I’ve ever had in one pastry!

document: Doughnut Plant. cuisine: Donuts Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Very tasty and delicious fresh donuts. Staff was friendly, attentive and handled the line traffic well. It can easily get overwhelming in such a busy and popular public transportation space but they do an excellent job maintaining their delightful little shop. Always a special treat to pick up a unique donut on the way home. 🍩 ✨

Hands down, the best doughnuts I’ve ever had—to die for. Doughnut Plant absolutely lives up to the hype and then some. Every bite was incredibly fresh, perfectly balanced, and bursting with flavor. These aren’t just doughnuts—they’re a full experience.

The texture was flawless: soft, light, and never greasy. You can taste the quality in every detail, from the dough to the glazes and fillings. It’s clear why this place is legendary in NYC—once you try them, nothing else compares.

If you’re in New York City and don’t stop by Doughnut Plant, you’re seriously missing out. Worth every calorie and every minute of the wait. I’ll be dreaming about these doughnuts for a long time. 🍩🔥

My sister really wanted to try a Crème Brulee doughnut. We came to the location in Grand Central Station one evening, but they had run out. So we went the next day, earlier in the day, and we were able to get one! They have a case at the front that shows what they have available, so we were able to see if they had them in stock before we went up to the register. We ordered one doughnut, and it was $5. The person who took our order was very nice. It was a very interesting and unique doughnut. It was very sticky and there was not as much cream filling on the inside as I would have hoped- but the flavor was really good, and the texture was nice. They have a special Grand Central Station doughnut that is made to look like the ceiling, which is super cute! I would definitely come back to try a different flavor.

Grand Central is a unique setting so that's the atmosphere, but the service was poor. The skinny guy looked so grumpy and told me there was no jam donuts when their holiday special has jam! The Grand Central mini donut was a little stale or it had been soaked in something. The crème brûlée donut was tasty. The custard filling was nice and the texture was good.

Red offered a great service! I really loved the raspberry filled donut, just the right amount of sweetness. I’ll definitely stop by every time I’m in town. If you’ve got a major sweet tooth, I’d definitely recommend.

document: Takahachi SA. cuisine: Bakeries Sushi Bars Japanese. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Takahachi Bakery has a cozy and elegant vibe with beautifully made Japanese-style pastries. The matcha cream roll and red bean desserts were light, balanced, and not overly sweet — you can really taste the craftsmanship.

Everything looks picture-perfect, and the staff are kind and polite. Prices are a little high and some popular items sell out quickly, but the overall quality makes it worth a visit. A lovely spot for anyone who enjoys delicate, well-made pastries

Mango pudding? Yes, mango pudding. Delicious, creamy, lusciousness.
Also tried a mango specialty drink, refreshing, palate cleansing. Had just smashed half a chorizo burrito from Derrick2 food truck(it was amazing), and needed a good palate sweeper to clear the hot sauce before trying the pudding.
We also split a ham and onion pastry, not sure what it was called. Thin sliced high quality ham, caramelized onion on a flaky pastry, nuff said.

I hate having to leave a negative review, but the last time I was there it left me expecting better. It wouldn’t hurt them to say if they’re busy and that they’d take a little longer to make some orders, but I don’t like being left to wait guessing whether or not my order was lost and feeling like I’m in the wrong for waiting longer than other customers for one thing. I get if I’m not a regular or spend a lot here, I think their service needs to be better, because their food is good. Their attentiveness needs some improvement, and I don’t see myself coming back, despite being the few (or only) Japanese bakeries in the area.
Everything I’ve had here is delicious and I plan on eventually trying everything!!! The sandwich was a favorite. Also the fish pastries are incredible. I love the huge pot of miso soup as well. 🥣

Absolutely incredible bakery, I could tell the moment I stepped inside. Everything on display tastes as incredible as it looks- I tried a beef curry pan and it was one of the finest things I’ve eaten, so I got a bunch to go. The pastries were incredible and I’m excited to try more when I return. The prices are also absolutely a highlight. Definitely merits a trip across the city on its own!

document: Kumo Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Bubble Tea Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Kumo Cafe is one of those places you randomly walk into and end up coming back to. The drinks are really well made, not overly sweet, not watered down, and you can tell they actually care about quality. Their specialty coffees and milk teas are much better than the usual chains around here.
The space itself is clean, cozy, and thoughtfully designed. It feels like a neighborhood café but with a more polished, modern vibe. Staff are friendly and patient, even when it’s busy, and they’re happy to explain the menu if you’re not sure what to get.
I also love that they have unique items you don’t see everywhere, especially their desserts and ice cream. Everything I’ve tried so far has been consistently good.Definitely a hidden gem in the area,worth stopping by if you’re nearby.

Visited this neighborhood spot today and the interior is very cute and clean. We visited in the morning so it was nice and quiet and we were able to sit and take our time. We ordered an iced coffee, red velvet latte, the honey garlic chicken sandwich, and caramel cinnamon honey bread. The total was just under $40 which was very reasonable for the quality and quantity of food and beverage. The sandwich and honey bread came out quickly and were delicious! I’m excited to try more from their extensive menu. The staff were friendly and accommodating.

My absolute favorite place to eat breakfast in the neighborhood. I come every chance that I get. I love everything about this place from the quality of the food, drinks, hospitality and the cozy/welcoming environment. The staff is very kind and the prices are fair. My absolute favorite drink is the coffee frappe (: However, I look forward to eventually trying everything on the menu. My boyfriend and I are so honored to have been some of their very first customers upon opening because we got a special Kumo cafe coffee traveler cup-- which we fight over ownership of  regularly lol. I truly find such comfort in this place and wish it many, many years of success.

My friend and I stopped by Kumo Cafe to kill some time and grab a bite before leaving NYC, and I’m honestly sad I couldn’t try more of their menu! They have an amazing selection of coffees, desserts, breakfast food, boba, and more. I ordered the Nutella almond pancakes and they were absolutely delicious, and the sesame latte was incredible. I also grabbed one of their mocktails to go and it was super refreshing! The staff was so friendly and welcoming, the cafe was spotless, and there’s plenty of seating—such a cozy spot to relax. Pricing is very reasonable, especially for New York. Highly recommend checking this place out!

I had the Spinach Grilled Cheese Sandwich at Kumo Cafe, and wow ，it was absolutely amazing! The flavor was so unique and delicious, unlike anything I’ve tasted anywhere else. It’s the kind of sandwich that makes you stop mid-bite and say, “This is really good!”

I highly recommend Kumo Cafe to anyone who loves great food and cozy vibes. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!

name: Himitsu
document: Himitsu. cuisine: Sushi Bars Japanese Speakeasies. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Wow! What a gem. So glad I found this place on my last work trip. The staff and chefs are so friendly and incredibly helpful. The food was out of this world good. The seasonal menu of fish and items were to die for. The bar experience watching the sushi masters work is amazing too. The prices are so good, especially for California. The sake list is small but mighty too. Yes they have Sapporo too! Can’t wait to be back.

We went for the Valentine’s Day weekend omakase special lunch and had a truly 10/10 wonderful experience from start to finish.

Chef Mitsu and Chef Mickey created an incredible progression of courses — every dish was impeccable and clearly made with very high-quality ingredients. Each piece was thoughtfully prepared and honestly, every bite was delicious and memorable. The chefs also had such a fun, engaging energy, which made a big difference and added even more to the overall experience.

Our server Julia was such a delight and elevated the experience even more. She was warm, attentive, and made the whole meal feel personal and welcoming.

The vibe was casual, fun, and relaxing, which made the omakase even more enjoyable. It genuinely feels like a hidden gem and we will definitely be going back.

Highly recommend checking them out!

Lastly - Credit goes to @GarethEats on YouTube for the find!

My husband and I tried their once monthly Omakase held on Sunday evenings. It did not disappoint.

Ambience was intimate with seven other guests.

The staff service and all cooks were friendly and got to know the customers very well.

Chef Mitsu and his team's preparation was delicious and the non sushi dishes were different yet refreshing. Quality of fish was great and we always appreciate a no soy sauce sushi establishment.

We were unsure of how much food the omakase would provide, but were pleasantly surprised (and full). No add ons needed for us. We will be back for sure.

We went to Himitsu for the omakase to celebrate our nine year anniversary, and it ended up being exactly the experience we were hoping for. Chef Mitsu and his team put so much care into every course, and you can really feel the intention behind each piece. The whole team was incredible. Everyone was kind, attentive, and made the whole visit feel relaxed and welcoming without trying too hard.

It was a great way to spend the afternoon and mark a special milestone. We left genuinely happy. We’ll definitely be back.

IF you’re a sushi enthusiast I would highly recommend to skip this restaurant. The experience is mediocre at best for this price range. The owner is very energetic and friendly and service staff was very professional, but those are the only positives. I must say the fish quality and cuts were not very good at all.

I ordered Chirashi tokusen and my wife ordered a sushi platter. FIsh cutting was not clean with jagged edges, many pieces tasted bland or flavorless (either aged improperly or poor quality fish), chutoro was full of sinu, ikura was over marinated, crab leg meat were actually fishy and tasted “old”, portions were small. I upgraded to Hokkaido uni which tasted very good, but again for 16 dollars extra for 1 single piece I expected more generous portion for customers. OVerall I have the feeling that the restaurant is trying to squeeze profits rather than providing a great dining experience, especially with respect to the quality of the fish.

There is a mandatory 20% service fee which is not egregious for La jolla but why call it a tip at that point if it’s not optional and proportional to the service provided? Granted service for us was great and I would have tipped 20+% anyways, but having it mandatory I think is in bad taste, pretty much like a price hike on all items on the menu by 20%. If someone didn’t like the service I could imagine this being a bad situation. Perhaps the omakase could be better Judging from online photos but I won’t be returning to find out, especially at this price point.

google_reviews.text: A local and historic gem. Come on Friday or Saturday mornings from 730-1030, the rest of the time they're just for delivery / catering. I love this place is open only twice a week Friday and Saturday for a few hours each day.

name: What's 4 Dessert
document: What's 4 Dessert. cuisine: Desserts Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt Creperies. located in Queens. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: It was New Year's Day and we were looking for a quick little dessert place, and after googling we saw this place on the nautical mile was actually opened, so we went!! From the moment we walked in, it was a cute little place, and we were greeted by friendly staff! We had the Dubai chocolate brownie with ice cream, which was amazing..we were told about their "familiar face" rewards.. we will make ourselves as "familiar" as possible, as we will be back to sample more homemade, delish products!! Great place, great food, great staff!

What’s For Dessert absolutely blew us away. Every single item we ordered was creative, flavorful, beautifully presented, and most importantly delicious. If you’ve got a sweet tooth, this place needs to be on your list.

Here’s what we tried:

Mini Pancakes with Pistachio Dubai Chocolate Topped with pistachio chocolate drizzle, toasted kataifi, and crushed pistachios this one had texture, flavor, and elegance all in one bite. A standout dish.

Crepe Cookie Butter
Warm crepe filled with cookie butter, banana, and Biscoff cookies, drizzled in white chocolate and topped with a Lotus cookie. Sweet, gooey, and completely addictive. We added vanilla ice cream.

2 Oreo Crepes
Stuffed with Nutella, Oreos, strawberries, and topped with white chocolate drizzle. We added vanilla on one and cookies & cream ice cream on the other.  These were Rich, creamy, and perfect for sharing (or not).

Bubble Waffle  Cookie Butter Style
This one was a showstopper. Topped with cookie butter sauce, crushed Biscoff, white chocolate, and a Lotus cookie. We added vanilla ice cream. Every bite was warm, cold, crunchy, and creamy all at once.

Ice Cream Nachos
A fun twist. Waffle chips loaded with two scoops of ice cream (we chose vanilla ), brownie pieces, whipped cream, and cookie butter crumble. It’s wild, messy, and amazing.

Every dish looked as good as it tasted. The attention to detail in presentation and flavor really sets this place apart. Service was quick and friendly, and the portion sizes were generous perfect for sharing or treating yourself.

Yes, the photos are real no filters needed when the food looks this good.

Can’t wait to go back and try more. This place is a dessert lover’s dream.

Great crepes, friendly service, and all things Dubai chocolate! Love that they are open late for when that dessert craving hits. Everything we tried has been delicious! Between my whole family, the only thing we haven’t had is the brownie, but I’m sure that’s delicious as well. We had no problem making customizations and they were attentive to my son’s peanut allergy.

I LOVE what’s 4 dessert. My husband and I have come by a few times, and the staff is always so friendly and gives great recommendations. Sara and Eggy are the best! Everything is delicious but the atmosphere and service is the sweetest part of it all

I want to thank you for offering real, reusable mugs and plates to your customers!

By 2050, there will be more plastic in the ocean than fish, and over 95% of the plastic that we send to recycling does not actually get recycled.
