⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Nippon Cha’ – Flushing

Ramen with Purpose, Tea with Soul

いらっしゃいませ — and welcome to Nippon Cha’, one of Bayside’s  most thoughtful and quietly distinctive Japanese dining experiences.

Since opening in 2016, Nippon Cha’ has taken a refreshingly different approach: ramen and Japanese comfort food built around premium tea culture. This isn’t a gimmick — it’s a philosophy, and it shows in every bowl.

The Ramen

The standout is the Tochucha Ramen, a bowl that feels both comforting and refined. The broth is clean, balanced, and deeply savory without being heavy — a welcome contrast to overly fatty tonkotsu styles. There’s clarity here. Each sip tastes intentional.

The noodles have proper bite, the toppings are thoughtfully portioned, and nothing overwhelms the bowl. This is ramen you finish feeling satisfied, not sluggish — a true reflection of Nippon Cha’s health-conscious Japanese approach.

Tea as the Foundation

What sets Nippon Cha’ apart is its seamless integration of top-grade Japanese tea, including top 10% Kyoto matcha sourced through Ujien Seicha in Japan. Tea isn’t an afterthought — it’s woven into the menu, from tea-infused donburi to tea sushi, enhancing flavor while keeping the experience light and clean.

Drinks & Desserts

The matcha drinks are exceptional — vibrant, earthy, and never overly sweet. And the matcha tiramisu deserves special mention: rich but balanced, indulgent without heaviness, and one of the better tea-based desserts you’ll find in Queens.

Atmosphere & Service

The space is calm, modern, and welcoming — a place where you can slow down and actually enjoy your meal. Service is warm and sincere, reflecting the Japanese hospitality ethos that defines the restaurant’s identity.

Final Verdict

Nippon Cha’ is more than a ramen shop — it’s a tea-driven Japanese dining experience rooted in quality, balance, and intention. In a neighborhood full of bold flavors and competition, Nippon Cha’ stands out by doing something rarer: staying true to its philosophy.

「美味しいと笑顔に出来る」— Delicious food brings smiles.
Nippon Cha’ lives up to that promise.

Highly recommended for:
Ramen lovers, tea enthusiasts, health-conscious diners, and anyone looking for authentic Japanese flavors done with care.

We were all very satisfied and will definitely be coming back!

We’ve eaten at Tamashi Gold in Bayside several times and always had a great experience — delicious ramen, friendly service, and a fun atmosphere. This time, we came as a group of four and were told we needed to wait until everyone arrived before being seated, which we understood.

A few minutes later, though, we noticed another group (party of three, with only two present) being seated right away. We’re a mixed couple, and while we’re not saying it was about race, it did feel off. More than anything, it just seemed like inconsistent policy and poor judgment.

We’ll still come back because the food here is excellent — especially the ramen — but we hope the staff applies their seating rules consistently to everyone in the future.

google_reviews.text:
This is my second visit here and I always end up ordering more food than I plan to 🤣. The sashimi is so fresh, and food overall is creative and well prepared. We ordered the ika uni, premium sashimi platter, green tea and red bean ice cream, hand rolls (yellowtail and spicy yellowtail), tamago sushi, and then received free appetizers on the house (fried scallops and avocado squid hand rolls).

This is a special date night or big group space, and the service is fantastic. They go out of their way to make sure you enjoy the food and your time there. This place is a gem!

Plenty of parking. Big space in the restaurant for all sized groups. Interestingly there’s also both a nice bar set up with big flat screen TVs for people who want to watch a game, then also seating for diners who want to be at the sushi bar. Great things ahead for this place!

The interior is stunning and very modern, unassuming from the exterior.

This is one of the very few sushi places that have a ton of room and the tables are nice and spaced far apart instead of crammed close together.

The staff is incredibly kind, from everyone we encountered, everyone was extremely nice and polite. The staff is overall incredible, one of the best service experiences I have had in a while.

Moving on to the food, they gave complementary miso soup and salad which were both good. We were also given a nice little complementary sushi appetizer as well that was also great. The double salmon roll & crazy yellow tail roll were both really fresh and tasted incredible. My friends double salmon roll was also great!

Happy to have another good sushi spot to add to the rotation. Will certainly be back soon.

Had a late lunch here and oh my word~ the food was spectacular. I’ve had a lot of sushi’s around NoVA but this one may be the new top tier. The sushi quality is unbelievably fresh and the flavor combination is really well balanced with all of their dishes. I will definitely be coming back to try all their menu items!

The other elements were on par as well. Atmosphere and service were great with polite staff members.

Just had lunch here.

The decor was nice and clean.  Good use of dividers to give sense of personal space while dining.

Waitress was on point and made sure we had everything.  Checked in on us several times to make sure we’re good.

The food is amazing.  This is probably some of the freshest if not THE freshest fished in sushi I’ve had in all of NoVa.  Every bite was clean and didn’t leave a trace of bad fishiness.

10/10 would come again and I highly recommend for regular dining as well as special occasions.

The server was quick, attentive, and friendly. He made our selections easy with his recommendations stating which were the most popular dishes.

There is a generous happy hour menu that goes from 3-6PM everyday and all the options we got were fantastic!

Everything was cooked to order and came out plated nicely and tasted fresh and delicious.

I would say the place is worth the price 100% especially considering the portion sizes you get. I will be coming back a lot more often!

name: Youta Ramen - Mineola
document: Youta Ramen - Mineola. cuisine: Ramen. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: My brother recommended this restaurant, and I can see why this place is a hidden gem right here in Long Island. Though this place is small and its menu is simple,  everything about it all is authentic and tasteful from its atmosphere to its food. For appetizers, we ordered Youta Dumpling, Shishamo Tempura, and Shishito Truffle Salt. The Dumplings is full of flavor. The Shishamo is new to me, but surprisingly taste similar to sardines and very soft. The Shishito tastes good, but wished that it was a bit more roasted. We then ordered the Katsu Curry, Shrimp Katsu Curry, and Shouu Truffle Ramen. The curries are to the point! They have a bit of a kick, but they definitely hit the spot! The crispness and the curry blends well with the rice. The Ramen is great, filled with the mushroom broth and it's flavor. For dessert, shared the Mango Parfait, which is sweet and tasty with the crisps and waffle! We definitely recommend coming here, but definitely come in early or make a reservation.

I was really excited to eat here since it brags about how it is one of the top ramen restaurants in LI as well as “Top 2 in the World” according to a poster in front of their entry door. A party of two with water, 2 ramen and a very pricy appetizer was around $60ish with a 20+% tip. Let me start with the appetizer. We got the Carpaccio with some wasabi soy glaze. Six average bite sized slices for $16. Definitely could’ve gotten sushi or more for $16 but it was my loss. The ramen. How disappointing. Their “18 hour cooked to perfection broth” was quite upsettingly comparable to the $1.25 tonkotsu instant ramen from the dollar tree, (not even kidding try the tonkotsu instant ramen and make chashu yourself). I had the Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen and the Youta Ramen, (the main bowl to get from here). $18-$20 each depending on what you add on to it. The bowl straight from the menu for both ramens only come with four things plus garlic paste for the Youta version, bamboo, chashu, scallions, and egg, (spicy tonkotsu came with spicy paste that you have to mix in). Overall, just very disappointing as a ramen place the boasts about being one of the best in LI/America. If you do plan on visiting this place, they do not take reservations so try to get in early on their wait list in house and it is not made for more than 20 people sitting in the restaurant so be prepared to share a table with someone else if they are busy.

Wow amazing food and service!! I got the Niku ramen I definitely recommend it, one of the best meals I’ve had. My partner had the tonkatsu ramen, he said in his opinion if you’re looking for crunch inside, add the chicken appetizer to the ramen and it’s perfect. The only slight problem was it’s very tiny, and the place fills up QUICK! But I see how this place was nominated #2 nationwide for ramen, great spot.

Definitely a trendy spot — about 80% full within 15 minutes. Just like authentic ramen shops in Japan, the seating is tight, but that’s part of the vibe.

The tori karaage — oh my goodness — absolutely delicious and generously portioned. The tempura was also excellent, with a light, thin batter that wasn’t greasy. These two dishes easily rank in the top three of all the places I’ve ever tried.

If I had to nitpick, the taro was slightly undercooked.

Living up to its “Top 3 Ramen of 2024” reputation, it did not disappoint. The broth was rich and flavorful, the chashu melted in your mouth, and best of all, it didn’t leave you desperately chugging water afterward like some overly salty ramen does.

Youta Ramen on Old Country Road is an absolute gem — easily one of the best Japanese comfort-food spots I’ve tried in New York. Everything we ordered was beautifully presented and full of flavor.

We started with the sashimi dishes, and they were outstanding.
• Hamachi in ponzu was incredibly fresh, buttery, and perfectly balanced with citrus and herbs.
• The salmon carpaccio with ikura was another highlight — rich, silky slices with just the right amount of sauce and texture.

The ramen is where Youta truly shines. The broth was rich and comforting, the chili paste added a perfect kick, and the chashu melted in your mouth. The seasoned egg was cooked perfectly with that golden, jammy center.

We also tried the fried smelt, which came out hot, crispy, and lightly seasoned — perfect with a squeeze of lemon. The pork bowl was another winner: tender, flavorful slices over a bed of fresh green onions, topped with two perfectly cooked eggs.

Overall, the quality, flavor, and presentation were top notch. Whether you’re craving ramen, fresh sashimi, or great small plates, Youta Ramen is absolutely worth the visit. I’ll definitely be back!

name: Modoo - Chicken & Noodle Bar
document: Modoo - Chicken & Noodle Bar. cuisine: Chicken Wings Korean Ramen. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Wings, thai tea, korean coffee were fire.
The ramens had nice soft beef. However the broth was bland so we didn’t end up finishing them.

Love that the place is halal. We didn’t wait at all. We were seating between two couples, so it was hard to focus on my conversation because of the proximity of the tables. Would come again for the wings. 10% discount if you use cash

I recently tried Modoo Chicken & Noodle Bar, and overall it was a solid and enjoyable experience. There were definitely some standout dishes along with a few that were just okay.

The chicken katsu was excellent—crispy on the outside, tender inside, and served with great flavor. It was easily one of the highlights of the meal. The boneless thigh and wings were also excellent, perfectly fried with great seasoning and texture. If you’re craving good Korean-style fried chicken, Modoo definitely delivers on that front.

The beef spicy stir-fried udon, however, was just okay. It had good spice and decent flavor, but it didn’t have the same level of depth or excitement as the other dishes. It wasn’t bad—just nothing memorable compared to the rest.

The biggest surprise of the night was the strawberry matcha, which was truly beyond excellent. Refreshing, balanced, and unique, it’s the kind of drink I’d come back for on its own.

Service was decent, and the atmosphere was casual and comfortable. Overall, Modoo is a good spot with some standout items. I’d definitely return for the fried chicken and that incredible strawberry matcha.

We were skeptical to dine in as wasn't sure about their halal status.  We were really happy to see their menu as it clearly says zabiha halal, they also have halal certifications on display.

Ambiance was good. It wasn't that busy. We had
bulgogi loaded fries
Spicy Beef Ramen
Udon noodle
Sizzling cheese chicken

And blue lemonade, One orange drink and Japanese Soda.

Everything was good. Would be coming back to explore their menu.

Overall ambiance was good. They do have covered outside sitting along few tables inside. Restaurant appeared clean, staff was attentive,  friendly and co-operative.

We were able to find parking upfront,not sure how the parking would be on busy days though.

I would give this place 2.5 stars. The appetizers were amazing, but the main dishes are just decent—nothing life-changing. The fried chicken is frozen and store-bought. I literally saw the bags of frozen chicken sitting out on the side. I can’t lie though, it was still delicious lol.

I ordered the spicy beef ramen. The broth was good, but the rest of the ramen was ehhh—you can tell the quality isn’t great. They definitely use dehydrated mushrooms; you can tell as soon as you bite into them. The tofu isn’t soaked in the soup, and they’re very frugal with the beef. The beef was also really dry.

This place was okay, but a bit inconsistent. The bulgogi was alright, though the beef wasn't as savory as other versions I've tried. The chicken katsu was also just fine—nothing special. The kimchi was stale, didn’t have that burst of flavor. The real standout was the wings; they were juicy, well-cooked, and a good size. I'd definitely recommend ordering those if you come here.

One odd note was that the utensils and glasses were all plastic. For the setting, it felt a little out of place. It gave cheap and tacky. I hope management improves this.

name: Mr KeKe Ramen
document: Mr KeKe Ramen. cuisine: Ramen Dim Sum Hot Pot. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Every visit feels like a little comfort escape. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The ramen is rich and comforting, the noodles are perfectly cooked, the dumplings are crispy and delicious, and every dish tastes like it was made with care and intention.

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, perfect for a relaxed dinner, and the service is consistently kind and attentive. You can truly feel the love they put into their food.

If you’re craving authentic flavors, generous portions, and a place that never disappoints, Mr. Keke is absolutely worth it. Highly recommend this spot keeps me coming back every time!

Visiting Mr Keke on December 24, 2025, “ which should be called “The Hidden Gem”felt less like dining out and more like being welcomed into a beautifully curated home where food, warmth, and hospitality take center stage. From the moment you step inside, the presentation and décor immediately set the tone—tasteful, thoughtfully arranged, and effortlessly elegant without feeling pretentious. The space strikes a rare balance: polished yet cozy, refined yet deeply inviting.

The atmosphere is one of Mr Keke’s greatest strengths. There is an undeniable sense of comfort that wraps around you, making it easy to relax and enjoy the experience. Conversations flow naturally, laughter feels encouraged, and the overall energy is friendly and genuine. It’s the kind of place where time slows down, and you find yourself wanting to linger just a little longer.

The food, however, is the true star of the experience. Especially the dumplings!  which I learned the owner herself makes from a family recipe directly from china! And trust me you can taste the difference from what other commercial restaurants offer with pre made frozen versions.  Each dish arrives perfectly cooked, showcasing skill, consistency, and care in execution. The flavors are confident and well-balanced, suggesting both experience and respect for quality ingredients. Portions are generous, offering excellent value, yet the quality of the food easily could justify an even higher price point , all the dishes are reasonably priced for the quality you are receiving ! Mr Keke delivers a level of craftsmanship that rivals restaurants charging significantly more.

Equally impressive is the service. The owners and staff are not just polite—they are genuinely kind, warm, and attentive. Their presence enhances the experience rather than interrupting it. They check in thoughtfully, anticipate needs, and make every guest feel seen and appreciated. This level of hospitality is increasingly rare and leaves a lasting impression.

In every sense, Mr Keke earns its well-deserved 5-star rating. It is a restaurant that excels not only in food but in creating a complete, heartfelt dining experience. Whether you’re there for a casual meal or a special occasion, Mr Keke delivers excellence with soul—and makes you feel like you are experiencing an authentic cuisine at a restaurant in China while feeling right at home while doing it.

I have attached some photos below, notice how everything fried is a lite golden color and while eating , it does not taste or feel greasy.  This is a sign of a well attentively kept clean kitchen which is an attributed to the owners to deliver high-quality food to their guests. You can definitely see and feel how they take pride in their craft.

If you have not visited Mr. KeKe , or as I like to call it, “ The Hidden Gem”  treat  your self to a truly pleasurable authentic dinning experience.  Thank you Mr KeKe for a delightful culinary ride to the far east right in my own back yard. I am already looking forward to my next experience with your restaurant and I will be back very soon.

This is the third time we’ve eaten here and it’s been consistently wonderful. We shared a miso soup and it had nice little onion crunchies in it! The Thai Curry came out boiling hot and stayed warm through the whole meal. It was perfectly spicy and savory. The Glazed Ginger Chicken and Shrimp was flavorful and lovely as well.
Excellent service and food! Love this place. We loved our Singapore noodles. The green tea is so yummy and the wonton soup is very nice.
Food is delicious and the atmosphere is beautiful. Great service! Wishing this business continued success 💜

name: Katsuno
document: Katsuno. cuisine: Japanese Sushi Bars. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
We have been going to Katsuno for many years since we moved to the area 10 years ago. I’m from Japan and can vouch first-hand that this is very authentic and delicious Japanese food. It’s run by a Japanese couple in a very intimate space. It is now reservations-only, which is very easy to set up.

This was the place we went to for our first night out as parents, and to celebrate birthdays, including for our daughter who requests dinners here. Whenever anyone asks me for local recommendations, especially Japanese food, I mention Katsuno.

Since I love sushi, I always order the nigiri sushi set (pictured but missing some pieces I already ate!), but we also often order the hijiki ingen salad, ume inaniwa udon, and rolls. I have also had tempura and the black cod and they’re also highly recommended.

The sushi quality is so much higher here than anywhere else nearby (and far), and offer unadulterated Japanese flavors which are surprisingly very hard to find. I look forward to supporting them for years to come!

ありがとうございます！

Called a week beforehand to make a reservation for 6:15. There was only one other party dining at the same time. I actually appreciate that they are reservation only - it does make for more quality conversation with your party.

We ordered the Agedashi tofu and Magritte duck as appetizers. Both were delicious and had really great sauces that paired well with the dish. For entrees we ordered their black cod, pork hirekatsu, sashimi plate, and their snow crab avocado roll.

The black cod was absolutely delicious, so tender, cooked to perfection, jam packed with flavor but not tough or mushy. The hirekatsu was another hit - four large pieces, fried to perfection. The pork itself was still moist and juicy. The sashimi?? So fresh and cleaned perfectly! The quality is definitely on par with what I get in the city so the price is absolutely reasonable to me. Lastly their snow crab and avocado roll - also really good! I love how sweet the snow crab was, there also wasn’t too much rice on the roll which was appreciated.

Overall, we had a wonderful time dining at Katsuno. While the prices may seem a bit high and portions of certain items may not be the largest, the flavor really is authentic and the quality of ingredients used are good too. We will be back!

This place does not accept walk-ins, making it very a nice, quiet, lowkey spot. The service here is also very nice and their matcha dessert was EXQUISITE. What threw me off the most was the food and how they priced it.

Considering how “exclusive” and expensive this restaurant is, it gives the impression that their food would be out of this world. But honestly…it was a bit lacking in my opinion. Definitely better than your local, go-to sushi restaurant but they’re easily beat by competitors like Takesushi. Plus, portions are so small. Felt scammed at the end of our meal.
Traditional Japanese styles. I love Octopus And Cucumber Vinaigrette. And I ordered Zaru twice. That’s so good. Good Sushi and nice services.

Honestly I was disappointed and frustrated (but, in all fairness, I did research this after my meal and before posting, and my experience below apparently is in line with Japanese tradition).  I ordered a market-price cheekbone fish for $55 and my wife ordered the $28 black cod.   On my plate was my piece of fish, one lemon slice, and one tablespoon of some kind of cold white stuff, like a piece of finely grated daikon.  Nothing else.  No sauce, no greens or garnish of any kind.  And no silverware either.  After trying to pull pieces of well-done fish off the otherwise barren plate with my chopsticks, I gave up and asked for a fork and a knife.  You want white rice with that?  That'll be a $4 charge, thank you, for a small bowl on the side.  Soy sauce?  Gotta ask for that.   My wife's experience was similar.

However, like I said up front, I guess this is the way it's done if you want a real Japanese experience - up to and including the $4 charge for the rice because apparently that's true to tradition and practice.   And the food was very good - not enough to make for a satisfying meal, but enjoyable.  It's just not what this Western palette was expecting, that's all.  More experienced connoisseurs than I would probably appreciate these nuances.  After my meal, I grabbed two orders of dumplings at a nearby place and that was my dessert.

name: Grand Sichuan
document: Grand Sichuan. cuisine: Szechuan. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Finally tried dining in after ordering takeout from here many times. The peppercorn beef was my favorite! It’s very tender with a strong numbing flavor. The Zigong spicy frog with ginger was also excellent, with tender meat and a bold sour-spicy broth that goes great with rice.

Great spot for anyone who loves authentic, bold Sichuan flavors！

If you’re looking for truly authentic Sichuan food in New Jersey, this place (formerly Da Sichuan, now Mala Temptation) is absolutely worth a visit. You can tell the kitchen really understands Sichuan flavors — the spice is layered, the numbing is balanced, and the aroma comes from proper technique rather than heavy oil.

The spicy boiled fish was excellent (tender, clean flavor, not greasy), the Zigong ginger frog tasted fresh and well-handled, and the mao xue wang was rich but not overwhelming. The grilled fish was consistently flavorful throughout, and even the Chongqing-style noodles showed great attention to detail.

This is not a toned-down version of Sichuan food — if you love real spice and depth of flavor, it’s a place you’ll want to come back to.

Spice Spirit, imo, is easily one of the best Sichuan spots in Jersey City. Such a hidden gem. Their fish and frog dishes are standouts!Both are fragrant and packed with that numbing-spicy Sichuan flavor! You can really taste the freshness and technique in every bite.

I also love the open kitchen setup where you can watch the chefs cooking everything fresh to order. The heat, the aromas, and the wok action make the whole dining experience even better. Trust me, this is definitely a must-visit for Sichuan food lovers.

Small place, big surprise. One bite and I felt like I was back in Chengdu. We tried four dishes and every single one was a hit. The owner told us they just hired a chef from Mala Temptation—totally explains the flavor!
Top picks:
🔥 Spicy Chicken (辣子鸡) – crispy outside, tender inside, super fragrant.
🔥 Numbing Pepper Beef (椒麻牛肉) – real Sichuan heat, spicy and addictive.
🔥 Garlic Grilled Fish (蒜香烤鱼) – fried first, full of garlic aroma; tastes even better the next day.
If you love authentic spicy food, this place is a must-try!

I understand Grand Sichuan recently changed ownership/management.

My family always ordered the triple vegetable.  The new version is similar, but adds sweet potato and onions.  It's a bit enhanced.

We ordered the 1,000 pages of tofu, which was also very good.  However, I felt the Sichuan peppercorn oil was excessive for my tastes, and made part of my mouth numb for a couple minutes.  I wouldn't order it again unless they reduced the peppercorn oil.

We ordered several lo mein dishes.  The servings were quite generous.

Water was served in paper cups, which was a bit unusual.  Service was good.

I received a free drink for an honest review.

Will certainly look to dine in next time we’re in Virginia. If you want good service with mediocre food, visit Peking Gourmet… last I checked nobody is ordering Chinese food for the service.

The restaurant was clean, the staff up front put their phones down long enough to speak and appear to seat us. 👍. All of the food was being brought out fresh and filled. A person was there doing the hibachi and they were friendly and doing a fine job. Our waitress was attentive and very pleasant as well. There was not a lot of sushi out yet but it was being made. Prince Coffe House is a fantastic place to relax and enjoy a great coffee. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, making it perfect for meeting friends or taking a quiet break during the day. The experience made me feel like the way I looked that day meant I didn’t belong there. Feeling watched but not welcomed is not a good feeling for any customer.

I ended up going across the street to Noya Café, dressed the exact same way, and was greeted immediately with kindness, smiles, and professionalism.

I’m sharing this because every customer deserves to feel acknowledged and welcomed when they walk into a business.

name: Sundays Off Cafe
document: Sundays Off Cafe. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Bakeries. located in Bronx. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Adorable little coffee shop! Hitting the road and we were looking for coffee for the drive. This was the cutest spot that popped up thanks to Google.

It’s a small space, grab and go or outdoor seating. Love the vibes though and the gentleman at the counter was super friendly and patient.

Great menu, I got the veggie bagel (Rosemary sea salt), chocolate chip cookie, basque cheesecake, vanilla latte, annnnd drumroll for the black sesame latte…. Wow! So unique for coffee, loving and enjoying every sip.

Thanks so much for the wonderful experience, hope y’all have many, many years here. 🩷

First time coming to this coffee shop. They don’t have any seating inside but there is outside seating. I got the maple, sage and cinnamon latte which was amazing. The hot apple cider was literally a 10/10. It reminded me of fall. Lastly the garlic bagel was the best part. I have never tried a bagel so good. It was soft even when toasted and the seasoning was amazing. I would come back for another one. Thank you sundays best!

Sundays Off is a great cafe in the neighborhood. It’s a small place on Crosby Avenue that is painted an adorable mint green color on the outside. The menu has options for coffee and tea lovers alike. My go to order is an Iced Matcha. It’s high quality and mixed correctly. If you are a regular matcha drinker, you know some places won’t whisk well and you end up with lumps of matcha in your drink. Thankfully that has never happened to me here. They do serve it unsweetened as it’s meant to be. However, there’s a station by the door with sugar and simple syrup if you want to add it yourself . I have also tried their seasonal latte flavors; all were hits. The pastries are freshly baked and they sell some artisanal snacks there too. My favorites pastries are the almond croissant and cheese danish. You really can’t go wrong with any of the choices though.  There has not been a time I’ve come by and received poor customer service. The staff is genuinely kind. If you’re in the neighborhood or just want to pop by this quaint cafe, I’d highly recommend it.

P.S. They have a few tables outside when the weather is warmer.

I came to visit after hearing so many good things about the shop. I wanted to explore more about the various coffee shops in our area. It is a very small space. Just enough room for a hand full of people to order and leave. There is outdoor seating but is more of a grab and go establishment. There is no indoor seating whatsoever. Overall, the coffee was good! I ended up getting an iced black sesame latte, and was truly impressed! I also ordered an iced chai latte, and it was meh (mostly milk? Very subtle hits of chai). I would come back for a quick fix if in the area.

Cute little coffee shop for a quick grab and go. I got their everything bagel toasted with cream cheese and an iced maple, sage, cinnamon almond milk latte.
The bagel was SO GOOD. You can tell it was fresh, tasty and soft. The latte was also so good! I’ve never had a coffee with maple and sage but it was an interested and yummy blend of flavors. As a local to the neighborhood, I would go again!

name: Dukagjini Burek
document: Dukagjini Burek. cuisine: Bakeries Coffee & Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Great spot for authentic Albanian burek.  Food was great, immediately out the oven and the price is great.  My Albanian friend took us all the way here from Manhattan specifically to try the best burek he knows and grew up eating.

Randomly walked in outta curiosity...i got two  slice. 1 spinach & cheese & 1 meat. $6.75 each
It was really really good😍😌

Of all the burek spots in New York, Dukagjini’s is the absolute best. We usually get the spinach and meat pies, and the cheese pie is just as delicious!

The people who make the bureks do so with care and consistency - every burek we have is always as amazing as the last. Strongly recommend getting a small cup of yogurt to pair with your burek, especially if you get the meat pie! This is my husband’s favorite combo. Yum 😋

Thank you to the Dukagjini Burek team, you all are the best!!

Staff is friendly and make you feel like you’re at home. You can tell that this burek is special and is the only one that tastes authentic. Always stop here if you’re in the Bronx. Pite me mish (meat pie) is unreal.

The spinach and cheese burek is extraordinary. When it comes fresh out of the oven, its a explosion of flavor and warmth. We also had the cheese burek - also tasty but perhaps not as much as the spinach and cheese one. The place has a limited menu (including homemade yogurt) but each item on the menu is super delicious. The folks at the counter are very kind and friendly. If you are ever in the area visiting the Bronx zoo or the Botanical gardens, this is definitely the place to grab dinner. The place is tiny with around 5 tables and very bare-bones decor, but the bureks are worth it. They are $5 each. A whole burek pie costs $20.

De Lillo—Celebrating 100 Years of Sugar, Butter, and a Lot of Bronx Pride

name: Artizen
document: Artizen. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I recently hosted my bon voyage party at Artizen, and it was absolutely wonderful! The space was perfect for my 50 guests — stylish, comfortable, and full of great energy. From start to finish, Maria went above and beyond to make everything seamless. She was attentive, creative, and made sure every detail was taken care of.

We outsourced some of the decor and wine bar to add a touch of elegance to an already elegant space, and Artizen personally catered the passed appetizers which were excellent. Adam and the rest of the staff made everyone feel right at home with a perfect playlist to add to the vibe. I couldn’t have asked for a better send-off celebration. If you’re looking for a cozy café that also offers event space and catering, I highly recommend Artizen. It’s a true gem!

This place is centrally located and they serve the best lattes! Service is courteous and done with a smile.  We sat outside and it was lovely. The inside is clans neat and they serve a plethora of food items, even vegetarian treats! Check this space out, it’s worth it!

Great space with beautiful decor. There’s always new, great food and drinks being added to their menu. They have great, personal service that I really appreciate. Their co-working space is a life saver in the Riverdale area. They offer quiet personal rooms that are great for my meetings when I need to brainstorm. 10/10 recommend.

I really liked this coffee, super cozy space that doubles as a coffee shop and a coworking space, the coffee was delicious and de bakery even more, I had the almond croissant and I loved it. They roast their own origin coffee and make their own blend, they even have filtered methods. Would definitely come back !!!

I keep coming back to Artizen Cafe, and it's easy to see why. The baristas are super friendly and always suggest the best drinks, which makes the whole experience feel personal rather than just another coffee run.
I love how inventive they are with their seasonal lattes that actually taste as good as they sound. The lavender honey one surprised me with how well-balanced it was. And while I usually just grab coffee, the sandwiches here have turned me into an occasional customer - the bread is always fresh, and they don't skimp on the good ingredients.

What really makes this place special is how versatile it is. They have a work space upstairs for people that need to use their laptops and I always see lots of people in the neighborhood who swing by, yet the space somehow accommodates everyone without feeling chaotic. The lighting is just right, the music is great, and there's always at least one open seat by the window.  It's become my go-to spot when I want to treat myself to something nicer than chain coffee shops but don't want to deal with pretentious cafe attitudes. Just consistently good drinks, tasty food, and a welcoming vibe.

document: Lloyd's Carrot Cake. cuisine: Bakeries Desserts. located in Bronx. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: My coworker went out her way to way to get me a slice of the carrot cake and a slice of the strawberry coconut cake! Both delicious and like a big back I had the carrot cake for lunch! Very moist and flavorful and can taste the culture of my race!! Got me in a trance! 😍🥰😘

I discovered this bakery on Instagram and made a mental note to visit the next time I was nearby. A few weeks later, I finally had the opportunity to stop by and picked up a few slices of the various flavors they offered.

First, I want to mention that this is not a large bakery at all; it appears to be a family-oriented establishment. I specifically went there for the carrot cake, which they offer with or without nuts, available either as a whole cake or by the slice.

I purchased one slice of each flavor, and although I don’t remember the exact prices, they were reasonable. As for the carrot cake, it was just okay. I wasn't particularly impressed; I've had better. While it was tasty, it was a bit dry. My mom, who is the "carrot cake queen," agreed with me without me prompting her, so I knew my opinion was confirmed.

On a positive note, I really enjoyed the coconut scone—it was moist and not overly sweet. I didn't taste the chocolate slice, and the strawberry slice was just okay. Overall, I believe the visit was worth it, but I might choose to pass on this bakery in the future. I do want to commend them for being a small, Black-owned business that has made a name for itself, so kudos to them!

Fresh tasty bread - Cookies - italian baked treats - clean - Attentive, friendly staff - fairly priced.

Bakery Review: Incredible Bread, Questionable Attitude

If you’re looking for the best bread in town and don’t mind a side of mild emotional abuse, this bakery is the place for you.

The Bread? Life-Changing.

The moment you take a bite, you’ll wonder if you were born in the wrong century, because this bread tastes like it was handcrafted by medieval monks using ancient secrets. Crust? Perfectly crisp. Inside? Fluffy, warm, and borderline spiritual. You’ll want to buy extra just to apologize to your past self for ever eating store-bought bread.

The Staff? Hilariously Rude.

Ever been judged for your pastry choices? You will be. Ask a question, and you’ll get a look that says, “You seriously don’t know that?” Order too slowly? Expect an exaggerated sigh. But somehow, it adds to the charm—like a grumpy grandma who secretly loves you but would never admit it.

Final Verdict

Come for the unreal bread, stay for the comedic hostility. Just don’t expect warm smiles—unless you count the warmth of a fresh baguette smacking you with judgment. 10/10 would get roasted again.

google_reviews.text: Wonderful place..delicious coffee, great options for breakfast (savory and sweet) and the service is excellent. Nice atmosphere and the prices are affordable. It is becoming our favorite spot ❤️

Received an email, not a call, shortly after ordering, letting me know that the omelette was removed from the order. Called to see if I could replace it but they said their griddle is broken so they can't make omelettes or bagels. Yet they can still make pancakes and crepes?
When food did not arrive for 2 hours I tried calling again, multiple times, but they took their phone off the hook and I was not able to get through. When order finally arrived my vanilla latte was a milkless coffee with sugar and the food is cold and tasteless. They must microwave frozen pancakes. Would give zero stars if I could.

A taste of je n'ai sais quoi? In Riverdale!
This up and coming creperie touches the Bronx with a bit of Europe. Try their Italian Gelato or their freshly made crepes.  Your taste buds will thank you for it! And did I hear that crepes were low in carbs?!

I wanted to love Lava House, especially as a new addition to the neighborhood, but unfortunately, I'm not sure this restaurant will last long unless some things improve. The service left much to be desired—the lady who took our order seemed disengaged, not rude but definitely not friendly. My daughter enjoyed her waffle stick with Fruity Pebbles, but my Nutella crepe with strawberries and bananas was soggy.

My husband's $12 avocado toast was disappointing—just a slice of untoasted whole wheat bread with feta and capers, neither of which were listed on the menu behind the counter and neither of which he eats. Rather than complain, he scraped it off, but we both felt it wasn’t worth the price. On top of that, the utensils were flimsy disposable plastic despite being served on glass plates.

I’m all for eco-friendly practices, but the mismatch made it difficult to enjoy the food properly. It’s hard to justify the $60 we spent for what we received. I genuinely hope they can work out these kinks because I want to see them succeed, but there’s a lot of room for improvement.

google_reviews.text: Run out of my decaf at my local store in Harrison, decided to come here in person. What a great quality service! Staff was super accommodating and nice. Not only do they have the best decaf coffee that carried me through pregnancy and breastfeeding, but the service and atmosphere are too notch.
The barista made the cutest coffee art for our oat milk lattes and went out of his way to come let us know that the vegan pastries had been delivered. Great place for a casual and tasty breakfast.

I came in with pretty high hopes after seeing the 4.6 stars and 1,000+ reviews, but my experience was honestly underwhelming. The shop itself is super vibey and clearly popular - it was packed when we arrived.

We ordered a cold brew and an iced latte with sweet cream (+$2). The cold brew was literally 99% ice and 1% coffee - which is fine, I know a lot of places do that - but the problem was it had **no taste at all**. It didn’t even taste like coffee, just straight water. *(Photo below shows how much ice was still left even when it was already about 50% melted - still packed with ice.)*

The latte also tasted like pure milk with barely any espresso flavor, so between the two drinks, we basically ended up with one cup of water and one cup of milk.

I went up to ask for an extra espresso shot since my latte tasted way too milky. Before I could even finish explaining, the barista cut me off with a quick “Sure!” and added the shot. Then I realized I was charged for it - which I wouldn’t have minded, but I just wish I could’ve finished explaining first.

Overall, the atmosphere and vibe were great, but the drinks and service didn’t live up to the hype for me. Probably wouldn’t come back if I’m in the area again.

Listen, I need to report a crime. But I can't call the police because I’m an accessory to it.
​Lickity Split, New Holland's legendary ice cream and sandwich shop, isn't running a sandwich shop; they are running an international trade cartel. Okay, maybe not international, but certainly inter-county. They have figured out the ultimate cheat code for printing money in Lancaster County:
​Drive 60 miles north to Tamaqua.
​Load a truck with that premium, high-octane Leiby's Ice Cream.
​Bring it back to New Holland.
​Watch locals lose their absolute minds.
​I walked in there thinking I was supporting a local churn. I looked at the menu and realized, "Wait a minute... I know this texture. I know this density. This isn't Dutch Country farm magic; this is Coal Region Gold."
​They aren't just selling scoops; they are selling a nostalgic addiction with a markup. And you know what? I respect the hustle.

It’s rare to find a spot that stays true to its roots while still evolving, and Lickity Split nails it every time. Keep up the great work!

This is one of the most beautiful and delicious coffee shops I have ever visited!  The atmosphere is curated to be elegant and goth.  Very dark, beautiful, and cozy!  They have a few merch items for sale that fit the vibe from local artists.  The staff is SO friendly and the owner chatted for a bit and was so sweet!

We had gotten the Souixsie and Majesty coffees and The Fat Bee and The Yule Feast croissants and everything was DELICIOUS.  The Fat Bee is one of the best things I have ever eaten, and the coffee was so unique.  I will definitely be coming back!

There are only a few places where one who has always lived on the perimeter of societal norms feels at home and Nightshade Coffee is one of those places. The black walls adorned with gothic decor warmed my black heart. Staff was helpful and friendly, and they make outstanding coffee! The Cemetery Dusy and Deadly Nightshade did not disappoint. Flavorful and bold coffee drinks served ice cold. And the croissants were insanely large! The Little Lad was not so little, but a creamy delight that was enjoyed by your narrator. Fresh berries and delicious cream encased in a fluffy and fresh pastry. This place has to be one of NJ’s best coffee shops. The aesthetics alone are worth a visit, but the food and drink are the nails in the coffin! Can’t wait to go back.

Heard a lot this fun new shop and had to check it out. Went on a Saturday morning and it was alittle busy but was still able to get a table. The staff was awesome and we ended up getting a couple iced drinks (Cemetery Dust is AMAZING) and treats from the pastry case (I’m sorry- FUNFETTI SCONE?! Yes please!). Everything was really good and we even got some beans to bring home. Will definitely be back again!

Was in the area and decided to stop by as I've heard great rhings about this cafe on TT.  Love the vibe and aesthetic in here!  Spacious, good to hang out/ catch up woth friends.  Counter seating available for those who fly solo.  Service is welcoming and friendly.  They are very patient if you want to customize drinks or have any questions regarding the menu.  They sell other cool things like sprays, candles, and incense.

Cemetery Dust wasn't too sweet, and I liked how I can actually taste the coffee.  Howevwr, it's just too much chocolate for my liking.  The Cure is my favorite.  They actually whisk the matcha!  There's many flavors of syrups to create your own flavor combo.  My only regret was not trying their sandwiches, which looked fresh and delicious.  Portions seemed big as well!

Parking lot (paid) behind the establishment or free street parking (2hr limit).  There is another lot a few blocks away.  I went on a weekday, at 1pm, and found st parking just fine.

I don't live close, otherwise I'd be here every week to try out all the different drinks and flavors!

Love love love the vibe here. We went the first Saturday after it was highlighted on a popular instagram so it was BUSY, but the cashier had such a nice candor and was so helpful. The wait was worth it -- I got a Type O and it was awesome. My girlfriend's Cemetery Dust could have been a bit stronger but was still delicious. I'm truly taken aback by how reasonable the prices are.

The decor and menu was really cool and intentional, didn't seem like a business person just googled "goth aesthetic" and threw stuff up. Loved seeing local spooky art and witchy wares for sale as well.

My family lives in Westwood and I never really go anywhere except for their houses, so i'm excited to have a reason to come to town early before a visit!

name: Off-Peak Coffee
document: Off-Peak Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Quaint straight to the point shop with just a large, long beautiful green marble counter where you order and the drinks are made. They have one cool painting in the back on the left side of the wall. The menu is super unique with the different combination of flavors. I tried the salted yuzu dirty and the iced mango strawberry matcha. I loved both because neither was too sweet. The fruity mango foam almost tasted like a creamy mango gelato. The strawberry they used you can tell was a house made smashed strawberry puree and I enjoyed that it wasn’t too sweet and had small, not mushy, strawberry pieces. The flavors for the matcha blended perfectly- it’s like 2 drinks in 1- you start with the mango foam so you’re enjoying a mango matcha but then once that foam is gone you’re enjoying a strawberry matcha. The only thing I hated was the size they give was a little too small for me because half the strawberry puree was lost in all the ice and I couldn’t enjoy & finish it all. Overall I enjoyed the matcha because it was smooth, creamy and they were generous on the matcha amount + it was the right amount of milk. Most places get you because they put so much milk and you’re not even getting real matcha flavor so shout out to the team for the golden portion. The salted yuzu dirty was definitely unique but if you don’t like too much citrus with your caffeine, you should try something else. Overall I’d come back to get the other drinks and would recommend you check it out too!

Visited Off-Peak Coffee for the first time. Tried the Strawberry Mango Matcha and the Black Sesame Latte, both were excellent. It was my first time having a Strawberry Mango Matcha and I really enjoyed the balance of flavors; the matcha wasn’t overpowering at all. The black sesame foam was also delicious. Great quality for the price. Smaller space with no seating, takeout only. Would definitely visit again soon.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the Rooicoco drink from Off-Peek Coffee, and I must say it was an absolute delight! This refreshing cold brew features a creamy foam topping made from coconut, which adds a luxurious touch to the drink. The combination of coconut water and rooibos tea creates a wonderfully unique flavor – the essence of tropical bliss in every sip.

One of the standout aspects of the Rooicoco is its sweetness. Unlike many other drinks that can lean too heavily on sugary flavors, this one strikes the perfect balance. It’s sweet enough to be enjoyable but not overwhelming, allowing the natural flavors of the coconut and tea to shine through. The added coconut flakes provide a delightful texture that complements the smoothness of the drink perfectly.

The Rooicoco truly feels like a must-try for anyone seeking a refreshing beverage that also feels indulgent. Whether you're lounging by the pool or looking for your next favorite coffee shop treat, this drink is guaranteed to brighten your day. Highly recommend it!

The strawberry mango matcha from Off-Peak Coffee is a delightful blend of flavors that excites the palate. The luscious sweetness of strawberries, tropical mango, and earthy matcha come together in perfect harmony, creating a mesmerizing taste experience. This creative concoction is a must-try for any flavor enthusiast!

**** RESPOND****
Thank you for responding. I want to clarify why this review was left. The experience wasn’t a single moment or misunderstanding — it was a back-and-forth interaction that felt dismissive and uncomfortable, which is why it stood out enough for me to speak up.

google_reviews.text: I have been coaching Little League for many years! As parents ask questions about bat size, gloves, uniforms and everything else I suggest they go to bases loaded. They have almost  everything a player would need in stock. The customer service is fantastic. My son who is 8 years old also plays travel ball and wanted to get a USSSA bat watched the bat bros reviews. He had a top 3 of bats that he wanted to try out in the hitting area of bases loaded. His top choice was the Easton Dub, followed by the Supra and the hype fire. He had his heart set on the Dub when we left the house. After trying all 3 bats his swing was the worst with the Dub. I videoed the hitting session and showed him. I told him he did best with the Supra. The employee of bases loaded who was a very young man spoke with my son about how the he was hitting with the bat and what he thought was best for him. When a child gets really good feedback from someone that’s not their parent it confirms to them maybe this isn’t the best product for me. After my son spoke to the employee my son looked at me and said I’ll have to look at more videos on bats. I think the low pressure chill environment is fantastic. I would recommend anyone go to bases loaded and see what it’s about! You won’t be disappointed!

On 2/28/2026 between 2:00 p.m. and 3:00 p.m., I drove 45 minutes to Bases Loaded to replace my son’s all-leather glove that was recently stolen. I had previously had a good experience there, which is why I chose them over closer stores.
An employee — the only female employee working at the time who was not wearing a Bases Loaded shirt — approached us. Based on how she spoke, she appeared to be in a managerial role. While we were casually browsing bats, she began giving unsolicited and incorrect information about BBCOR regulations. I explained that I coach Pony baseball and understand league rules, and that we were not purchasing a bat. Instead of respecting that, she redirected her comments to my son and incorrectly told him he could not use BBCOR.
When I asked to see high-quality all-leather gloves — Heart of the Hide or equivalent — she told me they run $320 and asked if I was “ready to pay that.” The tone was dismissive. I came prepared to purchase a premium glove, not to be questioned about affordability.
Another employee helped us select a glove. When I requested break-in service, I was told (incorrectly) that even with break-in, my son would not be able to use it for eight months. That is simply inaccurate.
The only positive part of the visit was the young man who broke in the glove. He was thorough, patient, and ensured my son could close it properly. However, during the process, another employee questioned him in front of us about whether we were being charged separately for each break-in method — after we had already paid.
The original employee later returned, sarcastically asked if we had “ended up picking a glove,” laughed, and walked away.
I spent nearly $400 and left feeling disrespected. As a coach who regularly purchases equipment and makes recommendations to baseball families, this experience was disappointing enough that I will not be returning.
Ownership should be aware.

name: The Punch Bowl
document: The Punch Bowl. cuisine: Irish Pub. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I visited last Saturday, and the experience wasn’t quite what we expected. I had seen several videos on TikTok and was excited to give it a try. When we first arrived, we had trouble figuring out how to get from the parking garage to the entrance. We asked an employee for help, but he wasn’t sure how to direct us.

The first-floor décor and ambiance were beautiful, and we really enjoyed the silent party, that’s definitely something we would come back for. We had a reservation, but there were a lot of kids running around and even sitting at the bar area, so we tried to find another spot. We went to another bar and waited for about 5–10 minutes, but no one greeted us, so we returned to our original area.

Our server (who just recently started working there) was very attentive and respectful. The food was amazing, but the drinks were disappointing and tasted more like juice. My boyfriend ordered a Long Beach (a Long Island without soda, made with cranberry juice), and I ordered a margarita, both were extremely sweet and lacked balance.

Overall, we enjoyed the look and vibe of the venue, but the execution didn’t fully meet our expectations.

I booked a Bowling Lane for 1pm on a Sunday and we had a blast. You want your whole party to be there before your time starts and they were flexible with us, thank you Jude! We enjoyed food and drinks, and recommend the Elote Dip, Pretzel Bites, Cilantro Lime Wings, and Tacos. After the bowling we were able to get a table and play fusball on the biggest fusball table ever! They allowed us to bring our own birthday cake. Huge shout out to Noel, who provided 5 star 🌟 service and made sure our little party had the best time!

The dips platter with chips and veggies was all very good. I brought a bakery cake and our server Julia brought out a really nice cake platter to hold and display the cake which was very unexpected and welcome.

The bowling was easy to play and a staff member setup the names for us. Julia was friendly and ensured our soft drinks were always full. Frank the manager was very friendly and both welcomed us and checked on us after to ensure we were taken care of.

For the price point, the service and gaming experience exceeded a previous work event at Top Golf. Bonus points for easy and cheap garage parking, elevated service, and food that is both delicious and kept warm.

I wanted to share my experience with punch bowl social!

I typically visit this place about once a month and always have a great time. In the one instance that I did not, this establishment immediately responded, and fixed the issue. The customer service here is amazing!

The food was phenomenal, as always! I will recommend this place to ANYONE in the DMV area.

Punch Bowl Social has officially become our secret spot! The tacos here are amazing, we tried both the shrimp and the pork, and they were packed with flavor and super fresh. Honestly, some of the best bar-style tacos we’ve had.

But what keeps us coming back is the whole experience. Whether we’re playing darts, bowling, or ping pong, it’s always a good time. The atmosphere is fun, the service is great, and it’s the perfect place to unwind, eat well, and play a few games.

We love this place! highly recommend it!

google_reviews.text: This is my lowkey hookah place to head to because it’s typically not crowded, close to home, service is fast, and now, everyone gets their own hookah. Music is a little loud but that’s because there’s 4 speakers in a not super large space. If you don’t smoke hookah, it might not be as appealing because your cover includes a hookah, so I’d say go into it knowing that.

Lotus Lounge has a stylish look and a friendly/accommodating staff (which is always appreciated). However, this spot may not be the best fit if you’re looking for a traditional Arab-style shisha café.

The vibe here leans heavily toward a club-like atmosphere, with very loud music that makes it tough to hold a conversation. It’s more of a nightlife setting than a relaxed lounge. All the TVs were playing the same baseball game, so there wasn’t much variety in entertainment, and without games or other activities to engage with, it’s hard to stay for long.

The shisha itself looked good but unfortunately lacked flavor, which was a bit disappointing.

Overall, if you’re looking for a quiet, cozy place to enjoy shisha, chat with friends, or play board games, this may not be the best match. But if you’re in the mood for loud music and a more club-like energy, it might be worth a try.

google_reviews.text: If you want good Puerto Rican food go to Mi Casita Lounge. The first time we went hubby got the steak white rice & red beans. The next time hubby got the grilled chicken sandwich with lettuce/tomato and onions with some kind of sauce between two long split plantains. He enjoyed it. I got the sliders that come with French fries and coleslaw. Coleslaw was good and French fries. The burger was ok; it comes with cheese, lettuce/tomato and onions but no onions were there. The wings are usually decently sized but this time they were the smallest I've ever seen at a restaurant. Paying $1.50 per wing for these is insane.

Im going to start off by saying my waitress Lala was AWESOME… beyond that, good luck to this establishment on this up and coming neighborhood. The customer service is lacking tremendously. We walked in and were greeted and told to sit wherever we liked. We sat and we not approached for 20 minutes. I then approached the hostess and asked who our service was and she just tossed it to the closest person she was standing there talking to. Our waitress did her due diligence to get our order in before the kitchen and bar closed but when I say the BAR/BARTENDER NAMED ZEE WAS SLOWWWWW… she didn’t have the ticket due to the late entry but as i approached the bar to inform her of my order, she proceeded to inform me that two individuals that just entered the establishment were “her guests” and she would put my order in after. ABSOLUTELY NOTTT…. The entitlement was ridiculous and she was so disrespectful to us as customers but also the manager. It was my friends birthday and she TOTALLY KILLED THE VIBE. With the most condescending demeanor. I was utterly disgusted. She sat at the bar telling other customers how it was a “personal problem” and she could careless. Lol and I should’ve walked out at the moment. Trash but the ambiance was nice .

Honestly, I don’t write negative reviews, but unfortunately, I was disappointed at this place. The service was subpar. They were either short-staffed or overwhelmed, and the registers were down for about 30 minutes. We didn’t have cash either, and they couldn’t remember our orders. It was a frustrating experience.

To make matters worse, another customer asked us how the place was after hearing us complain about the slow service. It was disheartening to tell her that I wouldn’t order food from here if the bar was slow, who knows how the food would have tasted.

While I understand that this place could do better, it didn’t work out for us.

I hate giving low scores when it comes to giving reviews. First I would like to say the service and atmosphere was great. Our servicer was amazing. And I love set ups. I will definitely come here to play pool and watch some sports..

The food wasn’t that good. I had the Philly and it was just ok. Nothing special. And the drinks taste weak. I had a Long Island top self and it didn’t taste like it was top self. Overall the place and service was great. But the food and drinks wasn’t.

Come here maybe once a month and the food is always delicious and atmosphere is always fun and the crowd is always friendly. The servers are very nice and MOST of them are amazing and attentive. I understand the business and the economy so I always ask for additional assistance when the service is slow, every single time, another party steps up and corrects it. I don't run to give a bad review because a server was overwhelmed. Crowds can be unpredictable and many times people fault the people who show up and do their jobs when other people call out of work. I would like to shout out the young lady that is about 5'9 with red hair. She was absolutely amazing. She worked on a HOLIDAY, and we appreciate it. We had a great time!

document: LIT Sports Lounge & Grill. cuisine: Lounges Sports Bars American. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
We found yet another cool local bar to enjoy whenever we visit New Rochelle. We visited this place on a Saturday night as soon as they opened, so we had the place to ourselves.

Lit is a fun place to get drinks, play a few games and enjoy your night.

During our short visit we played connect four and Jenga.

The drinks were delicious, pricey but well made.

The only drawback was the drinks were served in cheap plastic cups instead of glassware. This is unfortunate because it takes away from the class of the place.
It gives the place a cheap vibe.

At almost $30 for two drinks…. Glassware would have been a better representation!

This saloon is worthy of its name. They have a whole day happy hour on Thursdays and we spent $19 for 4 beers and 2 nice drinks. Tracey, one of the bartenders, was so sweet. Her drinks brought us to life, especially the rum punch. If you're in the New Rochelle area, then that's your place on Fridays and Saturdays. Or, if you need to catch a football or baseball match, they have numerous monitors. We will certainly return just because of their hospitality.

While there was not any issues with food or drinks, I was told by the waitstaff that WiFi is not available for customers? Really? I’m with friends spending hundreds of dollars in this establishment for hours but can’t access their WiFi? This will make me think twice about coming back.
First time but drinks were good and strong. The wings!! The wings though were delicious, garlic parm! Definitely will be back.
Went to LIT this past weekend with a group of friends and we had an amazing time! Great music, food and drinks. Tracy was so nice and loved her bartenders. Definitely will go back!

google_reviews.text:
Felt like a stepped into a Bar Rescue episode -except in a good way! This place is HUGE. Based on the pics I took walking around, I believe it's standing room friendly.
Right across the street from Yankee Stadium, it appears this place is a good place before and after the game.
I came before waiting for a friend and was pleasantly surprised.
The front bar/first bar is the only one where they serve draft beer. As of 4/2/25 it's Stella Artois and Legend beer.
Their menu is small yet efficient. It corresponds with their small kitchen, smh. I thought it was a separate kitchen for those in the back but it may be one whole kitchen for the whole establishment as I didn't see another kitchen area.
gotta add this place still looks fairly new. I saw a couple of reviews from 6 months prior. It's vibe is very no frills.
Seems like a dope place to chill. Haven't seen a game at the new stadium except when it opened so I'm excited for tonight's game.
Go Yanks!
Sincerely, your local BX native 🩷

Nikki took care of the food (thank you for the "special order" salad, it was delicious!), and Jasmine took care of the great and refreshing drinks. They are both great at their jobs and make you feel welcome and comfortable, allowing you to enjoy yourself to the fullest. Needless to say, this is a great "pre" & "post" game bar to go to anytime of the year, I love the vibe.....
Stopped for a drink before the game, great location and the proces were lower than anticipated.  Smiles all around, good place!

I don’t leave reviews but an employee helped me tonight and I wanted to thank them. I rolled my ankle in my new gym shoes and took a tumble, cutting my knee during the fall, on the sidewalk out front in the Yankees post-game crowd. An employee, guy with curly brown hair under a cap, got me a bandaid (after I bought a beer) and I’m grateful. Thank you for taking the time to help me.

Went to this place for the 1st time before a day game. Great people. Can't say enough about the service. Prices were very reasonable and staff was VERY helpful to us "out of towners". Looking for ward to going back the next time we go to a game.

name: Rambling House
document: Rambling House. cuisine: Pubs Irish. located in Bronx. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Always a lovely experience. This place provides a place for the community to gather and share their love of a variety of music. I usually go to their monthly hosting of the Central Ohio Hot Jazz Society's jam session where SwingColumbus teaches a dance lesson at the beginning and then the floor is open for dancing. It has been a staple for jazz lovers and certainly for our dance scene. We're hoping the next owners do the business justice. Maybe they can fix up the floor so it can be an even better dance space.

This is a terrific small venue for drinks and live music. Theres plenty on tap to please the most uptight IPA’er and several great homemade n/a sodas.

Sound quality and mix is excellent for such a small room. Plus the lighting is amazingly appropriate for the stage size.

Consider the Rambling House for your next gig.

Small but excellent venue for live music. Parking can be a problem as it is limited. There is a small parking lot… very small. There is street parking available near the club. Be aware that it may say tickets are sold out online but there are a limited number of spots open for those who didn’t score a ticket. Drinks are reasonably priced. Come early. Bluegrass, open mic, country and lots of fun… Definitely a go to again place.

I love the Rambling House with my whole heart❤️ I’ve heard some of the best live music at this venue. Also, their ginger beer is a must have.

My band has performed here as well, and the staff have always been very accommodating and welcoming. Check this place out if you’re looking for a place with great vibes and awesome music👍

Rambling House is a hidden gem for music enthusiasts! The atmosphere is lively, the staff is friendly, and the diverse range of live performances is unbeatable. Whether you're into blues, folk, or rock, this venue has it all. The cozy ambiance and well-stocked bar add to the overall experience. It's my go-to spot for a night of fantastic tunes and good vibes. Highly recommended!

document: Louie & Ernie's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Bronx. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Yes it’s always in the “top 10 best pizza in NYC” lists — and it’s great. But it’s not worth a trip from more than a borough away. We had the margarita (which has great mozzarella and a very bright vibrant red sauce) and a very good sausage pie (the fennel sausage is great!).
Nice old style pizzeria. Rustic interior. Delicious pie. Crispy crust. Super hot on the plate. Deserves to be on the New York times best list

Was told by so many people that this was the spot to go visit. I finally went ahead and listened and pay them a visit, I went with the family and ordered 2 large pies one just cheese that was for my kids and one cheese and sausage that was my wife and I. I must say we got our first pizza which was the cheese pizza large (the kids pizza ) and I was so disappointed in how burned the underneath was I mean my kids started eating and immediately started making weird faces there mom and I asked what’s wrong they replied this thing is super burned at first we were like no way it’s fine just eat it but then we decided to try it and were absolutely stunned on how charred it was underneath I mean I had coal fire pizza before but this was definitely left unattended for a while then served it was super burned. We were very angry that the kids had to go through that but we’re also not the type of people to complain at the moment just to avoid any animosity nor any smart remarks on behalf of the staff. We then received our second pie and that was much better I even had to stop eating my portion which was half the pie that had cheese to offer it to my kids cause they were very hungry there mom had her side which was the sausage side and finished hers. All I’m saying is that if you’re going to visit this location tell then from the very beginning not to burn the pizza or leave it too long cause you will not enjoy it. This fits as a learning lesson through our process it sucks cause we were really looking forward to this but hey it’s ok maybe next time. Take care folks and enjoy just be sure to mention not to burn the pie and you should be good.

Wish I can rate this pizza. I did not get to try it because it’s cash only. I understand businesses like this don’t like to report all earnings to the IRS. But it’s 2026. We live in a time where almost no one carries cash. I was offered to use the ATM there but I shouldn’t have to be forced to pay an ATM fee and a foreign fee from my bank. I think it’s time for all businesses to not discriminate against people who don’t like to carry cash and get a machine to accept card payments
Classic Bronx pizza! Long standing, popular pizza parlor is cozy and inviting. Delicious regular pie and broccoli rabe calzone. Cash only, street parking.

name: Pugsley's Pizza
document: Pugsley's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Pugsley Pizza is a true hidden gem in the Bronx. The food is excellent, especially the pizza, and everything comes out fresh and exactly how you want it. They’re more than happy to customize your order, which makes the experience even better.

Sal behind the counter is a big part of what makes this place special. He’s incredibly friendly, provides great service, and really puts on a show. Whether he’s joking around with customers or breaking out the saxophone, he brings a fun energy that makes the visit memorable.

The Philly cheesesteak is also outstanding and definitely worth trying. The spot is close to the Bronx Zoo, making it a great stop before or after a visit. It can get busy, but that just tells you how good it is. If you’re in the area, this place is absolutely worth checking out.

Really glad Bae found this spot for our pizza fix after our nearby botanical garden visit. Can’t believe I haven’t come here before. It is off the beaten path on a side street so there was no chance of randomly passing by and spotting while in the area. Luckily they have their own parking lot which is surprising and much appreciated so parking was a breeze. The shop is family run and I love that for them. The slices are really, really good. You have to try the home made hot oil/ sauce. The slices were so good I had to take two home for later. This is definitely the to go pizza shop when in the area.
The inside restaurant is very eclectic. Kinda dirty looking with worn out cushioned benches but perhaps that’s the charm.

A real college greasy spoon kind of place. The 1st thing you see on entering is a walnut dining room table an chairs... right out of grandma's house. You order your pizza, then sit at a cozy booth surrounded by grafitti on the walls. Signatures and epithets from customers in years gone by. When your order is ready, the pier man strikes a large gong! The food was great, and the place was a fun visit!

Rustic college pizzaria next to Fordham Univ. Eclectic atmosphere with wooden bench booths. Had pepperoni slices and garlic knots with can of soda = $16. I wanted to like it but both dishes were bland and disappointing. Little to no seasoning on the pizza/pepperoni, with somewhat mushy dough. Acompanying marinara sauce was thin and didn't stick to the knots when dipped. I only ate 1. Friendly service.

Humongous slices and the loveliest people working there!!

We got a whole penne vodka pizza and it took us 4 meals to finish, so worth the money.

document: Prizreni Grill. cuisine: American Pizza Creperies. located in Bronx. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Another local gem that my sister and I found. First time trying Albanian food and it was fantastic. Now we like to meet there with our friends for Brunch. Will definitely be going there very often. Their beef byrek is great.

I just wanna start off by saying how nice and welcoming the staff are inside the establishment. The hospitality in here is very nice and makes me feel like I’m back home in the balkans. My sister and I ordered the Margarita cheese pizza, goulash, and tres leches (trileqe) homemade cake. Everything is beautiful inside, of photos, decorum, and the bathroom is very pretty as well. I’m beyond pleased and satisfied of how I was treated, greeted, and welcomed in the establishment and I wish them success from one business owner to another, you guys did great. Don’t miss out on this amazing gem here in the Bronx.

Fantastic experience at Prizreni Grill. The staff treats you like family and the food is consistently delicious. The qebapa, grilled chicken, and traditional sides are all top quality. One of the best Balkan restaurants around!

Went for a date night and it did not disappoint. I am thrilled that an authentic, family/friend run Albanian restaurant is on Morris Park. We ordered a lot of food and enjoyed it ALL! The flavors are great and you can’t find a great pour of wine for the price anywhere else! We will be back! Thank you Prizenri Grill!

Our absolute favorite Albanian restaurant! The food is always fresh, authentic, and made with so much care. Every dish reminds us of home and the flavors are truly incredible. From the appetizers to the main dishes and desserts, everything is consistently delicious and beautifully prepared.

What makes this place even more special are the owners, Mirlinda and Levent. They are truly amazing people who go above and beyond to make every guest feel welcomed and appreciated. Their hospitality, kindness, and attention to detail create such a warm and family-like atmosphere.

You can really see the passion they have for their restaurant and for the Albanian community. If you’re looking for authentic Albanian cuisine and outstanding service, this is the place to go. Highly recommended  we will always keep coming back! 🇦🇱❤️

name: Luciano's Pizza
document: Luciano's Pizza. cuisine: Pizza. located in Bronx. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Love this place.  My 'Go To' Italian.  Laughing at the haters.  Great menu, food is excellent, prices are very reasonable and service is always good.  So this isn't high end Italian, but is solid cheap, good Italian.  And a very nice place.  Had a pasta and then got a cannoli - which was excellent.  So their red sauce isn't awesome, but it's fine.  Their pizza was pretty good as well.  Been in town for 3 months and think I've gone here 5 times already.  It's a solid place worth giving a try.

Service was awesome. Food was good, especially sesame bun when we sat down, and good tomato brushetta. Not a fan a dogmatic menu statements against substitutions, etc. Also my wife was not impressed with having to ask for (and pay extra) for a tiny bowl of side pasta for chicken parm. Tables seem to be too close together. Overall OK experience being our first time there.

Nice spot nestled in Hunter mill plaza. Very cool atmosphere doesn’t feels like you are in Italy, chunky tomatoe sauce was spectacular as it is imported from Italy, and lasagna was delicious. Salad was fresh and tasty, highly recommend Luciano’s. Server was great too.

And the spaghetti with meat sauce and wedding soup was great, the service was fantastic, reasonably priced.

As they should the server checked up on us a couple times after the food was delivered.

There is one improvement I'd recommend they make, on the check there's a QR code to pay your bill at the table but it only works with an iPhone it will not work with Android, which doesn't make any sense since Android has a much larger market share than iPhone does nowadays.

Luciano’s – A Go-To Spot in Oakton for Authentic Italian

🍕 Incredible Pizza
Must-Try: White/Cheese Pizza
The White/Cheese Pizza is unbeatable—the crust strikes the perfect balance of crispy and chewy, while garlic, olive oil, pecorino, and mozzarella make it rich without being too heavy. I’ve tried much of the menu, but this one keeps me coming back.

🍷 Wine & 🍨 Dessert
Wine: Not the largest selection, but carefully chosen and pairs well with pizza and pasta.

Ice Cream: Smooth, creamy, and the perfect way to wrap up dinner.

🏠 Atmosphere
Warm, consistent, and welcoming. Whether it’s a family dinner, casual night out, or a quick bite, Luciano’s always feels like home.

🤝 Service
Friendly, attentive staff who keep the experience consistently excellent. That consistency is why this place has been a favorite of mine for years.

✅ Bottom Line:
If you’re in the Vienna/Oakton area and love Italian food, Luciano’s is a must-visit. After all these years, it’s still one of my absolute favorites.
