name: Banhmis Asian Cuisine & Bubble Tea
document: Banhmis Asian Cuisine & Bubble Tea. cuisine: Vietnamese Bubble Tea Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
It was an online order:

Very disappointing experience. Out of our $60 order, the only good item was the stewed pork burger — everything else went in the trash.

The Pad Thai was inedible due to an overly sour sauce that tasted nothing like traditional Pad Thai, and didn’t even include dried tofu. The sliced beef pho was completely bland and lacked seasoning. The fresh salad was missing the avocado listed in the description and was watery from excess moisture in the greens. Although the ingredients seemed fresh, the dishes had no real flavor — even after we added our own spices.

Unfortunately, this was our first and last time ordering from this restaurant.

Small storefront in a strip mall on Hylan Blvd. near Nelson Ave. More of a takeout place  but some small tables to eat in. First thing on the table was some chips with an interesting dipping sauce. Sort of a pico de gallo with fish sauce. Very tasty. I ordered from the regular menu instead of a lunch special. I was pleasantly surprised when the won ton soup arrived with excellent garlic bread on the side. Won tons were small but there was plenty of them. My banh mi was nicely filled on good bread. My only complaint would be there was too little daikon,  mostly carrots. Service was quick and friendly. I'll b e back for some pho.

If you’re looking for a place that serves fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented Vietnamese food, Banhmis is the spot. The attention to detail in both the food and service is outstanding.

We ordered a sampler platter, and it was nothing short of amazing. The shrimp spring rolls were light, fresh, and packed with crisp veggies perfectly paired with a rich peanut dipping sauce. The crispy egg rolls had a golden crunch and burst with savory filling, especially delicious with the sweet chili sauce. Their Vietnamese sausage had that satisfying smoky-sweet flavor, while the fried chicken wings were juicy, crispy, and addictive. Every bite felt thoughtfully prepared and authentic.

What really stood out were the dipping sauces. Each one brought a unique balance of sweet, savory, and tangy flavors that elevated the dishes. It wasn’t just a meal, it was an experience in how flavors can complement each other.

The presentation was beautiful too
served on a bamboo tray with fresh lettuce and vibrant colors that made the whole spread feel inviting.

Banhmis strikes the perfect balance between homestyle comfort and restaurant quality refinement. Whether you’re coming for a casual lunch, a dinner with friends, or just craving fresh and bold Vietnamese flavors, this place should be at the top of your list.

Highly recommend you won’t be disappointed!

I have to say, the General Tso’s chicken  is easily one of the best I’ve had. The chicken was perfectly crispy on the outside yet tender and juicy on the inside. The sauce struck that ideal balance of sweet, savory, and tangy with just the right amount of heat, coating every piece without being too heavy

rice was light and fluffy, soaking up the flavors beautifully, and the broccoli added a fresh crunch to round out the dish. The portion was generous, and every bite was satisfying from start to finish.

Lovely place to get a bite to eat! I have had my eye on this place and it does not disappoint. The staff were very kind and the atmosphere was relaxing. The food was light and filling. Definitely coming back, Vietnamese food is one of my go to foods when I'm hungry
Amazing food and service! The pho portions are very generous for the price and it is so flavorful. The staff members are kind and friendly. Can’t wait to come back!

google_reviews.text:
Prices have gone up quite a bit. Other than that….

Jade Island is a true Staten Island gem that offers a perfectly nostalgic and delightful dining experience. From the moment you walk in, the fun, classic tiki atmosphere sets a fantastic mood. The food is always fresh and satisfying, with their signature Cantonese and Polynesian dishes hitting all the right notes. Whether you're enjoying a legendary Pu Pu Platter or a flavorful Mai Tai, Jade Island provides great service and an atmosphere that guarantees a memorable time.

My grandparents, parents, and now myself and my siblings have come to Jade Island for decades. Now living in PA, we aren’t able to come as often but to this day after living in PA for over 15 years, Jade Island is still our favorite Chinese restaurant and food! Nothing compares. Atmosphere, vibes, food, even the kindness of John and the staff. While some may say the inside is outdated, I truly believe that it adds to the charm. I never want it to change lol. And while my family member, a weekly visitor to Jade Island, was in the hospital they sent along his favorite drink as a treat in an awful time and offered to visit. when I tell you this place is a complete hidden gem (not so hidden since it is still pretty popular) but all my years living in this island, i’ve never had it. such amazing authentic chinese food. best on the island, not fast food, real cooked meals. great family meal deals and even had a ton of food left over it was amazing great service, the staff were so welcoming and friendly. will definitely be coming back for more!

Giving it 3 stars -
The food is still great, the only "old school" Chinese dine in restaurant left in my opinion. We drive over an hour from northern New Jersey just to have their lobster cantonese! Spare ribs are still great. In reality only true place to get roast pork fried rice, and you can't beat the shrimp with lobster sauce.
But what I've noticed the last three times we've been there is the amount of food that leaves the table to be packed to take home is never the amount of food when we open the containers later.
I was extremely confident about the amount of roast pork fried rice that left our table, not less then the little bit in the smaller container. Definitely left two large shrimp, only one in the container. Roast pork with string beans, only had a few string beans on the container. I find it extremely disappointing as I've been a patron here for almost fifty years. I did call the next day and spoke with a woman who claimed to be a manager, she was going to call me back...
She knew exactly who we were as she knew the total of our bill @$279.00, plus $50 cash tip.
We order to take food home.
Sad that I'll never go back, our loss.

Best of the best! Makes me wish I still live on Staten Island, but we make it a point to go there every single time we visit. I grew up on Staten Island and this place has not changed one bit. It's 50+ years old, and everything around it has changed dramatically, but yet they still have top shelf old school NYC Chinese food. This place is a real treat don't miss it!!!!

Once upon a time you came here for a good meal at a reasonable price. You arrived and the walls, adorn with portraits of politicians and Hollywood elites, welcomed you into the hallowed main dinning room. They elevated the atmosphere, but the overall retro feel balanced the scale, good food, fair price, strip mall, next to a convenience store or two selling malt liquor and 40ozs.

Fast forward to today. $18 cocktails, $80 duck, $49 Leek Spouts with Shrimp. The portraits have yellowed with age, the staff is still very helpful, but balance it once had is off kilter now. It's still next to a convenience store, in a strip mall, is fine overall food, but the prices are higher than downtown DC. In my opinion, the prices are just too high for the level of food.

You can tell by the ambiance that you've stepped into a place that had served famous people.  There is an old time classic Chinese restaurant vibe here.
The ambiance is gorgeous, the decor is history, with pictures of patrons from wall to wall.

The servers and staff are professionally dressed, I felt underdressed

Walked into the place around 2:50pm, as i read through the menu, and decide on the lunch special, the waiter says, sorry but it's after 3pm (3:02pm) no more lunch special.  Bummed, as now the prices from lunch to dinner are a 3-4 dollar amount difference, portion might be larger, but for one person, I didn't need more of just one dish, I wanted variety.

Everything was just basic, and the fried calamari's funnel cake like batter was quite sweet and greasy for me.

This place is one of the most famous Peking duck restaurants in the area, so it was incredibly crowded when we visited. The duck itself was delicious, and the other dishes were all above average as well. The service wasn’t unfriendly, but it wasn’t particularly warm either—pretty much what you’d expect from a typical busy Chinese restaurant.

Peking Gourmet Inn is an absolute legend in Falls Church. This place has been a community staple for decades, and it shows everyone from local families to politicians and celebrities has eaten here, and for good reason.

Their signature Peking Duck is the star of the show. It comes out perfectly roasted, and the staff slices it right in front of you with the kind of precision that turns dinner into a performance. The crispy skin, the warm homemade pancakes, the fresh scallions grown on their own farm every detail is next-level.

The restaurant itself is spacious and classic, but don’t let that fool you it gets busy fast. Reservations are definitely recommended. Parking can be tough (the lot is small and always packed), but once you’re inside and tasting that duck, you’ll realize it was absolutely worth the effort.

The Peking Gourmet Inn 🇨🇳 clearly has had better days…also prices are severely inflated and quality/price ratio is not there (xtip $222 for 2 adults + 2 kids).

Probably in a large group setting cost will get diluted, but still found prices too high for the experience and the food itself. Happy to have a second go to try other dishes, but I was not impressed.

Food wise the Snow peas with roasted garlic were very good, the ribs appetizer was ok, the rice and lo mein were also ok, and the famous Peking duck was a 7 out of 10 (the pancakes were dry & flour forward).

🦆 🍜 🫛

Attaching a few pictures of the same

Six family members went here for dinner on a busy Saturday night. It was a wonderful dining experience. We were seated promptly as per our reservation time, and our orders were taken smoothly and with all the menu changes we requested. Very accommodating.

The food was delicious, fresh, and with generous portions. This is definitely a cut above most Chinese restaurants. I've read some negative reviews complaining about the service and food, and can definitely say that was the opposite of what we experienced. The barbecue spare ribs were among the best we've ever had, the shrimp were nice and fresh, and the steamed vegetables were perfectly prepared. The menu is extensive.

The tables were spaced far enough apart so we could hear ourselves talk and didn't feel crowded even though the restaurant was busy.

The restaurant is in a strip mall with lots of free parking, which is very convenient.

We definitely will return and recommend this place for excellent Chinese food. It's also a great place for lunch and takeout.

This is one of my go-to Chinese restaurants in the area. Over the last few years, I have been ordering from here consistently. We often do takeout more often than dine in, because the atmosphere of the restaurant is not worth going to. The food here is usually prepared fast, so it is a perfect option if you are on a time crunch.

We had not gone to this restaurant in the last 3 months, but tried it again last night and found that the foods were less flavorful and did not have as much oil. Maybe they changed their chef?

My future reviews are a mix of all the dishes we have tried over the years. I also included my recent thoughts on the dishes and how they have changed.

Steamed Vegetable Dumplings: we found these dumplings very bland and unflavorful. They came with green veggies inside, and neither the veggies nor the dumpling had any seasoning.

Dan Dan Noodles: these noodles are a household favorite. The noodles are soft and perfectly chewy, and the oil has sichuan in it and is very flavorful. We always remove the meat, and have found the dish a bit too oily but it is still very good.

Scallion Pancake: so we loved these pancakes too (we had to stop ordering them because they are so fried we are scared of getting a heart attack) but they are perfectly crispy, and have a strong flavor of garlic and green onions.

Wonton Soup: this soup was also not good. The soup itself was very bland (it felt like it was just water) and the dumplings inside are not flavorful.

Hot and Sour Soup: the hot and sour soup here is DEFINITELY HOT. so beware

Egg Drop Soup: the egg drop soup here is also fine. It has that gelatin texture and the egg sometimes freaks me out because i can’t remember getting eggs in water.

Chicken w. Broccoli: the chicken and broccoli is always ordered in my house for the people who don’t like very spicy food. It has a sweetness to it, and i personally love the broccoli because it is soaked in the sauce

Shredded Chicken w. Garlic Sauce: we used to order this chicken a lot, and stopped recently. It has a pink/reddish color and the garlic sauce tasted more like tomato.

Diced Chicken Sautéed w. 3 Types of Pepper: this 3 pepper chicken is ALWAYS ordered in my house. It is fried and tossed in a sichuan oil with 3 different peppers (they are very spicy). Every time we order this dish, it always tastes different. Sometimes softer, sometimes chewier, sometimes there are bigger pieces.

Braised Flounder Filet and Napa Cabbage in Chili Oil Sauce: we have recently started to order this dish and it tastes like the 3 pepper chicken, just oiler. There are soft and tender pieces of fish drenched in a soup of sichuan pepper oil. I am not a big seafood person, but this dish does not taste very fishy.

Vegetable Fried Rice: this fried rice is a bit bland, so we always order it to have with a chicken or tofu dish. The flavbvor is there, but you have to focus very hard to taste it. The rice tastes a bit undercooked sometimes, but i prefer the texture and taste. It is tossed in egg, mushrooms, and peas, and has a bit of a saltiness flavor. I recommend getting it, just don’t plan to have it plain.

Vegetable Chow Mein: i never really liked chow mein, and the one from china chalet is not very good. It is a bit bland, and does not have many veggies.

Singapore Rice Noodles: these rice noodles are very different from the rest of the menu because instead of being very saucy, it is so heavily spiced that you can taste the texture of the spice in your mouth. The spice is not spicy, but instead tastes like a curry.

Ma Po Tofu: the mapo tofu here is also another staple in our house. It also comes in a chili oil, and the tofu basically melts in your mouth.

Home Style Tofu w. Black Mushrooms: this tofu dish has quickly become one of my favorite. The tofu pieces are large and are pan fried, so they have a nice crispy crust. The sauce is not spicy, but instead brings flavor that the mushrooms are also drenched in.

My husband and I both ordered the same meal: the apple pie pancakes (of course!), eggs with cheese, and chicken sausage. I paired mine with a fresh-squeezed orange juice, while he enjoyed a mimosa. The bill was very reasonable for the quality and portions we received, especially in NYC. Overall, it was a great experience, and I’ll definitely continue to be a supporter. If you’re a pancake lover, this spot is always worth the visit!

Extremely welcoming and a lovely place to visit, a hidden gem within the subway but not one to miss!

Truly a happy accident!!! 🙏🏽❤️

Sometimes the best mornings are the ones you don’t plan. After an early subway misadventure that landed us in the Bronx instead of Battery park for coffee and sunrise… (OOPS).

My wife and I didn’t mind, We grabbed a quick breakfast sandwich, stayed positive and happy as we headed back toward Manhattan to find coffee and plan the rest of our day. As we were walking out of the subway station, we stumbled upon a small underground café that felt like pure magic.

What truly made the experience unforgettable was meeting E, the barista. He wasn’t even supposed to be working that morning, which made our encounter feel like fate. From the moment we walked in and heard him chatting with the customers we felt his energy.

We ordered and sat down. In between customers when it was quiet, we laughed, swapped stories, and totally vibed with E!!! We ended up staying nearly two hours, playing chess and having a truly fantastic experience. Exactly what we had wanted in a NYC coffee shop.

The cappuccino was absolutely phenomenal!!! And more than the delicious drinks, it was the feeling of connection and serendipity that made this café stand out.

This whole morning was a happy accident, the wrong train, the unexpected detour, and the chance meeting with E all came together to create one of the most memorable café experiences we’ve ever had.

If you ever find yourself wandering Manhattan, don’t be afraid to take a wrong turn, you might just stumble into something wonderful too.

Cheers to Happy Accidents, Fate and Love!!! ☕️

We are coming back into the city Dec 1st-5th and we will be sure not to miss Tiny Dancer! We look forward to meeting the other tiny dancers, but if we wanted to catch E,  when would be a good time to stop in?

Flat white is so good and the pastry in the picture is soooo good (but I forgot the name) there’s also chess to play and many coffee beans to get too! Super friendly staff

It was nice to finally visit the brick and mortar location of a brand I usually buy at Sprouts. I ordered a vanilla latte with whole milk, added a touch of simple syrup, and topped it with cinnamon. It ended up being a fantastic drink, perfectly made.

First of all, it is not DoorDash Only, I don’t know why the title says that. You can order from the official Xi’an Famous food website or the Four Mile website. I have visited this restaurant many times before in NYC, including the flagship Flushing location. Happy this one opened in the DMV. The good: the burgers are on point, the cold noodles are yum. The bad: the flat wide noodles do not travel well. I had to drive 30 mins home after the pick up, and the chew in the noodles probably lasted maybe 3 mins after I started eating. The taste is good. They need to open a spot with seats so the noodles can be enjoyed immediately. I heard they are actively looking for a Maryland location with sit-down options. Can’t wait!

So glad Xi’an Famous Foods has finally made it to the DMV! I took my parents to their NYC location many years ago, driven by homesickness after weeks of traveling in the U.S. The chewy, hand ripped noodles instantly transported us back to northern China, where wheat noodles are widely loved and celebrated. They still remember that meal to this day.

Fast forward to now, I ordered via DoorDash after doing some research. Since it’s a shared space with other vendors, there’s no dine in option, and the parking and pickup process can be a bit confusing, as others have mentioned. But nothing you can’t figure out.

We ordered the lamb and pork noodles, cold gluten salad, pork dumplings, and pork burgers. We reheated the noodles after the car ride, which softened them slightly, but the flavor was exactly how I remembered - bold, savory, and spicy. The noodles were well ripped, with a wide, smooth surface. The gluten salad was tangy and refreshing, and the pork burgers were packed with juicy braised meat in firm bread.

The dumplings are real surprise. I usually make dumplings at home and don’t often order them out, but Xi’an Famous Foods is an exception. Their spicy and sour pork dumplings are actually regional specialties and definitely worth trying.

For drinks, I recommend the Sour Hawberry and Chrysanthemum Tea. The hawberry is fruity and refreshing, while the chrysanthemum is cooling and calming, both perfect to balance out the richness of the food.

If you’re a first-timer, I highly recommend the lamb hand ripped noodles + spicy & sour pork dumplings + sour hawberry tea.

Hope I can enjoy those perfectly chewy noodles fresh out of the pot soon! Will be on the lookout for their full service location.

Drove over for pick up(only option) on a Sunday afternoon around 2:30.  Be aware the pickup location is behind the 7-Eleven.

Parking is difficult and very tight when busy. There is no where close to sit and eat. Also when you ask for cutlery they don't include in your order they put it in a basket for you to grab. No napkins.  Forks were grab and go and not wrapped separately. You walk in find your order in the website based on text and a locker opens with your food. Pretty straight forward interesting concept.

We ordered 3 different dumplings. These were probably our favorite.   Cucumber salad was very good.  We also ordered 3 different kinds of noodles. Lamb, pork, and beef. All were good though we were hoping for more. One friend who goes often to New York mentioned the noodles weren't as good here.

For us the food wasn't good enough to deal with the hassle of the location. If they moved though we would definitely give it another try or when we go to New York.

An honest review from a longtime New Yorker who used to walk 10+ blocks every week just to get my Xi’an Famous Foods fix: the taste here is exactly as I remembered from the NYC locations, so that’s a big win. I highly recommend the spicy lamb hand-ripped noodles and the stewed pork burger. My favorite dish back in New York was the cold noodles, and while I didn’t realize this location’s version comes without noodles, no problem—I just cooked some at home and added them in.

The sour hawberry tea was the perfect palate cleanser after the rich, spicy meal.

This location is a bit far for us, and since there’s no dine-in option, the food had to sit through a long car ride - unfortunately the noodles got a bit soggy. But I was happy to read in other reviews that the ghost kitchen setup is temporary and that they’re opening full locations closer to my home. When that happens, I’ll definitely be back to my weekly visits.

name: Shu Jiao Fu Zhou
document: Shu Jiao Fu Zhou. cuisine: Chinese. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
When we walked in, there was a long line, but it moved quickly. I only waited about 5–7 minutes to order. They have signs on the wall saying you should know your order before stepping up and clean up after yourself, but I noticed a lot of people don’t really pay attention to that — so just be prepared.

What I ordered:

Wheat Noodles with Peanut Sauce (#5) – It was good, but I wish the sauce was thicker and more buttery so it would coat the noodles better. It was a bit watery, so the sauce kept sliding off when I picked up the noodles. Adding the chili oil from the table definitely helped improve the flavor.

Small Pork-Filled Fish Ball Soup (#11) – Pretty good overall. The broth was clean and hot (though it cooled down quickly). The fish balls tasted like real fish paste, not the powdery hotpot-style.

Overall, it was a good experience — two dishes for under $10 is hard to beat. Service was quick and efficient as long as you’re ready to order without hesitation. Also, it’s cash only.

We got our food to go, but would have sat inside if we didn’t need to be someplace shortly after our stop in. We got the wheat noodles with peanut butter sauce and the pork and chive dumplings and with tip it was $10 for two people for lunch! What a bargain. The noodles were delightful and we added the leftover dumpling sauce, had we ate there I would have added Sriracha to it and it would have been perfect. The dumplings were crisp and steaming hot and delicious, though they did short us one so we only got seven instead of the eight we ordered. Make sure you count before you leave! We will be back and dine in to enhance our experience.

We tried to go here a couple of weeks ago, but the line was long and we were very hungry, so we left. Good news was that today the line was short, but ended up pretty long by the time we left. It seemed to move quickly though. They also have plenty of tables, so by the time you order one is usually available before your food is ready. Given the lines, I was expecting the food to be better. We got a #1a and a #11. The noodles and meat in 1a were ok, but not great. The broth wasn’t super flavorful. I’m not sure if it’s what we ordered, but this was probably the first place from the infatuation best noodles in nyc place where we said we don’t need to come back. Note, I love spicy food. Like really, really spicy. They didn’t really have anything spicy, minus the chili oil, which isn’t even spicy. It also was one of the most unappetizing things I have seen in a while. I am not sure how long it was been there, but I think it has more nastiness in it than bob Marley’s hair. I am not sure what the red sauce is, but it isn’t sriracha.

Absolutely delicious food and quick service. BRING CASH! It’s very busy inside but it’s common for you to ask to sit at a table with other people if seats are open. I got the wheat noodles with peanut butter sauce and vegetable dumplings for $8.25! Wow such a steal. I’m vegetarian and with my two dishes I left full and satisfied. My friend recommended the wheat noodles vs the thick rice noodles because she thinks they soak up the sauce more and I was happy with them! I’m sure personal preference factors into preferred noodle type. No frills place, but can’t beat the price or the flavor here. I think it’s worth the hype

I came here for lunch with a few friends who have never tried Fuzhounese food before. We ordered fried dumplings, steamed dumplings, peanut butter noodles, wonton soup, and fish ball soup. We all enjoyed the food and left super full. The prices are very affordable, we only spent $35 for a total of 4 people. There are a good amount of tables and also a bathroom for customers. I definitely will be coming back here soon!

name: Very Fresh Noodles
document: Very Fresh Noodles. cuisine: Taiwanese Chinese Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Very Fresh Noodles—Not Every Long Line is Worth It. This One Is.

I’ve been to Chelsea Market a few dozen times and that Very Fresh Noodles line was always there to greet me…the kind of crowd that makes you wonder if some celebrity is handing out autographs inside. I always moved on, but this day the line was manageable, so I finally made my pilgrimage.

Watching those noodle masters work right in front of you is worth the price of admission alone — this place runs like an air traffic control tower, every move calculated and nothing left to chance.

I bravely tackled the Seaweed Salad first and those long rubbery strips put up a mean fight against my feeble chompers and my chopsticks.

This experience was more like navigating an obstacle course than a side dish. I did not enjoy the texture of this offering and the spice level was not for the common man.

Then the La Mei Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup landed and completely reset the table. Slow-braised beef shanks, hand-pulled noodles, pickled mustard greens, bok choy, scallion — all swimming in one of the most deeply layered broths I’ve encountered in this city.

This broth has a memory — the kind that stays with you long after the bowl is empty…I found myself slowing down just to make it last. Full stop.

Some lines in this city aren’t worth the wait. This is not one of them. I would gladly queue up any day of the week and twice on Sunday.

• Delicious soup and noodles! I really loved the fresh, firm noodles paired with the hot broth and beef.
• The soup was well-seasoned, though during our last visit I found it a bit too oily—I also would’ve loved more broth. The beef was good but could be more tender.
• Staff are kind and service is very quick.
• Will definitely be back to try other variations. A must-try in Chelsea! 🍜

This was our second visit with family, and it’s clear this spot consistently delivers excellent food.

Tucked into a small nook inside Chelsea Market, this vendor always seems to draw a line before opening — especially compared to many other stalls in the market — which speaks to how many regulars it has. Watching the chef knead and hand-pull the noodles right in front of you is both impressive and genuinely fun, adding to the overall experience.

We ordered the tingly and spicy noodles with beef, opting for the soup version because the broth is so flavorful (though you can also order it “dry” if you want to focus purely on the noodles). The broth is consistently savory with a deep umami richness, and the noodles are delicate yet pleasantly chewy — soft, fresh, and incredibly satisfying. Combined, it’s the ultimate comfort food, especially on a cold day.

Portions are generous, particularly with the beef, and service moves fairly quickly given the popularity. This easily ranks as one of the best dishes we’ve had at Chelsea Market, and it’s a place we’ll happily return to again.

Very Fresh Noodles is awesome. Yes there will be a long line of people waiting, yes make the line, it will be worth it.  I had the La Mei Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup, and it was just delicious! Spicy, beefy, warm and prefect for the cold weather, the noodles are freshly made and they were just perfection. This place is 10/10 when it comes to the food. It will be hard to find a place to sit but again, totally worth the hassle.

Located within the Chelsea Market, this noodle spot is a favourite for tourist and locals alike.

The Taiwanese beef noodle soup - is indicated on the menu as best seller, and I can see why!

The soup base is a rich broth full of flavour, it can be ordered mild or spicy. I choose mild and it was spot on.
There is plenty of beef and the fresh hand stretched noodles as excellent topped with coriander, and spring onions.
Highly recommend!
This was a perfect dish.

document: Han Dynasty. cuisine: Szechuan Beer, Wine & Spirits. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The restaurant was clean and nice. The food was beautifully presented and delicious. Everyone has their own taste. In my personal opinion, the roast duck was too greasy. The skin wasn't crispy. Except for that dish, the other dishes were all good.

Food was good on average. Favorites were the fried glutinous rice dumplings and the duck.
The rice noodle rolls didn’t have as much elasticity than other places I’ve tried.
The congee was good, but the chicken was on the dry side. We got it with preserved egg and it came with chicken in the base. Would get it without chicken next time if that’s an option.

Astonishingly good.  Can’t go wrong with this order:  beef chow fun, Chinese broccoli with garlic, salt fish fried rice with chicken.  Always read into the reviews before you dine… this place has bad reviews because of service…which I’ll agree is average.. but the food is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING.  We ordered a to go order 30 minutes before closing and it came out perfect.  You see this sear on this garlic clove.. I can’t begin to describe the attention to detail to cooking surfaces, heat, and the right amount of oil to sear garlic in this way.  Nothing was burnt, veggies were crispy, everything was fresh, beef in the Chow Fun was a melty tender ribeye.  Superb… just flawless execution here.  This is attentive cooking in high temp woks using fresh ingredients and clean oil.
Will certainly look to dine in next time we’re in Virginia. If you want good service with mediocre food, visit Peking Gourmet… last I checked nobody is ordering Chinese food for the service.

Han Place is the perfect spot for anyone looking to enjoy an elevated Chinese dining experience. The elegant and upscale interior sets it apart from your usual Chinese restaurant, making it ideal for celebrating special occasions. The menu feels more refined, with carefully crafted dishes that highlight both flavor and presentation. Their dim sum is especially noteworthy – beautifully made, delicious, and served with attention to detail. If you’re in the mood for a premium Chinese dining experience, Han Place is highly recommended.

Been here many times, the food has always been ok, the restaurant decor is very good, servers always friendly. Today the food was more disappointing, we order 2 pork ribs both were sour, the meat was clearly bad. We also ordered beef dry chow fun, also the beef was sour.
The duck was cheap at $58 but it also feels like it wasn’t recently made… good value but quality is so so
However something that they do consistently well is their congee and fried rice. Overall i think it’s a 3-3.5/5 restaurant. If the quality of the food improved, it would be one of the top in dmv

google_reviews.text: We had the most amazing and flavorful Szechuan style sliced pork belly. The Chinese bacon with cauliflower was also fabulous. Even though this sounds random, the fried rice cake with brown sugar is my personal favorite. The sweet rice dumplings were also good. You should give it a try. You probably won’t regret it.

This place feels genuinely Sichuan the moment we walk in—bold aromas and unapologetic spice.
The standout is the hot & spicy shredded beef with radish, a dish I haven’t found anywhere else.
The beef is tender and packed with chili heat, while the crisp radish balances it perfectly.
It’s spicy, fragrant, and layered rather than overwhelming.
If you’re craving real Sichuan flavors, this spot delivers.

Some of the most authentic Sichuan food I’ve had in NYC (and I love Sichuan food and eat it maybe too much lol). The 辣子鸡 (dry fried chicken with peppers) and mapo tofu is the best I’ve had in Manhattan. This place is more of an old school/traditional spot. The location definitely surprised me as it’s right by Port Authority but it’s a real hidden gem. No frills, no fuss but the food does not play around. Cabbage with pork was very good, perfect flavors. And the mapo tofu had a great numbing flavor - that’s how you know it’s legit. I think a lot of Sichuan restaurants tone down the mala, but this place doesn’t shy away from the numbing spice which I love.

Sky Pavilion is a great spot for authentic Chinese comfort food.
I ordered a braised beef dish with rice, and it was rich, flavorful, and very well balanced — the beef was tender and the sauce was perfect with rice. Portions were generous and everything tasted freshly made.

Service was friendly and efficient, and the atmosphere felt warm and casual, great for both quick meals and sitting down with friends.
Highly recommend if you’re looking for real Chinese flavors. Will definitely come back.

document: Joe's Shanghai. cuisine: Shanghainese Seafood Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Would recommend coming. Even With a long wait time(we didn't wait that long) as it'll be worth it. The food tasted so fresh. It comes piping hot. Great choices and will happily alter dishes to suit your taste(take out certain veggies or sauces). Quick and attentive service. The chicken and corn soup was incredible dont be fooled that its just a 'soup'. The crab and pork soup dumplings another top recommendation. Chow mein noodles were good but not overly 'wow'. The chicken in sesame *chefs kiss*.

Joe’s Shanghai in Chinatown NYC absolutely lives up to its reputation for soup dumplings. We got the crab and pork soup dumplings, which are apparently what they’re famous for—and for good reason. They were fantastic, full of flavor, and easily the highlight of the meal.

I was honestly shocked when I first walked in. I’m used to seeing mostly locals eating at restaurants in Chinatown, but this place was packed with a very diverse crowd, all clearly there for the soup dumplings. That alone says a lot.

That said, not everything was a hit. I wouldn’t recommend the General Tso’s chicken—it tasted more like cheap boneless wings than a proper Chinese dish. We also ordered the seafood pan-fried noodles. It had a nice variety of seafood, but there were definitely more vegetables than meat. I’ve heard the pork version comes with a lot more meat, so I’d probably try that next time.

Overall, it’s still a fantastic place and absolutely worth visiting, especially for the soup dumplings. Just be warned: it fills up quickly because they’re famous, and pro tip—bring cash, because they don’t take credit cards.

Standard American Chinese food. Cash only and kind of sus that they have 2 little ATMs right at the entrance so they can get a cut from both the ATM and not having to report cash income lol. Food came out very hot but broccoli was cold - not because it was out but because it was served raw.

Wasn't a fan of the waiters standing right next to us and hovering over us. Overly attentive for no reason as the drinks are canned (no refills) and there's nothing for you to really need except for your food and maybe an extra set of utensils if you dropped yours. Chili oil was great. Nice looking restaurant tho.

Bathrooms need help. 2 of the 3 toilets were dirty.

And yes, standard 18% tip. You pay in cash and the waiters still ask "do you want your change?"  YES. I do want my change, you already charged the tip so why would I tip again for subpar service?

I grew up in the Bay Area, so when I say this place has the best xiao long bao (pork soup dumplings) I have ever had, it is not a statement I make lightly. All of the food here is really delicious. The scallion pancake and salt & pepper pork were also highlights, but everything else we've tried here has been solid. It is CASH ONLY, so remember to bring some with you when you come here. But definitely come for the soup dumplings, and then stay and get stuffed on everything else!

It’s a tradition to eat at Chinatown during the lunar new year celebrations and this place unfailingly always makes every visit memorable. Awesome Chinese food and the best people and service. Can’t really go wrong with anything. This time we got schezwan fish and crispy chicken and they were amazing.

Astonishingly good.  Can’t go wrong with this order:  beef chow fun, Chinese broccoli with garlic, salt fish fried rice with chicken.  Always read into the reviews before you dine… this place has bad reviews because of service…which I’ll agree is average.. but the food is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING.  We ordered a to go order 30 minutes before closing and it came out perfect.  You see this sear on this garlic clove.. I can’t begin to describe the attention to detail to cooking surfaces, heat, and the right amount of oil to sear garlic in this way.  Nothing was burnt, veggies were crispy, everything was fresh, beef in the Chow Fun was a melty tender ribeye.  Superb… just flawless execution here. Will certainly look to dine in next time we’re in Virginia. If you want good service with mediocre food, visit Peking Gourmet… last I checked nobody is ordering Chinese food for the service.

If you’re in the mood for a premium Chinese dining experience, Han Place is highly recommended.

name: Cafe China
document: Cafe China. cuisine: Szechuan. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A Chinese Sichuan menu amid upscale 1930s Shanghai-inspired decor. The atmosphere is classy and unique, perfect for a nice dinner date or a small private gatherings (there are themed rooms that beautifully decorated). Great for a little photoshoot, too. Food is also delicious!

Celebrated Lunar New Year at Cafe China in NYC and it was nothing short of spectacular. The food was the real star. Every dish captured the bold, complex flavors that make authentic Szechuan cuisine so unforgettable—fragrant chili oil, mouth-tingling Sichuan peppercorns, deep layers of spice balanced with precision. You can tell this is the real deal, not a watered-down version. Each plate arrived beautifully presented and bursting with flavor.

What impressed me most was the abundance of vegetarian options. So often, celebratory meals revolve around meat-heavy dishes, but here the vegetable preparations were just as thoughtfully crafted and deeply satisfying. From perfectly stir-fried greens to richly seasoned tofu dishes, every bite felt intentional and celebratory.

Cafe China made our Lunar New Year feel truly special—authentic cuisine, vibrant flavors, and a menu inclusive enough for everyone at the table. Already looking forward to coming back. 🧧✨
Many of my colleagues recommended this restaurant. However me and my other colleagues from China did not really like the food. In short, they were too salty and greasy.

Great spot if you are craving family style Sichuan cuisine.

The portions were generation and they did not skip over the seasoning. Staff is very attentive and the aesthetics of the restaurant reminds me of a Wong Kar-Wai film.

I have been wanting to try this place for a very long time. finally pop in for a visit during lunch time on a weekday. it really exceeded my expectation. there are so many sichuan restaurants in NYC and it's already hard to top one another. but the food here is really unique and the service is a top notch. Love their old shanghai decor makes it cozy and quiet enough to be able to talk to each other without screaming. there are multiple floors even seats that best for solo as well.

The dish most wows me is the spicy soft shell crab. there are so much crab in it and loaded with flavor.
Tea Smoked Duck is very juicy with smoky taste.
Pork Dumplings in Chili Oil is one of the best flavor in NYC, it's very authentic taste with a little sweet and a little spicy.
the lucky cup sake is very easy to drink if you want to take advantage of their happy hour price for only $8

There are some lunch bento specials as well, if you are not a person to share. there are also plenty to choose from.

google_reviews.text:
Nice casual Chinese food. No wait for walk in Friday night. Really liked the liquid egg yolk bun and bean curd puff. Soup dumplings could have been more flavorful. String bean eggplant was a bit too sweet snd saucy. The shredded beef was decent but flavors seemed a bit generic.

Overall nice place, good service, and decent selection of dim sum and Shanghai style dishes.

I had the pleasure of going here a couple of times in the past week and was impressed by the menu and the service each time. We were immediately greeted and sat at a table in the back dining room, which can be mostly private or lively, especially as there are some larger tables back there. We had the xiao long bao, both pork and crab and they were nicely prepared and flavored, with the traditional vinegar served and we carefully navigated getting them off the paper in the dim sum steamer and onto the soup spoon. Warm, brothy and tasty! We had some shumai and pan seared pork dumplings that also were nicely prepared.

As we were celebrating a special occasion we had a dish off the menu, scallion and ginger crab. It was expertly prepared and the delicate crab and the tasty sauce mixed well together. The standout dishes continued with the dry sautéed crispy shredded beef, the Tingling Curry Chicken hot casserole, and the red cooked short ribs in Hang Chow style being ultimate comfort food in the cold weather. The Shanghai fried rice was also top notch as an accompaniment or could be a main course. We had some pea shoots as well as some water spinach (off the menu). Both brought clean, bright flavors and some greens to the mix, though the beef ribs come with some greens as well.

Service was attentive and the water glasses and tea cups were kept full throughout our meals.

It is an excellent, traditional Shanghainese restaurant and the casserole recipes have been handed down from generation to generation, bringing deep, wonderful flavors, as they are slow cooked to perfection.

Great Dim Sum and really good Lychee Martinis.  Was walking by and had a craving for dim sum.  This atmosphere is lovely and the staff were so friendly.  Steamed dumplings were excellent.  They were light and so tasty. Truly authentic upscale Chinese food. Happy Hour 3-6 with great pricing.

name: Xi'an Famous Foods
document: Xi'an Famous Foods. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Burgers. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Take out on August 31, 2025.

Stop complaining about the noodles being cold when you bring them home. Just warm them up for 1 minute in the microwave or eat it in the car. It’s not a big deal, not sure why this has become a point of conversation in these reviews. Food was delicious. This is special food from Xi’an, China. Thank you for bringing this chain to the DMV. Hope to see a proper sit down restaurant soon.
谢谢!

First of all, it is not DoorDash Only, I don’t know why the title says that. You can order from the official Xi’an Famous food website or the Four Mile website. I have visited this restaurant many times before in NYC, including the flagship Flushing location. Happy this one opened in the DMV. The good: the burgers are on point, the cold noodles are yum. The bad: the flat wide noodles do not travel well. I had to drive 30 mins home after the pick up, and the chew in the noodles probably lasted maybe 3 mins after I started eating. The taste is good. They need to open a spot with seats so the noodles can be enjoyed immediately. I heard they are actively looking for a Maryland location with sit-down options. Can’t wait!

So glad Xi’an Famous Foods has finally made it to the DMV! I took my parents to their NYC location many years ago, driven by homesickness after weeks of traveling in the U.S. The chewy, hand ripped noodles instantly transported us back to northern China, where wheat noodles are widely loved and celebrated. They still remember that meal to this day.

Fast forward to now, I ordered via DoorDash after doing some research. Since it’s a shared space with other vendors, there’s no dine in option, and the parking and pickup process can be a bit confusing, as others have mentioned. But nothing you can’t figure out.

We ordered the lamb and pork noodles, cold gluten salad, pork dumplings, and pork burgers. We reheated the noodles after the car ride, which softened them slightly, but the flavor was exactly how I remembered - bold, savory, and spicy. The noodles were well ripped, with a wide, smooth surface. The gluten salad was tangy and refreshing, and the pork burgers were packed with juicy braised meat in firm bread.

The dumplings are real surprise. I usually make dumplings at home and don’t often order them out, but Xi’an Famous Foods is an exception. Their spicy and sour pork dumplings are actually regional specialties and definitely worth trying.

For drinks, I recommend the Sour Hawberry and Chrysanthemum Tea. The hawberry is fruity and refreshing, while the chrysanthemum is cooling and calming, both perfect to balance out the richness of the food.

If you’re a first-timer, I highly recommend the lamb hand ripped noodles + spicy & sour pork dumplings + sour hawberry tea.

Hope I can enjoy those perfectly chewy noodles fresh out of the pot soon! Will be on the lookout for their full service location.

Drove over for pick up(only option) on a Sunday afternoon around 2:30.  Be aware the pickup location is behind the 7-Eleven.

Parking is difficult and very tight when busy. There is no where close to sit and eat. Also when you ask for cutlery they don't include in your order they put it in a basket for you to grab. No napkins.  Forks were grab and go and not wrapped separately. You walk in find your order in the website based on text and a locker opens with your food. Pretty straight forward interesting concept.

We ordered 3 different dumplings. These were probably our favorite.   Cucumber salad was very good.  We also ordered 3 different kinds of noodles. Lamb, pork, and beef. All were good though we were hoping for more. One friend who goes often to New York mentioned the noodles weren't as good here.

For us the food wasn't good enough to deal with the hassle of the location. If they moved though we would definitely give it another try or when we go to New York.

An honest review from a longtime New Yorker who used to walk 10+ blocks every week just to get my Xi’an Famous Foods fix: the taste here is exactly as I remembered from the NYC locations, so that’s a big win. I highly recommend the spicy lamb hand-ripped noodles and the stewed pork burger. My favorite dish back in New York was the cold noodles, and while I didn’t realize this location’s version comes without noodles, no problem—I just cooked some at home and added them in.

The sour hawberry tea was the perfect palate cleanser after the rich, spicy meal.

This location is a bit far for us, and since there’s no dine-in option, the food had to sit through a long car ride - unfortunately the noodles got a bit soggy. But I was happy to read in other reviews that the ghost kitchen setup is temporary and that they’re opening full locations closer to my home. When that happens, I’ll definitely be back to my weekly visits.

name: Uluh
document: Uluh. cuisine: Tea Rooms Asian Fusion Szechuan. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
My parents are from Sichuan/Chongqing and I can tell you this is easily one of the best, if not the best, Sichuan/Chongqing spicy Chinese food restaurants. They use fresh red chilies in many of their dishes. Some other dishes feature freshly ground green peppercorn, and various kinds of pickled chilies. If you’re an expert in Sichuan cuisine, then you’d know that the peppercorns need to be freshly ground and the chilies need to be freshly picked as well, and this place does exactly that. The spice level for the dishes here are truly authentic, and they add some creative twists to traditional recipes as well , e.g. the cold chicken appetizer is a modern twist of the classical “mouth watering chicken”, except they use fresh limes instead of vinegar, and fresh mint leaves instead of cilantro.

Their menu changes regularly. Every time we come there seem to be new dishes to try out. The menu clearly indicates how spicy each dish is: even the one pepper sign can be really spicy for most Americans. If you love spicy Chinese food, this restaurant is just perfect for you!

(If you don’t love spicy food, they do have some non-spicy dishes)

Incredibly gas Chinese food in Manhattan! We got the 干煸四季豆, Mapo Tofu, Xiaolongbao and one more chicken dish I can't remember. Everything was exquisite with a deep and fresh taste without too much MSG. In particular the dumplings were so juicy. 10/10 would recommend!

We came here as a group of three and ordered four dishes — everything was fantastic! The Peking duck was absolutely bomb, and the spicy fried chicken was another favorite. Service was great, and Jasmin gave us amazing recommendations that made the meal even better. Definitely coming back for sure!

While I may not have eaten all the soup dumplings in the Big Apple, I know that the ones I have eaten were not particularly good. Here at uluh’s the pork soup dumplings are the finest in all of Manhattan. These have wafer thin translucent skin bursting with hot flavorful broth and enough meat. This was my second visit. I enjoyed it. The scallion pancakes with shredded duck on the other hand was served almost cold. I ate it but complained to the server. Last lunch I ate tasty beef ribs with rice as rice is not included with a dish. The restaurant is pretty and large. The location is excellent as it's bang next to La Cabra.

We love the pecking duck and the pickled cabbage fish here. In general, the food is VERY spicy. I usually have to mild and it’s still very spicy but manageable. The green beans and crab roe tofu are also great choices. For appetizers their little pan fried buns are delicious. Lines can be pretty long on weekends around prime dinner time, but we came for Sunday dinner and were able to walk right in! There are around 4-5 outdoor tables as well. Interior is beautiful and a great place for a date, dinner w friends, or take your parents out. I would focus on the food and skip the dessert. Very authentic and clean tasting Chinese food - not greasy. One of my favorites for sure. Takeout is great as well!

The flavors are excellent, but the ambiance and upkeep need attention.

I celebrated my anniversary here, and the food was absolutely incredible. I was really surprised by how generous the portions were, every dish was perfect for sharing and truly delicious. The atmosphere makes you feel like you’re inside a castle, which made the experience even more special. I’ll definitely be back. 100% recommended!

google_reviews.text: A great Chinese restaurant offering tasty Sichuan cuisine in a relaxed setting. This is a fairly casual restaurant, but they serve some expertly mad dishes. The atmosphere is cute with their corrugated metal roof ceiling and the exposed brick floor. The haw flakes at the end threw me back to my 90s childhood! Will definitely be coming back for sure! 10/10

name: Excellent Dumpling House
document: Excellent Dumpling House. cuisine: Dim Sum Shanghainese. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Short review/recommendations: XLB/Xiao Long Bao, Hot & Spicy Wontons (mild but excellent,) Honey BBQ Spare Ribs, and Shanghai Style Fried Noodles.

Originally opened as a small restaurant in Chinatown on Lafayette, right off Canal, this spot serves Shanghainese and Cantonese food with a wide selection of dim sum. I was here with a very large group a good while back, and the friendly staff was very happy to accommodate all of us, with our group taking up two large tables and then some. They had the typical selection of beers and other soft drinks, but as per usual in less fancy Chinese spots, I stuck with tea.

We first received a lot of dim sum. The Steamed Crabmeat & Pork Xiao Long Bao, which includes 6 pieces for $11.95, was above average. The skin was thin, the inside had a good, meaty filling, and the soup was well-flavored, mostly with pork and a bit of crab. It wasn't the best XLB I've had, but it got the job done.

Also good was the Hot & Spicy Wonton, made with mixed pork and shrimp and served with hot oil and peanut sauce. These included  7 pieces, and the price at $10.75 was comparable to most Szechuan places. I wish the sauce had been more pungent, but it's a Shanghainese place, so that's a bit more typical. Again, the wrapper was thin, and the filling was generous.

For the same price and portion size, you can also order Pork Dumplings, either steamed or fried. We got both, and I, as per usual, preferred the steamed variety. These were more standard but fine, with my definite preference being the other dumplings we had.

There was also the Walnut Rock Shrimp. As we ordered 3, I presume it was around $12, but I don't remember the price, and it's not listed on the online menu or in any photos I can find on Yelp. I've never been a huge fan of this dish, as I generally only like the larger prawn variety found in many Cantonese places, where you can taste the shrimp better, but this was good. The batter was light and not overly sweet.

We also got two of the siu mei/roasted meats. I don't see the Honey BBQ Spare Ribs listed, but I presume they were around $15 or $16. This was a very tasty version, with the ribs falling off the bone yet retaining some texture. Also, compared to most Chinese-American spots, the ribs weren't overly sweet.

The BBQ Roast Pork for $15.45 was alright. I've had this dish from too many spots not to compare it to the better places around Chinatown and other neighborhoods, and this was just OK. I liked the mix of fatty and lean pieces, but the leaner ones weren't super flavorful and were also a bit dry. I wouldn't recommend this as much./

The remaining plates were larger. The Shanghai-Style Fried Noodle, available with a choice of protein, was good for $14.75. The noodles were the best part, with a good wok hei and a nice, slightly chewy texture. I probably would have preferred them with beef or pork, as there wasn't too much shrimp, but otherwise, no real complaints.

The Young Chow Fried Rice for $15.25 was, in many ways, the opposite of the noodles. By comparison, the dish had plenty of protein, but the rice itself felt a bit lacking in flavor and wok hei. It was decent

For a veggie, there were the Sauteed Snow Pea Leaves With Garlic for $22.75. The leaves were cooked nicely, and there was plenty of garlic flavor. In other words, nothing to complain about and nothing particularly notable, so it was a good standard variant. It was also the expected price for these usually expensive greens.

Last was the Sizzling Ginger Beef in Basil Sauce, consisting of beef with ginger, scallion, and onion in basil sauce for $24.75. The beef was tender, but the sauce was a bit milder than expected. It was still tasty, and the portion, as expected for the price, was generous.

This is a tasty Chinese place with a couple of excellent dishes. Bumping it up a good amount, given the neighborhood and the general quality as if this was closer to Chinatown, it would be closer to a lower 4/upper 3.

Had such a great experience here! You have to ask for Mike to be your server when you go! He is so welcoming and a great worker! The food is spicy and delicious. As a spicy lover, I was very pleased with all the dishes. Of course you can ask to modify the spice level if you want more or if you want less or are dining with people who cannot handle spice, there are other dishes that are more mild on the menu. The pricing is great, the food is great and the service was impeccable! Thank you so much! I will definitely be back!

Dropped in for a late-ish dinner on a Tuesday night. It was pretty quiet and we got served nice and fast. Good food. Our favorites were the Dan Dan Noodles, Cold Sesame Noodles, String Beans, and the Twice Cooked Pork Belly. I thought the pea shoots needed more seasoning and the Sichuan dumplings were a bit flat and could use more filling.

My co diner was very happy to have good new place in her neighborhood.

Ah this place was so yummy to get some authentic Chinese food. I really got to fine out what I liked and what just wasn’t for me. I personally believe all the dishes were amazing. There was one dish I personally just didn’t have the taste buds for but my friend really loved it so it might be your thing might not. The entire atmosphere was so nice and calming. I love how they had a sink separate for the bathroom so you don’t take up a toilet to wash your hands. Super nice and good pricing.

name: Pig Heaven
document: Pig Heaven. cuisine: Barbeque Szechuan Dim Sum. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Haven’t come here in a while. I ordered fried meat dumplings and soup dumplings to start my dinner. The dried dumplings came suspiciously fast, and I was right. They were precooked and kept heated. The dumpling itself was nice. The flavor was nice. It was the texture that was a bit off. The bottom was burnt but not crispy enough. A few of them were broken and the filling was visible.

The soup dumplings were okay. It was steaming hot. The wrapping was nicely done, but just a bit too thick to my liking. The flavors inside were a little bland. I didn’t like it with soy sauce, so I asked for vinegar, and it immediately made it better.

For main course, I got an orange beef. It was cooked very nicely. The beef was cut into bite size, and fried until they were golden and crispy. However, a few pieces were quite tough and hard to chew. The steamed broccoli was cooked perfectly! It was green and crunchy. It paired well with the dish. The rice was okay.

Overall, it was a nice meal. A little more expensive than I remembered, and the food quality was a little not as good as I remembered.

My second time dining here after visiting the MET. Completely satisfied with the food and service both times.
First time I ordered Cantonese duck, which was cooked to perfection. This time I ordered crispy pork,  which was a perfection 👌! Right amount of spices, crispy, generous portion.  It marked with one pepper 🌶  on the menu, but really not that hot, hits all the right spots.
The service is quick and friendly.
Highly recommend this place for a family dinner or evening with the friends.

10/8/25

We were in the neighborhood for an appointment and decided to stop for lunch.

BBQ Ribs are delicious, most Chinese restaurant makes them but are usually tough but these were tender and so flavorful.  I wish they were near home hehehe.

Peking Duck, while it was super crispy outside and tender inside it was not seasoned.  Without the hoisin sauce it would have been a waste of money...

Bok Choy with Garlic is delicious, I wish I could make it this good hehehe.

If we are ever in the area we would definitely go back.

Lots of pig related decorations, cute! Hehehe

With a name like Pig Heaven, I would not expect, as a vegetarian, to give this restaurant a good review. However, they have delicious vegetarian options. The waiter made a record of vegetables with pancakes. It was excellent.

The background music was funny. Piano versions of Christmas carols - in August - without words.

I would go back. It was a great experience

First time coming here from Houston, yes I understand we are in New York but my server was extremely rude, interrupted me every time I tried to order. Plus nobody was here so I don’t know why she was rushing me . I didn’t like my plate but switched plates with my friend which was great but horrible service. Also  Didn’t check on us once, had other servers to do stuff for her and completely avoided us. Not sure if it was racism or what. Completely unacceptable . The other servers that helped us were amazing though, kept out water filled the whole time!

name: EAK Ramen
document: EAK Ramen. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I came here for their dinner service and thought that it was solid! Located in Hell’s Kitchen, this Japanese spot offers a variety of Japanese dishes from sashimi to rice bowls to ramen to other small bites. Service here was fairly quick.

We ordered their takoyaki, spicy fried rice, mapo ramen, and their zebra ramen. Everything was pretty good! The takoyaki was crispy and had big pieces of octopus in it (I just wish they also added bonito flakes to the takoyaki), and the spicy fried rice was full of flavor. Both of our ramen choices were full of depth and great for a cold day. Not a bad spot for some casual Japanese food!

Delicious ramen menu with very rich and  flavourful broths. They have very distinct options for adventurous palates, like the Wasabi marinated raw octopus. I recommend all and any of their ramen with pork, chicken and vegan options. I used to attend 3-4 times per week during fall so I got to try all of them. They have seasonal ramen options as well. The service was always attentive and kind. They also have very tasty calpico.

The ramen spot was a total vibe. Clean setup, chill lighting, and that cozy kind of place where you could hang with friends for hours. The broth was actually really good—rich, flavorful, and not crazy salty like some places. The noodles had that perfect bite, and everything looked fresh. The food itself? Solid.

The service though… not it. I had to literally flag someone down just to order, then again to pay. It wasn’t even packed, so that part felt off. Maybe they were short-staffed or just not paying attention, but it kinda killed the flow.

I’m from Houston, so maybe I’m biased, but the meat portions were weak. For what you’re paying, I expected more. The flavor carried, but it didn’t give that “wow, I need to come back tomorrow” feeling. More like, “yeah, that was decent.”

Overall, it’s a chill spot if you’re craving ramen and want a cool atmosphere. The broth and noodles do their job, but nothing here screams life-changing. Worth trying once, but probably not a regular go-to

Solid ramen if a bit inconsistent, but their broth is amazing. Ordered the EAK and the Zebra. EAK broth was sublime, some of the best I’ve had in the city. Noodles were fine and chewy, but the pork was VERY dry and disappointing.

Zebra broth was rich but not as buttery as I expected (in a good way) - the garlic flavor hits you over the head more than the butter. Noodles were too mushy, and the pork was a little more tender than in my bowl but still dry. If they could improve the chashu and maintain consistent quality across bowls, EAK would be a serious contender for best ramen in the city.

Very good ramen noodles (not overcooked and springy) with good chashu and broth. I had the butter version which is creamier. Good size chicken karaage appetizer with different sauces options. There's a line even on weekdays but the food hit the spot, especially on a cold day.

The only issue is the tables are literally next to each other to maximise space so it is very crowded and noisy.

name: Menkoi Sao
document: Menkoi Sao. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Excellent! This place makes really good, unpretentious ramen. I really like the al dente consistency of the noodles. At some ramen spots, the broth is just too rich and heavy for me. I eat half the bowl, but then feel like I've hit my limit for fat and salt. Menkoi Sato is much more balanced. Their ramen is hearty without being overwhelming.  The owner is a nice chap. I see that they closed temporarily. I hope they reopen soon.

My second time here - good ramen, glad to hear they were able to reopen after a brief closure.

Super offputting to see a rising sun flag, however. Honestly so surprised to see this in the wild here. Not sure if this is new or if I missed it last time, but you should definitely remove that.

I visited this place after seeing it featured on the New York couple Instagram page (@뉴욕부부), but unfortunately, the experience did not live up to the hype at all.

I ordered chicken karaage and was asked if I wanted mayonnaise. I said yes, assuming it was included, but later realized I was charged $2 for a small portion without it being clearly explained. That felt misleading.

On top of that, a can of Coke was $4 — I honestly have never seen a place charge $4 for a canned soda. The pricing overall felt excessive for the quality and portion size.

The service also felt very disorganized. They repeatedly came back to confirm whether the order was correct, which made me uneasy. At one point, food was brought to the wrong table and then taken back. I honestly felt uncomfortable, worrying whether something that had already gone to another table might be served again.

The restaurant was extremely loud and chaotic, and overall the experience did not match what was portrayed on social media. This visit honestly made me rethink how much I trust Instagram recommendations. Definitely not worth it, and I won’t be returning

I stopped by this ramen spot around 3pm and had a great experience. The service was friendly and quick, and the ramen was genuinely very good—rich flavor, fresh ingredients, and super satisfying. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more items on the menu. Highly recommend if you’re craving quality ramen!

One of the worst ramens I’ve had. Even shio was so thick, salty and heavy. Ingredients tasked stale. The scallions on top were so pungent you knew they were from last week. I got a single dry piece of chasu that tasted like it was turning sour.

Food aside, the wait for our ramen was 30 minutes, and tipping was defaulted up to 30%. Makes me laugh. For $20+, there are so many better options in nyc. Go somewhere else.

google_reviews.text: My husband and I visited Decmeber 2025. We made reservations and was seated right away. Food came out pretty quickly, and the service was great. My husband ordered an extra bowl of noodles! The ramen was delicious and perfect for a cold day. Would recommend!

great ramen. local spot with fantastic ramen. the miso tofu is my fav - the broth is so creamy and flavorful. lots of variety and good spice. fast service and great pace on water refills. great happy hour too.

name: Naruto Ramen
document: Naruto Ramen. cuisine: Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Naruto Ramen is in a great location, though it has very limited seating. It honestly feels just like being in Japan! There’s a waiting list outside where you have to write your name down on a paper, we waited about 10-15 minutes, which wasn't bad at all.

The experience wasn't disappointing because the staff was accommodating from the start. It’s very entertaining because they cook the food right in front of you! It’s definitely a busy spot, but I can see why people love it. We ordered the karaage and the Naruto ramen, and both were honestly worth it.

Yeni was attentive and gracious, setting a welcoming tone right from the start. The miso vegetable ramen was comforting and full of flavor, while the fried chicken wings had a unique twist that made them stand out. The shrimp ramen was outstanding, spicy and tangy at the same time, with the veggie gyoza and edamame rounding out the meal perfectly. If you enjoy cozy hole in the wall spots with freshly prepared ramen and pho, Naruto in New York City is well worth a visit.

It's a warm and small environment. The food is flavorful and the waiters are very nice. I do not recommend bringing a lot of people as it is a bit of a cramped space (3 is fine). But this is how some ramen spots in Japan are and appreciate it being a small place. I had the Naruto Ramen, hence the name of the restaurant. The paintings on the wall are anime themed and is a fun place to go for a reasonable price.

Date of visit: 10/11/25

Been going here for years, but hadn't had the time to make a review. This is a Japanese style Ramen restaurant with some dumplings, fried rice selection. Space is very limited and tight. Mostly counter seating, and a 2 seater by the window. Do not come in large groups. Prefer 2 people, 3 people max. Lines and wait can get a bit long especially during winter. Overall, good quality ramen, for the price it's not bad. 100% recommend. Hard to find parking at times, especially during weekdays. Weekends are better.

Ramen texture was perfect. I had the original with added spice and it was good to just give a kick. Service was smooth and good. Booth seatings were bit cramped and there are some seats near the fryer. But overall a cheerful place to have a quick meal.

name: Ramen Ishida
document: Ramen Ishida. cuisine: Ramen Noodles Soup. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’ve loved this ramen spot for years! Ramen is so yummy.
Small place with limited seating, a few vegan options! which is always amazing.
Although, It feels like there could be a little more of the toppings, and meat / tofu.
The wait might be long since there are not a lot of seats.
I recommend trying this place for the great flavor, the coziness and the service.

Solid bowls in this hole in the wall. Got the New Tokyo and every component was great altogether a very satisfying and filling bowl.  The chicken and pork pieces were cooked well, and I liked the thin noodles they used. Service was nice! Came at 12:15 when the first seating had already gone in and we only had to wait 20 minutes.

Some of the best ramen I've ever had, feels extremely authentic. And the flavors are perfect. Noodles were perfect and broth were immaculate but not too heavy like tonkotsu can be sometimes.

Restaurant is very small, you'll likely have to wait outside but the immediate area is interesting and fun to explore. Once you give your name at the counter it'll be written in a notebook and you'll be given a time, which usually goes fast because this is not a "sit around and chat" kind of joint. You come in, get your ramen and eat it quickly as soon as it comes out.

An excellent experience as a ramen lover and the people I brought with me ended up wanting to go back on their own.

I arrived around 7:30 pm on a weekday and was seated about 30 minutes later. The waitlist was well managed, so the wait felt smooth.

I ordered the New Tokyo Style Shoyu, which had a deeply satisfying flavor and tasty thin flour noodles. I also enjoyed having both chashu pork and chicken breast. The soup temperature was perfect. The truffle is a signature touch, but I think the ramen is great even without it—since you can control when to mix in the truffle paste, I’d suggest starting without it.

I also had the crab cream croquette. It was good, though not especially memorable.

I would recommend trying this place. The flavors are light and satisfying, leaving no heaviness afterward. Ramen is often oily and salty, but their chicken broth ramen feels gentle and balanced. It’s mild yet full of depth, a genuinely pleasant experience. Even if you have to wait around 30 minutes during peak hours, it’s worth it. Note that there’s no public restroom, and the shop is quite small with a 20 minute dining limit after your order arrives. They won’t rush you out, but it’s not really a place for lingering.

Despite the indoor heat, the food and service made the experience worthwhile. We recommend this restaurant for a fantastic meal in Pistoia.

Another great meal in Italy, tonight was a couple mussel dishes, porccini mushroom pasta( they are in perfect season right now and are beautiful). Very much a ‘locals’ spot, and for good reason - the food was fabulous! Fresh, tasty and perfectly cooked (open kitchen) pasta and veal. Cosy and comfortable atmosphere, but can get really busy.

we found this cozy restaurant in the heart of Pistoia in a quiet and nice alley. we ordered crostini toscani which is my absolute favorite, tartare, tagliata and roasted potatoes. the wine was good and the atmosphere was peaceful. the staff were very friendly and welcoming

Absolutely amazing. Great service, excellent food, nice setting. Absolutely recommended! Also, the staff is the best and the kitchen seems to work in perfect harmony with the waiters. Thank you for this nice experience.

The roasted seabream was fresh and firm with clean taste. The meatballs were soft, juicy and savory. They also have an extensive wine list.  Their Tiramisu was the freshest that I ever had. The service, however, was extremely slot that night for some reason…maybe it was an off night.

We had a great night at Osteria del Bianco. The staff set the mood right away. They were kind, attentive, and easy to talk to. Nothing felt scripted. They checked in when needed and made sure we were comfortable the whole time. It really felt like above-and-beyond service.

The food was the kind that makes you slow down. The lasagna at our table was rich tasted like true north Italian cooking. I ordered the mushroom risotto, and it was exactly what I hoped for—creamy, earthy, and balanced. The pastas around the table were fresh and full of flavor.

We left feeling happy and satisfied. It was one of those dinners where everything just came together. Authentic food, good service, and a place that makes you want to return. We genuinely enjoyed our time there.

It is the kind of restaurant you leave feeling full and happy. I will definitely be going back.

Our first visit to this authentic neighborhood Italian restaurant.  Enter via side gangway. I had the carbonara which was the best I have ever tasted (I make my own and this was even better!)...house made sausage as well as the pancetta, just the right amount of pepper and cheese.  Companion had the papperdelle which (I sampled) was very good too. Server said these two items are the most popular.  Nice selection of wines and craft cocktails.  We also indulged and ordered the hazelnut tart (sweet without being overly sweet and perfect flaky crust) and the pecial apple cider bread pudding which was outstanding!  Would definitely recommend this restaurant, I now understand the reason reservations are usually booked up!

google_reviews.text: Paesano in Little Italy was excellent from start to finish. We ordered the calamari and the bruschetta, which was fresh and phenomenal. They immediately brought us bread, filled our glasses with fresh water, and gave us the menus. They very attentively explained the dishes we were going to order and which wine would best complement them. The place was completely full, yet the bottle of wine and food arrived in 20 minutes. My sister ordered pasta quattro Formaggi, and I was given a bistec primavera. The pasta was perfectly cooked and smelled wonderful. document: Poseidon Bakery. cuisine: Bakeries Greek Desserts. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Came here for the first time just a few days ago and have been thinking of all the years I've wasted in NYC by not eating these delicious pastries.
I have been craving more and will be going back next week.
Because there's quite a few options,  my advice if you can't decide is to get everything.
