name: Ortobello Restaurant
document: Ortobello Restaurant. cuisine: Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Foods great, cozy location, dont let the front storefront fool you, looks run down.  Food is great, sauce is top notch  Seafood salad is perfect, fillet capricicosa is delicuous, my go to dish, sometimes not on the menu but the can make for you a fried fillet of sole with tomato and onion and i think with balsamic.  Been going to this place for years.  Eggplant parm is great which i havent had for awhile, chicken francese is very tasty, chicken parm is piping hot and chessy, hot as in heat temp for some reason cutting and eating its stay hot.  Vokda shrimp is great.   All dishes at this place is fantaatic.  If you like octopus that is also great.  Also tirumsu is the best in Brooklyn and maybe NYC

We changed the reservation time maybe that’s why we had to wait. Other than that the food was amazing! Everything seemed fresh and delicious. Loved the homemade balsamic glaze! The eggplant Parmesan was melting in my mouth lol. The shrimp was bomb, fried calamari was definitely a hit. Everything was very good. Hands down this place is one of the best authentic Italian places. Definitely must go places! Loved the Italian old school vibes.
Been looking for a new restaurant since my old stable closed years ago. This restaurant is definitely the new one, amazing food and people. Feels like I've been going there for years. Top notch 👌

I’ve passed here often but never had a chance to visit. Yesterday I decided to give it a shot. The restaurant isn’t much to look at from the outside but that doesn’t mean much. The food was amazing. I went with the baked clams for my appetizer. Which were very good. For my main I couldn’t decide between the tortellini bolognese or the penne vodka with shrimp. So I asked my waiter’s opinion & he suggested combining the two. So I took his advice & had tortellini vodka with shrimp. It was extremely delicious, the vodka sauce was especially creamy & both the shrimp & pasta were fresh. It was an extremely filling meal as well. On a side note you may want to avoid eating the pre meal bread with butter & save the bread for the excess sauce from your main. I usually prefer NY style cheesecakes but since they were serving a HOMEMADE ricotta cheesecake I had to take a slice to go. I couldn’t eat another bite after that amazing dinner. The restaurant is on the small side & can probably seat around 40 people. It has an old school vibe to it & the food is amazing. I had half of the slice of cheesecake for breakfast this morning. It was surprisingly delicious & moist (I often find Italian cheesecake to be dry). I would definitely recommend stopping here for dinner.

Very cozy and clean restaurant with nice ambiance! The staff were friendly and welcoming. We were seated right away and the gentleman who waited on us was very efficient.

We were first served some bread and butter - the bread was one of the best I’ve had! Adding the butter to the bread made the bread taste even more heavenly.

We ordered the ravioli and the chicken parm with a side of broccoli. The dishes were served in big portions  and were delicious! They were big enough that we felt like we could have ordered one dish for 2 people.

Whenever you get a chance to visit this restaurant, please remember to bring enough cash since it is a cash-only restaurant.

Only found out after eating here that the restaurant is family-owned and has been around for decades. So glad we found this hidden gem!

document: Bamonte's. cuisine: Italian Seafood. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I wanted to try this old fashioned highly rated Italian restaurant. We went for lunch so it wasn't crowded. The food was on par with some of the other Italian restaurants we have dined at. If you like ambience and old world charm, this place is for you. Old carpets, paneling, pictures on the wall. The service was pretty good and the lady manager checked on us to see if everything was satisfactory. As some of the others have mentioned, a bit pricey.

First time at the old fashioned Italian Restaurant where I felt like i was in a Mafia movie with the lighting & the music but all seriousness,  the food was delicious and plentiful. Their fried calamari, fried eggplants and baked clams were great. Their Osso buco was divine. And of course their chicken parmagiane was to die for.  I'm getting hungry writing this review. Place had valet parking. Would definitely recommend.

The food at Bamonte’s was absolutely delicious—classic, comforting, and full of flavor. We also really appreciated that they were able to accommodate our reservation on very short notice. Overall, we had a nice experience, though the service felt a bit uneven at times and not quite as warm as expected. That said, the food truly stood out, and I hope future visits reflect that same level of care throughout🍝✨

#CallSana #CallSanaRecommends #SanaApproved #TravelingRealtor #TasteOfTheCity 😘

Amazing food. Fantastic service. Great atmosphere. There is almost always a wait here so call ahead. Everything they cook is fantastic. I can't wait till my next visit. Last time I had Chicken catchitore.

Bamonte’s was absolutely amazing from start to finish. The environment and lighting set the perfect tone, and the staff was truly extraordinary—welcoming, attentive, and knowledgeable. The food was out of this world. I couldn’t pronounce half the menu, so I trusted the specials and ordered the eggplant—no regrets. The meatballs were incredible, and the pasta is still living rent-free in my head. I can’t wait to come back for the fresh seafood. A must-visit spot.

name: Aurora
document: Aurora. cuisine: Italian Comfort Food Cocktail Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We came here for Valentine’s Day and had such a great experience! Every single detail about this place is impressive. The staff is absolutely amazing — friendly, attentive, and always working hard to keep everything running smoothly.

The food is incredible. Everything is fresh, delicious, and constantly refilled. There were no empty trays at any point, even on a busy holiday. The ramen station and the made-to-order items were super efficient — no long lines, and everything was prepared quickly. You can really tell they care about quality and organization inside the restaurant.

The only small suggestion I would make is about the waiting area. The system of just giving a number and calling it out can feel a bit chaotic, especially when the wait is around 40 minutes. It might be even better if they collected phone numbers and sent a text or called when the table is almost ready. That would make the experience more comfortable while waiting.

Overall, this place is fantastic, and we’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!

Very nice buffet restaurant, good food selection. We've been several times for lunch and dinner...weekend and week days. The food has been delicious every time. They have hibachi grill, fresh sushi and seafood. Dinner and weekend they serve fresh crabs and crab legs. The price is reasonable and they also offer take out which they just weigh and charge per pound. They have a large party room for events. The decor is cool. They have baked fish, fried fish, jumbo shrimp, etc as well as Asian dishes like lo mein and chicken and broccoli. This has become our new favorite restaurant and it's affordable enough to feed a family or a few friends. They offer a senior citizen discount, military discount and discount for small children.

Good bubble tea. frog legs were very fresh. Lobster is very good. Sushi is good. Crawfish is my favorite. Flounder was fantastic. Ribs are bbq fall of the bone ribs - not deep fried. I liked all of the food that I tried.
The food here tastes fresh and is of a higher quality than other buffets in the area. I would recommend their seafood and ramen as they were my favorite dishes. Definitely would come back again.

This seafood and grill buffet was absolutely amazing! Everything was so fresh and delicious, with a great variety to choose from. I loved that bubble tea was included, and the ramen was a huge bonus—so comforting and flavorful. Our server, Iris, was outstanding. She was friendly, attentive, and made the whole experience even better. Highly recommend this place, and I’ll definitely be coming back!

document: Al Di La Trattoria. cuisine: Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: We wanted to come to al di lá for a while and glad we finally did. Made a reservation beforehand since this place does get busy on the weekend and glad we did. The drinks were delicious, we got a nice recommendation from a gentleman working here. The pasta was good - definitely fresh and quality ingredients but that’s it. There’s a lot of pasta shops in the area and they all sit at the same level of taste. Would definitely stop by again if I was ever in the mood for pasta and wanted to eat out.
Great food, ambiance and selection. I will be returning again for dinner. My only gripe was it was a little tight for seating but other than that 5/5!

We have been coming here on and off for years and enjoyed the consistency of the dishes but last night we went for appetizers and pasta, ordered 2 portions of the Paccheri Pasta. We were shocked when it came out at the skimpiness of the portion. It was like they split one serving for both plates. I think for $28 a plate it was pretty cheeky to let that leave the kitchen and be sent to the table. In these more trying times the last place we want to see shrinkflation is when it gets put down in front of us at a restaurant we like, just sours the taste of the whole meal.

I came here on a cold Wednesday night with a good friend in early January who lives nearby. I’m not sure when he booked the reservation but I would recommend making a reservation as the restaurant seemed quite crowded, but not packed.

The restaurant is very quaint and feels like a neighborhood staple right when you come through the door. The food was good to great, but not amazing. The service was also good, but not exceptional. The cocktails and drink menu were also nice. This very much seems like the type of place where you would have want to have a nice meal with friends close to home.

I would recommend and I would go back.

This Italian restaurant is one of the few places in NYC where you’ll find rabbit on the menu—and it’s prepared exceptionally well. The pear cake was another highlight, perfectly balanced and memorable. The food remains consistently excellent, served in a warm, authentic setting. Also, returning after several years, we were thrilled to find the same high quality and familiar menu we remembered.

name: Carmentas Italian Specialties
document: Carmentas Italian Specialties. cuisine: Italian Sandwiches. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This is the type of place worth gate keeping but I love it too much to do such a thing. This is one of the rare places where everything on the menu is delicious and well thought out. Everything is so fresh and they have their own signature unique flavor. Truly, ditch the candlelit Italian dinner places and come get this divine food.

The pasta has a perfect al dente bite and all the options are varied and great in their own ways. My personal favorites for pasta are the spicy pork rigatoni vodka sauce and the butternut squash with sausage.

For sandwiches they have my favorite turkey sandwich in the city. The salsa verde and vinegar gives it such a full flavor that complex enough to not feel samey after a few bites. My second favorite is the Dom G which is my ideal eggplant sandwich (It has ricotta and mint) and it stands its ground as a great sandwich even up against meat options.

For dessert, the banana bread is something DIFFERENT. It’s almost hard to call it banana bread because it’s so dense and rich and full bodied with its chocolatey flavor. Make sure to savor each bite since it gets better as you chew it. Truly don’t skip it.

Also honorable mention is the white bean, kale and andouille sausage soup. It is sooooo comforting when coming in from the cold and it had and appropriate amount of big ol veggies in it that were all soft from this nice fatty yet clear broth
Chicken parm was delicious. Bread was crispy chicken and sauce was flavorful. Rice balls one of the best I've had. Definately coming back to try other sandwiches.

Randomly checked this placed out on a spontaneous walk and now it’s my personal favorite. The aroma of garlic and herbs takes you in as soon as you open the door. The pasta is fresh and the sauce savory and rich. This place lit me up enough to write a review, because something this good should be well known. Authentic and amazing quality. You will definitely see me again!

Summary: Warming with Great Food

Carmenta’s is a great place for food but specifically their sandwiches. This small but inviting cafe has a warm, welcoming vibe the moment you step in. The intimate setup, with the kitchen right in front of you, makes for a unique and personal experience. The staff is friendly and attentive, adding to the vibe of the place.

We tried two sandwiches, the meatball sub and the Dom G. While both were excellent, the Dom G was the standout. As a meat lover, I was shocked at how flavorful and satisfying this vegetarian sandwich was. Every bite was packed with rich, balanced flavors that left me perfectly content.

Overall, Carmenta’s is an outstanding experience with great food and a cozy atmosphere. Highly recommend.

Stopped in for dinner and it was delicious!

I wish the seating situation was better, its more of a deli atmosphere than a sit down dinner spot, which is fine but I wasn't expecting it.

document: Gino's Restaurant. cuisine: Pizza Italian Wine Bars. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We always order the pizza and its delicious! This past weekend we stayed at Madison Vines and had dinner here! I highly recommend the chicken parmesan meal! It was crispy chicken, savory sauce and pasta was perfect! Along with the bread! Also the steak and cheese sub was amazing! The next day we went back for lunch and the chicken ceaser was amazing! Just lunch, date night, dinner out as a family or grabbing a pizza to share this is a great place!!!

I had the super steak and cheese sub and it was one of the best steak and cheese subs I've ever had. It was loaded with meat and vegetables and cheese, the only thing that could have made it any better would be if they had a house sauce they could put on it instead of mayonnaise

Called in an order for two steak and cheese subs — one without onions or tomatoes, and one without tomatoes and lettuce. I was told the order would be ready in 10 minutes. I intentionally arrived after that timeframe had already passed in order to avoid waiting.

Upon arrival, I was informed there had been a mix-up in the kitchen regarding the toppings and that the sandwiches were being remade. While standing at the counter, I observed the sandwiches come out of the kitchen window, only for the front counter employee to check them and send them back because they were still incorrect. At that point, they were being prepared for a third time.

These were straightforward modifications clearly communicated when the order was placed. The purpose of calling ahead was to avoid a delay, yet I experienced a significantly extended wait solely due to repeated preparation errors.

When I expressed concern about the situation and stated that I did not believe I should be responsible for paying full price after multiple mistakes and delays, the owner became involved. During that conversation, he suggested that perhaps his staff was “having a bad day.” While I understand that employees can have off days, that explanation does not change the customer experience. In a food service establishment, management is ultimately responsible for ensuring order accuracy, quality control, and professional service regardless of internal circumstances.

My initial payment was voided, but it was not clearly communicated whether the corrected sandwiches would still be provided. It became clear that if I wanted the food, I would need to pay again. No apology was offered for the repeated errors or extended wait time, and no attempt was made to offer any concession for the inconvenience.

I contacted the family member the order was for, and they still wanted the sandwiches. I paid again and waited again. When the sandwiches were handed to me, I checked them before leaving and found that they were still not prepared according to the requested modifications. At that point, my only options were to have them remade yet again or accept them as they were. Given the time constraints and the prior delays, I chose to leave with them as prepared.

I also requested printed confirmation that my original credit card transaction had been voided. I was initially told that printing such confirmation was not possible and that it would only show as voided on their point-of-sale screen. After pressing the issue, a void receipt was printed without difficulty. The initial claim that this could not be done was concerning.

Mistakes can happen in any restaurant. However, best practices in food service include accurately following clearly communicated modifications, verifying orders before they leave the kitchen, honoring quoted pickup times, communicating transparently about delays, and taking responsibility when service falls short. In this case, those standards were not met.

In total, I paid over $28 for two sandwiches that were made incorrectly after three attempts and a prolonged wait, without an apology or meaningful effort to restore the customer experience. That level of service is disappointing and not what customers should reasonably expect

Came in for a late lunch/early dinner. Ordered Spinach and artichoke dip and the Meat lover pizza. We asked for light on the pizza sauce, but also for a cup of pizza sauce on the side because I like sauce, but my mother doesn't. The servers kept trying to bring the wrong food to our table. First, they brought over meatball spaghetti, then someone came over with French fries. They gave us a number for the table, but took it away after we got the spinach dip. Kept telling them that isn't what we ordered. So, they just  need to work out a few kinks with service. The pizza was delicious. A lot of meat and a lot of cheese. We ate almost the entire pie except one slice. They didn't bring me the side cup of sauce. I didn't bother asking for it again. All in all I think this will be a nice addition to this town.

Yummy pizza! We got some appetizers and they automatically add .50 to each one for the dipping sauce (marinara and ranch) without asking which isn’t a big deal but feel like they should just add that to the price for transparency. Food was pretty good- worth a stop for lunch or dinner in you’re hungry in the area!

name: Daphne's
document: Daphne's. cuisine: Italian. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Walked in and luckily we were able to be seated at the bar (best to make reservations ahead even if it says there are time slots open)
The beet salad was delicious, especially with the bits of dates to add a touch of sweetness. The Caesar salad was a nice portion (not pictured). The rigatoni was excellent, really love how large the pasta was, and the sauce had a great butteriness to it; nice short rib flavor as well. The coffee and creme desert was a highlight; the description also said small lady fingers but it resembles Rice Krispies to me, either way, delicious.

To be honest I wasn’t expecting much, I think there are way too many of this kind of restaurant out there, but I was SHOCKED at how good everything was. The delicata squash tempura was FANTASTIC. It was so unassuming but the light batter leaves room for the sweetness of the squash to come through.

The focaccia was fantastic although $3 extra for a singular tablespoon of salted butter is kind of off-putting.

The half chicken was INCREDIBLE. It might’ve been the juiciest chicken I’ve ever had in my life. The fries were really well salted which is HUGE

And the spicy rigatoni is not to be slept on! Pasta was the perfect doneness and the sauce was really perfect. I was worried it would be a throwaway dish but for a classic it was UNIQUELY good.

Amazing! Can’t wait to come back
The pastas were delightful. Really loved the textures and different combinations of flavors. The menu is definitely small. It would be a better place for an intimate meal for a smaller group.

While I came just before closing after being denied service/food at Les Mars (Thai)-which closed at 10 (I arrived at 9:50) so I applaud the kitchen/bar for serving me just before kitchen closing rendering  service until the closing hour.  So had a quick meal of a Caesar Salad-excellent, Tanqueray Martini and an Iberico Pork Chop with a seared cabbage and pear soubise-very good.  I think my only observation is that if you serve a guest(s) just before closing, you accept the responsibility of giving the same service for a 7 pm reservation at nearly 11 pm walk in.  I’m a professional chef and while I’m not being as critical as in the 80’s or 90’s, service should not taper off-at the bar where I sat or  at a table to be lackluster at best.  I will return as I have always had a curiosity about this place since it opened-so I took a chance.  I’ll return at a more decent hour and Jackie-thank you.  I enjoyed my food and experience.

Daphne’s is a true neighborhood gem. I had my birthday dinner here for a group of 10 and everything was fantastic—from the vibes to the food and wine. The pasta was especially delicious and flavorful, crudo was beautiful, and pork chops were juicy and tasty.

The staff were incredibly accommodating and helpful in hosting our group, and the personalized menus were such a thoughtful + tasteful touch. A great spot for special occasions and everyday dining. Can’t wait to come back!

name: Aromi
document: Aromi. cuisine: Italian Pizza. located in Brooklyn. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: My husband and I recently visited this place and we are absolutely impressed. The pizza is worth every penny — incredibly delicious and generously topped. The cocktails are amazing, and the service is even better than you could expect or wish for. We truly and wholeheartedly recommend it!

Eating Italian food outside of Italy is always a bit of a risk, but this restaurant completely exceeded our expectations. We truly felt like we were eating at home — if not even better. The food was authentic, full of flavor, and prepared with great care and passion.
The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the waitstaff were exceptional: friendly, attentive, and genuinely kind, making us feel comfortable from the moment we arrived. Prices were absolutely fair and well justified by the quality of the food and the overall experience. Everything was perfect from start to finish. Highly recommended — we will definitely be back.

What a phenomenal dinner!!! Omg!!! Best pizza - hands down!!! (Did not have such a delicious pizza in Italy). Try MBP - mortadella, burrata, pistachio- thank me later - your life will never be the same.
- crispy calamari- not greesy, perfectly crunchy and the black ink mayo brings it to another level.
- branzino with clams and mussles  - wow! Fish was flacky and moist - phenomenal!
- tiramisu - so rich and satisfying.
And the atmosphere of this restaurant is amazing: it is busy, lively, happy, and makes you feel like you are somewhere in Italy: the waiters are very knowledgeable and professional. Our waiter gave us great recommendations for food and wine. The hostess is accommodating and welcoming.
I cannot wait to be back! (That's the thought I have in my head every time I leave this restaurant

Another perfect meal and night at Aromi! The pizza is divine and hospitality warm and welcoming! We have become regulars since we discovered them in the nearby Carroll Gardens neighborhood. My favorite is the margherita pizza and salamino picante and the delicious polpette. The regular drink is the Aromi Lemonade.

First time at Aromi, and what can I say? Highly recommended! If you’re looking for a cozy place with great pizza, good drinks, and a lovely atmosphere, this is the place to come. Tip: make sure to save room for dessert, and don’t miss the grissini with Nutella!

google_reviews.text:
This place is overrated as heck.
I made a reservation in advance, ask for the side room because the main room is like a pesach program - way too many ppl, no space to go to the bathroom
The service was good and the ambience was nice. But the but the best thing in the restaurant was the style of the dishes. The food was ich
I got spicy vodka pasta- pasta was hard
Pizza was ehh
Fries were ok
Lemonana was yum but was such a tiny portion like a four year old, mostly ice
Cheesecake with the blueberry was good but the gelato ice cream tasted like frozen whip cream with cocoa powder

Overall, nice place to visit but not for food

​We were privileged to visit Castell's restaurant last night. It was a truly wonderful experience, from the first step inside. The unassuming facade hides an old world ambience inside. Walking down the entry hall you are transported to a large room tastefully appointed with beautiful murals, luxury chairs, and a bar that spans an entire wall. The wait staff are  plentiful yet unobtrusive. We began with delicious focaccia bread with high quality herb infused olive oil. I thoroughly enjoyed the tuna carpaccio. The eggplant parmesean was both crispy and creamy, making it easily the best I have ever had. The zucchini topped pizza was a delight that can not be missed. I did not taste the onion soup but my family was very impressed. I ordered the sole almondine with spinach on the side.  It was delicious and perfectly cooked. I paired it with a young Sauvignon Blanc from New Zealand which was crisp and vibrant with complex fruit notes. It was an excellent pairing, suggested by our server. Brown butter ravioli with jammy soft egg was topped with freshly shaved white truffle. That was next level outstanding. The portions were so plentiful that I could not possibly finish them . I am trying to think of something constructive to suggest to add to this experience but this is as close to perfection as I have ever experienced. I heartily encourage everyone to give this a try . You will not be disappointed .

We felt like royalty! Our bartender was fantastic - creative, professional, and attentive. He whipped up amazing cocktails and helped us navigate the menu with ease. The service was top-notch, and we'd definitely recommend stopping by!

5-Star service, food and ambiance. This place really takes it to the next level! There’s so much to enjoy - the pasta, the apps, the pizza!! Who would go to a place for pizza?! I would! And it was NOT a mistake. Really a special place to have an incredible night out!

Came here for a party on a Sunday.  difficult to park. Restaurant has no sign so unless you know where to go you arent getting in.

Place is immaculate, very well set up. Very old school professional waiters. Bathroom is very clean.

Now the food. Portions are very good. The food is well seasoned and very well put together. The wait staff are very attentive. I highly recommend the pizza the Cesar salad and the bronzino.

And the coffee vodka martini is AMAZING

Special mention to Paolo, who from the beginning has been especially attentive to our needs.

Tried **Willow & Whisk** and loved it! The food was really good and the portions were super filling. Definitely recommend making a reservation because it gets busy. Matt was our server and he was fantastic; friendly, attentive, and made the experience even better. Will definitely be back!

The key ingredients for the perfect brunch spot are ambiance, good food, and friendly service. Willow & Whisk serves up all three in spades. As we were being led to our table, we couldn't stop saying things like, "This is so nice!" or "Wow, this space is so cute." It's a brightly lit space, made to feel more open with huge windows and a flowering tree in the middle. On the flip side, this is a place that attracts the crowds, so prepare for long waits - especially on weekends. We waited close to an hour for a table for Sunday brunch.

The menu offers up some tantalizing eats with a strong emphasis on the breakfast game. Since it was later in the day, we all went with sandwiches and salads, but it didn't stop me from glancing enviously at the beautiful, fluffy pancakes at a neighboring table. My chicken caprese sandwich was delicious, with a heartily sized, perfectly grilled chicken. Another couple ordered their burgers, which also looked amazing. If there was any fault, the fries were cold and oversalted.

Service is great. Our server stopped by our table frequently to check on us or clear away dishes, and there was no overt pressure to finish or hurry our meal.

Had brunch here for a friend’s birthday and the food was solid! The frittata was delicious amongst everything else we ordered. I had the SoCal Crispy Chicken with truffle fries and it was very good!

Our server was very attentive and super generous (pretty sure we asked for a million requests and he still remained calm lol). Vibe of the restaurant was super cozy and perfect for any celebration.

Overall, highly recommend if you’re in the area. Definitely make reservation during the weekend since it does get packed.

The best dish was definitely the Espresso French Toast.
The coffee-flavored cream was excellent, and the toast itself had a rich caramel taste that paired really well with the bananas.

The Mushroom Bisque had a strong truffle aroma and came out piping hot, which made it incredibly delicious. I highly recommend it.

The Smoked Salmon Benedict was also quite good. The salmon tasted fresh, and the hollandaise sauce wasn’t too heavy.

This place is great for brunch, and the dishes are consistently high in quality 🍽️

Inspired by both classic Japanese flavors and modern techniques, Vert Frais brings the essence of Japanese comfort and culinary tradition to LIC. This restaurant offers a wide variety of drinks and dishes that reflects a harmonious blend of traditional craftsmanship and contemporary flair.

Vert Frais offers popular delicious Japanese dishes such as Omurice, Hamburg Steak, and Souffle Pancake. While my friends and I didn't have the chance to try the Souffle Pancake, we were able to try the Omurice and Hamburg Steak. The Omurice was perfect, a nice blend of flavor between the rice and egg and ketchup. The ketchup added a good depth without overwhelming either the egg or rice. The Hamburg Steak was cooked perfectly, letting the knife cut right through. The demi-glace sauce was also beautifully made to balance the flavor.

I highly recommend ordering a drink from here to. All of their drinks are aesthetically pleasing and definitely photogenic! A note of advice: mix the drink very well! You have to make sure the drink gets fully mixed otherwise it may taste overly sweet. It was like that for the Lavender Lemonade, Berry Bliss, and Blue Moon Latte. All tasted sweet despite the "mixing", but after mixing much more thoroughly, it becomes a nice blend where you can taste all the flavor.

I visited this beautiful Japanese-style café for a collaboration and was blown away by the quality, flavors, and aesthetic of everything I tried. It’s the perfect spot for a chic brunch that feels like a mix between a dessert café and a brunch restaurant, depending on how sweet your mornings are!

•	MONT BLANC SOUFFLÉ PANCAKE with chestnut purée and sweet white bean paste — the most comforting fall-winter vibe!

I also tried their FONDANT AU CHOCOLAT, which is a warm chocolate lava cake paired with vanilla ice cream and berries, an indulgent dream.

And not to forget the OMURICE, a savory touch to balance the meal, made with bacon fried rice, mushrooms, and a flavorful demi-glace.

Their latte art is next level! I had a Lavender Latte, Rose Matcha Latte, and a Noir Latte. Each one was smooth, aromatic, and heart-topped with love.

name: Micco Cafe
document: Micco Cafe. cuisine: Taiwanese Breakfast & Brunch Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: This was my first time at Micco Cafe, and I was immediately impressed by how warm and inviting the space felt. The soft lighting, greenery, and wooden structure create a cozy atmosphere that makes you want to stay awhile. I ordered an iced brown sugar matcha latte, and it was smooth, well-balanced, and not overly sweet. The pastry display was hard to ignore, so I tried the blueberry crumb cake, which was flavorful and perfectly crumbly on top. Everything tasted freshly made. The seating layout makes it easy to relax and is very spacious and clean. Overall, Micco Cafe is the kind of place you visit once and immediately want to return to.

Wow, where do I even begin with my visit to Micco Cafe? I stumbled upon this spot while looking for a place to study, and I have absolutely no regrets. I ordered the strawberry matcha latte with oat milk, and it was amazing with the perfect balance and just the right amount of sweetness. I was also pleasantly surprised by the wide selection of milk options, which makes it very accommodating for different preferences.

To eat, I ordered a chocolate chip cookie and the Micco platter. The cookie genuinely reminded me of my grandma’s homemade cookies, and I later found out that all of their desserts are made in house, which makes total sense. The Micco platter was just as impressive, with the sausage having the perfect level of spice without being overwhelming.

Another huge plus was the staff. The two young men who helped me were incredibly welcoming and made me feel like a regular even though it was my first visit. The music playing throughout my stay was also on point and really added to the relaxed, study friendly atmosphere.

Overall, Micco Cafe is a must visit if you’re in the area and looking for a chill cafe with great drinks, food, and vibes. Pro tip bring cash. There is a $10 card minimum, but you will get a 5 percent discount if you pay with cash. I will definitely be back!

Have been coming to Micco Cafe for a while now. Staff is super nice and knowledgeable on recommendations. Comfortable seating but a little tight, great for studying/focus session. Menu has a large variety of drinks, breakfast, and dessert options. Solid coffee (iced brown sugar oatmilk espresso recommended) and best mango/strawberry matcha lattes in the area.

Love their Taiwanese options, especially the fantuan, great flavorful combination of crunchy youtiao, soft purple rice, and pickled cabbage. Hope they come out with some more Taiwanese desserts and more pastries to choose from.

Definitely worth checking out if you’re in the area! And bring cash (10 dollar min for cards)!!

This cafe a very cute and calm location. Everyone that goes these is very respectful and quiet. 100% recommend if you are looking for a space to study that is 1 Million times better than your average Starbucks.

Had brunch here. Besides the Taiwanese desserts and matcha drinks. They make excellent American style breakfast, pancakes, avocado 🥑 toast, eggs. Their breakfast is actually a lot better than local "American" dinners and less expensive. Nice music & vibe cafe. Modern and healthy

name: Gatsby's Landing
document: Gatsby's Landing. cuisine: New American Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
We came here last night for my mom’s birthday dinner and had an amazing experience from start to finish. We were a group of six, and the service was great. Our waitress, Noah, was the absolute sweetest, so attentive, kind, and made the night feel extra special. Every staff member we interacted with was welcoming and on top of everything.

The food was delicious across the board, from the appetizers to the main courses and even dessert. Everything we ordered was a hit, steak, salmon, pasta.

The ambiance was lively and a bit loud, but still very enjoyable. I loved how the restaurant is set up, with a cozier, darker section in the back, a brighter well-lit area, and the bar in the front. It felt well balanced and inviting.

Highly recommend, we will be back✨

It was a fantastic experience to have lunch here with my friend's family the day before Father's Day.
This restaurant's setting is very clean and quiet, especially for conversation. All the dishes were beautifully decorated, and my friend and his wife appreciated the flavor of every menu item. Of course, nothing is complete without wine, and the wine here tastes great, too. Red wine was a golden pairing with the dishes here.
The service at this restaurant was also exceptionally good. The waitress was very friendly and patient, and she always had a smile on her face when communicating with us. I asked her to divide a dish into three portions, only to have all three portions beautifully re-decorated when she brought three plates again! It was really a surprise since I had never seen such a service for similar requests in other places.
I felt that all the people in this restaurant were very passionate about their work, and the owner must be very friendly to the fellows as well. A restaurant that has been running for a long time must have its reasons.

To celebrate Valentine's Day, my wife and I enjoyed a $38 three-course prix fixe lunch. Although the public parking lot was full, we managed to find a spot for $2 for two hours. The restaurant, Gatsby's Landing, draws its name from the romantic nostalgia of The Great Gatsby. Situated near the Long Island Sound and Roslyn Pond, the setting offered a beautiful waterfront ambiance.

My wife opted for the Baby Roasted Beets Salad, Salmon, and Crème Brûlée, while I chose the Lobster Bisque, Squid Ink Tonnarelli, and Tiramisu. The menu highlights their commitment to fresh, organic, and locally sourced ingredients - a promise they certainly delivered on. The dishes were both delicious and generously portioned. It was clear the kitchen doesn't skimp on quality; for instance, the lobster bisque was loaded with tender lobster meat, the squid ink tonnarelli featured an abundance of blue crab, and the salmon was a substantial, thick-cut fillet.

The chef clearly possesses a mastery of technique, knowing exactly how to pair garnishes and balance flavors in perfect harmony. Furthermore, the waitstaff was both diligent and courteous. We can see why this establishment is so popular--the combination of exceptional cuisine, attentive service, and the serene lake views is hard to beat.

However, there is one area for improvement: the restaurant should consider replacing their current chipped plates with larger, more elegant dinnerware. High-quality presentation would better reflect the dignity and caliber of the food they serve.

Beautiful setting and nicely decorated interior, which makes for a good first impression. The food, however, was a bit hit or miss, and not always worth the higher prices. Service was friendly, but overall, more style than substance.

We visited this restaurant to celebrate my son’s birthday. All the food was high quality and absolutely delicious. Our server was very kind and attentive, which we really appreciated. At the end of the meal, they even brought out a small sparkling birthday candle to help us celebrate. It was a joyful and memorable experience.

google_reviews.text: This was my first time dining at Sanfords and it did not disappoint! Sat at the bar which was such a vibe and they were playing good music in the background.  We had the prime skirt steak ciabatta sandwich, the pecan crusted organic chicken salad, and the banana caramel cheesecake xangos. Highly recommend their Sanford old fashion! Overall had an amazing experience and big shoutout to Ali, Bar Manager, who took great care of us. Will definitely be coming back and recommend this place to everyone...CHECK THEM OUT!

If I was rating solely the food here and not the service  I’d give them 3.5 stars.  Overall the food was decent, but they had amazing desserts.  I’m deducting a star because two minutes after receiving our appetizers we were served our entrees!  We each ordered French Onion  soup and literally just took two spoonfuls and our waiter put the entrees on the table!  By the time we finished our appetizers our entrees were cold!  I never had my entree served when I just got my appetizer in my entire  life!  A word of advice don’t put your dinner order in until you finish eating your appetizer!  For entrees my husband and sister ordered a burger and fries both were decent.  I had their  lobster ravioli, and it was TERRIBLE!  The sauce was bland and the lobster in the ravioli tasted extremely fishy like old fish!  The desserts however were all delicious!  The fried cheesecake was FANTASTIC!  The brownie and peanut butter pie was very good!  Decent place overall, but not great with terrible service!

First thing I noticed when I entered was the decor and vibe. Very cozy but upscale at the same time. The waiters were really on point and super attentive. We started with the Risotto Ball which was scrumptious. It wasn’t dry inside and the mushroom gave it a nice meaty texture.

I then had the Sesame crusted Yellowtail Tuna. I absolutely loved it. It comes in top of a bed of Jasmin rice and some vegetables. Truly packs a great amount of flavor.
It's a just plane neighborhood restaurant, so you can visit it anytime comfortably. The food is average, and the service is truly businesslike. But considering the price, I think I'll go back again.

Heard they had some delicious filet mignon springs rolls here and had to give them a try and they were really good! document: Roast & Co. cuisine: Juice Bars & Smoothies Sandwiches Breakfast & Brunch. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’d been hearing about Roast E7 from my friend Sanu for the last couple of years but never got around to trying it. I was in the area recently and finally decided to give it a go.

I ordered a large lamb doner with spicy chips and a drink. The portion size was generous and everything tasted spot on. The lamb was well cooked, the chips had a proper kick, and it all came together really well.

Glad I finally tried it and I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommend this place if you’re nearby and want a solid meal.

Absolutely outstanding experience. The lamb chops and ribs were hands down the best I’ve ever had — perfectly cooked, incredibly tender, and packed with flavour. Every bite was exceptional.

Mr Adam looked after us and the service was top-class from start to finish — attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming. This meal exceeded all expectations, and I’ll definitely be returning. Highly recommended.

I went to this place in a group of 7. The service was great and staff were friendly. I counted about 8+ workers behind the counter all busy making fresh food - this clearly indicates how popular and busy the place is.

The food was fresh, tasty and worth the price. It is slightly more expensive than your typical chicken and chips shop but I would compare this place to Nandos.

Went here with a group of friends as we’ve been going since the beginning and hadn’t visited in a while.

Opted for pure meat range: lamb doner and chips, lamb chops, wagyu ribs etc.

The prices were very high I have to say. The lamb doner was good quality but I feel the salt to flavour ratio could’ve been better.

The lamb chops were excellent. The tenderness of the meat was really good.

The wagyu ribs fell short of adequate to be honest. The price they charged was very high (almost £25) but the quality of the ribs wasn’t all that. There was barely and rib meat, it was just laced with an overflow of sauces to try and compensate the lack of meat.

Price to quality ratio was adequate. Price to quantity ratio was poor. It was very noisy when we went, and table space was limited, so you may need to wait a while.

Miss the old days of Roast when the quality, prices and services were all simultaneously exceptional. Improvements need to be made .

We called a week in advance to confirm whether they take reservations, and they told us they do, so we booked a table for three people.

Fifteen minutes before arriving at Roast & Co, we placed a fairly large order over the phone, and they confirmed it would be ready in 15 minutes.

However, when we arrived, they told us there were no reservations. Apparently, they do not take reservations at all and operate on a first-come, first-served basis. We were shocked, especially as the restaurant was full, and we had to look around for a table ourselves.

After waiting nearly 30 minutes, we finally received our food, and it was very disappointing.

We ordered:
•	Donner
•	Half chicken
•	Mozzarella sticks
•	Wagyu burger
•	Lamb chops
•	Chilli chips

Overall, the food was 1/5.

The chilli chips were just covered in chilli sauce. The Wagyu burger tasted like a standard burger. The lamb chops had no flavour and were mostly cover fat oil. The donner tasted the same as the chilli chips just covered in chilli sauce. The only good thing was the bread that came with the donner, unfortunately.

Overall experience: 1/5.

My advice don’t fall for the social media advertising. The place feels more like a basic chicken and chips shop than a restaurant

name: Little Pepper
document: Little Pepper. cuisine: Szechuan. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I have to say I was pretty disappointed with the food. The Sliced Pork Belly w. Chili Garlic Sauce was actually sweet, which threw me off. I lost interest after just one bite. The so-called “paper-wrapped lamb” was really just cumin lamb served on a piece of foil. It wasn’t terrible, but it wasn’t particularly good either, and it was quite salty. The biggest letdown was the mapo tofu. The tofu had no flavor at all, and the sauce wasn’t numbing or spicy. Mapo tofu is supposed to be one of the signature dishes of Sichuan cuisine, and seeing it done so poorly was honestly frustrating. The rest of the dishes were more or less acceptable, but the fish had a noticeably not-so-fresh texture. Ironically, the best thing I had was the simple scallion fried rice, though even that was a bit salty.
On the bright side, the owner clearly has some artistic talent, all the paintings in the restaurant were his own work.

Delicious birthday dinner for our family group. Indeed a "Mom & Pop" operation, but our varied dishes came out at a good clip & all were excellent. Good value price-wise. Leftovers to take home. Friendly service. Deserves to be busier!

I ordered Yangzhou Fried Rice, which was great, plus the Beef with Broccoli, which I asked via the Uber Eats app to make not spicy, plus asked for utensils. The Beef arrived swimming in hot sauce with bits of hot peppers, and no utensils. Please read the instructions next time!

Feeling lucky to try out before they close.. the owner told us they are about to retire. If u r around the area, visit once for authentic Chinese food! Plus, super nice pricy.
Sharing some dishes I remember below.

💚🍚🥄Green onion fried rice was super special. Look might weird but smelled really good and the taste was simple but rich.

🍤✨Fried shrimp was delicious. Simply pick the one you like.

🍲Fish soup was good too.

🥔fried shredded potato in sour sauce was good toooooo! Highly recommend this one.

Little Pepper: A Hidden Gem in Whitestone

Little Pepper is a delightful, unassuming restaurant nestled in Whitestone. Street parking was readily available on a Saturday morning. The clean interior and friendly service created a welcoming atmosphere. Our server was exceptionally patient, especially with my son's enthusiasm for authentic Szechuan cuisine.

We were thoroughly impressed by every dish we ordered, particularly the mapo tofu and chicken with three type of mushrooms. Even as someone who isn't a fan of spicy food, I found plenty of delicious options to enjoy.

Without a doubt, Little Pepper is highly recommended. We'll definitely be returning to savor more of their fantastic food.

Lunch included Classic Caesar and Marinated Beet salads, then Farfalle & Sausage, Chicken Parm and Prime Hanger Steak.  All delicious ✅

document: Tuscan Hills. cuisine: Italian Pizza Wine Bars. located in Queens. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
We had such a wonderful experience at Tuscan Hills on 2/11 for Restaurant Week! I took my father-in-law and fiancé out for dinner, and from the moment we arrived, everything was exceptional.
We had a reservation and were seated promptly. The staff was extremely helpful and attentive throughout the evening, and the host was absolutely amazing — warm, welcoming, and engaging. A special touch that really elevated the night was when the host personally cut open the Caciucco alla Livornese tableside, adding a bit of flair and making the experience feel even more authentic and memorable.
For appetizers, we shared the pane al pomodoro, insalata di campo, and arancini (ham and peas over fresh tomato sauce). Each dish was delicious. The pane al pomodoro was fresh and vibrant, the insalata di campo was crisp and beautifully dressed, and the arancini were perfectly crisp on the outside with a flavorful, savory filling that paired wonderfully with the tomato sauce.
For our entrées, I had the eggplant rigatoni (Rigatoni alla Norma), which was outstanding — perfectly cooked pasta, tender eggplant, and a rich, balanced sauce that brought everything together beautifully. My father-in-law and fiancé both ordered the Caciucco alla Livornese, and they couldn’t stop raving about it. The seafood was incredibly fresh, the broth was deeply flavorful, and the presentation (especially with the tableside touch) made it even more special.
We paired dinner with a Sauvignon Blanc called The Little Sheep, which was crisp, refreshing, and complemented the seafood and pasta perfectly.
Dessert was the perfect ending to the meal — cannoli with a creamy, lightly sweet filling and crisp shells, a rich and indulgent pistachio cheesecake, and a silky panna cotta that was smooth and delicately flavored.
Overall, Tuscan Hills delivered an exceptional dining experience from start to finish. Between the outstanding food, thoughtful service, and welcoming atmosphere, it was a perfect Restaurant Week dinner. We will absolutely be back!

name: Rialto Ristorante
document: Rialto Ristorante. cuisine: Italian Wine Bars Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
FOOD: Every bit was delicious.

Antipasta: We began our meal with the Caprese which was wonderful fresh and perfectly drizzled with basaltic and olive oil. Which was paired with two different types of bread for dipping the remaining oil.

Main: We had the seafood linguini with red sauce. This was a massive portion, loaded with a medley of seafood including calamari, clams, muscles, scallops and shrimp. This dish is highly recommended.

In addition we tasted the bacon wrapped veal. Wow was this a punch full of beautiful contrasting flavors. The fatty salt from the bacon hits your tastebuds first. Then you savor the crunchy thin veal meat which provides both a new texture and aromatic to this dish. It’s paired with homemade mashed potato’s and a green that I couldn’t put my finger on. All surrounded by a rich sauce.

Dessert: To finish we relieved the tiramisu, which was delightfully light creamy and moist. There was a raspberry reduction sauce surrounding the cake, which was a delightful twist to this classic. Additionally, we ordered the passionfruit sorbet. We were surprised to get a large serving, and the sorbet was surprisingly sweet the tartness from the fruit did not overpower this survey. I would absolutely order the survey over again and again.

DRINKS: this restaurant has a decent wine menu. Of course they would. It’s an Italian restaurant. You can order bottles of wine or glasses. My group was in the mood for cocktails.

My only critique of this restaurant is that there are no suggested cocktail menus. Our server told us we could order any drink that we would like, and they would make it. We ordered a vodka gimlet, and a Moscow mule. Both drinks were delicious and I have no complaints. Having said that, I would prefer if the restaurant had a list of available cocktails to choose from.

SERVICE: this restaurant features wonderful staff who are career servers. They take great pride in their work and you can tell this crew has been doing this for a while and are great at what they do.

We noticed that there was no one server for our table. The entire weight staff worked as a team and we were able to make requests and orders to any of this staff.

ATMOSPHERE: the dining room room was very clean and sophisticated. The dining room felt elevated without being pretentious. The decor on the wall were simple with extra extravagant chandeliers and sconces as the highlight of the room. There were beautiful photos featuring locations in Italy, as well as Venetian masks displayed on the walls.

This place was perfect for our party of three, but we also saw a large group enjoying a meal as part of their gathering. There are also spaces where you can have private dining for your large party making this restaurant ideal for different party sizes.

This restaurant is only seven months old and is planning to continue to grow and expand their footprint. I am looking forward to returning and having another delicious meal at this Astoria local Italian restaurant.

100% recommended

The food is out of this world! We tried the Cacio e Pepe, Lemon Chicken, Clams and Tiramasu. They all had a fantastic depth of flavor. The Cacio e Pepe in particular is one of the best I’ve had in a while.

I also want to point out the incredibly nice staff. My partner has a serious gluten allergy, and they actually made him a new dish free of charge when he realized he accidentally ordered a dish with gluten. He didn’t get sick at all from the new dish they made him!

My only complaint is that they were hosting a private party the night we went, and the music from the party was distractingly loud. The walls were vibrating and you could hear the music pretty clearly from the restaurant which disrupted the ambience a little bit. They did their best to cover it but I would suggest to them to try to avoid having the music too loud in the future.

That being said, all things considered I would definitely come back here and hopefully on a night where there isn’t a private party!  This is one of the best Italian spots in Astoria.

What a hidden gem!! Astoria is obviously filled with tons of great restaurants but you MUST not skip Rialto. From the moment you enter you are warmly welcomed by a very hospitable staff. The owner Dominic is a class act gentleman!

The food was outstanding, baked clams, beef carpaccio, beet salad, soups, cacio e Pepe and steak were all divine. But the service and ambience is what tied everything together. I truly cannot wait to return.

Also!! They have an incredible event space downstairs can cater to all size groups, and a wonderful patio. Can’t wait for the weather to get nice again so we can check it out.

name: Valdari NYC
document: Valdari NYC. cuisine: Italian Pizza Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.0 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: It was a wonderful experience having dinner here. We loved the atmosphere, and the customer service was excellent. Our server, Julio, was very nice and friendly. The food was delicious, and we truly enjoyed our time here. We will definitely be coming back! 🥰

It was my first time going to Valdari with high expectations due to reviews of the food. It is Valentine’s Day and we made a 7:45pm reservation.
As I walked in with my fiancé, there was a crowd of people waiting at the entrance not taken care of. I’ve seen waitresses walking past the front at least 5 times within the few mins to charge people’s credit cards and taking care of the drinks. We spoke to a couple that was there before us and they had a 7:30 reservation and weren’t taken care of and not greeted. They stated the waitress just walked off. As 10-15 minutes past, we waived down
a waitress who walked by the front to ask about our reservation. We checked in with her and we were seated in few minutes. it’s safe to assume that if we didn’t flag someone down.. we definitely were not going to be “checked in” or even taken care of. No one was managing the front as there were a swarm of guests waiting. The second we told the waitress we had an appointment, everyone else came behind to tell her as well.

Im unsure of how the team operates but 30 mins passed by no one took our orders and not even water was served. 40 mins later, someone finally got to us and took our orders. We find out that we can only order from the Valentines dinner set menu because the chefs from the kitchen want to push out the food ASAP since they are super backed up and busy. It was an unexpected last minute notice because my fiancé wanted to order from their daily menu and that was also the whole point of coming. The appetizers took about 30 minutes to come out, the entree took about 1 hour to come out. So by that time, we have sat down for almost about 2 hours. It was like 9:50 PM by then. I was about to fall asleep but luckily my date kept me up by talking. 😂
We ordered burrata, it was a 10/10, me and my fiancé both agreed was the best dish out of everything we had.

The shrimp was soggy and one of the shrimp was burnt. once it was put down the table my fiancé could tell it was not going to be good.

I ordered steak cooked medium. it came out beyond well done. One of the sides was burnt, it was chewy and dry. I did not enjoy the steak, but did not want to make a scene nor did I have patience to request it remade. It was very disappointing. I cut up my steak and gave half of it to my fiance to help me eat it he only took a bite and agreed with my assessment. we really did not want to waste food but parts of the steak was so unimaginably dry my fiance started laughing hysterically saying he could save it and use it as a fire starter.

The truffle burger (has no truffle 😂) was dry… my fiance only ate half of it and couldn’t do it anymore. There were no condiments on the burger and tasted very bland. I tried a bite and agreed. It was very dry..

Fair warning, people get automatically charged 20% gratuity and it says on the receipt depending on what the bill comes out to.

Based on the service and food today it is hard for me to think of retrying this place again.
____
update - nothing new from emailing management. Been few weeks now. Downgraded 1 more star off for service.

Valdari is nestled on a small block off of Bell Blvd in Bayside, one block from the train station. Their pizzas from their large wood fired oven are unbeatable in terms of value, taste, and presentation. My favorite is their Tartufo pizza with truffle and ricotta cheese.

The restaurant is fit for small groups up to 4 and they have one table for 8. Their bar fits about 6 individuals but there is plenty of room for couples or parties of 2. Reservations are not required and you will be promptly seated. The pastas, pizzas, and appetizers are delicious and  their drinks are beautifully made.
Really amazing food and services. Got the mushroom paste and steak with some appetizers. They were all good!

Bread was so good, one of the best breads i’ve had (and it was free!). Octopus and calamari app was delicious, pasta was also great and the eggplant parm was amazing. Not a fan of the burger but it was cooked to the exact temp I asked for (medium) - just felt like it needed some more seasoning; fries were great! Loved the chocolate cake desert and the donuts with nutella sauce. Customer service was one of the best i’ve had in Queens... the waiter on the rooftop made the experience 10/10. Would come back jyst for the wood fire pizza it was the best!!!

document: Sotto La Luna. cuisine: Italian Pizza Sandwiches. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: What a lovely gem we stumbled upon! The Lime Gnocchi with raw shrimp was such a nice departure from the usual.  The Fritto Misto was cooked perfectly.  And the staff - lovely and attentive.  A really nice airy space as well.  Highly recommend.

I chose this place to have my bday lunch because they offered the cheese bowl pasta performance. Haha. Have always wanted to see it and try it. Getting here by google maps was easy taking the train. This was located in Astoria, NY. If driving, you can find parking but I would not drive in NY.

This was a nice quaint spot for locals. Very beautiful inside with lots of green plants and big windows to see through. I saw there is outdoor seating if it’s possibly crowded inside. I can tell it would be more busy with locals in the evening. It’s a nice spot to have a date or have a group dinner. We made reservations for our family of 6 but it was not crowded on a Friday late lunch. The staff were very welcoming and attentive.

Everyone chose a different dish to try out. I had a Peach Moscow Mule cocktail to start. It was good and strong.

Choose:
Casio e Pepe (****) - spaghetti with pecorino cheese and black pepper. The cheese bowl soaked in pure cheese and probably a little pasta water. They gave a lot and my daughter and I both got this. We should have shared.
Margherita pizza (***) needed more cheese. Haha
Calamarata pasta (****) - ring pasta with small bites of salmon. Would have been good if it had bigger pcs of salmon.
Gnocchi (***) - gnoochi with cherry tomatoes and raw shrimp and cheese. I just didn’t like the raw shrimp but that was me.
Ragu (***) - fettuccine with fillet mignon.  The meat was more than the pasta and needed cheese.

They had other dishes I wanted to try. I love pasta and cheese! They also gave us a round of shots but not sure what it was but it was delish. All in all, the service was good, location and restaurant were nice, prices were decent for an Italian restaurant, and some of the dishes I would get again. I would recommend it here.

Too loud, stuffy environment.    The food is mediocre to say the least.   Took 25 minutes for appetizers and another 35+ minutes for the main entree.   My mixed grill overcooked,  the breaded lamb chops were seasoned well, but the meat itself had zero seasoning.    The risotto looked more like a congee rice, the shellfish was just thrown in there, no seasoning whatsoever.    The desert was made by a 2 year old literally.
We got take out for lunch. The gnocchi was very good. The breadcrumbs and lime flavor was delicious. Everything tasted great.
Loved the pasta and seafood, the drinks were great, and the staff was so attentive and nice.

google_reviews.text:
A cozy local Queens gem with traditional European interiors and a classic feel.
The Vongole Oreganata (baked clams) appetizer was the highlight of the meal—rich in flavor and generously portioned. We also spotted the melon and prosciutto at a nearby table that looked just as amazing. The flourless chocolate cake rounded out the meal nicely. Overall, great food in a warm setting.

Considering it was empty, the service was slow, but it was kind of worth it for how good the food was. Risotto was flawless despite the sauce being a bit broken. The crostini was great, the salmon was fully cooked but moist, and level of spice in my pasta dish was well above par. I'll come back in better weather to try their backyard patio. 👍🏽

google_reviews.text: Went for a birthday celebration right before the snow storm hit and I am so glad we ventured out in the cold. Everything was exceptional from the moment we walked in. Great staff, AMAZING food and beautiful atmosphere. Will definitely take the trip from Baltimore again.

Pretty swank place that serves up seafood, steak and delicious desserts. While the atmosphere was really nice, it was overly crowded and somewhat pretentious. I can't say the crab was remarkable either. The oysters were good and the steak was exactly at temperature. However, no part of the meal dazzled me enough to warrant hype around eating here. The servers were highly intelligent and very friendly, but I noticed that they were just trying to clear tables, so there were times when the support staff would come and just take things off of our table without asking even if we were still eating it, this was especially annoying with the appetizers. Would go again, but would not seek this place out.

The attention to detail with the entire experience was incredible between the food, service, and atmosphere. Further, as someone with Celiac, I can truly say the restaurant went above and beyond to accommodate me, while also already offering a fantastic selection of gluten-free items that were actually celiac/allergy safe. Can’t recommend Joe’s enough.

My family and I had an excellent experience at Joe’s steak and seafood restaurant. Our server was attentive and made the evening very enjoyable. I ordered the sea bass and had Joe’s chopped salad to go with it. The glaze on the sea bass just made the dish that much better. Others in my party had the New York strip steak. Both were perfectly cooked and full of flavor. We also shared some asparagus, sautéed mushrooms, and the lobster mac & cheese. The asparagus seemed under cooked (it was a little hard) but all of the other sides were perfect.

For dessert, we shared a slice of the Chocolate Fudge Pie, The Boston Cream Pie, and the Key Lime pie.  I didn’t care much for the Chocolate Fudge Pie but the Key Lime Pie was simply amazing and I highly recommend it. The atmosphere was elegant, with the staff dressed sharply, though the restaurant was a little on the loud side. We arrived 15 minutes early for our reservation and were seated right away without any wait, which was a nice touch. Overall, it was a memorable dining experience.

I recently hosted a private dinner for 13 people at Joe's. The execution of the dinner was exceptional.  Our dinner coordinator for the evening made the event feel special with her attentiveness to my guests and her flawless timing on getting the food to the table.  The food was delicious, absolutely 5 stars.  Guests raved about it all, but especially the deconstructed seafood towers.  If you are hosting a private event, it's worth it to splurge for the seafood towers as an appetizer.

google_reviews.text:
In Times Square I ate on the restaurant a some years ago and we had a great experience. The review below represents what we typically order everytime we go to Carmines.

I have been to Carmine's in NYC, Washington, DC and Las Vegas and each and every time it is on point!!! I am not sure why i have never left a review but I will be fixing that today. I took photos and a copy of the receipt from Las Vegas so yall can see everything we ordered to go.. the only difference is the bread doesn't transport well with cheese i will remove the cheese next time. But other than that food was really good and so consistent. Yes its pricey and its also family style so its not for a sinlge person unless you are going to graze on it for a few days. I will tell you that marinara get extra...i forgot so you cna dip your bread it... so worth it. 10/10 definitely recommend!!

The show is amazing and the actors and actresses are so great. It was very entertaining.  My only issue was the food. They give a great amount of food but not enough time to eat it. You are sharing plates with 10 different people. you serve yourself a little at first so everyone can eat.  They then would send you to do a task and when u came back they would clear the entire table.  We had full plates of food left and you think you are going to go back to finish it but it’s gone. They don’t mention that they are going to take everything away.    For the price you are paying it should give an option to take leftovers home.

Definitely a tourist restaurant that serves family size portions. I haven’t been here in years and decided to give it a try.  The portions are large, the menu is large and the flavors are not bad at all.  It is standard Italian food, cooked well and served in a friendly atmosphere.  It is a great restaurant if that is what you want.  I came first lunch and had two appetizers, fried zucchini and stuffed artichokes.  Zucchini was good, thinly sliced, lightly battered and fried well.  Artichokes also good, leaves were very tender and easy to eat.  The artichoke was a little too stuffed for me but I would prefer that to not enough stuffing because it’s very easy to just take some of the stuffing out.  The stuffing was a little under seasoned but overall a good dish.

Want the feel of family style Italian? This is the place to go. We started with drinks from the bar. Of course we had a Manhattan. You have to when you're in Manhattan. We had the baked clams as an appetizer.  So good. We also got the Carmine Salad. The dressing was so good and not over done. This restaurant serves family style so come hungry or bring a group with a wallet. Since it was just the two of us and we didn't need leftovers,  we order the shrimp parmesan with some angel hair pasta. It did not disappoint.  It was a good compromise for us since I wanted seafood and he wanted the chicken parmesan.  Plan ahead to get in. A reservation is a must. Put it in the list when you visit NY.

I'm so glad, I gave me the opportunity to visit Carmine's for my birthday. It was an amazing experience. The food quality is super. Service top notch 👌. And atmosphere simply the best you can find. I totally recommend this restaurant make sure to come hungry because you will for sure get enough food. Thank you to all the staff you customer service is above and beyond.

document: Armondo's Italian Restaurant. cuisine: Italian. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

The food is good.  My mom found her Seafood Risotto a little underseasoned but that's a matter of taste.  It had a lot of Seafood in it.  My Veal was nice and tender. The staff who all spoke Italian seemed to know everyone in the restaurant except a few of us yet we felt like we were part of the neighborhood.  I think the mistake many people make is looking for a famous tourist trap.  Eat where the locals eat and you will experience the best of an area.

What a great spot! Found it after playing pool with friends nearby. We were a group of 5, and got a table immediately without reservation. The food came pretty fast, we shared a bunch of dishes together. My absolute favorites were shrimps (the sauce was fantastic) and the eggplant. I will happily come back here.

Wow!! Amazing food, service and atmosphere!!!
As a traveling businessman, I make it possible to stop at every corner restaurant that my co-workers recommend as being “the best”.
Armando’s Italian Restaurant in Jackson Heights definitely is top of the line. We had a fantastic time there this past week before heading up to Vancouver and Miami Florida.
I highly recommend this restaurant. You must try their filet mignon and their famous seafood special.🙏🏼 Yes, you will come back for more👍🏼

name: Patrizia's Of Maspeth
document: Patrizia's Of Maspeth. cuisine: Italian Pizza Salad. located in Queens. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I went on a Thursday afternoon and had a grilled chicken panini sandwich with arugula and honey mustard & comes with house salad. The food was really good!
I gave 4 stars bc I felt the service could’ve been better. Other than that I would come back.

A few weeks ago, someone recommended this restaurant to me. I went there in person to make a reservation because it was a special occasion, and I wanted to make sure everything went smoothly. I wanted to see the place before making any decisions. I went in, and when I arrived, a couple of employees looked me up and down. I think they thought I was poorly dressed and assumed I was a delivery driver or didn't need special attention. However, I decided to proceed, and I noticed someone watching me who then left the counter. Another person attended to me and took my information. I left my details and went on my way. When the time of my reservation arrived, I entered the restaurant and told a waiter that I had a table reserved. He was about to attend to me very kindly, but suddenly someone without a uniform stepped between the waiter and me, blocking my view of him. I don't know who he was or what his position was, but what I do remember very clearly was that it was the same person who had only looked at me before and hadn't wanted to serve me. The service was mediocre; the table service was somewhat distant, neither pleasant nor friendly. This person only focused on the basics, fulfilling their task, but I must say that we didn't feel comfortable with their service. They weren't rude or disrespectful, but I think their treatment was somewhat dismissive towards us, perhaps because we weren't white. They simply did the bare minimum, and perhaps that's acceptable, but I was looking for a pleasant and family-friendly atmosphere to have a good time. I must say that the food was impeccable, and the timing between each course was perfect. The temperatures and portions were just right. The pizza deserves special mention because its flavor was amazing. The beef, however, was a bit small compared to the other dishes, but like the pizza, it had a great flavor and freshness. I'm writing this somewhat lengthy review because I think the place is highly recommended, but this employee should reconsider their approach when deciding who deserves good service, because at the end of the day, anyone can be a potential customer, regardless of how they're dressed, how they speak, or where they come from, whether someone comes in for a glass of water or a dinner for six.

I hate to leave bad reviews but this restaurant completely disappointed my husband and I. We were there for Valentine’s Day and had a bad experience yet we decided to give it another shot tonight! We called prior to coming in to make a reservation as it is our anniversary. We specified we wanted to be seated upstairs because we wanted to have a little more privacy. When we got to the restaurant other people who got there after us but seemed to know the manager were sat instantly while we waited for about 15 minutes. When we finally got a table we were told we could not be accommodated upstairs because there was a “big party” going on. We were there for nearly two hours and no party ever arrived. Yet two couples came and were sat upstairs. We decided not to make a fuzz and sat wherever we were told. Our server took our order and never came back to check on us. We waited over 45 minutes for our main entree (lamb chops), another server was kind enough to apologize and take over the table for the rest of the time there. It is unfortunate that we had to go through this on our anniversary night!

A great place for a party.  We had twenty people, we had a pre-fix family style—the food was flowing.  The ingredients are fresh and the tomato sauce has no sugar in it (which is typical of low end Italian restaurants).

Be warned-this is a party warehouse environment…the Lee are rows of tables with large groups.  This means very loud and we must have celebrated 20 happy birthday songs during our 4 hours there.

Not for a quiet and intimate meal.

Patrizia’s is a warm, popular, friendly Italian restaurant with amazingly good food and great service. The arancini were delightful and the linguine vongole had more than 50 baby clams. I was delighted! There were several delivery bike people who came and picked up food for delivery elsewhere (parking is limited). I would come here again.
