document: Palermo Restaurant & Bar. cuisine: Italian Bars. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We ordered from here last night and let me tell you, the food was beyond disappointing and ESPECIALLY for the price. The Caesar salad, I’m almost positive, had to bagged lettuce and bottle dressing. For a “higher end” Italian restaurant, I absolutely expected homemade salad. The vodka rigatoni and charm parm are mid at best. Didn’t feel fresh or tasty at all. We ordered pizza which was superrrrr thin and bland. Tasted horrible. The clams were a little bit better and the tiramisu was good. Everything else felt like boxed food. For a higher end restaurant, it should definitely feel like all the food is homemade or at least the pricing should reflect that. This felt like takeout food from an ok pizzeria. Super super disappointing.

Palermo has become my go-to spot in Astoria, and honestly, it's one of the best neighborhood restaurants I've ever experienced. From the moment you walk in, the warm, welcoming vibe hits you—cozy brick interior, friendly staff who remember regulars, and that perfect mix of intimate and lively energy, especially with outdoor seating in nice weather.
The food is outstanding: homemade pastas that are perfectly al dente, generous portions, and flavors that taste like they come straight from Italy. Their meatballs with penne are legendary—juicy, flavorful, and paired with a sauce that's rich but not heavy. The brick-oven pizzas are crisp and charred just right, the burrata is creamy heaven, and don't skip the tiramisu—it's one of the best I've had anywhere. Seafood dishes stand out too; everything feels fresh and thoughtfully prepared.
What seals it as a true essential? Consistency. Whether dine-in or takeout, the quality never dips—every order arrives hot, accurate, and delicious. Service is attentive without being overbearing, and the value is spot-on for the quality ($$ but worth every penny).
In a city where chains keep popping up, places like Palermo keep Astoria's soul alive. Support local spots like this—they make the neighborhood special. Team Palermo, you're killing it! Grazie mille—I'll be back soon (and often).
Highly recommend to anyone craving elevated Italian comfort food without leaving the hood. 5 stars all the way!

What a wonderful place! We had the good fortune of eating here often & are forever happy with the entire experience at Palermo! Our wait person, Frida, is superb! She is extremely knowledgeable & very friendly, she makes you feel like you’re home! Magda offers an incredible experience with delicious food & a warm welcoming! It never disappoints! And, of course, the bartender Panos is charismatic & engaging!    Frankly the entire staff, Frida, Marina & Vinny are beyond comparison, they are the best! It doesn’t hurt that the food is excellent, mouth watering & you leave happier than you came! Thank you always for a wonderful time! Denis Diaz & John Holden

I’ve ordered delivery from Palermo a bunch of times and it’s always been great, but actually coming in to eat with my family was even better. The food was amazing, everything came out hot and full of flavor, and the portions were solid. The vibe was relaxed, the staff was super nice, and it just felt like an easy, really good family meal. Definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to, whether it’s delivery or dining in.

Palermo in Astoria is an absolute neighborhood gem. The food is consistently delicious, with classic Italian flavors that feel both comforting and thoughtfully prepared. Everything tastes fresh and homemade, from the perfectly cooked pasta to the rich, flavorful sauces. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, making it a great spot for a relaxed dinner or a special night out. What really sets Palermo apart is the friendly, attentive service—you’re made to feel like a regular even on your first visit. If you’re looking for authentic Italian food in Astoria with heart and soul, Palermo is a must-visit.

Seems like any choice of dessert is a good choice.

But, and this a huge but, and be forewarned. The wait time is excessive. We were a party of three and it took us more than 2 1/2 to complete our dinner. The drinks took about 20+ minutes to arrive. The appetizers took more than half an hour to arrive. The entrees took almost an hour to arrive. And the desserts took about half an hour to arrive.

I inquired from our waitress regarding the wait time for the food and she replied that the kitchen is limited in size and that perhaps the wait time is not what we were accustomed to. It appears that the restaurant expanded its interior but expansion of the kitchen did not take place.

A very nice restaurant with mostly very good cuisine. However, don't arrive too hungry or you'll be sorry.

The music is loud with a great DJ, definitely not the spot if you’re trying to catch up and have a long conversation, but perfect if you want to enjoy the music, dance, eat, and drink. The servers were good about keeping the unlimited brunch drinks flowing. I really enjoyed the appetizer empanadas, but I wasn’t happy with my burger. I ordered it medium, but it came out well-done with a “well” tag on it. I even reconfirmed with the server, but unfortunately, it was overcooked and lacked flavor, so I didn’t finish it. Overall, I’d recommend this place for the vibes, drinks, and appetizers, but not so much for the main course.

#whereisweekes....We had a great time celebrating GiGi's Pre Birthday Brunch. The food was ok. My shrimp & grits were runny, the birthday gurl change her food twice, the chicken & waffles looked very dry. The drinks kept coming and the atmosphere was on point.  We were dancing  drinking and having fun

I’ve lived in the area for quite some time but had never been to Sangria Cafe until recently—mainly to catch my favorite saxophonist performing live (and he did not disappoint! 🎷).

The atmosphere was lively, and the music truly made the evening special. However, the food was a bit underwhelming. My meal arrived cold at first, but the staff did kindly take it back to reheat. Unfortunately, once the steak came back, it was no longer cooked medium as requested.

That said, the chicken empanadas and dessert were a hit—definitely recommend those! Overall, it was a nice night thanks to the music and the vibes, but the food and execution could be improved.

google_reviews.text: If you haven’t gotten the chance to try Sweet T’s Southern Eatery you are missing out. I would say this restaurant is pretty valid. I definitely threw down. The catfish and grits were pretty good especially if you like cheesy grits. Surprisedly I liked the devil eggs and I’m not a devil eggs person at all but they were actually pretty good. The Sweet T's Fried Shrimp with their tartar sauce was also delicious and I enjoyed that. My mother got the Sweet T's 1Lb Texas Braised Beef Short Rib but she wasn’t a big fan of it. I think it was a bit too much meat for her. So if you aren’t a big meat eater I would say stay away from that because it is a big piece of meat. Overall the portions are fair and filling. The service was awesome and we loved the ambiance and they played some fire music. When it comes to the bill gratuity is already included so keep that in mind.

Title: WE WOULD NOT RETURN

We planned a dinner on Wednesday night at 7:30pm via Resy to celebrate the end of our women’s Book Club, and we were very excited. The four of us entered the restaurant happily, but we were immediately met by a greeter who was not friendly or welcoming. She didn’t welcome us just asked where we wanted to sit. We asked if we could sit by the window and join the chairs and she said NO! This was disappointing from the start and the place was close to empty.

After being seated, we were left to navigate the iPad menu on our own. No waiter came over to introduce themselves or explain the daily specials. After waiting patiently for what seemed like 7 minutes, we had asked the greeter about the menu and she sighed and said she didn’t know and that she would go to call a waiter over.

He came and over but never welcomed us or asked what we wanted to drink but when asked informed us that some of the menu items shown on the iPad were not available at the Montclair location but only at another location.

When we asked what specials were available, he mentioned an eight dollar mocktail special but had to check if there were any other specials.

The first ten minutes were not a great experience, and we were hesitant about continuing.

We ordered appetizers, (that were FREE with the purchase of a $8 mocktail) which arrived within about 15 minutes. Unfortunately, the only item we enjoyed was the biscuits and gravy, which were very good, but the drinks were flavorful.

The eggs were underseasoned, and both the shrimp and fish batter lacked flavor (a little salt would go a long way).

Out of the four appetizers we ordered, we only liked one, the biscuit!

For entrées, one person ordered chicken, another ordered shrimp and grits, I ordered the salmon cheesesteak, and another ordered fish.

Since we did not enjoy the batter on the appetizers, we hoped the entrées and side accompaniments would be a better combination, we even asked for extra sauce on the side.

Unfortunately, they were not tasty. None of us ate more than a few bites of our entree, and we all packed up our food to go, with hopes that we could take it home to add some seasonings and sauces of our own. If this was not a book club event I would have sent my food back.

The only item we truly enjoyed from the entree were the grits that came with the shrimp.

Overall, the food was very underseasoned and seemed to lack care and attention.

One of the co owners came out during our visit and did not appear very friendly.
He walked past us without acknowledging us. It was only 3 parties in the entire restaurant and one was packing to leave. He could have said hello.

When my friend asked the waiter if he was an owner, he confirmed that he was one of the owners.

Although it was close to closing time, the co owner was counting cash at the register and never stopped to check on us, ask how our food was, or welcome us to the restaurant.

No one said welcome to Sweet T’s, not the greeter, not the waiter, and not the co owner.

We were extremely disappointed and I will NOT be returning.

We truly wanted to support a Black owned business, which makes this experience even more disappointing to write about.

Our bill was close to $200, with almost $40 of it being a mandatory tip.

The good news is that with Resy and Amex I got $100 off the bill. YAY! That made me feel sort of good since I was treating the entire group.

While our waiter was polite and seemed to try his best, he could benefit from additional training to improve professionalism and menu knowledge.

The restaurant was not busy, with only two other parties present at closing, so this experience wasn’t because they were busy.

NOTE: The presentation of all of the food looked was VERY good, just not the taste. This is from someone that comes from the south and has visited so many southern eateries.

Five stars for Sweet T’s! The food was great and I loved how many vegetarian options there were. The cornbread with the butter is an absolute must — so good. And the teas are phenomenal. No matter what you order, DEFINITELY get one.

Also, don’t skip the grits — they’re incredible. Everything was comforting, flavorful, and done right. Can’t wait to go back!

This was my 2nd time to this location and the food was amazing!   This time I got to enjoy my friends reactions to the food that I have already had.  I delightfully enjoyed the Beef short rib grilled cheese.  The crunchy toast, with the savory beef short rib and the 2 types of cheese was delicious!   Along with the side of potato wedges was everything I needed.  I had to order a side of the candied yams as well.  And to wash it all down I had the Pear Apple T with was refreshing.  I am already planning my next visit.

I had the opportunity to visit Sweet T’s Southern Eatery this past weekend after hearing so much about it. I drove over an hour to try the food, so I came in with high expectations.

First, I have to say the ambiance is beautiful. The atmosphere is stellar, and the presentation of the food was impressive. Everything looked amazing when it came out.

Unfortunately, the taste did not live up to the presentation. I ordered the breaded shrimp, and while it looked great, the batter was completely lacking seasoning. The fried catfish was also disappointing and did not have the flavor or depth you expect from well-seasoned Southern-style fish. The mac and cheese with turkey was underwhelming and needed more seasoning.

The yams tasted like they came straight out of a can and were served as-is — no cinnamon, no brown sugar, no butter, no warmth or depth of flavor. They lacked that homemade Southern touch that really makes the dish special.

As someone who genuinely appreciates Southern cuisine and has dined at places like Sylvia’s in Harlem and My Father’s House in Nyack, I know what properly seasoned Southern food should taste like. Compared to those experiences, this meal fell short.

Overall, I was really disappointed in the taste of the food. document: The Pelican Room. cuisine: Cafes Desserts. located in Bronx. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I brought my niece for dinner, and the experience was exceptional from start to finish. The staff was absolutely incredible with her, so kind and attentive.  My niece told Gemma it was her favorite restaurant, which says it all.

The food was outstanding. Everything salmon was a wow, and it was great to see so many gluten-free options available. We ended the meal with cappuccinos, including a toddler-friendly one for my niece, which was such a thoughtful touch.

Amazing food, welcoming atmosphere, and staff that truly goes above and beyond. We can’t wait to come back. Thank you Gemma!

I love this place!!!!! The manager and host were very sweet! Our server was so kind. The food and drinks were delicious!!!!! The portions were big, I ended up taking food home. Love the ambiance too, it’s giving speakeasy. Tbh I might consider filming in this restaurant. Check it out!!

I went to The Pelican Room on Saturday night with high expectations after reading the glowing reviews in Westchester Magazine. Overall, it’s a place I like—and with a few tweaks, one I’d happily return to.

The atmosphere is a real strength: warm, flattering lighting and a lively crowd that still allows for easy conversation at the table. (one side note--sitting in a booth is not super comfortable).  Appetizers were excellent, especially the endive salad and the dates. Entrees, however, were more inconsistent. The salmon, highly praised by others, arrived less than hot, as if it had been sitting under a warmer, and the tuna belly special, while clearly fresh fish, seemed composed some time before serving. Both were tasty, but not as good as they could have been if prepared and plated to order.

Service was young but eager to please. A bit more familiarity with the wine list—at least recognizing the names being ordered—would improve the experience. We didn’t make it to the speakeasy this visit, but plan to check it out soon. With better timing in the kitchen and some polish on service, The Pelican Room could easily live up to the hype.

Just wow. 11/10. As a person who was a local as of 4 days ago, boy am I sad to leave this place. (I know, I know, the picture in this review isn’t great quality- I didn’t want to be that person putting on her flash) but holy smokes. The smoked beet tartar is out of control- but you need to use the lemon! Or maybe not.. but the lemon made it even over the top. Third time here, in love with everything I’ve eaten (maybe minus the side of Mac and cheese, needs breadcrumbs!).

Service is phenomenal. Everyone here is trained so well and that I love most is the sweetness, the kindness, I overheard the person training staff. Really wonderful environment and the music is impressive.

The drinks are superb, every bar tender I’ve encountered is so knowledgeable and talented. Immensely grateful to see such a bipoc staff. Will be coming back for a date night so soon.

We came for brunch the 2nd weekend they started offering it but the restaurant opened this summer. It feels like they’re still figuring out staffing and other logistics but the atmosphere, cafe and food are great.

My friend ordered the strawberry mocha latte and I had the matcha. After trying my friend’s latte I asked for some strawberry syrup on the side to add to my match and it was a 10/10. However, they did charged me $1 for the small dish of syrup.

For food, we ordered the pelican platter, the roasted cauliflower salad, and the side of black pepper bacon. The highlight of the pelican platter were old bay tater tots and the pancake. The pancake was thick and fluffy, and it came with this delicious strawberry sauce. The roasted cauliflower salad was also great, but it had a lot of parsley and the cauliflower wasn’t very roasted. The black pepper bacon was extremely peppery, we had to scrape some off to finish the last slice.

The owners and staff have that personal touch with their service that feels like I'm visiting an old friend. They're also very passionate about their extensive tea knowledge for avid drinkers like me or newbies - which is very helpful when exploring their amazing tea menu (I'm still working on trying every tea they have). Absolutely love this place! The vibe is super cozy and aesthetic — perfect spot to chill, catch up with friends, do your school work or work period… just relax with a good cup of tea. The owners are super sweet and welcoming, and you can tell they really care about the place and their customers. It’s one of those spots that just makes you feel comfortable the moment you walk in. Definitely my new go-to tea shop! 🌿☕💛

Great atmosphere. Cozy location in the Bronx on the Grand concourse. Conveniently located near mass transit. Nextdoor to The board of elections. Specializes in tea of all kinds. Stop by and give them a try & say HI. 😀👍

google_reviews.text:
A Parisian Brunch Experience Worth Repeating

Having been to Paris once, I can honestly say this brunch captured that same cozy bistro charm — a little slice of Paris tucked into New York. The $44 Brunch Prix Fixe was the best choice of the day.

The atmosphere was lively yet relaxed, with soft live jazz setting the tone. The staff was warm and attentive, and even the bread with French butter and black sea salt was unforgettable — rich, creamy, and definitely not your standard butter!

I started with the Salmon Tartare, fresh and flavorful with vibrant pesto and crisp baguette toasts. My husband’s butternut squash soup was smooth, lightly sweet, and perfect for a rainy day.

For entrées, my smoked salmon buckwheat crêpe with a sunny-side egg was delicate and delicious, while his steak sandwich with brie, pickled shallots, aioli, and pomme frites was a hit.

We ended with the Chocolate Mousse, served tableside from a large tureen — airy, rich, and absolutely divine.

Every detail, from the music to the service, made this brunch feel special. A delightful experience we can’t wait to repeat.

This was my first French restaurant and it was amazing! I was completely happy with their service and food. Our waiter Medina was phenomenal. For starters we had the ravioli and French onion soup and for entree we had the Hanger Steak and Duck. Everything was delicious. I highly recommend this place.

A cute local french restaurant with super friendly service and owner. The restaurant offers indoor and outdoor seating. Ambiance is great - not too lowkey or too fancy which is perfect for a comfortable catch up. The food came out quickly and generous portion. There is no dedicated parking but metered parking in the area. Overall a great experience and would come back again to try dessert and other dish.

This is my second time coming here and I will continue to go as a special occasion spot. It is not a snooty type of French establishment. It’s very quaint and the staff make it very warm. The food is delicious, well seasoned, and fresh. Salmon tartare and oysters are very fresh. Lamb was not gamey at all, cooked to perfection.

Our servers were wonderful, both were fluent French speaking. Very personable and made the experience much better. Even gave my nephew hugs.

Restrooms are beautiful and clean. They smell very good.

Highly recommend.

Came here bc they had happy hour at the bar on a Saturday. Took advantage of their oysters at $2 each which were clean and the escargot also delish. Also ordered their bar steak (cooked perfectly at medium rear) and burger with fries and the Creme Brulee for dessert. Our waitress was attentive and pleasant as well as the manager and the staff in general. The ambience was lovely and romantic

document: El Pabellon De Oro. cuisine: Latin American Asian Fusion Mexican. located in Bronx. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The food was good I enjoyed the pork fried rice and the shrimp with lobster sauce which a bit on the salty side but enjoyable nonetheless. I also ordered the rib tips as well as the bbq ribs as well as the pork chops which was also good .  I will definitely go back again.

Ok, i've lived in the Bronx for a good amount of years & learned about this place as of recently.

Its in a really busy area under elevated trains & lots of little shops that seem to sell specialty items, music is abundant, loud & proud  & parking is double & triple everywhere.

You get to the corner where its situated and are instantly taken aback by a 'B' rating, which has 6 months to be taken care of in NYC.

The decor is dated but cozy there is a restaurant portion, where i saw 1st date in lust couples happily eating. The front is more bar-esque with bar seating and a counter. The staff is somewhat attentive & courteous whilst juggling phone orders & language barriers, they all look like members of a Korean boy band 😃

They ONLY accept cash!

The food is portioned well & although was nothing like what i expected, tasty. The pork fried rice is 'Not' the old school fried rice of lore i was expecting, no egg, shallots, sprouts, just a lot of soy sauce & onion, not the de jour hood yellow rice we all endure now, but tasty.

The Bistec Palomilla was not guisado as per tradition but seared nicely & flavorful 👍🏽

The shrimp Mofongo was not traditionally infused with garlic or cracklin or anything, just plantain. Which is fine because i've had it this way too, where the sauce is the star. This restaurants take on it did not falter, although tiny baby shrimp was used, but once again i was pleasantly surprised because the sauce was tasty.

The Ropa Vieja was my least favorite as it was nothing like  Cuban ropa vieja, the meat used was not shredded but thinly sliced fatty cuts. Kudos for the attempt & the chefs interpretation but alas Not ropa vieja, but tasty nonetheless.

The popular iced tea they sell, tastes just like the old school 4c powdered ice tea, we all grew up with.

Oh the eggrolls! Cannot forget the eggrolls!! They were not the size of a burrito like days long gone, more like spring rolls now, but they seemed 'meatier' than the hood variants we all endure & once again tasty 👍🏽

Would i come back...Probably, if on a fine Summers day, i wanted some chino latino or a different take on chinese food, didnt want to spend a lot of money & there was actually parking 🤗
the food was amazing the service was great this place gets a 10/10 for me and i had more than enough to take home

BETTER THAN SABROSURA! Please excuse the term but as far as Chinese & Spanish Cuisine aka "chino cubano" goes this place is the best.  Chicharron de pollo is amazing, chicken and broccoli gravy actually tastes better than others, despite the different color gravy, but what blew my mind, and the reason for this rave review, is the BEEF LOMEIN.  OMFG! They actually put steak in the beef lo-mein, as opposed to the cheap shreds of beef other places use, and it is delicious! Just make sure you take cash they do not accept any other payment.

Have been going here my entire life. Food, flavors, and hospitality haven’t changed a bit. It’s a true Bronx gem and the best Latin Chinese fusion spot in nyc. I recommend the broiled fish and shrimp, pork fried rice, and the batida de piña (pineapple milkshake). Honestly, everything I’ve tried is great!

google_reviews.text: We sat at the bar with Kevin who was superb.  Fair prices and good food, perhaps a bit underseasoned.  The shrimp and grits were excellent.

WAIT!!!!! I ALMOST FORGOT ABOUT THE STEAK BITES!! Get the cowboy butter steak bites. If you get nothing else, get these. I don’t even care if you’re vegan, get these. You can even ask for extra grilled bread, they’ll give it to you to soak up the sauce.

Man. The food here is legit and so are the people and so are the bathrooms. Cute glassware too!
We loved the new design of the restaurant. A perfect location for a local spot. Amazing pizza!! Try the eggplant pizza with pesto.

document: Roberto's. cuisine: Italian. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Roberto's Ristorante Italiano is an absolute gem! We had an incredible evening here celebrating a special occasion, and everything exceeded our expectations. The authentic Italian cuisine shines through with fresh, high-quality ingredients—their fried zucchini blossoms and smoked burrata appetizer were divine, perfectly crispy and flavorful. For mains, the homemade pasta dishes (especially the gnocchi and risotto) were cooked to perfection, with sauces that were rich yet balanced, not overpowering.
The ambiance is charming and upscale—beautiful Chihuly-style chandeliers, elegant Italian decor, and a cozy yet sophisticated vibe that feels like a little escape to Italy right in Vienna. Service was warm, attentive, and welcoming; the staff (including the friendly longtime waiter) made us feel like family. Portions are generous, and the wine list pairs beautifully with the food.
If you're looking for genuine, chef-driven Italian dining without pretension, Roberto's is a must-visit. We'll definitely be back—highly recommend! Grazie mille! 🍝🇮🇹

Delightful NYE’s dinner experience at Roberto’s - on the special prix-fixe menu set for the occasion to celebrate the arrival of 2026, great options were offered, and there was truly the embarrassment of choice!

We had “assaggini” to get us started, then the true appetizer, and primo and secondo course, and dessert - all delicious, super well presented, and very creative.

One member of our dinner party needed also a GF pasta option, and it was graciously made available too.

The wine list at Roberto’s is simply stellar, and the service was quite attentive.

The dinner event was concluded by a Prosecco toast to the New Year and a lovely taste of the ultimate post-midnight Italian tradition, cotechino with lentils!

Bravissimo Roberto!

We had an amazing dinner here. The ribeye steak with red wine sauce was cooked perfectly, juicy and full of flavor. My wife loved the gnocchi with truffle, creamy and rich in every bite. The beef tongue was so tender it melted in our mouths. It was also our first time trying drop peppers and they turned out to be a great surprise, sweet and slightly smoky.

The complimentary breads were really good too, we finished them all before the main dishes even came out.

We ended the meal with their deconstructed tiramisu, which was beautifully presented and tasted incredible. The decoration and atmosphere were spot on, warm and elegant at the same time. You can tell they pay attention to every detail. Definitely one of the better Italian restaurants around and we will be back for sure.

Such a splendid experience here! We had Italian style beef strip and foie gras, and ordered duck, steak, braised fish for entrees. Impressed by the tenderness of steak, probably cooked in low heat for a long time. The fish is among the best I had in western cuisines, good combination of roasted outskirt and softness, original seafood flavor and sauce. Usually western cuisines cook all meat with the logic (or standard) of a steak, such as duck, pork & fish. We loved the beef stripes whose flavor was well covered by the sauce. The Foie gras was great from my perspective, and a different variety from common paste form, but it does leave a strong gamey flavor afterwards. I will definite come back and try the whole fish! Last I have to mention their outstanding service which made you at ease with respect. Most waiters here seem quite aged and just walk around the restaurant like at their home, with right amount of formal attitude.

Rare to find a real Italian restaurant these days.

I thoroughly enjoyed my group dinner experience here. The menu was enticing and I knew it was real when I saw the Osso Bucco come out. The Calamatra was excellent with the variety of seafood and the red sauce was excellent along with the homemade pasta. The bread basket was unique with a few different bread types. Enjoyed the wine selection and both the Pinot noir and Italian red were pleasing.

It’s a lovely spot for a real Italian meal and I would imagine coming back for date night

google_reviews.text: A friend had recommended this place and so we tried it. It’s definitely a no-frills kind of environment so you definitely don’t go for the service. They are very fast and efficient but it feels more of an effort to flip the table. We sat downstairs, but there’s also a large area upstairs that had seating and was a lot quieter. The dishes are HUGE and 2-3 people could split a main dish with the portion sizes. The chicken Parmesan hit the spot and I’d come back for that alone. We also tried the stuffed artichoke, but it wasn’t great.

My father took me here 50 years ago. They wrote the menu on a paper bag and hung it on the wall. They have a menu now for those who need it. Great southern Italian food at reasonable prices. They use san marzano tomatoes and extra virgin olive oil which are the highest quality ingredients. I highly recommend a visit.

“I have eaten as much as I can, not as much as I want to, but as much as I can.”

The mussels starter with tomatoes sauce was outstanding.  Omg.  I usually only eat mussels with butter and garlic but I am converted!

Ossobuco, Roast Pork and Cabbage, and Lamb Chops were truly excellent.  The steak was declared very good (and fully consumed).  The potatoes with the steak were fine but not life changing.  This might be because the dishes were on the upper range of perfectly salty.  By contrast the potatoes were not salted.

One sits family style, sharing tables for 8 (or 12) with other patrons.  On a gentler day we might have made some new friends, but we came hungry and impatient today.  We love this style of eating, and have been here before.

document: Borgatti's Ravioli & Egg Noodles. cuisine: Noodles Pasta Shops. located in Bronx. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Best Fresh Pasta in the Bronx – Borgatti’s is a True Icon!

Borgatti’s Ravioli & Egg Noodles is hands down one of the best pasta shops in all of New York. Located right in the heart of Arthur Avenue, this family-owned gem has been serving up fresh, handmade pasta the old-school way for generations.

Their ravioli is perfectly filled and tender, and the egg noodles are silky, flavorful, and cook to perfection every time. You can literally taste the tradition and quality in every bite. Whether you’re making a Sunday sauce or a quick midweek meal, Borgatti’s pasta elevates everything.

The staff is friendly, knowledgeable, and always ready with a recommendation. The shop itself is charming and full of that classic Bronx Italian character you just can’t fake.

If you’re serious about pasta, Borgatti’s is a must. It’s a Bronx institution and an essential stop for anyone who loves authentic Italian food.

Ordered a box of small manicotti ravioli and a box of small meat and spinach ravioli and had it sent to FL for the Thanksgiving holiday.  You can tell it's fresh.  Everyone loved it, with an even split of who thought which kind was best.  Will definitely order again.  Can't wait to try other items/varieties!
The noodles and ravioli are always fresh and delicious. The Borgatti family is highly respected and the store is very clean and well kept. Thank you for the awesome food !

Borgattis in the Bronx is entirely worth being brave and waiting out the cold with long lines to get fresh pasta and ravioli.

Highly recommend getting fresh spaghetti,  cheese raviolis, and cavatelli.

They also have gluten free dried pasta and imported pasta from Italy.

If you’re a pasta lover, Borgattis is not to be missed! 100% bucket list place for any and all occasions.

Borgattis hold a special place in my heart.
My Italian grandfather always made homemade pasta but when his eyesight didn't allow it anymore he would have me take him to Borgattis.
He used to look forward to going there because he said it was as close to his as could be.
He loved walking in and looking at the pasta width card even though he had trouble seeing it he always took the time to look at it.
He would always get multiple pounds of #2 and #3.
If they had squid ink pasta then he was really happy ! The staff was always so good with him and always made him feel welcome.
On a personal note I always appreciated the picture of St.  Mother Theresa on the wall behind the counter.
Borgattis is as authentic as it gets. If you have never had homemade pasta, do yourself a favor and take a ride to Borgattis and try it, you will never want to eat store bought again.

document: Casa Della Mozzarella Italian Deli. cuisine: Delis Cheese Shops. located in Bronx. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Casa Della Mozzarella—A Bronx Institution That Demands Your Pilgrimage

Tucked away in the Arthur Avenue area of the Bronx, Casa Della Mozzarella is the kind of place that makes you understand why people talk about New York delis with reverence.

Getting to your sandwich is a rite of passage. The narrow corridor is packed with people squeezing past each other, hanging salamis overhead, and the chaotic energy of a place that knows exactly what it’s doing. You have to earn this meal.

I ordered The Casa: prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, sun-dried peppers, and balsamic glaze on a classic Italian sub roll. The bread was phenomenal. The prosciutto was paper-thin, delicately sweet and salty, with that silky texture that melts on your tongue. The mozzarella was pillowy perfection, clean buttery notes, and just the right amount of salt. And that balsamic glaze? Thick, velvety, darkly sweet with a fruity tang.
It’s more than reasonably priced for the little piece of heaven you get.

If you’re in the Bronx, Casa Della Mozzarella isn’t optional. It’s mandatory.

If you’re anywhere near Arthur Avenue and don’t stop here, you’re doing New York wrong. Casa Della Mozzarella is tiny, packed wall-to-wall with Italian imports, and home to what might be the freshest mozzarella you’ll ever put in your mouth. The sandwich I had was delicious prosciutto layered with mozzarella, a drizzle of balsamic, and just the right chew on the bread to have you wanting more.

It’s one of those sandwiches where you take the first bite and immediately stop talking because your brain needs a second to process how good it is. Everything tastes artisan, balanced, and deeply satisfying, like someone’s grandma made it with love in the back.

Highly recommend for the experience alone!

Traveled over an hour to visit here.  Went to visit where my grandfather lived in 2015 on Arthur Ave. First, I will say the fresh mozzarella cheese was incredible.

However, I am concerned that we paid ($14) alot of money for pistachio cheese, which expired in December (30 days prior). I did Facebook messaged them a week ago ( but no response).

It’s disappointing & kind of crappy of them.

Omg, Italian deli.

I wasn't ready and missed the sandwich menu which is hanging from the ceiling behind all of their other amazing offerings. But i managed to eek out a decent order of a hero with mortadella, sun dried tomatoes,  red peppers and fresh mozzarella...... it was nuts. Hella good sandwich,  got some goat cheese,  and a pesto sauce. Thr brah on my sandwich was crispy,  held up and was easy to eat.

Stoked to go back and order off the menu. Totally staying on the map.

What the hell is the magic they put on their sandwiches!! Old school New York Italian deli literally makes the perfect sandwich!!
Get the Bronx Bomber and get a trip to Sandwich heaven!! Treated us great with an extra sample of their house pulled mozz… No one does it like Casa Della Mozarella

The Calabria Pork Store is an absolute treasure on Arthur Avenue. From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with the mouthwatering aroma of cured meats and the sight of dozens of homemade soppressata hanging from the ceiling—it’s old-school Italian at its finest.

Their selection of fresh pork cuts, house-made sausages, salami, and dry-cured specialties is unbeatable. Everything is made with care, tradition, and top-tier ingredients. You can taste the difference—this is the kind of quality that’s getting harder to find.

Fumo: A Must-Visit Italian Gem in Harlem
​Fumo on Amsterdam Ave and 137th Street is, without a doubt, a must-visit culinary destination in Harlem. My recent dinner here with my wife was nothing short of exceptional, offering a perfect blend of great atmosphere, attentive service, and truly amazing food.
​From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was vibrant yet cozy, setting the ideal stage for a memorable night out. The energy is fantastic without being overwhelming, making it a perfect spot for either a special occasion or a casual weeknight treat. The service was equally good—our server was helpful, prompt, and genuinely friendly, ensuring we felt welcomed and well-cared for throughout the meal.
​The true highlight, however, was the food. I ordered the classic Spaghetti Carbonara and it was sublime. The sauce was rich and creamy, coated the perfectly al dente pasta, and was exactly the comforting, authentic dish I was craving. The Garlic Bread served alongside was crisp, buttery, and the ideal accompaniment.
​My wife opted for the Penne alla Vodka and was equally impressed. The sauce achieved that perfect balance—tangy from the tomato and decadent from the cream—a clear testament to high-quality ingredients and skillful preparation.
​Fumo offers a complete and unforgettable dining package. If you’re in the area and looking for high-quality Italian cuisine that backs up its reputation, stop searching. This place is an absolute gem.
​Highly, highly recommended!

We were promptly seated inside and served shortly after. The first server, Steven, took our drink orders and gave us a little time to peruse the menu. We ultimately chose a rigatoni bolognese (friend's daughter), a penne vodka with meatballs (friend), a naked penne vodka for my mom and I had a spaghetti vongole. For drinks, my mom and I each had a raspberry lemonade and my friend and her daughter had a Fumo mocktail and a coke, respectively.

Now after enjoying our meals, two other servers came and we requested extra bread from one and he never brought it, even after asking an additional time. Steven immediately brought it right after we were able to get his attention. Also while busting the table, the other server from the two mentioned earlier, reached across without asking for clearance which rubbed us all the wrong way because he passed really close to my face.
This turned us off from tipping extra because the service was not great and I just thought I should make a note of it but other than that, everything else was good to go. I'll be back to try the brunch and other menu items.

name: Trattoria Vivolo
document: Trattoria Vivolo. cuisine: Italian. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I wish I could gatekeep this place but it’s hard not to brag about it. The vibe is visually beautiful, elite lighting and cozy. The staff is extremely kind and friendly. I have tried multiple dishes at this point: the spicy bucatini, the bolognese, and even the steak. They have all been 10/10 dishes, made with fresh ingredients. They accommodated my allergies with no problem. I celebrated my birthday here, and have also had solo dinner: both wwre lovely experiences. I love their little bar area, as well as their cozy booths. Although they are very accommodating, I definitely recommend calling to make a reservation in advance, as it can get busy pretty quickly. They have an excellent wine selection. There is a parking lot right across the street, but it’s a typically calm/quiet area. This is definitely one of my favorite Italian spots in NY.

We enjoyed our early dinner on January 14th, 2026. The food was very tasty and the portions were huge. The service was very friendly. There is very little street parking. Prices were a bit high for the items ordered in our group of six, but the quality was there. If you are looking for a good Italian place in Harrison and don't mind paying a little more, Trattoria Vivolo is the place for you.

🍷🍝⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

From the first moment I walked into Trattoria Vivolo, I knew it was pure magic. The warm light, the soft chatter, the scent of garlic and good wine — it feels like stepping straight into an Italian dream. Every visit feels like being welcomed home.

Dean, the owner, is truly the heart of the place — always making you feel like family the moment you walk in. He has that rare warmth that turns dinner into something personal, memorable, and special every single time. And Maria… she’s a legend. She’s been there forever, the kind of server every great restaurant dreams of having — graceful, kind, and always making sure everything is just right. The rest of the team follows her lead — attentive, professional, and genuinely caring.

And then comes the food. The Fritto Misto — light, crispy, impossible to stop eating. The Cozze Bianco — mussels in a broth so good you’ll want to drink it straight from the bowl. The Vitello Prosciutto — tender, rich, and unforgettable. The Linguini Nere — you won’t find pasta like this anywhere else. The Lasagna al Forno tastes like it came from an Italian grandmother’s kitchen, bubbling with love. And the pizza… oh, the pizza. Thin, blistered, perfect — I’ve never had pizza like this anywhere in Westchester. I dream about it and always come back for it.

The back room is a world of its own — perfect for birthdays, date nights, and special family dinners. It’s intimate, dramatic, and full of that old-school charm you can’t fake.

Every meal here is a celebration. The wine is always flowing, the specials are always tempting, and just when you think you’re done, the Bomba Baci and cannoli arrive to remind you that there’s always room for dessert.

This isn’t just dinner — it’s a memory every single time. A place that feels like home. We love it here and we’ll always keep coming back… if we can get a reservation, ha!

Absolutely top tier dining experience. From the moment you walk in the door it is clear that customer service and hospitality are very important to Trattoria Vivolo's staff and management. Lindsey, behind the bar, works as if she has 8 arms, never slowing down or losing her cool despite the tickets piling up. Every single staff member was genuinely engaged, attentive, and thorough. As someone who runs a business in a adjacent industry I am beyond impressed with the staff presentation/service. The main dining room feels like a renovated classic diner? Not from the area so dont know the history but I like it. Outdoor seating area was spacious and clean.
Moving from the best food state (NJ) I am still struggling to find places to get the staples in local spots around Westchester County. Happy to say Bruschetta and Chicken Parm are now checked off the list. Bruschetta was a little soft and unwieldy but the end pieces that were a little burnt were perfect. 8/10. How are you supposed to eat bruschetta without making a mess? Chicken parm. Super simple but its crazy how many places will mess it up. Trattoria Vivolo's chicken parm was consistent in size and texture throughout. On the thinner side for a cutlet (preferred). Sauce and spaghetti were on point as well. All ingredients were great, fresh, and well presented. Looking forward to coming back. Oh, right. Tiramisu was difficult to eat an enjoyable pace but please do yourself a favor and slow it down so you can fully enjoy it.

We came here for the first time and were absolutely blown away. We had a delicious dinner that tasted very good. Our waitress Dacka was so kind and was super attentive. She made sure we had enough drinks and even recommended us certain dishes that she thought were very good. She also recommended some dessert drinks that are very popping Italy, so we tried them out. The menu has many different options to choose from and you can have either fish, meat, chicken, or pasta. We were in the outside seating area and it was a bit chilly. But they took care of that immediately as they had on the big heaters and placed them all around us. The wind was not a problem as we were very warm and still got to enjoy our food. We left very satisfied and want to come back soon to try some other dishes that sound very interesting.

Parking is pretty much street. Use caution when parking at a meter, but plenty of street parking without a meter on Kimball Avenue.

Glad I gave this place a shot and I'd definitely return here.

I asked for chicken cutlet instead of shrimp with my pasta, and they bring me grilled chicken and tell me that’s all they were able to do. They brought us regular cheesecake, not even a hint of crème brûlée, and the cannolis were hollow in the middle. I thought we were going somewhere nice for Thanksgiving but it was all and all a disaster. Never again.

name: Lady Wong
document: Lady Wong. cuisine: Desserts Bakeries. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
All their desserts are so good and not too sweet!! Def go for their niangao

- Black sesame passionfruit cake: 8/10, bought this for my friend’s bday. Solid flavor! Light and airy and not too sweet

One of the most memorable bakery visits I’ve had in NYC! I tried four of their cakes and each one was a work of art in both flavor and presentation. My absolute favorite was the Black Sesame Passion Fruit. The mousse was perfectly nutty, the caramel balanced, and the sesame crunch gave the best texture contrast.

The Ube Blackberry was a dream for ube lovers, layered textures with fragrant ube caramel and a subtle citrus note. The Blackout Noir is a chocolate lover’s fantasy, deep Valrhona chocolate, silky ganache, and coffee caramel that’s rich and indulgent. The Mont Blanc Chestnut Mille Crêpes was delicate, creamy, and lightly sweet with a very refined chestnut flavor.

Also tried their Pandan Latte, which was aromatic and unique, a cozy companion to the desserts.

Everything here feels thoughtfully created, from flavor pairings to textures. This place is definitely a hidden gem for elevated, modern pastries and I’ll absolutely be coming back for more!

I brought Lady Wong Patisserie to a birthday and accidentally became that person everyone asks:
“Where did you get this?!”

We ordered a variety of pastries and every single one hit, but the flavor combos deserve their own spotlight:

- Strawberry Guava – bright, fresh, not cloying
- Ube Blackberry – earthy, jammy, deeply satisfying
- Black Sesame Passion Fruit – UNREAL. Nutty, tangy, perfectly balanced. My absolute favorite.
- Panna Cotta – silky, elegant, quietly flexing

This is pastry for people who say “I don’t like sweets” and then somehow eat three.

Pro tip from experience: order a full-sized cake in advance. The value is excellent, the execution is flawless, and it saves you from the regret of wishing you had more once the boxes are empty.

Lady Wong is doing refined, modern pastry without the sugar overload or gimmicks. Just thoughtful flavors, beautiful textures, and desserts that feel special without trying too hard.

10/10 would bring to another birthday.
11/10 would hoard for myself.

This place just has a high seating bar inside with about five seats and then there’s three seats in a metal table outside. My only complaint is that I wish there was more seating and I wish it was more comfortable however that’s a small complaint not a personal choice.

I was really impressed by this cake. It has a simple and modern design, with multiple layers with a great combination of flavor and texture. I could never imagine black sesame go so well with passion fruit. Highly recommended!

Great little place in C-Ville. The food is terrific, you can’t go wrong with anything on the menu. We had the cheese board and cauliflower/Brussel sprout appetizer. The appetizer was really good, strongly recommend. The mushroom pasta and the fried chicken breast were well cooked. A ton of mushrooms in the pasta. Very good wine list thats not overpriced or overwhelming.
Very worth the visit.

We picked The Local based on the menu options.  We were traveling and didn't want anything fast, so we looked up food near me.  The Local popped up, was rated high and we always enjoy seeing fresh food options and unique entrees, so decided to give them a try.    When we arrived, the ambience appeared to be casual and comfortable. Our focus is always the food, service, and ambiance.  All areas met my expectations.  I was excited about the crab soup, but unfortunately sold out.  My other appetizer options were crispy shrimp and fried cauliflower & Brussel sprouts.  The flavor of the aioli and seaweed salad on the crispy shrimp was top notch flavorful as well as Sriracha aioli on cauliflower dish.  I would have been happy with both as my main dish.  Our entree was Crispy Fried Trout, a unique twist on fish.  I've never had fish with okra.  It made the dish a bit heavy, but I enjoyed it.  The fish was perfectly cooked and fresh, it was the rice and sauce that made it heavy.  Not sure if I would order again as I prefer my fish with light flavors.  Overall, we enjoyed dining here and our server was pleasant, attentive and personable.  Give it a try, I'm sure you will enjoy your experience.

We hosted a rehearsal dinner Friday night and I cannot thank The Local team enough for such a fantastic event. Our guests loved the food and the service - it was a true celebration. We hosted the rehearsal dinner and then a welcome party in the Opal Lounge and all had a fantastic time!  Thank you all for creating such a memorable celebration for our family!

Wow wow wow this place is excellent. From start to finish the service, food and drinks were phenomenal. They have lots of nice specials, an extensive wine menu and fun cocktails. We got the ribs and sirloin and they were both cooked perfectly.

This tiny spot is a hole in the wall in the best way — serving the best food we had in Charlottesville. The dishes were fresh and fantastic, highlighting locally sourced ingredients and thoughtful seasonal flavors that stand out from the usual tourist fare. The atmosphere was cozy and authentic, making you feel like you’re truly experiencing something unique. If you want a memorable meal that showcases Charlottesville’s farm-to-table scene, this should be at the top of your list.

document: Original Pancake House. cuisine: Pancakes Waffles Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Let’s talk about the Dutch Baby. Not a human, not a pet, but a glorious, puffy oven-baked pancake that deserves its own fan club. It takes 15–20 minutes to cook, but honestly that just gives you time to emotionally prepare for greatness. When it arrived, golden and dramatic, I swear the room went silent. The edges were crispy, the middle custardy, and I immediately questioned why I’ve ever wasted my life on ordinary pancakes.

Because moderation is overrated, I also went for the avocado toast with poached eggs. Those eggs? Perfect. Yolk flow so beautiful it should be set to slow-motion music. It was one of those “don’t eat too fast or you’ll regret not savoring it” situations.

And then came the sunny side up eggs with turkey sausage and wheat toast. The sausage was actually juicy and seasoned (not the cardboard diet version), and the toast hit that sweet spot of crispy without being a dental hazard. Even the “basic” items here feel elevated.

Service was fast, cheerful, and didn’t even flinch when I basically treated the menu like a challenge. The vibe is welcoming, the food comes out hot, and the portions remind you this is a place that respects breakfast.

Bottom line: this isn’t just breakfast — it’s an event. The Dutch Baby is the Beyoncé of pancakes, the poached eggs deserve their own TV show, and the sausage might have ruined me for every other turkey link. If you love breakfast, stop reading reviews and just go already.

One thing though. They close at 2pm and they are super busy on weekends. Service is a little slow but worth the wait

They have some of the best gluten free pancakes I’ve had! They also have sugar free syrup so folks watching sugar intake can eat out with family and friends like normal. It is my go to place for brunch while pregnant and I have food restrictions. Thanks for catering to those of us with dietary restrictions!
Bacon is thick cut and delicious and we have enjoyed everything we have ordered here!

Ordered chicken and waffles and it was terrible. Chicken was SUPER hard and OLD. Looked like it was overheated in the microwave. It was so hard that you can't bite it or use a fork BUT have to forcefully tear it apart. When I asked for a new chicken, they gave me only two small pieces which seems like it was heated up in the microwave as well. At least the waffles were good. I've been here a few times but after today, NEVER again.

We have visited this restaurant multiple times and have always been pleased with the food quality and generous portions. It's our go-to spot for satisfying our cravings for a big breakfast. After reading other reviews, we agree that the food can take some time to be served. In terms of the restaurant itself, it's clean, but the decor could be more memorable.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

The Original Pancake House is a must-visit spot for breakfast lovers, offering some of the best pancakes and breakfast dishes you can find. The food here is absolutely 5-star quality, with generous portions, high-quality ingredients, and a menu that caters to all kinds of breakfast cravings.

Food – ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

The pancakes are hands down the best you’ll find anywhere—fluffy, rich, and full of flavor. Some of the standout items include:

Dutch Baby – A giant oven-baked pancake with crispy edges and a soft, custardy center. Served with powdered sugar, lemon, and butter, it’s a unique and must-try dish.

Apple Pancake – Almost like a dessert for breakfast! Loaded with caramelized apples and cinnamon, this oversized pancake is indulgent and delicious.

Buttermilk Pancakes – Classic and perfectly executed, these pancakes have a light texture and a slightly tangy flavor.

Bacon & Eggs – The thick-cut bacon is cooked to perfection, crispy on the edges but meaty in the center. Paired with eggs cooked to order, it’s a simple but satisfying choice.

Omelets – Massive, fluffy, and packed with fillings, the omelets here are a meal on their own. The Western and Spinach & Cheese varieties are both excellent.

Everything is cooked with quality ingredients, and you can tell the difference compared to typical breakfast chains.

Service – ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

The service is generally good, but during busy hours, it can be a bit slow. The staff is friendly and accommodating, but you might have to wait for refills or extra condiments. That said, they do their best to keep things moving in a packed restaurant.

Atmosphere – ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)

This isn’t a fancy, modern brunch spot—it has a more old-school diner feel, which some people love, but others might find a bit outdated. It’s cozy but can get very crowded, and the noise level can be high during peak times. The seating is functional, but don’t expect anything too stylish.

Final Thoughts

If you're looking for amazing breakfast food and don’t mind a bustling, no-frills atmosphere, the Original Pancake House is worth the visit. The food is absolutely the star here, and while the service and ambiance could be improved, the flavors make up for it.

✅ Must-Try: Dutch Baby, Apple Pancake, Buttermilk Pancakes
⏳ Best Time to Visit: Early morning to avoid long wait times
💲 Worth the Price? Yes – portions are generous and food quality is excellent

Would definitely recommend for breakfast or brunch, especially if you're a pancake lover!

google_reviews.text: This area has a lot of cute cafés. This one was perfect for a good hangout. Has more seating in the back, free wifi, delicious triangle kimbap. Savoury and sweet things. Matcha cake and Egg and Mayo Croissants are the best!

It was a rainy day in Toronto and I wanted something sweet. I walked past the shop and liked the colors and how peaceful yet bustling it was. I went inside and saw all sorts of desserts in different shapes, sizes, colors, and flavors. The waitresses were very friendly and smiling. I ordered a matcha chocolate cake; it was perfect and super fluffy. The presentation was excellent, and I also liked the variety of teas.

I had visited this café before, but this time I decided to give it a second chance and try their choux pastries. Unfortunately, I really didn’t like them at all.

First of all, the jasmine flavor strongly reminded me of matcha. When I brought this up in order to return the pastry, the staff member did not understand me at all. She simply stood there smiling and insisting that everything was correct. The first time I tried matcha, I found it overly sweet, and this jasmine pastry gave me exactly the same impression.

What upset me the most was the reaction of the staff. They made no attempt to resolve the situation or find a solution — they just smiled and did nothing. It felt like they were robots placed there purely for appearance, not for customer service.

Will I come back? Absolutely not. I didn’t like anything there except the beautiful presentation. The pastries themselves still need serious improvement in flavor, and the staff clearly needs proper training.

Pros: nice visual presentation
Cons: staff (a major downside)

I ordered the matcha sundae. It had a generous amount of toppings and I really liked how the rice krispy bits added a small crunch. The matcha ice cream was great, not too sweet and it paired really well with the red bean paste and mochi that was included.

The service was amazing, very kind and friendly staff that had our orders out very quickly!

The atmosphere was very calm. It had some quiet music playing, but it was still easy to hear others while conversing in the cafe.

Overall, I had a really great experience and I would definitely come back again to try some other items on the menu!

Empire Szechuan
52 W. Madison Ave.
Dumont, NJ 07628

General Tso’s Chicken Dinner Combo
Boneless Spare Ribs Dinner Combo

Located on the intersection of Madison Avenue and Veterans Plaza is a locally owned Chinese takeout spot.

Out of all the choices on the takeout menu, I decided to explore the two most popular plates.

General Tso’s Chicken Dinner Combo:
The hot, spicy chicken is chewy on the inside while slightly crunchy on the outside; expect a mild kick.

I’m satisfied broccoli was included, but my only critique is that I would have preferred that the vegetable was mixed in with the tangy sauce.

Also included with this combo is pork fried rice and wonton soup.  The three wontons and the broth were piping hot.

The noodles go hand in hand with the soup.  It is a win win whether you choose to have them dry or soaked.

Boneless Spare Ribs Dinner Combo:
The ribs are tender and chewy with a savory taste.

For this combo, I explored the white rice and egg roll.  This appetizer was filled with cabbage and ground pork.  I enjoyed it, but the size of the egg roll could have been slightly larger with a tad bit more pork.

Both combos can also be purchased as a lunch special if you arrive between 11:00 AM and 3:00 PM.

An adequate amount of seating is available if you decide to dine in.

Empire Szechaun is open six days per week; arrive any day except Tuesday.

I highly recommend this location if you are on the go and need a quick meal, especially the two popular menu items.

This place is a veritable cornerstone of Pasadena and a hidden gem. They’ve been around for decades and have some of the best orange chicken you’d ever care to taste. It has a somewhat “hole in the wall” atmosphere but that’s what makes it special. Anthony Bourdain would have loved this place for the no-frills food. Just a solid family run business serving exceptionally yummy chicken dishes.

I can’t speak to the seafood options but I don’t think that’s meant to be the star anyway.

As to the pricing- Pasadena is something of an old school community. It’s highly blue collar in most areas and many folks just haven’t come to terms with inflation yet. This place has been in service to the community for 15+ years and they shouldn’t have to starve themselves to do it. The costs of basic goods increases overtime. You can spend $10-$15 on a meal from McDonalds or you can get yourself some of the best orange or general Tao’s chicken in Maryland. I moved out of state and still drive 1.5 hours to this spot on occasion. Try the orange chicken, general tso chicken, shrimp toast, and the egg rolls. The egg drop soup is solid and I believe they also have great hot and sour soup. You can’t go wrong with these options 👍🏼.

For the rest of you complaining, I was born and raised in Pasadena. It doesn’t need another McDonald’s or Royal farms. You talk about supporting your community, but try to negatively impact a locally owned and operated establishment with 1 star reviews because you don’t like the prices? Try reaching out to the owners and having a conversation next time before you jump on your soapbox and lose one of the last remaining family run businesses in the area. Show up in a positive way for your community and watch it begin to change.

To the folks at Ho Wok- thank you for the awesome memories and food over the years. As a kid, I’d always request Ho Wok orange chicken for my special “birthday meals” and it always meant the world to me. Thank you for giving back to Pasadena over the years.

My partner and I had v-day dinner last night here, and he found it based on his search for jersey’s best Italian places. We love Italian, like LOVEE. We travel to find and dine in at the best places possible and La Campagnola was an incredible experience. No one asked me to write this, insisted or hinted at it nonetheless. I’m eating my left over chicken alla vodka as I’m writing this. My partner made a reservation, we were quickly seated and served all night. Our waiter and his assist were so delightful and sweet! He made us laugh all night. Such great service, we really appreciated it. My partner had their steak and vegetables, cooked to perfect medium rare, and I the chicken all vodka with blush sauce. It was perfect and all so delicious. Live music, beautiful ambiance that reminded us of our travels in Portugal. It’s the perfect anniversary, holiday, celebration or even go to date night spot in our opinions. For the dinner, a few drinks, dessert, bill turned up all for about $130. Which provided us both lunch the next day! Compared to PA and North NJ locations we’ve travled to, we’ll be back again!

Was recommended by my husband’s cousin to come here for our anniversary dinner and I am SO GLAD we came. Our server was a delight. The girl assisting the server was sweet, the bus boys were sweet. The entire experience was a 10. The food was honestly perfect. From the appetizer, to the soup, the vegetables, to the entree. Phenomenal. Will definitely come back.

This place is consistently superb.  The staff is always welcoming.  I have enjoyed a few meals here and was never disappointed.  I LOVE their horseradish sauce.  (So if you don’t order a prime rib sandwich, try it with the green bean appetizer.). And the crab cake sandwich reminded me of Key West.  All lump crab:)
Specialty drinks are made with care too.  I enjoyed their spicy margarita!  Shout out to Nick, the bartender.

La Campagnola - Shamong - Returned for some more delicious food, great vibes, live music! The chef select garlic steak was delicious. As was the bone in Delmonico (ribeye). Once again they impressed me from the food and service! #italian #steak #livemusic #hashtagstevej

My boyfriend and I went for our Valentines Day dinner and the service was top notch, I wish I could remember my waiters name but he was excellent. All of the staff were welcoming and friendly. Our group of four had varied opinions about the food, which made the experience interesting. I personally enjoyed the dishes, finding them flavorful and well-prepared. Good stop for Italian food lovers! The pasta was quite good. The pasta took time to get ready, but it was not a problem for me - it tasted fresh.

I spent the better part of 16 hrs at the airport and on a plane from Europe, when the airline informed me that my new layover was gonna be 6 hrs I figured I should at least make the most of it and get some good food.
Thankfully I found this place on yelp close to Newark international and went over to have an early supper.
Started wine, clams, olives, then carbonara, and even more wine. Spending the whole time taking in the “old jersey” feel of this place, eating incredible food, watching New York hockey, and having a tremendous conversation about the world, bird dogs, and everything in between with the owner.This place made me feel right at home and if I had more time they’d have probably had to have kicked me out of there. I recommend this place highly and if you’re in the area, check them out… I know I’ll be back.

We had the pleasure of speaking with the manager, Noah, who let us know they also have a Staten Island location definitely adding that to our list. If you get the chance, don’t walk to this place run. Our favorites were the Aunt Honey pizza and the special vodka sauce pizza… unreal.

Came on. Sunday
Aunt Honey (Soppressata, chili flakes hot honey)- while the pizza is delicious for a standard pizza. I wish it had more hot honey flavor as that was supposed to be one of the topping
Brussel sprouts and calamari - no comment 10/10 would get again. Brussel sprouts was nicely seasoned and crispy.
Best pizza I’ve ever had in New York! 🍕✨ The Salsiccia flavor was absolutely amazing — rich, full of taste, and perfectly balanced. If you love pizza, you have to try this one. Highly recommend!

What a treasure! This spot was such a great find for a pizza lover like me! Excellent restaurant, but tucked away location. All of the dishes our party had were aromatic and delicious. Nice interior decor, extremely clean throughout. At present they have an A rating with the health department, no doubt they have earned it. Customer service was friendly without being overbearing. The floor to ceiling windows brighten up a dreary winter day. Highly recommend if you’re in this part of Staten Island.

name: Piccolino's
document: Piccolino's. cuisine: Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: My grandson Googled Italian restaurant, that was what he wanted to eat. Found this place, and it was amazing. We were greeted upon entering and told to sit where we wanted. There were four of us, we ordered drinks, I had a half lemonade half tea, and an appetizer of fried mushrooms, they were delicious. They brought bread and marinara sauce even a bottle of olive oil. I had the veal parmesan and my wife had the small shrimp Alfredo, my grandson had the large shrimp Alfredo with extra shrimp, and my granddaughter had the vegetarian lasagna. The food dishes were all delicious, but one exception, my veal was a bit  on the tough side. Even though it was delicious with all the perfect taste I was a little disappointed with the veal. Our waitstaff was very polite, professional and friendly. Great atmosphere, very clean restaurant and bathrooms. Because it is Santa Fe NM things are a bit on the pricey side. This is a must return and try another different dish for sure. Overall the taste of the food dishes were impressive. As far as deserts, the cappuccino getato and the tieramesu was excellent.

The food was amazing. The service was just as good. Jacob did an amazing job at telling us what everything on the menu was. The wine he suggested was spot on. We will be going back! We got dessert but to go. We had shrimp and scallops with saffron sauce and 1/2 duck with red cabbage and steamed potatoes. The duck was cooked perfectly and the honey sauce made it even better.

I was looking for a good Italian place in town and I was recommended this place by a friend. Needless to say, it did not disappoint. Piccolino is one of those hidden gems in Santa Fe that you probably wouldn't know about if someone didn't tell you. It's a bit out of the way from the main roads like Cerrillos so unless you stumble across it by accident, you wouldn't see it unless you're deliberately looking for it.

I ordered the Chicken Chardonnay with the Mozzarella Marinara for an appetizer for lunch takeout. They told me it should take about 15-20 minutes for the food to cook and I arrive accordingly. Got there, went to the front counter, paid for the food, waited about 2-3 minutes for it to finish cooking, then I was on my way.

When I got home, I was immediately surprised by the portioned size. It was certainly enough for one person and so I had some of it for dinner as well. The cream gravy in Chicken Chardonnay was savory and went well with the 3 tender chicken breast mixed together. It came with spaghetti as the pasta which I wasn't expecting but it was good. It needed a pinch of salt but YMMV. I didn't really give the vegetables much attention at all, but 🤷‍♂️. The bread on the side was also delicious dipping in the the gravy.

I think this place is worth a try if you're looking for authentic Italian food to try especially if you're out of town. Granted, the food can be a little pricey, but I think this is a great place to go you're looking for something a bit different and if you want a place to sit with family, friends, or colleagues to eat.

Wednesday, Sept 24  12:00 pm

Piccolinos is clearly a popular place, ranked #1 by the Santa Fe Reporter many years in a row. We arrived at a full parking lot, yet were greeted and seated right away.  And even though they were busy, our server came immediately. The dining room is crisp and bright with walls hung with Italian themed posters and art. There is an extensive and exclusively Italian menu with Ravioli, Pastas, Baked Dishes like Lasagna and Stuffed Eggplant and Pizzas with plenty of add-ons. Appetizers and salads were creative and interesting. Mains are listed by Seafood, Veal and Chicken. We began with a surprise of a complimentary starter of warm Italian bread with olive oil and a spicy tomato dipping sauce. We shared a Capri Salad (mozzarella, slices of tomato, basil, carrots and crispy, cold lettuce with vinegar and olive oil jugs to mix your own dressing.) Our main course was a large (16”) Pizza Stagione with sundried tomatoes, artichoke hearts, black olives and sausage (substituted for the standard pepperoncini,) ample for two and satisfying. Our beverage, Pellegrino sparkling water came in a frosted mug with a big lemon wedge on the rim. We appreciated these kinds of thoughtful details. There was a quiet hum in the dining room (72dB) making it easy to converse. We especially enjoyed this lunch and will return.  Pellegrino's is very reasonably priced, especially for the quality of the food.

A busy local Italian restaurant that was packed with locals on a Tuesday night. Definitely worth a visit for good food in a casual atmosphere. Generous servings for reasonable prices. Services was good and everyone so pleasant and helpful.

I was visiting my home town of Rahway NJ and stopped in for a bite to eat. Juan the owner made us feel so welcomed, and even joined us for a moment at the table. I cannot say enough good things about Il Forno a Legna. From the moment you walk in, the vibe is cozy and welcoming, making it the perfect spot for anything from a casual family dinner to a special celebration. The beef lasagna yummy, arancini delicious and vodka penne great.   The server was nice and the restaurant had a quaint atmosphere.  We took the cannolis to go.   I would go back. If you are in the area check it out.

Ordered three brick oven pizza. First was plain my wife liked it, 2nd was margarita which was very good and third was the tri color with pesto,vodka and tomatoes which we really didn't like. We sat outside on a beautiful day. Music was good but to loud and hard to talk. Overall good place.

google_reviews.text: Love it! Food was great! Ambience's cozy!  They were accommodating! I recommend you try this Italian restaurant and trust me, you won't regret it!

The food was DELICIOUS!!  Way better than the chain restaurants. Everything tasted fresh and seasoned perfectly. Staff was super friendly, everyone was smiling, just all around great vibes. Definitely recommend 10/10!

Ive been living in Bayonne over 6 years now and didn't realize this Italian restaurant near my place. Had it I recently and the pasta is great. I had the rigatoni with meatballs and it was cooked well and the meat balls tasty.

Walked in around 5pm without a reservation and asked for a table for two. We were seated within minutes. Our host and waiter were fantastic. The food we ordered was delicious and came out at appropriate intervals. The drinks were perfectly made. Even though it got busy and tables were filling up with guests we were not rushed to settle the bill. A perfect dining experience.

I visited Cafe Bello on a Monday evening for dinner and the place was surprisingly packed.

Parking
It’s not easy to find a parking spot in the area. You might need to park a few blocks away so keep that in mind.

Reservations
They take reservations but I didn’t make one since I went on a Monday evening but there were only 2 available tables once I arrived so next time I will reserve.

Food
Food is DELICIOUS. They give a complimentary garlic bread which is great. Fried calamari and the 5 cheese pizza were also delicious. I was afraid the pizza was going to have a strong cheesy flavor but it was just like a cheesy margherita, I definitely recommend it.

Ambiance
It’s a small restaurant and when it’s crowded the acoustic is bad, it’s difficult to hear and have a conversation with someone across from you. This is the only thing I didn’t like about this place. Once some people left it got better. They had some ambiance music but you couldn’t hear anything, just people talking loud.

Price
Price is fair for the quality of the food. Make sure you ask for the drink menu, I have no idea why the waiter didn’t bring it along with the other menus once we arrived.

document: Dani's Italian Bistro. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Dani’s is one favorite place to have dinner at on Staten Island. Great food, great service and a for sure a date spot. You can’t go wrong with any food here, and they’re pretty big portions. My go-to is the chicken parm or chicken florentine, all pasta are great and if I had to pick one dessert for the rest of my life I would have their homemade apple crumb cheesecake. Highly recommend if you haven’t been here

I  recently dined at Dannie's Italian Bistro in Staten Island and had a wonderful experience! The food was delicious and authentic, with generous portions and flavorful dishes. The service was top-notch, with friendly and attentive waitstaff who made sure our needs were met.

The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with only about 10 tables, making it a great spot for a date night or special occasion. The prices were a bit on the higher side, but the quality of the food and service made it well worth it.

Overall, I would highly recommend Dannie's Italian Bistro to anyone looking for a great Italian meal in Staten Island. Be sure to make a reservation, as the small size of the restaurant means tables can fill up quickly!

Rating: 4.5/5 stars

Price Range: Average to High ($20-$40 entree range)

Recommended for: Date Night, Special Occasions, Italian Food Lovers

Dani’s Italian Bistro a small family owned restaurant restaurant in Staten Island.  The best of restaurants is when the owner is the chef those are my favorite to dine at.  This restaurant also had a really nice intimate atmosphere, and it’s the perfect date spot or just a great place if your looking for a delicious authentic Italian meal.   I had the Mozzarella en Carrozza appetizer which was good, but I prefer mine with less breading.  The sauce it came with was excellent though, and I scooped whatever was left with my spoon!  I ordered one of the dinner specials of the night which was the striped bass over broccoli rabe risotto in a marinara sauce.  I was quite impressed with that dish!  They gave such a generous piece of striped bass here!   It was absolutely delicious!  The marinara sauce was to die for, and the fish was cooked to perfection!  I loved that it came over such a delicious broccoli rabe risotto as well!  You can tell the chef put a lot of love in that dish!  They had a great selection of house made desserts here, and I ended up choosing the apple crumb cheesecake.  It was so good!  When I received my bill I was surprised how low the prices were too which was another plus!  The generous piece of striped bass I was served was only $29!   Just to note I’ve been to the restaurant across the street before DeLuca’s, and Dani’s Italian Bistro blew them away with their food, reasonable pricing, service and atmosphere!  They also had a nice selection of filet mignons on their menu for only $31 as well.  Service was excellent, and the owners are warm and welcoming.  I highly recommend dining here!

Appreciate the small antipasto plate for each table. Ordered from the daily special- a nice portion of Halibut on artichoke risotto. Dish was tasty but visually bland (fish and rice same color) and i didnt see/taste artichoke but rice was still good.  Needed a green vegtable, two or three asparagus across the top or some broccoli or green zucchini slices on the side would have really helped balance the plate.  Veal Saltimbocca (hubby choice from menu) was just okay...plenty of fresh spinach but the prosciutto was too thick and difficult to cut through (not sure if it needed the hardboiled egg across the top..?).   For appetizer, Clams casino very tasty and yummy and would order again.  Place has loyal customers and a friendly/cozy vibe.  Will visit again for sure.
