document: Ita Italian Kitchen. cuisine: Pizza Italian Cocktail Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Hands down, one of the best restaurants I’ve ever eaten at. I want to start by extending my compliments to the chef, Theo Giordani.

Let me take you through the meal.

We began with the mac and cheese, served in a mini cast iron skillet—absolutely immaculate. The top had the perfect crunch, giving way to rich, creamy, cheesy goodness underneath. Comfort food done exactly right.

For our entrées, we ordered the black squid ink pasta, which was to die for. The balance and generosity of the clams, squid, and shrimp paired beautifully with the pasta—each bite felt intentional and indulgent. We also had the branzino with mashed potatoes and vegetables. The skin was perfectly crisp, while the fish itself melted in your mouth—truly the best branzino I’ve ever had. The freshly made mashed potatoes were a refreshing reminder of what real, thoughtful cooking tastes like, especially in a dining scene where so many places cut corners.

By the time dessert came around, I didn’t think I had room—but I’m so glad I did. The cobbler was unforgettable. If I could have an entire pan to myself, I absolutely would. Much appreciation as well to Mark for the baked ricotta and bread—simple, warm, and executed beautifully.

There’s still so much on the menu left to try, and I will definitely be back. My stomach and my taste buds were thoroughly pleased

I don’t even have the words for how good that Branzino and mashed potatoes dish is. And the apple cobbler at brunch? Please. Someone hand me three to-go boxes because there’s a limited amount and I’m not pretending to share.

All jokes aside, Chef Theo is incredible, and these new specials are on another level. I couldn’t choose between the three, so I did the only logical thing: ordered all of them. The burrata is outstanding. I’m not even a fig person, but the beet-and-fig combo with the carrot purée is unlike anything I’ve tasted before. The pumpkin ravioli? Amazing. Actually amazing. And the baked ricotta definitely got an upgrade, I just wish they’d send out a little more focaccia with it.

Service was on point too. Shoutout to Amber, the bartender was great, and the whole vibe was 10 out of 10. Spectacular food, great energy. Highly recommend.

We arrived early without realizing the restaurant didn’t open until 5:30, and the owner was incredibly kind and welcoming, letting us sit and relax while we waited. From the first bite, the pasta dinners completely blew us away, rich, flavorful, and absolutely delicious! The drinks were just as fantastic, perfectly crafted and refreshing. Add in the amazing atmosphere, and it was an unforgettable dining experience. We’ll definitely be back!

I love this place. I went here for my birthday and couldn’t decide what meal I wanted so ordered multiple of them! They have half off pasta and pizza on Wednesdays. The management is always present as well as the owners. Staff is phenomenal and treats you like family. The Chef Theo came out to speak to me after my meal - I had to compliment her on the cook of my fish. Literal Chef’s Kiss. 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥

7 Spicy Vodka Rigattoni Pasta
7 Calamari
6.75 Chicken Parmegiana: Spicy Vodka Rigattoni

Fried Calamari was fresh and delicious. The chicken parmigiana was dry, tough, and Chewy. I think they over cooked it. I will absolutely not buy that chicken again.

document: The Sicilian Guy. cuisine: Italian Soup Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: We made a trip during a long layover from the Newark airport. Food was amazing and the service was awesome. The owner was so friendly and you could tell how passionate he was about his food. We had the sausage/meatball platter, a prosciutto sandwich with fresh mozzarella, focaccia bread and some cannolis. Some of the best and most authentic Italian food I’ve ever had. Have thought about the food regularly since we went. Can’t recommend enough.

My fiancé and I finally tried the Sicilian Guy after always passing it on Newark and OMG the food is unreal! We got the cold chicken cutlet sandwich for lunch and then the stuffed peppers and lasagne for dinner. Everything was incredible and the sauce had so much flavor! We ended up going back a couple days later to try their hot sandwiches, splitting the meatball parm and sausage and peppers. Again, everything was absolutely incredible! The owner was so kind and let us try some of the ziti he just made. We will definitely be back to try the kick ass soup 😄

the food was divine and the service was top notch. I called ahead to see if they had space for us and they were so accommodating. I got the half chicken and half meatball sandwich and a sicilian pistachio cannoli. 10/10 recommend

Wife and I decided to swing in as she was craving a sandwich. Transparently, we’ve never been very drawn to the place, but that’s changed. Walking in, the place smells great. We grabbed an eggplant sandwich and it was fantastic. Soft homemade bread coupled with excellent sauce and tender eggplant. We don’t feel heavy afterwards and will def be back soon.

It pains me to leave this review, because their service was so good, but I just got a chicken parm sandwich and the breading was so soggy. It was so wet I couldn’t finish the sandwich because the texture was throwing me off, the breading so wet it had congealed into jacket of sorts on the chicken. I don’t know how long that cutlet was sitting there, but it was not fresh. An $17 sandwich should be filled with crispy cutlets and not a soggy messy.

I also got the soup with the bread, which was very good and saved this meal. I cannot excuse a sad, sorry cutlet sandwich when Jersey City is bursting with great Italian spots so I don’t think I’ll be returning.

Overall, would return for a reliable, decent American bite if I have another concert nearby. Spacious restaurant, clean restrooms, and helpful staff.

I went to Blue Dog NYC for an early dinner, and the experience was surprisingly warm and satisfying. One of the first things people ask is “Is Blue Dog good for dinner or mainly brunch?” —and honestly, their dinner options were just as solid as their daytime menu. The ambience was cozy and inviting, with a relaxed atmosphere that made it easy to unwind.

I felt my wings. We can't wait to come back and focus on shared plates.

We celebrated my grandma’s 88th birthday last night at Amelia's by the Farmers Rail, and it was truly unforgettable. From start to finish, everything was absolutely amazing.
We started with the lobster sliders (phenomenal), and my grandma had the filet ...which she declared the best steak she has ever had in her 88 years of life. That alone says everything. I had the lobster linguine, which was incredible, and we shared the Brussels sprouts with dinner. Every bite was perfection.
We finished with carrot cake for dessert, and it did not disappoint. Our server, Desiree, was unbelievable. She was attentive, warm, knowledgeable, and made the entire evening feel extra special for my grandma.
The atmosphere was unique, authentic, and welcoming...the kind of place that makes a celebration truly memorable. We can’t wait to come back. Highly recommend!

Overall the experience was really good! Almost everything was positive: the ambiance was nice and the decor was fun, the food was really fantastic, and our server (Desiree) was delightful and fun. We understand that it wasn't the hostesses fault but not having anyone apologize for that is kind of rude. We also had plans afterwards and had to cancel them because of that so that's a bit frustrating. But aside from that, everything was great! The pork belly, brussel sprouts (a must try!) and duck confit were delicious! Desiree was a delight and turned our mood around so thanks again to her!

We had a great time at Amelia’s! The drinks were great and the atmosphere was amazing. The service was great as well. The food was not mind blowing. And for the price I don’t think I would come back. It was very pricey but we did get appetizers and drinks. I think I would enjoy more pasta options!

The staff is so accommodating, informative and friendly. The cocktails are top notch. It felt like I was sitting at a password needed secret restaurant in a big city. The only thing I’d add would be a little more light. There were times when I couldn’t see what I was eating because the lights were too dim over our table. The lamp on the table did not help.
Overall an incredible experience and we’ll definitely be returning!

One of the best Mediterranean restaurants in nyc! The food was outstanding, starting with the hummus, simple, warm, and delicate to the octopus that was cooked to perfection, super tender and absolutely a must-try. The schnitzel was also very good.
We discovered this place by chance, and it turned out to be a wonderful surprise. And don’t skip dessert—the dark chocolate mousse was unreal!
Great place! We ordered the shakshuka and schnitzel, everything was delicious. Cozy atmosphere, great food, and definitely worth a visit. I’d happily come back!

Shoo Shoo is one of those spots where the vibe instantly pulls you in—laid-back yet stylish, with such a warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes you want to linger. The energy of the place is just as memorable as the food, and together they create such a standout dining experience.

We started with the hummus, and it was absolutely outstanding—so fresh, silky smooth, and bursting with flavor. It paired beautifully with the warm bread and set the tone for the rest of the meal. The fries and sweet potato fries deserve a special mention too: perfectly crispy, piping hot, and honestly addictive. They’re the kind of sides you keep reaching for long after you’re full.

For mains, the lamb shawarma was excellent, with a distinctly gamey flavor that made it rich and satisfying without being overpowering. It felt authentic and hearty. But one of my favorite parts of the meal was the Israeli chopped salad on tahini. It was bright, refreshing, and balanced, with that creamy tahini base tying everything together beautifully. It was light yet flavorful, the kind of dish you could eat every day and never get tired of.

Everything about Shoo Shoo—from the fresh, flavorful food to the great ambiance and attentive service—makes it a place I can’t wait to return to. It’s perfect whether you’re coming for a casual meal, a night out with friends, or just to enjoy really well-executed Mediterranean dishes in a space that feels good to be in.

document: The Blue Box Cafe. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Cafes French. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is very_expensive.

google_reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of enjoying the afternoon tea experience at the Blue Box Café, and it was truly a memorable and elegant outing. The atmosphere was exactly what you would expect from Tiffany & Co.—refined, stylish, and beautifully designed with the iconic Tiffany blue that creates a sophisticated yet welcoming setting.

During the experience, I ordered the scallops with spinach, which were perfectly prepared and full of flavor. The dish was light yet satisfying and paired wonderfully with the overall afternoon tea service. I also enjoyed a glass of champagne, which added a celebratory touch to the meal and complemented the food nicely.

The service was attentive and professional throughout the visit, making the experience feel relaxed and special. From the presentation of the food to the ambiance of the dining room, everything reflected the level of quality and elegance that Tiffany is known for.

Overall, the afternoon tea at the Blue Box Café was a delightful experience that combines excellent food, beautiful surroundings, and exceptional service. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a refined and memorable dining experience in New York.

I had the opportunity to enjoy breakfast at Blue Box Café by Daniel Boulud, and overall the experience was truly impressive. I tried both the Breakfast at Tiffany and Tea at Tiffany menus.

The Breakfast at Tiffany menu stood out in particular, the egg topped with caviar was absolutely exceptional. The balance, texture, and depth of flavor were remarkable and easily at a Michelin star level. Daniel Boulud’s culinary signature is clearly present in this dish.

The Tea at Tiffany experience is visually generous, with portions that almost play with perception. While the quality and flavors were very good, from a gastronomic standpoint it felt slightly behind some afternoon tea experiences I’ve had in England. That said, enjoying this ritual within the iconic Tiffany setting was still a wonderful experience.

The service deserves special recognition warm, highly professional, elegant, and respectful. The staff made the experience feel refined and personal without ever feeling forced or artificial.

Overall, Blue Box Café is more than just a restaurant; it is an iconic experience. The fusion of the Tiffany world with Daniel Boulud’s culinary vision makes this a destination well worth experiencing at least once.

As a longtime fan of Tiffany & Co., I was thrilled to celebrate my birthday and our 10th anniversary at the Blue Box Cafe, inspired by Audrey Hepburn. After learning that reservations open a month in advance on the Resy app, I set an alarm to snag our table right at midnight. Thankfully, we were able to book it just in time!

Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted by the staff. There was a short wait of about 5-10 minutes to be seated, but the manager offered us complimentary champagne while we waited, which was a lovely surprise. The service throughout our visit was exceptional.

While the food was good but not extraordinary, the overall experience was truly memorable. The washroom was beautifully designed, and we enjoyed browsing the stunning jewelry pieces during our time there. Even with the holiday rush, we felt well taken care of. I highly recommend visiting the Blue Box Cafe for a special occasion!

Tiffany's Blue Box Cafe is on every girl's wish list! I didn't make a reservation, but I showed up around 10 am and was able to get a spot at the bar top about 10:30 am. This is the cutest little spot! While I was waiting for my spot, I wandered around the beautiful store a bit. The staff is so friendly and everyone has a story about how they started at Tiffany's and why they love it SO much. It is practically a museum and definitely worth stopping in and checking out some of the different floors. I think there were at least 7. And, all of the flowers that are everywhere are ALL real. =O

I ordered Holly's Plate and a glass of champagne and enjoyed every moment and bite. They truly want you to leave with a long-lasting memory.

The food took me by surprise. I expected a middling level of quality for tourist centric destination - even with Chef Boloud’s reputation. I was wrong. The food was excellent.

I had the Breakfast at Tiffany’s while my fiance went for the High Tea. Menu highlights for were the caviar egg and fruit salad.

If you’re going to Blur Box expect a certain demographic and to pay more than you probably should for the amount of food. But while you’re there take in the sights of the iconic storefront. You won’t be disappointed.

name: Brioche NYC
document: Brioche NYC. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Coffee & Tea Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I’ve spent enough time in NYC cafes to expect the usual: cramped seating, frantic energy, and prices that feel like a personal insult. Brioche, however, is a brunch of fresh air.

Tucked away on West 37th Street, it’s an unassuming hidden gem that would be absolutely overrun by legions of tourists if it were on a busier block.
You order from a kiosk—which usually signals a lack of soul—but here, the execution is flawless and the staff is actually attentive and wonderful.

I went for a build-your-own brunch plate, and it was deeelicious! The ingredients were incredibly fresh—perfectly over-easy eggs, a generous fan of avocado, and sausage and bacon that actually tasted like they came from a kitchen rather than a laboratory. Even the side salad and potatoes were handled with the utmost care.

It’s a rare spot that values fresh ingredients and a relaxing ambiance over a pretentious markup.
If you’re looking for a fantastic brunch and a moment of genuine culinary clarity, look no further. It is absolutely worth it.

Overall okay. Lots of seating. They have a kiosk to order at but if you order at the kiosk they make your food to go? That’s what happened to me! I wish I knew I would’ve ordered at the counter. Salmon Benedict was just alright. I tried the sweet corn latte too. Good - strong corn flavor and different! Just no caffeine :( overall good lunch spot

Great brunch/cafe spot in the city. Ordering was smart--order at the kiosk at the door where you can dine in with a table number OR take out. Bright and cozy atmosphere with music played at a nice volume in the background.

There's a wide variety of options to order (coffee and espresso drinks; smoothies; sparkling ades; toasts; brunch plates; soups and salads; and sandwiches and sides as well)-- we ordered the classic French toast (with caramelized banana) and persimmon toast with coffees, strawberry banana smoothie, and a side of yuzu bacon. All delicious and perfectly portioned.

Since we opted to dine in at a table, it would have been nice to receive our coffee beverages in mugs but totally understand the idea of serving as takeaway. Wonderful service all around though.

Saving this place as one of my favorites as I'll definitely be back!

Brioche NYC is a year old capacious cafe on West 37th Street a few doors down from Cafe China. There is a Bar Menu with coffees, smoothies, speciality drinks and sparkling mocktails. On the Kitchen Menu, the French Toast is popular and at $14 quite reasonably priced. In the "Build Your Own" menu one can choose from a selection of base, protein, vegetable and drink. This can range up to $20 which for some is affordable. Since I had eaten lunch at Cafe China, I wanted a hot cappuccino and a sweet cake and chose a currant scone. The coffee was hot and warming. The scone seemed rather dry. I sat there for over an hour relaxing. The floor is pretty as it's made of small colored stones. Cece made my visit enjoyable,l.

A newly opened cafe in K-town blending Japanese and Korean vibes. The specialty lattes are super creative! My favorite was the yuzu matcha — perfectly sweet and tart. The corn latte had a strong corn flavor, though the syrup was a bit too sweet for my taste. I couldn’t really taste the pistachio in the pistachio latte — still waiting to find one with a rich nutty aroma!

The savory dishes were great — both the smoked salmon Benedict and the prosciutto spinach plate were delicious. The scrambled eggs were soft and creamy. The tiramisu was smooth and silky once it thawed — definitely worth the wait!

name: Freemans
document: Freemans. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Lounges American. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
A couple of months ago I stopped by here with a longtime friend from my youth just to check it and the alley out. Even though we were not going to eat, we were warmly welcomed and shown the restaurant by Alyssa. After that experience we decided that this would be the next stop in our every month or so lunch

Yesterday we returned for lunch and the experience was equally impressive. We were greeted and seated by friendly Willa and served by Myles who knew to do the little things that make a good dining experiences into a great one. More on that later!

We ordered a burger and a chicken bacon club sandwich. Because we had told Myles we couldn't make up our minds and were going to split the entrees, she (without our having to ask) had the kitchen cut both sandwiches in half before serving them. The burger was full size and flavorful (perhaps cooked a bit more than what I had hoped medium rare would be but still excellent) and the chicken club sandwich delicious. The club sandwich came with salad and the burger with fries.  I am not usually overly enthusiastic about fries, but these were amzaing - fresh, hot and flavorful!

Thank you Freemans for an outstanding culinary experience!

*I apologize if I did not spell the names of those to whom I gave shout outs! :-)

Very solid dining experience.   Food was good, I really enjoyed the tuna tartar... pork chop was cooked nicely, but a little too much sauce, etc. which led to an odd savory/sweet combo that didn't quite hit the mark for me. Server seemed to be thoroughly uninspired.

I wavered between a 4 and a 5 but decided on the higher rating due to overall experience. Absolutely beautiful restaurant. Down a graffiti filled alley, multiple rooms and two bars. Charming at the highest level. You felt like you were in a few hundred year old home. We ended up in an almost private room at the back of the restaurant because we were a larger group and it was perfect. We started with devils on horseback and artichoke dip.  Both excellent. The dip was not overly cheesy or greasy but had great flavor. The bread was nothing special but the dip was great. The devils on horseback were cooked well. Dark rich flavor. The bacon wasn’t greasy and it had a perfect amount of cheese.   We shared both the kale caesar and grain salad and would order both again. Both were not overly dressed and had great flavor. We added bacon to the caesar and it was a generous portion and crispy. The grain salad had a little tang to it and was very refreshing.  Also shared the Nashville hot chicken. Again generous portion. Chicken was cooked really well, very moist on the inside and crunchy and sticky on the outside. I don’t think it had much of a kick heat wise but was very tasty.   The waffle was a little disappointing. It was barely warm when served and didn’t have much flavor, definitely did not taste any cheddar. I didn’t taste the English breakfast or pancakes but both looked delicious and the people who ordered them enjoyed them. We also tried the ginger shots and they were great. The restaurant is definitely not cheap and we had a couple of things that were not perfect but overall the experience of the actual restaurant and the food is worth a visit or two or three. Will definitely return to try more food options .

ABSOLUTE GEM

The interior is very pretty and welcoming. It can be over whelming to walk into a PACKED restaurant, but you’ll have the best time!!

The Mac and Cheese - TO DIE FOR
Meatballs and Burrata - DELISH. The sauce is really good!!!
Salt and Vinegar Fingerling Potatoes - less vinegary than hoped, but still really crispy and salty!
Broccolini - TENDER, a little too much soy, but still very delightful

THE PORKCHOP - STUNNING. The apple slaw brought a rich, bright tang. The pickled red cabbage brought strong earthiness. The porkchop was smooth, tender, and full of flavor — melts in your mouth.

DESSERT:
Sticky toffee pudding? Inject it INTO MY VEINS.

The ice cream — seasonal and sourced locally. Solid, no complaints

The no flourless chocolate cake with cream was fine — not sure i’d  get it again, however it pairs well with the ice cream (we opted for vanilla)

Service exceptional. No notes. Can’t wait to come back!!

This place is so nice. The tables aren’t too close together so having a convo is not impossible. The Chilaquiles were so good. Perfectly spiced! My friend had the French toast and she it was the best she has ever had! Highly recommend!

name: Little Ruby's SoHo
document: Little Ruby's SoHo. cuisine: Burgers Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I recently visited this café and had a really nice experience. Gabe provided excellent service he was direct, informative, and very knowledgeable about the menu. He took the time to explain the options and was more than willing to accommodate my preferences, which I really appreciated. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. I ordered the pasta, and it was both fulfilling and very tasty. Overall, the food and service made for a great visit.

I would definitely recommend stopping by!

Came here for lunch. Had to wait a little bit for a table as we walked in as a party of 6. The place had a really nice atmosphere. Service was fast. Everyone I was with really enjoyed their food but mine was quite bland and did not have much flavor. It did not come with the scallion salsa that was indicated on the menu. Would not recommend for vegans as I had very few options to choose from, but otherwise it was a really nice spot.

The place is small and can get quite busy. The food was decent overall. The hotcakes were a bit heavy, but that's expected for pancakes. My breakfast sandwich was flavorful and just enough to satisfy, though the bottom of the bread was soggy. My companions enjoyed their big breakfast and the classic cheeseburger with sweet potato fries. We also ordered regular fries with truffle, which were tasty. The service was great, and the prices were affordable. If you're looking for a quick brunch in the area, this place has a variety of other options too.

I was in Soho last Tuesday and decided to meet up with some friends of mine who were also in the neighborhood. They suggested we visit Little Ruby's since I've never been there and it was close to where we already were. The place was packed and the atmosphere was such a vibe. Loved the decor and the overall feel of this place.

We were greeted by one of the servers with menus and automatically knew what we wanted to order when we saw the selection of food.

I ordered The Ruby's Ragu: braised beef short rib with pappardelle noodles, pecorino and burrata.

Friend number two ordered The Pesto Pasta: spaghetti, zucchini, baby peas, snap peas, kale, parmesan, creamy pumpkin seed pesto.

Friend number three ordered The Classic Cheeseburger: two 3oz beef patties, L.T.O., pickles, American cheese, special sauce on a potato bun. We also had a large Margarita Pitcher to share.

My Ragu was good, not over seasoned and the braised beef was cooked to perfection. The noodles were also good and all the ingredients together served its purpose. My friends enjoyed their meals as well because their plates were all licked clean. The one thing I wish I was able to order was some Tequila, however, they only had wine and beer on the menu. Great conversations were had over some good food and Margaritas in this cozy place full of great vibes. Definitely worth checking out.

a bit crowded but lovely lovely place. shrimp pasta was amazing! a lot of people were raving about it so i decided to get it too. bouncy juicy shrimp came deveined and deshelled, was creamy without being too heavy, and pasta was cooked perfectly. the creamy chicken pasta was good too but i preferred mine lol 😝 portions were perfect, not too full but left me completely satisfied. but the banger was the banana bread we overheard other tables talking about, IT WAS DELICIOUS!! it came with a passionfruit butter and honestly the passion fruit flavor was so clear and tart that it cut thru the actual taste of the butter so it tasted more like a jam. the banana bread was quite expensive but very worth it, slightly crispy crust and actual bread reminded me of a sponge cake, it was so pillowy soft. so glad i came here on a whim. also the bathroom lights burnt out 😭 don’t care tho the food was so good and i left so happy

document: The Marshal. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch American Pizza. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
The Marshal is a small but very cozy spot serving elevated American food. There are some highlights: our server was great, even as the restaurant got very busy at peak times on Saturday. Food wise, their small plates were very good. The deviled eggs were the best I've had, and we also enjoyed the tomato sides and bread.

Some space for improvement (or things that were not for us): some of entrees really didn't have that much depth of flavor--the gnocchi, for example, tasted too much like cream of mushroom of soup.

We'd come back, if only to try some of their other small plates.

Delicious food and great customer service! The Mac and cheese and chicken wings were very good and the breadsticks for starters are delicious! Would definitely recommend and make a reservation as they were full on a Sunday night!

It’s a very small restaurant with cute interiors.

We’re not super hungry so we had three appetizers and a salad to share which was more then enough. We had Mac and cheese, chicken wings, and ribs. For the salad we had beets salad. All were delicious.

For dessert we had the cobbler. The only issue I had was they don’t serve decaf coffee which was a bit odd!
The bbq rib to share and short rib were fantastic as well as a pear pizza. The service was friendly and helped create a cozy environment on a cold winter afternoon.
It’s a nice small intimate restaurant. I highly recommend the burrata and chicken salad. We also ordered two pizzas but we weren’t a fan of them.

Hootch & Banter in downtown Frederick is a win. The Filet Wellington minis were tender, flaky, and packed with flavor from the truffle duxelle and demi-glace. Excellent service from start to finish and delicious food/drinks! We sat upstairs at the bar which was gorgeous with the natural lighting and exposed brick walls. I wasn’t expecting a whole lot from the turkey sandwich, but boy was that a mistake, because I cannot explain to you how GOOD this sandwich was. The fries are also incredible. Highly recommend for brunch or lunch in Fredrick!

name: Remi43 Flower & Coffee
document: Remi43 Flower & Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Florists. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’m sitting now at Remi Flowers Coffee on 42nd and 2nd, and honestly, this place hits the sweet spot. Easy to walk in, full of plants and color — you just feel good being here. There’s something about the mix of energy and calm: people working on their laptops, chatting, taking meetings, but it still stays peaceful.

The coffee’s excellent — rich, well-made, and they serve it in these nice “to stay” cups that make the whole experience feel more intentional. No one hurries you to finish or leave, which I really appreciate.

It can get a bit busy at times, so if you’re tight on schedule, maybe peek first. I came around 11:30 and it was perfect — no line, just great vibes. Definitely one of my favorite Midtown spots to take a breather, work, or just enjoy a proper cup of coffee.

One of our favorite coffee shops in NYC. Been coming here since it opened and absolutely love all of the plants you are surrounded by! It's always busy and full but you can usually find a seat.  The lavender latte is the best I've had and the barista's are incredibly talented at latte art every time.  Don't miss this spot!

Flowers and plans live here hello!! Amazing staff and great vibes! Not very quiet but perfect to lock in or chat ! Not the best location for a work call but the music and atmosphere is top tier !! I got a hot apple cider .

I was pleasantly surprised by this coffee shop! Located in Midtown East, this two-story cafe is a spacious and stunning space to catch up with friends or get some work done (they have wi-fi here)!.

I got their maple latte while my friend got their rose one, and both drinks were delicious (although we both like my maple one more). Would definitely come back to get some work done here!

I liked all the flowers and greenery dispersed around the coffee shop. My favorite spot is the upper floor accessible via the spiral staircase. If you need access to outlets the ground floor is the better option. I chose the hot berry matcha latte. It was delicious and smooth! I think I will return when the weather is warmer and the flowers are blooming!

document: Quality Bistro. cuisine: French Steakhouses New American. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: Had a reservation for 9:15 but ended up getting a seat around 10:15. They were running late on seating. A waiter handed out Champagne while we were waiting. After we got seated, they offered us free salad and a side dish for the steak. The food was great and everything was served quick after we got seated.

Extraordinary bistro just steps away from Mid-Town Hilton Hotel. Perfect lunch stop after checking into Hilton, cold Dec 31 afternoon, windy NewYear’s Eve as we celebrated our 46th wedding anniversary. This cold day was modulated by hot French Onion Soup and extraordinary Mac & Cheese…hot, stringy and perfect spices with amazing top browned to perfection in the oven.
A wonderful exotic cocktail at next table called, Spicy Bird, served in a large fun  porcelain tropical peacock bird…mug! Where else but New York?
Perfect food, easy prices, fun delicious epicurean delights. Located on 55th street and Avenue of the Americas. 🏆🏆🏆🏆🏆⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

The atmosphere was refined and cozy, the kind of place where you want to slow down and enjoy the evening. The beef tartare was truly outstanding, perfectly seasoned and full of flavor. The yellowtail appetizer, however, felt a bit out of place in a French restaurant, you naturally expect to taste the classics.

For the main course, the scallops were soft and tender, and the white fish was incredibly delicate. As a compliment, they served crème brûlée unexpectedly salty, but it added a memorable twist to the evening.

Of course, I would like for the second knives for the main course to be brought together so that I wouldn't have to ask again.

But overall the service was good, they found my favorite rose wine, which wasn't on the menu. The waiters were quite friendly.

Surprisingly, even on a Wednesday, all the tables were taken, and the place was quite lively clearly a popular spot.

Overall, it’s an elegant restaurant with great attention to detail. Next time, I’d focus more on their traditional French dishes.

Took my wife and kids to this amazing french restaurant for son’s birthday. Food is solid 9.8/10. Atmosphere 10/10. Service is amazing 10/10.  Gentleman in a beige suit, think he was the manager, went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience. Definitely will be back for more!

We had dinner at Quality Bistro, and although our table took about 40 minutes to be ready (even with a reservation), the team handled it with class. They offered us complimentary champagne while we waited, which was such a nice gesture and one of the many reasons we keep coming back as regulars.

Once seated, everything was outstanding as always. The food was a solid 10/10, and we were treated to complimentary starter and dessert, making the evening feel extra special.

A huge shoutout to our server Ciro, who was attentive and warm throughout the night, and to Declan at the bar.

Quality Bistro continues to impress us with its service, atmosphere, and consistently amazing food. Definitely one of our go-to spots in NYC.

name: Upland
document: Upland. cuisine: New American Burgers. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: First time here and WOW. The server, Joel was super attentive and nice, I think my water was refilled 9 times, new plates/silverware with each course, very impressed with the service. The food was outstanding, starting with the complimentary bread, so soft and amazing butter. Then the burrata, margarita pizza, cacio &peppe and rigatoni for our table, all so tasty and you can tell it’s made with fresh ingredients and homemade pasta! We didn’t leave a crumb behind. We got the olive oil cake too and they put a candle in it for my bday. To top it off, the atmosphere was intimate with lovely booths yet lively! Can’t wait to return!

We were so excited to try this restaurant after seeing its aesthetic interior on our Instagram feed. The food was just as good and the flavors of each dish were really well-balanced. We tried the pappardelle and the salmon. ALSO there's free bread. It was the fluffiest ever and we devoured the loaf. I was surprised that the miso caramel cheesecake had a thick drizzle of caramel but was somehow not too sweet, and the olive oil cake was also amazing.

I went here for dessert because I couldn’t get in at dinner time. We were 4 people, and the service was very friendly and attentive. The dessert was both excellent and exactly what we needed after a long, rainy day walking around NYC. We got the following: Cheesecake, Limoncello Olive Oil Cake, Affogato, and Decaf Cappuccino. Highly recommend for a post-dinner treat.

Busy active Resturant with mix of regular dinners and business lunch crowd. Buzzing but still comfortable level to talk. Food came out in a timely manner, staff was very accommodating and attentive. Group of 7 and we all truly enjoyed our lunch. Will be back!

*UPDATE*
Upland reached out and apologized for everything. They remedied the situation and invited me back to try again. I live in Canada but have a trip to NYC coming up again soon. I plan to come by and give them a try again. Will update again once I give them another try.

This restaurant was highly recommended to me and I was excited to try it. We arrived before opening and patiently waited until they opened. The hostess was Incredibly rude and snooty when I informed her that I didn’t have a reservation. She told me if we promised to be quick she could seat us. Which we were. When we were seated the original waiter gave us the dinner menus. After we received our drinks the new waitress realized the mistake and brought us the lunch menu. She was very flippant, wasn’t informative and barely came to the table. The actual food was a 5/10. The portions were tiny. The noodles weren’t even al dente and the sauce was barely flavourful. There’s much better places in NYC than upland.

name: Fossetta
document: Fossetta. cuisine: Italian Wine Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I came here as a party of four walk-in for Saturday brunch. I typically do not write poor reviews for restaurants, but the service during our meal there was poor and left us feeling negatively after our meal.

Our waitress would drop our plates down on the table roughly and we had to ask multiple times for cutlery. She made a mistake and added berries to our pancakes (which is extra $) when we said we didn’t want berries, and when we brought up that we did not add berries to it she said she would take it off our bill. However, the berries were not taken off our bill, so we did end up paying for something we did not order. It’s my fault for not checking before paying and leaving, but it’s frustrating to have to check the bill ourselves for that correction when we were told it would be taken off. The waitress’s attitude was unfriendly overall and while I understand brunch service is busy, it would have been nice to have felt more welcomed here and not be charged extra for something we did not ask for.

The food was fine. Our personal favorites were the mortedella sandwich and the pancake so we would recommend that.

Came in on a busy Saturday night but they were able to give us bar seating which wasn’t a problem, they have a very nice kitchen layout which you can clearly look into while you enjoy your food. We got an olive oil and sea salt focaccia which was possibly the highlight of the meal, very tasty and not too overpowering. The picture is of our entrees which was their lasagna and a pork milanese. Lasagna was great, but the milanese was a little on the saltier side, although still very good. This is a nice spot for a dinner and pretty well located to several nearby bars for after your meal, if that’s your thing. Could see myself coming back in the future

stopped in, was unpleasantly surprised that they only serve the full menu during certain hours, but was pleasantly surprised by the food itself.

we felt bad coming in and just leaving before ordering, so we stayed. we could only eat off of the bar menu, so we just had some meatballs and bread. it was actually pretty good but took forever to come out. the drink had an ample pour

wish we came during a “meal time” so we could’ve tried their actual food. the interior is so cute and i would’ve loved to enjoy a meal there.

edit: i’m sorry i didn’t look at the hours.

I ate here two months ago and have NOT stopped thinking about that caesar salad. It was the best caesar salad I have ever had. I might get on an airplane and return to Fossetta to get another caesar salad.

great spot for Italian food. service was quick and amazing. absolutely love everything I had. I highly recommend getting the pancake if you come for brunch. It’s super fluffy and so good with the maple syrup. for the pasta, the chicken liver was interesting and added lots of flavor to the sauce.

name: By & By
document: By & By. cuisine: Cafes Cocktail Bars Coffee & Tea. located in Manhattan. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
By & By nails the whole “slow morning done right” vibe. The breakfast bagel sandwich was next-level — soft, chewy, perfectly toasted bagel loaded with melty cheese, fluffy egg, and that savory hit of sausage that just makes everything better. Simple, but done with total precision.

The hot latte? Smooth, cozy, and exactly what you want in your hand while people-watching from a sunlit corner. There’s tons of seating too — the kind of place you could hang for hours with a good playlist and pretend you’re writing your next big idea. By & By just gets it — calm, delicious, and effortlessly cool.
It felt very homey and comfortable. The service was friendly, and the food was good. It’s just around the corner from the hotel, making the location very convenient.

Please note, this is based on my experience at By & By. Hopefully the owner sees this. The garlic bagels that were on special probably sounded good in your head, however, as soon as I could smell the garlic burning I knew it was too late. Burned garlic is not appetizing and should be avoided at all costs. Please taste your food and if it tastes bad don't serve it. The coffee was good, the atmosphere was chill.

We stopped in for brunch and coffee on a Sunday morning in early March while traveling. We arrived just before 11a - a lot of the tables were full but the line to order wasn’t very long.  The barista/cashier was friendly.

We ordered coffee, a breakfast sandwich, a banana and a BLT.  We were able to get a table inside but I see they do have some outdoor seating which would be nice in warmer weather.  The coffee was hot and good. The food was good as well.

There was a live 3-piece band playing some tunes in the front window. That was cool and they weren’t so loud so it was it was a nice unexpected experience.

I would for sure come here again if ever in town.
This is my favorite cafe in town. Always friendly staff. Food is always good. And such a cozy environment. Highly recommend!

Highly recommend a (or multiple) visits to Zofia's. The cocktails are in a word stunning. Zofia's shared with us the most interesting Christmas cocktail list that we sampled and loved... the common spicy espresso Martini, the pumpkin apple pie followed by a Zombie and Pain killer....very very well mixed. Generous and complex. Thank you Zofia for creating this very cosy and welcoming environment.  Loved the music, atmosphere, service and of course, the magical cocktails.
Highly recommend.

What a welcome addition to the neighborhood! I came in for a drink and stayed the whole night. The atmosphere is very cozy, and Zofia's drinks are amazing! Everything was memorable down to the details of glassware, drink stirrers, etc. And Zofia herself is a gem. Can't wait to become a regular here!

So thrilled to have a tiki bar in the neighborhood! There’s a mix of classic tiki and modern twists. They also have beer available. Really love the vibes here and the bartenders are great. I had the painkiller and it was a 10/10. They make their own coconut cream!

google_reviews.text:
we had soo much fun here!!! i was worried that we’d have to ask for a table with views but literally every single table has a wonderful view. the table setup is immaculate and it was so easy to find the entrance. my parents and i had a wonderful time!

the food and drinks were both wonderful! the chicken sliders were actually one of the best i’ve ever had. the sauce was spicy and the chicken was  not skimpy. it was crispy and juicy and just big enough for the buns. it was accompanied with a nice tangy pickle and a crunchy lettuce.
my favorite drink was the pear drink! it was lovely! it tasted like fruit and cinnamon and probably one of the best mixed drinks i’ve had.

the hostess and the guy running the coat closet were SO nice. the bathroom attendant was a little scary tho

Made a stop to the Skylark Rooftop Bar on a Friday evening and this was a great start the NYC weekend. The food was great. Buffalo chicken sliders and fries were a nice filler. The spicy ketchup was plus too. Of course the views of midtown Manhattan from  here are worth the visit. Good cocktails and deejays. I love the vibe of this location. I know some were disappointed with service, but we we were treated great and had no reservation. We actually was told we could have a high top table for a short while due to a later reservation for others, however, we were later told to stay as long as we want and we did! You gotta vibe at this spot when in Midtown. Note that this location is  only Monday thru Friday unless you have it reserved for the weekend.

I was genuinely excited when we arrived. The long, dimly lit hallway leading to the elevator created this mysterious, almost theatrical build-up. Unfortunately, that excitement vanished the moment we were seated at what was basically an end table jammed beside the service entrance. Every time a server pushed through the curtains no more than three inches behind my chair I felt a full gust of air. It didn’t even feel like a space meant to hold a dining table.

I went back to the host stand and politely asked if we could be moved. They told me the only other options were high-top tables and that the couch-style seating was reserved for larger parties. That made sense to me at the time—there were only two of us, and we were more than happy to take a high-top just to get out of the service doorway.

But then we sat there and watched multiple couples—just two people each—being seated on the couch-style section we were told was strictly for larger groups. Meanwhile, we waited another 30–35 minutes with no update and no attempt to move us. Nothing.

At that point, we asked for the check and left.

The only bright spot was Helen—she was fantastic, warm, and truly the highlight of an otherwise disappointing experience.

Very great service. The staff was very kind and polite and fast with getting the drinks out. They gave us 2 drinks on the house before closing our tab too, which was a pleasant surprise. They seated us right in front of the Empire State Building which was very nice too.

Stunning views, but frustrating service

The views from The Skylark rooftop are absolutely breathtaking, offering sweeping panoramas of Midtown Manhattan — easily the highlight of the experience.

Unfortunately, the service was very disappointing. Despite having a reservation for a birthday party and specifying the importance of rooftop outside seating, we were initially told that no outdoor reservations were available and were offered lounge seating instead. After much discussion, we were finally seated outside — only to notice reserved tables contradicting what staff had told us.

google_reviews.text:
Just want to say WOW, what an amazing iconic piece of history tucked away just off Times Square if you are a boxing fan this bar is a must.

We stumbled across this place on our last day in New York and wow it completely rounded the trip off for me it’s my favourite place in New York, prior to walking in despite being a massive boxing fan I had no knowledge of this bars existence or even who Jimmy was but we went in and were surrounded by legendary photographs and memorabilia and we ended up sitting down having a couple pints ($3 a pint btw on Times Square!!!!) and we looked around the bar then began to read online about Jimmy and the bar and what an amazing guy he was, RIP Jimmy Glenn I’m so glad we were blessed just to randomly walk in your bar on our absolute last stop in the last hour of being in New York it felt like fate.

We also read online that apparently property developers are fighting to have the bar evicted and I just want to say now hand on heart that this little bar has more history, character and authenticity about it than any of these fancy new sky scrapers/view points.

Whilst being in Jimmys Corner I got a real feel for New York, bar has been unchanged since 1971 and that includes the prices, I only wish I found this place sooner and I’d of spent every night in there.

The guy on the bar was friendly too he seen me taking pictures and in awe of the place and he came and gave me a Jimmys Corner sticker so thank you for that if you read this and keep up the great work.

Hopefully next time I visit New York this amazing place is still here, best of luck to everybody involved❤️.

Hands down my favorite dive bar near Times Square. I don’t know what these other people are talking about but I felt welcomed when I visited. I got my beer, and sat down at a table no problems. We stopped by Jimmy’s Corner around 9:30 PM while walking through Midtown Manhattan — and the place was already buzzing with energy. If you’re looking for a classic, no-frills New York bar experience, this is definitely the kind of spot you’ll want to check out — with a few things to keep in mind. 😉

When we arrived, the bar was pretty full, but we managed to grab two seats right at the bar, near the bartender. We ordered a round of beers, and service was quick 🍺✅

The atmosphere? Loud, lively, and a little chaotic — in a good way. People were talking, laughing, drinking, and enjoying the vibe. There was even live music, which added a fun touch and made the place feel very alive 🎶🗣️

💭 The interior definitely feels stuck in time — and that’s part of its charm, depending on your taste. The decor is old-school, the lighting is dim, and everything has that been-here-forever feel. If you’re into modern, sleek bars, this might not be your scene. But if you’re down for a bit of gritty NYC character — this bar leans into it unapologetically.

🚻 Small note: There’s only one restroom stall for everyone. It’s tiny, and for such a packed place, it felt like not nearly enough. But hey — it’s a small, narrow bar, and space is clearly limited.

In short:
✨ A great place for a quick drink and soaking up some vintage New York bar vibes
⚠️ Don’t expect anything fancy — this place is all about the feel, not the finishes
💡 Probably not ideal if you’re looking for a quiet conversation — this one’s all about noise, nostalgia, and night-out energy

⭐️ Overall, I’d give it a solid 3.5 out of 5.
It delivers on the atmosphere it promises — just know what you’re walking into.

👉 RECOMMEND 🍻 (Personally mine)

name: Room 207
document: Room 207. cuisine: Cocktail Bars Speakeasies Venues & Event Spaces. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
If you’re looking to escape the city's noise, Room 207 is a masterclass in the speakeasy aesthetic. This cozy bar feels like a well-kept secret, blending the intimate energy of a jazz music bar with a sophisticated craft cocktail program. Between the dim lighting and the soulful live music, it’s easily the most atmospheric cocktail bar in the East Village.

The menu is a thoughtful curation of forgotten cocktails and vintage cocktails, proving that classic cocktails, when executed with this much precision, are truly timeless.

The Drinks
We spent the evening exploring two standouts that perfectly showcased the bar’s range:

- El Diablo: My choice was a refreshing, bubbly delight. The Los Siete Misterios Doba Yej provided a smoky foundation, while the crème de cassis and ginger beer added a bright, acidic zing with a subtle, creeping spice.

- Bijou: My partner opted for this herbal masterpiece. It was beautifully "botanicalized" with Tanqueray gin, Cocchi vermouth, and Green Chartreuse. The orange bitters made it incredibly aromatized and complex—a must for fans of spirit-forward drinks.

The Vibe
There is something genuinely magical about listening to jazz in such a compact, intentional space. Room 207 isn't just a place for a drink; it’s a sanctuary for anyone who appreciates high-quality spirits and the timeless allure of a hidden East Village gem.

Honestly?? one of the best bars I’ve ever been to (budget-wise) I didn’t expect much since it seemed to be a newly opened place but mann did it exceed my expectation. Love the expresso martini and the high ball. Im not sure if it was just my imagination but the bees knees with Brooklyn honey had a slightly fishy taste on the first sip, which I didn’t enjoy as much but overall, it was ABSOLUTELY a nice experience. The employees were super friendly and attentive. Here are the drinks menu in case anyone wants to check it out before coming here since I didn’t find myself beforehand. Definitely coming back here!

My friends and I didn’t have a plan for Christmas, but we saw they were still taking reservations and decided to check it out with no expectations. The food was honestly amazing, and the service was top-notch. All the servers were super friendly and made sure we had everything we needed. We ended up staying until closing because we lost track of time having such a good time. Highly recommend the highball, espresso martini, and the humble potato (not in pictures) ! Definitely coming back again as this could easily become our new favorite spot, and we might even turn into regulars.

An excellent addition to East Village, with reimagined classics. I loved the Bee’s Knees made with local honey, Old Fashioned & Flip cocktail. So delightful on the palate! The interior is crimson and sultry - you can easily get lost in the moment & forget about time here. We sure did. 🫶🏼

Fantastic new spot on East Village! Fantastic cocktails and the food was excellent. I tried the shishito peppers which had a soy glaze but the humble potato is something I’ll come back for over and over. My favorite cocktail was the bees knees (made with local NY honey for the win). Next time I’ll try the Enigma menu and live music on the weekends! Perfect classy vibe, can’t wait to come again!

The food was delicious and the drinks were extra yummy too. We tried the mai tai and it had a good punch. Unfortunately, I did not get even a little bit of a buzz from it. at $15 for the Matai I expected a little bit more. The flavor was good. Our waitress was very nice and very accommodating for some of the à la carte items that we requested. The menu has a great variety of stuff to choose from but you will not find it other location. The music was a little bit loud, but we were still able to hear each other. There is very low light, so come prepared with your cell phone lights if you’re challenged with reading in low light. All in all it was a lot of fun.

My new favorite (practically only) tiki bar in Sacramento. They have a number of themed menus and events (Sippin' Santa & various holiday and Disney things) through the year. Food is better than usual for a bar, and drinks are excellent.

For the second year in a row we enjoyed Jungle Bird's Holiday Pop-Up. Decorations abound and the drinks have holiday names and flavors. I absolutely loved the Holiday on Ice drink, while my partner savored a Wreck the Halls. The environment is vibrant and full of holiday cheer. Check it out before it goes away -- and if you miss it, put a reminder for next year.

Had a great time for our daughter's birthday.  The food was fantastic. I definitely loved the drinks. Tge place has a totally cute ambiance. And my only complaint was that the souvenir cups were very confusing...
We have been before and it was great! This time, we went for the Haunted Mansion pop-up. The food was delicious, the drinks were as well, and the service was even better!

name: The Upside
document: The Upside. cuisine: Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Great location with many options. My husband and brother got burgers from Ghostburger. The Best menu item was the handmade pupusas from Lili's. I has the chicken and pork pupusas. I know this was for Hispanic Heritage but I wish it could be an all-year item. Also if it does become all-year...could you add the cheese and loroco!

Met a friend for dinner here and there are a lot of options. There is Mexican, pizza, burgers, Asian/noodles, a full-service coffee place, bar, and a sandwich/salad place. The nice thing is that all of the options are contained in the same QR code menu, so you can order whatever you want and it's delivered to your table. The service was very fast. We got tacos and a quesadilla and everything felt very fresh. So I do think it's a great option because everybody can get exactly what they want. My only criticism is that the furniture in the dining area feels cheap and the first table we sat at was wobbly. Overall though it's a great experience and reasonably priced for what you get.

Lily was very helpful and thoughtful. She always approached us with a smile and asked us if she could assist us (plate clearing, asked about if we enjoyed the food, etc).  She’s an asset to your staff!

Loved the Filipino Hawaiian place. Absolutely delicious.  We know that genre of food and can vouch for the flavors- will recommend !

Ordered a martini. And the tip was included on the bill. I was alone. Not a group people. They didn't even say "hi or how are you" to me and a guy was giving me side eye, then asking for tip?! So ew. I really like to come here, but I won't be here again! So disappointed. BE AWARE: THEY'RE ADDING THE TIP !

An excellent spot with a wide variety of high-quality food that rivals higher-end restaurants. The service was incredibly friendly, which made the experience even better. It was the perfect choice for our group after a long day visiting the Smithsonian museums, especially since everyone wanted something different. The prices were reasonable, and we really enjoyed the outdoor seating. Highly recommend.

document: TALEA - Bryant Park. cuisine: Beer Bar Coffee & Tea Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The bartenders were very welcoming and nice! The drinks were a nice treat after work, especially when you’re unwinding with your friends and coworkers. I would say after 6 PM, the vibes do pick up but so do the music so if you want a nice quiet place for the evening, this might not be the place. The pretzels were AMAZING, the snack ones and the soft pretzel.
Very fun flight! Recommend tasting more than one beer here— unique flights that actually work and solid west coast IPAs with an east coast flare.

Fantastic brewery just steps from Bryant Park. The food was delicious and thoughtfully paired with the drinks. The atmosphere was lively yet relaxed—perfect for unwinding without missing the city’s energy.

Checked out this location with coworkers for a drink after work since it’s close to the office. This location is on the smaller side compared to the other locations in the city. We were able to grab a table at 5pm for 6 people. The staffs could be a little bit more friendly and smile more. One of the older female staff rudely said to us that the path had to be clear of any chairs and all we were trying to do was exactly that; she could’ve asked nicely instead. Some of us ordered the beer flights and some the individual glasses (they do have cocktails if beer isn’t your thing). We also shared the Bavarian pretzel and added the beer cheese (which is not worth the additional $4 btw).

ABSOLUTELY. LOVE. THIS. PLACE. It’s such a vibe and the beers are on point! We got the Al Dente Italian Pils & got a pickle back shot too! Bill is a great bartender who’s been in the scene for a minute! Definitely check this place out and get you some great beer. You can buy beer to go too!

name: Bathtub Gin
document: Bathtub Gin. cuisine: Speakeasies Cocktail Bars New American. located in Manhattan. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: A true speakeasy experience. We just went for a after-dinner drink but would love to go back for the entertainment. The vibe is retro and the service attentive. It wasn't very crowded when we arrived but I could imagine the small space might get overwhelmed later in the evening. Drinks were tasty, especially the BTG espresso martini.

Popped in for a drink as the name caught my eye. Ambiance wise its a tight spot that gets loud so if you're looking for something more relaxing, or intimate I would not recommend this spot. Their drinks are okay, but they do have a nice selection of gin, however I would of hoped to have more of a variety in their cocktail menu that extended well into their very diverse gin menu. They do have a mandatory coat check, which I think its a good call considering it gets crowded. Overall the decor was nice, but unfortunately was not a huge fan of the spot as it felt it was more emphasized in the decor rather than the cocktail experience as a whole.

1920s inspired anything is my kind of place so this speakeasy hit the spot for me! I went with a group of coworkers. The food is small bites and all very good. The specialty cocktails were tasty and the staff friendly. The ambience is great and you should definitely stay to watch the burlesque show!
Very cool spot, and the drinks were great. Smaller venue that fills up pretty quickly, so reservations are recommended.

Stop.  Put this spot on your list as a must-visit.  This is one of my favorite bars in Manhattan.  The drinks are on point, the staff is exceptional at everything and the vibe is super chill.  The bouncer got us in quickly, we got our drinks in short order and when a table opened up, one of the servers actually came over to us to get us seated (even though we weren't technically waiting for a table!!!).  There was a DJ there when we visited, who was excellent.  It was busy but never got overcrowded.  The cocktails were delicious.  Can't wait to go back.

document: Raines Law Room at The William. cuisine: Lounges Cocktail Bars Venues & Event Spaces. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Food 4.75/5
Service 5/5
Ambiance 4.75/5

Raines Law Room is an intimate, dimly lit speakeasy known for its crafted cocktails and luxurious Victorian era vibe.

I came here recently to celebrate my friend’s intimate wedding with about 40 guests, and honestly, this might’ve been some of the best wedding food I’ve ever had. From cocktail hour to the main course, everything was a hit.

Cocktail Hour:
Caviar toasts – 5/5: Fan favorite for sure!! The butter on the toast paired perfectly with the caviar.

Potato balls – 4.25/5: More classic, but still really good and comforting.

Fries – 5/5: Possibly some of the best fries I’ve ever had — we ordered so many more.

Beef sliders – 4.5/5: Perfect brioche-to-beef ratio, and the beef was super juicy.

Truffle pastry (not sure of the name) – 5/5: Rich truffle + buttery pastry = an unreal combo.

Main:

tuna tataki – 4.75/5: tasted fresh, and was abs delish

Steak with fries – 5/5: Cooked to a perfect medium rare, it was tender, juicy, and simply delish.

And ofc, the cocktails here are top tier using top shelf liquor which you can tell!

Big wow for this place with amazing drinks !
And super nice atmosphere, I really love this place.
Rest room was clean and very good smell 😁,  I love the wallpapers actually.

Staff were so nice and friendly service.
We ordered Old fashion/ No man’s Land / Pandora’s Journey/ Archer’s Draw / Verde Breeze … There were super good . We loved its all. And will come back for sure !

Orlando was AMAZING! so attentive & loved that we got to have a good chat. Full of great recommendations. Treated my daughter & I so well for her birthday trip. would recommend anyone to come here & ask for him! amazing!

My fiancé (now husband) and I recently got married at Raines Law Room at the William. We cannot stress enough how incredible the team was in making our day extra special and one to remember (extra shoutouts to Lauren & Alex!). The full venue team helped us with every detail in making our day one to remember — from having our ceremony in the library room, hosting our tasting, to creating custom cocktails to highlight the importance of many special cities in our lives. We will 1000% visit again in the future to re-celebrate our special day and thank the team for all of their efforts in making our day so special. If you are seeking to have a small intimate wedding, definitely consider Raines Law Room at the William in your planning! Thank you all again so much again for everything!

I celebrated my 30th Birthday on 081525 with a Black tie theme dinner party. Lauren Davis was very hands on and very helpful in catering what my party needed. She was very accommodating with my ideas and my vision, and made everything possible. The food was beyond what we expected, it was amazing! The open bar was one of the highlights of my party, the barista did a great job for the unending drinks that we requested. All of the staff that were assigned to my party were all nice and did an excellent service. Ive heard from my guests that they were very nice and kind with all their requests. For the price, I think I did get what I paid for (they are very flexible and generous with discounts, feel free to ask Lauren, she is very easy to speak with) Overall it was a great 10/10 experience!

name: Barcelona Bar
document: Barcelona Bar. cuisine: Dive Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Super friendly staff and great service.
The wagyu was tasty, though a little salty for my preference.
The seafood rice was amazing, easily my favorite dish.
Really enjoyed the overall vibe of the restaurant.
It does get pretty lively inside, so you might need to speak up a bit.

Always a vibe.  Service was impeccable and food was perfect.  Originally my party of 2 sat at a 4-top.  About 10 mins in, the manager asked if he could move us to a 2-top to accommodate a larger party.  I don't hesitate as the 2-top was in an area with less foot traffic.  The manager comped a charcuterie board appetizer and a round of drinks for the inconvenience despite me insisting it was better for us.  Incredibly gracious and I appreciated the gesture.  Munched on the charcuterie board, then followed with patatas bravas, broccolini, and gambas before olive oil cake for dessert.  Do NOT sleep on the olive oil cake.

Great vibe, great tapas and a wide selection of drinks, what more can you ask for. Had a wide range of tapas, but the best items were the albondigas, croquetas, and the patatas. They were the meatballs, fried ball of jamon and manchego (the best item on the menu) and the potatoes which were topped in a delicious sauce. Honestly happy hour is the best time to go before it gets quite loud and the deals they have are excellent. You can order 3 items for 14.5 dollars and we found it worth while as well as some cheap martinis to sip on. We also tried the salmon crudo which was a bit too salty for me. The shrimp and empanadas are also excellent, the shrimp are soaked in a delicious garlic sauce while the empanadas are perfectly cooked with a delicious inner filling. I’ve been here prior and the food was delicious and nothing had changed since then. Highly recommend you get reservations if you’re going late at night.

Barcelona Wine Bar is one of the best DC happy hour spots if you’re craving tapas and great cocktails.

I visited for their afternoon happy hour (which is rare to find in DC), and it genuinely felt like a mini trip to Spain. I ordered the mini espresso martini with Irish cream and a chamomile cosmo both were well-balanced, smooth, and not overly sweet.

The tapas-style bites are perfect for sharing, making this a great option for date night, girls’ night, or a casual group dinner. The atmosphere has that warm, cozy European vibe while still feeling lively and social.

If you’re looking for a DC happy hour with strong cocktails, small plates, and a great ambiance, Barcelona Wine Bar is definitely worth adding to your list. I’ll absolutely be back to try more.

My husband and I had our Valentine’s Day celebration at Barcelona and it was an exceptional experience. We knew it would be chaotic that evening, and we braved the crowd of walk-ins at the host stand, but we were seated within two minutes of our reservation time, which was a first good sign. Our table was in the middle of the dining room, usually not an ideal place for us, but our servers Will and Maria were immediately and consistently warm, friendly, and attentive all throughout the evening, and we felt like we had an ideal table in the end. The food was delicious (tapas and paella), our wine fabulous. Regional Manager Ian stopped by to chat, and seemed genuinely interested in us, which impressed us. In all, thank you for making this couple of old gay guys feel welcome and special.

document: Bedford Falls. cuisine: Bars New American Beer Gardens. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: First time visit for my husband and I; it won't be our last! 🙂 We shared loaded fries and they were scrumptious. The gravy made them extra tasty.  Our waiter, Louie, was extremely helpful by suggesting some of the more popular dishes.  He was very attentive and did a wonderful job packing our to go items. Loved this local experience and would recommend it highly.

My wife and I had a late flight to Charleston and by the time we made it out of the airport, it was tough to find a place with an open kitchen. We lucked into this one, and it instantly became our favorite restaurant in town.

My wife had a cheesesteak that was her favorite ever. I had fish and chips. The fish was delicious and cooked just right, and the fries were perfect.

We will absolutely eat here every time we’re in town. Highly recommend!

My in-laws frequent this spot since they live near (and my daughter has gone with then multiple times), but my husband and I finally met up with them for a brunch. There’s a wide variety of options on the brunch menu (as well as the regular menu), so there’s something for everyone. My daughter has had their chicken and waffles multiple times, but she enjoyed the huevos rancheros. The rest of us had the Bedford Burger, the Cheesesteak, and the Florentine Omelette. Usually my daughter has the doughnuts, but she said she didn’t have enough room this time. Our server was also fantastic! Very friendly and attentive. Highly recommend!

We cannot stay away from this place! When we moved downtown we decided to wander the city and eat brunch somewhere new every Saturday. Then we ate at Bedford and find it hard to try a new place over the incredible experience that we know we will have there. The food is top notch, the play list and environment spot on, and the service is incredible. They remember you and it feels a little like sitting in your favorite aunt's kitchen (if she was super creative in her menu planning and totally obsessed with your taste buds). The pricing doesn't make sense to me, the experience is elevated. I have been resistant to talk about how great they are because I want them to continue to be accessible. It is a hidden gem. Great food, people, prices and ambience. In two words, elevated quaint.
It's patio season in Charleston! I enjoyed a delicious and filling brunch on the welcoming patio. Friendly and attentive service. The inside looks like a busy sports pub.

name: Bar Snack
document: Bar Snack. cuisine: Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I stumbled into Bar Snack on a weekday afternoon with no reservation, just 3 friends and no agenda. What we found was a casual bar that punches above its weight: elevated cocktails in an approachable East Village setting that’s equal parts neighborhood hangout and destination spot.

Bar Snack has already earned serious accolades, from landing spots on lists of the city’s best bars to being celebrated as one of New York’s top drinking destinations.  ￼The interior leans into a retro, wood-lined warmth, giving the space a relaxed, lived-in feeling that invites conversation and lingering.

We opted for three different cocktails, and while none completely blew our minds, each was well-composed and enjoyable. All 3 drinks were creative twists on classics that show the thoughtful hand behind the bar. This is the kind of place where drinks are meant to be savored, not rushed.

We also shared the snack bag, a casual mix of chicken tenders, fries, peppers, and an egg. It hit the mark as satisfying bar fare, though a touch more seasoning would elevate it further. The accompanying dipping sauce helped pull the components together, and overall it paired nicely with the cocktails.

Service on a midweek afternoon was excellent: attentive and friendly without ever feeling rushed. The atmosphere was easygoing and convivial, the kind of place where strangers chat over drinks and everyone feels at home.

google_reviews.text:
UPDATE: So I went ahead and ordered from Fabrique on Fat Tuesday/Mardi Gras even though I was disappointed with the one I had initially, and as you can see on the second image on this review it's a lot better! Bun is fluffy, cream is great, color is spot on. It could have a bit more almond creme, but it's still enough to be nice. Thanks for the delivery to the Instagram office!

Cosy cafe, but as a Swede with high standards, their Semla does not cut it.

At an initial look, the size is great. Not too much, but still substantial, and the whipped cream looks smooth. However, it's.. grey?! Not sure if they just forgot to add egg when baking the buns, but looks a bit sad.

When starting to eat, there are three things to observe: 1) the whipped cream is smooth, well done on that part. 2) the bun is not fluffy, actually closer to dry, making the whole Semla quite boring. 3) waaaay to little almond creme. A boring bun can be saved by a lot of almond creme, however there is a minimal amount in this one. Even if the bun was perfect I'd be disappointed.

Overall this is a 2 or 3 on a scale of 5. The only reason it could be a 3 is because there are very few places that offer Semla in NYC. That said, if you're one of the few Swedish bakeries in town, you have a responsibility to represent the country in a better way than this. Especially when you charge an outrageous $9.5 for it.

Back to the drawing board Fabrique, this is not good.

Otherwise the cafe is cosy and the people working there seem friendly.

I visited Fabrique Bakery in New York, and it completely exceeded my expectations.

I stumbled upon it while walking toward the Arte Museum, and it turned out to be one of those unexpected gems you feel lucky to discover. As soon as you step inside, you’re greeted with the warm aroma of fresh bread, and the atmosphere is beautifully cozy and stylish.

The quality of the pastries and bread is outstanding — the texture, the aroma, everything feels like an authentic European bakery experience. Honestly, it’s been a while since I’ve had bread this good in New York.

I went in without any expectations but walked out genuinely impressed.
If you’re anywhere near the Arte Museum, this spot is absolutely worth stopping by.

I ordered the cardamom bun. It had a lovely texture, but the cardamom flavor was pretty subtle.

Warning: the seating is limited and it definitely gets crowded. Sometimes you can squeeze in on the bench, but you won’t have a table.

I couldn’t believe my eyes nor contain my excitement when I learned the renowned Swedish bakery had a shop stateside. Americans seem to be afraid of cardamom and never use enough to actually taste the spice. These cardamom buns are to die for. I ordered a couple to take home to Virginia because it’s so hard to find such good buns anywhere else. They have more than just cardamom buns; their bread is also great artisanal quality as well. If you’re looking for Scandinavian quality baked goods (they’re better than the French and the Germans) then this is your spot! I was even able to practice Swedish with the workers behind the counter which added to the experience. It made me miss Stockholm. A must stop every time I am in Chelsea.

Came here specifically because of the cardammon bun rave reviews, but what passes as such on my visit was underwhelming and over rated.
My biggest disappointment was that the cardammon was sprinkled on top, rather than being incorporated in the dough pre baking. That is how one gets the full flavor and range of this wonderful spice. Cracked over a finished baked good is the easy way out and doesn’t do the spice any justice.
On top of it the dough is chewy, slightly undercooked and pale looking.
Late was ok and served in a nice stoneware cup.
Tables are tiny, and there is a cramped feeling if the place is full. I was flanked by a rack of trays on my left.

Clean, pretty, prepared foods heaven. I miss places like dean and deluca on prince street , so this betterfield market is one of the next best things.

Honestly no notes on this soft serve froyo. It’s great. The texture is perfect. The peanut butter flavor in the PB frozen yogurt was great.
