My one complaint is that the line moves SLOW. Like it doesn’t take long for them to make the froyo, but their points system at check out is the bottleneck. It just takes so long to put in an email & phone number.

They have all sorts of other desserts, meals, prepped food that looks super good. Good selection of gluten free and vegan options.

On this episode of finding the best grocery store rotisserie chicken, we have Butterfield Market in the Upper East Side. It’s the land of Alo Sweats, Aritzia Puffers, and $10 rice and peas. Their whole vibe is trying to be like the Erewhon of NY.

I must note, there is an asterisk on this review. They only had a cold rotisserie chicken that ran $20.99. When I asked the guy at the deli counter if they made any hot tissis, he said no but he could heat it up and it would still be good. As annoyed as I was at the pricepoint of $20.99, I respect the hell out of them for wanting smoke. Let the record show, Butterfield is ducking NO smoke.

One can’t help but wonder why they only sell a cold rotisserie chicken in the first place. What is the best use case for that? Kind of hurts my head…

Nonetheless, I got the heated up chicken and took it over to central park to rip the deceased bird limb from limb. Things started off well with the breast, as I felt it was going to land in the low 7 range. I was shocked how decent it was for it being heated up.

But then, the leg came a long. It was essentially inedible. Plywood dry. Sahara Desert dry. The dryness from the reheat reared its ugly head. I winced right as I bit into it, simultaneously reaching for the $5 Voss water I had just bought.

Final score was a 5.3/10. Terrible. But again, respect to Butterfield for stepping up to the plate. I also don't know if this really counts. I would absolutely come back to re-rate if they start selling a hot bird.

name: Cafe Sabarsky
document: Cafe Sabarsky. cuisine: German Austrian Coffee & Tea. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Beautiful dining room and prompt service and gorgeous plating. The waiters can’t really pronounce the names of the menu items either so English or pointing works well. I decided to add rum to the Viennese hot chocolate and it was perfect. The whipped cream was rich but not sweetened which balanced out the sweetness of the hot chocolate. It was also served at the perfect temperature. Hubby got the smoked trout crepe which was delicious. My roasted potatoes with egg, cheese, bacon, and pickles was also tasty although I did add salt and pepper. The bread and butter that came with the entrees was a nice touch. There were two types of bread. My only complain is that the butter could’ve been a bit softer for spreading purposes. We arrived right at 9:00 (opening time) and there were already a few people in line ahead of us.

Note: The Cafe is in a museum. Your bags will be searched upon entry and they also dump out any water bottles you may have. There is a water filling station in the basement near the restrooms that can be visiting after your meal.

(July 5, 2025)
This restaurant was in my bucket list for about a year then as an Austrian cuisine restaurant where I wanted to try the Sacher Torte cake. The décor was posh with tall ceilings and live piano music.
The three of us tried the following:

1. Beet salad -- Cold and refreshing. The beets were sweet in a nice way.
2. Pea soup -- Warm and thick. Felt wholesome. The floating oil (unmixed with the soup) was noticeable to taste. Went well with the bread.
3. Sachet torte --- It was NOT like the original in Vienna. The icing isn't solid enough, the cake isn't chocolatey enough. It felt like "too much alcohol", my friend pointed out.

A fancy place at a very nice location that requires advance table reservations where the food is decent and somewhat overpriced.

Typically only walk in only (unless you're a member), but worth the wait! Beautiful sprawling tall ceilings and tiny marble tables. Once you are seated, service is quick and precise. Any of the open face fish sandwiches are a great choice, along with a nice slice of chocolate cake to top off the brunch. Beware, the coffee is VERY STRONG (rightly so), I had to ask for extra steamed milk.

As a Swiss person, I was so pleasently suprised by this place. You can expect veeery authentic Austrian dishes, I loved the Schnitzel, Sauerkraut and Kaiserschmarrn. Really so good, also the ambiente felt like in a Café in Vienna. Absolutely loved it!

Stumbled upon this charming austrian restaurant for breakfast on our first day in New York, completely unaware of its Michelin-star status until we arrived. From the moment we stepped inside, it was an unforgettable experience. The security protocols were impressively thorough, and the staff made us feel right at home. The interiors, with their old English charm, added a timeless elegance to the setting.

Regina, our server, was exceptional—attentive, knowledgeable, and even offered fantastic recommendations for places to visit nearby. It’s the little details that make all the difference, and this restaurant got them all right.

The portions were generous, and every dish was spot on. The Apfelstrudel dessert was the perfect finishing touch to a flawless meal.

Friendly tip: Be sure to book in advance! Walk-ins can expect at least a 30-minute wait.

If you have some extra time to spare, the art gallery upstairs is definitely worth a visit! ❤️

google_reviews.text: Cute little coffee shop, with friendly staff and delicious coffee. My favorite is their cold brew. google_reviews.text: The place is really nice inside, very aesthetic. name: Pi Bakerie
document: Pi Bakerie. cuisine: Bakeries Greek Caterers. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Pi Bakerie has really become my go to local coffee shop in SoHo. It’s one of those places that manages to feel both casual and elegant at the same time. The space is bright, warm, and always smells like fresh baked pastries right out of the oven. They serve excellent coffee perfect for starting the morning or taking a mid day break and their Greek dishes are genuinely authentic and flavorful.
I’ve tried a few of their salads and each one has its own personality, but the watermelon feta salad really stands out with its refreshing balance of sweet and savory. The orange cake is another must try moist, fragrant, and perfectly sweet without being heavy. They also offer several different types of baklava, including some modern or “downtown” variations that are a fun twist on the traditional Greek classic.
Everything I’ve ordered has always been fresh and beautifully presented. The staff here are consistently friendly, attentive, and seem to genuinely enjoy what they do, which adds to the overall atmosphere. Whether you’re stopping in for coffee, lunch, or dessert, Pi Bakerie is a gem in SoHo that never disappoints.

One of my favorite things about coming to New York is stumbling into a place completely at random, taking a chance on a dish, and getting absolutely blown away by it. Pi Bakerie was exactly that type of moment.

I ordered the pastitsio and it stopped me in my tracks.. rich, comforting, a little sweet in that warm-spiced way. After eating it, I did what I always do now and looked up the story behind the restaurant. And that was just as good as the food.

Learning about Regina, her roots, and the history behind this place made the whole experience even better. There are so many incredible stories behind small restaurants in this city, and this one was a fun one to discover.

I’m taking inspiration back to the Midwest after this meal. Amazing work all around ... the food, the vibe, the heritage behind it. 👏

Excellent cafe with a variety of home cooked style food! Tasty bakery and coffee, plus delicious baklava. Loved stuffed pepper, it’s a common dish enjoyed in Eastern Europe, so I felt happy to eat my familiar cuisine.

I would give it six stars if I could. Ate spanikopita, baklava, orange pie, lentil salad, and chickpea salad. All were exceptional. Star of the show was the lentil salad as the sherry vinegar dressing really shines thru alongside the green onions. Orange pie was a powerful experience as well. Not too sweet and perfectly moist. Will be back. Yammas.

Randomly visited this place and was pleasantly surprised! We tried their in-house desserts, and they were absolutely delicious,fresh, flavorful, and perfectly sweet. If you're in the area, I highly recommend stopping by and treating yourself. You won’t regret it!

google_reviews.text:
Qahwa Cafe, located inside a mosque in Sterling, VA, offers a warm, well-lit environment. It features tasty espresso beverages like Dulce de Leche and Matcha Latte, along with a selection of teas, baked goods, and sweets. Both the Dulce de Leche and Matcha Latte were flavorful and not diluted, demonstrating quality, and the homemade-style brownie was enjoyable without being overly sweet. However, drink preparation times were quite long, even though no other customers were waiting. Cleanliness was an issue due to food on the floor.

Additionally, there was no signage indicating the cafe's location in the area or outside the building, which appears to be a mosque from the exterior. We had to drive through the parking lot to find the entrance, and more apparent signs could help visitors locate the cafe more easily.
Very nice people. The boys working here are very polite and warm. Their chamomile tea was one of the best I got. I set outside on the deck and was able to charge my phone.
The cafe worker Reda was friendly, fast, and made my drink exactly how I wanted it. He made the whole place feel welcoming, and I’d definitely come back because of his great service.

Great atmosphere and rich drinks!! If you see the other pics of the iced drinks you know how mouth-watering they look. I was so happy with my iced Cherry Blossom Latte, which has the hint of flavor without overpowering the coffee!

For those who are non-Muslim, please don’t go here! I don’t understand why there is no disclosure that this place is open exclusively for Muslims.

It’s located inside a mosque, which I thought it was just a regular coffee shop (they should disclose this information - maybe they don’t wanna sound discriminatory). When arrived there, I was not welcomed there, and when I asked how to could get to the coffee shop (assume it might be different entrance from the Mosque) I was told by the person that literally stand in front of the door to go ask somebody else how we can get in (at this rate, obviously I was not welcome!)

Again, for those who are non Muslims, don’t come here!!!!!

name: About Coffee
document: About Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Manhattan. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Before & After Café is an absolute surprising delight nestled in the small town of Sperryville. We stopped by didn’t know what to expect and were seriously impressed. The croissant breakfast sandwich was perfectly flaky, buttery and perfectly seasoned, the quiche was hearty and came with a fresh, crisp side salad.

The espresso drinks are also beyond expectations. We ordered a latte and a hot chocolate, and both were beautifully crafted and rich in flavor—honestly better than many cafés in NYC. In a world of burnt beans and sad milk foam, this was a much-needed reset.

The café’s quirky charm adds to the experience—vintage decor, cozy seating, and lots of duck-themed personality (thanks to SperryFest).

Highly recommended for Shenandoah travelers.

Wonderful cafe located just ~30 minutes away from the entrance to Shenandoah National Park! I stopped by Before & After while driving up to Shenandoah for a weekend hiking trip. It started to rain in the late morning, so I figured I might as well take a beat to grab some food and read until it was possible to get outside again. I was super impressed by Before & After -- the space is super cozy and was filled with hikers who had my same line of thought, as well as a bunch of locals enjoying their weekends. The staff was incredibly friendly, and I loved chatting with them and browsing all the merch they had around the store, including a book about the Shenandoah Valley written by a Sperryville local (who one of the guests sitting next to me apparently knew personally!). I cozied up next to the fireplace with a latte and ginger scone, and it was a delightful way to spend the late morning. The latte was solid, and the scone was giant and super tasty. It had a great gingery kick and wasn't overly sweet at all, and it was buttery, slightly soft, and moist in the center with a nice crunchy exterior studded with ginger sugar. They also have a rotating seasonal scone, so I'm sure it'll be a hard choice between the ginger scone -- their all-time best-seller -- and whatever seasonal item they have in stock the next time I visit.

Nice little cafe right in front of the Shenandoah National Park. One thing I noticed right away was that they use Intelligentsia Coffee beans. Their Black Cat Classic is one of my favorites, and I was pleasantly surprised they were using this particular brand.

Oftentimes, local cafes tend to use their own roast or locally sourced beans, which can be hit or miss. Don't get me wrong, there are lots of great local coffee beans in Virginia, but I was so glad to see a coffee taste I can just feel safe with.

So naturally, I ordered an Iced Americano, and it was delicious.

For a quick lunch, I ordered a Sausage Quiche, and it was great. The quality of the sausage in the quiche was amazing. It didn't feel salty, and the quiche itself had a little seasoning, so it balanced out nicely. The side salad that came with the quiche had a mango white vinaigrette dressing, I believe, and it offset the heaviness of the quiche.

They have a cute little river walk right behind their storefront, so you should definitely check that out as well.
Amazing place to go grab breakfast or coffee. Scones and bakery were great. I really liked the outdoor sitting space with river. Plenty of parking. Definitely go here.

Beautiful gem of a place, the atmosphere was lovely and the coffee was perfect. The food was solid but packaged in a way that was not great to eat on the go. We got icee Honeysuckle and Black Bear Lates as well as the breakfast sandwich, breakfast burritos, and a cinnamon roll coffee cake muffin. The black bear late was a perfect raspberry mocha. It had great seating inside and riverside seating out back with a decent amount of parking.

google_reviews.text:
One of the best pourovers I've had in a cafe in a long time! Loved this cafe. The baristas are super nice and very skilled, which is hard to find in a lot of the country.

I ordered a washed anaerobic Colombian from their Competition series. Sometimes these coffees can be a bit over fermented for my taste, but this was probably the best anaerobic I've ever tried. The barista brewed in an origami dripper. Such a nice acidity and balanced flavor that was sweet and fruity tasting. My wife got a hot chocolate that she very much enjoyed as well.

Coffee Project New York is hands down one of the best coffee spots I’ve ever visited in the city! The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee filling the air. Their baristas are incredibly skilled and friendly — they truly care about every cup they serve. I tried their signature deconstructed latte, and it was an experience in itself — rich, smooth, and beautifully balanced. The minimalist decor and chill vibe make it perfect for relaxing or getting some work done. Definitely a must-visit for true coffee lovers in NYC!

Coffee Project in the East Village is a small, modern spot with a Euro-café vibe (bonus points for the no-laptop policy). Their medium-roast blend—Colombia meets Guatemala—hits a sweet spot: smooth milk-chocolate body with a caramel finish, zero bitterness, and plenty of flavor.

I ordered an almond croissant, and the staff offered to pop it in the oven. It came out crisp outside, soft and fragrant inside—no sogginess. They even let us enjoy a couple of pastries we’d picked up elsewhere at their outdoor table, all with genuine warmth.

Friendly people, thoughtful touches, and a medium roast I’d gladly order again. Perfect coffee-and-pastry stop in the neighborhood.

Phenominal coffee selection here. A decent breadth of flavors. I had an anaerobic Columbian coffee that was the perfect balance of jammy, funky ferment while being light bodied and quite sweet.

The barista was nice and helped me pick a coffee. I was inclined towards a Myanmar coffee simply because I've never tried one before, but she steered me to the Columbian one and that was a great choice.
Second time here.  Last time was 5 months ago.  Great latte with beautiful latte art.  Nice people.  Right around the corner from Standard East Village and Bowery hotels.

name: Supermoon Bakehouse
document: Supermoon Bakehouse. cuisine: Bakeries Desserts Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Their pastries are SO good omg. I’ve been back so many times, and they have seasonal items. The vibe of the place is um interesting tho o_o reminds me of a meat packing warehouse bc it looks um sterile? LOL

Come early tho, their pastries sell out, and most things won’t be available in the afternoon and later even tho they close late

- Ube eclair: 11/10, pricey but honestly similar price and quality to the ones I had in Paris. Best eclair I’ve had in nyc so far. Must get!
- Strawberry matcha croissant: 11/10, the cream is so yummy!! I’m not usually a fan of matcha flavors, but it pairs so well with the strawberry cream
- Scallion pancake danish: 10/10, surprisingly SO good. The one I got was a little on the burnt side, but the flavor and texture was amazing. Very fragrant and flakey!

Got the spicy nyc croissant (savory, not really spicey, has cream cheese inside with hints of black pepper), and scallion pancake Danish (i like this savory croissant, not spicey, has nice crunch texture, very good, would get this again)

Thai tea eclair also very good, tasty, taste just like Thai tea 😁

I was able to sit inside, limited seating.  Also it gets busy, so go early,things could sell out and they will post a sold out label in front of the items. I don't go often, but every time I come here there's always a variety of pastries to choose from sweet to savory and all good and worth trying.

TLDR: crème brûlée danish that was over baked, the crème itself didn’t have much flavor either

Pastries are hitting $10 now after tax and before tip which is getting a bit egregious. I love crème brûlée so I ordered the crème brûlée danish and it did not go well. The danish itself was seriously over baked. It was a  bit tough and one bite led to everything spilling out everywhere. The flavor of the crème was very subtle as well.

Supermoon is a fun stop for inventive pastries with a quirky display of realistic-looking sample items lined up with descriptions (though prices would’ve been helpful). We tried the Ube Éclair, which was rich and creamy inside with a crisp and flaky shell. The Mont Blanc was a refreshing coffee drink - an iced espresso topped with a citrusy orange cream that was bright and refreshing.

Came to try gelato. I got the pandan with Kay’s coconut. Even though the ice cream was perfect flavor wise and texture wise (not too melty, good mouthfeel), for the size of an $9 scoop I felt ROBBED. Additionally, they don’t do samples so you should have a lot of faith in what you’re getting. My friend got the ube ice cream sandwich which I felt was worth the $11 price tag. Atmosphere is brutalist, hostile architecture galore

name: Bluestone Lane Upper East Side Café
document: Bluestone Lane Upper East Side Café. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch. located in Manhattan. with 3.8 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This location is really nice, you’ve probably already seen it in pictures. It’s a very small coffee shop, but worth visiting because of its unique setting.

The food was good, but the smoothies were extremely cold and a bit tasteless, probably due to the frozen fruit and extra ice.

The seating isn’t ideal, with mostly high and shared tables, but I went early in the morning, so it was fine.

The space is small so be prepared but the food was amazing. I had the chicken avacado and my daughter had the banana bread with the yogurt and fruit. We sat by the door so it was cold but our server Abel helped us with a heater nearby and also provided a blanket for my daughter which was very sweet. Definitely want to come back

Stopped by Bluestone Lane mid-day on Sunday and really enjoyed the food and coffee! The space itself is striking. It’s connected to the Church of the Heavenly Rest, which makes for a beautiful setting.

It’s a small café, so there was about a 10-minute wait for a table. My friend and I sat at a communal table with three other people. I ordered the iced mocha, my friend had the blueberry matcha, and we split the avocado toast. Everything was delicious! I especially appreciated that the avocado toast was fresh, with the perfect avocado-to-bread ratio…no soggy toast here, just crisp and easy to eat.

Exactly as our food arrived, the hostess asked us to move to another table to accommodate a larger group. While the request was a bit abrupt, we didn’t mind once we settled into our new seats.

The only other downside was the menu, which was a little hard to read because of the plastic cover. Overall, a beautiful café with great food and drinks, though it might not be ideal for remote work due to the limited space.

The banana, spinach, almond butter smoothie is divine.

Staff are very kind and adding up with the location, it makes a must visit place when in the Upper East Side.

Their filtered coffee taste really nice too.
Altogether my husband and I visited the coffee shop 3x this week, after our central park morning runs. Loved it, recommend it and we’re going to miss this cozy coffee shop with delicious food.

I loved the blueberry matcha so much 😍 It was one of the best matchas I’ve ever had! Thank you for the recommendation, David! And David and Tanzim were soooo friendly — my friend and I really enjoyed our time here. Thank you for making it such a great experience!

google_reviews.text:
Charming, festive little spot! The food was delicious, bread and jam, coffee, avocado toast, and eggs Benedict, but what truly stood out was the fantastic service.
My daughter and I were warmly welcomed by the manager, Nenad, who went above and beyond to ensure we were well seated.  Our waiter, Bozidar, was attentive and friendly throughout. Great spot, atmosphere and staff! Highly recommend!

Overall great experience, the service was fenominal as well as the ambiance. The aesthetic was very well put together and felt as decadent as the pastries and cakes that they offered. Not long after we were escorted to our table our waiter came to introduce himself and very kindly asked if there were any dietary restrictions that he should be aware of. I thoroughly enjoyed my salad and salmon, but I was a little bit surprised that the bread was not warm and the artichoke salad had so much parm it almost didn't feel like a salad.
Overall positive experience, thank you!

This was an incredible spot. We dined while visiting New York from Chicago and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The food was incredible, and the overall ambiance was moody, vibey, and rich. Our waitress Lina was also amazing! She gave such good recommendations, and made us feel welcome and celebrated!

I love coming here it’s one of my favorite little spots. If you plan to eat in, I definitely recommend making a reservation. I’ve noticed a lot of people don’t, and it fills up quickly. The quality of both the food and the coffee is excellent, and the overall atmosphere makes it worth coming back. The only slightly confusing part can be figuring out where to check in, but beyond that, it’s a really great place to dine.

Amazing service and atmosphere and excellent food. The lentil salad, linguine with clam sauce as the tagliatelle bolognese were all excellent. Great local feel to the place, and the servers make you feel like you’re part of the family. The pasta dishes took forever to be served, but they made up for it with a free dessert cookie.

Perfect coffee shop. I was here waiting after dropping off my son at a birthday party.  Found this place and just totally enjoyed it. The chai was awesome and the bagel with smoked salmon was just right.  Relaxed here for three hours and I highly recommend to anyone.

My husband and I were in from out of town and came across this place while looking for coffee. I am so glad we found this place. We were in VA for 5 days and had coffee and breakfast from there. I tried a new one each day and loved all of them (Peanut Butter Mocha, Iced white chocolate raspberry mocha, Iced chai, and the Mounds mocha). The food is really what made this place sparkle though. I got the sausage breakfast burrito which was cheesy, flavorful, and HUGE. I also got the NYC lox bagel, veggie egg and cheese English muffin, and a pumpkin danish; all of which were phenomenal. document: Charlotte Cafe. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch Sandwiches. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This is the first place we stopped when arriving in town and it was amazing. The restaurant has a beautiful country farmhouse atmosphere. The staff was polite and attended to our table readily but without that hovering feeling. The food was extraordinary.   The pot roast melt was mouth watering. So many flavors perfectly blended. The owner even took time to recommend some local site to check out in town.  Do not miss this stop if you are in Berkley Springs. And don't forget the fresh baked goods!

We walked into Charlotte's Cafe and received a friendly greeting. It's a very casual, unassuming, and small restaurant.

The pastries were fine, not amazing, so I had low expectations for our meals, but the food was surprisingly delicious!

The menu is somewhat limited, but what they make they make very well.

It was also beyond plentiful for the prices being charged.

Our server was very friendly and quick, which we greatly appreciated.

I would certainly return (though I'd skip the pastries).

Food was so good that if it was socially acceptable, I would’ve licked the plates clean. It was also so good that I couldn’t wait to take a picture before diving in. Also get two donuts instead of one, especially if it’s a strawberry cheesecake stuffed donuts :)

Food is plentiful and tasty. Highly recommend bowls & banana bread! and if you can get there when Charlotte makes donuts - they are fabulous! Had the studded coconut donut with meringue topping when there and it was fantastic!

We stopped in for a Saturday morning breakfast around 930, had to wait just a minute or two for a table to clear, I think we had just missed the morning rush. Definitely get some pastries, the peach cobbler coffee cake stole the show, the cinnamon roll was also delicious. I had the special which was a Korean Bbq eggs benedict. I don't really know how to say this, in that it was a very tasty dish, but not something I'd rush back for. My wife got one of the breakfast bowls which was a big portion and very good. My daughter had chicken strips and onion rings, which looked average to me. The wait staff was friendly and really hustle. They also have some fun breakfast (or lunch) cocktails. The apple cider margarita was tasty. This has a very homey/family run feel and feels genuine, and they're doing good food. We'd definitely stop in again.

I hope this place flourishes for years to come! If you are looking for a boba place, go to Cana! You’ll love it!

name: Setsugekka East Village
document: Setsugekka East Village. cuisine: Tea Rooms. located in Manhattan. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Visited this place to try the traditional matcha that is prepared by hand. It’s a very small place, the dining area is mostly tatami with tea wares, and there is just a big enough for a few customers to stand. You may sit on the tatami, but if you will place your feet on it, I would recommend you to remove your shoes. The shop itself is in a place where if you blink you’ll miss it. Their operating hours are limited, and I was unsure as to whether I’d be able to see the server prepare the matcha by hand before going, as nobody answered the phone when I called to ask. However, I was pleased when I arrived and ordered the traditional hot matcha. When I visited, I was offered a choice of two different types of ceremonial matcha: Jobetsugi (refreshing flavor and light-bodied), or Unjonotomo (thick with deep umami flavor). I went with Unjonotomo for an umami flavor. Surely enough, the server prepared the tea by hand. The taste of the matcha was absolutely satisfying. This place definitely offers a traditional matcha experience. I believe they offer special ceremonies and events, but you will have to check their website for the schedule and to make a reservation.

Very calm, quiet and intimate environment. Really good quality matcha. The woman working there was very nice and knowledgeable about each item. Will be visiting every time I’m in NY. Highly recommend if you’re heavily into matcha

Calm spot for specialized matcha. There are only 5 seats to watch the matcha preparation, but then you have to go with the drink as a takeout item. The quality of the matcha here is quite good. The staff is extremely friendly and kind, and also very knowledgeable about the origin of the matcha they are serving. Strong recommend if you are a big matcha enthusiast.

A very methodical matcha preparation inside a quiet space taken up mostly by a tatami mat floor and some interesting art such as a mill machine. The front desk for seating and paying is much further in. It seems this store prioritizes takeout over sit in. You can watch the staff member take pride in preparing your drink methodically and delicately. Overall a soothing relaxing place place to be in to wait for your order.

Hidden gem in NYC

When you walk in, you are transported to a tea house on the other side of the world. The calm, quiet atmosphere accented by traditional Japanese flute music provides a beautiful respite from chaotic Manhattan. There is a variety of seating, including an intimate table where the owner expertly explains the different matcha grades and takes you through a traditional preparation (ceremony).

I can’t praise the owner, Souheki, enough — kind, knowledgeable, and so humble. She told me of her farms visits in Japan, pointing to photographs she took that hung in the shop. She was warm, welcoming, and happy to answer all my questions.

For the people here complaining about the price — you missed the point. This isn’t the fad matcha drink from Starbucks. You are getting such a richer, deeper experience. You’re getting hundreds of years of knowledge and culture. You’re getting the highest grade organic matcha hand served to you by the only certified tea shop in New York City.  Have some respect.

Setsugekka also offers contemporary matcha delicacies including an iced strawberry matcha and a matcha affogato. This place is a must-go.

document: Copper Leaf Bakery. cuisine: Bakeries Coffee & Tea Wine Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
This new bakery is such a gem! As someone who regularly visits cafés, this will become my new go-to.

Food: The heirloom avocado toast is definitely worth the money. They were generous with the avocado and it was bursting with flavor. It had a hint of umami, sweet, sour, and spicy. It was a unique take on avocado toast but I really loved it; it was delicious and surprisingly filling. The copperleaf egg sandwich is a simple, delicious sandwich. The daily granola yogurt was really good. It had so many fresh toppings and the yogurt was thick and flavorful. The coffees were also great. Very strong and rich coffee.

Service & Atmosphere: The servers were very friendly and professional. The café was also very clean, I loved the clean decor. I'd definitely come back for the food and to work/read.

So happy that this place opened on my block! Great cafe. Breads and pastries baked fresh. I enjoyed the butternut squash soup, which came with some baguette slices. The atmosphere is laid back but refined. Easy to come with kids or with friends. Baguette was perfect (although a bit pricey). I will be back!

This was a delicious adventure! This cafe is a great new addition to Harlem. The staff were friendly and knowledgeable, the atmosphere was perfect, and most of all the food was impeccable! document: The Uncommons. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Tabletop Games Beer Bar. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: 15 dollars an hour for a table. Unless you’re not playing board games. Very cozy atmosphere and perfect if you and your friends love board games. Not a huge selection of drinks but enough. They host a lot of events and the people there for the events get priority when it comes to tables. My friends and I got lucky and it wasn’t too busy when we were there so we got to sit for however long we wanted.

I really liked it! My friends and I go crazy for board games, this was a really nice place for 10 dollars per person for 3 hours. The workers are very very nice, they were clear, helpful and immediately explained the rules and everything. They were active and the games were very organized. You also have a lot of option to even buy the games. There were 1 floor to ceiling wall of playable games and 3 walls and displays of buyable games. Not kid friendly though, a lot of adults males playing role play boardgames (the ones that are long, takes 1-3 hours to play and require a lot of experience). Loved the experience I will be returning ❤️ The bad reviews about the broken AC did not occur for us, the rooms were nicely aired and it was completely normal. I recommend going around 11-12, after it might get busy.
They easily host the best One Piece nights in the city. The vibes are high and Cooper is a great host who is always looking out for the players. "City on a Hill" for what the LGS should be

This place is a true NY gem! I had previously visited but completely forgot to share my experience. As I was passing by through the neighborhood and had some time to spare I went in and Cooper took care of me. He had helped me pick this awesome game for a Friendsgiving and this time I had to thank him for guiding me with that choice. This place has any board game you could think of and the atmosphere is very friendly and welcoming. Please visit and bring friends to share yummy snacks and possibly challenge those friendships 😅

Not wanting to travel all the way to Brooklyn, you would not believe my shock when I discovered a board game café in Midtown Manhattan! After paying, you and your friends can eat (cost separate) and play for up to 3 hours! They have tons of classics such as CATAN, Sorry, Candy Land, and Taboo. However, they also have unique and uncommon games such as Haiclue, Daybreak, and Telestrations.

My advice: definitely come early! Tables and seats are limited to a first-come-first-serve basis. You should also plan ahead of what you want to do. Some of these games take an hour or two, while others are fast a couple of minutes. Nonetheless, have fun and check out their shop section where you can buy some of the games too.

name: Grandma's Home
document: Grandma's Home. cuisine: Chinese Cocktail Bars. located in Manhattan. with 4.2 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: This place is both good and bad. Starting with the good: the atmosphere is perfect. It feels very homey, authentic, and cozy, living up to the restaurant’s name and theme perfectly. The service is also amazing, with our food coming quickly. Now to the food. The food was frankly disappointing. The flavors felt muted and muffled, with the sting of the peppercorns being just enough to make it slightly uncomfortable. The shrimp, however, was absolutely delicious, and so were the dumplings and cucumbers. Don’t get me wrong, some dishes lived up to or even surpassed my standards. However, some just weren’t that excellent, like the pepper chicken and vegetable fried rice. I would love if the chefs would be bolder and more willing to take risks and play with flavors rather than keep them muted. And I’m not saying this place is bad—it just wasn’t exactly for me. If you enjoy mild, safe Chinese cuisine with a homey accent, this place is for you. But if you are a bold individual who enjoys strong and punchy flavors, maybe search for another Chinese place.

The food and drinks were amazing. Our server was also so friendly and nice and on top of everything. Food is a bit pricey and portions are a little small especially if you go with a bigger group. Must orders are definitely the lotus root with sticky rice, the hong shao rou, and the crispy eggplant. The juju bao fish was good especially with the garlic however, for the price you pay, there wasn’t enough fish to enjoy

very solid chinese food. the soup dumplings were fine. the mapo tofu was a bit different than the ones i’m used to. but the real star was the crispy eggplant dish. crispy with a sweet glaze, but hot and soft inside. very addictive.

Grandma’s Home in Chelsea has truly become our neighborhood staple — we’ve been here 20–30 times since it opened, and it never disappoints. It is the most authentic Shanghai/Hangzhou style Chinese restaurant in Manhattan. We usually order 3–4 dishes and everything comes out within 10-20 minutes.

This most recent visit was a little different — the dishes came one at a time about 20 minutes apart. However, the managers Laura and Kailee(?)  handled it with such professionalism and warmth. They immediately addressed the issue, took great care of us, and made sure we left happy.

We’ll absolutely continue coming back — the food and hospitality keep us loyal. Highly recommend the crispy skin chicken and the crispy eggplants — must-order dishes every time.

Upon arrival you’re introduced to Grandma’s Home with it’s beautiful and immersive decor honoring Chinese culture. The tableware is intentional as well, where the chopstick rests are carved to represent the 12 different animals from the Chinese zodiac.

Their food is homey yet unique, all the classic dishes you would want with a modern twist. If you like century egg, I recommend that for appetizer. The sauce has a tanginess to it that contrasts the creaminess of the egg. My favorite was their seafood fried rice, each grain cooked to golden perfection. It’s hard to find good fried rice in nyc but they do it brilliantly. The black pepper, pork belly, and salted yolk were good as well. You can’t go wrong with any of the dishes to be honest. Lastly, we finish off our meal with coconut pudding with red bean paste and guava and coconut shaved ice. However, I do believe their dessert changes every so often.

The servers could be slightly faster and more attentive but they make it up with the atmosphere and food.

document: New Chinatown  Asian Cuisine/ Bar. cuisine: Asian Fusion Thai Chinese. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Childhood staple for me! They have a great dim sum but don't sleep on lunch and dinner too. Fresh lobster, dungeness crab, soft shell crab, roast duck...etc.
-IG/TT:  SpicyAivy

My family and I have been eating here for over 20 years, ever since this restaurant was still in Eden Center! Our favorite Chinese restaurant always. The service is kind, we love seeing our favorite waitresses and we come so often they remember our family and our favorite orders. The scallop dumplings, barbecue pork rice crepes, and steamed tripe are our dim sum favorites. We love both the dry beef chow fun and beef chow fun with gravy, they're our family's staple, no other Chinese restaurant makes it the way we like it except Vinh Kee- perfect rice noodles, good quality beef and vegetables never overcooked, you can taste the char of the wok, and the sauce is not too salty. The Kung Pao chicken is also the best we've had across all Chinese restaurants, the flavor is perfect, perfectly tender, charred, and well spiced. The steamed house chicken is always tender and delicious. The roast pig crispy pork belly is so succulent and not too greasy. The seafood casserole is always well made and comforting. My personal favorite, the steak with black pepper sauce, is so tender and flavorful and comes out sizzling. We will always come here, we have so many memories- mothers day, fathers day, birthdays, new year, graduation, or just craving Chinese food...so much nostalgia with this restaurant since I was little, and it will always be my favorite Chinese comfort food spot. I'm so sad to see the mixed reviews. I've been to some of the "best" Chinese restaurants all over the country and other countries, and nothing replaces Vinh Kee in my heart!! I pray this restaurant always stays open because I want to eat here for years to come and bring my own family here one day!!

My wife and I visiting relatives in DC area, found this restaurant for lunch. Very unique to this family from Florida! Because the menu was so much fun, we ordered way too much food. They had giant oysters, biggest I have ever seen. I tried steamed chicken feet and steamed beef tendon, really great flavors and texture. We ordered some shrimp and vegetables wrapped in rice paste, also steamed, never seen anything like it and very good. We had selections of steamed pork buns, cuttlefish with pickled vegetables, it goes on and on. The servers were super nice and helpful. The restaurant is very basic, but busy even at lunch. A super experience.

Their food is really hit or miss. I was impressed with their stir fry dishes like their chow fun and gai lan - both had excellent wok hay and was cooked to perfection and served hot. However, their dim sum dishes were quite disappointing - they claimed that their egg tarts were “baked fresh from the oven” but when I bit into it, the custard was stone cold and the pastry itself was very doughy. A lot of the other typical dim sum pastries were also doughy and were not fresh.

Service was quite slow and they weren’t super busy when we went in on a Sunday. We were there for almost 1.5 hours and had to constantly ask the waiter when our food was coming out. They also had a miscommunication where they forgot to bring out something and we had to remind the staff that we ordered it and then they brought out the wrong item.

Overall pretty mid experience, would order some of the specific dishes again but most of them were unfortunately a miss for me.

I ordered takeout from this place and was shocked by the quality. The chicken was severely undercooked — the bones were still red with visible blood. It’s clear that no one even bothered to check before packing it up and sending it out.

This is a serious food safety violation. Eating raw chicken can cause dangerous foodborne illnesses. Very careless and unacceptable.

document: Peng's Noodle Folk. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Ramen. located in Manhattan. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: This place was okay. There is a cute interior and fine service but the food was just alright. I got chicken katsu ramen which was a lot better reheated than it was at the actual restaurant. The vegetable dumplings were pretty good though. We were a party of two with no reservations on a Sunday evening and we were seated immediately. Perfect for groups of 2-4. The atmosphere is very quiet, you can hear everyone’s conversations.

Absolutely scrumptious, we were trying to find some yummy noodle soups in a clammy rainy day. This was the perfect stop. The add-ons for the ramen increase the price quite a bit so be careful there. Otherwise loved the service, ambiance, food was delicious. Price was reasonable.

Outstanding tonkotsu chashu pork ramen and pork dumplings. The handmade noodles are perfectly chewy, and the broth is very flavorful. Cozy, cute ambiance. They have a drink deal Mon - Fri for 16oz Sapporo beer for ~$8. Would definitely recommend!

I am currently visiting New York City for a few days, and with so many incredible food options in this city, it can be honestly overwhelming trying to decide where to eat. However, I can confidently say that stumbling into Peng’s Noodle Folk on the Upper East Side was one of the best decisions I’ve made on this entire trip. It was exactly the kind of meal I was looking for—comforting, authentic, and incredibly delicious.

The moment I walked in, I fell in love with the atmosphere. It feels like a true hidden gem away from the chaotic tourist traps. The space is cozy, warm, and inviting, with a really cool aesthetic that makes you feel instantly relaxed after a long day of walking around the city. The staff was also wonderful—super friendly and attentive to us visitors.

Now, onto the food, because it was spectacular. We started with the Steamed Chicken Dumplings, and they were hands down some of the best dumplings I have ever had. The wrappers were perfectly thin and delicate (clearly handmade), and the chicken filling was so savory and juicy. They were served steaming hot, and the dipping sauce they came with was the perfect tangy complement. I highly recommend starting with these.

For my main course, I ordered the Fried Chicken Ramen (Chicken Katsu Ramen), and it completely blew me away. I wasn't sure what to expect with fried chicken in soup, but it works perfectly. The chicken cutlet was massive—breaded to perfection with a serious crunch that held up beautifully against the rich broth. The broth itself was creamy, flavorful, and soul-warming, and the noodles had that perfect springy chewiness.

Peng’s Noodle Folk is the kind of place I wish I had back home. If you are visiting NYC and find yourself near the Upper East Side, do not skip this place. It was a 10/10 experience and I will definitely be coming back the next time I am in town!

So about the food I got the crispy fried vegetable balls as an appetizer and Loved it… didn’t even really need the dipping sauce tbh. The chili oil is good. If you like spicy food or Dan Dan Noodles you’ll love the Tan Tan Men Noodles here I like spicy food so I got medium level. Before I was half way down I was SWEATING!!!🥵 But I enjoyed it 🥴🤷🏽‍♂️. I got a small hot sake for $9 and it was totally worth it, that vessel in the pic held enough Sake for me to fill my glass almost 3times 🕺🏾. Last but not least about the pricing… I got everything you see in the pictures for $40.58 that’s amazing to me for the UES… I left full and tipsy 🥴. Will definitely visit at least 2 a month. 🙌🏽

document: San Wei. cuisine: Bubble Tea Chinese Pop-Up Restaurants. located in Manhattan. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
San Wei has an excellent team—the staff were friendly and welcoming, and they offered generous samples so I could try most of the menu. Ivan took great care with my order, offering helpful suggestions that really paid off. The food is outstanding. You can tell everything is slow-cooked with care.
The pastrami, which they make fresh every two hours, was incredibly tender and full of flavor—just like the beef stew. They also serve a variety of sandwiches, rice bowls, and several types of noodles, all of which were delicious.
San Wei is a fantastic addition to the mall—definitely worth a visit!
I ordered the beef noodle soup and the short ribs rice, and both were absolutely delicious! The meat was incredibly tender, and everything was well-seasoned. Definitely worth trying 💯

A good dining experience that could’ve been great.

I learned about San Wei and their pastrami while reading an article while walking around the mall. The employee behind the counter greeted me and explained the difference between the two pastrami bowl offerings. I ordered a pastrami bowl, which comes with white rice, a ramen egg, and your choice of broccoli or bok choy. I asked for the more flavorful option and he gave me broccoli. I also ordered a fruit tea.

My meal came to $20. The rice was a bit sticky which wasn’t surprising because it had likely been sitting for a while on this quiet Monday afternoon. I enjoyed the pastrami and went back to order another bowl to take home. That’s when I noticed Combo B, which is basically what I ordered, plus spring rolls and soup, for about $5 less than what I paid. Yep, my fault for not reading, but it would’ve been nice for the employee to make me aware of the combo option. I approached the same employee (who was in the process of putting out fresh white rice) and asked why I wasn’t charged for a combo. He said that I didn’t ask for it. Fair enough, but I decided that I didn’t want to spend more money than I had already spent/wasted.

I would return, but I would definitely make sure I’m getting the most bang for my buck.

San Wei is a nice addition to the Queens Center Mall food scene if you’re craving casual Chinese food. I stopped by recently and had a pretty decent overall experience. The menu offers a good variety of Chinese staples, and the pricing is fair for the portion sizes and mall location.

We tried a few different items to get a feel for the place. The dumplings were one of the highlights fresh, flavorful, and nicely cooked. I also ordered a single dish set, which came with a generous portion of rice and a main dish. I chose the San Wei rice and Bang Bang shrimp. The rice was tasty, warm, and comforting, but the shrimp unfortunately fell a little flat in flavour, it looked promising but lacked the punch I was hoping for.

We also ordered the pork belly baos. The pork belly itself was actually quite good well-seasoned with a nice balance of fat and lean meat. However, the bao bun was on the dry side and started to fall apart when we picked it up, which took away from the overall experience of that dish.

What stood out aside from the food was the staff. The employees were friendly, attentive, and helpful in explaining menu options. Service was fast and smooth, even with a steady flow of customers.

While a few items could use some improvement, San Wei offers a satisfying, quick, and convenient Chinese meal for anyone spending time at the mall. It’s a solid spot if you’re in the area and want something more flavorful than your usual food court fare. I’d definitely consider coming back to try more from the menu.

Was intrigued by this new addition to the mall so we had to try it.

The cashier, who was also the lady that cut our pastrami was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. We had a bunch of questions and she was able to answer all of them well.

I ordered a three protein combination bowl with San Wei rice, pastrami, short ribs and sweet & sour pork belly. This was a great value for the price. I really enjoyed the pork belly. It was tasty and tender and really flavorful. The pastrami was good, but odd combo as an Asian style bowl. Our least favorite was the short ribs. It was like a beef stew style protein with carrots and potatoes. The San Wei rice was definitely a better choice than plain white rice.

The second item I ordered was beef soup with hand pulled noodle. This was disappointing. The pro: I really liked the hand pulled noodles-- it was bouncy and chewy. The big con: the soup wasn't really a soup instead it was a whole wad of oil and cilantro. It was really oily and not enjoyable. It also didn't come with the a choy like it said.

name: Twilight Lounge
document: Twilight Lounge. cuisine: Chinese Venues & Event Spaces Asian Fusion. located in Manhattan. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Twilight Lounge is a fantastic find near NYU in the East Village, offering both great atmosphere and seriously good food. We ordered the BoomBoom Crunch Ribs (Lingnan pork ribs), which were incredibly juicy with a tea-marinated flavor and an addictive crispy rice crust. The Laifeng Pickled Cabbage Fish was perfectly balanced—tender fish fillets in a comforting, tangy broth with tofu and napa cabbage—while the Pickled Chili Beef delivered just the right level of heat and freshness. We also loved the wok-charred green beans and the fried eggplant in garlic sauce, both full of wok flavor. The Twilight Special Fried Rice with shrimp, sausage, egg, and XO sauce was the perfect way to end the meal. Stylish lounge vibes, generous portions, and consistently delicious dishes make this a spot I’d happily return to and recommend.

Overall, the dining experience was quite pleasant. We arrived close to closing time, yet the staff were still warm and welcoming, showing no signs of impatience—something that truly deserves recognition. From ordering to food service, the process was smooth and efficient, with dishes arriving promptly, which is a definite plus for diners who are short on time.

As for the food, portion sizes were on the smaller side, so those with a bigger appetite may want to order a few extra dishes. The flavors were generally solid and reliable—nothing particularly outstanding, but also nothing disappointing. The Suancai Fish was well-executed, with a good balance of sourness and saltiness, making it a safe and steady choice. The standout dish, however, was the Salted Egg Yolk Tofu, which was excellent and easily the highlight of the meal.
Overall, strong service and efficiency are the key strengths here. If you’re looking for a place for a quick and hassle-free meal, this restaurant is certainly worth considering.

Lunch special $12-14 for entree + spring rolls and garlicky cucumber salad is great as of November 2025. One heads up, make sure to indicate what spice level you want or they’ll default to mild. I was eating the chicken and said “It’s good but mild” only to see mild on the receipt. The portions are nice for sharing. I liked the purple rice option. I might suggest a reservation.

I was looking for a Chinese restaurant around the West Village, and this place popped up on Google Maps. The menu looked interesting, so I decided to give it a try.

I went around 1:30 PM, and it was quite busy - probably because there was only one server handling the whole place. It felt a bit hectic when many customers arrived at the same time, but everything was still managed well.

After being seated, the server explained the lunch specials and the regular menu. I ordered two lunch specials, which both came with crispy spring rolls and a cucumber salad, Kung Pao Chicken and Crispy Garlic Fish, both served with jasmine rice. I also ordered an extra dish that wasn’t part of the lunch special, Lava Salted Egg Tofu, because it sounded delicious.

Kung Pao Chicken – I ordered medium spicy, but it wasn’t as spicy as I expected. That said, the flavor was good, and you can ask for chili oil on the side if you want more heat.
Crispy Garlic Fish – Fried fish fillet with garlic sauce (not spicy). The fish was crispy, and the fried garlic added great flavor. The garlic was a bit salty on its own, but adding the plum sauce and chili oil on top made it amazing.
Lava Salted Egg Tofu – Fried tofu tossed with salted egg sauce. The salted egg flavor was there but I was hoping for a bit more sauce to coat the tofu. It was slightly dry. Still the taste was good overall.

The price was reasonable, and the portions were generous enough to share. If you like spicier food, I recommend ordering spicy or asking for extra chili oil.

Lastly, the server was incredibly kind and hardworking, managing a full house all by herself. I really appreciated her effort and service.

This place was unexpectedly so good! We tried so many dishes, and everything was full of flavor. My favorite was the Duck Fried Rice — rich and perfectly cooked — and the Spicy Fried Fish was another must-try. Highly recommend this spot if you’re looking for great Thai food with a cozy vibe!

While my husband thought the food was just ok, I’m bumping my rating from 4 to 5 stars because of the customer service.

I recently tried the buffet at Hunan Village and unfortunately had a disappointing experience.

For $15.99, they offer a wide variety of Asian and Indian dishes that look very appealing. On my first round, I had fried rice, black pepper chicken, and the Mongolian beef. The fried rice was adequately warm, but both meat dishes were only lukewarm.
On my second round, I tried the chicken biryani and a curry chicken from the Indian section. Both dishes were cold.

I informed the sole employee working the main floor that the food was cold. He adjusted a knob on the warming cart and mentioned he had just turned it on, advising me to give it 5–10 minutes for the food to heat up. A few minutes later, I went back for a third round: fried rice, orange chicken, Mongolian beef, and black pepper chicken. The rice was warmer and the orange chicken was hot, but the black pepper chicken and Mongolian beef still weren’t hot enough to my liking.

Another surprise was that they did not offer white steamed rice with the Asian dishes, which I’ve never seen at a buffet before.

Service was also lacking. Employees walking from the kitchen to the floor did not engage with me aside from occasional eye contact. The employee I spoke to about the food being cold did not interact with me beyond turning the knob and later processing my payment.

Overall, while the selection is broad and visually appealing, the lack of consistently hot, fresh food and minimal customer engagement was disappointing. Based on this visit, I would not recommend it.

As a constructive suggestion to the owner: small changes could significantly improve the atmosphere. A simple greeting when guests enter, one proactive check-in during the meal (“How is everything?”), and a brief, courteous interaction at checkout can transform an environment that feels indifferent into one that feels welcoming. Hospitality doesn’t require over-the-top enthusiasm—just acknowledgment, attentiveness, and basic warmth. Those small efforts would go a long way.

I’m not happy with my first experience here. I decided to try this place based on the good reviews (which I normally rely on) and ordered veggie lo mein to go. I was expecting the standard lo mein noodles, but instead I received thin noodles, which was disappointing and not what I anticipated.
On top of that, I visited during lunch hours and clearly told the cashier that I wanted a regular order, not the lunch size. There seemed to be some confusion, as I was charged $10.55 (the regular price) and then later asked to add more money due to the misunderstanding on her end. Overall, the experience was confusing and disappointing. I wouldn’t be visiting again.

After watching a generational stage talent hone her craft (cough cough Sarah Snook in The Portrait of Dorian Gray cough cough), a nip was in order, and I had zero interest in lingering anywhere near the Broadway/Times Square area. My top-tier chum who literally went to the school of hospitality and I initially Ubered over to nearby Orient Express (one of my faves), but it was too crowded so after walking past a few other packed establishments, we saw this - a subtle basement-level bar with a small handful of customers. My kind of jam. It also feels like being in a basement, in the best possible way. There's a lot of wood paneling that felt like the merging of my grandparents' finished basement from back in the day, but with a lot of modernist touches. And of course, oodles of art featuring ducks, the go-to decoy for waterfowl hunting. Very into it. It's dark so if you're looking for gorgeous lighting, I'd keep walking, but I think you sort of know not to expect that going in when it comes to basement bars.

The cocktail situation here was excellent and very innovative. As with the bar food, there was a distinct Asian influence, which isn't something I encounter regularly so it was a pleasant change of pace (though my favorite wine, gewurztraminer, has those vibes by virtue of its lychee notes). We tried a few items on this menu, but the best was probably Golden Yuen, which my chum LOVED, and she's pretty picky especially when it comes to tequila-based beverages. It had a sweet yuzu foam on top, and the ginger paired really well with the tarter fruits in it - you had a long of strong flavors that were kept in check, which was impressive. Really strong item. I also opted for a Nectar of Wukong, which was as close as I could find to a bourbon-based drink (it was scotch). Decent with a solid presentation value; per the accompanying pic, it had a bubble on top that was reminiscent of the toadstools from Mario. Little too sweet for my palate though.

The food rivaled the drinks, which is saying something. I wasn't insanely hungry but had bypassed dinner so the compromise there seemed to be some dumpling action - I'm always down for a dumpfest. We ordered multiple dumplings, including the Five Flavor Chicken (the bartender's recommend), the Pan Fried Lamb, the Shrimp/Snow Peas, and the Oxtail. We diverged considerably on our opinions here, but the Chicken probably WAS the best, though it was very peanut buttery - not something I'm always in the mood for. That's not to say I had a negative opinion of the other dumplings, but they were all pretty much on the same playing field for me, tasty and flavorful, but not quite to the level of the Chicken.

Honestly, the only negative, and it's definitely a "your mileage may vary" situation, is that it's pretty pricey. The cocktails were all hovering in the $20 range, and the dumplings were close to $25, despite only having four each in an order. We ended up spending over $200 here, which is fine and something we're both willing to do on a city excursion like this, but it's arguably not worth the price given the portion sizes. I thought the price point for the cocktails was the more reasonable of the two, when you considered how high quality they were and that you're in the West Village - this stuff is just going to cost a few more dollars than it would in the suburbs.

Really solid recommend overall. The service was excellent, and we both really appreciated that the staff let us linger and didn't try to push us out despite our being the only customers there for a significant stretch (I think they were still technically open the entire time, but the foot traffic was going into the nearby Alehouse - hard pass for me). And who doesn't like sipping on a cocktail whilst gazing at a duck portrait?

Warning: check your receipt very carefully before paying.

This restaurant automatically adds a mandatory 20% tip to the bill and includes it in the total. After that, the payment screen still asks for an additional tip, which can easily cause customers to tip twice without realizing it.

The situation is made worse by the extremely dim lighting — we were practically eating in the dark — making it very difficult to clearly read the receipt before paying.

This practice feels misleading and deceptive. Customers deserve transparency, not pressure or confusion at checkout.

For clarity, I have already uploaded the receipt with my review, and it clearly shows the issue.

As shown on the bill:
•	Subtotal: $64.00
•	A mandatory 20% tip ($12.80) was added before calculating the total
•	Tax: $5.68
•	Total charged: $82.48

However, after this total, the payment screen then prompted for an additional tip with suggested percentages (2%, 3%, 5%, 7%), which are calculated on top of a bill that already includes a mandatory tip.

This creates a very real risk of customers tipping twice, especially given the extremely dim lighting in the restaurant, which made it difficult to carefully review the receipt before paying.

Regardless of intent, this setup is objectively misleading:
•	A mandatory gratuity is already included in the total
•	Yet the system still prompts for extra tipping without a clear warning
•	The lighting conditions further prevent transparency at checkout

Customers deserve clear, unambiguous billing practices — not confusion or pressure at the point of payment.

I appreciate you investigating this matter and hope appropriate steps will be taken to ensure this does not happen to other customers.

document: Baby Blues Luncheonette. cuisine: Greek. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
Cute spot with comforting food.
This restaurant is styled as a traditional luncheonette with a counter and table seating. The atmosphere is definitely a highlight but the space is small and I can imagine it fills up VERY quickly on weekends. On this visit we enjoyed the banana date shake, an iced coffee, the Sparta plate, the Zorba plate, the blueberry and cream pancakes and the baklava banana waffles.

The banana date shake is rich and creamy with a perfect, deep sweetness from the dates and a comforting scent from the banana. The shake should be served with a larger/boba straw as it is impossible to drink through the one provided. There were some larger date chunks at the bottom that should have been blended a bit more.

The iced coffee was notable as it was nicely sweet even without sugar. I really enjoyed my coffee.

The Sparta plate is served with savory eggplant patties that provide a texture reminiscent of sausage patties. The eggs served at this restaurant are visible good quality with golden orange yolks and rich velvety textures. There is also a red pepper sauce which works well with everything on the plate. The plate is flavorful but I would probably choose a different option next time. The serving is too light and I am not vegetarian so there isn’t a reason for me to get it again.

The zorba plate is much heavier and just as delicious. A plate with halloumi is always appreciated and this dish delivers on all fronts of flavor.

The baklava banana waffle is great but the description is a bit off. I wouldn’t say it’s heavily baklava, more candied pecans/walnuts. Delicious but it would be complete with a honey forward butter syrup. The flavor profile just needed some completion.

The blueberry and cream pancakes are fluffy and tender. The blueberries are excellent quality and the cream cuts through the heavy textures to balance the dish. Really delicious and classic.

The price point here is JUST a little bit high. I had two full plates of food and had room to spare when I left. For two people it was over $100 which is just a lot for breakfast food and nothing here is hefty.

thoroughly enjoyed everything about this diner. from the space to the service everything was flawless and as an aficionado of diners i love how they’re doing some traditional style greek food without frills or breaking the bank. everything was perfect literally. frothy coffee i asked not too sweet was dope, the breakfast plates filled me up, and the baklava flared pancakes just topped it off. can’t wait to come back

The food was fantastic and you could tell they used good quality ingredients. The Zorba platter was filling, fresh, and hit the spot. The blueberry baby cakes were amazing.

There was a funny picture frame in the bathroom titled Baby of the year with a Google review of someone who said the food was great, but the service was bad. Just found that funny; nothing else to say.

Stopped by on a random weekday and waited for about 15 minutes. The restaurant has cute retro diner vibes, it's a small space, and our server was friendly. There are a lot of healthy options to choose from. We ordered the Zorba Plate, Like a Greek Bagel, Lamb Burger, Blueberry Baby Cakes, and a frappe.

Zorba Plate - Loved the variety, but the potatoes took up the majority of the plate. Still, everything was really good and well-seasoned. I just wish it came with more pieces of halloumi.

Like a Greek Bagel - Came with a long piece of crispy sourdough instead of an actual bagel. It was creamy and zesty, served with a side of smoked salmon.

Blueberry Baby Cakes - Fluffy and amazing; no syrup needed. So good!

Will be back if I venture out to Williamsburg again.

Retro diner with decent food. The blueberry baby cakes were a standout -- so perfectly fluffy that I didn't even realize I forgot the maple syrup halfway through! The lamb smash burger was stellar. It came with a side of potatoes that were a tad on the greasy side. If you got the 1 in 5 chance of getting the crispy ones, they were amazing, but the 4 in 5 chance of getting an oil soaked potato was not worth it -- I would sub for a salad instead. The eggplant fritters were ... edible? Zero crisp, zero flavor. If something is on the menu and I'm waiting an hour for it, I think it should at least taste like something. I would come here again if I was in the neighborhood and there was no wait. But definitely not worth the wait.

The chicken was juicy and perfectly seasoned with a touch of sweetness and spice, the roasted cauliflower was tender with a great char, and the salchipapas were crispy and fun to share.

The atmosphere is warm and stylish, and the service was friendly and attentive. You can tell the food is made with care and quality ingredients. Definitely a place worth coming back to for both the food and the vibe!

This place is excellent!! The pan con tomate was a great starting point. Really fresh and great for a winter tomato! The roasted cauliflower was unreal!! Kale Dino was fresh, delicious, and tender. I’m not huge on pork belly but we got it per the server’s recommendation. The sauce was delicious and the pickled radish was the perfect amount of acid with the fatty pork. The Calabrian chicken though… INCREDIBLE. A bite of the crispy chicken with the Salchipapas dipped in the sauce was one of the most incredible bites I’ve had in a long time. Finished with the Gianduja fudge which was the perfect little sweet bite to end the meal with. It was so smooth and, again, just so delicious. Overall everything was just so well thought out and amazing quality. Our wines were both superb as well. We can’t wait to come back!!

name: June
document: June. cuisine: Wine Bars Tapas/Small Plates New American. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
This place is fantastic. Some of the signage feels a bit aggressive - but I get that they're trying to create a positive atmosphere and vibe (I'd just prefer less in-your-face, maybe kinda antagonistic, signage to create that atmosphere - it probably seems a bit hostile to some people, who have mentioned it in their reviews).

The music theme is fun. You can tell a lot of thought and intentionality went into making this space beautiful and enjoyable. I loved all the music that was playing. Anyone who loves music, especially older rock or blues type music, I think would like this place.

I met up with coworkers here and we had a lovely tea / breakfast before carpooling to a meeting further away. The parking lot was good for that, and we returned to the other cars later.

The tea tray was epic. See it in the pics.

This is my favorite cozy and cute local cafe with plenty of seating and lots of free parking! Whenever I go here to study or do work, I’m able to get so much done because of the quiet and productive atmosphere. The coffees, teas, food, and pastries here are a delicious study break treat too! My go-to order is an iced latte with a croffle, my order comes out perfect every time. I, also, love how the baristas at Cafe June always greet you as you enter and help you out with what to order! They are so kind and take their time to write thoughtful messages on everyone’s cups. It makes my day to read them! Cafe June is a solid 10/10 local cafe that I will always go to.

Today I had the most delicious quinoa Oat waffle.  The roobis tea was especially wonderful with the fresh honey to sweeten. The staff was so friendly and the atmosphere is great with old time music playing. I can't wait to return and try more fabulous options!

Really pretty and aesthetic cafe! Definitely come here at least once. The drinks are good and the cake is very well decorated, although it does taste like it has been out in the fridge for a while. Overall, good experience.

I used to come to this place for years. It started with good coffee, excellent acai berry, and very inviting atmosphere. Over time, the coffee became generic, food items became smaller, more expensive, and average quality, and atmosphere became intolerable. I fully support business having the rights to ask customers to leave for taking up space too much for too long, to allow other customers to use the place. But, the 90 minutes seating policy and no laptops or tablets makes this place like MVA. If this place were a diner, I would understand, but the place is a cafe. Designating the majority of space as “unplugged zones” makes no longer possible enjoying the coffee while having a thoughtful moment or two under 90 minutes.

name: Cafe Mado
document: Cafe Mado. cuisine: Diners Venues & Event Spaces Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: It’s great for shareable plate and date night, so get 4-6 dishes will be idea! We loved salad, freshly grated cheese created a umami taste and it was very refreshing! Pork was juicy and tender which we also enjoyed. Ragu was alright - way too al dente and salty in our opinion.

We LOVED our dinner experience in their cutest backyard, super peaceful and memorable! We also really enjoyed the food, the butter was out of this world, the baguette was amazing, the eggplant sesame dip was delicious, the smoked date provolone farinata was insane, the Caesar salad was perfect, the cabbage dish was soooo mouthwatering and my favourite dish of all, followed by the bean purée and the crazily yummy sourdough bread next to it as rank two! I didn’t try the rib chops but my friends were dying for it loool
The only thing I didn’t like (but the rest of tbh party did) was the trout crudo, for which I blame Theodora for shooting my expectations for crudos to the roof! Also I couldn’t get my head around the price for that little amount of harissa, which wasn’t even that special, neither were the fries (and this one, everyone else was on the same page as me)
Oh and there was this empanada shaped dumpling bread dish that we loved but don’t recall the name.
Overall, we really enjoyed our meal and we will be back :)

Delicious and refreshingly original take on lunch and brunch. Every dish is refined and inventive, blending different cuisines and flavors in a way that really works. Most of our dishes had a subtle kick.
The experience felt energizing compared to the usual predictable brunch scene.

Very interesting place with not too big, but very creative menue. You better ask the server or Google some terms that they using to describe their dishes. But don't get me wrong,  this sophistication matches the taste. Everything including bread was a top notch.  Personally my favorites were the pasta, skate wing and the pork. Unfortunately I was so full that had no space for a dessert,  but from what other people having it looked very interesting.  The place has inside seating as well as outside on the backyard.  They are quite popular so reservation is highly recommended.
Delicious food, we were 5 people and got around 10-12 dishes as our server recommended. Everything beautifully made & ever sauce that came with the dishes was 10/10

name: Dinner Party
document: Dinner Party. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Desserts. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: I've been to Dinner Party many times, and would always go back! The rotating menu makes each dinner here feel exciting and new, but also thoughtful and well executed. Food is fresh, delicious, and colorful. The ambiance is fantastic - cozy, warm, and social. I will always recommend this spot to someone visiting from out of town, or looking for a special place to celebrate a birthday. I love you Dinner Party!

My favorite dinner spot in Clinton Hill this year by far. every dish felt intentional and balanced.  nothing felt too heavy or predictable. Also, the atmosphere felt so homey. the service was warm and the pacing of the meal was perfect!!! They have a rotating menu which makes it feel special :)

I loved every minute of my meal at Dinner Party! The vibe is warm and welcoming, staff friendly, and the food was spectacular. You can tell so much thought goes into each menu they create.  Great to go with friends or family, or even to meet a fun stranger sitting across from you at the communal table. Adding this to my ‘always eat here’ list whenever I’m in NY!

Will never forget my meal at Dinner Party! This place is so special, from the incredible food (we clearly very much enjoyed our desserts) to the communal set-up and super warm & inviting team. The menu changes all the time, which is just a great excuse to come back. Would recommend to anyone looking for a chic little date night or a birthday dinner in BK!!

Dinner Party is always a fabulous time! The restaurant has a cozy atmosphere, warm hospitality, and incredibly yummy food. In the four or so times I’ve been there in the past year, I’ve always left feeling satiated and excited for the meal and experience I just had.

I last went to Dinner Party last Tuesday for their current pre-fixe menu and it was so delicious. The citrus and persimmon salad was a great way to start before diving into a perfectly fried snapper. To finish, they had this amazing sticky toffee pudding-esque dessert.

Their menu changes every two weeks and it’s always fun to see what new menu the team comes up with and try it out. Highly recommend as a date night spot or a place to catch up with friends!
