name: La Bicyclette Bakery
document: La Bicyclette Bakery. cuisine: Bakeries. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Saw a YouTube video about this place with Action Bronson and had to try. Everything was good but I expected more from the baguette. The best thing we had was the  ircular raise bread.

The crossaint was on the better side as well from other venues.

"Loved the authentic local vibe here! It doesn't feel like a tourist trap, but a true neighborhood gem. The moment you walk in, the smell of fresh bread is amazing. The baguette sandwiches are fresh, crusty, and absolutely delicious. Highly recommended if you want real artisan bread in Brooklyn!"

Been on the hunt for the best ham and cheese baguette and La Bicyclette does a solid job. The flavors of the ham and comté were a bit strong for me but the baguette was a nice contrast — light and fluffy. I do think better can be found but definitely recommend stopping by for a hearty sandwich!

This is my happy place whenever i come to NY. The vibe takes you back to Paris where great quality bread and community connections are the key focus. My go-toa are the comte jambon baguette,pain au chocolat and the financiers. Do note as this is French style the baguette is served cold and not toasted,hence it can be a bit crusty or hard for your teeth.

Stopped in as it was mentioned many times as a bakery to visit when in the area, so I did.

I arrived right before they opened so they had a full case of pastries. The space is small like most nyc businesses but the staff were friendly.

While it’s hard to follow this with somewhere like radio bakery I tried to be open minded. I was upset to see they are on the trend of a case full of laminated pastries. We get it. If you can make 4 laminated pastries we believe you can make 10.

So unfortunately it makes the selection feel small. I went with the pear almond tarte which was decent. It was probably average over all. Nothing remarkable but certainly not bad enough to say “I can’t even finish this”.

Over all I think it’s an average bakery from what I experienced and while I’d stopping if in the area I would inconvenience myself to go here.

With that said if you’re in the area drop by and pick something up

name: Yafa Cafe
document: Yafa Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Middle Eastern Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Truly a fantastic experience!
After a frosty commute, I began warming up with a hearty cup of Qishr tea. After sometime, I ordered one of the best, tasty sandwiches I’ve had since the womb, an experience I won’t ever have until the hereafter.

Everything was on point, the tasty food, the vigorous customer service, and the welcoming atmosphere. Shoutout to all staff working this Saturday shift, very good people (including the chefs, don’t ever forget them.)

More importantly props to Yusuf, he truly went above and beyond to serve me with such hospitality. The way he prepared orders and moved through the floor was beyond elegant almost as he was flowing with the air under his feet.

Loved the Baraka Milk, it just clicks and feels like home.

After attending the pop-up with Akram Cooks, we decided to come back the next morning for breakfast at Yafa Café—and I’m so glad we did! My sister is actually a regular here, but this was my first proper visit. I usually stick to the typical pancakes, but I wanted something different, and Yafa’s menu did not disappoint.

The variety was so impressive that we honestly had a hard time deciding what to order—we almost got everything! Every single dish that came out was perfect to the tee: fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. You could really taste the love and quality put into the food. I enjoyed every bite from start to finish.

The atmosphere is warm and inviting, the staff are friendly and attentive, and the overall vibe makes it the kind of place you can happily linger in. If I lived in New York, I could absolutely see myself becoming a regular here. Since I only visit once a year, I’ll be looking forward to making Yafa Café one of my must-stops every trip.

Convenient corner cafe near 45th street station.  Been going here for nearly a year now, I’ve gotten their breakfast burrito (the green wrap one) and their sunny breakfast dish. They’re all good, I especially like their matcha and coffee. They’re make the matcha by hand from their Matcha that they fetch (you can also buy the Matcha can, it’s good quality) from somewhere. It’s very authentic and I honestly love this cafe. Rush hour start (8am ish) gets very crowded so if u want coffee you should go early ☕️
Amazing customer service by the man, the myth, the legend, Sarhad Hamrukulov. The food was absolutely delicious, and lastly the atmosphere was out of this world!! 10/10 experience 👏

Absolutely love this place -- my neighborhood go-to. Always a pleasure, staff super friendly, atmosphere very welcoming, and some of the best Yemeni coffee in NYC (and that's a high bar!). I buy my beans here too, and it's definitely worth the price tag. Very proud to be a regular here!

Adding my favorites and recommendations to my review: For drinks, I'm a huge fan of the classic adeni chai. The baristas here are so talented at getting the milk steamed perfectly and the sweetness at an excellent level (compared to somewhere like Qahwah House, where the drinks are super sweet). The seasonal honey butter latte was an immediate favorite as well.
The lamb stew is phenomenal. I have celiac disease and can't confirm how good the sandwiches are, but every friend I bring here is obsessed with the chicken and lamb. I've had friends come all the way down from upper Manhattan just to get the sandwiches again. Staff are super accommodating about dietary restrictions. The fries are fantastic as well and I regularly get them as a side or on their own with a coffee.

google_reviews.text:
We had a blast at September Farm Cheeses! If you think there's only cheese, go inside and prove yourself wrong 😉

The staff there were all extremely polite, kind, helpful and pleasant. Can't say enough good things about the girl who was running the cash register for the sandwich shop today at around 12:45. I should have gotten her name so I could put a good word in with the manager, but I was flying solo today with three kids, so I didn't think of that. I'll find out who it was next time we go.

I had one of the best turkey melts I've ever had in my life today. The kids had fun meals of chicken nuggets and smiley fries with Capri Suns. After that, we had delicious, super moist chocolate chip cookies. They also have ice cream (looked homemade, but we didn't try any today – next time!!)

After lunch, the kids played at the playground on site.

Amazing food served with a smile. Their cheese curds are tops. I tried both deep fried and fresh, both were stellar.
Coffee was fresh and well brewed.

People from my work have brought in their cheesecake tarts, which are unbelievably good.  So, I decided to stop in and check the place out for myself.

We walked around the store, which is a very nice upscale kind of farm market. Your greeted right at the door by the case of cheesecake tarts. They have an ice cream area to the left and a cafe in the back.

Everything was good and I would visit again.

Wonderful place.  From the quaint country feel, to the friendly counter service girl, to the delicious quality food.  We had Suarkraut sandwiches, fried cheese, coleslaw which was my fav.  The store had plenty of wonderful food gifts I brought home to my children!!! Fun and memorable visit while here in Lancaster County!

Very beautiful place surrounded by farm land . They have all kinds of cheeses. Very good sandwiches. The crew is so professional and very courteous. They have very delicious tarts. Today was my second time here .

document: Covert Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: COVERT COFFEE was a perfect experience with a calm and upscale atmosphere. It is a wonderful spot for high quality coffee and a relaxed vibe and we highly recommend it

Love everything about this place and the staff are so helpful and friendly. Daiki-san, Kuro-san, Atsuko-san, and Gen-san have the best customer service.

Highly recommend if you’re a coffee lover

I unexpectedly discovered COVERT COFFEE. The staff carefully explained the characteristics of the coffee, asked about my preferred taste, and then helped me choose the right coffee. From the moment I ordered, it was a wonderful experience. I'm so glad I found such a great coffee shop. The staff's fluent English and handsome appearance were also a big plus.

I really enjoyed my experience at covert and the coffee was superb.
The staff were welcoming, polite and helpful and provided a fantastic overview of the coffee, how it is best enjoyed and the types of bean profiles on offer.
The coffee itself was exquisite and I loved the changing flavour profile as I progressed through the cup.
There were lots of seating options - most tables were taken up with happy patrons but it is isnt a small tuckshop space like a lot of other cafes.  We weren't pressured to leave immediately so it was a great place to stop and collect ourselves before we continued with our day.

Coffee is on the pricier side but the taste and service makes up for it. The staff will explain the variety and origin of the beans and recommends base on your taste profile. The coffee is good, fruity and no sour.  Great experience for people who can afford.

As I was buying my lunch, Jeff Buckley's "Lover, you should've come over" came on, and I nearly collapsed in heartbreak. The vibes are calm and composed. Best croissant around the area very buttery and flaky 10/10 recommended

Spiffy interior. Delicious coffee drinks with plant based milks. All of their muffins are vegan: Strawberry Ginger, Morning Glory, Blueberry. Yay! No other vegan options, alas. At least they have one option and almond milk!

Great expresso coffees, which can be difficult to find. Amazing pastries and breads that are fresh each day. The service is friendly and helpful delivered with a smile.

document: The Xperience Coffee House & Juice Bar. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Juice Bars & Smoothies. located in Brooklyn. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I ate at The Xperience Coffee House a few days ago. I got there pretty early and had to come back because they were on "holiday hours." Jo & Tash assured me they would be open and it be worth my while. I can confirm they did not disappoint 😂🔥🫡 To the walk in "He's back!" To them asking what did I wanna try, what made me come there, they were very attentive followed through and delivered! I had eggs w/ cheese, a side of turkey bacon & sausage, Hawaiian roll cinnamon French Toast,  a Waffle Lovers Board (it came with 3 types of waffles) and a Mango Lemonade drink from their  juice bar. I can't wait to go back ‼️ 10/10

The Xperience was definitely an experience!
Let’s start by complementing the venue on being a breath of fresh air & I love the open concept of this Coffee House. I was reading reviews and someone said it gives “The Den” from Moesha .. and I agree. Somewhere you can come and create as well as eat, chill and just kick it.

Ok now, the food!
I loved the creativity of the menu with the stuffed festivals. They have so many flavors 🙀(Shrimp, jerk chicken, oxtail, turkey bacon egg cheese,
curry goat, cheeseburger & more ! My favorite was the oxtail, it was just so flavorful and full of the meat no skimping 👍🏽They have a full menu of West Indian foods, pastries, protein shakes & lemonades✨

If you’re in the neighborhood, pop out on Chris!

I noticed the new building in the neighborhood, and gave it a shot. To my amazement, the staff was very courteous! Since it was my first time, Chris recommended me a strawberry cheesecake pastry and a non-alcoholic cocktail. It's was "chef's kiss" good!!! I am pleased to have a clean area with good food,service and atmosphere to chill or work, so closeby.
Thanks for the xperience😃!

Edit:

The video shows what type of amazing things you can create and name that is part of the Xperience! Can't spill the beans on my flavors!

First time I walked in I was mesmerized, it took my breath away. The atmosphere is calming and I immediately felt a sense of peace. The choice of music that was been played was so beautiful and relaxing. I was greeted with a friendly smile and welcome by the owner Chris, the staff also was extremely friendly. Junior the chef had a pleasant smile and inviting attitude and after he prepared our meal he personally walked over to our table and presented it to us. I have found a new home. Did I mention how DELICIOUS the food is, it’s bursting with FLAVOR, so far there’s nothing there I don’t like, the drinks, coffee and shakes are just awesome. !

I was told to come to this location by a friend and it did NOT disappoint. Met the owner, high energy human being, friendly staff, PLEASE get a stuffed festival. Moist, slightly sweet, and savory. They didn't have the rest of the menu available but it didn't matter. The fried chicken hit on all cylinders and the cranberry BBQ sauce was amazing. Definitely can go there and study, have a bev, relax. Black owned in the heart of the flossy. Have an Xperience!

document: Saturn Road. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Wine Bars Beer Bar. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Cute Coffee shop that also serves Cocktails.  I thought I would come in and get a regular Cocktail.  I ordered a Maple Old Fashioned, it wasn't Whiskey based.  It was made with Sake and Maya Blanco, spicy Maple Syrup and Bitters.  I was pleasantly surprised,  it was delicious.   The prices are reasonable.  It's a good place to go to study or work.  The front is narrow but there's a small backroom with couches.  The backyard is spacious.  They also have events.  It is dog friendly.  It's a good place to have in the neighborhood.

We loved the vibe of this coffee shop/bar in Cobble Hill. They have a great space inside plus a large outdoor seating area in the back of the property. We just had espresso tonics, but they were so good and the staff is really nice. Definitely a great place to eat, drink and meet up with friends.

This place is LOVELY. So cozy. Great outdoor area. Super nice people.
Lots of place to sit. But it gets crowded on the weekends (couldn’t find a spot Saturday morning).
Cool merch.
Onlyyyy downside is that the coffee takes a little while after ordering.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Saturn Road is such a gem in Cobble Hill! The owners are two incredible women from Texas who’ve made Brooklyn home, and you can really feel their warmth and hospitality in every detail of this space. They hosted our baby’s first birthday in their gorgeous backyard, and it couldn’t have been more perfect. The staff is beyond friendly and welcoming, the drinks are excellent, and the whole vibe makes you want to stay awhile. Whether you’re stopping by for coffee, wine, or just good company, Saturn Road is a neighborhood treasure.

Small bar and cafe serving up fresh and flavorful coffee.
Register located at the entrance and tap to pay is easy.
Menu is located right above the register on the wall.

Cappuccino 8/10
It has fruity sweet notes which is pleasant and it feels like a smooth light roast.

document: Head Hi. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Bookstores Art Galleries. located in Brooklyn. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: A superb addition to the neighborhood!! A wonderful multi-disciplinary space selling thoughtful art books, delicious coffee + pastries and other unique books. The pastries and coffee are top quality, and the selection of magazines, books and zines is really excellent -- from rare artist monographs to contemporary philosophy and funky artist-made zines.  A TRUE NEIGHBORHOOD GEM!

Nice and relaxing coffee shop tucked away on a busy street. The service here is great and they had a good amount of options to choose from. A little on the pricey side but worth it. The turmeric latte was delicious and would come back again for that. Stop by if you’re in the area!

great space for a slow coffee or to shop for gifts / books - not a good spot if you’re looking to get work done (no laptops or calls) but I still grabbed an iced coffee and worked across the street!

really love the space and shop, so definitely recommend coming on a weekend or if you’re catching up with someone

Great coffee (beans are from a neighbourhood roastery). Finally a NY barista who doesn't make flat whites too milky as the other cafés do.
Nice selection of pastries - like the tasty (gluten free) hazelnut cookie. And in the weekend I believe they have sandwiches too.
A peaceful cozy coffee shop. The coffee is from Parlor Roesters, just across the street.

name: 787 Coffee
document: 787 Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Empanadas Breakfast & Brunch. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Found this little shop on a whim and it did not disappoint! The vibe is instantly set with tons of fresh indoor plants and Puerto Rican flags (Hello? Bad Bunny? Wya?)
We ordered a Conquito & Horchata latte both with oat milk. 10/10.
Cool thing about this place is that they have 3 different bean choices as well that they roast themselves.
Cindy was so helpful with suggestions and handled multiple customers seamlessly and with care 🤍🖤

Would def return when I come back to NYC.

Awesome coffee find!
Double espresso was perfect! You can choose the variety of bean.
Also tried a cream cheese and honey pastry this was also great.
Great vibes, close to Penn Station, and funky interior.
Server/owner was very friendly.
Great experience, put this one on your list of most visits if you want seriously good coffee.

Best coffee option near penn station, opens early. Plus lots of outlets. They were out of tres leches so I got dulce de leche instead. It was good—but the horchata was DIVINE! Shout out Cindy for beautiful latte art & kind energy ☺️

FINALLY a good coffee!
Brenda and her team are super friendly and create such a welcoming atmosphere.
We’d been searching for a good coffee for five days, and after visiting this place, we can finally say — we found it!
Delicious coffee, cozy vibes, and the perfect spot to take a break from the busy city.
If you’re looking for a great coffee within walking distance of Madison Square Garden, this is the place to go! ☕💛

Stopped in here spontaneously and am so happy that I did. When you choose a latte, they have you choose which beans you want. I had the RumChata, which was so excellent!! I also grabbed a fresh quesito for a snack. I’ll be back!

name: Nostrand Cafe
document: Nostrand Cafe. cuisine: Korean Breakfast & Brunch Coffee Roasteries. located in Brooklyn. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Listen, I have been a regular at this cafe for years, and I spend a lot of money here and love going in. I go multiple times a week to buy lattés, and I tip well.
The way the staff navigates customers using the bathroom makes you feel totally unwelcome. Your customers are being treated like a nuisance and it is poor hospitality and it makes me not want to come back here unless something changes around this. It is the second time I had a really unpleasant experience about this issue specifically and frankly, it is humiliating, disrespectful, and degrading. Give your customers some dignity, we are your neighbors supporting your business.

I have tried a bunch of different coffee shops in the neighborhood. This one is my favorite and honestly has the best matcha i’ve had(maybe ever?) They get the color right every time!! And it’s reasonably priced(compared to others) Love it!!! :)
Walked in to this coffee spot and enjoyed an Oat Latte with Vanilla Syrup and enjoyed it.  Service was nice and quick.
Great micro-roaster/cafe with Korean food, breakfast sandwiches and friendly service. So happy I stumbled on this place! I ordered the bibimbap (hot bowl) and it was delicious! Will def be back.

Wrestled between leaving a 2 or 3 stars review. Settled on 3, because I am hopeful.
A year ago, I would have rated this place 4.5.
This used to be my go to place for coffee in the neighborhood. I would either get an amazing or mid cappuccino here. It was inconsistent but still good overall.
Lately, my cappuccinos have been rather bad to mid. Today, I literally had to throw away one after 3 sips. I have literally never had to do this before, anywhere! The coffee itself tasted burnt and the oat milk was so grainy, omg! I couldn't believe how bad it was, as I took the 3 sips.
The food quality has always been consistent though, 5/5.
Sadly, now I have to go literally anywhere else for coffee. I will try again in a few months. Just sad.

name: Anmwey Eatery
document: Anmwey Eatery. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Haitian Soup. located in Brooklyn. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: We had such a lovely time at Otway! The food was incredibly delicious, but what really made the evening special was Miranda..She took care of us, she was warm, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. Her recommendations were spot-on, and thanks to her we got to try some amazing dishes. The chef was also super friendly, creating such a welcoming atmosphere. We’ll definitely be coming back!
I can’t wait to go back for dinner. Very cute small space for brunch! We got the salad and 2 sandwiches. Staff was very friendly and everything tasted great.

Stumbled in and had the best experience. My server Karissa recommended the egg sandwich with lamb and I couldn’t be happier. Tasted great and the service was excellent. Lovely atmosphere will definitely be coming back. Thanks again Karissa!

First; the bread is next level. 6 stars for the bread. And overall this is a good restaurant that’s mostly hits but has a few details I would change. This was almost a 4 for me, but I’m swaying in the 4.5-4.6 direction so full 5 star credit is granted.

The drinks are quite good and the Tepeche is  something I haven’t seen before! It’s a mild pineapple kombucha; super tasty. The margarita was also top notch, not overly sweet. These are from a well considered bar.

The bread is life changing. The butter is perfect. Why have dinner after? Just get a loaf. In all seriousness it was a generous portion of amazing sourdough and it changed my life and became my friend for just a moment.

The melon is far too simple of a dish and needs to be portioned differently and come with some other flavors in tow. It’s just a slice of cantaloupe and salt; so this was a let down after the divine bread. We found the burger and desert to be spectacular (that’s strawberries and cream), although the cream leans into feeling a bit oily and the dish could have been slightly colder.

The steak was another slight miss. It was good but for the price point ($40+), I need to see something really amazing to not feel out of sync here. Meat was slightly dry, could have been more tender. Nothing much to say about its flavor and it wanted to be part of the sauce but was plated oddly and separately… sort of inviting you not to mix them. The accompaniments were ok, a little too much salt forward-ness in the mushroom marmalade. But it was tasty overall: would rather have had 2 burgers. Fries were on point and well cooked. A lot of unique savory notes in the burger that put it a cut above competitors.

I know it feels like I’m roasting this place, but I’ve been to restaurants at every price so I have hundreds of points of context for this review. It’s a top 50 in Brooklyn, brunch is awesome here apparently, but it’s not in my top 10-20, roughly.

Anyway; that’s the review. Thanks for reading! Enjoy!

I thought the food was great. The presentation was really good. The burger was juicy, the Paris sauce with the gnocchi was fresh and tasty. The chocolate mousse was lighter than I hoped, but still good. Overall very enjoyable, and I'd like to try more things. Nice airy space.

name: The Showroom Bakehouse
document: The Showroom Bakehouse. cuisine: Bakeries. located in Brooklyn. with 3.6 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
The Showroom Bakehouse was such a treat to visit. The cookies are similar to the famous Levain cookies, but noticeably lighter in density. I was able to almost finish an entire cookie in one sitting—which is impossible for me with a Levain cookie!

I enjoyed my first cookie with a warm cup of ginger tea, and the second (a chocolate chip) paired perfectly with a scoop of vanilla ice cream absolutely delicious.

The shop itself is super cute, with plenty of options to choose from, including cronuts, macarons, and a wide variety of hot beverages. This is the perfect time of year to stop by. The packaging was also adorable.

I was in a rush and didn’t get a chance to take photos of the shop, but if you’re in the neighborhood, it’s definitely worth a visit. The staff is friendly, and the space is clean and pleasant an all-around enjoyable experience.

Pastries and donuts buy one get one free after 5pm?! Incredible.

They have quite the assortment of desserts, but as others mentioned, only two seats inside.

Bought a raspberry doughnut and was very disappointed with the filling. I understand that companies need to make money, but, as the picture shows, when you lack to provide any raspberry filling in something as small as a doughnut, you can’t really expect me to give you five stars or give you a good review. Very disappointed in this bakery after recently just moving to the neighborhood. I hope you understand why I posted this review, but the picture speaks for itself. I will not be going back to this bakery in the near future, or in any future.

Cute small place , there are two tables inside and a few outside . The pastries were tasted good, tasted like homemade ones . Not too much sugar. The only thing it’s a bit pricey, I’ve paid $25 for  5 pastries

Cheery, bright environment. Had the friendliest staff person who seemed genuinely happy to help. Only tried a donut (5/5 taste texture and ratio) but everything else looked delicious as well. Somewhat pricey but worth it. No seating or bathroom.

name: Lincoln Station
document: Lincoln Station. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Sandwiches Beer Bar. located in Brooklyn. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
LOVE this place. Big upgrade to bare burger which had gotten old. We had the cheese burger and the Veggie sandwich and they hit the spot perfectly.
So happy they’ve opened one up in the slope!

So, out with Bareburger, and in with a new cafe that looks like a coffee shop as you peer through the windows catching a glimpse of all of the small round 2 person tables with a few supporting laptops - about 15 tables in all. Moving on, the cafe offers sandwiches, breakfast, and some other options in addition to espresso drinks - what I ordered - a cappuccino to go, which had a nice punch to it, in a good way.
It appears that this place opened recently, maybe today, so I would expect growing pains, while they feel things out.
A big plus to this location are the roll up garage doors, which are extra welcoming when they are rolled up in nice weather in addition to providing more space to sit in the event this place becomes real popular. My rating is for the coffee as I have not sampled any food yet.

I’ve had the pleasure of eating here a few times and appreciated it all. Ambiance, music level, service and of course the food. Solid pastries, quality coffee and an egg sandwich that due to the subtle, tangy sauce stands apart from the rest.

I stopped in to grab lunch on this cold and rainy Thursday. The menu offers hot and cold entrées, coffee drinks and an assortment of pastries. The meatball sandwich was a recommendation and I also ordered a ginger beer. I was looking forward to the hot Meatballs on a Ciabatta Roll. Unfortunately, I was very disappointed! The sandwich was not seasoned. The only thing I really tasted was the cheese and the drink. Here's a suggestion: salt, pepper, onion and garlic with a touch of red pepper flakes or maybe some oregano and basil. The bland combination of sauce and meat with a $5 drink, left me underwhelmed.

I cannot say enough good things about Lincoln Station, in Park Slope. The meatball sandwich is incredible. The salads are delicious. And the sides are amazing too- the broccoli in particular. The biggest gamechanger was them getting gluten free bread. It's my new go-to for lunch!

name: Before Coffee
document: Before Coffee. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Brooklyn. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
This place.. Their Egg Tart……… totally a crime. Get it. Some seats for ppl to stay a little bit with great pastries and drinks. Reasonable prices which I do appreciate.

💛✨🌟Egg tart was soooo moist! Soft filling that collapsed with flaky layers outside. (If u r Taiwanese, think about a LFC egg tart but bigger and butter.)

💚Match latte was pretty a classic but creamy.

Greattttt coffee spot! Deserving of all 4.9 stars here on Google maps. The matcha was strong and great , and well priced (less than $6 matcha latte after tax).
They have some fun seasonal drinks.
Their pastries look great. Including a lot of yummy scones and an everything croissant.
Small space to sit.
Super nice staff.

Nothing getting better with a croissant and latte to start a day. I read the reviews for this cafe and wonder if it is worth to give it a try.
I ordered a latte,  almond croissant and an egg tart to share with my friend. Oh my! The egg tart was soft and creamy not hard at all. The croissant was fluffy and with bold almond flavor. We enjoyed them till the last bite.
We decided to have a second visit a day after. I ordered the strawberry match latte this time, it was fabulous! It blended matcha’s bitterness ( not strong ) with a hint of strawberry, this combination refreshed my taste buds and made my day well. Of course, egg tart for this trip again.😊
The cafe only has 2 benches for you to wait for your order, most people come for take out.

While visiting New York stumbled upon this lovely little coffee shop on my way to the train 🍵

🍓 the strawberry matcha was divine. Imagine your favorite hq matcha meets the strawberry milk of your childhood dreams. They get happily married and make this insanely delicious treat. I wish i could teleport this back to my local coffee shop in Chicago. Definitely get this. Promise that it’s the perfect balance of sweet and earthy.

👯‍♂️👯‍♀️ during the early morning rush this place is TIGHT. Not much space to wait for your coffee but luckily enough the turnaround time was quick and the overall disposition of the coffee cravers was lovely.

🥐 i got a everything filled croissant from the case and holy moly, crispy crunchy and buttery. It was a bit messy to eat (no complaints), but was a bit too overstuffed with cream cheese (slight complaint). Only note to self, and to you reader, is to ask for it warmed- would have probably enjoyed it a bit more if so.

So glad we came here ! We saw all the reviews & wanted to try ourselves !
The strawberry matcha latte is above expectation. I usually go to KIJITORA, but guys, this one is also delicious.
The egg tart was also really really good ! We Will come back for sure ! (& we live in UES - it’s worth the trip)

It’s in a good location, in the McPherson Square metro station - right down the escalator by the entrance, or right by the exit (depending on which way you’re coming from). This store is a hidden gem but so worth it.  Owner has been there I believe he said 34 years. Stock a sweet person with good deals only souvenir place item while entries is closed.

John is such a friendly and welcoming person. We had a wonderful time shopping for souvenirs at his store. I would definitely recommend Metro Variety Souvenirs to anyone looking to buy keepsakes in Washington, D.C.

document: Daisy’s Café. cuisine: Cafes Coffee & Tea. located in Brooklyn. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Great customer service, every staff member we met was overly courteous.

Food was delicious and a great value. I really enjoyed the buns on the hot dog and the burger. Truffle fries had excellent flavor and seasoning. Chai was really well balanced. And the cappuccino was really good.

Parking can be validated by the restaurant just ask the hostess. We parked in a free lot across from the main parking lot.

Would love to come back here again to try their breakfast.

A great spot for brunch after a North bank trail hike. Me and my girlfriends were at this beautiful restaurant last month when the weather was great and was given the patio seating overlooking the James River on a beautiful day. The waitress was very sweet and friendly. Its a precise menu with a few options, but the food was delicious. I had the breakfast Sammie which I really enjoyed, especially the side of potatoes(they were addictive). My friends had the breakfast burrito with chicken which was very filling. I especially loved the hot Mocha.. that was my favorite.

We stopped in for a quick brunch, and this place was wonderful! Our drinks were lovely, and the French toast and breakfast burrito were both incredible. And the breakfast potatoes might be some of my favorite that I've ever had! Ive been to many coffeeshops and this is among the nicest and most pleasant experiences I have had yet! The coffees are exquisite, delicate and floral and pure delight. The store is bright and beautiful.
The baristas however are what sets this shop apart! AP and Miguel are the friendliest, kindest and coolest baristas ever! I enjoyed our conversation so much- just the most interesting organic awesome warm chat about New York City livin…

This cafe in Bushwick is a great place to grab some coffee with friends and chat! Super colorful inside, it's very lively and a good place to start your mornings at.

My friends and I just swung by here pretty briefly, and I tried their seasonal peppermint mocha, which was really good. While I originally got recommended this place to do work, I think with how lively it is, it is a much better spot to just hang out with friends at.

The drink was average but I liked the latte art. The place is very cute with colorful chairs and tables. But the sound of the coffee roaster is pretty loud, so I would not choose this spot for a long stay.

I had an issue before with this place but it was solved almost immediately. Now I am a forever fan of them. The sandwiches are THE BEST! Coffee is incredible! Most of the coffeeshops and brunch places in this area have to literally look up into THIS quality! Thank you from the bottom of my heart that you make my breakfasts the best! Honestly, I would give A LOT for your BLT with avocado and would eat it 3 times a day ahahaha🫶🏻🫶🏻🫶🏻🫶🏻🫶🏻

Loveless Coffee nails that sweet spot between light and medium roast with their Rosegold Espresso. The blend—Brazil Capixaba and Ethiopian Siko—tastes like raw honey up front, then drifts into cherry, nougat, and a long dark-chocolate finish. It shines in their flat white, giving just enough fruity sparkle without losing body.

I tried both a flat white and a cortado. The milk stayed cool and silky, letting the espresso do the talking. In the cortado the cherry acidity popped; in the flat white the nougat note felt richer and rounder. Each sip stayed balanced all the way down.

The shop feels welcoming and easy. Staff are quick to chat beans, and they keep things moving without rushing you out. Shelves of their 11-ounce boxes line one wall, so you can take the same coffee home for twenty-two bucks and try dialing it in yourself.

If you’re chasing a roast that lands right in the middle—bright but still sweet—Loveless is worth the stop. Flat white, cortado, or even a filter pour, that Rosegold espresso holds its own.

document: PLG Coffee House and Tavern. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch Sandwiches. located in Brooklyn. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Moved a family member into the neighborhood the day before so we popped in here on Sunday morning for some breakfast. Had bacon, egg and cheese on an onion bagel and it was delicious. Coffee was great too. We’ll definitely be back when we visit! 🥯☕️

I enjoyed my Turkey Club sandwich but GOOD GOLLY this economy is hitting me hard. The sandwich is $12.5 and I DID elect to pay an additional $3.50 for an additional egg, so should be 2 eggs total because hey momma needs that protein.

So when I got this square sandwich that cost me $21 including tax and tip I’m just like.. what in the world is going on??

I had to double check that I did in fact get the 2 eggs, it just wasn’t as fluffy as I was expecting. Server seemed super annoyed I even asked lol but hey this cost me an additional $3.5 are you sure? He didn’t like that. Oh well.

Also, 0.85 for a “delivery fee” and when I asked what that was about, he said it was actually a credit card fee.. and I’m like ok well … what. you know the feeling.

Service was good, I like the food.
Graffiti benches and overall wood/brick feel is nice. I learned PLG stands for Peace Love and Gratitude

Man, I’m super disappointed in this neighborhood coffee shop. Went there this morning and waited 25 minutes for 2 Breakfast Sandwiches and after 25 minutes of waiting, one came out wrong and had to be remade (another 10 minutes). The chef behind the counter (Glinda, I think) was on her phone the entire time I was there which is fine, but very unsanitary to be cooking and tapping on your phone at the same time. Made me lose my appetite watching her go phone talking and tapping on her phone to assembling sandwiches. Which it could have been a better experience or at least refunded for the mistake and amount of time I had to wait (~35 minutes for 2 sandwiches…)

I have been living in the area for 15 years, and I have been client of PLG Coffee House and Tavern since they opened. In past, cafe used to have beer on tap. Anyways, that was in past.
Food was always consistently great, since the day cafe was open. In my opinion, sandwiches still are one of the best in the area.
But service, only so-so. During my last two visits to establishment, in both occasions I left unhappy. Two weeks prior my last visit, we had lunch in the cafe. As I understood, counter person stepped out and kitchen crew were filling in. Because person who serviced us at the counter couldn't figure out how to apply rewards to my order. I let it slide at that time. Same person prepared our sandwiches and send it out, one by one. Why entire order was not prepared and send it out at the same time, it's mystery to me. I had coffee which I think is good, and my guest wanted to have decaf tea. Problem was that person serving us was clueless which tea in their selection (which is decent), were decaf. That we had to figure out ourselves.
On second occasion, I made take out order over the phone. I tried use their mobile app, but that thing been not functional for some time. When I got to cafe to pick up my order, food already was prepared. We got The Club sandwich, The Farm System, I also added two plain croissants( for next days breakfast) and two pieces of Lemon loaf.
This time again, person at the counter couldn't figure out how to apply rewards. After I told him that I have some rewards on my account, and I would like to redeem it, he ensured  me that it will be applied at the end when payment will be processed. It didn't happen. When I got home and checked the receipt, no redeemed awards were showing.
Why PLG Coffee House running their rewards program, if no-one trains the staff how properly apply it to costumer's orders? And like I mention before, mobile app is not functioning at all.  For some people this may be minor issue. But in my opinion: either you doing good, or don't do it at all.
Now about food. As I mention before, sandwiches are still one of my favorites in the area.  Croissants were good as well. Lemon Loaf was old and dry. Definitely not that day's baked batch. And if you charging $4.50 for relatively small piece, at least have decency to sell ONLY freshly baked. I didn't get any beverage on my last visit. But I think their coffee is good and teas are delicious. On both occasions we visit cafe around 3pm.
That said, I don't think I'm going there any time soon. Luckily, there is more cafes and sandwich shops opens in the area. I probably will explore some new ones, before I order from this business again.

Their food prep area seemed like a simple assembly station, but their eggs were freshly scrambled and quite tasty. However, they use foil to wrap so after they cut the burrito in half, bits of foil gets included in your food so had to watch out the first few bites.

Chai was from a box mix and tasted watery/weak. Also got a Cortado, which was strong! They were busy on a Saturday morning...good thing, lots of local patrons. The counter service person was fast and efficient at handling all customersand making drinks. Kudos to him!

Nice outdoor seating area. The also hosted a neighborhood fridge for food drop off to share as well. What a wonderful gesture!

My wife and I had breakfast a little after 10am on a Monday morning. Parking right next to the cafe may be limited during peak times but parking very close to the entrance was easy to find during the weekday morning.  The atmosphere is about what you'd expect from a cafe of this type and it wasn't crowded at all during the time we visited.
We ordered the Bananas Foster French Toast and the "Happy Scramble", which are pictured.  The food seemed to take longer than we expected to be served since it was not crowded at all, but it was hot and tasty and well-seasoned.  The crinkle fries were surprisingly excellent - hot and crispy.  To drink, we had a pistachio latte, which was very good and a medium to dark roast coffee.  They do have a couple different blends of coffee to suit your taste.
The service was okay.  The servers really didn't smile or interact much the customers, but seemed to be nice people.
Our food cost was about $20 per person (a little more with tax and tip) and we thought it was a bit expensive for what you got for your money.
Overall, it's a nice place to enjoy a coffee and quiet breakfast.  We'll definitely try it out for lunch soon to see how the lunch menu tastes.

Great place to work with fast WiFi. Since the moment I entered the staff was super welcoming and kind. They definitely care about the customers and the quality of what they serve. name: Nili
document: Nili. cuisine: Cafes. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: I ordered takeout from Nili by the Miss Ada Team and the food was outstanding. The falafel was one of the best I’ve ever had—flavorful, not dry, and beautifully seasoned without being heavy or greasy. Every bite had that perfect balance of texture and spice that’s hard to find elsewhere. The sides complemented the falafel perfectly and tasted incredibly fresh. The drawback was the portion size. For the price, I expected a bit more food. Still, the quality and flavor were great, and the takeout packaging kept everything warm and well-presented. Even though it’s on the pricier side for the amount you get, the taste and freshness make it worth an occasional splurge.

Unfortunately the food is inconsistent. It can be good and then all of a sudden it can be really bad. One day I got the Sabich dish with the egg undercooked and heavily burnt eggplant that made me really sick.

Had brunch with family and it was delicious!!! I love that they have both indoor outdoor dining area! And they have plenty of seatings. We did the outdoor because the weather was good.

The latte I had was good too! I enjoyed their mushroom, egg & cheese pita a lot! It’s like a sandwich!

It was like a self-serve place that you need to clean up your table after finishing your meal. There’s one thing I noticed and very appreciated was they use everything bio-degradable, such as the straws! They plate, bowl they offered were not one time use, I truly admired that and supported these contribution! Will visit again!

Amazing cafe. The food is stellar and it is located conveniently next to the train. We have lunch from this place every time we’re in Brooklyn. We order the cauliflower shawarma hummus bowl every time (vegan).  It’s a perfect lunch portion, delicious and flavorful. Comes with cauliflower, cabbage, pickles, hummus, and warm, delicious bread. It’s a 10/10. Last visit we also tried the crispy cauliflower hummus bowl. It is also delicious! The cauliflower is deep fried and is tossed in a yummy sweet glaze. It’s spectacular but because it’s a bit more indulgent we wouldn’t get for lunch every time but is a must have if you like crispy, sweet fried cauliflower. We also tried the falafel (not vegan, has feta cheese) and it was good too.

It’s pricey for a bowl (around $40 for 2 bowls) for sure but we enjoy the food every time, it’s consistent, and high quality. We will go back again and again for our usual cauliflower shawarma bowl.
Food was amazing. Their chicken shawarma on pita is so good. The lady who served my coffee was exceptionally kind and exactly who I’d like to be getting my coffee from. Shoutout to her. Great vibes

google_reviews.text: We were here for a quick weekend trip having to go the convention center all weekend. We tried here because it was close by and I’m glad we did. The burgers were delicious and so were the other food that was ordered. For a burger joint I was happy with what I got and would eat here again if in the area. Overall, good experience.

We were in DC for a quick trip and happened upon Ghostburger. I love the order set up. We walked in and placed our order for dine in and found a nice little table. The food was really delicious. My only complaint is that there was no actual cheese available-American and “whiz” maybe there was blue cheese, but I’m not a blue cheese kind of person. So both me and my daughter opted for no “cheese” on our meals. The food was delicious. It was fresh. It was fast. The milkshake was tasty.  I highly recommend - especially if you like “whiz.”

I highly recommend the Frenchie burger.  It's loaded with mushrooms and caramelized onions and Bleu cheese.  Yum!

The interior is interesting.  It's got that downtown diner vibe.  The service is very friendly.

This place is one of the options you have for meals if you're visiting the Walter E. Convention Center. It was actually on my way to the parking garage, so I decided to try it. I wasn't too hungry, but the good reviews about the shakes persuaded my legs in the direction of its entrance.

I quite like the decorations. The pink walls pop. The black and white tiles give a vintage vibe. The cement counters, neon logo, and subtle light balls all worked well together for me. The staff was friendly too. However, I'm afraid the shakes and sliders were mediocre. The sliders tasted okay, but it felt like I was served a microwavable one. The shake was too sweet for me. It's an average American shake. The reviews deceived me. I probably won't be back unless it's for happy hour drinks and to talk.

Staff is great, attentive and sweet.
Food ia full of flavor and makes you want more. I enjoyed every bite. I had the Buffalo Bleu Chicken Sammy and Ghost fries. Dining room is clean. Decor is contemporary art with black and white floors and a pink accent to the theme. There's a wheelchair ramp. My visit was immediately after a snow storm, so outside views weren't ideal but I can forsee a livily summer vibe. That private dining area appears to have and pure street corner view, so watch the City come to Life.

name: Xi'an Famous Foods
document: Xi'an Famous Foods. cuisine: Chinese Noodles Burgers. located in Brooklyn. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Take out on August 31, 2025.

Stop complaining about the noodles being cold when you bring them home. Just warm them up for 1 minute in the microwave or eat it in the car. It’s not a big deal, not sure why this has become a point of conversation in these reviews. Food was delicious. This is special food from Xi’an, China. Thank you for bringing this chain to the DMV. Hope to see a proper sit down restaurant soon.
谢谢!

First of all, it is not DoorDash Only, I don’t know why the title says that. You can order from the official Xi’an Famous food website or the Four Mile website. I have visited this restaurant many times before in NYC, including the flagship Flushing location. Happy this one opened in the DMV. The good: the burgers are on point, the cold noodles are yum. The bad: the flat wide noodles do not travel well. I had to drive 30 mins home after the pick up, and the chew in the noodles probably lasted maybe 3 mins after I started eating. The taste is good. They need to open a spot with seats so the noodles can be enjoyed immediately. I heard they are actively looking for a Maryland location with sit-down options. Can’t wait!

So glad Xi’an Famous Foods has finally made it to the DMV! I took my parents to their NYC location many years ago, driven by homesickness after weeks of traveling in the U.S. The chewy, hand ripped noodles instantly transported us back to northern China, where wheat noodles are widely loved and celebrated. They still remember that meal to this day.

Fast forward to now, I ordered via DoorDash after doing some research. Since it’s a shared space with other vendors, there’s no dine in option, and the parking and pickup process can be a bit confusing, as others have mentioned. But nothing you can’t figure out.

We ordered the lamb and pork noodles, cold gluten salad, pork dumplings, and pork burgers. We reheated the noodles after the car ride, which softened them slightly, but the flavor was exactly how I remembered - bold, savory, and spicy. The noodles were well ripped, with a wide, smooth surface. The gluten salad was tangy and refreshing, and the pork burgers were packed with juicy braised meat in firm bread.

The dumplings are real surprise. I usually make dumplings at home and don’t often order them out, but Xi’an Famous Foods is an exception. Their spicy and sour pork dumplings are actually regional specialties and definitely worth trying.

For drinks, I recommend the Sour Hawberry and Chrysanthemum Tea. The hawberry is fruity and refreshing, while the chrysanthemum is cooling and calming, both perfect to balance out the richness of the food.

If you’re a first-timer, I highly recommend the lamb hand ripped noodles + spicy & sour pork dumplings + sour hawberry tea.

Hope I can enjoy those perfectly chewy noodles fresh out of the pot soon! Will be on the lookout for their full service location.

Drove over for pick up(only option) on a Sunday afternoon around 2:30.  Be aware the pickup location is behind the 7-Eleven.

Parking is difficult and very tight when busy. There is no where close to sit and eat. Also when you ask for cutlery they don't include in your order they put it in a basket for you to grab. No napkins.  Forks were grab and go and not wrapped separately. You walk in find your order in the website based on text and a locker opens with your food. Pretty straight forward interesting concept.

We ordered 3 different dumplings. These were probably our favorite.   Cucumber salad was very good.  We also ordered 3 different kinds of noodles. Lamb, pork, and beef. All were good though we were hoping for more. One friend who goes often to New York mentioned the noodles weren't as good here.

For us the food wasn't good enough to deal with the hassle of the location. If they moved though we would definitely give it another try or when we go to New York.

An honest review from a longtime New Yorker who used to walk 10+ blocks every week just to get my Xi’an Famous Foods fix: the taste here is exactly as I remembered from the NYC locations, so that’s a big win. I highly recommend the spicy lamb hand-ripped noodles and the stewed pork burger. My favorite dish back in New York was the cold noodles, and while I didn’t realize this location’s version comes without noodles, no problem—I just cooked some at home and added them in.

The sour hawberry tea was the perfect palate cleanser after the rich, spicy meal.

This location is a bit far for us, and since there’s no dine-in option, the food had to sit through a long car ride - unfortunately the noodles got a bit soggy. But I was happy to read in other reviews that the ghost kitchen setup is temporary and that they’re opening full locations closer to my home. When that happens, I’ll definitely be back to my weekly visits.

The fufu was perfectly prepared — smooth, soft, and fresh, with that authentic stretch and texture that tells you it was made with care. The egusi soup was rich, flavorful, and deeply comforting. The location is part of a residential building, but has plenty of parking.   Once you walk in, you notice the two story ceilings and trees.   This is a much larger and nicer location than the Plainview one and I enjoyed it.

The food and the drinks are just as good as the other Sheds, so I had no issues coming back here a few times.  Happy to be a regular!

Each dish felt thoughtfully made and beautifully presented. Beyond the food, the service was warm, attentive, and welcoming, which made the entire experience even better. The atmosphere at The Shed is cozy, inviting, and perfect for a relaxed meal or a night out.

Overall, The Shed exceeded our expectations in every way. With great food, great service, and a great vibe, it’s a place we’d happily return to again and again. Highly recommended!

The brunch is exceptional✨️—beautifully prepared and absolutely delightful—making it the perfect place to begin your day on a high note. Highly recommended.

I came here on the morning of December 6 2025 just to try their Dutch baby for breakfast. I’ve heard many good things about Kunst and made time to come here on my day off and they did not disappoint! I ordered a side of sausage, the lemon curd blueberry Dutch Baby and an iced honey spice latte. The atmosphere was beautiful with a lot of plants and the food was very good, I highly recommend coming here to try the Dutch Baby!

Kunst Coffee Haus is one of those cafés that feels like a hidden little sanctuary. The space is filled with greenery, flowers, and small artistic touches from lush plants to handmade crochet animals that give it a cozy, creative vibe. It’s the kind of place where you can sit back, relax, and just enjoy the atmosphere.

I ordered the Blue Ocean Latte, made with espresso, their homemade Blue Ocean syrup, and blue spirulina powder. Not only was it visually stunning, but the flavor was smooth, balanced, and had just the right touch of sweetness. Definitely a drink that stands out and feels unique compared to your usual latte.

The staff are friendly, and the overall atmosphere is both welcoming and inspiring. Between the floral arrangements, calming design, and the little details that make the space feel personal, Kunst Coffee Haus is more than just a coffee shop it’s a spot where you want to linger.

If you’re in the area, it’s worth a stop, whether you’re looking for a pretty latte, a peaceful work corner, or simply a beautiful place to chill. 🌿☕✨

I had the blueberry matcha latte and my husband got a cold brew.. both were great. The sandwiches were amazing too! They definitely don’t skimp on the avocado on the ham, cheese, avocado, and tomato sandwich, and my brie prosciutto sandwich was delicious! The vibe was so peaceful and nice. Our baby enjoyed his milk too! We’ll definitely be back!

We thoroughly enjoyed their berry mix breakfast, but the maple syrup iced latte fell short of our expectations. Despite this minor setback, the atmosphere was perfect for a romantic date, and the service was excellent. We highly recommend this place and would definitely return for more.

name: Café Henri
document: Café Henri. cuisine: French Breakfast & Brunch Cafes. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The place is a nice restaurant overall, with beautiful decoration and a great atmosphere. The waitresses were friendly and welcoming, which made the experience pleasant.

However, I found the food to be quite average, especially considering the price. The portions are not very generous, and many dishes are fairly simple (sandwiches, crêpes, pasta, etc.), which made the quantity-to-price ratio a bit disappointing.

We ordered an onion soup, a quiche Lorraine with a side salad, and the “merguez with strong mustard” sandwich, also with salad. For dessert, we had a crème brûlée (which was very good) and a sugar crêpe that was a bit dry.

Overall, it’s a nice place for the ambiance and service, but I expected a bit more from the food.

Visited today after a 12-mile run and had a disappointing experience. I ordered the Henri Burger cooked medium-well, but it arrived medium-rare. The portion size was also noticeably small for the price point. Unfortunately, the best thing about the order was the salad. While I appreciate what the restaurant is going for, the execution didn't quite land for me.
Service felt rushed and impersonal—our server offered minimal interaction, which left me wanting more engagement. Overall, the experience didn't meet expectations, but I'd be open to giving it another shot if they tighten up the quality and service consistency.

I love Cafe Henri. The food is delicious in the service is very good. I love the environment, especially on days when it's not busy. It never gets crowded because they don't have the tables on top of each other. You might wait for a short period of time if it's busy, but never had to wait super long. It's wheelchair accessible, which is nice. My favorites are the burger and the mussels. I've never had a bad meal there at all. It's always super good. The kitchen is right there next to the dining room and you can see everything when they are cooking, which I like. The music can be a little repetitious, but it's mostly for ambience. I would like to see some more traditional kind of fun French music. Maybe some Stephane grappelli, Django, or Edith Piaf.
Charming spot for brunch. Staff was great. Eggs Benedict, omelette, crepes, espresso martini were highlights. Overall everything came together nicely.

Very nice rustic feeling cafe. The food was great, burger was cooked to perfection and pricing is good for the quality.
I will be coming back, thank you.

name: The Pomeroy
document: The Pomeroy. cuisine: New American Bars. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Made a reservation for 5:30 PM on a Saturday however I showed up a half hour early and the place was somewhat empty so unsure if reservation was truly necessary.

After we settled down and ordered our startup cocktail, we proceeded to the dinner menu and to be quite honest, everything came out appealing and very appetizing. I have nothing negative to comment.

Overall, a nice local establishment with great hospitality and I will no doubt I’ll be back soon and try the rest of the menu.

The place was empty when we arrived, so I’m not sure if reservations are necessary. It was nicely decorated for the holidays, which gave it a warm, festive feel. Service was good, and the burger was solid fries were good too. Overall, a pleasant experience and I’d go back.

Unfortunately, I have to lower my rating to 2 stars.  Six months ago I did enjoy my meal here, but things went downhill on my second visit.  The same salad we ordered on our first visit wasn’t that great and the dressing tasted off.  I also ordered the same Mac and cheese which I had on my previous visit and this time it was terrible!  It was overloaded with big, chunky breadcrumbs and the cheese used wasn’t tasty.  My husband didn’t enjoy his Fried chicken and thought it tasted off.  My sister thought her Chicken sandwich was good.  I can’t recommend after my last meal here.

The Pomeroy was absolutely incredible! Carmine and his staff did an exceptional job hosting our baby shower, and we couldn’t be happier with how everything turned out. Our guests raved about the food, and with a guest list of over 60 people, there was more than enough to go around. They did not skimp on the food or the drinks, and every dish was delicious.

The entire team was extremely pleasant, attentive, and easy to work with from start to finish. We felt truly taken care of, and our event couldn’t have gone more smoothly. Highly recommend The Pomeroy for any special occasion!

Fantastic all around.  Small but nice restaurant/bar. I got the gnocchi and was impressed.  All the meals were really delicious. Fish tacos were plain per a 9 year old, don't blame the restaurant for the appearance
Service was attentive and friendly. We had the pleasure of meeting the owner as well. Very kind people.

name: Cafe Xochimilco
document: Cafe Xochimilco. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Cafes Mexican. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Chilaquiles and breakfast platter are both tasty. Was also surprised by their empanada Salteñas. Staff is friendly and service is pretty good. Will definitely go back.

I happened to be in the Long Island City neighborhood and was looking for a place to have dinner. While checking Google, I came across this Mexican spot called Xochimilco. I’ve actually been to this city in Mexico before, so I thought I’d give it a try. The great star ratings were well deserved—this place is very authentic.

I met Johnny, one of the staff members (possibly the owner), and he was incredibly friendly. I ordered the torta al pastor, and it was amazing. I travel a lot and visit Mexico often, and I can honestly say this is one of the best—if not the best—I’ve ever had.

I’ll definitely be back and am looking forward to trying more items on the menu. I also had a jamaica drink, which was perfectly balanced—not too sweet, just right.

Highly recommend!

I’ve been on a hunt for the best chilaquiles all over NYC, and honestly, most spots in Manhattan are way overrated. This place, though—absolutely amazing! The chilaquiles were so delicious, full of flavor and perfectly done. The customer service was just as impressive—everyone was super friendly and attentive, making me feel right at home. Brooklyn spots never disappoint, and this one is definitely authentic. I’m sure I’ll be back very soon!
Spectacular spot with loving attention to detail. Buenísima comida y atención. Some of the best chilaquiles I’ve had anywhere, Mexico or internationally. Such a gem. Una joya total.

I stayed in the hotel nearby and came here twice during my 3 days stay with friends in NYC. Chilaquiles verdes were amazing, I highly recommend Cafe de Olla as well. The French toast was insanely delicious with lots of berries and bananas, definitely an unexpected good surprise. Plates are big enough to share. Thank you a lot for the amazing service, you made me feel home!!!

name: Twisted Fork Brunch Company
document: Twisted Fork Brunch Company. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Coffee & Tea American. located in Queens. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
My husband and I recently dined for brunch at the Twisted Fork, and it was one of the best spontaneous discoveries I've enjoyed in awhile!

Yes, brunches, especially those worth wild, are incredible busy, as was Twisted Fork, however, you could queue your place in line long before reaching the restaurant, a feature I absolutely love!

We were in the area running errands, I looked up Twisted Fork, got on the 40 minute wait list, arrived 15 minutes early, and was sat within minutes!

The service was absolutely great, from hostess to waitress transition. The boozy and food menu options were plenty and delicious! And most importantly to me, we weren't squeezed in like a can of sardines! Very nice floor plan to accompany both couples and groups. We sat between a party of four (4) and a party of three (3) with a large party of at least eight (8) behind us and we had plenty of room to enjoy ourselves and for the service team to get through with ease.

We started with the French Toast appetizer before moving on to our steak and Benedict entrees. The drinks were so good and the food was even better. As a southerner, I appreciate a warm and soft biscuit! Mm!

Thank you so much for your service, we enjoyed every minute of it.

The chocolate covered strawberry mimosa was great! However, their shrimp and grits gotta go!! It didn’t have any texture to them and there was this weird jelly in it that took away from the dish. I would suggest heading down south and tasting real shrimp and grits! Disappointing, but would head back here to try the other breakfast items.

If you’re thinking of going, GO! I would make a reservation especially on a Saturday but really delicious food, excellent service, Giselle our server was fantastic! We decided to try somewhere new and visit Twisted Fork on a Saturday morning for brunch. It was busy but we were seated pretty quickly. The steak and eggs was so tender and flavorful, I love the twisted steak sauce. My husband had the shrimp and grits and said the grits were so creamy and delicious. Our kid had the crème brûlée French toast and ate all of it and wanted one to go. We will back! Thanks for a great start to our family day.

Enjoyed breakfast here on Sunday morning. There was no wait around opening time. The Service was excellent. The food was good and came out very quickly We had pancake tacos and the spicy Seoul Benny. Both were excellent. Our lattes were very good as well. My only complaint would be about the home fries. They do throw a few sweet potatoes into the mix which is great but overall the home fries are just too soft and tasteless. They are not worth adding on as a side dish. We would definitely come back to try some of the other main dishes that all sound and look delicious.

Twisted Fork Brunch Company hits that balance most brunch spots miss. The food is thoughtful, flavours land clean, and their matcha and coffee are genuinely well-made — smooth, consistent, and never watered down. It’s the kind of place you end up revisiting because they actually care about quality, not just presentation.

name: Cafe 1 Of A Kind
document: Cafe 1 Of A Kind. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Breakfast & Brunch Beer Bar. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Peaceful vibes with a kind, friendly staff. A small neighborhood cafe, with metered parking in front, and a lot in the back as well. You walk in and the ambiance of the cafe makes you feel right at home. The staff greets you with a warm smile and all the food options are laid out in front of you at the register. If you’re looking for coffee, they have quite a few options. The same applies for the food. Whatever you choose, I think you’ll enjoy. Many of the dishes that came out of the kitchen were pleasing to the eyes and stomach.

My wife and I ordered two dishes and a coffee, as seen in the photos, and we weren’t disappointed for the most part. We just had one small issue with seasoning because it was on the lighter flavor size. A little salt and pepper goes a long way, but if you’re health conscious, then the food is perfectly fine. The prices were really reasonable, given the portion size, and the items served.

Overall, it was a very nice experience and would definitely return.

Review date: 02/28/26
Second Time to the location and unfortunately didn’t go as well. We ordered our food and waited 25 minutes and still didn’t arrive. I told the staff we needed to be somewhere and to pack it to go. The food then came out on plates and needed to be sent back to package it up. Between repacking and walking to the parking lot with an insulated food bag, the food was cold. Overall disappointing experience this time around. Hopefully, this time was just one instance and next time will be better.

We were looking for a cute place to have brunch and found Cafe 1 of a Kind—and it was perfect! The avocado toast with mozzarella cubes came with a delicious glaze that was so yummy. I added poached eggs on top and they were cooked perfectly. We even got a free strawberry lemonade, which was refreshing and such a nice surprise. The berry smoothie was honestly the best smoothie ever! The grilled cheese sandwich was also amazing—comfort food done right.
On top of the great food and drinks, the decor is adorable, and I loved the cute animal-shaped ice cube. Such a fun touch! Highly recommend this place for a cozy and delicious brunch.

UPDATE: This weekend I went to my all time favorite cafe and I was disappointed. Apparently there is a new owner and I he quality of the food changed significantly. I had the grilled cheese sandwich with a soup. The grilled cheese may have had one slice of cheese. The soup bowl had less then half of soup. My cousin had the avocado toast with mozzarella cheese; there was barely a spread of avocado. We went at 10:30 a.m. and the bathroom was very dirty. In the years I’ve been going I have never seen the bathroom that dirty. I was so disappointed. The staff continues to be very pleasant and the cafe space is clean.

Original message from 3 months ago:  All time favorite cafe to have a quality meal at a leisurely pace. I typically meet my cousins for brunch and spend a few hours eating and having their specialty coffees. The staff are very sweet.

The food has a comfort level that lacks in most places. The chef definitely takes their time with each dish. Each placement of the toppings on my simple avocado toast was evident. It was healthy and delicious at the same time. I will for sure be going back! They are a bit understaffed for the rush they see - but the staff tried so hard to accommodate everyone.

I came here with my wife after church for brunch.  For drinks, we ordered the Mango Lemonade and the Rose Lemonade and they tasted so good!  We also got a tonkatsu sando and a spicy pork bulgogi wrap with a side of fries.  All of it delicious.  I recommend this place if you are looking for calm cafe vibes and brunch.

document: Margie's. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: One of the best dinners I have had in a while. Thomas is the best server; he is both highly attentive and friendly. A 5 star experience. The food and drinks at Margie’s are delicious. Nice atmosphere & ambiance. The cookie skillet was the cherry on top to the night. Excellent service & flavors. Still thinking about the pasta.

My sister had her birthday here. When I tell you they kept bringing food. It was nice.  The food tasted great.the sizes and portions were perfect on everything except the sausage, they were huge!!!! The fruit was great. The pancakes  breakfast sandwhiches.... everything for the group was present able

Margie’s is a locals favorite hangout and tourists best option for dinner while in rockaway beach. The food is fantastic, the service is great and the atmosphere is awesome! We had the burger one night (not pictured) and the chicken Milanese the next. It was one of the best chicken cutlets I have ever had and the Cesar salad on top really was a great addition and nice twist on the dish. Be careful when ordering the filthy martini, it WILL taste like ocean water and might make you nauseous but apparently that’s how the locals like it! All in all, highly recommend and will be dreaming of the chicken Milanese. If you enjoy this review feel free to give us a follow on IG: @noasarc

I found this spot on a list of the best breakfast places  — and that was enough to convince us to go. We decided to make a little day of it: brunch first, then a walk along the beach.

The interior is lovely, with stylish locals adding to the vibe. The team was warm and welcoming, and the service was smooth. The food? Solid. Classic American breakfast staples — well-made, satisfying, but nothing that made us go “wow.”

Still, it’s a great place to start the day if you’re in the area. The check for three people with tips came to $140.
Had a wonderful solo date at Margie’s. I ordered a half dozen oysters with a glass of white wine and turkey pot pie. Delicious.

name: Oxomoco
document: Oxomoco. cuisine: Mexican. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text: We felt genuinely welcomed from the moment we walked in, almost as if we were dining with family. My daughter, who is usually a very selective eater, ended up having one of the best meals she’s ever had thanks to the thoughtful recommendation from the team at Oxomoco. The service, the flavors, and the atmosphere all exceeded expectations. Highly respected, highly recommended, and I truly can’t wait to go back.

This Mexican place is fusion but has its own character. We enjoyed the twist in octopus and fish ceviche because the charred octopus added more flavor. The catch of the day tacos are amazing, with Thai basil and other fresh herbs make it so refreshing to balance the fried fish! Beef cheek tacos are also very flavorful and tender :) Lastly dont miss to finish with chocolate mousse with espresso ice-cream, you won’t regret that!

Went there for Lunch and had an amazing. Our waiter John did an amazing job explaining the offerings in the menu and recommended things we ended up absolutely loving. The bar had an incredible selection of quality tequila and mezcal. Great for connoisseurs. The food is $$$. But worth every penny with how delicious it is. Will definitely go back again.

Being my first time in New York City I was taken to a quaint little Mexican restaurant in Brooklyn. Now coming from Los Angeles where we have exceptional Mexican food all over the city. Try some outside of California is a bit of a treat. Oxomoco has some very good dishes on an elevated level. They use high quality ingredients for all there dishes lending to elevated taste. The fish tacos were great tender flaky fish with a nice not too spicy slaw on top. Chips and salsa that had multiple levels of heat you get five salsas to try. The crab tostada was nice a flavorful and the wagyu beef cheek were tender with a nice mole sauce. They also have a nice mix of tequila and mezcal drinks for you to choose from. The menu is small but has something for everyone. All the dishes we had were very delicious and the atmosphere was great. Indoor and patio dining is available. Oh make sure you make  reservations so you don’t have to wait if you want inside. If you’re in Brooklyn swing by and give them a try. You won’t be disappointed.

WOW—is all I can say! Probably the best meal I’ve ever had in my life. We were an hour early to our dinner reservation and the kindly sat us. Immediately our waitress asked for our dietary restrictions and allergies and she talked us through the menu and was so knowledgeable. For drinks we had a guava mezcal margarita and the frozen IXMAND which were both super yummy. The guacamole and pink moon oysters were so fresh and delicious with every bite. We then had the beef tartar tostada which was my favorite and the carne asada platos. The service, atmosphere, all
the flavors were absolutely Phenomenal we will be back!

name: Paratha Wala
document: Paratha Wala. cuisine: Indian Halal Bangladeshi. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I don’t see what’s all the hype about from this place. It doesn’t even have any flavor to the food but they charge high prices compared to a fancier spot. The foods are pretty bland and not that good. Growing up eating flavorful food and trying places that have flavor and spices from the food isn’t that hard to distinct. I came to try the viral smash burger it’s literally so bland the burger meat itself has no flavor.. The only food that tasted okay at best was the lamb shank biryani rice was dry but it had some what spice on it. The other dishes are pretty bland and mid to be honest better off at any other spots and top of that the host is kinda picky offering free desserts to certain guests and showing it off loud and proud. Don’t come here it’s not worth the hype it died out back in the day and isn’t the same as before.

Vibes were great — loved the gol gappa and drinks. For the main course, we had butter chicken and paneer roll, which were just okay. The desi fries are definitely a skip.

I was a bit disappointed because I had called ahead to arrange a surprise cake for my friend’s birthday. They forgot about it, and while the staff apologized and eventually brought the cake out, they took the bill back to charge me full price for it — which felt a little unfair since the surprise was already missed.

Honestly disappointed was very excited to try the paratha smash burger and chicken tikka bowl. The food was very greasy and made all of us feel very queasy afterwards. Additionally, one of our water cups had some sort bug/ miscellaneous item inside. The food also took quite a while to come out around 45 minutes, which isn’t always the worst but the restaurant seemed mostly empty when we went. However, our waitress was very kind and professional which was the saving grace of our experience

Definitely a place anyone who eats out at on Metro should try out.
Service (especially Vani is great!) and food is reliably good, and appreciate the thought put into the decor and fun atmosphere - there's a Street Fighter arcade machine and foosball table, and the courtyard/back room suited us well for 40 guests when we rented it.

I had a wonderful experience at Parathawala today !!! The staff were incredibly friendly, welcoming, and made us feel comfortable from the moment we arrived. What made the visit truly special was how they went out of their way to celebrate my birthday 🥺🥺🥺 it was such a thoughtful and memorable gesture. The atmosphere was cozy, the service was excellent, and the overall experience left me really happy. Highly recommend this place for great food and even better hospitality. I’ll definitely be coming back!
