document: La 15 Bar & Restaurant. cuisine: Bars. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I found my Haitian restaurant in Northern Queens at Iliana's Bar Lounge. This place is a rare gem in the midst of a sea of Spanish restaurants. In Northern Queens, you'll find a bunch of great Spanish restaurants, but if you're looking for new flavors, a different vibe bringing the culinary arts of Haiti & the Caribbean, check out Illiana's.

FYI if you are familiar with College Point Queens, than you know parking is a nightmare. There was a dedicated parking lot two or three blocks away from restaurant.

Let's talk about the food 😋. For my first visit, I had to test out the griot (marinated, braised pork shoulder, and fried served with pikliz (a spicy pickled slaw) it didn't disappoint. My daughter and I went to town. We both pointed out how tender the cut was 🤤. Truly everything was a beautiful mashup. We ate everything.

The bar had a deep selection of liquors available Although I didn't get to drink that day 😕 I will be back.

The music was a vibe as I waited for my food to come. My server was Mary, who told me about the live DJ who comes Saturday and Sunday. I'll definitely be back for that experience.

This restaurant has been on my list to try. Happy I finally I got to pay a visit. The food was freshly prepared and flavorful, really enjoyed the Acra and Pwason (fish) with sauce. I appreciate the Diri Djon Djon being a sufficient amount to eat with the food. Overall, great customer service, nice music, and chilled vibes. Will definitely come back again soon.

1st time going.  My friend saw the advertisement on IG. What a great surprise to get real haitian for that was so we'll seasoned in College Point! Every thing was absolutely delicious!

The goat taso was top tier. I took an extra plate home.  I had the stew chicken seen in the photo. So good! For appetizers we had the yropical shred and the boulette - really as delicious and seasoned as something my mom would make.

I had the hibiscus run punch and Loretta, our waitress, gave me a small sample of the voodoo punch.  Maaaannn... all I can say is fresh fruit juices made both so refreshing and tasty.

I'll be back much sooner than later to try out the other dishes!

I had the honor yesterday to celebrate my 61st birthday at Lliana’s Bar and Lounge. And after relocating from Florida my husband who’s Haitian and I’m trini was looking for a very good sit down Haitian restaurant and I decided to try Lliana’s since the reviews were very good and we did want Haitian food that taste like American food . So the The Verdict is in . From the time you walked in we were greeted with a welcoming smile and seated. I ordered the spicy margarita for my birthday drink it was delicious, for dinner I had the Poison En Sauce ( fried red snapper in sauce)and the black rice,  my husband had the Legume with meat of his choice with white rice and beans, my daughter had the Griot ( fried pork) sauce on the side with rice and peas, my son had the Chimichurri vegan burger either fries. We dug rite in do no pictures of our dishes but let me tell you the presentation was beautiful and the Haitian dishes stayed true to themselves 💯. Everyone of us was very impressed and satisfied we were so full that we didn’t order dessert but the staff took it upon themselves to surprise me with a chocolate lava cakes dessert with the Haitian birthday song in the background along with them blowing whistles clapping like a real celebration. It was so beautiful. I was surprised and overwhelmed at the same time. It was the most beautiful thing I experienced. I really had a great great time over here and I highly recommend recommend them 100% in more.. they are a small intimate restaurant and bar and I will be coming back here even though the parking is tough but it’s worth it even my kids said it. They’re willing to walk park anywhere and walk. We were lucky enough to find a park right in front of it, but they had to park a block away , but it’s worth it guys once u experience the hospitality like us , will be going back . You will not be disappointed. Trust me.

Intimate and cozy restaurant with friendly staff! Staff were friendly and welcoming. The food was delicious, generous portions and well worth the price! The drinks were tasty and strong! Loved the rum cake! Will definitely be back, support this establishment! 🇭🇹

document: Tropix Bar & Lounge. cuisine: Lounges American Latin American. located in Queens. with 3.7 stars (good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Tropix is a restaurant lounge and bar that has become a go-to spot for my Retro Fitness crew when it comes time to celebrate birthdays and other occasions. We have been going there for years and it has always delivered a good time.

The vibe is fun, the music is generally solid, and there is a dance floor to make use of if you are in the mood. Fair warning though — the speakers are close and the floor can get crowded, so be mindful of where you position yourself or you will be hearing ringing for days afterward. I have actually started considering bringing earplugs on future visits to protect my hearing. It is that kind of loud.

As for drinks, I cannot speak to those since I do not drink alcohol. What I can tell you is that the water was perfectly hydrating. The DJ does the usual DJ things — occasionally cuts a song too early or drops something you are not feeling — but overall the music selection works and keeps the energy up.

I would not come here for a quiet meal. The environment is not built for that. But as a place to gather with friends, celebrate something, and have a genuinely good time, it is a solid local gem.

I booked a party for my dear friends 50th birthday and everything went off without a hitch. The finger food choices were great! The drinks were delicious. We booked a room in the back on the ground floor. It was perfect for the party. The DJ started spinning at 9pm and we danced the night away. They were kind enough to refrigerate the cake. Our waitress was attentive to us. She kept clearing our table and asking us if we were okay. I can't remember her name but she had dimples and a warm welcoming smile. The party was so good and doing business with Gary went smooth that I am booking my birthday party next! Can't wait to go to TROPIX again! Thanks Gary & staff! 🙏🏼🫶🏼

Such a great local spot! The owner is genuinely one of the nicest people you’ll meet… You can tell they genuinely love what they do, and it shows in the vibe of the whole place. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming back to!!!

Highly recommend this place , I had my daughters 30th birthday party here last Sunday April 21st 2024. The owner Gary and his associate were so kind and made this event memorable!
We rented the upstairs lounge decorated it, ordered the food and drinks and everyone really enjoyed themselves! Most importantly, my daughter her friends and my family were satisfied with the party results. Highly recommend this quaint bar lounge space, the waitress assigned was also on her game as well her assistant!

name: Rogue Bar
document: Rogue Bar. cuisine: Bars. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Rogue BBQ Pittsburgh delivers one of the best all-around dining experiences in the city. From the moment you walk in, the hospitality stands out—warm, welcoming, and genuinely kind staff who make you feel right at home. It’s a family-owned establishment located on Amity Street in Homestead, and you can feel the care they put into every detail.
Rogue BBQ offers dine-in and takeout options, a full bar, off-site catering, and even a food truck you can catch around the Burgh. They also have a stand at Kennywood, which feels very on-brand and very Pittsburgh.
They recently revamped their menu, striking the perfect balance between keeping longtime fan favorites and introducing new, exciting options. The wing board completely exceeded expectations. The presentation was impressive, and the wings themselves were outstanding.
Guests can choose between fried wings or smoked whole wings, and all sauces are made in-house. The flavors are innovative yet familiar—classic BBQ profiles with thoughtful twists. The dry rub smoked wings paired with the horseradish lemon Alabama white sauce were especially memorable, bold, and incredibly well-balanced.
One standout that deserves special mention is the PB&J-flavored wings. While unexpected, the flavor combination works surprisingly well and ends up being one of the most satisfying bites on the table.
Their homemade corn bread is flakey and flavorful.  Plus we snagged some Brisket Rolls to go (because had to try but so full!).  They make all their pizza dough in house so imagine fresh dough, smoked brisket, a cheese blend and tangy BBQ sauce all rolled up!!!
Overall, the food is bold and exciting, the space feels wholesome and inviting, and the experience is one you’ll want to repeat. Rogue BBQ isn’t just a place to eat—it’s somewhere you genuinely want to be.

My girlfriend and I were biking along the trail on our way to a brewery when we smelled a wonderful, smokey bbq joint. We decided to stop and we were very happy that we did. Solid beer selection, great service and the food was spot on. Brisket nachos were loaded with meat and cheese - loved the smoke in the brisket. The Mac and cheese with the pulled pork sandwich topped with Cole slaw was excellent. Definitely recommend and will come back.

We were really excited to try Rogue BBQ after a recent review online. We walked in with 2 parties in front of us and were quoted an hour wait. Stupid, but we waited. (Spoiler….we should have left) We were seated in 30 minutes. The “hostess” was  also a bartender or a server or something. No “wait to be seated” signs. People walking in and taking tables. So disorganized. We get to the table order apps and drinks. Takes a half hour to get soup and oysters. Another 45 to get food. Food was wrong. We ordered fries…. got haluski….table across from us got fries and ordered haluski. No silverware. Food was mediocre at best. No beer list at the table. Couldn’t see the chalkboard. Server bridget??? Had no clue what beers were on tap. What a joke! Child drink $3….never offered one refill in 2.5 hours. She was kind to our child, but wasn’t enough for us to ever go back. I worked in the service industry for years. I start my tip at 30% and this was the absolute worst service of my life. Worst experience. Came in at 4:45….nearly 7:30 when we left. Oysters were good, but never again.
Should have went to Dukes.

The cocktails were creative and perfectly made. The food was outstanding.  Husband had 1/2 rack of ribs with the bourbon sauce. He enjoyed every bite but the order was large so he had leftovers. I had thr brisket sandwich with the brisket baked beans..so tender and they are not shy on the meat. Great wait staff and atmosphere! We will definitely return!

I got take out. Only thing that was good was the pulled pork. I also got no sauces and they usually provide some. The chicken was dry, the brisket was the worse I ever had in my life. It was straight fat, not lean whatsoever. I couldn’t even eat it. Creamy corn and baked beans were just okay. I won’t be back.

google_reviews.text:
This review is for their bottomless brunch. It definitely seems more suited as a nightclub than brunch. We were a large party of 13 and when we arrived we were told to go all the way upstairs to their rooftop. The seating available up there doesn't have much table space which would have made it hard to eat, so we were sent back down where we entered. It seemed like they didn't know where to place us until finally deciding to move some tables around to accommodate for us. We were also the only group there so it felt pretty lonely until halfway through another group came. Even then it was just us two groups the whole time.

For food I got the chicken and waffles which was actually not bad. The chicken was fried and seasoned well. They were out of the salmon lox bagel which some people in our group wanted, and another mishap occurred when one person in our group ordered a chicken sandwich and they brought back a breakfast sandwich with sausage. They kept telling them they didn't have a chicken sandwich ordered until 10 minutes later it arrived. They did mention brunch was new for them and they're still working things out.

For drinks we did bottomless mimosas and they have three options for the juices; orange, cranberry and pineapple. Out of all three the pineapple is definitely the best.

Overall I didn't feel too impressed with how brunch was, but I know it's new and I hope that within a couple months they'll be more equipped.

my first time here, came on a Tuesday for a friends birthday. Our waitress there was really nice and accommodating, the mocktails and hookah flavors were amazing. Also the food surprisingly was really good as well. We got chicken vindaloo and chicken tikka masala w garlic naan and both were prepared really well. The music was also trendy and was consistent with the vibe of the lounge. Would definitely recommend just coming to chill with friends if you’re bored in queens and want a small restaurant/ lounge with a modern cool vibe. The chef was so nice, not sure how he knew (we never mentioned it) but he sent complimentary kulfi cake for the birthday girl which was really delicious, and chai. Gotta come back here soon.

Been coming here for years!!! Before they had alcohol(they still have cocktails) and the L.E.D hookahs. Loved it then and still love it now! You can come here and smoke a hookah for hours and it would still be good! Their food is delicious and so was our server she was so nice and made sure to check in numerous times on Mother’s Day! My go to flavors is frozen fruit loops in their led hookah, I highly recommend it. Their coconut shrimp and wings are amazing as well as ALL of their cocktails and mocktails! This place is perfect for a girls date during the day time and night out on the weekend! They also have belly dancing on Saturdays! There’s nothing negative I can say about this establishment I have been here countless times and always received top tier service.

100% Halal and the food is delicious, they also have an attached restaurant next door called Aroma, which makes their extensive menu even better! For starters we had the papri chaat, samosa chaat, and bbq wings. They were off the charts. For the entrees we had the butter chicken, bhindi masala, saag, shahi korma, garlic naan and white rice. Every item had the perfect taste just wished it was a bit more flavorful for the bhindi. For dessert we had the death by chocolate shake, Nutella cheesecake, vanilla graham crackers s’mores shake and the ras malai tres leche. The best one of the deserts were the ras malai and death by chocolate. We also had the blue Hawaiian mock tails which were so delicious! However as great as the food sounds, I do have to say for someone being big on hookah, their hookah is not good at all. The coals are too big, and it gets harsh fast. The flavors are not there to last as many of the places I’ve went too, so they need to figure out how to fix that. The customer is amazing as well. Other than that they would’ve gotten a 10/10 from me. If you’re in the area do give them a try!

A Pint of Shelter: Dodging D.C. Storms at Kelly’s The Irish Times

Kelly’s The Irish Times on Capitol Hill was the perfect place to swerve into to avoid an incoming storm approaching Washington, D.C. (Fri, May 30, 2025). The Irish pub had caught our eye during our earlier visit to D.C. the previous weekend.

Not only was it smaller than the surrounding buildings, but it had a much bigger Irish-looking neighbor that somehow made Kelly’s look more authentic, and that told us it had character - and we were right.

Kelly’s The Irish Times was a lively, atmospheric bar, self-described as “sometimes boisterous.” It was established in 1978 and is presumably named after the owner, Mr Brendan Kelly.

We sat at the bar and ordered:

🍺 Black & Blue = $8.62
🍺 Blue Moon x 2 = $16.36
⛔️ Alcohol Free Heineken x 3 = $21.00
😢 Tax = $4.60
💰 Total = $50.58

We left a gratuity that reflected the swift and attentive service. We enjoyed our time there and it was the kind of place we could’ve stayed all night, but the next day we were flying out of D.C. so needed to get some sleep.

Noticing a slight lull in the rain, we took our leave, pleased to have found hydration inside rather from the storm outside!

name: Faarzi Himalayan Bar & Grill
document: Faarzi Himalayan Bar & Grill. cuisine: Wine Bars Himalayan/Nepalese Cocktail Bars. located in Queens. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
If you want to experience traditional Nepali decor, this place is a must visit, they’ve absolutely nailed the aesthetics. While it isn’t the most spacious restaurant, it’s comfortable enough. Weekends can get quite busy, so a reservation is recommended.
I really enjoyed the overall vibe, immaculate interiors, friendly service, and live music that adds to the atmosphere. But as a foodie, I felt the food could’ve been better. The presentation doesn’t quite make up for the lack of depth in flavor, just my personal take.
That said their cocktails are excellent and definitely worth trying. Overall, a good experience.

I was very excited to see a Himalayan spot opening up on this side of Elmhurst because I felt there was a need for more diverse food anyways.

The exterior is very eye-catching especially with all of the decorations and colors the owners put effort into. The interior is just wow, different colors - lots of greens, purple & brown. The seating and tables are very pretty and the lighting is perfect.

I haven’t tried too much food here, but so far I have had the: Buff chow mein, Chatamari Set (Nepalese style folded pizza with spiced meats and vegetables), Kathmandu Ko Faarzi Jhoi Momo Cha (Nepalese style dumplings with flavorful fillings served with special tangy sauce) and Baudha Ko Faarzi Cheu Momo (steamed momo with flavorful juicy buttery fillings served with 2 different sauces). There’s a lot of interesting aromatics in the food and their momo’s are delicious! I can’t eat much spicy foods, so I chose the ones that were mild or not spicy.

The bar menu had an assortment of drinks and cocktails. I’ve tried a few of the cocktails at Faarzi and they are on point.

Overall, a pleasant experience if you’re looking for a different type of cuisine and atmosphere. The staff here are very nice & welcoming. The music is also very relaxing and when you’re here, you forget you’re even in NYC.

The food was good overall, although I’m not a huge fan of spicy food and a lot of the menu had a bit of a kick. That’s just personal taste though.

We went during the NYC snowstorm and the staff were really friendly and welcoming, clearly putting in a lot of effort even when many other places were closed.

Nice atmosphere with good live music, which made the experience enjoyable. The momo and chowmein were tasty and definitely recommended.

Unfortunately, the “Masu Jindabaad” platter was a big letdown. Although it looks good in the picture attached, the portion size was way too small for a $50 platter and not worth for the price. I would not recommend ordering this platter.

Overall, good place for ambiance and select dishes, but skip the Masu Jindabaad platter.

Walking into this restaurant feels like stepping into a little corner of Nepal. The cozy décor, warm lighting, and inviting atmosphere create a sense of comfort that immediately transports you, almost like being in a Himalayan teahouse.

Sadly, the food did not match the charm of the setting. The flavors were underwhelming, and for the high prices charged, the quality felt disappointing. It left me wishing the dishes carried the same authenticity and warmth as the ambiance.

Overall, the restaurant is a lovely, cozy place that captures the spirit of Nepal in its atmosphere. But if you’re seeking truly satisfying food at a fair price, the experience may fall short.

document: Cooper Bluff. cuisine: Bars. located in Queens. with 3.7 stars (good).

google_reviews.text:
Cooper’s Bluff – Oyster Bay’s Best-Kept Secret

I almost don’t want to write this because Cooper’s Bluff is a true hidden gem. Locals and those who grew up around here know the magic of this spot. Tucked away with stunning views, there’s usually live music, tons of seating, and a relaxed, welcoming vibe.

Whether you’re coming by land or boat, it’s the perfect place to unwind. The nearby parks and the town make for a great afternoon stroll, maybe even a drink or two. I had the lobster roll—yes, it’s a bit pricey, but you’re paying for the location and the atmosphere.

A special place to kick back with friends… but let’s keep this one between us. Shhh…

It's a great spot especially when the weather is nice.  Prices on food are less than competitive, quite expensive, but I think you are paying for the atmosphere.  Cold frozen drinks are plentiful, few different beer options in can or tap but come for the views. Pet and children friendly. Often live music.

I had the BEST time at Cooper Bluff in Oyster Bay yesterday! So, I'd been seeing all these cool vids on Insta and TikTok, and I just had to check it out in person.

When I got there, there was plenty of parking space, and they had this adorable little pink Bluff Bus that could take you to the restaurant. The driver was super nice and made the whole thing feel like a fun adventure. But if you're up for it, you can also just take a stroll to get there.

Now, let me tell you, the view from Cooper Bluff is out of this world! It's seriously breathtaking. I could have just sat there all day, taking in the beautiful scenery. And to make things even better, they had live music playing, which just added to the awesome vibe.

They had all the classics like cheeseburgers and nuggets, and their drink selection was on point too. I mean, they had everything from wines to cocktails to the most delicious frozen drinks.

One thing that totally blew me away was the ladies' restrooms. Get this, they were inside a regular truck, but they looked like regular bathrooms you'd find in a fancy place. So cool!

Honestly, I'm already planning my next afternoon back to Cooper Bluff. It was such a blast, and I can't wait to go again. If you're looking for a rad place to chill, have amazing food and drinks, and enjoy a killer view, you gotta hit up Cooper Bluff in Oyster Bay. It's totally worth it! 🙌

1st time and let me say it didn't disappoint! Atmosphere is great with the live music and you're right on the oyster Bayfront with amazing views of not only the bay but the many yachts, they have live bands and great food and cocktails. Staff is amazing 👏

First time here. Great spot to kick back, relax, drink, eat and listen to live music. Definitely a fun spot with a nice staff and great views of the water.

They have some delicious frozen drinks.  I loved the Pomergant Margherita and my wife enjoyed the Pina Colada.

The food truck had a delicious Lobster Roll and Fish Tacos....the fries were terrific as well.

Everything is a bit pricey....but you are paying for a great experience. So no complaints from me. I can't wait to come back!

google_reviews.text: Lucky Dog is THE premier animal rescue organization in the DMV. This well organized, and talented staff makes the process of finding the fur family member both rewarding and successful. We adopted “Rosie” aka “Pocky” on December 28th. Our daughter saw her posted photo a few months back and we decided that 2026 was the perfect time to bring her into our family. The “meet & great” in Bethesda was an exciting moment for us! Our timid little addition took to our home immediately! She is now a member of a 3 furry pack that just happens to include her big brother “Harper Cat!”  It is LOVE all around with our Rosie!

My husband and I just adopted our first dog together from Lucky Dog, and it was a great experience! We went to their DOG adoption event held at PetSmart, where we first met our dog Maple. The staff was super helpful giving us all the information needed to pre-apply for her. This was my first time owning and adopting a dog, so Lucky Dog made the whole process so seamless for the next few days we went through the adoption process. We worked with Annika and Kady and they were super responsive in our interview and answered any questions we had, also helped with scheduling everything when picking up Maple from her Foster and continue to assist us with resources as we adjust. 10/10 would recommend Lucky Dog, so happy with the newest member of our fam!!!

We've adopted 2 dogs from Lucky Dog over the course of the last 7 years and it's been an amazing experience each time. They care so much about all the dogs they rescue, have excellent fosters, and are dedicated to making sure each family goes to the right home. Our first Lucky Dog, Quinn, was a red bandana (problem child), and it took years of work but now 9 years old, she's thriving and has worked past her dog reactivity, you would never have guessed she was once a "bad dog". But that's why Lucky Dog is so great, they give these dogs that have had a rough go at life so far another chance, and I'm so grateful Quinn and Roux have gotten a second chance with us. Adopt don't shop at Lucky Dog, there are amazing dogs out there all looking for a loving home!

Adopting Panela was one of the best decisions I’ve ever made! Lucky dog staff was kind, professional, and truly cared about finding the right home for each animal. The process was smooth, transparent, and supportive from start to finish. I’m so grateful for the amazing work they do thanks to them, I found the sweetest, funniest and most loving dog. name: Hug Esan
document: Hug Esan. cuisine: Thai. located in Queens. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I’ve been wanting to try a restaurant in New York that serves authentic Isan/Northern Thai food, and we found this spot in Queens. It’s not in Manhattan, but I’m telling you — it’s worth the trip.

It’s located right next to Little Thailand and easy to find with Google Maps. One downside is that the space is very small. They only have four small tables for two and one larger table for 3–4 people, so it might be difficult for bigger groups unless you make a reservation. We arrived right after they opened, and not long after, the whole place was packed.

Besides the size, the restaurant is really pretty and cozy. The menu is interesting and offers a wide variety of dishes — fried, stir-fried, grilled, soups, and more.

Here’s what we ordered:

Crab Fried Rice – We ordered it without much thought, just to try it, and it ended up being one of the best Thai dishes we’ve ever had. Even my husband (who is Laos/Thai) loved it. He rarely gets to eat crab because his mom has a severe allergy, so this was special for him too. (We forgot take picture lol)

Crispy Pork Belly – Served super hot and crispy. I love that they battered it instead of just deep-frying it plain. It had great texture and was so flavorful.

Tum Thai (Thum Mak Hoong) – We ordered it very spicy and asked if they could make it Laos-style. They tried, and it was pretty good. It was slightly lacking the strong fermented fish sauce (padek) punch that gives it that bold, pungent flavor. But honestly, it’s still very close to Northern style — just more approachable and less intense, so more people can enjoy it.

Sticky Rice – Served the traditional way in a bamboo basket (aep khao) with a lid, which keeps it piping hot. I love when restaurants keep it authentic like that.

We wanted to order more because there were so many options, but just three dishes were already enough for us — we even had leftovers. They packed everything very securely; I carried the papaya salad around all day and it didn’t spill at all.

It is pretty pricey, but honestly, it’s worth trying at least once for the quality and authenticity.

We’ll definitely bring his parents here next time we’re back in NYC.

The taste is really good, all spices are perfect for me. Not too sweet and spicy. It’s like spicy and salty which I like. The waitress is nice, the place is not that big but neat and tidy. It’s better to take the reservation if you have big party.

Sensational meal and dining experience at Hug Esan! While I am a huge fan of Thai food in general, this was my first time trying cuisine from this particular region and it surely did not disappoint. Highly recommend this great BYOB in Jackson Heights/elmhurst.

Truly differentiated northern Thai cuisine. Expertly prepared and all delicious. It's a small place so you may have to wait if it's busy. Service is informative, efficient and pleasant. They don't serve alcohol but you can bring it in and pay a small corkage fee. Also they don't take credit cards but do accept venmo.

Can't believe out of all the places around little Thailand Hug Esan was last on my list.

Everything was amazing. The food blew me away and I'll be back for the rest of the menu.

document: Dar Lbahja. cuisine: Halal Moroccan. located in Queens. with 4.3 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
I tried Dar Lbahja today and it was amazing. Highly recommend! The harira soup was on point honestly the best I’ve had compared to other Moroccan restaurants.

All the appetizers were incredible. Every single one was so flavorful and satisfying  I honestly feel like I could eat those appetizers every day if I could.

Every dish we ordered was great and the food came out very fast. The service was amazing and you can really tell the chef knows what they’re doing. The prices are very reasonable too.

It’s also a great place to go for iftar the setup was beautiful and everything felt very welcoming. Definitely a spot I would come back to!

Honestly, this place is such a gem. It doesn't even feel like a restaurant, it feels like you’re eating at a friend's house. Chef Touria is amazing and you can tell she puts so much love into the food!!
We got the chicken bastilla, the lamb tajin with prunes, and the royal couscous, and everything was so fresh and authentic. We finished with the Jawhara dessert, which was the perfect move,super light, refreshing, and just really hit the spot. Plus, the staff are all so nice. If you want the real deal Moroccan food, go here!

I was so excited to try this hidden gem in Astoria and it didn’t disappoint. I felt like I was transported to Morocco in a homey way. The appetizers were deliciously savory from the Chicken Bastilla to the Moroccan cookies. Even the tea was hands down one of the best teas I’ve had at restaurants. The bread as well was fresh and soft paired with the Beef Tagine that was cooked with tender love. You really feel like you’re sitting down at a family friend’s house - Youssef our waiter was attentive and friendly. He made us feel right at home asking us if we had any questions and provided his recommendations.

If you're looking for authentic Moroccan cuisine, stop searching and head to Dar Elbahja in Astoria.

This isn't just the best Moroccan restaurant in Queens--in my opinion, it's one of the best in all of New York City.

The chef, Touria Lamtahaf is doing something truly special here. Warm hospitality, cozy atmosphere, and food that transports you straight to Morocco. Come hungry and save room for dessert and fresh mint Tea.
Worth the trip to Astoria. 5 stars without hesitation.

We came to Dar Lbhaja for iftar, and from the very beginning the hospitality, service, and food were nothing short of impeccable. Truly a meal fit for kings and queens.

We initially walked in without a reservation and were told there were no seats available. Before we even left, the host sent us off with dates and chebakia so we wouldn’t miss breaking our fast — an above-and-beyond gesture that speaks volumes. Ten minutes later, she called to let us know she had made room for us, and we rushed back, ready to begin our Moroccan food journey.

My father was born and raised in Morocco, and I can confidently say this is some of the most authentic Moroccan food I’ve had in the States.

The harira immediately transported me back to childhood — a warm, comforting tomato-based soup that truly soothes the soul.

We ordered hummus (not traditionally Moroccan), but it was incredibly fresh, and you could taste the quality of the olive oil drizzled on top.

The chicken bastilla was outstanding — perfectly nutty, sweet, and savory. It’s a dish that’s hard to come by, and when I see it on a menu, I must order it.

For mains, we had the lamb with prunes, one of my favorite dishes in the world, and they absolutely did it justice. The lamb was tender, falling right off the bone, paired with traditional Moroccan bread to soak up every drop of the sweet, spiced broth.

Lastly, the national dish of Morocco — couscous. Fluffy, hearty, and clearly made with love. Packed generously with root vegetables, this dish felt like home.

Come hungry and bring friends — portions are large, meant to be shared, and this is a meal you’ll want to experience together.

Love this Argentinian bakery. It’s a small establishment where you take out mostly a variety of baked goods… but we love to stay and have some of their goodies there. So you line up for service, and it can be slow- the servers are meticulous to each customer and there is no way to “self serve” so each person has to be taken care of. You order, then pay, and whatever they cannot give you in a tray or bag, they will bring to your table in a bit. We usually have weekend breakfast with chorizo sandwich, a couple empanadas and a couple facturas, café con leche or a soft drink… and so we eat on the empanadas while we wait for the chorizo sandwich and coffees that usually arrive a bit later. Then we roll out the door taking our pastries (facturas) home for a later snack. So much delicious food!

I am writing this review to denote the rather unsavory experience of my visit to Topos today, 11/06.

Reading about the profound philosophy selection that pertains to fundamental radical text, I was eager to ask the staff about the information I was searching for. I also shared my interest in this (political advocacy).

One worker was flipping through a book when I remarked on hearing a lot about it, and asking if they were interested in related subjects. The response was "I can't talk, I  am actually busy listing the prices." To which I took at face value, and sincerely apologized because I did not want to overstep. However, I noticed this employee the reminder of the time there was very laidback and on the cell phone and talking to the coworker. Alone, there is nothing wrong with this -- work is exhausting. But ultimately, as a well-meaning patron, it reads as insincere and mean to brush a patron of your business off.

I also came up to the counter because I wanted to support an establishment committed to educating locals on what overwhelmingly seems like radical theory. I asked if the worker knew any books on  sovereignty, because I wanted to read something novel while also supporting this shop's cause. They seemed very busy, so I abandoned that query and said I was going to sit down.

Later, the same worker suggests John Locke. I explain that I am grateful for their efforts but I am not interested in this. I justify it and say I am curious about formerly colonized nations, not Europe. The responses were unsavory...Justifying myself, which felt like nails on chalkboard to get what I am looking for, landed me in them  ultimately saying something alongside "Sounds like you should consult JSTOR, or maybe your school library."
Taking this at face value, I replied: "Oh, sometimes it is difficult to find something interesting for what you're looking for."
To which they replied, "Well that's where getting research skills come in."
That felt uncalled for. I try and reconcile. "Well, what do you like to read?" "Fiction, and I guess some non-fiction science." I inquire as to what exactly, and they are largely silent. It was about 1 minute where we stared at each other to where I realize: this is a very cold interaction.

I will not be made to feel stupid for trying my hardest to support Topos. Ultimately, their message is very confused by the people they have selected to represent them -- white people. Their customer base is largely white people. The book I was suggested today emphasizes Eurocentric worldviews. Whoever hired these people did not investigate their values or knowledge -- or potentially had installed them in this role on purpose. When people say this place is off-putting, I feel sympathetic to these claims. That interaction where I worked to be sincere and maintained politeness, left me feeling stupid.

No, I would not recommend this establishment. And I do not think I will return. Ultimately, the two stars is because I did like my drink. But I would rather go to Bakeri to get the same quality drink and interact with the sweetie staff who will not talk down on me.

But Brian wasn't having it, he was unhappy that UPS failed us both. Imagine my surprise when a few days later I received another box of the Lamington cakes! I was not expecting that. I was perfectly fine with the outcome but Brian again is an amazing person and he didn't appreciate that this was a representation of his bakery by UPS's failings. So now I have plenty of Lamington cakes and they are freezable so I put a few away so I can enjoy them later.

As far as being true Lamington cake like the original in Australia, it took me right back to Adelaide where I had my very first one! Oh my goodness they're so good! And did I mention they're gluten-free?!

I cannot thank Brian and Sans Bakery enough for making my Unbirthday amazing and tickling my palette enough that I sent pictures to my cousin in Melbourne Australia taunting her a little. She can pick them up at the Woolworth. ;-)

google_reviews.text:
Sweet Harbor Coffee in Roslyn is a great addition to the village and easily stands out as the only true coffee-focused spot in the area right now. The café has a warm, Brooklyn-inspired vibe with a cozy, welcoming atmosphere that makes it a nice place to sit or grab something on the go. I ordered the iced cortado and it was excellent — smooth, balanced, and clearly made with quality espresso and attention to detail.
The shop was very busy when I visited, which shows how quickly the community has embraced it. The wait for my coffee was a bit longer than expected, so a bigger machine or expanded setup in the future could help with efficiency during peak times. Overall, Sweet Harbor Coffee is a strong addition to Roslyn village with high-quality drinks, a thoughtful aesthetic, and a genuine neighborhood feel.

I ordered a large iced salted caramel latte.

name: Sey Coffee
document: Sey Coffee. cuisine: Coffee Roasteries Coffee & Tea. located in Queens. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
A visit to Sey Coffee is nothing short of a pilgrimage for anyone serious about specialty coffee. This is a world-renowned roastery whose coffees are celebrated in some of the best specialty cafés globally — including Motors Coffee — and experiencing it at the source is something special.

The top-shelf espressos were absolutely mind-blowing. Clean, expressive, layered — every shot showcased precision and a deep respect for the coffee itself. You can taste the intention behind every detail.

A special thank you to Daniel and Lorenzo for making my visit unforgettable. Their knowledge, hospitality, and genuine passion elevated the entire experience.

Sey continues to set the bar for what modern specialty coffee can be.

There is no hype behind this coffee shop, hyperbole over the quality of exacting standards in this veritable laboratory where cups of coffee are constructed. Plant lined walls and ceilings reminiscent of your favorite rain forest. While lines may at times seem lengthy, to cue for coffee is indeed worth the wait for a liquid masterpiece. Friendly staff, plethora of flavors and alternatives -hot dark chocolate for the non-coffee drinkers. Delicious and chill without laptops or wifi -come to drink and socialize

One of the best iced coffees I’ve ever had.

Everything here seemed to revolve around the roast. No trendy drinks, no syrups, just coffee and tea. They rotate the roast for their iced coffee, and the one they were using when I went was incredibly fruity. Even served cold, it maintained onto that bright acidity you usually only get from a well-made filtered coffee.

The best part was that they serve it with a free cup of sparkling water. Taking a sip of the coffee and then a sip of the sparkling water added this unexpected dimension. Almost like a deconstructed espresso tonic. For whatever reason, the fizz gave it a lightly sweet finish that wasn’t there on its own. I tried pouring a bit of the sparkling water into the coffee at the end, but it didn’t hit the same.

Sey is the kind of coffee café that makes you rethink what coffee can be.

Tucked away in Bushwick lies coffee lovers paradise! The space is airy, minimal, and filled with natural light—basically a sanctuary for coffee purists.

There are no gimmicks, it’s all about highlighting the beans and their origins with precision.
Sey is a great spot if you want to slow down. The vibe is calm, almost gallery-like, with greenery softening the industrial setting.

The baristas know their craft inside out and are always happy to walk you through the tasting notes like you’re about to embark on a tiny flavor journey. The staff are all super great, love their vibes!

My pour-over was Ethiopian coffee. Never in my life have a tasted Ethiopian coffee bean. Sey is not your average cup of coffee, it’s an experience.

Bottom line: Sey is a temple for serious coffee lovers, and once you’ve tasted their beans, it’s hard to go back to regular drip.

Excellent coffee quality, clean environment,Hands down one of my favorite coffee spots! Amazing drinks, great vibes, and the baristas know their craft. Whether you’re meeting friends or enjoying some solo time, this place never disappoints.
This coffee shop is a gem. The coffee is rich and flavorful, the pastries are always fresh, and the staff makes you feel genuinely welcome. The ambiance is calm and inviting—definitely a place I’ll keep coming back to.and friendly service. Consistently great experience every visit. Highly recommend.

name: Dagny
document: Dagny. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Cocktail Bars Wine Bars. located in Queens. with 3.9 stars (good).

google_reviews.text: My boyfriend ordered an iced mocha and they forgot to put espresso in it. You can see in the picture that the color is lighter than normal. He also asked for extra chocolate but she didnt really put much. The barista looked very busy to accommodate the incoming orders coming in. We usually come in often but the drinks being made have been inconsistent. Paid 8$ for a chocolate milk.

Updating my 5 star rating from 3 years ago to 2 stars. This place is truly fumbling itself into the ground and is completely oblivious to what the demographic of their customer is: people looking for a nice space to get some work done solo or in small groups. They seem resentful of this demographic.

Everyone here is with their laptop looking to work, study, or connect with 1-3 other people with coffee and pastries. Yet, they are blasting reggaeton and tiktok songs with free Spotify ads at *truly* incredible volumes throughout the place – they can see everyone is using noise-cancelling headphones to try to get work done (and it still isn’t enough to block the noise). They close at 3pm on weekdays and 5pm on weekends for some reason, forgoing many primetime hours for their young working demographic with a dearth of “third spaces” in the area, but serve wine & beer?  And there are not nearly enough outlets for all of the people on their devices.

They are charging $18 for a small omelette with spinach and tomato. You pay $9 to wait 15-20 minutes for a single employee to make a pretty bad coffee for you along with the 7 other people on line. They used to ask if you were staying and give you mugs; they used to have more food and quality drinks in the to-go area – now it’s just sodas and beers and the food is often empty. And the pastry quality/selection is so bad.

They completely removed the back glass-enclosed room for public use, and roped off more than half of the back area as “dining only” (the only area that has any backs to any of the chairs). And they’re all empty/unenforced anyway. The manager will pressure you to try ordering something from the menu (the kitchen stops serving at 3pm and the places closes at 5pm, but the place is still mostly “dining only” from 3pm to 5pm. It makes no sense.), but will make sure to let every single table know at 3:45pm that the place closes at 5pm and try to take a cup you are actively drinking from.

It used to be a great “third place” I would recommend to everyone. Now, it reminds me of a chain hotel lobby. The place doesn’t know if it wants to be a café, a bar, a restaurant, or a venue, and it is doing all of them badly. I truly loved this place so much, and it is a shell of the potential it once had.

[Entirely my own opinion: just abandon the entrée food entirely. Lean more into café and bar as the only other major option nearby is Chateau Le Woof and that is a very distinct niche/demographic. Turn down (or off) the music. Add extension cords. Make it so you can order with a table number with a QR code directly from the table instead of the confusing system currently in place. Maybe experiment with a ‘day/evening pass’ if you cannot be profitable with that alone and you don’t want people using the space without larger purchases – Astorians are desperate for the type of place you have the potential to be with some thought & care.]
My husband and I love DAGNY! Diego makes amazing lattes! Staff is so nice and the environment is so cozy and welcoming.

I really want to love, support, and patronize this place, but they make it so hard!

Let's start with the good.

The space is very clean, organized, comfortably furnished, and generally elegant. There are few spaces like it in Astoria. Most other cafes and restaurants around here are small and crowded.

The menu is elevated comfort and diner food. The food is consistently good, and there's something for everyone. It's a good spot for brunch, or lunch, or a very early dinner, because they close pretty early, like 5-7, that seems to change often.

Now the bad.

Every time I have been there, the music is excessively loud, converting an elegant space into a hostile atmosphere.

And every time I have asked the waiter or manager to please consider turning it down, especially when there are few other customers, they have deflected in one way or another.

One time, a very friendly waiter said it was unfortunately not up to them, and she profusely apologized that the manager would not turn it down.

Another time, a male server behind the counter said he would turn it down, but then he did not. My friends and I could not enjoy our conversation over there, the music was so overbearing, so we went back home to hang out.

So long story short, 1) great space and 2) solid menu, but 3) excessively loud music creating a hostile atmosphere :-(

google_reviews.text: We had a delicious brunch, despite the staff being obviously overwhelmed with about 20 customers waiting for drinks. We actually got our food before the matcha latte. Brunch burger was perfectly cooked, well-seasoned and moist. My husband said his eggs Benedict and scotch egg were fantastic. The decor is whimsical, in keeping with their theme. We'll definitely be back!

This place gets bonus stars just for the hobbit theme. The atmosphere is fantastic. It is a cozy spot with thoughtful decorative touches inspired by Lord of the Rings and other fantasy elements, like a modern take on the Green Dragon. The seating and tables feel homey and comfortable, which adds to the overall vibe. The One Ring breakfast sandwich and the hash browns were excellent and highly recommended.

My first visit was for their new afternoon tea service with 5 friends to celebrate my birthday. The food was amazing (homemade hashbrowns with caviar was the savory favorite!), the service lovely and atmosphere was cozy, whimsical and right on theme. They gave me flowers, tea & a card. I also got a special mug (which I wanted to steal it was beautiful and the right “feel) and plate. They sang happy birthday to me and everything was plated beautifully. The tea was also amazing! My only suggestion is we should have been reserved for a bigger table or the food should be staggered. The table was very full with 6 people, their food and drinks. Otherwise I highly suggest checking it out especially for the tea service.

Finally stopped into here on Friday. There was a line at 9 am which is great, glad they’re getting business. The decor inside is fun and charming as well.

However— they have a couple of paper menus that the print is so faded on them you have to strain to actually read them. On top of that, there is not a single price anywhere in house. No drink prices, no food prices. I was planning on ordering the maple latte, but to my surprise they were out of maple syrup at 9:05 in the morning! Bummer, because a lot of their drink menu is pumpkin forward and doesn’t offer many other options for the speciality lattes.

We ordered the eggs Benedict ( $15) a matcha ube latte ($9) a waffle ($9) and hashbrown ($8) and lastly avocado toast ($9) with a black coffee ($5). The food tasted great, very eye appealing but the portions are quite small. We thought the eggs Benedict could have used some toast or potatoes (that’s a big part of the theme) to mop up the tasty hollandaise sauce, especially for $15. The waffle did not taste like a waffle at all, it was good! But almost like a very dense biscuit.

I probably won’t return, because I don’t live too close but I could see this being a very fun place to be a regular.

My daughter (in her 20s) and I thoroughly enjoyed afternoon tea at Elevenses. The food was delicious, service was excellent and friendly, and atmosphere was charming. It was a perfect mother-daughter outing. We've eaten here several times, and will continue to be regulars. I highly recommend the afternoon tea; it will warm you up on these winter days.

name: PACIFIC MOON
document: PACIFIC MOON. cuisine: Chinese Japanese Seafood. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
Late one Monday evening in December, five of us were looking for a Pho noodle place in the vicinity and this Pacific Moon restaurant pops up on Google Maps.  It was nearing 9pm and this was the only restaurant not closing soon and stayed open late.

We get to the restaurant and the waitress immediately confirms that they do not serve Pho noodles.  I ask one of the waitresses why this restaurant is featured as selling Pho and she just shrugs.

We're hungry so we sit down and look at the menu and order Tempura Shrimp, Salmon Ceviche as appetizers and the four meals you see in the pictures - Loco Moco, Mark and Mike, Ramen and Pad Thai type of noodles.

When the appetizers came out, I immediately recognized the style of the tempura, which is not even supposed to be called tempura.  It was a Korean style Yachae Twigim (Fried Vegetable) with a piece of shrimp attached to it.  So I figure, okay, this must be a fusion place and really looked forward to having the rest of the meals.

The four entrees are served and we dive into the dishes only to realize that they are horrible renditions of popular ethnic food.
Mark and Mike bowl, the top listed specialty was UNEDIBLE.  I don't know what this dish is supposed to be, but I've never thrown away an entire meal because of some vile unfamiliar taste and smell.

I don't know if the chef ever had a Loco Moco.  Reminiscing about what I had in Hawaii, I was really hoping it would taste authentic but again, I didn't know what this dish was supposed to be.  I didn't even touch the noodles after this, and lastly, WHO SERVES INSTANT RAMEN in a restaurant?  I genuinely thought this was a Japanese style ramen when I was ordering it, only to be extremely frustrated when I saw Shin Ramyeon served.  It was not even cooked right - there was too much water so the soup was bland and the noodle was overcooked.

The servers were relatively prompt and friendly but this restaurant is taking advantage of people who never had authentic ethnic food and basically ripping them off.

The only authentic item I had all night here was bottled Stella Artois.

If you thought you were eating authentic food here, you have been lied to all along.  Find a better place to eat.

This place was not worth it. I went with friends and everyones food was either too salty or didnt taste like anything. Crab turnovers were straight onion. One person got the $30 dollar salmon just for it to be way overdone and dry. On the table they had chili oil that I kid you not was grey/brown from being burnt. The bathroom stall doors felt exposing and a ceiling fan looked like it was about to collapse. I told our waitress I was allergic to meat then found chunks of what I'm assuming was beef in my soup. All that just to have a bill of $50 for 2 people. The only good part was the house sake and the rest, disappointing. What a waste of time and money. Also we all were met with stomach pains immediately after.

Came here for a lunch meeting with coworkers and the experience was extremely disappointing.

We started with crab cakes and crab dip, both of which were pretty bad. Several people at the table didn’t care for the food at all. Unfortunately it only got worse from there. I ordered the sesame chicken and sat there while everyone else received their meals and finished eating. Turns out the restaurant completely forgot to place my order.

By the time they realized the mistake, the meeting was basically over. They did remove the item from the bill and the staff was polite, but that doesn’t change the fact that I sat through the entire meal without food while everyone else ate.

Between the poor food and completely forgetting my order, this was a very frustrating experience. I won’t be coming back.

name: Taste of Chengdu
document: Taste of Chengdu. cuisine: Szechuan Dim Sum Asian Fusion. located in Queens. with 4.2 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
All right... this place is a mix of emotions.
The flavor profiles are spot on. Considering the owners are from Chengdu. A city in the Szechuan province, the main chefs are from there too. So you're getting the full flavor profile.

Portion sizes..... this is where it gets tricky... and expensive. If you get the stir fried cabbage, a heaping portion comes out. Cabbage is cheap. But if you get the stir fried pea shoots, like I did, it's enough for maybe 2 people. In the picture, that's my hand over the entire plate.  Twice cooked pork, crispy beef, portion sizes are small...for about 25 dollars per plate...your money isn't going far. As I said, you're just there for the flavor profiles. I kind of think of it as a very expensive tasting. If asked, would I go back... the portion sizes and prices would keep me away. Rice...a staple in Chinese meals. Plain old long grain rice. For the price of the dishes, I was expecting something better, jasmine? Medium grain rice? Or is it that's what they only serve in Chengdu?

Service wise, very attentive, until it gets busy.  Then you have to flag down anyone to get your bill. Pretty much the same anywhere else.

Locations, there is one in Baldwin Park, and another one on West Colonial.

Like I said, go for the flavors, but be prepared to empty your wallet.

I am Chinese. This restaurant is rated 4.3 stars and I feel responsible to leave my review. We come here all the time if not twice a week. We have toured almost all the Chinese restaurants in Orlando that look promising on Google. Many of them have better reviews but non beat this one. This is THE BEST Chinese restaurant in Orlando. The Goat.

1. Majority of people who eat here are Chinese. Today I saw only one white person. They don’t cater to American taste. They are more on the salty / spicy side but they are authentic.

2. If you feel a numbing sensation it’s from the sichuan peppercorn- you aren’t having a stroke and don’t freak out.

3. If you see other Asian fusion restaurants with thousands is reviews and 4.9 stars in winter park, it’s ok. They aren’t better. That’s why you see mostly non Asian people go there.

4. It’s always fast service. Plates are clean. They don’t say “how are you my name is… I will be your server today” because they are from mainland China and they aren’t being rude to you. It’s just very authentic service style lol.

5. They have two locations - owner/boss is always at the west colonial one.

Love this restaurant. It is by far the best Sichuan cuisine restaurant in Orlando. The staff is always friendly and the food is always hot, fresh, and comes out quick. This restaurant's specialties are in the dishes from Sichuan province. Don't come here and order General Tso's chicken, you will be doing yourself a disservice.
Absolutely amazing food and service. I’m from China myself and this is hands down the best place in town. It’s like i’m back in my hometown again. 10/10 recommend

Highly recommend this place if you love spicy Sichuan cuisine!

google_reviews.text: One of the remaining old school sit down Chinese restaurants with white table cloth. Prices are fair, food is fresh, service is great. Have passed by Pearl East For years . Have been meaning to try it after seeing it on a cooking show . Didn’t know anything about it . Got the idea to go on New Years Eve and wow what an experience. Greeted by a nice hostesss and also the reservation desk. The ambiance just felt right very bright good noise level good energy . The menu is extensive and seems like classic Chinese cuisine along with some sushi. Great decor. So many great choices couldn’t decide so got the orange crispy duck and some pork soup dumplings. Both were very authentic and full of flavor reminds me of great Chinese food of years ago. Waiters and staff were very friendly it just seemed like a timeless place great experience . I recently visited Pearl East with a friend to celebrate a personal event. My friend had been to this restaurant several times and highly recommended it, so I decided to give it a try—and I’m glad I did!
From the moment we arrived, I was impressed. Pearl East has a humongous parking lot, with free parking both in front and behind the restaurant, including convenient spots for people with disabilities right in front of the entrance. We went for lunch, which is served from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. at a fixed price, with plenty of options on the menu.
For appetizers, I ordered fried dumplings, and my friend opted for an egg roll. For our main courses, I had shrimp with mixed vegetables, while my friend chose crispy shredded beef. Both meals came with fried rice, and we also enjoyed tea along with pistachio and strawberry ice cream for dessert. To accompany our meal, I had a glass of Prosecco, and my friend enjoyed a Margarita on the rocks.
While the portions of the appetizers weren't very large, the main courses were generous enough to leave us feeling full and satisfied.
The service was outstanding. Our waiter, Philip, was incredibly knowledgeable about the menu. He managed to always be attentive without being intrusive—never missing a sign when we needed him. He was constantly refilling our water glasses, even though we hardly noticed him moving around.
The ambiance of Pearl East is worth mentioning as well. The interior is elegant, with carpeted floors, beautifully arranged tables, and nice touches like cloth napkins. Even the bathroom was well-maintained, with glass doors and a remarkable chandelier that added to the overall experience. The restaurant was clean, quiet, and had a comfortable atmosphere, with enough space between tables for different group sizes. We also noticed security cameras inside, which added a sense of protection.
Overall, I highly recommend Pearl East for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion or just have a nice lunch while catching up with friends. My experience was delightful from start to finish, and I’m giving this place a well-deserved 5 out of 5. Thank you, Pearl East!

This is the best restaurant I have ever been to in my entire life. The food is fresh and delightfully gourmet and the staff provided outstanding beyond imaginable service. I am obsessed. And can’t wait to return. It is an amazing place for friends to meet for a night out if you’re looking for an A+ dining experience. Highly recommend!

name: Four Seasons Joyful
document: Four Seasons Joyful. cuisine: Szechuan Bubble Tea Juice Bars & Smoothies. located in Queens. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Going to keep rolling my eyes every time I see an Eater food critic rave about “best mapo tofu” they recently discovered at Breeze. Don’t get me wrong I’m not a Breeze hater, but mapo tofu here is where it’s at. In fact any staple chinese dish you name: Stir fried string beans, double cooked pork, cabbage casserole, mei cai braised pork belly, I’ve tried them all here and they are all at the level of what I’d expect to get from a halfway decent restaurant in China, with good, varied spices and that signature wok hay.

It will be pungent, in your face, sometimes more seasoned or oily than you’d like, but so is a lot of Chinese food when you eat out for hunan/sichuan food, known as “下饭菜” (dishes that accompany the rice). Order a veggie dish as a side for balance!

Have not tried the dim sum or American Chinese food here so will not comment, but those are not the reasons I go to this restaurant anyway. Just happy to have this gem of a restaurant/chef in the neighborhood, which had so few options (especially at the price point) before.

I ordered the beef short rib noodle soup, not knowing it is huge! No problem! The beef was tasty and melted in my mouth! Wonderful! The twice cooked pork was delicious, but I couldn’t eat much of it as the soup filled me up! Not to worry, I’ll enjoy it tomorrow. Very good dinner!
I ordered soup dumplings and beef and broccoli. The soup dumplings were ok. Not super soupy. And the beef and broccoli was crazy greasy! Decent taste but not fast.

I ordered the shredded beef with scallion and white rice lunch special, plus an extra serving of rice, as Chinese spots tend to give you so much meat and not enough veggies/rice to balance it out. Well… it felt like I had ordered onions with a bit of beef and a pinch of scallions lol. The onions were a tasty addition but the ratio neeeds to be adjusted! If I were someone who didn’t like onions I would’ve been livid about my meal as the menu didn’t even say it came with onions. Overall the food was good enough. And they never gave me the $2 extra white rice (nor the water that was supposed to come with the special) but I didn’t need it anyway, all I had leftover were a few bits of onion 🙃

The scallion pancakes were very good! Maybe could’ve had more scallion as well but overall I was satisfied.

I really didn’t want to give three stars, but my main meal just wasn’t what was advertised on the menu. I will return to try again and hope I can improve my rating!

Overall it’s a cute clean place with kind employees. And their bubble tea is really good!

Everything I've gotten here is on par with the best Szechuan food I've had elsewhere, including Chinatown. I love the double-cooked pork. Today, I thought I'd ordered a lunch special but failed to actually complete my order in time. So I changed course and ordered a dan dan noodle to go. It completely went off with delicious, herbacious, numbing, savory, and spicy flavors. Thanksfully I had some black vinegar at home that paired with it perfectly.

I hope the neighborhood continues to support this special that brings us big, bold flavors in an unpretentious, affordable package.

One thing to watch out for - the "stir-fried" beef is actually deep fried beef, and sweet. Which I typically love, but it's not the numbing spice flavor I was looking forward to. Still very good, though, well-made.

document: Shanghai Chinese Restaurant. cuisine: Chinese. located in Queens. with 3.3 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Listen, maybe my expectations have really cratered since moving here, but I was genuinely excited to see a Chinese takeout restaurant opening in the neighborhood that doesn’t also have subs on the menu. I ordered the pork with garlic sauce (listed as 鱼香肉丝 on the menu in Chinese which literally translates to “fish fragrance thinly sliced pork”). It’s a dish I would usually order to judge the quality and flavor of a Chinese restaurant. It is a very popular and basic dish, I think of it as the equivalent of a Margherita pizza in a Neapolitan pizza joint. It’s a dish that cannot hide behind a spicy sauce such as the dry pots (干锅） or the broth (水煮）dishes. It demonstrates the basic knife skills of the chef and whether they can get the sauce flavor and consistency right.

It left much to be desired, to say the least. The meat was tough (not silkened) and in various shapes, the sauce flavor is off and too runny. Deeply disappointing.

I also ordered the spicy pork wontons - they were under seasoned and the sauce was lacking. I can confirm that these are indeed made fresh in house because I saw one person making it when I was picking up.

I understand this is, after all, just a takeout restaurant. And they recently opened so I will return and try something else and report back.

Ordered the double cooked sichuan pork, stir fried green beans, and pickled cabbage cabbage + fish soup. They were all delicious, decently portioned and came with a small box of rice each. The soup in particular was a standout, really enjoyed it. It’s a takeout only spot, the whole place was really clean. 10% off if you pay in cash. I would order their chinese chinese food, not their American chinese food or dumplings which seem to be less good.

Our order was only ready 30 min after the estimated pick up time (so 50 min after ordering). Unfortunately they don’t pick up on the phone number provided when you place an order, so there’s no way to check if your order’s ready soon except to go there in person. And the waiting area is unheated….so wait for the text message saying your food’s ready!

I understand it’s a small operation that just opened and they seem understaffed, plus I ordered on a busy Friday night. Hopefully they can fix these issues soon! They are really nice. Five stars still because the food was really good and it’s awesome to have an actual chinese place in the neighborhood.

The place is just a long and narrow people with two employees. You order on a screen and wait. There are zero chairs or ambiance but the food is DELICIOUS. I would say the dumplings are on par with what we get from Rockville. Really, really good food.

Extremely good Szechuan food for Chinese takeout prices. Even the normal American Chinese takeout items like the pork fried rice noodles has some extra flavor, and the more specialized items like the dry hot pot are excellent examples of Szechuan cooking. On busy days like holidays, give them some extra time but otherwise it's a reasonable turnaround on take out orders. There's no seating at the restaurant, but you can save money by ordering direct and paying cash.

We ordered dan dan noodles and spicy chili dumplings after a long day of travel.  Not sure what they're trying to pass as dan dan noodles but there was barely any sauce, no ground pork and no peanuts. They're literally lo mein noodles with a tiny bit of oil so they don't stick together and nothing else. The dumplings were overcooked and the wrapper was falling apart when i tried to pick up with chopped sticks.  Tried calling the restaurant four times to get answers/partial refund and no answer.

name: SUKI Japanese Hibachi Ramen Noodles & Tea House
document: SUKI Japanese Hibachi Ramen Noodles & Tea House. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Queens. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Great hole in the wall Japanese hibachi. We were here for a hibachi dinner. The cook entertained us and cooked good food. The steak was perfect. Chicken was tender. Shrimp and salmon were very tasty. Great service. We made reservations but saw a lot of people just walk in.

Suki is delicious Japanese food! Small but cozy & clean restaurant. Great food & friendly service. They have a nice size menu & it’s not overwhelming so it’s easy to order. Our entrées came out piping hot, so delicious and flavorful.Highly recommend!

I’ve been coming here for years because the food is consistently flavorful and satisfying. One of the main reasons I’ve continued to return is the availability of vegetarian and vegan options, which can be hard to come by at ramen spots. As a vegan, I’ve always appreciated that they offer multiple plant-based ramen choices.

That said, I’ve never been impressed by the service—it’s generally been mediocre—but the quality of the food made up for it. However, I feel compelled to share a recent experience that has deeply affected my trust in this establishment.

During my last visit, I ordered a vegan ramen and requested a substitution for a different type of noodle. Although my request was initially overlooked, the staff quickly corrected it when I brought it to their attention, which I appreciated.

Unfortunately, the real issue came afterward. While eating, I unexpectedly bit into something with a distinct meaty texture. It had been hidden in the broth, so I didn’t notice it until it was already in my mouth. I immediately spit it out, and upon closer inspection—and with confirmation from my friend, the waitress, and the chef—it turned out to be pork.

As someone who is vegan, this was deeply upsetting. I explained this to the staff, and while they apologized, their response was concerning; they said people make mistakes. When I asked how they would have handled the situation had it been a food allergy, their answer was, “Call an ambulance.” They obviously didn’t care about the situation.

This interaction left me questioning the kitchen’s attention to detail and the seriousness with which they handle dietary restrictions. Mistakes happen, but the response to such a serious oversight should be handled with more care and professionalism.

Regrettably, I won’t be returning, and I caution others—especially those with allergies or strict dietary needs—to be very careful when dining here.

My husband and I ordered food from here for the first time (pickup). When I entered, there was almost nowhere to stand and nobody at the front podium. After waiting for 10 minutes, a woman came over and asked for the phone number from the order, stopped me halfway through, and then cleaned the hibachi counter, sat a group who was waiting, took drink orders, made drinks, and took food orders, but never returned to the front. There are now 4 people waiting for pickup orders. More time passes and a man comes a dumps a number of takeout orders on an open table and walks away. The four of us start scouring the bags to find our orders. It was chaos. Get home (it’s a 5 minute drive) and my food is ICE cold. We will never order from here again.
Cute seating available for groups and the food is great. Extensive menu. Appetizers were also great. Limited alcohol options but what is offered is very tasty.

google_reviews.text:
Outstanding restaurant all around! The location is very convenient with parking on the street or two lots across the street…all free. The are is also super safe with plenty of foot and vehicle traffic. The restaurant has a well appointed Asian vibe and is neat and clean. Service is very friendly and attentive. We found the menu to have a nice selection without being overwhelming as many Asian restaurant menus are. Now the food, WOW, beautifully presented and exceptionally tasty. Heads up they do not serve alcohol.

My friend recommended this restaurant, so my mother and I decided to stop in tonight since we were in the area. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, & we had really nice time while we were there.

When we entered my mom had brought her pizza with from mod to eat, but I wanted to try some ramen. The host looks & asks 2, I said yes, she won't be eating but I will. He was understanding of this and sat us at a booth table near the door. There was a woman sitting by my mom who sared her mango ice dessert with both of us (the flavor is just like eating a frozen ripe mango), & gave the rest of her jasmine hot tea to my mom. I ordered the combo meal of vegetable goyza and the beef ramen, and got the mango bubble tea (which had fresh fruit slices in it & a great mango flavor). The staff continually checked on us to see how things were & if we needed anything, they were also nice about getting things the woman asked for so she could shared her dessert & tea with us.

The host came over to our table when there was a lull in incoming patrons. He again was very nice and asked how my mango tea was, we discussed my mom's mod pizza, & the fact that the green tea is actually what they call just jasmin tea. It was an enjoyable conversation. Then, I got the check... But didn't realize it until after we left that I wasn't charged for my drink, I thought maybe the gentleman host had comped it. We will definitely be back again, this was the best dinning experience we've had in a long time!

I recently visited Kinya Ramen for the first time with my son, and it was an absolutely wonderful experience from start to finish. The moment we walked in, we were greeted with such genuine warmth. The gentleman at the front was incredibly pleasant and welcoming, setting the tone for a great meal. The entire staff was kind, attentive, and made us feel right at home.

The atmosphere at Kinya is beautiful 😍 everything is so thoughtfully designed, from the soft lighting to the clean, modern decor that still feels cozy and inviting. It’s truly picturesque; every corner looks like it was created with care, making the whole dining experience feel special.

And of course, the food was fantastic — comforting, flavorful, and beautifully presented. You can tell they take pride in every detail, from the rich broth to the artful arrangement of toppings.

We love Kinya! My family dines here when we have a taste for ramen outside of our home. The servers are so sweet and the food is delicious. We love the apps and the customizable ramen. Our son creates his own bowl each time. Of all the places we have gone for ramen, this is one of the best. The noodles are tasty and the broths are flavorful. Their chicken is yummy and not weird looking. Also the bubble teas are delicious. This is a must-try!

Kinya Ramen and Sushi delivered a memorable dining experience from the first bite to the last. The meal showcased thoughtful preparation and bold, well-balanced flavors. The Purple Sweet Potato Korokke was a true standout — beautifully textured, visually striking, and filled with a naturally sweet, creamy center that paired perfectly with its crisp exterior.

The ramen was deeply comforting, with a rich, layered broth and toppings that felt both generous and intentional. The noodles were perfectly cooked, absorbing flavor without losing their bite.
