We visited La Casa in Bronxville hoping to enjoy their brunch. We arrived around 3:30 PM, well before the posted 4:00 PM brunch cutoff. Unfortunately, things started off on the wrong note as soon as we were seated, our server handed us dinner menus. When we politely asked if brunch was still available, the waiter seemed annoyed by the question, which made the start of the experience feel a little uncomfortable. Despite that, we decided to stay and give the food a try.
We ordered their carne asada which was a small fish compared to their brunch price. We also ordered the chilaquiles which were drenched in the salsa Verde, eggs and bite sized steak bites. This meal cost $24. The tortillas were soggy along with the mini slices of avocado they scarcely provided. The menu overall for a brunch option was not well thought out for an visually appealing restaurant. Everything seemed mediocre and basic. The cost of upgrading your protein from one dish to the next changed, even though it was the same protein. To add steak to one dish, it was $10 but to another it was $14. Very confusing. The server basically also rushed us to order.  We tried to pick something off the dessert menu, but pretty much it was your basic churros and flan at a price point of $13.00. This is a very unoriginal, mediocre and catered restaurant, to the community it's in. The price points on the menu options are ridiculous when you have food that lacks seasoning and a waitstaff that doesn't check back on the tables, or ask to refill your coffee. I'd recommend try another Authentic spot, that doesn't rush you and actually serves delicious food.

The restaurant was super busy, and check-in felt a little chaotic, but I have to give major credit to the hostess. She handled the crowd with patience and professionalism, even going above and beyond by bussing tables and bringing drink orders. She deserves a raise for sure.

Unfortunately, the food was underwhelming. The guacamole really needed salt, the beans were dry, and overall the flavors just didn’t impress. If you’ve never had authentic Mexican or Spanish cuisine, you might find it decent, but for me it fell flat.

I wouldn’t come back for the food, but I could see myself stopping in for drinks thanks to the good service and atmosphere.

Street parking available. Free after 7

Casa Bronxville offers a pleasant dining experience in a well-designed space with a stylish, modern vibe. The ambiance is inviting and the staff is courteous and attentive, which definitely adds to the overall experience.

That said, the food itself felt pretty standard—well-prepared but not particularly memorable. The menu leans toward safe, familiar choices rather than bold or creative dishes. It’s the kind of place that’s easy to enjoy, but not one that stands out for culinary innovation or flavor.

Drinks were solid, and service was efficient throughout the evening. It’s a good option for a casual dinner or a nice night out, but if you’re looking for something that truly surprises or impresses, this might not be the place.

What can I say, another incredible meal at La Casa Bronxville! Lately, I’ve been sticking to a few favorite spots, and this place always gives me a reason to come back. Each time, I try something new from the menu, and I’m consistently amazed by the delicious flavors, high quality, and beautiful presentation.

Today’s favorites include the savory steak taco and the tasty chicken taco (see pictures below), along with some delectable churros for dessert—simply incredible! The service is excellent, and the staff are consistently warm and inviting, making you feel right at home. It's truly a local treasure.

We came here to try something interesting and this place did not disappoint. I opted to get an outdoor reservation, and I'm glad that I did. After we arrived, the restaurant was quickly filling up. The staff greeted us as we entered and they were very welcoming and seated us quickly.

We started off with some Pellegrino, chips and guacamole, and ceviche. Normally I don't like ceviche but I wanted to try it and it was actually very good. I'm not sure what kind of meat was in it, but it doesn't matter because it was absolutely succulent. The guacamole was fantastic as well, and the fresh fried chips were to die for. Our appetizers were accompanied by a spicy margarita and tamarind margarita, both of which were some of the best margaritas I've ever had. Beware, the spicy one is actually spicy and I absolutely loved it. We got a second set of margaritas, but the second one I ordered had mezcal in it, which was equally as delicious.

For the entrees, my date got the Carne Asada medium rare, and I got two pairs of tacos; The Carnitas and the Oyster tacos. The presentation of all three dishes made us even hungrier. The carne asada was perfectly cooked, and perfectly portioned. The chimichurri and avocado went very well with the steak, and the side of rice beans and maduros complemented it so well. The tacos are a bit on the smaller side, similar to street tacos. The saving grace is that they're packed with so much meat that you don't even notice the smaller tortilla size. The carnitas was easily the favorite of the two for us. Whatever sauce is served on the side with it makes it taste a thousand times better, and that's not saying that they're not good without it. Either way you can't go wrong with them. The oyster tacos on the other hand weren't a favorite of ours. It tasted a little too fishy for us, which I don't think is necessarily a bad thing. I think it's for someone who wants that flavor, which neither of us particularly did but I enjoyed it anyway. Overall the food was spectacular, and even though the oyster tacos weren't our favorite, they were still good overall.

The service here was excellent and quick. As stated prior, they had a good amount of people inside the restaurant yet we didn't have to wait long for food or for a waiter to check in on us. We did sit outside, so I can't comment too much about the interior and how clean it was. From the quick glance that we got from the entrance, the restaurant seemed very well maintained and cozy.

Overall, this restaurant was a fantastic find. I would highly recommend it to anyone wanting to try a different take on Mexican food in a cozy romantic atmosphere. The only reason I didn't give it five stars was because of the oyster tacos. Again, they weren't terrible by any means, but not what we were expecting flavor wise. I recommend making a reservation sense they're easier enough to make and it would guarantee you a seat. I forgot to mention that parking here is pretty easy as there is a garage right across the street, but you may get lucky finding parking in front of the entrance. Nonetheless, if you're thinking about trying this restaurant definitely give it a go. We will definitely be returning!

name: The Red Maple
document: The Red Maple. cuisine: Breakfast & Brunch Burgers Sandwiches. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text:
We were looking for a special place to celebrate a birthday and online reviews had said The Red Maple was good so we made a reservation.

Service overall was not good.  Literally the day before we got a message saying that the restaurant only had two seating options available as there were other tables or we could cancel; given the late notice we chose the wine rooms.  While private, it was also secluded so if we needed anything we would have to go and get the staff since there were infrequent checkups.

To add insult to injury, the food was not that great.  We had the spinach casserole to start followed by the catfish, shrimp and hamburger.  while portion size was decent, flavor and taste quality were lacking.

overall poor service and average to below average food made this a disappointing experience

Phenomenal all around! Servers were fantastic, attentive, and very personable. The spinach casserole appetizer was a great start. Our 4 year old loved the kid's Catfish and fries. My wife had the Catfish Pecan and I had the Fig Glazed Roasted Duck, both paired with Sweet Potato Souffle. 10/10 for everything we ate and really a place to return to on future nights out!

Phenomenal 👌
We've passed this place so many times and finally decided to give it a try, so glad that we did! AMAZING 👏

The steak was like butta and was seasoned so perfectly. One of the best steaks I've ever had, hands down. I loved the baked potato as well.

Excellent service, really cool vibe, neat decor, and I loved that there's a cemetery behind the venue.. I thought that was cool 😁

We were going to another restaurant down the block, but they didn't have parking, which the Red Maple does have across the street. It was an amazing find. The restaurant itself is quite unique as it is what appears to be a large converted residence. It is beautiful and comfortable inside. There are several dining areas and a dimly lit swanky bar area. They take walk-ins and reservations. There is no dress policy, but the clientele does dress nicely. Our server Maria was wonderful! The food was very good. This was a wonderful find for us. If you're in the neighborhood or surrounding area, go get yourself a wonderful and relaxing meal.
Excellent food and service! We were there on steak night and the steak was amazing. Plus, we finished with an awesome cream brulee. Highly recommended!

name: Soledad
document: Soledad. cuisine: Mexican. located in Bronx. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
What an incredible dining experience! From the moment we sat down, everything about this restaurant felt warm, welcoming, and thoughtfully curated.

The food was absolutely amazing — every dish that came to the table was beautifully presented and packed with flavor. You can truly tell that a lot of care goes into both the quality of the ingredients and the presentation. It felt like every plate was crafted with attention to detail.

Beyond the food, the service made the experience even more special. Our server Pablo was outstanding — attentive, friendly, and professional. He made sure we were comfortable the entire time and gave great recommendations. Nicolas, the runner, was efficient and kind, making sure everything arrived promptly and checking in with a smile. And a special thank you to the Manager, Rebeca, who was incredibly lovely and welcoming. She took the time to make us feel valued and ensured everything was perfect for our table.

It’s rare to find a place that delivers both exceptional food and such genuine hospitality, but this restaurant truly does. We left happy, satisfied, and already looking forward to coming back. Highly recommended! 🌟

Came here for a few weeks ago and loved it! I think it's relatively new to the area but I would definitely come back again! For a Tuesday evening it was pretty lively which bodes well for its popularity I think. Despite being busy, the service was efficient and staff members were friendly! We tried a few different items including the tuna tartar tacos, ensalada de verano, enchiladas soledad, pato con mole (duck carnitas), and pasta seca. I have to say the tacos and enchiladas were my favorite but there's so much more on the menu we didn't get to try. For a group of 5 people this was a good  amount of food though I'm sure we could have finished another entree if we tried. Will definitely return in the future!

We had a great meal at Soledad last night. We had a reservation for four, and were seated promptly at wonderful table at the front windows. Rafael took great care of us, considering he was also tending to a rather large group sitting on the other side of the door. Modelos were fresh. Drinks and cocktails were delicious, but took a while to make their way from the bar. We had the Carnitas Sushi to start. Then the ladies both got the Loma Saltido, while I had the Carne Asasa, and my friend ordered the Pato Mole. All dishes were so delicious and different from most other Latin fare that we’ve enjoyed. The desserts were also top-tier- churro sundae and Zanahoria (Carrot) Tres Leches Cake. I highly recommend this place for an elevated date spot- prices weren’t cheap (just under $100/pp) but the food and drink were memorable, and the female manager who stopped by our table was so hospitable and invited us back with our dogs to sit out front. All four of us can’t wait to return!

I’ve been to Soledad a few times, twice for brunch and once for dinner. The food is beyond delicious and presented really well. The service is always friendly and the whole place has such a nice vibe. I’ll be back many more times!

We went to Soledad last night for the first time. We enjoyed the food, but especially the drinks. It's a great place to have a date. Rebeca and Carla were super friendly and made our experience even better.

name: The Good Good
document: The Good Good. cuisine: New American Lounges Cocktail Bars. located in Bronx. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Never a bad meal at The Good Good.
Consistency is key...and that is never over looked at this restaurant.
From the moment you walk in and are greated, to the waitress staff and the bartender the energy is always vibrating on a pleasant HiGH!
Always a pleasure to visit.
There is not a Miss on the menu.
My faves honestly are the curried carrots and Brussels sprouts (minus the Bacon...sorry- My Mom would be proud...lol)

Went here for the first time on a post valentines date. Really surprised by the amount of intentional cuisine there. The service was pretty good I forgot our servers name but he was laid back and kind. I took his recs and they were perfect. the bartender made great drinks also for I got the house sour. The fried chicken was a a good 8.7/10 I would get again but would have enjoyed more breading. The cod fish fritters was at 10/10 no question along with the Brussels. Probably wouldn’t get the plantains again just liked them more ripe (personal preference). I enjoyed the jerked mushrooms too. Definitely coming back.

We visited this place for Valentine’s Day and had a fantastic time!

The atmosphere is lovely and very soul-warming. While the seating is a bit snug, it actually adds to the overall cozy vibe. The interior is fascinating to look at with so many cool details—especially the massive, stylish arrangements of budding branches and dried flowers. They really set a unique mood. Plus, they have a cloakroom (coat check) and the background music was spot on.
Food-wise: I had the burger and my wife had the salmon with egg. Both dishes were prepared perfectly and were absolutely delicious. The prices are very reasonable for this level of quality.

A huge shoutout to the staff—the servers were incredibly sweet and attentive, keeping an eye on everything without being intrusive. We’ll definitely be back!

i had a nice time brunching at the good good and i am open to returning! i had the fried chicken benny which was good and the pulman french toast which was delicious! the service was good and the interior was cute as well. and i always love to support a black-owned business! i would def recommend to other people looking for a cute brunch spot.

If you know the Edge then you already know what to expect! Fantastic menu that represents a true fusion of Caribbean flavors honoring the el barrio/harlem neighborhood as well as a solid Manhattan haunt for the kind of brunch that New Yorkers/True Yorkers love. Solid fish options and the aesthetic is quite different from their west side cousin. Enjoyed it and highly recommend. Great staff behind the bar - well done.

name: The Row Harlem
document: The Row Harlem. cuisine: Lounges Breakfast & Brunch Desserts. located in Bronx. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
It was so good !! It's not my first time but for my husband yes and we went for our marriage anniversary, he loved the food!  We got of corse the macaroni and cheese, the best in the city, food presentation as well always nice, atmosphere amazing,good music, perfect vibes ! we love the fact it's small cozy and so nice just perfect.
When I called for to make a reservation, staff and the manager are wonderful,  hospitality 💯 and all that in the most beautiful place in the city, Harlem !  This place and harlem location means a lot  sentimentaly,

This restaurant was over-hyped. They have a "no hats" rule, but apparently only for men. Also, they serve canned sodas. Got the salmon plate with "collard greens" and mashed potatoes. Plus oxtail empanadas and fries. It was overall bad. It should note STEAMED collard greens. Because that's all it was. Lightly cooked leaves. The empanada was just a little slightly seasoned meat in crust. And a lot of air. I was not a fan. But the BBQ jerk sauce wasn't bad. The fries were really good. Did I mention that they also serve canned sodas? Servers were polite, but loudly discussed their sports bets while they enjoyed football games on TV. There were no follow up visits to refill water or check on food quality or correctness.  It certainly didn't warrant an automatic 20% gratuity. Overall, the price doesn't match the food quality or atmosphere provided.

Saturday afternoon shortly after opening with just a few patrons in the space was the perfect low-key enviornment for a nice lunch.  Very good start!

Ordered the frozen GOTTI which is citrusy, refreshing, not too sweet, and has a '1-2-punch' that kinda' sneaks up on you.  Very good sneaky drink!

Ordered the brussel sprouts (which were gone as soon as they hit the table), lobster mac & cheese, and the kale caesar salad w/ salmon.  Very good!  Very delicious!

Our server, Sky, gave us the perfect balance of attention and distance.  He made sure that the food came out hot ... and that the drinks were served cold.  Very impressive!

If you looking for a low-key and quaint spot this is a place to go in Harlem. It's a bar/restaurant with great music. Nice vibes!!!
I went for drinks with friends we sat at the bar and listened to music. The drinks are strong.
The bartender is friendly and attentive to her customer's wants. She was engaged with her patrons in conversation. That's awesome!!
The prices are reasonable for a NYC bar.
The place is not big but enough for you to enjoy the atmosphere.
The location is quite busy. So, finding parking is not easy. There is street parking if you grab a space.

Very small, yet intimate, venue. Not really suited for large party walk-ins...but they will try to accommodate. Parties of 2 to 4 at best. It fills quickly. There is additional outdoor seating which was closed when we dined. If you're looking for some place to quickly dine n dash this AINT it. Bring some good company and good energy, they definitely serving a steamy fusion of comfort food for the soul. We were a group of 5 (walk-in) from Htown and waited at the bar about an hour for a table. I utilized this time to enjoy a frozen Sangria and catch up conversation w/my group. The sangria is EVERYTHING... and yes, you only need ONE if you ladylike, two if ya' flirty, lol. Once seated our food came out within 20-25 minutes...but NOTHING was re-heated, microwaved, etc.... all cooked to order!

The jerk mac n cheese is a masterpiece and it's large enough for 2 to share. Nuff said.

The oxtail samosas with white bean were extremely tender and seasoned well (2 per order). You can tell it was pulled and stuffed by hand and cooked to order. Mine had more fatty meat but the fat was tender and flavorful too. My only suggestion is to have a sauce option other than BBQ.

I also appreciated the sautéed collard greens which were sooo flavorful and HEALTHY since the life wasn't cooked out of them. My only suggestion is to either get rid of the large stems or tenderize them a lil' more.

Last, our table had 2 orders of the lamb chops which they cleaned to the bone! Overall, I enjoyed the vibe and being able to taste the passion added into the food. A piece of my heart was left in this gem of a place. I'll be back!

document: Madison Cafe and Grill. cuisine: Lebanese Breakfast & Brunch American. located in Bronx. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I had breakfast at this place and everything was absolutely wonderful. The food was delicious and beautifully presented. The Turkish music and overall atmosphere made me feel like I was traveling somewhere far away, which made the experience even more special.
Special thanks to my waiter, Hector, who was incredibly polite, friendly, and genuinely made my morning brighter. And many compliments to the chef for the amazing food. Thank you for such a memorable experience! I can’t wait to come back!

Today I went to Madison Café & Grill and had an excellent experience.
They serve the best pancakes in Edgewater, all gluten-free, homemade, and prepared fresh to order.

The food is fresh and truly authentic, with a delicious Mediterranean touch. The hummus and babaganoush were absolutely exquisite, full of flavor and perfectly made.

The pancake I highly recommend is the lemon ricotta pancake — incredibly soft, light, and with the perfect balance between sweetness and citrus 🍋. Truly delicious.

The service was outstanding. We were taken care of by Héctor, a very kind, attentive server who was always happy to help and answer any questions.

I highly recommend this place and would definitely come back.

We love having breakfast at Madison Café & Grill; it's a great option here in Edgewater, primarily because it opens very early and, more importantly to me, because most of their dishes are not just very good, but you can feel the emphasis they place on using quality ingredients to offer real food—food that is both nourishing and enjoyable.
​The breakfasts are particularly excellent. They have many choices, and our favorite is the Mediterranean Breakfast, but the Eggs Benedict are also delicious. Just keep in mind that they don't allow flexibility for ingredient substitutions, so I recommend trusting the chef's suggestions, which the staff is always happy to gently share.
​We love the drinks; the coffee is particularly good, and if you like it very strong, we highly recommend the Turkish coffee—it's exquisite.
​I'd like to make a special mention of all the servers here. They always greet us with a smile, their treatment is impeccable, they are kind, and they know exactly how to make patrons feel right at home. This truly makes a difference.
​It's not a very expensive place, but it's not cheap either. It is definitely worth enjoying the experience.

Our waiter, Hector, was so kind and very willing to help and give advice on how to eat each dish to its fullest. The food was amazing, not too overly seasoned. The pita chips were delicious and the minted lemonade was amazing. The service and atmosphere were great. Hector was an awesome waiter and made the overall atmosphere better.

EDIT: Came here once again and our waiter Hector once again was polite and the food was great as before. Everyone we come here it is a delight.

EDIT 2: I came here once again and it’s just as it was before. Every time I come here I always leave happy and full, and Hector and everyone else is always welcoming. The food is delicious and has a nice balance of flavors.

First time coming here and it won’t be the last! The food and service were FABULOUS. Hector, our server was attentive and friendly…..but did I mention the FOOD??? I have never tasted a “Benedict “ as wonderful as the Birria Benedict! Presentation of the food was next level. This was truly an added gem to our travels.

name: Augustine's Salumeria
document: Augustine's Salumeria. cuisine: Italian Cocktail Bars Sandwiches. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: Host, waiter, buses, and Manager were al very attention. My water glass was never empty. Generous wine pours. Mussels, ox tail gnocchi and cannoli were perfect. The mussel presentation was only amplified by the smoky, tarragon aroma. Wow! Will be back!

This spot has become our absolute go-to for local date nights and special celebrations! The staff goes above and beyond, ensuring top-notch service and exceptional food. One of the things I love most is the ever-changing seasonal menu—always fresh, always inspired by the best produce from the farmers market. Every visit feels like a new but familiar experience, and we can't wait to come back!

Modern Italian restaurant with sophisticated menu options.  In other words, this place rocks!  This is not the place for Chicken Parm.  However, if you're looking for interesting Italian menu choices, then this is the right place.  We started with the Burrata, but this was no ordinary Burrata.  The squash puree with maple dressing was an incredible, delectable combination.  For my main, I had the Mafalda pasta.  It was fresh, tasty, and not salty.  In other words, it was delicious.  We also had the Roasted Brussels Sprouts as a side.  They were crispy and mouth watering.  My wife had the Linguine Nero which was simply amazing.  For dessert, we shared the Cinnamon Bread Pudding.  It was fresh, warm,  moist and very comforting.  Service was incredibly friendly and gracious.  Overall, an excellent dining experience.

Had such a beautiful dinner at Augustine’s and every bite felt like a little celebration. First off, let’s talk about the Fairy Godmother cocktail - gorgeous deep purple, topped with a sparkly rock candy stick, and totally delicious. A drink that’s as fun to look at as it is to sip!

We started with the mussels - plump, perfectly cooked, and served in a rich tomato broth with sausage and fennel. Just wow. Perfectly mopped up with that hearty slice of seeded bread.

The Cauliflower Diablo was another standout - perfect texture, spicy, and finished with pine nuts for the perfect texture pop. If you like heat, don’t miss it. The grilled asparagus and cheese croquettes were another unexpected star - runny yolk, creamy center, and just the right amount of char. Who knew that combo would be such a hit?

The pappardelle with beef cheek was rich and comforting, like the best homemade Sunday dinner you never made. And then there was the tiramisu - so airy and light it basically floated off the plate. The cocoa powder and powdered sugar dusting made it extra dreamy.

From cocktails to dessert, every course was thoughtful and delicious. Thank you to the team for making it such a special evening—we left full, happy, and already plotting our next visit!

Great restaurant.  The space is small so it can get loud during peak dining times. The menu has many standard Italian dishes with interesting twists. The service was great and our waiter was well versed in the full menu. He answered a few questions and led us to some great dishes we might has overlooked.

google_reviews.text:
We came here to this super cozy and chill restaurant that feels really friendly and welcoming for any type of crowd.

We sat down by their lovely flower pots and ordered a classic burger and a salmon burger. Honestly, I’d give the salmon burger a 10 out of 10—it’s unbelievably delicious! The classic burger was tasty too, but you’ve got to come here for their salmon burger, it’s just amazing!
Considering the neighborhood and location, their prices are really great; especially since the food is super fresh and high-quality.
I definitely recommend not just walking past this place!

My friend and I were recently raving about a few neighborhood restaurants when someone overheard us and recommended we try the Grand Feast on 102nd Street. We both live on West End Ave so we made it a point to try it for lunch—and we’re so glad we did! The atmosphere was cozy with nice background music, and best of all, our meals and the service were excellent. I had the burger, and I honestly can’t remember having a fresher, more delicious one. My friend loved her dish as well. Naturally, we had to try the desserts: she enjoyed the tiramisu, and I had an incredibly moist carrot cake. Philippe, the attentive and friendly maître d’, happily brought hot milk for my coffee. Also, kudos to the talented chef, Jose! It’s a pleasure having such delicious and well-prepared food in our neighborhood. We’ll definitely be back many more times.

My wife and I stopped by for a glass of wine and thoroughly enjoyed it. We also ordered some nachos with steak, which perfectly complemented our quick but delicious meal. I highly recommend this place!

I read in another view that the caramelized onions on their cheeseburger were fantastic. I was judging for a cheeseburger and love caramelized onions. This burger was so much more. The roll was so soft and delicious. The fries were piping hot. It was perfection.

And my server was absolutely charming. This will be the place I go when I need a good burger. Apparently they also have a great brunch Wednesday through Sunday with an outrageous amount of food for $20. I’ll report back!
Came here for brunch. Got the eggs Benedict with Canadian bacon. Excellent! My regards to the chef. The waitress was so kind and considerate as well! Highly recommend

google_reviews.text: My twin brother and I chose The Hamilton for lunch to celebrate our birthday, and it was an outstanding experience. The atmosphere was welcoming, the food was beautifully prepared, and every dish we tried was flavorful and satisfying. What truly elevated our visit was the exceptional service. CJ, the manager, ensured everything ran smoothly and made us feel genuinely valued, while Emma from the crew was attentive, friendly, and professional throughout our meal. Their hospitality turned a lovely lunch into a memorable celebration. We had a fantastic experience and would highly recommend The Hamilton to anyone looking for great food and excellent service.

Hamilton Restaurant in D.C. is a consistently great spot that delivers on food, drinks, and atmosphere. It’s one of those places that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for meeting friends or out-of-town guests.
The menu is extensive and well-executed, with something for everyone, and everything is prepared with care and solid flavor. Portions are generous, quality is reliable, and the dishes strike a nice balance between comfort and polish.
The drink selection is excellent, and the space itself is lively without feeling chaotic — energetic, classic D.C. vibes with professional, attentive service.
Overall, Hamilton is a dependable favorite in the city: good food, good drinks, great location, and an atmosphere that always feels right. A solid choice anytime you’re downtown.

The food is great but let’s talk about the music venue. This place is what those of us who are 45+ and used to go to the 930 club need. It has food, it has service, it has tables and CHAIRS. Don’t get me wrong we still stand to dance and carry on but to have the option to sit, sip our drinks *that get brought to us* and eat chicken wings in the process is just next level civilized. The vibe is speak-easy and super chill. The service can be a bit slow, but honey, I got a chair, so just bring me two at a time.

This deserves better than its current rating!  Having tried Old Ebbit’s and Joe’s last trip to DC, tried Hamilton post-show and was I glad. The decor was warm and nice, service was attentive and friendly and good note was made of my son’s nut allergy and food properly marked safe. The dishes were top notch and it was hard to agree which was best amongst pork chop, lobster pasta and short rib/meatball rigatoni. The sides were all well executed and desserts of apple tart and chocolate bread pudding polished off happily. We also like the bird theme and all the bird art work!

Took my European family here for lunch after walking the mall for a few hours. The lobster roll was stuffed filled with lobsters in a delicious brioche bun. Accompanied by crunchy fries, and homemade coleslaw. This was a perfect pick me up. My dad had the lobster pasta. The crustaceans were juicy, and they didn’t skimp on the meat. I didn’t get a photo of the octopus ink colored linguine with fruit di mare but my nephew confirmed that it was absolutely delicious. Our server was pretty busy during the lunchtime rush. We thoroughly enjoyed it though. Definitely a great spot to take out of towners.

151 is a hidden gem 💎.  I love the vibes here.  My Seastar introduced me last year and it's been my regular spot since.  The food and happy hour selection is great! If you ask for a manager,  they're polite when they approach you and will quickly  resolve your concerns.  You can wait long if there's one server during the week or a big party. My daughter and I came as she returned from college.  I was shocked 😲 to see that the Happy Hour menu changed drastically.  There were barely any items,  thankfully my wings were still there.  So it's a win 🏆! However, my favorite coconut margaritas were gone guys! We could no longer get flavored margaritas at the HH price. It would be $17 versus $8.  Also, we could now only order 2 food items at HH price. Thats insane. I asked for a manager in disbelief as there was no mention of changes prior. The manager accommodated us, which I greatly appreciated. However,  I'll honestly say that the changes in HH has reduced my frequency as the deals aren't that great anymore. The overall vibe is still dope 👌🏾and I always enjoy when I'm there.

We need a loyalty program for VIP guest so that we continue to get the deals were accustomed to! We recommend you guys.  We host large tables and it's a favorite dating spot for me as I feel safe being familiar with all the staff present. So please hear us!! We want the old menu and schedule for HH. I get maybe not on the weekends as most restaurants don't usually have, however it also set you apart from others!🙏🏾

google_reviews.text:
The Snug bar is a brilliant Irish pub located in Wantagh just across from the train station!
The bar is decorated really nicely and it is very clean! There is a long bar with stools, loads of seating around the bar and great back patio that is outside to relax in if you are looking to be in the open air!
The satff are really friendly and attentive. We had a great time chatting to Kim since it was 16:30 in the day when we were there and there was only a few people in the bar at that time.
I have to give a shout out to Kim as she was really great!
For drinks, there was a fantastic selection of Whiskey and there is a nice selection of beers to choose from as well.
We decided to have a couple of pints of Guinness that were really cold and they hit the spot on a hot day!
There are a few tv's dotted around the bar but I highly recommend coming here for the company rather than watching something on tv!
One major point to note for any Irish person who may enter The Snug, is that they offer a cheese Toastie made with "Brennan's Bread"! As any Irish person living abroad will know its hard to come by good Irish bread!
If you are in the Wantagh area I recommend that you stop by for a couple of cold pints of Guinness in The Snug near the Wantagh train station!

This latest Irish bar in Wantagh lives up to it's name. A quaint little place just off the train station that makes you feel snug. The drinks are great with both indoor and outdoor seating arrangements, but most importantly is the staff. Joe is the best bartender in town hands down, you can't find a nicer or more friendly guy, on top of serving you a delicious drink. The place has a few TVs for any major games being played and some small food options in case you want something to snack on. Will gladly come back here for drinks any time. Warning though, dedicated parking leaves something to be desired, your best bet is to park in the train station parking lot behind the building or across the street and walk a little.

She pointed at the tables so I assumed that meant I'm free to sit wherever. I sat down and after 5 min I had not been given a menu or offered a beverage. So then I thought maybe there's no table service, so I approached another staff member and asked him if I must go to the bar to order or if there's table service. He said there's table service and so I asked him for a menu and took a seat. He brought me the drinks menu and promptly disappeared. After another 5 minutes, I flagged down a staff member who was checking on a table close to mine and I asked her if there is a food menu and she said yes and gave me one. google_reviews.text: The view of the water was the highlight of my visit. You could see the strong currents and boats passing by. For three diners, $122 (without tip included), we had two soft drinks, the 16 oz ribeye with fingerling potatoes and mashed potatoes side, firecracker shrimp, cup of broccoli cheddar soup, bowl of broccoli cheddar soup, french fries, cheese grits and the cheese cake brownie. I noticed other reviews of the soup had a much better presentation with scallions and seasoning, but ours last night had bacon pieces thrown on top. Everything was absolutely delicious. The broccoli cheddar soup special was a puree, the steak was perfect and the grits were excellent. Vegetarian options are limited, so I ordered "sides" to make my meal. That doesn't bother me and I'm used to it. It would be great if they had a veggie burger or something more substantial than a salad offered, but I'm happy with the food I had!

I've been hearing about and seeing this restaurant on IG. So I booked a reservation, the best decision ever.
This restaurant is everything and then some. The decor is upscale but not stuffy so you can still enjoy. You can tell alit of thought wss hiven to the concept of the space and decor. The staff at the front desk is very welcoming. The atmosphere of Native is a whole vibe. The music had us both singing a dancing in our seats, kudos to the DJ. The whole place was a vibe!!
We celebrated my niece's birthday there last night and I loved it!! From the food to the entertainment to the tasteful decor everything was top-notch!!
There was a lengthy wait to be seated but that was the end of my complaints everything else was phenomenal and in hindsight the wait was worth it!! Try to be back very soon with my husband so he can experience Native Harlem!!

What a night!! A few friends and I went to Native on a Sunday evening and we had an absolute blast!! First the host staff was very kind and welcoming, once seated I was pleasantly  surprised that they had a DJ.  We were moving before even sitting down.  We ordered the Suya wings, must try! they are soo good!! The calamari was our other appetizer dish, it was crispy, not chewy, and greasy.  Loved them and the sauce provided.  Our mains were the jollof with goat, jollof with snapper and salmon and mashed potatoes.  Baby!! All the food was scrumptious. The drinks! Woo, hats off to the mixologist! I had the native punch and another pineapple drink(?) both were very good.  My friends also raves about their drinks.  The price range was comparable to what any NY restaurant would charge for an establishment of the same caliber.  I was very pleased.  The cherry on top were the dancers! They have an elevated stage in the middle of the dinning room where dancers perform coordinated dancers.  They even pull people up there and leave them through some dances.  It was so entertaining and a nice touch!!! They even walked around to engage the guests.  The DJ kept the night flowing quite well.  The crowd joined in on a few dances and filled the aisles as we collectively got down!! Awesome night, superb food, great service, top notch experience!! I'll be back!!

It was my first time there with  my friend I was impressed how beautiful the restaurant is. The red velvet was good not too sweet.  We got the chance to see dancing performance🕺🏿💃🏾🕺🏿💃🏾  there it was excellent 👏🏾👏🏾 I will definitely go back again. Thank you

What an aesthetically pleasing atmosphere! Very cute for a lunch or dinner date, and I can definitely see it as a nice after-work spot.
Let me start with the service our waitress was awesome. She suggested a few items from both the food and drink menus. We both tried the “Native Lunch,” which was very tart similar to rum punch. I didn’t end up ordering a second drink and switched to the Water No Get Enemy, which was actually really tasty!
For my entrée, I ordered the escovitch fish with red stew rice. I honestly didn’t expect to receive half of a fried snapper with jasmine rice and a side of red stew sauce. I wouldn’t necessarily recommend it there were way too many bones, and from my understanding, escovitch fish is typically prepared with peppers and more of that classic tangy topping. I probably should have asked more questions beforehand.
My date ordered the Kingston jerk chicken, which he enjoyed. However, in my opinion, none of the dishes were really worth the price.
The seating was cozy, but the velvet chairs and couches tend to trap food, so it seems like they would need to be vacuumed after each party leaves. The bathroom was super cute again, very aesthetically pleasing!
One major downside: I was freezing! It was way too cold and honestly killed the vibe. I was this close to putting my coat back on.
Overall, it’s a cute spot with great ambiance, but definitely overpriced for what you get.

google_reviews.text:
I am usually very good about leaving positive reviews where I enjoy the food... I have to say while the food and tea were wonderful I was quite surprised at the fact that their bathroom was out of order. Of course at first I didn't think anything of it and respectfully asked where I could go to wash my hands and use the bathroom. I was told to walk over to Ralph's and so I went. To my surprise I was told the bathroom inside Ralph's was out of order as well. Then I started noticing that all the businesses along this row were either closed or had no bathrooms for public use. (Except the pizza place-which I promptly will support going forward). For being a tea house and a space where you expect people to hang out and spend money on food a bathroom should be a minimum requirement. Not only for your staff so that they can wash their hands but also for your customers. I did not complain about the issue however as I figured this was an anomaly. So imagine my surprise when I have mentioned the place to a few friends and pointed out that the bathroom was out of order just to find out that not only they have been out of order every time all of my friends have visited but that this has spanned over a long period of time. I am super disappointed in this aspect of this store and will probably not visit there again unless they make their bathroom available to the public again. To expect someone to come and spend time in your coffee shop but not be able to wash their hands before they eat or use the bathroom when you're selling tea (a liquid) is silly.

My biggest issue though is the bold-faced lie that the bathroom is out of order instead of "we don't want to allow the public to use our bathroom". And if your bathroom is really out of order how much does it cost to bring in a plumber because I spent over $100 buying tea, refills and desserts in the hour I was there.

google_reviews.text:
Such a cute spot with a real Manhattan vibe. The space is cozy, stylish, and perfect to relax or get some work done.

One of my favorite places to get work done. The drinks are amazing, the service is amazing, and the vibes with the music are always great.

I’ve always had a great experience at Off Grid, with my favorite drink being the hojicha latte (though the matcha is great too). Something I really love is how attentive the employees are when taking your order to make sure the drink matches your exact preference. I went with my friend, and they asked so many thoughtful questions — like how many shots, how sweet, and of course, the classic: “Is whole milk okay?” I’m used to only being asked about milk, so being asked about other aspects actually made me start questioning my own preferences since I usually just drink whatever other cafes give me. Sometimes I think, hmm, this isn’t as sweet as I wanted, or this drink just isn’t that good. But at Off Grid, every time I’ve ordered the hojicha, it’s been consistently amazing. My friends who come with me (usually ordering an iced latte) always agree that their drinks are great too, and they really like being able to adjust the sweetness. The staff are also super transparent about how much sweetness goes into your drink, which really helps you figure out what you like.

The service here is truly next-level. I’m used to picking up my drink at the counter when my name’s called, but at Off Grid, they always bring it right to your table. That’s just one of the many ways the employees show how attentive they are to making sure everyone has a great experience. For example, one time my friend sat at a table near the end where there aren’t many outlets, and the only one was an extension cord tucked behind a plant. The employee noticed her sitting there and, without her even asking, offered to plug in the extension cord so she could charge her devices. Another time, a friend of mine was about to move to a newly available table, and before he could, the employee stopped him — just to wipe it down, even though it wasn’t dirty. Little things like that really show how exceptional the service is and how much they care about keeping customers comfortable and focused while studying.

Also, the music that day was on point — it really helped keep me motivated to study.

And this might sound random, but the restroom is always stocked with toilet paper and paper towels — another example of how attentive they are to keeping everything in order so customers never have to worry about anything.

If I had to point out one con, it would be the limited study space since there aren’t that many seats. But honestly, the drinks, service, and overall vibe are so good that I don’t mind taking my chances on finding a seat whenever I go. As someone who’s been to a lot of cafes, Off Grid definitely stands at the top when it comes to both service and drinks — I’d highly recommend it to anyone who wants to study or just enjoy a genuinely great cafe experience.

Bonus: Matcha + Hojicha are all hand-whisked!

google_reviews.text: What a quaint and warm place to have French pastries and crepes. The owners were very friendly and warm to everyone who came in. They had a new item that day and it was delicious! Cinnamon bread with light custard; not too sweet with just the right cinnamon taste. Cappuccino is very good, no burnt taste of the espresso at all. All in all I enjoyed my time here, will look forward to have one of their quiches as they all sound so good. 😊

I thoroughly recommend the Petit Bretagne French cafe!  It feels like you're in Europe, and the coffee and food (pastries, sandwiches, crepes) are fantastic.  We are coffee aficionados and have tried all the cafes in Mamaroneck; we think that Petit's expresso and cappucino are the best in Mamaroneck (it's flavorful and smooth, not at all bitter).  The owner and staff are extremely welcoming and friendly, and it feels like we're visiting friends.  We have also visited their cafe in Rye and enjoyed it there too.

Walking in, you feel instantly transported to France—everything from the café’s name to the chef and waitress’s accents, the décor, the French music, and even the little signs on the wall feels authentically French.

The crêpes are outstanding—thin, delicate, and flavorful, one of the best I’ve had outside of France. The croque madame was rich and comforting, with a perfectly fried egg on top. The macarons were a touch dense but still very enjoyable. Coffee is available, though the cappuccino was just average, not the star of the show. We even picked up some French chocolate, which had nothing different from American ones :D.

This café nails the vibe: cozy, charming, and thoroughly French. Come here for the food and stay for the atmosphere. A gem in town.

This afternoon I walked into a local Persian Cafe in my neighborhood. Out of the assortment of pastries available. I zoned in on the Linden Chocolate Chippers. Not something I would typically desire to get. Ironically. The Linden Cookies had a significant meaning in my life in the late 80’s. Attending Junior HS in The Bronx. Kids would line up around the cafeteria to get their Linden Cookies with their lunch. I never had a chance to get Linden Cookies because I only had enough money for lunch which was 75 cents at that time. A majority of the kids at the school got lunch for free and used their lunch money for cookies.
I felt like an outcast and ridiculed because I didn’t have extra money for cookies and had to pay full price for lunch.
The struggle was real and one afternoon. I ended up using a portion of my lunch money to purchase a pack of Linden Chocolate Chip cookies for 30 cents. Leaving me short to buy lunch and raise a brow with school staff. As it was mandatory for all students to buy lunch.
The incident escalated to my folks and they were concerned, what happened to money for lunch. Being 13 years old I was timid and simply told them “how come I can't have free lunch like the rest of the kids at school! They all make fun of me because I have to pay for it.”
My folks impulsively responded back and told me “it’s because the  kids at my school are from lower income neighborhoods. That’s why they get lunch for free and use the money from the government for cookies.”
As a 13 year old. I didn’t know what  they said. All I cared about was fitting in. The next morning. Before,
my dad dropped me off at school. He gave me $1.35. Enough money for lunch and 2 packs of cookies.
It was the best day of my life and I felt my blood sugar sky rocket standing in line for cookies.
When it was my turn. They sold out of the chocolate chip cookies. My only options were Peanut Butter and Chocolate Chocolate Chip. I took it and feared rejection on another level with kids in the cafeteria. Surprisingly they were curious about my choices. I traded what I got for Chocolate Chip.
I gained acceptance and all the kids were able to look past our economical differences.
Today. I am fortunate to be able to afford a pack of Linden Chocolate Chips and not feel self conscious about being different!

They adjusted the cake design promptly according to my budget and even sent a detailed design draft for approval. It was the first time I experienced such smooth, efficient communication with a bakery. Within a very short timeframe, they delivered a custom cake that exceeded expectations ✨.

As for the taste, I didn’t personally try it due to dietary differences, but my friend mentioned it tasted good — slightly sweeter than a typical cake, yet otherwise comparable in texture and flavor. Most importantly, he absolutely loved the design ❤️.

Overall, this bakery stands out for its responsiveness, customization flexibility, and thoughtful service — a reliable option for those with dietary restrictions or anyone seeking a beautifully executed custom cake.

I think this place has the most delicious and beautiful cakes. They are gluten and dairy free which really helps make you not feel sick after eating. They’re not too sweet and the price is so reasonable. I have used them for 2 years and it’s my go-to a special occasion cake. Great shop!

Incredible GF baked goods!!!
It's so nice looking around and seeing that you can have everything.

I got the creme puff, red velvet bundtette, and chocolate chip cinnamon muffin.

Everything was soo yummy and fluffy and well made.

Would like to go back and get the coffee some other time.

Cute little shop. I needed my cake same day. $50 was a steal for a delicious chocolate layer cake. We got a coffee and got a cupcake for free! I'm all about the surprise specials. The young lady who served us was friendly and helpful. It's great to get a cake that's dairy free and gluten free without being vegan.

This place is incredible! Delicious cakes, muffins, and pastries that are not only gluten-free, but also dairy free and kosher. My friend adored the brownie and he isn’t even gluten or lactose intolerant. Everyone can enjoy this place. The help is also very friendly and they have incredibly cute birthday candles for sale.

document: Early Bird Coffee & More. cuisine: Coffee & Tea Cafes Bakeries. located in Bronx. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Earlybird Coffee & More in Cresskill is such a great find. The barista was very friendly and welcoming. The pastries were amazing — fresh, flaky and baked on premises. Their espresso drinks are excellent, smooth and well-crafted. I also noticed how popular their matcha drinks were while I was there — almost everyone seemed to be ordering one. A true hidden gem in the suburbs that brings genuine city café vibes. ☕✨

Stopped by Early Bird Coffee & More and really liked the vibe.

I got the matcha ginger yuzu — the flavors were on point, but the matcha itself didn’t have that punch I usually look for.

Also grabbed an apricot croissant, which was tasty, just didn’t really feel local or homemade.

Overall though, it’s a super cute new spot with really good, friendly service, and I’m glad we have something like this in the area. I’m hoping as they settle in, they up their pastry game a bit.

I’d definitely come back to work from here or grab a coffee again.

I am a huge boutique coffee shop fanatic and have a dream to own an automotive inspired coffee shop one day. Of all the amazing shops I have been to, I have never felt more comfortable, welcomed, or treated better in any other coffee shop. Early Bird Coffee Co. treats everyone like family, offers amazing coffee and pastries and sets a great vibe whether you’re there to meet someone or get some work done solo. Thank you  Danny for creating a great place for people to call home and for building a great team of Baristas!

I visited Early Bird Cafe today (Saturday) around 1:30 PM with my mother. We ordered two drinks—a chai and a latte. Unfortunately, both drinks were below average.

More concerning was the service. The employee at the front counter who took our order was rude from the beginning. We did not ask about or order any pastries, yet she abruptly asked if we were planning to eat pastries. When we asked whether they were complimentary, she laughed at us openly with what appeared to be the owner/manager. This happened directly in front of us and felt extremely disrespectful.

Throughout the interaction, her attitude toward me and my mother was noticeably different compared to how she treated other customers, particularly white customers, who were spoken to politely and respectfully. The experience made us feel uncomfortable and singled out, and it strongly came across as discriminatory.

I left feeling embarrassed, confused, and honestly shaken. No customer should feel this way simply for ordering coffee. Between the poor service and unimpressive drinks, I would not recommend this cafe and will not be returning.
First time here and loved it. Super cool spot & the coffee/ latte quality is great! Been on the search for a great latte in Bergen County & this one is at the top of the list. Highly recommend.

document: Starving Artist Cafe & Gallery. cuisine: Art Galleries Themed Cafes. located in Bronx. with 4.9 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
If you see me in Stockton NJ, this is where it’ll be. Cozy, artist forward cafe run by beautiful peeps making delicious homestyle food. Super casual, genuinely super. Live music, byob, open mic, real humans.
See the art… be the art… and eat.

We went to this café because my nephew was playing in a band that night, his first show ever. This band is made up of 13, 14  and 15-year-olds, and the fact that the owner of this café gives bands like this a place to play is outstanding. It’s such a cool little place and you instantly feel welcome. On to the food. As I said, we went there to hear music and it’s about a 45 minute ride and I would go there again tomorrow for the food. Everything is made fresh and delicious. I am not a vegetarian, but I ordered the vegetarian sandwich and it blew me away. We had seven people at our table and every single person raved about their food. The cooking in this place is no joke, it’s seriously delicious food. We will be back.

The best little joint around. Great homemade food served by the nicest people. Owner owned and operated.  Owner is a phenomenal cook and musician and has music most nights. Food very reasonably priced. Byob.  If you're a musician he welcomes you to come play his guitars, sing, eat, talk share. Truly a gem of a place run by a gem of a human.

Food is always absolutely delicious! Generous portions and everything is fresh. Todd and the staff are so kind and fun to hang out with. My husband and I just love going here. Love the live music too, who wouldn’t!

Great local vibe and delicious, freshly made food. My meatballs were obviously made there and were light with great Italian seasoning. The sauce, made on site, was not overcooked or acid, but was tomato sweet. My spouse's vegetable dish surprised us with the generous amount and was complex and nicely grilled. You have to try the octopus fries, fun and quite tasty. There is live music on the weekends.

document: Anthony's Famous Gourmet Deli. cuisine: Delis Sandwiches. located in Bronx. with 3.9 stars (good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Just had knee surgery, so I ordered a salad on UE under the name Anthony's Famous Salad Bar. Of course I knew it was a deli, this is how they get us. This was the worst salad I've ever had. The greens were old and withered and wet and tasted just like dirt. You can tell they didn't wash them. The tomatoes were mushy. They're passing off pepitas (green pumpkin seeds) as sunflower seeds. They gave about a teaspoon of dressing and it tasted like spoiled mayonnaise. Will never get so much as a candy bar from here again. Notice the dark green mushy leaves and pumpkin seeds in the Pic

Anthony’s Famous Deli in The Bronx is an absolute neighborhood favorite and a place I truly appreciate. Being open 24 hours is a huge convenience and makes it a reliable spot no matter the time of day or night. The chicken quesadilla is always delicious, fresh, and satisfying, and my favorite sandwich, The Mr. T, never disappoints with its great flavor and generous portions. Anthony’s Famous Deli delivers great food, convenience, and quality, and I highly recommend it.

My absolute favorite deli. They have the widest selection of sandwiches, salads and freshly made juices. The staff is professional, fast and the food is delicious! The deli is ultra clean and you have the best customer service experience every time you go. I absolutely adore the folks on the grill. Truly the best deli ever

This is the BEST deli I've been to located at E. Gunhill RD, in my opinion. The food is always fresh with a plethora of options to choose from. There is also a huge variety of beverages and snacks. Our first time at this cute spot and the coffee did not disappoint. I tried their Dominican Mocha Latte and it was not overly sweet but so delicious. That’s
how you can tell it’s quality coffee - when you don’t need all those sweet syrups. Hubby tried their Dulce De Leche Latte and he loved it! We will definitely be back.

I come here for their maduro matcha. It is one of the best matchas I’ve ever had. It’s a banana syrup based Matcha. I get it with oat milk. Everyone there is friendly. The space is really cute. They always have good music playing, however, give yourself some time in case there’s a line. It’s only usually one person working, and that person is taking the order and making the drinks.

This is the best coffee spot in westchester county specifically New Rochelle. They don’t only offer coffee, they offer a community, seasonal drinks, activities, events and more. If you need to join a book club, this is the spot. If you need a coffee cart for an event, this is the spot. If you need to vent about your job, this is the spot. I’m excited for their plans in 2026!

Literally the best coffee in New Ro hands down. Their recipes and baristas are top tier - my coffee comes out consistently good so the beans are quality! I buy their roasted beans as well. They also have pastries from Balthazar’s, need I say more! Run don’t walk. Oh and they actually care about community and have book clubs here - that’s a dying art in 2026! I love to sit and people watch and ponder at their window seats.

Pleasant sunlit cafe with a corner lounge, board games, and great coffee. Came here while traveling because it was close to the train station, and got the Dominican Mocha Latte — strong bitter chocolate flavors, very very good and came out super fast!

document: ÜMACHA. cuisine: Bubble Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Boba made from real tea, slow cooked tapioca, and water views of Manhattan from the window.  We have been here a number of times and the drinks are highly consistent and great quality.  The staff is also great with extra questions and special dietary needs. A yummy treat for all!

Umacha has severely updated their menu, service, and has changed locations. Their previous location was not serving them at all, and was just a few steps away from where they’re currently located.

Parking can be difficult depending on the day. Weekends and holidays are much busier than weekdays. But the service is always outstanding and the same. The girls here are so enjoyable to talk to! Even when I’m taking a photo or video in this aesthetic environment they’re so nice about it!!

This place is almost always busy now, and good they deserve it!

It’s super pretty inside. The seating is much better compared to the old place. I’m very happy Umacha had a full on glow up! These workers know how to handle the flow of traffic with efficiency, cleanliness, and timeliness. They should all be commended!

My boyfriend and I always get their strawberry matcha latte and it’s delicious! With real strawberries at the bottom! I want to try some of their other menu items too. The waffles look delicious. I would include their previous setting photos, but that would be selling them short because they’re so amazing now. I’m glad I came back because at their old location I had a horrible experience.
Love this place! Great to satisfy my bbt craving as I shop! Love their brown sugar bbt and they even have brown sugar milk version for my daughter (no caffeine).

I love that the drinks here are not super sweet! Everything has a very good balance of flavor and you can actually taste the matcha in your drink. Boba is also flavorful and perfectly soft and chewy!

Unfortunately, I felt like it was a bit too pricey for its portion size. Additional toppings are also relatively expensive starting at $1/addition. And if you’re lactose intolerant, expect to pay for substitutions as well.

Very good flavorful bubble tea well priced. Much better than the fake sugary bubble tea in mitsuwa.

I got the mango lemonade with no sugar and it was sweet and sour and had a bright refreshing taste. I loved the star jelly, it was firm and chewy and fruity.

google_reviews.text:
Stopped in for a chicken parm hero and some fresh mozzarella since in the area.
Very delicious hero. Finished in no time.
The cheese was fresh and thick. Good consistency. Not so wet and gooey if you know what I mean. I enjoyed at my work desk the next week.

Great eggplant parm for lunch came with a large chunk of bread. The deli counter is over the top! We are out of towners and had never had a true Italian deli experience. (They didn’t call back but I saw later that they did initiate a refund.)

This is an extremely authentic Italian joint on Arthur Avenue.

I had a ham and egg omelet and coffee.  Simple but perfect.  All fresh.  Prompt service with a smile.  Loved it!

Lots of prepared food behind the glass.  All of it looks amazing.

We've been going to Tino's for 20+ years and every time we go to Arthur Ave I have to stop in. I head straight for the owner, Giancarlo, to get olive oil, olives, etc. for my house. He is very honest and full of knowledge, so is his wife Rosa and the rest of the staff.

On my last visit I got organic Sicilian olive oil that was just pressed the prior month... talk about fresh. We've had the fresh pasta to cook at home but next time I need to have a true Italian combo hero.

Salute to Giancarlo, Rosa and family!

document: I Like It Black. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Bronx. with 4.4 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
I had an incredible experience at I Like It Black this past weekend. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and full of genuine community. Aliyyah, the owner, was absolutely amazing—super friendly, engaging, and intentional with every person who came through the door. We had a great conversation, and it was clear how much heart she pours into her work and community.

The coffee was outstanding—beautifully crafted and full of flavor.

I also want to add that I’ve been a fan of Aliyyah’s bakery, Make My Cake, for many years now. I’ve visited countless times over the years, and the quality, consistency, and care have always been top tier. It’s no surprise that the same excellence and hospitality show up in her coffee shop as well.

If you’re in Harlem, both of these spots are absolute must-visits—exceptional products, authentic service, and a true sense of community. I’ll definitely be back.
Extremely warm and inviting vibes, adorable aesthetic, and great service. Matcha is very high quality and they just started offering student discounts! Owner Aliya is a delight.

My first time staying in Harlem and I stumbled on an incredible Black-owned coffee shop that was an absolute vibe. The owner radiates a vibrant, beautiful energy, the space is visually on point, and the coffee and food were outstanding.

I ordered the Morningside sandwich, a blueberry muffin, and an oat-milk latte—10/10 across the board. The hot-sauce kick on the “crisps everything” butter croissant was next-level, and that muffin has no business being that good.

Black ownership x Black & Brown coffee-maker supporters—you simply can’t go wrong here. I’ll definitely be back.

Awesome coffee, and awesome pastries!!! Muffins are some of the best I’ve tried, love the lemon poppy one! They aren’t too sweet which is awesome. Owner is super nice too, she struck up a convo with me and even offered to connect me with some people in my industry. Really nice environment and great service overall.
The Morningside breakfast sandwich is incredible. Can order on an everything flavored croissant, which is delicious. Coffee is great too!

document: Dynasty. cuisine: Chinese Chicken Shop. located in Bronx. with 2.6 stars (decent). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: Was in mood for Chinese food and we were recommended to this restaurant. We ordered combination fried rice, combination lo mein, and pan fried vegetable dumplings. Everything was good. The dumplings weren’t the best I’ve had but it wasn’t bad. The fried rice was delicious. It’s a solid choice! They even have family prices to enjoy a little bit of everything. Once we placed the order, the food came out fast. I also liked that they served hot tea. At the end of your meal, they will give you a hot towel to clean your hands. Would come again.

I was referred by a friend, so this was my first time. All the food was good, but I’m not use to shrimp fried rice, where you can hardly see the shrimp, it was little pieces, same thing with the Mei Fun chicken, hardly any chicken just noodles and a little vegetables.. The chicken and broccoli were fine and the General Tao Chicken was good.

We checked on House of Dynasty online and it had good reviews. The prices were somewhat high but I thought that meant the food was good. Otherwise, they wouldn’t charge so much. We ordered carry out for pickup. When we got to the restaurant my husband went down to pick up the order. He got back to the car and was very excited. He said the smell of the food in the restaurant was good, it seemed busy inside even though it was around 3pm on a Sunday, and the staff was friendly. He was so happy he even brought a carry out menu for next time. Well, there will not be a next time from House of Dynasty. The chicken corn soup, which was enough for 1 person, looked a weird yellow color and the taste was off. I couldn’t taste chicken or corn. The rest of the food was okay, if I had gotten it from a buffet. It tasted and seemed not freshly made. The meal was definitely not worth the $90 it cost. They charge for the hot chili oil and if you want fried rice instead of white rice it is an additional $4.80. My stomach was not happy with the meal and I immediately threw out the carry out menu.

Haven't been here in years. I was in the area and decided to stop on in.
I remember back in the day, this place was great. Can't say it now.
My snow peas were soft and mushy, the chicken dish I ordered had no taste, the chicken wasn't tender.
The peking duck was not flavorful at all. Their prices are higher than other restaurants, so I would expect better quality, etc. Oh well..
I guess the next time I'm in the area and craving some good Chinese food, I will have to look elsewhere.

This restaurant used to be a favorite but the quality has been disappointing for some time now.  We decided to give it another try and ordered carryout.  We ordered a chicken entree and the chicken was very tough (probably thighs) and the sauce was overly sweet.  We also ordered special rice noodles which had absolutely no flavor despite having lots of chicken and vegetables.  The crispy fried shrimp we ordered as an appetizer was very soggy and overly breaded.  The hot and sour soup was just ok.  We spent $118 (food, tax, tip and delivery) and ate very little of it.  We don’t like to waste food, but we tossed most of it because it was almost inedible.  Very disappointed.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at the Chinese buffet, and I must say it was quite an experience. The establishment garnered a range of opinions from customers, and here's my take on it.

Upon arriving, I was pleased to find attentive and friendly customer service, which set a positive tone for the evening. The seating area, while slightly cramped, became busier as the evening progressed, indicating its popularity among diners.

One standout moment was when a server surprised our table with a generous portion of whole lobster, a delightful touch that showcased the staff's willingness to go the extra mile. The overall cleanliness of the place, including the bathrooms, added to the pleasant dining environment.

The buffet's array of options was impressive, spanning around 4 to 5 rows of dishes. While predominantly Chinese cuisine, the variety encompassed other cuisines as well, ensuring there was something for everyone. I particularly enjoyed the well-seasoned Chinese dishes and the addition of sushi to the spread.

The dessert section was decent, with the cheesecake standing out as a personal favorite. Although I was eager to explore more, my stomach's capacity reached its limit. The inclusion of ice cream in the freezer added a magical touch to the culinary adventure.

While the restaurant had its strengths, it's worth noting that service had its moments of inconsistency, as mentioned in one of the reviews. Nonetheless, the balance of good food and reasonable prices made it a worthwhile experience. During the week, the $14 price tag was a steal, offering good value for the variety of food available. However, weekends saw a slightly steeper price of $26, which might be a consideration for those looking to visit during peak times.

In conclusion, my experience at the Chinese buffet was satisfactory. With an impressive selection of dishes, varying in quality, and a cozy atmosphere, it's a dining spot that caters to a diverse range of tastes. Whether you're craving authentic Chinese flavors or simply seeking a satisfying buffet adventure, this place is worth a visit.

name: China Palace
document: China Palace. cuisine: Chinese. located in Bronx. with 3.6 stars (good). price level is cheap.

google_reviews.text: The service was amazing! The food was incredible. I suggest the dumplings, it's beef and when you bite into in it, the juice seeps out and into you mouth. Its delicious. The food was actually hot rather than other places. Its really not busy at all. The prices are like 10-20 dollars. And guess what... they even box you food for you! I highly suggest this place.

Very nice people, seems to be family business, place looks neat too. Love the chicken wings that come with fried rice or fries option. The price for serving is reasonable.  I would recommend this place to try.

Read The Reviews before you order food here. I ordered a simple carry-out shrimp dish for $25. The guy taking my order hung up on me without a thank you, without confirming anything, nothing. I had to call back just to make sure they got it right. That should have been my first warning. Rude!

The food arrives 40 minutes later. The driver is not too sharp.
First shrimp? Horrible.
Second shrimp? Spit it out.
Third shrimp? Mealy, mushy, absolutely unacceptable.

I’ve eaten seafood in hole-in-the-wall joints all over the world, and I have never had shrimp this bad.

I called them politely to let them know — and instead of doing the normal thing (like replacing the food), they told me to drive back with the order. Most people would not do this. But I did. I am on a fixed income, and 25 dollars is a lot of money for food; I would not feed my dog. So I drove it back. Big mistake.
When I got there, the owners didn’t apologize, didn’t show any concern — they wanted to argue. Not just the husband but the wife tried to double-team me. “No one has ever complained about our shrimp.” Congratulations. I’m the first. It’s bad. It was inedible. Pretending otherwise doesn’t make it edible.
Then they had the nerve to offer me part of my money back.
For food, I couldn’t eat. A lot of owners came from cultures where there is no such thing as “the customer is always right.”
Arguing is normal
Replacing food is seen as “losing face” or “being weak”
I know I have been all over the world.
So when you say the shrimp was bad, instead of fixing the dish, they try to “win the argument.”
That doesn't work here, Jack, this is America!

So here’s your review:
Your shrimp is bad, your customer service is worse, and the way you handle complaints is laughable.
I paid $25 and got $4 worth of experience — and that’s being generous. Do yourself a favor and go literally anywhere else.

The General Tso chicken was disgusting all breading & the flavor was nasty. I gave 2 stars because the fried rice was ok, just ok not good.  I won’t be returning or recommending & will probably talk anyone out of eating here if they mention it. Hands down the worst General Tso chicken I have ever had in my life.

I’ve been a regular customer for many years, probably more than eight. But about two weeks ago, I didn’t feel like cooking, so we ordered delivery. What we received was watered-down wonton soup (which it used to be my favorite).

It would have been much more appreciated if they had simply said, “No, I am sorry, we are out.” Instead, they chose to send us “two large containers of watered-down soup”. I was truly disappointed, and we no longer trust them. They’ve lost a loyal customer due to their dishonesty.

google_reviews.text: Ordered the chicken and broccoli combination with wonton soup. Fresh food, just ok flavor, but prices were great. The meal left an aftertaste. I’m searching for a Chinese food joint that offers homemade duck sauce, in the little tiny containers, not the packets. If you know of a place let me know.

This place has really good food. Not oily like most Chinese food. Fresh ingredients. Fried stuff has a pleasant crunch. Dining area is clean. Service is great. (cashier speaks English and Spanish in addition to his native Mandarin). Very reasonable prices, too. Glad we found this place.

I’m not from Lancaster,  I’m from Harrisburg  and was iffy on where to eat Chinese out here, I actually ate here before pickup and the food was good. I ordered delivery tonight 2 combination platters general tos with pork fried rice 10/10, shrimp and broccoli pork fried rice 10/10… order of chicken wings my son enjoyed them 10/10…. And to my surprise I tried the honey wingsssss and baby they are greattttttttt 20/10! We enjoyed everything prompt delivery and a 2liter cost me $42 not bad because I actually enjoyed every bite food was fresh and hot!

I order Shrimp Egg Foo young, and cheese wonton. I don't know how you can mess up on egg foo young, but the eggs was burned,  over cook, no seasoning,  the cheese wonton seem to be old, and I wanted the sweet one. I don't like when I pay for food that is not good...however the driver was very pleasant...it is so important to serve fresh tasteful food, but this food wasn't that!

I ordered delivery tonight using the online order feature on their website. Beef and broccoli, chicken with chinese vegetables and two egg rolls. google_reviews.text:
Best Chinese food in the world. Everything was so delicious and cooked to order quickly. We are there on a trip and made sure to stop back on our way home to try other dishes.
The family meal deal was exceptional and a great value. We had 3 entrees the first time and 4 the second time. (We were going to get all new dishes but the orange chicken was so good we needed to order it again).
Beautiful dining room and obviously popular for take out. Service was excellent and it was great seeing food being prepared by one person in the dining room and a kid doing stuff quietly in the corner booth.
If you are driving on I-81 and going by Woodstock VA, make sure you stop by for great food.

I almost always order take out, but we have enjoyed sitting down for dinner here too.
I have never had anything bad! Everything is cooked fresh and to order! I love their crab Rangoon, they are one of my favorite places for that. Everything is always delicious! The people are awesome and very friendly too!!

I don't know if they are related to the other China Wok by the Foodlion. Ive accidently called in an order over there, and I was not impressed with that one at all.So, We don't go to that one. We didn't get the quality of food or the top notch service we get from this one. So if you order, make sure it's the China Wok on West Reservoir beside the walmart!!! They are the best!

Great for a little lunch. The food was good. The service was excellent.  The lady who waited on me was so sweet and a very hard worker.  She took phone orders, waited tables, took care of the take-out orders, and folded napkins when she had a little break. This lovely Asian lady deserves a raise. She did it all with a smile while quietly humming to the background music. Not pretty inside, but clean and neat.
