google_reviews.text: I've seen this place change hands and name a few times. Anise disappointed me at first, but has significantly improved over the years. Food is great always comes fresh and piping  hot, service is always good

Ordered the shrimp pho & shrimp summer rolls and they were both quite delicious! Food took less than 10 minutes to come out. Only minus was that it was pricier than I thought it would be for a bowl of pho, but recommend trying it! Cute restaurant

I ordered take out pho, I ordered the round ey steak. The broth was good but lacked depth of flavor. I was originally nervous that they had sent the veggie broth instead of the pho broth. Otherwise, the soup was pretty good! Service was fantastic, they were fast and kind. I would give it another try some time!

Had the Chicken stay skewer, Hanoi style vermicelli with grilled pork, and Tofu noodle with shrimp paste.

Really enjoyed the skewer and vermicelli, tasted pretty fresh, light. The skewer came with a peanut type sauce and some vinegary cucumber. Was nice and light. The fish sauce for the vermicelli has some chili pepper to it, and the side salad had some cilantro and basil.

Complimentary water had lime in it.

Thought the tofu noodles were noodles made of tofu, but it was just noodles with a side of fried tofu triangles. The shrimp paste was too strong for me. Heard it's an acquired taste.

Pho with meatballs and eye round came out super quick. Was great.

Vermecelli with chicken and spring roll was great. Ample fish sauce, comes with carrot, lettuce. Crushed peanuts, and fried onion bits. Crispy spring roll.

--

Clean single room bathrooms, one for male and  a separate room for females.

Server was quite attentive. Food comes out very quickly.

Only gripe is the cold comes in quickly when the door is opened.

Tried out this Anise Viet Cuisine location for an early Friday dinner. We were immediately seated in the large dining area, which had other diners already eating. The menu was large and varied, with way more grilled items than I typically see which was a nice addition. Service throughout was quick, and the actual pho and summer rolls we received were delicious. Good service, tasty pho, and fair prices - had a great time!

Full Update February 18 2020:
Ok First things first, I do not work for or have any working relationship with this restaurant or its workers. Now that being said, I love food and I am the kind of person that tries restaurants once and if I like what I get in the form of service and food Quality/Quantity will keep coming back for more. I no longer can have raw fish/seafood so I cannot attest to their variety of raw plates but the ones that I have eaten are above par.

Before I found this place I did a google search of the top sushi places around my area, and this little place was number 3 in The Bronx and on the top 25 places in the whole city....THAT IS IN THE TOP 25 PLACES IN THE BRONX, QUEENS, MANHATTAN AND BROOKLYN.

I love their service regardless if you are eating in or taking out, they are always courteous, friendly and fast.  the restaurant has 2 sections to eat in the one in front has tables and chairs  and tables and benches, the back part of the restaurant is more Japanese traditional  with the small tables that are very close to the floor and where you have to kneel/sit on floor.

The prices of the food are very reasonable, the quality of the food is exceptional, and the presentation of the plates is beautiful.

I have been coming to this little restaurant now for almost 4 years, I try to get my food at least once a month, and even do is hard since I do not have a car and have to take a cab round trip (30 bucks) I need to eat from here.

Now think about that, I am willing to spend 30 bucks to take a cab to eat here when I could just take a quick train hop to go somewhere else closer... That should tell you everything you should know about this place..

my favorite plates are: House special fried rice( I order with soy sauce, but it comes with out) Dragon Roll, California Roll, Zombie Roll, Spicy Kani Roll.  Also  the Chicken or the Beef  Teriyaki Bento Plates among every other thing I have eaten here.

Great Food (a bit pricey)... but it was worth it. My Daughters first time having Sushi... they definitely want to go back.
They absolutely loved their dessert.

This was my first time here with my family.  Ever since I moved to the Bronx, I've been on the search for a good sushi restaurant.  This restaurant has really fresh fish!  We all ordered the sushi roll combo that either comes with a miso soup or salad.  The food was a good amount that we were stuffed.  Also, they had the special appetizer that was delicious - ribs that they marinated overnight.  The ribs were tender and flavorful.  We had the fried banana for dessert and thst was amazing!  The only thing that you need to know before dining here is that they no longer accept credit cards, CASH ONLY.  They have an ATM inside their restaurant, but who wants to pay a surcharge fee?!  The wait staff was attentive and helpful with menu recommendations.  I will definitely dine in or order from here again.

document: Mama Hen House. cuisine: Korean Chicken Shop Comfort Food. located in Bronx. with 4.9 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Absolutely blown away by this place. My boyfriend and I were so happy to stumble upon this gem just minutes from his town. The space is incredibly cozy, and from the moment we walked in, the energy was warm and welcoming.
We were greeted by Jenny, who was an absolute delight and kindly answered all of our menu questions. It was my first time ever trying ramyun, and wow — it did not disappoint. I ordered the vegetarian version, which had the perfect kick of spice and so much flavor. Babe went with the bulgogi bento box and added a side of truffle fries, and every single bite rocked our socks.
We left feeling genuinely happy — amazing food, above-and-beyond customer service, and such a beautiful family-owned atmosphere. Truly top-tier. Huge compliments to the chef 🙏🏽 We’re so grateful for the experience and can’t wait to come back.

Update: I've started ordering here a minimum of 3 times a week since discovering the place. Go-to order is spicy pork kimbap, I bring it with me to work the next day and it still tastes good cold! Cannot recommend it more, it really is made with love and you can feel it. The ddeokboki had a complex flavor too which I never experienced before (or knew was possible). Jenny, the receptionist is also always super kind and lovely to talk to. I really love this place!

truly delicious food. i was in the mood for sweet and spicy chicken and this place delivered beyond my expectations. pretty spicy but such great flavor and paired well with the house made peach iced tea! will definitely be recommending this place

I want to say this place was great in food, vibes, and coziness. This is a great definition of a mom and pop restaurant.

Firstly the food.
I had the bulgogi bento. The bulgogi looked, smelled, and tasted amazing. It had the normal bulgogi flavor with that nice hit of smokiness almost like wokhay from Chinese cooking. I loved each bite as the smokiness hit my mouth and nose. The sides of the bento was good too, the dumplings were nice and crunchy with a nice but just a tad bit bland filling, tho to be fair the filling is fairly standard for korean dumplings. The kimichi is what I prefer, which is the more freshly made kind. And the rice was cooked as I expected from a Korean restaurant, which is good. The salads were fine again its a salad, but it was nice that they added kale to the salad adding this bit of variety. The salad dressing was sweet and a bit tangy, mostly sweet which I do like since I have a sweet tooth.

The other bento was the shrimp tempura, I did get one of the shrimp tempura and it was good. The crunchy and breading was nice and you had the shrimp flavor that was still there.

Finally the tteokbokki. It was great. The rice cakes were chewy and soft and the fish cakes were soft and not mushy. The flavor of the sauce was great too, it had this nice umami to it and was the perfect level of spicy to enjoy.

The price for the food was also reasonable. Both bento costed roughly $18 each and the tteokbokki costed $12. They also had an interesting line up of drinks that was nice.

All this aside I want to also note how cozy and welcoming it felt. The lady that was serving us was very kind and caring. She even asked about how the addition of kale to the salad was because it was a new addition that they changed because people liked kale. I really liked that attention to detail. The store was medium sized with some odds and ends here and there but that added to the charm of the place.

I went on a Thursday during lunch time and it had a good amount of business via pick up but I was there alone with the person I was with dining in.

Overall as a Korean I think this place hits better then certain places in mind the food was good and the atmosphere was comforting.

I do regret not trying some of the other menu items I guess I have to return for some more.

For the sake of Google reviews I gave everything a 5. My personal score may be closer to a 4.4 which is high for my own personal score

Place has good bento box (bulgogi) and decent kimbap (spicy tuna) but the KFC is weak. Sauce (soy garlic) is pretty good but it is VERY fried with minimal chicken. Would not return personally as I’m looking for more meat in my KFC.

google_reviews.text:
Small confession: I don't like ramen. But I had a lunch date friend with a friend here, so I was elated to find an entire page of the menu dedicated to curry entrees.

Here's the short end of it: if you're on the fence about ramen, you can still have a great meal here.

I ordered the Karaage curry, which came with four chunky pieces of fried chicken between a mound of rice and an impressive pool of beef curry. I love curries, and this was no exception. There's just nothing like that characteristic smokey, flavor-blasted blend of spices in Japanese curries. On the slight downside, there wasn't a ton of beef in the curry, but it sure made it exciting when I happened upon occasional bites with meat chunks.

The Japanese iced coffee is a presentation unto itself. A small pourover sits above a cup, ensuring a fresh brew. That drips onto a small puddle of condensed milk while a cup of ice stands ready by the side. It's a zazzy, interactive process toward a cup of iced coffee that tasted just fine.

There's a lovely, cozy vibe to this restaurant that the warm, non-hurried service just accentuates. Service was attentive without intrusion throughout. There's a small, free parking lot right in front, which is certainly a boon in the parking-less void that is this part of Englewood.

A good find ramen place. They have these combo deals and it's a really good value. Very creamy and rich broth. I got the spicy sesame ramen, I think it could be a tad spicier imo. A good size portion too. We all came in hungry on a cold night and we left satisfied.

It is rare to find seafood handled with such reverence, where the natural brininess of the scallop is elevated rather than masked by unnecessary garnishes. name: Taqueria El Chiltepin
document: Taqueria El Chiltepin. cuisine: Mexican. located in Bronx. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Hands down one of the best dining experiences I’ve had!
I found this restaurant through a TikTok video that mentioned they serve barbacoa de chivo (tender goat meat) on weekends—so I decided to take my dad here for Father’s Day. We ordered the birria tacos with handmade tortillas, and let me tell you… those tortillas are a 10/10—absolutely worth it!

My dad got the ribeye, and he gave it a solid 10/10 as well. Of course, we came for the barbacoa, and it did not disappoint. Words can’t describe how good it was  tender, flavorful, and unforgettable.

The drinks were also amazing. My mom loved the tamarind, and I personally went for the Jamaica. Both perfectly refreshing and just the right amount of sweetness to complement the food.

To top it all off, we had the homemade flan and churros absolutely delicious.

But what really made the experience even better was the outstanding service. Shoutout to Alex and Paulina for taking the time to explain the menu and make sure everything was perfect from the moment we walked in to the moment we left. Their hospitality was top-tier.

This is a family-owned Mexican restaurant that I would 100% recommend to anyone in the area—or even if you have to make a little trip. It’s so worth it! 🙌🏼🌮🇲🇽

Sometimes the best meals are born out of a delivery mix-up; and that was exactly the case with our recent experience at Taqueria El Chiltepin. What started as a frustrating DoorDash snafu (where our food arrived suspiciously packaged as Wendy’s) quickly turned into a culinary redemption story, thanks to the kindness and professionalism of the team behind this Bronx gem.
Upon calling the restaurant, we were warmly greeted by Paulina, whose tone and hospitality instantly shifted our mood.

She not only apologized mind you this had nothing to do with their restaurant; but invited us to come directly to the restaurant to receive the correct order. Once we arrived, the energy and ambiance of El Chiltepin swept us into what felt like a brief getaway to the heart of Mexico; rich with authenticity, vibrant decor, and a sincere sense of community.

While picking up our original order, we couldn’t help but be enticed by the menu and ended up ordering three more items, bringing our total to five:
* Three orders of Cheese Flautas
* One order of Steak Nachos
* One Horchata beverage
The Flautas were crispy, golden, and generously filled, satisfying both in flavor and portion. Upon chatting with Alex; who matched Paulina's level of graciousness; we discovered we had been over-ordering in previous visits.

We had been getting three-piece Flauta orders at $30 each, when we could’ve gotten five sticks instead. His transparency and care in educating us on the best way to order not only saved us money but solidified our trust in the business.

The Steak Nachos were a savory standout; freshly fried chips loaded with seasoned steak, gooey cheese, and a medley of toppings that didn’t overwhelm. And the Horchata? Smooth, creamy, and perfectly spiced; an ideal refresher to top off the meal.
Final Thoughts: Taqueria El Chiltepin is more than just a local taqueria; it’s a whole experience. The food is consistently satisfying, but it’s the people like Paulina and Alex who elevate the visit into something memorable. Whether you're dining in or recovering from a DoorDash disaster, this is the kind of place that makes you feel seen, heard, and well-fed. Highly recommend.

Then, I ordered the same meal I had last time I was here. The steak was half the size as last time with picture proof, burnt, and didn’t come with potatoes. It was pitiful.

When I sent back the food, they were receptive and apologized, but the manager offered a free dessert as an apology. After having bad service for two hours, do I really want to wait for a dessert? He also sent the waitress to deliver the message instead of coming and personally apologizing. As a business owner, you should care about customer relationships and not have your waitress do your dirty work.

I want to like this place, as our first experience was great, but in the few weeks difference of coming, the quality has gone down hill severely. The waitresses and food runners and hostesses were very nice, but management needs to be on top of how often they check in with tables and have a better system in place. Also, food quality should be consistent each visit. You can’t build a community of regulars if this is where you’re performing shortly after opening.

We just went our first time. We knew from the free popcorn we got that this place was going to be good!

We got the ravioli which was great.

My wife got the short rib, and it was delicious, and so much food. She ate about a third of it and took the rest home.

I got the drunken ribeye, and it was great. A bigger flatter steak, but I really enjoyed it. Fries were good and plenty of those. I’m surprised I ate it all.

Brussel sprouts were a little spicy and a little asainy. Really great.

We got the peanut butter pie. So good! The peanut butter was really thick in an awesome way. I thought about asking if I could buy a whole pie.

The only negative was that our table was a bit wobbly. I mentioned it to the server, and I actually think he might follow through and get them fixed.

We will be back!!

As a WV native, I appreciate what Nettie’s is trying to do in creating a WV-inspired restaurant. While they’ve correctly picked up on the importance of Italian food in WV culture, they’ve fumbled the iconic state food—the pepperoni roll.

A true pepperoni roll is characterized by its simplicity—soft, white bread and pepperoni. Usually no cheese, and definitely no tomato sauce. It’s all about execution. The pepperoni fat should infuse some of the bread as it bakes, creating a pleasant fusion of sweet bread and savory meat. Serving the pepperoni roll room temp brings out the sweetness.

What was served at Nettie’s? A glorified pizza roll, filled with as much cheese as pepperoni, piping hot, and served with a side of tomato sauce. The worst part was the bread. Far from fluffy, the bread had the appearance of an egg roll, and was crunchy on the outside and doughy on the inside. It dripped grease as I bit into it. I mostly skipped the sauce, which masks the flavor of the dish.
We really enjoyed this place. Burger was fantastic. Chicken Parmesan sandwich was okay. Service was great. Beer was fresh.  I would definitely recommend this place.

google_reviews.text:
We love the place the food is amazing and very delicious. It is different than other restaurants and very home you can bring your own wine bottle
Pumpkin soup, fried cauliflower, and beets and carrots salad absolutely a must taste.

Honestly, this restaurant is Michelin-star standard. From presentation to flavor, everything is spot on. You can truly feel the chef’s passion in every dish—each plate is crafted with fresh ingredients that allow the natural flavors to shine through. The duck was absolutely delicious, cooked to perfection and bursting with taste. It’s an elevated fine dining experience without any pretense, just pure excellence on the plate. Highly recommend giving it a try—you’ll be impressed from the very first bite to the last!

This is one of my favorite family-run neighborhood restaurants. The food is always delicious and beautifully presented. It may take a little time to prepare, but isn't that kind of the point of a farm to table restaurant where everything is made from scratch?

The restaurant is located in the Bay Ridge section of Brooklyn.  They prepare American cuisine with an additional variety of options.  The food is "farm-to-table" with breakfast and dinner menus.  Customers can choose fruit, breads, eggs, omelets, pancakes and french toast for breakfast.  Dinner choices include soups, salads, entrees with handmade pasta, local vegetables or pasture-raised meat and desserts. I ordered the Amish cheeseburger which included  lettuce, tomato, pickle, bacon and french fries.  The food was very good and well-prepared.  The prices are above average.

We’ve been coming to Beets and Carrots for over five years, and it’s still one of the best-kept secrets in Bay Ridge. The food is consistently exceptional — made with care, creativity, and heart. If this restaurant were on the Michelin radar, I truly believe it would have a star.

The Beets and Carrots salad is fresh, flavorful, and beautifully composed. The mac and cheese is always a standout — especially the seasonal variations. We were obsessed with the pumpkin mac and cheese, and most recently tried the lobster mac and cheese — possibly the best we’ve had in our lives. Rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced.

Everything about this place — from the ingredients to the execution — feels intentional. It’s a local gem and a must-visit if you appreciate food that’s soulful and thoughtfully made.

Thank you Chef! We are lucky to have you in our community ❤️❤️

google_reviews.text: Great food and decent prices. We loved the spicy garlic shrimp, and the schabowy. The Portuguese steak   was good but the cut of strip was not the highest quality  but for $25 one can't complain.  Sangria was definitely a must as well.

This is a place I've passed by so often, I always wondered about it. The foodvis amazing, the ambiance is excellent. The only downside is parking. This is a neighborhood eatery and does not have dedicated parking. I didn't have too much trouble finding street parking. I had the shrimp and scallops for an appetizer, my mother had the Branzini fish entree. She said it was amazing.

Despite that I lived in this area years ago I never visited this place in the past until this December of 2025. My visit exceed all my expectations and Eliana provided me with amazing service. It still has European food and beers with with an amazing latin work force.
It could be somewhat difficult to park depending on the day and time but this place definitely worth the visit.

Mediocre food and service.
Really not impressed by the food and service.

Had the worst perogies here.(It was extremely dry on the inside and hard on the outside?? Like it's been frozen for a long time. It was disgusting 🤮) The Garlic clams are too salty. The pancakes  were alright but the only thing I really liked was the coleslaw and the water🌚😂 I really question the 4.5 rating of this place.🤔

The service is slow on everything. We waited for awhile to be greeted and seated. No one came to help us untill much later, then when we entered, there was 4 empty tables in the back. They didn't serve us bread until we asked about 3 times. Never refilled our water the whole time we're there.

The outdoor seating did not have enough heaters. A lot of the customers were visibly cold.

This is a Restaurant and Bar that refers to itself as American and European. The menu has a mixture of Polish and Portuguese. I believe originally it was owned by a married couple who happened to be Polish and Portuguese. Therefore that marriage led to its diverse menu. It was later sold to one of the workers who is Ecuadorian and kept many of the restaurant’s favorites.

Today we had the Polish cuisine. The waiter and waitress were attentive and professional. They shared the history of the restaurant.

We were happy to their large selection of beers especially the Polish beer which is a favorite of mine. They brought some bread and butter. The bread appeared to be a little stale and wasn’t tasty.

We asked about their pierogi and were told they purchase them from an outside supplier so we elected not to order them. We asked about their potato pancakes which are homemade. They were 4 pieces and thicker than we had at other Polish restaurants. They were good but missed the mark for us.

Next was the Polish pork cutlet served with mashed potatoes and three salads ( beets, coleslaw and red cabbage).

The mashed potatoes were fresh and creamy. The salads were fresh and tasty.

The pork cutlet was a little overcooked and dry. It was thicker than we were accustomed too.

The restaurant was cheerful and a nice decorative. The place is clean and well lit. The bar is well stocked. The restaurant also has outdoor seating.

There is no parking lot but the restaurant has parking arrangements with gasoline station across the street.

We would go back again and try their Portuguese selection but pass on the Polish entrees.

My friend and I went for brunch today, and we were truly impressed. name: Next Door Provisions
document: Next Door Provisions. cuisine: Filipino Noodles Desserts. located in Staten_Island. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Food 4.75/5
Service 5/5
Ambiance 5/5

Amazing Filipino fusion spot!!

Tucked away right next to a cute apartment building, this restaurant is a gem. They use fresh, seasonal ingredients and keep the menu exciting with a rotating selection and different weekend brunch items, you definitely won't get bored!

We loved the super huge portion sizes (we definitely over ordered for two!) and the beautiful presentation of every dish.

What we got:

Kare-Kare (4.75/5): Our absolute favorite! The flavors were spot on, and the twist, using fresh Italian noodles, was new and delicious. The Peruvian pepper, served slightly pickled, added an amazing complementary kick! (Minor note: the meat itself was a bit dry).

Pinoy Breakfast (5/5): A perfect dish. The meat was wonderfully tender, and everything balanced beautifully with the fresh tomatoes, rice, and a touch of vinegar for taste

Street Style Chicken (3.5/5): While I appreciated that they debone the chicken, the white meat part I tried was quite dry. My husband enjoyed the dish or didn’t mind it though

Squid Ink Pasta (4.25/5): A decent dish with a good portion of seafood.

All in all they serve high quality, creative food, big portions, and they even have their own parking area! We will absolutely be back to try the rest of the menu!

SOBRANG SARAP!!! 😋🤤

Kare Kare Mafaldini (5/5) - I had to use all my willpower to not lick leftover sauce from my plate. It was so delicious
Squid Ink Palabok (4.5/5) - I don't usually like squid ink, but to my surprise I still loved this dish nonetheless!

James was so accommodating too. He explained how some of the dishes are made. Fresh ingredients, high quality pasta, and a whole lot of love. We'll definitely be back! 🩵

This spot puts a creative twist on traditional Filipino dishes, elevating them with higher-end—and dare I say, healthier—ingredients than you’d typically expect. (My wife and I ordered brunch specials: Pinoy Plate and Torta Talong.) Unfortunately, it doesn’t quite hit the mark -surprisingly, I missed the oily and salty flavors that is usual on Filipino plates. 🙂

That said, the staff were exceptional—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. The dishes were beautifully presented, and the space itself was well-lit, relaxed, and carried a subtle sense of class. Since this was my first visit, it definitely warrants another try before I make a final judgment.

We tried the French toast, kare-kare malfadini, and tortang talong (stuffed eggplant) at the restaurant, then brought home the adobo and carrot cake. Everything was superb—layers of complex flavors that make you immediately want more. If it’s your first time, I definitely recommend dining in; even the plating feels like artwork. We’ll absolutely be back!

We have come over to this restaurant over 5 times now and everything we had has been delicious. You can feel free to pick any item from the menu. And the service is just excellent!!! This has become our favorite spot in Jersey City!

name: Korai Kitchen
document: Korai Kitchen. cuisine: Bangladeshi Halal. located in Staten_Island. with 4.8 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
Such a great experience!

The food was absolutely phenomenal- I ordered on Sunday for takeout- I ordered the chicken curry and the Sunday breakfast special, which was excellent. They were quite busy when I arrived to pick up my food and it took a little bit longer, but it was well worth the wait.  Which stood up to me most with the hospitality, even though it was a carry out order- A handwritten note was left with my food, apologizing for the wait; and they shared an extra little bite of lentils, which were also delicious. To me, this is true hospitality. They also wrote a nice note on the outside the bag saying eat with your hands and to enjoy the food and thanked me for coming. I highly recommend dining at this restaurant which also offers a tasting menu on Friday and Saturday nights. I am now a lifelong customer.

The food was exemplary, reminiscent of Bengali and Bangal food back home in Kolkata and Bangladesh. I got the rui mach curry and plain rice and because it was my first time ordering out, they added a Dal as well, which was very flavorful and had a 'bhindi' masala aftertaste making it's flavor very different than home but novel. They also added a very sweet note for people ordering for the first time to make added memories for customers.
Overall a terrific experience and I'd highly recommend this restaurant offering authentic Bengali food as the only authentic Bengali restaurant in and near Jersey City.

We had the 3-hour course meal for dinner and it was truly an unforgettable experience. It was such a pleasure meeting the chef and her daughter, who run the place so smartly and gracefully. I absolutely loved how Bangladeshi cuisine was introduced and presented — it's incredibly rare to find a restaurant that stays true to authentic Bangladeshi flavors without mixing in Indian dishes just to please the crowd.

The chef’s creativity really stood out. As someone who’s quite picky and critical with food, I was blown away. It takes a truly talented chef to make you crave another bite even when you’re completely full — and that’s exactly what happened. The food was fresh, lightly marinated, and full of flavor. My husband was transported back to the taste of his mother’s cooking, and I left feeling inspired to try making some of the dishes at home.

This kind of authenticity and warmth is so hard to come by — I’ve already told all my NYC friends about it and will definitely be coming back. A beautiful, delicious, and heartwarming experience all around.
Delightful DAWAT experience.  Thank you so much.  Mrs Korai is a very kind lady and consummate cook. Her daughter is a great host. Every dish had a story.  Can’t wait to go back

I absolutely loved this experience! From the moment I walked in, I could tell this place was something special. The atmosphere was intimate and full of personality—but the real magic? The food.

Every dish felt personal, full of depth and care. You could taste the heart and soul in every bite—so much love went into the cooking. The flavors were rich and complex, but still comforting and familiar. It was the perfect introduction to Bangladeshi food.

If you're looking for something unique, genuine, and truly delicious, this is it. I’ll be thinking about this meal for a long time.

document: True Food Kitchen. cuisine: New American Breakfast & Brunch Comfort Food. located in Staten_Island. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
True Food Kitchen Misses the Mark in Reston

We went with the simple aim of trying something new and arrived at True Food Kitchen with tempered expectations: a casual, health-minded franchise promising balance, freshness, and ease. The experience, however, felt oddly disconnected from that promise.

The seasonal market salad set the tone—wilted greens, muted flavors, and little sense of intention. The butternut squash came in a surprisingly tiny portion and leaned watery, though not unpleasant. French fries ordered for two arrived cold and meager, accompanied by condiments that didn’t resemble mayo or ranch in either taste or texture. The tuna poke disappointed most: a small bowl with flat seasoning and rice so undercooked it crunched. Entrées held the line without distinction—the chicken parmesan and Thai panang curry bowl were serviceable, nothing more.

Service was friendly but hesitant, with a forgotten item and uneven pacing. The dining room, especially for dinner, felt stale and distant rather than lively or welcoming. At nearly $160 for three people, the value equation collapsed. Health-forward food need not sacrifice warmth or execution—but here it did. Two out of five stars.

As a big fan of both pizza and sweet treats, I was excited to find a place that offers healthier choices without sacrificing flavor. The fact that they focus on being seed oil free is what initially caught my attention, and I am so glad it did. Everything tasted fresh and satisfying, proving that better ingredients truly make a difference. The interior also has a warm and inviting feel that makes you want to stay and enjoy your time. A fantastic experience from start to finish.

I like this place, which is why I’m only taking off one star. They use decent ingredients and most of the time — probably about 70% of the time — they get things right.

I remember when I first bought the Bison Egg pizza here and it was fantastic. But recently my DoorDash orders haven’t been like it used to be, including a burger order and this pizza.

I ordered the Sausage & Smoked Gouda Pizza because the photo looked amazing, but what I received looked nothing like the picture and was surprisingly bland. We each tried a piece hoping it would get better, but it didn’t and the rest ended up getting thrown away.

I still think the place has potential, but the consistency and presentation need some work, especially when the photos set certain expectations.

True Food Kitchen is one of the best and healthiest restaurants! The plant-based burger and wild-caught shrimp are absolutely delicious and full of flavor. The flourless chocolate dessert was shockingly good! 100% recommended!

I had a good experience at True Food. The service was friendly and the atmosphere was inviting. I ordered the tenderloin steak for $37 — the portion was on the smaller side and the cut thinner than what you’d get at a steakhouse, though the meat was tender. The nice part is that it’s grass-fed, which adds to the value.

google_reviews.text: Sunset Park icon. No food but they don't care if you bring your own. Support the local legends.

Came to New York for Christmas and New Year’s to have a good time ten amazing days, great people, great places… and then Irish Haven had to be the one spot that reminded us some places still don’t know how to treat customers with basic respect.

One of my friends had been there earlier and got sleepy after a few drinks. He was quiet, not bothering anyone. Instead of handling the situation professionally, the bartender decided to act tough, talk down to us, and escalate things for no reason. Yes, my friend reacted out of frustration, but what followed was totally unnecessary. Aggressive attitude, rude language, and physical pushing while we were already closing out.

And then the comments about “being Irish” and implying he could fight us? Yeah… that energy was not it. As international students and people of color, the whole interaction felt hostile, intimidating, and honestly discriminatory. We’ve been to countless bars including Grumpy Cat Bar this same trip and had nothing but kindness and respect. So trust me, the problem isn’t us.

To top it off, when I came back to pick up my ear muffs and gloves I accidentally left behind, the female bartender started yelling at me from the door like she owns the sidewalk too. Wild behavior for people who clearly don’t know how to handle customers properly.

We respect rules. We respect safety policies. What we don’t respect is unprofessional behavior, power-tripping staff, and hostility toward people who are just trying to enjoy their night. We read other reviews later, turns out we’re not the only ones who felt this way.

Irish Haven didn’t ruin our trip. It just reminded us that not every place deserves our money or our presence. We’ll take our good vibes and business elsewhere. ✌🏽

Arrived before 11pm with a presale ticket to attend the Boys Noize and Juliana Huxtable show on Feb 14th 2026 but was rejected at the door after a 10 second bouncer check.

I’ve played at, produced, and attended thousands of events in my 25+ years of being involved in nightlife and have never discriminated or been discriminated against. I helped bring Boys Noize to the US for his first tour in 2009 and have put hundreds of thousands of dollars into the pockets of marginalized, alternative artists as a promoter.

I get what they are trying to do but this has more in common with discriminatory conservative politics than the electronic music culture I’ve championed for more than half my life. I understand they are trying to emulate Berlin clubs like Berghain but applying these policies in Queens betrays a fundamental misunderstanding of what makes the dance music scene so great.

I’m sure this review won’t make a difference but I feel compelled to say something. Consider supporting other venues with your body, energy, and wallet that don’t have this “you can’t sit with us” exclusionary energy. I take comfort in two truths I know deeply after my time in the scene: This type of venue behavior is thankfully an extreme minority, and everything in nightlife is temporary. How many hundreds of venues named Basement have come and gone over the decades?

In closing, I strongly urge the management who set up this system and designed the layout of the entry area to take seriously the safety of their staff. I’ve seen terrible things happen to door crew over the years and with such a confrontational attitude it’s a matter of when, not if, an angry patron is going to do something stupid that gets the bouncers hurt. There are zero security measures in place ahead of them; this is sadly another fundamental difference between the US and Europe that Basement either doesn’t understand or doesn’t care about.

document: Cave Restaurant. cuisine: Lounges Hookah Bars. located in Staten_Island. with 3.1 stars (decent). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: The tour was well worth the ticket price. Lots of interesting structures to see and our guide (Amber) made the experience a treat. Highly recommend this and a quick pitstop to route 11 potato chip factory to see the production.

Highly recommend going here! I've been to Carlsbad Caverns, the Moaning Caverns and the Black Chasm Caverns and this place is also memorable and different.

You are able to get really close to the structures and cave walls. The route through the cave is also quite memorable. I forget what the structure was called maybe it was called a knight but you see it at first from far away and I was spending time to get the right picture and later on the tour ncame right up to it and since we kind of loop around on the route you will get another chance to get those pictures.

There are some low parts that get as low as 4 ft 4 in. Another memorable is the fact that they put gravel on the floor to make it safer to walk through the cave, which is unlike in other caverns I visited. When you get to see an example of how the cavern floor looks, you will understand why they did it.

The gift shop is also memorable because as soon as you enter there is a gate in the center of the store because actually the entrance to the caverns below.

To the side and upstairs are window displays of yesteryear. Very interesting and I'll leave it at that. Check it out for yourself.

I ended up getting souvenir cup, but I regret not getting one of the geodes. Very fairly priced and would have made another good keepsake.

Tour guide was very knowledgeable and friendly and kept the tour interesting. You can also rent this space for private events.  You don't need to be in shape to go here and the tour takes about an hour but it doesn't feel like it.

Beautiful caverns! I enjoyed the charm of this spot compared to other nearby caverns. They've kept history of the caverns on the walls and have a lovely Cafe with 1950s barstools. The soda fountain was fun - different syrup flavors though our sodas were watered down. I loved the guided tour. Our tour guide was lovely and turned out all the lights, pitch cave black. Really enjoyed this trip.

This is not a comprehensive review, as I was simply passing through on my way back from Georgia to Philadelphia. I decided to make a brief stop of about half an hour to explore Shenandoah Caverns and see what the welcome center had to offer. The welcome center itself was quite impressive, with plenty of gift ideas and souvenirs available. There was also a charming little luncheonette, though unfortunately it was closed until Wednesday. The retro vibe gave it a nostalgic feel, reminiscent of the 1950s.

The entrance to the caverns was conveniently located right inside the welcome center. It had been approximately 35 years since I last visited a cave, with Crystal Cave in Pennsylvania being the most recent. Looking at the pictures, I could see that there were more than 70 steps leading down into the cavern, but there was also an elevator available for those who needed it.

Since I didn't have time to explore the cavern itself, I spent my time in the upstairs museum, which featured animatronics from yesteryear. The pictures on display truly spoke for themselves, showcasing what a fantastic place Shenandoah Caverns is for families and friends to visit. I learned that the tour lasts about an hour, and the temperature inside the cavern is a cool 54°, so it's advisable to bring a sweater or sweatshirt. The overall distance walked during the tour is approximately a mile.

One of the best cavern experiences I have been to. Our guide was extremely knowledgeable. I'm 6'3" and had no problem navigating the caves. There are only a few spots where you need to duck. Overall beautiful and I'll be recommending in the future.

google_reviews.text: A few weeks ago, my friends and I came here to celebrate our friend’s and my boyfriend’s birthdays. Still to today, my boyfriend is talking about what a great experience he had! We learned a lot about a culture and a people we previously knew little about through the family history and the drinks they have crafted for their menu. The bartenders were very patient as my boyfriend asked many questions. We tried quite a few drinks and were impressed with every one. One thing that was interesting is that they used a website system for consumers to open/close tabs and order drinks. This was so useful for us because my boyfriend and I are watching our spending and we could visibly see how tab and how much everything would cost before going to order another drink. I genuinely enjoyed the drink titled Bear on a Plane- it actually comes with a folded paper plane, too! While we were there, there was a live band that were chill.

If you’re looking for a distillery that knows how to mix nostalgia with a modern twist, 3BR Distilling is your new best friend. Their Comrade Pepper is like that childhood favorite soda you secretly still crave, but with a grown-up kick that is both refreshing and dangerously smooth. And then there is the Kofitini. If espresso martinis were a competition, this one would win gold, silver, and bronze all at once. Bold, balanced, and smooth enough to make Sabrina Carpenter proud, though I can’t promise she has tried it yet. Bottom line, if you want to impress your taste buds and maybe even your  crush, start here. 3BR Distilling is serving up drinks that are as clever as they are delicious. Cheers to that!

I can not say enough amazing things about 3BR. We go there pretty often and we held our engagement party there! From the customer service, events, moody space to the high quality cocktails, it is one of the best finds in New Jersey.  Everyone there is amazing!

The drinks are absolutely delicious and creative, the atmosphere is just super cool, and the staff are so sweet and attentive. Our friends had the best time. The staff was knowledgable and attentive and as a small but meanful bonus each bathroom stall was stocked w menstral products. Little touches go a long way. google_reviews.text:
My wife and I have been visiting this brewery since their Long Island City days back in 2015–2016, and from our very first visit, we were impressed by the exceptional quality of their ales. This isn’t your typical brewery serving IPAs, sours, or lagers—instead, they specialize in outstanding ales, some of the finest I’ve ever tasted thanks to their craftsmanship and attention to quality.
The Brooklyn Navy Yard location is a bit more polished than the original Long Island City spot, which had a certain charm with its rustic, industrial vibe. One-of-a-kind brewery@
I must say it is hard to point out my favorite beer! Original tastes, but if I must try A2 intense flavors indead! one favoritesvorite!

Had a great time at Transmitter Brewing. Getting there from Midtown was a breeze—the ferry ride was under 20 minutes, and it’s less than a five-minute walk from the landing to the brewery. We recently stopped by Maison De Viennoiserie, an Algerian-style coffee shop that brings together the best of North African hospitality with a French pastry tradition. The café serves lattes, coffees, soft drinks, and a lovely assortment of Algerian cookies and specialties.
The highlight is undoubtedly their French pastries and viennoiseries. The showcase was filled with beautifully presented treats, from tarts and éclairs in several flavors—chocolate, coffee, vanilla, and more—to the classic mille-feuille, here called “Napoleon.” Everything looked fresh and inviting.
We ordered a coffee and a latte, both excellent and clearly made with quality beans. My wife tried the coffee éclair: while not the very best we’ve ever had (we’re admittedly picky), it was still fresh, tasty, and enjoyable.
During our visit, we overheard someone ordering a sandwich, possibly tacos or another light option, which the staff seemed to prepare in the back. It’s nice to know they also offer savory items beyond pastries.
The atmosphere felt warm and authentic, and the service was excellent—professional, attentive, and welcoming. We’re happy to add this new Algerian spot to our list of go-to places in Brooklyn and look forward to returning to explore more of their menu.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Maison de Viennoiseries at 8101 5th Avenue in Brooklyn, and it’s safe to say this place is a pastry lover's dream! The moment you walk in, you're greeted by the delightful scent of fresh-baked goods, and it only gets better from there.
Their selection of pastries is absolutely top-notch. The croissants are a standout—perfectly flaky, buttery, and golden brown, just as they should be. The pain au chocolat is equally impressive, with just the right amount of rich, melty chocolate that complements the light, airy pastry.
What I love most about this place is the authenticity. The quality and care put into each pastry are clear in every bite. Whether you're enjoying your pastries with a cup of coffee or taking them to go, you can tell you're getting the real deal.
The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, making it easy to ask for recommendations or get a little insight into the ingredients and process behind each treat. It’s a cozy spot that offers a little slice of France right here in Brooklyn.
If you’re in the area, do yourself a favor and stop by Maison de Viennoiseries—you won’t be disappointed!

name: The Morning Roast
document: The Morning Roast. cuisine: Coffee Roasteries. located in Staten_Island. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Absolutely loved our visit to Morning Roast Coffee Shop in Cranford, NJ ☕️✨

Walked in with friends and instantly felt the warmth—not just from the coffee, but from the people. We ordered a flat white and a cortado, and both were beautifully crafted: smooth, perfectly balanced, and clearly made by baristas who really know their coffee. Every sip was a reminder that this place takes quality seriously.

And then came the surprise favorite: their customized hot chocolate flight - such a fun, thoughtful touch and executed to perfection. Rich, indulgent, and playful without being over-the-top. It’s rare to find a coffee shop that does both coffee and hot chocolate this well.

But honestly, the best part? The fabulous service. The baristas are genuinely friendly, welcoming, and happy to chat, recommend, and make you feel right at home. There’s an easy, joyful vibe here—the kind of place you come for a quick coffee and end up lingering because it feels so good to be there.

Morning Roast is the kind of neighborhood gem that turns first-time visitors into regulars. Can’t wait to be back.

Amazing coffee!!! I love interesting and creative takes on food and beverages so I knew I had to try this coffee. I was absolutely blown away, my husband got the sticky rice coffee and I got the seasonal special jelly donut coffee with raspberry cold foam, both were unique and beyond delicious. One of the best coffees I’ve ever had.
But what truly makes this place special is the owner Alex. He’s not only warm and charming but he’s also incredibly knowledgeable and you leave feeling like you just visited a wise friend who is coffee obsessed. This is the type of establishment you think about because of the quality and want to support because of the creative and kind person behind it. Wishing endless success to this little gem of a coffee spot.

A true community gem!

We first visited The Morning Roast for a mommy-daughter date, and it quickly became so much more than just a coffee stop. My husband and 5-year-old soon joined us, and now our youngest (15 months!) is just as obsessed with Alex as we are.

This cozy coffee bar has become our second home — our little one literally falls asleep to the comforting hum of the espresso machine and the warm hugs from Alex (not just the “hug in a cup” 🥰).

The drinks are simply the best handcrafted coffees we’ve ever had — made with love, care, and attention to detail. Beyond the incredible coffee, it’s the kindness, warmth, and sense of community that make The Morning Roast our #1 coffee spot, hands down.

Thank you, Alex, for creating a place that truly feels like home. ☕💛

What a fun place to grab a cup of coffe! Alex, the owner, really knows his stuff and strives for perfection. Well the coffee really was perfect, one of the best cups of coffee I’ve had in awhile. And that’s coming from
A Cranford coffee girl (we know all the different options!). Stop in here for a great cup of coffee and a smile. Also a cool plus is that dogs are welcome!

I stopped by The Morning Roast today just for an ice coffee. I ended up having the best and more unique coffee experience I’ve ever had. Alex was so wonderful, approachable and knowledgeable about everything! The location is perfect, inside it is comfortable and you can play a game of darts and it is a perfect place to bring friends. The coffee is outstanding and completely personalized and curated by Alex. Whether you’re a coffee snob or not, Morning Roast accessible for everyone, even non-coffee drinkers. I can’t say enough good things, you have to go and experience it for yourself!! Thank you again Alex can’t wait to come back

name: KK's Cafe
document: KK's Cafe. cuisine: Cafes Coffee & Tea Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: Had lunch here & loved the variety!  Excellent service, & the food came out quick!  My salad was pretty & delicious, both.  My only regret, I should have asked about the Chicken Stew I ordered...I was imagining Chicken Fricassée, like chicken over rice with gravy, but it was more like a "roux soup" with small pieces of chicken. (Not sure why I only photographed my guests' food!)😜 Over all, an A+, & we'll be back!

If you haven’t tried this restaurant you are missing out. I consider this place the gem of Youngsville ❤️❤️ the food is top notch! I work a graveyard shift so at 7 am I want dinner sometimes instead of breakfast! I’ve had crawfish ettoufee at 8 am and it was so good!!!!! This time I had breakfast.  So many options to choose from! The wait staff is excellent and the people who eat here are friendly too. The atmosphere is warm and down home , great family place. And don’t leave without beignets or cheese cake to go!! Try KK’s if you haven’t yet, you WON’T be dissatisfied!!! They are the best!

The service was excellent. The food was great and with that being said the place was crowded. We didn't have to wait at all but I think almost every table was full. It seems to be a really popular place. Overall it was great.

I would give KK’s a thousand gold stars if it would let. I went there with my Aunt Pat today around noon to eat some amazing breakfast that I’ve had so many times over at KK’s until the table next to us ordered and received the most delicious looking CHICKEN FRIED STEAK with mashed potatoes and white gravy…. After watching this gentleman take his first 3 bites with a huge smile on his face then sharing a bite with of his family members and witnessing their faces. I decided to order the CHICKEN FRIED STEAK for myself and so did my sweet Aunt Pat..  ok now for mine and my Aunt’s descriptions for  this was “The Very BEST Chicken Fried Steak” which was a  HUGE PORTION” (2) steaks per plate😲🤤.. and  the BEST we have ever eaten in our entire lives  by far the best in the state of Louisiana hands down. The Chicken Fried Steak was so tender with a crunchy texture that came out hot and fresh.. The white gravy was so delicious and we have never had such an amazing tasting white gravy that was perfectly seasoned and you would want to drink a bowl of it at least we definitely would. On to the mashed potatoes, they are absolutely home cooked and so very delicious and steaming hot of course they were topped with some more white gravy (yummy). The Fried Pistolette that came with the meal was delicious as well.
I forgot to mention our best ever appetizer which was fried Okra and (2) gigantic buttermilk homemade biscuits.! As you can tell I’m a #1 fan of KK’s amazing food.!!! I live in Lafayette and will continue to drive here for amazing home cooked breakfast, lunch and dinner as often as twice a week or even more.
They have a drive thru that makes it convenient when I’m in a hurry but otherwise I love eating in the perfect environment and music experience ever. The owners are there every day I go and are always checking on all tables which is very important. I ask God to continue to bless everyone involved. Well that’s all I gotta say about KK’s right now 🎤. I really can’t say enough about every experience or this would be too long. Thanks for taking the time to read. Have a blessed day 🙏🏼❤️🇺🇸

My wife & I love this little joint!
There's something for everyone on the menu, and it's a full menu all day!
So while my wife is enjoying her avocado toast, I'm devouring corn & crab bisque with some fried okra on the side.
Haven't tried one of their homemade cheese cakes yet, but there's always tomorrow!

name: Kijitora
document: Kijitora. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: I've been there 3 times already and wow, we tried their black sesame latte with white chocolate and the matcha with white chocolate, also matcha sweetened with maple syrup, and matcha with honey – all of them delicious! And don't even get me started on their mochi brownie, absolutely amazing! So if you're a matcha lover, you have to check this place out! 💚🍵

I got a black sesame latte with white chocolate and my chummy over here got a matcha hot white chocolate. IT WAS SO GOODDDDD especially for the chilly season. And the white chocolate was an amazing sweetener. I was a little intimated because of how cute and small the shop was but the worker was so so nice and made me feel really comfortable. The shop was nice and warm too and there was a lot of cute cat themed stuff. I literally couldn’t stop thinking about the drinks throughout the rest of my journey in the day and I tried my buddy’s drink. Quite the quality drink, the matcha came through really well.

We were lucky to stumble across this little hole in the wall! The tiramisu and black sesame latte were perfectly balanced, velvety, rich, hugs in cups. Definitely go with the sesame latte (without white chocolate) if you want something unique and not too sweet. Our barista was kind and quick. The place is very small so you’ll be taking your coffee to go, but the decor is minimalistic yet warm and we enjoyed browsing the cat themed trinkets for sale. Highly recommend!

In a neighborhood saturated with coffee shops… this is my favorite spot for matcha especially their outrageously good iced strawberry matcha- but also they have a black sesame latte that feels like a full body hug. Seriously.

It’s tiny and they have cutesy art items, coffee and tea for purchase, some baked goods. I really really like this spot and may be in my top three
coffee shops I Brooklyn.

A perfect pit stop on Driggs Ave. Whether I’m heading into the city or just about to start my day, Kijitora never disappoints. Their croissants—plain or chocolate—are on another level, genuinely the best I’ve had in Brooklyn, baked fresh right there in the shop. Every pastry feels like it just came out of the oven, and you can taste the care in each bite. Drinks are always spot-on too, consistently balanced and smooth. It may be a small café without a full kitchen, but the atmosphere and quality are insanely good. A true neighborhood gem.

name: Gumption Coffee
document: Gumption Coffee. cuisine: Coffee Roasteries Coffee & Tea Sandwiches. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text: My wife and I visited NYC during a blizzard and stopped to warm up with coffee and an almond milk matcha. They are top atmosphere is fun, coffee tasty and high quality, and the matcha was very healthy and could use some added sugar to sweeten it up. The baristas were awesome and provided fun and great service. We really enjoyed our first time to Gumptown.

Gumption clearly prides itself on deep coffee knowledge and serious experience — and they make sure you know it. Unfortunately, the focus seems to lean more toward coffee than toward people.

I had a cortado, which is usually my benchmark for judging bean quality, extraction, and latte art. Sadly, none of the three really stood out. Perfectly drinkable, but far from memorable — especially considering the reputation.

But here’s the bigger issue: coffee simply never tastes as good when the people serving it make you feel like you’re not particularly welcome in their shop. Expertise is great; hospitality is better.

Too bad, because the potential is clearly there.

I've walked by this coffee shop a few times, and it definitely catches your eye -- vibrant colors, cool art, and a really nice setup even though the space is small. I tried the iced pistachio salted caramel latte from their seasonal menu, but it was way TOOOOOO sweet for me. The pistachio flavor completely overpowered everything, and I couldn't taste the caramel at all. Not really a fan of this one. Meh.

Was looking for some coffee after trying the "espresso" at our hotel and this place DID NOT DISAPPOINT. The decor is cute and welcoming, the staff was super friendly, and the coffee was delicious and made up fast. My brother and I got the Bananas in Pajamas (tasted like warm bananas 🤤) and the Pistachio & Salted Caramel Latte. Could not believe how good they were. Highly recommend!

I was so excited to have a slice of home so close to my hotel, and it didn't disappoint.

The coffee was silky with a beautiful crema. Just the way coffee should be served. It has a bit of an Australian taste to it, so slightly less roasted than Italian blends.

The location is small, but there was sitting and it was comfortable.

name: Qahwah House
document: Qahwah House. cuisine: Coffee & Tea. located in Staten_Island. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Qahwa Cafe, located inside a mosque in Sterling, VA, offers a warm, well-lit environment. It features tasty espresso beverages like Dulce de Leche and Matcha Latte, along with a selection of teas, baked goods, and sweets. Both the Dulce de Leche and Matcha Latte were flavorful and not diluted, demonstrating quality, and the homemade-style brownie was enjoyable without being overly sweet. However, drink preparation times were quite long, even though no other customers were waiting. Cleanliness was an issue due to food on the floor.

Additionally, there was no signage indicating the cafe's location in the area or outside the building, which appears to be a mosque from the exterior. We had to drive through the parking lot to find the entrance, and more apparent signs could help visitors locate the cafe more easily.
Very nice people. The boys working here are very polite and warm. Their chamomile tea was one of the best I got. I set outside on the deck and was able to charge my phone.
The cafe worker Reda was friendly, fast, and made my drink exactly how I wanted it. He made the whole place feel welcoming, and I’d definitely come back because of his great service.

Great atmosphere and rich drinks!! If you see the other pics of the iced drinks you know how mouth-watering they look. I was so happy with my iced Cherry Blossom Latte, which has the hint of flavor without overpowering the coffee!

For those who are non-Muslim, please don’t go here! I don’t understand why there is no disclosure that this place is open exclusively for Muslims.

It’s located inside a mosque, which I thought it was just a regular coffee shop (they should disclose this information - maybe they don’t wanna sound discriminatory). When arrived there, I was not welcomed there, and when I asked how to could get to the coffee shop (assume it might be different entrance from the Mosque) I was told by the person that literally stand in front of the door to go ask somebody else how we can get in (at this rate, obviously I was not welcome!)

Again, for those who are non Muslims, don’t come here!!!!!

google_reviews.text: Firth River is a little gem in the River District Market Place in Sperryville VA. This delightful coffee shop knows how to make an excellent brew. Masters of cold brew, French press, espresso or pour over, your barista will make you a delicious cup of coffee that will satisfy your coffee cravings. Be sure to check out the gelato too, it’s sweet creamy taste is sure to bring back memories of wandering the streets in Rome.

We visited early on a Sunday morning. The coffee shop opens BEFORE the restaurant and shops. The service was excellent in a very cute setting with parking right next to the river walk to continue your journey. I got the cardamom latte. They make the syrup in house and don’t mess around. If you a cardamom latte that actually tastes like cardamom, with a nice warm spicy punch. Perfect for fall.

We couldn't be more pleased with our experience at Firth River Coffee Company! Kerry and Bridget, our two points of contact, provided us with excellent communication, customer service, and hospitality during our small gathering event at their location. They went above and beyond to make sure we felt welcomed and had all we needed. They personalized our food selections to represent and reflect us as a couple as well as acknowledge and support severe allergies we had noted in our food selections.

We will forever share how wonderful our experience was with you and we can't wait to come back and visit!

Kerry and Bridget, thank you for being such a special part of our day!
Fun, vibrant spot with delicious coffee drinks and gelato. It has a delightful front porch to enjoy the weather. There is an artisan market next door that is worth a visit!

Thoroughly enjoyed Sunday's "Boarding School for Cheese and Charcuterie" event - to discover how to prepare and present beautiful and absolutely delicious cheese, charcuterie, vegetable, and fruit boards.  On arrival, a table was set as an elegant and beautiful feast, with each item intended for use in our creations.  Once the table offered up its wealth, the "boards" themselves became the visible -- and edible -- bounty.  Local wines were part of our learning experience, as was camaraderie and good conversation.  A wonderful way to move into the holidays with fresh ideas, delivered lovingly and generously by Bridget Kosene, along with her obvious skill.  A joy from start to finish.  Highly recommend this experience, so well served by the atmosphere of the historic Marketplace.

document: Ayala Coffee. cuisine: Cafes Coffee & Tea Filipino. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: I loved this cafe! The service was quick and friendly. The atmosphere was wonderful and very aesthetic. I really love the wall with all of the different Filipino decor. We got the tocino breakfast sandwich, the onion bistek burger, and the sisig flatbread. For drinks, I got the cardamom and fig latte and my boyfriend got the ube latte. We LOVED the sandwiches especially for the portions and our drinks (my bf finished most of his drink before the food even came out). For the sisig flatbread, we thought the egg yolk overpowered the dish a little bit, but we still thought it was delicious. Overall, we will definitely come back again to try the other options :)

I come here at least once a week with friends, we either get the smash burger which is amazing, or the sisig flatbread which is also amazing. The staff is friendly, patient, and the ambiance is chill and lively. For Valentine’s Day they had a special menu and I got the calamansi cake and the raspberry cake, both were amazing and made my partner very happy (they are Filipino). My only complaint is that they don’t have a rewards program for frequent customers because I would definitely sign up 🫡

Coming from the old location, everything is still top quality! The pandan Katie is just as full of flavor when it was in a smaller setting. I’m glad Matt and Trixie stayed true to there vision.

The addition of food and pastries is welcome addition. The pastry chefs are top tier, such good stuff coming from the back of the house.

I believe you will enjoy everything, and find yourself coming back to try the other options on the menu. Thanks!

Came on an early monday and the place was already busy. We found a spot for two but by 10:30am almost all the seats were taken.

We got their spamganisa and tocino sandwich, pastries and of course their lattes. Surprisingly, I enjoyed the tocino more than the spam as the latter didnt really taste exactly like spam as it was flavored differently. Lacked the salty and savory taste i was used too lol The tocino though was sweet and had that savory taste which i liked. The pastries were good and i actually loved the ube champorado croissant.

for the lattes, i tried their apple pie. I shouldve thought about how im not really info fruity lattes so this was a no-go for me - shouldve just gotten their signatures but i tend to try something new so there’s that. Would still love to come back though! My first ube, pandan and cassave lattes (from their old location) was sooo good and memorable! Gonna have to pay attention to how to make it one of these day and copy them at home lol

I absolutely love Ayala Coffee! The coffee and matcha are of high quality, the pastries are always fresh, and the food is phonemail!

I have my go-to order - an egg & cheese with a strawberry matcha - but every time I branch out and try something new, I end up finding another favorite. The consistency never misses.

The staff are very personable and make a genuine effort to remember my name and even my usual order, which makes every visit feel welcoming! Thank you to Trixie and the entire team for the amazing hospitality, coffee and food!

Had the flat white, service was great but the flat white did not taste strong at all it was mostly milk, I could taste the coffee quality but the milk overpowered it
A nice lil coffee Hot spot! Loving this Bronx corner coffee shop! Wish we had one right on the edge Texas!! ☕️  delicious 😋

This is literally the only legit coffee spot on 8th Ave or nearby and while it’s a shame they do not have any seating, I still highly recommend it.

Not many places in the U.S. sell coconut latte, but they do and it’s not powder!

It’s a tiny but popular coffee spot even if it’s on the pricier side. What makes them stand out is their service. They do a great job at making the coffee and they have the best service I’ve ever experienced in Chinatown and heck even in NY.

Leo, the barista, was also very sweet and kind and has a great memory. I hope the owner is able to acknowledge his hard work.

If you’re looking for a good quick coffee stop around 8th avenue this is a great spot; especially since there aren’t many around the area it immediately catches your attention. They have a small menu to choose from but super interesting flavors like their seaweed coffee. I got the brown sugar shaken this time and i was blown by how good it was. The coffee was not overly sweet and had cheese foam on top. This is one of my favorite orders and they nailed it here.

name: The Monroe
document: The Monroe. cuisine: Themed Cafes. located in Staten_Island. with 4.9 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
Just go. Do yourself the biggest favor and go.

When I tell you everything here is just perfection, I mean it. From their service (shout out Stephanie & Dani!) to their vibes to their food! The aesthetic and vibes are immaculate - Its’s fun with a hint of moodiness.

I tried their Kung Pao Cauliflower and Fried Chicken. A few friends tried their salmon and burger. Their food was made thoughtfully with fresh ingredients and portions were excellent. Their fried chicken was salted to perfection with the right amount of spices and THAT CRISP will send you outta this world. I don’t know how their chicken remained moist and tender! The Mac n cheese is also to die for - noodles were al dente with the right amount of cheese.

I was here with a large group and Stephanie serviced us seamlessly. The entire staff was so nice and friendly! Catch the chef throwin the peace sign!

From start to finish the meal for our party of 3 was superb. For the first time in a while, the food at a restaurant has warranted the tab at the end of the night. The food was amazing!! Seriously hit the spot. Biscuits and gravy are elite, and honestly a great appetizer to start your meal. Everything came out hot, fresh, and cooked right.

Dinner, on the other hand—WOW. We came last week and that fried chicken meal with the mac and cheese and mashed potatoes was 10/10 (really 100000/10). Absolutely delicious!

The service is always great here, too—the servers are attentive and make the experience even better. I’ll definitely be back for dinner, and I’d be open to giving brunch another shot.

The Monroe truly surprised me in the best way. I spend a lot of time in the area, and this is hands-down my favorite brunch so far. Every dish was balanced...nothing felt over-sauced or overworked. From sweet to savory, everything tasted intentional and well-executed. And the mocktails absolutely live up to their name and price point. They were thoughtfully crafted, refreshing, and definitely not just juice over ice. Overall, such a great experience from start to finish.

P.s. The breakfast sandwich is not small but it is so so good.

We did come more towards early dinner. It was pretty empty which was nice. The venue is an older joint.  You can tell it's been around and done it's time.  Usually a clear indicator that the food should be good! I'm not supposed to be around a lot of people so the fact it was empty made me feel comfortable eating here. We walked in and were greeted.  Homie wasn't the nicest but he got us sat. The menu is quite huge! I love all the options available. And the prices! The prices of everything was reasonable.

As much as I wanted something huge and hearty, I ordered the won ton soup with egg noodles.  I thought the broth would be good for my soul since I have been living off of hospital food for the last week. I don't think my stomach could handle such a big, hearty meal.  Nothing sounds more delicious than 7 or 8 different dishes with a huge bowl of steamed rice.

The won ton came out in these big beautiful white bowls. You can smell the sesame oil from the broth.  You see chunky pieces of the won ton. A good portion of egg noodles. And gracious portions of bok choy.

The broth hit so good with that first sip.  It was rich and savory. You can tell that broth had been cooked for a long time. The won tons were not lacking.  They were meaty and salty. You get 6 big pieces of won ton.  The noodles had a slight chew to them which was nice.  Soggy noodles isn't it! I enjoyed a majority of my broth.  I did eat a won ton and some of the noodles.  That's all my stomach would allow.

He was interacting with us, got us to go containers and our bill.  I feel like that's your basic baseline of service and our original server failed.

I know I will be back.  I have read the reviews about their dim sum and they seem pretty legit. I enjoy the carts of dumplings and fried vodka being pushed around .  The sound of people's chopsticks hitting plates.  The loud noise of eating and being merry. It's the sound of my childhood growing up in the Bay Area and u can't wait to relive it! I guess I will finalize my ranking in a couple weeks when I got this joint up.  But for today, they were ok with food and service combined.

Bay Ridge just got itself a brand‑new Chinese spot, and let me tell you—Lucky Xin Hui Chinese Inc. is already living up to its name. This place is lucky to have landed in our neighborhood, and we’re even luckier to have discovered it early. If the locals show this place some love, it has every chance of becoming a long‑standing favorite.

My man and I started with an order of fried wontons, planning to split them as a light appetizer. They arrived crisp, golden, and perfectly snackable—exactly the kind of warm‑up you want before diving into the real stars of the menu.

Now, let’s talk about the combination platters, because this is where Lucky Xin Hui truly shines.

My Man’s Dish: Roasted Pork with String Beans in Garlic Sauce (over white rice)
I have never—never—tasted pork like this from a Chinese takeout spot. Usually, roasted pork tends to mimic that familiar “pork rib” flavor profile, but this? This was something entirely different. The pork had its own distinct identity: deeply savory, beautifully umami, and unbelievably tender. Paired with crisp string beans and a fragrant garlic sauce, the whole platter was absolutely scrumptious. My man was in heaven, and honestly, I kept stealing bites.

My Dish: Roasted Chicken & Eggplant in Garlic Sauce (over fried rice)
This is one of my all‑time favorite Chinese dishes, and I’ve ordered it from countless places over the years—but Lucky Xin Hui’s version is on a whole different level. The roasted chicken was juicy and flavorful, the eggplant silky and rich, and the garlic sauce had the perfect balance of savory heat without overwhelming the palate.

And the fried rice? Don’t let its pale color fool you. I took one look and thought, “Oh no, this is going to be bland.” I was so wrong. The flavor was explosive—light, aromatic, and the perfect companion to the chicken and eggplant. Every bite was a little firework.

A Neighborhood Newcomer Worth Supporting
Lucky Xin Hui is new to our neighborhood, and you can feel the heart they’re putting into their food. This is the kind of place that deserves a loyal local following—the kind of spot that becomes your Chinese place, the one you recommend to friends, the one you crave on a random Tuesday night.

We walked away completely in love with the food and the restaurant itself. It’s official: we’ve found our new Chinese spot, and we’re rooting for Lucky Xin Hui to thrive here for years to come.

google_reviews.text:
We’ve eaten at a few Bib Gourmands in the past and we mean it when we say it: this place deserves a star. We had a reservation and the place was so packed it had a line around the block at the opening for dinner service. The wait was about 15-20 minutes from when they opened as they were working quickly to get everyone seated and setup. We were seated at their family sized tables in the back and the service was fantastic. We ordered quite a bit of food since we had a large party so here’s a list of what we got:

Pork dumplings 8/10 - devoured in minutes within our party, everyone loved it.
Salt & pepper spare ribs 10/10 - some of, if not, the best we’ve ever had. Perfect seasoning and chew to them.
Fried rice 9/10 - just delicious, nothing special about it and yet still amazing.
Ginger scallion crab 6/10 - seafood is not really our thing to be fair, but we still did enjoy the meat, the sauce was a bit of a miss though.
Duck bone soup 9/10 - unbelievably good, the cilantro and onion pack it with flavor and the consistency is great.
Broccoli, beef, and string beans 8/10 - a classic just done right, seasoned well and broccoli with a good chew; beef perfect texture and velvety.
Chicken chow mein 10/10 - perfect chew, perfect flavor. Would’ve ordered another if we weren’t so full.
Peking duck with steamed buns and flat bread 11/10 - on this scale an 11 denotes it’s the best we’ve ever had, just in case you thought we failed 1st grade math. Crispy skin and delicious, tender meat.

Great China is undoubtedly some of the best Chinese food we’ve ever had. Add onto the fact that it’s at a better value than other places and it becomes clear that this is a special place. The food itself deserves a star but sprinkle in the service and it begs the question as to why it doesn’t have one. More on the service actually, they were incredibly patient as we ordered many dishes with different requests and were on top of everything from refilling water and tea to removing plates. When the only issue with a place is the parking situation then you know it’s good. (Side note: parking is pretty hard to find and we saw a lot of cars getting tickets for invalid parking so keep an eye out). That shouldn’t deter anyone though as this place might just be worth that fine, half kidding. Do yourself the favor and come here at all costs.

The service is average but is sort of typical for Chinese restaurants...live with it.  Tried a few new dishes this time and they were amazing...Chinese Green Beans is a new favorite!

And the steak dishes are always tender which is not always the case as most Chinese food establishments.  Service is quick and efficient.   I’ve never found better Chinese anywhere.  The quality is definitely worth the price.

The food was great. The tang su yuk could have been better if it had been cooked crispier. It was a bit soggy with the sauce, but the pork and vegetables were well-cooked and complemented the sauce harmoniously.

I was pleasantly surprised by the eggplant dish. The sauce was delicious.

I didn’t expect that the black fungus would be so good with both dishes. I enjoyed the texture.

We visited this restaurant on a Friday during peak hours, so we had to wait for about 10 to 15 minutes. However, it was worth the wait. The atmosphere was vibrant and filled with joy. I would definitely visit again.

We came here to celebrate a birthday and ordered the Peking Roast Duck, Double Skin, Zhen Jiang Spareribs, and Chinese String Beans with Beef and Mushrooms.

The Peking Roast Duck and the Double Skin were both excellent! The whole duck was deboned and came with 24 pancakes, which you can pair with plum sauce and scallions. My favorite dish was the Double Skin; it was my first time trying it. It came with Mung bean noodles, carrots, cucumber, egg crepe, calamari, shrimp, sea cucumber, onions, mushrooms, and pork. The combo of ingredients created a flavorful and unique texture that I really enjoyed. I highly recommend this dish! The other dishes were also quite good.

*Make sure to make a reservation online to avoid a long wait. Parking is a bit difficult around the area.
