name: Shang Gong Chu
document: Shang Gong Chu. cuisine: Chinese. located in Staten_Island. with 4.5 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I’m so glad this restaurant is here. The interior is very elegant, with comfortable seating that makes it easy to relax and enjoy your time.

The manager, Nate, is incredibly friendly and accommodating. I reserved two tables ahead of time for a group of 16, and he took the time to make sure everything went smoothly, even offering great food recommendations. The service was superb.

Food we ordered: Highly recommend the roast Peking duck, which comes with soup. I also really enjoyed their other soups as well.

All the ladies had a wonderful time, and we never felt rushed to leave.

We had been to this restaurant a few times on weekdays for lunch. The decor was modern and service friendly.

Dishes were nicely presented and we liked most of what we tried including Garlic shrimp on an iron plate, Scallion stir-fried beef, Sauteed beef with cilantro, and Hot green pepper with chicken.

Their Peking duck was good, but the skin could be crispier and the wrappers didn't have the right texture and tend to stick together. We didn't like the Claypot tofu dish. It was a bit bland.

Glad to have this restaurant near where we live.

We came by for their authentic Chinese dishes and particularly enjoyed their taro with pork. The roasted duck was fairly standard, but the wrap was an odd choice. The mushroom and eggplant were a good amount of spice that paired well with rice.
The overall decor was nice - I enjoyed the bonsai. It can get a bit loud at times
Nicely presented dishes in upscale interior setting.  Liked the string beans out of what we ordered.  Solid Peking duck for NJ.

What happens when wealthy Mainlanders grow out of their wild Manhattan party days (and nights) to settle down in Jersey City?

The authentic, high-quality Chinese restaurants follow suit. You go where the money is, folks.

Shang Gong Chu is yet another example of this trend, opening in a haunted restaurant space that never saw much success and was most recently occupied by a place that offered Japanese-Malaysian food (wut?).

While SGC has stiff competition from some top-notch Chinese restaurants within the immediate area, it quite admirably holds its own as a newcomer. Our dishes, from best to worst:

- Braised Hyacinth Beans With Pounded Chili: I don't see these beans often, and they offer that wet crunch that I love so much in beans. Get this for umami legume goodness.

- Pork Belly With Shredded Bamboo Shoots: Channel your inner panda with this tasty dish. Bamboo shoots also offer that wet crunch texture I love, and this comforting dish made great use of them.

- Salted Egg Yolk Mushrooms: Well-marinated and perfectly seasoned

- (Free) Yunnan Spicy Minced Pork With Chili And Herbs: We spun the wheel at the entrance and won this tasty appetizer. It was savory and delicious, like your grandma's heartiest stir-fry.

- Claypot Tofu: Solid tofu texture but a bit under-seasoned

- Crispy Fried Pork Bites: To satisfy all our inner Popeyes kids

- Garlic Shrimp On Ironplate: Not really sizzling, like ironplates usually are, but loaded with enough plump, juicy shrimp for our group of 6. Be warned: You have to reeeeally like minced garlic (and don't kiss anyone for like two hours afterward)

- Chongqing Style Fried Chicken: Just okay. Not spicy enough and not crispy enough, especially with Peppercorn Station around the corner wearing the crown for years

- Steamed Egg: We actually forgot we ordered this, and so did the staff, so we didn't get it until we were nearly done. I don't know if the late serving influenced my perception, but I found the dish lackluster and not worth the price.

Service was decent overall, though they were a bit busy and hard to flag down in the middle of our meal. The decor is on par with most of the good Chinese restaurants in downtown Jersey City, mixing classical Chinese aesthetics with modern touches. Shang Gong Chu might carve out its niche by being the most spacious of the top-quality Chinese restaurants--great for large groups. In fact, given the price points and portion sizes, I don't think I'd come with any group smaller than five people.

Also, it's always fun to spin a wheel of (Chinese) fortune.

Last night, my neighbor stopped by unexpectedly. We decided to order crispy duck as we love Peking Gourmet in Fall Church and haven’t been in years. Colossal mistake. This was NOT that.

The first thing we immediately noticed after opening the container was what appeared to be a   large, chewed up bone sitting on top of the bit of crispy skin. B/C it was mostly bare, we were confused. Why anyone would think to include it? Was this a mistake? Was I given an employees meal by accident? Was it a disgusting mistake?

After removing the gnawed on bone, we saw the duck meat looked old, gross and gray. Samantha took a bite and said it was tasteless and rubbery. I called the restaurant and spoke to the same guy who’d sold me the culinary catastrophe. I emphasized the random, chewed up bone and he stated I could bring it back for a refund.

Today, as soon as I entered, I was met with contemptuous glares by the cooks; an old man in a dusty blue hat and filthy apron sitting in the back of the restaurant & an old woman picking her greasy scalp while cooking without gloves. REPULSIVE. It was a look behind the curtain that I never asked for. I couldn’t unsee it, though I desperately wanted to.

The cooks began yelling at each other and pointing to the bag of BS I’d brought back. Then, as I’m handing the cashier my card for the refund, the old man comes over and begins to scream in my face. I don’t speak the language but I smelled his hot & sour halitosis breath. I turn my face and take a step back in an attempt to shield myself from his offensive stench. It was repulsive, ungodly and deliberate.

Curious but calm, I asked the cashier what the old man said and he laughed at me. I asked again and he nervously said, “nothing, nothing, nothing. It’s ok. Everything ok” as the old woman aggressively stomped by me to trash her gastronomic repugnance.

I must’ve stuck a cord as it seems most reviewers state they took the loss. Glad I was reimbursed but my goodness, talk about insult to injury! Do yourself a favor: forgo the trauma, drama and vulgarity. Get the duck from Peking Gourmet Inn, in Falls Church and get the MSG anywhere else.

document: Istanbul Grand Bazaar. cuisine: International Grocery Specialty Food Farmers Market. located in Staten_Island. with 4.8 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
We visited the Grand Bazaar several times as we were staying close by, and it’s an incredible place to experience. It’s always very busy and absolutely buzzing with activity, with hundreds of stalls both inside and out. You can find pretty much everything imaginable here — from clothing, jewellery and souvenirs to spices, leather goods, lamps, and homeware. There are also plenty of restaurants and coffee shops dotted throughout, making it easy to stop for a break.
The quality of the goods on offer is generally very good, and one thing I really appreciated was that the sellers weren’t pushy. If you’re not interested, they leave you alone, which makes browsing much more enjoyable.
The only downside is that prices can be a little higher than elsewhere in the city, as it’s clearly a tourist hotspot. My advice would be to take note of what you want and compare prices, as you’ll find similar items sold all over Istanbul.
Overall, it’s a brilliant experience and somewhere you absolutely have to visit. 4 out of 5 – a must-see when in Istanbul.

The Grand Bazaar is a fascinating place to visit and definitely one of the most unique experiences in Istanbul. The market is huge, with countless shops selling everything from spices and sweets to lamps, textiles, jewelry, and souvenirs. Walking through the covered streets and seeing the colorful displays is an experience in itself.

At the same time, it does feel a bit like a hustler’s den, as many shopkeepers are very eager to get your attention and bring you into their stores. It’s all part of the atmosphere, but it’s good to come prepared to politely decline and take your time browsing.

Even if you’re not planning to buy much, it’s still worth visiting to see the historic market, explore the maze-like corridors, and enjoy the lively energy of the place.

"A vibrant, historic city like Istanbul wouldn't be complete without its legendary Grand Bazaar. Given its prime location on the Silk Road and the Spice Road, the deep history of this place is 'crystal clear.' It’s a place where you can still feel the echoes of Constantinople’s golden age.

Yes, it is incredibly crowded—more than words can describe!—but it is an absolute 'must-visit.' Amidst the hustle and bustle, if you look closely, you can still find authentic, original handmade crafts and treasures. It’s a refreshing change in a world dominated by mass-produced items. Walking through these ancient corridors is like stepping back in time. Prepare for the crowd, but definitely don't miss the experience!"

Got there early for dinner and was seated right away. I love that they offered the Japanese skewers. We ordered pork belly, beef, and shrimp. All were amazing! We wish we ordered more of them. Also ordered the Gyoza that had pork and chicken in them. They were good but the ponzu sauce wasn’t the best. I ordered the Sake Don which was raw salmon with seasoned sushi rice. Service was outstanding, and the vibe was cozy with relaxing background music. Overall, a very satisfying experience—I’ll definitely come back!

Thank you so much!

New favorite sushi restaurant in the neighborhood! The crabmeat rangoon and red roof roll were delicious, flavorful and very fresh. Sometimes this restaurant runs BOGO deals on Uber Eats (and maybe other food delivery platforms) so definitely take advantage of that!

As a Virginia resident, I typically avoid the trek into DC due to the notorious traffic. However, knowing the owner of this sushi restaurant and his reputation for impeccable Japanese craftsmanship, I decided to make the journey—and it was absolutely worth it.

From the moment I stepped inside, I was welcomed by a serene and inviting ambiance that set the stage for an exceptional dining experience. The owner’s dedication to authentic Japanese hospitality is evident in every detail, from the decor to the service.

The sushi here is nothing short of extraordinary. Each piece is crafted with the utmost care, showcasing the freshness of the ingredients. The flavors are vibrant and harmonious, with the fish practically melting in your mouth. The rice is perfectly seasoned, complementing the fish beautifully.

One of the standout aspects of this restaurant is the presentation. Every dish is a visual masterpiece, arranged with an artist’s eye for detail and aesthetics. The colorful and elegant plating enhances the overall dining experience, making it as visually satisfying as it is delicious.

Despite the high quality of the food and presentation, the prices are surprisingly reasonable. This balance of affordability and excellence is rare and makes the restaurant even more appealing.

In conclusion, this sushi restaurant in DC is a hidden gem that is worth braving the traffic for. The combination of incredible freshness, exquisite flavors, beautiful presentation, and reasonable prices, all delivered with genuine Japanese craftsmanship, makes it a must-visit. For anyone seeking a top-tier sushi experience, this place is not to be missed.

google_reviews.text: We were seated and waited on very quickly. Ordered some Chashu Buns as our app,which were decent, but we've had better. Mr. Bin often comes over a to check up on the table and make sure that everything is up to his standards. His sushi & oysters are delicious. We will be back!

Some of the best sushi around. They have omakase and really fresh fish flown in for their specials. My wife and I shared the sushi/sashimi for two. Fish was fresh and tasty. Mr Bin is friendly and will tell you the specials to try.
One of the better places, but rice is too cold.. doesn't adhere as sushi. Memu is fresh and selection varies. Sashimi> sushi

google_reviews.text:
Let me start by saying that from the outside, Izakaya doesn't look like much—just a modest storefront that could easily blend into the street. But the second you walk through the door, the vibe completely shifts. The interior is sleek and inviting, with warm lighting, modern Japanese-inspired decor, and a cozy atmosphere that instantly makes you feel like you've stepped into something special.

We kicked off the meal with a couple of standout appetizers: the crispy rice topped with tuna and the filet mignon. Both were executed perfectly—the crispy rice had that ideal crunchy texture with fresh, melt-in-your-mouth tuna, and the filet was tender and richly flavored without being overpowering.

For the main event, we dove into the sushi rolls: the Disney roll (playful and packed with surprises), the Hawaiian roll (tropical and refreshing), the Tom roll (bold and inventive), and a classic spicy tuna roll. Everything was incredibly fresh, with vibrant flavors that balanced heat, sweetness, and umami just right. The fish tasted like it had come straight from the market that morning. We paired it all with a selection from their wine list, and the pairings were spot-on—crisp whites that cut through the richness beautifully.

The staff deserve a shoutout too: friendly, and attentive without hovering.

Overall, Izakaya is a fantastic new sushi spot that's punching way above its unassuming exterior. It's the kind of place that's perfect for a casual date night or a fun dinner with friends. I would definitely recommend it and can't wait to go back soon.

Thank you to the team for a great experience—keep doing what you're doing!

I loved the food here and the price wasn’t bad. Our waitress Vicky was lovely. I especially liked the crispy calimari it had such a good spice level to it. In total we got 5 rolls and calimari for $45 (including tip). Out of all the sushi places on this street I think this is one of the best, and I’ve lived here a long time!!!

Before you even eat, the atmosphere and design is great, and it sets the tone for the quality of the restaurant as a whole. The service was top notch, and they took good care us and made sure we were happy, which we definitely were once the food came out. If everything else wasn’t enough to convince you to come here, the food will be. 10/10

Amazing  place with amazing  sushi  awesome  sake and beer. The service  is  amazing. Loved every  minute of being there. Also love oysters  that they  serve.  I ordered  a dozen  but  easily  could  have ordered  more.  The sake is awesome I included  a picture  and it was cold sake. Also one of the great  beers  from Japan I tried  and was awesome. Definitely  a place  worth  coming  for.

These pictures  are from two visits

One of the visits  was for lunch time.

The restaurant is located in the Sheepshead Bay section of Brooklyn.  They prepare Japanese cuisine.  Soups, salads, appetizers, noodles, sushi, entrees, desserts and beverages are available.  During my order I was able to receive a discount from an offer attached to the menu.  I ordered the Izakaya pizza appetizer which consisted of a pancake with spicy salmon and special sauce.  The yuzu honey salmon entree with a side salad included asparagus and zucchini in a honey miso sauce.  The sushi platter entree consisted of nine pieces of sushi and one spicy tuna roll.  The food was well-prepared, tasty and fresh.

name: Salmon Noodle 3.0
document: Salmon Noodle 3.0. cuisine: Noodles. located in Staten_Island. with 5.0 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
I tried the crab ramen and the truffle salmon ramen. Both offered a unique experience, especially for those who prefer creamy, seafood-forward broths. The space was nice and clean with a casual vibe.

• Crab Ramen: The broth was creamy and on the sweeter side with a nice seafood flavor that wasn't fishy. I ordered the spicy version; while the slight heat was a good addition, it wasn't very spicy. I would have preferred the option to make it a bit hotter. The thick noodles had a good, firm texture, and the fried shallots added a nice crunch.
• Truffle Salmon Ramen: This was more savory and had a cheesy quality to it. The broth was thinner and not sweet. The salmon was well-cooked and flavorful. While I personally didn’t care for this flavor profile, I could see it being enjoyable for someone who likes those specific savory notes.

Overall, it’s a unique experience and worth trying if you're looking for a different, creamier take on ramen.

Incredible salmon ramen! Such a unique and rich umami flavor, you have to try it to understand. I had the spicy salmon ramen had the perfect kick and my friend said the regular was tasty too. The portion look small but was solid, I was definitely full. I also recommend their fried chicken, it came out steaming hot and crispy. Service was also great, very chill and nice people working there. Highly recommend!

Passed by many times and decided to drop by for a late lunch around 3PM. It is spacious inside and it was not busy so we were allowed to sit where we wanted. Kochiro San who served us recommended the truffle series with thick noodles so we ordered the truffle salmon and truffle crab with soft shell crab along with the salmon rice to start. Of the three, we would get the truffle salmon ramen or truffle crab ramen again on a return visit. The fried salmon with a touch of ikura on top of the mixed salmon rice was nice but the salmon that was mixed in the rice was a bit dry. The truffle and seafood umami  of the broth for the crab ramen stood out so I would recommend this for anyone who wants a stronger flavor. The truffle flavor for the salmon ramen is a bit lighter but also tasted sweeter.  The presentation is lovely and the bowl looks shallow but realized it is quite deep upon finishing the broth and noodles. The staff is friendly and we were able to enjoy a leisure lunch. Overall, worth the price and a repeat visit.

I had an incredible experience at Salmon Noodle 3.0 in Soho. The ramen here is on another level — rich, aromatic, and full of layered umami.

I tried the Truffle Lobster Ramen, which comes with half a roasted lobster, and the flavor was absolutely amazing. The broth is deep and comforting without being heavy, and the truffle aroma makes the whole bowl feel elevated. The Truffle Crab Ramen was equally impressive — especially the spicy version, which warms you up instantly on a cold day.

The atmosphere is cozy, calm, and perfect for enjoying a hot bowl of noodles. Service was friendly, and everything came out beautifully presented.

Their mochi dessert and yuzu liquor were the perfect finishing touches — refreshing, light, and balanced.

Definitely one of the best ramen spots in New York right now. A must-visit if you love seafood ramen or want something warm and comforting in Soho

We stumbled upon this new ramen place in downtown NYC right on the edge of Chinatown.  We were pleasantly surprised how good it was!  Our taste buds are on the stronger flavored side (but not salty or overpowering) so we really enjoyed how rich and flavorful the broth were!  We had the crab ramen truffle & shrimp ramen spicy (slightly only)—both delicious!  The staff, Jason & Sebastian were very helpful & courteous.  Clean & nicely lay out restaurant.  Will definitely come back.

document: KPOT Korean BBQ & Hot Pot. cuisine: Korean Hot Pot Barbeque. located in Staten_Island. with 4.0 stars (very good). price level is expensive.

google_reviews.text:
Dale was absolutely incredible! He was so friendly, entertaining, and genuinely attentive the entire time. He checked in with us often, made sure we were taken care of, and talked with us like we were all friends. His kindness and great energy made the whole experience even better.
The food was bomb and the soup was great too! Dale kept giving us awesome recommendations, and everything he suggested was delicious. KPOT is just awesome overall.
If you want to know what’s good, ask for Dale — he’ll definitely take care of you! Highly recommend!

So, first things first...

Our server's name was Amanda and she was fantastic!!! She made the entire experience better and was extremely hospitable, helpful, and kind. Thanks Amanda for taking our picture!

Regarding the rest of the review, the food and accompanying dishes at this location were great. We got the Korean BBQ only, but everything came out quickly and was very fresh. For folks reading, don't be afraid to ask your server to turn your cooker up a little higher! They often start them low to get things going and need adjusted throughout your meal.

All the bars and sauces were great too. They also had good drink specials/prices and a nice selection!

The only downside of this visit was the hostess/reception. From the moment we walked in, the hostess had her face tethered to the screen in front of her. We stood there for almost 6 minutes before another employee came over; we had to tell them that we were waiting to get on the wait list while the guests to the right of us were trying to respond to their table text.

I have no idea what maneuvering could've been happening in that tablet that was more important than the line of 10-15 guests building up in front of that hostess. My advice to her would be to look up every 60-90 seconds to greet people and help them get a table.

Finally, the restrooms could've used some tlc. The soap dispensers were nearly empty and one of the stalls had zero toilet tissue. This was at 7 PM, so they may want to have staff check them mid rush. Easier said than done, I know.

Short of those two things, the experience was great. Again, our server Amanda made the situation better through her diligent service with a smile.

We would visit again. 😊

This location in Fairfax actually seemed to have more selections of food than the one in Falls Church. Maybe we just came at a time when they had new things on the menu. The apple mango soju mule was really good. Dale was very friendly and charismatic. We wouldn’t have known this location was here because we never paid attention to the sign from the street. They should maybe put the sign in a more noticeable place. Other than that, loved it 🥰

For my first time having this experience , I would definitely come back. Awesome experience! Dale was our server and he was amazing. Actually, that’s an understatement. Extremely professional, personable and knowledgeable on his recommendations. Give that man a raise! (Lol) I enjoyed every part of it. The sauce selections and buffet was a great add on to this buffet. Ice cream was the cherry on top. Every worker was polite and working hard. Didn’t see one slacker. The music was even good (lol) Love love love this place. You’ll be seeing me again.

This spot offered a wider selection of meats compared to other Korean BBQ places I’ve been to, which was a nice plus. They also allow a 2-hour dining limit instead of the usual 90 minutes, so the experience felt more relaxed. Ordering was super convenient thanks to the tablet at the table. Once we submitted our selections, the food arrived within about five minutes, making it easy to pace the meal and keep the grilling going.

We stuck with the barbecue option, though they do require the entire table to choose hot pot if anyone opts for it, which seems pretty standard for places that offer both. Our server and the rest of the team were friendly, attentive, and quick to refill drinks, clear plates, and help with cooking the meat.

Every so often, they do a birthday celebration where the servers sing loudly and bring out a cake. It’s fun if you’re into that kind of energy, but it can be a bit loud or distracting if you’re not.

Overall, we had a good experience and enjoyed our time here.

Absolutely love this place. The food is amazing, very tasteful! My daughter and I love to come here for pho. Only thing I can say that might make this place better is maybe greeting people as they come in or atleast talk to them. It’s always so so quiet, which for me is perfect. Review: Bowls and Noodles

Great food, great ambiance, great service, great value, just GREAT!

Great hibachi restaurant with generous portions! Food is prepared over a grill in front of you and the cook entertains you.

name: Muteki Ramen
document: Muteki Ramen. cuisine: Ramen Noodles. located in Staten_Island. with 4.3 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text: Loved the ramen here. Best spot in the area. I had the Vegetarian Ramen. It has fried tofu pieces, thick noodles, loads of veggies, spring mix! I think it tastes better with the chili oil. Note: They do charge you a dollar for that. Anyway will definitely visit again.

My favorite place for ramen. I've tried almost everything on the menu, and it's all delicious! I'm very happy that there is a large selection of non-spicy ramen. The staff are always friendly, and the interior is nice!

I wanted to love this place because it's the closest thing to a traditional ramen shop (a la Ippudo, Ichiran, etc.) that DTJC has. Alas, the experience was as mixed as a controversial Sundance film.

Our Muteki Wings had good texture, but were supposed to come with a yuzu miso sauce--but it didn't taste like yuzu or miso, just lots of thick sugar.

My Spicy Tonkatsu Ramen was as bland as a potato salad with raisins: no spice, no umami, just a boringly unflavored broth with nice noodles. On the other hand, the Yuzu Shio Ramen was a winner and satisfied a deeply unaddressed part of my appetite that hasn't gotten a good yuzu-based broth since NYC's Mentoku Ramen closed (RIP forever and ever).

I'll likely come back...but with less excitement.

Muteki Ramen in Jersey City is such a lovely little find. It’s a small, cute spot tucked on a side street just off York, and it really feels like a cozy escape from the busier main roads.

I ordered a ramen ($19) and a pork bun ($9). At first glance, the prices felt slightly high, but when you think about the location—literally a stone’s throw from New York City—it’s actually very reasonable. The same meal across the river would easily be close to $50, so for the area, I think it’s a great value. The food itself was delicious. The broth was rich and comforting, and the pork bun was super tasty and well done.

Service was excellent. My waiter was attentive, kind, and very helpful, especially since it was my first time there and I wasn’t sure what to order. He made a great recommendation. The food also came out super fast, which I really appreciated.

The decor is another highlight. Inside, it genuinely feels like you’ve been transported to Tokyo—intimate, stylish, and warm. It’s the kind of place where you can just relax and enjoy your bowl of ramen.

A couple of small downsides:
•	There’s only one unisex bathroom, which can be a bit of a wait if it’s busy.
•	Parking in the area is a bit challenging, so plan ahead if you’re driving.

Overall, though, I loved my experience at Muteki Ramen and would absolutely come back. Great food, great service, and a fun Tokyo-style vibe right in Jersey City.

I stopped in to get lunch. When I arrived I walked in and was greeted. I was sat and served by Kelly and Kelvin and they were nice! I ordered the Thai Green Curry Ramen. It came out in about 15 minutes. I enjoyed the ramen and it's flavors! All in all a good experience!

The atmosphere makes you feel like you’ve stepped into another country or another time altogether. Japanese culture is beautifully preserved here, and the level of authenticity is honestly mind blowing. Words won’t do it justice, so I’ll be sharing photos and videos.
The food was incredible, authentic and mouth watering. so I’ll let the visuals speak for themselves.

One unforgettable moment was when my son accidentally ate a chunk of wasabi… I honestly panicked because I didn’t know what was happening and then Jennifer jumped in to action to attend to him and the chef suggested oolong tea after making sure he was fine without hesitation, I joined him in the pain by eating an even bigger chunk of wasabi which felt like dying and coming back to life yet even without oolong tea, took it like a champ! I told him that’s how the OG does it. So I could remind him that when he starts fighting with me lol. A core memory unlocked. My son also learned how to use chopsticks in under three minutes n so did I.
The chefs did an outstanding job the food impressed my son, which says a lot because he’s not easy to please.
I rambled on for so long just because the entire experience was amazing.
I can’t thank the GM Brian enough for having an excellent team of staff that made me and my son feel at home and for giving us an unbelievable amount of joy. We are eagerly waiting for the next experience at the hotel.

As a newly engaged couple, my fiancé and I decided to host our parents’ meetup dinner at AOI, and we were blown away by the service and hospitality. Our waiter Ben was an incredible host and made us all feel so comfortable— he even memorized all our names by the end of the night.

We ordered the sushi dinner + sashimi boat w additional appetizers and rolls and enjoyed every dish. We particularly loved the uni and spicy scallop roll. Thank you AOI for making this a special night for us to remember!

Aoi Japanese Restaurant & Bar is an absolute gem! From the moment you step in, the atmosphere feels warm and inviting, with an authenticity that instantly transports you to Japan.

The fact that the owner, sushi chef, and staff are all Japanese really shines through in both the hospitality and the cuisine.

The food is nothing short of outstanding. Every bite was fresh, full of depth, and crafted with care. The menu is refreshingly authentic, offering a true taste of Japan that I have never found in NJ. Dining here honestly made me feel like I was on vacation in Japan without leaving town.

If you’re looking for exceptional Japanese food paired with a genuine cultural experience, Aoi is the place!

Made 6pm reservation for two on Saturday. We arrived on time, had to wait for a few minutes to get seated because there were only 3 wait staff including the manager working. Placed order for 5 items including 2 entrees and 3 appetizers. 1 appetizers came after about 20 minutes, 1 entree came out 15 to 20 minutes later, another appetizer(sashimi sampler) came after another 10 minutes, second entree came out 10 minutes later, which was about an hour after order was placed, the last appetizer didn't come out. The waitress actually checked with us whether we got the appetizer, then she came back to ask whether we wanted sashimi or sushi, although the photo showed the sushi version. We told her we wanted sushi, but it never came. The wait staff were okay, the restaurant got busier after 6:30pm. Management should work on staffing issue. Okay fish, but we paid Manhattan price. 2 entrees and two appetizers, no drinks, the bill came out to 150 including a 18% tips.

If you want authentic Japanese and don't want to travel to NYC or northern Jersey, Aoi is the place to go. High quality sashimi and sushi. I always go for the Chirashi bowl. For rolls, I go with the caterpillar roll. They do omakase (I believe on the weekends only) and offer hot noodle soups and rice dishes. For dessert, you can never go wrong with the black sesame panacota!

name: Ramen Misoya
document: Ramen Misoya. cuisine: Ramen. located in Staten_Island. with 4.7 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text:
It had probably been close to ten years since my last visit to Ramen Misoya, and I still remembered it as the best ramen I’d had in the suburbs. After moving to the city and then bouncing around to a few different states over the past few years, we were finally back home for the holidays and craving a comforting bowl of ramen. This was the first place that came to mind.

I vividly remember the lines out the door back in the day, so we made sure to get there right when they opened. We were seated immediately, which felt like a win. I also noticed their menu has expanded quite a bit since my last visit, which was a nice surprise.

And I can confidently say they are still hands down the best ramen in the suburbs. The broth was rich and flavorful, the noodles perfectly cooked, and everything tasted just as good as I remembered, if not better. Service was quick and friendly, and even the hot green tea (whatever brand they use) absolutely hit the spot.

Overall, a 10/10 experience. So glad this place is still just as amazing after all these years. Already looking forward to coming back. 🍜

Their Haikido Spicy Ramen is absolutely outstanding—rich, flavorful broth with the perfect level of heat, and every bite feels thoughtfully crafted. You can really taste the depth and balance that sets it apart from other ramen spots. On top of that, the service was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. Great food, great vibes, and great people. Can’t wait to come back!

There’s ramen, and then there’s RAMEN! Came here on a whim craving ramen, and this place did not disappoint. Everything was so fresh, the broth was rich in flavor. Overall, it was a great experience. Will definitely come back.

It is very good, solid, ramen; however, not the best I have ever had.  You can tell this place is popular.  It is a small hole-in-the-wall place in the middle of a strip mall.  There is not too much seating inside.  So there is a kiosk set up at the doorway to place yourself on a virtual waiting line.

The service is bare bones.  The menus are on the table.  The servers take your order, drop off your food, and take care of the bill.  Serviceable, but not much extra.

The ramen itself is above average, but not the best I have had.  And maybe it is just a matter of each individual’s palate.  The broth was flavorful, but I have had others with much more depth.  The charu has a grilled taste.  This is different than other charu I have had which had more a velvety fatty taste to them.  And I absolutely do not understand the pieces of French fries in the ramen.  The longer they sit in the broth, the mushier they became.  And I did not like the fried potato taste with the ramen.  It seemed out of place.

As popular a this ramen restaurant seems, they seem to be doing something right.  As I said, to me with my palate, I think this is an above average bowl of ramen.  I enjoyed my time here.

You’re welcomed in and seated as soon as you come in, which I think is super nice! The food tastes amazing, I mean my friends and I couldn’t put the chopsticks down. 😅 Plus, bowls are big enough so you get full and get to take leftovers home!

document: Takumi Sushi. cuisine: Japanese. located in Staten_Island. with 4.6 stars (exceptional).

google_reviews.text: This contemporary sushi bar has great sushi, but also offers satisfactory dishes from the kitchen.  My wife had the maki rolls which she said were excellent.  I had the beef terriyaki.  It was served with the terriyaki sauce on the side.  I prefer the beef to be smothered in the sauce as it helps to tenderize the meat.  It also makes a more inviting presentation.  The steak was also a bit fatty on some of the pieces.  I had started with the shrimp tempura appetizer.  This was light, crunchy and delicious.  It was also a large enough portion which was perfect for sharing.  My son had the fried rice which was also a generous portion and was tasty.  The service was a bit spotty.  Although very friendly and hard working, our server did not have a full grasp of the menu.  On one occasion, my son had to remind our server to bring the miso soup which came with the fried rice.  On another occasion, my white rice suddenly appeared with my terriyaki when I was almost done.  If you want excellent sushi, and decent items off of the kitchen menu, then Takumi can be a wise choice.

Got delivery from here and these were some really nice rolls.  The Hurts roll was nice being a bit of shrimp tempura deluxe roll. Got the hot mama roll which was a lot like a yummy roll. Definite favorite was the Takumi roll.  Very nice flavors.  I haven't had anything like it.  Truffle with tuna avocado and some other stuff.  Absolutely delicious.  Everything was presented nicely and would love to visit sometime to experience the atmosphere and maybe some of their other options.

The pasta with shrimp was slightly on the drier side, but still satisfying and generous in portion. The real standout, though, was the seafood risotto — incredibly flavorful and so filling I couldn’t even finish the plate.

Overall, Piccante offers generous portions, comforting flavors, and a laid-back vibe that makes it a great spot for a casual Italian dinner in Bay Ridge. I’d definitely come back to try more from the menu.

This has became one of our favorite places to eat at. My Husband and I go there once a week and we either have Mark as our waiter or Nicole as our waitress. They are both personable and make us feel so welcomed and loved.The food is absolutely incredible. We have tried so many of Their dishes as well as desserts, and I love every single one of them. The decor, ambience dim lighting and brick walls just makes It feel so cozy, romantic, and just gives me a happy feeling. This is a must try in Bay Ridge if you haven’t tried them already!

The reason I gave it 4 stars was the price. The pasta prices are reasonable considering they’re homemade and the portion is big but the prices for appetizers I find to be ridiculous. The calamari was $19 and I find that to be a bit much. A lot of the appetizers cost that much which is crazy. For 3 people and 2 alcoholic drinks we paid $156. Overall the food is great.

Finally got a chance to check this place out. The new location is really nice and thankfully is able to hold many more tables. Nice crowd for a Monday night. It’s great to see a local business upgrade to a bigger place in such a tough industry. Food was great, service was great. Looking forward to trying more dishes for sure ! Highly recommend

*** update ****
After dozens of visits since the initial review I can confidently call Piccante one of my favorites in the neighborhood. Food and desserts are delicious! Mark and Nicole always provide top tier service and make us feel like family. Keep it up!

I visited Picante at Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, and I have to say, this place is absolutely amazing. From the moment you step inside, the atmosphere is warm, inviting, and full of charm. It has a cozy Italian vibe that instantly makes you feel like you’ve been transported straight to Italy, right here in Brooklyn.

The staff are incredibly kind, attentive, and professional. Every interaction felt genuine, friendly, and welcoming. They make you feel at home with their service, always checking in with the perfect balance of care and professionalism. My server, in particular, was outstanding truly one of the best I’ve ever had.

And the food? Absolutely delicious. Every dish bursts with authentic Italian flavors, rich and fresh, and you can taste the quality in every bite. It’s like having the real taste of Italy right in your mouth, in the heart of Brooklyn.

For dessert, I tried the pistachio tiramisu paired with an espresso, recommended by my Great Server “Liza” and it was nothing short of heavenly. The balance of flavors, the creaminess, and the perfect nutty touch of pistachio made it unforgettable. It’s a dessert that proves the chef has true artistry, especially with pastries. Compliments to the chef for creating such a masterpiece.

This restaurant isn’t just good, it’s phenomenal. The combination of the food, the atmosphere, and the service makes Picante a true hidden gem in Bay Ridge. If I could give it more than 5 stars, I would this is a 10 out of 10 experience. Highly recommended for anyone who wants amazing food, a great vibe, and outstanding service.
Thank You Liza

name: All' Assassina
document: All' Assassina. cuisine: Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 4.4 stars (very good).

google_reviews.text:
First time here, and honestly, it was such a pleasant surprise! At first, we almost left because the setup made it seem like a fast-food pasta spot, but I’m so glad we stayed. The staff were super nice and helpful, and the food came out hot and fresh.

The garlic cheese flatbread was amazing — soft, cheesy, and perfect with the marinara sauce. I got the chicken alfredo with linguine, and it was incredibly creamy and rich — super cheesy and flavorful. The chicken pesto pasta with roasted red peppers, caramelized onions, and mushrooms was also delicious, with a strong pesto flavor (in a good way!).

The owner was there and she was so kind — we sat by the window, and she even came over to ask if we wanted the curtains down since the sun was shining right in. Little touches like that made the experience even better.

Big portions, great service, and everything tasted freshly made. I just wish they had more drink options, but overall, definitely worth it. I’d go back for sure — and next time, I’m trying the desserts!

We were watching ATK (America's Test Kitchen) and there was an episode about preparing Spaghetti all'Assassina (Assassin's Spaghetti). So we looked up where we can taste it in NYC before trying to recreate it in the kitchen - the closest place to Manhattan is in Union, NJ. So we went on a (short) road trip. It's a 30' drive from the city.

When you pull up to All' Assassina in Union it is very unassuming- there is a Greek restaurant in the corner called Souvlaqueria with the same owner.

The interior is unpretentious- bright and more of an upscale pizza parlor feel. You order at the counter and then they bring the order to your table. They have regular and San Pellegrino flavored drinks as well as Coca Cola in glass bottles. If you don't want one of their signature dishes, the menu at All’ Assassina is highly customizable. You can build your own pasta dish by selecting a fresh sauce, fresh pasta, proteins, and up to three toppings.

We ordered the meatballs and their signature pasta that shares the name of the restaurant.  The spicy, partially pan-fried spaghetti dish is as unusual as it is incredibly delicious. It is the perfect combination of texture and spice and the optional Stracciatella Cheese balances the heat.

The meatballs were also amazing - you can taste the freshness in the tomato sauce - it's just right and the bread basket is served warm - the perfect complement for dipping.

We met the owner Marinos who gave us a taste of his short rib ragu which was off the hook!

The meal ended with homemade cheesecake with berries and a berry sauce - insane. And of course espresso with just the right crema.

Next time you are thinking of going to Belmont Tavern or another Italian destination in the tri-state area, go here, you will not be disappointed. The food is amazing, the atmosphere is bright, it's BYO in case you want a bottle of wine, it's a great value, and the staff is friendly and attentive. Definitely worth the trip from NYC!

The restaurant celebrates its two year anniversary on March 7, 2026 and I hope it's there for many years to come. We will be back.

Blown away. The pasta here is killer! Fresh ingredients, mouthwatering veggies in my pesto chicken penne. We wandered in here by chance after a swim meet. And now, we will need to make the drive out here just for pasta. You will not regret it. And the staff are muah!

Some of the best customer service I've ever had from a counter. Was patient and super knowledgeable about all the dishes and made recommendations. I had the Chicken Parm with fettuccini. It was huge but not super flat like those fake places do. Crispy and juicy. Yum!
The best pasta I've had in a while. The owners were kind and they made everyone's day better. It didn't feel robotic more inclusive.

name: KP Sarelli’s
document: KP Sarelli’s. cuisine: Italian. located in Staten_Island. with 4.1 stars (very good). price level is moderate.

google_reviews.text:
The Eggplant Parmesan was Very good with the hot Spaghetti..  The bread hot and fluffy with butter... Sal was very attentive and Russell also... The atmosphere great with soft oldies music! I will be back to try the appetizers and dessert!! Thank you Sal.. AMARETTO di SARONNO best Italian liquor on the planet! Fantasia SUSANA is the Best Salad on the MENU !!!... Eggplant Rollatini best appetizer on the Menu...
Joaquin and Rosa very good waitors...At my big birthday bash we ordered appetizers, all delicious plus the spinach and special roasted potatoes!! Great Party !🎉🌲🎁🥳... Today December 28 we had the Divine SALMON... WOWOWOW melted in my mouth... Full of great flavors 😋 Always great service!

Our friends from Bayonne introduced us to this place. The restaurant has been open here at this very location for generations. Besides their chairs and tables being old, which is expected for how old the restaurant is, everything edible is fresh! Every bite is flavorful and satisfying. The service was quick, and the waiters and waitress were very friendly and paid attention to us. We came back from the beach and were just chugging water but they refilled our water bottle timely constantly.

Came here with my parents. I really like this place! So warm and cozy inside. It was pretty busy on a Saturday night, we didn’t have a reservation but there was a table available and we also got parking on the street outside. Next time I’m going to call for a reservation!

Waiter was super nice and funny. They have an option for half pitcher of sangria for only $14! It lasted for 5 glasses of sangria! The sangria was very sweet but I liked it.

Bread is given for the table. My chicken parm was good, it wasn’t a huge portion though. And the tomato sauce was a bit too spicy for me. The chicken was thin, juicy and tender. My mom’s chicken wasn’t as tender it and it was more chewy, it was chunks of chicken, It was the pollo scarpariello. My dad got the halibut and my husband got the sole, the sole was my fav dish! It was so soft and the flavor was light and it tasted very good. Desserts were affordable and tasty. Nothing spectacular but still very good.

All in all the food and drinks were great and I would go back!

I love this place amazing food…service is amazing…. Sal and everybody here is amazing. Never fails. Thank you for the amazing food!!!!! Prices are also great!!! If you’re ever in Bayonne, you must try!!! A beautiful gem in Bayonne
Amazing delicious authentic Italian food in a cozy restaurant. The service is great and the ambiance is nice and chill. The prices are very reasonable too. I’d definitely go back again.
